is conducive to Naraka. Hence one who seeks lasting welfare should avoid filthy lucre.

## \|\| 1.32.42 \|\|

*yorthena sādhyate dharmaḥ kṣayiṣṇuḥ sa prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ punastapasā sādhyaḥ sa mokṣāyeti me matiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Virtue achieved through wealth is well-known as transitory. What is achieved through penance is conducive to salvation. This is my opinion.

## \|\| 1.32.43 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*jīryaṃti jīryataḥ keśā daṃtā jīryaṃti jīryataḥ \|*  
*cakṣuḥ śrotre tathā puṃsastṛṣṇaikā taruṇāyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

43\. As one grows old, the hairs get decayed and fall off; the teeth grow shaky and fall off. So also the eyes and ears of a man. But thirst (covetousness) alone remains ever young.

## \|\| 1.32.44 \|\|

*sūcyā sūtraṃ yathā vastraṃ saṃcārayati sūcikā \|*  
*tadvatsaṃsārasūtraṃ ca vāṃchayātmā nayatyasau \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Just as a needle puts a thread through cloth by means of its eye, so also the Ātman stitches the Cosmic thread through desire.

## \|\| 1.32.45 \|\|

*yathā śṛṃgaṃ hi kāyena varddhamānena vardhate \|*  
*tadvattṛṣṇāpi vittena varddhamānena varddhate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Just as a horn (of an animal) grows as the body grows up, so also, thirst (greed) increases as the riches grow.

## \|\| 1.32.46 \|\|

*anaṃtapārā duṣpūrā tṛṣṇā duḥkhaśatāvahā \|*  
*adharmabahulā caiva tasmāttāṃ parivarjayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thirst (greed) is unlimited, difficult to be fulfilled and it involves hundreds of misdeeds. Hence one should eschew it.

## \|\| 1.32.47 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭaḥ kena cālyo'sti phalairapi vivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sarvopīndriyalaulyena saṃkaṭe bhramati dvijāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Gautama said:

47\. By whom can a man of contentment be agitated, even if he is deprived of the fruit? O Brāhmaṇas, all ordinary persons get involved in difficulties due to the cravings of the sense-organs.

## \|\| 1.32.48 \|\|

*sarvatra saṃpadastasya saṃtuṣṭaṃ yasya mānasam \|*  
*upānadgūḍhapādasya nanu carmāstṛteva bhūḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. To a man whose mind is contented there are riches everywhere. If one has protected one’s feet with shoes, one will find the whole ground covered with leather.

## \|\| 1.32.49 \|\|

*saṃtoṣāmṛtatṛptānāṃ yatsukhaṃ śāṃtacetasām \|*  
*kutastaddhanalubdhānāmitaścetaśca dhāvatām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Men of quiescent mind, pleased with the nectar of contentment have great happiness. How can people covetous of wealth who run about here and there, get that happiness?

## \|\| 1.32.50 \|\|

*asaṃtoṣaḥ paraṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham \|*  
*sukhārthī puruṣastasmātsaṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Discontent is the greatest misery and contentment is the greatest happiness. Hence a person seeking happiness should always be contented.

## \|\| 1.32.51 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*kāmaṃ kāmayamānasya yadi kāmaḥ sa sidhyati \|*  
*tathānyo jāyate puṃsastatkṣaṇādeva kalpitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

51\. One may eagerly seek the fulfilment of one wish. If that wish is realized, another one of the same sort immediately arises in men.

## \|\| 1.32.52 \|\|

*na jātu kāmī kāmānāṃ sahasrairapi tuṣyati \|*  
*haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva vāṃchā tasya vivardhate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Never does any passionate person feel contented with thousands of wishes fulfilled. His desires become increased just as a fire blazes when offerings of clarified butter are made.

## \|\| 1.32.53 \|\|

*kāmānabhilaṣanmohānna naraḥ sukhamāpnuyāt \|*  
*śyenālayatarucchāyāṃ vrajanniva kapiñjalaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A man cherishing more and more desires, out of delusion, never attains happiness, like a Kapiñjala bird (small Cātaka or Ṭiṭṭiri) that resorts to the shade of a tree on which vulture has its abode (nest).

## \|\| 1.32.54 \|\|

*nityaṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ yo bhuṅkte pṛthivīmimām \|*  
*tulyāśmakāścanaścaiva sa kṛtārtho mahīpateḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A person viewing a piece of stone and a lump of gold as equals is more blessed and contented than a king who always enjoys the earth encircled by oceans.

## \|\| 1.32.55 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*yo'rthaṃ prāpyādhamo vipraḥ śocitavyepi hṛṣyati \|*  
*na ca paśyati mandātmā narakaṃ cā kutobhayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

55\. A base Brāhmaṇa who feels delighted after obtaining wealth, although it is something to be regretted, is a dull-witted person who pretending to be fearless does not see Naraka.

## \|\| 1.32.56 \|\|

*pratigrahasamarthānāṃ nivṛttānāṃ pratigrahāt \|*  
*ya eva dadatāṃ lokāsta evāpratigṛhṇatām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Persons who deserve gifts but who abstain from receiving them, will attain those regions which the donors themselves attain.

## \|\| 1.32.57 \|\|

*arundhatyuvāca \|*  
*bisataṃturyathā'nanto nālamāsādya saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tṛṣṇā caivamanādyantā sthitā dehe śarīriṇām \|\| 57 \|\|*

Arunddhatī \[Arundhatī?\] said:

57\. Just as many lotus-fibres occupy the stalk of a lotus, similarly beginningless and endless covetousness occupies the body of beings.

## \|\| 1.32.58 \|\|

*yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ \|*  
*yā'sau prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Happiness belongs to a person who eschews covetousness that is very difficult to forego for persons of wicked mind-covetousness that never fades away even if a person gets old and that is a veritable ailment ending only with the end of the life.

## \|\| 1.32.59 \|\|

*caṇḍovāca \|\| sarpādivaddhanādyasmādbibhyatīme mameśvarāḥ \|*  
*yatastato viśeṣeṇa kasmāttasmādbhayaṃ mama \|\| 59 \|\|*

Caṇḍā said:

59\. My Lords are afraid of wealth as though of serpents. Hence especially why should I have fear from it.

## \|\| 1.32.60 \|\|

*paśumukha uvāca \|\| yadācaranti vidvāṃsaḥ sadā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tadeva viduṣā kāryamātmano hitamicchatā \|\| 60 \|\|*

Paśumukha said:

60\. A wise man who desires his own welfare should follow that which learned men devoted to piety adopt and practise.

## \|\| 1.32.61 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā hemagarbhāṇi tyaktvā tāni phalāni ca \|*  
*ṛṣayo jagmuranyatra sarva eva dṛḍhavratāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

Sūta said:

61\. After saying this, all those sages of steady resolve abandoned those fruits with gold pieces stuffed in and went away.

## \|\| 1.32.62 \|\|

*camatkārapurekṣetre viviśuste tataḥ param \|*  
*dadṛśuḥ sahasā prāptaṃ parivrājaṃ śunomukham \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They entered the holy place of Camatkārapura thereafter. They saw a sage Śunomukha (Dog-faced) who arrived there accidentally.

## \|\| 1.32.63 \|\|

*tenaiva sahitāstatra gatvā kiñcidvanāntaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭavantastato hṛdyaṃ saraḥ paṃkajaśobhitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Accompanying him they reached another forest region. They saw a charming lake too, beautified with lotuses.

## \|\| 1.32.64 \|\|

*tato bubhukṣayāviṣṭā bisānyādāya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*tīre nikṣipya sarasaścakruḥ puṇyāṃ jala kriyām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Overwhelmed with great hunger, they collected a lot of lotus-stalks, placed them on the banks of the lake and took their holy plunge.

## \|\| 1.32.65 \|\|

*athottīryajalātsarve te sametya parasparam \|*  
*bisāni tānyapaśyanta idaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. They emerged from the water and met together once again. Unable to see the lotus-stalks they spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.32.66 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kena kṣudhābhitaptānāmasmākaṃ nirdayātmanā \|*  
*mṛṇālāni samastāni sthānādasmāddhṛtāni ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

The sages said:

66\. Who is that ruthless soul by whom all the lotus-stalks belonging to us have been taken away from this place?

## \|\| 1.32.67 \|\|

*te śaṃkamānā anyonyamṛṣayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*pracakruḥ śapathānraudrānātmanaḥ praviśuddhaye \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Suspecting one another those sages of esteemed holy vows pledged their words awfully to clear themselves.

## \|\| 1.32.68 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*sarvabhakṣaḥ sadā so'stu nyāsalobhaṃ karotu vā \|*  
*kūṭasākṣitvamabhye tu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Kaśyapa said:

68\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be an indiscriminate eater of all sorts of things always or one who misappropriates the deposit kept in trust or let him practises perjury.

## \|\| 1.32.69 \|\|

*dharmaṃ karotu daṃbhena rājānaṃ copasevatām \|*  
*madhumāṃsaṃ sadāśnātu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. May the stealer of the lotus-fibres be a hypocrite in the practice of piety; may he be a servile attendant of a king and may he always eat meat and drink liquor.

## \|\| 1.32.70 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*anṛtau maithunaṃ yātu divā vāpyatha parvaṇi \|*  
*atithiḥ syāttato'nyonyaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

70\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who indulges in sexual intercourse outside the period enjoined after the days of menstruation, or during the day time or during Parvan days. Let him be a mutual guest with another.

## \|\| 1.32.71 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*yodhigamya guroḥ śāstraṃ niṣkrayaṃ na prayacchati \|*  
*tasyainasā sa yuktostu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

71\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks incur the sin of that person who, after getting instruction in the scriptural texts from a preceptor, does not give the prescribed fee.

## \|\| 1.32.72 \|\|

*nṛśaṃso'stu sa sarvatra samṛddhyā cāpyahaṃkṛtaḥ \|*  
*matsarī piśunaścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. May the thief of the lotus-stalks be a ruthless and wicked person; may he be one arrogant due to prosperity all round; may he be inimically jealous; and may he be a slanderer.

## \|\| 1.32.73 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*ekākī mṛṣṭama śnātu praśaṃsyādatha cātmanaḥ \|*  
*vedavikrayakartāstu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

73\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who enjoys by himself delicious dishes, or who indulges in boasting about himself or a person who sells the Vedic text.

## \|\| 1.32.74 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*kanyāṃ yacchatu vṛddhāya sa bhūyādvṛṣalī patiḥ \|*  
*astu vārdhuṣiko nityaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

74\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who gives a girl in marriage to an old man, who becomes the paramour of a Śūdra woman, or one who maintains himself by usary always.

## \|\| 1.32.75 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*sa gṛhṇātvavikādānaṃ karotu hayavikrayam \|*  
*prakaro tu gurorniṃdāṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

Gautama said:

75\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who accepts the gift of an ewe, one who sells horses or one who censures the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.32.76 \|\|

*atriruvāca \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ nityaṃ durmatiḥ so'vamanyatām \|*  
*śūdraṃ pṛcchatu dharmārthaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

Atri said:

76\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be an evil-minded person who always insults his father and mother or one who consults a Śūdra in religious matters.

## \|\| 1.32.77 \|\|

*pratiśrutya na yo dadyādbrāhmaṇāya gavādikam \|*  
*tasyainasā sa yujyeta bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\|\|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who incurs the sin of not making the gift of cows etc., to a Brāhmaṇa after having promised the same before.

## \|\| 1.32.78 \|\|

*aruṃdhatyuvāca \|*  
*karotu patyuḥ pūrvaṃ sā bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*nārī duṣṭasamācārā bisastainyaṃ karoti yā \|\| 78 \|\|*

Arundhatī said:

78\. May the woman who steals the lotus-stalks be on a par with that woman of evil conduct who takes food or goes to bed before her husband.

## \|\| 1.32.79 \|\|

*caṇḍovāca \|*  
*svāminaḥ pratikūlāstu dharmadveṣaṃ karotu ca \|*  
*sādhudveṣaparā caiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yā \|\| 79 \|\|*

Caṇḍā said:

79\. May the woman who steals the lotus-stalks be on a par with a woman engaged in hating good people and pious activities as well as being antagonistic to her lord and master.

## \|\| 1.32.80 \|\|

*paśumukha uvāca \|*  
*svāmidroharato nityaṃ sa bhūyātpāpakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*sādhu dveṣaparaścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

Paśumukha said:

80\. May the man who steals the lotus-stalks be on a par with a sinful man engaged in hating good people and acting treacherously against his master.

## \|\| 1.32.81 \|\|

*śunomukha uvāca \|*  
*vedānsa paṭhatu nyāyādgṛhasthaḥ syātpriyātithiḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ vadatu cājasraṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

Śunomukha said:

81\. May the stealer of the lotus-stalks be one who tells the truth always, who recites the Vedas properly and a householder who likes his guests.

## \|\| 1.32.82 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*iṣṭa eva dvijātīnāṃ yastvayā śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*bisastainyaṃ hi cāsmākaṃ tannūnaṃ bhavatā kṛtam \|\| 82 \|\|*

The sages said:

82\. The way in which you pledged the words is what is actually desired by the twice-born. Hence it is certain that the theft of our lotus-stalks is committed by you.

## \|\| 1.32.83-84 \|\|

*śunomukha uvāca \|*  
*mayā hṛtāni sarveṣāṃ bisānīmāni vo dvijāḥ \|*  
*dharmānvai śrotukāmena māṃ jānīta puraṃdaram \|\| 83 \|\|*

*yuṣmākaṃ parituṣṭo'smi lobhābhāvāddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsvargaṃ mayā sārddhaṃ śīghramāgamyatāmiti \|ा \|\| 84 \|\|*

Śunomukha said:

83-84. O Brāhmaṇas, your lotus-stalks have been taken by me because I wanted to listen to the statement about Dharma. Know ye all that I am Purandara (Indra), O excellent Brāhmaṇas. I am indeed much pleased with the absence of covetousness in you all. Hence, all of you be pleased to accompany me to heaven quickly.

## \|\| 1.32.85-86 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*mokṣamārgaṃ samāsaktā na vayaṃ svargalipsavaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttapaścariṣyāmaḥ sarasīha vimuktaye \|\| 85 \|\|*

*pūrṇā sāgaraparyaṃtāṃ caritvā pṛthivī mimām \|*  
*prāṇayātrāṃ prakurvāṇā mṛṇālairmunisattamāḥ \|*  
*tasmādgaccha tava śreyo bhūyādasmātsamāgamāt \|\| 86 \|\|*

The sages said:

85-86. We are inclined towards the path of salvation. We are not enamoured of heavenly pleasures. So, we are going to perform penance here at this lake for the purpose of liberation. We are among those excellent sages who undertake pilgrimage all over the earth bounded by the oceans. Sustaining ourselves by means of lotus-stalks. Hence do go. Let this association do good to you.

## \|\| 1.32.87 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syātkadācidapi suvratāḥ \|*  
*tasmādgṛhṇīta yaccitte sadābhīṣṭaṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

Śakra said:

87\. O sages of excellent vows, viewing me shall never be fruitless. Hence accept a boon whatever has been cherished in the heart for a long time by you.

## \|\| 1.32.88-89 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\|*  
*āśramo'yaṃ suvikhyāto bhūyācchakra mahītale \|*  
*nāmnāsmākaṃ tathā nṛṇāṃ sarvapātakanāśanaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*vayaṃ sthāsyāmahe nityamatraiva surasattama \|*  
*tapo'rthaṃ bhāvitātmāno yāvanmokṣagatirdhruvā \|\| 89 \|\|*

The sages said:

88-89. O Śakra, may this hermitage be well-known on the entire earth after our name. May it be the destroyer of all sins of men. O most excellent one among Suras, we shall stay here only for ever for the sake of penance. We shall maintain the purity of the soul. We shall be here until the achievement of salvation becomes certain.

## \|\| 1.32.90 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*trailokye'pi suvikhyāta āśramo vo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tathā kāmapradaścaiva lokānāṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 90 \|\|*

Indra said:

90\. Your hermitage will become well-known in all the three worlds. It shall fulfill the desires of all the people.

## \|\| 1.32.91 \|\|

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya śrāddhamatra kariṣyati \|*  
*śrāvaṇe paurṇamāsyāṃ ca sa taṃ sarvamavā psyati \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Whoever performs a Śrāddha here on the Full-Moon day in the month of Śrāvaṇa with any desire in the heart, shall surely attain it entirely.

## \|\| 1.32.92 \|\|

*niṣkāmo vā naro yastu śrāddhaṃ dānamathāpi vā \|*  
*prakariṣyati mokṣaṃ sa samavāpsyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A man devoid of any desire who performs Śrāddha or Dāna rite shall undoubtedly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.32.93 \|\|

*ye cātra dehaṃ tyakṣyaṃti yuṣmākaṃ cāśrame śubhe \|*  
*api pāpasamāyuktāste yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Those who cast off their bodies in this splendid hermitage of yours will attain the greatest goal even if they are sinners.

## \|\| 1.32.94-95 \|\|

*iṃgudairbadarairvāpi bilvairbhallātakairapi \|*  
*pitṝnuddiśya yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kariṣyati samāhitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*sa yāsyati parāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ stūyamānaśca kiṃnaraiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. One who performs Śrāddha with mental concentration and purity using Iṅgudas, Badaras, Bilvas and Bhallātakas (cashewnuts) with ancestors in view will attain the greatest goal inaccessible even to Devas. He shall be rid of all sins and be eulogized by Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.32.96 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sahasrākṣastaiḥ sarvairabhinaṃditaḥ \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ te'pi sthitāstatra dvijottamāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

Sūta said:

96\. Saying thus the Thousand-eyed One vanished after being duly commended by them. Those excellent Brāhmaṇas stayed there itself.

## \|\| 1.32.97 \|\|

*tataḥ kāle gate te'pi kṛtvā tīvraṃ mahattapaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. In due course of time, by performing great and severe penance, they attained the greatest region bereft of old age and death.

## \|\| 1.32.98 \|\|

*taistatra sthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanādeva naraḥ pāpādvimucyate \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas was installed by them there. Merely by viewing it, a man is rid sins.

## \|\| 1.32.99 \|\|

*yastalliṃgaṃ punarbhaktyā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*arcayetsa dhruvaṃ muktiṃ prāpnoti dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, one who adores that Liṅga with devotion and offers flowers, incense and unguent shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.32.100 \|\|

*etatpavitra māyuṣyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*saptarṣoṇāṃ samākhyātamāśramasyānukīrtanam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. This description of the hermitage of the Seven Sages is sacred, conducive to long life, and destructive of all sins. It has been duly narrated.

## Chapter 33 - Greatness of Agastya’s Hermitage

## \|\| 1.33.1-4 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*agastyasyāśramo'nyosti tathā tatra dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭhati viśvātmā svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ caitramāse divākaraḥ \|*  
*svayamabhyetya deveśaṃ pūjayatyeva śaṃkaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasmādanyo'pi yastasyāṃ bhaktyā cāgatya śaṃkaram \|*  
*tameva pūjayedbhaktyā sa yāti devamandiram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*pitarastasya tṛpyaṃte pitṛmedhe kṛte yathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Note: This story is based on Mbh, Vana, chs. 101-105. Mbh does not mention Camatkārapura. But the Purāṇa author locates Agastya’s hermitage here for the glorification of this place. Mbh, Vana, 87.20 locates the Āśrama near Nasik (Maharashtra).

Sūta said:

1-4. There is another hermitage there, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that of Agastya. It is there that Lord Maheśvara himself, the immanent soul of the universe, abides.

On the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Cakra, Sun-god himself comes there and worships Śaṅkara, the Lord of Devas. Hence anyone else who comes there and adores devoutly Śaṅkara on that day, goes to the place of the Lord.

If any one duly performs Śrāddha with ardour and faith, the Pitṛs become pleased with him as when Pitṛmedha is performed.

## \|\| 1.33.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*agastyasyāśramaṃ prāpya kasmāddevo divākaraḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāṃ prakurute vadaitanme suvistaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. Why does Sun-god come to the hermitage of Agastya and perform the rite of circumambulation? Narrate this in detail to us.

## \|\| 1.33.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kathayāmi kathāmetāṃ śṛṇuta dvija sattamāḥ \|*  
*asti viṃdhya iti khyātaḥ parvataḥ pṛthivītale \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. I shall narrate this story. Listen, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. There is a mountain on the earth well-known as Vindhya.

## \|\| 1.33.7 \|\|

*yasya vṛkṣāgraśākhāyāṃ saṃlagnāstaraṇeḥ karāḥ \|*  
*puṣpapūgā ivādhaḥsthairlakṣyaṃte mugdhasi ddhakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The rays of the Sun falling on the tops of the trees on this mountain are taken to be a mass of flowers by the confused Siddhaka, stationed beneath it.

## \|\| 1.33.8 \|\|

*anabhijñāstamisrasya yasya sānunivāsinaḥ \|*  
*ratnaprabhāpraṇunnasya kṛṣṇapakṣaniśāsvapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Even during the nights of the dark half of the month, the inhabitants of the ridges of this mountain are never aware of darkness as it is dispelled by the lustre of the jewels.

## \|\| 1.33.9 \|\|

*yasya sānuṣu muṃcaṃto bhāṃti puṣpāṇi pādapāḥ \|*  
*vāyuvegavaśānnūnaṃ nīraugha nīradā iva \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When the trees drop down flowers on its ridges as the gusts of wind blow, they appear like clouds pouring down a flood of waters.

## \|\| 1.33.10 \|\|

*yasminnānāmṛgā bhāṃti dhāvamānā itastataḥ \|*  
*kalatraputrapuṣṭyarthaṃ lobhārthaṃ mānavā iva \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The different kinds of deer and other animals run about here and there on that mountain and they appear like men covetously inclined to bring up and nurture their wives and children.

## \|\| 1.33.11 \|\|

*niryāsacchadmanā bāṣpaṃ vāsitāśeṣadiṅmukham \|*  
*muñcaṃti taravo yatra dantidantakṣatatvacaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With their barks scratched off by the tusks of elephants, the trees there appear to shed tears under the pretext of the exudation that rendered all the quarters fragrant.

## \|\| 1.33.12 \|\|

*cīrikāvirutairdīrghai rudaṃta iva cāpare \|*  
*hastihastahatā vṛkṣā manyante yasya sānuṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Other trees on its ridges are thought as though they are wailing through the cries of the crickets, when they are hit by trunks of elephants.

## \|\| 1.33.13 \|\|

*itaścetaśca gacchadbhirnirjharāṃbhobhirāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*śuśubhe sitavastrāḍhyaiḥ pumāniva vibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The mountain shone like a man adorned with white cloths etc., as it was sprayed by the waters of rivulets, flowing here and there in different directions.

## \|\| 1.33.14 \|\|

*yasya sparddhā samutpannā pūrvaṃ saha sumeruṇā \|*  
*tataḥ prāha sahasrāṃśuṃ gatvā sa krodhamūrcchitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Formerly a rivalry arose between it and Sumeru mountain. Hence Vindhya became highly enraged. He went to the Sun-god and said:

## \|\| 1.33.15 \|\|

*kasmādbhāskara merostvaṃ prakaroṣi pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*kulaparvatasaṃjñe'pi na karoṣi kathaṃ mayi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “O Bhāskara, why do you circumambulate Meru? Although I too am called a Kulaparvata, you do not go round me”

## \|\| 1.33.16-17 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*na vayaṃ śraddhayā tasya gireḥ kurmaḥ pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*eṣa me vihitaḥ panthā yenedaṃ vihitaṃ jagat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasya tuṃgāni śṛṃgāṇi vyāpya khaṃ saṃśritāni ca \|*  
*tena saṃjāyate tasya balādeva prada kṣiṇā \|\| 17 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

16-17. We do not go round it because of any faith in that mountain. This has been ordained as our path by the being that created the universe. Further its lofty peaks have spread through the space. It is due to compulsion that the circumambulation is caused.

## \|\| 1.33.18 \|\|

*etacchrutvā viśeṣeṇa saṃkruddho viṃdhyaparvataḥ \|*  
*provāca paśya bhāno tvaṃ tarhi tuṃgatvamadya me \|*  
*rurodhātha nabhomārgaṃ yena gacchati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing this Vindya Mountain became further enraged. He said: “O Bhānu (Sun-god), then you shall see my loftiness as well.” He blocked the path of the sky by which the Sun used to go round.

## \|\| 1.33.19-21 \|\|

*atha ruddhaṃ samālokya mārgaṃ vāsaranāyakaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa citte sve sāṃprataṃ kiṃ karomyaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

*karomi yadyahaṃ cāsya parvatasya pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*tadbhaviṣyati kālasya calanaṃ bhuvanatraye \|\| 20 \|\|*

*māsartubhuvanānāṃ ca tathā bhāvī viparyayaḥ \|*  
*agniṣṭomādikāḥ sarvāḥ kriyā yāsyaṃti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*naṣṭayajñotsave loke devānāṃ syānmahāvyathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. On seeing his way blocked, the Lord of the Day thought within himself: ‘What shall I do now? If I circumambulate this mountain also there shall be a disturbance of time in all the three worlds.

The months, seasons and the regions around shall become unsettled. Agniṣṭoma and other rites will become defunct If Yajña and other festivities were stopped the Devas will be hurt much.’

## \|\| 1.33.22-23 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃcintya cittena bahudhā tīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*jagāma manasā bhītaḥ so'gastyaṃ munipuṃgavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nānyosti vāraṇe śakto viṃdhasyāsya hi taṃ vinā \|*  
*agastyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. After thinking thus in various ways, the Hot-rayed One (Sun-god) became afraid and thought of Agastya, the eminent sage.

‘Excepting Agastya, the progeny of Mitra and Varuṇa, the most excellent one among Brāhmaṇas, no one else is competent to restrain this Vindya.’

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*tato dvijamayaṃ rūpaṃ sa kṛtvā tīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*camatkārapurakṣetre tasyāśramapadaṃ yayau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Hot-rayed One (Sun-god) then adopted the guise of a Brāhmaṇa and went to his (Agastya’s) hermitage in the holy spot Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.33.25 \|\|

*tatastu vaiśvadevāṃte vedoccāraparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*provāca so'tithiḥ prāptastavāhaṃ munisattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. At the conclusion of Vaiśvadeva Yajña (the Sun-god in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa) uttered Vedic passages and said, “O excellent sage, a guest has come to you.”

## \|\| 1.33.26-27 \|\|

*tato'gastyaḥ kṛtānandaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune \|*  
*manoratha ivādhyāto yo'gnikāryāṃta āgataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ brūhi muniśreṣṭha yaddadāmi tavepsitam \|*  
*adeyaṃ nāsti me kiñcitkāle'sminprārthitasya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Agastya was delighted. He said: “O great sage, welcome to you. One who has arrived at the conclusion of the rites performed in the sacred fire is like an ardent wish meditated upon. Hence tell me, O excellent sage, what thing wished by you shall I give you. There is nothing that you desire which cannot be given by me if I am requested at this time.”

## \|\| 1.33.28-30 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ bhāskara āyāto viprarūpeṇa sanmune \|*  
*sarvakāryakṣamaṃ matvā tvāmekaṃ bhuvanatraye \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tvayā pūrvaṃ surārthāya prapītaḥ payasāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*vātāpiśca tathā daityo bhakṣito dvijakaṇṭakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tasmādgatirbhavāsmākaṃ sāṃprataṃ munisattama \|*  
*devānāmiha varṇānāṃ tvameva śaraṇaṃ yataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

28-30. O good sage, I am Bhāskara (Sun-god) come here in the form of a Brāhmaṇa in the belief that you are the only person in all the three worlds competent to accomplish any task. Formerly the ocean, the storehouse of waters, was drunk up by you for the sake of Suras. Similarly Daitya Vātāpi, a thorn unto the Brāhmaṇa community, was swallowed. Hence, O excellent sage, be our refuge now, because you are the sole shelter unto Devas and the different castes of people here.

## \|\| 1.33.31 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa munirviprā viśeṣeṇa praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*arghyaṃ dattvā dineśāya tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sūta said:

31\. O Brāhmaṇas, on hearing his words the sage was exceedingly pleased. After offering Arghya to the Lord of Day, he respectfully said:

## \|\| 1.33.32 \|\|

*dhanyo'smyanugṛhītosmi yanme tvaṃ gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*tasmādbrūhi kariṣyāmi tava vākyamakhaṃḍitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “A favour has been done to me. I am blessed because you came to my abode. Hence tell me; I shall completely carry out your wish.”

## \|\| 1.33.33-34 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*eṣa viṃdhyācalo'smākaṃ mārgamāvṛtya saṃsthitaḥ \|\| \|*  
*sparddhayā girimukhyasya sumerormunisatama \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sāmādyairvividhopāyaistasmādenaṃ nivāraya \|*  
*kālātyayo yathā na syādgaterbhaṃgastathā kuru \|\| 34 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

33-34. O excellent sage, due to his rivalry with Sumeru the principal mountain, this Vindhya Mountain is blocking our way. Hence avoiding further delay, restrain him by means of the different expedients like peaceful conciliation etc. Do bring about the cessation of the blocking of our path.

## \|\| 1.33.35 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te vārayiṣyāmi vardhamānaṃ kulācalam \|*  
*svasthānaṃ gaccha tasmāttvaṃ sukhībhava divākara \|\| 35 \|\|*

Agastya said:

35\. I shall restrain that Kulaparvata that has begun to grow in size. Hence, O Divākara, go to your abode and relax.

## \|\| 1.33.36 \|\|

*tataḥ sa preṣitaste na bhāskarastīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*svaṃ sthānaṃ prayayau hṛṣṭastamāmaṃtrya munīśvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thus dismissed by him, Bhāskara, the hot-rayed (god), joyously went to his abode after duly taking leave of the lord of sages.

## \|\| 1.33.37-38 \|\|

*agastyo'pi drutaṃ gatvā viṃdhyaṃ provāca sādaram \|*  
*nyūnatāṃ vraja madvākyācchīghraṃ parvatasattama \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dākṣiṇātyeṣu tīrtheṣu snāne jātādya me matiḥ \|*  
*tavāyattā gire saiva tatkuruṣva yathocitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Agastya hastened to Vindhya and spoke respectfully: “O excellent mountain, at my request, do shorten your stature quickly. I am now feeling inclined to take the holy plunge in the southern Tīrthas. All that depends on you. Hence do what is proper.”

## \|\| 1.33.39 \|\|

*sa tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā viṃdhyaḥ parvatasattamaḥ \|*  
*abhajannimnatāṃ sadyo vinayena samanvitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing his words, Vindhya, the excellent mountain, became humble and stooped down immediately.

## \|\| 1.33.40-41 \|\|

*agastyo'pi samāsādya tasyāṃtaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*tvayaivaṃ saṃsthitenātha sthātavyamityuvāca tam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yāvadāgamanaṃ mahyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*no cecchāpaṃ pradāsyāmi yena saṃyāsyasi kṣayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. O Brāhmaṇas, after crossing over to its southern side, Agastya said to him: “You shall continue to stay thus till I return. No hesitation in this respect. Otherwise I am bound to curse you, whereby you will attain destruction.”

## \|\| 1.33.42 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya śāpādbhīto nagottamaḥ \|*  
*na jagāma punarvṛddhiṃ tasyāgamanavāṃchayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Afraid of the curse that excellent Mountain promised, “It shall be so.” He did not grow in size further in the expectation of his return.

## \|\| 1.33.43 \|\|

*so'pi tenaivamārgeṇa nivṛttiṃ na karoti ca \|*  
*yāvadadyāpi vipreṃdrā dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśrita taḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Till now, O Brāhmaṇas, that sage has resorted to the southern region and so has not returned that way.

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*atha tatraiva cānīya lopāmudrāṃ munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*samāhūya sahasrāṃśuṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Lord of sages brought Lopāmudrā there. He then called the Thousand-rayed One and eagerly said to him:

## \|\| 1.33.45 \|\|

*tava vākyānmayā tyaktaḥ svāśramastīkṣṇadī dhite \|*  
*tavārthe ca na gaṃtavyaṃ bhūyastatra kathaṃcana \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O Hot-rayed One, my hermitage has been abandoned by me at your instance. It is in your interest that I should never return there again.

## \|\| 1.33.46 \|\|

*tasmānmadvacanādbhāno caturdaśyāṃ madhau site \|*  
*yanmayā sthāpitaṃ tatra liṃgaṃ pūjyaṃ hi tattva yā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hence, O Bhānu, at my instance, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Cakra, the Liṅga that has been installed by me should be worshipped by you.”

## \|\| 1.33.47-48 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ mune kariṣyāmi tava vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*pūjayiṣyāmi talliṃgaṃ varṣāṃte svayameva hi \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yo'nyo hi taddine liṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*mama lokaṃ samāsādya sa bhaviṣyati muktibhāk \|\| 48 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

47-48. O sage, I shall undoubtedly do thus at your instance. At the end of every year I shall myself worship that Liṅga. Any other man who worships that Liṅga on that day shall attain my world and then salvation.

## \|\| 1.33.49-50 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇāttatra bhagavāṃstīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ kurute sadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhūyo vadata vai kaścitsaṃdehaśce ddhṛdi sthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Sūta said:

49-50. It is for this reason that the Hot-rayed Lord always presents himself there on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Caitra.

Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything that I have been asked has been narrated. If you have any other doubt in your heart do tell me.

## Chapter 34 - Fight between Devas and Asuras

## \|\| 1.34.1-2 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ taṃ muniṃ prati sūtaja \|*  
*tvayā purā surārthāya prapītaḥ payasāṃnidhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ sūtaja no brūhi vistareṇa mahāmate \|*  
*yathā tena purā pīto muninā payasāṃnidhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaja, about that sage (Agastya) you have said: “For the sake of Suras the ocean, the storehouse of waters, was drunk by you (Agastya) formerly.” O highly intelligent one, describe in detail how the storehouse of waters was drunk up by that sage formerly.

## \|\| 1.34.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kāleyā iti vikhyātāḥ purā dānavasattamāḥ \|*  
*saṃbhūtāḥ sarvadevānāṃ vīryotsāhapraṇāśakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. Formerly the foremost among Dānavas, famous by the name Kāleya, became the cause of the loss of vigour and enthusiasm of all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.34.4 \|\|

*tatastaiḥ pīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*trailokyaṃ śaktiyogena prokto devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the entire range of the three worlds trembled by their enormous powers, Lord Maheśvara was thus told by Viṣṇu the powerful one:

## \|\| 1.34.5 \|\|

*etadīśāna daiteyaistrailokyaṃ paripīḍitam \|*  
*kālikeyairmahāvīryestasmātkāryo mahāhavaḥ \|*  
*adyaiva taiḥ samaṃ deva samāsādya dharātalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O Īśāna, this entire range of the three worlds is tormented by Kālikeyas of great power. Hence, O Lord, we have to go to the earth now itself and carry on a great fight with them.”

## \|\| 1.34.6 \|\|

*tato viṣṇuśca rudraśca sahasrākṣaḥ suraiḥ saha \|*  
*śitaśastradharāḥ sarve saṃprāptā dharaṇītalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereupon Rudra, Viṣṇu and the Thousand-eyed One (Indra) armed themselves with sharp weapons and accompanied by Suras all of them arrived on the earth.

## \|\| 1.34.7 \|\|

*atha te dānavāḥ sarve śrutvā devānsamāgatān \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ sahasā jagmuḥ saṃmukhāḥ kopasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On coming to know that all the Devas had assembled together, all those Dānavas angrily came face to face with them quickly for fighting them off.

## \|\| 1.34.8 \|\|

*tato'bhavanmahāyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*trailokyaṃ kaṃpitaṃ yena samastaṃ bhaya vihvalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then ensued a great fight between the Devas and the Dānavas, wherein the entire range of the three worlds trembled with fear and agitation.

## \|\| 1.34.9 \|\|

*atha kālaprabhonāma dānavo balagarvitaḥ \|*  
*sa śakraṃ purato dṛṣṭvā vajrocchritakaraṃ sthitam \|*  
*provāca prahasanvākyaṃ meghagambhīraniḥsvanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, arrogant with his might a Dānava named Kālaprabha saw before him Śakra with the Vajra lifted up in his hand. He then laughed and said these words in a voice majestic like the report of thunder:

## \|\| 1.34.10 \|\|

*muṃca vajra sahasrākṣa paśyāmi tava pauruṣam \|*  
*cirātprāpto'si me dṛṣṭiṃ diṣṭyā tvaṃ tridiveśvaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “It is after the passage of a long time that the Lord of heaven has fortunately come within our vision. O Thousandeyed One, release your Vajra. Let me witness your manliness.”

## \|\| 1.34.11 \|\|

*tataścikṣepa saṃkruddhastasya vajraṃ śatakratuḥ \|*  
*so'pi tallīlayā dhṛtvā jagṛhe savyapāṇinā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11..Thereupon, the enraged Śatakratu hurled the Vajra at him. The demon sportingly caught hold of it with his left hand.

## \|\| 1.34.12 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraṃ samuddiśya gadāṃ gurvīṃ mumoca saḥ \|*  
*sarvāyasamayīṃ raudrāṃ yamajihvāmivāparām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then aiming at Śakra he threw a huge club entirely made of iron. It was very terrific and appeared like another tongue of Yama.

## \|\| 1.34.13 \|\|

*tayā hataḥ sahasrākṣo visaṃjño rudhiraplutaḥ \|*  
*dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritya saṃniviṣṭo rathopari \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On being struck by it, the Thousand-eyed One became unconscious. Drenched in a pool of blood he somehow remained on the chariot with the help of the flagstaff.

## \|\| 1.34.14 \|\|

*atha taṃ mātalirdṛṣṭvā visaṃjñaṃ valaghātinam \|*  
*prāṅmukhaṃ ca rathaṃ cakre saṃsmaransārathernayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Mātali saw the Slayer of Bala (Indra) unconscious. Remembering the conventional duty of a charioteer he turned the chariot eastward (away from the battlefield).

## \|\| 1.34.15 \|\|

*tataḥ parāṅmukhībhūte rathe śakrasya saṃgare \|*  
*dudruvurbhayasaṃtrastāḥ sarve devāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, as the chariot of Śakra was turned away in the course of the battle, all the Devas became excessively frightened and they fled in all directions.

## \|\| 1.34.16 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrā viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*vrīḍāṃ vihāya vidhvastāḥ pṛṣṭhadeśe śitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, and the group of Maruts shamelessly (fled away). They were hit on their backs with sharp arrows and were shattered.

## \|\| 1.34.17 \|\|

*atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavairmadhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*āruhya garuḍaṃ tūrṇaṃ kālaprabhamupādravat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing the army shattered by the Dānavas the Slayer of Madhu (i.e, Viṣṇu) immediately mounted Garuḍa and rushed against Kālaprabha.

## \|\| 1.34.18 \|\|

*tataste dānavāḥ sarve parivārya śitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*samyagācchādayāmāsurgarjamānā muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then all the Dānavas surrounded him roaring aloud repeatedly. They covered him with sharp arrows.

## \|\| 1.34.19 \|\|

*sa tairācchādito viṣṇuḥ śuśubhe ca samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*samyakpulakitāṃgaśca raktācala ivāparaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Enveloped by them all round, Viṣṇu shone like another red (bloody) mountain with the boldly experiencing horripilation.

## \|\| 1.34.20 \|\|

*tataḥ śārṅgavinirmuktaiḥ śaraiḥ kaṃkapatatribhiḥ \|*  
*chedayitveṣujālāni daiteyānnijaghāna saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He then split the volleys of arrows by means of arrows fitted with feathers of heron, discharged from his Śārṅga bow and killed the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.34.21 \|\|

*tato daityagaṇāḥ sarve hanyamānā surāriṇā \|*  
*trātāraṃ nābhyagacchaṃta mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Being annihilated by Murāri (Viṣṇu) all those groups of Daityas resembled deer oppressed by lions. They did not find any saviour.

## \|\| 1.34.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare daityaḥ kālakhaṃja iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa kopavaśamāpanno vāsudevamupādravat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime a Daitya remembered as Kālakhañja furiously rushed at Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.34.23 \|\|

*sa hatvā pañcabhirbāṇairvāsudevaṃ śilā śitaiḥ \|*  
*jaghāna garuḍaṃ kruddho daśabhirnataparvabhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Striking Vāsudeva with five arrows very sharp and hard as rocks, he furiously hit Garuḍa with ten flat-jointed arrows.

## \|\| 1.34.24 \|\|

*tataḥ sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ tasya daityasya mādhavaḥ \|*  
*pramumoca vadhārthāya jvālāmālāsamāvṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter Mādhava discharged the discus Sudarśana for slaying that Daitya. It was encircled by a series of sparks of fire.

## \|\| 1.34.25 \|\|

*so'pi taccakramālokya vāsudevakarāccyutam \|*  
*āgacchaṃtaṃ prasāryāsyaṃ grastuṃ tatsaṃmukho yayau \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing that discus that issued from Vāsudeva’s hand coming towards him, the Daitya opened his mouth wide to swallow it and stood facing it.

## \|\| 1.34.26 \|\|

*agrasacca mahādaityastiṣṭhatiṣṭheti cābravīt \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ samuddiśya tataścikṣepa sāyakān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The great Daitya did swallow it and said “Wait! Wait!” Then he discharged arrows aiming at Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.34.27 \|\|

*tataścakrī sa daityena grastacakreṇa tāḍitaḥ \|*  
*suparṇena samāyukto jagāma viṣamāṃ vyathām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Being struck by the Daitya who had swallowed the (Sudarśana) discus, Vāsudeva along with Garuḍa experienced acute pain.

## \|\| 1.34.28-29 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kruddho bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā hariṃ tathābhūtaṃ śakraṃ cāpi parāṅmukham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tataḥ śūlaprahāreṇa taṃ nihatya danoḥ sutam \|*  
*śaraiḥ pinākanirmuktairjaghānoccaistathā parān \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. In the meantime the enraged Lord, the Slayer of Tripuras, saw Hari in the plight and Śakra with averted face. He then hit the son of Danu with his trident, he killed the others by means of the arrows discharged from his Pināka bow.

## \|\| 1.34.30 \|\|

*kālaprabhaṃ prakālaṃ ca kālāsyaṃ kālavigraham \|*  
*jaghāna bhagavāñchaṃbhustathānyānapi nāyakān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Lord Śaṃbhu slew Kālaprabha, Prakāla, Kālāsya, Kālavigraha and other leaders.

## \|\| 1.34.31 \|\|

*tataḥ pradhānāste sarve dānavā apidāruṇāḥ \|*  
*palāyanaparā jātā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then all those hideous Dānavas, despite their importance, became bereft of enthusiasm in the conquest of their enemies. They began to flee.

## \|\| 1.34.32 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraśca viṣṇuśca labdhasaṃjñau dhṛtāyudhau \|*  
*ślāghayaṃtau mahādevaṃ saṃsthitau raṇamūrdhani \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then Śakra and Viṣṇu regained consciousness and took up again their weapons. They congratulated Mahādeva and stood ready for the battle on the field.

## \|\| 1.34.33 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare bhagnānsamudvīkṣya danoḥ sutān \|*  
*jaghnuḥ śaraśataiḥ śastraiḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In the meantime all the Devas including Vāsava observed that the sons of Danu were smashed. They then began to exterminate them with hundreds of arrows and other weapons.

## \|\| 1.34.34-35 \|\|

*atha te hatabhūyiṣṭhā dānavā balavattarāḥ \|*  
*hanyamānāḥ śitairbāṇaistridaśairjitakāśibhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*agamyaṃ manasā teṣāṃ praviṣṭā varuṇālayam \|*  
*śastraiśca kṣatasarvāṃgā hatanāthāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Most of the powerful Dānavas had been killed or were being killed with sharp arrows by the Devas proud of their victory. They, therefore, entered the ocean which the Devas could not reach even mentally. Thus the Daityas became leaderless and miserable. All their limbs had been mutilated.

## Chapter 35 - Installation of Citreśvara Pītha

## \|\| 1.35.1-8 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ teṣu prabhagneṣu hateṣu ca surottamāḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve stutvā devaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tenaiva cātha nirmuktāḥ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*svaṃsvaṃ sthānamathājagmuḥ śakraviṣṇupuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*te'pi dānavaśārdūlā hatāśāśca surottamaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtraṃ pracakrire sarve nāśāya tridivaukasām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ maṃtrayatāmeṣa niścayaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*nānyatra dharmavidhvaṃsāddevānāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasmāttapasvino yai ca ye ca yajñaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tathānye niratā dharme nihantavyā niśāgame \|\| 5 \|\|*

*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā niṣkramya varuṇālayāt \|*  
*rātrau sadaiva nighnaṃti janāndharmaparāyaṇān \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yatra yatra bhavedyajñaḥ satraṃ 'pyutsavo'thavā \|*  
*tatra gatvā niśāyoge prakurvaṃti janakṣayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*taiḥ prasūtā makhā dhvastā dīkṣitā vinipātitāḥ \|*  
*ṛtvijaśca tathānye'pi sāmānyā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-8. When those Daityas had been shattered and slaughtered by Lord Maheśvara, rendered free from danger by him alone, the excellent Suras with Śakra and Viṣṇu as their leaders became delighted in their minds. All of them eulogized Lord Maheśvara and bowed down to him repeatedly. Then they went to their respective abodes.

With their hopes thus shattered by the excellent Suras, the tiger-like Dānavas consulted one another for ways and means of bringing about the destruction of heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.35.4-5 \|\|

*teṣāṃ maṃtrayatāmeṣa niścayaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*nānyatra dharmavidhvaṃsāddevānāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasmāttapasvino yai ca ye ca yajñaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tathānye niratā dharme nihantavyā niśāgame \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. As they consulted one another and discussed thus, it was decided by them that except putting obstacles in the performance of religious rites, there was no other means for destroying Devas; hence ascetics, people interested in Yajñas and the virtuous ones should be killed at nightfall.

## \|\| 1.35.6 \|\|

*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā niṣkramya varuṇālayāt \|*  
*rātrau sadaiva nighnaṃti janāndharmaparāyaṇān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After deciding thus, they used to come out of the abode of Varuṇa (i.e. the ocean) always at nightfall and began killing people engaged in religious acts.

## \|\| 1.35.7 \|\|

*yatra yatra bhavedyajñaḥ satraṃ 'pyutsavo'thavā \|*  
*tatra gatvā niśāyoge prakurvaṃti janakṣayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Wherever there was any Yajña, Sattra or religious festivities, they went there at nightfall and carried on annihilation of those people.

## \|\| 1.35.8 \|\|

*taiḥ prasūtā makhā dhvastā dīkṣitā vinipātitāḥ \|*  
*ṛtvijaśca tathānye'pi sāmānyā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Many Yajñas were spoiled by them, Dīkṣitas (persons who were initiated for Yajñas) were struck down and Ṛtviks (priests) and ordinary good Brāhmaṇas were killed.

## \|\| 1.35.9 \|\|

*āśrame munimukhyasya śāṃḍilyasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ bhakṣitaṃ tairdurātmabhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A thousand leading Brāhmaṇas were eaten up by those evil-hearted ones, in the hermitage of the noble-souled Śāṇḍilyā, a leader of sages.

## \|\| 1.35.10 \|\|

*śatāni ca sahasrāṇi nihatāni dvijanmanām \|*  
*viśvāmitrasya pañcaiva saptātreścaiva dhīmataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hundreds and thousands of Brāhmaṇas were killed. Five thousand followers of Viśvāmitra and seven thousand of intelligent Atri were destroyed.

## \|\| 1.35.11 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu samastaṃ dharaṇītalam \|*  
*naṣṭayajñotsavaṃ jātaṃ kāleyabhayapīḍitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the same time, the entire surface of the earth was afflicted by the fear of Kāleya and all Yajñas and religious festivals became defunct.

## \|\| 1.35.12 \|\|

*na kaścicchayanaṃ rātrau prakaroti mahī tale \|*  
*dhṛtāyudhā janāḥ sarve tiṣṭhaṃti saha tāpasaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. No one on the earth dared to sleep during nights. People well-equipped with weapons stood by the ascetics.

## \|\| 1.35.13 \|\|

*rātrau svapaṃti ye kecidviśvastā dharmabhājanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmasthīni dṛśyaṃte prātareva hi kevalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A few virtuous people who confìdentally took repose during nights (were killed) and only their bones were seen in the morning.

## \|\| 1.35.14 \|\|

*atha devagaṇāḥ sarve yajñabhāgavinākṛtāḥ \|*  
*prajagmuḥ paramāmārti brahmaviṣṇupurassarāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All the groups of Devas with Brahmā and Viṣṇu as their leaders, who were deprived of their shares in the Yajñas suffered the greatest distress.

## \|\| 1.35.15 \|\|

*tato gatvā samudrāṃtaṃ vadhāya suravidviṣām \|*  
*na śekurviṣamasthāṃstānmanasāpi pradharṣitum \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In order to slay the enemies of Suras, they entered the ocean too but could not assail them even mentally because they were placed in a very difficult position.

## \|\| 1.35.16-18 \|\|

*tataḥ samudranāśāya maṃtraṃ cakruḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*tasminnaṣṭe bhavantyeva vadhyā dānavasattamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*agastyena vinā naiṣa śoṣaṃ yāsyati sāgaraḥ \|*  
*tasmātsaṃprārthayāmotra kṛtye gatvā munīśvaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*camatkārapure kṣetre sa tiṣṭhati ca sanmuniḥ \|*  
*tasmāttatraiva gacchāmo yena gacchati satvaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Deeply grieved thereupon they consulted (each other) for drying up the ocean. (They thought that) ‘the leading Dānavas could be killed when the ocean no longer existed. Without (the help of) Agastya, the ocean will not become dry. Hence we shall go to that leading sage and make a request to him in this matter. That excellent sage resides in the holy place of Camatkārapura. So we shall go there itself and he will come quickly (to our help).’

## \|\| 1.35.19 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya te sarve tridaśāstasya cāśramam \|*  
*saṃprāptā munimukhyasya mitrāvaruṇa janmanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After deciding thus, all of those Devas went to the hermitage of the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, the important sage.

## \|\| 1.35.20 \|\|

*so'pi sarvānsamālokya saṃprāptānsurasattamān \|*  
*prahṛṣṭaḥ sammukhastūrṇaṃ jagāmātīva sanmuniḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing all the excellent Suras gathered together before him, the good sage became delighted.

## \|\| 1.35.21 \|\|

*provāca prāṃjalirvākyaṃ harṣa gadgadayā girā \|*  
*brahmādīṃstānsurāndṛṣṭvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Seeing Brahmā and other Suras, the eyes of the sage gleamed with delightful surprise. With palms joined together in veneration, he spoke these words in a voice choked with excess of delight:

## \|\| 1.35.22-23 \|\|

*camatkārapuraṃ kṣetrametanmedhyamapi sthitam \|*  
*bhūyo medhyataraṃ jātaṃ yuṣmākaṃ hi samāśrayāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasmādvadata yatkṛtyaṃ mayā saṃsiddhyate'dhunā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ prakariṣyāmi yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. “Though already sacred and pure, this holy place Camatkārapura has become more sacred by your presence. Hence speak out ye all, what task should be carried out by me now. I shall carry it out even if it be very difficult.”

## \|\| 1.35.24-26 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kāleyā iti daityā ye hataśeṣāḥ suraiḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*te samudraṃ samāśritya nighnaṃti śubhakāriṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śubhe nāśamanuprāpte dhruvaṃ nāśo divaukasām \|*  
*tasmātteṣāṃ vadhārthāya tvaṃ śoṣaya mahārṇavam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yena te gocaraṃ prāptā dṛṣṭerdānavasattamāḥ \|*  
*badhyaṃte vibudhaiḥ sarve jāyaṃte ca makhā iha \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Devas said:

24-26. The Daityas named Kāleyas who have survived a general slaughter by the Suras, are now taking shelter in the ocean and killing the performers of auspicious rites. If auspicious rites are defunct, the destruction of heaven-dwellers is certain. So, in order to facilitate their annihilation, do make the great ocean dried up. Thereby the leading Dānavas will be visible to our eyes. They then could be killed by Devas and Makhas (sacrifices) could be resumed here.

## \|\| 1.35.27 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ saṃvatsarasyāṃte śoṣayiṣyāmi sāgaram \|*  
*vidyābalaṃ samāśritya yoginīnāṃ surottamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Agastya said:

27\. O excellent Suras, by the end of a year I shall gain the Vidyā (magical lore) of Yoginīs and on the strength thereof I shall dry up the ocean.

## \|\| 1.35.28 \|\|

*tasmādvrajata harmyāṇi yūyaṃ yāti hi vatsaram \|*  
*yāvadbhūyo'pi varṣāṃte kāryamāgamanaṃ dhruvam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence do ye all go to your abodes. A year will pass presently. At the end of the year, do certainly come back.

## \|\| 1.35.29 \|\|

*tato mayā samaṃ gatvā śoṣite varuṇālaye \|*  
*haṃtavyā dānavā duṣṭā hanta yaiḥ pīḍyate jagat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You can come along with me. After the ocean has been dried up, the wicked Dānavas by whom the world is being afflicted should be killed.

## \|\| 1.35.30 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve gatāḥ svesve niketane \|*  
*agastyo'pi samudyogaṃ cakre vidyāsamudbhavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter all the groups of the Devas went to their respective abodes. Agastya carried on his endeavour for the acquisition of the Vidyā.

## \|\| 1.35.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvāṇi pīṭhāni yāni saṃti dharātale \|*  
*tāni tatrānayāmāsa maṃtraśaktyā mahāmuniḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then all the Pīṭhas (shrines of Mother Śakti) on the earth were brought together by the great sage through the power of his Mantras.

## \|\| 1.35.32-34 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ teṣu saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*yoginīnāṃ ca vṛndāni kanyakānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vidyāṃ viśoṣiṇīnāma samārādhayata dvijaḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā diśāṃ pālānkṣetrapālānapi dvijaḥ \|*  
*ākāśacāriṇīṃ caiva devatāṃ śraddhayā dvijaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte prasannā tasya devatā \|*  
*provāca vada yatkṛtyaṃ siddhāhaṃ tava sanmune \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. On the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, he devoutly worshipped the groups of Yoginīs and Kānyakās (Virgins) in particular therein.

## \|\| 1.35.35 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*yadi devi prasannā me tadāsyaṃ viśa satvaram \|*  
*yena saṃśoṣayāmyāśu samudraṃ devi vāgyataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Thus the Brāhmaṇa propitiated the Vidyā named Viśoṣiṇī (that which dries up). Further the Brāhmaṇa worshipped devoutly and with faith the Guardians of Quarters, the Kṣetrapālas (guardians of holy shrines) and the deity roaming through the skies with great faith. At the close of the year the deity became pleased and said: “Do tell me what should be done, O good sage. I have been won over by you.”

Agastya said:

35\. O goddess, if you are pleased, do enter my mouth quickly. I shall restrain speech and dry up the ocean by means of that power.

## \|\| 1.35.36 \|\|

*sā tatheti pratijñāya praviṣṭā satvaraṃ mukhe \|*  
*saṃśoṣaṇī mahāvidyā tasyarṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. That great Vidyā named Saṃśoṣaṇī said, “It shall be so” and entered his mouth presently as the sage had perfectly purified his soul.

## \|\| 1.35.37 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*dhṛtāyudhakarā hṛṣṭāḥ saṃnaddhā yuddhahetave \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the meantime all the Devas including Vāsava came there joyously holding the weapons and ready for the battle.

## \|\| 1.35.38 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃprasthito vipro devaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vārirāśiṃ samuddiśya saṃśuṣkavadanastadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then the Brāhmaṇa who had kept his mouth dry set off with mental concentration and purity, towards the ocean in the company of all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.35.39 \|\|

*atha gatvā samudrāṃtaṃ stūyamāno divālayaiḥ \|*  
*pipāsākulito'tīva sarvāndevānuvāca ha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Being eulogized by the heaven-dwellers he approached the shore of the sea. Agitated by thirst very much, he spoke to the Devas:

## \|\| 1.35.40 \|\|

*eṣo'haṃ sāgaraṃ sadyaḥ śoṣayiṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*yūyaṃ bhavata sodyogā vadhāya suravidviṣām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “I am now going to dry up the ocean immediately. Be prepared for the act of annihilating the enemies of the Suras.”

## \|\| 1.35.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā muniḥ so'tha matsyakacchapasaṃkulam \|*  
*helayā prapapau kṛtsnaṃ grāhaiḥ kīrṇaṃ mahārṇavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

41\. After saying thus, the sage sportingly drank the entire vast expanse of water agitated by fishes and turtles and abounding in alligators.

## \|\| 1.35.42 \|\|

*tataḥ sthalopame jāte te daityāḥ surasattamaiḥ \|*  
*vadhyante niśitairbāṇaiḥ samantādvijigīṣubhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The ocean came to be on a par with the bare ground and the Daityas were killed by the excellent Suras desirous of the ultimate victory everywhere by means of their sharp arrows.

## \|\| 1.35.43 \|\|

*atha kṛtvā mahadyuddhaṃ yathā śaktyātidāruṇam \|*  
*hatabhūyiṣṭhaśeṣā ye bhittvā bhūmiṃ gatā adhaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After fighting to the best of their ability in the terrific battle, those who survived after most of them had been killed, pierced the ground and went beneath to the nether worlds.

## \|\| 1.35.44-45 \|\|

*tataḥ procuḥ surāḥ sarve stutvā taṃ munisattamam \|*  
*parityaja jalaṃ bhūyaḥ pūraṇārthaṃ mahodadheḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*naiṣā vasumatī vipra samudreṇa vinākṛtā \|*  
*rājate vastusaṃtyaktā yathā nārī vibhūṣitā \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. After eulogizing the excellent sage, all the Suras said to him: “Give out the water again for filling up the great ocean. O Brāhmaṇa, bereft of the sea, the earth does not shine like a lady worthy of being adorned but bereft of property and possessions.”

## \|\| 1.35.46 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|\| \|*  
*yā mayā'rādhitā vidyā varṣaṃyāvatpraśoṣaṇī \|*  
*tayā pītamidaṃ toyaṃ pariṇāmagataṃ tathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

Agastya said:

46\. The water has been drunk by the Vidyā named Praśoṣaṇī which had been propitiated by me. It has been digested too.

## \|\| 1.35.47 \|\|

*eṣa yāsyati vai pūrtiṃ bhūyo'pi varuṇālayaḥ \|*  
*khātaścāgādhatāṃ prāpto gaṃgātoyaiḥ sunirmalaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This ocean will get again filled up unfathomably with the waters of Gaṅgā free from impurities after being dug up.

## \|\| 1.35.48 \|\|

*sagaronāma bhūpālo bhaviṣyati mahītale \|*  
*tatputrāḥ ṣaṣṭisāhasrāḥ khaniṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. There will be a king on the Earth named Sagara. His

## \|\| 1.35.49 \|\|

*tasyaivānvayavānrājā bhaviṣyati bhagīrathaḥ \|*  
*sa jñātikāraṇādgaṃgāṃ brahmāṃḍādānayiṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. There will be born in the same race a king named Bhagīratha. For the sake of his kinsmen, he will fetch Gaṅgā from the Cosmic Egg.

## \|\| 1.35.50 \|\|

*pravāheṇa tatastasyāḥ samaṃtādaṃbhasāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati susaṃpūrṇaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With her flooding waters gushing all round, the ocean will become perfectly filled up. The truth has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.35.51 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devakṛtyaṃ muniśreṣṭha bhavatā hyupapāditam \|*  
*tasmātprārthaya cittasthaṃ varaṃ sarvaṃ munīśvara \|\| 51 \|\|*

The Devas said:

51\. O excellent sage, the task of the Devas has been completed by you. Hence, O lordly sage, request for any boon you have cherished in your heart.

## \|\| 1.35.52 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre mayā pīṭhānyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ānītāni prabhāvena maṃtrāṇāṃ surasattamāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Agastya said:

52\. O excellent Suras, all the Pīṭhas have been completely gathered together in the holy spot of Camatkārapura by the power of Mantras.

## \|\| 1.35.53 \|\|

*tasmātteṣāṃ sadā vāsastatraivāstu prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ yoginīnāṃ ca mātṝṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. By the power of all the Yoginís and the Mātṛs in particular, let the Pīṭhas stay there itself.

## \|\| 1.35.54 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tāni yaḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati tasya syātsamastaṃ manasepsitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. May a person endowed with ardent faith, who worships them on eighth and fourteenth lunar days, attain everything mentally desired.

## \|\| 1.35.55-57 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yasmāccitrāṇi pīṭhāni tvayānītāni tatra hi \|*  
*tasmāccitreśvaraṃ nāma pīṭhamekaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tatra pūjāṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*yoginīnāṃ ca vidyānāṃ mātṝṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*taṃtaṃ kāmaṃ naraḥ śīghraṃ saṃprāpsyati mahāmune \|*  
*asmākaṃ varadānena yadyapi syātsupāpakṛt \|\| 57 \|\|*

The Devas said:

55-57. Since the wonderfully variegated Pīṭhas have been gathered together, they will constitute one Pīṭha named Citreśvara. A man who worships Yoginīs, Vidyās and Mothers in particular there, with any desire meditated upon, O great sage, will soon obtain that desire, due to this offer of the boon by us, even if he be a great sinner.

## \|\| 1.35.58-59 \|\|

*evamuktvā surāḥ sarve tamāmantrya munīśvaram \|*  
*gatāstriviṣṭapaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ so'pyagastyaḥ svamāśramam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā sa payasāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*agastyena purā pīto devakāryaprasiddhaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. After saying thus, all the Suras took leave of the leading sage and joyously went to heaven. Agastya went to his hermitage.

## Chapter 36 - Greatness of Citreśvarī Pīṭha

## \|\| 1.36.1-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*citreśvaramidaṃ pīṭhamagastyamuninirmitam \|*  
*yatpramāṇaṃ yatprabhāvaṃ tadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya pīṭhasya māhātmyaṃ vaktuṃ no śakyate dvijāḥ \|*  
*sahasreṇāpi varṣāṇāṃ mukhānāmayutairapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra siddhimanuprāptāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*anudhyānasamāyuktā yoginaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*anyapīṭheṣu yā siddhirvarṣānuṣṭhānato bhavet \|*  
*dinenaikena tāṃ siddhiṃ labhaṃte yogino dhruvam \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-4. Do describe to us the extent and the power of this Pīṭha named Citreśvara created by Sage Agastya.

## \|\| 1.36.5 \|\|

*yastatrātha rvaṇānmaṃtrāñjapecchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*teṣāmarthodbhavaṃ kṛtsnaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti sa dhruvam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

O Brāhmaṇas, it is impossible to describe the greatness of that Pīṭha in the course of a thousand years by ten thousands of mouths.

Hundreds and thousands of Yogins of esteemed holy vows, fully endowed with meditation, have attained Siddhi there.

Within a day Yogins certainly attain that Siddhi which is attained in other Pīṭhas after practice for a year.

5\. One who, with ardent faith, performs the Japa of Atharvaṇa Mantras certainly attains the entire fruit stated in the Mantras.

## \|\| 1.36.6 \|\|

*putrakāmo narastatra puṃliṃgānyo japennaraḥ \|*  
*sa labhetepsitānputrānyadyapi syājjarānvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A man who is desirous of a son and performs the Japa of Pulliṅgas (masculine names) shall obtain desired sons though he may be old.

## \|\| 1.36.7 \|\|

*garbhopaniṣadaṃ tatra putrakāmo japennaraḥ \|*  
*api vandhyāprasaṃgena syātsa putrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A man desirous of sons should recite the Grabhopaniṣad there. He shall beget sons even by cohabiting with barren women.

## \|\| 1.36.8 \|\|

*śatrulokavināśāya yo japecchatarudriyam \|*  
*tasminpīṭhe'rayastasya sadyo gacchaṃti saṃkṣayam 0 \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If a devotee recites Śatarudriya with the aim of the destruction of enemy hosts in that Pīṭha, his enemies meet with destruction immediately.

## \|\| 1.36.9 \|\|

*bhūtapretapiśācādirakṣārthaṃ tatra mānavaḥ \|*  
*yo japedvāmadevyaṃ ca sa syāddhi nirupadravaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A man who recites Vāmadevya Sāman for the sake of protection from evil spirits, ghosts and vampires and the like shall be rid of all torments.

## \|\| 1.36.10 \|\|

*ko'dāditi narastatra kanyārthaṃ yo japedṛcam \|*  
*yāṃ kanyāṃ dhyāyamānastu sa tāṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A man who performs the Japa of the Ṛk beginning with ko’dāt. While meditating upon a virgin of his choice shall undoubtedly obtain her.

## \|\| 1.36.11 \|\|

*yo bhūpālaprasādārthamimaṃ devā niśaṃ japet \|*  
*nirargalaḥ prasādaḥ syāttasya pārthivasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If a devotee constantly recites IMAM DEVĀ for gaining favour of the king, he shall have the favour of the king unhindered.

## \|\| 1.36.12 \|\|

*svastrīsnehakṛteyastu taṃ patnībhiriti dvijāḥ \|\| \|*  
*japedbhāryā bhavetsādhvī tasya sā snehavatsalā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Brāhmaṇas, if a person recites the Mantra TAM PATNĪBHIḤ for getting his own wife’s affection, his wife shall be a chaste lady with abundance of love for him.

## \|\| 1.36.13 \|\|

*yo lokānugrahārthāya japedaditirityapi \|*  
*tasya lokānurāgaḥ syātsalābhaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If one performs the Japa of Aditi for obtaining the blessings of people, he will have a profitable affection of the people.

## \|\| 1.36.14 \|\|

*vittārthī yo japettatra śrīsūktaṃ manujo dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarvatastasya vittāni samāgacchaṃtyanekaśaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brāhmaṇas, if a man seeking wealth repeats Śrī Sūkta there, riches will move unto him from all directions.

## \|\| 1.36.15 \|\|

*bhūmīti yo japetsāma bhūmyarthaṃ tatra mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa bhavedbhūpatirnūnaṃ nīcajātirapi dhruvam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If a devotee performs the Japa of the Sāman Mantra bhūmi for the sake of realm there, that man shall certainly be the lord of earth even if he is of low birth.

## \|\| 1.36.16 \|\|

*japedrathaṃtaraṃ sāma yānārthaṃ tatra yo naraḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnoti hi yānāni śīghragāni śubhāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If a man for the sake of vehicles performs the Japa of the Rathantaram Sāman there, he obtains splendid and swift vehicles.

## \|\| 1.36.17 \|\|

*gajārthī yo japettatra gaṇānāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnoti gajānmartyo madaplāvitabhūtalān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if a devotee who seeks elephants repeats the Mantra gaṇānām etc. there, that man obtains elephants that flood the ground with their ichor.

## \|\| 1.36.18 \|\|

*na tadrakṣeti yo mantraṃ japedra kṣākṛte naraḥ \|*  
*tasya syātsarvato rakṣā sameṣu viṣameṣu ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If a man repeats the Mantra na tadrakṣa etc. for the sake of security, he will obtain it from everywhere when chances are favourable or adverse.

## \|\| 1.36.19 \|\|

*saptarṣaya iti śreṣṭhāṃ yo japettu samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ṛcaṃ rogavināśāya sa rogaiḥ pari mucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One who repeats with concentration and mental purity the excellent Ṛk beginning with saptarsayaḥ for the destruction of ailments, is rid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.36.20 \|\|

*yadubhī yo japettatra grahapīḍārdito janaḥ \|*  
*sānukūlā grahāstasya prabhavaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If people oppressed by malefic Planets perform the Japa of the Mantra beginning with yadubhī there, undoubtedly the Planets become favourable to them.

## \|\| 1.36.21 \|\|

*bhūtapīḍārdito yaśca bṛhatsāma japennaraḥ \|*  
*pitṛvajjāyate tasya sa bhūto'pyaṃtako'pi cet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If a man assailed by the affliction of evil spirits repeats the Bṛhat Sāman, the evil spirits and even the god of Death becomes like a father unto him.

## \|\| 1.36.22 \|\|

*yātrāsiddhikṛte yaśca japetsūktaṃ ca śākunam \|*  
*tasya saṃsidhyate yātrā yadyapi syādakiṃcanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If a person repeats the Śakuna (pertaining to omens) Sūkta for successful conclusion of his journey, he shall accomplish it even if he is impoverished.

## \|\| 1.36.23 \|\|

*sarpanāśāya yastatra sārpasūktaṃ japennaraḥ \|*  
*na tasya maṃdire sarpāḥ praviśaṃti kathaṃcana \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If a man recites the Sarpa (pertaining to serpents) Sūkta for the destruction of serpents, they do not at all enter his abode.

## \|\| 1.36.24 \|\|

*viṣanāśāya yastatra japecchra ddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*uttiṣṭheti viṣaṃ sadyastasya nāśaṃ prayāsyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who is endowed with ardent faith and performs there the Japa of the Mantra beginning with uttistha for the purpose of quelling poison, will find that the poison is immediately dispelled.

## \|\| 1.36.25 \|\|

*sthāvarajagamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ yadi vā viṣam \|*  
*tasya nāmnā viniryāti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Whether poison arises from an immobile being or a mobile being or if it is artificial, it goes away even when his name is uttered, like darkness at the rise of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.36.26 \|\|

*vyāghrasāma japedyastu tatra śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tasya vyāghrādayo vyālā jāyaṃte saumyacetasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If a devotee with ardent faith, performs there the Japa of Vyāghra Sāman, pythons, tigers etc., become gentle in regard to him.

## \|\| 1.36.27 \|\|

*kṛṣikarmaprasi ddhyarthaṃ yo japellāṃgalāni ca \|*  
*vṛṣṭihīne'pi loke'sminkṛṣistasya prasidhyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If a devotee performs there the Japa of the Mantra lāṅgalāni etc. for prosperous increase in agricultural work, even when the whole world is without rain, cultivation will be achieved by him.

## \|\| 1.36.28 \|\|

*ītināśāya tatraiva japeddevavrataṃ naraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃkīrttanā deva ītayo yāṃti saṃkṣayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. For the destruction of Ītis (natural calamities) a man should perform there the Japa of the Mantra devavrata. Thereby, mere utterance Ītis get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.36.29 \|\|

*anāvṛṣṭihate loke paṃceṃdraṃ tatra yo japet \|*  
*tasya hastakṛte home tanmaṃtraiḥ syājjalāgamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the world is affected by drought a devotee should perform there the Japa of Pañcendra Mantra. If Homa is performed by himself with his own hands repeating those Mantras, there shall be the coming in (supply) of water.

## \|\| 1.36.30 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrābhyā miti yastatra naraścaurārditaḥ paṭhet \|*  
*nopadravo bhavettasya kadāciccaurasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If a man afflicted by thieves and robbers recites the Mantra beginning with daṃṣṭrābhyām, never will he be tormented by thieves.

## \|\| 1.36.31 \|\|

*vivādārthaṃ japedyastu saṃsṛṣṭamiti tatra ca \|*  
*vivāde vijaya stasya pāpasyāpi prajāyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. For success in argument, a devotee should perform there the Japa of the Mantra beginning with saṃsṛṣṭam. Even if he is a sinner, he will win the argument.

## \|\| 1.36.32 \|\|

*yo ripūccāṭanārthāya naro rudraśiro japet \|*  
*tasya te ripavo yāṃti deśaṃ tyaktvā kubuddhitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. For the sake of driving away enemies a man should perform the Japa of Rudraśiras. Thereupon his enemies with crooked intellect will abandon that land and go away.

## \|\| 1.36.33 \|\|

*mohanāya ripūṇāṃ ca yo japedviṣṇusaṃhitām \|*  
*tasya mohābhibhūtāste jāyaṃte ripavo dhruvam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. For the enchantment of the enemies, a devotee should perform the Japa of Viṣṇusaṃhitā. His enemies will certainly be deluded and enchanted.

## \|\| 1.36.34 \|\|

*vaśīkaraṇahetoryaḥ kūṣmāṃḍīḥ prajapennaraḥ \|*  
*śatravo'pi vaśe tasya kiṃ punaḥ pramadādayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. For the purpose of captivating people, a man should perform the Japa of Kūṣmāṇḍīḥ Mantra. Even enemies will be under his control, to say the least about young women etc.

## \|\| 1.36.35 \|\|

*yaḥ staṃbhāya ripūṇāṃ vai prājāpatyaṃ ca vāruṇam \|*  
*maṃtraṃ japeddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ samyakchraddhāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*maṃtrasaṃstaṃbhitāstasya jāyaṃte sarvaśatravaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. For the purpose of stunning and paralysing enemies, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a man with ardent faith should perform the Japa of Prājāpatya and Vāruṇa Mantras. All his enemies become paralysed by means of these Mantras.

## \|\| 1.36.36 \|\|

*japetkālī karālīti yaḥ śoṣāya naro dvijāḥ \|*  
*sa śoṣayati tatkṛtsnaṃ yaccitte dhārayennaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Brāhmaṇas, for the purpose of drying up things a man should perform the Japa of the Mantra kālī karālī etc. Whatever the man thinks about, he can dry it up entirely.

## \|\| 1.36.37 \|\|

*eṣa maṃtrastadā japto hyagastyena mahātmanā \|*  
*yatprabhāvānnadīnāthastena saṃśoṣito dhruvam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. This Mantra was repeated by the noble-souled Agastya then. By means of the power thereof the Lord of Rivers was dried up by him.

## \|\| 1.36.38 \|\|

*etatprabhāvaṃ yatpīṭhaṃ maṃtrāṇāṃ siddhikārakam \|*  
*aihikānāṃ phalānāṃ ca tanmayā vaḥ prakīrtitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Such is the power of the Pīṭha that causes the Siddhi of Mantras. It yields worldly pleasures also. It has now been described unto you.

## \|\| 1.36.39 \|\|

*yo vāṃchati punaḥ svargaṃ sa tatra dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ karotu dānaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ cāpi viśeṣataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who desires heavenly pleasures, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, should perform there the rites of holy bath, Dāna and Śrāddha in particular.

## \|\| 1.36.40 \|\|

*atha vāṃchati yo mokṣaṃ virakto bhavasāgarāt \|*  
*niṣkāmastatra saṃtuṣṭastapastapyetsubuddhimān \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If, on the other hand, one is detached and wishes for liberation from the ocean of worldly existence, let him be contented and free from all desires. Let that sensible man perform penance there.

## \|\| 1.36.41 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*maṃtrajāpyasya māhātmyaṃ yattvayā naḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*tatkathaṃ siddhimāyāti maṃtrajāpyaṃ hi sūtaja \|\| 41 \|\|*

The sages said:

41\. The great efficacy of the Japa of the Mantras has been described by you. But, O Sūtaja, how does this Japa of the Mantras become fruitful.

## \|\| 1.36.42 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra tatkathayiṣyāmi yanmayā pitṛtaḥ śrutam \|*  
*vadato brāhmaṇeṃdrasya purā durvāsaso muneḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sūta said:

42\. In this context I shall tell you what has been heard from my father (i.e. Lomaharṣaṇa). He was expounding this to Sage Durvāsas.

## \|\| 1.36.43 \|\|

*tena pūrvaṃ pitā'smākaṃ pṛṣṭo durvāsasā dvijāḥ \|*  
*maṃtravādakṛte yacca śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O Brāhmaṇas, formerly our father was asked by Durvāsas in regard to Mantravāda. This, you do listen, with great mental concentration.

## \|\| 1.36.44 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*sādhayiṣyāmyahaṃ mantramabhīṣṭaṃ kamapi vratī \|*  
*tasya siddhikṛte brūhi vidhānaṃ śāstrasaṃbhavam \|\| 44 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

44\. I have observed Vratas and am practising a certain desired Mantra. Do tell me the procedure as laid down in the Śāstras for its success.

## \|\| 1.36.45 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*maṃtrāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ kaṣṭaṃ sarveṣāmapi sanmune \|*  
*pratyavāyasamopetaṃ bahucchidrasamākulam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

45\. O good sage, the practice of Mantras is painful and difficult affair unto all. It is likely to be obstructed and it is full of loopholes.

## \|\| 1.36.46 \|\|

*tasmānmaṃtrakṛte siddhiṃ yadi tvaṃ vāṃchasi dvija \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre tatra tvaṃ gaṃtumarhasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇa, if you desire fruitful result of the practice of Mantras, it behoves you to go to the holy spot of Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.36.47 \|\|

*tatra citreśvarīpīṭhamagastyena vinirmitam \|*  
*sadyaḥ siddhikaraṃ proktaṃ mantrāṇāṃ hṛdi vartinām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Citreśvarīpīṭha thereof has been created by Agastya. It is said to be one that brings about achievement of the fruit of Mantras retained in the heart

## \|\| 1.36.48 \|\|

*na tatra jāyate chidraṃ pratyavāyo na ca dvija \|*  
*nāsiddhirvaradānena sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Due to the boon granted by all the heaven-dwellers, there is no possibility of any loophole there. There is no hindrance or impediment there, O Brāhmaṇa, nor lack of fulfilment.

## \|\| 1.36.49 \|\|

*cāturyuṃgyaṃ hi tatpīṭhaṃ sthitānāṃ siddhimāha ret \|*  
*yugānurūpataḥ sadyastato vakṣyāmyahaṃ dvija \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. That Pīṭha belongs to all the four Yugas. It accords Siddhi unto those who stay there, in accordance with the Yuga and that too instantaneously. Hence I speak so, Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.36.50 \|\|

*yo yaṃ sādhayituṃ mantramicchati dvijasattama \|*  
*sa tasya pūrvamevātha lakṣamekaṃ japennaraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, if a person wishes to practise (Japa) of any Mantra, he should at the outset perform the Japa of that Mantra a hundred thousand times.

## \|\| 1.36.51 \|\|

*tato bhavati saṃsiddho maṃtrārhaḥ sa naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*japedbrāhmaṇaśārdūla tato lakṣacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*daśāṃśena tu homaḥ syātsusamiddhe hutāśane \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereby he becomes a Siddha, a man of purity qualified for the Mantra. Then, O tiger among Brāhmaṇas, he should repeat it four hundred thousand times. A tenth of that is the number of Homas performed in a well-kindled fire.

## \|\| 1.36.52-53 \|\|

*tatastu jāyate siddhirnūnaṃ tanmaṃtrasaṃbhavā \|*  
*tatra saumyeṣu kṛtyeṣu homaḥ siddhārthakaiḥ sitaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*jātīpuṣpaiśca viprendra smṛto brāhmaṇa bhojanaiḥ \|*  
*tathā raudreṣu kṛtyeṣu raktapuṣpaiḥ saguggulaiḥ \|*  
*tarpaṇaiḥ kanyakānāṃ ca homaḥ syātsa phalapradaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Thereby the Siddhi originating from that Mantra is certain. In regard to gentle activities, the Homa is done by means of white mustards, Jāti flowers and the feeding of Brāhmaṇas.

O leading Brāhmaṇa, in regard to violent activities, it is done by means of red flowers along with Guggula (aromatic resin). Virgins should also be propitiated. Then the Homa shall be fruitful.

## \|\| 1.36.54 \|\|

*etatkṛtayuge proktaṃ maṃtrasādhanamutta mam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ sādhakānāṃ ca mayā proktaṃ dvijottama \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. This mode of practising Mantras mentioned by me, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, is to be adopted in Kṛtayuga and by all Sādhakas (aspirants).

## \|\| 1.36.55 \|\|

*etattretāyuge proktaṃ pādonaṃ mantrasādhanam \|*  
*yugmārdhaṃ dvāpare kāryaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In Tretā Yuga, the practice of Mantras is reduced by a quarter. It should be performed to the extent of a half in Dvāpara and a fourth in Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 1.36.56 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samāsādya siddhiṃ maṃtrasamudbhavām \|*  
*tatra pīṭhe tataḥ kṛtyaṃ sādhayetsvecchayā naraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. After attaining the Mantra-Siddhi there in that Pīṭha a man should employ it and accomplish any task.

## \|\| 1.36.57 \|\|

*śāpānugrahasāmarthyasaṃyutasteja sā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*ajeyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sādhūnāṃ saṃmatastathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He shall become equipped with capacity to curse or to bless. He shall be brilliant. He cannot be conquered by any living being. He will become one approved of by good people.

## \|\| 1.36.58 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa munistasya piturmama vaco'khilam \|*  
*tataścitreśvaraṃ pīṭhaṃ samāyāto'tha sanmuniḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

Sūta said:

58\. On hearing all the speech of my father that good sage came to Citreśvara Pīṭha.

## \|\| 1.36.59 \|\|

*tatra saṃsādhayāmāsa sarvānmaṃtrānyathākramam \|*  
*vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. There with ardent faith, he practised (mastered) all the Mantras in the due order in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.36.60 \|\|

*iti saṃsiddhamaṃtraḥ sa camatkārapuraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ prārthanārthāya bhūmikhaṃḍakṛte dvijāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After a successful practice of the Mantras thus, he went to Camatkārapura, O Brāhmaṇas, in order to request the Brāhmaṇas for the sake of plots of land.

## Chapter 37 - The Palace Called Duśśīla

## \|\| 1.37.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*athāpaśyatsa viprāṇāṃ vṛndaṃ vṛndārakopamam \|*  
*saṃniviṣṭaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe līlābhāji dvijottamāḥ \|\| \|\| 1 \|\|*

*eke vedavidastatra vedavyākhyānatatparāḥ \|*  
*parasparaṃ susaṃkruddhā vivadaṃti jigīṣavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yajñavidyāvido'nye'pi yajñākhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tatra viprāḥ pradṛśyaṃte śataśo brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he saw a group of Brāhmaṇas comparable to Devas. They were seated on the playground. Some were well-versed in the Vedas and they were ready for expounding the same. They were eager to defeat others and were angrily disputing with one another.

Others were well-versed in the science of Yajñas. They were busily discussing (the details of) Yajñas. There hundreds of Brāhmaṇas were seen expounding Brahman.

## \|\| 1.37.4 \|\|

*anye brāhmaṇaśārdūlā vedāṃgeṣu vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*pravadaṃti ca saṃdehānvṛndānāmagrataḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Others were tiger-like Brāhmaṇas expert in Vedāṅgas. Standing in front of the groups of people, they were clearing the doubts.

## \|\| 1.37.5 \|\|

*vedābhyāsaparāścānye tāranādena sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*nādayaṃto diśāṃ cakraṃ tatra samyagdvijottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, still others were busy in reciting Vedic passages loudly. They were making the quarters reverberate.

## \|\| 1.37.6 \|\|

*anye kautūhalāviṣṭāḥ saṃcarānviṣamānmithaḥ \|*  
*papracchurjahasuścānye jñātvā mārgapravartinam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Others were full of curiosity. They asked one another questions about difficult passages. Still others laughed at the person engaged in the (exposition of) passages.

## \|\| 1.37.7 \|\|

*smṛtivādaparāścānye tathānye śrutipāṭhakāḥ \|*  
*saṃdehānsmṛtijānanye pṛcchaṃti ca parasparam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Others were engaged in discussing the Smṛtis. Still others were reciters of the Veda. Others asked and clarified the doubts pertaining to the Smṛti texts.

## \|\| 1.37.8 \|\|

*kīrtayaṃti tathā cānye purāṇaṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*vṛddhānāṃ puratastatra sabhāmadhye vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Other excellent Brāhmaṇas were expounding the Purāṇa to elders. They were seated in the midst of the assembly.

## \|\| 1.37.9 \|\|

*atha tānsa munirdṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇānsaṃśitavratān \|*  
*abhivādya tataḥ prāha sādaraṃ vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing those Brāhmaṇas of esteemed vows, the sage humbly bowed down to them and said respectfully:

## \|\| 1.37.10-11 \|\|

*mama buddhiḥ samutpannā śambhorāyatanaṃ prati \|*  
*kartuṃ brāhmaṇaśārdūlāstasmātsthānaṃ pradarśyatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tavāhaṃ devadevasya śambhoḥ prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*vidhāyārādhayiṣyāmi tameva vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. “O tigers among Brāhmaṇas, I am feeling inclined to erect a temple of Śaṃbhu. Hence let a suitable place be pointed out. I shall build an excellent mansion of Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas. I shall propitiate the same Bull-emblemed Lord there.”

## \|\| 1.37.12 \|\|

*sa evaṃ jalpamāno'pi muhurmuhurataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*na teṣāmuttaraṃ lebhe śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Although he repeatedly said so energetically, he did not get from them any reply good or otherwise.
