## \|\| 1.37.13 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā samunistāndvijottamān \|*  
*śaśāpa tāraśabdena yathā śṛṇvaṃti kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The sage became excessively furious. He cursed those excellent Brāhmaṇas in a loud voice so that all could hear.

## \|\| 1.37.14 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*vidyāmado dhanamadastṛtīyo'bhijanodbhavaḥ \|*  
*ete madāvaliptānāmeta eva satāṃ damāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

14\. The pride of learning, that of affluence and the third one arising from nobility of birth: In the case of arrogant persons these are inebriating factors; but in that of good people, they are means of self-control.

## \|\| 1.37.15 \|\|

*tatra ye'pi hi yuṣmākaṃ madā eva vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*yatastato'nvaye'pyevaṃ bhaviṣyati madānvitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Everyone of you appears to be inebriated. Hence only such inebriate ones will be born in your families.

## \|\| 1.37.16 \|\|

*sadā sauhṛdanirmuktāḥ pitaro'pi sutaiḥ saha \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti pure hyasminkiṃ punarbāṃdhavādayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In this city all fathers will be devoid of friendliness or affection for sons, still more so in the case of other kinsmen?

## \|\| 1.37.17 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa viprendro nivṛttastadanantaram \|*  
*apamānaṃ paraṃ prāpya brāhmaṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, feeling insulted by the Brāhmaṇas, the eminent Brāhmaṇa Durvāsas said this and turned away.

## \|\| 1.37.18 \|\|

*atha tanmadhyago vipra āsīdvṛddhatamaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*suśīla iti vikhyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Among them there was a wise elderly Brāhmaṇa well-known as Suśīla. He was a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.37.19 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā taṃ muniṃ kruddhaṃ gacchaṃtamapamānitam \|*  
*satvaraṃ prayayau pṛṣṭhe tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti ca bruvan \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He saw the sage going away furiously after being insulted. He quickly followed him saying “Stop! Stop!”

## \|\| 1.37.20-22 \|\|

*athāsādya gataṃ dūraṃ praṇipatya muniṃ ca saḥ \|*  
*provāca kṣamyatāṃ vipra viprāṇāṃ vacanānmama \|\| 20 \|\|*

*etaiḥ svādhyāyasaṃpannairna śrutaṃ vacanaṃ tava \|*  
*nottaraṃ tena saṃdattaṃ satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasmādbhūmirmayā dattā śaṃbhuharmyakṛte tava \|*  
*asminsthāne dvijaśreṣṭha prāsādaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. By this time the sage had gone very far. But the Brāhmaṇa overtook him. He bowed down to him and said: “O Brāhmaṇa, on my request, please forgive the Brāhmaṇas. These were busy in the recitation of their respective Vedic passages and so did not hear your words. Therefore they did not reply. This is the truth I am telling you. So, for the sake of a mansion dedicated to Śaṃbhu a plot of land is offered by me to you. In this spot, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, it behoves you to build a temple.”

## \|\| 1.37.23 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā durvāsā harṣasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kṣitidānodbhavāṃ cakre svasti brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ nirmame paścāttasya vākye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On hearing his words, Durvāsas became delighted. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he hailed him for the gift of the plot. Afterwards in accordance with his word, he built a palace (shrine) there.

## \|\| 1.37.24-32 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇā jñātvā suśīlena vasundharā \|*  
*devatāyatanārthāya dattā tasmai tapasvine \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sarve kopasamāyuktāḥ suśīlaṃ prati te dvijāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tataḥ procuḥ samāsādya yena śaptā durātmanā \|*  
*vayaṃ tasmai tvayā dattā prāsādārthaṃ vasundharā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmāttvamapi cāsmākaṃ bāhya eva bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*suśīlo'pi hi duḥśīlo nāmnā saṃkīrtyase budhaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*eṣo'pi tāpaso duṣṭo yaḥ karoti śivālayam \|\| \|*  
*naiva tasya bhavetsiddhiścāpi varṣaśatairapi \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tathā kīrtikṛtāṃ loke kīrtanaṃ kriyate naraiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpaśyatāṃ cāsya kīrtirnāsya tu durmateḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*eṣa duḥśīlasaṃjño vai tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*prāsādo nāmamātreṇa na saṃpūrṇaḥ kadācana \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yasmātsauhṛdanirmuktāḥ kṛtāstena vayaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*madaistribhiḥ samāyuktāḥ sarvānvayasamanvitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmādeṣo'pi pāpātmā bhaviṣyati sa kopabhāk \|*  
*taptaṃ taptaṃ tapo yena saṃprayāsyati saṃkṣayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

24-32. Those Brāhmaṇas came to know that a plot of land was given to the sage by Suśīla for erecting a temple. All those Brāhmaṇas became very angry with Suśīla.

## \|\| 1.37.33 \|\|

*evamuktvātha te viprāḥ kopasaṃraktalocanāḥ \|*  
*duḥśīlaṃ saṃparityajya praviṣṭāḥ svapure tataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Coining upto him they said: “A piece of land has been given by you for the sake of a palace to be dedicated to that wicked-minded one by whom we have been cursed. Hence you will be excommunicated by us. Though your name is Suśīla, you will be proclaimed Duśśīla by learned ones.

This wicked ascetic intends to build a Śiva temple. Even in hundreds of years, he will not realize his wish.

Those who earn reputation in the world are glorified by men. So also those who see things correctly, but not this evil-minded one.

This palace shall be named Duśśīla after your name. It shall be a mansion only in name. But it will never be completed.

Since we Brāhmaṇas have been made bereft of friendliness (for our sons) and associated with three kinds of arrogance along with our entire line of descendants, therefore this sinful person too shall be erascible (prone to be angry), thereby while he goes on performing penance, his penance will become futile.”

33\. After saying thus with eyes reddened with anger, those Brāhmaṇas left Duśśīla there and entered their city.

## \|\| 1.37.34 \|\|

*duḥśīlo'pi bahiścakre gṛhaṃ tasya purasya ca \|*  
*devaśarmā yathāpūrvaṃ saṃtyaktaḥ puravāsibhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Excommunicated by the residents of the city like Devaśarman before, Duśśīla built his house outside the city.

## \|\| 1.37.35 \|\|

*tasyānvaye'pi ye jātāste bāhyāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*bāhyāḥ kriyāsu sarvāsu sarveṣāṃ puravāsinām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Those who were born in his family were proclaimed “Outsiders”. They were excluded from all the holy rites of all the citizens.

## \|\| 1.37.36 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ teṣu dvijeṃdreṣu śāpaṃ dattvā gateṣu ca \|*  
*durvāsāḥ prāha duḥśīlaṃ kopasaṃraktalo canaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sūta said:

36\. After the departure of those leading Brāhmaṇas after cursing thus, Durvāsas said to Duśśīla angrily with eyes turned red:

## \|\| 1.37.37-38 \|\|

*mama siddhiṃ gatā maṃtrāḥ samarthāḥ śatrusaṃkṣaye \|*  
*ātharvaṇāstathā cānye vedatrayasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tasmādetatpuraṃ kṛtsnaṃ paśupakṣi samanvitam \|*  
*nāśamadya nayiṣyāmi yathā śatrorhi duṣṭakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. “Mantras from the Atharvaveda and other three Vedas capable of annihilating enemies have been mastered by me. I shall destroy the entire city along with animals and birds therein like a ruthless (king) razing down the city of the enemy.”

## \|\| 1.37.39 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*naitadyuktaṃ naraśreṣṭha tava kartuṃ kathaṃcana \|\| \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ kṛte karma brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Duśśīla said:

39\. O excellent one among men, this is not at all proper to do against the Brāhmaṇas particularly by a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.37.40 \|\|

*nighnaṃto vā śapaṃto vā vadaṃto vāpi niṣṭhuram \|*  
*pūjanīyāḥ sadā viprā divyāṃllokānabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Whether they kill, curse or speak harsh words, Brāhmaṇas should always be worshipped by those who wish for divine worlds.

## \|\| 1.37.41 \|\|

*brāhmaṇairnirjitairmene ya ātmānaṃ jayānvitam \|*  
*tāmisrādiṣu ghoreṣu narakeṣu sa pacyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. One who considers himself victorious when Brāhmaṇas are vanquished (by him) is cooked in the terrible Narakas beginning with Tâmisra.

## \|\| 1.37.42-43 \|\|

*ātmanaśca parābhūtiṃ tasmādviprātsaheta vai \|*  
*ya icchedvasatiṃ svarge śāśvatīṃ dvijasattama \|\| 42 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ kṣetre siddhiṃ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*maṃtrāste tatkathaṃ nāśaṃ tvameteṣāṃ kariṣyasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, one who desires a permanent residence in heaven shall endure his own discomfiture at the hands of a Brāhmaṇa. Your Mantras have attained Siddhi in the holy spot of these leading Brāhmaṇas. How can you then cause their destruction?

## \|\| 1.37.44 \|\|

*brahmaghne ca surāpe ca caure bhagnavate tathā \|*  
*niṣkṛtirvihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Atonement has been enjoined by good people in the cases of a Brāhmaṇa-slayer, one who drinks liquor, a thief and one whose Vrata has been broken. There is no atonement for an ungrateful person.

## \|\| 1.37.45 \|\|

*tasmātkopo na kartavyaḥ kṣetre cātra vyavasthitaiḥ \|*  
*kṣamāṃ kuru muniśreṣṭha kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence those who stay in this holy spot should nfot be angry. O excellent sage, be compassionate towards me and forgive me.

## \|\| 1.37.46-48 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya tatra kṛtvāvasattapaḥ \|*  
*prāptaśca paramāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 46 \|\|*

*duḥśīlākhyaḥ kṣitau so'pi prāsādaḥ khyāti māgataḥ \|*  
*yasya saṃdarśanādeva naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasya madhyagataṃ liṃgaṃ śuklāṣṭamyāṃ sadā naraḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paśyati kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā narakaṃ sa na paśyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

Sūta said:

46-48. He promised “It shall be so”, performed penance and stayed there. Thereby he attained the greatest Siddhi inaccessible even to Devas.

That place (mansion of Śiva) became well known after the name Duśśīla all over the earth. Merely by visiting it, a man is rid of his sins. A man who always visits the Liṅga within it on the eighth day in the bright half of a month and meditates for a moment, never sees Naraka.

## Chapter 38 - Greatness of Dhundhumāreśvara (Dhundhumāra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.38.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ dhundhumāreṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*sarvaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā prāsādaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra kṛtvā'śramaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tapastepe sudāruṇam \|*  
*yatprabhāvādayaṃ devastasmiṃlliṅge vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya saṃnihitā vāpī kṛtā tena mahātmanā \|*  
*sunirmalajalāpūrṇā sarvatīrthopamā śubhā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. A Liṅga was installed there itself by king Dhundhumāra after erecting a very charming palace full of all kinds of jewels.

He built a hermitage there and performed a severe penance. It was, due to its power, that the Lord stationed himself in that Liṅga.

A tank near it was constructed by that noble-souled one, filled with water free from all impurities and very auspicious, comparable to all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.38.4 \|\|

*dhundhumāreśvaraṃ paśyettatra snātvā narottamaḥ \|*  
*na sa paśyati durgāṇi narakāṇi yamālaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. An excellent man who takes his holy bath there and visits Dhundhumāreśvara, never sees the impassable Narakas in the abode of Yama.

## \|\| 1.38.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhuṃdhumāro mahīpālaḥ kasminvaṃśe babhūva saḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle tapastaptaṃ tenātra sumahātmanā \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. In which race was King Dhundhumāra born? At what time was the penance performed by that very noble-minded one?

## \|\| 1.38.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sūryavaṃśasamudbhūto bṛhadaśvasuto balī \|*  
*khyātaḥ kuvalayāśveti dhaṃdhumārastathaiva saḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. A powerful son of Bṛhadaśva was born in the race of the Sun-god. He is well known as Kuvalayāśva as well as Dhundhumāra.

## \|\| 1.38.7 \|\|

*tena dhundhurmahādaityo nihato marujāṃgale \|*  
*dhundhumāraḥ smṛtastena vikhyāto bhuvanatraye \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The great Daitya Dhundhu was killed by him in Marujāṅgala. Hence he is remembered as Dhundhumāra. He became renowned in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.38.8 \|\|

*camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ sa gatvā pāvanaṃ mahat \|*  
*tapastepe vayoṃ'te ca dhyāyamāno maheśvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Towards the closing days of his life, he went to the great holy spot Camatkārapura and performed a penance meditating on Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.38.9 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya sumahalliṃgaṃ prāsāde ratnamaṃḍite \|*  
*balipūjopahārādyaiḥ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After installing the great Liṅga in the palace studded with jewels, he adored it along with oblations, offerings flowers, incense and unguents.

## \|\| 1.38.10 \|\|

*tatastasya mahādevaḥ svayameva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣo'bhūdvṛṣārūḍho gauryā saha tathā gaṇaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereupon Maheśvara, the great Lord, himself appeared before him seated on his bull and accompanied by Gaurī and the attendants.

## \|\| 1.38.11 \|\|

*uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasva yathepsitam \|*  
*sarvaṃ te'haṃ pradāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Lord said: “I shall bestow a boon. Request for anything desired by you. I shall grant you everything even if it be rare.”

## \|\| 1.38.12 \|\|

*dhundhumāra uvāca \|*  
*yadi deyo varo'smākaṃ tvayā sarvasureśvara \|*  
*saṃnidhānaṃ prakartavyaṃ liṃge'sminvṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 12 \|\|*

Dhundhumāra said:

12\. O Lord of all the Suras, if a boon has to be granted to us, O Bull-emblemed One, you should station yourself in this Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.38.13-14 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*caitre śuklacaturdaśyāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*ahaṃ sadā kariṣyāmi gauryā sārdhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatra vāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā yo māṃ saṃpūjayiṣyati \|*  
*liṃge'sminsaṃsthitaṃ bhūpa mama lokaṃ sa yāsyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

13-14. O excellent king, undoubtedly I shall always be present on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra along with Gaurī. A man who takes his holy plunge in the tank there and worships me present in the Liṅga shall go to my world, O king.

## \|\| 1.38.15 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*so'pi rājā prahṛṣṭā tmā sthitastatraiva muktibhāk \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sūta said:

15\. After saying this the Lord vanished. Delighted in his heart the king stayed there and attained salvation.

## Chapter 39 - Greatness of Yayātīśvara (Yayāti-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.39.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyaivottaradigbhāge dhundhumāreśvarasya ca \|*  
*yayātinā nareṃdreṇa sthāpitaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*devayānyā tathānyacca tathā śarmiṣṭhayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā bhūpatestasya sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. There is an excellent Liṅga installed by King Yayāti to the north of Dhundhumāreśvara. There is another Liṅga installed by Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā, his wives. It is the bestower of all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.39.3 \|\|

*sa yadā sarvabhogānāṃ tṛptiṃ prāpto dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tadā putrasya rājyaṃ svaṃ vapuścaiva nyavedayat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when he was completely satisfied with all worldly pleasures, he entrusted his son (Pūru)with the kingdom and gave back his youthful form.

## \|\| 1.39.4 \|\|

*jarāmādāya tadgātrādbhāryābhyāṃ sahitastadā \|*  
*papraccha vinayopeto mārkaṃḍaṃ munisattamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He took back the old age of his physical form. Accompanied by his two wives, he went to the excellent Sage Mārkaṇḍa and requested him humbly:

## \|\| 1.39.5 \|\|

*bhagavansarvatīrthānāṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ ca vadasva me \|*  
*yatpradhānaṃ pavitraṃ yattadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O holy Sir, describe unto us the most important and holiest of all the Tīrthas and holy spots.”

## \|\| 1.39.6 \|\|

*śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*kṣetrāṇāmiha sarveṣāṃ tīrthaiḥ sarvairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ sāṃprataṃ pratibhāti naḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said:

6\. It appears to us that the holy spot of Camatkārapura which is adorned by all the Tīrthas is the most important of all holy spots.

## \|\| 1.39.7 \|\|

*yatra viṣṇupadī gaṃgā jaṃtūnāṃ pāpanāśinī \|*  
*svayaṃ sthitā nṛpaśreṣṭha tathā devā harādayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O excellent king, Viṣṇupadī Gaṅgā, the destroyer of the sins of all creatures, and the gods including Hara, are themselves present there.

## \|\| 1.39.8 \|\|

*tathānyāni ca tīrthāni yāni saṃti dharātale \|*  
*teṣāṃ yatra ca sāṃnidhyaṃ sarvadā nṛpasattama \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O excellent king, similarly all other Tīrthas stationed on the earth are present there permanently.

## \|\| 1.39.9 \|\|

*śilā yatra dvipañcāśaddhastānāṃ parisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*pitāmahena nirmuktā pramodāya dvijanmanām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. For the delight of Brāhmaṇas, a big rocky slab fifty-two Hastas in extent has been left there by Pitāmaha.

## \|\| 1.39.10-11 \|\|

*yadanyatra śubhaṃ karma varṣeṇaikena sidhyati \|*  
*tattatra divasenāpi siddhiṃ yāti kṣitīśvara \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gatvā tapaḥ kuru mahīpate \|*  
*yena prāpsyasi cittasthāṃllokānbhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Whereas an auspicious rite performed elsewhere yields fruit (benefit) in the course of a year, O Lord of the earth, the same does there in a single day.

So, O Lord of the earth, go there quickly and perform a penance there in the company of your wives. By it you will attain the worlds cherished in your heart.

## \|\| 1.39.12 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa rājā nahuṣātmajaḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre bhāryābhyāṃ sahito yayau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On healing his words, the king, the son of Nahuṣa, went to the holy place of Camatkārapura accompanied by both of his wives.

## \|\| 1.39.13 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃsthāpya talliṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*samyagārādhayāmāsa śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He installed the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas and propitiated it well with the utmost faith.

## \|\| 1.39.14 \|\|

*tatastasya prabhāvena bhāryābhyāṃ sahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*vimānavaramārūḍho jagāma tridivālayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then, by its power, the king accompanied by his wives went to heaven riding in an excellent aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.39.15 \|\|

*kinnarairgīyamānaśca stūyamānaśca cāraṇaiḥ \|*  
*sparddhamānaḥ samaṃ devairdvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Kinnaras sang about him and Cāraṇas eulogized him. Emulating Devas he had the lustre of twelve Ādityas.

## Chapter 40 - Greatness of Citraśilā

## \|\| 1.40.1-2 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadeṣā bhavatā proktā brāhmī tatra mahāśilā \|*  
*mokṣadā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ tathā pātakanāśinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sā kathaṃ sthāpitā tatra kiṃprabhāvā ca sūtaja \|*  
*etanno brūhi niḥśeṣaṃ na hi tṛpyāmahe vayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaja, it has been mentioned by Your Holiness that a great rock (Slab) pertaining to Brahmā is present there. It accords salvation unto all the creatures and destroys sins. How was it installed there? What is its power? Do narrate this completely. We are not fully satisfied.

## \|\| 1.40.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*brahmalokaniviṣṭasya brahmaṇo' vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*purā'bhūnmahatī cintā tīrthayātrāsamudbhavā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. Brahmā, born of the Unmanifest One was stationed in Brahmaloka. Formerly he became very anxious to do pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.40.4-8 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ saṃti tīrthāni bhūtale \|*  
*muktvā māṃ tanmayā kāryaṃ tīrthamekaṃ dharātale \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yatra trikālamāsādya karma saṃdhyāsamudbhavam \|*  
*martyalokaṃ samāsādya karomi tadanaṃtaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tathānyadapi yatkiñcitkarma dharmyaṃ hitāvaham \|*  
*tatkaromi yathānye'pi cakrurdevāḥ śivādayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na svarge'sti hi kṛtyānāmadhikāro'tra kaścana \|*  
*śubhānāṃ karmaṇāmeva kevalaṃ bhujyate phalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmādyatra dharāpṛṣṭhe śileyaṃ nipatiṣyati \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ tatra gantavyamanuṣṭhānārthameva hi \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. “All the Devas have their own Tīrthas on the earth except me. Therefore, I shall have to make a Tīrtha on the earth that I can resort to in the mortal world and perform Sandhyā prayers thrice a day. Further like deities Śiva and others, I can also perform other virtuous rites conducive to welfare. Here in Svarga, there is no right to perform holy rites. Only the fruit of auspicious rites is enjoyed. Hence for the sake of regular performance of the rites of the three Sandhyās, I must go to that place on the earth where this rocky slab falls.”

## \|\| 1.40.9 \|\|

*evamuktvā suvistīrṇāṃ śilāṃ tāmā sanodbhavām \|*  
*pracikṣepa dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ samuddiśya pitāmahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying thus, a large slab from his seat was hurled by Pitāmaha to the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.40.10 \|\|

*atha sā patitā bhūmau sarvaratnamayī śilā \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre sarvakṣetramahodaye \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. That slab consisting of all jewels fell on the earth on the holy spot of Camatkārapura, The most prominent of all holy places.

## \|\| 1.40.11 \|\|

*tata āgatya lokeśaḥ svayameva dharātalam \|*  
*tatkṣetraṃ vīkṣayāmāsa vyāptaṃ tīrthaiḥ samantataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon the Lord of the worlds himself came to the earth and surveyed that holy place surrounded all round by Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.40.12 \|\|

*tataḥ puṇyatame deśe dṛṣṭvā tāṃ samupasthitām \|*  
*śilāmānaṃdamāpannaḥ provāca tadanantaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On noticing that the rocky slab came to rest at a very meritorious place he became delighted. Thereafter he said:

## \|\| 1.40.13-14 \|\|

*aho dhanyatamo matto nānyo'sti bhuvanatraye \|*  
*sarvatīrthamaye kṣetre yato jātātra saṃsthitiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*salilena vinā yasmānna kriyā saṃpravartate \|*  
*tasmādatra mayā kāryaḥ śucitoyo mahāhradaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. “Oh! There is no one more blessed than I in all the three worlds because the slab has come to rest in a holy spot full of all Tīrthas. Since no holy rite can be efficacious without water, a big tank full of pure water should be created here by me.”

## \|\| 1.40.15 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃciṃtayāmāsa svasutāṃ ca sarasvatīm \|*  
*jana saṃsparśabhītyā ca pātālatalavāhinīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then he thought of his daughter, River Sarasvatī, that flows beneath (the earth) in the nether worlds because it is afraid of contact with lay people.

## \|\| 1.40.16 \|\|

*atha bhūmitalaṃ bhittvā prādurbhūtā mahānadī \|*  
*tāṃ śilāmamalaistoyaiḥ kṣālayantī samaṃtataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereat the great river came into view piercing the ground and flooding the slab all round with her sacred water.

## \|\| 1.40.17 \|\|

*atha mūrtimatī bhūtvā provāca prapitāmaham \|*  
*kimarthaṃ saṃsmṛtā devamamādeśaḥ pradīyatām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Assuming a visible form she asked Prapitāmaha, “Why am I remembered, O Lord. May the command be pronounced.”

## \|\| 1.40.18-19 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tvayātraiva sadā stheyaṃ śilāyāṃ mama saṃnidhau \|*  
*saṃdhyātraye'pi tvattoyairyena kṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tathā ye mānavāḥ snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti jale tava \|*  
*te yāsyaṃti parāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ devā mānuṣaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

18-19. You must always stay here near me on the slab so that I can perform the holy rite in all the three Sandhyās by means of your water. So also, men who perform their holy bath with your water shall attain the greatest Siddhi inaccessible unto even Devas and human beings.

## \|\| 1.40.20-21 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ kanyā suraśreṣṭha pātālatalavāhinī \|*  
*janasparśabhayādbhītā nāgacchāmi mahītale \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tavādeśo'nyathā naiva mayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*evaṃ matvā suraśreṣṭha yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

20-21. O excellent one among Suras, I am a virgin flowing through the nether worlds. Since I am afraid of contact with lay people, I do not come up to the surface of the earth. It does not behove me to do contrary to your behest. Considering this aspect, O excellent one among Suras, do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.40.22 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tavārthe kalpayiṣyāmi sthāne'traiva mahāhradam \|*  
*agamyaṃ sarvamartyānāṃ tatra tvaṃ sthātumarhasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

22\. For your sake I shall make a great tank here itself in the holy spot. It shall be unapproachable to all mortals. It behoves you to stay there.

## \|\| 1.40.23 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa deveśaścakhāna ca mahāhradam \|*  
*tataḥ sarasvatī tatra svasthānamakaro datha \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After saying thus the Lord of Devas dug up a big tank there. Then Sarasvatī made it her place of residence.

## \|\| 1.40.24-25 \|\|

*tato dṛṣṭiviṣānsarpānādideśa pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmābhiḥ sarvadā stheyaṃ hradesmiñchāsanānmama \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yathā sarasvatīṃ martyā na spṛśaṃti kathaṃcana \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ sarvathā kāryaṃ tathā pannagasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Then Pitāmaha ordered serpents who can kill by mere looking (at a victim): “At my bidding all of you should always stay in this tank. O excellent serpents, you must carry out your task in such a manner as to prevent men from touching her.”

Sūta stud:

## \|\| 1.40.26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ brahmā vyavasthāpya tatra kṣetre sarasvatīm \|*  
*tāṃ ca citraśilāṃ madhye brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After establishing Sarasvatī thus in that holy spot and that Citraśilā (wonderful slab) in the middle, he went to the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.40.27 \|\|

*atha maṃkaṇakonāma maharṣiḥ saṃśitavrataḥ \|*  
*kṣetre tatra samāyāto viṣavidyāvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Once thereafter a great sage of esteemed holy vows, named Maṅkaṇaka, came to that holy place. He was an expert in the science of poisons.

## \|\| 1.40.28 \|\|

*sakramādbhramamāṇastu tasminsarpābhirakṣite \|*  
*taṃ muniṃ veṣṭayāmāsurbabandhuścaiva pāśakaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He went round that holy spot well-guarded by serpents. They coiled round the sage and bound him as though with cords.

## \|\| 1.40.29 \|\|

*so'pi vidyābalātsarpānnirviṣāṃstāṃścakāraha \|*  
*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtaḥ salilāttasmātkṛtakṛtyo mudānvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By the power of his Vidyā, he rendered all the serpents devoid of poison. He took his holy plunge there and sanctified himself. After offering libations to the Pitṛs, he came out of water joyously feeling blessed and contented.

## \|\| 1.40.30 \|\|

*tataścakre muniryāvatsamyakkuśaparigraham \|*  
*darbhāgreṇāsya hastāgraṃ pāṭitaṃ tāvadeva hi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. As the sage gathered together Kuśa grass the tip of his hand got pricked.

## \|\| 1.40.31 \|\|

*atha tasmātkṣatājjātastasya śākaraso mahān \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa viśeṣeṇa harṣito vismayānvitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. From that wound of his a large quantity of vegetable juice issued forth. On seeing it he was surprised but all the more delighted.

## \|\| 1.40.32 \|\|

*siddho'hamiti vijñāya nṛtyaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|*  
*brāhmīṃ śilāṃ samāruhya ānaṃdāśrupariplutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Knowing that he has become a Siddha, tears of joy flooded in his eyes. He climbed on the slab of Brahmā and then began to dance.

## \|\| 1.40.33 \|\|

*athaivaṃ nṛtyamānasya munestasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*lāsyaṃ cakre tataḥ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. As the noble-souled sage danced thus, the entire universe too consisting of mobile and immobile beings danced gracefully.

## \|\| 1.40.34 \|\|

*camatkārapuraṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhagnaṃ naṣṭā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*prāsādairdhvaṃsitaistatra hāhākāro mahānabhūt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The entire Camatkārapura became shattered. The excellent Brāhmaṇas were destroyed. As the mansions crumbled down there was a great cry of “Hāl Hāl”.

## \|\| 1.40.35 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve taddṛṣṭvā tasya ceṣṭitam \|*  
*lāsyasya vāraṇārthāya procurvṛṣabhavāhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing his action all the groups of Devas pleaded unto the Bull-emblemed Lord for restraining the dance.

## \|\| 1.40.36-37 \|\|

*anena nṛtyamānena jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*nṛtyaṃ karoti deveśa tasmādgatvā nivāraya \|\| 36 \|\|*

*nānyaḥ śaktaḥ suraśreṣṭha munimenaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*niṣedhayitumīśāna tataḥ kuru jagaddhitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. “O Lord of Devas, while he is dancing, the whole universe too consisting of mobile and immobile beings dances. Hence do go and get it stopped.

O Īśāna, O most excellent one among Suras, no one else is competent to forbid (and stop) the sage. Hence do what is good unto the universe.”

## \|\| 1.40.38 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā rūpaṃ dvijeṃdrasya tatsakāśamupādravat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing their words, the Bull-emblemed Lord adopted the guise of an eminent Brāhmaṇa and approached him.

## \|\| 1.40.39 \|\|

*abravīcca mune kasmāttvayaitannṛtyate'dhunā \|*  
*tasmātkāryaṃ vadāśu tvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He said, “O sage, why do you dance now? Speak out your intention at once. We have great curiosity.”

## \|\| 1.40.40 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa vipreṃdraḥ śaṃkareṇa dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*hastaṃ saṃdarśayāmāsa tasya śākarasānvitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on being asked by Śaṅkara thus, the leading Brāhmaṇa showed his hand covered with vegetable juice.

## \|\| 1.40.41-42 \|\|

*kiṃ napaśyasi me brahmankarācchākaraso mahān \|*  
*saṃjātaḥ kṣatavaktreṇa tasmātsiddhirupasthitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*etasmātkāraṇādvipra nṛtyametatkaromyaham \|*  
*ānaṃdaṃ paramaṃ prāpya siddhijaṃ siddhasattama \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. “O Brāhmaṇa, don’t you see that a large quantity of vegetable juice has come out of the opening in the wound? Hence Siddhi has come to me. It is for this reason that I dance, O Brāhmaṇa. O most excellent one among Siddhas, I am delighted as a result of the Siddhi gained.”

## \|\| 1.40.43-44 \|\|

*evaṃ tu vadatastasya bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhaṃ tāḍayāmāsa svāṃgulyagreṇa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

*niścakrāma tato bhasma himasphaṭikasaṃnibham \|*  
*kṣatāgrātsahasā tasya mahāvismayakārakam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Even as he said this, the Bull-emblemed Lord struck his thumb with the tip of his figure. Instantly sacred ash resembling snow and crystal issued forth from the opening of the wound causing great surprise (to the Brāhmaṇa).

## \|\| 1.40.45-47 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca taṃ vipraṃ sa devo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃguṣṭhāgrato mahyaṃ niṣkrāṃtaṃ bhasma pāṃḍuram \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tathāpyahaṃ muniśreṣṭha na nṛtyaṃ kartumutsahe \|*  
*tvaṃ punarnṛtyase kasmādapi śākarasekṣaṇāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

*virāmaṃ kuru tasmāttvaṃ nṛtyādasmādvigarhitāt \|*  
*tapaḥ kṣarati viprendra nṛtyagītāddvijanmanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Lord said to the Brāhmaṇa: “O excellent sage, from the tip of my thumb grey ash has issued forth. Still I am not eager to dance. Why then do you dance merely at the sight of the vegetable juice? Stop this despicable dance. O leading Brāhmaṇa, by dancing and singing the power of the penance of a Brāhmaṇa gets wasted.”

## \|\| 1.40.48 \|\|

*athāsau tatsamudvīkṣya kṣatādbhasmavisarjanam \|*  
*nṛtyaṃ vrīḍānvitastyaktvā tasya cakre namaskṛtim \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On seeing the feat of the discharge of ash from a wound, he became ashamed. Stopping his dancing activity, he bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.40.49 \|\|

*abravīttvāmahaṃ manye nānyaṃ devānmaheśvarāt \|*  
*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yathā na syāttapaḥkṣatiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then he said, “I think you are none other than Lord Maheśvara. Do this favour unto me. Let there be no wastage of my periance.”

## \|\| 1.40.50 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tapaste matprasādena vṛddhiṃ śasyati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*sthāne'tra bhavatā sārdhamahaṃ sthāsyāmi sarvadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

The Lord said:

50\. With my favour the power of your penance will increase day by day. I shall always stay with you in this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.40.51 \|\|

*ānanditena bhavatā prārthito'haṃ yato mune \|*  
*ānandeśvarasaṃjñastu khyātiṃ yāsyāmi bhūtale \|*  
*etatpuraṃ ca me nāmnā ānandākhyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sage, since I have been requested by you in a blissful mood, I will become well known all over the earth by the name Ānandeśvara. After my name, this city too will be called Ānanda (modern Vaḍnagar in Gujarat).

## \|\| 1.40.52 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahādevo gataścādarśanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*so'pi maṃkaṇakastatra tapastepe munīśvaraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After saying thus, Mahādeva vanished from there. Maṅkaṇaka, the leading sage, began to perform penance.

## \|\| 1.40.53-54 \|\|

*atha te pannagāḥ procuḥ praṇipatya munīśvaram \|*  
*bhagavannirviṣāḥ sarve vayaṃ hi bhavatā kṛtāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ no yathā syāddāruṇaṃ viṣam \|*  
*no cedvayaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ sarvaloka parābhavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Then the serpents bowed down to the leading sage and said: “O holy Sir, all of us have been deprived of our poison by your holiness. Do a favour unto us so that the terrible poison may come back. Otherwise, we will be subjected to great discomfiture by all the people.”

## \|\| 1.40.55 \|\|

*maṃkaṇaka uvāca \|*  
*anṛtaṃ na mayā proktaṃ svaireṇāpi kadācana \|*  
*tasmādevaṃvidhāḥ sarve jalasarpā bhaviṣyatha \|\| 55 \|\|*

Maṅkaṇaka said:

55\. Untruth has never been uttered by me even for the sake of a joke. Hence you will all continue to be like this as water-snakes.

## \|\| 1.40.56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛti saṃjātā jalasarpā mahītale \|*  
*tadvadrūpā dvijihvāśca kevalaṃ viṣavarjitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Sūta said:

56\. Ever since then all of them remained as water-snakes on the earth—two-tongued serpents in form but devoid of poison.

## \|\| 1.40.57 \|\|

*atha tasminhrade martyāḥ snātvā sārasvate śubhe \|*  
*spṛṣṭvā citraśilāṃ tāṃ ca prayāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then men began to take their holy plunges in that auspicious Sārasvata Tīrtha. After touching that Citraśīla (wonderful slab) they attained the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.40.58 \|\|

*atha bhītaḥ sahasrākṣo gatvā devaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*yamena sahitastūrṇaṃ provācedaṃ vacastadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Accompanied by Yama, the terrified Thousand-eyed One (Indra) went to Lord Pitāmaha and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.40.59-60 \|\|

*tvatprasādātsamudvīkṣya gacchaṃti manujā divam \|*  
*pitāmaha mahātīrthaṃ yattvayā vihitaṃ kṣitau \|*  
*sārasvataṃ narāstatra snātvā yāṃti triviṣṭapam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*api pāpasamācārāḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā śilāṃ spṛṣṭvā tadaivāyāṃti sadgatim \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. “O Pitāmaha, men take their holy bath in the Sārasvata Mahātīrtha created by you and go to heaven. Men merely visit the Lord and go to heaven. Even persons of sinful conduct, men excluded from all righteous rites, take their bath there, touch the slab and attain the greatest goal then itself.”

## \|\| 1.40.61 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*apramāṇaṃ vibho karma saṃprayātaṃ mamocitam \|*  
*śubhāśubhaparijñānaṃ sarveṣāmeva dehinām \|\| 61 \|\|*

Yama said:

61\. A careful scrutiny of the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of all embodied beings has been the duty assigned to me, O Lord. That has become invalidated now.

## \|\| 1.40.62 \|\|

*tasmāttyaja tvaṃ māṃ deva yadvā tattīrthamuttamam \|*  
*yatprabhāvājjanairhīnāḥ saṃjātā narakā mama \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Hence, O Lord, remove one of us—either me or that excellent Tīrtha. By its power my Narakas have become devoid of people.

## \|\| 1.40.63 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā yamasya prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*prāha pārśvasthitaṃ śakraṃ tattīrthaṃ naya saṃkṣayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On hearing the words of Yama, Prapitāmaha said to Śakra who was standing nearby, “Destroy that Tīrtha.”

## \|\| 1.40.64 \|\|

*tataḥ śakro hradaṃ gatvā pūrayāmāsa pāṃsubhiḥ \|*  
*hradaṃ sārasvataṃ taṃ ca tāṃ ca citraśilāṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thereupon Śakra went to that tank and filled it with dust particles, O Brāhmaṇas, both the Sārasvata Hrada as well as the Citraśilā.

## \|\| 1.40.65 \|\|

*adyāpi manujaḥ samyakta sminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ karoti tapaścaryāṃ sa śīghaṃ siddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Even today, a man who establishes himself perfectly in that holy spot and performs penance shall attain Siddhi soon.

## \|\| 1.40.66-68 \|\|

*so'pi maṃkaṇakastatra sārddhaṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*tiṣṭhatyadyāpi vipreṃdra pūritaṃ caiva pāṃsubhiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ maṃkaṇakanyastaṃ tatrāsti sumahodayam \|*  
*tatspṛṣṭvā mānavāḥ pāpairmucyaṃte dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*māgha śuklacaturdaśyāṃ yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*sa pāpairapi saṃyuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. That leading Brāhmaṇa Maṅkaṇaka stays there even today along with Lord Śaṃbhu. The Liṅga installed by Maṅkaṇaka and filled with dust particles is still there. It brings great prosperity, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Men who touch it are rid of sins. A man who worships it on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha is honoured in Śivaloka even though he may be defiled with sins.

## Chapter 41 - Manifestation of Jalaśāyin

## \|\| 1.41.1-4 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyaivottaradigbhāge devasya jalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*sthānamasti suvikhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yastatpūjayate bhaktyā śayane bodhane hareḥ \|*  
*upavāsaparo bhūtvā sa gacchedvaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aśūnyaśayanānāma dvitīyā dayitā tithiḥ \|*  
*sadaiva devadevasya kṛṣṇā suptasya yā bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ yaḥ pūjayettatra taṃ devaṃ jalaśāyinam \|*  
*śāstroktena vidhānena sa gacchati hareḥ padam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. There is the holy spot of Lord Jalaśāyin (one who lies down in the waters i.e. Lord Viṣṇu) on the northern side (of Ānandeśvara Liṅga).

It is well-known and is destructive of all sins. One who observes fast and worships there at the time of Śayana (going to asleep by the Lord on the eleventh day in the bright half of Āṣāḍha) and Bodhana (waking up on the eleventh day in the bright half of Kārttika) of Hari, with great devotion, shall go to the place of Viṣṇu.

The Dvitīyā (second lunar day) of the dark half (of Āṣāḍha) when the Lord of Devas is asleep, is liked well by the Lord. It is called Aśūnyaśayanā (not being levoid of lying down).

On that day, if a devotee worships Lord Jalaśāyin in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the scriptural texts, he goes to Hari’s place.

## \|\| 1.41.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*jalaśāyī kathaṃ tatra saṃprāptaḥ sūtanandana \|*  
*pūjyate vidhinā kena tatsarvaṃ vistarādvada \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. O Sūtanandana, how did Jalaśāyin come to that place? What is the procedure whereby he is worshipped? Mention everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.41.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāsīdbāṣkalirnāma dānavendro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ajeyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. Formerly there was a very powerful king of Dānavas named Bāṣkali. He could not be defeated by all the Devas, Gandharvas, Uragas and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.41.7 \|\|

*athāsau bhūtalaṃ sarvaṃ vaśīkṛtvā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tato daityagaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ jagāma tridaśālayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. This powerful Dānava brought the entire earth under his control and then proceeded to the abode of Devas along with groups of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.41.8 \|\|

*tatrābhavanmahāyuddhaṃ devāsuravināśakam \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca kruddhānāmitaretaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A fight took place between the furious Devas and the Dānavas. The great war caused the destruction of both the Devas and the Asuras.

## \|\| 1.41.9 \|\|

*varṣāṇāmayutaṃ tāvadahanyahani dāruṇam \|*  
*tatrāsṛkkardamo jātaḥ parvataścāsthi saṃbhavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Everyday there occurred terrible fight and it lasted for ten thousand years. It produced muddy slush mixed with blood and a huge mountain of bones.

## \|\| 1.41.10 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte daśame samupasthite \|*  
*jitastena sahasrākṣaḥ sasainyaḥ saparigrahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When ten thousand years were completed the Thousandeyed One (Indra) was defeated by him along with his armies and followers.

## \|\| 1.41.11 \|\|

*tataḥ svargaṃ parityajya sarvadevagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṃ viṣṇoḥ śvetadvīpaṃ pratiśrayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He left heaven along with all the groups of Devas and sought refuge in Viṣṇu seeking shelter in Śvetadvīpa.

## \|\| 1.41.12 \|\|

*yatrāste bhagavānviṣṇuryoganidrāvaśaṃgataḥ \|*  
*śayānaḥ śeṣaparyaṃke lakṣmyā saṃvāhitāṃghriyuk \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is there that the Lord lies down in his Yogic slumber on the couch of Serpent Śeṣa with his feet massaged by Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 1.41.13 \|\|

*tato vedodbhavaiḥ sūktaiḥ stutiṃ cakruḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tasya devasya sadbhaktāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then, all the Devas including Vāsava, who are good devotees of that Lord, eulogized him all round by means of Vedic Sūktas.

## \|\| 1.41.14 \|\|

*athotthāya jagannāthaḥ provāca balasūdanam \|*  
*kaccitkṣemaṃ sahasrākṣa sāṃprataṃ bhuvanatraye \|*  
*yattvaṃ devagaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ svayameva ihāgataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the Lord of the universe got up and spoke to the Slayer of Bala: “O Thousand-eyed One, I hope everything is quite all right now in all the three worlds. Wherefore have you yourself come here along with the groups of Devas?”

## \|\| 1.41.15 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*bāṣkalirnāma detyendro haralabdhavaro balī \|*  
*ajeyaḥ saṃgare devaistenāhaṃ vijito raṇe \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śakra said:

15\. There is a king of Daityas named Bāṣkali. He has become very mighty through the boons acquired from Hara. He is invincible to all the Devas in battle. I have been defeated by him in the battle.

## \|\| 1.41.16 \|\|

*saṃsthitiśca kṛtā svarge sāṃprataṃ madhu sūdana \|*  
*tenaiṣa śaraṇaṃ prāpto devaiḥ sārddhaṃ surottama \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Now, O Slayer of Madhu, he has established himself in heaven. Therefore, O most excellent one among Suras, I have sought refuge in you along with the Devas.

## \|\| 1.41.17 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣabhayāddevā hiraṇyakaśipoḥ purā \|*  
*tvayā trātā vayaṃ sarve tathānyeṣāṃ durātmanām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. We, the Devas, were formerly saved by you from the danger from Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu and also from other wicked-minded ones.

## \|\| 1.41.18 \|\|

*tasmādasmādapi trāhi dānavādbalavattarāt \|*  
*bāṣkalernāsti deveśa tvāṃ muktvānyā parā gatiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hence, O Lord of Devas, save us from this mightier Dānava, Bāṣkali also. Excepting you, we have no other greater resort.

## \|\| 1.41.19-20 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ taṃ nigrahīṣyāmi saṃprāpte samaye svayam \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ samayaṃyāvatkuru śakra tapo mahat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yena te jāyate śaktistapovīryeṇa vāsava \|*  
*vadhāya tasya daityasya balayuktasya bāṣkaleḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

19-20. O Śakra, I shall myself overpower him when the proper time comes. Till that time, perform a great penance, O Vāsava, whereby through the power of penance, you will get the needed strength for slaying that Daitya, Bāṣkali, who is very mighty.

## \|\| 1.41.21 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*kasminkṣetre jagannātha karomi sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*tasya daityasya nāśārthaṃ tada smākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 21 \|\|*

Śakra said:

21\. O Lord of the universe, in which holy place should I perform the great penance for the destruction of that Daitya? Do tell it unto us.

## \|\| 1.41.22 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhagavānviṣṇuḥ provācātha puraṃdaram \|*  
*ciraṃ manasi niścitya kṣetrāṇyāyatanāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sūta said:

22\. On hearing it, Lord Viṣṇu, after thinking in his mind for a long time about holy spots and shrines, spoke to Purandara:

## \|\| 1.41.23 \|\|

*camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ śakra siddhipradāyakam \|*  
*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gatvā tadvadhārthaṃ tapaḥ kuru \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O Śakra, the holy spot Camatkārapura is one that accords Siddhi. Hence hasten to that place and perform penance for slaying him.”

## \|\| 1.41.24-25 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*na vayaṃ bhavatā hīnā yāsyāmo'nyatra keśava \|*  
*bāṣkalerdānavendrasya bhayādbhītāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasmādāgaccha tatra tvaṃ svayameva sureśvara \|*  
*tvayā saṃrakṣito yena karomi sumahattapaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Śakra said:

24-25. O Keśava, we are mortally afraid of Bāṣkali, the king of Dānavas. So, without you, we will never go elsewhere. Hence, O Lord of Suras, you too do come there yourself, so that I can perform the great penance under your protection.

## \|\| 1.41.26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sa bhagavānviṣṇustathetyuktvā suraiḥ saha \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ kṣetramājagāma saha śriyā \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sūta said:

26\. Then Lord Viṣṇu said: “It shall be so.” Accompanied by Śrī and the Suras, he came over to the holy spot Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.41.27 \|\|

*atha devagaṇāḥ sarve tatra gatvā tadā'śramān \|*  
*cakruḥ pṛthakpṛthagghṛṣṭāstapo'rthaṃ kṛtaniścayāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All the delighted groups of the Devas went there. Having resolved to perform penance, they built separate hermitages.

## \|\| 1.41.28 \|\|

*vāsudevo'pi saṃsmṛtya kṣīrodaṃ tatra sāgaram \|*  
*ānināyāśu vistīrṇaṃ hrade tasminpurātane \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vāsudeva remembered his big Ocean of Milk and brought it quickly to that ancient tank.

## \|\| 1.41.29 \|\|

*cakāra śayanaṃ tatra śvetadvīpe yathā purā \|*  
*stūyamānaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ samaṃtādvinayānvitaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. As in the Śvetadvīpa before, he lay down there even as all the Suras humbly eulogized him all round.

## \|\| 1.41.30 \|\|

*athāṣāḍhasya saṃprāpte dvitīyādivase śubhe \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe sahasrākṣaṃ svayameva bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*provāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ bāṣpavyākula locanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the advent of the auspicious second lunar day in the dark half of Āṣāḍha Bṛhaspati himself spoke these gentle words to the Thousand-eyed One whose eyes became turbid due to tears.

## \|\| 1.41.31 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*aśūnyaśayanānāma dvitīyādya puraṃdara \|*  
*atīva dayitā viṣṇoḥ prasuptasya jalāśaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

31\. O Purandara, today it is the Dvītīyā (second lunar day) named Aśūnyaśayanā. It is very dear to Viṣṇu who is asleep in the watery expanse.

## \|\| 1.41.32-33 \|\|

*asyāṃ saṃpūjito viṣṇuryāvanmāsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*dadāti sakalānkāmāndhyātaścetasi sarvadā \|*  
*śāstroktavidhinā samyagvratastho jalaśāyinam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa caturo māsāndvitīyādivase harim \|*  
*pūjayitvā sahasrākṣastejasā sahito'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. On being worshipped on this day for four months and meditated upon in the mind always, Viṣṇu fulfills all desires.

The Thousand-eyed One observed perfect Vrata in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptures. For four months, he adored Hari, the Jalaśāyin, on the Dvitīyā day and became endowed with brilliance.

## \|\| 1.41.34 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tejasā yuktaṃ parituṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*provāca śakra gacchādya vadhārthaṃ tasya bāṣkaleḥ \|*  
*sarvairdevagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ vijayaste bhaviṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing (Indra) endowed with brilliance, Janārdana became pleased. He said: “O Śakra, go this day along with all the groups of Devas for killing that Daitya Bāṣkali. You will be victorious.”

## \|\| 1.41.35 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*bibhemi tasya devāhaṃ dānavendrasya durmateḥ \|*  
*tvayā vinā na gacchāmi sārdhaṃ sarvaiḥ surairapi \|\| 35 \|\|*

Śakra said:

35\. O Lord, I am afraid of that evil-minded king of Dānavas. Without you, I dare not go even in the company of all Suras.

## \|\| 1.41.36 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tvayā saha sahasrākṣa cakrametatsudarśanam \|*  
*gamiṣyati vadhārthāya madīyaṃ suravidviṣām \|\| 36 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

36\. O Thousand-eyed One, this discus of mine, Sudarśana, will go with you for the destruction of the enemies of Suras.

## \|\| 1.41.37 \|\|

*evamuktvā hariścakraṃ pramumoca sudarśanam \|*  
*vadhārthaṃ dānavendrāṇāṃ śakreṇa sahitaṃ tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After saying thus, Hari released the discus Sudarśana along with Śakra for killing the leaders of Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.41.38 \|\|

*śakro'pi sahitastena gatvā cakreṇa kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*sarvānutsādayāmāsa dānavānraṇamūrdhani \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After going in the company of the discus Śakra exterminated all the Dānavas in the course of the battle.

## \|\| 1.41.39 \|\|

*sa cāpi bāṣkalistena cchinnaścakreṇa kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*papāta dharaṇīpṛṣṭhe vajrāhata ivācalaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Bāṣkali too was cut up entirely. He fell on the ground like a mountain struck down by thunderbolt.

## \|\| 1.41.40 \|\|

*tathānye bahavaḥ śūrā dānavā baladarpitāḥ \|*  
*hatvā sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ bhūyaḥ prāptaṃ hareḥ karam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There were many other heroic Dānavas arrogant due to their might After killing them too, the discus Sudarśana once again returned to the hand of Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.41 \|\|

*te'pi śakrādayo devāḥ prahṛṣṭā gatasaṃśayāḥ \|*  
*bhūyo viṣṇuṃ sametyātha procurnatvā tataḥ param \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Śakra and other Devas were delighted. All their suspicions and fears vanished. They approached Viṣṇu again, bowed down to him and said:

## \|\| 1.41.42 \|\|

*prabhāvāttava deveśa hatāḥ sarve'marārayaḥ \|*  
*prāptaṃ trailokyarājyaṃ ca bhūyo nihatakaṃṭakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42.43. “O Lord of Devas, by your might all the enemies of Amaras (Devas) have been killed. The kingdom of the three worlds has been regained with all the thorns removed. So tell me my duty that shall be conducive to welfare, O Lotus-eyed One, and also still fear into the enemies.”

## \|\| 1.41.44 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*mayātraiva sadā stheyaṃ rūpeṇānena vāsava \|*  
*sarvalokahitārthāya hrade puṇya jalāśraye \|\| 44 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

44\. O Vāsava, for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds I have to remain in this form for ever in this pool, the store-house of meritorious waters.

## \|\| 1.41.45 \|\|

*tvayā tasmātsamāgamya cāturmāsyaṃ śacīpate \|*  
*prayatnena prakartavyamaśūnyaśayanaṃ vratam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Consort of Sacī, you should also come here and observe Aśūnyaśayana Vrata for the duration of the four months.

## \|\| 1.41.46 \|\|

*na bhavaṃti sahasrākṣa yena te pari paṃthinaḥ \|*  
*tathābhīṣṭaphalāvāptirmatprasādādasaṃśayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereby no one will dare to be antagonistic to you, O Thousand-eyed One. With my favour you will undoubtedly obtain the benefits desired.

## \|\| 1.41.47 \|\|

*anyo'pi yo naro bhaktyā pūjayiṣyati māmiha \|*  
*saṃprāpsyati sa tāṃllokāndurlabhāṃstri daśairapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Any other man who adores me with devotion here will gain all those regions inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.41.48 \|\|

*tasmādgaccha sahasrākṣa kuru rājyaṃ triviṣṭape \|*  
*bhūyo'pyatraiva deveśa draṣṭavyo'smi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kāryakāle samāyāte śvetadvīpe yathā tathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, do go back, O Thousand-eyed One, Rule over heaven. O Lord of Devas, here again I should be seen if there be an occasion for my action. I should be visited undoubtedly as at Śvetadvīpa.

## \|\| 1.41.49 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ dṛṣṭvā prajagāma śatakratuḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo'pi tatraiva sthito lokahitāya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sūta said:

49\. Śatakratu (Indra) bowed down to him and went away. Vāsudeva stationed himself there for the sake of the welfare of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.41.50 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra dvijaśreṣṭhā jalaśāyī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*sarvalokahitārthāya saṃsthitaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Janārdana, the great Lord, stationed himself there as Jalaśāyin for the sake of the welfare, of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.41.51 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One who is endowed with great ardour and faith and who devoutly worships him particularly in the course of the four months attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.41.52 \|\|

*tathā devagaṇaiḥ sarvairdvārakā tatra sā kṛtā \|*  
*saṃpūjya tu narā yāṃti cāturmāsye triviṣṭapam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It was converted into Dvārakā by all the groups of Devas. Men who worship there during the four months go to the heaven.

## \|\| 1.41.53 \|\|

*śeṣakāle'pi cittasthānkāmānmartyaḥ samāpnuyāt \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjyā sā dvārakā naraiḥ \|*  
*sarveṣvapi hi kāleṣu cātumāsye viśeṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On other occasions too a man shall attain the desires cherished in the heart. Hence that Dvārakā should be assiduously worshipped by men at all times and during the Cāturmāsya particularly.

## \|\| 1.41.54 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ devadevasya supuṇyaṃ jalaśāyinaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus the narrative of Jalaśāyin, the Lord of Devas, has been recounted to you in full. It is meritorious and destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 42 - Menakā Meets Viśvāmitra

## \|\| 1.42.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*viśvāmitrasamudbhūtaṃ kuṇḍaṃ tatrāparaṃ śubham \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhate dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra caitratṛtīyāyāṃ kṛte snāne bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*divyarūpadharaḥ sākṣātkāmo'nyo dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nārī vā śraddhayopetā tatra snātvā prajāvatī \|*  
*bhavetsaubhāgyasaṃyuktā spṛhaṇīyatamā kṣitau \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: This is a strange story. Here Menakā falls in love with Viśvāmitra. He is not tempted, for which she curses him and Viśvāmitra retaliates with counter-curse of old age. Both became free from old age after taking a bath in Tīrtha near which Viśvāmitreśvara is installed (Chs. 42-44).

Sūta said:

1-3. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there is another splendid Kuṇḍa (holy pit) pertaining to Viśvāmitra, situated there. It yields all desires.

If holy bath is taken there on the third lunar day in the month of Caitra, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a man becomes endowed with divine form like another Kama himself.

On taking the holy bath there, a woman with ardent faith becomes pregnant. She will be a most cove table one on the earth and endowed with all conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.42.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ tasya munestatra kasminkāle vyavasthitam \|*  
*nirmalaṃ kena niḥśeṣaṃ vada tvaṃ sūtanaṃdana \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

4\. O Sūtanandana, at what time was the Tīrtha of that sage established? How is it free from all impurities? Do tell us without dropping anything.

## \|\| 1.42.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatrāsti nirjharaḥ pūrvaṃ sāmānyo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*avadhūto dharāpṛṣṭhe māhātmyena vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there was formerly an ordinary waterfall there falling down on the ground and endowed with greatness.

## \|\| 1.42.6 \|\|

*yatra devanadī gaṃgā svayameva vyavasthitā \|*  
*yasyāṃ snātaḥ pumānsadyaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The divine river Gaṅgā herself is present therein. A person who takes the holy bath there is immediately rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.42.7 \|\|

*yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ pitṝnuddiśya bhāvitaḥ \|*  
*tadakṣayaṃ bhavecchrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tṛptikārakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. If a person remains pure and performs a Śrāddha there with the Pitṛs in view, it becomes everlasting in benefit giving satisfaction to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.42.8 \|\|

*yatkiṃciddīyata dānaṃ tasmiṃstīrthavare dvijāḥ \|*  
*hutajapyādikaṃ caiva tadanaṃtaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whatever is given as religious gift in that excellent Tīrtha, O Brāhmaṇas, will have lasting benefit of unlimited nature. Homa and Japa performed there too is similar (in benefit).

## \|\| 1.42.9 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya mṛgī vyādhaśarāhatā \|*  
*praviṣṭā salile tasmiṃstatra pañcatvamāgatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Once upon a time, a doe hit by the arrow of a hunter, entered the water there and died.

## \|\| 1.42.10 \|\|

*caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ madhyāhne dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*nakṣatre yamadaivatye mārtaṃḍasya ca vāsare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, it was also the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra. It was a Sunday with the constellation Bharaṇī. The time was midday.

## \|\| 1.42.11 \|\|

*atha tattoyamāhātmyānmenakānāma sā'bhavat \|*  
*apsarāstridaśeṃdrasya samaṃtāccāruhāsinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Due to the great power of that holy water she was transformed into an Apsarā of the Lord of the Devas. She was a lady full of charming smiles shedding lustre all round.

## \|\| 1.42.12 \|\|

*smaramāṇā'tha sā tasya prabhāvaṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*tīrthamāgatya sadbhaktyā snānaṃ tatra samācarat \|*  
*caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ yāmarkṣe sūryavāsare \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Remembering the efficacy of that Tīrtha the lady of excellent complexion used to come there regularly with great devotion and take her holy bath on the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra when the constellation happened to be Bharaṇī and the day Sunday.

## \|\| 1.42.13 \|\|

*ekadā divase tasminbhramamāṇo munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitra iti khyātastatrāyātastapo'nvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Once, on that day, an eminent sage possessing the power of penance and well-known by the name Viśvāmitra came there in the course of his journey.

## \|\| 1.42.14 \|\|

*sā'pi svargātsamāyātā devatādarśanārthataḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvātha taṃ devaṃ prasthitā tridivaṃ prati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She too who had come there for visiting the deity, concluded the adoration and was about to return to heaven.

## \|\| 1.42.15-17 \|\|

*sā dṛṣṭvā taṃ muniṃ tatra bhramamāṇamitastataḥ \|*  
*yauvanasthaṃ surūpāḍhyaṃ paṃcabāṇamivāparam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vrataprabhāvajairvyāptaṃ tejobhirbhāskaraṃ yathā \|*  
*bālyātprabhṛti cīrṇena tapasā dagdhakilbiṣam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sā tasya darśanādeva kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā \|*  
*sānaṃdāḥ suratārthāya samīpaṃ samupādravat \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. She happened to see the sage who was roaming about here and there. He was in the prime of his youth with handsome features as though he was another Lord of Love wielding the five arrows. He was endowed with the radiance born of the greatness of the Vratas performed by him. He was as brilliant as the sun with refulgent rays. He had burnt all his sins by means of the penance he had performed ever since the days of his childhood.

Merely at his sight, she became afflicted by the arrows of the god of Love. In the height of her delight, she came to the vicinity of the sage for the purpose of sexual dalliance.

## \|\| 1.42.18 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā'dṛṣṭapūrvāṃ tāṃ mārgapṛcchākṛte tataḥ \|*  
*sammukhaḥ prayayau tūrṇaṃ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On seeing the lady hitherto unseen, he hastened to her vicinity with a pleased mind. He stood in front of her as though he wanted to enquire about the way.

## \|\| 1.42.19 \|\|

*uvāca deśaṃ tāṃ pṛcchanstrīdharmāṃśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śubhalābho'stu te bhadre manasā karmaṇā girā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Apparently enquiring about the land, he spoke about the duties of women in particular. “O fair lady, may you acquire auspiciousness mentally, verbally and physically.

## \|\| 1.42.20 \|\|

*sadaiva vāsudevasya bhaktiścāvyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*kaccittvaṃ vartase putri patipādaparāyaṇā \|*  
*cāritravinayopetā sarvadā priyavādinī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Let there be unswerving devotion unto Vāsudeva for ever. I hope, O daughter, you are devoted to the feet of your husband and equipped with chastity and humility and always speaking pleasant things.

## \|\| 1.42.21 \|\|

*kaccittvaṃ sarvadābhīṣṭā patyurdānaistathārccanaiḥ \|*  
*baṃdhūnsvamitravargaṃ ca tatpuraḥ pṛṣṭhatopi vā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I hope you always endear yourself to your husband making gifts to his kinsmen and circle of friends and praising them whether in front of him or behind his back.

## \|\| 1.42.22 \|\|

*kaccidbhartari saṃsupte tvaṃ niśavaśameṣyasi \|*  
*utthānamaprabuddhe ca karoṣi varavarṇini \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O lady of excellent complexion, I hope, you always go to sleep after the husband is asleep and, I hope, you gel up even before he gets up.

## \|\| 1.42.23 \|\|

*kaccitprātaḥ samutthāya karoṣi gṛhamārjanam \|*  
*svayameva varārohe maṇḍanaṃ copamaṇḍanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I hope, you get up early in the morning and do the sweeping at home, O beautiful woman. All embellishments and beautifications thereof too you yourself do.

## \|\| 1.42.24 \|\|

*kaccidevānnamaskṛtya guruṃ ca tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*karoṣi tvaṃ prāṇayātrāṃ dattvānnaṃ śaktito jalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I suppose, you bow down to the deities and then to the elders. I hope, you give food and water to others in accordance with your capacity and then take your food.

## \|\| 1.42.25 \|\|

*kaccidastaṃgate sūrye nānnamaśnāsi bhābhini \|*  
*adattvā vā svabhṛtyebhyaḥ sādhubhyaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I believe, O beautiful lady, that you never take cooked food after the Sun has set. I hope, you never take food before offering it to your servants and in particular to saintly people.

## \|\| 1.42.26 \|\|

*kaccitpibasi pānīyaṃ saptavāraviśodhitam \|*  
*nibiḍena svavastreṇa pālayaṃtī jalodbhavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I hope, you always drink water after filtering it seven times with a thick cloth thus protecting the water-borns(?)

## \|\| 1.42.27 \|\|

*kacciddayāsamopetā gātrakleśakarānapi \|*  
*yūkāmatkuṇadaṃśādīnputravatparirakṣasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I hope, you are so kind-hearted as to preserve like your sons even lice, bugs and flies that afflict your limbs awfully (!)

## \|\| 1.42.28 \|\|

*kaccitsādhumukhānnityaṃ śivadharmaṃ subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇoṣi bhaktito bhadre prakaroṣi ca sādaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I hope, you always hear straight from the mouths of good people, the Śivadharma (auspicious religious acts or devotional acts pertaining to god Śiva) with great devotion. O fair lady, I hope, you respectfully follow them too.

## \|\| 1.42.29 \|\|

*kvacicchrutvā'gamaṃ puṇyaṃ prakaroṣi ca pūjanam \|*  
*śāstrasya vācakasyāpi vyākhyātuśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I believe that you do respectfully adore the scripture, the expounder and the person who reads it after listening to it.

## \|\| 1.42.30 \|\|

*kaccitpurāṇaśāstrāṇi praṇītāni janeśvaraiḥ \|*  
*saṃlekhyākṣararamyāṇi sādhubhyaḥ saṃprayacchasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I hope, you copy in beautiful handwriting the Purāṇas and the Śāstras composed by eminent people and then give away those manuscripts to good people.

## \|\| 1.42.31 \|\|

*yaḥ śrutvā sarva śāstrāṇi niṣkrayaṃ na prayacchati \|*  
*śāstracauraḥ sa vijñeyo na caivāpnoti tatphalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One who listens to all the Śāstras but does not give the prescribed fees should be considered as Śāstra-thief. He never attains the fruit thereof.

## \|\| 1.42.32 \|\|

*kaccicchivālaye nṛtyagītavādyādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*balipūjopahārāṃśca tvaṃ karoṣi ca śaktitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I hope that you make due arrangements within your capacity for dances, songs, musical instruments and the like in the temple of Śiva. I hope, you make the customary oblations, offerings etc., within your means.

## \|\| 1.42.33 \|\|

*kaccitprāvaraṇaṃ vastraṃ subhage sarvameva ca \|*  
*saṃprayacchasi sādhubhyaḥ praṇipātapuraḥsaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I hope, O excellent lady, that you offer shawls, blankets etc. to good people after respectfully bowing down to them.

## \|\| 1.42.34 \|\|

*vṛthā paryaṭanaṃ nityaṃ kaccinna paramaṃdire \|*  
*tvaṃ karoṣi viśālākṣi viśeṣeṇa niśāgame \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lady of wide eyes, I hope you avoid straying intonhe abodes of others unnecessarily without any work always, especially after nightfall.

## \|\| 1.42.35 \|\|

*kaccinnāśnāsi bhadre tvaṃ svabhartari bubhukṣite \|*  
*ājñābhaṃgaṃ prayatnena kaccittatra prarakṣasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I hope, O fair lady, you never take food while your husband is hungry. I hope, you take care to avoid disobedience to his command.

## \|\| 1.42.36 \|\|

*kaccitprakupite kāṃte nottarāṇi prayacchasi \|*  
*tasyakopapraṇāśārṣaṃ priyaṃ kaccicca jalpasi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I hope, you never retort when the husband is angry. I hope, you speak pleasant things to dispel his anger.

## \|\| 1.42.37 \|\|

*kaccittvaṃ proṣite kāṃte malināṃbaradhāriṇī \|*  
*jāyase ca tathā dīnā vivarṇavadanā kṛśā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I hope that when your husband is away from home you wear dirty clothes and become distressed, lean and pallid in face.

## \|\| 1.42.38 \|\|

*kaccinmaṃdirapṛṣṭhe tvaṃ na dhatse bhinnabhājanam \|*  
*ucchiṣṭaṃ vā janaistyaktamapi kāryopakārakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I hope that you never keep broken vessels in the backyard of the house or the remnants of food taken in by the people, though they may be of use.

## \|\| 1.42.39 \|\|

*kaccidvrajasi no rātrau jāgareṣu kathāsu ca \|*  
*nirjhareṣu vivikteṣu pulineṣu vaneṣu ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I hope, you never wander at night even for religious vigils and discourses, in streams, isolated places, forests and sand banks.

## \|\| 1.42.40 \|\|

*kaccinna kuruṣe maitrīṃ baṃdhakībhiḥ samaṃ śubhe \|*  
*dhātrībhirmālikastrībhī rajakībhiśca bhāmini \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O splendid lady, I hope, you never contract friendship with courtezans, nurses, a gardners’s wife and a washermen’s wife.

## \|\| 1.42.41 \|\|

*kañciddadhāsi nityaṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ kuṃkumaraṃjitam \|*  
*śiraḥ puṣpasamākīrṇaṃ netre kajjalaraṃjite \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I hope, you always keep your face brightly coloured with saffron, hairs decorated with flowers and the eyes darkened by collyrium.”

## Chapter 43 - Dialogue between Viśvāmitra and Menakā

## \|\| 1.43.1 \|\|

*\| menakovāca \|*  
*anyāstā nāyikā vipra yāsāṃ dharmastvayoditaḥ \|*  
*svecchācāravihāriṇyo vayaṃ veśyā divaukasām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Menakā said:

1\. O Brāhmaṇa, the women for whom the code of virtuous conduct you have spoken (prescribed) so far are different. We are, on the other hand, courtesans of Heaven-dwellers, who wander freely according to our sweet will.

## \|\| 1.43.2 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ vada mahābhāga kasmāddeśātsamāgataḥ \|*  
*mama cittaharo vāpi tīrthe dharmiṣṭhasaṃśraye \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Anyway, O highly esteemed one, tell me what is that land from which you have come? Even in this Tīrtha, the resort of Virtuous ones, you are the captivator of my heart.

## \|\| 1.43.3-4 \|\|

*tvāṃ dṛṣṭvāhaṃ mahābhāga kāmadeva samākṛtim \|*  
*pulakāṃcitasarvāṃgī kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasmādbhajasva māṃ raktāṃ no cedyāsyāmi saṃkṣayam \|*  
*kāmabāṇapradagdhā vai puro'pi tava tāpasa \|*  
*tataḥ strīvadhapāpena lipyase tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O highly fortunate one, your personal form is on a par with that of Kāmadeva. On seeing you I have become tormented by the arrows of Kāma. I experience horripilation all over my limbs.

So accept me and enjoy me. I am attached to you. If you do not, I will be doomed. Already scorched by the arrows of Kāma, O ascetic, I will die in front of you. Thereby you will incur the sin of the murder of a woman. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.43.5 \|\|

*tāpasa uvāca \|*  
*vayaṃ vratadharāḥ subhru brahmacaryaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mūrkhāḥ kāmavidhau bhadre niratāḥ śivaśāsane \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Tāpasa (Ascetic) said:

5\. O lady of excellent eyebrows, we are persons with holy vows, strictly adhering to the vow of celibacy. O fair lady, of course we are fools (totally ignorant) in the matters of love as we abide by the Śivaśāsana (Śaiva Śāstra).

## \|\| 1.43.6 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ vratināṃ mūlaṃ brahmacaryamudāhṛtam \|*  
*viśeṣācchivabhaktānāmevaṃ bhūyo vidhāsyasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Brahmacarya (celibacy) is cited as the root of all holy vows and restraints, especially in the case of devotees of Śiva. Hereafter you will do what is proper bearing this in mind (I am not a sex addict. Don’t court me—Editor’s footnote).

## \|\| 1.43.7 \|\|

*api varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ yattapaḥ kurute vratī \|*  
*sakṛtstrīsaṃgamānnāśaṃ yāti pāśupatasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A man of vows may perform penance for more than a hundred years. But sexual dalliance even once brings about utter destruction of his Pāśupata vow.

## \|\| 1.43.8 \|\|

*māṃ ca pāśupataṃ lubdhā kasmāttvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase \|*  
*īdṛkpāpatamaṃ karma garhitaṃ śivaśāsane \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O timid lady, why do you speak as though you are enamoured of me, a follower of Paśupati (Lord Śiva). Such a highly sinful activity as this is condemned in Śivaśāsana. (Śaiva Śāstra or Pāśupatism).

## \|\| 1.43.9 \|\|

*yaḥ strīṃ bhajati pāpātmā vṛthā pāśupatavratī \|*  
*so'tītāndaśa cādhāya puruṣānnarake pacet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A man of the holy vow of Pāśupatism, who enjoys a woman, becomes a false Pāśupata. Along with ten earlier generations of his family, he will be cooked in Naraka.

## \|\| 1.43.10 \|\|

*āstāṃ tāvatsamā saṃgaṃ saṃsparśaṃ ca varānane \|*  
*saṃbhāṣamapi pāpāya strībhiḥ pāśupatasya ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O lady of excellent countenance, leave alone sexual union or even touch of a lady, even conversation with a woman leads to a great sin in the case of a Pāśupata.

## \|\| 1.43.11 \|\|

*tasmād drutataraṃ gaccha sthānādasmādvarāṃgane \|*  
*yatrāvāpsyasi cābhīṣṭaṃ tatra tvaṃ gantumarhasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hence, O beautiful lady, go away from this place. It behoves you to go there where your desires can be fulfilled.

## Chapter 44 - Greatness of Viśvāmitreśvara

## \|\| 1.44.1-2 \|\|

*\| menakovāca \|*  
*nūnaṃ hi kāmadharme tvaṃ na pravīṇo mahādyute \|*  
*tena māmīdṛśairvākyairnivārayasi rāgiṇīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktastato bhūyo viśvāmitro'bravīdidam \|*  
*kopena mahatā yukto niḥspṛhastatparigrahe \|\| 2 \|\|*

Menakā said:

1-2. O highly lustrous one, you are not an expert in sexual acts indeed. That is why you restrain me, a loving woman, by means of words like these.

## \|\| 1.44.3 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ jīva gaccha vā mṛtyuṃ nāhaṃ kartāsmi te vacaḥ \|*  
*vratanāśāttu yatpāpamadhikaṃ strīvadhādbhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

On being told thus, Viśvāmitra who never desired to accept her as his wife, became very angry and he said thus:

Viśvāmitra said:

3\. You may live or court death. I will not carry out your words. The sin originating from the violation of one’s holy vow, is worse than that from the murder of a woman.

## \|\| 1.44.4 \|\|

*prāyaścittaṃ budhairuktaṃ vratināṃ strīvadhe kṛte \|*  
*na saṃgāttu punastāsāṃ tasmāttvaṃ gantumarhasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Expiation has been prescribed by learned men in regard to men of holy vows when the murder of a woman is committed but not when they come into carnal contact with them. Hence you may go away.

## \|\| 1.44.5 \|\|

*na kevalaṃ vratopetāḥ strīsaṃgātpāpamāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*vratabāhyā api narāḥ saktāḥ strīṣu pataṃtyadhaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is not that only men who have adopted holy vows incur sin from physical intimacy of women. Even men outside the pale of holy vows face downfall if they are attached to women.

## \|\| 1.44.6 \|\|

*saṃsārabhramaṇaṃ nārī prathamepi samāgame \|*  
*vahnipradakṣiṇā vyājanyāyenaiva pradarśayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even at the time of the first meeting under the pretext of circumambulating the sacred fire (in marriage ceremony) a woman indicates transmigration (coming and going) in Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 1.44.7 \|\|

*tasmātstrībhiḥ samaṃ prājñaḥ saṃbhāṣāmapi varjayet \|*  
*āstāṃ tāvatsamāsaṃgaṃ ya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence a wise man who desires his own welfare should avoid conversations with women, let alone physical, intimate contact.

## \|\| 1.44.8 \|\|

*aṃgāra sadṛśā nārī ghṛtakuṃbhasamaḥ pumān \|*  
*asparśāddṛḍhatāmeti tatsaṃparkādvilīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A woman is like a smouldering, charcoal. A man is like a pot of ghee. Avoiding the contact he remains strong (compact); by the contact he becomes ruined (melts).

## \|\| 1.44.9 \|\|

*striyo mūlamanarthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ bhuvi \|*  
*tasmāttyājyā sudūreṇa tāḥ svargasya nirodhakāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Women are at the root of all disasters and adversities of all the living beings on the earth. Hence they should be kept off at a safe distance, because they are obstacles to the attainment of heaven.

## \|\| 1.44.10 \|\|

*kulīnā vittavatyaśca nāthavatyo'pi yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*ekasminnaṃtare rāgaṃ kurvaṃtyetāḥ sucañcalāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Women of noble families commanding great affluence and having their own husbands begin to love someone else. They are very fickle.

## \|\| 1.44.11 \|\|

*na strībhyaḥ kiṃcidanyaddhi pāpāya vidyate bhuvi \|*  
*yāsāṃ saṃgasamāsādya saṃsāre bhramate janaḥ \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By coming into contact with women, people wander about in the worldly existence. Hence no one other than women contributes anything to sin on the earth.

## \|\| 1.44.12 \|\|

*nīco'pi kurute sevāṃ yastāsāṃ vijaneṣvatha \|*  
*virūpaṃ vāpi nīcaṃ vā taṃ sevante hi tāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Women attend to a base man who serves them in isolated places even if he be ugly and base-born.

## \|\| 1.44.13 \|\|

*anarthatvānmanuṣyāṇāṃ bhayātparijanasya ca \|*  
*maryādāyāmamaryādāḥ striyastiṣṭhanti bhartṛṣu \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Women of uncontrolled nature abide by the conventional decorum with their husbands only because they are afraid of the servants and danger from other men.

## \|\| 1.44.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbhartsitā tena menakā kopasaṃyutā \|*  
*śaśāpa taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ sphuramāṇoṣṭhasaṃpuṭā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. Thus rebuked by him Menakā became very angry. With her lips throbbing much through anger, she cursed that excellent sage.

## \|\| 1.44.15-16 \|\|

*yasmāttvayā parityaktā sakāmāhaṃ sudurmate \|*  
*tyajatā kāmajaṃ dharmaṃ tasmācchāpaṃ gṛhāṇa me \|\| 15 \|\|*

*adyaiva bhava duburddhe valīpalitasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*jarājarjjaritāṃgaśca tucchadṛṣṭirviraṃgitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. “O highly evil-minded one, by avoiding the sexual dalliance (with me) you have abandoned me though I am sexually excited. So, take this curse from me. Be now itself one with wrinkles and grey hair, one with the limbs shattered by old age, one of dim vision and bereft of colour, O evil-minded one.”

## \|\| 1.44.17 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*uktamātre tu vacane tatkṣaṇānmunisattamaḥ \|*  
*babhūva tādṛśaḥ sadyastayā yādṛkprakīrtitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sūta said:

17\. Immediately after these words had been uttered, the excellent sage came to be one as imprecated by her.

## \|\| 1.44.18 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā so'pi tāṃ śaptumudyataḥ \|*  
*kamaṇḍalorjalaṃ gṛhya saṃtāpādraktalocanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He too became highly furious and attempted to curse her. With eyes reddened due to distress, he took water from the waterpot.

## \|\| 1.44.19 \|\|

*nirdoṣo'pi tvayā yasmācchapto'haṃ gaṇikādhame \|*  
*tasmādbhava tvamapyāśu jarājarjaritāṃgikā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O basest courtezan, although I am blameless I have been cursed by you. So you too shall become one with the limbs shattered due to old age.”

## \|\| 1.44.20 \|\|

*sāpi tadvacanātsadyastādṛgrūpā vyajāyata \|*  
*yādṛśo'sau muniśreṣṭho valīpalitagātrabhṛt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At his words she too became one of that type of physical form as that of the excellent sage with the body covered with wrinkles and grey hairs.

## \|\| 1.44.21 \|\|

*atha tādṛksvarūpeṇa snātā tatra jalā śaye \|*  
*bhūyo'pi tādṛśī jātā yādṛśī saṃsthitā purā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then, along with such a hideous form she took her bath in the Tīrtha whereat she got transformed into her original form.

## \|\| 1.44.22 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā paramāścaryamatīva tvarayānvitaḥ \|*  
*so'pi tatrākarotsnānaṃ saṃjātaśca yathā purā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing that great miracle, he took in a very great haste, his bath there and became transformed as before.

## \|\| 1.44.23 \|\|

*tatastau tīrthamāhātmyādrūpaudāryaguṇānvitau \|*  
*mitha āmaṃtrya saṃhṛṣṭau gatau deśaṃ yathepsitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus, by the power of the Tīrtha both of them became endowed with handsome features, beauty and exalted virtues. They joyously took leave of each other and went to the place they desired.

## \|\| 1.44.24 \|\|

*evaṃ tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ vijñāya bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By coming to know the greatness of the Tīrtha in this manner, the holy sage installed the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.44.25 \|\|

*tapaścakāra sumahattasmiṃstīrthavare tadā \|*  
*kuśastambena kṛtavāṃstatsaro vipulaṃ vibhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The holy lord performed very great penance at that excellent Tīrtha. By means of the blades of Kuśa grass, he made the lake very wide.

## \|\| 1.44.26 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro yastu pūjayelliṃgamuttamam \|*  
*viśvāmitreśvaraṃ khyātaṃ sa gacchecchivamaṃdiram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A man who takes his holy bath there and worships the excellent Liṅga well-known as Viśvāmitreśvara shall go to Śiva’s palace.

## \|\| 1.44.27 \|\|

*adyāpi dṛśyate tatra gaṃgodakasamaṃ jalam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even today the water seen there is on a par with the water of Gaṅgā, meritorious, destructive of all sins and yielding all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.44.28 \|\|

*yastatra kurute snānaṃ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*sa devalokamāsādya pitṛbhiḥ saha modate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who takes his holy bath there with the mind sanctified by faith, shall attain the world of Devas and rejoice along with the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.44.29 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ khyātiṃ prāptaṃ mahītale \|*  
*pātāle svargaloke ca rūpaudāryapradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Ever since then that Tīrtha earned a great reputation that it bestows exalted handsomeness on men all over the earth, the nether world and the heavenly region.

## \|\| 1.44.30 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitreśa māhātmyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Viśvāmitreśa, that is destructive of all sins and about which I had been asked, has been completely narrated to you all.

## Chapter 45 - Greatness of Tripuṣkara

## \|\| 1.45.1-20 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraivāsti dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ supuṇyaṃ puṣkaratrayam \|*  
*yatra pūrvaṃ tapastaptamānartādhipabhūbhujā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yastatra kārtike māsi kṛttikāsthe niśākare \|*  
*madhyāhne kurute snānaṃ sa gacchati parāṃ gatim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tatra samāyātaṃ supuṇyaṃ puṣkaratrayam \|*  
*kasminsthāne ca vijñeyaṃ kaiścihnairvada sūtaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi yaiścihnaiḥ puṣkaratrayam \|*  
*prāgdṛṣṭaṃ muninā tatra viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*purā nivasatastasya viśvāmitrasya sanmuneḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptā kārtikī puṇyā kṛttikāyogasaṃyutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarvatīrthamayaṃ kṣetraṃ tadvijñāya taponidhiḥ \|*  
*tataśca cintayāmāsa svacitte gādhinandanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*adyeyaṃ kārtikī puṇyā kṛttikāyogasaṃyutā \|*  
*yasyāṃ snāne naraiḥ śreyaḥ prāpyate puṣkarodake \|*  
*ādyaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ dūre na gantuṃ śakyate'dhunā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmādatra sthitaṃ yacca tasminsnānaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*sa evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tataścānveṣayāmāsa puṣkarāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*bahutvāttatra tīrthānāṃ niścayaṃ nānvapadyata \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvā jalasthānaṃ snānaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|*  
*sa tadā śramamāpanno bhramamāṇa itastataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vṛkṣamūlaṃ samāśritya niviṣṭaśca kṣitau tataḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāvātha śucirbhūtvā śraddhayā ca tripuṣkaram \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

*madhyamādyojanaṃ svargaḥ kaniṣṭhādardha yojanam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhakuṇḍātpunaḥ khyāto hastaprāyaḥ śubhātmabhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pāvayaṃti hi tīrthāni snānadānādasaṃśayam \|*  
*puṣkarālokanādeva naraḥ pāpātpramu cyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*puṣkarāraṇyamāśritya śākamūlaphalairapi \|*  
*ekasminbhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*puṣkare duṣkaraṃ snānaṃ puṣkare duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*puṣkare duṣkaro vāsaḥ sarvaṃ puṣkaraduṣkaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge puṣkare snāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*sa kṣaṇānmucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇodbhavāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhe prātaśca madhyāhne madhyame snāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*kaniṣṭhe'stamite bhānau sakṛtsvargamavāpnuyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tāvattiṣṭhati deheṣu pātakaṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*yāvanna pauṣkaraistoyaiḥ snānaṃ vai kurvate narāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*divākarakaraiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ tamo yadvatpraṇaśyati \|*  
*puṣkarodakasaṃsparśācchīghraṃ gacchati pātakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtvāpi puruṣo bhuvi \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ puṣkare snātvā nirdoṣatvaṃ prapadyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

Note: Puṣkara lake is near Ajmer in Rajasthan. It is glorified in Mbh and ocher Purāṇas. God Brahmā performed a sacrifice here. This Purāṇa claims the existence of this holy place at Camatkārapura as well.

Sūta said:

1-2 O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there itself is the highly meritorious group of three Puṣkaras where penance was performed formerly by the king of Ānarta. One who takes his holy bath there at midday in the month of Kārttika when the Moon is in the constellation Kṛttikā (i.e. on the full-moon day) attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.45.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tatra samāyātaṃ supuṇyaṃ puṣkaratrayam \|*  
*kasminsthāne ca vijñeyaṃ kaiścihnairvada sūtaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:
