3\. O son of Sūta, do tell us how the highly meritorious group of three Puṣkaras happened to be there? At what holy spot should it be identified? What are the signs thereof.

## \|\| 1.45.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi yaiścihnaiḥ puṣkaratrayam \|*  
*prāgdṛṣṭaṃ muninā tatra viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. I shall describe unto you how the intelligent sage Viśvāmitra saw (recognized) the group of the three Puṣkaras formerly by what indicators.

## \|\| 1.45.5 \|\|

*purā nivasatastasya viśvāmitrasya sanmuneḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptā kārtikī puṇyā kṛttikāyogasaṃyutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Formerly when the excellent sage Viśvāmitra was staying there, the meritorious Kārttikī (full-moon day in the month of Kārttika) arrived when the constellation was Kṛttikā.

## \|\| 1.45.6 \|\|

*sarvatīrthamayaṃ kṣetraṃ tadvijñāya taponidhiḥ \|*  
*tataśca cintayāmāsa svacitte gādhinandanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The storehouse of penance, the son of Gādhi, realized that the holy spot consisted of all the Tīrthas. Then he thought thus in his mind.

## \|\| 1.45.7-9 \|\|

*adyeyaṃ kārtikī puṇyā kṛttikāyogasaṃyutā \|*  
*yasyāṃ snāne naraiḥ śreyaḥ prāpyate puṣkarodake \|*  
*ādyaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ dūre na gantuṃ śakyate'dhunā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmādatra sthitaṃ yacca tasminsnānaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*sa evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tataścānveṣayāmāsa puṣkarāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*bahutvāttatra tīrthānāṃ niścayaṃ nānvapadyata \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. ‘It happens that today is the highly meritorious Kārttikī with the Kṛttikā constellation. On this day, if men take their holy bath in the waters of Puṣkara, welfare is attained by them. The primordial Puṣkara is very far off. It is not possible to go there now. So, I shall take the holy bath in the Tīrtha situated here.’

After resolving thus with the mind sanctified by ardent faith, he began to search for the Puṣkaras all round. Due to the multiplicity of the Tīrthas, he could not come to a decision.

## \|\| 1.45.10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvā jalasthānaṃ snānaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|*  
*sa tadā śramamāpanno bhramamāṇa itastataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Wherever he saw a pool of water, he took his holy bath there. Wandering here and there he became tired.

## \|\| 1.45.11 \|\|

*vṛkṣamūlaṃ samāśritya niviṣṭaśca kṣitau tataḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāvātha śucirbhūtvā śraddhayā ca tripuṣkaram \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He came to the root of a tree. Standing there on the ground and remaining pure he faithfully eulogized Tripuṣkara:

## \|\| 1.45.12 \|\|

*madhyamādyojanaṃ svargaḥ kaniṣṭhādardha yojanam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhakuṇḍātpunaḥ khyāto hastaprāyaḥ śubhātmabhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “Svarga is within a Yojana from the middle Puṣkara and half a Yojana from the least (smallest) one. Splendid souls have proclaimed that Svarga is within the reach of a hand from the greatest Kuṇḍa (holy pit).

## \|\| 1.45.13 \|\|

*pāvayaṃti hi tīrthāni snānadānādasaṃśayam \|*  
*puṣkarālokanādeva naraḥ pāpātpramu cyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Other Tīrthas indeed sanctify the devotees undoubtedly who take holy plunge and perform Dāna. But, one is rid of sins merely by a visit to Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.45.14 \|\|

*puṣkarāraṇyamāśritya śākamūlaphalairapi \|*  
*ekasminbhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After arriving at the forest region of Puṣkara if one feeds a single Brāhmaṇa with greens, roots and fruits, it is as effective as though a core of Brāhmaṇas are fed.

## \|\| 1.45.15 \|\|

*puṣkare duṣkaraṃ snānaṃ puṣkare duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*puṣkare duṣkaro vāsaḥ sarvaṃ puṣkaraduṣkaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is very difficult (to get the opportunity of) having a holy plunge in Puṣkara; penance at Puṣkara is rarely achieved. Residence at Puṣkara is also very rare. Everything in Puṣkara is rarely achieved.

## \|\| 1.45.16 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge puṣkare snāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*sa kṣaṇānmucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇodbhavāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A man who takes his holy bath in Puṣkara on the occasion of Kārttikī along with the Kṛttikā constellation is instantly rid of sins incurred ever since birth and till death.

## \|\| 1.45.17 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe prātaśca madhyāhne madhyame snāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*kaniṣṭhe'stamite bhānau sakṛtsvargamavāpnuyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A man who takes but a single holy plunge in the morning in the biggest Puṣkara, at midday in the middle Puṣkara aṇd after sunset in the smallest Puṣkara shall attain Svarga.

## \|\| 1.45.18 \|\|

*tāvattiṣṭhati deheṣu pātakaṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*yāvanna pauṣkaraistoyaiḥ snānaṃ vai kurvate narāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sin abides in the bodies of the embodied beings only until they take their holy bath in the waters of Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.45.19 \|\|

*divākarakaraiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ tamo yadvatpraṇaśyati \|*  
*puṣkarodakasaṃsparśācchīghraṃ gacchati pātakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Just as darkness touched by the rays of the sun gets dissolved, so also sin vanishes quickly after coining into contact with the waters of Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.45.20 \|\|

*brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtvāpi puruṣo bhuvi \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ puṣkare snātvā nirdoṣatvaṃ prapadyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Even after committing Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and other sins on the earth, a person becomes free from defects (sins) if he bathes in Puṣkara on the Kārttikī day.

## \|\| 1.45.21 \|\|

*kiṃ dānaiḥ kiṃ vratairhomaiḥ kiṃ yajñairvahuvistaraiḥ \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ puṣkare snānaiḥ sarveṣāṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Of what avail is Dāna? Of what importance is Homa? Of what avail is elaborate Yajña? The benefit of all these is achieved through a holy baths in Puṣkara on the Kārttikī day.

## \|\| 1.45.22 \|\|

*yadyeṣā bhāratī satyā mayā samyamudīritā \|*  
*tanme syāddarśanaṃ śīghraṃ sadyaḥ puṣkarasaṃbhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If this statement perfectly uttered by me is true, let Puṣkara be seen immediately.”

## \|\| 1.45.23 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya bruvāṇasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*aśarīrā'bhavadvāṇī gaganāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even as the intelligent Viśvāmitra was saying thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there arose an unembodied voice from the sky.

## \|\| 1.45.24 \|\|

*viśvāmitra muniśreṣṭha sadā me gagane sthitiḥ \|*  
*muktvaikāṃ kārtikīṃ caiva kṛttikāyogasaṃyutām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “O Viśvāmitra, O most excellent one among sages, my perpetual residence is in the sky excepting the single occasion of Kārttikī accompanied by the Kṛttikā constellation.

## \|\| 1.45.25 \|\|

*tadatra divase vāso mama bhūmitale dhruvam \|*  
*asminneva vane puṇye tattvaṃ snānaṃ samācara \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Therefore on this day I certainly come to the earth in this very meritorious forest. Therefore you perform the rite of holy bath.”

## \|\| 1.45.26 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ śrūyate ca samāśrayaḥ \|*  
*tatkathaṃ vedmi tīrtheśa tvāmatraiva vyavasthitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

26\. We hear that this place is a supporting base in the case of all Tīrthas. O Lord of all the Tīrthas, how can I identify you stationed here itself.

## \|\| 1.45.27 \|\|

*tadotthitā punarvāṇī tārā gaganagocarā \|*  
*viśvāmitraṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ harṣayaṃtī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a loud voice originating in the aerial space rose up once more, delighting Viśvāmitra, the most excellent one among sages:

## \|\| 1.45.28-31 \|\|

*nātidūre vanādasmādatra saṃti jalāśayāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmekatame padmaṃ vidyate'dhomukhaṃ sthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ūrdhvavaktraṃ dvitīye ca tiryagvaktraṃ tṛtīyake \|*  
*tatrordhvāsyaiḥ sarojaiśca vijñeyaṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pārśvavaktrairdvijaśreṣṭha madhyamaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*adhovaktraistathā jñeyaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ puṣkaraṃ kṣitau \|\| 30 \|\|*

*etaiścihnairmuniśreṣṭha jñātvā snānaṃ samācara \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa munistūrṇaṃ samutthāya yayau tataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. “Not far from this forest there are (three) watery expanses (lakes). In one of them there is a lotus with face stooping down. In the second it has the face lifted up. In the third the face is turned sideways. Among them the Jyeṣṭha Puṣkara (the greatest Puṣkara) should be identified through the lotuses with faces lifted up.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the identification mark of the middle one is the lotuses with faces turned sideways. The smallest Puṣkara should be identified through the lotuses with faces downwards. O excellent Sage, after identifying them through these signs do perform your holy bath.”

On hearing it the sage got up and went away quickly.

## \|\| 1.45.32-35 \|\|

*tādṛśaiḥ kamalaistatra saṃsthitāste jalāśayāḥ \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā śraddhayopetaḥ kṛtvā snānaṃ yathākramam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tataśca vidhinā samyakcakārapitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tataḥ śākaiśca mūlaiśca nīvāraiḥ phalasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*cakāra vidhinā śrāddhaṃ tatraiva dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tatra tasyaiva tīrastho vīkṣāṃcakre samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge cihnadarśanalālasaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. Those lakes were seen with such lotuses. On seeing them the sage endowed with ardent faith performed the holy bath in due order. Then he offered libations to the Pitṛs in accordance with injunctions. Thereby, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he performed in accordance with the injuctions the rite of Śrāddha through greens, roots and Nīvāra rice-grains together with fruits. Thereafter he stood on the bank itself and began to look around with mental concentration. He was keen to see the signs of identification of the conjunction of Kṛttikā constellation with the Kārttikī day.

## \|\| 1.45.36 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ jāyate cihnaṃ kārtikyāṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare \|*  
*saṃprāpte kṛttikāyoge sarvaṃ tatra vadāśu naḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

36\. Of what nature is the sign in the greatest Puṣkara on the Kārttikī day when there is the conjunction of Kṛttikā constellation. Describe everything to us quickly.

## \|\| 1.45.37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge yadā gacchati caṃdramāḥ \|*  
*tadā niṣkrāmati śreṣṭhaṃ kamalaṃ jalamadhyataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sūta said:

37\. On the Kārttikī day when the Moon comes into contact with Kṛttikā constellation, an excellent lotus comes up from the middle of water.

## \|\| 1.45.38 \|\|

*tanmadhyeṃ'guṣṭhamātrastu puruṣo dṛśyate janaiḥ \|*  
*susnātaiḥ śraddhayopetaistatastīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Within it a being of the size of thumb is seen by the people endowed with ardent faith, who have taken their holy bath duly. Thereafter, a devotee obtains the merit of pilgrimage to the Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.45.39 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇātsnātvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*taccihnaṃ vīkṣayāmāsa mahadyatnaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It was for this reason that the great sage Viśvāmitra strenuously looked around for the expected sign after his holy bath.

## \|\| 1.45.40 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ vīkṣamāṇasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*ānartādhipatistatra prāpto rājā bṛhadbalaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even as the intelligent Viśvâmitra was watching thus, King Bṛhadbala, the overlord of Ānarta, came there.

## \|\| 1.45.41-42 \|\|

*atyaṃtaṃ mṛgayāśrāṃto hatvā mṛgagaṇānbahūn \|*  
*ṛkṣāṃścaiva varāhāṃśca sāraṃgānatha saṃbarān \|\| 41 \|\|*

*siṃhānvyāghrānvṛkāṃścaiva hiṃsānāraṇyacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*tathānyānapi madhyāhne tena mārgeṇa saṃgataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. He was extremely tired after hunting herds of deer, bears, boars, stags and Saṃbara bucks, lions tigers, wolves and other wild beasts of prey. He reached that place at midday along that path.

## \|\| 1.45.43 \|\|

*athāpaśyaddrumopāṃte viśvāmitraṃ munīśvaram \|*  
*upaviṣṭaṃ kṛtasnānaṃ vīkṣamāṇaṃ jalāśayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Near a tree he saw Viśvāmitra, the leading sage. He was seated there after his holy bath keenly watching the lake before him.

## \|\| 1.45.44 \|\|

*tatastaṃ praṇipatyoccairavatīrya turaṃgamāt \|*  
*śramārttaḥ salile tasminpraviveśa nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The king got down from the horse and bowed down to the sage. The excellent king was excessively tired and so entered the water of the lake.

## \|\| 1.45.45 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare toyātkamalaṃ tadvinirgatam \|*  
*sahasrapatrasaṃjuṣṭaṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In the meantime that lotus came up from the water. It had a thousand petals and its lustre was similar to that of twelve Suns.

## \|\| 1.45.46 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā sa mahīpālaḥ padmamatyadbhutaṃ mahat \|*  
*jagrāha kautukāviṣṭaḥ svayaṃ savyena pāṇinā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing that large wonderful lotus, the king was curious and he caught hold of it with his left hand.

## \|\| 1.45.47 \|\|

*spṛṣṭamātre tatastasminkamale dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*utthitaḥ sumahāñchabdo viśvaṃ yena prapūritam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, hardly had the lotus been touched When a loud report was heard which filled the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.45.48 \|\|

*taṃ śabdaṃ sa mahīpālaḥ śrutvā mūrchāmupāviśat \|*  
*patitaśca jale tasminpadmaṃ cādarśanaṃ gatam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing that sound, the king swooned and fell into the water. The lotus vanished.

## \|\| 1.45.49 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchreṇa mahatā karṣitaḥ salilādbahiḥ \|*  
*sevakairduḥkhaśokārttairhāheti pratijalpakaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. With very great difficulty, he was pulled out of the water by his attendants miserable and grief-stricken uttering cries of “Hā! Hā!"

## \|\| 1.45.50 \|\|

*tatastīraṃ samāsādya kṛcchrātprāpyātha cetanām \|*  
*yāvadvīkṣayati svāṃgaṃ tāvatkuṣṭhaṃ samāgatam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After reaching the banks, he regained consciousness with great difficulty. As he glanced over his body he found it affected by leprosy.

## \|\| 1.45.51 \|\|

*tato viṣādamāpanno dṛṣṭvā tādṛṅnijaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*śīrṇaghrāṇāṃghrihastaṃ ca ghargharasvarasaṃyutam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The nose, the hands and the feet were badly affected and decayed. His voice was gruff. He became sad and gloomy.

## \|\| 1.45.52 \|\|

*atha gatvā muneḥ pārśve viśvāmitrasya bhūmipaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ dīnaṃ bāṣpagadgadayā girā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Approaching Viśvāmitra, the king uttered wretched, feeble words choked with tears.

## \|\| 1.45.53-54 \|\|

*bhagavanpaśya me jātaṃ yādṛśaṃ vapureva hi \|*  
*akasmādeva magnasya salile'tra vigarhitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tatkiṃ pānīyadoṣo vā kiṃ vā bhūmermunī śvara \|*  
*yenedṛksahasā yātaṃ vikṛtiṃ me śarīrakam \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. “O holy sage, see how despicable my body has become all of a sudden as I went into the water. O leading sage, could it be any defect of the water or the soil beneath, that my body has suddenly attained this serious mal-transformation?”

## \|\| 1.45.55 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*sāvitraṃ padmamevaitadyatspṛṣṭaṃ bhūpate tvayā \|*  
*ucchiṣṭena ravirmadhye svayaṃ yasya vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

55\. This is a solar lotus. Within it Lord Sun himself is present. But you touched it with an Ucchiṣṭa (impure) body.

## \|\| 1.45.56 \|\|

*yadā syātkṛttikāyogaḥ kārtike māsi pārthiva \|*  
*śaśāṃkasya tadā caitajjāyate pauṣkare jale \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O king, when in the month of Kārttika the Moon comes into conjunction with Kṛttikā constellation, this comes up from the waters of the Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.45.57 \|\|

*tadidaṃ puṣkaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhavānyatra śramāturaḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ kārtikī cādya kṛttikāyogasaṃyutā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. This Puṣkara is the Jyeṣṭha (greatest) which you got into on being weary. Today is the Full-Moon day in the month of Kārttika and there is the conjunction of Kṛttikā constellation.

## \|\| 1.45.58 \|\|

*etadvīkṣya naro hyatra snānaṃ kuryājjalāśaye \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yuktaḥ sa gacchati parāṃ gatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After seeing this a man with ardour and faith should take his holy bath. He shall attain the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.45.59 \|\|

*ucchiṣṭena tvayā rājanharaṇāya hi kevalam \|*  
*etatsaroruhaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ tenedṛksaṃsthitaṃ phalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It was only to pluck it out, O king, that you touched the lotus and that too when you were Ucchiṣṭa (impure). Therefore this is the result.

## \|\| 1.45.60 \|\|

*bṛhadbala uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ me syānmuniśreṣṭha kuṣṭhavyādhiparikṣayaḥ \|*  
*tapasā niyamenāpi vratenāpi kṛtena vai \|\| 60 \|\|*

Bṛhadbala said:

60\. O excellent sage, how can I get rid of this fell disease of leprosy? Could it be through penance, observance of restraints and holy vows?

## \|\| 1.45.61 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*ārādhaya sahasrāṃśumasminkṣetre mahīpate \|*  
*tataḥ prāpsyasi saṃsiddhiṃ kuṣṭhanāśasamudbhavām \|\| 61 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

61\. Propitiate the Thousand-rayed Lord in this holy spot, O king. You will attain good result, ease and comfort arising from the destruction of (perfect cure from) leprosy.

## \|\| 1.45.62 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sa munervākyaṃ bhūmipālo bṛhadbalaḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇātsthāpayāmāsa sūryasya pratimāṃ tadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On hearing the words of the sage, King Bṛhadbala immediately installed an idol of Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.45.63-64 \|\|

*arcayāmāsa vidhivatpuṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yukto ravivāre viśeṣataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā raktacandanasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayanraktapuṣpaiśca śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. With great ardour and faith, he regularly adored the idol in accordance with the injunctions with flowers, incense and unguent. On Sundays he conducted special worship after observing fast. He faithfully adored with red flowers along with red sandal-paste.

## \|\| 1.45.65-66 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte sa babhūva mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭha vyādhi vinirmukto dvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tataḥ svaṃ rājyamāsādya bhuktvā bhogānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*dehāṃte dinanāthasya saṃprāpto maṃdiraṃ tathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. At the end of a year, the king experienced complete relief from the disease of leprosy. He regained the refulgence of twelve suns. Thereafter, he went back to his kingdom and enjoyed many pleasures. On death he attained the world of the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.45.67 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tatra dvijaśreṣṭhā viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*prakaṭaṃ sarvalokasya vihitaṃ puṣkaratrayam \|\| 67 \|\|*

Sūta said:

67\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, it was thus that the intelligent Viśvāmitra made the three Puṣkaras manifest and accessible to all the people of the world.

## \|\| 1.45.68 \|\|

*yastatra kārtike māse kārttikyāṃ kṛttikāsu ca \|*  
*prakaroti naraḥ snānaṃ brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A man who takes his holy bath there on days with Kṛttikā constellation, or on the full-moon day in the month of Kārttika goes to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.45.69 \|\|

*tathā yo bhāskaraṃ paśyedbṛhadvalapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*vatsaraṃ ravivāreṇa yāvatkṛtvā kṣaṇaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sa mucyate naro rogairyadi syādrogasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A man who visits Bhāskara (the Sun-god) installed by Bṛhadbala on all Sundays for a period of one year celebrating great festivals therein, shall be rid of all ailments he may be suffering from.

## \|\| 1.45.70 \|\|

*nīrogo vā naraḥ sadyo labhate manasepsitam \|*  
*niṣkāmo mokṣamāpnoti prasādāttīkṣṇadīdhiteḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A man without ailments immediately attains whatever he desires mentally with the favour of the Hot-rayed One. One without desires attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.45.71 \|\|

*kārttikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge vṛṣotsargaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*puṣkareṣu supuṇyeṣu so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One who performs the rite of Vṛṣotsarga (ritualistic releasing of a bull as dedication unto the deity) on the Kārttikī day when there is the conjunction of Kṛttikā constellation in the highly meritorious Puṣkaras, shall get the merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.45.72 \|\|

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyekopi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*yajeta vā'śvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One should desire to beget many sons so that one may go to Gayā, one may perform a horse sacrifice or one may ritualistically dedicate a ‘blue’ bull.

## \|\| 1.45.73 \|\|

*ekataḥ sarvatīrthāni sarvadānāni caikataḥ \|*  
*ekatastu vṛṣotsargaḥ kārtikyāṃ puṣkareṣu ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. All the Tīrthas or all the Dāna rites may be put on-one pan of the balance and in the other one, the dedication of a bull. Both are on a par with each other.

## \|\| 1.45.74 \|\|

*yaścaitacchuṇuyānnityaṃ paṭhedvā śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya sarvakāmānvai brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. One who listens to this always or reads with ardent faith, attains all desires and is honoured in Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 46 - Greatness of Sarasvatī Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.46.1-3 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*anyāni tatra tīrthāni yāni saṃti mahāmate \|*  
*tāni kīrtaya sarvāṇi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatra sārasvataṃ tīrthamanyadasti suśobhanam \|*  
*yatra snāto'timūko'pi bhavedvākyavicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*labhate cepsitānkāmānmānuṣāndaivikānapi \|*  
*brahmalokādiparyatāṃstathālokāndvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. O highly intelligent one, do narrate all the other Tīrthas that may be present there.

## \|\| 1.46.4 \|\|

*purāsītpārthivo nā्nā vikhyāto balavardhanaḥ \|*  
*samudravalayāmurvīṃ bubhuje yo bhujārjitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

There is another very splendid Tīrtha there, named Sārasvata Tīrtha. Even one who is dumb and mute but takes his holy bath there, shall become an expert in speech. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he gets all human and heavenly objects desired by him and also the worlds ending with Brahmaloka etc.

4\. Formerly there was a very famous king named Balavardhana. He enjoyed the ocean-girdled earth acquired through the might of his own arms.

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ samutpannaḥ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tasya nāma pitā cakre saṃprāpte dvādaśe'hani \|*  
*ambuvīciriti spaṣṭaṃ samāhūya dvijottamān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A son was born to him. He was endowed with all good features. On the twelfth day the father invited excellent Brāhmaṇas and clearly named him Aṃbuvīci.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vavṛdhe bālo lālitastena bhūbhujā \|*  
*mūkabhāvaṃ samāpanno na śakroti prajalpitum \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Fondled lovingly by the king, the boy grew up properly but due to dumbness he could not even lisp words.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*tato'sya saptame varṣe saṃprāpte balavardhanaḥ \|*  
*paṃcatvaṃ samanuprāptaḥ saṃgrāme śatrubhirhataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. While the boy was running his seventh year, Balavardhana was attacked by his enemies in battle and killed.

## \|\| 1.46.8 \|\|

*tato mūko'pi bālopi maṃtribhistasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*sa sutaḥ sthāpito rājye abhāve'nyasutasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereupon, in the absence of another son, that boy, although he was dumb, was crowned as the king of the kingdom by the ministers of the king.

## \|\| 1.46.9 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya mahīpasya rājyasthasya jaḍātmanaḥ \|*  
*bālatve vartamānasya rājyaṃ viplavamadhyagāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even as the sluggish king, not yet out of childhood; was thrust on the kingdom, there was a great revolt in the realm.

## \|\| 1.46.10 \|\|

*tato jalacaranyāyaḥ saṃpravṛtto mahītale \|*  
*pīḍyaṃte sarvalokāstu durbalā balavattaraiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The practice (Nyāya) of acquatic beings (called Mātsya Nyāya: ‘Might is right’) then prevailed on the earth. And strong men oppressed all weaker people.

## \|\| 1.46.11-12 \|\|

*tataste maṃtriṇaḥ procurvasiṣṭhaṃ svapurohitam \|*  
*vaco'rthaṃ nṛpaterasya kurūpāyaṃ mahāmune \|\| 11 \|\|*

*paśya kṛtsnaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe śūnyatāṃ samupasthitam \|*  
*jaḍatvānnṛpaterasya tasmātkuru yathocitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Thereupon those ministers spoke to Vasiṣṭha, their priest: “O great sage, find out some means to restore the power of speech to this king. See, the entire surface of the earth has become a void due to the defect of this king. Do something that is proper in this connection.”

## \|\| 1.46.13 \|\|

*tatastu suciraṃ dhyātvā dīnānprovāca maṃtriṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvānārtisamopetāñchṛṇvatastasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He meditated for a long time and then spoke to the distressed ministers, all of whom were extremely grief-stricken even as the king himself was listening:

## \|\| 1.46.14 \|\|

*asti sārasvataṃ tīrthaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tatrāyaṃ snātu bhūpatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “In the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, there is Sārasvata Tīrtha that grants all desires to men. Let this king go there and have his holy bath.”

## \|\| 1.46.15 \|\|

*atha tadvacanātsadyaḥ sa gatvā tatra satvaram \|*  
*snānāttīrthe'tha saṃjātastatkṣaṇātsa kala svanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At his instance, the king immediately rushed to the Tīrtha. Thanks to the holy bath in that Tīrtha, he became one with sweet voice.

## \|\| 1.46.16-21 \|\|

*tatprabhāvaṃ sarasvatyāḥ sa vijñāya mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yukto dhyāyamānaḥ sarasvatīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tatastūrṇaṃ samādāya mṛttikāṃ sa nadītaṭāt \|*  
*cakāra bhāratīṃ devīṃ svayameva caturbhujām \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dadhatīṃ dakṣiṇe haste kamalaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*akṣamālāṃ tathānyasmiñjitatāraka varcasam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kamaṇḍaluṃ tathānyasmindivyavāriprapūritam \|*  
*pustakaṃ ca tathā vāme sarvavidyāsamudbhavam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tato medhye śilāpṛṣṭhe tāṃ niveśya prayatnataḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa sadbhaktyā dhūpamālpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*cakāra ca stutiṃ paścācchraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*tadagre prayato bhūtvā svareṇa mahatā nṛpaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. Having clearly understood the power of Sarasvatī, the king equipped with great ardour and faith meditated upon Sarasvatī. He took some clay from the river-bank and himself made an image of Goddess Bhāratī having four arms.

In her right hand she held a very charming lotus. In the other hand there was an Akṣamālā (rosary of beads) that surpassed the stellar lustre. In another (third) hand she held a waterpot filled with divine water. Similarly in the left (fourth) hand she held the book containing all lores.

He then placed that image on a sanctified slab assiduously and devoutly worshipped it through incense, garlands and unguents. Afterwards the king stood before the image with bodily and mental purity. With the mind purified by ardent faith, he began to eulogize in a loud voice.

The prayer of Sarasvatī

## \|\| 1.46.22 \|\|

*sadasaddevi yatkiñcidbandhamokṣātmakaṃ padam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ guptayā vyāptaṃ tvayā kāṣṭhaṃ yathāgninā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O goddess, whatever there is Sat (manifest) and Asat (unmanifest), the place of bondage and that of liberation—all these are pervaded by you in a concealed form in the same manner as fuel is pervaded by fire.

## \|\| 1.46.23 \|\|

*sarvasya siddhirūpeṇa tvaṃ janasya hṛdi sthitā \|*  
*vācārūpeṇa jihvāyāṃ jyotīrūpeṇa cakṣuṣi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are stationed in the heart of everyone in the form of Siddhi (fulfilment), in the tongue in the form of speech and in the eye in the form of Jyoti (light, sight).

## \|\| 1.46.24 \|\|

*bhaktigrāhyāsi deveśi tvamekā bhuvanatraye \|*  
*śaraṇāgatadīnārtaparitrāṇaparāyaṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O goddess of Devas, One devoted to favour the wretched and the distressed who seek refuge in you, you alone are accessible and comprehensible through devotion in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.46.25 \|\|

*tvaṃ kīrtistvaṃ dhṛtirmedhā tvaṃ bhaktistvaṃ prabhā smṛtā \|*  
*tvaṃ nidrā tvaṃ kṣudhā kīrtiḥ sarvabhūtanivāsinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You are the goddess dwelling in all living beings. You are Kīrti (renown); you are Dhṛti. (fortitude). You are Medhā (intellect). You are Bhakti (devotion). You are remembered as Prabhā (refulgence). You are Nidrā (slumber). You are Kṣudhā (hunger). You are Kīrti (reputation).

## \|\| 1.46.26 \|\|

*tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirvapuḥ prītiḥ svadhā svāhā vibhāvarī \|*  
*ratiḥ prītiḥ kṣitirgaṃgā satyaṃ dharmo manasvinī \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You are Tuṣṭi (satisfaction), Puṣṭi (nourishment), Vapus (physical form). Prīti (love), Svadhā, Svāhā, Vibhāvarī (night), Rati (enjoyment), Prīti (affection), Kṣiti (Earth), Gaṅgā, Satya, Dharma and exaltedness of mind.

## \|\| 1.46.27 \|\|

*lajjā śāṃtiḥ smṛtirdakṣā kṣamā gaurī ca rohiṇī \|*  
*sinīvālī kuhū rākā devamātā ditistathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You are Lajjā (bashfulness), Śānti (peace), Smṛti (memory), Dakṣa (efficient), Kṣamā (forgiveness), Gaurī, Rohiṇī, Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, Devamātā (Aditi) and Diti.

## \|\| 1.46.28 \|\|

*brahmāṇī vinatā lakṣmīḥ kadrūrdākṣāyaṇī śivā \|*  
*gāyatrī cātha sāvitrī kṛṣirvṛṣṭiḥ śrutiḥ kalā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are Brahmaṇī, Vinatā, Śivā the daughter of Dakṣa, Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Kṛṣi (cultivation), Vṛṣṭi (shower), Śruti (Veda), Kalā (Art).

## \|\| 1.46.29 \|\|

*balānāḍī tuṣṭikāṣṭhā rasanā ca sarasvatī \|*  
*yatkiñcittriṣu lokeṣu bahutvādyanna kīrtitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You are the nerve vessel called Balā, Tuṣṭikāṣṭhā (acme of satisfaction), Rasanā (tongue), Sarasvatī. In fact, you are everything in all the three worlds not enumerated because of multiplicity.

## \|\| 1.46.30 \|\|

*iṃgitaṃ neṃgitaṃ tacca tadrūpaṃ te sureśvari \|*  
*gandharvāḥ kinnarā devāḥ siddhavidyādharoragāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Whatever is intended or not intended is your form, O goddess of Suras. Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Devas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Uragas,

## \|\| 1.46.31 \|\|

*yakṣaguhyakabhūtāśca daityā ye ca vināyakāḥ \|*  
*tvatprasādena te sarve saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Yakṣas, Guhyakas, Bhūtas, Daityas, Vināyakas—all these attained Siddhi, with your favour.

## \|\| 1.46.32 \|\|

*tathānye'pi bahutvādye na mayā parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ārādhitāstu kṛcchreṇa pūjitāśca suvistaraiḥ \|*  
*haraṃtu devatāḥ pāpamanye tvaṃ kīrtitā'pi ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Others too not mentioned due to multiplicity are also propitiated (by me) and worshipped with strenuous effort elaborately. Let those deities remove the sin. Thus you are glorified.

## \|\| 1.46.33 \|\|

*evaṃ stutā sā deveśī bhūbhujā tena bhāratī \|*  
*yayau pratyakṣatāṃ tūrṇaṃ prāha cedaṃ suharṣitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On being eulogized by that king the highly pleased goddess of Devas, Bhāratī, immediately manifested herself and spoke.

## \|\| 1.46.34 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*stotreṇānena bhūpāla bhaktyā susthirayā sadā \|*  
*parituṣṭāsmi tenāśu varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

34\. O king, I am pleased with this prayer of yours and the steadiest devotion. So choose your boon as you desire.

## \|\| 1.46.35 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti madvākyāttvayā stheyamasaṃśayam \|*  
*atrārcāyāṃ trilokesmi nyāvatkīrtirmama sthirā \|\| 35 \|\|*

The king said:

35\. From now onwards, at my request you shall undoubtedly stay in this idol as long as my fame is steady throughout the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.46.36 \|\|

*yastvāmārādhayetsamyagatrasthāṃ mannimittataḥ \|*  
*bhaktyānurūpamevāśu tasmai deyaṃ tvayā hi tat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If any devotee, urged by me, adequately propitiates you staying in this, you should immediately grant him everything befitting his devotion.

## \|\| 1.46.37-40 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*yo māmatra sthitāṃ nityaṃ snātvā'tra salile śubhe \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ pūjayiṣyati mānavaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tasyāhaṃ vāṃchitānkāmānsaṃpradāsyāmi pārthiva \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tatra sthitā devī svayameva sarasvatī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tataḥprabhṛti lokānāṃ hitāya parameśvarī \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāmupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yastāṃ pūjayate martyaḥ śvetapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sa syādvāggmī sumedhāvī sadā janmanijanmani \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

37-40. If any man takes his holy bath here in the auspicious waters on eighth and fourteenth lunar days and worships me present here, O king, I shall grant him all the cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.46.41 \|\|

*sarasvatyāḥ prasādena jāyamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*anvaye'pi na tasyaiva kaścinmūrkhaḥ prajāyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

Thus, from that day onwards, the greatest goddess Sarasvatī became stationed there herself for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds. A man who observes fast on eighth and fourteenth lunar days and worships her with white flowers and unguents, shall become very intelligent and eloquent always in every birth.

41\. He may have frequent rebirths. With the favour of Sarasvatī, no fool will be born in his family.

## \|\| 1.46.42 \|\|

*yo dharmaśravaṇaṃ tasyāḥ purataḥ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sa nūnaṃ vasati svarge tatprabhāvādyugatrayam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A man who listens to pious discourses in front of her, resides in heaven for three Yugas by her power.

## \|\| 1.46.43 \|\|

*vidyādānaṃ naro yaśca tasyā hyāyatane sadā \|*  
*karoti śraddhayā yuktaḥ so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A man endowed with ardent faith who makes the gift of learning in her shrine shall obtain the merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.46.44 \|\|

*yo yacchati dvijendrāya dharmaśāstrasamudbhavam \|*  
*pustakaṃ vājimedhasya sa samagraṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One who offers to a leading Brāhmaṇa a book on religious conduct shall obtain the full merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.46.45 \|\|

*yo vedādhyayanaṃ tasyāḥ karoti purataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*so'gniṣṭomasya yajñasya kṛtsnaṃ phalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. One who stands before her and recites the Vedas shall obtain the full merit of an Agniṣṭoma Yajña.

## Chapter 47 - Greatness of Mahākāleśvara (Mahākāla-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.47.1 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*mahākālasya māhātmyaṃ vistareṇa mahāmate \|*  
*asmākaṃ sūtaja brūhi sarvaṃ vetti yato bhavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O highly intelligent Sūtaja, tell us in detail the greatness of Mahākāla, because you know everything.

## \|\| 1.47.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsītpūrvaṃ mahīpāla ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ \|*  
*rudrasena iti khyātaḥ sarvaśatruniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. Formerly there was a king hailing from the family of Ikṣvāku. He was well-known as Rudrasena. He was the destroyer of all his enemies.

## \|\| 1.47.3 \|\|

*samudra iva gāṃbhīrye saumyatve śaśisaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*vīrye yathā sahasrākṣo rūpe kandarpasannibhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In majesty he was like the ocean; in gentleness he resembled the moon. In vigour he was on a par with the Thousand-eyed One (Indra); and in handsome features he was like Kandarpa (god of Love).

## \|\| 1.47.4 \|\|

*tasya kāṃtīti vikhyātā purī sarvaguṇānvitā \|*  
*rājadhānyabhavacchreṣṭhā proccaprākāratoraṇā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A city endowed with all the good features well-known as Kāntī was his capital. It was the most excellent one of all cities with lofty ramparts and ornamental gates.

## \|\| 1.47.5 \|\|

*tathaivāsītpriyā tasya bhāryā paramasaṃmatā \|*  
*khyātā padmavatīnāma rūpaudārya guṇānvitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. His beloved wife was well-known as Padmāvatī. She was honoured by the greatest people. She was endowed with exalted good qualities and beauty.

## \|\| 1.47.6 \|\|

*sa tayā sahito rājā vaiśākhyā divase sadā \|*  
*samabhyeti nijasthānātsainyenālpena saṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the day of Vaiśākhī (full-moon day in the month of Vaiśākha) he used to come out from his abode accompanied by her and a limited number of soldiers.

## \|\| 1.47.7 \|\|

*camatkārapure kṣetre pīṭhe tatra dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mahākālasya devasya purato rātrijāgaram \|*  
*karoti śraddhayā yuktaḥ sabhāryaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he used to perform Rātrijāgara (keeping awake at night) in front of Lord Mahākāla. The king was always accompanied by his wife and he was ardently faithful.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā dhyāyamāno maheśvaram \|*  
*gītavādyena hṛdyena nṛtyena dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*dharmākhyānena viprāṇāṃ vedādhyayanavistaraiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He used to observe fasts. He meditated upon Maheśvara. There used to be delightful singing and dancing with instrumental music, narration of religious discourses by Brāhmaṇas and elaborate chanting of Vedic Mantras.

## \|\| 1.47.9 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*dadau dānāni viprebhyastapasvibhyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Getting up early in the morning, he used to take his holy bath and wear clean and washed clothes. With purity of mind and body, he used to make gifts to Brāhmaṇas and ascetics in particular.

## \|\| 1.47.10 \|\|

*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇebhyaśca tathānyebhyaḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*varṣevarṣe sadaivaṃ sa samabhyetya mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhyāṃ jāgaraṃ tasya devasya purato'karot \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He distributed gifts to the blind, the wretched and the miserable people in thousands. Every year that king used to come thus and perform the rite of Jāgara in front of that Lord.

## \|\| 1.47.11 \|\|

*yathāyathā sa bhūpālaḥ kurute rātrijāgaram \|*  
*mahākālāgratastasya tathā vṛddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As the king continued to peform this holy rite of Jāgara in front of Mahākāla, he became more and more prosperous.

## \|\| 1.47.12-13 \|\|

*śatravo vilayaṃ yāṃti lakṣmīrvṛddhiṃ pragacchati \|*  
*ekadā sa samāyātastatra yāvanmahīpatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tatraiva divase tāvanmahākālasya cāgrataḥ \|*  
*apaśyadbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhānnānādigbhyaḥ samāgatān \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. All the enemies were destroyed. Fortune increased. Once when the king arrived there, he saw excellent Brāhmaṇas who had come from different quarters on that very day and had gathered before Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.47.14 \|\|

*vedādhyayanasaṃpannānvrataniṣṭhāparāyaṇān \|*  
*eke tatra kathāścakruḥ supuṇyā brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They were highly conversant with the Vedas. They were regular in the observance of vows. A few highly meritorious, excellent Brāhmaṇas narrated stories.

## \|\| 1.47.15 \|\|

*rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ tathā pare \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ ca tathā cānye brahmarṣīṇāṃ tathā pare \|*  
*yajñānāṃ sāgarāṇāṃ ca dvīpānāṃ ca manoharāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They narrated the stories of saintly kings. Others narrated the stories of ancient sages and Devas. Others enumerated the Tīrthas. Some of them told the stories of Brāhmaṇa-sages. The stories of Yajñas, oceans and continents were very charming.

## \|\| 1.47.16 \|\|

*atha tānpṛthivīpālaḥ sa praṇamya yathākramam \|*  
*upaviṣṭaḥ sabhāmadhye taiḥ sarvaiścābhinaṃditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The king bowed down to them in due order and sat in the middle of the assembly. He was heartily congratulated by all of them.

## \|\| 1.47.17 \|\|

*kasmiṃścidatha saṃprāpte kathāṃte te munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*papracchurbhūmipālaṃ tu kautūhalasamanvitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the close of the discourse, those leading sages asked the king eagerly:

## \|\| 1.47.18-20 \|\|

*vaiśākhīdivase rājaṃstvaṃ sadābhyetya dūrataḥ \|*  
*varṣevarṣe'sya devasya purato rātrijāgaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prakaroṣi prayatnena tyaktvānyāḥ sakalāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*snānadānādikā yāśca nirdiṣṭāḥ śāstraciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na te yadi rahasyaṃ syāttadā'śeṣaṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*nūnaṃ tvaṃ vetsi tatsarvaṃ yatphalaṃ rātrijāgare \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. “O king, every year you regularly come here from very far on the Vaiśākhī day. You assiduously perform the rite of Rātrijāgara in front of the Lord even abandoning all the other rites such as Snāna, Dāna etc. mentioned by those who expound the scriptural texts. If this be no closely guarded secret, do narrate everything in full. Of course you know the benefit that accrues from Rātrijāgara

## \|\| 1.47.21 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*rahasyaṃ paramaṃ caiva yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmābhiḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi tathāpyakhilameva hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

The king said:

21\. Well, this is indeed a very great secret, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that which you have asked me. Still I shall narrate everything unto you.

## \|\| 1.47.22 \|\|

*ahamāsaṃ vaṇigjātyā purā vai vaidiśe pure \|*  
*nirdhano baṃdhubhirmuktaḥ paribhūtaḥ padepade \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Formerly I was a merchant by caste in the city of Vidiśā. I was very poor and all my kinsmen abandoned and avoided me. At every step I met with discomfiture.

## \|\| 1.47.23 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya bhagavānpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*vaidiśe nākarodvṛṣṭiṃ sapta varṣāṇi paṃca ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On one occasion, the Lord of rain, the Slayer of Paka, did not shower rain at all in Vidiśā city for twelve years.

## \|\| 1.47.24 \|\|

*tato vṛṣṭinirodhena sarve lokāḥ kṣudhārdditāḥ \|*  
*annābhāvānmṛtāḥ kecitkeciddeśāṃtare gatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On account of drought, all the people were oppressed by hunger. Due to the absence of food, some people died and some went to foreign lands.

## \|\| 1.47.25-27 \|\|

*tato'haṃ svāṃ samādāya patnīṃ kṣutkṣāmagātrikām \|*  
*aśrupūrṇamukhīṃ dīnāṃ praskhalantīṃ padepade \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saurāṣṭraṃ manasi dhyātvā prasthitastadanantaram \|*  
*subhikṣaṃ lokataḥ śrutvā jīvanāya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*krameṇa gacchamāno'tha bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ \|*  
*ānartaviṣayaṃ prāptaścamatkārapurāṃtike \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. I took my distressed wife with me and set off thinking about Saurāṣṭra (Kathiawad) (as my destination). The lady was emaciated in every limb through starvation and tears welled up in her eyes. She was faltering at every step. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I had heard from people that there was plenty of food there. I duly proceeded ahead eating the food received as alms. Ultimately I arrived in the Ānarta country near Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.47.28 \|\|

*tatra ramyaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ padminīkhaṇḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*saraḥ svacchodakāpūrṇaṃ jalapakṣibhirāvṛtam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. There a beautiful lake was seen by me. It was adorned with clusters of lotuses and filled with clear water. Aquatic birds hovered around it.

## \|\| 1.47.29 \|\|

*tato'haṃ tatsamāsādya snātaḥ śītena vāriṇā \|*  
*kṣudhārtaśca tṛṣārtaśca śramārtaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Distressed with hunger and thirst and particularly exhausted due to the fatigue of the journey, I went in and took my bath in the cool waters thereof.

## \|\| 1.47.30-31 \|\|

*athāhaṃ bhāryayā prokto gṛhāṇeśa jalāśayāt \|*  
*jalajāni krayārthāya yena syādadya bhojanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*etatsaṃdṛśyate dūrātpuraṃdarapuropamam \|*  
*puraśreṣṭhaṃ samāsādya vikrayaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Then I was told by my wife: “O Lord, collect some lotus flowers from the lake so that some may buy them and we will have food for the day. Yonder, an excellent city is visible. It is like the city of Indra. It behoves you to go there and sell them.”

## \|\| 1.47.32 \|\|

*tato mayā gṛhītāni padmāni dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*vikrayārthaṃ prabhūtāni vācchamānena bhojanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, many lotus flowers were gathered by me for selling, as I desired food.

## \|\| 1.47.33 \|\|

*camatkārapuraṃ prāpya tato'haṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bhrāṃtastrikeṣu sarveṣu catvareṣu gṛheṣu ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Going into the city of Camatkārapura, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I wandered everywhere in the rows of houses and the crossings of three and four roads.

## \|\| 1.47.34 \|\|

*na kaścitpratigṛhṇāti tāni padmāni mānavaḥ \|*  
*mama bhāgyavaśālloko jātaḥ krayaparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It was my bad luck that the people were averse to buying. No man took those lotuses.

## \|\| 1.47.35 \|\|

*atha kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhasya śrāṃtasya mama bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*astācalamanuprāptaḥ saṃdhyākālastato'bhavat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even as I became utterly tired with the throat parched due to hunger, the sun reached Astācala (the mountain behind which the sun sets) and it was evening.

## \|\| 1.47.36 \|\|

*tato vairāgyamāpannaḥ supto'haṃ bhagnamaṃdire \|*  
*tāni padmāni bhūpṛṣṭhe nidhāya saha bhāryayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Utterly disgusted, I placed the lotuses on the bare ground and lay down there in a ruined temple along with my wife.

## \|\| 1.47.37 \|\|

*athārdharātre saṃprāpte śruto gītadhvanirmayā \|*  
*tataśca ciṃtitaṃ citte jāgaro'yamasaṃśayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When it was about midnight, the sound of music was heard by me and the thought occurred to me that this was the rite of Jāgara undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.47.38 \|\|

*tasmādgacchāmi cetkaścitpadmānyetāni me naraḥ \|*  
*mūlyena pratigṛhṇāti bhojanaṃ jāyate tataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. ‘Should I go there; some man might buy the lotuses and I could have meal for the price those might fetch.’

## \|\| 1.47.39 \|\|

*evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā padmānyādāya satvaram \|*  
*sabhāryaḥ prasthitastatra yatra gītasya niḥsvanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After deciding thus I accompanied by my wife took the flowers and hastened to the place from where the sound of music came.

## \|\| 1.47.40 \|\|

*tataścāyatane tasminprāpto'haṃ munipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*apaśyaṃ devadeveśaṃ mahākālaṃ prapūjitam \|*  
*agrasthitairdvijaśreṣṭhairjapagītaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O leading sages, I went into the temple. There I saw Mahākāla, the Lord of chiefs of Devas, worshipped by excellent Brāhmaṇas who were engaged in singing and were seated in front

## \|\| 1.47.41 \|\|

*eke nṛtyaṃ prakurvaṃti gītamanye japaṃ pare \|*  
*anye homaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā dharmākhyānamathāpare \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Some were dancing and others were singing. A few were performing Japa. Some excellent Brāhmaṇas were performing Homa and others were engaged in religious discussion.

## \|\| 1.47.42 \|\|

*tataḥ kaścinmayā pṛṣṭaḥ kriyate jāgaro'tra kim \|*  
*ka ete jāgarāsaktā lokāḥ kīrtaya me drutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. One of the assembled men was asked by me: “Is the rite of Jāgara being performed here? Who are these people engaged in the Jāgara? Do tell me quickly.”

## \|\| 1.47.43-45 \|\|

*tenoktameṣa devasya mahākālasya jāgaraḥ \|*  
*kriyate brāhmaṇairbhaktyā upavāsaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*adya puṇyatithirnāma vaiśākhī puṇyadā parā \|*  
*yasyāmasya puro bhaktyā naraḥ kuryātprajāgaram \|*  
*mahākālasya devasya saukhyaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saṃti padmāni me yaccha mūlyamādāya bhadraka \|*  
*bhojanārthamahaṃ dadmi kaladhautapalatrayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. He said: “This is the Jāgara of Lord Mahākāla. It is devoutly performed by Brāhmaṇas who have been observing fast. It is the holy lunar day named Vaisśākhī. It is highly meritorious. One should perform the rite of Jāgara devoutly before Lord Mahākāla. Thereby he undoubtedly attains happiness.

O fair Sir, you have lotus flowers; give them to me and take the price thereof. For your food I shall give you three Palas of silver.”

## \|\| 1.47.46-47 \|\|

*tato'vadhāritaṃ citte mayā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmi mahākālaṃ padmairetaiḥ sureśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*na mayā sukṛtaṃ kiṃcidanyadehāṃtare kṛtam \|*  
*niyataṃ tena saṃbhūta itthaṃbhūto'smi durgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Then I began to think on these lines, O excellent Brāhmaṇas: ‘Shall I worship Mahākāla, the Lord of Suras? No meritorious rites have been performed by me in the previous birth. Certainly that is why I have become very distressed in this manner.

## \|\| 1.47.48 \|\|

*paraṃ kṣutkṣāmakaṃṭheyaṃ bhāryā me priyavādinī \|*  
*annābhāvānna saṃdehaḥ prātaryāsyati saṃkṣayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. But my sweet-speaking beloved wife has become very hungry and her throat is parched. Want of food may doubtlessly cause her death in the morning.’

## \|\| 1.47.49 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayamānasya mama sā dayitā tataḥ \|*  
*provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ vinayāvanatā sthitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even as I was thinking thus my beloved wife spoke these sweet words after humbly bowing down to me:

## \|\| 1.47.50-53 \|\|

*mā nātha kuru padmānāṃ vikrayaṃ dhanalobhataḥ \|*  
*kuruṣva ca hitaṃ vākyaṃ yatte vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*upavāso balājjātaḥ sasyābhāvādasaṃśayam \|*  
*asmākaṃ jāgaraṃ cāpi bhaviṣyati bubhukṣayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tatrobhābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ snānaṃ divā sarasi śobhane \|*  
*gharmārttābhyāṃ śramārttābhyāṃ kṛtadevārcanaṃ tathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tasmāddevaṃ mahākālaṃ pūjayāmo'dhunā vayam \|*  
*padmairetaiḥ paraṃ śreya āvayoryena jāyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-53. ‘O Lord, do not sell the lotuses for the greed of money. Do according to my words conducive to welfare.

We had to observe fast under compulsion doubtlessly because there was not even a bit of greens. In this state of hunger, we shall have the rite of Jāgara too. Both of us had our holy bath in the splendid lake during the day, because we were distressed due to fatigue and heat. We worshipped the deity as well. Hence let us now worship Lord Mahākāla by means of these lotuses so that we may have great welfare.’

## \|\| 1.47.54 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*ubhābhyāmatha hṛṣṭābhyāṃ pūjito'yaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*taiḥ padmaiḥ sattvamāsthāya kṛtvā pūjāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

The king said:

54\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, with a mind full of Sattva (purity) both of us joyously performed the adoration of Maheśvara by means of those lotuses.

## \|\| 1.47.55 \|\|

*kṣutpīḍayā samāyātā naiva nidrā kathaṃcana \|*  
*svalpāpi maṃdire cātra sthitayorharasannidhau \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Due to the pangs of hunger we could not sleep at all by any means, as we continued to stay in the temple here in front of Hara.

## \|\| 1.47.56 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhātasamaye prodgate ravimaṃḍale \|*  
*mṛto'haṃ kṣudhayāviṣṭaḥ sthāne'traiva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then, in the morning, when the disc of the sun rose up, I died due to the overwhelming hunger in this very same place, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.47.57 \|\|

*atha sā dayitā mahyaṃ tadādāya kalevaram \|*  
*harṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭā praviṣṭā havyavāhanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thereupon my wife took my body and with great delight entered the funeral pyre.

## \|\| 1.47.58 \|\|

*tatprabhāvādahaṃ jātaḥ kāṃtīnātho mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*daśārṇādhipateḥ kanyā sāpi jātismarā satī \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thanks to the power thereof, I was born as a king and Lord of Kāntī. That chaste lady was born as the daughter of king of Daśārṇa with the power to recollect previous births.

## \|\| 1.47.59 \|\|

*tataḥ svayaṃvaraṃ prāptā māṃ vijñāya nijaṃ patim \|*  
*mayāpi saiva vijñāya pūrvapatnī samāhṛtā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Knowing me to be her own husband, she choose me in the Svayaṃvam. After knowing that she was my previous wife she was brought with me by me.

## \|\| 1.47.60-61 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādasya mahākālasya jāgaram \|*  
*varṣevarṣe ca vaiśākhyāṃ karomi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*anayā priyayā sārdhaṃ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā mahākālaṃ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. It is for this reason, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that on the Vaiśākhī day every year I perform the rite of Jāgara of Mahākāla along with this beloved of mine, after worshipping Mahākāla with flowers, incense and unguents. It is the truth that I have mentioned.

## \|\| 1.47.62 \|\|

*kṛto viprā mayā tveṣa sa tadā rātrijāgaraḥ \|*  
*yathāpyetatphalaṃ jātaṃ devasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. At that time the rite of Rātrijāgara was performed by me, O Brāhmaṇas. Thanks to the power of this Lord, this merit has accrued (to me).

## \|\| 1.47.63 \|\|

*adhunā śraddhayā yukto yathoktavidhinā tataḥ \|*  
*yatkaromi na jānāmi kiṃ me saṃyacchate phalam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Now with great ardour and faith, I am performing this in accordance with the injunctions. I do not know what fruit (reward) he will grant me.

## \|\| 1.47.64 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ mayā satyaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yena satyena tenaiṣa mahākālaḥ prasīdatu \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the entire truth has been related to you. May Mahākāla be pleased with the truth I have spoken.

## \|\| 1.47.65 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā dvijaśreṣṭhā vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*pracakrurjapatestasya sādhuvādānanekaśaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Sūta said:

65\. On hearing this, those excellent Brāhmaṇas with their eyes gleaming with wonder, exclaimed “Well done! Well done!”

## \|\| 1.47.66 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*satyamuktaṃ mahīpāla tvayaitadakhilaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*mahākālaprasādena na kiṃciddurlabhaṃ bhuvi \|\| 66 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

66\. O king, the entire truth has been spoken by you. Nothing is difficult (to be achieved) on this earth if there is the favour of Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.47.67 \|\|

*tasmādviśeṣataḥ sarve varṣevarṣe vayaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*kariṣyāmo'sya devasya śraddhayā rātrijāgaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Hence, O king, we shall also ardently perform the rite of Rātrijāgara of this Lord every year.

## \|\| 1.47.68 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivaste ca sarva eva dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*pracakrurjāgaraṃ tasya mahākālasya saṃnidhau \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then that king and all those Brāhmaṇas performed the rite of Jāgara in the presence of Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.47.69 \|\|

*viśeṣāddharṣasaṃyuktā vividhairgītavādanaiḥ \|*  
*dharmākhyānaiśca nṛtyaiśca vedoccāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*tadārabhya nṛpāḥ sarve pracakrurvismayānvitāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Ever since then all the kings swayed by wonder performed the Jāgara rite with special gaiety, singing and playing on instruments in diverse ways. There were religious legends, dances, recitation of Vedic passages of different contexts.

## \|\| 1.47.70 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale samutthāya sa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā mahākālaṃ tāṃśca sarvāndvijottamān \|*  
*anujñāpya yayau hṛṣṭaḥ sasainyaḥ svapuraṃ prati \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. When the day dawned clearly the king got up, worshipped Mahākāla and took leave of all those excellent Brāhmaṇas. Accompanied by his army, he joyously went to his city.

## \|\| 1.47.71 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena saṃprāpya dehāntaṃ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. In due course the king met with his death and attained the greatest region devoid of death and old age.

## \|\| 1.47.72 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ mahākālasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇa śreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Mahākāla has been fully spoken to you. It is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 48 - Installation of Umā-Maheśvara

## \|\| 1.48.1 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraivāsya samuddeśe hariścaṃdrasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*āśramo 'sti suvikhyāto nānādrumasamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This story is a new contribution of this Purāṇa. The sonlesmess of Hariścandra, the curse of Umā and establishment of an Āśrama etc. are not found in Mbh, Padma and other Purāṇas.

Sūta said:

1\. There itself in that very place is the hermitage of King Hariścandra. It is well-known and overgrown with various creepers and trees.

## \|\| 1.48.2 \|\|

*yatra tena tapastaptaṃ saṃsthāpyomāmaheśvarau \|*  
*yacchatā vividhaṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo'bhivāṃchitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Penance was performed there by him after installing Umā and Maheśvara. Further he distributed different kinds of gifts to Brāhmaṇas according to their desires.

## \|\| 1.48.3 \|\|

*āsīdrājā hariścaṃdrastriśaṃkutanayaḥ purā \|*  
*ayodhyādhipatiḥ śrīmānsūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly there was a king named Hariścandra, the son of Triśaṅku. The glorious king hailing from the solar race ruled over Ayodhyā.

## \|\| 1.48.4 \|\|

*na durbhikṣaṃ na ca vyādhirnākālamaraṇaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*tasmiñchāsati dharmeṇa na ca caurakṛtaṃ bhayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. While he was ruling virtuously there was no famine, no ailment and certainly no premature death. Nor was there any fear from thieves.

## \|\| 1.48.5 \|\|

*kālavarṣī sadā meghaḥ sasyāni pracurāṇi ca \|*  
*rasavaṃti ca toyāni sarvartuphalitā drumāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The clouds always showered rain at the proper time. The vegetation was luxurious. The waters were tasty and the trees bore fruits in all the seasons.

## \|\| 1.48.6 \|\|

*daṃḍastatrābhavadvāstau gṛharodho'kṣadevane \|*  
*eko doṣākaraścaṃdraḥ priyadoṣāśca kauśikāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Daṇḍa (punishment; a staff measuring four Hastas) existed only at the place where dwelling place is built There was Gṛharodha (closing of houses; attacking of houses) only in the game of dice. There was only one Doṣākara (storehouse of faults; the Moon, the cause of night) and it was the Moon. Only owls were Priyadoṣas (fond of faults; fond of nights).

## \|\| 1.48.7 \|\|

*snehakṣayaśca dīpeṣu vivāhe ca karagrahaḥ \|*  
*vṛttabhaṃgastathā gadye dānotthitirgajānane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There was Snehakṣaya (decrease in oil or affection) only in lamps. There was Karagraha (holding of the hands; levying of taxes) in marriages only. There was Vṛttabhaṅga (violation of Vṛtta i.e. prosody or decorum) only in prose. There was Dānotthiti i.e. elevation of Dāna (ichor; bribery) only in the face of an elephant.

## \|\| 1.48.8 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ guṇayuktasya sārvabhaumasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*eka eva mahānāsīddoṣaḥ putravivarjitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus the king was endowed with all good qualities and he had imperial authority. There was one great defect, that he was sonless.

## \|\| 1.48.9 \|\|

*tataḥ putrakṛte gatvā cakāra sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore he installed a Liṅga devoutly in the holy spot of Camatkārapura and performed very great penance for getting a son.

## \|\| 1.48.10 \|\|

*paṃcāgnisādhako grīṣme varṣāsvākāśasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*jalāśrayaśca hemaṃte sa dhyāyati maheśvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He used to meditate on Maheśvara and practised austerities: He sat inside five fires in the months of summer; during rainy season he stayed under the open sky; he resorted to water-lakes in Hemanta (winter).

## \|\| 1.48.11 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte tasya tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣo'bhūtsamaṃ gauryā gaṇasaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then at the end of a thousand years Maheśvara was pleased with him. He appeared before him along with Gaurí and surrounded by groups of Gaṇas (attendants).

## \|\| 1.48.12 \|\|

*uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasva yathepsitam \|*  
*ahaṃ te saṃpradāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He said: “I shall bestow boons. Request for anything desired. I shall grant it to you even if it be very difficult to get.”

## \|\| 1.48.13 \|\|

*tatastaṃ praṇipatyoccaiḥ stutvā sūktaiḥ śrutairapi \|*  
*provāca vinayopetaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereupon the king bowed down to him and eulogized through the Sūktas of the Vedas. With humility and palms joined in reverence he spoke:

## \|\| 1.48.14-16 \|\|

*tvatprasādātsuraśreṣṭha yatkiṃciddharaṇītale \|*  
*tadasti me gṛhe sarvaṃ vāṃchitaṃ svena cetasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*surūpāṇi kalatrāṇi rājyaṃ nihatakaṃṭakam \|*  
*śarīraṃ roganirmuktaṃ saṃkhyāhīnaṃ tathā dhanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ekaṃ me sumahadduḥkhaṃ yadapatyaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*tasmāddehi sutaṃ deva prasanno yadi śaṃkara \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. “O excellent one among Suras, whatever there is worthy of being mentally cherished on the earth is in my house. My wives are beautiful. The kingdom is devoid of thorns. The enemies have been exterminated. My body is without ailment. Unlimited and vast is my wealth. I have only one source of unhappiness that I have no issue. Hence, O Lord Śaṅkara, if you are pleased, grant me a son.

## \|\| 1.48.17 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*acireṇa nṛpaśreṣṭha putrastava bhaviṣyati \|*  
*matprasādānna saṃdehastasmādgaccha drutaṃ gṛham \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

17\. O excellent king, due to my favour, a son will be born to you ere long. There is no doubt about it Hence go home quickly.

## \|\| 1.48.18 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare gaurī kopasaṃraktalocanā \|*  
*bhartsayitvā mahādevaṃ tataḥ provāca taṃ nṛpam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sūta said:

18\. In the meantime Gaurī rebuked Mahādeva with eyes reddened due to anger. Then she spoke to the king:

## \|\| 1.48.19-20 \|\|

*yasmāttvayā mahāmūrkha na praṇāmaḥ kṛto mama \|*  
*harādanaṃtaraṃ tasmācchāpaṃ dāsyāmyahaṃ tava \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tava saṃlapsyate putro yathoktaḥ śūlapāṇinā \|*  
*paraṃ tanmṛtyujaṃ duḥkhaṃ tvaṃ śiśutvepi lapsyase \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. “O big fool, since you did not bow down to me after Hara, I am going to curse you. You will beget a son as said by the Trident-armed Lord. But you will also meet with the sorrow arising from his death even in infancy.”

## \|\| 1.48.21 \|\|

*evamuktvā bhagavatī sārdhaṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*adarśanaṃ yayau paścāttathānyairapi pārśvagaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After saying thus, the goddess vanished along with Śaṃbhu and the attendants too.

## \|\| 1.48.22 \|\|

*so'pi rājā varaṃ labdhvā śāpaṃ ca tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*na jagāma gṛhaṃ bhūyaścakāra sumahattapaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After the acquisition of the boon and having received the curse as well, the king did not go home. He performed a great penance once again.

## \|\| 1.48.23 \|\|

*ekāsanaṃ samārūḍhau kṛtvā gaurī maheśvarau \|*  
*tataścārādhayāmāsa samaṃ puṣpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He installed Gaurī and Maheśvara in the same seat (pedestal) and then propitiated them together, with flowers and unguents.

## \|\| 1.48.24 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa dadau dānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*bhūmiśāyī praśāṃtātmā ṣaṣṭhakālakṛtāśanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The king offered special gifts to Brāhmaṇas. He lay on bare ground. He kept himself quite calm. He took food once in two days.

## \|\| 1.48.25 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*pārvatyā sahito bhūyastasya saṃdarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then, at the end of a year the Bull-emblemed Lord appeared before him in the company of Pārvatī once again.

## \|\| 1.48.26 \|\|

*tataḥ sa nṛpatistābhyāṃ yugapadvidhipūrvakam \|*  
*kṛtvā natiṃ tato vākyaṃ vinayādidamabravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereupon the king bowed down before both of them duly and spoke these words humbly:

## \|\| 1.48.27-32 \|\|

*purā devi mayānaṃdapūre vyākula cetasā \|*  
*na natā tvaṃ na me kopaṃ tasmāttvaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dehārdhadhāriṇī devi sadā tvaṃ śūladhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*tadaikasminnate kasmānna natā tvaṃ vadasva me \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yastaṃ namati deveśaṃ tena tvaṃ sarvadā natā \|*  
*natāyāṃ tvayi deveśo nataḥ syāditi me matiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tathāpi ca pṛthaktvena mayā tvaṃ tu natā saha \|*  
*ekāsanaṃ samārūḍhā tatsamaṃ devi pūjitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yaḥ puroktaḥ purāriṇā \|*  
*sostu vai saphalaḥ sadyo varaḥ putrakṛte mama \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yayā vaṃśadharaḥ putro dīrghāyurdṛḍhavikramaḥ \|*  
*tvatprasādādbhaveddevi tathā tvaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. “Formerly, O goddess, my mind was overwhelmed with the flood of bliss. Hence I failed to bow down to you. It does not behove you to be angry on that account.

O goddess, you are always the occupier of half of the body of the Trident-bearing Lord. Hence, tell me how, when one of you is bowed to, you are not paid obeisance.

This is my opinion that you are always bowed to by one who bows to the Lord of Devas and when you are bowed to the Lord of Devas too is bowed to.

Still, you are also separately bowed to as together before. Now you have been mounted in the same seat. O goddess, you are worshipped along with him.

Hence be favourable to me. Let the boon given by the Enemy of the Puras earlier become fruitful immediately in regard to obtaining a son.

O goddess, it behoves you to do what is necessary to facilitate the birth of a son who will perpetuate the family line, who will be long-lived and whose valour will be steady with your favour.”

## \|\| 1.48.33 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*nānyathā me vaco rājañjāyate'tra kathaṃcana \|*  
*tasmādbālo'pi te putraḥ paṃcatvaṃ samupaiṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

33\. O king, my words cannot be otherwise on any account. Hence your son will meet with death though yet a child.

## \|\| 1.48.34 \|\|

*darśayitvā tu te duḥkhamalpamṛtyusamudbhavam \|*  
*bhūyaḥ saṃprāpsyati prāṇānacirānme prasādataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After giving you the sorrow arising out of early death, he will regain life ere long, with my favour.

## \|\| 1.48.35 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati ca dīrghāyustato vaṃśadharo jayī \|*  
*sārvabhaumapradhānaśca dānī yajvā ca dharmavit \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereafter he will live long; he will be victorious and perpetuate your race as an emperor of great eminence. He will be munificent and will perform Yajñas. He will be one conversant whh virtuous rites.

## \|\| 1.48.36 \|\|

*tasmādrājangṛhaṃ gatvā kuru rājyamabhīpsitam \|*  
*saṃprāpsyasi sutaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yādṛśaṃ kīrtitaṃ mayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. So, O king, go home and rule over your kingdom as you desire. You will beget a son of great excellance as proclaimed by me.

## \|\| 1.48.37-38 \|\|

*anyo'pi mānavo yo māṃ rūpeṇā nenasaṃsthitām \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati cātraiva samaṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tasyāhaṃ saṃpradāsyāmi putrānhṛdayavāṃchitān \|*  
*tathānyadapi yatkiṃcidacirānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. If any other man worships me installed here in this form along with Lord Śaṃbhu, I will grant sons of his choice and other things also ere long. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.48.39 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*bhūya eva nṛpaśreṣṭha mattaḥ prārthaya vāṃchitam \|*  
*na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syātsatyametadbravīmi te \|\| 39 \|\|*

Śrī Mahādeva said:

39\. O excellent king, once again beg of me whatever you desire. A visit of mine shall never be in vain. This is the truth that I speak.

## \|\| 1.48.40 \|\|

*hariścaṃdra uvāca \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyosmi deveśa sarvamasti gṛhe mama \|*  
*putraṃ tyaktvā tvayā so'pi datto vaṃśadharo jayī \|\| 40 \|\|*

Hariścandra said:

40\. O Lord of Devas, I am blessed and contented. Excepting a son there is everything in my house. Now you have given me a victorious son capable of perpetuating the line.

## \|\| 1.48.41 \|\|

*tathāpi na tavādeśo vyarthaḥ kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇāddeva yācayiṣyāmi vāṃchitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Still I cannot disregard your behest at all. For this reason I shall request for a desired object.

## \|\| 1.48.42 \|\|

*rājasūyakṛte'smākaṃ sadā buddhiḥ pravartate \|*  
*niṣedhayaṃti māṃ sarve mantriṇaḥ suhṛdastadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I have been thinking of performing a Rājasūya for a long time. But all my ministers and friends dissuade me.

## \|\| 1.48.43 \|\|

*sarvaistairjāyate yajñaḥ pārthivaiḥ karadīkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*yuddhaṃ vinā karaṃ te'pi na yacchanti yato vibho \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The reason is this. That Yajña is possible only when all the kings have been made to pay tribute. O Lord, they will not readily pay tribute without an actual fight.

## \|\| 1.48.44 \|\|

*tato yuddhārthinaṃ māṃ te vārayaṃti hitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛtotsāhaṃ makhaprāptau nītimārgasamāśritāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. When I opt for war they and my well-wishers oppose me though I am enthusiastic. They strictly abide by the path of good policy and ethics.

## \|\| 1.48.45 \|\|

*tasmāttava prasādena rājasūyo bhavenmakhaḥ \|*  
*avighnaḥ siddhimāyātu mama nānyadvṛṇomyaham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence, with your favour, may my Makha (Rājasūya sacrifice) be concluded without obstacles. I will not choose anything else.»

## \|\| 1.48.46-48 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya jagāmādarśana haraḥ \|*  
*so'pi labdhavaro bhūpaḥ svameva bhavanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*evaṃ tena narendreṇa pūrvaṃ tatra vinirmitau \|*  
*umāmaheśvarau paścānnirmitāvitarairapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yastābhyāṃ kurute pūjāṃ saṃprāpte paṃcamī dine \|*  
*phalaiḥ sarveṣu gātreṣu yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*sutaṃ prāpnoti so'bhīṣṭaṃ svavaṃśoddharaṇakṣamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

Sūta said:

46-48. Hara said: “It shall be so”, and vanished. After acquiring the boon, the king went to his abode. It was thus that Umā and Maheśvara were formerly installed by that king. Afterwards others too installed them. One who performs their adoration on the fifth lunar day for one full year, O Brāhmaṇas, with fruits placed on all the limbs of the idols of Umā and Maheśvara will get a son desired who will be capable of uplifting his race.

## Chapter 49 - King Kalaśa Turns into a Tiger

## \|\| 1.49.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraivāsti mahāpuṇyo hradatīre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kalaśeśvara ityākhyaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā pramucyate pāpānmanuṣyaḥ kalaśeśvaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 49-51 are meant for the glorification of Kalaśeśvara. King Kalaśa is cursed by sage Durvāsā to be a tiger, for feeding him with meat. But he assures him redemption when a cow, Nandinī by name, shows him the Śiva-liṅga adored by Bāṇa. When it took place and the king recovered his human form, he devoted himself to the adoration of that Liṅga which consequently came to be known after him as “Kalaśeśvara.” He built a temple of Umā-Maheśvara with a splendid Kuṇḍa in from, of a meritorious efficacy.

Sūta said:

1-2. There itself on the banks of the tank has been installed the highly meritorious deity called Kalaśeśvara. He is the destroyer of all sins. By visiting Kalaśeśvara, a man is rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.49.3 \|\|

*purāsītkalaśonāma yaduvaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*yajvā dānapatirdakṣaḥ sarvalokahite rataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly there was a king hailing from Yadu race, named Kalaśa. He performed Yajñas. He was vigilant and munificent. He was engaged in the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.49.4 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya durvāsā muni sattamaḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsyavrataṃ kṛtvā tadgṛhaṃ samupasthitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once upon a time, the excellent sage Durvāsas came to his abode. He had adopted the vow of Cāturmāsya.

## \|\| 1.49.5 \|\|

*athotthāya nṛpastūrṇaṃ sammukhaḥ prayayau mudā \|*  
*svāgataṃ svāgataṃ testu bruvāṇa iti sādaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The king immediately got up and joyously came forward to him, respectfully saying “Welcome, welcome to you.”

## \|\| 1.49.6 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ bhaktyā prakṣālya caraṇau svayam \|*  
*dattvārghamiti hovāca harṣabāṣpākulekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He devoutly bowed down to him, washing his feet himself. After offering Arghya he said with tears of joy welling up in his eyes:

## \|\| 1.49.7 \|\|

*idaṃ rājyamamī putrā imā nārya idaṃ dhanam \|*  
*brūhi sarvaṃ mune tvaṃ ca tava kāryaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “O sage, I shall give you all these things—this kingdom, these sons, these women, this wealth. Tell me your purpose (in coming here).”

## \|\| 1.49.8 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*yuktametanmahārāja vaktuṃ te kāryamīdṛśam \|*  
*gṛhāgatāya viprāya vratine'smadvidhāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

8\. O great king, it is proper on your part to say thus to a Brāhmaṇa like us, a person of vows who has come to your abode.

## \|\| 1.49.9 \|\|

*na me kiñciddhanaiḥ kāryaṃ na rājyena nṛpottama \|*  
*cāturmāsyavrato'to'haṃ pāraṇaṃ kartṛmutsahe \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent king. I have nothing to do with your riches nor with your kingdom. I have adopted the Cāturmāsya (vow extending to four months) Vrata. Hence I am eager to perform the Pāraṇā.

## \|\| 1.49.10 \|\|

*tasmādyatkiñcidannaṃ te siddhamasti gṛhe nṛpa \|*  
*taddehi bhojanārthaṃ me bubhukṣātīva vardhate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence, O king, whatever food is ready in your house, give it unto me for eating. My hunger is very great.

## \|\| 1.49.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sa pṛthivīpālo yathāsiddhaṃ susaṃskṛm \|*  
*annaṃ bhojyakṛte tasmai pradadau svayameva hi \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. Then the king himself served him the food well-cooked as it was.

## \|\| 1.49.12 \|\|

*vyañjanāni vicitrāṇi pakvānnāni bahūni ca \|*  
*peyaṃ coṣyaṃ ca khādyaṃ ca lehyamannamanekadhā \|*  
*tathā māṃsaṃ vicitraṃ ca lavaṇādyaiḥ susaṃskṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There were many types of sweet dishes and side-dishes of various kinds. There were four traditional types of food-stuff, viz. Peya (beverages), Coṣya (foodstuff worthy of being sucked), Khādya (food to be chewed) and Lehya (food worthy of being licked and lapped up). There were many meat dishes well sesoned \[seasoned?\] with salt etc.

## \|\| 1.49.13 \|\|

*athāsau bubhuje vipraḥ kṣutkṣāmastvarayānvitaḥ \|*  
*avindanna rasāsvādaṃ bṛhadgrāsairmudānvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The hungry and distressed Brāhmaṇa hurriedly gulped everything in big morsels without relishing the taste. Yet he was joyous.

## \|\| 1.49.14 \|\|

*atha tṛptena māṃsasya jñātastena raso dvijāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kopaparītātmā taṃ śaśāpa munīśvaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After getting satiated he realized that he had the taste of meat, O Brāhmaṇas. Thereupon the leading sage became furious and cursed him:

## \|\| 1.49.15 \|\|

*yasmānmāṃsaṃ tvayā dattvā vratabhaṃgaḥ kṛto mama \|*  
*tasmāttvamāmiṣāhāro raudro vyāghro bhaviṣyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Since you caused a violation in my Vrata by feeding me with meat, you will become a terrible carnivorous tiger.”

## \|\| 1.49.16 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhūpatirbhītaḥ praṇamya ca munīśvaram \|*  
*provāca dīnavadano vepamānaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The miserable king in utter fright, bowed down to the leading sage and said trembling with a distressed face:

## \|\| 1.49.17-18 \|\|

*tava kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhasya mayā bhaktiḥ kṛtā mune \|*  
*yathāsiddhena bhojyena tatkasmācchaptumudyataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me bhaktasya vinatasya ca \|*  
*śāpasyānugraheṇaiva śīghraṃ brāhmaṇasattama \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. “O sage, you had your throat parched with hunger. With great devotion I served you the meal cooked and ready. So why do you feel inclined to curse me? Be pleased with me, your humble devotee, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, by quickly changing your curse into a blessing.”

## \|\| 1.49.19 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*muktvā śrāddhaṃ tathā yajñaṃ na māṃsaṃ bhakṣayeddvijaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa vratasyāṃte cāturmāsyodbhavasya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

19\. Excepting in a Śrāddha and Yajña no Brāhmaṇa shall eat meat. Especially so at the conclusion of a Vrata pertaining to Cāturmāsya.

## \|\| 1.49.20 \|\|

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā māṃsamaśnāti yo dvijaḥ \|*  
*vṛthāmāṃsādvṛthā tasya tadvrataṃ jāyate dhruvam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If a Brāhmaṇa eats flesh after the observance of fast, certainly his Vrata becomes fruitless and the meat is futile.

## \|\| 1.49.21 \|\|

*tasmādvrataṃ praṇaṣṭaṃ me cāturmāsyasamudbhavam \|*  
*tena śapto'si rājeṃdra mayā kopena sāṃpratam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence my Vrata pertaining to Cāturmāsya has been fruitless, O leading king. So you have been now cursed angrily by me.

## \|\| 1.49.22 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tathāpi kuru me vipra śāpasyāṃtaṃ yathepsitam \|*  
*bhaktiyuktasya dīnasya nirdoṣasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

The king said:

22\. Still, O Brāhmaṇa, bring about the desired end to the curse given to me particularly since I am devout, wretched and blameless.

## \|\| 1.49.23 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*yadā te naṃdinī dhenurliṃgaṃ bāṇārcitaṃ purā \|*  
*darśayiṣyati te muktistadā tūrṇaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

23\. When the cow Nandinī points out to you the Liṅga formerly worshipped by Bāṇa, your liberation shall take place immediately.

## \|\| 1.49.24 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa viprendro jagāma nijamāśramam \|*  
*babhūva so'pi bhūpālo vyāghro raudratamākṛtiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After saying thus, the eminent Brāhmaṇa went back to his hermitage. The king too assumed the highly terrible form of a tiger.

## \|\| 1.49.25 \|\|

*naṣṭasmṛtistatastūrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā jaṃtūnpuraḥsthitān \|*  
*jaghānoccāṭitonyaiśca praviveśa mahāvanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He soon lost memory (of his antecedents). On seeing animals in front of him, he killed them and was dislodged from that place by other animals. He then entered a great forest.

## \|\| 1.49.26 \|\|

*atha te maṃtriṇastasya śāpasyātaṃ mahīpateḥ \|*  
*vāṃchatastasya tadrājyaṃ cakrureva surakṣitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The ministers of the king, desiring that there should be an end to his curse, protected the kingdom duly.

## Chapter 50 - Dialogue between the Cow and the Tiger

## \|\| 1.50.4-5 \|\|

*atha sā nijayūthasya sadāgre tṛṇavāṃchayā \|*  
*bhramamāṇā nikuñjāṃte liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*apaśyattejasā yuktaṃ svayameva vyavasthitam \|*  
*dvādaśārkapratīkāśaṃ cittāhlādakaraṃ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

I- 3. Thus, O Brāhmaṇas, a great deal of time passed, when that king in the form of a tiger roamed about in the forest killing different types of animals.

Once upon a time, O excellent Brāhmaṇas a beautiful herd of cows with the full complement of cowherds and cowherdesses came to that region.

In that herd there was a cow named Nandinī with stout udders and large hind quarters. She was of the colour of a swan and yielded (milk) in potfuls.

4-5. With a desire for grass, she used to go ahead of the herd always. Then she saw the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord within a bush. The refulgent Linga was present there by itself. It had the lustre resembling that of twelve suns. It was extremely delightful to the mind.

## \|\| 1.50.6 \|\|

*tatastasyopari sthitvā susrāva sumahatpayaḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yuktā tasya snānakṛte dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The cow stood above it and shed a great deal of milk for bathing it. She was endowed with great faith, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.50.7 \|\|

*evaṃ tāṃ snapanaṃ tasya sadā liṃgasya kurvatīm \|*  
*na jānāti janaḥ kaścidvane vṛkṣasamākule \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. No one in that forest with many trees growing all round, was aware of the fact that the cow had always been bathing the Liṅga thus.

## \|\| 1.50.8 \|\|

*anyasmindivase tatra sthāne vyāghraḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro mahākāyaḥ sarvajantubhayāvahaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On a certain day, a huge tiger of sharp fangs came to that spot. He instilled fear in all the creatures.

## \|\| 1.50.9 \|\|

*atha sā tatra āyātā patitā dṛṣṭigocare \|*  
*nandinī dvīpinastasya daivayogāddvijottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That cow Nandinī came there and fell within the range of the tiger’s sight by chance, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.50.10 \|\|

*tataḥ sā gokule baddhaṃ smṛtvā svaṃ laghuvatsakam \|*  
*atṛṇādaṃ payovṛttiṃ karuṇaṃ paryadevayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then she remembered her small calf that was tied in the cowpen. As she remembered that the calf could not eat grass and could be sustained only through milk, she lamented piteously:

## \|\| 1.50.11-12 \|\|

*adyaikāhaṃ ca saṃprāptā kānane janavarjite \|*  
*putraṃ bālaṃ parityajya gopairgoṣṭhe niyaṃtritam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yena satyena bhaktyādya snapanāyāhamāgatā \|*  
*śivasya tena satyena bhūyānme sutasaṃgamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. “Alas, I have come here alone to this forest devoid of people, leaving my infant calf kept tied up in the cowpen by the cowherds! May there be my re-union with my calf by the power of that truth that I have come here to bathe Śiva.”

## \|\| 1.50.13 \|\|

*evaṃ sā karuṇaṃ yāvannandinī vilapatyalam \|*  
*tāvadvyāghraḥ smitaṃ kṛtvā provāca paruṣākṣaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. While that cow Nandinī was lamenting thus piteously, the tiger smiled derisively and spoke in harsh words.

## \|\| 1.50.14 \|\|

*vyāghra uvāca \|*  
*pralāpānkiṃ mudhā dheno karoṣi vaśagā mama \|*  
*tasmādiṣṭatamaṃ devaṃ smara svargakṛte śubhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

The tiger said:

14\. Why do you lament in vain, O splendid cow? You have come within my grip. So you better remember your favourite Lord for the sake of heaven.

## \|\| 1.50.15 \|\|

*dhenuruvāca \|*  
*nāhamātmakṛte vyāghra vilapāmi suduḥ khitā \|*  
*śivārcanakṛte mṛtyurmama jātaḥ śubhāvahaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

The cow said:

15\. O tiger, it is not for my sake that I lament and feel miserable. My death is surely auspicious, in view of the adoration of Śiva (for which I came here).

## \|\| 1.50.16 \|\|

*vatso me gokule baddhaḥ smaramāṇo mamāgamam \|*  
*santiṣṭhate payovṛttiḥ kathaṃ syātsa mayā vinā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. My calf is being kept tied in the cowpen. It is eagerly waiting for my arrival. Its sole sustenance is my milk. How can it live without me?

## \|\| 1.50.17 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādvyāghra vilapāmi suduḥkhitā \|*  
*na cātmajīvanārthāya satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. It is for this reason, O tiger, that I lament and feel very miserable and not for the sake of my own life. I pledge myself truthfully (on my honour, I promise).

## \|\| 1.50.18 \|\|

*tasmānmuṃca mahāvyāghra māṃ sadyaḥ sutavatsalām \|*  
*sakhījanasya taṃ dattvā samāgacchāmi teṃtikam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hence, O great tiger, leave me immediately as I am fond of my calf. I shall entrust it to a companion of mine and return to you.

## \|\| 1.50.19 \|\|

*vyāghra uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ mṛtyumukhaṃ prāpya niṣkramya ca kathañcana \|*  
*bhūyastatraiva niryāsi tasmāttvāṃ bhakṣayāmyaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

The tiger said:

19\. How (can I believe) that after falling into the jaws of death and escaping somehow (from that) you will come back again? So I am going to devour you.

## \|\| 1.50.20 \|\|

*nandinyuvāca \|*
