*śapathairāgamiṣyāmi yaiḥ punarvyāghra teṃ'tikam \|*  
*tānākarṇaya me vaktrāttato yuktaṃ samācara \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

20\. O tiger, listen to my solemn oaths uttered by myself whereby I undertake to come back to you again and then do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.50.21 \|\|

*yatpāpaṃ brahmahatyāyāṃ mātāpitrośca vaṃcane \|*  
*tena pāpena lipyehaṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which is incurred on murdering a Brāhmaṇa or by deceiving parents.

## \|\| 1.50.22 \|\|

*vivastraṃ snānasaktānāṃ divāmaithunagāminām \|*  
*yatpāpaṃ tena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which befalls those who are eager to take bath in the nude and those who indulge in sexual intercourse in broad daylight.

## \|\| 1.50.23 \|\|

*rajasvalānusaktānāṃ yatpāpaṃ nagnaśāyinām \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which accrues to those who pursue women in their monthly periods and to those who go to bed in the nude.

## \|\| 1.50.24 \|\|

*viśvāsaghātakānāṃ ca kṛtaghnānāṃ ca yadbhavet \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which thosè who betray trust and are ungrateful, incur.

## \|\| 1.50.25 \|\|

*gokanyābrāhmaṇānāṃ ca dūṣakānāṃ ca yadbhavet \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which befalls those who defile and slander cows, virgins and Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.50.26 \|\|

*vṛthāpākaprakartṛṇāṃ vṛthāmāṃsāśināṃ ca yat \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin that befalls those who-cook in vain and eat meat in vain (just for the pleasure of it).

## \|\| 1.50.27 \|\|

*vratabhaṃgaprakartṛṇāmanṛtau gāmināṃ ca yat \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If I do not come back again, let me incur that sin which befalls those who violate holy vows and those who carnally approach their wives on the prohibited days of the menstrual cycle.

## \|\| 1.50.28 \|\|

*paiśunyasūcakānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ śastrakarmaṇām \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If I do not come back again, let me incur the sin of backbiters and talebearers as well as manufacturers of weapons.

## Chapter 51 - Greatness of Kalaśeśvara (Kalaśa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.51.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha tācchapathāñchrutvā sa vyāghro vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ matvā punaḥ prāha nandinīṃ putravatsalām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadyevaṃ tadgṛhaṃ gaccha vīkṣayasva nijātmajam \|*  
*sakhīnāmarpayitvātha bhūya āgamanaṃ kuru \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On hearing those solemn oaths, the tiger became surprised. Considering that it was the truth, he said to Nandinī fond of her calf: “If it is so, go home and meet your calf. Entrust it to your companions and return soon.”

## \|\| 1.51.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti vyāghravacaḥ śrutvā suśīlā nandinī tadā \|*  
*gatālayaṃ samuddiśya yatra bālaḥ sutaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. On hearing these words of the tiger, Nandinī of excellent conduct went homewards where her calf was tied.

## \|\| 1.51.4 \|\|

*athākālāgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātaraṃ trastacetasam \|*  
*raṃbhamāṇāṃ samālokya vatsaḥ provāca vismayāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The calf was surprised on seeing its mother coming back before the usual time in a frightened state of mind and lowing it said:

## \|\| 1.51.5 \|\|

*kasmāt prāptāsyakāle tu kasmādudbhrāṃtamānasā \|*  
*vāṣpaklinnamukhī kasmādvada mātardrutaṃmama \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “Why have you come back before the time? Why are you upset and bewildered? Why is your face drenched and full of tears? O dear mother, speak out quickly.”

## \|\| 1.51.6 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*yadi pṛcchasi māṃ putra stanapānaṃ samācara \|*  
*yena tṛptasya te sarvaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ tadvadāmyaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

6\. If you want to ask me anything, first you suck the udders. If you are fully satisfied after sucking the milk, I shall tell you everything.

## \|\| 1.51.7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*so'pi tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pītvā kṣīraṃ yathocitam \|*  
*āghrātaśca tayā mūrdhni tataḥ provāca satvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7\. At her instance the calf sucked up as much milk as it was wont to do. Then the mother sniffed at its head. The calf thereupon said immediately.

## \|\| 1.51.8 \|\|

*sarvaṃ kīrtaya vṛttāṃtamadyāraṇyasamudbhavam \|*  
*yena me jāyate svāsthyaṃ śrutvā mātastavāsyataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Tell all the news of the forest now. On hearing it, O dear mother, straight from you, I shall have some relief.”

## \|\| 1.51.9 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ gatā mahāraṇye hyadya putra yathecchayā \|*  
*vyāghreṇāsāditā tatra bhramamāṇā itastataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

9\. Dear son, I went to the great forest today and as I was roaming about as I pleased, I was held up by a tiger.

## \|\| 1.51.10-11 \|\|

*sa mayā prārthitaḥ putra bhakṣamāṇo nakhāyudhaḥ \|*  
*śapathairāgamiṣyāmi gokule vīkṣya cātmajam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sāhaṃ tena vinirmuktā śapathairbahubhiḥ kṛtaiḥ \|*  
*bhūyastatraiva yāsyāmi dṛṣṭaḥ saṃbhāṣito bhavān \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. When that wild animal with claws as his weapon was bent upon devouring me, I requested him on oath, “I shall come back after meeting my calf in the cowpen.”

I was allowed to come away after many solemn oaths had been taken. I shall go there again. I have met you and talked to you.

## \|\| 1.51.12 \|\|

*vatsa uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tatraiva yāsyāmi yatra tvaṃ hi pragacchasi \|*  
*ślāghyaṃ hi maraṇaṃ samyaṅmāturagre mamādhunā \|\| 12 \|\|*

The calf said:

12\. I shall go there where you are proceeding to. My death in front of my mother could be worthy of praise now.

## \|\| 1.51.13 \|\|

*ekākināpi martavyaṃ tvayā hīnena vai mayā \|*  
*vināpi kṣīrapānena svalpena samayena tu \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If I am deserted by you I am sure to die in a short while being left alone and denied the sucking of milk.

## \|\| 1.51.14 \|\|

*yadi mātastvayā sārdhaṃ vyāghro māṃ sūdayiṣyati \|*  
*yā gatirmātṛbhaktānāṃ sā me nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Mother, if the tiger kills me too along with you, I am sure to attain the goal of those devoted to their mothers.

## \|\| 1.51.15 \|\|

*athavā ye tvayā tasya vihitāḥ śapathāḥ śubhe \|*  
*te saṃtu mama tiṣṭha tvaṃ tasmādatraiva gokule \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Or, O splendid mother, let those solemn oaths taken before him by you be held in abeyance for me. Do remain here in the cowherds colony.

## \|\| 1.51.16 \|\|

*nāsti mātṛsamo bandhurbālānāṃ kṣīrajīvinām \|*  
*nāsti mātṛsamo nātho nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. To children sustained with milk there is no other kinsman on a par with the mother. There is no other leader and guide on a par with mother; there is no other place of resort equal to mother.

## \|\| 1.51.17 \|\|

*nāsti mātṛsamaḥ pūjyo nāsti mātṛsamaḥ sakhā \|*  
*nāsti mātṛsamo deva iha loke paratra ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There is no other person worthy of adoration on a par with mother. There is no other friend equal to and on a par with mother.

## \|\| 1.51.18 \|\|

*evaṃ matvā sadā mātuḥ kartavyā bhaktiruttamaiḥ \|*  
*tamenaṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ prajāpativinirmitam \|*  
*anutiṣṭhaṃti ye putrāste yāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With this consideration always excellent persons should evince ardent devotion to mothers. Those sons who follow this highest righteous rule ordained by Prajāpati, attain the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.51.19 \|\|

*tasmādahaṃ gamiṣyāmi tvaṃ ca tiṣṭhātra gokule \|*  
*ātmaprāṇaistava prāṇānrakṣayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Hence I shall go there. Do stay here in the cowherds’ colony. Undoubtedly I shall save your life by means of mine.

## \|\| 1.51.20 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*mamaiva vihito mṛtyurna te putrādya vāsare \|*  
*tatkathaṃ mama jīvaṃ tvaṃ rakṣasyasubhirātmanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

20\. On this day it is my death that has been enjoined, not yours, son. Hence, how will you save my life through yours?

## \|\| 1.51.21 \|\|

*apaścimamidaṃ putra mātṛsaṃdiṣṭamuttamam \|*  
*tvayā kāryaṃ prayatnena madvākyamanutiṣṭhatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Dear son, this is the ultimate and excellent message conveyed to you which you will assiduously carry out in pursuance of my direction.

## \|\| 1.51.22 \|\|

*bhramamāṇo vane putra mā pramādaṃ kariṣyasi \|*  
*lobhātsaṃjāyate nāśa ihaloke paratra ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. While roaming about in the forest, dear son, do not commit any mistake. Both here and in the other world, ruin is bound to occur through greediness.

## \|\| 1.51.23 \|\|

*samudramaṭavīṃ yuddhaṃ viśaṃte lobhamohitāḥ \|*  
*iha tannāsti lobhena yatra kurvaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Persons deluded by greed enter ocean, great forest and battlefield. Here there is nothing which men do not undertake due to greed.

## \|\| 1.51.24 \|\|

*lobhātpramādādviśraṃbhātpuruṣo vadhyate tribhiḥ \|*  
*tasmāllobho na kartavyo na pramādo na viśvaset \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person is doomed due to three things: covetousness, inadvertence and trust. Hence one should not covet, be inadvertent or trust blindly.

## \|\| 1.51.25 \|\|

*ātmā putra tvayā rakṣyaḥ sarvadaiva praya tnataḥ \|*  
*sarvebhyaḥ śvāpadebhyaśca bhramatā gahane vane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When you roam about in a deep forest with all efforts, dear son, your own self should be guarded by you always from the beasts of prey.

## \|\| 1.51.26 \|\|

*viṣamasthaṃ tṛṇānnādyaṃ kathaṃcitputraka tvayā \|*  
*naikākinā pragaṃtavyaṃ yūthaṃ tyaktvā nijaṃ kvacit \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You should not stray away from the herd anywhere, dear son. Should the grass, fodder etc., be in a risky place, you must not go there alone.

## \|\| 1.51.27-28 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbhāṣya taṃ vatsamavalihya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*śokena mahatāviṣṭā bāṣpavyākulalocanā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tataḥ sakhījanaṃ sarvaṃ gatā draṣṭuṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*nandinīṃ putraśokena pīḍitāṃgī suvihvalā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Thus that Nandinī addressed her calf and licked it repeatedly. She was overwhelmed with great grief and her eyes were dimmed with tears. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in that very state of excitement and afflicted utterly by the grief for her son, she went to meet with all her companions.

## \|\| 1.51.29 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tāḥ sarvā gatvā'raṇyaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*caraṃtīḥ svecchayā hṛṣṭā vāṃchitāni tṛṇāni tāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. She went to the great forest, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, where all of them were joyously grazing the grasses they liked and said to them:

## \|\| 1.51.30-32 \|\|

*bahule caṃpake dāme vasudhāre ghaṭasrave \|*  
*haṃsanādi priyānaṃde śubhakṣīre mahodaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tathānyā dhenavo yāśca saṃsthitā gokulāṃtike \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtu vacanaṃ mahyaṃ kurvaṃtu ca tataḥ param \|*  
*adyāhaṃ nijayūthasya bhramaṃtī nātidūrataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tataśca gahanaṃ prāptā vanaṃ mānuṣavarjitam \|*  
*vyāghreṇāsāditā tatra bhramaṃtī tṛṇavāṃchayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. (She addressed the companions individually:) “O Bahulā, O Caṃpakā, O Dāmā, O Vasudhārā, O Ghaṭasravā, O Haṃsanāḍī, O Priyānandā, O Śubhakṣīrā, O Mahodayā and other cows present here belonging to your cowherds colony, listen to my words. Thereafter do accordingly.

Today I was roaming about not very far from our herd. Then I entered the thick jungle devoid of men. Roaming there for the love of the green grass I was waylaid by a tiger.

## \|\| 1.51.33 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ darśanārthāya sutasaṃbhāṣaṇāya ca \|*  
*saṃprāptā śapathaiḥ kṛcchrāttaṃ viśvāsya nakhāyudham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By means of solemn oaths (for a sure-return to the tiger) after seeing you all and talking to my calf I was able to make that claw-weaponed one relent with very great difficulty, and I have now come back.

## \|\| 1.51.34 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaḥ saṃbhāṣitaḥ putraḥ śāsitaśca mayā hi saḥ \|*  
*adhunā bhavatīnāṃ ca pradattaḥ putrako yathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I have met and talked to my son. He has been suitably advised and admonished. Now this dear son is being entrusted to the care of all of you.

## \|\| 1.51.35 \|\|

*ajñānājjñānato vāpi bhavatīnāṃ mayā kṛtam \|*  
*yatkiṃcidduṣkṛtaṃ bhadrāstatkṣaṃtavyaṃ prasādataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O fair ones, it may be that I had committed some misdemeanour against you knowingly or otherwise. May that be forgiven with favour

## \|\| 1.51.36 \|\|

*anātho hyabalo dīnaḥ kṣīrapo mama bālakaḥ \|*  
*mātṛśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ pālyaḥ sarvābhireva saḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. My weak and distressed child, still feeding on milk, will now be helpless and all the more grief-stricken due to separation from its mother. All of you should rear him up.

## \|\| 1.51.37 \|\|

*bhramamāṇo'same sthāne vrajamāno'nyagokule \|*  
*akāryeṣu ca saṃsakto nivāryaḥ sarvadā'darāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Should he stray into other herds or roam about in uneven places or be engaged in misdeed of any sort, all of you will always dissuade him with care.

## \|\| 1.51.38 \|\|

*ahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi sa vyāghro yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*apaścimapraṇāmo'yaṃ sarvāsāṃ vihito mayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I am going to that place where the tiger is presenṭ This is my final adieu to all of you.”

## \|\| 1.51.39 \|\|

*dhenava ūcuḥ \|*  
*na gaṃtavyaṃ tvayā tatra kathaṃcidapi naṃdini \|*  
*āpaddharmaṃ na vetsi tvaṃ nūnaṃ yena pragacchasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

The cows said:

39\. O Nandinī, you should not go there at any cost. You are not aware of Āpaddharma (misdeed condoned during distress). Hence you are keen to go there.

## \|\| 1.51.40 \|\|

*na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti na strīṣu jātirna vivāhakāle \|*  
*prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre paṃcānṛtānyāhurapātakāni \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Utterance of falsehood on these occasion is not sinful: when death is imminent, when there is the likelihood of loss of all wealth, when indulging in a joke, when talking about castes among women, at the time of fixing up of marriages.

## \|\| 1.51.41 \|\|

*tasmāttatra na gaṃtavyaṃ doṣo nāstyatra te śubhe \|*  
*pālayasva nijaṃ putraṃ vrajāsmābhirnijaṃ gṛham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence, O fair one, you should not go there. In this you are not blameworthy. Bring up your calf. Come along with us to our adobe.

## \|\| 1.51.42 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*pareṣāṃ prāṇayātrārthaṃ tatkartuṃ yujyate śubhāḥ \|*  
*ātmaprāṇahitārthāya na sādhūnāṃ praśasyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

42\. O splendid ones, such a course is proper to be undertaken for the sake of saving the life of others. But in the case of good people it is not commended when the aim is saving one’s own life or furthering one’s own welfare.

## \|\| 1.51.43 \|\|

*satye pratiṣṭhito loko dharmaḥ satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*udadhiḥ satyavākyena maryādāṃ na vilaṃghayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The universe is well-established on truth. Piety is well-established on truth; the ocean does not transgress the limit on account of the truthful statement.

## \|\| 1.51.44 \|\|

*viṣṇave pṛthivīṃ dattvā baliḥ pātālamāśritaḥ \|*  
*satyavākyaṃ samāśritya na niṣkrāmati daityapaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Bali handed over the earth to Viṣṇu and took refuge in nether worlds. The king of Daityas did not back out after making his promise.

## \|\| 1.51.45 \|\|

*yaḥ svaṃ vākyaṃ pratijñāya na karoti yathoditam \|*  
*kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ caureṇākṛta buddhinā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If anyone promises anything but does not carry it out as promised, he becomes a thief of irresolute character. Has he not then committed a great sin?

## \|\| 1.51.46 \|\|

*sakhya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ naṃdini namaskāryā sarverapi surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*yā tvaṃ satyapratiṣṭhārthaṃ prāṇāṃstyajasi dustyajān \|\| 46 \|\|*

The companions said:

46\. O Nandinī, you are worthy of being bowed down to by all the Suras and Asuras for you have decided to give up your life for the preservation of truth. Life is not ordinarily given up easily.

## \|\| 1.51.47 \|\|

*kiṃ tvāṃ kalyāṇi vakṣyāmaḥ svayaṃ dharmārthavādinīm \|*  
*savareṃpi guṇairyuktā nityaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. What else shall we say, O auspicious one, to you already engaged in expounding pious themes, equipped with all the good qualities and always abiding by truth?

## \|\| 1.51.48 \|\|

*tasmādgaccha mahābhāge na śocyaḥ putrakastava \|*  
*bhavatyā yadvayaṃ proktāstatkariṣyāma eva hi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O highly esteemed one, do proceed ahead. Do not be worried for your child. What we have been told by you we shall cany out.

## \|\| 1.51.49 \|\|

*etatpunarvayaṃ vidmaḥ sadā satyavatāṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*na niṣphalaḥ kriyāraṃbhaḥ kathaṃcidapi jāyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This we know fully well that a task undertaken by truthful men never goes to waste.

## \|\| 1.51.50-51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbhāṣya taṃ sarvaṃ naṃdinī svasakhījanam \|*  
*prasthitā vyāghramuddiśya putraśokena pīḍitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śokāgnināpi saṃtaptā nirāśā putradarśane \|*  
*viyuktā cakravākīva lateva patitā taroḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

50-51. After addressing all the companions thus Nandinī started towards the tiger. She continued to be afflicted with the grief for her son. Giving up the hope of seeing her son again she was extremely distressed by the fire of grief. She was like a ruddy goose separated from her beloved. She was like a creeper fallen from a tree.

## \|\| 1.51.52-53 \|\|

*aṃdheva dṛṣṭinirmuktā praskhalaṃtī padepade \|*  
*vanādhidevatāḥ sarvāḥ prā'rthayacca sutārthataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*prasuptaṃ bhramamāṇaṃ vā mama putraṃ subālakam \|*  
*vanādhidevatāḥ sarvā rakṣaṃtu vacanānmama \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Like a blind one devoid of sight, she faltered at every step. For the sake of her child she prayed to all the sylvan deities:

“May all the sylvan deities guard my infant calf whether he is asleep or in the act of roaming. May they do so at my instance.”

## \|\| 1.51.54-55 \|\|

*evaṃ pralapya manasā saṃprāptā tatra yatra saḥ \|*  
*āste visphūrjitāsyaśca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro bhayāvahaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vyāghraḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaśca tasyā mārgāvalokakaḥ \|*  
*saṃraṃbhāṭopasaṃyuktaḥ sṛkkiṇī parilehayan \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Lamenting thus mentally, she reached the place where the terrible tiger with sharp fangs (curved teeth) was waiting for her. He was roaring like thunder with the throat parched due to hunger. He was displaying his fury and arrogance, licking the corners of the mouth.

## \|\| 1.51.56 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*āgatāhaṃ mahāvyāghra satye ca śapathe sthitā \|*  
*kuru tṛptiṃ yathākāmaṃ mama māṃsena sāṃpratam \|\| 56 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

56\. O great tiger, here I am. Abiding by my true and solemn oath I have came back. Now you can gratify yourself with my flesh.

## \|\| 1.51.57 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā so'pi duṣṭātmā vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*satyāśayā punaḥ prāptā saṃtyajya prāṇajaṃ bhayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Though he was wicked-minded he experienced a state of highest detachment on seeing her because she had come back without any fear for her life, only because she was clinging eagerly to the truth.

## \|\| 1.51.58 \|\|

*vyāghra uvāca \|*  
*svāgataṃ tava kalyāṇi sudheno satyavādini \|*  
*na hi satyavatāṃ kiṃcidaśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit \|\| 58 \|\|*

The tiger said:

58\. Welcome to you, O excellent cow of auspicious features and truthful speech. Nothing is inauspicious in the case of truthful ones.

## \|\| 1.51.59 \|\|

*tvayoktaṃ śapathairbhadre āgamiṣyāmyahaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tena me kautukaṃ jātaṃ kimeṣā prakariṣyati \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O fair one, pledging solemn oaths you said, “I will come again.” That provoked my curiosity as to what will this (cow) do?

## \|\| 1.51.60 \|\|

*so'haṃ bhadre durācāro nṛśaṃso jīvaghātakaḥ \|*  
*yāsyāmi narakaṃ ghoraṃ karmaṇānena sarvadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Ruthlessly killing living beings, I have been very wicked in conduct. On account of this perpetual activity, I am bound to fall into terrible Naraka.

## \|\| 1.51.61 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ me mahābhāge pāpāsyātidurātmanaḥ \|*  
*upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O highly esteemed one, it behoves you to do me the favour of imparting instructions to me though I am a sinner and utterly evil-minded.

## \|\| 1.51.62 \|\|

*yena me syātparaṃ śreya iha loke paratra ca \|*  
*na te'styaviditaṃ kiṃcitsatyācārānmatirmama \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thereby I will have the greatest weal in this world as well as in the other one. I believe that there is nothing not known to you, thanks to the truthful conduct.

## \|\| 1.51.63 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ dharmasarvasvaṃ saṃkṣepānmama kīrtaya \|*  
*satsaṃgamaphalaṃ yena mama saṃjāyate'khilam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Hence you describe to me succinctly the essence of piety and virtue. Thereby I will reap the fruit of association with the good entirely.

## \|\| 1.51.64-65 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛte praśaṃsaṃti tretāyāṃ dhyānameva ca \|*  
*dvāpare yajñayogaṃ ca dānamekaṃ kalau yuge \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva dānānāṃ nāsti dānamataḥ param \|\| 64 \|\|*

*carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāmabhayaṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*sa sarvabhayanirmuktaḥ paraṃ brahmā dhigacchati \|\| 65 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

64-65. They commend austerities in Kṛta Yuga and meditation in Tretā Yuga. In Dvāpara Yuga Yajña and Yoga are praise-worthy, but in Kali Yuga it is Dāna alone. One who gives freedom from fear to all living beings both mobile and immobile, becomes himself free from all fears and attains the greatest Brahman. Of all the types of Dāna there is nothing greater than this.

## \|\| 1.51.66-67 \|\|

*vyāghra uvāca \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ taddānaṃ yujyate śubhe \|*  
*ahiṃsayā bhavedyeṣāṃ prāṇayātrānnapūrvakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*na hiṃsayā vinā'smākaṃ yataḥ syātprāṇadhāraṇam \|*  
*tasmādbrūhi mahābhāge kiñcinmama sukhāvaham \|*  
*upadeśaṃ sudharmāya hiṃsakasyāpi dehinām \|\| 67 \|\|*

The tiger said:

66-67. O auspicious one, in the case of other living beings who sustain themselves through food (i.e. vegetation) without injuring anyone that type of Dāna may be relevant. On the other hand it is impossible for us to sustain ourselves without violence. Hence, O highly esteemed one, tell me something conducive to my happiness, an instruction in excellent piety though I am one who injures other living beings.

Nandinī said

## \|\| 1.51.68 \|\|

*nandinyuvāca \|*  
*atrāsti sumahalliṃgaṃ purā bāṇapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*gahane yatprabhāvena tvayā muktāsmyahaṃ dhruvam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Here there is a great Liṅga installed by Bāṇa in this forest. Certainly it is the power of that Liṅga whereby I have been liberated by you.

## \|\| 1.51.69 \|\|

*tasya tvaṃ prātarutthāya kuru nityaṃ pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*praṇāmaṃ ca tataḥ siddhiṃ vāṃchitāṃ samavāpsyasi \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Do get up early in the morning, circumambulate it everyday and then bow down to it. Thereby you will attain the desired fulfilment.

## \|\| 1.51.70 \|\|

*nānyasya karmaṇaḥ śaktirvidyate te nakhāyudha \|*  
*pūjādikasya hīnatvāddhastābhyāmiti me matiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O claw-weaponed one, this is my opinion that you do not have the ability to perform other rites such as adoration etc. in view of the fact that you do not have hands.

## \|\| 1.51.71 \|\|

*evamuktvātha sā dhenurvyāghrasyātha vanāṃtike \|*  
*talliṃgaṃ darśayāmāsa puraḥ sthitvā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, after saying thus that cow stood before the tiger at the outskirts of the forest and showed that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.51.72 \|\|

*so'pi saṃdarśanāttasya tatkṣaṇānmuktimāptavān \|*  
*vyāghratvātpārthivo bhūyaḥ sa babhūva yathā purā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thanks to its sight, he instantly got rid of his tiger-hood. He became a king as before.

## \|\| 1.51.73 \|\|

*śāpaṃ durvāsasā dattaṃ rājyaṃ svaṃ sahitaiḥ sutaiḥ \|*  
*sasmāra sa nṛpaśreṣṭhastataḥ provāca naṃdinīm \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The excellent king remembered the curse uttered by Durvāsas and his own kingdom along with his sons. Then he said to Nandinī:

## \|\| 1.51.74 \|\|

*nṛpaḥ kalaśanāmāhaṃ haihayānvayasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*śapto durvāsasā pūrvaṃ kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “I am a king named Kalaśa, born of the Haihaya race. I was cursed by Durvāsas earlier for certain reasons.”

## \|\| 1.51.75-76 \|\|

*tataḥ prasāditenoktastenāhaṃ naṃdinī yadā \|*  
*darśayiṣyati talliṃgaṃ tadā muktirbhaviṣyati \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sā nūnaṃ nandinī tvaṃ hi jñātā śāpāntato mayā \|*  
*tattvaṃ brūhi pradeśo'yaṃ katamo varadhenuke \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. When he was pacified he had said, “When Nandinī shows you that Liṅga you will become liberated.” It is now known that you are certainly that Nandinī because my curse has come to an end. So, tell me, O excellent cow, what is this part of the land.

## \|\| 1.51.77 \|\|

*yena gacchāmyahaṃ bhūyaḥ svagṛhaṃ prati satvaram \|*  
*mārgaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābhāge mānuṣaṃ prāpya kañcana \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Thereby I can quickly go back to my abode, O highly esteemed one, after meeting some human being and finding out my way.

## \|\| 1.51.78 \|\|

*naṃdinyuvāca \|*  
*camatkārapurakṣetrametatpātakanāśanam \|*  
*sarvatīrthamayaṃ rājansarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 78 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

78\. O king, this is the holy spot of Camatkārapura. It is destructive of sins. All the Tīrthas are present in it and it yields all desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.51.79-80 \|\|

*yadanyatra bhavecchreyo vatsareṇa tapasvinām \|*  
*dinenaivātra tatsamyagjāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*evaṃ matvā mayā liṃgaṃ snāpitaṃ payasā sadā \|*  
*etadyūthaṃ parityajya bhaktyā pūtena cetasā \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. I had thought thus, ‘There is no doubt about this that within a day one perfectly achieves that weal which ascetics get elsewhere in the course of a year.’ After thinking thus, I went away from my herd always with my mind purified by devotion and bathed the Liṅga with my milk.

## \|\| 1.51.81 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*gaccha nandini bhadraṃ te nijaṃ prāpnuhi bālakam \|*  
*gokulaṃ ca sakhīḥ svāśca tathānyaṃ ca suhṛjjanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

The king said:

81\. O Nandinī, god bless you! Do go back to your calf, the herd, your companions and other friends.

## \|\| 1.51.82-83 \|\|

*etatkṣetraṃ mayā pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mukhācchrutam \|*  
*vāṃchitaṃ ca sadā praṣṭuṃ na ca draṣṭuṃ prapāritam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*rājyakarmaprasaktena bhogāsaktena naṃdini \|*  
*svayamevādhunā labdhaṃ nāhaṃ santyaktumutsahe \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. I had heard about this holy spot from the report (speech) of some Brāhmaṇas earlier. I had wished to enquire about but I could not visit it, O Nandinī, because I was engaged in kingly duties or rather I was over-indulging in worldly pleasures. Since it has been achieved by myself I would rather not lose it.

## \|\| 1.51.84 \|\|

*diṣṭyā me muninā tena dattaḥ śāpo mahātmanā \|*  
*kathaṃ syādanyathā prāptiḥ kṣetrasyāsya suśobhane \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. It was a blessing to me that the lofty-minded sage cursed me, O splendid one. How could I have attained this holy spot otherwise?

## \|\| 1.51.85 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā mahīpālo nandinīṃ tāṃ visṛjya ca \|*  
*sthitastatraiva talliṃgaṃ dhyāyamāno divāniśam \|\| 85 \|\|*

Sūta said:

85\. After saying thus and bidding goodbye to that Nandinī, the king stayed there itself meditating upon that Liṅga day and night.

## \|\| 1.51.86 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ tatkṛte mukhyaṃ vidhāyādbhutadarśanam \|*  
*kailāsaśikharākāraṃ tapastepe tadagrataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. He built a wonderful mansion (shrine) as lofty as the peak of Kailāsa and performed penance before it.

## \|\| 1.51.87 \|\|

*tatastasya prabhāvena svalpaireva dinairdvijāḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ yājñikairapi \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, by its power within a few days he obtained the greatest fulfilment inaccessible even to those who regularly perform Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.51.88 \|\|

*tatra yaḥ kārtike māsi dīpakaṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. One who lights and offers a lamp there in the month of Kārttika will be rid of all sins and honoured in the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.51.89 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe ca samprāpte gītanṛtyādikaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*tadagre kurute bhaktyā sa gacchati parāṃ gatim \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. A man who makes arrangement for songs, dances etc. before it devoutly in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.51.90 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*kalaśeśvaramāhātmyaṃ vistareṇa dvijottamāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Kalaśeśvara, destructive of all sins, has been fully narrated in detail to you all.

## \|\| 1.51.91 \|\|

*bhaktyā paṭhati yaścaitacchraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*so'pi pāpavinirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. One who is endowed with great faith and reads this devoutly becomes liberated from sins and is honoured in the world of Śiva.

## Chapter 52 - Greatness of Rudrakoṭi

## \|\| 1.52.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*umāmaheśvarau tatra sthāpitau tena bhūbhujā \|*  
*prāsādaṃ paramaṃ kṛtvā sādhudṛṣṭisukhapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasyāgrataḥ śubhaṃ kuṃḍaṃ tatra caiva vinirmitam \|*  
*svacchodakena sampūrṇaṃ padminīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snātvā tatra naro bhaktyā tau paśyedyaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*māghaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ na sa bhūyo'tra jāyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Umā and Maheśvara were installed there by that king after building a great mansion (shrine) that gave pleasure to the eyes of righteous people.

In front of it, an auspicious holy Kuṇḍa (pit, small pond) was made and filled with clear water and adorned by clusters of lotuses.

A man who devoutly takes his holy bath there and visits (the idols) then, with mental concentration and purity, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha, is not reborn.

## \|\| 1.52.4 \|\|

*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge'gastyakuṇḍasamīpataḥ \|*  
*asti vāpī mahāpuṇyā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. To the eastern side thereof and near Agastyakuṇḍa, there is a highly meritorious tank that destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.52.5 \|\|

*tasyāṃ yaḥ kurute snānaṃ māsi vai phālgune naraḥ \|*  
*sopavāsaḥ sitāṣṭamyāṃ vāṃchitaṃ labhate ca saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A man who takes his holy bath therein on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Phālguna and observes fast, obtains all desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.52.6 \|\|

*tasyā dakṣiṇadigbhāge tatrāsti kapilā nadī \|*  
*kapilo yatra saṃprāptaḥ siddhiṃ sāṃkhyasamudbhavām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. River Kapilā flows on its southern side. It was there that Kapila attained Siddhi (spiritual perfection) through the practice of Sāṅkhya philosophy.

## \|\| 1.52.7 \|\|

*kapilāyāśca pūrveṇa siddhakṣetraṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*yatra siddhiṃ gatāḥ siddhāḥ purā śata sahasraśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The region to the east of Kapilā is glorified as Siddhakṣetra (Holy land of those who have attained spiritual fulfilment). Formerly hundreds and thousand of Siddhas had attained fulfilment there.

## \|\| 1.52.8 \|\|

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tapastatra samācaret \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare nūnaṃ sa tamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A man who cherishing any desire performs penance there, shall certainly realize it within six months.

## \|\| 1.52.9-12 \|\|

*tasyādhastācchilā viprā vidyate vaiṣṇavī śubhā \|*  
*bhramantī caturasrā ca sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sadā mahānadītoyakṣālitā muktidā nṛṇām \|*  
*gaṃgāyamunayormadhye saṃniviṣṭā sarasvatī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*triveṇī vahate tasyāḥ purato bhuktimuktidā \|*  
*tasyāmupari dagdhānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nūnaṃ muktirbhavetteṣāṃ citā bhasmani goṣpadam \|*  
*dṛśyate tatra tajjñātvā saṃskāryā brāhmaṇā mṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-10a. Beneath it, O Brāhmaṇas, there is a splendid, square, Vaiṣṇavī slab. It whirls and is destructive of all sins. It is perpetually washed by the waters of the great river. It bestows salvation on men.

10b-12. River Sarasvatī flows in between Gaṅgā and Yamunā. The Triveṇī (three rivers) thus flows in front of it. It yields worldly pleasures and salvation.

If Brāhmaṇas are cremated on its banks they will certainly obtain salvation. A Goṣpada (cow’s foot) becomes visible in the ashes of their pyre. After seeing it, obsequies of dead Brāhmaṇas must be performed.

## \|\| 1.52.13 \|\|

*tasyaivottaradigbhāge rudrakoṭirdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*asti saṃpūjitā viprai rdākṣiṇātyairmahātmabhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Rudrakoṭi is to the northern side thereof. It is adored by noble-souled southern Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.52.14-15 \|\|

*mahāyogisvarūpeṇa dākṣiṇātyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre śrutvā svayamumāpatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tataḥ kautūhalāviṣṭāḥ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*koṭisaṃkhyā drutaṃ jagmustasya darśanavāṃchayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The excellent Brāhmaṇas of the south had heard that the Consort of Umā was himself present in the form of a great Yogin in the holy place called Camatkārapura. Endowed with great faith and urged by curiosity ten million of them rushed in with a desire to visit the Lord.

## \|\| 1.52.16 \|\|

*ahaṃpūrvamahaṃpūrvaṃ vīkṣayiṣyāmi taṃ haram \|*  
*iti śraddhāsamo petāścakruste śapathaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Everyone of them said, “I will visit Lord Hara first.” They took oath thus on going there.

## \|\| 1.52.17 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ madhyato yastaṃ mahāyoginamīśvaram \|*  
*caramaṃ devamīkṣeta bhaviṣyati sa pāpakṛt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “The last person among these who visits the great Yogin Īśvara will become a sinner.”

## \|\| 1.52.18 \|\|

*tatasteṣāmabhiprāyaṃ jñātvā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhaktiprīto hitārthāya koṭirūpairvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Lord Maheśvara understood their intention and he was pleased with their devotion. So for their convenience and benefit, he established himself there in ten million forms.

## \|\| 1.52.19 \|\|

*helayā darśanaṃ prāptaḥ sarveṣāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti tatsthānaṃ rudrakoṭītiviśrutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he was thus visited very easily by all of them. Ever since then, that holy spot became well known as Rudrakoṭi.

## \|\| 1.52.20 \|\|

*tadarthaṃ paṭhitaḥ śloko nāradena purā dvijāḥ \|*  
*rudrāvartaṃ samālokya prahṛṣṭena dvijottamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Nārada was delighted on seeing this circle (multiplicity) of Rudras, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Then he recited a verse on that event.

## \|\| 1.52.21 \|\|

*āṣāḍhīṃ kārtikīṃ māghīṃ tathā caitrasamudbhavām \|*  
*dhanyāḥ pṛthivyāṃ lapsyaṃte rudrāvarte caturdaśīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “Only blessed people on the earth will obtain (a view) of Rudrāvarta (Rudrakoṭī \[Rudrakoṭi?\]) on the fourteenth day of the months of Āṣāḍha, Kārttika, Māgha and Caitra.

## \|\| 1.52.22 \|\|

*ājanmaśatasāhasraṃ kṛtvā pāpaṃ naraḥ kṣitau \|*  
*rudrāvartaṃ samālokya vipāpmatvaṃ prapadyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even after committing sins on the earth in the course of hundreds and thousands of births, a man shall be freed from those sins on viewing Rudrāvarta.

## \|\| 1.52.23 \|\|

*rudrāvartte naro gatvā dṛṣṭvā yogeśvaraṃ haram \|*  
*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ vipāpmā jāyate dhruvam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A man who goes to Rudrāvarta and views Hara, the Yogin Lord, on the fourteenth day in the bright half becomes certainly free from sins.”

## \|\| 1.52.24 \|\|

*yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ mahāyogipure dvijāḥ \|*  
*rudrāvarte sa cāpnoti phalaṃ śatamakhodbhavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Brāhmaṇas, one who performs Śrāddha at Rudrāvarta, the city of the great Yogin, obtains the merit of a hundred Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.52.25 \|\|

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā yaḥ kuryādrātrijāgaram \|*  
*kāmagena vimānena sa svarge yāti mānavaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A man who observes fast and keeps awake at night (i.e. performs Jāgaraṇa) goes to heaven in an aerial chariot that can go wherever one pleases.

## \|\| 1.52.26 \|\|

*tatra yaḥ kapilāṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye \|*  
*sa gaṇaḥ syānna saṃdeho harasya dayitastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One who gifts a tawny-coloured cow to a Brāhmaṇa who preserves the holy sacred Fires (Āhitāgni) shall undoubtedly become a Gaṇa and a favourite of Hara.

## \|\| 1.52.27 \|\|

*ṣaḍakṣaraṃ japedyastu mahāyogipuraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*maṃtraṃ tasya bhavecchreyaḥ ṣaṅguṇaṃ rājasūyataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If a devotee sits in front of the great Yogin and repeats the six-syllabled Mantra, he will get six times the merit of Rājasūya.

## \|\| 1.52.28 \|\|

*yastasya purato bhaktyā japedvā śatarudriyam \|*  
*caturṇāmapi vedānāṃ so'dhītānāṃ bhajetphalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who repeats Śatarudriya devoutly in front of the Lord, shall obtain the merit of reciting all the four Vedas.

## \|\| 1.52.29 \|\|

*gītaṃ vā yadi vā nṛtyaṃ tatpuraḥ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sa sarveṣāṃ bhajecchreyo makhānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A man who sings and/or dances in front of him (the Lord) shall undoubtedly obtain the merit of all Yajñas.”

## \|\| 1.52.30 \|\|

*evamuktvā dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sa munirbrahmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*virarāma tato hṛṣṭastīrthayātrāṃ gato drutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, after saying thus the sage horn of Brahmā (i.e. Nārada) stopped. Pleased much, he quickly proceeded on pilgrimage.

## Chapter 53 - Greatness of Bhrūṇagartā

## \|\| 1.53.1 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraivojjayanīpīṭhamasti kāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*prabhūtāścaryasaṃyuktaṃ bahusiddhaniṣevitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This chapter uses the legend of King Kalmāṣapāda in Mbh, Ādi, Chs. 175, 181, to glorify the Tīrtha called Bhrūṇa-Gartā.

Sūta said:

1\. There itself is Ujjayinī Pīṭha that grants whatever men desire. It is extremely miraculous and is resorted to by many Siddhas.

## \|\| 1.53.2 \|\|

*yasya madhyagato nityaṃ svayameva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*mahākālasvarūpeṇa sa tiṣṭhati dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Maheśvara himself is present in its centre in the form of Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.53.3-4 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāṃ yo narastatra kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ paśyati deveśaṃ mahākāla iti smṛtam \|*  
*pūjayeddakṣiṇāṃ mūrtiṃ samāśritya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*daśa pūrvāndaśātītānātmānaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*puruṣānsa samuddhṛtya śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. A man who has mental concentration and purity, who performs Śrāddha there on the Vaiśākhī day, who visits the Lord of Devas remembered as Mahākāla and who adores the Lord as Dakṣiṇāmurtī redeems ten generations of his ancestors, himself and ten generations of successors, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. He is honoured in Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.53.5-7 \|\|

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tatra pīṭhaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*saṃpūjya yoginīvṛṃdaṃ kanyakāvṛndameva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sa tatkṛtsnamavāpnoti yadapi syātsudurlabham \|*  
*tatra vaiśākhamāsasya paurṇamāsyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śraddhāyukto naro yo vā upavāsaparaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*karoti jāgaraṃ tasya purataḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-6a. After adoring the group of Yoginīs and the group of virgins, a devotee should worship the Pīṭha with any desire mentally conceived. He attains everything entirely even if it be very rare.

6b-7. A man who is endowed with faith, mental concentration and purity, remains physically clean and observes fast on the full-moon day of the month of Vaiśākha as well as keeps awake at night (i.e. performs Jāgaraṇa) in front of the deity faithfully, attains the greatest region devoid of old age and death.

## \|\| 1.53.8 \|\|

*kiṃ vrataiḥ kiṃ vṛthā dānaiḥ kiṃ japairniyamena vā \|*  
*mahākālasya te sarve kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Of what avail are Vratas? Of what worth are futile Dānas? Of what (more) advantage are Japas and observances? All these are not worth even a sixteenth fraction of (devotion to) Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.53.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraivāsti mahābhāgā bhrūṇagarteti viśrutā \|*  
*gartā suvipulākārā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9\. O highly esteemed ones, the holy chasm well known as Bhrūṇagartā is also there itself. It is very large in size and it destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.53.10 \|\|

*brahmahatyāvinirmuktaḥ saudāso yatra pārthivaḥ \|*  
*strīhatyayā vinirmuktaḥ suṣeṇo vasudhādhipaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. King Saudāsa was liberated from the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter at that place. Suṣeṇa, the overlord of the earth, was completely liberated from the sin of the murder of a woman.

## \|\| 1.53.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyā kathaṃ tasya saudāsasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇyasyāpi saṃjātā tadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 11 \|\|*

The sages said:

11\. How did that king Saudāsa who was a patron of Brāhmaṇas, incur the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter? Do narrate it to us.

## \|\| 1.53.12 \|\|

*śrūyate sa mahīpālo brāhmaṇānāṃ hite rataḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā brahmaghnaḥ so'bhavatkatham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is heard that the king was engaged in the welfare of Brāhmaṇas mentally, verbally and physically. How did he become a Brāhmaṇa-slayer?

## \|\| 1.53.13 \|\|

*vimuktaśca kathaṃ bhūyo bhrūṇagartāmupāśritaḥ \|*  
*sāpi gartā kathaṃ jātā sarvaṃ no vada vistarāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. How was he again liberated after resorting to Bhrūṇagartā? Further how did that Gartā (chasm) originate? Mention everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.53.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā liṃgasya pāto'bhūddevadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*tadā sa lajjayāviṣṭo liṃgābhāvāddvijottamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. When the penis of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas fell down, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he was overcome with shame due to the loss of the penis.

## \|\| 1.53.15 \|\|

*kṛtvā'tivipulāṃ gartāṃ praviveśa tataḥ param \|*  
*na kasyacittadātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa śūladhṛk \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He made a deep chasm and entered it. The Wielder of the Trident did not show himself to anyone.

## \|\| 1.53.16 \|\|

*evaṃ sā tatra saṃjātā gartā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*yathā tasyāṃ vipāpmābhūtsau dāsastadvadāmyaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that the chasm was formed there. I shall tell you now how Saudāsa became liberated from sin therein.

## \|\| 1.53.17 \|\|

*āsīnmitrasahonāma rājā paramadhārmikaḥ \|*  
*saudāsastatsutaḥ sākṣātsūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There was an extremely righteous king named Mitrasaha. Saudāsa was his son, a direct descendant of the solar race.

## \|\| 1.53.18 \|\|

*teneṣṭaṃ vipulairyajñaiḥ suvarṇavaradakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāni dānāni pradattāni mahātmanā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Elaborate Yajñas in which gold and other excellent things were gifted (as Dakṣiṇā) were performed by him. The great soul had performed numerous Dānas also.

## \|\| 1.53.19-20 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya satre dvādaśavārṣike \|*  
*vartamāne yathānyāyaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*krūrākṣaḥ krūrabuddhiśca rākṣasau balavattarau \|*  
*yajñavighnāya saṃprāptau saṃprāpte rajanīmukhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Once, while a Sattra lasting for a period of twelve years was going on duly in accordance with the procedure laid down in the scriptural injunctions, two very powerful Rākṣasas came there for creating obstacles in the Yajña. It was the beginning of the night.

## \|\| 1.53.21 \|\|

*rākṣasairbahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ tathānyairbhūtasaṃjñitaiḥ \|*  
*piśācaiśca durādharṣairyajñavidhvaṃsatatparaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They were also accompanied by many Rākṣasas, others called goblins and vampires who could not be assailed and who were eager to destroy the Yajña.

## \|\| 1.53.22 \|\|

*atha te rākṣasāḥ sarve kiṃcicchidramavekṣya ca \|*  
*viviśuryajñavāṭaṃ taṃ prasarpantaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Looking out for some opportunity and possible way of entry, all the Rākṣasas entered the sacrificial chamber and they spread all round.

## \|\| 1.53.23 \|\|

*nighnanto brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhānbhakṣayanto havīṃṣi ca \|*  
*tathā yāni vicitrāṇi yajñārthe kalpitāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They killed the Brāhmaṇas. They swallowed the holy Havis prepared there as well as other articles kept ready for the sake of Yajña.

## \|\| 1.53.24 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra hāhākāro mahānabhūt \|*  
*bhakṣyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu rākṣasairbalavattaraiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. While the Brāhmaṇas were being devoured by the more powerful Rākṣasas there was a great hue and cry.

## \|\| 1.53.25 \|\|

*tato maitrasahiḥ kruddhastyaktvā dīkṣāvrataṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ādāya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ dhvaṃsayāmāsa vīkṣya tān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thereupon the royal son of Mitrasaha became enraged. He set aside his initiation and holy vows and kept them in abeyance, took his bow and arrows and began killing them.

## \|\| 1.53.26 \|\|

*kṛtarakṣo vasiṣṭhena svayameva purodhasā \|*  
*krūrākṣaṃ sūdayāmāsa rākṣasairbahubhiḥ saha \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He himself was fully safeguarded by Vasiṣṭha, the priest. He slew Krūrākṣa along with many Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.53.27-28 \|\|

*krūrabuddhiratho vīkṣya hataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sahodaram \|*  
*taṃ ca pārthivaśārdūlamagamyaṃ brahmatejasā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*hataśeṣānsamādāya rākṣasānbalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*palāyanaṃ bhayāccakre kṣatāṃgastasya sāyakaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. On seeing that his excellent brother was killed and that the tiger among kings could not be approached due to the refulgence of the Brāhmaṇa, Krūrabuddhi took the surviving Rākṣasas and fled in great fright. Along with his soldiers, he too became wounded by his arrows.

## \|\| 1.53.29 \|\|

*tatastadvairamāśritya bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*chidramanveṣayāmāsa tadvadhāya divāniśam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Cherishing enmity due to the death of his elder brother, the demon looked out for an opportunity to kill him (the king), day and night.

## \|\| 1.53.30 \|\|

*evaṃ savīkṣamāṇasya tasya cchidraṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*samāptimagamadviprāḥ satraṃ taddvādaśābdikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even as vulnerable points of the noble-souled one were being watched, O Brāhmaṇas, the twelve-year long Sattra came to a close.

## \|\| 1.53.31 \|\|

*na sūkṣmamapi saṃprāptaṃ chidraṃ tena durātmanā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhavihitā rakṣā satre tasya mahīpateḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the course of the Sattra, due safeguard was accorded to the king by Vasiṣṭha and not even a smallest vulnerable point was seen by that wicked one.

## \|\| 1.53.32 \|\|

*athāsau brāhmaṇānsarvānvisṛjyāhitadakṣiṇān \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vasiṣṭhamidamabravīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then the king, after duly bidding farewell to the Brāhmaṇas after the due distribution of monetary gifts, spoke to Vasiṣṭha with the palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.53.33 \|\|

*svahastena gurodyāhaṃ tvāṃ bhojayitumutsahe \|*  
*kriyatāṃ tatprasādo me bhuktvādya mama mandire \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “O my venerable preceptor, I wish to feed you with my own hands. So be favourably disposed towards me and have food in my palace.”

## \|\| 1.53.34 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*kṣālitāṃghriḥ svayaṃ tena niviṣṭo bhojanāya vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sūta said:

34\. Vasiṣṭha, the excellent sage, assented saying “So be it.” The king washed the feet of the sage and sat down for the meal.

## \|\| 1.53.35 \|\|

*kūrabuddhiratho vīkṣya tadarthaṃ cāmiṣaṃ śubham \|*  
*susaṃskṛtaṃ vidhānena sūpakārairdvijottamāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Krūrabuddhi observed the splendid meat prepared duly by the cooks and then consecrated in accordance with the injunctions for the sake of the sage.

## \|\| 1.53.36 \|\|

*ukhāṃ kṛtvā tatastādṛktatpramāṇāmatarkitām \|*  
*mahāmāṃsābhṛtāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ jahārāmiṣānvitām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He made an ukhā i.e. a saucepan or vessel which can be put on fire. It was similar to and of the same dimension as the original (used by the king’s cook). He filled it with human flesh and served it as meat.

## \|\| 1.53.37 \|\|

*athāsau muniśārdūlo bhuṃjāno bubudhe hi tat \|*  
*mahāmāṃsamiti kruddhastatra provāca manyumān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The tiger among sages knew that the morsel he ate was human flesh. Enraged thereat, he said angrily:

## \|\| 1.53.38 \|\|

*mahāmāṃsāśanaṃ yasmātkārito'haṃ tvayādhama \|*  
*rakṣovadrākṣasastasmāttvamadyaiva bhaviṣyasi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “O base one, since you forced me to eat human flesh like a Rākṣasa, you shall just today itself become a Rākṣasa.”

## \|\| 1.53.39 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃśodhayāmāsa tasya māṃsasya cāgamam \|*  
*nipuṇaṃ sūpakārāṃstāndṛṣṭvā rājā pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The king met the cooks individually and tactfully tried to find out how human flesh had come therein.

## \|\| 1.53.40-41 \|\|

*te'bruvannaitadasmābhiḥ śrapitaṃ māṃsamīdṛśam \|*  
*śraddhīyatāṃ mahīpāla nānyena manujena vā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*rākṣasaṃ vā piśācaṃ vā dānavaṃ vā vinā vibho \|*  
*etajjñātvā tato nātha yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. The cooks said: “O king, such a piece of meat as this has not been cooked by us. Believe us. Nor could this have been done by another human being. O Lord, excepting a Rākṣasa, Piśāca or Dānava no one could have done this. Consider this, O Lord, and do what is proper.”

## \|\| 1.53.42 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*samāgatyābravītsarvaṃ tadrākṣasaviceṣṭitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In the meantime, Nārada, the excellent sage, came there and narrated everything perpetrated by the Rākṣasa.

## \|\| 1.53.43 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kopamāpannaḥ sa rājā śaptumudyataḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ svakare kṛtvā jalaṃ saudāsabhūpatiḥ \|*  
*śāpodyataṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārado vākyamabravīt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing it, King Saudāsa became furious. He took water in his hand and was about to curse Vasiṣṭha. On seeing him bent upon cursing, Nārada spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.53.44-45 \|\|

*nighnanto vā śapanto vā dviṣanto vā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*namaskāryā mahīpāla tathāpi svahitecchunā \|*  
*gurureṣa punarmānyastava pārthivasattama \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmānnārhasi śaptuṃ tvaṃ pratiśāpena sanmunim \|*  
*niṣiddhaḥ sa tathā bhūpastatastatsalilaṃ karāt \|*  
*pādayoḥ kṛtsnamupari pramumoca tataḥ param \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45a. “O excellent king, Brāhmaṇas have to be bowed down to by one who wishes for his own welfare even if they were to strike, hate or curse. Moreover, this is your preceptor and he has to be honoured by you. So, it does not behove you to curse the excellent sage in return.”

45b. Thus forbidden, the king let the entire quantity of water fall over his own feet from his hand.

## \|\| 1.53.46 \|\|

*atha tau caraṇau tasya tapta śāpodakaplutau \|*  
*dagdhau kṛṣṇatvamāpannau tatkṣaṇāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. His feet drenched with the water heated by the curse became burned. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they instantly turned black.

## \|\| 1.53.47 \|\|

*kalmāṣapāda ityuktastataḥprabhṛti sa kṣitau \|*  
*bhūpālo dvijaśārdūlā nā्mnā tena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Ever since then, O tiger among Brāhmaṇas, that king was specially called by the name Kalmāṣapāda.

## \|\| 1.53.48-51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare vipro vasiṣṭho lajjayānvitaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā dattaṃ vṛthā śāpaṃ tasya bhūmipatestadā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*uvāca vyarthaḥ śāpo'yaṃ tava datto mayā nṛpa \|*  
*na ca me jāyate vākyamasatyaṃ hi kathaṃcana \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ rākṣaso bhūtvā kañcitkālaṃ nṛpo ttama \|*  
*svarūpaṃ lapsyase bhūyo yasminkāle śṛṇuṣva tam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yadā tvaṃ krūrabuddhiṃ taṃ rākṣasaṃ nihaniṣyasi \|*  
*tadā tvaṃ lapsyase mokṣaṃ rākṣasatvātsudāruṇāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

48-51. In the meantime, Vasiṣṭha, the Brāhmaṇa, became ashamed on realizing that he had cursed the king unreasonably. He said: “O king, this curse had been given to you without any reason. But my words cannot be otherwise on any account. O excellent king, you will be a Rākṣasa for some time. Then you will regain your original form. Listen when it shall happen. When you kill a Rākṣasa named Krūrabuddhi you will get rid of the hideous state of Rākṣasa.”

## \|\| 1.53.52 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnantare rājā yātudhāno babhūva saḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvakeśo mahākāyaḥ kṛṣṇadanto bhayā nakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sūta said:

52\. In the meantime the king became a Yātudhāna (demon). He had a huge body with hairs standing upright. His teeth were black. He was awful altogether.

## \|\| 1.53.53 \|\|

*tato jaghāna viprendrānrākṣasaṃ bhāvamāśritaḥ \|*  
*yajñānvidhvaṃsayāmāsa munīnāmāśramānapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In this state of Rākṣasa he killed leading Brāhmaṇas and destroyed Yajñas and hermitages of sages.

## \|\| 1.53.54 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya krūra buddhiḥ sa rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā taṃ rākṣasībhūtamekadā'yudhavarjitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Once that Rākṣasa named Krūrabuddhi came to know that he had become a Rākṣasa himself and was without any weapon.

## \|\| 1.53.55 \|\|

*bhrāturvadhakṛtaṃ vairaṃ smaramāṇastataḥ param \|*  
*tadvadhārthaṃ samāyāto rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He recollected their previous enmity due to the slaying of his brother. Thereupon accompanied by many Rākṣasas he arrived there to kill him.

## \|\| 1.53.56 \|\|

*tatastaṃ veṣṭayitvāpi samaṃtādrākṣaso nṛpam \|*  
*provāca vacanaṃ kruddho nādenāpūrayandiśaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Encircling him all round, the Rākṣasa said to the king angrily as his loud roar was reverberating in all the quarters:

## \|\| 1.53.57 \|\|

*tvayā yo nihato'smākaṃ jyeṣṭho bhrātā sudurmate \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasya balādyajñe tasyādya phalamāpnuhi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. “O excessively wicked-minded one, our elder brother was killed by you by the strength derived from Vasiṣṭha in the course of the Yajña. Reap the fruit thereof now.”

## \|\| 1.53.58 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*yadbravīṣi durācāra karmaṇā tatsamācara \|*  
*śāradasyeva meghasya garjitaṃ tava niṣphalam \|\| 58 \|\|*

The king said:

58\. Only you of wicked behaviour, act according to what you say. Your roar, like the thunder of the autumnal cloud is futile.

## \|\| 1.53.59 \|\|

*evamuktvā samādāya tato vṛkṣaṃ sa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*prādravatsaṃmukhaṃ tasya garjamāno yathā ghanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. After saying thus the king uprooted a tree and with the tree he rushed towards him roaring like a rumbling cloud.

## \|\| 1.53.60 \|\|

*so'pi vṛkṣaṃ samutpāṭya krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*triśaṃkhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā tasyāpyabhimukhaṃ yayau \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He (Krūrabuddhi) too uprooted a tree. His eyes became red with rage. He knitted his eyebrows together into the shape of a trident and came face to face with him.

## \|\| 1.53.61 \|\|

*evaṃ dvāvapi tau śūrau vṛkṣayuddhaṃ mahābalau \|*  
*kṛtavantau vane tatra bahuvṛkṣakṣayāvaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus both of those mighty heroes continued this fight with trees resulting in the destruction of many trees.

## \|\| 1.53.62 \|\|

*atha taṃ śrāṃtamālokya kūrabuddhiṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*pragṛhya pādayorvegādbhrāmayāmāsa puṣkare \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Noticing that Krūrabuddhi had become tired the king caught him by the feet and whirled him quickly into the sky.

## \|\| 1.53.63 \|\|

*tataścāsphoṭayāmāsa bhūmau kopasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*cakre cāmiṣakhaṇḍaṃ sa piṣṭvāpiṣṭvā muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then with increased rage, he thrashed and dashed him on the ground. By pounding him repeatedly he turned him into a lump of flesh.

## \|\| 1.53.64 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu nihate śūre rākṣase sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*rākṣasatvādvinirmukto lebhe kāyaṃ nṛpodbhavam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. When the mighty Rākṣasa was killed the king got rid of the state of Rākṣasa and regained the physical form of a king.

## \|\| 1.53.65 \|\|

*tataste rākṣasāḥ śeṣāḥ samaṃtāttaṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*parivārya mahāvṛkṣairjaghnuḥ pāṣāṇavṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thereupon the remaining Rākṣasas surrounded him and struck him with huge trees and showers of stones and gravel..

## \|\| 1.53.66 \|\|

*tatastānapi bhūpālo jaghāna prahasanniva \|*  
*vṛkṣahastastu viśrabdho līlayā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, armed with a huge tree the king laughingly and easily killed them also with full confidence.

## \|\| 1.53.67 \|\|

*tataśca svapuraṃ prāptaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*rākṣasānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā labdhvā dehaṃ purātanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After killing the Rākṣasas and regaining his earlier body the king became delighted. He reached his city experiencing horripilation.

## \|\| 1.53.68-69 \|\|

*tatastaṃ tejasā hīnaṃ durgaṃdhena samāvṛtam \|*  
*brahmahatyodbhavaiścihnairanyairapi pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā te maṃtriṇastasya putra pautrāstathā pare \|*  
*nopasarpaṃti bhūpālaṃ pāpasparśabhayānvitāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Yet he was without the previous refulgence. He was stinking awfully. His ministers, sons, grandsons and others noticed these and various other sorts of signs of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. So they did not come near the king as if they were afraid of contracting his sins.

## \|\| 1.53.70-71 \|\|

*ūcuśca pārthivaśreṣṭha na tvamarhasi saṃgamam \|*  
*kartuṃ sārdhamihāsmābhirbrahmahatyā nvito yataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tasmādvasiṣṭhamāhūya prāyaścittaṃ samācara \|*  
*aśuddhaṃ śuddhimāyāti yena gātramidaṃ tava \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. They said: “O excellent king, since you have incurred the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter you do not deserve to come into close contact with us. Invite Vasiṣṭha and perform the rites of expiation whereby your impure body may regain purity.”

## \|\| 1.53.72 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivastūrṇaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ munipuṃgavam \|*  
*samāhūyābravīdvākyaṃ dūrastho vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereupon the king quickly called Vasiṣṭha, the leading sage, and spoke these words standing humbly at a safe distance:

## \|\| 1.53.73-75 \|\|

*tava prasādato vipra sa hato rākṣaso mayā \|*  
*muktaśāpo'smi saṃjātaḥ paraṃ śṛṇu vaco mune \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mama gātrātsudurgaṃdhaḥ samudgacchati sarvataḥ \|*  
*bhārākrāṃtāni gātrāṇi sarvāṇyevācalāni ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tatkimetaddvijaśreṣṭha tejo hāniratīva me \|*  
*maṃtriṇo'pi tathā putrā na spṛśaṃti yato'dya mām \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. “O Brāhmaṇa, that Rākṣasa has been killed by me with your favour. I have got rid of the curse too. But, O sage, listen further: Stinking odour emanates from my body and spreads around. All my limbs appear to be very heavy, benumbed and stiff. What is this, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. There is loss of refulgence. Why do the ministers and sons not even touch me today.”

## \|\| 1.53.76 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*rākṣasatvaṃ prapannena tvayā pārthivasattama \|*  
*brāhmaṇā bahavo dhvastāstathā vidhvaṃsitā makhāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tvaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha saṃspṛṣṭo brahmahatyayā \|\| 76 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

76\. O excellent king, many Brāhmaṇas were killed and Yajñas destroyed by you when in the state of Rākṣasa. Thus you have been assailed by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.53.77 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tadarthaṃ dehi me vipra prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*yena nirmuktapāpo'haṃ rājyaṃ prāpnomi cātmanaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

The king said:

77\. For that purpose, for the sake of purity, O Brāhmaṇa, tell me the requisite rite of expiation whereby I can be rid of sins and regain my own kingdom.

## \|\| 1.53.78 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*atrārthe tīrthayātrāṃ tvaṃ kuru pārthiva sattama \|*  
*nirmamo nirahaṃkārastataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 78 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

78\. For this purpose, O excellent king, undertake a pilgrimage free from egotism and sense of possession. Thereby you will attain fulfilment.

## \|\| 1.53.79 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivaśreṣṭhaḥ saṃyatātmā jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu snānaṃ cakre samā hitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thereafter, the great king practised self-control, conquered the sense-organs and performed the holy ablution in Prayāga and other Tīrthas with great mental concentration and purity.

## \|\| 1.53.80 \|\|

*na naśyati sa durgaṃdho na ca tejaḥ pravardhate \|*  
*na kāyo laghutāṃ yāti nālasyena vimucyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Still the stinking odour did not disappear; his refulgence did not increase, the body did not regain lightness and he was not rid of sluggishness.

## \|\| 1.53.81 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃbhramamāṇaśca kadāci ddvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre snānārthaṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Roaming about still further, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, once he happened to come to the holy place of Camatkārapura for the purpose of holy bath.

## \|\| 1.53.82 \|\|

*suśrāṃtaḥ kṣutpipāsārto niśīthe tamasāvṛte \|*  
*gartāyāṃ patito'kasmātpūrṇāyāṃ payasā nṛpaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The king was already weak and tired. He was distressed due to hunger and thirst. At midnight, in pitch darkness, he slipped down into a Gartā (pit) full of water.

## \|\| 1.53.83 \|\|

*kṛcchrāttato viniṣkrāṃtastīrthāttasmānmahīpatiḥ \|*  
*yāvatpaśyati cātmānaṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. With very great difficulty the king came out of that Tīrtha. When he looked at himself, he found that he had the lustre of twelve suns.

## \|\| 1.53.84 \|\|

*durgaṃdhena parityaktaṃ sodyamaṃ laghutāṃ gatam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca ciṃtayāmāsa nūnaṃ mukto'smi pātakāt \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On seeing himself bereft of the stinking smell, with the body light and active, he thought that he had become rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.53.85 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*harṣayantī mahīpālaṃ vimuktaṃ brahmahatyayā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. At the very same time, there was heard an unembodied voice delighting the king rid of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.53.86-90 \|\|

*vimukto'si mahārāja sāṃprataṃ pūrvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*tīrthasyāsya prabhāvena tasmādgaccha nijaṃ gṛham \|\| 86 \|\|*

*atra saṃnihito nityaṃ bhrūṇarūpeṇa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe viśeṣeṇa caturdaśyāṃ mahīpate \|\| 87 \|\|*

*yadā prapatitaṃ liṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*dvijaśāpena gartaiṣā tadānena vinirmitā \|\| 88 \|\|*

*lajjitena svavāsārthaṃ mahadduḥkhayutena ca \|*  
*satīviyogayuktena bhrūṇatvaṃ pragatena ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaharā tena garteyaṃ pṛthi vīpate \|*  
*bhrūṇagarteti vikhyātā tasya nāmā jagattraye \|\| 90 \|\|*

86-90. “O great king, by the power of this Tīrtha you are now relieved of all your previous sins. So do go back to your abode. Śaṅkara is always present here in the form of a Bhrūṇa (a very young child), O king, particularly on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half. When the penis of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas fell down due to the curse of Brāhmaṇas, he made this Gartā. He had become ashamed of the state of Bhrūṇa. He was very distressed due to separation from Satī. Therefore, O king, this Gartā is destructive of all sins. Named after the Lord (in the form of a Bhrūṇa) this Gartā became well known as Bhrūṇagartā in all the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.53.91 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha sā vāṇī virarāmāṃ'tarikṣagā \|*  
*so'pi pārthivaśārdūlaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ svapuraṃ yayau \|\| 91 \|\|*

Sūta said:

91\. After saying thus, that aerial voice stopped. That tiger among kings joyously went to his city.

## \|\| 1.53.92 \|\|

*tatastaṃ pāpanirmuktaṃ tejasā bhāskaropamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā putrāstathā martyāḥ praṇemustuṣṭisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. On seeing him freed from sins and appearing like the sun in refulgence, the sons and other men became delighted and bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.53.93 \|\|

*so'pi brāhmaṇaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhastaṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*samabhyetya tataḥ prāha harṣagadgadayā girā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Vasiṣṭha, a tiger among Brāhmaṇas approached the king and said with a voice choked due to delight:

## \|\| 1.53.94-95 \|\|

*diṣṭyā muktosi rājeṃdra pāpādbrahmavadhodbhavāt \|*  
*diṣṭyā tvaṃ tejasā yuktaḥ punaḥ prāpto nijaṃ puram \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tasmātkīrtaya bhūpāla kasmiṃstīrthe samāgataḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ muktaḥ pātakādghorādbrahmahatyāsamudbhavāt \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. “O leading king, luckily you have been relieved of the terrible sins arising from Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. Fortunately you have come again to your city with the full complement of your original radiance. Hence do say, O king, which Tīrtha did you go to and get relief from the terrible sin arising from Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.”

## \|\| 1.53.96 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa bhrūṇagartāsamudbhavam \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ tasya viprarṣeranubhūtaṃ yathā tathā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Thereupon he narrated all the events of the Bhrūṇagartā to the Brāhmaṇa-Sage in the manner he experienced.

## \|\| 1.53.97-98 \|\|

*tataste maṃtriṇo vṛddhāḥ sa ca rājā munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*putraṃ pratardanaṃnāma rājye saṃsthāpya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 97 \|\|*

*bhrūṇagartāṃ samāsādya tāmeva dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tapaścerurmahādevaṃ dhyāyamānā divā niśam \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. Thereupon the elderly ministers, the king and the leading sage crowned the son named Pratardana in the kingdom. Instantly they went to Bhrūṇagartā, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and performed penance meditating on Mahādeva day and night.

## \|\| 1.53.99 \|\|

*gatāśca paramāṃ siddhiṃ kālenālpena durlabhām \|*  
*bhrūṇarūpadharaṃ devaṃ pūjayitvā maheśvaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. By worshipping Maheśvara in the form of a Bhrūṇa, they attained the greatest Siddhi in a short time, though it is very difficult to be obtained.

## \|\| 1.53.100 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti sā gartā prakhyātā dharaṇītale \|*  
*bhrūṇagarteti vipreṃdrāḥ sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Ever since then, O leading Brāhmaṇas, that Gartā became well known over the earth as Bhrūṇagartā, which destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.53.101 \|\|

*tatra kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sa pitṝṃstārayennūnaṃ daśa pūrvāndaśā parān \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. A man who performs Śrāddha there on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of a month redeems ten ancestors and ten successors in his family.

## \|\| 1.53.102 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra śrāddhaṃ samācaret \|*  
*snānaṃ ca brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā dānaṃ vāpi svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, one should perform Śrāddha, Snāna (holy bath) and Dāna there in accordance with one’s capacity.

## Chapter 54 - Greatness of Carmamuṇḍā

## \|\| 1.54.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*carmamuṃḍā tathā devī tasminsthāne vyavasthitā \|*  
*nalena sthāpitā pūrvaṃ svayameva mahātmanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*abhyarcayati tāṃ bhaktyā yo mahānavamī dine \|*  
*sa kāmānvāṃchitāṃllabdhvā padaṃ prāpnoti śāśvatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: The Nala episode follows the Mbh story in general except verses 16-33 which are meant for the glorification of Carmamuṇḍā.

Sūtía said:

1-2. Goddess Carmamuṇḍā is also established in that holy spot. She was formerly installed by the noble-souled Nala himself.

One who devoutly worships her on the day of Mahānavamī (ninth day in the month of Āśvina) obtains desired benefits and attains the eternal state (i.e. Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.54.3 \|\|

*vīrasenasutaḥ pūrvaṃ nalonāma mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*āsītsarvaguṇopetaḥ sarva śatrukṣayāvahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly there was a king named Nala. He was the son of Vīrasena. He was endowed with all good qualities. He brought about the destruction of all enemies.

## \|\| 1.54.4 \|\|

*bhāryā tasyābhavatsādhvī prāṇebhyopi garīyasī \|*  
*damayaṃtīti vikhyātā vidarbhādhipateḥ sutā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. His wife was a chaste lady well-known as Damayantī. She was dearer to him than his own life. She was the daughter of the king of Vidarbha.

## \|\| 1.54.5 \|\|

*athāsau kalināviṣṭo dyūtaṃ cakre mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*puṣkareṇa samaṃ viprā dāyādena divāniśam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Brāhmaṇas, haunted by Kali, the king played the game of dice day and night with Puṣkara, his Dāyāda (kinsman).

## \|\| 1.54.6 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vyasanāsakto vāryamāṇo'pi sajjanaiḥ \|*  
*hārayāmāsa saptāṃgaṃ rājyaṃ muktvā ca tāṃ priyām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He indulged in this vice though forbidden by good people. He lost the entire kingdom consisting of seven Aṅgas, (constituent units such as arms) excepting his beloved.

## \|\| 1.54.7 \|\|

*atha tāṃ sa samādāya praviṣṭo gahanaṃ vanam \|*  
*nirjalaṃ lajjayāviṣṭo duḥkhavyākuliteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Taking her with him he entered a forest devoid of people. He was overwhelmed with shame and utterly distressed with grief.

## \|\| 1.54.8-10 \|\|

*tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa yadyeṣā bhīmamaṃdire \|*  
*yāti tanmucyate kaṣṭādvanavāsasamudbhavāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*na mayā tatra gaṃtavyaṃ kathaṃcidapi māninā \|*  
*tasmādenāṃ parityajya rātrau gacchāmi dūrataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yena tyaktā mayā sādhvī kuṇḍinaṃ yāti tatpuram \|*  
*sa evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā sukhasuptāṃ vihāya tām \|*  
*prajagāma vanaṃ ghoraṃ vanyaśvāpadasaṃkulam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Thereupon he thought: ‘If this gentle lady goes to the palace of Bhīma (her father), she can be relieved of painful sufferings due to the stay in the forest.

I have to maintain my prestige. So I should not go there at any cost. So I shall desert her at night and go very far. Abandoned by me, the chaste lady will go to his city Kuṇḍina.’

After deciding thus, he left her during sound sleep and went deep into the terrible forest infested by wild beasts of prey.

## \|\| 1.54.11 \|\|

*pratyūṣe cāpi sotthāya yāvatpaśyati bhābhinī \|*  
*tāvatpaśyatiśūnyaṃ svaṃ pārśvaṃ yatra nalaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Early in the morning, the lovely woman got up but found a void in the place where Nala had been before at her side.

## \|\| 1.54.12 \|\|

*tato vilapya duḥkhārtā karuṇaṃ tatra kānane \|*  
*jagāma mārgamāśrittha piturharmyaṃ śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Distressed with misery, she lamented piteously in the forest. She slowly proceeded ahead along the path and reached the palace of her father.

## \|\| 1.54.13 \|\|

*nalo'pi ca vane tasminbhramamāṇo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*ekākī vṛkṣakuṃjāni sevayāmāsa sarvadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. King Nala roamed alone all over the forest always resorting to clusters of trees and bushes.

## \|\| 1.54.14 \|\|

*tatastadvanamutsṛjya jagāmānyanmahāvanam \|*  
*nānāvṛkṣagaṇairyuktaṃ bahuśvāpadasaṃkulam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then he left that forest and went to another great forest full of trees of various kinds and infested with many beasts of prey.

## \|\| 1.54.15 \|\|

*evaṃ sa pṛthivīpālo bhramamāṇovanādvanam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetramāsasāda tataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Roaming thus from forest to forest, the king ultimately reached the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.54.16 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptaṃ tanmahānavamīdinam \|*  
*viśeṣādyatra bhūpālāḥ pūjayanti sureśvarīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the meantime there occurred the advent of that great Navamī day (ninth day) when kings perform special adoration of the goddesss of Suras.

## \|\| 1.54.17 \|\|

*tataḥ sa mṛnmayīṃ kṛtvā carmamuṇḍadharāṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*vibhavābhāvataḥ paścātphalamūlairatarpayat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The king made a clay icon of Carmamuṇḍadharā. Thereafter improverished that he was, be propitiated the goddess with fruits and roots.

## \|\| 1.54.18 \|\|

*tatastasyāḥ stutiṃ kṛtvā puraḥ sthitvā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yukto niṣadhādhipatiḥ svayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The king of Niṣadha endowed with great faith stood before the goddess with palms joined in reverence and eulogized.

Prayer of Carmamuṇḍā;

## \|\| 1.54.19 \|\|

*jaya sarvagate devi carmamuṇḍadhare vare \|*  
*jaya daityakulocchedadakṣe dakṣātmaje śubhe \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “Be victorious, O omnipresent goddess, O excellent Carmamuṇḍadharā. Be victorious, O splendid daughter of Dakṣa, efficient in the annihilation of the race of demons.

## \|\| 1.54.20 \|\|

*kālarātri jayācintye navamyaṣṭamivallabhe \|*  
*trinetre tryaṃbakābhīṣṭe jaya devi surārcite \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Be victorious, O Kālarātri, O incomprehensible one, O goddess fond of Navamī and Aṣṭamī (9th and 8th lunar days). O three-eyed one, O beloved of the Three-eyed One. Be victorious, O goddess adored by Suras.

## \|\| 1.54.21 \|\|

*bhīmarūpe surūpe ca mahāvidye mahābale \|*  
*mahodaye mahākāye jayadevi mahāvrate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O terrible one, O beautiful one, O great deity of learning of great power, O goddess of huge body and great prosperity. Be victorious, O goddess of great Vratas.

## \|\| 1.54.22 \|\|

*nityarūpe jagaddhātri surāmāṃsavasāpriye \|*  
*vikarāli mahākāli jaya pretajanānuge \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O mother of the universe, of permanent form, O goddess fond of liquor and meat and suet! O Mahākāll of hideous form, be victorious, O goddess with Pretas as followers.

## \|\| 1.54.23 \|\|

*śavayānarate ramye bhujaṃgābharaṇānvite \|*  
*pāśahaste mahāhaste rudhiraughakṛtāspade \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O beautiful goddess fond of corpse as vehicle. O goddess with serpents for ornaments! O goddess of huge hands armed with the noose, O goddess having flood of blood made as the place of residence.

## \|\| 1.54.24 \|\|

*phetkārā ravaśobhiṣṭhe gītavādyavirājite \|*  
*jayānādye jaya dhyeye bhargadehārdhasaṃśraye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O goddess splendidly shining with shouts and howls! O goddess shining with music of instruments and songs. Be victorious, O goddess without beginning. Be victorious, O goddess worthy of meditation, O goddess resorting to a half of the body of Bharga (Śiva).

## \|\| 1.54.25 \|\|

*tvaṃ ratistvaṃ dhṛtistuṣṭistvaṃ gaurī tvaṃ sureśvarī \|*  
*tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ ca sāvitrī gāyatrī tvamasaṃśayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Undoubtedly you are Rati, you are Dhṛti (fortitude), you are Tuṣṭi (satisfaction) O Gaurī; you are the goddess of Suras. You are Lakṣmī; you are Sāvitrī and Gāyatrī.

## \|\| 1.54.26 \|\|

*yatkiṃcittriṣu lokeṣu strīrūpaṃ devi dṛśyate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ tvanmayaṃ nātra vikalpo'sti mama kvacit \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O goddess, whatever is seen in the three worlds in female form is identical with you. Here I have no doubt at all.

## \|\| 1.54.27 \|\|

*yena satyena tena tvamatrāvāsaṃ drutaṃ kuru \|*  
*sānnidhyaṃ bhaktitastuṣṭā surāsuranamaskṛte \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On the basis of that truth whereby I believe so you shall be present here quickly. O goddess bowed down to by Suras and Asuras, pleased with my devotion, be present here.”

## \|\| 1.54.28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutā ca sā devī nalena pṛthivībhujā \|*  
*provāca darśanaṃ gatvā taṃ nṛpaṃ bhaktavatsalā \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sūta said:

28\. On being eulogized thus by King Nala, the goddess fond of her devotees appeared before him and said to him:

## \|\| 1.54.29 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭā'smi te vatsa stotreṇānena sāṃpratam \|*  
*tasmādgṛhāṇa mattastvaṃ varaṃ manasi saṃsthitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

29\. O my dear one, I am now pleased with this prayer of yours. So receive from me anything you desire as a boon.

## \|\| 1.54.30 \|\|

*nala uvāca \|*  
*damayantīti me bhāryā prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*sā mayā nirjane muktā \|*  
*vane vyālagaṇānvite \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nala said:

30\. Damayantī is my wife. She is dearer to me, more than my life. She has been deserted by me in a desolate forest infested by tigers and serpents.

## \|\| 1.54.31 \|\|

*akhaṇḍaśīlāṃ nirdoṣāṃ yathāhaṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|*  
*labhe bhūyo'pi tāṃ devi tathātra kuru satvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O goddess, immediately see to this that I regain her. She is faultless and is never cross at me. She cannot be called unchaste. With your favour, I shall get her again.

## \|\| 1.54.32 \|\|

*stotreṇānena yo devi stutiṃ kuryātpurastava \|*  
*tatraiva divase tasmai tvayā deyaṃ manogatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O goddess, if anyone were to pray to you reciting this hymn and standing before you, you must grant his wish on that day itself.

## \|\| 1.54.33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā tatheti pratijñāya jagāmādarśanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*so'pi pārthivaśārdūlo lebhe sarvaṃ tayoditam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sūta said:

33\. Saying “So be it” she vanished. The tiger among kings obtained everything mentioned by her.

## Chapter 55 - Greatness of Naleśvara (Nala-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.55.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyā eva samīpasthaṃ devadevaṃ naleśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā vimucyute pāpātsthāpitaṃ nalabhūbhujā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. The deity known as Naleśvara is near the shrine of Carmamuṇḍā. He was installed by Nala. By visiting Naleśvara, the Lord of Devas one is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 1.55.2 \|\|

*yastaṃ paśyennaro bhaktyā māghe ṣaṣṭhyāṃ site dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarva rogavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A man who visits the Lord on the sixth lunar day in the bright half of Māgha, O Brāhmaṇas, shall be free from all ailments and attain the highest status.

## \|\| 1.55.3 \|\|

*kaṇḍūḥ pāmātha dadrūṇi maṃḍalāni vicarcikā \|*  
*darśanāttasya naśyanti jantūnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Itching sensation, scab, herpes and cutaneous eruptions, leprosy with round spots-all these are cured in the case of creatures of purified souls.

## \|\| 1.55.4 \|\|

*asti tasyāgrataḥ kuṇḍaṃ svacchodakasupūritam \|*  
*matsyakūrmasamākīrṇaṃ padminīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It front of it there is a holy Kuṇḍa filled with clear water. It is adorned with clusters of lotuses and the holy pit is full of fishes and turtles.

## \|\| 1.55.5 \|\|

*yastatra kurute snānaṃ pratyūṣe somavāsare \|*  
*api kuṣṭhāmayamastaḥ sa bhūyaḥ syātpunarnavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even if one is afflicted by the fell disease of leprosy, one shall become fresh (and handsome) once again by taking the holy bath there at dawn on a Monday.

## \|\| 1.55.6 \|\|

*yadā saṃsthāpitaḥ śaṃbhurnalena pṛthivībhujā \|*  
*tadā tuṣṭena sa prokto brūhi kiṃ te karomyaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When Śaṃbhu was installed by King Nala, the Lord was pleased and he said to him, Tell me what shall I do for you?”

## \|\| 1.55.7 \|\|

*nala uvāca \|*  
*atra stheyaṃ tvayā deva sadā sannihitena ca \|*  
*sarvalokahitārthāya roganāśāya śaṃkara \|\| 7 \|\|*

Nāla said:

7\. O Lord Śaṅkara, you should stay here. You shall be present here always for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds and for the destruction (healing) of sickness.

## \|\| 1.55.8 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tvadvacanādrājansaṃprāpte somavāsare \|*  
*pratyūṣe ca nivatsyāmi prāsāde nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

8\. O king, at dawn on any Monday, I shall be here within the palace at your request. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.55.9 \|\|

*māghāṣṭamyāmahorātraṃ sakalaṃ ca mahīpate \|*  
*prāṇināṃ roganāśāya śuklapakṣe viśeṣataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O king, throughout the day and night on the eighth lunar day in the month of Māgha, especially in the bright half, I will be present here for the eradication of ailments of living beings.

## \|\| 1.55.10 \|\|

*yo māmatra sthitaṃ tatra divase vīkṣayiṣyati \|*  
*snātvā suvimale kuṃḍe samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tasya nāśaṃ prayāsyaṃti vyādhayo gātrasaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If a devotee takes his holy bath in the pure holy Kuṇḍa and sees me stationed here on that day with excellent ardour and faith, all the ailments of his body will perish.

## \|\| 1.55.11 \|\|

*yo'sya kuṃḍasya saṃbhūtāṃ mṛttikāmapi mānavaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhāsyati nije dehe somavāre niśākṣaye \|*  
*so'pi rogairvinirmuktaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati puṣṭimān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A man who takes the clay our of this Kuṇḍa and applies it over his body in the morning on Monday, shall become free from ailments. He will be strong too.

## \|\| 1.55.12 \|\|

*niṣkāmastu punaryo māṃ tasminkāle nṛpottama \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati sadbhaktyā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto mama lokaṃ sa yāsyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O excellent king, a man without any personal desire who worships me devoutly at that time with flowers, incense and unguents shall be rid of all sins. He will attain my world.

## \|\| 1.55.13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstrailokyadīpako haraḥ \|*  
*antardhānaṃ gato viprā yathā dīpo'tra tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sūta said:

13\. O Brāhmaṇas, after saying thus, Lord Hara, the illuminator of all the three worlds, vanished instantly like a lamp.

## \|\| 1.55.14-16 \|\|

*nalo'pi tuṣṭimāpannastamārādhya ciraṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tadāhūyākhilānviprāṃścamatkārapurodbhavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*eṣa saṃsthāpitaḥ śaṃbhurmayā yuṣmatpuroṃtike \|*  
*yena dṛṣṭena rogāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*adhunāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi svarājyāya kṛte dvijāḥ \|*  
*niṣadhāṃ ca purīmeṣa sarvaiḥ pūjyaḥ samāhitaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Nala too became satisfied, The king propitiated the Lord for a long time. Then he invited all the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura and said: “This deity Śaṃbhu has been installed by me very near your city. By visiting this Lord, all the ailments shall be destroyed.
