O Brāhmaṇas, I shall now go to the city of Niṣadha (modern Narwar, Rajasthan) for ruling over my kingdom. This deity should be adored by all with mental concentration and purity.”

## \|\| 1.55.17-18 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*evaṃ pārthivaśārdūla kariṣyāmaḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*tava devakṛte yatnaṃ yātrādyāsu kriyāsu ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tathā pūjāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ putrapautrā ye bhaviṣyaṃti tathā pare \|*  
*vaṃśajāste kariṣyaṃti pūjāmasya subhaktitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

17-18. O tiger among kings, we shall do so with mental concentration and purity. Our sons and grandsons and others too yet to be born in our family shall devoutly perform his adoration. In such rites as religious procession etc., for the deity installed by you and his adoration we shall make all efforts to carry them out.

## \|\| 1.55.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa bhūpālastairvipraistuṣṭisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pratasthe tānpraṇamyoccaiḥ sarvaistaiścābhinaṃditaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. On being told thus by those Brāhmaṇas the king became delighted. He was congratulated by them in loud voice. He bowed down to them and set off.

## \|\| 1.55.20 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavāñchaṃbhustasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokānāṃ sarvarogakṣayāvahaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It was thus that Lord Saṃbhu became established there for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds. He is the destroyer of all ailments.

## \|\| 1.55.21 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena vīkṣaṇīyaḥ sadā hi saḥ \|*  
*viśeṣātsomavāreṇa śāśvataṃ śreya icchatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence with all effort the Lord should be visited especially on Mondays by one who wishes for permanent weal.

## Chapter 56 - Greatness of Sāṃbāditya

## \|\| 1.56.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyāpi nātidūrasthaṃ sāṃbādityaṃ sureśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kāmānavāpnoti sarvānmartyo hṛdi sthitān \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yastu māghasya śuklāyāṃ saptamyāṃ ravivāsare \|*  
*bhaktyā saṃpaśyate martyo narakānna sa paśyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: The name of the deity (i.e., Sāṃbāditya) is later explained in verse 13. This has no relation to Kṛṣṇa’ son Sāmba, a devotee of the Sun-god.

1-2. By seeing the Lord of Suras named Sāṃbāditya who is not far from the previous shrine, a man obtains all the desires cherished in his heart.

A man who devoutly visits the deity on the seventh lunar day in the bright half of Māgha and on a Sunday, will never see hells.

## \|\| 1.56.3 \|\|

*āsītpūrvaṃ dvijo nāma gālavaḥ sa mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyanirato nityaṃ vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly there was a Brāhmaṇa named Gālava. That great sage was always engaged in the self-study of the Vedas. He was a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.56.4 \|\|

*śucivrataparaḥ śāṃto devadvijaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛtajñaśca suśīlaśca yajñakarmavicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was devoted to excellent holy vows. He was quiescent. He was engaged in serving gods and Brāhmaṇas. He was well-behaved and grateful. He was an adept in the sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 1.56.5 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya saṃprāptaṃ paścimaṃ vayaḥ \|*  
*aputrasya dvijaśreṣṭhāstato duḥkhaṃ vyajāyata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus he continued till he attained very old age. It was then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that he fuly experienced the misery of being without a son.

## \|\| 1.56.6 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvaṃ parityajya gṛhakṛtyaṃ sa bhaktimān \|*  
*sūryamārādhayāmāsa kṣetre'traiva samāhitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Therefore, he left all domestic activities, and in this very holy spot he devoutly propitiated the Sun-god with mental concentration and purity.

## \|\| 1.56.7 \|\|

*vaṭavṛkṣaṃ samāśritya śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*sthāpayitvā raverarcāṃ yathoktāṃ paṃcarātrike \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Equipped with great ardour and faith, he installed the image of the Sun-god at the foot of a banyan tree as mentioned in the Pañcarātrika scriptures.

## \|\| 1.56.8 \|\|

*varṣāsvākāśaśāyī ca hemaṃte jalasaṃśrayaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāgnisādhako grīṣme nirāhāro jitendriyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He abstained from taking food and kept his sense-organs under his control. During rainy season he stood under the open sky. During winter he remained in water and during summer he practised penance standing in the midst of five fires.

## \|\| 1.56.9 \|\|

*tataḥ paṃcadaśe varṣe saṃprāpte bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*vaṭavṛkṣaṃ samāśritya samīpasthamuvāca tam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When the fifteenth year approached the Sun-god appeared on the banyan tree and spoke to him as he stood nearby.

## \|\| 1.56.10 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*varadosmyadya bhadraṃ te varaṃ prārthaya gālava \|*  
*atidurlabhamapyāśu tava dāsyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śrī Sūrya said:

10\. Welfare unto you, O Gālava. Today I shall bestow boons on you. Do request for a boon. Even if it be very difficult to get, I shall undoubtedly grant it to you.

## \|\| 1.56.11 \|\|

*gālava uvāca \|*  
*aputro'haṃ suraśreṣṭha paścime vayasi sthitaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddehi sutaṃ mahyaṃ vaṃśavṛddhikaraṃ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

Gālava said:

11\. O excellent one among the Suras, I am without a son and I have reached old age. Hence bestow on me a son who will make the family flourish (and continue it).

## \|\| 1.56.12 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*vaṃśavṛddhikaro vipra putrastava bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tejasvī ca yaśasvī ca śāstrajño veda pāragaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Śrī Sūtya said:

12\. O Brāhmaṇa, your son will make the family flourish. He shall be brilliant, renowned, well-versed in scriptural texts and a master of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.56.15 \|\|

*saptamyaśca dvijaśreṣṭha nirāhārastu bhaktitaḥ yā \|*  
*sa prāpsyati na saṃdehaḥ putraṃ vaṃśavivardhanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The image made by you in the vicinity of the Sun-god along with the goddess (Sa-ambā) shall become well-known on the earth by the name Sāmbasūrya.

## \|\| 1.56.14-15 \|\|

*anyo'pi śradrayopeto ya enaṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa yāvaddvādaśa bhāskarāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saptamyaśca dvijaśreṣṭha nirāhārastu bhaktitaḥ yā \|*  
*sa prāpsyati na saṃdehaḥ putraṃ vaṃśavivardhanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A person who is endowed with ardent faith and abstains from food and devoutly worships the deity for twelve Saptamīs (seventh lunar days) coinciding with Sundays, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, shall undoubtedly obtain a son furthering the prosperity of the family.

## \|\| 1.56.16 \|\|

*evamuktvā ca saptāśvo virarāma divākaraḥ \|*  
*gālavo'pi prahṛṣṭātmā jagāma nijamaṃdiram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After saying thus the Seven-horsed Lord, Sun, stopped. Delighted in his mind Gālava went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.56.17 \|\|

*nātidīrgheṇa kālena tatastasyābhava tatsutaḥ \|*  
*yathoktastena devena sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Not long thereafter a son marked with all characteristic features, as mentioned by the Lord, was born to him.

## \|\| 1.56.18 \|\|

*tataścakre pitā nāma vaṭeśvara iti svayam \|*  
*vaṭasthena yato dattaḥ saṃtuṣṭenāṃśumālinā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Since the son had been granted by the delighted Sun-god appearing on the banyan tree, the father himself gave the name Vaṭeśvara to the son.

## \|\| 1.56.19 \|\|

*vaṭeśvarasutāndṛṣṭvā pautrāṃśca dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*gālavaḥ sūryamāpannaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Gālava saw the sons of Vaṭeśvara, his grandsons, performed very elaborate penance and attained identity with the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.56.20 \|\|

*vaṭeśvaro'pi saṃjñāya pitrā saṃsthāpitaṃ ravim \|*  
*tadarthaṃ kārayāmāsa prāsādaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After realizing that the Sun-god was installed by his father, Vaṭeśvara erected a charming mansion for him.

## \|\| 1.56.21 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti loke ca sa vaṭādityasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*putraprado hyaputrāṇāṃ vikhyāto bhuvanatraye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Ever since then, that deity named Vaṭāditya became well-known all over the three worlds as the bestower of sons on those without them.

## \|\| 1.56.22 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā saptarmārdvādaśa kramāt \|*  
*sa prāpnoti sutaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ svavaṃśasya vivardhanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person engaged in observing fasts, who worships the deity faithfully for twelve Saptamīs coinciding with Sundays (or/ and twelve Sundays) in the proper order shall obtain an excellent son making his family prosper and flourish (in progeny).

## \|\| 1.56.23 \|\|

*niṣkāmo vā naro yastu taṃ pūjayati mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa mokṣamāpnuyānnūnaṃ durlabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A man who has no desire and who adores the deity devoutly, shall certainly obtain salvation rarely obtained by even gods.

## \|\| 1.56.24 \|\|

*atha gāthā purā gītā nāradena surarṣiṇā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā putrapradaṃ devaṃ vaṭādityaṃ sureśvaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then there is a couple of verses sung by Nārada, the celestial sage, after visiting Vaṭāditya, the Lord of Suras and bestower of sons:

## \|\| 1.56.25 \|\|

*api varṣaśatā nārī vaṃdhyā vā durbhagāpi vā \|*  
*sāṃbasūryaprasādena sadyo garbhavatī bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “Even if a woman is hundred years old, barren or widow, she will quickly conceive with the favour of Sāṃbasūrya.

## \|\| 1.56.26 \|\|

*kiṃ dānaiḥ kiṃ vratairdhyānaiḥ kiṃ japaiḥ sopavāsakaiḥ \|*  
*putrārthaṃ vidyamāne'tha sāṃbasūrye sureśvare \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Of what avail is Dāna, Vrata, Japa and fast for the sake of sons when Sāṃbasūrya, the Lord of Suras, is present?

## \|\| 1.56.27 \|\|

*varṣamekaṃ naro bhaktyā yaḥ paśyetsūryavāsare \|*  
*kṛtakṣaṇo'tra putraṃ sa labhate cottamaṃ sukham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A man who makes it convenient to stay in the holy spot for a year and devoutly visits the deity on Sundays, shall easily obtain an excellent son”.

## \|\| 1.56.28 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena taṃ devaṃ yatnato dvijāḥ \|*  
*paśyedātmahitārthāya svavaṃśaparivṛddhaye \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of one’s own weal and for prosperity and growth of one’s own family, a devotee should assiduously visit the Lord.

## Chapter 57 - Bhīṣma’s Pilgrimage

## \|\| 1.57.1 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasminkṣetre tathādityaḥ sthāpito dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmeṇa brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ saṃmatena tathātmanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The aim of this chapter is to glorify ablution in Śarmiṣṭhā Tīrtha at Camatkārapura on Aṅgārakī Ṣaṣṭhī (6th lunar day on Tuesday).

Sūta said:

1\. Further, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Sun-god was installed in that holy spot by Bhīṣma himself honoured by leading Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.57.2 \|\|

*śaṃtanordayitaḥ putro gāṃgeya iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*āsītpurā varo nṛṇāmūrdhvaretāḥ suviśrutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly there was a well-known dear son of Śāntanu by the name Gāṅgeya. He was the most excellent one among men. He was reputed as Ūrdhvaretas (one whose semen goes upwards instead of downwards in the form of discharge i.e. a celibate man).

## \|\| 1.57.3 \|\|

*tasyāsīttumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhārgaveṇa samaṃ mahat \|*  
*trayoviṃśaddinānyeva devāsuraraṇopamam \|*  
*aṃbākṛte śitaiḥ śastrairastraiśca tadanaṃtaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A fierce fight has taken place between him and Bhārgava for a period of twenty-three days. It could be well compared with the fight between Devas and Asuras. It was with reference to Aṃbā (Princess of Kāśī) that they fought with sharp weapons and arrows.

## \|\| 1.57.4 \|\|

*tato brahmādayo devāḥ svayameva vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ nivāraṇārthāya śāṃtyarthaṃ sarvadehinān \|*  
*gatāśca te samutthāpya punareva triviṣṭapam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereafter Devas beginning with Brahma were engaged in making them desist from fighting for the purpose of peace among all embodied beings. After making them cease to fight, they returned to heaven.

## \|\| 1.57.5 \|\|

*aṃbāpi prāpya paramaṃ gāṃgeyotthaṃ parābhavam \|*  
*praviṣṭā koparaktākṣī susamiddhe hutāśane \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having suffered the most humiliating discomfiture from Bhīṣma, Aṃbā, with her eyes reddened with anger entered well-enkindled fire.

## \|\| 1.57.6 \|\|

*bhartsayitvā nadīputraṃ bāṣpavyākulalocanā \|*  
*tataḥprovāca madhyasthā vahneḥ kurupitāmaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Standing in the midst of fire, with her eyes bedimmed with tears, she rebuked the son of river (Bhīsma) i.e. the elderly grandfather of the Kurus and said:

## \|\| 1.57.7-8 \|\|

*yasmādbhīṣma tvayā tyaktā kāmārtāhaṃ sudurmate \|*  
*tasmāttava vadhāyāśu bhaviṣyāmi punaḥ kṣitau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*strīhatyayā samāyuktastvaṃ ca nūnaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ yadi dharmo'tra smṛtiśāstrasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. “O Bhīṣma, O extremely evil-minded one. You discarded me who was love-stricken. So I will born again on the earth in order to kill you. You will certainly be defiled by the sin of murdering a woman, if the word of Smṛtis and other scriptural texts is authoritative.”

## \|\| 1.57.9 \|\|

*tataḥ sa ghṛṇayā'viṣṭo bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṃḍeyaṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ papraccha vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereupon, overcome with disgust, Bhīṣma, the grandfather of Kurus, approached Mārkaṇḍeya, an excellent sage, and asked him humbly:

## \|\| 1.57.10-11 \|\|

*bhagavankāśirājasya sutayā me prajalpitam \|*  
*mama mṛtyukaraṃ pāpaṃ sakalaṃ te bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tatkiṃ syādvākyamātreṇa no vā brāhmaṇasattama \|*  
*atra me saṃśayastattvaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. “O holy Sir, daughter of the king of Kāśī prattles thus to me. ‘The entire sin of causing my death will incur to you.’ O excellent Brāhmaṇa, shall it be so merely because of her utterance, or not? I have a grerat doubt in this respect. It behoves you to clarify it duly.”

## \|\| 1.57.12 \|\|

*śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*ākṣiptastāḍito vāpi yamuddiśya tyajedasūn \|*  
*strījano vā dvijo vāpi tasya pāpaṃ tu tadbhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

Śrī Mārkaṇdeya said:

12\. If a woman or a Brāhmaṇa, on being insulted or beaten, were to cast off her or his life with direct reference to the person concerned, the sin thereof shall be that of the person so referred to.

## \|\| 1.57.13 \|\|

*striyaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vāpi tasmānnaiva prakopayet \|*  
*nighnaṃtaṃ vā śapaṃtaṃ vā yadīcchecchubhamātmanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence if one wishes for one’s own good, one should not enrage a woman or a Brāhmaṇa even if the woman or Brāhmaṇa were intent on killing or cursing.

## \|\| 1.57.14 \|\|

*tvayā punarvarākī sā kāmārtā samupekṣitā \|*  
*jitvā svayaṃvare pūrvaṃ tatkathaṃ syānna pāpabhāk \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In your case, the unfortunate pitiable girl was stricken with love. She had been won by you in (the battle following) the Svayaṃvara. Hence how can you escape being a sinner?

## \|\| 1.57.15 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*tadarthaṃ vada me brahmanprāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*tapo vā yadi vā dānaṃ vrataṃ niyamameva vā \|\| 15 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

15\. For the sake of that, O Brāhmaṇa, advise me as to the expiatory rite to be performed for the sake of purity, whether it be penance, or Dāna, Vrata or any special restraint.

## \|\| 1.57.16 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*daśānāṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ yadvadhe pātakaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tatpāpaṃ strīvadhe kṛtsnaṃ jāyate bharatarṣabha \|\| 16 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

16\. O bull among the descendants of Bharata, if a woman is killed, the sin accruing is equal to the entire sin that has been proclaimed in the scriptures to be incurred for the murder of ten leading Brāhmanas.

## \|\| 1.57.17 \|\|

*tadatra viṣaye dānaṃ na tapo na vratādikam \|*  
*tīrthasevāṃ parityajya tasmāttvaṃ tāṃ samācara \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence, excepting pilgrimage there is no other atonement such as Dāna, penance, Vrata and the like in this regard. So do undertake a pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.57.18 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparo bhūtvā babhrāma kṣitimaṃḍale \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sūta said:

18\. On hearing his words, Bhīṣma, the elderly grandfather of Kurus, roamed over the entire sphere of the earth in the course of his pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.57.19 \|\|

*tataḥ kramātsamāyāto bhramamāṇo mahītale \|*  
*camatkārapure kṣetre nānātīrthasamākule \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Roaming over the earth, in due course, he reached the holy spot of Camatkārapura full of many Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.57.20-28 \|\|

*athāpaśyanmahātmā sa supuṇyaṃ tadgayāśiraḥ \|*  
*snātvā śrāddhaṃ ca vidhivadyāvacchraddhāsama nvitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*cakre tāvannabhovāṇī vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*bhīṣmabhīṣma mahābāho nārhastvaṃ śrāddhajaṃ vidhim \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kartuṃ strīhatyayāyuktastasmācchṛṇu vaco mama \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhātīrthamityeva khyātaṃ pātakanāśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*asmātsthānātsamīpasthaṃ vāruṇyāṃ diśi puṇyakṛt \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃgārakaṣaṣṭhyāṃ yo naraḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sa strīhatyākṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādadya dine putra bhaumavārasamanvitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saiva ṣaṣṭhī tithiḥ puṇyā tasmāttatra drutaṃ vraja \|*  
*ahaṃ tava pitā putra śaṃtanuḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*strīhatyayānvitaṃ jñātvā tatastūrṇamihāgataḥ \|*  
*tato bhīṣmo drutaṃ gatvā tatra sthāne samāhitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*snānaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ śrāddhaṃ cakre śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tato bhūyaḥ samāgatya sa taṃ provāca śatanuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vipāpmā tvaṃ kuruśreṣṭha saṃjāto'si na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnijaṃ gṛhaṃ gaccha rājyaciṃtāṃ samācara \|\| 28 \|\|*

20-26a. Then that noble soul visited Gayāśiras. Endowed with faith he took the holy bath and performed Śrāddha duly; but during its performance an aerial voice spoke these words:

“O Bhīṣma O mighty-armed one, you do not deserve to perform a Śrāddha. You are defiled with the sin of a woman’s murder; you are not eligible to perform Śrāddha. Hence you listen to my words. Śarmiṣṭhā Tīrtha is well-known as destructive of sins. It is situated very near this spot. It is meritorious and is there to the west. A devout man should take his holy bath on Aṅgāraka Ṣaṣṭhī (sixth lunar day coinciding with a Tuesday) in a dark half. One who bathes thus is rid of the sin resulting from woman-murder. There is no doubt about it.

This day happens to be the same Ṣaṣṭhī coinciding with Tuesday, dear son. It is the meritorious Tithi. So go quickly to that place. Dear son, I am king Santanu, your father. On coming to know that you have been defiled by the sin of woman-murder I hastened hither.”

26b-28. Thereupon Bhīṣma went to that holy spot quickly with mental concentration. He took the holy bath and then performed Śrāddha with due faith. Thereat Śantanu came there again and said:

“O excellent one among the descendants of Kuni, you are free form the sin undoubtedly. So go home and carry on the administration of the kingdom.”

## \|\| 1.57.29-31 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo jñātvā tīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*vāsudevātmikāmarcāṃ tathānyāṃ kurusattamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pārijātamayīṃ mūrtiṃ raverlakṣaṇalakṣitām \|*  
*supramāṇāṃ surūpāṃ ca śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tathānyatsthāpayāmāsa liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*durgāṃ ca bhaktisaṃyukto vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. On coming to know the excellence of the Tīrtha he became surprised. The most excellent one among Kurus made another image of Vāsudeva. Then he made an idol of the Sun-god with Pārijāta wood. The idol was characterised with all regular features, the dimensions were proportionate and the form was fascinating. He made this with his mind purified by faith.

Then he installed a Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord He then with great devotion made the idol of Durgā in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.57.32 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvānsamāhūya sa viprānpurasaṃbhavān \|*  
*provāca kauravo bhīṣmo vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Bhīṣma, the descendant of Kuru, invited all the Brāhmaṇas of that city. Standing humbly he said to them:

## \|\| 1.57.33-34 \|\|

*mayā vinirmitaṃ viprā devāgāracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*etatkṣetre ca yuṣmākaṃ dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pālayadhvaṃ prayāsyāmi svagṛhaṃ prati satvaram \|*  
*preritaḥ pitṛbhirdivyaiḥ svargamārgasamāśritaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “O Brāhmaṇas, I have been urged by my divine ancestors already on the path to heaven and so have built four shrines in this holy spot of yours. Take pity on me and maintain these shrines. I am hastening back to my abode.”

## \|\| 1.57.35 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*gacchagaccha kuruśreṣṭha suviśrabdhaḥ svamāyayā \|*  
*vayaṃ sarve kariṣyāmo yuṣmacchreyo'bhivardhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

35\. O most excellent one among the descendants of Kuru, do go carefree and happily. We all will carry out what is conducive to the increase of your welfare.

## \|\| 1.57.36 \|\|

*devaśreṇiriyaṃ rājanyā tvayātra vinirmitā \|*  
*asyāḥ pūjādikaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ sadā vayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O king, a number of deities have been made by you here. We shall perform all the rites such as adoration etc. of these always.

## \|\| 1.57.37 \|\|

*tavāpi vinayaṃ dṛṣṭvā parituṣṭā vayaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*sarvānprārthaya tasmāttvaṃ varaṃ svaṃ manasi sthitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O king, we are pleased on seeing your humility. Hence do pray unto us all for any boon that you have cherished in your mind.

## \|\| 1.57.38 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*eṣa eva varo'smākaṃ yatsaṃtuṣṭā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tathāpyāśu vacaḥ kāryaṃ yuṣmadīyaṃ mayādhunā \|\| 38 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

38\. This alone is the excellent boon unto us that the excellent Brāhmaṇas have been pleased. Still I have now to cany out your instruction.

## \|\| 1.57.39 \|\|

*etāni devasadmāni madīyāni naro bhuvi \|*  
*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya pūjayecchraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*prasādādeva yuṣmākaṃ tasya tatsyādasaṃśayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If any man on the earh faithfully worships in these shrines built by me, with any desire in his mind, he shall undoubtedly obtain that due to your favour.

## \|\| 1.57.40 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ādityasya kariṣyāmo yātrāṃ bhādrapade vayam \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa sarvadaiva samāhitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

40\. We shall organize the Yatrā (religious procession) of Āditya in the month of Bhādrapada with great mental concentration, when the seventh lunar day coincides with a Sunday.

## \|\| 1.57.41 \|\|

*tathā śivasya cāṣṭamyāṃ caitraśukle viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*caturdaśyāṃ mahābhāga tava snehānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Due to your love, we shall organize Śiva’s Yatrā on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra.

## \|\| 1.57.42-43 \|\|

*śayane bodhane viṣṇoḥ saṃprāpte dvādaśīdine \|*  
*viṣṇorapi ca durgāyāḥ saṃprāpte navamīdine \|\| 42 \|\|*

*āśvine śuklapakṣe ca gītavāditranisvanaiḥ \|*  
*mahotsavaṃ tathā citrairhāsyalāsyaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. When the twelfth day of Āṣāḍha and Kārttika arrives at the time of Śayana (sleep) and Bodhana (waking up) of Viṣṇu we shall organize Viṣṇu’s Yātrā.

On the ninth day in the bright half of Āśvina, we shall organize the Yātrā of Durgā with songs and instrumental music. We shall have great festivities with dances and jokes of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.57.44 \|\|

*yastatra mānavo nityaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati ca gītādi sa yāsyati parāṃ gatim \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A man who is endowed with great faith always and performs the rites of Gīta (song) etc. shall attain the highest goal

## \|\| 1.57.45 \|\|

*vayaṃ tasya bhaviṣyāmaḥ sadaiva prītamānasāḥ \|*  
*pradāsyāmastathā kāmānmanasā vāṃchitānnṛpa \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. We shall always be pleased with him, O king, and shall grant him all the desires cherished in his heart.

## \|\| 1.57.46 \|\|

*evamuktvātha te viprāḥ svāni sthānāni bhejire \|*  
*bhīṣmo'pi harṣasaṃyuktaḥ svagṛhaṃ prasthitastataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying thus those Brāhmaṇas went back to their respective abodes. Bhīṣma too was delighted and started back homewards.

## Chapter 58 - Greatness of Śiva Gaṅgā

## \|\| 1.58.1-4 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃsthāpya gāṃgeyaḥ puṇyaṃ devacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃsthāpayāmāsa gaṃgāṃ tripathagāminīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kūpikāyāṃ mahābhāga śivaliṃgasya pūrvataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ provāca tānhṛṣṭaḥ saṃpūjya dvijasattamān \|\| 2 \|\|*

*asyāṃ yaḥ puruṣaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā māṃ vīkṣayiṣyati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śivalokaṃ prayāsyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kariṣyati tathā yastu śapathaṃ cātra mānavaḥ \|*  
*asatyaṃ yāsyati kṣipraṃ sa yamasya gṛhaṃ prati \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. After installing the four deities of great merit, Gāṅgeya (Bhīṣma) installed Gaṅgā of triple path in the Kūpikā (holy well) to the east of Śivaliṅga.

## \|\| 1.58.5 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahābhāgo bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svapuraṃ tasmāddharṣeṇa mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The highly esteemed one then joyously honoured the excellent Brāhmaṇas and said:

“A person who takes his holy bath in this and visits me shall become liberated from all sins and go to Śivaloka. Similarly a man who makes his solemn oath untrue (i.e. breaks it) will go to Yama’s abode quickly.”

5\. After saying this, Bhīṣma, the highly esteemed grandfather of Kurus, became extremely delighted and went to his city

## \|\| 1.58.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatrāsīcchūdrasaṃbhūtaḥ pauṃḍrakonāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*bālabhāve samaṃ mitraiḥ sa krīḍati divāniśam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. There was a boy born of a Śūdra and named Pauṇḍraka. During childhood, he used to play day and night.

## \|\| 1.58.7-8 \|\|

*hāsyabhāvācca mitrasya pustakaṃ tena coritam \|*  
*mitraiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ pauṇḍrakaḥ sa prāha naiva mayā hṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pustakaṃ caiva yuṣmākaṃ cintanīyaṃ sadaiva tat \|*  
*bhavadbhiryatnamāsthāya dṛśyatāṃ kvāpi pustakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Jokingly a friend’s book was stolen by him. On being asked by his friends, Pauṇḍraka said: “It has not been taken away by me. The book should have been well pondered by you all with great endeavour. Look out for it somewhere here.”

## \|\| 1.58.9 \|\|

*kṛtāśca śapathāstatra snātvā bhāgīrathījale \|*  
*aduṣṭacetasā tena dattaṃ tatpustakaṃ hṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Taking his bath in the waters of Gaṅgā solemn oaths were taken by him. (Later) when he ceased to be a wicked fellow the book that had been stolen was returned by him.

## \|\| 1.58.10 \|\|

*punaśca ruciraṃ hāsyaṃ kṛtvā tena samaṃ bahu \|*  
*athāsāvabhavatkuṣṭhī tatkṣaṇādeva garhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Again he cracked many charming jokes with him. Then he became a leper and immediately he became a despicable person.

## \|\| 1.58.11 \|\|

*sa tyakto bāṃdhavaiḥ sarvaiḥ kalatrairapi vallabhaiḥ \|*  
*tato vairāgyamāpanno bhṛgupātaṃ papāta saḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was abandoned by all the kinsmen and even by beloved wives. Thereupon he became dejected and he committed suicide by hurling himself down from the precipice.

## \|\| 1.58.12 \|\|

*jātaśca tatprabhāvena kuṣṭhena parivarjitaḥ \|*  
*śāstracauryakṛtāddoṣānmūkarūpaḥ sa hāsyakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By its power he became rid of leprosy. That person indulging in jokes became mute due to the fault of the theft of the scriptural text.

## \|\| 1.58.13 \|\|

*na kāryaḥ śapathastasmāttasyāgre'pi laghurdvijāḥ \|*  
*api hāsyopacāreṇa ātmanaḥ sukhamicchatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇas, in front of this deity, even the slightest solemn oath should not be taken by one who wishes for his own happiness, even a jocular vein.

## Chapter 59 - Vidura Builds the Lord’s Temple

## \|\| 1.59.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasminkṣetre raviḥ pūrvaṃ vidureṇa pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*śivaśca parayā bhaktyā tathā viṣṇurdvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yastānpūjayate bhaktyā mānuṣo bhaktitastataḥ \|*  
*sa yāsyati paraṃ sthānaṃ yajñairapi sudurlabham \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Formerly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Ravi, Śiva and Viṣṇu were installed by Vidura in that holy place. A man who worships them with great devotion attains the highest region, very difficult to be achieved even by Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.59.3 \|\|

*hastināpurasaṃsthena vidureṇa purā dvijāḥ \|*  
*gālavo muniśārdūlaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ svagṛhamāgataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly, O Brāhmaṇas, while Vidura was staying at Hastināpura he was visited in his house by Gālava, a tiger among sages. He (Gālava) was asked:

## \|\| 1.59.4 \|\|

*aputrasya gatirloke kīdṛksaṃjāyate pare \|*  
*etanme pṛcchato brūhi kṛtvā sadbhāvamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “Of what sort is the ultimate goal in the other world of one who has no son? Kindly be gracious to me and tell me even as I ask you this.”

## \|\| 1.59.5-6 \|\|

*gālava uvāca \|*  
*aputrasya gatirnāsti mṛtaḥ svargaṃ na gacchati \|*  
*dvādaśānāmapi tathā yadyeko'pi na vidyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aurasaḥ kṣetrajaścaiva krayakrītaśca pālitaḥ \|*  
*paunarbhavaḥ punardattaḥ kuṃḍo golastathā paraḥ \|*  
*kānīnaśca sahoḍhaśca aśvattho brahmavṛkṣakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Gālava said:

5-6. There is no salvation unto one who has no son. On death he does not go to heaven if he has none of these twelve (types of sons): (1) Aurasa (bosom-born), (2) Kṣetraja (son born to his wife), (3) Krayakrīta (one who is bought on payment), (4) Pālita (one who is brought up), (5) Paunarbhava (widow’s son after remarriage), (6) Datta (adopted), (7) Kuṇḍa (son born in adultery), (8) Gola (widow's bastard), (9) Kānīna (son of an unmarried woman), (10) Sahoḍha (son of a woman pregnant at the time of marriage), (11) Aśvattha (banyan tree) (see verse 12 below), (12) Brahmavṛkṣaka (religious fig tree).

## \|\| 1.59.7 \|\|

*eteṣāmapi yadyekaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ na jāyate \|*  
*tannūnaṃ narake vāsaḥ puṃsaṃjñe vai prajāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. If men do not have any one of these, they will have to stay surely in the Naraka named Puṃ.

## \|\| 1.59.8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya gālavasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*aputratvātparaṃ duḥkhaṃ jagāma vidurastadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

8\. On hearing the words of the noble-souled Gālava, Vidura became extremely distressed because he had no sons.

## \|\| 1.59.9-11 \|\|

*taptastaṃ gālavaḥ prāha mā tvaṃ duḥkhapadaṃ vraja \|*  
*madvākyātputrakaṃ vṛkṣaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñaṃ drutaṃ kuru \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmātprāpsyasi niḥśeṣaṃ phalaṃ putrasamudbhavam \|*  
*gatvā puṇyatame deśe raktaśṛṃgasya mūrdhani \|\| 10 \|\|*

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvavṛddhiśubhodaye \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vidurastatkṣaṇādyayau \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Vidura was dejected and Gālava said to him: “Do not grieve over it. At my instance make the tree named Viṣṇu (i.e. Aśvattha) your son quickly. Thereby you will obtain the entire benefit of having a son. Go to the holy place on the top of the mountain Raktaśṛṅga, to the holy spot named Hāṭakeśvara that is the cause of (i.e. which gives) all prosperity and auspicious well-being.”

On hearing his words Vidura instantly started:

## \|\| 1.59.12 \|\|

*tatsthānaṃ gālavoddiṣṭaṃ harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*tatrāśvatthataruṃ sthāpya putratve cābhiṣecya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With great joy he went to the place indicated by Gālava. There he planted an Aśvattha tree and consecrated it as his son.

## \|\| 1.59.13 \|\|

*vaivāhikena vidhinā kṛtakṛtyo babhūva ha \|*  
*tato babhrāma tatkṣetraṃ tīrthayātrāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He became contented with that sort of marital rite. Thereafter he went round that holy place like engaged in pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.59.14 \|\|

*kīrtitāni vicitrāṇi rājarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*śrutvā sthānāni gatvā ca dadarśa sthānadevatāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He had heard the glorification of various wonderful holy spots connected with noble-souled saintly kings. Now he travelled and visited the different deities of those holy Spots.

## \|\| 1.59.15 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā kuruvṛddhasya kīrtanāni mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tataścakre matiṃ tatra divyaprāsādakarmaṇi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He visited the glorified shrines of the noble-souled, elderly member of the Kuru clan (i.e. Bhīṣma) and intended to build places to the deities.

## \|\| 1.59.16 \|\|

*tato māheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ vaṭādhastādvidhāya saḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ ca sthāpayāmāsa aśvatthasya taroradhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then he installed the Liṅga of Maheśvara beneath the Vaṭa (holy fig tree). He then installed Viṣṇu beneath the Aśvattha tree.

## \|\| 1.59.17 \|\|

*niveśya ca tathā divyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nyavedayat \|*  
*etaddevatrayaṃ kṣetre yuṣmākaṃ hi mayā kṛtam \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ sakalā cāsya cintākāryā sadaiva hi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After consecrating the deities he pleaded to the Brāhmaṇas: “These three deities have been installed by me in your holy place. All the affairs (services) of these should be considered and managed by you all.”

## \|\| 1.59.18-19 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vayamasya kariṣyāmo yātrādyāḥ sakalāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tathā vaṃśodbhavā ye ca putrāḥ pautrāstathāpare \|*  
*kariṣyaṃti kriyāḥ sarvāstvaṃ gaccha svagṛhaṃ prati \|\| 19 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

18-19. We shall perform all the rites such as the Yātrā (religious procession) etc. of these deities. Our sons, grandsons and others hailing from our families shall continue to perform all the requisite rites. Do go back home.

## \|\| 1.59.20 \|\|

*tato jagāma viduraḥ svapuraṃ prati harṣitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyo dvijāste ca cakrurvākyaṃ tadudbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereupon Vidura joyously went back to his city and was contented. Those Brāhmaṇas too carried out the requests made by him.

## \|\| 1.59.21 \|\|

*māghamāsasya saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa yo naraḥ \|*  
*pūjayedbhāskaraṃ tatra sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A man who worships Bhāskara (the Sun-god) there on the seventh lunar day in the month of Māgha coinciding with a Sunday attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.59.22 \|\|

*śivaṃ vā somavāreṇa śuklāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śayane bodhane viṣṇuṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Or he should worship Śiva on a Monday particularly coinciding with the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month. He should worship Viṣṇu with full faith at the time of Śayana (Āṣāḍha) and Bodhana (Kārttika) (on the eleventh days in the bright half of Āṣāḍha and Kārttika).

## \|\| 1.59.23 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena devānāṃ tattrayaṃ śubham \|*  
*pūjanīyaṃ viśeṣeṇa naraiḥ svargatimīpsubhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence with all endeavour that splendid trio of deities should be worshipped particularly by men desirous of attaining the goal of heaven.

## \|\| 1.59.24 \|\|

*tatra siddhiṃ gatāḥ pūrvaṃ munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*vidureśvaramārādhya śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hundreds and thousands of sages of esteemed vows have attained Siddhi there formerly by propitiating Vidureśvara.

## \|\| 1.59.25 \|\|

*tatastatsiddhidaṃ jñātvā liṃgaṃ vai pākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*pāṃsubhiḥ pūrayāmāsa yathā kaścinna budhyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thereupon, realizing that the Liṅga is the bestower of Siddhi, the Chastiser of Pāka (i.e. Indra) filled it with dust particles so that none will come to know of it.

## \|\| 1.59.26 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya vidurastatra cāgataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā lopagataṃ liṃgaṃ duḥkhena mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Once thereafter Vidura happened to come there. On seeing that the Liṅga had vanished ḥe felt very miserable.

## \|\| 1.59.27-28 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*mā tvaṃ kuru viṣādaṃ hi liṃgārthe vidurādhunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yo'yaṃ sa dṛśyate vālo vaṭastasya tale sthitā \|*  
*devadroṇiḥ sureśena pāṃsubhiḥ paripūritā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. At the same time an unembodied voice spoke: “O Vidura, do not feel sorry now. Yonder there appears a sapling of Vaṭa tree. The divine Droṇī (tank) beneath it has been filled up with dust particles by the Lord of Suras.”

## \|\| 1.59.29 \|\|

*tato gajāhvayāttūrṇaṃ samānīya dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*śodhayāmāsa tatsthānaṃ divārātramatandritaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thereupon he brought much wealth from Hastināpura and renovated the entire place working day and night untiringly.

## \|\| 1.59.30 \|\|

*tato vilokya tāndevānharṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ nirmame teṣāṃ yogyaṃ sādhvabhisaṃsthitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then he saw the deities and was delighted very much. He built palaces befitting them and well constructed.

## \|\| 1.59.31-33 \|\|

*kailāsaśikharākāraṃ bhāskarārthe mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*jaṭāmadhyagataṃ dṛṣṭvā vaṭasya ca maheśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prāsādaṃ nākarottatra liṃgaṃ yāvanna cālayet \|*  
*vāsudevasya yogyāṃ ca kṛtvā śālāṃ bṛhattarām \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dattvā vṛttiṃ ca saṃhṛṣṭo brāhmaṇebhyo nivedya ca \|*  
*jagāma svāśramaṃ bhūyo viprānāmaṃtrya tāṃstataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. The great sage built a palace as lofty as the peak of Kailāsa for the Sun-god. He observed that Maheśvara had got entangled with the hanging roots of the Vaṭa tree. So he did not build a palace lest the Liṅga should be displaced. He built a big chamber befitting Vāsudeva. With great delight he offered means of sustenance to the Brāhmaṇas. He took leave of the Brāhmaṇas then and went to his hermitage.

## Chapter 60 - Greatness of Narāditya

## \|\| 1.60.1 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*māhittheyaṃ tvayākhyātā yā purā sūtanandana \|*  
*kena saṃsthāpitā tatra vada sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta-nandana, earlier you had mentioned the deity Māhitthā. By whom was the deity installed? Do describe every thing without leaving anything.

## \|\| 1.60.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śoṣaṇīnāma yā vidyā purāgastyena sādhitā \|*  
*ātharvaṇena mantreṇa svayaṃ ca parameśvarī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃśoṣitastena sa samudro mahātmanā \|*  
*mitrāvaruṇaputreṇa sā proktā purataḥ sthitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2-3. The Vidyā (divine power) named Śoṣaṇī was propitiated by Agastya. The great goddess was propitiated through Ātharvaṇa Mantra. Then the ocean was dried up by the noble-souled son of Mitra and Varuṇa. He addressed the goddess standing before.

## \|\| 1.60.4-7 \|\|

*māhitthaṃ sādhitaṃ yasmāttvayā me sakalaṃ śubham \|*  
*māhitthānāma tasmāttvaṃ devatā saṃbhaviṣyasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*camatkārapurakṣetre pūjāṃ prāpsyasyanuttamām \|*  
*yastvāmātharvaṇairmantraistatrasthāṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pūjayiṣyati vṛddhiṃ ca sarvakālamavāpsyati \|*  
*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha mayā sārddhaṃ purottame \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvijānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya nityaṃ saṃnihitā bhava \|*  
*evaṃ sā tatra saṃbhūtā māhitthā varadevatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7a. “Since Māhittha (?) has been adopted by you, everything is auspicious unto me. Therefore you will become the deity named Māhitthā. In the holy place of Camatkārapura you will get excellent adoration. One who is endowed with devotion and adores with the Ātharvaṇa Mantras, you who are stationed there, shall obtain prosperity always. Hence hasten to that excellent city along with me. Be present there for ever in order to protect Brāhmaṇas.”

7b. It was thus that the excellent deity Māhitthā happened to manifest there.

## \|\| 1.60.8 \|\|

*yayā'yaṃ calitaḥ śailaḥ svaśaktyā niścalīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*skandeneha dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ śaktyā viddhastadagrataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This mountain that had been moving was rendered immobile by that deity. It was here, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that the mountain was pierced by Skanda with his Śakti (Tri-dent) formerly.

## \|\| 1.60.9 \|\|

*narādityastataścānyo yo nareṇa pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ taṃ sūryavāreṇa dṛṣṭvā pāpātpramucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Another deity named Narāditya was installed by Nara. One who visits him on the sixth lunar day coinciding with a Sunday is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 1.60.10 \|\|

*na śatrūṇāṃ parābhūtiṃ prayāsyati yathārjunaḥ \|*  
*rogī vimucyate rogāddaridro dhanamāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Like Arjuna, he will never suffer defeat from enemies. A sick man is rid of his ailments. Poor people will attain wealth.

## \|\| 1.60.11 \|\|

*tathā govardhanadharaṃ tatra devaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*yaḥ paśyetkārtike śukle saṃprāpte prathame dine \|*  
*tasya gāvaḥ prabhūtāḥ syurnīrogā dvisattamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Similarly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas one who visits Lord Janārdana who lifted up the mountain Govardhana there, on the first day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika, will have many cows devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.60.12 \|\|

*narasiṃhavapuḥ sākṣāttathā devo hariḥ svayam \|*  
*tathā vināyakastatra sarvakāmapradāyakaḥ \|*  
*sarvavighnaharaścaiva sthāpitaścārjunena hi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Lord Hari himself directly in the guise of the Man-lion and Vināyaka, the bestower of all desires and the remover of all obstacles, was installed by Arjuna.

## \|\| 1.60.13 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā caturthyāṃ modakāśanaiḥ \|*  
*sa sarvavighnanirmukto labhate vāṃchitaṃ phalam \|*  
*tatra sthito dvijeṃdrāṇāṃ hitāya dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who devoutly worships him on the fourth lunar day through sweetmeats and other foodstuffs shall be liberated from all obstacles. He will get desired benefit. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he is stationed there for the welfare of leading Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.60.14 \|\|

*yastamātharvaṇairmaṃtraiḥ pūjayeddvādaśīdine \|*  
*kārtikasya site pakṣe sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One who worships him through Ātharvaṇa Mantras on the twelfth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.60.15-16 \|\|

*tathā tatra dvijaśreṣṭhā naranārāyaṇāvubhau \|*  
*devau paramatejasvī yastau paśyati bhaktitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pūjayecca dvijaśreṣṭhā dvādaśyā divase svayam \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, both the deities Nara and Nārāyaṇa are present there. One who is greatly rediant and visits them devoutly and worships them on the twelfth day, attains the highest place devoid of old age and death.

## \|\| 1.60.17 \|\|

*tīrthayātrākṛtāraṃbhaḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre samāyāto dvijottamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Dhanañjaya (Arjuna) who undertook his pilgrimage came to the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.60.18 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tatpāvanaṃ kṣetraṃ tīrthapūgaprapūritam \|*  
*ādityaṃ sthāpayāmāsa prāsāde sumanohare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On seeing that sacred holy spot full of many excellent Tīrthas, he installed Āditya in a very charming mansion (temple).

## \|\| 1.60.19 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇau devau tasyāgre sthāpitau tataḥ \|*  
*tathā govardhanadharastatra devaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Lords Nara and Nārāyaṇa were installed afterwards in front of him (i.e. Āditya). Similarly the Lord holding the mountain Govardhana was also installed.

## \|\| 1.60.20 \|\|

*narasiṃhaṃ tathaivānyaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃsthāpya kauṃteyo devagṛhasupaṃcakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Another deity was also installed by him with great faith, namely Narasiṃha. Thus the son of Kuntī established five shrines.

## \|\| 1.60.21 \|\|

*tato viprānsamāhūya sarvāṃstānpurasaṃbhavān \|*  
*provāca praṇato bhaktyā dhanaṃ dattvā supuṣkalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then he summoned all the Brāhmaṇas hailing from that city, gave them ample cash and spoke after duly bowing to them with devotion:

## \|\| 1.60.22 \|\|

*mayā saṃsthāpitaḥ sūryaḥ sarvarogakṣayāvahaḥ \|*  
*tathārpitaśca yuṣmākaṃ ciṃtanīyaṃ sadaiva tu \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “The Sun-god, the destroyer of all ailments, has been installed by me and entrusted to you all. It is your duty always to look after the shrine.

## \|\| 1.60.23 \|\|

*viprā ūcuḥ \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ pāṃḍavaśreṣṭha suviśrabdhaḥ svamālayam \|*  
*vayaṃ sarve kariṣyāmastavaśreyo'bhivardhanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

23\. O excellent one among the sons of Pāṇḍu, do go home with full confidence. All of us will carry out what is conducive to what is good for you.

## \|\| 1.60.24 \|\|

*tato'rjunaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā tebhyo dattvā dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*tānāmaṃtrya namaskṛtya jagāma svapuraṃ prati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereupon Arjuna was delighted. He gave much wealth to them. He took leave of them, bowed to them and went to his city.

## \|\| 1.60.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ narādityasya saṃbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ śṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sūta said:

25\. Thus everything concerning the greatness of Narāditya has been narrated to you, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. It destroys the sins of the listeners.

## Chapter 61 - Birth of Viṣakanyā

## \|\| 1.61.1-3 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhātīrthamityuktaṃ tvayā yacca mahāmate \|*  
*kathaṃ jātaṃ mahābhāga kiṃprabhāvaṃ tu tadvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsīdrājā vṛkonāma somavaṃśa samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca sarvalokahite rataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā pativrataparāyaṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. O highly intelligent one, you spoke of the Śarmiṣṭhā Tīrtha. O highly fortunate one, do tell us how it originate? What is its power?

## \|\| 1.61.4 \|\|

*atha tasyāṃ samutpannā prāpte vayasi paścime \|*  
*kanyakā divase prāpte sarvaśāstravigarhite \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

There was a king named Vṛka born in the lunar race. He was a patron of learned Brāhmaṇas, a person worthy of being a shelter on refuge, always engaged in the welfare of all the worlds.

His wife was a chaste lady dearer to him than even his own life. She was endowed with all good characteristics and a devoted, faithful and chaste wife.

4\. In her late life, a daughter was born to her on a day condemned by all scriptural texts (i.e. considered inauspicious by them).

## \|\| 1.61.5 \|\|

*tata ānīya viprānsa jyotirjñānavicakṣaṇān \|*  
*papraccha kīdṛśī kanyā mameyaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereupon, he summoned Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Science of Astrology. He asked, “Of what sort will this daughter of mine be?”

## \|\| 1.61.6 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yā kanyā prāpnuyājjanma citrāsaṃsthe divākare \|*  
*caṃdre vāpi caturdaśyāṃ sā bhavedviṣakanyakā \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

6\. If a girl is born when the Sun is in the constellation Citrā or the Moon in the fourteenth lunar day, she will become a Viṣakanyakā (a poison girl).

## \|\| 1.61.7 \|\|

*yastasyāḥ pratigṛhṇāti pāṇiṃ pārthivasattama \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuṃ sa prāpnoti naro dhruvam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A man who grasps her hand in marriage, O excellent king, will certainly meet with his death within six months.

## \|\| 1.61.8 \|\|

*yasminsā jāyate harmye ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare ca tat \|*  
*karoti vibhavairhīnaṃ dhanadasyāpyasaṃśayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She will render the mansion wherein she is born, even if it be that of Kubera, a place devoid of riches within six months.

## \|\| 1.61.9 \|\|

*seyaṃ tava sutā rājanyathoktā viṣa kanyakā \|*  
*paitṛkaṃ śvāśurīyaṃ ca haniṣyati gṛhadvayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Such is, O king, your daughter who is called a Viṣakanyakā. She will destroy the two families, viz. that of parents and that of her father-in-law.

## \|\| 1.61.10 \|\|

*tasmādimāṃ parityajya sukhī bhava narādhipa \|*  
*śraddadhāsi vaco'smākaṃ hita muktaṃ yadi prabho \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence, do be happy, O king, by abandoning her if you have faith in our words, spoken by us for your good, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.61.11 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tyakṣyāmi yadi nāmaitāṃ dhārayiṣyāmi vā gṛhe \|*  
*anyadehodbhavaṃ karma phaliṣyati tathāpi me \|\| 11 \|\|*

The king said:

11\. Whether I abandon her or keep her in the house my Karma of the previous body (of the previous birth) will certainly fructify.

## \|\| 1.61.12 \|\|

*śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ na tu śakyaṃ prarakṣitum \|*  
*tasmātkarma puraskṛtya naiva tyakṣyāmi kanyakām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Whether auspicious or inauspicious (evil), nothing can be prevented. With this Karma in view I will not abandon my daughter.

## \|\| 1.61.13 \|\|

*yenayena śarīreṇa yadyatkarma karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tenatenaiva bhūyaḥ sa prāpnoti sakalaṃ phalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Any man doing anything with whatever body of his attains the entire fruit further with the same (or similar) body

## \|\| 1.61.14 \|\|

*yasyāṃ yasyāmavasthāyāṃ kriyate'tra śubhāśubham \|*  
*tasyāṃ tasyāṃ dhruvaṃ tasya phalaṃ tadbhujyate naraiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Auspicious or inauspicious act may be done in different states or situations. Certainly the fruit thereof is experienced in the same or similar situation by men.

## \|\| 1.61.15 \|\|

*na naśyati purākarma kṛtaṃ sarveṃdriyairiha \|*  
*akṛtaṃ jāyate naiva tasmānnāsti bhayaṃ mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. An action of the previous birth done by any of the organs does not perish. Nothing results from what has not been done. So I am not afraid.

## \|\| 1.61.16 \|\|

*āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanameva ca \|*  
*pañcaitāni hi sṛjyante garbhasthasyaiva dehinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Span of life, Karma, wealth, learning and dealth-these five are ordained even as the embodied being is in the womb itself.

## \|\| 1.61.17 \|\|

*yathā vṛkṣeṣu vallīṣu kusumāni phalāni ca \|*  
*svakālaṃ nātivartaṃte tadvatkarma purākṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Just as flowers and fruits on trees and creepers do not deviate from their fixed lime, so also the previous Karma.

## \|\| 1.61.18 \|\|

*yenaiva yadyathā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*sa eva tattathā bhuṃkte nityaṃ vihitamātmanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Only the doer experiences always the good (or adverse) result of his own good or bad act in the manner previously done.

## \|\| 1.61.19 \|\|

*yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram \|*  
*tathaivaṃ koṭimadhyasthaṃ kartāraṃ karma vindati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Just as a calf finds out its mother cow among thousands of cows, so also Karma finds out the doer from among ten million doers.

## \|\| 1.61.20 \|\|

*anyadehakṛtaṃ karma na kaścitpuruṣo bhuvi \|*  
*balena prajñayā vāpi samarthaḥ kartumanyathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. No man on the earth can by means of his might or intellect alter a Karma done in the previous body.

## \|\| 1.61.21 \|\|

*anyathā śāstragarbhiṇyā dhiyā dhīro mahīyate \|*  
*svāmivatprākkṛtaṃ karma vidadhāti tadanyathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A sensible man with intellect penetrating deep into the scriptural texts, is honoured otherwise. But the Karma previously done alters it like the master.

## \|\| 1.61.22 \|\|

*svakṛtānyupatiṣṭhaṃti sukhaduḥkhāni dehinām \|*  
*hetubhūto hi yasteṣāṃ so'haṃkāreṇa badhyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The happiness and misery of embodied beings depend on their own acts. He who is the cause thereof is bound to them by Ahaṃkāra (feeling of I and mine).

## \|\| 1.61.23 \|\|

*suśīghramabhidhāvantaṃ nijaṃ karmānudhāvati \|*  
*śete saha śayānena tiṣṭhantamanutiṣṭhati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. One’s own action pursues one, even if one runs very fast: when one lies down the action too lies down and when one stands it too stands by.

## \|\| 1.61.24 \|\|

*yathā chāyātapau nityaṃ susaṃbaddhau parasparam \|*  
*tathā karma ca kartā ca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Just as shade and sunshine are well inter-related, so also action and doer. No worry need be entertained in this regard.

## \|\| 1.61.25 \|\|

*yena yatropabhoktavyaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhameva vā \|*  
*naraḥ sa baddho rajjveva balāttatraiva nīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If a man is destined to experience happiness or misery in any sphere, he is led there by force like one bound by ropes.

## \|\| 1.61.26 \|\|

*pramāṇaṃ karmabhūtānāṃ sukhaduḥkhopapādane \|*  
*sāvadhānatayā yacca jāgratāṃ svapatāmapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Karma is the authority to bring happiness and misery to living beings even when they are watchfully alert or continue to sleep.

## \|\| 1.61.27 \|\|

*tailakṣaye yathā dīpo nirvāṇamadhigacchati \|*  
*karmakṣaye tathā jaṃturnirvāṇamadhigacchati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Just as a lamp goes out when oil is used up, so also a creature is liberated when Karma is exhausted.

## \|\| 1.61.28 \|\|

*na mantrā na tapo dānaṃ na tīrthaṃ na ca saṃyamaḥ \|*  
*samarthā rakṣituṃ jaṃtuṃ pīḍitaṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Neither Mantras nor penance, neither Dāna nor Tīrtha nor even perfect self-control can be competent to save a creature afflicted by the previous Karmas.

## \|\| 1.61.29 \|\|

*saṃgatyā jaṭhare nyasto retobinduracetanaḥ \|*  
*ṛtukāle manuṣyeṇa vṛddhiṃ gacchati karmataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. An insentient drop of semen deposited in a womb by intercourse during the prescribed menstrual period by a man grows up in accordance with the previous Karma.

## \|\| 1.61.30 \|\|

*annapānāni jīryaṃti yatra bhakṣyaṃ ca bhakṣitam \|*  
*tasminnevodare garbhaḥ kathaṃ nāma na jīryati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Why does not the foetus get dissolved in the very same belly where foodstuffs and beverages get digested, what is eaten gets dissolved?

## \|\| 1.61.31 \|\|

*tasmātkarmakṛtaṃ sarvaṃ dehināmatra jāyate \|*  
*śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpamiti me niścayaḥ sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Hence this is my decision once and for all that the merit and sin of embodied beings is the result of the action done.

## \|\| 1.61.32 \|\|

*arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daivarakṣitaṃ surakṣitaṃ daivahataṃ vinaśyati \|*  
*jīvatyanātho'pi vane visarjitaḥ kṛtaprayatno'pi gṛhe na jīvati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. What is apparently unprotected stands firm when protected by fate; what is well guarded perishes when struck by fate. A seemingly helpless person left in forest survives but one well protected in the house may not continue to live.

## Chapter 62 - Greatness of Śarmiṣṭhā Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.62.1 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā pārthivo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*nātyajattāṃ tathokto'pi daivajñairviṣakanyakām \|*  
*dīyamānāmapi prītyā na ca gṛhṇāti bhūbhujā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. That king decided thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. He did not abandon that Viṣakanyakā though advised by the astrologers.

## \|\| 1.62.2 \|\|

*śarmaṇaṣṭhīvanaṃ yasmāttayā svapiturāhitam \|*  
*śarmiṣṭheti suvikhyātā tataḥ sā hyabhavadbhuvi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She became well known by the name Śarmiṣṭhā as she was like spittle (Ṣṭhīvana) of happiness (Śarman) that had been thrown out by the father. She was being given by the king lovingly but none accepted her.

## \|\| 1.62.3 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasya śatravaḥ pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*sarvataḥ pīḍayāmāsa rāṣṭraṃ krodhasamanvitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the meantime the enemies of that king angrily attacked him and the kingdom from all sides.

## \|\| 1.62.4 \|\|

*athā sau pārthivaḥ kruddhaḥ svasainyaparivāritaḥ \|*  
*yuddhāya niryayau sthānānmṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartane \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The enraged king set off from his place surrounded by his army for a fight thinking that if he were to return it would be (no better than) death.

## \|\| 1.62.5 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃprāpya tāñchatrūṃścakāra sa mahāhavam \|*  
*caturaṃgena sainyena yamarāṣṭravivardhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He fell upon the enemies and fought a great battle with his army consisting of four divisions and increased the population in the country of Yama (by killing enemies).

## \|\| 1.62.6 \|\|

*tataśca daśame prāpte śatrubhiḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*nihato divase sarvairveṣṭayitvā samantataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the tenth day all his enemies encircled him and killed him.

## \|\| 1.62.7 \|\|

*tatastasya narendrasya hataśeṣāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*bhayārtāste drutaṃ jagmuḥ svapuraṃ prati duḥkhitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The men of that king who survived the battle, were frightened and distressed. They fled to the city quickly.

## \|\| 1.62.8 \|\|

*tepi śatrugaṇāḥ sarve saṃprahṛṣṭā jigīṣavaḥ \|*  
*tatpuraṃ veṣṭayāmāsustatputrocchedanāya vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All the hosts of the enemies were highly delighted. Desirous of gaining further victory they besieged the city in order to exterminate his sons.

## \|\| 1.62.9 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare paurāḥ sarve śokaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*jagarhuḥ paruṣairvākyairduṣṭāṃ tāṃ viṣakanyakām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the meantime all the citizens in the height of their grief rebuked and reviled the wicked Viṣakanyakā with very harsh words.

## \|\| 1.62.10-13 \|\|

*asyā doṣeṇa pāpāyā mṛtaśca sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tathā rāṣṭrasya vidhvaṃse bhaviṣyati puraḥ kṣayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*uktaḥ sa nṛpatiḥ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇairjñānibhistadā \|*  
*tyajaināṃ bahudoṣāḍhyāṃ ninditāṃ viṣakanyakām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*na tena tatkṛtaṃ vākyamapi teṣāṃ hitaiṣiṇām \|*  
*snehapāśanibaddhena dayāḍhyena mahātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmādadyāpi pāpaiṣā vadhyatāmāśu kanyakā \|*  
*niryāsyatāṃ purādasmādyāvanna syātpurakṣayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. “It was the result of the (ominous) defect of this sinful girl that the king died. The annihilation of the country will follow the ruin of the (capital) city. The king too had been told then by the learned Brāhmaṇas: ‘Abandon this censured Viṣakanyakā who is full of many defects.’ But the noble-minded, compassionate king was fettered by bonds of affection. So he did not abide by the advice even of those well-wishers. Hence, at least now, let this sinful girl be killed quickly or banished from the city lest the city should be ruined.”

## \|\| 1.62.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sāpi śrutvā janoktāṃstānapavādānpṛthagvidhān \|*  
*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gatvā niṃdāṃ cakre tathātmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. She too heard the diverse kinds of derogatory remarks of the people. She became disgusted much and censured herself.

## \|\| 1.62.15 \|\|

*tato rātrau viniṣkramya bhayaśokasamanvitā \|*  
*pratasthe'raṇyamāsādya maraṇe kṛtaniścayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Filled with terror and grief, she went out at night and proceeded towards the forest where she had determined to die.

## \|\| 1.62.16 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭaṃ tayā kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarajaṃ mahat \|*  
*tapasvibhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ cittāhlādakaraṃ param \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the great sacred place of Hāṭakeśvara was seen by her. It gave much solace to her mind as it was filled with sages.

## \|\| 1.62.17-18 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ smṛtirjātā pūrvajanmasamudbhavā \|*  
*caṃḍālatve mayā pūrvaṃ gaurekā vitṛṣīkṛtā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tatprabhāvādahaṃ jātā supuṇye nṛpamaṃdire \|*  
*kṣetrasyāsya prabhāvena tasmādatraiva me sthitiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Thereupon, she recollected the incidents of the previous birth: “As a Cāṇḍāla woman I had quenched the thirst of a cow. By its power I was reborn in the palace of a king. It was due to the power of this holy spot. Hence I shall stay here only.”

## \|\| 1.62.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*anyadehāṃtare hyāsīccaṃḍālī sā vigarhitā \|*  
*bahuprasūtisaṃyuktā daridreṇa kadarthitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. In the previous birth she was a despicable Cāṇḍāla woman distressed with poverty and overburdened with many children.

## \|\| 1.62.20 \|\|

*atha sā bhramamāṇā'tra kṣetre prāptā tṛṣārditā \|*  
*madhyaṃdinagatesūrye jyeṣṭhamāse sudāruṇe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the course of her ramblings she came to this holy spot. She was overcome with thirst. It was the time when the Sun was overhead at midday in that terrible (very hot) month of Jyeṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.62.21 \|\|

*athāpaśyatstokajalāṃ sā tatra laghukūpikām \|*  
*tṛṣārtāṃ kapilāṃ gāṃ vartamānāṃ tadāṃ tike \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. She saw a small well with very little water. Near it she saw a tawny-coloured cow standing by.

## \|\| 1.62.22 \|\|

*tato dayāṃ samāśritya tyaktvā snehaṃ sutodbhavam \|*  
*ātmanaśca tathā prāṇāngāṃ vitṛṣṇāmathākarot \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the height of her compassion she left off all thoughts of love to her children and her own life. She made (allowed) the cow to quench her thirst.

## \|\| 1.62.23 \|\|

*jalābhāve tathā sā ca samastairbālakaiḥ saha \|*  
*vaivasvatagṛhaṃ prāptā gobhaktidhṛtamānasā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Her mind had been swayed by devotion to the cow. Due to the lack of water she met with death along with the children.

## \|\| 1.62.24 \|\|

*tato nṛpagṛhe jātā tatprabhāvāddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pūrvakarmavipākena saṃjātā viṣa kanyakā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, she was reborn in the palace of a king by the power thereof; but she was born as a Viṣakanyakā as an inevitable result of the previous Karma.

## \|\| 1.62.25 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kena karmavipākena saṃjātā viṣakanyakā \|*  
*svakulocchedanakarī sarvaṃ sūta bravīhi naḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

The sages said:

25\. What was that Karma as the inevitable result of which she was reborn as a Viṣakanyakā? She had exterminated her own family. O Sūta, narrate everything to us.

## \|\| 1.62.26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*caṃḍālatve tayā viprā vartaṃtyā bhramamāṇayā \|*  
*devatāyatane dṛṣṭā gaurī hemamayī śubhā \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sūta said:

26\. O Brāhmaṇas, even as she was rambling as a Cāṇḍāla woman, she went into a temple where there was a splendid gold image of Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.62.27 \|\|

*tatastāṃ vijane prāpya gatvā deśāṃtaraṃ mudā \|*  
*yāvatkaroti khaṃḍāni vikrayārthaṃ suniṃditā \|*  
*tāvadanveṣamāṇāstāṃ saṃprāptā nṛpasevakāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That being a deserted place, she got hold of the gold image joyously and went to another country. The despicable woman wanted to cut the image into pieces for selling. Even as she was engaged in it the officers of the king who had been searching for her overtook her.

## \|\| 1.62.28 \|\|

*atha te tāṃ samālokya bhartsayitvā muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*saṃtāḍya lakuṭāghātairloṣṭaghātaiśca muṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On meeting her they rebuked hex repeatedly and hit her with their fists, pelted with clods and struck her with sticks.

## \|\| 1.62.29 \|\|

*tataḥ suvarṇamādāya tyaktvā tāṃ rudhiraplutām \|*  
*avadhyaiṣeti saṃciṃtya svapuraṃ prati te gatāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They seized the gold and left her in a pool of blood. Thinking that she (being a woman) should not be killed thus, they returned to the city.

## \|\| 1.62.30 \|\|

*yattayā pārvatī spṛṣṭā tato vai khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtā \|*  
*tena karmavipākena saṃjātā viṣakanyakā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. She had touched (and defiled) the image of Pārvatī. Further she cut it into pieces. It was a result of this evil deed that she was reborn as a Viṣakanyā.

## \|\| 1.62.31 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃsmṛtimāsādya pūrvajanmasamudbhavām \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ jaladānasya gopītasya vicārya ca \|*  
*cakāra kūpikāsthāne taḍāgaṃ vimalodakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. She then recollected the incidents of this previous birth. Pondering over the greatness of the gift of water drunk by the cow she now dug a big lake of clear water in the place of the earlier small well.

## \|\| 1.62.32-33 \|\|

*samudrapratimaṃ cāru padminīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*matsyakacchapasaṃkīrṇaṃ śiśumāravirājitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sevitaṃ bahubhirhaṃsairbakaiścakraiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*agādhasalilaṃ puṇyaṃ sevitaṃ jalajaṃtubhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. It was a big lake like a sea. It was beautifully embellished with clusters of lotuses. Fish and turtles abounded in it and porpoises added to its glory. Many swans, cranes anḍ ruddy geese resorted to it all round. The water was unfathomable and the aquatic creatures took delight therein.

## \|\| 1.62.34 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ tatsamīpasthaṃ sādhu dṛṣṭimanoharam \|*  
*kārayitvātisaṃbhaktyā kailāsaśikharopamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. With great devotion she got a charming mansion lofty like a peak of Kailāsa erected near it pleasing to the eyes of the good.

## \|\| 1.62.35 \|\|

*tatastatra tapastepe gaurīṃ saṃsthāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tadagre vratamāsthāya yathoktaṃ śāstra saṃbhavam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then she devoutly installed Gaurī and performed a penance. Before the goddess she observed the Vrata as laid down in the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.62.36 \|\|

*prātaḥ snātvā tu hemaṃte gaurīṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*balipūjopahāraiśca vipradānādibhistathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Even in Hemanta (early winter) she used to take bath in the morning and worship Gaurī devoutly with adoration and offerings of oblations and making gifts to Brāhmaṇas and the like.

## \|\| 1.62.37 \|\|

*tataśca śiśire prāpte sāyaṃ prātaḥ samāhitā \|*  
*ekāṃtaropavāsaiḥ sā snānaṃ cakre nṛpātmajā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. That princess used to take bath both in the morning and in the evening during Śiśira (late winter) with great mental concentration and purity. She used to observe fast on alternate days.

## \|\| 1.62.38 \|\|

*vasaṃte nṛtyagītaiśca toṣayāmāsa pārvatīm \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhakālāśanā sādhvī sasyadānaparā yaṇā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. During spring season the pious lady propitiated Pārvatī through dances and songs. She used to take food only once in six times (i.e. in three days). She was engrossed in making gifts of food-grains.

## \|\| 1.62.39 \|\|

*pañcāgnisādhakā grīṣme phalāhāraṃ tapasvinī \|*  
*cakāra śraddhayopetā vṛkabhūmipateḥ sutā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The daughter of king Vṛka endowed with great faith performed penance in the midst of five fires during summer. Fruits alone constituted her diet.

## \|\| 1.62.40 \|\|

*varṣāsu ca jalāhārā bhūtvā sā viṣa kanyakā \|*  
*ākāśe śayanaṃ cakre parityaktakuṭīrakā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. During rainy season water constituted her intake. The Viṣakanyā abandoned her hut and lay down under the open sky.

## \|\| 1.62.41 \|\|

*vāyubhakṣā satī cā'tha sā'nayaccharadaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*kṛtajapyaparā nityaṃ pārvatīgatamānasā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then she spent autumn by taking in only air. She was always engaged in Japa with her mind meditating on Pārvatī.

## \|\| 1.62.42 \|\|

*evamārādhayaṃtyāśca tasyā devīṃ gireḥ sutām \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālo na lebhe phalamīhitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Even as she continued to propitiate thus, the goddess, the daughter of the Mountain, a long time elapsed; but she did not obtain any desired benefit.

## \|\| 1.62.43 \|\|

*mukhaṃ valibhirākrāntaṃ palitairaṃkitaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*kanyābhāvepi vartaṃtyā na ca tuṣṭā harapriyā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Continuing her state of virginity, her face was full of wrinkles and her head was marked with greying hairs; but the Beloved of Hara did not get pleased (with her).

## \|\| 1.62.44 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tatparīkṣārthameva sā \|*  
*śakrāṇīrūpamāsthāya tataḥ sandarśanaṃ gatā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After some time had elapsed, once the goddess adopted the form of Śakrāṇī in order to test her. Thus she appeared before the princess.

## \|\| 1.62.45-46 \|\|

*sudhāvadātaṃ sūryābhaṃ kailāsaśikharopamam \|*  
*supralaṃbakaraṃ mattaṃ caturdaṃtaṃ mahāgajam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*samāsthāya vṛtā strībhirdevānāṃ sarvato diśam \|*  
*dadhatī mukuṭaṃ mūrdhni hārakeyūrabhūṣitā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. She was seated on a great elephant with four tusks and a very long trunk. It could be compared to the peak of Kailāsa. It resembled the Sun in lustre. It was as white as lime powder and in the state of rut.

She was surrounded on all sides by the wives of Devas. She was adorned with necklaces and bracelets and she wore a crown on her head.

## \|\| 1.62.47 \|\|

*pāṃḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani \|*  
*sevyamānā'psarobhiśca stūyamānā ca kinnaraiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A white umbrella was held above her head. She was attended upon by celestial damsels and was eulogized by Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.62.48-50 \|\|

*gandharvairgīyamānāsīttataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*varaṃ yacchāmi te putri prārthayasva yathepsitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*anena tapasā tuṣṭā puṣkalena tavādhunā \|*  
*ahaṃ bhāryā surendrasya śacīti parikīrtitā \|*  
*trailokye'pi svayaṃ prāptā dayāṃ kṛtvā tavopari \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tvayā mahattapastaptaṃ dhyāyaṃtyā haravallabhām \|*  
*tapasā tuṣṭimāyātā bhavānī na suniṣṭhurā \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. She was sung about by Gandharvas. She then spoke respectfully, “O daughter, I shall grant a boon unto you. Request for whatever you desire.”

I am the wife of the Lord of Suras and am glorified as Śacī in all the three worlds. Now I am pleased with this excellent penance of yours. Taking pity on you, I have myself come to you.

A great penance has been performed by you meditating on the Beloved of Hara. Yet the highly ruthless Bhavānī has not become pleased by your penance (so seek a boon from me).”

## \|\| 1.62.51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā tasyā vacanaṃ śrutvā śakrāṇyā viṣakanyakā \|*  
*namaskṛtvā'tha tāmūce kṛtāṃjalipuṭā sthitā \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

51\. On hearing the words of Śakrānī the Viṣakanyakā bowed down to her, standing with palms joined in reverence and spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.62.52 \|\|

*viṣakanyovāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ tvatto varaṃ devi prārthayāmi kathañcana \|*  
*tathānyāsāmapīṃdrāṇi devatānāmasaṃśayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

The Viṣakanyā said:

52\. O goddess, I don’t intend to request you for anything. Similarly, O Indrāṇī, I don’t wish to request other deities too. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.62.53 \|\|

*apyahaṃ narakaṃ raudraṃ pragacchāmīṃdravallabhe \|*  
*harakāṃtā samādeśānna svarge'pi tavājñayā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O beloved of Indra, I may go to a hideous Naraka by the command of the wife of Hara; but I will not go even to heaven by your command.

## \|\| 1.62.54 \|\|

*anādimadhyaparyyantā jñānaiśvaryasama nvitā \|*  
*yā devī pūjyate devairvaraṃ tasyā vṛṇomyaham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I will choose a boon from that goddess who is adored by Devas, who has neither a beginning, nor a middle nor an end and who is endowed with glory and perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.62.55 \|\|

*yāmārādhayate viṣṇurbrahmā rudraśca vāsavaḥ \|*  
*vāṃchitārthaṃ sadā devīṃ varaṃ tasyā vṛṇo myaham \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I will choose a boon from that goddess whom Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra and Vāsava propitiate. I will seek the object I desire from that goddess alone.

## \|\| 1.62.56 \|\|

*yayā vyāptamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*strīrūpairvividhairdevyā varaṃ tasyā vṛṇomyaham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I will choose a boon from that goddess by whom the entire range of the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings, is pervaded by means of diverse kinds of female forms.

## \|\| 1.62.57 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ bhāryā surendrasya prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*mamājñāṃ pālayanti sma devadānavapannagāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

57\. I am the wife of the Lord of Suras. I am dearer to him than his life. Devas, Dānavas and Pannagas obey my order.

## \|\| 1.62.58 \|\|

*kiṃnarā guhkā yakṣāḥ kiṃ punarmartyadharmiṇaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ kiṃ na gṛhṇāsi varaṃ mattaḥ kutāpasi \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Kinnaras, Guhyakas and Yakṣas too obey. Then why not those of mortal activities? So, O bad ascetic woman, why don’t you receive a boon from me?

## \|\| 1.62.59-64 \|\|

*tannūnaṃ vajraghātena cūrṇayiṣyāmi te śiraḥ \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā tāpasyatha tato dvijāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dhairyamālaṃbya tāṃ prāha bhūya eva sureśvarīm \|*  
*svāminī tvaṃ hi devānāṃ satyametadasaṃśayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*yasyāḥ prāptaṃ tvayaiśvaryaṃ parā tāṃ toṣayāmyaham \|*  
*svalpamapyaparādhaṃ te na karomi sureśvari \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tathāpi vadhayogyāṃ māṃ manyase vikṣipāyudham \|*  
*anyaccāpi vaco mahyaṃ śakrāṇi śṛṇu sādaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tacchutvā kuru yacchreyo vicintya manasā tataḥ \|*  
*na tvaṃ na te patiḥ śakro na cānyepi surāsurāḥ \|*  
*māṃ niṣūdayituṃ śaktāḥ pārvatyāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatām \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tasmāddrutaṃ divaṃ gaccha mā tvaṃ kopaṃ vṛthā kuru \|*  
*sanmārge vartamānāyāṃ mama sarvasureśvari \|\| 64 \|\|*

59-60a. Hence I shall certainly shatter your head with a blow of the thunderbolt.

60b-64. O Brāhmaṇas, on hearing her words the ascetic woman took enough courage to tell the goddess of Suras once again: “You are the mistress of Devas. This is undoubtedly true. I am propitiating that supreme goddess from whom you have received your power and glory. O goddess of Suras, even the least of a fault has not been perpetrated against you by me. Still, if you consider me as one deserving death, do hurl the weapon. O Śakrāṇī, do listen attentively to another word of mine also. On hearing it, you ponder over it fully and do what is beneficient. Neither you, nor your husband Śakra nor the other Suras and Asuras are capable of slaying me, as I have sought refuge in Pārvatī. So hasten to heaven kindly; do not waste your fury over me, O goddess of all Suras, as I strictly abide by the right path.

## \|\| 1.62.65 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sā tāṃ śacīmuktvā duḥkhitā viṣakanyakā \|*  
*cintayāmāsa tadidaṃ maraṇe kṛtaniścayā \|\| 65 \|\|*

Sūta said:

65\. After saying this to Śacī, the miserable Viṣakanyā decided to die and thought thus:

## \|\| 1.62.66-70 \|\|

*na prasīdati me devī yasmātparvatanaṃdinī \|*  
*tasmānmāṃ yadi śakrāṇī naiṣā vyāpādayiṣyati \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tannūnaṃ jvalanaṃ dīptaṃ sevayiṣyāmi satvaram \|*  
*athāpaśyatkṣaṇenaiva taṃ cairāvaṇavāraṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*dugdhakuṃdendusaṃkāśaṃ saṃjātaṃ sahasā vṛṣam \|*  
*tasyopari sthitāṃ devīṃ śaṃbhunā saha pārvatīm \|\| 68 \|\|*

*caturbhujāṃ prasannāsyāṃ divyarūpasamanvitām \|*  
*śuklamālyāṃbaradharāṃ candrārdhakṛtamastakām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tataḥ samyaksamālokya jñātvā tāṃ parvatātmajām \|*  
*viṣakanyā stutiṃ cakre praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

66-70. ‘Since the goddess, the Daughter of the Mountain is not pleased with me, and if this Śakrāṇī too does not kill me, I shall certainly resort to the burning fire immediately.’ Thereafter she saw presently the elephant Airāvaṇa turning all of a sudden into the Bull having complexon like milk, jasmine and moon. She saw Goddess Pārvatī seated on it along with Śambhu. The goddess had four arms. Her face was beaming pleasantly in her divine form. She was wearing white garlands and garments. The crettent moon adorned her forehead. Then the Viṣakanyā looked at her closely and realized that it was Pārvatī the unborn. Then she repeatedly bowed down and eulogized.

Prayer of Viṣakanyā:

## \|\| 1.62.71 \|\|

*namaste devadeveśi namaste sarvavāsini \|*  
*sarvakāmaprade satye jarāmaraṇavarjite \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. “Obeisance to you, O goddess of the chiefs of Devas. Obeisance to you, O goddess abiding in everything, O truthful goddess devoid of old age and death, O bestower of everything desired.

## \|\| 1.62.72 \|\|

*śakrādayo'pi devāste paramārthena no viduḥ \|*  
*svarūpavarṇanaṃ kartuṃ kiṃ punardevi mānuṣī \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O goddess, even Śakra and other gods do not know how to extol your real form. How can I, a mortal woman, do it?

## \|\| 1.62.73 \|\|

*yasyāḥ sarvaṃ mahīvyomajalāgnipavanātmakam \|*  
*brahmāṃḍamaṃgasaṃbhūtaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You are the goddess from whose person was born the Cosmic Egg constituted of Earth, Ether, Water, Fire and Air and consisting of Devas, Asuras and human beings.

## \|\| 1.62.74 \|\|

*na tasyā janmani brahmā na nāśāya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pālanāya na goviṃdastāṃ tvāṃ stoṣyāmyahaṃ katham \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Brahmā is not competent to give birth to her; Maheśvara is not competent to destroy her; and Govinda is not competent to protect her. How can I adequately eulogize you?

## \|\| 1.62.75 \|\|

*tathāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ yasyāḥ svābhāvikaṃ param \|*  
*nirastātiśayaṃ loke spṛhaṇīyatamaṃ sadā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. You are the goddess who are the possessor of the highest eightfold perfection by your very nature; which has nothing superior to it in the world, and is always the most desirable thing.

## \|\| 1.62.76 \|\|

*yasyā rūpāṇyanekāni samyagdhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*dhyāyaṃti munayo bhaktyā prāpnuvaṃti ca vāṃchitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. You are the goddess whose diverse forms the sages engaged in perfect meditation think of devoutly and obtain what they desire.

## \|\| 1.62.77-78 \|\|

*hṛdi saṃkalpya yadrūpaṃ dhyānenārcaṃti yoginaḥ \|*  
*samyagbhāvātmakaiḥ puṣpairmokṣāya kṛta niścayāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tāṃ devīṃ mānuṣī bhūtvā kathaṃ staumi maheśvarīm \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. The Yogins who are determined to attain salvation conceive your form in the heart and adore it by means of the flowers of genuine sentiments. Being a human being, how can I eulogize that Maheśvari?

## \|\| 1.62.79 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭāsmi te putri varaṃ prārthaya suvrate \|*  
*asaṃdigdhaṃ pradāsyāmi yatte hṛdi sadā sthitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

The Devī said:

79\. O daughter, I am happy with you. O lady of excellent Vratas, choose your boon. I shall grant you certainly what has been cherished for ever in your heart.

## \|\| 1.62.80 \|\|

*viṣakanyovāca \|*  
*bharturarthe mayā devi kṛto'yaṃ tapaudyamaḥ \|*  
*tatkiṃ tena kariṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ jarayāvṛtā \|\| 80 \|\|*

Viṣakanyā said:

80\. It was for the sake of (obtaining) a husband that I endeavoured thus, O goddess, by means of the penance. Now that I have been overcome by old age, what can I do with him?

## \|\| 1.62.81 \|\|

*tasmādatrā'śrame sākaṃ tvayā stheyaṃ sadaiva tu \|*  
*hitāya sarvanārīṇāṃ vacanānmama pārvati \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Hence I shall have to stay here in this hermitage for ever along with you. O Pārvatī, at my instance and for the welfare of all women you must stay here always.

## \|\| 1.62.82 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛtyahaṃ bhadre śreṣṭhe'sminnāśrame śubhe \|*  
*svamāśramaṃ kariṣyāmi yatte hṛdi samāśritam \|\| 82 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

82\. O fair lady, from now onwards, I shall make my hermitage in this excellent and auspicious penance grove of yours. (I Hope) this has been thought of by you within the heart.

## \|\| 1.62.83 \|\|

*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ yā 'tra snānaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*nārī sā matprasādena lapsyate vāṃchitaṃ phalam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. A woman who takes her holy bath here on the third lunar day in the bright half of Māgha, shall, due to my favour, obtain the desired benefit.

## \|\| 1.62.84 \|\|

*api kṛtvā mahāpāpaṃ nārī vā puruṣo'thavā \|*  
*yatra snātvā prasādānme vipāpmā saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Even after committing great sins, a woman or a man shall,with my favour, be free from sins after taking the holy bath here.

## \|\| 1.62.85 \|\|

*atra ye phaladānaṃ ca prakariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*saphalāḥ sakalāsteṣāmāśāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. If men make gifts of fruit here, all their hopes and expectations shall become fruitful undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.62.86 \|\|

*api hatvā striyaṃ martyo yo'tra snānaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ vipāpmā sa bhaviṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Even after killing a woman, a man who takes his holy bath here on the third lunar day in the bright half of Māgha, shall become free from sins.

## \|\| 1.62.87 \|\|

*yā tatra kanyakā bhadre snānaṃ bhaktyā kari ṣyati \|*  
*tasmindine patiśreṣṭhaṃ lapsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. O fair lady, a girl who takes her holy bath on that day with great devotion shall undoubtedly obtain an excell ant husband.

## \|\| 1.62.88 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā tato gaurī tāṃ ca pasparśa pāṇinā \|*  
*tataśca tatkṣaṇājjātā divyarūpavapurddharā \|\| 88 \|\|*

Sūta said:

88\. After saying this, Gaurī touched her with her hand. Thereby she instantly became one possessing a divine form.

## \|\| 1.62.89 \|\|

*vṛddhatvena parityaktā divyamālyānulepanā \|*  
*pīnonnatakucābhogā pramattagajagāminī \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Old age disappeared from her. She had divine garlands and unguents. With protruding thick bosom, she became a woman with the gait of an elephant in rut.

## \|\| 1.62.90 \|\|

*tatastāṃ sā samādāya vidhāya nijakiṃkarīm \|*  
*kailāsaṃ parvataśreṣṭhaṃ jagāma harasaṃyutā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then she made her own maid. Taking her she went to Kailāsa, the excellent mountain, along with Hara.

## \|\| 1.62.91 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ śarmiṣṭhātīrthamucyate \|*  
*prakhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Ever since then that Tīrtha is called Śarmiṣṭhā Tīrtha. It is well-known in all the three worlds as one that destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.62.92 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ yathāvaddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, one should duly take one’s holy bath there assiduously on the third lunar day in the bright half of Māgha.

## \|\| 1.62.93 \|\|

*etatpavitramāyuṣyaṃ sarva pātakanāśanam \|*  
*strītīrthasaṃbhavaṃ nṝṇāṃ māhātmyaṃ yanmayoditam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. This narration of mine of the greatness of the Strītīrtha is sacred, conducive to longevity and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.62.94 \|\|

*yaścaitatprātarutthāya sadā paṭhati mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa sarvāṃllabhate kāmānmanasā vāṃchitānsadā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. A man who gets up early in the morning always and reads this, shall obtain all desires of his mind.

## \|\| 1.62.95 \|\|

*tathā parvaṇi saṃprāpte yaścaitatpaṭhate naraḥ \|*  
*śṛṇoti cāśu bhaktyā yaḥ sa yāti śivamaṃdiram \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Similarly a man who reads this or listens to this on festive occasions with devotion, shall go to Śiva’s palace.

## Chapter 63 - Greatness of Somanātha

## \|\| 1.63.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha someśvarākhyaṃ ca tatra liṃgaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*asti khyātaṃ triloke'tra svayaṃ somena nirmitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*somavāreṇa yastatra vatsaraṃ yāvadarcayet \|*
