*kṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sa rogeṇa dāruṇenāpi mucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yakṣmaṇāpi na saṃdehaḥ kiṃ punaḥ kuṣṭhapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena rogārttastaṃ prapūjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Now there is an excellent Liṅga there named Someśvara. It is well known in all the three worlds. It was installed here by the Moon-god himself.

One who makes it a point to stay there for a year and adores it on every Monday, becomes relieved even of awful ailments.

There is no doubt that he is relieved of even tuberculosis, leaving aside (smaller ailments, like) leprosy etc. Hence by all means a man distressed with ailments should worship it.

## \|\| 1.63.4 \|\|

*tadārādhya purā somaḥ kṣayavyādhisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*babhūva nīrugdeho'sau yathā pāṃḍyo narādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly the Moon-god propitiated it when he was afflicted by the ailment of tuberculosis. He became one with a body free from ailments like King Pāṇḍya.

## \|\| 1.63.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*oṣadhīnāmadhīśasya kathaṃ somasya sūtaja \|*  
*kṣayavyādhiḥ purā jātā upaśāṃtiṃ kathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. O Sūtaja, how did Soma, the Lord of the medicinal herbs, become afflicted by tuberculosis formerly. How did he get the relief?

## \|\| 1.63.6 \|\|

*etannaḥ sarvamācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmate \|*  
*tathā tasya mahīpasya pāṃḍyasyāpi kathāṃ śubhām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O highly intelligent one, narrate this to us in detail. So also relate the auspicious story of that Pāṇḍya king.

## \|\| 1.63.7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dakṣasya kanyakāḥ pūrvaṃ saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*upayeme niśānātho devāgnigurusaṃnidhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7\. Formerly the Lord of night (Moon) married in the presence of Fire-god and Guru (Preceptor, Bṛhaspati), the twentyseven daughters of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.63.8 \|\|

*nakṣatrasaṃjñitā loke kīrtyaṃte yā dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*daivajñairaśvinīpūrvā rūpaudāryaguṇānvitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They are being glorified by excellent Brāhmaṇas well-versed in astrology by the name Nakṣatra (Star). Of them Aśvinī is the first. All of them are endowed with qualities like beauty, liberal-mindedness etc.

## \|\| 1.63.9 \|\|

*atha tāsāṃ samastānāṃ madhye tasya niśāpateḥ \|*  
*rohiṇī vallabhā jajñe prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Out of them all, Rohiṇī was the most beloved to the Lord of night, dearer than his own life.

## \|\| 1.63.10 \|\|

*tataḥ samaṃ parityajya sarvāstā dakṣakanyakāḥ \|*  
*rohiṇyā saha saṃyuktaḥ saṃbabhūva divāniśam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence he abandoned all the other daughters of Dakṣa and stayed with Rohiṇī day and night.

## \|\| 1.63.11 \|\|

*tatastāḥ kāma saṃtaptā daurbhāgyena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*procurduḥkhānvitā dakṣaṃ gatvā bāṣpaplutānanāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hence all of them who had thus become unfortunate became all the more distressed with passion (love). They went to Dakṣa with faces drenched with tears and said;

## \|\| 1.63.12 \|\|

*vayaṃ yasmai tvayā dattāḥ patnyarthaṃ tāta pāpine \|*  
*ṛtumātramapi prītyā so'smākaṃ na prayacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “Dear father, we have been given by you to a sinner as his wife. He does not lovingly give us (enjoyment) even on the Ṛtu days (i.e. prescribed days after the menstrual flow, for cohabitation).

## \|\| 1.63.13 \|\|

*tasmātprāṇānvihāsyāmaḥ saṃpraviśya hutāśanam \|*  
*avilaṃbānmahābhāga satyaṃ brūmastavāgrataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence we shall cast off our lives entering fire ere long. O highly exalted one, we are telling you the truth.”

## \|\| 1.63.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣo duḥkhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sarvāstāḥ svayamādāya jagāma śaśisaṃnidhau \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. On hearing their words, Dakṣa was also distressed. He himself took them all and went to Śaśin (Moon-god).

## \|\| 1.63.15 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca so'nvakṣaṃ tāsāṃ dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*bhartsayanparuṣairvākyairniśānāthaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the presence of all of them, Dakṣa, the Prajāpati (Patriarch), spoke to the Lord of night, rebuking him repeatedly with very harsh words:

## \|\| 1.63.16-18 \|\|

*kimidaṃ yujyate kartuṃ tvayā rātripate'dhama \|*  
*karma mūḍha satāṃ bāhya dharmaśāstravigarhitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ṛtukāle'pi saṃprāpte sutā mama samudbhavāḥ \|*  
*yanna saṃbhāṣasi prītyā dharmaśāstraṃ na vetsi kim \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṛtu snātāṃ tu yo bhāryāṃ saṃnidhau nopagacchati \|*  
*ghorāyāṃ bhrūṇahatyāyāṃ yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. “O base Lord of night, O foolish one, is this proper on your part to do. It is what is censured in the Dharmaśāstras (codes of ethics), O base one excluded by the good. Even when the Ṛtu days come, you do not speak lovingly to my daughters. Don’t you know Dharmaśāstra? One who does not go to his wife after she has had Ṛtu bath undoubtedly incurs the awful sin of foeticide.”

## \|\| 1.63.19 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā salajjo rātrināyakaḥ \|*  
*provācādhomukho dakṣaṃ prakariṣye vacastava \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing his words, the Lord of night became ashamed. With face bent down, he spoke to Dakṣa: “I shall carry out your behest.”

## \|\| 1.63.20 \|\|

*tato hṛṣṭamanā dakṣaḥ sutāḥ sarvā himadyute \|*  
*nivedyāmaṃtrya taṃ paścājjagāma nijamaṃdiram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereupon, Dakṣa became delighted in his mind. He left all his daughters to the care of the cool-rayed Moon, took leave of him and went back to his own abode.

## \|\| 1.63.21 \|\|

*candro'pi pūrvavatsarvāstāḥ parityajya dakṣajāḥ \|*  
*rohiṇyā saha saṃsargaṃ pracakārānurāgataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. But Candra did everything as before. He ignored all other daughters of Dakṣa and continued his passionate association solely with Rohiṇī.

## \|\| 1.63.22 \|\|

*atha tā duḥkhitā bhūyo jagmuryatra pitā sthitaḥ \|*  
*procuśca bāṣpapūrṇākṣāstatkālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then all those miserable ones again went to their father and spoke to him with tears in their eyes, words befitting that occasion:

## \|\| 1.63.23-26 \|\|

*etattāta mahadduḥkhamasmākaṃ vartate hṛdi \|*  
*yaddaurbhāgyaṃ prasaṃjātaṃ sarvastrījanagarhitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yatpunastvaṃ kṛtastena kāmukena durātmanā \|*  
*vyarthaśramo'pramāṇīva kṛte'smākaṃ gataḥ svayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadduḥkhaṃ na vayaṃ śaktā hṛdi dhartuṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*ramate sa hi rohiṇyā caṃdramāḥ sahito'niśam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*viśeṣāttava vākyena niṣiddho rātrināyakaḥ \|*  
*anujñāṃ dehi tasmāttvamasmākaṃ tatra sāṃpratam \|*  
*daurbhāgyaduḥkhasaṃtaptāstyajāmo yena jīvitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. “O father, this is our greatest sorrow in our heart that a misfortune hated by all women has befallen us.

Your effort has been rendered ineffective by that lecherous fellow of wicked soul. Your authority has been flouted by him in our case.

We cannot bear in our heart that misery at all. That Candramas is diverting himself with Rohiṇī always.

Particularly despite the fact that he has been prohibited by your order, the Lord of night has done this. Permit us now to cany out our intention in this regard. Distressed by the misery of absence of conjugal felicity, we shall give up our lives.”

## \|\| 1.63.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaḥ kopasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*śaśāpa śarvarīnāthaṃ gatvā tatsaṃnidhau tataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. On hearing their words, Dakṣa became very angry. He went to the Lord of night and cursed him:

## \|\| 1.63.28 \|\|

*yasmātpāpa na me vākyaṃ tvayā dharmasamanvitam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tasmātkṣayavyādhistvāṃ grasiṣyati dāruṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “O sinner, my advice of righteous import has not been followed by you. So the fell disease of tuberculosis will oppress you.”

## \|\| 1.63.29 \|\|

*evamuktvā yayau dakṣaścandro'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādyakṣmaṇāśliṣṭaḥ kṣayaṃ yāti dine dine \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After saying thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Dakṣa went away. Candra was instantly afflicted by tuberculosis and began to decline in strength day by day.

## \|\| 1.63.30 \|\|

*tato'sau kṛśatāṃ prāptaḥ saṃparityajya rohiṇīm \|*  
*aśaktaḥ sevituṃ kāmaṃ vabhrāma jagatītale \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He became emaciated. Incompetent to continue the dalliance of love, he forsook Rohiṇī too and roamed all over the earth.

## \|\| 1.63.31 \|\|

*kṣayavyādhipraṇāśāya pṛccha mānaścikitsakān \|*  
*auṣadhāni vicitrāṇi prakurvāṇo jitendriyaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He began asking physicians about the ways and means of curing the disease of tuberculosis. Controlling his sense-organs, he had the medication of herbs of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.63.32 \|\|

*tathāpi mucyate naiva yakṣmaṇā sa niśāpatiḥ \|*  
*dakṣaśāpena raudreṇa kṣayaṃ yāti dinedine \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Still the Lord of night was not rid of the tuberculosis. Due to the terrible imprecation of Dakṣa he grew more and more emaciated every day.

## \|\| 1.63.33 \|\|

*tato vairāgyamāpannastīrthayātrāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūva śraddhayāyuktastyaktvā bheṣajamuttamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thereupon, he eschewed the excellent medication. He became endowed with ardent faith. In this attitude of disgust, he undertook pilgrimage to holy spots.

## \|\| 1.63.34 \|\|

*athāsau bhramamāṇastu tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*saṃprāpto brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Roving over the tīrthas and shrines, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he arrived at the excellent holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.63.35-36 \|\|

*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā prabhāsaṃ vīkṣya rātripaḥ \|*  
*yāvatsaṃprasthitonyatra tāvadagre vyavasthitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*apaśyadromakaṃnāma sa muni saṃśitavratam \|*  
*tapovīryasamopetaṃ sarvasattvānukampakam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The Lord of night took his holy bath there and gained purity. After visiting the deity of Prabhāsa, he wanted to go elsewhere when he saw the sage named Romaka standing in front. The sage was a man of esteemed holy vows. He was endowed with vigour due to penance. He was one who took pity on all living beings.

## \|\| 1.63.37 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa praṇamyoccai stataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*kṣayavyādhiyutaścandro nirvedāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing him, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Candra afflicted with the disease of tuberculosis bowed to him and spoke loudly and respectfully exhibiting the disgust he felt:

## \|\| 1.63.38-40 \|\|

*parikṣīṇo'smi vipreṃdra kṣayavyādhiprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*tasmātkuru pratīkāra mahaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mayā cikitsakāḥ pṛṣṭāstairuktaṃ bheṣajaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*anekadhā mahābhāga parikṣīṇo dinedine \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yadi naivopadeśaṃ me kañcittvaṃ saṃpradāsyasi \|*  
*vyādhināśāya tattena tyakṣyāmyadya kalevaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. “O eminent Brāhmaṇa, I have become utterly exhausted as a result of the disease of tuberculosis. I seek refuge in you. Kindly do something to cure this.

O highly esteemed one, many physicians have been consulted by me. I have taken medicines prescribed by them in diverse ways but I am getting weaker and weaker every day.

If you cannot give any suggestion for quelling the disease, I will cast off my body.”

## \|\| 1.63.41 \|\|

*romaka uvāca \|*  
*anyasyāpi niśānātha na śāpaḥ kartumanyathā \|*  
*śakyate kiṃ punastasya dakṣasyāmitatejasaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Romaka said:

41\. O Lord of night, even the curse of an ordinary person cannot be altered; the curse of Dakṣa of immeasured splendour is all the more so.

## \|\| 1.63.42 \|\|

*tasmādatropadeśaṃ te prayacchāmi susaṃmatam \|*  
*yena te syādasaṃdigdhaṃ kṣayavyādhi parikṣayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. So I shall give you an advice commonly accepted, whereby your tuberculosis can surely be cured.

## \|\| 1.63.43 \|\|

*nādeyaṃ kiṃcidastīha devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*saṃprahṛṣṭasya tadvākyāttasmādārādhayasva tam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There is nothing which cannot be given by the Tridentbearing Lord of Devas, if he is pleased. Hence propitiate him at my instance.

## \|\| 1.63.44-45 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu satyaṃ vāsaḥ sadā kṣitau \|*  
*teṣu saṃsthāpya talliṃgaṃ tasya nāśāya rātripa \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ārādhaya tato nityaṃ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*saṃprāpsyasi na saṃdehaḥ kṣayavyādhi parikṣayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Satī stays (Read satyā vāsaḥ instead of satyam vāsaḥ in the Text) always in sixty-eight Tīrthas on the earth. Install the Liṅga in all of them, O Lord of night, for removing (the disease). Then propitiate the Liṅga every day with a mind sanctified by faith. There is no doubt, you will get relief from tuberculosis.

## \|\| 1.63.46 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭo niśāpatiḥ \|*  
*tasminprabhāsake kṣetre divyaliṃgāni śūlinaḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya pūjayāmāsa svanāmāṃkāni bhaktitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

Sūta said:

46\. On hearing his words, the Lord of night became delighted. He installed the divine Liṅgas of the Trident-bearing Lord in the holy place of Prabhāsaka marking them with his names. He devoutly worshipped them.

## \|\| 1.63.47 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevastasya saṃdarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*provāca varado'smīti prārthayasva yathepsitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thereupon the great Lord was pleased and appeared before him. He said, 1 shall bestow boons. Request for whatever is desired by you.”

## \|\| 1.63.48 \|\|

*candra uvāca \|*  
*paraṃ kṣīṇo'smi deveśa yakṣmaṇāhaṃ padāṃtikam \|*  
*prāptastasmātparitrāhi nānyatsaṃprārthayāmyaham \|\| 48 \|\|*

Candra said:

48\. O Lord of Devas, I am immensely tired and exhausted by the disease of tuberculosis. I have sought refuge at your feet. Save me from it. I do not request for anything else.

## \|\| 1.63.49 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*dakṣamāhūya tatraiva tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On hearing his words the Bull-emblemed Lord summoned Dakṣa there itself and spoke respectfully:

## \|\| 1.63.50 \|\|

*eṣa caṃdrastvayā śapto jāmātā na kṛtaṃ śubham \|*  
*tasmādanugrahaṃ cāsya mama vākyātsamācara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This Candra, your son-in-law, has been cursed by you. This is not good. Hence at my behest do bless him now.”

## \|\| 1.63.51 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*mayā dharmyamapi prokto vākyameṣa kubuddhimān \|*  
*nākaronme puraḥ procya kariṣyāmītya satyavāk \|\| 51 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

51\. He has a crooked mind. I gave him a sound advice of righteous import. After undertaking to abide by it before me he failed to do it and he became untruthful in his words.

## \|\| 1.63.52 \|\|

*tena śaptastu kopena sutārthe vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*hāsyenāpi mayā proktaṃ nānyathā saṃprajāyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. So, O Bull-emblemed Lord, for the sake of my daughters I cursed him angrily. Even what I utter jokingly cannot become changed.

## \|\| 1.63.53 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti sarvāstāḥ sutā eṣa niśākaraḥ \|*  
*samāḥ saṃvīkṣate nityaṃ mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

53\. At my bidding, this Lord of night will see all your daughters impartially from now onwards. There is no doubt.

## \|\| 1.63.54 \|\|

*tasmātpakṣaṃ kṣayaṃ yātu pakṣaṃ vṛddhiṃ pragacchatu \|*  
*yena te syādvacaḥ satyaṃ matprasādasamanvitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Hence let him waste away for a fortnight and wax again for a fortnight. Thereby your words can be true along with my favour.

## \|\| 1.63.55 \|\|

*tato dakṣastathetyuktvā jagāma nijamandiram \|*  
*devo'pi śaṃkaro bhūyaḥ provāca śaśalāṃchanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then Dakṣa said “So be it” and went to his abode. Lord Śaṅkara said to the Moon again:

## \|\| 1.63.56 \|\|

*bhūyo'pi prārthayābhīṣṭaṃ mattastvaṃ śaśalāṃchana \|*  
*yena sarvaṃ prayacchāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “O Moon, you can once again request for something desired. I shall grant everything even if it be rare.”

## \|\| 1.63.57 \|\|

*candra uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*tatsthāpiteṣu liṃgeṣu mayā sarveṣu sarvadā \|*  
*saṃnidhānaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ lokānāṃ hita kāmyayā \|\| 57 \|\|*

Candra said:

57\. O Lord of Devas, if you are pleased, if a boon has to be granted to me, you must be present always in the Liṅgas installed by me for the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.63.58 \|\|

*deva uvāca \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu liṃgeṣu sthāpiteṣu tvayā vibho \|*  
*somavāreṇa sāṃnidhyaṃ kariṣye vacanāttava \|\| 58 \|\|*

The Lord said:

58\. At your request I shall be present on all Mondays in the sixty-eight Liṅgas installed by you.

## \|\| 1.63.59-61 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*candro'pi harṣasaṃyuktaḥ samaṃ paśyati tāstataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sutā dakṣasya vipreṃdrā śaṃkarasya vacaḥ smaran \|*  
*tato harṣa samāyuktā vabhūvustadanaṃtaram \|\| 60 \|\|*

*evaṃ someśvarāstatra babhūvurdvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu tathānyeṣu tataḥ param \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. After saying thus the Lord of Devas vanished. Candra too joyously and impartially saw them all. He saw the daughters of Dakṣa impartially as he remembered the words of Śaṅkara. They also became delighted thereafter. It was thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Someśvaras came into being there in the sixty-eight Tīrthas and in the others thereafter.

## Chapter 64 - Greatness of Camatkārī Durgā

## \|\| 1.64.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*camatkārī purā devī tatraivāsti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*camatkāranareṃdreṇa sthāpitā śraddhayā purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yayā sa mahiṣaḥ pūrvaṃ nihato dānavo raṇe \|*  
*kaumāravratadhāriṇyā māyāśatasahasradhṛk \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadā tannirmitaṃ tatra puraṃ tena mahātmanā \|*  
*tasya saṃrakṣaṇārthāya tadā sā sthāpitā dvijāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. The great goddess Camatkārī is there itself, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. It was formerly devoutly installed by King Camatkāra.

It was by her that the demon in the form of a buffalo (Mahiṣa) was killed in battle. The demon who could wield thousands of Māyās was defeated by the goddess who adopted the Kaumāra Vrata (holy vow of celibacy).

When the noble-souled king built the city there, O Brāhmaṇas, she too was installed there for its protection.

## \|\| 1.64.4 \|\|

*purasya tasya rakṣārthaṃ tathā tatpuravāsinām \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ bhaktyā bhāvitacetasām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She was there for guarding that city and to protect all the leading Brāhmaṇas, the inhabitants of that city, because they had purified their minds by means of devotion.

## \|\| 1.64.5-6 \|\|

*yastāmabhyarcayetsamyaṅmahānavamivāsare \|*  
*kṛtsnaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ tasya na bhayaṃ jāyate kvacit \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhūtapretapiśācebhyaḥ śatrutaśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*rogebhyastaskarebhyaśca duṣṭebhyo'nyebhya eva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. If any one adores her duly on the day of Mahānavamī, he will not have any cause of fear during the entire year from goblins, corpses, ghosts, vampires, enemies in particular, illness, thieves, wicked people or others.

## \|\| 1.64.7 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyañchuklāṣṭamyāṃ naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*tāṃ pūjayati sadbhaktyā sa tamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A man should be pure in body and mind on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month. Whatever he thinks of at the time of worshipping devoutly, he attains it undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.64.8 \|\|

*niṣkāmaḥ sukhamāpnoti mokṣaṃ nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasyā devyāḥ prasādena satyametanmayoditam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The truth has been averred by me that by the grace of the goddess a person (worshipping her) without any desire will undoubtedly attain liberation from Saṃsāra quite easily.

## \|\| 1.64.9 \|\|

*tāmārādhya gatāḥ pūrvaṃ siddhiṃ bhūrirmahībhujaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇāśca tathānye'pi yoginaḥ parameśvarīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Formerly many kings, Brāhmaṇas, Yogins and others had propitiated the supreme goddess Parameśvarī and attained Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.64.10 \|\|

*yastasyāḥ śraddhayopetaḥ prakaroti pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*nityaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvattiryagyonau na sa vrajet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One who is endowed with faith and scrupulously circumambulates her every day for a year, can avert being born in a brutish womb.

## \|\| 1.64.11 \|\|

*tasyā āyatane pūrvamāścaryamabhavanmahat \|*  
*yattadvaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Listen attentively. I shall narrate unto you the great miracle that happened formerly in her shrine.

## \|\| 1.64.12 \|\|

*āsīccitrarathonāma pūrvaṃ pārthivasattamaḥ \|*  
*daśārṇādhipatiḥ khyātaḥ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Formerly there was an excellent king named Citraratha. was well-known as, the overlord of the Dasārṇa country and as the slayer of all enemies.

## \|\| 1.64.13 \|\|

*śuklāṣṭamyāṃ sadā bhaktyā sa tasyāḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ yāvatpracakāra pradakṣiṇām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Always on the eighth lunar day of the bright half of the month, he faithfully and devoutly circumambulated the goddess a hundred and eight times.

## \|\| 1.64.14 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya tāṃ devīṃ saṃprayāti punargṛham \|*  
*sainyena caturaṃgeṇa samaṃtātparivāritaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, he used to bow down to the goddess and then go home surrounded on all sides by his army consisting of the four divisions.

## \|\| 1.64.15 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya nareṃdrasya pradakṣiṇaratasya ca \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālo devyā bhaktiratasya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus, a great deal of time passed by even as the leading king continued to be devoted to the goddess scrupulously making the circumambulations.

## \|\| 1.64.16 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya sa rājā tatra saṃgataḥ \|*  
*apaśyadbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāndevīgṛhasamāśritān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Once, when that king went there, he saw some excellent Brāhmaṇas resting in the shrine of the goddess.

## \|\| 1.64.17 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ devīṃ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*agrasthāṃstāndvijānsarvānnamaścakre samāhitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the king circumambulated the goddess and bowed down with concentration to all the Brāhmaṇas stationed before.

## \|\| 1.64.18 \|\|

*tatastaiḥ sahitaistatra sahāsīnaḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ viprarṣīṇāṃ cakāra ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereafter, he sat down along with them (listening to) the narration of splendid stories of saintly kings and ancient Brāhmaṇa-sages.

## \|\| 1.64.19 \|\|

*tataḥ kasminkathāṃte sa pṛṣṭastairdvijasattamaiḥ \|*  
*kautūhalasamopetairvinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At the conclusion of one story-session, the king was asked as he stood there politely by those excellent Brāhmaṇas who were very curious (to know the king):

## \|\| 1.64.20-22 \|\|

*rājanpṛcchāmahe sarve tvāṃ vayaṃ kautukānvitāḥ \|*  
*tasmātkīrtaya cedguhyaṃ na tattava vyavasthitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*māsimāsi sadāṣṭamyāṃ tvaṃ śuklāyāṃ sudūrataḥ \|*  
*āgatya devatāyāśca prakaroṣi pradakṣiṇām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yatnenānyāḥ parityajya sarvāḥ pūjādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ vetsi phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yatpradakṣiṇasaṃbhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. “O king, we are asking you out of curiosity. Hence recount in detail if there is no secret about your engagements. Always, in every month, on the eighth lunar day in the bright half, you come here from a very distant place and carry out your rite of circumambulation. You carefully avoid all other pious rites such as worship etc. Indeed you may be knowing the entire benefit that accrues from circumambulation.”

## \|\| 1.64.23 \|\|

*rājovāca \|\| satyametaddvijaśreṣṭhā yadbhavadbhirudāhṛtam \|*  
*rahasyamapi vaktavyaṃ yuṣmākaṃ sāṃprataṃ mayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

The king said:

23\. This is the truth, O excellent Brāhmaṇas; what you say is true. Even a secret has to be shared with you by narrating it to you.

## \|\| 1.64.24 \|\|

*ahamāsa śukaḥ pūrvamasminnāyatane śubhe \|*  
*devyāḥ paścimadigbhāge kulāyakṛtasaṃśrayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Formerly I was a parrot in this splendid shrine of the goddess. I had built a nest in the western section of the temple and lived there.

## \|\| 1.64.25 \|\|

*tatra nirgacchato nityaṃ kurvataścapraveśanam \|*  
*pradakṣiṇābhavaddevyā nityameva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Every day I went out of the temple and returned later. This constituted a circumambulation of the goddess, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.64.26 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena me mṛtyuḥ saṃjāto'traiva maṃdire \|*  
*tatprabhāveṇa saṃjāto rājā jātismaro'tra hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In due course death overtook me here in the temple itself. As a result thereof, I was reborn as a king with the power to recollect the previous birth and activities.

## \|\| 1.64.27 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddūrātsamabhyetya pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*karomyasyā dvijaśreṣṭhā devatāyāḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That is the reason why, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I come here over a long distance and circumambulate the goddess with concentration and mental purity.

## \|\| 1.64.28-29 \|\|

*purā bhaktivihīnena kulāye vasatā mayā \|*  
*kṛtā pradakṣiṇā devyāstena jāto'smi bhūpatiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*adhunā śraddhayā yukto yatkaromi pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*kiṃ me bhaviṣyati śreyastanna vedmi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Earlier I had no devotion at all, and I stayed in a nest But I circumambulated the goddess. Thereby I became a king. Now I circumambulate with full faith but I do not know what (better) welfare is in store for me, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.64.30-31 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā tasya te viprā vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*sādhuvādaṃ tathā cakrustasya bhūpasya harṣitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa pārthivaḥ sarvānpraṇamya dvijasattamān \|*  
*anujñāpya yayau tūrṇaṃ svagṛhāya sasainikaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sūta said:

30-31. On hearing it, the Brāhmaṇas’ eyes widened with surprise. Joyously they congratulated the king. Then the king bowed down to all the Brāhmaṇas, received their assent and went homewards along with his army.

## \|\| 1.64.32 \|\|

*adhunā śraddhayā yukto yaḥ karoti pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto labhate vāṃchitaṃ phalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Now, one who is endowed with faith and performs the circumambulation, shall be liberated from all sins and obtain the desired benefit.

## \|\| 1.64.33-35 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te viprāḥ sarve bhaktipuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ cakrustathānye muktihetave \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prāptāśca paramāṃ siddhiṃ vāṃchitāṃ tatprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tāṃ devīmiha saṃśrayet \|*  
*sarvakāmapradāṃ nṛṇāṃ tasminkṣetre vyavasthitām \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Ever since then, those Brāhmaṇas endowed with great devotion and others as well, circumambulated the deity for the sake of salvation. They did attain great Siddhi they desired, by its power. The Siddhi they attained in this world and in the other world has been rarely achieved even by gods. Hence by all means, one should resort to that goddess stationed in that holy spot bestowing all desires on men.

## Chapter 65 - Greatness of Ānartakeśvara and Śūdrakeśvara

## \|\| 1.65.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti taḍāgaṃ devanirmitam \|*  
*yatrānarto nṛpaḥ siddhaḥ suhayo nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tenaiva bhūbhujā tatra liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ śubham \|*  
*ānarteśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca sarva siddhipradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatrāṃgārakaṣaṣṭhyāṃ yastaḍāge snānamācaret \|*  
*sa prāpnoti naraḥ siddhiṃ yathā'nartādhipena ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

\[Full title: Greatness of Ānartakeśvara (ānartaka-īśvara) and Śūdrakeśvara (śūdraka-īśvara)\]

Sūta said:

1-3. Similarly there is another lake there dug by Devas. It was there that a king of Ānarta named Suhaya became a Siddha.

The same king installed a splendid Liṅga there named Ānarteśvara. It is the bestower of all Siddhis on men.

A man who performs his holy ablution there on a Tuesday coinciding with the sixth lunar day, there in the lake, attains Si\[???\] \[??\] \[=Siddhi in ?\] same way as it was by the Lord of Ānarta.

## \|\| 1.65.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ siddhistu saṃprāptā ānartena mahātmanā \|*  
*sarvaṃ kathaya tatsūta sarvaṃ vetsi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

4\. How was Siddhi attained by the noble-souled king of Ānarta. O Sūta, narrate everything. Undoubtedly you know everything.

## \|\| 1.65.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ānartaḥ suhayo nāma purāsītpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*sarvāribhirhato yuddhe palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*ucchiṣṭo mlecchasaṃspṛṣṭa ekākī bahubhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. Formerly there was a king of Ānarta named Suhaya. He was attacked by all the enemies in battle and he fled. He became Ucchiṣṭa (polluted by partaking remnants of food) and was touched by a barbarian. He was alone and was surrounded by many.

## \|\| 1.65.6 \|\|

*atha tasya kapālaṃ ca kāpālika vratānvitaḥ \|*  
*jagṛhe nijakarmārthaṃ jñātvā taṃ vīrasaṃbhavam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then a certain person following the vow of Kāpālikas seized his skull for the purpose of his black magic after knowing that he was born of a heroic warrior.

## \|\| 1.65.7-9 \|\|

*ānarteśvarasāṃnidhye vasamāno vane sthitaḥ \|*  
*sa rātrau tena toyena sarvadevamayena ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*taḍāgotthena saṃpūrṇaṃ rātrau kṛtvā pramuṃcati \|*  
*āsītpūrvaṃ vaṇiṅnāmnā siddhasena iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*dhanī bhṛtyasamopetaḥ sadā puṇyaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kasyacittvatha kālasya paṇyabuddhyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*prasthitaścottarāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ sa sārthena samanvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. This (Kāpālika) stayed in a forest in the vicinity of Ānarteśvara. He used to fill the skull at night with the water of the lake where all the Devas are present and then used to pour it off (in the morning after use).

Formerly there was a Vaṇik (merchant) remembered by the name Siddhasena. He was very rich and accompanied by his servants, he always engaged himself in meritorious rites. Once, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he set off towards the north accompanied by his caravan for doing business.

## \|\| 1.65.10 \|\|

*atha prāptaḥ kramātsarvaiḥ sa gacchanmarumaṃḍala m \|*  
*vṛkṣodakaparityaktaṃ sarvasattvavivarjitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Going ahead gradually along with every one, he reached a desert area devoid of trees and water and abandoned as it were by all living beings.

## \|\| 1.65.11 \|\|

*tatra rātriṃ samāsādya śrāṃtāḥ pāṃthāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*suptāḥ sthānāni saṃsṛtya gatā nidrāvaśaṃ tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At nightfall all the travellers became tired. Occupying different positions they all slept soundly.

## \|\| 1.65.12 \|\|

*tataḥ pratyūṣamāsādya samutthāya ca satvaram \|*  
*prasthitā uttarāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ muktvaikaṃ śūdrasevakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At daybreak they all woke up quickly and started towards the north leaving behind there a Śūdra servant.

## \|\| 1.65.13 \|\|

*sa vai mārgapariśrāṃto gatvā nidrāvaśaṃ bhṛśam \|*  
*na jajāgāra jāte'pi prayāṇe bahuśabdite \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He had become too tired to get up from sleep. Even when the onward journey started with a lot of noise he did not wake up.

## \|\| 1.65.14 \|\|

*na ca taiḥ sa smṛtaḥ sārthairyaiḥ samaṃ prasthito gṛhāt \|*  
*na ca kenāpi saṃdṛṣṭaḥ sa tu rodhasi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He was not remembered by the members of the caravan with whom he had travelled from the original home. The fact that he was on the banks was not noticed by any one.

## \|\| 1.65.15 \|\|

*evaṃ gate tataḥ sārthe prodgate sūryamaṃḍale \|*  
*tīvratāpaparispṛṣṭo jajāgāra tataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus the caravan left the place and the sun began to rise up. The Śūdra felt the intense heat and woke up thereafter.

## \|\| 1.65.16 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyati no kiñcittasminsthāne sa sārthakam \|*  
*na ca teṣāṃ marau tasmiṃllakṣyate padapaddhatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He looked ahead but could not see any member of the

caravan at that place. In the desert region their footprints too could not be traced.

## \|\| 1.65.17 \|\|

*tato duḥkhaparītātmā dhāvamāna itastataḥ \|*  
*patito medinīpṛṣṭhe madhyāhne kṣuttṛṣārditaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He became overwhelmed with grief. He ran here and there. At midday he was excessively distressed by hunger and thirst. He sprawled himself on the ground.

## \|\| 1.65.18 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya tṛṣārtasya patitasya dharātale \|*  
*dhṛtaprāṇasya kṛcchreṇa saṃyāto'stācalaṃ raviḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Despite his distress due to thirst, he somehow held on to his life lying on the ground. By that time the sun too set.

## \|\| 1.65.19-20 \|\|

*tataḥ kiṃcitsasaṃjño'bhūnmaṃdībhūte divākare \|*  
*cintayāmāsa cittena kvāhaṃ gacchāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na lakṣyate kvacinmārgo dṛśyate na ca mānuṣam \|*  
*nātra toyaṃ na ca cchāyā nūnaṃ me mṛtyu rāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. When the sun’s warmth became reduced he regained consciousness somehow. He thought within himself. 'Where shall I go now? No pathway is seen. No one is to be seen. There is neither water nor shade. Indeed my death is approaching.’

## \|\| 1.65.21 \|\|

*evaṃ cintāprapannasya tasya śūdrasya nirjane \|*  
*marau tasminsamāyātā śarvarī tadanantaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When that Śūdra was mentally worried thus in the lonely desert region, night set in.

## \|\| 1.65.22 \|\|

*atha kṣaṇena śuśrāva sa gītaṃ madhuradhvani \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ nandivṛddhānāṃ tathā śabdaṃ manoharam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Soon he heard the sweet sound of music and the fascinating voice of the chanting Nandi Vṛddhas (elderly goblin attendants of Śiva).

## \|\| 1.65.23 \|\|

*athāpaśyatkṣaṇenaiva pretasaṃghaiḥ sabhāvṛtam \|*  
*pretamekaṃ ca sarveṣāmādhipatye vyava sthitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In an instant he saw a Preta (ghost) who seemed to be the leader of the gang and he was surrounded by groups of Pretas.

## \|\| 1.65.24 \|\|

*tataste pārśvagāḥ pretā eke nṛtyaṃ pracakrire \|*  
*tatpuro gītamanye tu stutiṃ caiva tathā pare \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Some of the attending Pretas began to dance. Others sang before him. Still others began to eulogize.

## \|\| 1.65.25 \|\|

*athāsau prāha taṃ śūdramatithe kuru bhojanam \|*  
*svecchayā piba toyaṃ ca śreyo yena bhavenmama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The (leader) said to the Śūdra: “O dear guest, have your meal. Drink water as you please so that it may result in my weal.”

## \|\| 1.65.26 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhojanaṃ cakre kṣudhārtaśca papau jalam \|*  
*bhayaṃ tyaktvā suviśrabdhaḥ pretarājasya śāsanāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The hungry Śūdra had a hearty meal and drank water. At the bidding of the king of the Pretas, he became carefree and fearless.

## \|\| 1.65.27 \|\|

*tataḥ pretāśca te sarve pretatvena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathānyāyaṃ pracakrurbhojanakriyām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then all the Pretas endowed with the characteristic features of the Pretas took their food duly sitting in the order of their seniority.

## \|\| 1.65.28 \|\|

*evaṃ teṣāṃ samastānāṃ vilāsaiḥ pārthivocitaiḥ \|*  
*atikrāntā niśā sarvā krīḍatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all of them were engaged in games and sports with royal grace and charm till the night came to a close.

## \|\| 1.65.29 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṃḍale \|*  
*yāvatpaśyati śūdraḥ sa tāvattatra na kiñcana \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The day dawned clearly and the disc of the sun rose high into the sky. When the Śūdra looked before him there was nothing.

## \|\| 1.65.30-31 \|\|

*tataśca cintayāmāsa kimetatsvapnadarśanam \|*  
*cittabhramo'thavā'smākamindrajālamathāpi vā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*athavā satyametaddhi yato me tṛptiruttamā \|*  
*saṃjāteyaṃ kṣudhārttasya pipāsākulitasya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Then he thought, ‘Was this a dream? My hallucination? Or some jugglery? Or rather is it something real? I was distressed with hunger and thirst but I am satisfied now.

## \|\| 1.65.32 \|\|

*evaṃ cintayamānasya bhāskaro gaganāṃgaṇam \|*  
*samāruroha tāpena tāpayandharaṇītalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Even as he mused thus the sun rose very high in the sky and scorched the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.65.33 \|\|

*tataḥ kaṃcitsamāśritya svalpacchāyaṃ mahīruham \|*  
*prāptavāndivasasyāṃtaṃ kṣutpipāsāprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He resorted to the foot of a tree which had but a small area of shade to offer. He was excessively distressed due to hunger and thirst and somehow spent the time till the close of the day.

## \|\| 1.65.34 \|\|

*tato niśāmukhe prāpte bhūyo'pi pretarājakam \|*  
*pretaistaiścasamopetaṃ tathārūpaṃ vyalokayat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At nightfall he saw the king of the Pretas of the same form as before and accompanied by the other Pretas.

## \|\| 1.65.35 \|\|

*tathaiva bhojanaṃ cakre tasyātithyasamudbhavam \|*  
*bhayena rahitaḥ śūdro harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the same manner he took the food, the result of his hospitality. The Śūdra eschewed all fear. He was delighted much.

## \|\| 1.65.36 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya niśāvaktre nityameva sa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*ātithyaṃ prakarotyeva samāgatya tathaiva ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thus the king (of the Pretas) came every day at nightfall. On coming he used to extend his hospitality.

## \|\| 1.65.37-38 \|\|

*tato'nyadivase prāpte tena śūdreṇa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭaḥ kimetadāścaryaṃ dṛśyate rajanīmukhe \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vibhavaste mahābhāga praṇaśyati niśākṣaye \|*  
*etatkīrtaya me guhyaṃ na cetpretapa saṃsthitam \|*  
*atra kautūhalaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvedaṃ suviceṣṭitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then one day, the ghost king was asked by the Śūdra: “What is this miracle seen every day at nightfall? O highly esteemed one, your riches come to an end when the day dawns. Do explain this position, if it is not a secret, O king of Pretas. On seeing this strange occurrence, my curiosity has been aroused.”

## \|\| 1.65.39 \|\|

*preta uvāca \|*  
*asti puṇyaṃ mahākṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva sthite tatra ca saṃgame \|\| 39 \|\|*

The Preta said:

39\. There is a great meritorious holy spot named Hāṭakeśvara. Gaṅgā and Yamunā have a confluence there.

## \|\| 1.65.40 \|\|

*tābhyāmatisamīpasthaṃ śivasyāyatanaṃ śubham \|*  
*mahāvratadharastatra tapasyati sunaiṣṭhikaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Very close to both of them there is an auspicious temple of Śiva. There a Sunaiṣṭhika (a sage of continued celibacy) performs penance there adopting a great Vrata.

## \|\| 1.65.41-42 \|\|

*sa sadā rātriśaucārthaṃ kapālaṃ jalapūritam \|*  
*madīyaṃ śayane cakre tatra kṛtvā nijāṃ kriyām \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tatprabhāvānmameyaṃ hi vibhūtirjāyate niśi \|*  
*divā rikte kṛte yāti bhūya eva mahāmate \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. At night he keeps my skull filled with water intended for toilet purposes and kept near his bed. By its power at night, I get all these riches. During the day time the skull is kept dry and empty after the toilet is over at night. O highly intelligent one, all my riches vanish then.

## \|\| 1.65.43 \|\|

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me tatra gatvā kapālakam \|*  
*cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā madīyaṃ tattasmiṃstoye vinikṣipa \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Do a favour unto me. Go there and shatter the skull to pieces and cast them into the water.

## \|\| 1.65.44 \|\|

*yena me jāyate mokṣaḥ pretabhāvātsudāruṇāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereby I shall get rid of my hideous ghostly form.

## \|\| 1.65.45 \|\|

*tathā tatrāsti pūrvasyāṃ diśi tattīrthamuttamam \|*  
*gayāśira iti khyātaṃ pretatvānmuktidā yakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Moreover, there is an excellent Tīrtha well-known as Gayāśiras to the east thereof. It can accord salvation from ghost-hood.

## \|\| 1.65.46 \|\|

*tatra gatvā kuru śrāddhaṃ sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ mahāmate \|*  
*dṛśyate tava pārśvasthā bhadra saṃpuṭikā śubhām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O highly intelligent one, go there and perform the Śrāddha of all of us. O gentle Sir, a bundle of papers is seen there near you.

## \|\| 1.65.47 \|\|

*asyāṃ nāmāni sarveṣāṃ yathājyeṣṭhaṃ samālikha \|*  
*tataḥ śrāddhaṃ kuruṣvāśu dayāṃ kṛtvā garīyasīm \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Write the names of all in these sheets in the order of seniority. Have great pity on us and perform the Śrāddha quickly.

## \|\| 1.65.48 \|\|

*vayaṃ tvāṃ tatra neṣyāmaḥ sukhopāyena bhadraka \|*  
*nidhiṃ ca darśayiṣyāmaḥ śrāddhārthaṃ sumahattaram \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O fair Sir, we shall easily carry you to that place and also show you a very big treasure to meet the expanses of Śrāddha.

## \|\| 1.65.49 \|\|

*tatheti samanujñāte tena śūdreṇa satvaram \|*  
*ninyustaṃ skandhamāropya śūdraṃ kṣetre yathoditam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The Śūdra agreed to it readily saying, “So it shall be.” As promised they took the Śūdra to the holy spot after placing him on their shoulders.

## \|\| 1.65.50 \|\|

*darśayāmāsurevāsya nidhānaṃ bhūrivittajam \|*  
*tadādāya gatastatra yatrāsau naiṣṭhikaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They showed him the treasure containing ample wealth. The Śūdra took it and went to the place where the Naiṣṭhika was present.

## \|\| 1.65.51 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ bhaktyā katha yāmāsa vistarāt \|*  
*tasya bhūtapateḥ sarvaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He bowed to him devoutly and told him humbly the full details of the ghost-king.

## \|\| 1.65.52 \|\|

*tato labdhvā kapālaṃ taccūrṇayitvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāyamunayormadhye pracikṣepa mudānvitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Śūdra received the skull. With great concentration he reduced it to powder and joyously cast it into the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

## \|\| 1.65.53 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare preto divyarūpavapurdharaḥ \|*  
*vimānastho'bravīdvākyaṃ śūdraṃ taṃ harṣasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In the meantime the Preta appeared before the Śūdra; he was seated in an aerial chariot in a divine form. Then he joyously told him:

## \|\| 1.65.54-55 \|\|

*prasādāttava mukto'haṃ pretatvāddāruṇāditaḥ \|*  
*svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tridivālayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*eteṣāmeva sarveṣāmidānīṃ śrāddhamācara \|*  
*gatvā gayāśiraḥ puṇyaṃ yena muktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. “Thanks to your favour, I have been liberated from the hideous form of ghost. Hail unto you! I shall now go to heaven. Go to the sacred Gayāśiras now and performed the Śrāddha unto all these, so that they too can get salvation.”

## \|\| 1.65.56 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭasteṣāmeva pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ cakre ca bhūtānāṃ nityameva samāhitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He was surprised. With great concentration and mental purity, he performed the Śrāddha unto all the ghosts severally.

## \|\| 1.65.57 \|\|

*te'pi sarve gatāḥ svargaṃ pretāstasya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*daduśca darśanaṃ tasya svapre harṣasamanvitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All those Pretas went to heaven by its power. They joyously revealed themselves to the Śūdra in his dream.

## \|\| 1.65.58 \|\|

*tataḥ śūdraḥ sa vijñāya tatkṣetraṃ puṇyavardha nam \|*  
*na jagāma gṛhaṃ bhūyastatraiva tapasi sthitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The Śūdra realized that the holy spot contributes to the increase of merit. Therefore he did not return home. He stayed there itself performing penance.

## \|\| 1.65.59 \|\|

*gaṃgāyamunayoḥ pārśve śūdrakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*ligaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ tena sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The Liṅga named Śūdrakeśvara was installed by him near Gaṅgā and Yamunā. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.65.60-61 \|\|

*yastayorvidhivatsnānaṃ kṛtvā pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*śūdrakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca liṃgaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*sa sarvaiḥ pātakairmuktaḥ prayāti śiva maṃdiram \|*  
*stūyamānaśca gaṃdharvairvimānavaramāśritaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. A man who duly takes his holy bath in their confluence and worships the Liṅga named Śūdrakeśvara with great ardour and faith becomes liberated from all sins and goes to Śiva’s palace riding in an excellent aerial chariot and being eulogized by Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.65.62 \|\|

*yastatra tyajati prāṇānkṛtvā prāyopaveśanam \|*  
*na ca bhūyo'tra saṃsāre sa janmāpnoti \|mānavaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A man who performs Prāyopaveśana (religious fast unto death) and casts off his life, is not reborn in this world.

## \|\| 1.65.63 \|\|

*gaṃḍūṣamapi toyasya yastasya nivasanpibet \|*  
*so'pi saṃmucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇāṃtikāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One who stays there and drinks even a mouthful of its water is liberated from the sins committed between birth and death.

## \|\| 1.65.64 \|\|

*yastatra brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ saṃprayacchati bhojanam \|*  
*pitarastasya tṛpyaṃti yāvatkalpaśatatrayam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If any one gives food to leading Brāhmaṇas there, (his) Pitṛs become satisfied for a period of three hundred Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.65.65 \|\|

*truṭimātraṃ ca yo dadyāttatra svarṇaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnoti phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. One who, with mental concentration and purity, makes a gift of a piece of gold of the size of an atom there, obtains the entire benefit of Rājasūya and Aśvamedha.

## \|\| 1.65.66 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tattīrthavaramāśrayet \|*  
*ya icchecchāśvataṃ svargaṃ sadaiva manujo dvijāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇas, a man who wishes for eternal Svarga shall resort to that excellent Tīrtha by all means.

## \|\| 1.65.67 \|\|

*atra gāthā purā gītā gautamena maharṣiṇā \|*  
*gaṃgāyamunayostaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ vīkṣya vismayāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On being pleasantly surprised at the sight of that power of Gaṅgā and Yamunā, a Gāthā (a conplet in this connection) was sung formerly by the great sage Gautama.

## \|\| 1.65.68 \|\|

*gaṃgāyamunayoḥ saṃge naraḥ snātvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*śūdreśvaraṃ samālokya sadyaḥ svargamavāpnuyāt \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. “A man with mental concentration, who takes his holy bath in the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā and visits Śūdreśvara, shall immediately attain Svarga.”

## \|\| 1.65.69 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ gaṃgāyamunayormayā \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Gaṅgā and Yamunā has been entirely narrated to you all. It is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 66 - Murder of Jamadagni

## \|\| 1.66.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā tatrāsti vikhyātaṃ rāmahrada iti smṛtam \|*  
*yatra te pitarastena rudhireṇa pratarpitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra bhādrapade māsi yo'māvāsyāmavāpya ca \|*  
*pitṝnsaṃtarpayedbhaktyā so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: The story of Paraśurāma is used in Chapters 66-69, to describe the efficacy of Paraśurāma Hrada for performance of Śrāddha. The Hrada was created by Paraśurāma to avenge the murder of his father Jamadagni by King Sahasrārjuna, a Kṣatriya. For this act of one Kṣatriya, Paraśurāma attempted, genocide of Kṣatriyas and filled a pit (pool) with the blood of Kṣatriyas and performed the Tarpaṇa of his father.—Just because the Hrada proved efficacious to Paraśurāma, it is recommended to others for Śrāddha. The exploits of Paraśurāma are described in Mahābhārata, Ādi. 2.5-7. and in other Purāṇas.

Sūta said:

1-2. Further there is a famous Tīrtha which is well-known and remembered as Rāmahrada (the tank of Rāma or Paraśurāma). It was here that his Pitṛs were propitiated by him (Rāma) with libations of blood.

He who devoutly offers libations to Pitṛs on the New-Moon day in the month of Bhādrapada shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.66.3-5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*atyāścaryamidaṃ sūta yadbravīṣi mahāmate \|*  
*yattena pitarastatra rudhireṇa pratarpitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pitṛṇāṃ tarpaṇārthāya medhyāḥ saṃkīrtitā budhaiḥ \|*  
*padārthā rudhiraṃ proktaṃ rākṣasānāṃ pratarpaṇe \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca karma sadbhirvigarhitam \|*  
*jāmadagnyena taccīrṇaṃ kasmātsūta vadasva naḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

3-5. This is something very mysterious that you say, O highly intelligent Sūta, that the Pitṛs were propitiated with libations of blood by him (Rāma).

Sacred things have been prescribed by learned men for the purpose of offering libations to Pitṛs. Blood is prescribed in the case of the libations of Rākṣasas.

An action contrary to the dictates of Śruti and Smṛti, and despised by good people has been performed by the son of Jamadagni. Why did he do so? Tell us, O Sūta.

## \|\| 1.66.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tena kopavaśātkarma pratijñāṃ parirakṣatā \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ tarpitā yena pitaro rudhireṇa te \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. It was done so by him out of anger, in order to abide by his promise and vow. That was why the Pitṛs were propitiated with the libation of blood.

## \|\| 1.66.7 \|\|

*pitā tasya purā viprā jamadagnirnipātitaḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyeṇa svadharmastho vinā doṣaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. His father Jamadagni, O Brāhmaṇas, who abided by his duty and was faultless, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, was struck down by a Kṣatriya.

## \|\| 1.66.8 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītena tena proktaṃ mahātmanā \|*  
*raktena kṣatriyotthena saṃtarpyāḥ pitaro mayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereupon, when his anger was roused, the noble-souled sage (Paraśurāma) said: “My Pitṛs should be propitiated by me with the blood flowing out of the Kṣatriyas.”

## \|\| 1.66.9 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāttena rudhireṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*pitarastarpitā samyaktilamiśreṇa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It was for this reason that the Pitṛs were propitiated with blood libations mixed with gingelly seeds by that noble-souled one with devotion.

## \|\| 1.66.10 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*jamadagnirhataḥ kasmātkṣatriyeṇa mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*kiṃnāmā sa ca bhūpālo vistarādvada sūta tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

The sages said:

10\. Why was the great Sage Jamadagni killed by a Kṣatriya? What is the name of that king? O Sūta, narrate it in detail.

## \|\| 1.66.12 \|\|

*catvārastasya putrāśca babhūvurguṇasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*jaghanyo'pi guṇajyeṣṭhasteṣāṃ rāmo babhūva ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

The son of Ṛcīka is remembered as Jamadagni. Formerly he was in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara where all his sins were burnt.

12\. He had four sons endowed with good quality. Rāma was the most junior among them, but he was most superior in good qualities.

## \|\| 1.66.13 \|\|

*kadācidvasatastasya jamadagnermahāvane \|*  
*putreṣu kandamūlārthaṃ nirgateṣu vanādbahiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Jamadagni continued to stay in a great forest. Once his sons had gone out to forest for gathering roots and bulbous roots.

## \|\| 1.66.14 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto haihayādhipatirbalī \|*  
*sahasrārjuna ityeva vikhyāto yo mahītale \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the meantime, the powerful king of Haihayas, who was well-known ail over the earth as Sahasrārjuna, happened to come there.

## \|\| 1.66.15 \|\|

*mṛgalipsurvane tasminbhramamāṇa itastataḥ \|*  
*śramārto vṛṣarāśisthe bhāskare dinamadhyage \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It was the season of summer and the Sun was in the Zodiac of Taurus. Desirous of hunting deer, the king had been roaming here and there in the forest. At midday he became very distressed due to weariness.

## \|\| 1.66.16 \|\|

*tatastamāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā nānādruma samākulam \|*  
*caturaṃgena sainyena sahitaḥ praviveśa ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing the hermitage full of different kinds of trees, he entered it with his army having four divisions.

## \|\| 1.66.17 \|\|

*athāpaśyatsa tatrasthaṃ jamadagniṃ mahāmunim \|*  
*upaviṣṭaṃ kṛtasnānaṃ devārcanaparāyaṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There he saw the great sage Jamadagni seated. He had concluded his bath and was engaged in worshipping the deities.

## \|\| 1.66.18 \|\|

*atha taṃ pārthivaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa munistuṣṭisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*arghaṃ dattvā yathānyāyaṃ svāgatenābhinaṃdya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On seeing the king, the sage was pleased. He duly offered him Arghya and honoured him with due greetings.

## \|\| 1.66.19 \|\|

*so'pi taṃ praṇipatyoccairvinayena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*pratisaṃbhāṣayāmāsa kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He too bowed down to him with great humility; humbly enquired about his health and happiness when speaking to him, in return.

## \|\| 1.66.20 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kaccitte kuśalaṃ vipra putraśiṣyānvitasya ca \|*  
*sāgnihotra kalatrasya parivārayutasya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

The king said:

20\. O Brāhmaṇa, I hope you are hale and hearty in the company of your wife, sons, disciples and attendants. I hope you duly maintain the sacrificial fires.

## \|\| 1.66.21 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ ca me \|*  
*yattvaṃ taponidhirdṛṣṭaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Today my birth has become fruitful and the life meaningful since you, the storehouse of penance, bowed down to by all the worlds, are seen.

## \|\| 1.66.22 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa rājarṣirviśramya suciraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pītvāpastamuvācedaṃ praṇipatya mahāmunim \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After saying thus the saintly king rested there for a long time. After drinking water, he bowed down to the great sage and said to him:

## \|\| 1.66.23 \|\|

*anujñāṃ dehi me brahmanprayāsyāmi nijaṃ gṛham \|*  
*mama kṛtyaṃ samādeśyaṃ yena te syātprayojanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “If there be any job for me whereby your purpose may be served, it may be mentioned, O holy Brāhmaṇa. Permit me, I shall go home.”

## \|\| 1.66.24 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*devatārcanavelāyāṃ tvaṃ me gṛhamupāgataḥ \|*  
*manoratha iva dhyātaḥ sarvadevamayo'tithiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

24\. You have come to my house at the time of the worship of the deities. You are my guest and have been regarded as though (you are) the desire cherished. A guest is identical with all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.66.25 \|\|

*tasmānme'sti parā prītirbhaktiśca nṛpasattama \|*  
*tatkuruṣva mayā dattaṃ svahastenaiva bhojanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. So, O excellent king, I am pleased much and I have great devotion unto you. Hence take the food offered by me with my own hands.

## \|\| 1.66.26 \|\|

*rājā vā brāhmaṇo vātha śūdro vāpyaṃtyajo'pi vā \|*  
*vaiśvadevāntasaṃprāptaḥ so'tithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Whether it is a king or a Brāhmaṇa, or a Śūdra or one of low caste, if a guest comes at the conclusion of Vaiśvadeva rite, he is one who will take one to heaven.

## \|\| 1.66.27 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*mamaite sainikā brahmañchataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tairabhuktaiḥ kathaṃ bhoktuṃ yujyate mama kīrtaya \|\| 27 \|\|*

The king said:

27\. O holy Brāhmaṇa, I have here with me hundreds and thousands of soldiers. Without their being fed, is it proper for me to take food? Do tell me.

## \|\| 1.66.28-29 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ sainikānāṃ te saṃpradāsyāmi bhojanam \|*  
*nātra ciṃtā tvayā kāryā munirniṣkiṃcano hyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yaiṣā paśyati rājeṃdra dhenurbaddhā mamāṃtike \|*  
*eṣā sūte manobhīṣṭaṃ prārthitā sarvadaiva hi \|\| 29 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

28-29. I shall serve food unto all of your soldiers. In this respect, you need not worry at all, though I am a sage without any property. O leading king, the cow seen yonder, tethered very near me, yields whatever I desire, always on being requested.

## \|\| 1.66.30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataśca kautukāviṣṭaḥ sa nṛpo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva saṃprocya tasminnevāśrame sthitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sūta said:

30\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the king became full of curiosity. Saying “So be it, he stayed on in the hermitage itself.

## \|\| 1.66.31-33 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃtarpya devāṃśca pitṝṃśca tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*pūjayitvā havirvāhaṃ brāhmaṇāṃśca tataḥ param \|\| 31 \|\|*

*upaviṣṭastataḥ sārdhaṃ sarvairbhṛtyairbubhukṣitaiḥ \|*  
*śramārtairvismayāviṣṭaiḥ kṛte tasya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa prārthayāmāsa tāṃ dhenuṃ munisattamaḥ \|*  
*yo yatprārthayate dehi bhojyārthaṃ tasya tacchubhe \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. After propitiating Devas and Pitṛs thereafter, he worshipped Havirvāha (Fire-god) and then Brāhmaṇas. Thereafter, he sat along with all the hungry servants and followers who were weary and distressed, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. They were overwhelmed with wonder for him (his spiritual power?) Then the excellent sage prayed to the cow, “O splendid one, give unto everyone whatever food he asks for.”

## \|\| 1.66.34 \|\|

*tataḥ sā suṣuve dhenurannamuccāvacaṃ śubham \|*  
*pakvānnaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa cittāhlādakaraṃ param \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thereupon the cow yielded splendid food of various kinds. The sweetmeats in particular were highly pleasing.

## \|\| 1.66.35 \|\|

*tataḥ khādyaṃ ca cavyaṃ ca lehyaṃ coṣyaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*vyaṃjanāni vicitrāṇi kaṣāyakaṭukāni ca \|*  
*amlāni madhurāṇyeva tiktāni guṇavaṃti ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then there were foodstuffs that could be chewed,

masticated, swallowed, licked and sucked. There were diverse kinds of side-dishes and pickles. Some tasted astringent, some sour and hot. There were sweet and bitter foodstuffs too and all of them were of good quality.

S6. Thus that king became extremely satisfied on being fed with foodstuffs born of ambrosia. Thanks to the cow, he became pleased along with his servants and soldiers.

## \|\| 1.66.37 \|\|

*tato bhuktyavasāne tu prārthayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ dhenuṃ vismayāviṣṭo jamadagniṃ mahāmunim \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. At the conclusion of the meal, the king who was pleasantly surprised, requested the great sage Jamadagni for that cow:

## \|\| 1.66.38-40 \|\|

*kāmadhenuriyaṃ brahmannārhāraṇyanivāsinām \|*  
*munīnāṃ śāntacittānāṃ tasmādyaccha mama svayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yenā'karānkaromyadya lokāṃstasyāḥ prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*sādhayāmi ca durgasthāñchatrūnbhūribalānvitān \|\| 39 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛte tava śreyo bhaviṣyati ca sadyaśaḥ \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva tasmātkuru mayoditam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. “O holy Brāhmaṇa, this Kāmadhenu does not deserve to be kept with sages of quiescent mind permanently residing in forest So give it to me.

Thereby I can make people exempt from taxation. Depending upon its power, I can tackle all my enemies even if they are entrenched in fortresses and equipped with formidable armies.

If this is carried out it will be to your own credit and wellbeing in this world as well as in the other one. So do as I say.”

## \|\| 1.66.41 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*homadhenuriyaṃ rājanmamaikā prāṇasaṃmatā \|*  
*adeyā sarvadā pūjyā tasmānnārhasi yācitum \|\| 41 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

41\. O king, this is my only Homadhenu (cow intended for the purpose of sacrificial rites). It is as dear to me as my own life. It is worthy of being worshipped always and so can not be given away. Hence it does not behove you to request for it.

## \|\| 1.66.42 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ śatasahasraṃ te yacchāmyasyāḥ kṛte dvija \|*  
*dhenūnāmaparaṃ vittaṃ yāvanmātraṃ pravāṃchasi \|\| 42 \|\|*

The king said:

42\. O Brāhmaṇa, in return for this cow I shall give you a hundred thousand other cows and also wealth as much as you wish for.

## \|\| 1.66.43 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca \|*  
*avikreyā mahārāja sāmānyāpi hi gauḥ smṛtā \|*  
*kiṃ punarhomadhenuryā prabhāvairīdṛśairyutā \|\| 43 \|\|*

Jamadagni said:

43\. O great king, even an ordinary cow is declared as one that should not be sold. It is much more so in the case of this Homadhenu which has powers like these.

## \|\| 1.66.44 \|\|

*vimohādbrāhmaṇo yo gāṃ vikrīṇāti dhanecchayā \|*  
*vikrīṇāti na sandehaḥ sa nijāṃ jananīmiha \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A deluded Brāhmaṇa who sells a cow prompted by greed for wealth, undoubtedly sells his own mother.

## \|\| 1.66.45 \|\|

*surāṃ pītvā dvijaṃ hatvā dvijānāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ smṛtā \|*  
*dhenuvikrayakartṝṇāṃ prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Means of expiation has been laid down in the Smṛtis in regard to the Brāhmaṇas who imbibe liquor or kill other Brāhmaṇas. But there is no atonement in the case of those who sell cows.

## \|\| 1.66.46 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*yadi yacchasi no vipra sāmnā dhenumimāṃ mama \|*  
*balādapi hariṣyāmi tasmātsāmnā pradīyatām \|\| 46 \|\|*

The King said:

46\. O Brāhmaṇa, if you do not give me this cow on being requested politely, I will take it by force. It is better if given when requested peacefully.

## \|\| 1.66.47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā kopasaṃyukto jamadagnirdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*astramastramiti procya samuttasthau sabhātalāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sūta said:

47\. On hearing it, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Jamadagni became furious. He got up from the seat in the assembly shouting, “Weapon! Weapon!”

## \|\| 1.66.48 \|\|

*tataste sevakāstasya nṛpateścittavedinaḥ \|*  
*aprāptaśastraṃ taṃ vipraṃ nijaghnurniśitāyudhaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereupon the attendants who knew the mind of the king killed the Brāhmaṇa with sharp weapons even before he could lay his hands upon any weapon.

## \|\| 1.66.49 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ vadhyamānasya jamadagnermahātmanaḥ \|*  
*reṇukākhyā priyā bhāryā papātopari duḥkhitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When the noble-souled Jamadagni was being butchered thus, his beloved wife named Reṇukā fell on his body in utter grief.

## \|\| 1.66.50 \|\|

*sā'pi nānāvidhaistīkṣṇaiḥ khaṇḍitā varavarṇinī \|*  
*āyuḥśeṣatayā prāṇairna kathaṃcidviyojitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. That lady of excellent complexion was hit and wounded by different kinds of sharp missiles but did not die, for she was destined to live yet there.

## \|\| 1.66.51 \|\|

*evaṃ hatvā sa viprendraṃ jamadagniṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ dhenuṃ kālayāmāsa yatra māhiṣmatī purī \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After thus killing Jamadagni, the leading Brāhmaṇa, the king drove the cow to the city of Māhiṣmatī.

## \|\| 1.66.52 \|\|

*atha sā kālyamānā ca dhenuḥ kopasamanvitā \|*  
*jamadagniṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rarambha karuṇaṃ muhuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Driven thus forcibly and observing killing of Jamadagni; the cow became enraged and so lowed piteously.

## \|\| 1.66.53 \|\|

*tasyāḥ saṃrambhamāṇāyā vaktramārgeṇa nirgatāḥ \|*  
*pulindā dāruṇā medāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Even as she lowed thus, Pulindas, Medas and hundreds and thousands of other terrible fellows came out of her mouth.

## \|\| 1.66.54 \|\|

*nānāśastradharāḥ sarve yamadūtā ivāparāḥ \|*  
*procustāṃ sādaraṃ dhenumājñāṃ dehi drutaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. They wielded different kinds of weapons. All of them were like another set of Yama’s messengers. They respectfully said to the cow, “Command us quickly.”

## \|\| 1.66.55 \|\|

*sā'bravīddhanyatāmetaddhaihayādhipaterbalam \|*  
*atha taiḥ kopasaṃyuktairdāruṇairmlecchajātibhiḥ \|*  
*vināśayitumārabdhaṃ śitaiḥ śastrairnirargalam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. She said, “May this army of the king of the Haihayas be killed.” Thereupon the terribly angry barbarians began to destroy the army with sharp weapons ruthlessly.

## \|\| 1.66.56 \|\|

*na kaścitpuruṣasteṣāṃ sammukho'pyabhavadraṇe \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ sahasā yoddhuṃ bhayena mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. No man from among them came face to face with them, because everyone was afraid much, not to speak of a direct fight.

## \|\| 1.66.57 \|\|

*atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*pulindairdāruṇākāraiḥ procustaṃ mantriṇo nṛpam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On seeing the army shattered by the terrible Pulindas, the ministers spoke to the king:

## \|\| 1.66.58-60 \|\|

*tejohāniḥ parā te'dya jātā brahmavadhādvibho \|*  
*tasmāddhenuṃ parityajya gamyatāṃ nijamaṃdiram \|\| 58 \|\|*

*yāvannāgacchate tasya rāmonāma suto balī \|*  
*no cettena hato'traiva sabalo vadhameṣyasi \|\| 59 \|\|*

*naiṣā śakyā balānnetuṃ kāmadhenurmahodayā \|*  
*śaktirūpā karotyevaṃ yā sṛṣṭiṃ svayameva hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. “O Lord, you have lost much of your refulgence due to this murder of a Brāhmaṇa. Hence let this cow be left alone. Be pleased to go to your own palace.

It is better you go away before his powerful son named Rāma returns. Otherwise, you will be killed along with all your soldiers here itself.

This Kāmadhenu of great power cannot be taken away by force. In the form of divine Śakti, she herself can create thus.”

## \|\| 1.66.61 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivo bhītasteṣāṃ vākyādviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*jagāma hitvā tāṃ dhenuṃ svasthānaṃ hatasevakaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thereupon, the king became afraid particularly at their words. With all his attendants killed, he left the cos there and went to his own abode.

## Chapter 67 - Sahasrārjuna Killed

## \|\| 1.67.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāpto rāmo bhrātṛbhiranvitaḥ \|*  
*phalāni kandamūlāni gṛhītvā'śramasammukhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sa dṛṣṭvā svāśramaṃ dhvastaṃ pulindairbahuśo vṛtam \|*  
*lakuṭāśmaprahāraistu tāṃ dhenuṃ jarjarīkṛtām \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. In the meantime Rāma came there to the hermitage accompanied by his brothers carrying fruits, roots and bulbous roots.

He saw the hermitage damaged and surrounded by a large number of Pulindas and the cow grievously hurt with stones and sticks.

## \|\| 1.67.3-5 \|\|

*papraccha kimidaṃ sarvaṃ vyākulatvamupāgatam \|*  
*āśramāspadamābhīraiḥ pulindaiśca samāvṛtam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kenaiṣā māmikā dhenuḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtā \|*  
*tāpasyastāpasāḥ sarve kasmādete rudanti ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kva sa me'dya pitā vṛddho mātā ca sutavatsalā \|*  
*na māmadya yathāpūrvaṃ snehāccāyāti sammukhī \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. He asked: “How has this catastrephe \[catastrophe?\] happened? The penance grove is surrounded by Ābhiras and Pulindas. By whom has this cow of mine been beaten and wounded? Why do these ascetic men and women weep? Where is my old father? Where is my mother fond of her sons? Why does she not approach me lovingly as before?”

## \|\| 1.67.6 \|\|

*atha tasya samācakhyurvṛttāṃtaṃ sarvatāpasāḥ \|*  
*yathādṛṣṭaṃ suduḥkhārtā sahasrārjunaceṣṭitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereupon all those ascetics utterly grief-stricken narrated to him all the events in detail, all the acts of misdemeanour of Sahasrārjuna as witnessed by them.

## \|\| 1.67.7-8 \|\|

*tataste bhrātaraḥ sarve vajrapātopamaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ śastraiḥ khaṃḍitaṃ janakaṃ nijam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mātaraṃ kṣatasarvāṅgīṃ prāṇaśeṣāṃ vyathānvitām \|*  
*ruruduḥ śokasantaptā muktvā rāmaṃ mahābalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. All the brothers heard the stunning words that smote them like thunderbolt. On hearing it and seeing their father cut with weapons and their mother too grief-stricken with all the limbs injured, but somehow breathing alive, they began to cry in despair but not the all-powerful Rāma.

## \|\| 1.67.9 \|\|

*ruditvātha ciraṃ kālaṃ vipralapya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*antyeṣṭiṃ cakrire tasya vedoktavidhinā tataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After crying for a long time and lamenting repeatedly, they performed the obsequies in accordance with the injunctions in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.67.10 \|\|

*atha dāhāvasāne te kṛtvā gartāṃ yathocitām \|*  
*muktvā rāmaṃ dadustoyaṃ pituḥ putrāstilānvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After the cremation, all the others except Rāma, made a befitting deep pit and offered libations to their father along with gingelly seeds.

## \|\| 1.67.11 \|\|

*athānyaistāpasaiḥ prokto rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*na prayacchasi kasmāttvaṃ pretapitre jalāṃjalim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The other ascetics asked Rāma, the most excellent one among wielders of weapons: “Why don’t you offer handfuls of libation to your dead father?”

## \|\| 1.67.12 \|\|

*athāsau bahudhā pro ktastāpasairjamadagnijaḥ \|*  
*prahārāngaṇayanmātuḥ śitaśastravinirmitān \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This son of Jamadagni was asked thus many times even as he was engaged in counting the number of wounds inflicted by sharp weapons on the body of his mother.

## \|\| 1.67.13-17 \|\|

*tatastānabravīdrāmo viniḥśvasya munīśvarān \|*  
*niṣedhastoyadānasya śrūyatāṃ yanmayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aparādhaṃ vinā tātaḥ kṣatriyeṇa hatomama \|*  
*ekaviṃśatiḥ prahārāṇāṃ māturaṃge sthitā mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tasmānniḥkṣatriyāmurvīṃ yadyahaṃ na karomi vai \|*  
*prahārasaṃkhyayā viprāstanme syātsarvapātakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pitṛmātṛvadhājjātaṃ yatkṛtaṃ tena pāpmanā \|*  
*kṣatriyāpasadenātra tathānyadapi kutsitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tatastasyaiva cānyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ durātmanām \|*  
*rudhiraiḥ pūrayitvemāṃ gartāṃ pitṛjalocitām \|*  
*tarpayiṣyāmi raktena pitaraṃ nāhamaṃbhasā \|\| 17 \|\|*

13-17. Then Rāma heaved a sigh and spoke to those leading sages: “You may now be pleased to hear why I refused to offer water libations. My father was killed by a Kṣatriya without any fault on his part. There are twenty-one wounds on the body of my mother. Hence, O Brāhmaṇas, if I do not exterminate Kṣatriyas from the earth as many times as there are wounds (on my mother’s body) I will incur all sins. In addition to the murder of my father and mother that sinful base Kṣatriya has perpetrated other foul deeds.

Therefore I shall fill this pit with his blood as well as that of other wicked-souled Kṣatriyas, though it is usually filled with libations of water. I shall propitiate my father with libations of blood, not of water.”

## \|\| 1.67.18 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā te dāruṇāṃ tasya pratijñāṃ tāpasottamāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ vismayamāpannā nocuḥ kiṃcittataḥ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sūta said:

18\. On hearing his dreadful vow, the excellent ascetics were struck with awe and were mystified. They did not say anything further.

## \|\| 1.67.19 \|\|

*athāśaucāṃtamāsādya rāmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tīkṣṇaṃ paraśumādāya māhiṣmatyunmukhaṃ yayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then, after the days of pollution (due to death) were over, the furious Rāma, seized his axe and proceeded in the direction of Māhiṣmatī.

## \|\| 1.67.20 \|\|

*sarvaistaiḥ śabaraiḥ sārdhaṃ pulindairmedakaistathā \|*  
*baddhagodhāṃgulitrāṇairvarabāṇadhanurdharaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He was accompanied by all those tribal people, the Pulindas and the Medakas. They had fastened their arms with alligator skin to prevent injury. They had similar finger protections too. They had excellent arrows and bows.

## \|\| 1.67.21-22 \|\|

*tathā'rjuno'pi taṃ śrutvā samāyātaṃ bhṛgūttamam \|*  
*sainyena mahatā yuktaṃ pratijñādhāriṇaṃ tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatastu sammukho dṛṣṭo yuddhārthaṃ sa viniryayau \|*  
*sārdhaṃ nānāvidhairyodhaiḥ sarvairdevāsuropamaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. On hearing that the scion of the family of Bhṛgu was advancing accompanied by a great army after taking a vow, Arjuna was delighted. He too set out facing him for fighting, along with different kinds of warriors who could be compared to Devas and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.67.23 \|\|

*athābhavanmahāyuddhaṃ pulindānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*haihayādhipateryodhaiḥ sārdhaṃ devāsuropamaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereafter, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a great battle ensued between the Pulindas and the warriors of the king of Haihaya, who could be compared to Devas and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.67.24 \|\|

*tataste haihayāḥ sarve śarairāśīviṣopamaiḥ \|*  
*vadhyante śabaraiḥ saṃkhye garjamānairmuhurmuhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then all the followers of Haihaya were killed with arrows on a par with poison-breathing serpents, by the tribals who were repeatedly roaring while fighting.

## \|\| 1.67.25 \|\|

*brahmahatyāsamutthena pātakena tataśca te \|*  
*jātā nistejasaḥ sarve prapataṃti dharātale \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Due to the sin arising from Brāhmaṇa-slaughter all of them were lustreless and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 1.67.26 \|\|

*na kaścitpauruṣaṃ tatra saṃpradarśayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*palāyanaparā sarve vadhyante niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. No one was competent to show valour. As they fled, all of them were killed with sharp arrows.

## \|\| 1.67.27 \|\|

*atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā haihayādhipatiḥ krudhā \|*  
*svacāpaṃ vāñchayāmāsa sajyaṃ kartuṃ tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*śaknoti nāropayituṃ suyatnamapi cāśritaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing his army broken up, the Lord of Haihayas became furious. Hurriedly he desired to string his bow, but could not do so although he tried the utmost.

## \|\| 1.67.28 \|\|

*tataścākarṣayāmāsa khaṅgaṃ kośātsunirmalam \|*  
*ākraṣṭuṃ na ca śakroti vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then he wanted to draw out the clean sword from its sheath; but he failed to do so. He felt a great discomfiture.

## \|\| 1.67.29 \|\|

*gadayā nirjito raudro rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*yayā sāpyapataddhastāttatkṣaṇātpṛthivītale \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. His club too fell down on to the ground in an instant. It was the club with which the terrible Rāvaṇa, who used to make people cry in despair, was defeated.

## \|\| 1.67.30 \|\|

*narmadāyāḥ pravāho yaiḥ sahasrākhyaiḥ karaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*vidhṛtastena te sarve babhūvuḥ kampavihvalāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. These were the very hands which once used to restrain the flooding current of Narmadā. All his splendid hands numbering a thousand became agitated with great tremor.

## \|\| 1.67.31 \|\|

*na śastraṃ śekuruddhartuṃ daivayogātkathaṃcana \|*  
*divyāstrāṇāṃ tathā sarve mantrā vismṛtimāgatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. As ill luck would have it, they were too weak to life the weapons at all. Further all the Mantras of the divine missiles became forgotten.

## \|\| 1.67.32 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare rāmaḥ saṃprāptaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*tīkṣṇaṃ paraśumudyamya tatastaṃ prāha niṣṭhuram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the meantime Rāma came there with his fury at its zenith. He lifted up his axe and said to him these harsh words:

## \|\| 1.67.33 \|\|

*haihayādhipate pāpa yaiḥ karairjanako mama \|*  
*tvayā vinihatastānme śīghraṃ darśaya sāṃpratam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “O sinner, king of Haihayas, quickly show me those hands with which my father was killed by you.”

## \|\| 1.67.34 \|\|

*brahmatejohataḥ so'pi proktastena suniṣṭhuram \|*  
*novāca cottaraṃ kiṃcidālekhye likhito yathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He too, already struck down by the Brāhmaṇical splendour did not say anything by way of reply though harshly taunted thus. He remained like one painted in a picture.

## \|\| 1.67.35 \|\|

*tato bhujavanaṃ tasya rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*muhurmuhurvinirbhartsya pracakarta śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then Rāma, the most excellent one among those who wield arms, rebuked him repeatedly and slowly cut off the row of his hands.

## \|\| 1.67.36 \|\|

*tataśchittvā śirastasya kuṭhāreṇa bhṛgūdvahaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha rudhiraṃ yatnātprahārebhyaḥ svayaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then the scion of the family of Bhṛgu cut off his head with his axe. Assiduously he himself collected the blood from the wounds, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.67.37 \|\|

*pūrayitvā mahākumbhāñchabarebhyo dadau tataḥ \|*  
*mlecchebhyo lubdhakebhyaśca tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He filled big pots and handed them over to the hunters. Then he respectfully spoke to the barbarians and the fowlers (hunters):

## \|\| 1.67.38-40 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre gartā me bhrātṛbhiḥ kṛtā \|*  
*pitṛsaṃtarpaṇārthāya salilena pariplutā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*prakṣipadhvaṃ drutaṃ gatvā tasyāṃ raktamidaṃ mahat \|*  
*pāpasyāsya sapatnasya mamādeśādasaṃśayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yena tātaṃ nijaṃ bhaktyā tarpayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*ṛṇasya muktirbhavati yena me paitṛkasyaca \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. “A big pit has been dug by my brothers in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara. It was filled with water for the purpose of propitiating the Pitṛs. At my behest go there quickly and unhesitatingly pour therein the large quantity of blood of my sinful enemy. Thereby I shall devoutly propitiate my father in accordance with the injunctions. Thereby I shall be liberated from indebtedness to my father.”

## Chapter 68 - The Sea Recedes

## \|\| 1.68.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha te śabarā yatnādraktaṃ taddhaihayodbhavam \|*  
*tatra ninyuḥ sthitā yatra gartā sā pitṛsaṃbhavā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhārgavo'pi ca taṃ hatvā raktamādāya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa yatra gartā'tha paitṛkī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*na sa bālaṃ na vṛddhaṃ ca parityajati bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*yauvanasthaṃ viśeṣeṇa garbhasthaṃ vātha kṣatriyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Then those hunters carefully carried the blood taken out from the Haihayas to the place where the pit was dug for offering libations to the Pitṛs.

Bhārgava too after killing him (i.e. Sahasrārjuna) collected the entire blood and sent it to the place where the pit connected with his father was present.

Bhārgava did not spare any Kṣatriya whether a child, young man or an old man. In particular he did not leave off even a child in womb.

## \|\| 1.68.4 \|\|

*svayaṃ jaghāna bhūpānsa teṣāṃ pārśve tathā parān \|*  
*vidhvaṃsāyayati kruddhaḥ sainikaiśca samantataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He killed the kings himself and others also on their sides. He caused the death of the soldiers as well in the height of his anger.

## \|\| 1.68.5 \|\|

*tathaivāsṛkpragṛhṇāti gṛhṇāpayati cādarāt \|*  
*teṣāṃ pārśvaistatastūrṇaṃ preṣayāmāsa tatra ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He eagerly collected the blood and made his attendants collect too. Then he used to send it through them to that place.

## \|\| 1.68.6 \|\|

*evaṃ niḥkṣatriyāṃ kṛtvā kṛtsnāṃ pṛthvīṃ bhṛgadvahaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre jagāma tadanantaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thus the scion of the family of Bhṛgu made the entire earth devoid of Kṣatriyas. Thereafter he went to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.68.7 \|\|

*tatastai rudhiraiḥ snātvā samādāya tilānbahūn \|*  
*apasavyaṃ samādhāya pracakre pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He took his bath in blood. He took up a large quantity of gingelly seeds and offered the libation pouring it anticlockwise.

## \|\| 1.68.8 \|\|

*pratyakṣaṃ sarvaviprāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ tapasvinām \|*  
*pratijñāṃ pūrayitvā'tha viśokaḥ sa babhūva ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the presence of all Brāhmaṇas and other ascetics, he did thus and fulfilled his vow. Thus he became free from grief.

## \|\| 1.68.9 \|\|

*tato niḥkṣatriye loke kṛtvā hayamakhaṃ ca saḥ \|*  
*prāyacchatsakalāmurvīṃ brāhmaṇebhyaśca dakṣiṇām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the world thus deprived of Kṣatriyas he performed a horse-sacrifice and gifted away the entire earth to Brāhmaṇas along with monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.68.10 \|\|

*atha labdhavarā viprāstamūcurbhṛgusattamam \|*  
*nāsmadbhūmau tvayā stheyameko rājā yataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After receiving all those excellent gifts the Brāhmaṇas to the most excellent scion of the family of Bhṛgu: “You cannot stay in our land because it has been laid down in the Smṛtis that there can be only one king.”

## \|\| 1.68.11-12 \|\|

*so'pi bāḍhamiti procya harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*mahīparyaṃtamāsādya provācātha nadīpatim \|\| 11 \|\|*

*āropya sumahaccāpamāgneyāstraṃ prayujya ca \|*  
*triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā kopena mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Highly delighted he said, “So be it.” Then he went to the end of the land and told the Ocean after stringing his very big bow and fitting an Āgneya missile (missile the deity of which is Fire-god) to it. He knitted his brows in great fury:

## \|\| 1.68.13 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*mayā niḥkṣatriyā bhūmiḥ kṛtā śailavanānvitā \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyastato dattā vājimedhe mahāmakhe \|\| 13 \|\|*

Rāma said:

13\. The earth consisting of mountains and forests was rendered devoid of Kṣatriyas. Thereafter in the great horse-sacrifice, it was gifted to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.68.14 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ dehi me sthānaṃ kṛtvā'pasaraṇaṃ svayam \|*  
*na hi dattvā grahī ṣyāmi viprebhyo medinīṃ punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After gifting the earth to the Brāhmaṇas I will not take it back from them. Hence you recede and give me some space of land.

## \|\| 1.68.15 \|\|

*na karoṣyathavā vākyaṃ mamādya tvaṃ nadīpate \|*  
*sthalarūpaṃ kariṣyāmi vahnyastrapariśoṣitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In case, O Lord of rivers, you do not act according to my direction now, I will dry you up by means of the fire-missile and convert you into a piece of land (i.e. completely devoid of water).

## \|\| 1.68.16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā samudro bhayasaṃkulaḥ \|*  
*apasāraṃ tataścakre yāvattasyābhivāṃchitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sūta said:

16\. On hearing his words, the Ocean became frightened. He receded as far as he desired that he should.

## \|\| 1.68.17 \|\|

*tataścakāra tatraiva vasatiṃ sa bhṛgūdvahaḥ \|*  
*tapaścaryāsamāyuktaḥ piturvadhamanusmaran \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The scion of the family of Bhṛgu made his residence there performing penances (though) he continued to remember the murder of his father.

## \|\| 1.68.18 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvānpulindāṃśca śavarānmedasaṃyutān \|*  
*bhūmyante dhārayāmāsa parvateṣu sa bhārgavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then Bhārgava made all the Pulindas, Śabaras and Medas inhabit the mountains at the frontier of the earth.

## Chapter 69 - Creation of Rāma Hrada

## \|\| 1.69.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato niḥkṣatriye loke kṣattriṇyo vaṃśakāraṇāt \|*  
*kṣetrajānbrāhmaṇebhyaśca suṣuvustanayā nvarān \|\| \|\| 1 \|\|*

*te vṛddhiṃ ca samāsādya kṣetrajāḥ kṣatriyopamāḥ \|*  
*jagṛhurmedinīṃ vīryātsaṃnirasya dvijottamān \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve paribhūtipadaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*procurbhārgavamabhyetya duḥkhena mahatānvitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Thereafter when the earth became devoid of Kṣatriyas, Kṣatriya women desirous of perpetuating their race had union with Brāhmaṇas and gave birth to excellent Kṣetraja sons (sons born from others in one’s wives).
