These Kṣetraja sons grew up and prospered. They came to be equal to Kṣatriyas. With their valour, they expelled the excellent Brāhmaṇas and took possession of the earth.

## \|\| 1.69.4-5 \|\|

*rāmarāma mahābāho yā tvayā vasudhā ca naḥ \|*  
*vājimedhe makhe dattā kṣatriyaiḥ sā hatā balāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasmānno dehi tāṃ bhūyo hatvā tānkṣatriyādhamān \|*  
*kuru śreyo'bhivṛddhiṃ tāṃ yadyasti tava pauruṣam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Thereby the Brāhmaṇas became distressed much on being thus utterly humiliated. They approached Bhārgava and said:

4-5. “O Rāma, O Rāma of powerful arms, the earth that was granted to us by you at the time of the horse-sacrifice, has been forcefully taken possession of by Kṣatriyas. Hence, if you have enough manliness left, kill those base Kṣatriyas and grant us the land once again. Increase our prosperity."

## \|\| 1.69.6 \|\|

*tato rāmaḥ krudhāviṣṭo bhūyastaiḥ śavaraiḥ saha \|*  
*pulindairmedakaiścaiva kṣatriyāṃtāya niryayau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereupon the anger of Rāma was greatly roused. He once again set out along with those Śabaras, Pulindas and Medakas for the extermination of the Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 1.69.7 \|\|

*tatraiva kṣatriyānhatvā raktamādāya tadbahu \|*  
*tāṃ gartāṃ pūrayāmāsa cakāra pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There too he killed the Kṣatriyas, collected much blood, filled the pit dug already and offered libations to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.69.8 \|\|

*pradadau brāhmaṇebhyaśca vājimedhe dharāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*taiśca nirvāsitastatra jagāmodadhisaṃnidhau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the horse-sacrifice performed again, he granted the earth to Brāhmaṇas. On being denied residence (therein) by them, he went back to the seashore.

## \|\| 1.69.9 \|\|

*evaṃ tena kṛtā pṛthvī sarvakṣattravivarjitā \|*  
*triḥsaptavāraṃ vipreṃdrā dvijebhyaśca niveditā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus the earth was rendered devoid of all Kṣatriyas, twenty-one times by him, O eminent Brāhmaṇas. It was then granted to the Brāhmaṇas too.

## \|\| 1.69.10 \|\|

*tarpitāḥ pitaraścaiva rudhireṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*pratijñā pālitā tasmādvikopaśca babhūva saḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Libation was offered to the Pitṛs by that noble-souled one through blood. The vow made was kept up and therefore he became free from anger.

## \|\| 1.69.11 \|\|

*ekaviṃśatime prāpte tataśca pitṛtarpaṇe \|*  
*aśarīrā'bhavadvāṇī khasthā pitṛsamudbhavā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After the libation was offered on the twenty-first time, there was heard an unembodied aerial voice originating from the Pitṛs:

## \|\| 1.69.12-14 \|\|

*rāmarāma mahābhāga tyajaitatkarma garhitam \|*  
*vayaṃ te tuṣṭimāpannāḥ svavākyaparipāla nāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yattvayā vihitaṃ karma naitadanyaḥ kariṣyati \|*  
*na kṛtaṃ kenacitpūrvaṃ pitṛvairasamudbhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmāttuṣṭā vayaṃ vatsa dāsyāmaścitta vāṃchitam \|*  
*prārthayasva drutaṃ tasmāddurlabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. “O Rāma, O highly exalted Rāma, put a stop to this despicable act. We are pleased with you because you kept your word.

What has been done by you, no one other than you, will do; it has not been done by anyone before as a result of the enmity arising from father’s (murder).

So we are all pleased, O dear one. We shall grant you what has been cherished in the heart by you. Therefore, be quick in requesting for it even if it be inaccessible unto even the Devas.”

## \|\| 1.69.15 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*pitaro yadi tuṣṭā me yacchaṃti yadi vāṃchitam \|*  
*tasmāttīrthamidaṃ puṇyaṃ mannāmnā lokaviśrutam \|*  
*raktadoṣavinirmuktaṃ sevitaṃ varatāpasaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Rāma said:

15\. If the Pitṛs are pleased, if they give what is desired, may this meritorious Tîrtha become well known all over the world after my name. Let it be devoid of the defect of blood pollution. Let it be resorted to be excellent sages.

## \|\| 1.69.16 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ \|*  
*pitṛtarpaṇajā gartā tvayā yeyaṃ vinirmitā \|*  
*rāmahrada iti khyātiṃ prayāsyati jagattraye \|\| 16 \|\|*

The pitṛs said:

16\. This Gartā (Pit) made by you, where the libation to the Pitṛs was offered will become famous all over the three worlds as Rāma Hrada.

## \|\| 1.69.17 \|\|

*yatra bhaktiyutā lokāstarpayiṣyaṃti vai pitṝn \|*  
*te'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya prayāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Those people endowed with devotion who offer to the Pitṛs the requisite libation here, will obtain the benefit of Aśvamedha and attain the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.69.18-19 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ māsi bhādrapade naraḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati ca yaḥ śrāddhaṃ bhaktyā śastrahatasya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*api pretatvamāpannaṃ narake vā samāśritam \|*  
*uddhariṣyati sa pretamapi pāpasamanvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. A man who devoutly performs the Śrāddha unto one killed by weapons on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Bhādrapada will cause the redemption of that ancestor even if he had attained the state of a Preta or fallen into Naraka. It docs not matter if he was a sinner.

## \|\| 1.69.20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā tu rāmaṃ te viremustadanaṃtaram \|*  
*rāmo'pi ca tapastepe tatraiva krodhavarjitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sūta said:

20\. After saying thus to Rāma, they ceased (to speak and disappeared). Thereafter Rāma eschewed his anger completely and performed penance there itself.

## \|\| 1.69.21 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra śastrahatasya ca \|*  
*tasmindine prakartavyaṃ śrāddhaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence by all means, one should perform Śrāddha with full faith, to the person killed by a weapon on the same day (occurring every year).

## \|\| 1.69.22 \|\|

*upasarga mṛtānāṃ ca sarpāgniviṣabandhanaiḥ \|*  
*tatra muktipradaṃ śrāddhaṃ dine tasminnudāhṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Śrāddha on the concerned day is cited as that which yields salvation unto those dead due to violent injury, serpent bite, fire, eating poison or hanging.

## \|\| 1.69.23 \|\|

*yaḥ pitṝṃstarpayettatra pretapakṣe jalairapi \|*  
*sa teṣāmanṛṇo bhūtvā pitṛloke mahīyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. One who performs libation rites to the Pitṛs even with water during the Pretapakṣa (dark half of Bhādrapada) becomes free from indebtedness to them and he is honoured in Pitṛloka.

## \|\| 1.69.24 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ rāmahradasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus everything connected with Rāmaharda has been entirely recounted to you. The greatness thereof is detractive of all sins, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.69.25 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle naro bhaktyā yaścaitatpaṭhati svayam \|*  
*sa gayāśrāddhajaṃ kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A man who devoutly reads this himself at the time of Śrāddha shall undoubtedly obtain the entire benefit arising from Gayā Śrāddha.

## \|\| 1.69.26 \|\|

*parvakāle 'thavā prāpte paṭhedbrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau \|*  
*pitṛmedhasya yajñasya sa phalaṃ labhate 'khilam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One should read this in the presence of Brāhmaṇas at the time of Parvans (festive occasions). Thereby one obtains the entire benefit of Pitṛmedha (Yajña pertaining to Pitṛs).

## \|\| 1.69.27 \|\|

*śṛṇuyādvāpi yo bhaktyā kīrtyamānamidaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sautrāmaṇau kṛte kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A man who devoutly listens to this on being recited obtains undoubtedly the entire benefit of Sautrāmaṇi Yajña.

## Chapter 70 - Birth of Kārttikeya (Skanda)

## \|\| 1.70.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti śaktiḥ pāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*kārtikeyena nirmuktā hatvā vai tārakaṃ raṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathāsti sumahatkuṇḍaṃ svacchodakasamāvṛtam \|*  
*tenaiva nirmitaṃ tatra yaḥ snātvā tāṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*sa pāpānmucyate sadya ājanmamaraṇāṃti kāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle vinirmuktā sā śaktistena no vada \|*  
*kimarthaṃ svāminā tatra kiṃprabhāvā vada svayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: Birth of Skanda or Kārttikeya and his exploit of killing the Dānava Tāraka are described in Mahābhārata, Vana Ch. 226 and in other Purāṇas. It is adapted here to claim that the Śakti with which Skanda killed Tāraka is in Camatkārapura. Similar claim is made in the Revākhaṇḍa of Skanda Purāṇa for Bhṛgu Kaccha. The differences of the story in (his Purāṇa and in Mahābhārata are noticed at proper places.

Sūta said:

1-3. Similarly there is another Śakti there that destroys sins. It is the Śakti (holy javelin) discharged by Kārttikeya after killing Tāraka in battle.

Further there is also a very great Kuṇḍa filled with clear water caused by himself (Kārttikeya). One who takes his holy bath there and performs the worship is immediately liberated from the sin committed ever since birth and until death.

## \|\| 1.70.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāsīttārakonāma dānavo'tibalānvitaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣasya dāyādastrailokyasya bhayāvahaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

At what time was that Śakti discharged by him? Tell us. Why was it discharged by the Lord? What is its efficacy? Do narrate it yourself.

Sūta said:

4\. Formerly there was a very powerful Dānava named Tāraka. He was successor of Hiraṇyākṣa and he caused terror in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.70.5 \|\|

*sa jñātvā janakaṃ dhvastaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tapastepe tatastīvraṃ gokarṇaṃ prāpya parvatam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After coming to know that his father had been killed by the powerful Viṣṇu, he went to Gokarṇa mountain and performed a very severe penance.

## \|\| 1.70.6 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ śīrṇaparṇā śanaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyamāno mahādevaṃ kāyena manasā girā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He sustained himself by consuming withered dry leaves and continued the meditation on Mahādeva for a thousand years mentally, verbally and physically.

## \|\| 1.70.7-8 \|\|

*varupūjopahāraiśca naivedyairvividhaistataḥ \|*  
*tato varṣasahasrāṃte sa daityo duḥkhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*jñātvā rudramasaṃtuṣṭaṃ tato raudraṃ tapo'karot \|*  
*viniṣkṛttyātmamāṃsāni juhotisma hutāśane \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. He offered excellent articles of worship and different kinds of food-stuffs. Even at the end of those thousand years, Rudra was not pleased. This made the Daitya distressed and he performed still severer penance. He cut off pieces of flesh from his body and consigned them into the sacred fire.

## \|\| 1.70.9 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevo vṛṣārūḍha umāpatiḥ \|*  
*sarvaireva gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ tasya saṃdarśanaṃ yayau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereupon Mahādeva was pleased. Riding on his bull, the Consort of Umā appeared before him along with all his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 1.70.10 \|\|

*tatra provāca saṃhṛṣṭastāranādena nādayan \|*  
*diśaḥ sarvā mahādevo harṣa gadgadayā girā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In words faltering with excessive delight, Mahādeva joyously rendered all the quarters resonant with his voice of high pitch and spoke:

## \|\| 1.70.11 \|\|

*bhobhostāraka tuṣṭo'smi sāhasaṃ medṛśaṃ kuru \|*  
*prārthayasva mano'bhīṣṭaṃ yena te pradadāmyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “O Tāraka, I am pleased. Do not persist further in a risky venture like this. Request for anything you may desire, so that I can grant the same.”

## \|\| 1.70.12 \|\|

*tāraka uvāca \|*  
*ajeyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvatprasādādahaṃ vibho \|*  
*yathā bhavāmi saṃgrāme tvāṃ vihāya tathā kuru \|\| 12 \|\|*

Tāraka said:

12\. O Lord, thanks to your favour, let me be invincible unto all the Devas. Make it possible for me to defeat all in battle except you.

## \|\| 1.70.13 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*matprasādādasaṃdigdhaṃ sarvametadbhaviṣyati \|*  
*tvayā yatprārthitaṃ daitya tvameko balavāniha \|\| 13 \|\|*

The Lord said:

13\. With my favour, all this will happen. Undoubtedly, O Daitya, whatever has been requested for by you will become effective. You shall be the sole mighty warrior.

## \|\| 1.70.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahādevaḥ svameva bhavanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tārakaścāpi saṃhṛṣṭastathaivanija mandiram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After saying this, Mahādeva went to his abode. The delighted demon Tāraka too went home.

## \|\| 1.70.15 \|\|

*tato dānavasainyena mahatā parivāritaḥ \|*  
*gataḥ śakrapurīṃ yoddhuṃ vikhyātāmamarāvatīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, accompanied by a vast army of Dānavas, he went to Amarāvatī, the well-known city of Indra, for fighting with him.

## \|\| 1.70.16 \|\|

*athābhavanmahāyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃte mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, a great battle of Devas with Dānavas ensued

and continued for a thousand years when the god of Death never turned back.

## \|\| 1.70.17 \|\|

*tatrābhavatkṣayo nityaṃ devānāṃ raṇamūrdhani \|*  
*vijayo dānavānāṃ ca prasādācchūlapā ṇinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Devas faced destruction every day in the battlefield and the Dānavas gained victory with the favour of the Trident-bearing Lord.

## \|\| 1.70.18-20 \|\|

*tataścakrurupāyāṃste vijayāya divaukasaḥ \|*  
*varmāṇi suvicitrāṇi yantrāṇi parikhāstathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*anyānyapi śarīrasya rakṣaṇārthaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tathaiva yodhamukhyānāṃ viśeṣāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sasṛjuste surādhīśā dānavebhyo divāniśam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. For the purpose of ultimate victory, the Heaven-dwellers resorted to all possible means. Various kinds of armours, mechanical devices, trenches etc., for the sake of general protection were ardently prepared by them, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Other things also they got ready for protecting the bodies of the principal warriors in particular. The chiefs of Suras created various things to guard themselves from Dānavas day and night.

## \|\| 1.70.21 \|\|

*mudgarā bhiṃḍipālāśca śataghnyo'tha vareṣavaḥ \|*  
*prāsāḥ kuntāśca bhallāśca tasminkāle vinirmitāḥ \|*  
*viśeṣāhavasaṃbandhavyūhānāṃ prakriyāśca yāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At that time Mudgaras (hammer-like rods), Bhindipālas (a short javelin), Śataghnīs (cannon-like devices capable of killing a hundred at a time), excellent arrows, Prāsas (javelins), Kuntas (spears), Bhallas (spike-like weapons) etc. were prepared. They evolved strategic modes of special battle arrays also.

## \|\| 1.70.22 \|\|

*tathānyāni vicitrāṇi kūṭayuddhānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*bhīṣikāḥ kuhakāścaiva śakrajālāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Kūṭayuddhas (deceptive warfare) of diverse kinds, threats, hoodwinking tricks and Indrajāla (wizardry) were made use of entirely.

## \|\| 1.70.23 \|\|

*na ca te vijayaṃ prāpustathāpi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*dānavebhyo mahāyuddhe prahārairjarjarīkṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Still, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they did not gain any victory over the Dānavas. Smitten and shattered in the great battle they became distressed.

## \|\| 1.70.24-26 \|\|

*atha prāha sahasrākṣo bhayatrasto bṛhaspatim \|*  
*dinedine vayaṃ daityairvijayāmo dvijottama \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yathāyathā raṇārthāya sadupāyānkaromyaham \|*  
*tathātathā parābhūtirjāyate me mahāhave \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tadupāyaṃ surācārya svabuddhyā tvaṃ pracintaya \|*  
*yena me syājjayo yuddhe tava kīrtiraninditā 0 \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Then the frightened Thousand-eyed One (Indra) said to Bṛhaspati: “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, every day we are getting defeated by the Daityas. The more I get ready with better means of warfare, the greater is our defeat in the tremendous war. Hence, O preceptor of Suras, think of some intelligent means whereby I can win the war and you, a blameless reputation as its result.”

## \|\| 1.70.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato bṛhaspatiḥ prāha ciraṃ dhyātvā śacīpatim \|*  
*prahṛṣṭavadano jñātvā jayopāyaṃ mahāhave \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. Then Bṛhaspati thought for a long time. After finding out the means of victory in the great battle, his face beamed with delight. Then he said to the Consort of Śacī:

## \|\| 1.70.28-34 \|\|

*mayā śakra parijñātaḥ sa upāyo mahāhave \|*  
*jīyante śatravo yena līlayaivāpi bhūriśaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yadābhīṣṭaṃ varaṃ tena prārthitastripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*tadaivaṃ vacanaṃ prāha praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ajeyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvatprasādādahaṃ vibho \|*  
*yathā bhavāmi saṃgrāme tvāṃ vihāya tathā kuru \|\| 30 \|\|*

*na taṃ svayaṃ mahādevaḥ svaśiṣyaṃ sūdayiṣyati \|*  
*viṣavṛkṣamapi sthāpya kaśchinatti punaḥ svayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yo vai pitā sa putraḥ syācchrutivākyamidaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tasmājjanayatu kṣipraṃ harastannāśakṛtsutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yena senādhipatye taṃ viniyojya mahāhavam \|*  
*kurmo daityaiḥ samaṃ śastraiḥ prāpnuyāma tato jayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*eṣa eva upāyo'tra mayā te parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*vijayāya sahasrākṣa nānyo'sti bhuvanatraye \|\| 34 \|\|*

28-34. “That means has been found out by me, O Śakra, whereby most of the enemies can be sportingly defeated in the great battle.

When the Slayer of the Three Puras was requested by him for the desired boon, the Daitya had repeatedly bowed to him and spoken these words:

'O Lord, let me be invincible unto all the Devas with your favour. Make it possible for me to defeat all in battle except you.’

Mahādeva himself will never slay him who is his disciple. Who thinks it fit to cut down even a poisonous tree, should he happen to be the one who had planted it?

‘He who is the father shall be the son as well.’ This Vedic statement is often proclaimed. So let Hara procreate a son who will slay him (Tāraka).

Then we shall appoint him as the commander-in-chief and fight a bitter fight with the Daityas and ultimately gain victory.

This is the means which I just explained, O Thousand-eyed One. There is no other means of victory in all the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.70.35 \|\|

*tato devagaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ sametaḥ pākaśāsanaḥ \|\| \|*  
*tamarthaṃ proktavāñchaṃbhuṃ vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereafter the Slayer of Pāka went to Śaṃbhu along with the groups of Devas and requested him after bowing down to him humbly:

## \|\| 1.70.36-38 \|\|

*sutasya jananārthāya kuru yatnaṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*yena senādhipatye taṃ yojayāmi divaukasām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*prāpnomyahaṃ ca saṃgrāme vijayaṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|*  
*nihatya dānavānsarvāṃstārakeṇa samanvitān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nānyathā vijayo me syātsaṃgrāme dānavaiḥ saha \|\| \|*  
*iti māṃ prāha devejyo jñātvā samyaṅmahāmatiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. “O Bull-emblemed One, it behoves you to exert yourself for the procreation of a son, so that I can appoint him as the commander-in-chief of the Heaven-dwellers.

With your favour I shall gain victory in the battle after killing all the Dānavas including Tāraka.

There is no other means for my victory in the battle with the Dānavas. So says the highly intelligent Devejya (Preceptor of gods i.e. Bṛhaspati) after perfectly considering everything.”

## \|\| 1.70.39-40 \|\|

*athovāca vihasyoccaiḥ śaṃkarastridaśeśvaram \|*  
*kariṣyāmi vacaḥ kṣipraṃ tava śakra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*putramutpādayiṣyāmi sarvadaityavināśakam \|*  
*yaṃ tvaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā jayaṃ prāpsyasi sarvadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Thereupon Śaṅkara laughed boisterously and spoke to the Lord of Devas: “O Śakra, I shall soon do what you suggest There is no doubt about it. I shall procreate a son who will destroy all the Daityas. You can make him the commander of your army and be crowned with success always.”

## \|\| 1.70.41 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahādevo gatvā kailāsa parvatam \|*  
*gauryā samaṃ tataścakre kāmadharmaṃ yathocitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After saying thus Mahādeva went to the Kailāsa mountain and started a befitting sexual dalliance with Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.70.42 \|\|

*hāvairbhāvaiḥ samopetaṃ hāsyairanyaistadātmikaiḥ \|*  
*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ divyaṃ caiva nimeṣavat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It was fully accompanied by coquettish blandishments, emotional fervour, jocular remarks and other things of the sort. A period of a thousand divine years passed like a moment.

## \|\| 1.70.43 \|\|

*atha devagaṇāḥ sarve bhayasaṃtrastamānasāḥ \|*  
*cakrurmaṃtraṃ tadarthaṃ hi tārakeṇa prapīḍitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Here, all the groups of Devas, harassed by Tāraka and hence utterly terrified in their minds met together and had consultations with one another:

## \|\| 1.70.44-45 \|\|

*sahasraṃ vatsarāṇāṃ tu ratāsaktasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*atikrāṃtaṃ na devānāṃ tena kṛtyaṃ vinirmitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmādgacchāmahe tatra yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhate samaṃ gauryā kailāse vijane sthitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. “A thousand years have elapsed and the Tridentbearing One is continuously engaged in the sexual dalliance. He has not carried out the task of Devas. Hence we shall go to the Kailāsa mountain where Lord Maheśvara is in union with Gaurī in a secluded spot.”

## \|\| 1.70.46 \|\|

*tatastatraiva saṃjagmuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*udvahantaḥ parāmārtiṃ tārakārisamudbhavām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In the height of their distress arising from the frustrated hope about (the birth of) an enemy of Tāraka, all the Devas including Vāsava went there itself.

## \|\| 1.70.47-48 \|\|

*atha kailāsamāsādya yāvadyāṃti bhavāṃtikam \|*  
*niṣiddhā naṃdinā tāvanna gaṃtavyamataḥ param \|\| 47 \|\|*

*rahasye bhagavānsārdhaṃ pārvatyā samavasthitaḥ \|*  
*asmākamapi no gamyaṃ tasmāttāvanna gamyatām \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. They reached mount Kailāsa and attempted to go near Bhava. But they were prevented by Nandin saying, “You must not go beyond this. The Lord is present here in a secluded spot along with Pārvatī. Even we have no right to enter. Do not go.”

## \|\| 1.70.49 \|\|

*tatastairvibudhaiḥ sarvaiḥ preṣitastatra cānilaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ karoti mahādevaḥ śīghraṃ vijñāyatāmiti \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then all the Devas sent the Wind-god there. They told him, “Let this be quickly found out what Mahādeva is doing there.”

## \|\| 1.70.50 \|\|

*atha vāyurgatastatra yatrāste bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*gauryā saha ratāsakta ānandaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then the Wind-god went to that spot where Lord Śiva was in the acme of bliss in the act of sexual dalliance with Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.70.51 \|\|

*atha pracalite śukre sthānādaprāptayonike \|*  
*devena vīkṣito vāyurnātidūre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There was an emission of the semen but it did not reach the vaginal aperture. At that time the Lord saw Vāyu standing not very far away.

## \|\| 1.70.52 \|\|

*tato vrīḍā samopetastatkṣaṇādeva cotthitaḥ \|*  
*bhāvāsaktāṃ priyāṃ tyaktvā mā mottiṣṭhetivādinīm \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Feeling abashed very much the Lord got up instantly leaving his beloved alone in the acme of excitement and emotion saying, “Oh, don’t get up.”

## \|\| 1.70.53 \|\|

*abravīdatha taṃ vāyuṃ vinayāvanataṃ sthitam \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tvamihāyātaḥ kaccitkṣemaṃ divaukasām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He then said to Vāyu who was standing humbly, “Why did you come here? I hope the Heaven-dwellers are all right.”

## \|\| 1.70.54 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*ete śakrādayo devā naṃdinā vinivāritāḥ \|*  
*tārakeṇa hatotsāhāstiṣṭhaṃti girirodhasi \|\| 54 \|\|*

Vāyu said:

54\. Here Śakra and other Devas have been stopped by Nandin. All of them are dispirited and without enthusiasm. They are now waiting on the ridge of the mountain.

## \|\| 1.70.55 \|\|

*tasmādetānsamābhāṣya samāśvāsya ca sādaram \|*  
*preṣayasva drutaṃ tatra yatra te dānavāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. So, do talk to them and console them with encouraging words. Send them also immediately to the place occupied by the Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.70.56 \|\|

*atha tānāhvayāmāma tatkṣaṇāttripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāha caviṣaṇṇāsyaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭānsthitān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Instantly the Slayer of the Three Puras summoned them. With dejected face, he addressed them as they stood with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.70.57 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yuṣmatkṛte samāraṃbhaḥ putrārthaṃ yo mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*svasthānāccalite śukre kṛto moghodya vāyunā \|\| 57 \|\|*

The Lord said:

57\. I started my endeavour for the procreation of a son for the sake of you all. The seminal fluid has been displaced from the organ of secretion but rendered ineffective by Vāyu (by his intervention).

## \|\| 1.70.58 \|\|

*etadvīryaṃ mayā dhairyātstaṃbhitaṃ liṃgamadhyagam \|*  
*amoghaṃ tiṣṭhate sarvaṃ kva dadhāmi nivedyatām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It (seminal fluid) has been retained with great restraint by me within the penis. It cannot go in vain. Tell me where I can deposit it.

## \|\| 1.70.59 \|\|

*yena saṃjāyate putro dānavāṃtakaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*senānāthaśca yuṣmākaṃ durddharaḥ samare paraiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It is from that, that a great son who will destroy the Dānavas is to be born. He shall be the leader of your army. He will be irresistible in the battle by his enemies.

## \|\| 1.70.60 \|\|

*etatkalpāgnisaṃkāśaṃ dhartuṃ śaknoti nāparaḥ \|*  
*vinā vaiśvānaraṃ tasmāddadhātveṣa sanātanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Except Vaiśvānara (Fire-god) no one else is capable of retaining it. It resembles the Kalpāgni fire. So let him come forward and retain this eternal fluid.

## \|\| 1.70.61 \|\|

*yena tatra pramuñcāmi sutāya vijayāya ca \|*  
*etadvīryaṃ mahātīvraṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then only can I release this intensely powerful seminal fluid lustrous like twelve suns (united together) for the sake of a son in order to win victory.

## \|\| 1.70.62 \|\|

*atha prāhuḥ surāḥ sarve vahniṃ saṃślāghya sādarāḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ dhārayāgne vaktrāṃte vīryametadbhavodbhavam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then all the Suras praised Vahni (Fire) and eagerly said to him, “O Agni, do hold this seminal fluid of Bhava within your mouth.”

## \|\| 1.70.63 \|\|

*tataḥ prasārayāmāsa svavaktraṃ pāvako drutam \|*  
*kurvañchakrasamādeśamavikalpena cetasā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Carrying out the behest of Śakra unhesitatingly Pāvaka (Fire) quickly opened his mouth.

## \|\| 1.70.64 \|\|

*śaṃkaro'pyakṣipattatra kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*gaurīṃ bhagavatīṃ dhyāyannānandaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Śaṅkara who had been afflicted by the arrows of Kama thought of goddess Gaurī, experienced the bliss of orgasm and deposited the fluid there (in Agni’s mouth).

## \|\| 1.70.65 \|\|

*pāvako'pi bhṛśaṃ tena kalpāgnisadṛśena ca \|*  
*dahyamāno'kṣipadbhūmau śarastaṃbe suvistare \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Being scorched by that fluid that resembled fire appearing at the end of the universe, Pāvaka dropped it on the ground in the spacious grove of reeds.

## \|\| 1.70.66 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā bhramamāṇā itastataḥ \|*  
*bhāryāstatra munīnāṃ tāḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṭkṛttikāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In the meantime the auspicious six Kṛttikās, the wives of the six sages who had been wandering here and there came to that place.

## \|\| 1.70.67-68 \|\|

*tāsāṃ nideśayāmāsa svayameva śatakratuḥ \|*  
*etadbījaṃ trinetrasya paripālyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*atra saṃpatsyate putro dvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*bhavatīnāmapi prāyaḥ putratvaṃ saṃprayāsyati \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Śatakratu himself gave them this direction: “This seminal fluid of the Three-eyed Lord should be preserved cautiously (by you). Herefrom will be born a son having the lustre of twelve suns. He will be almost a son unto ye all.”

## Chapter 71 - Installation of Skanda’s Śakti

## \|\| 1.71.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tāstatheti pratijñāya cakrustacchakraśāsanam \|*  
*sūtikāgṛhadharme yattaccakrustasya sarvaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*athānyadivase bālo dvādaśārkasamadyutiḥ \|*  
*saṃjajñe tena vīryeṇa dvibhujaika mukhaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yathāsau jātamātrastu praruroda suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā ruditaṃ sarvāḥ kṛttikāstamupāgatāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Assenting “So be it”, those ladies carried out the behest of Śakra. They performed all his post-natal rites to be performed in the lying-in-chamber.

The next day, the boy gained the lustre akin to that of twelve suns. He was born with two arms and a single face.

As soon as the auspicious child was born he miserably cried. On hearing his cry, all the Kṛttikās came to him.

## \|\| 1.71.4 \|\|

*mahāseno'pi saṃvīkṣya mātṝstāḥ samupāgatāḥ \|*  
*sotkaṇṭhaḥ ṣaṇmukho jāto dvādaśākṣabhujastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing those mothers approaching, Mahāsena became anxious and one with six faces, twelve eyes and twelve arms.

## \|\| 1.71.5 \|\|

*ekaikasyāḥ pṛthaktena prapapau prayataḥ stanam \|*  
*dvābhyāmāliṃgayāmāsa bhujābhyāṃ snehapūrvakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With great affection, he embraced each of them separately with two arms and sucked the milk from the breast of each.

## \|\| 1.71.6 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*sarve devāḥ sahendreṇa gandharvāpsarasastathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the meantime Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and all other Devas, Gandharvas, Apsarās came there along with Indra.

## \|\| 1.71.7 \|\|

*mahotsavo'tha saṃjajñe tasminsthāne nirargalaḥ \|*  
*gītavādyapraṇādena yenaviśvaṃ prapūritam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At that spot, great festivities were held without any restraint. The entire universe was filled with the sound of music and musical instruments.

## \|\| 1.71.8 \|\|

*raṃbhādyā nanṛtustasya vilāsinyo divaukasām \|*  
*jaguśca mukhyagandharvā ścitrāṃgadamukhāśca ye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Raṃbhā and other graceful maidens of Heaven-dwellers danced there. Gandharva chiefs such as Citrāṅgada and others sang.

## \|\| 1.71.9 \|\|

*tatastu devatāḥ sarvāstasya nāma pracakrire \|*  
*skandanādretaso bhūmau skanda ityeva sādaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then all the Devas respectfully gave him the name Skanda because the seminal fluid was spilled on the ground.

## \|\| 1.71.10 \|\|

*atha tasya kumā rasya tadā tatrābhiṣecanam \|*  
*senāpatyaṃ kṛtaṃ sākṣāddevānāṃ śaṃbhunā svayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the coronation of that boy as the commander-in-chief of the army of Devas was performed by Śaṃbhu himself.

## \|\| 1.71.11 \|\|

*tasya śaktiḥ svayaṃ dattā vidhinā'dbhutadarśanā \|*  
*amoghā vijayārthāya daityapakṣakṣayāya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A Śakti of miraculous appearance and unfailing forever was given to him by Vidhi (Brahmā) for gaining victory (of Devas) and the destruction of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.71.12 \|\|

*mayūro vāhanārthāya tryaṃbakeṇa suśīghrataḥ \|*  
*divyāstrāṇi mahendreṇa viṣṇunātha mahātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A Mayūra (peacock) was quickly given by the Three-eyed Lord as the boy's vehicle. Divine weapons were given by Mahendra and the noble-souled Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.71.13 \|\|

*tato'bhīṣṭāni śastrāṇi devaiḥ sarvaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*tasya dattāni saṃtuṣṭaistathā mātṛgaṇairapi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereafter the desired missiles were given severally by all the Devas and the groups of mother goddesses who were delighted.

## \|\| 1.71.14 \|\|

*tatastamagrataḥ kṛtvā senānāthaṃ sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*jagmuḥ sasainikāstatra tārako yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then keeping him in the forefront as the leader of the armies, the chiefs of Suras and their soldiers went to the place where Tāraka was present.

## \|\| 1.71.15 \|\|

*tārako'pi samālokya devānsvayamupāgatān \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ harṣasaṃyuktaḥ sammukhaḥ satvaraṃ yayau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On observing that Devas themselves had come for fighting, Tāraka was delighted. Hurriedly he came face to face with them.

## \|\| 1.71.16 \|\|

*tato'bhūtsumahadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*kopasaṃraktanetrāṇāṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A great battle ensued between Devas and Dānavas. With their eyes redened with anger, they set at nought the fear of death.

## \|\| 1.71.17 \|\|

*atha skandena saṃvīkṣya dūrasthaṃ tārakaṃ raṇe \|*  
*samāhūya tato muktā sā śaktistasya mṛtyave \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing Tāraka far away in the battlefield, Skanda challenged him and hurled the Śakti towards him to kill him.

## \|\| 1.71.18 \|\|

*athāsau hṛdayaṃ bhittvā tasya daityasya dāruṇā \|*  
*camatkārapuropāṃte patitā rudhirokṣitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The terrible Śakti pierced the heart of the Daitya and fell down at the outskirts of Camatkārapura. It was besmeared with blood.

## \|\| 1.71.19-20 \|\|

*tārakastu gato nāśaṃ muktaḥ prāṇaiśca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve saṃhṛṣṭāstaṃ mahābalam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*stotrairbahuvidhaiḥ stutvā procustasminhate sati \|*  
*gatāśca tridivaṃ tūrṇaṃ saha śakreṇa nirbhayāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Tāraka was doomed. In an instant his life became extinct. Then all the groups of Devas became delighted. They eulogized the mighty Lord Kārttikeya with hymns of diverse kinds when Tāraka fell dead. Free from fear, they went quickly to heaven along with Indra.

## \|\| 1.71.21 \|\|

*skando'pi tāṃ samādāya śaktiṃ tatra purottame \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa yenaiva raktaśṛṃgo'bhavaddṛḍhaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Skanda took up that Śakti and fixed it there in the excellent city whereby Raktaśṛṅga became firm and steady.

## \|\| 1.71.22 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*raktaśṛṃgaḥ kathaṃ tena niścalo'pi dṛḍhīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*kasya vākyena no brūhi vistareṇa mahāmate \|\| 22 \|\|*

The sages said:

22\. That Raktaśṛṅga which was already motionless was rendered firm by him? At whose instance? O highly intelligent one, tell us in detail.

## \|\| 1.71.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā vai bhūmikampastu saṃprajātaḥ sudāruṇaḥ \|*  
*raktaśṛṅgaḥ pracalitaḥ svasthānādativegataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:

23\. There was a terrible earthquake once when Raktaśṛṅga swayed from its position violently.

## \|\| 1.71.24-25 \|\|

*tasya daityasya pātena yathānye parva tottamāḥ \|*  
*atha harmyāṇi sarvāṇi camatkārapure tadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śīrṇāni calite tasminparvate vyathitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*prāyaśo nidhanaṃ prāptāstathā'nye mūrchayārditāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The earthquake was due to the fall of that Daitya. Like the other excellent mountains, Raktaśṛṅga too swayed. Further all the mansions in Camatkārapura crumbled down. When the mountain swayed to and fro the Brāhmaṇas became distressed. Most of them lost all their possessions and became poor. Others became afflicted by loss of consciousness.

## \|\| 1.71.26-27 \|\|

*hataśeṣāstato viprā gatvā skandaṃ krudhānvitāḥ \|*  
*procuśca kimidaṃ pāpa tvayā kṛtamabuddhinā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nāśaṃ nītā vayaṃ sarve saputrapaśubādhavāḥ \|*  
*tasmācchāpaṃ pradāsyāmo vayaṃ duḥkhena duḥkhitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The Brāhmaṇas who survived rushed to Skanda angrily and said, “O sinner, what is this done by you foolishly? We are all ruined along with our sons, kinsmen and cattle-wealth. So due to our excess of misery, we will curse you.”

## \|\| 1.71.28 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokānāṃ mayaitatsamanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*yaddhato dānavo raudro nānyathā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Skanda said:

28\. This has been carried out by me for the welfare of all the worlds. The terrible Dānava has been killed. This could not have happened otherwise, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.71.29-30 \|\|

*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ tasmānmānyā me brāhmaṇāḥ sadā \|*  
*mṛtānapi dvijānsarvānahaṃ tānamṛtāśrayāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*punarjīvitasaṃyuktānkariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tathā suniścalaṃ śailaṃ kariṣyāmi svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Be pleased therefore. Brāhmaṇas are always worthy of my honour. By resorting to Amṛta (Nectar) I shall resuscitate the dead Brāhmaṇas once again. There is no doubt about it. Similarly, with my Śakti I shall make the mountain very stable.

## \|\| 1.71.31 \|\|

*evamuktvā samādāya tāṃ śaktiṃ rudhirokṣitām \|*  
*cakre sthāpanamasyāstu raktaśṛṅgasya mūrdhani \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After saying thus, he took up the Śakti besmeared with blood and installed it on the top of Raktaśṛṅga.

## \|\| 1.71.32 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca saṃhṛṣṭo devatānāṃ catuṣṭayam \|*  
*āṃbavṛddhāṃ tathaivāmrāṃ māhitthāṃ ca camatkarīm \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then he spoke joyously to the four deities viz. Āmbavṛddhā, Āmrā, Māhitthā and Camatkarī:

## \|\| 1.71.33-34 \|\|

*yuṣmābhirniścalaḥ kāryo bhūyo'yaṃ nagasattamaḥ \|*  
*pralaye'pi yathā sthānādraktaśṛṅgaścalennahi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sadaiva khyātimāyātu mannāmnā puramuttamam \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ sarve pūjāṃ dāsyaṃti sarvadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “This excellent mountain should be kept stable and motionless again by you all, so that this Raktaśṛṅga shall not move from its place even at the time of Pralaya. Let this excellent city be well-known forever after my name. All the Brāhmaṇas will adore you always.”

## \|\| 1.71.35 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva tāḥ procya caturdikṣu tataśca tam \|*  
*śūlāgraiḥ sudṛḍhaṃ cakruḥ skandavākyena harṣitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Delighted by the words of Skanda, they said: “Of course”. With the tips of tridents fixed in all directions, they steadied it further.

## \|\| 1.71.36 \|\|

*tataścāmṛtamādāya mṛtānapi dvijottamān \|*  
*skando jīvāpayāmāsa dvijabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then Skanda ardent in the devotion to Brāhmaṇas, took Amṛta and enlivened the dead excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.71.37 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāstatra saṃhṛṣṭā varamuttamam \|*  
*dadustasya sa ca prāha mannāmaitatpurottamam \|*  
*sadaiva khyātimāyātu etanme hṛdi vāṃchitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The delighted Brāhmaṇas granted him the excellent boon. He said, “Let this excellent city become well known forever after my name. This is my desire.”

## \|\| 1.71.38 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*etatskandapuraṃnāma tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ tadvatsāṃprataṃ surasattama \|\| 38 \|\|*

The sages said:

38\. O most excellent one among Suras, this excellent city now called Camatkārapura will be known also by the name Skandapura after your name.

## \|\| 1.71.39 \|\|

*pūjāṃ tava kariṣyāmaḥ kṛtvā prāsādamutta mam \|*  
*tathaiva devatāḥ sarvāścatasro'pi tvayā dhṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. We shall erect an excellent mansion (temple) and shall offer worship to you as well as the four deities supported by you.

## \|\| 1.71.40 \|\|

*sarvāḥ saṃpūjayiṣyāmaḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sādaram \|*  
*etāṃ caṃ tāvakīṃ śaktiṃ sadā suravarottama \|*  
*viśeṣātpūjayiṣyāmaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. We shall evince respectful reverence in all our rites, O most excellent one among the chiefs of Suras, we shall always worship this Śakti of yours faithfully on the sixth lunar day.

## \|\| 1.71.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa brāhmaṇaiḥ prokto mahāseno mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sthitastatraiva tadvā kyājjñātvā tatkṣetramuttamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

41\. Promised thus by the Brāhmaṇas, the mighty Mahāsena stayed there itself at their instance after realizing that it was an excellent holy place.

## \|\| 1.71.42 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā caitraṣaṣṭhyāṃ subhāvataḥ \|*  
*śuklāyāṃ tasya saṃtuṣṭiṃ kurute barhivāhanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If any one devoutly worships him with great emotional fervour on the sixth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, the Peacock-vehicled Lord will make him satisfied.

## \|\| 1.71.43 \|\|

*tasyāṃ śaktau naro yaśca kuryātpṛṣṭhinigharṣaṇam \|*  
*pūjayitvā tu puṣpādyaiḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa na syādrogasaṃyukto yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O Brāhmaṇas, a man who worships that Śakti with perfect faith with flowers etc., and then rubs his back against the Śakti shall never fall sick for a whole year.

## \|\| 1.71.44 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra dhṛtā śaktistena skandena dhīmatā \|*  
*raktaśṛṃgasya rakṣārthaṃ tatpurasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus his Śakti was fixed there by the intelligent Skanda for the protection of Raktaśṛṅga and that city in particular.

## Chapter 72 - Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s Pilgrimage to Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.72.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*duryodhanena cālokya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle narendreṇa dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*tatra saṃsthāpitaṃ ligaṃ vada tvaṃ raumaharṣaṇe \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 72-74 describe when and why Dhṛtarāṣṭra (Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas) installed Liṅga at Hāṭakeśvara. The story has no basis either in Mahābhārata or in Bhāgavata but the author wishes to record the visit of these celebrities to Hāṭakeśvara.

Sūta said:

1-2. A Liṅga was installed there by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and also by Duryodhana. Viewing it, one is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.72.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsīdbhānumatīnāma balabhadrasutā purā \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā rūpau dāryaguṇānvitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

O son of Romaharṣaṇa, when was the Liṅga installed there by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra? Do tell us.

Sūta said:

3\. Formerly Balabhadra had a daughter named Bhānumatī. She was richly endowed with all the excellent features. She was endowed with good qualities, beauty etc.

## \|\| 1.72.4 \|\|

*tāṃ dadāvatha patnyarthe dhārtarāṣṭrāya dhīmate \|*  
*duryodhanāya saṃmantrya viṣṇunā saha yādavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The scion of the Yadava family consulted Viṣṇu (i.e. Kṛṣṇa) and gave her to Duryodhana, the intelligent son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, as his wife.

## \|\| 1.72.5 \|\|

*atha nāgapurātsarve bhīṣma droṇādayaśca ye \|*  
*kauravāḥ prasthitāstūrṇaṃ purīṃ dvāravatīṃ prati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then Bhīṣma, Droṇa and all the Kauravas started immediately for the city of Dvārakā from Hastināpura.

## \|\| 1.72.6 \|\|

*tathā pāṃḍusutāḥ paṃca parivārasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*saubhrātraṃ manyamānāste duryodhanasamanvi tāḥ \|*  
*jagmurdvāravatīṃ hṛṣṭāḥ sainyena mahatānvitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In view of their excellent fraternal consideration, all the five sons of Pāṇḍu and their attendants and followers joyously accompanied Duryodhana and proceeded towards Dvārakā along with their vast army.

## \|\| 1.72.7 \|\|

*atha krameṇa gacchaṃtaste sarve kurupāṇḍavāḥ \|*  
*ānartaviṣayaṃ prāptā dhanadhānyasamākulam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Proceeding thus gradually, all the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas reached the land of Ānarta prosperous with wealth and food-grains.

## \|\| 1.72.8 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ yatra tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradevasya vikhyātaṃ bhuvanatraye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is the land where the excellent meritorious place of Lord Hāṭakeśvara is situated. It is well-known in all the three worlds as destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.72.9 \|\|

*atha prāha viśuddhātmā vṛddhaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpālaṃ saputraṃ prahasanniva \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then (Bhīṣma) the elderly grandfather of pure soul, the grandfather of Kurus, laughingly said to King Dhṛtarāṣṭra accompanied by his sons:

## \|\| 1.72.10 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*etadvatsa purā dṛṣṭaṃ mayā kṣetramanuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradevasya sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

10\. Dear son, this excellent holy place of Lord Hāṭakeśvara has already been visited by me. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.72.11 \|\|

*atrāhaṃ caiva ni rmuktaḥ strīhatyodbhavapātakāt \|*  
*tasmādatraiva rājeṃdra tiṣṭhāmaḥ paṃcavāsarān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Further, in this holy spot, I was liberated from the sin of the murder of a woman. Hence, O great king, we shall stay here itself for five days.

## \|\| 1.72.12 \|\|

*yena sarvāṇi paśyāmastīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*yānyatra saṃti puṇyāni munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus we can visit all the Tīrthas and shrines situated here. They are the meritorious holy places of sages of purified souls.

## \|\| 1.72.13 \|\|

*atha tadvacanādrājā dhṛtarāṣṭroṃ'bikāsutaḥ \|*  
*śatasaṃkhyaiḥ sutaiḥ sārdhaṃ kautūhalasamanvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then, at his instance King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Aṃbikā, became interested therein. Accompanied by his sons numbering a hundred, he immediately started.

## \|\| 1.72.14 \|\|

*jagāma satvaraṃ tatra yatra tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*tapasvigaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ yuktaṃ caivāśramaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He soon went to where the excellent holy place is situated. It was full of splendid hermitages and groups of ascetics.

## \|\| 1.72.15 \|\|

*brahmaghoṣeṇa mahatā nāditaṃ sarvatodiśam \|*  
*vahnipūjotthadhūmreṇa kaluṣīkṛtapāda pam \|*  
*krīḍāmṛgaiśca saṃkīrṇaṃ dhāvadbhirbahubhistathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All the quarters reverberated with the loud chanting sounds of Vedic passages. The smoke arising from the adored sacred fire had rendered many trees therein black. Many antelopes sported about and ran here and there.

## \|\| 1.72.16-18 \|\|

*tato nivārya sainyaṃ svamupadravabhayānnṛpaḥ \|*  
*pañcabhiḥ pāṃḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ śatasaṃkhyaistathā sutaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhīṣmeṇa somadattena bāhlīkena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*droṇācāryeṇa vīreṇa tatputreṇa kṛpeṇa ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*saubalena ca karṇena tathānyairapi pārthivaiḥ \|*  
*parivāraparityaktaistasminkṣetre cacāra saḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Afraid of harassment likely to be caused to the residents of the hermitages, the king stopped the entire army. He moved about in that holy spot accompanied by only the five sons of Pāṇḍu, his own hundred sons, Bhīṣma, Somadatta, Bāhlīka, heroic Droṇācārya, his son Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, Saubala (i.e. Śakuni), Karṇa and a few princes without their attendants.

## \|\| 1.72.19 \|\|

*te'pi sarve mahātmānaḥ kṣatriyāstatra saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*cakrurdharmakriyāḥ sarvāḥ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. All the noble-souled Kṣatriyas stationed there, performed all sacred rites with minds sanctified by faith.

## \|\| 1.72.20 \|\|

*snānaṃ cakrurvidhānena tīrtheṣu dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bhrāṃtvābhrāṃtvā supuṇyeṣu śrutvāśrutvā dvijanmanām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they duly took their holy baths in the Tīrthas of great merit where they wandered listening (to the chantings) of the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.72.21 \|\|

*dānāni ca viśiṣṭāni daduriṣṭāni cāpare \|*  
*dīnebhyaḥ kṛpaṇebhyaśca tapasvibhyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They made excellent gifts as desired. Others distributed gifts among the distressed and the wretched and also ascetics in particular.

## \|\| 1.72.22 \|\|

*cakruḥ śrāddhakriyāścānye pitṝnuddiśya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ cānye tilamiśra jalena ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Others devoutly performed Śrāddha rites with the Pitṛs in view. Still others offered libations to the Pitṛs with water mixed with gingelly seeds.

## \|\| 1.72.23 \|\|

*anye homakriyā bhūpā japamanye nirargalam \|*  
*svādhyāyamapare śāntāḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Other kings performed Homas. A few continously repeated holy names in Japa. Others endowed with faith and quiescence studied the Vedas of their respective Śākhā.

## \|\| 1.72.24 \|\|

*devatāyatanānyanye māhātmyasahitāni ca \|*  
*śrutvā pūrvanṛpāṇāṃ ca pūjayaṃti viśeṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Others performed special Pūjā (worship) in the holy temples of exalted state, listening to the glory of previous kings.

## \|\| 1.72.25-26 \|\|

*balidānaiḥ suvastraiśca gandhapuṣpopalepanaiḥ \|*  
*mārjanaidhvajadānaiśca tathā prekṣaṇakaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*maṃḍanaiḥ puṣpamālābhiḥ samaṃtāddvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*hastyaśvarathadānaiśca gorbhirvastraiśca kāṃcanaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtārthā brāhmaṇāḥ sarve kṛtāstai statra bhaktitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Brāhmaṇas there were rendered happy and contented by means of offerings, oblations, excellent garments, fragrant flowers, unguents, rubbings, gifts of banners, splendid spectacular shows, decorations with flower garlands and gifts of elephants, horses, chariots, cows, garments and gold.

## \|\| 1.72.27 \|\|

*evaṃ snātvā tathā'bhyarcya devānviprānnṛpottamāḥ \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭrasamāyuktā jagmuḥ svaśibiraṃ tataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After bathing and worshipping the deities and the Brāhmaṇas, the excellent kings accompanied by Dhṛtarāṣṭra entered their respective camps.

## \|\| 1.72.28 \|\|

*śaṃsanto vismayā viṣṭāstīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tasminkṣetre dvijāṃścaiva tāpasānsaṃśitavratān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Struck with wonder, they praised the Tilths, the shrines, the Brāhmaṇas and the ascetics of esteemed Vratas in that holy spot.

## Chapter 73 - Pilgrimage of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Others

## \|\| 1.73.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te kauravāḥ sarve pāṃḍoḥ putrāśca śālinaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsthānāttato jagmuryatra dvāravatī purī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā vivāhaṃ tu cakruḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*duryodhanasya bhūpasya bhānumatyā samaṃ tadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nānāvāditraghoṣeṇa vedadhvaniyutena ca \|*  
*gītairmanoharaiḥ pāṭhairbandināṃ ca sahasraśaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. All those brilliant sons of Pāṇḍu and Kauravas went from that holy place to the place where the city of Dvārakā was situated. After going there with delighted minds, they performed the marriage rite of king Duryodhana with Bhānumatī. On the occasion festivities were marked with the loud sound of different musical instruments combined with the sound of the Vedic chant, charming songs and recitations by thousands of bards.

## \|\| 1.73.4 \|\|

*evaṃ mahotsavo jajñe tatra yāvaddināṣṭakam \|*  
*yādavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca militānāṃ parasparam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The celebrations continued for eight days, which the Yadavas and Kauravas enjoyed together.

## \|\| 1.73.5 \|\|

*kṛtārthāstatra saṃjātāḥ sūtamāgadha bandinaḥ \|*  
*cāraṇā brāhmaṇeṃdrāśca tathānye'pi ca tārkikāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Sūtas, Māgadhas and Bandins (bards), Cāraṇas, leading Brāhmaṇas and other Tārkikas (Logicians) became satisfied.

## \|\| 1.73.6 \|\|

*tatastu navame prāpte divase kurupāṃḍavāḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmādyāḥ puṃḍarīkākṣamidamūcuḥ sasauhṛ dam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the ninth day, Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas including Bhīṣma spoke in a friendly spirit to the lotus-eyed Lord (Kṛṣṇa).

## \|\| 1.73.7 \|\|

*na vayaṃ puṃḍarīkākṣa tava rāmasya cāśrayam \|*  
*kathaṃcittyaktumicchāmaḥ snehapāśaniyaṃtritāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “O lotus-eyed one, we do not wish at all to leave the resort of yours as well as Rāma’s. We are so much bound by the bonds of affection.

## \|\| 1.73.8 \|\|

*tathāpi ca pragantavyaṃ svapuraṃ prati mādha va \|*  
*balabhadrasamāyuktastasmānnaḥ kuru mokṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Still, O Mādhava, we have to go to our city. Hence permit us with, the consent of Balabhadra.”

## \|\| 1.73.9 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*na tāvadvatsaro jāto na māsaḥ pakṣa eva ca \|*  
*sthitānāmatra yuṣmākaṃ tatkimautsukyamāgatam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) said:

9\. A year has not elapsed since you came to stay here, nor a month nor even a fortnight. Then why this eagerness to go?

## \|\| 1.73.10-11 \|\|

*tasmādatraiva tiṣṭhāmaḥ sahitāḥ kurupāṃḍavāḥ \|*  
*yūyaṃ vayaṃ vinodena mṛgayākṣodbhavena ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śastraśikṣākriyābhiśca damanena ca dantinām \|*  
*tathābhivāṃchitairanyaiḥ sneho'sti yadi vo mayi \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Therefore, O Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, you and we shall stay here together engaged in various pastimes of hunting and playing at dice, training and practising the use of missiles, taming and controlling elephants and other desirable activities. This is my suggestion if you entertain any love for me.

## \|\| 1.73.12 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*upapannamidaṃ viṣṇo yattvayā vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ śṛṇuṣva me vākyaṃ yadarthaṃ hyutsukā vayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

12\. Proper indeed, O Viṣṇu, are the words uttered by you. But please listen to my words indicating why we are eager (to go).

## \|\| 1.73.13-15 \|\|

*ānartaviṣaye'smābhirāgacchadbhistavāṃtikam \|*  
*dṛṣṭamatyadbhutaṃ kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarajaṃ mahat \|*  
*tatra liṃgāni dṛṣṭāni bhūpatīnāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sūryacandrānvayotthānāmanyeṣāṃ ca mahātmanām \|\| 14 \|\|*

*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca munīnāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sākārāṇi sutejāṃsi nānāprāsādabhoji ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. While we were coining to you here, the wonderful holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara was visited by us in the land of Ānarta. There the Liṅgas were seen installed by the noble-souled kings born in the Solar and the Lunar dynasties as well as others. So also the Liṅgas installed by Devas, Dānavas and more particularly by sages. They are refulgent and shapely enshrined in different kinds of suitable palatial temples.

## \|\| 1.73.16 \|\|

*tataśca kurumukhyānāṃ pāṃḍavānāṃ ca mādhava \|*  
*liṃgasaṃsthāpanārthāya tatra jātā matirdṛḍhā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hence, O Mādhava, we have felt inclined to install Liṅgas there on behalf of the chiefs of Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas.

## \|\| 1.73.17 \|\|

*te vayaṃ tatra gatvāśu yathāśaktyā yathecchayā \|*  
*liṃgāni sthāpayiṣyāmaḥ svānisvāni pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. We shall therefore go there and install separately several Liṅgas in accordance with our desire and capacity.

## \|\| 1.73.18 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāttūrṇaṃ calitā vayamacyuta \|*  
*na vayaṃ tava saṃgasya tṛpyāmo'bdaśatairapi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is for this reason, O Acyuta, that we are in a hurry to move. In fact even after staying with you for hundreds of years, we cannot be fully satisfied.

## \|\| 1.73.19 \|\|

*tasmādājñāpayasvādya kṛtvā cittaṃ dṛḍhaṃ vibho \|*  
*bhūyo'pyatrāgamiṣyāmastava darśanalālasāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Therefore O Lord, make up your mind and allow us to proceed. We shall come again as we too shall be eager to see you.

## \|\| 1.73.20 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ jānāmi tatkṣetraṃ supuṇyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*tāpasaiḥ kīrtitaṃ nityaṃ mamānyaistīrthayātrikaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

20\. I know that highly meritorious holy spot that destroys sins. It is being glorified everyday by ascetics and other pilgrims in my presence.

## \|\| 1.73.21 \|\|

*tasmāttatra sameṣyāmo yuṣmābhiḥ sahitā vayam \|*  
*liṃga saṃsthāpanārthāya kṣetradarśanavāṃchayā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence we shall also accompany you there for the purpose of installing the Liṅgas and fulfilling the desire of visiting the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.73.22 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchutvā kauravāḥ sarve paraṃ harṣamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*tathā pāṃḍusutāścaiva ye cānye tatra pārthivāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sūta said:

22\. On hearing it all the Kauravas, the sons of Pāṇḍu and all other kings who were present there became highly delighted.

## \|\| 1.73.23 \|\|

*te tu saṃprasthitāḥ sarve militāḥ kurupāṃḍavāḥ \|*  
*gajavājivimardena kampayanto vasundharām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. All the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas started together making the earth quake with the heavy pressure of the elephants and horses.

## \|\| 1.73.24 \|\|

*atha tatkṣetramāsādya dūre kṛtvā niveśanam \|*  
*kauravā yādavā mukhyāścamatkārapuraṃ gatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They reached the holy place. After making the army encamp at a distance the Kauravas and Yādava chiefs entered Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.73.25 \|\|

*tatra sarvānsamāhūya brāhmaṇānvinayānvitāḥ \|*  
*procurdattvā vicitrāṇi bhūṣaṇācchādanāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There they invited all the Brāhmaṇas. After offering them presents of ornaments and garments of diverse kinds, they spoke to them politely:

## \|\| 1.73.26 \|\|

*vayaṃ sarve'tra vāṃchāmo ligasaṃsthāpanakriyām \|*  
*kartuṃ prāsādamukhyānāṃ pṛthaktvena svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “All of us wish to perform the rite of installing Liṅgas. In addition we wish to erect grand palaces according to our capacity.

## \|\| 1.73.27 \|\|

*tasmātkṛtvā prasādaṃ no dayāṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*ājñāpayata śīghraṃ hi yena karma pravartate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Take a sympathetic and favourable view, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and give the necessary instructions quickly so that the work can start.

## \|\| 1.73.28 \|\|

*bhaviṣyatha tathā yūyaṃ hotāraḥ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*na cānyo brāhmaṇo bāhyo yadyapi syādbṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Further you alone should be the Hotṛs in all the rites (but) no other Brāhmaṇa from outside even if he be Bṛhaspati.

## \|\| 1.73.29 \|\|

*yato'smābhiḥ śrutā vārtā kīrtyamānā purātanī \|*  
*viṣṇunā tasya rājarṣeḥ pretaśrāddhasamudbhavā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. For, in this connection an ancient legend has been heard by us narrated by Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) in regard to the Pretaśrāddha of a saintly king.

## \|\| 1.73.30-31 \|\|

*yathā tena kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ pituḥ pretasya yatnataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ puro'nyeṣāṃ yathoktānāmapi dvijāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yathoktavidhinā tīrthe nāgānāṃ paṃcamīdine \|\| \|*  
*śrāvaṇe māsi no muktaḥ pitā tasya tathāpi saḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The Śrāddha of his departed father was carefully performed by him in front of other Brāhmaṇas as well as the Brāhmaṇas duly specified. O Brāhmaṇas, on the Nāga Pañcamī day, this was performed in the Tīrtha in accordance with the injunctions in the month of Śrāvaṇa. Yet his father was not liberated.

## \|\| 1.73.32 \|\|

*pretatvātsarpadoṣeṇa saṃjātā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*devaśarmapuro yāvattatkṛtaṃ śrāddhamādarāt \|*  
*tāvatpitā vinirmuktaḥ pretatvāddāruṇāddvijāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The father was not liberated from the state of Preta due to Sarpadoṣa (the defect of serpent-bite), O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

When the Śrāddha was performed respectfully in the presence of Deva Śarman, O Brāhmaṇas, the father was liberated from the awful state of Preta.

## \|\| 1.73.33 \|\|

*yadatra kriyate kiṃcitkarma dharmyaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tadbāhyaṃ ca bhavedvyarthametadvidmaḥ sphuṭaṃ vayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Whatever may be the religious rite performed here, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if that were to be performed with external (priestly) help, it cannot but be futile. This we know very clearly.

## \|\| 1.73.34 \|\|

*prārthayāmo viśeṣeṇa tena dainyaṃ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ tasmādājñāṃ yacchata mā ciram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. We are feeling miserable. Hence we make this special request Please do us this favour and kindly order (the concerned persons) without delay.”

## \|\| 1.73.35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇāste parasparam \|*  
*mantraṃ cakrustadarthaṃ hi kiṃ kṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sūta said:

35\. On hearing their words, those Brāhmaṇas had mutual consultations to decide what would be the best procedure in the matter.

## \|\| 1.73.36-37 \|\|

*eke procurna dāsyāmaḥ prāsādārthaṃ vasundharām \|*  
*eteṣāmapi caikasya tasmādgacchaṃtu satvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*paṃcakrośapramāṇena kṣetrametadvyavasthitam \|*  
*pūrveṣāmapi devānāṃ prāsādaistatsamāvṛtam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Some said, “We will not grant ṇ plot of land for the construction of a palace (temple) to even one person among these. Let them go away at once. This holy spot is extended to an area of only five Krośas. Further it is full of the palaces of the earlier deities.”

## \|\| 1.73.38-39 \|\|

*anye procurdhanomattā yūyaṃ ca sukhamāśritāḥ \|*  
*dāridyārtiṃ na jānītha brūtha tena bhṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmādvayaṃ pradāsyāma eteṣāṃ hi vasu ndharām \|*  
*arthasiddhirbhavedyena bhūṣā sthānasya jāyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Others said, “You are arrogant on account of your affluence and happy life. You do not know the distress due to poverty. That is why you say so much. So we shall surely grant these the required plot of land so that we will get some cash and the place shall also be beautified (with temple).”

## \|\| 1.73.40-42 \|\|

*tathānye madhyamāḥ procuryatra sākṣājjanārdanaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ prārthayate bhūmiṃ tatkasmānna pradīyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tasmādyatra samāyātāḥ kurupāṃḍavayādavāḥ \|*  
*prādhānyena prakurvaṃtu prāsādāṃstena cāpare \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yācate yatra gāṃgeyaḥ svayameva tathā paraḥ \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputraśca pāṃḍavāśca mahābalāḥ \|*  
*liṃgasaṃsthāpanārthāya niṣedhastatra nārhati \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Others of impartial view said: “When Janārdana himself requests for a plot of land, how can it be denied? So, now that the Kauravas, Pāṇḍavas and Yadavas have assembled together, let them and others as well erect palaces in accordance with their importance. When Gāṅgeya himself requests, so also Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the company of his sons and the very powerful Pāṇḍavas make this request for the installation of Liṅgas, refusal is not proper.”

## \|\| 1.73.43 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pratipannaṃ dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*nirdhanaiḥ sadhanaiścāpi saspṛhairniḥspṛhairapi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing their words the proposition was accepted by the excellent Brāhmaṇas irrespective of the fact whether they were rich or poor, greedy or disinterested.

## \|\| 1.73.44 \|\|

*tataḥ sametya te sarve brāhmaṇāḥ kurusattamān \|*  
*yādavānpāṃḍavānprocuḥ kṛtvā vai mantraniścayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then they came back. All the Brāhmaṇas told the excellent Kauravas, Yadavas and Pāṇḍavas about their decision after consulting one another.

## \|\| 1.73.45 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*etatsvalpataraṃ kṣetraṃ sarveṣāmapi bhūbhujām \|*  
*prāsādaiḥ sarvato vyāptaṃ tatkiṃ brūmo'dhunā vayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

45\. Indeed this holy spot is very small in area. It is already filled with the temples of all sorts of kings all round. What shall we say now?

## \|\| 1.73.46 \|\|

*tadbhavaṃtaḥ prakurvaṃtu prādhānyena yadṛcchayā \|*  
*kṣetre'traivābhimukhyena prāsādānsumanoharān \|*  
*yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathāśreṣṭhaṃ pṛthaktvena vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. So, you may build fascinating palaces in accordance with your importance, wish, seniority and excellence in this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.73.47 \|\|

*atha harṣasamāyuktā dhṛtarāṣṭramukhāḥ kramāt \|*  
*prādhānyena yathāśreṣṭhaṃ cakruḥ prāsādapaddhatim \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others became delighted. They arranged for the erection of a senes of palaces according to seniority and excellence.

## Chapter 74 - Installation of Liṅgas by Kauravas, Pāṇḍavas and Yadavas

## \|\| 1.74.1-5 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa bhūpena śataputrānvitena ca \|*  
*liṃgānāṃ sthāpitaṃ tatra śatamekottaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathā ca pāṃḍavaiḥ sarvaiḥ sthāpitaṃ liṃgapaṃcakam \|*  
*draupadyā cā'tha kuntyā'tha gāṃdhāryā'tha yadṛcchayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhānumatyā ca gaurīṇāṃ sthāpitaṃ ca catuṣṭayam \|*  
*vidureṇātha śalyena kaliṃ gena yuyutsunā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bāhlīkena saputreṇa karṇenātha sasūnunā \|*  
*tathā śakuninā tatra droṇena ca kṛpeṇa ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*aśvatthāmnā pṛthaktvena liṅgamekaikamuttamam \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ parayā bhaktyā varaprāsādamāśritam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-5. O Brāhmaṇas, one hundred one Liṅgas were installed by king Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the company of his hundred sons at that place.

Similarly five Liṅgas were installed by all the Pāṇḍavas. Four idols of Gaurī were installed by Draupadī, Kuntī, Gāndhārī and Bhānumatī according to their wish. One Liṅga was installed by each of the following: Vidura, Śalya, Kaliṅga, Yuyutsu, Bāhlīka with his son, Karṇa with his son, Śakuni, Droṇa, Kṛpa and Aśvatthāman severally, Thus the excellent Liṅgas were installed with great devotion along with excellent palaces to house them in.

## \|\| 1.74.6 \|\|

*tathā saṃsthāpitaṃ tatra viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*liṃgaṃ prāsādamādhāya prottuṃgaśikharānvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. So also a Liṅga was installed there by the highly powerful Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) after erecting a palace with lofty turrets.

## \|\| 1.74.7-8 \|\|

*sātvatenāpi sāṃbena balabhadreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*pradyumenāniruddhena tathānyairmukhyayādavaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*cārudeṣṇādibhiḥ putrai rukmiṇyā daśabhiḥ sutaiḥ \|*  
*liṃgānāṃ daśakaṃ mukhyaṃ sthāpitaṃ śraddhayānvitaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Sāttvata, Sāṃba, the intelligent Balabhadra, Pradyumna, Aniruddha and other important Yādavas also installed the Liṅgas. Ten important Liṅgas were installed with devotion by ten sons of Rukmiṇī beginning with Cārudeṣṇa.

## \|\| 1.74.9 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃsthāpya liṅgāni te sarve kurupāṃḍavāḥ \|*  
*yādavāśca susaṃhṛṣṭā kṛtakṛtyāstadā \|'bhavan \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After installing the Liṅgas thus, all the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas and Yādavas became delighted and contented.

## \|\| 1.74.10-13 \|\|

*tatra sthitvā ciraṃ kālaṃ dattvā dānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*dhanāḍhyānbrāhmaṇānkṛtvā camatkārapurodbhavān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dattvā tebhyo varānnāgānha yāñjātyānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*sadgrāmāṇi vicitrāṇi kṣetrāṇi ca sudhenavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mahokṣāṃśca suvastrāṇi bhūsthānānyāśrayāṃstathā \|*  
*dāsīdāsāṃstathā bhṛtyāndānāni vividhāni ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tata āmantrya tānsarvānpraṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*svasthānaṃ prati saṃhṛṣṭāḥ prajagmuḥ sarva eva te \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. They stayed there for a long time, made many gifts and rendered the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura wealthy. They gave them cash, excellent elephants, horses of the finest breed, diverse kinds of holy spots and fertile fields including excellent villages, good cows, huge bulls, good garments, plots of lands, places of resort, male and female slaves, servants, and different kinds of gifts. Thereafter all of them bowed (to the elders) repeatedly, took leave of one another and joyously went to their respective places.

## \|\| 1.74.14-16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ sthāpitaṃ tena bhūbhujā \|*  
*tathā taddhṛtarāṣṭreṇa liṃgaṃ pātakanāśanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathānyairapi bhūpālaiḥ prādhānyena vyavasthitaiḥ \|*  
*pāṇḍavairyādavaiścaiva pṛthaktvena vyavasthitaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yastāni puruṣaḥ samyakpūjayedbhaktibhāvitaḥ \|*  
*sa labheccākhilānkāmānvāṃchitānsvena cetasā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14-16. Thus everything has been narrated to you about how a sin-destroying Liṅga was installed by that king Dhṛtarāṣṭra (and others), by the Pāṇḍavas and Yādavas separately arrayed in accordance with their prominence.

A man urged and sanctified by devotion, who worships those Liṅgas well, shall attain all things desired in their minds.

## Chapter 75 - Greatness of Yajñabhūmi

## \|\| 1.75.1-4 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*purā kalpe bhagavatā etatkṣetramanuttamam \|*  
*rudreṇa brahmaṇe dattaṃ tuṣṭena dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadā tu sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*devaiḥ prītena rudreṇa pradattaṃ brahmaṇe punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etatkṣetraṃ tadā dattaṃ śaṃbhunā ṣaṇmukhasya ha \|*  
*rakṣaṇārthaṃ hi viprāṇāṃ kalikālādidoṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*brahmaṇā prārthitenedaṃ svayamādimamuttamam \|*  
*pitrādiṣṭastu gāṃgeyastatra vāsamathākarot \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. In an earlier Kalpa this excellent holy place was given to Brahmā, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, by Lord Rudra who was delighted. When the Liṅga named Hāṭakeśvara was installed by Devas what had been given to Brahmā by the delighted Rudra, viz. this holy place, was then given to Ṣaṇmukha for according protection to the Brāhmaṇas from the defects of Kalikāla (period of Kali etc.) when he was requested by Brahmā. On being commanded by his father Gāṅgeya (i.e. Ṣaṇmukha) stayed there, in the primordial excellent holy spot.

## \|\| 1.75.5 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge yaḥ kuryātsvāmidarśanam \|*  
*saptajanma bhavedvipro dhanāḍhyo vedapāragaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He who visits the Lord on the Kārttikī day when there is the conjunction of Kṛttikā constellation shall be born as a Brāhmaṇa in seven successive rebirths. He will be wealthy and a master of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.75.6-8 \|\|

*mahāsenasya devasya prāsādaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*uccaiḥ sthitaṃ sarvaloke pātukāmamivāṃbaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā vibudhāḥ sarve kautukādetya satvaram \|*  
*vīkṣāṃcakrustato gatvā dṛṣṭvā medhyatamaṃ puram \|\| 7 \|\|*

*prāsādasyottare deśe prācye deśe tathā dvijāḥ \|*  
*yajñakriyāsamāraṃbhāṃścakurviprairyathoditān \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Vibudhas (Devas) heard that the palace of Lord Mahāsena was fascinating and it stood very high as though it was desirous of protecting the sky. All of them, out of curiosity, hurried to the city and visited the holiest city. Through Brāhmaṇas they made preparations for the sacrificial rites in the manner stipulated on the northern as well as eastern side of the palace.

## \|\| 1.75.9-10 \|\|

*iṣṭvā ca vibudhāḥ sarve dattvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām \|*  
*jagmustriviṣṭapaṃ hṛṣṭā labdhvā tatsthānajaṃ phalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatastu devayajanaṃnāma tasya babhūva ha \|*  
*yadanyatra śataṃ kṛtvā kratūnāṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tadatraikena labhate kratunā dakṣiṇāvatā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. All the Vibudhas (Devas) performed the sacrifice and offered monetary gifts to them. Thereafter they joyously went to heaven after obtaining the benefit arising from that holy spot.

Then its name came to be Devayajana. By means of a single Kratu (sacrifice) here, with the due monetary gifts, one shall get the same benefit as is obtained elsewhere by means of a hundred sacrifices.

## Chapter 76 - Installation of Muṇḍīra, Kālapriya and Mūlasthāna

## \|\| 1.76.1-4 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti bhāskaratritayaṃ śubham \|*  
*yaistuṣṭaistriṣu lokeṣu mānavo muktimāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*muṇḍīraṃ prathamaṃ tatra kālapriyaṃ tathāparam \|*  
*mūlasthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca sarvavyādhivināśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra saṃkramate sūryo muṃḍīre rajanīkṣaye \|*  
*kālapriye ca madhyāhne mūlasthāne kṣapāgame \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasminkāle naro bhaktyā paśyedapyekamevaca \|*  
*kṛtakṣaṇo naro mokṣaṃ satyaṃ yāti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Further there is a splendid set of three Bhāskaras. If they are pleased in the worlds, one shall attain salvation.

There the first one is Muṇḍīra; the next one is Kālapriya and the third is Mūlasthāna that is destructive of all ailments.

When the night ends, the Sun passes on to Muṇḍīra, to Kālapriya at mid-day and to Mūlasthāna at nightfall.

A man who devoutly visits even one at any time after getting the requisite opportunity undoubtedly attains salvation. This is true.

## \|\| 1.76.5-6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*muṃḍīraḥ pūrvadigbhāge dharitryāḥ śrūyate kila \|*  
*madhye kālapriyo devo mūlasthānaṃ tadantare \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatkathaṃ te trayastatra saṃjātāḥ sūta bhāskarāḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvaṃ no brūhi vistarāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:

5-6. Verily it is heard that Muṇḍīra is on the eastern side of the earth. Lord Kālapriya is in the middle and Mūlasthāna is beyond them. Well, O Sūta, how did those three Bhāskaras happen to rise there, on the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara? Do narrate everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.76.7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*asti sāgaraparyaṃte viṭaṃkapuramuttamam \|*  
*samudravīcisaṃsaktaproccaprākāramaṇḍanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7\. There is that excellent Viṭaṅkapura on the seashore. It is embellished with high rampart walk washed by the waves of sea.

## \|\| 1.76.8 \|\|

*tatrābhūdbrāhmaṇaḥ kaścitkuṣṭhavyādhisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*pūrvakarmavipākena yauvanesamupasthite \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There was a Brāhmaṇa there who became afflicted by leprosy at the advent of his youth as a result of the previous Karmas.

## \|\| 1.76.9 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī kulīnā śīlamaṃḍanā \|*  
*tathābhūtamapi prāyaḥ sā paśyati yathā smaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. His wife was a chaste lady of noble birth. She was endowed with good behaviour. Despite the fact that he was in such a state, she used to look upon him like the god of love himself.

## \|\| 1.76.10 \|\|

*auṣadhāni vicitrāṇi mahārghyāṇyapi cādade \|*  
*tadarthamupalepāṃśca pathyāni vividhāni ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. For his sake, she used to bring costly medicines of various kinds, ointments to be smeared with, and wholesome foodstuffs of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.76.11 \|\|

*tathā bhiṣagvarānnityamānināya ca sādaram \|*  
*tadarthe na guṇastasya tathāpi syāccharīrajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Further the brought excellent physicians respectfully for his sake. Still there was no good effect on his body.

## \|\| 1.76.12 \|\|

*yathāyathā sa gṛhṇāti bheṣajāni dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhena sarvagātreṣu vyāpyate ca tathātathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the more he continued the treatment, the more the fell disease of leprosy continued to spread over all his limbs.

## \|\| 1.76.13 \|\|

*athaivaṃ vartamānasya tasya vipravarasya ca \|*  
*gṛhe'tithiḥ samāyātaḥ kaścitpāṃthaḥ śramānvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Even as that excellent Brāhmaṇa continued to suffer in the house, a certain weary traveller came there as his guest.

## \|\| 1.76.14 \|\|

*atha vipraṃ gṛhaṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya satī priyā \|*  
*ajñātamapisadbhaktyā sūpacārairatoṣayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing a Brāhmaṇa as a guest in the house, his chaste wife rendered good service to him and delighted him though he was previously unknown.

## \|\| 1.76.15 \|\|

*atha taṃ snātamācāṃtaṃ kṛtāhāraṃ dvijottamam \|*  
*viśrāntaṃ śayane vipraḥ provāca sa gṛhādhipaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When he saw that the excellent Brāhmaṇa had concluded his bath, holy sipping of water, and meal and had due rest in his bed, the Brāhmaṇa host, the householder, said:

## \|\| 1.76.16 \|\|

*tejo'nvitaṃ yathā bhānuṃ rūpaudāryaguṇānvitam \|*  
*yauvane vartamānaṃ ca mūrtaṃ kāmamivāparam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He said to the other one who was refulgent like the Sun, endowed with handsome features and exalted qualities, and in the prime of his youth like another god of Love incarnate:

## \|\| 1.76.17 \|\|

*kuṣṭhyuvāca \|*  
*kuta āgamyate vipra kva yāsyasi vadā'dhunā \|*  
*evaṃ lāvaṇyayukto'pi kimekākī yathārtibhāk \|\| 17 \|\|*

The leper said:

17\. O Brāhmaṇa, where do you come from? Where will you go now? Tell me, though you are endowed with handsome features thus, why you are alone like a distressed one.

## \|\| 1.76.18 \|\|

*pathika uvāca \|*  
*asti kāntīpurīnāma puraṃdarapurī yathā \|*  
*susthitaiḥ sevitā nityaṃ janairdharmavratānvitaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

The traveller said:

18\. There is a city named Kāntipurī. It is like the city of Indra. It is always inhabited by persons of good status and endowed with righteousness and holy vows.

## \|\| 1.76.19 \|\|

*tasyāmahaṃ kṛtāvāso gṛhasthāśramamāvahan \|*  
*grastaḥ kuṣṭhena raudreṇa yathā tvaṃ dvijasattama \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I was staying there leading the life of a householder, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, then I was afflicted by the fell disease of leprosy like you.

## \|\| 1.76.20 \|\|

*tataḥ śrutaṃ mayā tāvatpurāṇe skāndasaṃjñite \|*  
*bhāskaratritayaṃ bhūmau sarvavyādhivināśanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then I heard that it is mentioned in the Skandapurāṇa that the trinity of Bhāskaras in this world is destructive of all ailments.

## \|\| 1.76.21 \|\|

*tato nirvedamāpanno bheṣajaiḥ kleśitaściram \|*  
*kṣāraiścāmlaiḥ kaṣāyaiśca kaṭukairatha tiktakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I was disgusted with medicines of all sorts taken for a long lime—all salty, pungent, sour, astringent and bitter.

## \|\| 1.76.22 \|\|

*tato viniścayaṃ citte kṛtvā gṛhya dhanaṃ mahat \|*  
*muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ gatvā sthitastasyaiva sannidhau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then I resolved mentally, took with me much cash and went to Lord Muṇḍīra and stood before the deity.

## \|\| 1.76.23 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya nityaṃ paśyāmi taṃ vibhum \|*  
*pūjayāmi svaśaktyā ca praṇamāmi tataḥ param \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereafter, I regularly got up early in the morning and visited the Lord. I used to perform rites of adoration within my capacity and bow to him.

## \|\| 1.76.24 \|\|

*sūryavāre viśeṣeṇa nirāhāro yatendriyaḥ \|*  
*karomi jāgaraṃ rātrau gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Particularly on Sundays I used to observe fast and control

all sense-organs. I kept awake at night singing and playing on instruments.

## \|\| 1.76.25 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte taṃ praṇamya dinādhipam \|*  
*kālapriyaṃ tataḥ paścācchraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then at the end of the year I bowed down to that Lord of the day:

Thereafter I went to Kālapriya, endowed with great faith.

## \|\| 1.76.26 \|\|

*tenaiva vidhinā vipra tasyāpi divaseśituḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ karomi madhyāhne śraddhā pūtena cetasā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. With the mind sanctified with faith, I performed, in accordance with the same procedure (as with Lord Muṇḍīra), the rite of adoration of the Lord of day too at mid-day.

## \|\| 1.76.27 \|\|

*tato'pi vatsarasyāṃte taṃ praṇamyātha śaktitaḥ \|*  
*mūlasthānaṃ gato devamaparasyāṃ diśi sthitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Further at the end of the year I bowed down to that Lord with concentration. Then I went to Mūlasthāna, the Lord stationed in the west.

## \|\| 1.76.28 \|\|

*tenaiva vidhinā pūjā tasyāpi vihitā mayā \|*  
*saṃdhyākāle dvijaśreṣṭha yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The rite of adoration for that Lord too was performed by me in accordance with the procedure as before during the dusk. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, thus I stayed there for the whole of the year.

## \|\| 1.76.29 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte svapne māṃ bhāskaro'bravīt \|*  
*sametya prahasanvipraḥ saṃprahṛṣṭena cetasā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then at the end of the year, O Brāhmaṇa, Bhāskara appeared before me in dream. With a delighted mind, he laughed and spoke to me:

## \|\| 1.76.30 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te vipra karmaṇā'nena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*mamārādhanajenaiva tasmātkuṣṭhaṃ prayātu te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “O Brāhmaṇa, I am pleased with you by your devotion and this rite. Hence let your leprosy vanish as a result of this rite of propitiating me.

## \|\| 1.76.31 \|\|

*gaccha śīghraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śrāṃto'si nijamaṃdiram \|*  
*paśya baṃdhujanaṃ sarvaṃ sotkaṇṭhaṃ tatkṛte sthitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, you are tired. Go home quickly and meet all your relatives. See, they are waiting for you anxiously.

## \|\| 1.76.32 \|\|

*tvayā hṛtaṃ purā rukmaṃ brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tena karmavipākena kuṣṭhavyādhirupasthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Formerly, gold belonging to a noble-souled Brāhmaṇa was stolen by you. As a result of that commission of sin, the disease of leprosy has afflicted you.

## \|\| 1.76.33 \|\|

*sa mayā nāśitastubhyaṃ prahṛṣṭenādhunā dvija \|*  
*etajjñātvā na kartavyaṃ suvarṇaharaṇaṃ punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. That has been eradicated by me for your sake. O Brāhmaṇa, I am pleased with you. Realize this and stop indulging in stealing gold hereafter.

## \|\| 1.76.34 \|\|

*dṛśyante ye narā loke kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇaharaṇaṃ sarvaistaiḥ kṛtaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All the men seen in this world as afflicted and distressed by the disease of leprosy had been previously great sinners and had stolen gold.

## \|\| 1.76.35 \|\|

*tasmāddeyaṃ yathāśaktyā na steyaṃ kanakaṃ budhaiḥ \|*  
*icchadbhiḥ paramaṃ saukhyaṃ svaśarīrasya śāśvatam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hence gold should never be stolen by sensible persons. It should be given away as gift if people wish for permanent happiness of their bodies.”

## \|\| 1.76.36 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ ca vismayāviṣṭaḥ protthitaḥ śayanāddrutam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After \[????\] \[saying?\] this the Thousand-rayed One vanished. I got up hurriedly from my bed with a great but pleasant surprise.

## \|\| 1.76.37 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyāmi dehaṃ svaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhiparicyutam \|*  
*dvādaśārkaprabhaṃ divyaṃ yathā tvaṃ paśyase dvija \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Lo, I beheld my body free from the foul disease of leprosy. It had the divine lustre of twelve Suns, O Brāhmaṇa, as you see now.

## \|\| 1.76.38 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi vipreṃdra bhaktyā tadbhāskaratrayam \|*  
*anena vidhinā paśya yena kuṣṭhaṃ praśāmyati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Hence, O leading Brāhmaṇa, you too visit the trio of Bhāskaras in accordance with the same procedure, so that your leprosy may subside and be healed.

## \|\| 1.76.39 \|\|

*kimauṣadhaiḥ kimāhāṃraiḥ kaṭukairapi yojitaiḥ \|*  
*sarvavyādhipraṇāśeśe sthite'sminbhāskaratraye \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When this trinity of Sun-gods—Lords competent to quell ailment, is present, of what avail are medicines and pungent and astringent foodstuffs taken in?

## \|\| 1.76.40 \|\|

*svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tāṃ purīṃ prati \|*  
*gṛhe'dya tava viśrāṃto yathā vipra nije gṛhe \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Hail unto you, O Brāhmaṇa! I have relaxed myself today in your house as though in my own. I shall now go to that city.

## \|\| 1.76.41 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa pāṃthena tena vipraḥ sa kuṣṭhabhāk \|*  
*vīkṣāṃcakre tato vaktraṃ svapatnyā duḥkhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On being told thus by the traveller, the Brāhmaṇa afflicted by leprosy cast a miserable glance at the face of his wife.

## \|\| 1.76.42-43 \|\|

*sā'bravīdyuktamuktaṃ te pāṃthenānena vallabha \|*  
*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha yatra tadbhāskaratrayam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tvayā samaṃ tatra śuśrūṣāniratā satī \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi na saṃdehastasmādgaccha drutaṃ vibho \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. She said: “O my dear, the traveller has given you the most appropriate advice. So do go to that place where the trio of Bhāskaras is present. I shall also, no doubt, accompany you and be engaged in serving you. O Lord, do hurry along.”

## \|\| 1.76.44 \|\|

*evamuktastayā so'tha vittamādāya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*prasthitaḥ kāṃtayā sārdhaṃ muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ prati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On being urged thus by her, the Brāhmaṇa took with him a lot of cash and set off along with his wife to Lord Muṇḍīra.

## \|\| 1.76.45 \|\|

*pratijñayā gamiṣyāmi draṣṭuṃ taddevatātrayam \|*  
*muṃḍīraṃ kālanāthaṃ ca mūla sthānaṃ ca bhāskaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He told himself, “I vow that I shall go to visit the trio of deities viz. Muṇḍīra, Kālanātha (Kālapriya) and Bhāskara named Mūlasthāna.”
