## \|\| 1.76.46 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchreṇa mahatā kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃprāptaḥ sa dvijottamāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the person afflicted by leprosy reached the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara with great difficulty.

## \|\| 1.76.47 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā sumahatkṣetraṃ tāpasaughaniṣevitam \|*  
*nirviṇṇaḥ kuṣṭharogeṇa pathi śrāṃto'bravītpriyām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On seeing the great holy spot resorted to by groups of sages, the Brāhmaṇa afflicted by the disgusting disease of leprosy and fatigued by the journey, said to his wife:

## \|\| 1.76.48-49 \|\|

*ahaṃ nirvedamāpanno rogeṇātha bubhukṣayā \|*  
*muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ yāvanna śakromi prasarpitum \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tasmādatraiva dehaṃ svaṃ vihāsyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ gaccha svagṛhaṃ kāṃte sārthamāsādya śobhanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. “I have become dejected and disgusted due to this disease and the enormity of hunger. I find it impossible to go so far to Lord Muṇḍīrasvāmin. O my beloved, I shall cast off my body here itself undoubtedly. You go home along with some good caravan.”

## \|\| 1.76.50 \|\|

*patnyuvāca \|*  
*abhukte tvayi no bhuktaṃ kadācitkāṃta vai mayā \|*  
*ekāṃte'pi mahābhāga na suptaṃ jāgrati tvayi \|\| 50 \|\|*

The wife said:

50\. O my Lord and beloved one, O highly esteemed one, I have never taken food when you were hungry nor have I gone to sleep while you were awake.

## \|\| 1.76.51 \|\|

*tasmādetanmahākṣetraṃ saṃprāpya tvāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*paralokāya saṃtyajya kathaṃ gacchāmyahaṃ gṛham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Having come to this great holy place, how can I leave you alone to proceed to the other world and myself go home?

## \|\| 1.76.52 \|\|

*darśayiṣye mukhaṃ teṣāṃ tvayā hīnā ahaṃ katham \|*  
*bāṃdhavānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca anyeṣāṃ sudṛdā mapi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. How can I show my face to my kinsmen and elders and friends after going there alone without you?

## \|\| 1.76.53 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā samaṃ nātha pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam \|*  
*snehapāśavinirbaddhā satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Hence this is my solemn oath that I would rather enter fire along with you, my Lord, as I have been so bound with you with the cords of affection.

## \|\| 1.76.54 \|\|

*yāvatastava saṃjātā upavāsā mahāmate \|*  
*tāvaṃtaśca tathāsmākaṃ kathaṃ gacchāmi tadgṛham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O highly intelligent one, I have kept all those fasts you have observed. How can I then go home?

## \|\| 1.76.55 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyā viditvā sa niścayaṃ brāhmaṇastadā \|*  
*citiṃ kṛtvā tu dāhārthaṃ tayā sārdhe tato'viśat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On coining to know of her determination the Brāhmaṇa built a pyre for self-immolation and entered it along with her.

## \|\| 1.76.56 \|\|

*bhāskaraṃ manasi dhyātvā yāvadagniṃ samādade \|*  
*tāvatpaśyati cāgrasthaṃ sudīptaṃ puruṣatrayam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Meditating on Bhāskara, he set it on fire when he saw in front of him a highly refulgent set of three persons.

## \|\| 1.76.57 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭaḥ ka ete puruṣāstrayaḥ \|*  
*na kadācinmayā dṛṣṭā īdṛktejaḥsamanvitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On seeing them, he was struck with wonder. ‘Who are these three persons? Persons with such refulgence and splendour have never been seen by me.’

## \|\| 1.76.58 \|\|

*puruṣā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mā tvaṃ mṛtyupathaṃ gaccha kṛtvā vairāgyamākulaḥ \|*  
*vyāvṛtya svagṛhaṃ gaccha sva bhāryāsahito dvija \|\| 58 \|\|*

The persons said:

58\. O Brāhmaṇa, do not tread the path of death out of your excitement and dejection. Turn back and go home along with your wife.

## \|\| 1.76.59-60 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*pratijñāya mayā pūrva gṛhaṃ muktaṃ nijaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā'nyaṃ kālavallabham \|\| 59 \|\|*

*mūlasthānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ tataḥ sasyaprabhakṣaṇam \|*  
*so'haṃ tānavilokyātha kathaṃ gacchāmi mandiram \|*  
*bhakṣayāmi tathā sasyaṃ tena tyakṣyāmi jīvitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

59-60. Earlier I left home with the solemn vow that I will take food there after seeing Muṇḍīrasvāmin, Kālavallabha and Mūlasthāna. Hence without seeing them how can I go home? How can I take food? Hence I shall cast off my life.

## \|\| 1.76.61 \|\|

*puruṣā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ te bhāskarā brahmaṃstrayo'traiva samāgatāḥ \|*  
*tvadbhaktyākṛṣṭamanaso brūhi kiṃ karavāmahe \|\| 61 \|\|*

The persons said:

61\. O holy Brāhmaṇa, we are those three Bhāskaras come here attracted by your devotion. Tell us what shall we do (for you).

## \|\| 1.76.62 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*yadi yūyaṃ samāyātāḥ svayameva mamāṃtikam \|*  
*trayo'pi bhāskarā nāśameṣa kuṣṭhaḥ pragacchatu \|\| 62 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

62\. If you three Bhāskaras have come here yourselves, let this leprosy disappear.

## \|\| 1.76.63 \|\|

*tathā'traiva sadā stheyaṃ kṣetre yuṣmābhireva hi \|*  
*sāṃnidhyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu gantavyaṃ ca yathā purā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Further, you all should stay here itself forever keeping your presence in the three worlds as well as before.

Bhāskaras said

## \|\| 1.76.64 \|\|

*bhāskarā ūcuḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vipra kariṣyāmaḥ sthāsyāmo 'tra sadā vayam \|*  
*tvaṃ cāpi roganirmuktaḥ sukhaṃ prāpsyasyanuttamam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Brāhmaṇa, we shall do so. We shall stay here for ever. You too shall be free from ailments and gain excellent happiness.

## \|\| 1.76.65 \|\|

*prāsādatritayaṃ tasmādasmadarthaṃ nirūpaya \|*  
*yena trikālamāsādya gacchāmaḥ saṃnidhiṃ dvija \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Brāhmaṇa, arrange for three (temples) palaces for our sake, so that we can be present on three occasions (times) a day.

## \|\| 1.76.66 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu te sarve gatāścāddarśanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*so'pi paśyati kāyaṃ svaṃ yāvadrogavivarjitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After saying thus all of them vanished. He too saw that his body had become free from the ailment.

## \|\| 1.76.67 \|\|

*dvādaśārka pratīkāśaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*tataḥ provāca tāṃ bhāryāṃ vinayāvanatāṃ sthitām \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. His body had the refulgence of twelve suns and marked with all the (auspicious) characteristics. He then told his wife who was standing there modestly:

## \|\| 1.76.68-69 \|\|

*paśya tvaṃ subhrūrme gātraṃ yādṛgrūpaṃ punaḥ sthitam \|*  
*prasādāddevadevasya bhāskarasyāṃśumālinaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*so'hamatra sthito nityaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi bhāskaram \|*  
*na yāsyāmi punaḥ sadma satyametanmayoditam \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. “O lady of excellent eyebrows, see that my body has become as beautiful as before with the favour of Bhāskara, the Lord of Devas. I shall stay here and adore Bhāskara always. I will never go home. This is the truth uttered by me.”

## \|\| 1.76.70 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa viprendrastasminkṣetre suśobhane \|*  
*prāsādatritayaṃ ramyaṃ nirmame bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. After saying thus, that leading Brāhmaṇa endowed with devotion built three beautiful palaces in that splendid holy place.

## \|\| 1.76.71 \|\|

*muṇḍīrasvāminaścaikamanyatkālapriyasya ca \|*  
*mūlasthānasya cānyattu satpatākāvibhūṣitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. All of them were embellished with excellent banners; one for Muṇḍīrasvāmin, another for Kālapriya and still another for Mūlasthāna.

## \|\| 1.76.72-73 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi teṣāṃ tu sādhvarcāḥ śāstrasūcitāḥ \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa sūryāṇāṃ hastārke sūryavāsare \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tatastāḥ puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ samabhyarcya ciraṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ kramaśaḥ prāpto dehāṃte bhāskarālayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. He installed excellent images for all the three Bhāskaras as explained in the scriptures, on a Sunday when the Sun was in the Hasta constellation. Then the Brāhmaṇa adored them with flowers, incense etc., for a long lime thrice a day. On death he went to the region of Bhāskara.

## \|\| 1.76.74-75 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te tatra saṃjātāstrayo'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bhāskarā bhaktalokasya sarvavyādhivināśakāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yastānpaśyati kāle sve yathokte sūraryavāsare \|*  
*sa vāṃchitāṃllabhetkāmāndurlabhānapi mānavaiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

Sūta said:

74-75. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, those three Bhāskaras came to be present there as the destroyer of all ailments of devotees. One who visits them at their respective periods of time on a Sunday specified above, shall all cherished desires inaccessible to men.

## Chapter 77 - Importance of Harāśraya Vedikā

## \|\| 1.77.1-4 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tatra tau parameśvarau \|*  
*umāmaheśvarau sūta hariścandreṇa bhūbhujā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kṛtau kathayasītyevaṃ vedimadhyaṃ samāśritau \|*  
*utānyau sthāpitau tatra camatkārapurāṃtikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vedimadhyagatau nityaṃ pārvatīparameśvarau \|*  
*etatsaṃśrūyate sūta vivāhaḥ prāgabhūttayoḥ \|*  
*oṣadhiprasthamāsādya puraṃ hima vataḥ priyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*atra naḥ saṃśayo jātaḥ śraddheyamapi te vacaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā kiṃ vā bhramaste'yaṃ kiṃ vā'smākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-4. O Sūta, with reference to the installation of Umā and Maheśvara performed by King Hariścandra you say that they resorted to the middle of the Vedi (Altar). Is it so? Or another set was installed at Camatkārapura? This is what is heard by us always that they are in the middle of the altar as their marriage took place in Oṣadhīprastha, the favourite spot of Himālaya. Here we are in doubt. In fact your words deserve credence. Are we confused even after hearing your words? Or you have committed a slip? Clarify this kindly.

## \|\| 1.77.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nāsmākaṃ vibhramo jāto yuṣmākaṃ tu dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ yatkāraṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tadbravīmi nibodhyatām \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there is no confusion in me (my speech) but it is yours. However know the reason of it as I explain to you fully.

## \|\| 1.77.6-7 \|\|

*ya eṣa oṣadhiprasthe vivāhaḥ prāgabhū ttayoḥ \|*  
*umātrinetrayo ramyaḥ sarvadevapramodakṛt \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vaivasvate'ntare pūrvaṃ saṃjāto dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*saptamasya tu vikhyāto yuṣmākaṃ vidito'tra yaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Formerly it was in the Vaivasvata Manvantara that the fascinating marriage of Umā and Trinetra (Śiva) took place in Oṣadhīprastha delighting all the Devas. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this seventh Manu is well known and you all know the same.

## \|\| 1.77.8 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yaścodvāhastayorabhūt \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvamanorādye sa saṃjātaḥ suvistaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. But their marriage which took place in Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra was celebrated with great fanfare in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara of the first Manu.

## \|\| 1.77.9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vivāha oṣadhiprasthe yaḥ purā samabhūttayoḥ \|*  
*pārvatīharayoḥ sūta so'smābhirvistarācchrutaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:

9\. O Sūta, the marriage of Pārvatī and Hara that took place earlier in Oṣadhīprastha has been heard by us in detail.

## \|\| 1.77.10-11 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre dakṣayajñe manohare \|*  
*vivāho vṛṣayānasya manau svāyaṃbhuve purā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*so'smākaṃ kīrtanīyaśca tvayā sūtakulodvaha \|*  
*vistareṇa yathā vṛttaḥ etanna kautukaṃ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The marriage of the Bull-vehicled One which took place in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara during the charming Yajña of Dakṣa occurred in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara. O scion of the family of Sūta, that should be duly narrated to us by you in detail just in the way it had occurred. This is our great curiosity.

## \|\| 1.77.12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*vivāhasamayaṃ samyagdevadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12\. Here I shall completely narrate the sin-destroying marital function of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.77.13 \|\|

*brahmaṇo dakṣiṇāṃguṣṭhāddakṣaḥ prācetaso'bhavat \|*  
*śatāni pañca kanyānāṃ tasya jātāni ca dvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Brāhmaṇas, Dakṣa, the Prācetasa, was born from the right thumb of Brahmā. A hundred and five daughters were born to him.

## \|\| 1.77.14 \|\|

*tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhatamā sādhvī satīnāma śucismitā \|*  
*babhūva kanyakā sarvairguṇairyuktā'yatekṣaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The eldest of those daughters was Satī by name. The chaste lady of splendid smiles and long eyes was endowed with all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.77.15 \|\|

*na devī na ca gaṃdharvī nāsurī na ca nāgajā \|*  
*tādṛgrūpā'bhavaccānyā yādṛśī sā sumadhyamā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. No girl either from Deva or Gandharvas or Asura or Nāga clans was as beautiful as that girl of excellent waist.

## \|\| 1.77.16 \|\|

*atha tāṃ pradadau dakṣaḥ patnyarthaṃ śūla pāṇaye \|*  
*prārthitāṃ bahuśo yatnātsaspṛhāya spṛhānvitām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Dakṣa gave her to the Trident-bearing Lord as his wife. She had been repeatedly requested by him. He was desirous of her and she of him.

## \|\| 1.77.17 \|\|

*tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ kanyādānasya sa kṣamam \|*  
*saṃdhyāya sasutāmātyaḥ sabhṛtyaḥ samupasthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He thought of the holiest of holy spots befitting the rite of Kanyādāna (marriage) and came there along with his daughter, ministers and servants.

## \|\| 1.77.18 \|\|

*tataścodvāhayogyāni vasuni vividhānyapi \|*  
*ānayāmāsa bhūrīṇi māṃgalyāni viśeṣataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then he brought in great quantity different kinds of articles all highly auspicious and especially befitting marriage celebrations.

## \|\| 1.77.19 \|\|

*atha caitrasya śuklasya nakṣatre bhagadaivate \|*  
*trayodaśyāṃ dine bhānoḥ samāyāto maheśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Maheśvara came there on the thirteenth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra coinciding with a Sunday and the constellation Pūrvāphālgunī.

## \|\| 1.77.20 \|\|

*sarvaiḥ suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ devaviṣṇupuraḥsaraiḥ \|*  
*ādityairvasubhī rudrairaśvibhyāṃ ca tathā'paraiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He was accompanied by all the groups of Suras with Lord Viṣṇu at their head, Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Āśvins and others.

## \|\| 1.77.21 \|\|

*siddhaiḥ sādhyagaṇairbhūtaiḥ pretairvaināyakaistathā \|*  
*gandharvaiścāraṇaughaiśca guhyakairyakṣarākṣasaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Groups of Sādhyas, Siddhas, Bhūtas, Pretas, Vināyakas, Gandharvas, groups of Cāraṇas, Guhyakas, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were also with him.

## \|\| 1.77.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare dakṣaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*prayayau saṃmukhastasya yuktaḥ sarvaiḥ suhṛdgaṇaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meanwhile, Dakṣa whose, hair stood on end due to excessive joy, accompanied by his friends and relative came forward to receive him personally.

## \|\| 1.77.23 \|\|

*vādyamānairmahāvādyaiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ \|*  
*paṭhadbhiḥ sarvato'nekairgāyadbhirgāyanaistathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Great musical instruments were being played by Sūtas, Māgadhas and Bandins (all different kinds of bards). Many people recited Mantras. Many musicians sang songs.

## \|\| 1.77.24 \|\|

*tataḥ sarve surāstatra svayaṃ dakṣeṇa pūjitāḥ \|*  
*yathāśreṣṭhaṃ yathājyeṣṭhamupaviṣṭā yathākramam \|*  
*parivāryākhilāṃ vediṃ maṃḍapāṃtaravartinīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All the Suras were duly honoured by Dakṣa himself in accordance with their seniority and importance. They were seated in due order all round the Vedi erected within the pavilion.

## \|\| 1.77.25-26 \|\|

*tataḥ pitāmahaṃ prāha dakṣaḥ prītipuraḥsaram \|*  
*praṇipatya tvayā karma kāryaṃ vaivāhikaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*svayameva sutā'smākaṃ yena syātsubhagā satī \|*  
*putra pautravatī nityaṃ suśīlā pativallabhā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Dakṣa bowed down to Pitāmaha with great pleasure and requested: “O Lord, all the rites in connection with the celebration of the marriage should be performed by you. Bless her yourself so that my daughter shall be fortunate, beautiful, loyal, well-behaved, dear to her husband and blessed with sons and grandsons.”

## \|\| 1.77.27 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva so'pyuktvā prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*samutthāya tataścakre kṛtyamarhaṇapūrvakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “So be it,” said he with a delighted mind. Getting up he performed all the rites beginning with the honouring (of the elders).

## \|\| 1.77.28 \|\|

*saṃpradānakriyāṃ kṛtvā tatraiva vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*tato hastagrahaṃ tābhyāṃ mithaścakre yathākramam \|*  
*mātṝṇāṃ purato vedhāḥ satīśābhyāṃ yathocitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He performed the rite of Saṃpradāna (giving away the daughter in marriage) there itself in accordance with the injunctions. In front of Mātṛs (Mothers) Vedhas (Brahmā) made Satī and íśa grasp each other’s hands in the proper manner.

## \|\| 1.77.29 \|\|

*atha vediṃ samāsādya gṛhyoktavidhinā'khilam \|*  
*agnikāryaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ cakārātha suvistaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then he came to the Vedi (Altar) and performed all the rites in the fire as mentioned in the Gṛhya Sūtra texts in full detail.

## \|\| 1.77.30 \|\|

*yathāyathā sa ramyāṇi vīkṣateṃ'gāni kautukāt \|*  
*satyāḥ pitāmaho hṛṣṭaḥ kāmārto'bhūttathātathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. As he eagerly and enthusiastically looked at the beautiful limbs of Satī, Pitāmaha became delighted and distressed with lust

## \|\| 1.77.31 \|\|

*tenaikaṃ vadanaṃ muktvā tasyā vastrāvaguṃṭhitam \|*  
*vīkṣitā'tismarārtena yathā kaścinna buddhyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Excepting her face hidden behind the veil, all the other limbs were glanced at by that lascivious one in a manner unknown to anyone else.

## \|\| 1.77.32 \|\|

*na śaṃbhorlajjayā vaktraṃ pratyakṣaṃ sa vyalokayat \|*  
*na ca sā lajjayāviṣṭā karoti prakaṭaṃ mukham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He did not look directly at Śaṃbhu’s face out of shame. She too was very bashful and hence did not reveal her face.

## \|\| 1.77.33 \|\|

*tatastaddarśanārthāya sa upāyaṃ vyalo kayat \|*  
*dhūmadvāreṇa kāmārtaścakāra ca tataḥ param \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then Brahmā began to look for ways and means to see the face (of Satī). He thought of doing so through smoke as he became more and more distressed with lust.

## \|\| 1.77.34 \|\|

*ārdreṃdhanāni bhūrīṇi kṣiptvākṣitvā vibhāvasau \|*  
*svalpājyāhutivinyāsādārdradravyodbhava stathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He put many wet sacrificial twigs into the fire repeatedly. The clarified butter was reduced in quantity when poured. Thus the wet things became prominently used.

## \|\| 1.77.35 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare dhūmaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tādṛgyena tamobhūtaṃ vedimūlaṃ vinirmitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the meantime columns of smoke enveloped the place all round. The foot of the Altar became completely enveloped in darkness.

## \|\| 1.77.36 \|\|

*tato dhūmākulenetre bhagavāṃstripu rāntakaḥ \|*  
*hastābhyāṃ chādayāmāsa ye'nye tatra vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With eyes distressed with smoke Tripurāntaka (Śiva) and all members present covered their eyes with hands.

## \|\| 1.77.37 \|\|

*tato vastraṃ samutkṣipya satīvaktraṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*vīkṣayāmāsa kāmārtaḥ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The lascivious Brahmā lifted the veil of Satī and looked at her face delightedly.

## \|\| 1.77.38 \|\|

*tasya retaḥ pracaskanda tatastadvīkṣaṇāddrutam \|*  
*patitaṃ ca dharāpṛṣṭhe tuṣāracayasaṃnibham \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. As a result thereof there was an emission of the semen of Brahmā which fell on the ground like a man of snow drops.

## \|\| 1.77.99 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The Lotus-born One (Brahmā) immediately covered that man of semen with sand-particles lest anyone should see it

## \|\| 1.77.40 \|\|

*atha tadbhagavāñcchaṃbhurjñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|*  
*reto'vaskandanāttasya kopādetaduvāca ha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Lord Śaṃbhu knew it through his divine perception. Being angry at the emission of semen, he said:

## \|\| 1.77.4144-44 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 4144 \|\|*

*tasmātspṛśa nijaṃ śīrṣaṃ brahmannetadasaṃśayam \|*  
*yāvadevaṃ gate brahmā śiraḥ spṛśati pāṇinā \|*  
*tāvattatra sthitaḥ sākṣāttadrūpo vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

4144a. “O sinner, what a despicable act has been committed by you! It does not behove you to look at my wife’s face lustfully. You seem to think that all these activities were not noticed by Śaṅkara. O Vidhi, is there anything concealed from me in all the three world? How can they be?

O foolish one, I am in the interior of everything in all the three worlds whether it u mobile or immobile, like oil latent in a gingely seed. Hence give up this your head, O Brahmā, undoubtedly.”

44b. As this transpired, Brahmā touched his head with his hand (The root √spṛś means ‘to touch’, ‘to give up’ etc.). Presently the Bull-vehicled One stood there in his own form.

## \|\| 1.77.45 \|\|

*tato lajjāparītāṃgaḥ sthitaścādhomukho dvijāḥ \|*  
*indrādyairamaraiḥ sarvaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvataḥ sthitaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, he was completely overwhelmed with shame and stood there with face cast down. Further, all the Devas beginning with India were standing around.

## \|\| 1.77.48 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa mastakasthena vai tataḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ kuru samādhistho mamārādhanatatparaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

48\. With this form held on your head perform penance. Meditate on me with eagerness to propitiate me.

## \|\| 1.77.49 \|\|

*khyātiṃ yāsyati sarvatra nāmnā rudraśiraḥ kṣitau \|*  
*sādhakaḥ sarvakṛtyānāṃ tejobhājāṃ dvijanma nām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You will become well-known under the name Rudraśiras all over the earth. You will be the accomplisher of all tasks of the Brāhmaṇas endowed with refulgence.

## \|\| 1.77.50 \|\|

*mānuṣāṇāmidaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasmāccīrṇaṃ tvayā'dhunā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā vicariṣyasi bhūtale \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Since this act has been perpetrated by you—on act befitting only human beings—you will become a man and roam about on the earth.

## \|\| 1.77.51-52 \|\|

*yastvāṃ cānena rūpeṇa dṛṣṭvā pṛcchāṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*kimetadbrahmaṇo mūrdhni bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tataste ceṣṭitaṃ sarvaṃ kautukācca śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*paradārakṛtātpāpāttato muktiṃ prayāsyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. One who sees you in this form and enquires: “What is this? Lord Tripurāntaka over the head of Brahmā?” and eagerly hears about your act, shall become rid of the sin of cohabiting with another man’s wife.

## \|\| 1.77.53 \|\|

*yathāyathā janastvetatkṛtyaṃ te kīrtayiṣyati \|*  
*tathātathā viśuddhiste pāpasyāsya bhaviṣyati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The more people go on narrating this act of yours, the more your sin will get dissolved and you will become purified.

## \|\| 1.77.54 \|\|

*etadeva hi te brahmanprāyaścittaṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*janahāsyakaraṃ loke tava garhākaraṃ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Brahmā, this alone is spoken as the atonement for you, as people of the earth will laugh at you and ridicule you very much.

## \|\| 1.77.55 \|\|

*etacca tava vīryaṃ tu patitaṃ vedimadhyagam \|*  
*kāmārtasya mayā dṛṣṭaṃ naitadvyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Your semen that dropped down in the middle of the Vedī as you were distressed with lust, has been noticed, by me. It shall not go in vain.

## \|\| 1.77.56 \|\|

*yāvanmātraiḥ parispṛṣṭametatsaikatareṇubhiḥ \|*  
*tāvanmātrā bhaviṣyaṃti munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As many particles of sand came into contact with the semen so many sages of esteemed holy vows will arise from it.

## \|\| 1.77.57 \|\|

*vālakhilyā iti khyātāḥ sarveṃ'guṣṭhapramāṇakāḥ \|*  
*tapovīryasamopetāḥ śāpānugrahakārakāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All of them will be of the size of a thumb and be famous as Vālakhilyas. They will be capable of cursing and blessing. They will be endowed with the power of penance.

## \|\| 1.77.58 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasmādvedimadhyācca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhakapramāṇāni niṣkrāntāni dvijottamāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In the meantime, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, eighty-eight thousand sages of sanctified souls, all of the size of a thumb, came out of the centre of the Vedī.

## \|\| 1.77.59 \|\|

*tataste praṇipatyoccaiḥ procurdevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*sthānaṃ darśaya nastāta tapo'rthaṃ kalivarjitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. They bowed down to Lord Pitāmaha and spoke to him loudly, “O father, show us a place devoid of Kali (quarrel) for performing austerities.”

## \|\| 1.77.60 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca \|*  
*asminkṣetre mayā sārdhaṃ kurudhvaṃ putrakāstapaḥ \|*  
*gamiṣyatha parāṃ siddhiṃ yena loke sudurlabhām \|\| 60 \|\|*

Pitāmaha said:

60\. O dear sons, perform penance in this holy spot along with me. Thereby you will attain the greatest Siddhi rare in the world.

## \|\| 1.77.61 \|\|

*te tatheti pratijñāya kṛtvā tatrāśramaṃ śubham \|*  
*vālakhilyāstapaścakruḥ saṃsiddhiṃ ca parāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All those Vālakhilyas promised to do so. They erected a splendid hermitage, performed penance and attained the greatest Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.77.62 \|\|

*atha brahmāpi tatkarma sarvaṃ vaivāhikaṃ kramāt \|*  
*samāptimanayatproktaṃ yacchrutau tena ca svayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Brahmā too duly completed himself the rites of the marriage in the way in which it has been enjoined in the Śruti.

## \|\| 1.77.63 \|\|

*patatsu puṣpavarṣeṣu samantādgaganāṃgaṇāt \|*  
*vādyamāneṣu vādyeṣu gīya mānaiścagītakaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Showers of flowers fell around from the sky. Musical instruments were played and songs were Sung.

## \|\| 1.77.64 \|\|

*paṭhatsu vipramukhyeṣu nṛtyamānāsu rāgataḥ \|*  
*raṃbhādiṣu purandhrīṣu devānāṃ dṛṅmanoharam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Eminent Brāhmaṇas chanted the Vedic Mantras. The celestial damsels beginning with Raṃbhā began to dance passionately fascinating the eyes of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.77.65 \|\|

*evaṃ mahotsavo jajñe tata stuṃburupūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*gīyamāneṣu gīteṣu yathāpūrvaṃ triviṣṭape \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thus a great festival went on there even as Tuṃburu and others sang in the manner they used to sing in heaven earlier.

## \|\| 1.77.66-67 \|\|

*atha karmāvasāne sa bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*provāca padmajaṃ bhaktyā dakṣiṇāṃ te dadāmi kim \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vaivāhikī suraśreṣṭha yadyapi syātsudurlabhā \|*  
*brūhi śīghraṃ mahābhāga nādeyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. At the conclusion of the celebration of marriage, Lord Tripurāntaka devoutly said to the Lotus-born One: “O excellent one among Suras, what monetary fee shall I give you for this celebration of marriage? Tell me quickly, even if it be too high, O highly esteemed one, there is nothing which cannot be given my me.”

## \|\| 1.77.68 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa vedyāmasyāṃ sureśvara \|*  
*tvayā stheyaṃ sadaivātra nṛṇāṃ pāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

Pitāmaha said:

68\. O Lord of Suras, you should stay in this Vedī in this very form always, for the purification of the sins of men.

## \|\| 1.77.69 \|\|

*yena te sannidhau kṛtvā svāśramaṃ śaśiśekhara \|*  
*tapaḥ karomi nāśāya pāpasyāsya mahattamam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O Moon-crested Lord, I shall make my hermitage in your vicinity and perform the penance for the destruction of this sin.

## \|\| 1.77.70 \|\|

*caitraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ nakṣatre bhagadaivate \|*  
*sūryavāreṇa yo bhaktyā vīkṣayiṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tadaiva tasya pāpāni prayāsyanti ca saṃkṣayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A man who visits the deity devoutly on the thirteenth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra coinciding with Sunday and the constellation Pūrvāphālgunī, will find his sins dissolved at the very same time.

## \|\| 1.77.71 \|\|

*yā nārī durbhagā vandhyā kāṇā rūpavivarjitā \|*  
*sā'pi tvaddarśanādeva bhaviṣyati surūpadhṛk \|*  
*prajāvatī subhogāḍhyā subhagā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A woman who is unlucky, barren, squint-eyed and ugly shall become beautiful by visiting you. Undoubtedly she shall become fortunate, enjoying excellent pleasures and giving birth to good children.

## \|\| 1.77.72 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokānāṃ vedyāmasyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*sthāsyāmi sahitaḥ patnyā satyātva dvacanādvidhe \|\| 72 \|\|*

Maheśvara said:

72\. O Vidhi, at your true instance I shall remain in the Vedī accompanied by my wife for the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.77.73 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstatra sabhāryo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*vidyate vedimadhyastho lokānāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ 0 \|\| 73 \|\|*

Sūta said:

73\. Thus the Bull-bannered Lord stands in the centre of the Vedī along with his wife, destroying the sins of all people.

## \|\| 1.77.74 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā tasya purā'bhavat \|*  
*vivāho vṛṣanāthasya manau svāyaṃbhuve dvijāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Thus, O Brāhmaṇas, it has been fully narrated to you how formerly in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara the marriage of Vṛṣanātha took place.

## \|\| 1.77.75-76 \|\|

*vivāhasamaye prāpte prārambhe vā śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*etadākhyānamavyagraṃ saṃpūjya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*tasyā'vighnaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ karma vaivāhikaṃ ca yat \|\| 75 \|\|*

*kanyā ca sukhasaubhāgya śīlācāraguṇānvitā \|*  
*tathā syātputriṇī sādhvī pativrataparāyaṇā \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. If on the occasion of a marriage or at the beginning, anyone listens to this narrative after adoring calmly the Bull-bannered Lord, all the rites of the marriage celebration shall become unhindered. The bride shall become endowed with happiness, conjugal felicity, good qualitic \[quality/qualites?\] and conduct; she shall be chaste and loyal and give birth to sons.

## Chapter 78 - Greatness of Rudraśīrṣa

## \|\| 1.78.1-3 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā katame sthāne tatra sūta kṛtaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*vālakhilyaiśca taiḥ sarvairmunibhiḥ śaṃsitavrataiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyā vāyavyadigbhāge haravedyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*samyakchraddhāprayatnena brahmaṇā vihitaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paścime vālakhilyaiśca japasnānaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tatrāścaryamabhūdyadvai pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇa sattamāḥ \|*  
*āśrame caturāsyasya tadvo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. At what place there, O Sūta, was the penance performed by Brahmā along with the sages (named) Vālakhilyas of esteemed holy vows?

## \|\| 1.78.4 \|\|

*tatra duścāriṇī kācidrātrau brāhmaṇavaṃśajā \|*  
*devadattaṃ samāsādya vallabhaṃ ramate sadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, penance was performed by Brahmā with proper devotion and endeavour on the north-western side of the Vedī of Hara. Vālakhilyas engaged themselves in Japa and holy ablution and performed the penance on the western side. Now I shall narrate to you, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the wonderful thing that happened in the hermitage of the Four-faced Lord.

4\. A certain woman of loose conduct, though hailing from a Brāhmaṇa family, always used to dally with her paramour named Devadatta, at the place.

## \|\| 1.78.5 \|\|

*ajñātā patinā mātrā tathānyairapi bāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ samāsādya vijane hṛṣṭamānasā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She used to come to this place with a happy mind during the nights of the dark half without the knowledge of her husband, mother and other relatives.

## \|\| 1.78.6 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya dṛṣṭā sā kenaci ddvijāḥ \|*  
*tatrasthā jārasaṃyuktā svabhartuśca niveditā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once, O Brāhmaṇas, someone saw her in the company of the paramour and intimated it to her husband.

## \|\| 1.78.7 \|\|

*athāsau kopasaṃyuktastasyā bhartā suniṣṭhuraiḥ \|*  
*vākyaistāṃ garhayāmāsa prahāraiścāpya tāḍayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The husband became furious. He rebuked her with very harsh words and also thrashed her with blows.

## \|\| 1.78.8 \|\|

*atha sā dhārṣṭyamāsādya strīsvabhāvaṃ samāśritā \|*  
*provāca bāṣpapūrṇākṣī dīnāṃjalipuṭā sthitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She shamelessly shed tears profusely in accordance with her womanly nature and said in piteous tones with palms joined together

## \|\| 1.78.9-10 \|\|

*kiṃ māṃ durjanavākyena tvaṃ tāḍayasi niṣṭhuraiḥ \|*  
*prahārairdoṣanirmuktāṃ tvatpādapraṇatāṃ vibho \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tvāṃ śapathaṃ kṛtvā bhakṣayitvā'tha vā viṣam \|*  
*praviśya havyavāhaṃ vā kariṣye pratyayānvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. “O my Lord, I am blameless. I am one bowing down at your feet. Still why do you beat me harshly and ruthlessly solely relying in the words of some wicked man? I can convince you of my innocence by taking solemn oaths, by drinking poison or by entering blazing fire.”

## \|\| 1.78.11 \|\|

*atha tāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prāha yadi tvaṃ pāpavarjitā \|*  
*purato devaviprāṇāṃ kuru divyagrahaṃ svayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon the Brāhmaṇa said to her, “If you are sinless then take up Divyagraha (ordeal through fire etc.) in front of the deities and Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 1.78.12 \|\|

*sā tatheti pratijñāya sāhasena samanvitā \|*  
*divyagrahaṃ tataścakre yathoktavidhinā satī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Bold and venturesome that she was, she consented saying “So be it” and took up Divyagraha (the ordeal) in accordance with the convention.

## \|\| 1.78.13 \|\|

*śuddhiṃ ca prāptā sarveṣāṃ bandhūnāṃ ca dvijanmanām \|*  
*purataśca gurūṇāṃ ca devānāmapi pāpakṛt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Though really a sinner, she came out unscathed after the ordeal in front of all the kinsmen, elders, Brāhmaṇas and the deities.

## \|\| 1.78.14 \|\|

*etasminnantare tasyāḥ sādhuvādo mahānabhūt \|*  
*dhikchabdaśca tathā patyuḥ sarvairdattaḥ sugarhitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the meantime (as a resuṭt of this) she was admiringly congratulated and the husband was roundly condemned and despised with words like “Fie upon you!”

## \|\| 1.78.15 \|\|

*aho pāpasamācāro duṣṭo'yaṃ brāhmaṇādhamaḥ \|*  
*apāpāṃ dharmapatnīṃ yo mithyādoṣeṇayojayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Alas, this wicked and base Brāhmaṇa is the real sinner! He has falsely accused his virtuous wife free from sins.”

## \|\| 1.78.16-17 \|\|

*evaṃ sa nindyamānastu sarvalokairdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kopaṃ cakre tato vahniṃ samuddiśya saduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śāpaṃ dātuṃ matiṃ cakre tato vahneḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*abravītparuṣaṃ vākyaṃ nindamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, thus, he was rebuked by all the people. He became very miserable and was furious with the Fire-god. In his great misery he felt inclined to curse the Fire-god. Censuring him (Fire-god) repeatedly, he spoke these harsh words:

## \|\| 1.78.18-19 \|\|

*mayā svayaṃ pradṛṣṭeyaṃ jāreṇa saha saṃgatā \|*  
*tvayā vahne supāpeyaṃ na kasmādbhasmasātkṛtā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tasmāttvāṃ pāpakarmāṇamasatyapakṣapātinam \|*  
*asaṃdigdhaṃ śapiṣyāmi raudraśāpena sāṃpratam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. “She has been seen by myself in a very compromising situation in the company of her paramour. O Vahni, she is a great sinner; why is she not reduced to ash by you? Hence you are an abettor of her crime. You are partial to an indecent one. Now I shall curse you undoubtedly with a terrible imprecation.”

## \|\| 1.78.20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃkruddhasya dvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*saptārcirbhayasaṃtrastaḥ kṛtāṃjaliruvāca tam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sūta said:

20\. On hearing those words of the furious Brāhmaṇa, the Fire-god became terrified. He said to him with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.78.21 \|\|

*agniruvāca \|*  
*naiṣa doṣo mama brahmanyanna dagdhā tava priyā \|*  
*kṛtāgasā'pi me vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣvātra sphuṭeritam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Agni said:

21\. O Brāhmaṇa, it is not my fault that your beloved wife was not burnt in spite of her sinful offence. In this connection listen to my dear statement.

## \|\| 1.78.22 \|\|

*anayā parakāṃtena kṛtaḥ saha samāgamaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃ kālaṃ dvija śreṣṭha tvayā jñātādya vāsare \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Sexual intercourse is being conducted by this woman with her paramour. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, it has been so for a long time, though you knew it only this day.

## \|\| 1.78.23 \|\|

*paraṃ yasmādviśuddhaiṣā mayā dagdhā na sā dvija \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ tacca te vacmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. But, O Brāhmaṇa, I shall tell you the reason why she has not been burnt and why she is declared pure. Listen attentively.

## \|\| 1.78.24 \|\|

*yatrānayā kṛtaḥ saṃgaḥ parakāṃtena vai dvija \|*  
*tasminnāyatane brahmā rudraśīrṣo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Brahmā with Rudra on his head is stationed in that shrine, O Brāhmaṇa, where this woman’s contact with the paramour has been going on.

## \|\| 1.78.25 \|\|

*tatra kṛtvā rataṃ citraṃ parakāṃtasamaṃ tadā \|*  
*paśyati sma tato rudraṃ brahmamastakasaṃsthitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After the various kinds of dalliance with her paramour, she used to see the deity Rudra stationed on the head of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.78.26 \|\|

*tataḥ prakṣālayatyaṃgaṃ kuṇḍe tatrāgrataḥ sthite \|*  
*kṛtapāpāpi tenaiṣā śuddhiṃ yāti śucismitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereafter she used to wash her limbs in the holy pit present in front. Thereby this woman of sparkling smiles attains purity despite her sinful crime.

## \|\| 1.78.27 \|\|

*atra pūrvaṃ vipāpmā'bhūdbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*satīvaktraṃ samālokya kāmārto'pi sa pāpakṛt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It was here that formerly Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, became liberated form his sin. His sinful offence was that he looked at the countenance of Goddess Satī after being overwhelmed by lust.

## \|\| 1.78.28 \|\|

*tasmānnāstyatra me doṣaḥ svalpo'pi dvijasattama \|*  
*rudraśīrṣaprabhāvo'yaṃ tasya kuṇḍodakasya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I cannot be blamed in the least. It is the power of Rudrasīrṣa and the holy water of the sacred pit.

## \|\| 1.78.29 \|\|

*tasmādenāṃ samādāya saṃśuddhāṃ pāpavarjitām \|*  
*gṛhaṃ gaccha dvijaśreṣṭha satyametanmayo ditam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, take this woman home. She has become sanctified and so she is free from sins. What has been said by me is the truth.

## \|\| 1.78.30 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*yā mayā sahasā dṛṣṭā svayameva hutāśana \|*  
*parakāṃtena tāṃ nādya śuddhāmapi gṛhaṃ naye \|\| 30 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

30\. O Hutāśana (Fire-god), I will not take her home though she might have become pure. I did see myself, her in the company of her paramour, in her rash action!

## \|\| 1.78.31 \|\|

*ityuktvā ca dvijaśreṣṭhastāṃ tyaktvāpi śucivrataḥ \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ paścāttathā jagmurjanā gṛhān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After saying this, the excellent Brāhmaṇa of pure holy vows, abandoned her also and went home later. The people too went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 1.78.32-33 \|\|

*sāpi tena parityaktā patinā hṛṣṭamānasā \|*  
*jñātvā tattīrthamāhātmyaṃ vaiśvānaramukheritam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tenaiva parakāṃtena viśeṣeṇa ratikriyām \|*  
*tasminnāyatane cakre kuṇḍe toyāvagāhanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Abandoned thus by her husband, she became highly delighted in her mind. After knowing the greatness of that Tīrtha directly uttered by Vaiśvānara, she continued her dalliance with the paramour with added zest in the same shrine and later took her plunge in the holy Kuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.78.34-36 \|\|

*athānye paralokasya bhītyā'tīva vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*vimukhāḥ paradāreṣu nāryaścāpi pativratāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dūrato'pi samabhyetya te sarve tatra maṃdire \|*  
*rudraśīrṣābhidhānaṃ ca pracakruḥ suratotsavam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nimajjaṃti tataḥ kuṇḍe tasminpātakanāśane \|*  
*bhavaṃti pāpanirmuktā rudraśīrṣāvalokanāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Thereafter, even men with their faces averted from other men's wives, and women with strict adherence to the vow of fidelity used to come to that holy shrine from places very far off. They were scrupulous in everything because of their fear of what was in store for them in the other world. They indulged in sexual intercourse in that shrine called Rudrasīrṣa. Thereafter, they used to take their holy bath in that Kuṇḍa destructive of sins, They were liberated from their sins by seeing Rudraśīrṣa.

## \|\| 1.78.37 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare naṣṭo dharmaḥ patnīsamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*puruṣāṇāṃ tataḥ strīṇāṃ nijakāṃtāsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the meantime all virtuousness of men in regard to their fidelity towards their wives and that of women in regard to their faithfulness to their husbands got lost.

## \|\| 1.78.38 \|\|

*yo yāṃ paśyati rūpāḍhyāṃ nārīmapi kulodbhavām \|*  
*sa tatrānīya saṃhṛṣṭo bhajate dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. (There was shameless promiscuousness in sexual relations, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.) Whoever sets his eyes on a comely woman, be she of a noble family, he used to take her to that holy spot for joyous indulgence.

## \|\| 1.78.39 \|\|

*tathā nārī surūpāḍhyaṃ yaṃ paśyati naraṃ kvacit \|*  
*sāpi tatra samānīya kurute suratotsavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly if any woman finds any handsome man anywhere, she used to take him over there for joyous sexual enjoyment.

## \|\| 1.78.40 \|\|

*lipyate na ca pāpena kathaṃcittakṛtena ca \|*  
*naro vā yadi vā nārī tattīrthasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Neither the man nor the woman was contaminated by the sin thereof even in the least, thanks to the power of that Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.78.41-42 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tatra rājā vidūrathaḥ \|*  
*ānarttaviṣaye jajñe vārdhakyaṃ ca kramādyayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasya bhāryā'bhavattanvī taruṇī vararūpadhṛk \|*  
*paścime vayasi prāpte prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Once there was a king named Vidūratha in the land of Ānarta, who became old in due course. Though he was old, he had a young maiden of excellent beauty as his wife whom he loved more than his own life, even though he had reached old age.

## \|\| 1.78.43 \|\|

*na tasyāḥ sa jarāgrastaścitte vasati pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe samāgatya vāṃchitaṃ ramate naraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The king affected by senile atrophy never found a place in the heart of that woman. She used to come to this holy shrine and divert herself with any man of her choice.

## \|\| 1.78.44-45 \|\|

*pārthivo'pi parijñāya tasyāstacca viceṣṭitam \|*  
*kopāviṣṭastato gatvā tasminkṣetre suśobhane \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatkuṇḍaṃ pūrayāmāsa tataḥ pāṃśūtkarairdrutam \|*  
*babhaṃja taṃ ca prāsādaṃ tataḥ provāca dāruṇam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. After coming to know of her misconduct, the king became very furious. He went to that splendid shrine and quickly filled the holy Kuṇḍa with dust particles and broke the palace to pieces. Thereafter he spoke these terrible words:

## \|\| 1.78.46-47 \|\|

*yaścaitatpūritaṃ kuṇḍaṃ pāṃśunā nikhaniṣyati \|*  
*prāsādaṃ ca punaścainaṃ kariṣyati punarnavam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*paradārakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tasya saṃpatsyate'khilam \|*  
*yadatra prakariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ kāmamohitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. “If anyone digs again this Kuṇḍa now filled with dust particles and renovates this temple, he will fully incur the sin of coming into intimate contact with other men’s wives as in the case of men deluded by lust who will indulge in sinful conduct.”

## \|\| 1.78.48 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa pārthivaḥ procya tāmādāya tataḥ priyām \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ paścātprahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 48 \|\|*

Sūta said:

48\. After declaring thus the king took his beloved back to his abode. He was evidently pleased much in his heart.

## \|\| 1.78.49 \|\|

*atha tāṃ viratāṃ jñātvā so'nyacittāṃ priyāṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*yatnena rakṣayāmāsa viśvāsaṃ naiva gacchati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The king knew that his beloved wife thought of other men previously but had ceased to be so. Yet he guarded her with effort and alertness and did not fully believe in her.

## \|\| 1.78.50 \|\|

*anyasmindivase śastraṃ sūkṣmaṃ veṇyāṃ nidhāya sā \|*  
*jagāma śayanaṃ tasya vadhārthaṃ varavarṇinī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One day the lady of excellent complexion concealed a very small weapon in her plaited hairs and went to bed with the intention of killing him.

## \|\| 1.78.51 \|\|

*tatastena samaṃ hāsyaṃ kṛtvā kṣatriyabhāvajam \|*  
*surataṃ rucirairbhāvairhāvairbhūribhireva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. She indulged in sexual dalliance and jocular remarks with him as befitting the emotions of a Kṣattriya along with conquettish manner and sensuous movement of limbs.

## \|\| 1.78.52 \|\|

*tato nidrāvaśaṃ prāptaṃ taṃ nṛpaṃ sā nṛpapriyā \|*  
*svaveṇyāḥ śastramādāya nijaghāna sunirdayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When the king fell into a sound sleep the ruthless beloved of the king took off the weapon from her braid of hairs and killed him.

## \|\| 1.78.53 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya phalaṃ jātaṃ sadyastīrthasya bhaṃgajam \|*  
*ānartādhipate raudraṃ sarvalokavigarhitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thus the Lord of Ānarta immediately reaped the fruit of his act of destroying the Tīrtha. The act was indeed violent and despised by all people.

## \|\| 1.78.54 \|\|

*adyāpi tatra deveśo rudraśīrṣaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|*  
*liṃgabhedabhayāttena na sa bhagno dvijottamāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the king was afraid of shattering the Liṅga. Hence Lord Rudraśīrśa was not broken by him. The deity stands even now.

## \|\| 1.78.55-59 \|\|

*yastasya purataḥ sthitvā japedrudraśiraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*māghaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ pūjayitvā sragādibhiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vāṃchitaṃ labhate cāśu tasyeśasya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ yāvadyo japetpurataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*rudraśīrṣaṃ na saṃdehaḥ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*ekavāraṃ naro yo vā tatpuraḥ paṭhati dvijaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*nityaṃ dinakṛtātpāpānmucyate dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ rudraśīrṣasamudbhavam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpānāṃ sadyo nāśanakārakam \|*  
*maṃgalaṃ paramaṃ hyetadāyuṣyaṃ kīrtivardhanam \|*  
*rudraśīrṣasya māhātmyaṃ tasmācchrotavyamādarāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

55-59. One who remains pure, stands in front of the deity and recites Rudraśiras Mantras on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of Māgha after the adoration with garlands etc. obtains immediately all desired benefits by the power of the Lord.

One who stands in front of the deity and chants Rudraśīrṣa one hundred eight times attains the greatest goal undoubtedly.

One who recites it once in front of the deity everyday, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, gets rid of the sins of that day.

Thus everything connected with the greatness of Rudraśīrṣa has been narrated to you. It destroys all sins immediately. It is highly auspicious and increases fame. Hence the greatness of Rudraśīrṣa should be listened to respectfully.

## Chapter 79 - Greatness of Vālakhilyāśrama (Vālakhilya-āśrama)

## \|\| 1.79.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyaiva dakṣiṇe bhāge vālakhilyaiḥ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*liṃgamasti suvikhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yamārādhya ca taiḥ pūrvaṃ śakrāmarṣasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*garuḍo janitaḥ pakṣī khyāto viṣṇuratho'tra yaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ teṣāṃ samutpannaḥ śakrasyopari sūtaja \|*  
*prakopo vālakhilyānāṃ saṃjajñe garuḍaḥ katham \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. To the south itself thereof is the well-known Liṅga installed by Vālakhilyas. It is destructive of all sins. It is by propitiating that liṅga that those who were extremely furious with Śakra created Garuḍa, the bird who became the well-known vehicle of Viṣṇu here.

## \|\| 1.79.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purā prajāpatirdakṣastasminkṣetre suśobhane \|*  
*cakāra vidhivadyajñaṃ saṃpūrṇavaradakṣiṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

O Sūtaja, how did Vālakhilyas become angry with Śakra and how was Garuḍa born?

Sūta said:

4\. Formerly Dakṣa, the Prajāpati (Patriarch), duly performed in that splendid holy spot a Yajña with profuse distribution of monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.79.5 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrādayo devāḥ sahāyārthaṃ nimaṃtritāḥ \|*  
*dakṣeṇa munayaścaiva tathā rājarṣayo'malāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Therein Śakra and other Devas, sages and pure saintly kings, were invited for assistance by Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.79.6 \|\|

*tathā vedavido viprā yajñakarmavicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*gṛhasthāśramiṇo ye ca ye cāraṇyanivāsinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. So also were invited Brāhmaṇas fully conversant with the Vedas and clever in the rites of Yajña, those who were in the stage of householders and those who were permanent residents of forests.

## \|\| 1.79.7 \|\|

*atha te vālakhilyākhyā munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*ekāṃ samidhamādāya sāhāyyārthaṃ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*prasthitā yajñavāṭaṃ taṃ bhārārtāḥ kleśasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Vālakhilyas, the sages of esteemed holy vows, started towards the sacrificial hall for assisting Prajāpati. They were carrying a single sacrificial twig all by themselves but still they were distressed due to its burden.

## \|\| 1.79.8 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ samastānāṃ mārge goṣpadamāgatam \|*  
*jalapūrṇaṃ samāyātamakālajaladāgame \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Due to the advent of untimely rains, a pit created by cow’s foot that was on their path, got filled with water.

## \|\| 1.79.9-10 \|\|

*tatastarītu kāmāste kliśyamānā itastataḥ \|*  
*samidbhāraśramopetā devarājena vīkṣitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*gacchatā tena mārgeṇa makhe dakṣaprajāpateḥ \|*  
*tataściraṃ samālokya smitaṃ kṛtvā sa kautukāt \|*  
*jagāmātha samullaṃghya aiśvaryamadagarvitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. As they were eager to cross it and were straining themselves under the weight of the sacrificial twig; the king of Devas who was also travelling by the same path towards the sacrificial place of Dakṣa, the Prajāpati, happened to see them. He looked at them out of curiosity for a long time and then smiled. In the height of his arrogance on account of his affluence, he went ahead crossing over them.

## \|\| 1.79.11 \|\|

*tataste kopasaṃyuktāḥ śakrāddṛṣṭvā parābhavam \|*  
*nivṛtya svāśramaṃ gatvā cakrurmaṃtraṃ saniścayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In view of this disrespect shown by Śakra, they became very angry. They turned back to their hermitage and took counsel with one another with a final decision:

## \|\| 1.79.12-14 \|\|

*śākraṃ padaṃ samāsādya yasmādetena pāpmanā \|*  
*atikrāṃtā vayaṃ sarve tasmātpātyaḥ sa satpadāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*anyaḥ śakraḥ prakartavyo maṃtravīryasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*ātharvaṇairmahāsūktairābhicārikasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yena vyāpādyate tena śakro'yaṃ madagarvitaḥ \|*  
*makhamāhātmyasaṃpannaḥ svalpabuddhiparā kramaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. “On getting the position of Śakra, this sinful one has crossed over all of us! He should be pulled down from his excellent post. Another Śakra should be created by the power of Mantras, the great Sūktas from the Atharva Veda, after applying them for Abhicāra rites (Black Magic).

This Śakra, haughty and intoxicated with power, endowed with greatness due to the sacrifices (performed by him for getting Indra-hood) should be overthrown. His intellect and exploits are meagre.”

## \|\| 1.79.15-16 \|\|

*tataste śucayo bhūtvā skaṃdasūktena pāvakam \|*  
*juhuvuśca divārātrau kṣurikoktena sodyamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*garbhopaniṣadenaiva nīlarudrairdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*rudraśīrṣeṇa kāmyena viṣṇusūktayutena caṃ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Thereafter, they remained pure mentally and physically and performed Homa in the holy fìre day and night. With great earnestness, those excellent Brāhmaṇas recited Skandasūkta as mentioned in the Kṣurikā section, Garbhopaniṣad, Nīlarudra passages, charming Rudraśīrṣa etc., along with Viṣṇu Sūkta.

## \|\| 1.79.17 \|\|

*nidhāya kalaśaṃ madhye maṃḍalasyodakāvṛtam \|*  
*homāṃte tatra saṃsparśaṃ cakrustasya jalaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. They placed a pot filled with water in the centre of the Maṇḍala. At the conclusion of the Homa they touched (all Homa articles with) that sacred water.

## \|\| 1.79.18 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śakraḥ prapaśyati sudāruṇān \|*  
*utpātānātmanāśāya jāyamānānsamaṃtataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the meantime Śakra saw frightening, evil-foreboding omens arising all round pointing at his own destruction.

## \|\| 1.79.19 \|\|

*vāmo bāhuśca netraṃ ca muhuḥ sphurati cāsya vai \|*  
*na ca paśyati nāsāgraṃ jihvāgraṃ ca tathā hanum \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. His left arm and left eye throbbed. He could not see the tip of his nose or tongue or the chin.

## \|\| 1.79.20 \|\|

*śirohīnāṃ tathā chāyāṃ gagane bhāskaradvayam \|*  
*aruṃdhatīṃ dhruvaṃ caiva na ca viṣṇupadāni saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He saw his own shadow bereft of the head and two Suns in the sky. He was unable to see Arundhatī star and Dhruva (Pole Star) or portions of the firmament.

## \|\| 1.79.21 \|\|

*na ca maṃdaṃ na cākāśe saṃsthitāṃ svardhunīṃ hariḥ \|*  
*svapanpaśyati kṛṣṇāṃgīṃ nityaṃ nārīṃ dhṛtāyudhām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hari (Indra) could not see the planet Saturn and the heavenly river stationed in the sky. While sleeping he used to dream of a woman of dark complexion, armed with weapons.

## \|\| 1.79.22-24 \|\|

*muktakeśīṃ vivastrāṃ ca kṛṣṇadaṃtāṃ bhayānakām \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā sa mahotpātāndevarājo bṛhaspatim \|\| 22 \|\|*

*papraccha bhayasaṃtrastaḥ kimetaditi me guro \|*  
*jāyaṃte sumahotpātā durnimittāni vai pṛthak \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kiṃ me bhaviṣyati prājña vināśaḥ sāṃprataṃ vada \|*  
*kiṃ vā trailokya rājyasya kiṃ vā vittādikasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. She was hideous and frightening and naked, she has dishevelled hairs and black teeth.

On observing these omens of great magnitude, the King of Devas asked Bṛhaspati in great fear: “Omy preceptor, what is this? Terrible ill omens and scenes foreboding evil occur severally. O wise one, will destruction overtake just now? Do tell me. Will my kingdom of the three worlds be affected? Will my fortune etc., suffer?”

## \|\| 1.79.25 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*ye tvayā madamattena vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*ullaṃghitāḥ sthitā mārge goṣpadaṃ tarttumicchavaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

25\. You have been arrogant. The great sages, Vālakhilyas, who had been held up on the way in their intention to cross the Goṣpada (Puddle of water caused by cow's foot) were transgressed by you.

## \|\| 1.79.26 \|\|

*tairevātharvaṇairmaṃtraistvakṛte'sti śacīpate \|*  
*kṛto homaḥ susaṃpūrṇaḥ kalaśaścābhimaṃtritaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Consort of Śacī, they have performed a perfect Homa by means of the Mantras of Atharva Veda against you. The water-pot has also been charged with the Mantras.

## \|\| 1.79.27 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ suvināśāya sarvadevādhināyakaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdeho maṃtrairātharvaṇairhariḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There is no doubt about it that another Hari (Indra), the Lord of all the Devas, will spring up as a result of these Ātharvaṇa Mantras in order to bring about your destruction.

## \|\| 1.79.28 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sahasrākṣo bhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*dakṣaṃ gatvā ca dīnāsyaḥ provāca tadanaṃtaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing his words, the Thousand-eyed One became afraid. He went then to Dakṣa with a sad face and said to him:

## \|\| 1.79.29-30 \|\|

*asmannāśāya munibhirvālakhilyaiḥ prajāpate \|*  
*prodyamo vihitaḥ samyakchakrasyānyasya vai kṛte \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tānvāraya svayaṃ gatvā yāvanno jāyate paraḥ \|*  
*śakro'smaddhvaṃsanārthāya nāsti teṣāmasādhyatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. “O Prajāpati, the Vālakhilya sages have endeavoured to destroy us and create another Śakra. Do go there yourself and prevent them before another Śakra is born for destroying us. There is nothing that they cannot do.”

## \|\| 1.79.31 \|\|

*atha dakṣo drutaṃ gatvā śakrādyairamarairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*prahasaṃstānuvācedaṃ vinayena samanvitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Accompanied by the Devas beginning with Śakra, Dakṣa hurried to that place and spoke to them laughingly yet with humility:

## \|\| 1.79.32 \|\|

*kimetatkriyate viprāḥ karma raudratamaṃ mahat \|*  
*trailokyaṃ vyākulaṃ yena sarvametadvyavasthitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O Brāhmaṇas, why is this most terrible act being done by you whereby the entire range of the three worlds has become upset.”

## \|\| 1.79.33 \|\|

*atha te dakṣamālokya samāyātaṃ svamāśrayam \|*  
*saṃmukhāścābhyayustūrṇaṃ pragṛhītārghyapāṇayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing Dakṣa coming to their place of residence, they hurriedly proceeded towards him with Arghya in their hands.

## \|\| 1.79.34-35 \|\|

*arghyaṃ dattvā yathānyāyaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvātha bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*procuśca praṇatā bhūtvā svāgataṃ te prajāpate \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ādeśo dīyatāṃ śīghraṃ yadarthamiha cāgataḥ \|*  
*api prāṇapradānena kariṣyāmaḥ priyaṃ tava \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. After duly offering the Arghya and adoring him devoutly they bowed to him and said: “O Prajāpati, welcome to you. May we be commanded at once. Why have you come here? Even by offering our lives we shall do what is pleasing to you.”

## \|\| 1.79.36 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*etadraudratamaṃ karma sarvadevabhayāvaham \|*  
*tyājyaṃ yuṣmābhiravyagrairetadarthamihāgataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

36\. This highly terrifying rite that has instilled fear into Devas should be discontinued by you all unexcitedly. I have come here for this purpose.

## \|\| 1.79.37 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ śakreṇa te yajñe samāyātāḥ subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*ullaṃghitā madodrekātkṛtvā hāsyaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

The sages said:

37\. We were coming devotedly to attend your Yajña. But, in his height of arrogance, Śakra repeatedly indulged in laughing at us and transgressed us.

## \|\| 1.79.38 \|\|

*śakrocchedāya cāsmābhiḥ śako'nyo vīryamaṃtrataḥ \|*  
*prārabdhaḥ kartumatyugrairhomāṃtaśca vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In order to exterminate this Śakra, we, the agitated angry ones, began to create another Śakra by means of the Mantras of great power. The Homa too has been concluded.

## \|\| 1.79.39 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ maṃtravīryaṃ tatkriyate moghamityaho \|*  
*vedoktaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa tasmādatra vada prabho \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence, tell us, O Lord. How can the power of the Mantra be rendered ineffective after it has been created by the Vedas?

## \|\| 1.79.40 \|\|

*tvameva yadi śaktaḥ syādanyathā kartumeva hi \|*  
*kuruṣva vā svayaṃ nātha nāsmākaṃ śaktirīdṛśī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Lord, if you yourself are competent to alter it, do it. We are powerless in this respect.

## \|\| 1.79.41 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāgā yadyuṣmābhiḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*nānyathā śakyate kartuṃ vedamantrodbhavaṃ balam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

41\. O highly esteemed ones, what has been said by you all is true. The power generated by the Vedic Mantras cannot be rendered otherwise.

## \|\| 1.79.42 \|\|

*tadya eṣa kṛto homo yuṣmābhirvedamaṃtrataḥ \|*  
*devarājārthamavyagraiḥ kalaśaścābhimaṃtritaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Homa has been performed by you all by means of the Vedic Mantras. For the purpose of (creating) a king of Devas, the water-pot has been charged with Mantras by you all in a cool and calculated manner.

## \|\| 1.79.43 \|\|

*so'yaṃ madvacanādrājā bhaviṣyati patatriṇām \|*  
*tejovīryasamopetaḥ śakrādapi suvīryavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At my instance, he shall become the king of birds. He will be endowed with refulgence and vigour. He will be superior even to Śakra.

## \|\| 1.79.44 \|\|

*etasya devarājasya kṣaṃtavyaṃ mama vākyataḥ \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ mūḍhabhāvena yadanena viceṣṭitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Again at my instance, what has been perpetrated by this king of Devas should be forgiven. He has done this foolishly.

## \|\| 1.79.45 \|\|

*evamuktvātha teṣāṃ taṃ sahasrākṣaṃ bhayāturam \|*  
*darśayāmāsa dakṣastu vinayāvanataṃ sthitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. After saying thus, Dakṣa pointed to the fear-stricken Thousand-eyed One standing humbly.

## \|\| 1.79.46-47 \|\|

*te'pi dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṃ vepamānaṃ kṛtāṃjalim \|*  
*procurmā'tikramaṃ śakra brāhmaṇānāṃ kariṣyasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

*bhūyo yadi diveśānāmādhipatyaṃ pravāṃchasi \|*  
*api mando'pi mūrkho'pi kriyāhīno'pi vā dvijaḥ \|*  
*nāvajñeyo budhaiḥ kvāpi lokadvaya mabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. On seeing the Thousand-eyed One standing with palms joined in reverence and trembling much, they said: “O Śakra, do not transgress Brāhmaṇas hereafter.

Do not do so again if you wish for the overlordship of the heaven-dwellers. Even a stupid, foolish Brāhmaṇa who does not regularly perform his sacred rites should not be insulted by sensible persons desirous of attaining the pleasures of the two worlds.”

## \|\| 1.79.48 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*ajñānādyadi vā jñānādyanmayā kukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tatkṣaṃtavyaṃ dvijaiḥ sarvairviśeṣāddakṣa vākyataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Indra said:

48\. This misdemeanour of mine knowingly or unknowingly committed by me should be forgiven by all the Brāhmaṇas especially at the instance of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.79.49 \|\|

*pragṛhyatāṃ varo'smākaṃ yaḥ sadā vartate hṛdi \|*  
*pradāsyāmi na saṃdeho nādeyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. May a boon cherished in the heart always, be received from me. I shall undoubtedly grant it. There is nothing which I cannot give.

## \|\| 1.79.50-52 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*asminkuṇḍe naro homaṃ yaḥ kuryācchraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*etalliṃgaṃ samabhyarcya tasyā'stu hṛdi vāṃchitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*indra uvāca \|*  
*etalliṃgaṃ samabhyarcya yo'tra homaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*kuṃḍe'tra vāṃchitaṃ sadyaḥ saphalaṃ sa hi lapsyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

*niṣkāmo vā'tha saṃpūjya liṃgametacchubhāvaham \|*  
*prayāsyati parāṃ siddhiṃ tridaśairapi durlabhām \|\| 52 \|\|*

The sages said:

50-52. If any man endowed with faith worships this Liṅga and performs Homa in this Kuṇḍa let him get what he desires.

## \|\| 1.79.53-54 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sahasrākṣo vālakhilyānmunīśvarān \|*  
*airāvataṃ samāruhya dakṣayajñe tato gataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*dakṣo'pi vidhivadyajñaṃ cakāra dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*saṃhṛṣṭairvālakhilyaistairupaviṣṭaiḥ samīpataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

Indra said:

He who adores this Liṅga and performs Homa in the Kuṇḍa shall immediately attain the desired benefit.

One without desire who worships this auspicious Liṅga will attain the greatest Siddhi inaccessible even to Devas.

Sūta said:

53-54. After saying thus to the Vālakhilya Sages, the Thousand-eyed One (Indra) mounted his Airāvata and took (them?) to the Yajña of Dakṣa.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Dakṣa too duly performed the Yajña while the delighted Vālakhilyas sat near.

## Chapter 80 - Importance of the Sight of Viṣṇu

## \|\| 1.80.1-2 \|\|

*\| atha suparṇākhyamāhātmyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃti \|*  
*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tejovīryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*garuḍastena saṃjajñe munīnāṃ homakarmaṇā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ tatra saṃbhūta etanno vistarādvada \|*  
*vinatāyāḥ samudbhūta ityeṣā śrūyate śrutiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 80-85 contain the story of Suparṇa i.e. Garuḍa. Here the author skilfully weaves the future events in Kṛṣṇa’s Avatāra. Garuḍa lost both his wings due to his baseless derogatory remarks against women in general. The celibate old Śāṇḍilī did not like it. Her mental disapproval deprived Garuḍa of his wings. This episode is therefore the glorification of the local deity Suparṇeśvara, at Camatkārapura.—The birth of Subhadrā with a horse’s face and Kṛṣṇa’s penance to make her beautiful again is attributed to the curse of Lakṣmī who however, though cursed with an elephant’s head, frees herself from it by performing penance instead of depending on Viṣṇu.

The sages said:

1-2. It has been mentioned by you that Garuḍa endowed with refulgence and vigour was born from the Homa performed by the sages (Vālakhilyas).

How was he born there? Tell us this in detail. We have heard that he was born of Vinatā.

## \|\| 1.80.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yo'sāvātharvaṇairmaṃtraiḥ kalaśaścābhimantritaḥ \|*  
*tairmaṃtrairvālakhilyaiśca mahā'marṣasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nivāritaiśca dakṣeṇa sūcite vihagādhipe \|*  
*kaśyapastaṃ samādāya kalaśaṃ prayayau gṛham \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3-4. The water-pot was charged with the Mantras of Atharvarveda by Vālakhilyas swayed by great indignation. They were restrained by Dakṣa and the Lord of the birds was indicated by him. Thereupon Kaśyapa took that Kalaśa (pot) and went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.80.5-6 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca saṃhṛṣṭo vinatāṃ dayitāṃ nijām \|*  
*etatpiba jalaṃ bhadre mantrapūtaṃ mahattaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yena te jāyate putraḥ sahasrākṣādhiko balī \|*  
*tejasvī ca yaśasvī ca ajeyaḥ sarva dānavaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Then he joyously said to his beloved wife Vinatā: “O fair lady, drink this holy water highly sanctified by Mantras. Thereby a son will be born to you, who will be stronger than the Thousandeyed One. He will be refulgent and famous. He cannot be conquered by all the Dānavas combined.

## \|\| 1.80.7 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tatkṣaṇādeva saṃpapau \|*  
*tattoyaṃ sā varārohā sadyo garbhaṃ tato dadhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing his words, that beautiful lady drank that water instantly and conceived immediately.

## \|\| 1.80.8 \|\|

*evaṃ tajjalapānena tejovīryasama nvitaḥ \|*  
*kaśyapādgaruḍo jajñe sarvasarpabhayāvahaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It was thus that Garuḍa who strikes terror into all the serpents was born to Kaśyapa but through the imbibing of that holy water.

## \|\| 1.80.9 \|\|

*yenāmṛtaṃ hṛtaṃ vīryātparibhūya puraṃdaram \|*  
*mātṛbhaktiparītena sarpāṇāṃ saṃniveditam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It was he who defeated Purandara heroically and carried away Amṛta (Nectar). Endowed with devotion to his mother, he offered it to the serpents.

## \|\| 1.80.10 \|\|

*yo jajñe dayito viṣṇorvāhanatvamupāgataḥ \|*  
*dhvajāgre tu rathasyāpi yaḥ sadaiva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It was he who became a great favourite of Viṣṇu after attaining the (high) status of being his vehicle. He is always present on the flag at the top of his chariot.

## \|\| 1.80.11 \|\|

*yena pūrvaṃ tapastaptvā kṣetre'traiva mahātmanā \|*  
*trinetrastuṣṭimānīto gatapakṣeṇa dhīmatā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It was he who performed penance formerly and the Three-eyed Lord was propitiated by that noble-souled one who became sensible after losing his wings.

## \|\| 1.80.12 \|\|

*pakṣāptiryena saṃjātā yasya bhūyo'pi tādṛśī \|*  
*devadevaprasādena viśiṣṭā cā'tha nirmitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Similar wings were acquired by him once again with the favour of the Lord of Devas. Actually they were made better.

## \|\| 1.80.13 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tasya gatau pakṣau garuḍasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*punarlabdhau kathaṃ tena kathaṃ tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*etanno vistarādbrūhi sūtaputra yathātatham \|\| 13 \|\|*

The sages said:

13\. How did the noble-souled Garuḍa lose his wings? How did he get them back? How was Maheśvara propitiated? O son of Sūta, narrate this in detail as it had occurred.

## \|\| 1.80.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāsīdbrāhmaṇo mitraṃ bhṛguvaṃśakulodvahaḥ \|*  
*garuḍasya dvijaśreṣṭhā bālabhāvādapi prabho \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. Formerly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, ever since his childhood, Garuḍa had a Brāhmaṇa friend hailing from the family of Bhṛgu.

## \|\| 1.80.15 \|\|

*tasya kanyā purā jātā mādhavī nāma saṃmatā \|*  
*rūpaudāryasamopetā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. This friend had a daughter named Mādhavī who was endowed with exalted qualities of beauty etc. and marked with all (auspicious) features. She was honoured by all.

## \|\| 1.80.16 \|\|

*na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī na ca pannagī \|*  
*tādṛgrūpā mahābhāgā yādṛśī sā sumadhyamā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Neither a Deva lady, nor a Gandharva woman, neither an Asura lady nor a Pannaga woman had such a beauty of form as that of the highly esteemed slender-waisted one.

## \|\| 1.80.17 \|\|

*atha tasyā varārthāya garuḍaṃ vihagādhipam \|*  
*sa provāca paraṃ mitraṃ vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. That intimate friend humbly requested the Lord of birds to assist him in getting a bridegroom for her:

## \|\| 1.80.18 \|\|

*etasyā mama kanyāyā varaṃ tvaṃ vihagādhipa \|*  
*sadṛśaṃ vīkṣayasvādya yena tasmai dadāmyaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “O Lord of birds, find out a suitable bridegroom for this daughter of mine so that I can offer her in marriage to him.”

## \|\| 1.80.19 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*mama pṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya samastaṃ kṣitimaṃḍalam \|*  
*tvaṃ bhramasva dvijaśreṣṭha gṛhītvemāṃ ca kanyakām \|\| 19 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

19\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, take this daughter with you and ride on my back. Thus roam over the entire range of the world.

## \|\| 1.80.20 \|\|

*tatastasyāḥ kumāryā vai anurūpaṃ guṇānvitam \|*  
*svayaṃ cāhara bhartārameṣā maitrī mamodbhavā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then you yourself select a suitable husband endowed with good qualities for this girl. This is an act of friendship on my part.

## \|\| 1.80.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamukto'tha vipraḥ sa tatkṣaṇātkanyayā saha \|*  
*ārūḍho gāruḍaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ varārthāya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sūta said:

21\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on being told thus that Brāhmaṇa rode on the back of Garuḍa along with his daughter in search of a bridegroom for her.

## \|\| 1.80.22 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ paśyati vipraḥ sa kumāraṃ taruṇākṛtim \|*  
*sa sa no tasya cittāṃte vartatesma kathaṃcana \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Whatever young men the Brāhmaṇa saw none of them appealed to him.

## \|\| 1.80.23 \|\|

*kasyacidrūpamatyugraṃ na kulaṃ ca sunirmalam \|*  
*kulaṃ rūpaṃ ca yasya syāttasya no guṇasaṃcayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The features of a son of someone were very handsome but his family was not spotless. One whose family and features were good did not have good qualities.

## \|\| 1.80.24 \|\|

*yasya vā guṇasandohastasya no rūpamuttamam \|*  
*pakṣapātaṃ ca vittaṃ ca tathānyadvaralakṣaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who had all good qualities did not possess excellent handsome features. Nor did he have the other esseṇtial features of a good bridegroom, such as wealth and inclination (towards good men).

## \|\| 1.80.25 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃte bhramatastasyabhūtalam \|*  
*viprasya pakṣināthasya varārthāya drijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus for a thousand years the Brāhmaṇa and the Lord of birds roamed about the earth for the sake of a suitable bridegroom, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.80.26 \|\|

*kadācidatha tau śrāntau bhramamāṇāvitastataḥ \|*  
*kṣetre'traiva samāyātau vāsudevadidṛkṣayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the course of their wanderings they were tired very much. They reached this very holy spot (of Vāsudeva). They had a desire to meet Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.80.27 \|\|

*śvetadvīpaṃ samālokya tathānyāṃ badarīṃ śubhām \|*  
*kṣīrodaṃ ca savaikuṇṭhaṃ tathānyaṃ tasya saṃśrayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They had already visited Śvetadvīpa, the splendid Badarī, the Milk Ocean, Vaikuṇṭha and other habitual resorts of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.80.28 \|\|

*atha tābhyāṃ munirdṛṣṭo nārado brahmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*sāṃtvapūrvaṃ tadā pṛṣṭo viṣṇuṃ brahma sanātanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then Sage Nārada, the son of Brahmā, was seen by them. The gently asked him about Viṣṇu, the eternal Brahman:

## \|\| 1.80.29 \|\|

*kva devaḥ puṃḍarīkākṣaḥ sāṃprataṃ vartate mune \|*  
*viṣṇusthānāni sarvāṇi vīkṣitāni samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*āvābhyāṃ saṃprahṛṣṭābhyāṃ na saṃdṛṣṭaḥ sa keśavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O Sage, where is the Lotus-eyed Lord now? All the abodes of Viṣṇu have been visited joyously by us both. But Keśava was not seen.”

## \|\| 1.80.30 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*jalaśāyisvarūpeṇa yāvanmāsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sa saṃtiṣṭhati sarvadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nārada said:

30\. He always stays in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra for a period of four months in the form of Jalaśāyin (one who lies down in water).

## \|\| 1.80.31 \|\|

*tasmāttaddarśanārthāya gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram \|*  
*yena sandarśanaṃ yāti dvābhyāmapi sa cakradhṛk \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Hence go immediately to that place for meeting him. The Discus-bearing Lord may come within the range of vision of both of you.

## \|\| 1.80.32 \|\|

*ahamapyeva tatraiva prasthitastasya darśanāt \|*  
*prasthitaśca tvayā yuko devakāryeṇa kenacit \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I too have started for the purpose of meeting him in connection with a certain task of Devas. I shall now accompany you.

## \|\| 1.80.33 \|\|

*atha tau pakṣiviprendrau sa ca brahmasuto muniḥ \|*  
*prāptāḥ sarve sthito yatra jalaśāyī janārdanaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Both of them, the prominent bird and the leading Brāhmaṇa as well as the sage, the son of Brahmā, all these reached the place where Janārdana was present in the form of Jalaśāyin.

## \|\| 1.80.34 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā mahattejo vaiṣṇavaṃ dūrato'pi tam \|*  
*brāhmaṇaṃ garuḍaḥ prāha nāradaśca munīśvaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing the great refulgence of Viṣṇu from afar Garuḍa and the leading sage Nārada spoke to that Brāhmaṇa:

## \|\| 1.80.35-37 \|\|

*atraiva tvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tiṣṭha dūre'pi tejasaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavasya sutāyuktaḥ kalpāṃtāgnisamam va \|\| 35 \|\|*

*no cetsaṃpatsyase bhasma pataṃga iva pāvakam \|*  
*samāsādya niśāyoge mūḍhaṃ bhāvaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*āvābhyāṃ tatprasādena soḍhametatsuduḥsaham \|*  
*na karoti śarīrārti tathānyadapi kutsitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, stāy here itself along with your daughter far away from the refulgence of Viṣṇu that is on a par with the fire appearing at the end of a Kalpa.

Otherwise you will be reduced to ash like a moth that falls into fire, deluded during the night.

This unbearable splendour has been endured by us both due to his favour. So it does not cause distress to our bodies or any other similar adverse effect.”

## \|\| 1.80.38 \|\|

*evaṃ taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tatra muktvā dūre sutānvitam \|*  
*gatau tau tatra saṃsuptastoye yatra janārdanaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After leaving the Brāhmaṇa thus along with his daughter very far away, both of them went to that place where Janārdana was asleep.

## \|\| 1.80.39 \|\|

*divyastutiparau mūrdhni dhṛtahastāṃjalīpuṭau \|*  
*pulakāṃkitasarvāṃgāvānandāśruplutānanau \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Placing the palms joined together in reverence on their heads, they engaged themselves in the divine eulogy. Hairs stood on ends all over their body. Tears of joy welled up in their eyes and drenched their faces.

## \|\| 1.80.40 \|\|

*triḥparikamya taṃ devamaṣṭāṃgaṃ praṇatau harim \|*  
*dṛṣṭavantau ca pādāṃte saṃniviṣṭāṃ samudrajām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After circumambulating thrice, they bowed down to Hari and prostrated before him. They saw the Daughter of the Ocean (i.e. Lakṣmī) seated near the feet.

## \|\| 1.80.41 \|\|

*pādasaṃvāhanāsaktāṃ viṣṇu vaktrāhitekṣaṇām \|*  
*athāparāṃ vayovṛddhāṃ śvetavastrāvaguṃṭhitām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She was joyously engaged in massaging his feet with her eyes riveted to the face of Viṣṇu. They saw another lady too, an elderly one with a white veil covering her face.

## \|\| 1.80.42 \|\|

*sanniviṣṭāṃ tadabhyāśe samyagdhyānaparāyaṇām \|*  
*dvādaśārkaprabhāyuktāṃ kṛśāṃgīṃ pulakānvitām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. She was also seated near her, engaged in deep meditation. She had slender limbs with horripilation manifest on them. She possessed the lustre of twelve suns.

## \|\| 1.80.43 \|\|

*atha tau viṣṇunā harṣādubhāvapi praharṣitau \|*  
*saṃbhāṣitau ca saṃpṛṣṭau yadarthaṃ ca samāgatau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Both the visitors were delighted when Viṣṇu joyously engaged himself in conversation with them asking them why they called.

## \|\| 1.80.44 \|\|

*śrīnārada uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ hi surakāryeṇa saṃprāpyo'tra tavāṃtikam \|*  
*garuḍo vai brāhmaṇāya yanmāṃ pṛcchasi keśava \|\| 44 \|\|*

Śrī Nārada said:

44\. I have come to you on an errand from Devas. Garuḍa has come for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa. O Keśava, this is the reply for what you ask. (What else do you ask?)

## \|\| 1.80.45 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*kaccitkṣemaṃ muniśreṣṭha sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*kaccinneṃdrasya saṃjātaṃ bhayaṃ dānavasaṃbhavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

45\. I hope, O excellent sage, all the Heaven-dwellers are happy and well. I hope there is no situation fearful to Indra caused by Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.80.46 \|\|

*yajñabhāgaṃ labhaṃte sma kacciddevāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*kaccinna dānavaḥ kaścidutkaṭo'bhūddharātale \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I hope, all the Devas including Vāsava are regularly receiving their due share in the Yajñas. I hope, there is no powerful Dānava coming into predominance on the earth.

## \|\| 1.80.47 \|\|

*śrīnārada uvāca \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ dharaṇī prāptā caturvaktrasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*rorūyamāṇā bhārārtā dānavaiḥ pīḍitā bhṛśam \|*  
*provāca padmajaṃ tatra duḥkhena mahatā'nvitā \|\| 47 \|\|*

Śrī Nārada said:

47\. Now, recently the (goddess) Earth came to the presence of the Four-faced Lord. Distressed with the burden and afflicted much by Dānavas she lamented much before the Lotus-born One to whom she said feeling greatly by miserable:

## \|\| 1.80.48 \|\|

*dharaṇyuvāca \|*  
*kālanemirhato yo'sau viṣṇunāprabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*ugrasenasutaḥ kaṃsaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ sa mahāsuraḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Dharaṇī (Earth) said:

48\. The great Asura named Kālanemi who was killed by the powerful Viṣṇu is now born as Kaṃsa, the son of Ugrasena.

## \|\| 1.80.49-50 \|\|

*ariṣṭo dhenukaḥ keśī pralambonāma cāparaḥ \|*  
*tathānyā tu mahāraudrā pūtanā nāma rākṣasī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*itaścetaśca dhāvadbhirdānavairebhireva ca \|*  
*vṛthā me jāyate pīḍā tathānyairapi dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, Keśi, Pralaṃba, the extremely terrible Pūtanā—all these and other terrible ones run about here and there causing me unnecessary pain.

## \|\| 1.80.51 \|\|

*ūrdhvabāhustathā jāto martyaloke jano'dhunā \|*  
*bahutvānna pramāti sma kathaṃciddhi mamopari \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. People of the mortal world have raised up their arms for succour. On account of their multiplicity, they cannot be accommodated on my surface.

## \|\| 1.80.52 \|\|

*bhārāvataraṇaṃ deva na kariṣyasi cāśu cet \|*  
*rasātalaṃ prayāsyāmi tadā'haṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Lord, if you do not reduce the burden immediately, I shall undoubtedly sink into Rasātala (nether world).

\[Nārada continued:\]

## \|\| 1.80.53 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaṇā lokakartṛṇā \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya vibudhaiḥ sārdhaṃ preṣito'haṃ tavāṃtikam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On hearing her words, Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, held consultation with Devas and he has now sent me to you.

## \|\| 1.80.54 \|\|

*proktavyo bhagavānvākyaṃ tvayā devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*yathā'vatīrya bhūpṛṣṭhe bhāramasyāḥ praṇāśayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. (His message is:) “The Lord should be told by you thus: ‘Lord Janārdana should take an incarnation on the Earth and reduce the burden (completely).’”

## \|\| 1.80.55 \|\|

*tasmādbhūbhitale deva kṛtvā janma svayaṃ vibho \|*  
*bhāraṃ nāśaya medinyā etadartha mihāgataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Hence, O powerful Lord, take up your birth on the Earth and reduce the burden of the Earth. It is for this purpose that I have come here.

## \|\| 1.80.56 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*evaṃ mune kariṣyāmi saṃmaṃtrya brahmaṇā saha \|*  
*bhārāvataraṇaṃ bhūmeḥ sākaṃ devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

56\. O sage, it shall be (done) so, I shall consult Brahmā along with Devas including Vāsava and reduce the burden of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.80.57 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha taṃ viṣṇurnāradaṃ munipuṃgavam \|*  
*tataśca garuḍaṃ prāha tvaṃ kimarthamihāgataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After saying thus to Nārada, the leading sage, Viṣṇu said to Garuḍa: ‘Why have you come here?’

## Chapter 81 - Fall of Suparṇa’s Wings

## \|\| 1.81.1-5 \|\|

*\| śrīgaruḍa uvāca \|*  
*mamāsti dayitaṃ mitraṃ brāhmaṇo bhṛguvaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*tasyāsti mādhavīnāma kanyā kamalalocanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*na tasyāḥ sadṛśaḥ kāṃtaḥ prāptastena mahātmanā \|*  
*yatastato'hamādiṣṭaḥ kāṃtamasyāstvamānaya \|*  
*anurūpaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha yadyahaṃ saṃmatastava \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tato mayā'khilā bhūmistadvarārthaṃ vilokitā \|*  
*na tadarthaṃ varo labdhaḥ sarvaiḥ samucito guṇaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tatastvaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa mama citte vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*anurūpaḥ patistasyāḥ sarvaireva guṇairyutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasmātpāṇigrahaṃ tasyāḥ svīkuruṣva sureśvara \|*  
*atyantarūpayuktāyā mama vākyapraṇoditaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śrī Garuḍa said:

1-5. I have a very close friend, a Brāhmaṇa hailing from the family of Bhṛgu. The name of his lotus-eyed daughter is Mādhavī. A husband befitting her could not be found by that noble-souled one. Therefore, he said to me: “O excellent bird, bring a husband suitable to her, if you consider me worthy of honour.” Then the entire earth was searched by me for a bridegroom befitting her. But no bridegroom endowed with all good qualities could be obtained. Then, O Lotus-eyed One, you were recollected by me in my mind as a befitting husband for her. You are endowed with all good qualities. Hence, O Lord of Suras, accept her. Hold her hand in marriage. She is very beautiful. I pray to you with this appeal of mine.

## \|\| 1.81.6 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*atrānaya dvijaśreṣṭha tāṃ kanyāṃ kamalekṣaṇām \|*  
*yena dṛṣṭvā svayaṃ paścātprakaromi yathoditam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

6\. O excellent bird, bring that lotus-eyed girl here. On seeing her myself, I shall do as spoken by you.

## \|\| 1.81.7 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*tava tejobhayādeva sā kanyā janakānvitā \|*  
*mayā dūre vinirmuktā tatkathaṃ tāmihānaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

Garuṣa said:

7\. It is on account of our fear from your refulgence that the girl and the father had been kept far away by me. How can I bring her here?
