## \|\| 1.81.8 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*atra tāṃ mama tattejo janakena samanvitām \|*  
*na hi dhakṣyati tasmāttvaṃ śīghraṃ dvijavarā'naya \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sri Lord said:

8\. My refulgence will not scorch her and her father here. Hence, O excellent bird, bring her quickly.

## \|\| 1.81.9 \|\|

*evamuktastatastena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tāṃ kanyā mānayāmāsa taṃ ca viprabhṛgūdvaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On being told thus by that powerful Viṣṇu he brought her and also the Brāhmaṇa, a descendant of the family of Bhṛgu.

## \|\| 1.81.10 \|\|

*athāsau praṇipatyoccairbrāhmaṇo madhusūdanam \|*  
*lakṣmīvannyaviśatpārśve garuḍasya samīpataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Brāhmaṇa bowed down to Madhusūdana and came to the side of Viṣṇu, near Garuḍa, like Lakṣmī herself.

## \|\| 1.81.11 \|\|

*sāpi kanyā varārohā bālyabhāvādaninditā \|*  
*śayyaikāṃte samāviṣṭā dakṣiṇe muravidviṣaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Due to child-like innocence the blameless beautiful girl sat at the end of the bed to the right of the Enemy of Mura.

## \|\| 1.81.12 \|\|

*atha kopaparītāṃgī mahiṣyādharmamāśritā \|*  
*lakṣmīḥ śaśāpa tāṃ kanyāṃ sapatnīti vicintya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereat, Lakṣmī who had the status of the chief queen became extremely furious thinking her to be her co-wife and cursed the girl:

## \|\| 1.81.13 \|\|

*yasmānme purataḥ pāpe kāṃtasya mama harṣitā \|*  
*śayyāyāṃ tvaṃ samāviṣṭā lajjāṃ tyaktvā sudūrataḥ \|*  
*tasmādaśvamukhī nūnaṃ vikṛtā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “Since, verily in my very presence, O sinful girl, you set aside all bashfulness and joyously took your seat on the bed of my husband, you will become a hideous Aśvamukhī (Horse-faced).”

## \|\| 1.81.14 \|\|

*evaṃ śāpe śriyā datte hāhākāro mahānabhūt \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ tatra saṃsthānāṃ kopaścāpi dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the curse was thus uttered by Śrī, there was a great hue and cry among all those present there. The Brāhmaṇa became angry.

## \|\| 1.81.15 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*sahasraṃ yācyate kanyā karotyekaḥ karagraham \|*  
*vāṅmātreṇa na tasyāḥ syātpatnībhāvaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 15 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

15\. A thousand persons have been requested on behalf of the girl. Not even a single one among them has accepted her even verbally, let alone grasping her hand. How can she have the status of a wife?

## \|\| 1.81.16 \|\|

*yāvannāgnidvijātīnāṃ pratyakṣaṃ gurusaṃnidhau \|*  
*sasaṃkalpaṃ svayaṃ dattā gṛhyoktavidhinā janaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As long as she has not been handed over with a prior resolve, in accordance with the injunctions of the Gṛhyasūtras and in the presence of the holy fire, Brāhmaṇas and elders (she has no status of a wife).

## \|\| 1.81.17 \|\|

*tasmāttaddoṣanirmuktā sapatnyeṣā samā tvayā \|*  
*kṛtā vājimukhī pāpe tvaṃ gajāsyā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence she is blemishless. But you regarding her on a par with your co-wife, have made her horse-faced. O sinful one, you will also be elephant-faced.

## \|\| 1.81.18 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa vipreṃdrastataḥ provāca keśavam \|*  
*ātithyaṃ vihitaṃ hyetattava patnyā yathocitam \|*  
*tasmāttatra prayāsyāmi yatra syāttādṛśī sutā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After saying thus the leading Brāhmaṇa spoke to Keśava: “A befitting hospitality has been extended to me by your wife! Hence I shall go to that place where such a daughter shall be born.”

## \|\| 1.81.19 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*na santāpastvayā kāryaḥ kṛtyesmindvijasattama \|*  
*mamāṃtike prayātānāṃ nāśubhaṃ jāyate kvacit \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

19\. In this matter, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, do not be so enraged. Never can inauspiciousness befall those who come to my vicinity.

## \|\| 1.81.20 \|\|

*tasmānnāśvamukhī hyeṣā janmanyasminbhaviṣyati \|*  
*gṛhītvemāṃ gṛhaṃ gaccha prayaccha svepsitāya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Hence she will not become horse-faced in this birth. Take her and go home. Give her to a desirable person.

## \|\| 1.81.21 \|\|

*śayane vāmadigbhāgaḥ kalatrāṇāmudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇe bandhulokānāṃ tatkālocitaśāyinām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It is the left side in the bed that has been assigned to wives and the right side to kinsmen who may lie for the nonce.

## \|\| 1.81.22 \|\|

*seyaṃ tava sutā vipra baṃdhusthānaṃ samāśritā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati tato jāmiḥ kaniṣṭhā me'nyajanmani \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Here, your daughter, O Brāhmaṇa, has occupied the spot reserved for kinsmen. So she will be born as my younger sister in the next birth.

## \|\| 1.81.23-24 \|\|

*avatīrṇasya bhūpṛṣṭhe devakāryeṇa kenacit \|*  
*vājivaktradharā proktā yadyeṣā mama kāṃtayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tato'haṃ sumahatkṛtvā tapaścaivānayā saha \|*  
*kariṣyāmi śubhāsyāṃ ca tathā lakṣmīmapi dvija \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. I will incarnate then on the earth on account of some task of Devas. Since she has been cursed to become a horsefaced one by my wife, I will perform great penance along with her and transform her into one of splendid face, O Brāhmaṇa, I will make Lakṣmī too so.

## \|\| 1.81.25 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavānvipraṃ taṃ santoṣya tadā girā \|*  
*garuḍena samaṃ cakre kathāścitrā manoramāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After consoling that Brāhmaṇa with his words, the Lord continued the narration of charming stories of diverse kinds in the company of Garuḍa.

## \|\| 1.81.26 \|\|

*atha tasminkathāṃte sa garuḍaḥ puruṣottamam \|*  
*provāca tāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛddhāṃ tejaḥsamanvitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the close of the narration, Garuḍa looked at the aged lady endowed with refulgence and spoke to Puruṣottama:

## \|\| 1.81.27 \|\|

*apūrveyaṃ suraśreṣṭha strī vṛddhā tava pārśvagā \|*  
*kimarthaṃ keyamākhyāhi kutaḥ prāptā janārdana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “O Janārdana, O most excellent one among Suras, this elderly lady sitting near you seems to be someone not seen before. Do tell me who she is. Where has she come from? Why has she come?”

## \|\| 1.81.28-29 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*eṣā khyātā khagaśreṣṭha loke'sminvṛddhakanyakā \|*  
*śāṃḍilīnāma sarvajñā brahmacaryaparāyaṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tapovīryasamopetā sarvadevābhivaṃditā \|*  
*nāsti vai cedṛśī nārī khagendrātra jagattraye \|\| 29 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

28-29. O most excellent one among birds, this is the elderly maiden well-known in this world by the name Śāṇḍilī. She is omniscient and strictly adhering to celibacy. She is endowed with the power of penance. She is venerated by all the Devas. O leading bird, there is no woman like her in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.81.30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vihasya vihagādhipaḥ \|*  
*provāca vāsudevaṃ ca tāṃ vilokya ciraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sūta said:

30\. On hearing his words, O Brāhmaṇas, the Lord of the birds looked at her for a long time, then laughed and ultimately spoke to Vāsudeva:

## \|\| 1.81.31-32 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*naitaccitraṃ tapo yacca kriyate sumahattaram \|*  
*yathā ca dīyate dānaṃ yacca tatrāsti cādbhutam \|*  
*tathā ca kriyate yuddhaṃ saṃgrāme yuddhaśālibhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nāścaryaṃ citrametacca brahmacaryaṃ tadadbhutam \|*  
*viśeṣādyauvanāvasthāṃ saṃprāpya puruṣottama \|\| 32 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

31-32. It is not unusual that a very great penance is performed. Similarly if gifts are made it is not a wonder. Further if a battle is fought by able warriors, what is surprising in that? But, O Puruṣottama, this is unusual that one maintains celibacy especially during the prime of youth.

## \|\| 1.81.33-35 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa ca nārībhiratra na śraddadhāmyaham \|*  
*avaśyaṃ yauvanasthena tiryagyonigatena ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vikāraḥ khalu kartavyo nādhi kārāya yauvanam \|*  
*yadi na prāpnuvaṃtyetāḥ puruṣaṃ yoṣitaḥ kvacit \|\| 34 \|\|*

*anyonyaṃ maithunaṃ cakruḥ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhinaṃ vyādhitaṃ vāpi sthaviraṃ vyaṃgameva ca \|*  
*apyetāḥ puruṣābhāve manyaṃte paṃcasāyakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. More so in the case of women. I do not have any faith in this respect. Emotional outlet is essential in the case of lower animals. Youth is not for supression of rights. If women do not get access to men anywhere, they will indulge in mutual sexual alliance when afflicted by the arrows of Kāma. In the absence of suitable men, they will consider a leper, a sick one, and an old man and one short of a limb or two on a par with the Five-arrowed One (Kāma).

## \|\| 1.81.36 \|\|

*nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ \|*  
*nāṃtakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Fire is never satiated completely with fuel, nor the great sea with the rivers flowing into it. The god of Death cannot be surfeited with all living beings nor a woman with men.

## \|\| 1.81.37 \|\|

*na paratra bhayādetā maryādāṃ vidadhuḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*muktvā bhūpabhayaṃ caikamathavā gurujaṃ bhayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If women keep a limit, it is not due to the fear of the other world. Except the fear of the king or that of the elders (there is nothing to restrain them).

## \|\| 1.81.38 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā śāṃḍilī brahmacāriṇī \|*  
*maunavratadharā'pyevaṃ hṛdi kopaṃ dadhāra sā \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sūta said:

38\. On hearing these words of his, Śāṇḍilī, the celibate woman, had in her heart the surging emotion of anger, although she was under the vow of silence.

## \|\| 1.81.39 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasya pakṣināthasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*ubhau pakṣau gatau nāśaṃ ruṇḍākāro'tra so'bhavat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In the meantime both the wings of the Lord of the birds got destroyed and he became mutilated in shape.

## \|\| 1.81.40 \|\|

*māṃsapiṃḍamayo raudraḥ sarvarogavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*aśaktaśca tathā gantuṃ padamātramapi kvacit \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Though he was really ferocious and devoid of all ailments, he could not go ahead even a step. He was no better than a mass of flesh.

## Chapter 82 - Greatness of Suparṇeśvara (Suparṇa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.82.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā puṃḍarīkākṣo garuḍasya viceṣṭitam \|*  
*vismitaściṃtayāmāsa kimidaṃ sāṃprataṃ sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*api vajraprahāreṇa yasya romāpi na cyutam \|*  
*tau pakṣau sahasā cāsya kathaṃ nipatitau bhuvi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nūnametena yā strīṇāṃ kṛtā niṃdā mahātmanā \|*  
*dūṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yacchāṃḍilīṃ samavekṣya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*anayā pātitau pakṣau tapaḥśaktiprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*nānyasya vidyate śaktirīdṛśī bhuvanatraye \|\| 4 \|\|*

Note: The story of Garuḍa’s loss and restoration of wings is adopted from Mahābhārata, Udyoga 119 to glorify Suparṇeśvara at this sacred place.

Sūta said:

1-4. On seeing the condition of Garuḍa, the Lotus-eyed One was wonder-struck. He thought: ‘What could be this present situation? Even when struck with Vajra not even a single hair from his body fell down! How then did his wings fall on to the ground all of a sudden?

Indeed, the fact that this noble-souled one censured women in general and derided their celibacy after casting a meaningful glance at Sāṇḍilī has made her strike down the wings by the power of her penance. In the whole of the three worlds, no one else has such a power.’

## \|\| 1.82.5 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa śāṃḍilīṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*tadarthaṃ vinayopetaḥ smitaṃ kṛtvā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Garuḍa-emblemed One (Viṣṇu) humbly propitiated Sāṇḍilī on behalf of Garuḍa, after smiling a little.

## \|\| 1.82.6 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*sāmānyavacanaṃ proktaṃ sarvastrīṇāmanena hi \|*  
*tatkimarthaṃ mahābhāge tvayā caivedṛśaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

6\. O highly esteemed one, only a general statement was made by him about all the women. So, why was he made thus by you?

## \|\| 1.82.7 \|\|

*śāṃḍilyuvāca \|*  
*mama vaktraṃ samālokya smitaṃ cakre janārdana \|*  
*strīniṃdā vihitānena svamatyāpi jagadguro \|\| 7 \|\|*

Śaṇḍilī said:

7\. O Janārdana, he looked at my face and smiled. O preceptor of the universe, a censure of woman-folk was also made by him wantonly.

## \|\| 1.82.8 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādasya nigraho'yaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*manasā na ca vākyena na ca keśava karmaṇā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is for this reason that he has been thus chastised by me. O Keśava, it is not mental, verbal or physical attack.

## \|\| 1.82.9 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tathāpi kuru cāsya tvaṃ prasādaṃ gatakalmaṣe \|*  
*mama vākyānurodhena yadimāṃ manyase śubhe \|\| 9 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

9\. Still, O sinless one, O auspicious lady, if you honour me, do a favour unto this fellow at my instance.

## \|\| 1.82.10 \|\|

*śāṃḍilyuvāca \|*  
*manasāpi mayā dhyātaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadivā'śubham \|*  
*nānyathā jāyate deva viśeṣātkopayuktayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śāṇḍilī said:

10\. O Lord, whatever is conceived by me in my mind, good or otherwise cannot become otherwise, especially if my anger is aroused.

## \|\| 1.82.11 \|\|

*tasmādeṣa mamādeśādārādha yatu śaṃkaram \|*  
*pakṣalābhāya nānyasya śaktirdātuṃ vyavasthitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hence at my behest, let him propitiate Śaṅkara for the restoration of the wings. No one else has enough competence vested in him to grant him (the wings).

## \|\| 1.82.12 \|\|

*athavā puṃḍarīkākṣa rūpamīdṛgvyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*eṣa saṃsthāsyate loke satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Otherwise, O Lotus-eyed One, he will have to go permanently like this in the world. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 1.82.13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā taṃ provāca janārdanaḥ \|*  
*garuḍaṃ dainyasaṃyuktaṃ bhāsapiṃḍopamaṃ sthitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sūta said:

13\. On hearing her words Janārdana said to Garuḍa who continued to be in that wretched plight akin to a mass of flesh.

## \|\| 1.82.14 \|\|

*eṣa eva varaścāsyā dvipadeśyā dvijottama \|*  
*pakṣalābhāya yatproktaṃ tava śaṃbhuprasādanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O excellent bird, this alone is the boon granted by this lady, the greatest one among bipeds i.e. human beings. She has told you to propitiate Śaṃbhu for the acquisition of the wings.

## \|\| 1.82.15 \|\|

*tasmādārādhaya kṣipraṃ tvaṃ devaṃ śaśiśekharam \|*  
*avyagraṃ cittamāsthāya divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hence with a concentrated mind, quickly apply yourself day and night energetically to the propitiation of the Moon-crested Lord who is immutable.

## \|\| 1.82.16 \|\|

*yena te tatprabhāvena bhūyaḥ syāttādṛśaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*tasya devasya māhātmyādacirādapi kāśyapa \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereby, O Kaśyapa’s son, by the greatness of that Lord and his power, your body shall ere long be as it was before.”

## \|\| 1.82.17 \|\|

*tacchrutvā garuḍastūrṇaṃ dhṛtapāśupatavrataḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya devamīśānaṃ tatastaṃ toṣamānayat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing it, Garuḍa immediately adopted Pāśupata Vrata after installing Lord Īśāna and then propitiated him. He thereby caused delight to him.

## \|\| 1.82.18 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tathā sāṃtapanāni ca \|*  
*prājāpatyāni cakre'tha pārākāṇi tadagrataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He performed the rites of Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, Sāntapana, Prājāpatya and Pārāka thereafter.

## \|\| 1.82.19 \|\|

*snātvā triṣavaṇaṃ paścādbhasmasnāna parāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*japanrudraśiro rudrānnīlarudrāṃstathāparān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He took holy baths thrice a day. Thereafter he smeared ash all over his body by way of Bhasma Snāna and performed the Japa of Rudraśiras, Rudra verses and other Nīlarudra passages.

## \|\| 1.82.20 \|\|

*cakre pūjāṃ svayaṃ tasya snāpayitvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*balipūjopahārāṃśca vidhānena prayacchati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He himself performed the worship after bathing him duly. Then he offered oblations, and gifts of offerings, and adoration in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.82.21 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya vratasthasya japapūjāparasya ca \|*  
*tato varṣasahasrāṃte gatastuṣṭiṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*abravīdvarado'smīti vṛṇuṣveṣṭaṃ dvijottama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus he continued performing the Vrata rites, Japa and Pūjā. Then at the end of a thousand years Maheśvara became pleased. He said, “O most excellent bird, I shall grant boons. Choose whatever is desired.”

## \|\| 1.82.22-23 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*paśyāvasthāṃ mameśāna śāṃḍilyā yā vinirmitā \|*  
*pakṣapātaḥ kṛto'smākaṃ tamahaṃ prārthayāmi vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tvayātraiva sadā liṃge stheyaṃ hara mamādhunā \|*  
*mama vākyādasaṃdigdhaṃ yadi ceṣṭaṃ prayacchasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

22-23. See my plight, O Īśāna, brought about by Śāṇḍilī. My wings have been caused to fall down. This is what I request you further, O Hara, that you should stay here always in the Liṅga at my instance, unhesitatingly, if you are to grant me what is desired by me.

## \|\| 1.82.24-25 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti me cātra liṃge vāso bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tvaṃ ca tadrūpasaṃpanno viśeṣādbalavegabhāk \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi na saṃdeho matprasādādvihaṃgama \|*  
*evamuktvātha taṃ devaḥ svayaṃ pasparśa pāṇinā \|\| 25 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

24-25. From today onwards my stay shall be here in this Liṅga. You will also be endowed with that original form, particularly possessing special strength and speed. This shall undoubtedly take place with my favour, O bird.

After saying this to him, the Lord himself touched him with his hand.

## \|\| 1.82.26 \|\|

*tato'sya pakṣau saṃjātau tatkṣaṇādeva sundarau \|*  
*tathā romāṇi divyāni jātarūpopamāni ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the very instant beautiful wings grew. So also divine hairs comparable to gold appeared thereon.

## \|\| 1.82.27 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ devaṃ prahaṣṭaḥ sa vihaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*gataḥ svabhavanaṃ paścādanujñāpya maheśvaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the delighted bird bowed down to the Lord. Afterwards he took leave of Maheśvara and went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.82.28 \|\|

*devopi vacanāttasya tasmiṃlliṃge sadā haraḥ \|*  
*nivāsamakarotsamyakprāpte saṃdhyātraye sadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At his request, Lord Hara always resided in that Liṅga during the three Sandhyās (dusks and midday).

## \|\| 1.82.29 \|\|

*tasya cāyatane puṇye yogātprāṇānparityajet \|*  
*prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtvā na sa bhūyo'pi jāyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A devotee shall adopt Prāyopaveśana (fast unto death) rite in that meritorious shrine and cast off the life through Yoga. He is never reborn.

## \|\| 1.82.30 \|\|

*api pāpa samācāraḥ kaulo vā nirghṛṇo'pi vā \|*  
*brahmaghno vā surāpo vā cauro vā bhrūṇahā'pi vā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He may be a man of regular sinful conduct, a Kaula, a ruthless fellow (perpetrator of great sins), a Brāhmaṇa-slayer, liquor-drinker, thief or one guilty of foeticide (he is redeemed).

## \|\| 1.82.31 \|\|

*trikālaṃ pūjayanyastu śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| \|*  
*saṃvatsaraṃ vasetso'pi śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One who worships thrice a day with the mind sanctified by faith and stays here for a year is honoured in Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.82.32-33 \|\|

*athavā somavāreṇa yastaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā kṣaṇaṃ subhaktyā yo yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*so'pi yāti na saṃdehaḥ puruṣaḥ śivamandire \|*  
*vimānavaramārūḍhaḥ sevyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Or a man who seizes an opportunity and visits the year, O Brāhmaṇas, shall undoubtedly go to Śiva’s palace riding on an excellent aerial chariot and waited upon by groups of celestial damsels.

## \|\| 1.82.34 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kalikāle viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*draṣṭavyo vai suparṇākhyo devaḥ śraddhāsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence particularly in Kali age, the Lord named Suparṇa (Suparṇākhya) should be visited by persons endowed with faith with all efforts.

## \|\| 1.82.35 \|\|

*saṃtyājyāśca tathā prāṇāstadagreprāyasaṃśritaiḥ \|*  
*vāṃchadbhiḥ śivasāṃnidhyaṃ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In front of that deity, people should adopt the Prāyopaveśa vow and cast off their life, if they desire Śiva’s proximity. This is the truth uttered by me.

## Chapter 83 - Greatness of the Deity Suparṇa

## \|\| 1.83.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatrāścaryamabhūtpūrvaṃ yattadbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi purāṇe yadudāhṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*veṇurnāma mahīpālaḥ purāsītsūryavaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*sadaiva pāpasaṃyukto durmedhāḥ kāmapīḍitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śāsanāni pradattāni brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*anyaiḥ pārthivaśārdūlaistena tāni hṛtānyalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall narrate to you a miracle that occurred there formerly. It has been cited in the Purāṇa.

Formerly there was a king of the Solar dynasty named Veṇu. He was a person of vicious mind, always afflicted by lust and engaged in committing sins.

Royal charters and grants awarded to noble-souled Brāhmaṇas by other leading kings formerly were forfeited by him.

## \|\| 1.83.4 \|\|

*vidhvaṃsitāḥ striyo naikā vidhavāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kumāryo rūpavatyaśca tathā nija kulodbhavāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Many women and widows in particular were ruined by him. So also beautiful virgins as well as those belonging to his own family.

## \|\| 1.83.5 \|\|

*devatārādhanaṃ pūjāṃ kartuṃ naiva dadāti saḥ \|*  
*na ca yajñaṃ na homaṃ ca svādhyāyaṃ na ca pāpakṛt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. That sinful king never allowed anyone to propitiate deities or adore them. Neither Yajña, nor Homa, nor Vedic Studies (Svādhyāya) were permitted by him.

## \|\| 1.83.6-7 \|\|

*provācātha janānsarvānmāṃ pūjayata sarvadā \|*  
*na māmabhyadhiko'nyo'sti devo vā brāhmaṇo'pi vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mayā tuṣṭena sarveṣāṃ saṃpatsyati hṛdi sthitam \|*  
*iha lokeṣvasaṃdigdhaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He used to tell all the people: “Worship me always. There is no one superior to me, whether a Deva or a Brāhmaṇa. If I am pleased, everything that all of you cherish in your hearts whether good or bad, shall become realized in this world undoubtedly.”

## \|\| 1.83.8 \|\|

*tena śastravihīnānāṃ viśvastānāṃ vadhaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*saṃtyaktāḥ śaraṇaṃ prāptāḥ puruṣā bhayavihvalāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Unarmed persons with implicit faith in him, were killed by him. Those who sought refuge in him were forsaken. All persons became overcome with fright

## \|\| 1.83.9 \|\|

*naṣṭo mahāhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatrusaṃghānupasthitān \|*  
*kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ parityajya prāṇarakṣārthameva hi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing the groups of enemies assembled for a great

fight, he forsook the duty of a Kṣatriya and he used to flee to save his own life.

## \|\| 1.83.10 \|\|

*acaurāḥ pragṛhītāśca caurāḥ saṃrakṣitāḥ sadā \|*  
*sādhavaḥ kleśitā nityaṃ teṣāṃ saṃharatā dhanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Persons other than thieves were held captive by him and thieves were given protection. Good people were always subjected to torture and their wealth and property were confiscated.

## \|\| 1.83.11 \|\|

*na kṛtaṃ ca vrataṃ tena śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*na dattaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaśca na ca yaṣṭaṃ kadācana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He did not observe any Vrata with a mind sanctified by faith. He did not offer anything to Brāhmaṇas nor did he perform any Yajña at any time.

## \|\| 1.83.12 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya narendrasya pāpāsaktasya nityaśaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhirabhūdugro vaṃśocchedaśca saddvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, while the king continued to be engaged in sinful activities, a severe fell disease of leprosy attacked him resulting in the ruin of the family itself.

## \|\| 1.83.13 \|\|

*tatastaṃ vyādhinā grastaṃ putrapautravivarjitam \|*  
*dāyādāḥ sahasopetā rājyaṃ jahrustataḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. As he was assailed by the disease and as he had no son or grandson, the cousins suddenly attacked him and seized his kingdom.

## \|\| 1.83.14 \|\|

*taṃ ca nirvāsayāmāsustasmāddeśātpadātikam \|*  
*ekākinaṃ parityaktaṃ sarvairapi suhṛdgaṇaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He became isolated and abandoned by all the groups of friends. Then they banished him from the kingdom. He was forced to go out on foot.

## \|\| 1.83.15 \|\|

*so'pi sarvaiḥ parityaktastena pāpena karmaṇā \|*  
*kalatrairapi cātmīyaiḥ smṛtvā pūrvaviceṣṭitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He was abandoned thus by all due to his sinful activity, even by his wives and close relatives, remembering his past (mis) deeds.

## \|\| 1.83.16 \|\|

*ekākī bhramamāṇo'tha so'pi kaṣṭavaśaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*kṣuttṛṣṇāsupariśrāṃtaḥ kṣetre'traiva samāgataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Caught in this grievous plight he wandered alone and ultimately weary with hunger and thirst, he reached this place in the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.83.17 \|\|

*tataḥ prāsādamāsādya suparṇākhyasamudbhavam \|*  
*yāvatprāptaḥ parityaktastāva tprāṇairupoṣitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He came near the palace (shrine) of the deity (called Suparṇa) and in that state of starvation itself he ceased to live.

## \|\| 1.83.18 \|\|

*tato divyavapurbhūtvāvimānavaramāśritaḥ \|*  
*jagāmaśivalokaṃ sa durlabhaṃ dhārmikairapi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereupon he assumed a divine body. Seated in an excellent aerial chariot, he went to the world of Śiva that is rarely attained even by righteous persons.

## \|\| 1.83.19 \|\|

*sevyamānopsarobhiśca stūyamānaśca kinnaraiḥ \|*  
*gīyamānaśca gandharvaiḥ śivapārśve vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Attended upon by celestial damsels, eulogized by Kinnaras and sung about by Gandharvas, he got stay near Śiva.

## \|\| 1.83.20 \|\|

*atha taṃ saṃnidhau dṛṣṭvā gaurī papraccha sādaram \|*  
*ko'yaṃ deva samāyātaḥ sukṛtī tava mandire \|*  
*anena kiṃ kṛtaṃ karma yatprāpto'tra vibhūtidhṛk \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing him very near, Gaurī asked respectfully: “Who is this meritorious person, O Lord, who has come to your palace? What excellent deed has he performed that he has come here in all glory with holy ash smeared over?”

## \|\| 1.83.21 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*eṣa pāpasamācāraḥ sadā'sītpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*veṇusaṃjño dharāpṛṣṭhe kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

21\. This is a king named Veṇu who had been committing sins on the earth. He was afflicted by the fell disease of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.83.22 \|\|

*sa saṃtyakto nijairdāraiḥ śatruvargeṇa dharṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhramamāṇaḥ samāyātaḥ suparṇākhyasya mandire \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Abandoned by his wives and all close relatives, he was attacked by groups of his enemies. Wandering everywhere he ultimately came to the palace of the deity Suparṇākhya (Suparṇa by name).

## \|\| 1.83.23 \|\|

*upavāsapariśrāṃtaḥ sāṃnidhyaṃ mama yatra ca \|*  
*sarvaprāṇaiḥ parityaktastasminnāyatane śubhe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Exhausted by starvation, he reached the shrine sanctified by my presence. Ultimately he breathed his last in that auspicious shrine.

## \|\| 1.83.24-26 \|\|

*tatprabhāvādiha prāptaḥ satyametanma yoditam \|*  
*anyo'pyanaśanaṃ kṛtvā prāṇānyastatra saṃtyajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sa sarvābhyadhikāṃ bhūtiṃ prāpnuyādvaravarṇini \|*  
*yānetānvīkṣase devi gaṇānme pārśvasaṃsthitān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*etaistatra kṛtaṃ sarvairdevi prāyopaveśanam \|*  
*api kīṭapataṃgā ye paśavaḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ \|*  
*prāsāde tatra nirmuktāḥ prāṇairyāṃti mamāṃtikam \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. He reached this place on account of that. What I say is the truth. O lady of excellent complexion, anyone else who observes fast and gives up his life there shall attain a glory and prosperity superior to everything else.

You see here, O goddess, all these Gaṇas of mine standing at my sides. All these had performed Prāyopaveśana there. Even worms and moths, animals, birds and beasts, liberated from their vital airs, come near me.

## \|\| 1.83.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā pārvatī vākyaṃ proktaṃ devena śambhunā \|*  
*vismayāviṣṭahṛdayā sādhu sādhviti sā'bravīt \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. On hearing the statement made by Lord Śaṃbhu, Pārvatī was overwhelmed by wonder in her heart. She said, “Excellent! Excellent!”

## \|\| 1.83.28-30 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti loke'tra puruṣā muktimicchavaḥ \|*  
*dūrato'pi samabhyetya svānprāṇāṃstatra tatyajuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtvā śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*gacchanti ca parāṃ siddhimapi pāpaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*suparṇākhyasya māhātmyaṃ yanmayā svapituḥ śrutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Ever since then all the persons on the earth desirous of salvation came there from far-off countries and gave up their life there by means of Prāyopaveśa.

Endowed with great faith, they attain the greatest Siddhi, although they might have been sinners.

Thus everything regarding the greatness of Suparṇākhya has been narrated to you. It was heard by me from my father. It is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 84 - Mādhavī Born as Subhadrā

## \|\| 1.84.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ devadevena viṣṇunā \|*  
*mādhavīṃ bhaginīṃ prāpya janmāṃtaramupasthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aśvavaktrāṃ kariṣyāmi tapasā suśubhānanām \|*  
*sā kathaṃ vihitā tena tapastaptaṃ tathā katham \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūta, you said that Viṣṇu, the Lord of Devas, had told that when Mādhavī became his sister in her next birth as a horse-faced one he would perform penance and turn her into one of splendid countenance. How was she rendered thus? How was the penance performed? Describe everything in detail. Our curiosity is indeed great.

## \|\| 1.84.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nāradasya samākarṇya taṃ sandeśaṃ surodbhavam \|*  
*gatvā viṣṇuḥ suraiḥ sārddhaṃ pracakre maṃtraniścayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. On hearing the message of Suras from Nārada, Viṣṇu went to heaven and held consultation along with Suras.

## \|\| 1.84.4 \|\|

*bhārāvataraṇārthāya dānavānāṃ vadhāya ca \|*  
*vasudevagṛhe śrīmāndvāparāṃte tato hariḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was for the purpose of reducing the burden of the earth and killing Dānavas that the glorious Lord Hari took birth in the house of Vasudeva towards the end of Dvāpara.

## \|\| 1.84.5 \|\|

*devakyā jaṭhare devaḥ saṃjāto daityadarpahā \|*  
*tathānyā rohiṇīnāma bhāryā tasya ca yā'bhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Lord, the destroyer of the arrogance of Daityas, was born of the womb of Devakī. He (Vasudeva) had another wife named Rohiṇī.

## \|\| 1.84.6 \|\|

*tasyāṃ jajñe halīnāma balabhadraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*tṛtīyā suprabhānāma vasudevapriyā ca yā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Of her was born the valorous son named Balabhadra otherwise known as Plough-wielder (Halin). A third wife, the beloved of Vasudeva was known as Suprabhā.

## \|\| 1.84.7 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sā mādhavī jajñe aśvavaktrasvarūpadhṛk \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtākārāṃ sutāṃ jātāṃ ca suprabhā \|*  
*vāsudevasamāyuktā viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Mādhavī was born of her assuming the form of a horse-faced one. One seeing the daughter born with such a hideous form, Suprabhā and Vasudeva became grief-stricken.

## \|\| 1.84.8-9 \|\|

*atha te yādavāḥ sarve kṛtaśāntikapauṣṭikāḥ \|*  
*svastisvastīti saṃtrastāḥ procurbhūyātkule'tra naḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*evaṃ sā yauvanopetā tathā duḥkhasamanvitā \|*  
*na kaścidvarayāmāsa vājivaktrāṃ vilokya tām \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then all the Yādavas performed the Śāntika (pacificatory) and Pauṣṭika (nourishing) rites. In their excessive terror, they said, “Svasti, Svasti, may it be veil!”. “In our family growing up as a young woman, she is sure to be unhappy. On seeing a girl with horse-face, no one will marry her.”

## \|\| 1.84.10-11 \|\|

*tataśca bhagavānviṣṇurjñātvā tāṃ bhaginīṃ tathā \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva tathā duḥkhasamanvitau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tāmādāya gatastūrṇaṃ baladevasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tapastaptuṃ tataḥ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Lord Viṣṇu, on coming to know that his sister was like that and the parents were highly distressed, took her with him. Accompanied by Baladeva he quickly went to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara for performing a great penance.

## \|\| 1.84.12 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ toṣayāmāsa samyagyajñaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*vrataiśca vividhairdānairbrāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Properly engaged in Yajña, he propitiated Brahmā through different: kinds of Vrata and Dāna and propitiations of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.84.13 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭiṃ gato brahmā varṣāṃte tasya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|*  
*uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasvābhivāṃchitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the end of a year, Brahmā was pleased with the Śārṅga-armed One. He said “I shall grant boons. Request for the desired thing.”

## \|\| 1.84.14 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*eṣā me bhaginī deva jātā'śvavadanā kila \|*  
*tava prasādātsadvaktrā bhūyādetanmamepsitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

14\. O Lord, this sister of mine is born as a horse-faced one. Let her be one of excellent countenance. This is my desire.

## \|\| 1.84.15 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*eṣā śubhānanā sādhvī matprasādādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*subhadrā nāma vikhyātā vīrasūḥ pativallabhā \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

15\. With my favour this good lady shall be one with excellent countenance. She will become well-known by the name Subhadrā. A beloved of her husband, she will give birth to a heroic son.

## \|\| 1.84.16-17 \|\|

*etadrūpāṃ pumānyo'tra pūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*etāṃ viṣṇo tvayā sārdhaṃ tathānena ca sīriṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dvādaśyāṃ māghamāsasya gaṃdhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*so'pyavāpsyati yaccitte vartate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. A man who devoutly worships her in this form here, O Viṣṇu, along with you and also this Sīrin (Balabhadra) on the twelfth lunar day in the month of Māgha with sweet scents, flowers and unguents shall attain undoubtedly what is cherished in his mind.

## \|\| 1.84.18-19 \|\|

*yā nārī patinā tyaktā vaṃdhyā vā bhaktisaṃyutā \|*  
*tṛtīyādivase caitāṃ pūjayiṣyati keśava \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati suputrāḍhyā subhagā sā sukhānvitā \|*  
*aiśvaryasahitā nityaṃ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. A barren woman or one abandoned by her husband, who devoutly worships her, O Keśava, on the third lunar day, shall become fortunate, happy and blessed with good sons. She will be always rich and prosperous and endowed with all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.84.20 \|\|

*evamuktvā caturvaktro virarāma tataḥ param \|*  
*vāsudevo'pi hṛṣṭātmā yayau dvāravatīṃ purīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying thus, the Four-faced One ceased to speak. Delighted in himself, Vāsudeva went to the city of Dvārāvatī.

## \|\| 1.84.21 \|\|

*tāmādāya viśālākṣīṃ caṃdrabiṃbasamānanām \|*  
*baladevasamāyukto hyanujñāpya pitāma ham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He took leave of Pitāmaha. Accompanied by Baladeva, he took the large-eyed lady with the countenance resembling the lunar disc.

## \|\| 1.84.22 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sā mādhavī viprāḥ subhagārūpamāsthitā \|*  
*avatīrṇā dharāpṛṣṭhe lakṣmīśāpaprapīḍitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sūta said:

22\. It was thus that Mādhavī who was afflicted by the curse of Lakṣmī was born on the earth (and later) attained the beautiful form of a Subhagā (a fortunate lady).

## \|\| 1.84.23 \|\|

*upayeme sutaḥ pāṃḍoryāṃ pārthaścāruhāsinīm \|*  
*jajñe tasyāḥ suto vīro'bhimanyuriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Pārtha, the son of Pāṇḍu, married that lady with charming smiles. A heroic son well-known as Abhimanyu was born to her.

## \|\| 1.84.24 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ mādhabījanmasambhavam \|*  
*suparṇākhyasya devasya kathāsaṃgāddvijottamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything connected with the birth of Mādhavī has been narrated to you as incidental to the narrative of Lord Suparṇākhya.

## \|\| 1.84.25 \|\|

*yaścaitatpaṭhate martyo bhaktyā yuktaḥ śṛṇoti vā \|*  
*mucyate sa naraḥ pāpāttaddinaikasamudbhavāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A man who devoutly reads or listens to this becomes rid of sins incurred only on that day.

## Chapter 85 - Greatness of Mahālakṣmī

## \|\| 1.85.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*mādhavyāḥ padmayā datto yaḥ śāpastasya yatphalam \|*  
*pariṇāmodbhavaṃ sarvaṃ śrutamasmābhiradya tat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tena yatkamalā śaptā brāhmaṇena mahātmanā \|*  
*sā kathaṃ gaja vaktrā'tha punarjātā śubhānanā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: This is not the deity Mahālakṣmī of Kolhapur. Here the adj. ‘Mahā-’ is applied to glorify Lakṣmī (see v.12).

The sages said:

1-2. Everything connected with the sequence and result of the curse uttered by Padmā in the case of Mādhavī has been heard by us today.

Kamalā was cursed by that noble-souled Brāhmaṇa. How did she become elephant-faced and then get transformed into one of splendid countenance?

## \|\| 1.85.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śāpena tasya viprasya tatkṣaṇādeva sā dvijāḥ \|*  
*gajavaktrā samutpannā mahāvismayakāriṇī \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. By the curse of that Brāhmaṇa, O Brāhmaṇas, she (Lakṣmī) became instantly an elephant-faced one, causing great wonder.

## \|\| 1.85.4-5 \|\|

*sā proktā hariṇā tiṣṭha kiñcitkālāṃtare śubhe \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa yāvatsyāddvāparakṣayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tato'haṃ medinīpṛṣṭhe hyavatīrya samudraje \|*  
*tapaḥ śaktyā kariṣyāmi bhūyastvāṃ tu śubhānanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. She was told by Hari: “O splendid daughter of the Ocean, stay in this very form for some time till the close of the Dvāpara Yuga. Then I shall incarnate on the earth. By the power of my penance I shall make you splendid-faced once again.”

## \|\| 1.85.6 \|\|

*avajñāyātha sā tasya tadvākyaṃ śārṅgadhanvinaḥ \|*  
*śubhāsyatvakṛte tepe tapastīvraṃ suharṣitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She ignored those words of the wielder of Śārṅga bow. She joyously performed a very severe penance for the sake of a splendid face.

## \|\| 1.85.7 \|\|

*etatkṣetraṃ samāsādya trikālaṃ snānamācarat \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ toṣayāmāsa divārātrimataṃdritā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She came to this holy spot and took the holy bath thrice a day. She was active and alert day and night and propitiated Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.85.8 \|\|

*tāmuvāca tato brahmā varṣāṃte tuṣṭimāgataḥ \|*  
*varaṃ prārthaya tuṣṭo'haṃ tava keśavavallabhe \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Becoming pleased with her at the close of a year Brahmā said to her: “O beloved of Keśava, I am pleased with you. Request for a boon.”

## \|\| 1.85.9-10 \|\|

*lakṣmīruvāca \|*  
*gajāsyāhaṃ kṛtā deva śāpaṃ dattvā sudāruṇam \|*  
*brāhmaṇena sukruddhena kasmiścitkāraṇāṃtare \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmāttadrūpiṇīṃ bhūyo māṃ kuruṣva pitāmaha \|*  
*yadi me tuṣṭimāpanno nānyatkiṃcidvṛṇomyaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

Lakṣmī said:

9-10. For some reason, O Lord, I have been transformed into an elephant-faced woman by an extremely furious Brāhmaṇa by uttering a terrible curse. Hence, O Pitāmaha, if you are pleased, change me back again into the old form. I do not choose anything else.

## \|\| 1.85.11 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*bhaviṣyati śubhaṃ vaktraṃ matprasādādasaṃśayam \|*  
*tava bhadre viśeṣeṇa tasmāttvaṃ svagṛhaṃ vraja \|\| 11 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

11\. O fair lady, with my favour, your face will undoubtedly become splendid all the more. So go home.

## \|\| 1.85.12 \|\|

*mahattvaṃ te mayā dattamadyaprabhṛti śobhane \|*  
*mahālakṣmīti te nāma tasmādatra bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O splendid lady, Mahattva (greatness) has been granted to you by me from today. Hence your name here will be Mahālakṣmī.

## \|\| 1.85.13 \|\|

*gajavaktrāṃ naro yastvāṃ pūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa gajādhipatirbhūpo bhaviṣyati ca bhūtale \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A man who devoutly worships you as elephant-faced, shall become a king on the earth and Lord of elephants.

## \|\| 1.85.14-15 \|\|

*dvitīyādivase yastvāṃ mahālakṣmīriti bruvan \|*  
*śrīsūktena subhaktyā'tha devi saṃpūjayiṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saptajanmāṃtarāṇyeva na bhaviṣyati so'dhanaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā caturvaktro virarāma tataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On the second lunar day, O goddess, one who calls you Mahālakṣmī and devoutly worships you through Śrīsūkta will never become poor during seven successive births.

After saying this the Four-faced God ceased (to speak).

## \|\| 1.85.16 \|\|

*sā'pi hṛṣṭā gatā devī yatra tiṣṭhati keśavaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. That goddess joyously went to the place where Keśava was staying.

## Chapter 86 - Greatness of Saptaviṃśatikā

## \|\| 1.86.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athānyāpi ca tatrāsti saptaviṃśatikā tathā \|*  
*nakṣatraiḥ sthāpitā devī vāṃchitasya pradāyinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dakṣasya tanayā pūrvaṃ saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*udvāhitā hi somena pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ madhye 'bhavaccaikā rohiṇī tasya vallabhā \|*  
*prāṇebhyo'pi sadāsaktastayā sārdhaṃ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: This numerical name is given to Goddess Durgā as she was installed by the twenty-seven daughters of Dakṣa (see vv. 1 and 23).

Sūta said:

1-3. There is another deity named Saptaviṃśatikā. She is the goddess installed by the constellations (stars). She bestows everything desired.

Formerly twenty-seven daughters of Dakṣa were married by Soma (the Moon). Among them Rohiṇī was his sole beloved, more than his very life. He remained attached to her and always stayed near her.

## \|\| 1.86.4 \|\|

*tato daurbhāgyasaṃtaptāḥ sarvā stā dakṣakanyakāḥ \|*  
*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gatvā kṣetre'smiṃstapasi sthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Distressed due to their unfortunate plight all those daughters of Dakṣa became highly disgusted with worldly life. They began to perform penance in this holy place.

## \|\| 1.86.5 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya devatāṃ durgāṃ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*balipūjopahāraistāṃ pūjayaṃtyaḥ sureśvarīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Endowed with great faith, they installed the deity Durgā. They worshipped the goddess of Suras with oblations, adorations and holy presents.

## \|\| 1.86.6-7 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tāsāṃ sā tuṣṭimabhyagāt \|*  
*abravīcca pratuṣṭo'haṃ varaṃ dāsyāmi putrikāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasmāttatprārthyatāṃ citte yadyuṣmākaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*sarvaṃ dāsyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ yadyuṣmākaṃ hṛdi sthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. After a long time she became pleased with them and said: “O my daughters, I am delighted and I shall grant you a boon. So let what is cherished in your minds be requested for. Undoubtedly I shall grant whatever is present in your heart.”

## \|\| 1.86.8-10 \|\|

*tataḥ procuśca tāḥ sarvāḥ prasādāttava vāṃchitam \|*  
*asmākaṃ vidyate devi yāvattrailokyasaṃsthitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ekaṃ patyuḥ sukhaṃ muktvā yatsaubhāgyasamudbhavam \|*  
*tasmāttaddehi cāsmākaṃ yadi tuṣṭāsi caṃḍike \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vayaṃ daurbhāgyadoṣeṇa sarvāḥ kleśaṃ paraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*na śaknumaḥ priyānprāṇāndehe dhartuṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Then all of them said: “O goddess, with your favour we have everything desirable in all the three worlds excepting one thing, namely, the happiness from our husband, that which is the outcome of conjugal felicity. Hence O Caṇḍikā, if you are pleased, give us that (bliss). Due to adverse fate all of us have undergone great hardships. We are unable to retain our vital airs in our body by any means”

## \|\| 1.86.11 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti yuṣmākaṃ saubhāgyaṃ patisaṃbhavam \|*  
*matprasādādasaṃdigdhaṃ bhaviṣyati sukhodayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

11\. By my grace from today onwards you will have conjugal bliss from your husband, enhancing your happiness undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.86.12-14 \|\|

*anyāpi yā patityaktā strī māmatra sthitāṃ sadā \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati sadbhaktayā caturdaśyāmupoṣitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sā bhaviṣyati saubhāgyayu्ktā putravatī satī \|*  
*yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ tāvadekabhaktaparāyaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*akṣāralavaṇāśā yā nārī māṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*na tasyāḥ patijaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurbhāgyaṃ vā bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Another woman, also abandoned by her husband, who staying here always worships me with great devotion and observes fast on the fourteenth lunar day, shall become blessed with conjugal felicity and good sons. She should take only one meal everyday for the period of a year. If the woman worships me abstaining from astringent or saline item in her diet, she will never have any trouble from her husband nor adverse luck.

## \|\| 1.86.15 \|\|

*āśvinasya site pakṣe saṃprāpte navamīdine \|*  
*upavāsaparā yā māṃ niśīthe pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*tasyāḥ saubhāgyamatyugraṃ sarvadā vai bhaviṣyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If the woman observes fast on the ninth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Āśvina and worships me at midnight her conjugal felicity will always be at its best.

## \|\| 1.86.16 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu sā devī virarāma dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tāśca sarvāḥ susaṃhṛṣṭā jagmurdakṣasya maṃdiram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After saying thus that goddess ceased (to speak), O excellent Brāhmaṇas. All of them (the Constellations) of stars became delighted and went to the palace of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.86.17 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare dakṣa āhūtaḥ śūlapāṇinā \|*  
*proktaḥ kasmāttvayā candro yakṣmaṇā saṃniyojitaḥ \|*  
*tadayuktaṃ kṛtaṃ dakṣa jāmātā'yaṃ yatastava \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the meantime Dakṣa was summoned by the Tridentbearing One and was asked: “Why was Moon caused to be afflicted by the disease of tuberculosis? O Dakṣa, an improper act has been committed by you as he is your son-in-law.”

## \|\| 1.86.18 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*anena tanayā mahyamaṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*ūḍhā akhaṇḍacāritrāstāstyaktā doṣavarjitāḥ \|*  
*muktvaikāṃ rohiṇīṃ deva niṣiddhena mayā'sakṛt \|\| 18 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

18\. My daughters, numbering twenty-eight in all have been married by him. All of them are of unbroken fidelity and blemishless. Yet they were abandoned by him, O Lord, except one namely Rohiṇī, though he had been warned by me many times (for his negligence of others).

## \|\| 1.86.19 \|\|

*tato mayā'tikopena niyukto rājayakṣmaṇā \|*  
*asatyajalpako mandaḥ kāmadevavaśaṃ gataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He proved himself as one prattling falsehood, a slow-witted one under the full control of the god of Love. So I have angrily caused him to be afflicted by the disease of tuberculosis.

## \|\| 1.86.20 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti sarvāsāṃ samaṃ sa pracariṣyati \|*  
*madvākyānnātra saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

20\. From today he will behave with all of them impartially at my behest. There is no doubt about it. What I have uttered is the truth.

## \|\| 1.86.21 \|\|

*tvayāpi yadvacaḥ proktamasatyaṃ syānna tatkvacit \|*  
*tasmādeṣa kṣayaṃ pakṣaṃ vṛddhiṃ pakṣaṃ prayāsyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Of course, the words uttered by you can never be untrue. So he will wane for a fortnight and wax for the next.

## \|\| 1.86.22 \|\|

*dakṣo'pi bāḍhamityeva tatproktvā ca yayau gṛham \|*  
*caṃdrastu dakṣakanyāstāḥ samaṃ paśyati sarvadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Dakṣa too said, “So be it” and went home. Candra thereafter began to treat all the daughters of Dakṣa alike for ever.

## \|\| 1.86.23 \|\|

*gacchamānaḥ kṣayaṃ pakṣaṃ vṛddhiṃ pakṣaṃ ca saddvijāḥ \|*  
*sāpi devī tataḥ proktā saptaviṃśatikā kṣitau \|*  
*sarvasaubhāgyadā strīṇāṃ tasminkṣetre vyavasthitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He goes on increasing and decreasing in alternative fortnights, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. That goddess therefore was called Saptaviṃśatikā on the earth. She was established in that holy spot. She bestows all conjugal felicity on women.

## \|\| 1.86.24 \|\|

*yaścaitatpuratastasyāḥ saṃprāpte cāṣṭamīdine \|*  
*śucirbhūtvā paṭhedbhaktyā sa saubhāgyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who remains pure and reads this in front of the deity with devotion on the eighth lunar day shall attain all good fortune.

## Chapter 87 - Greatness of Soma’s Shrine

## \|\| 1.87.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā tatrāsti viprendrāḥ somasyāyatanaṃ śubham \|*  
*yasyāpi darśanādeva mucyate pātakairnaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*somavāre tu saṃprāpte somasya grahaṇe naraḥ \|*  
*yastaṃ paśyati pāpo'pi narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Similarly, O leading Brāhmaṇas, there is the splendid shrine of Soma there. By visiting it alone, a man is liberated from sins.

Even a man of sinful deeds who visits the deity on a Monday or at the time of lunar eclipse will never see Naraka.

## \|\| 1.87.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ dṛśyaṃte'tra samāśrayāḥ \|*  
*atra caṃdrasya caivaikaḥ kathaṃ jātaḥ samāśrayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. In a holy place only the resorts of all the Devas are usually seen. How did it happen that a resort of Candra too has been created here?

## \|\| 1.87.4 \|\|

*etannaḥ sūtaputrāticitraṃ manasi vartate \|*  
*tasmādvada mahābhāga sarvaṃ tvaṃ vetsyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Sūta-Putra, this is a very surprising thing that lurks in our mind. Hence, O highly esteemed one, do explain this. You know everything entirely.

## \|\| 1.87.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*enajjagaddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvaṃ somamayaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tasmātpratiṣṭhite tasmiṃstrailokyaṃ syātpratiṣṭhitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the entire universe is proclaimed as Somamaya (identical with and influenced by Soma). When Soma is well established, all the three worlds too will be (automatically) well established.

## \|\| 1.87.6 \|\|

*etāścauṣadhayaḥ sarvāḥ sasyādyāśceha bhūtale \|*  
*sarvāḥ somamayāstāśca yābhirjīvaṃti jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All these medicinal herbs, all these beginning with Sasya (vegetables and food-grains) on the earth are also Somamaya (permeated by Soma). All creatures are alive due to them.

## \|\| 1.87.7 \|\|

*tasmādbrahmādayo devāḥ somaṃ prāpya kramāddvijāḥ \|*  
*tṛptiṃ yāṃti parāṃ hṛṣṭā yatastasmādvaro'tra saḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Since, O Brāhmaṇas, Devas beginning with Brahmā attain the greatest satisfaction after duly getting Soma and become joyous, therefore he is considered excellent here.

## \|\| 1.87.8 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādayo yajñāstathā some pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*tasya pānādyatastṛptiṃ tatra yāṃti dvijottamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly the Yajñas beginning with Agniṣṭoma are dependent on Soma because the excellent Brāhmaṇas derive satisfaction by imbibing it.

## \|\| 1.87.9 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇātsomaḥ sarveṣāmadhikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca sa hi pūjyatamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. For this reason Soma is proclaimed as superior to all the Devas and Dānavas. Indeed he is the most worthy of being worshipped by them.

## \|\| 1.87.10 \|\|

*yathānyeṣāṃ surendrāṇāṃ harmyāṇi dharaṇītale \|*  
*kriyante rātrināthasya tadvatkurvaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Men erect palaces on the earth for the Lord of the night in the same manner as they are erected for other leading Suras.

## \|\| 1.87.11 \|\|

*yairyernarairniśeśasya prāsādo vihitaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*tete muktipadaṃ prāptāḥ kṛtvā'tha śubhasaṃcayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All those men by whom palaces (shrines) were made for the Lord of the night on the earth have accumulated a lot of merit and attained liberation.

## \|\| 1.87.12 \|\|

*yanmaheśvaraharmyāṇāṃ sahasreṇa bhavecchubham \|*  
*tadeke naiva caṃdrasya prāpnuvaṃti śubhaṃ narāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By means of a single mansion of the Moon, men obtain that merit which is attained by a thousand mansions (temples) of Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.87.13 \|\|

*atha candrotthaharmyasya māhātmyaṃ taddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*jñātvā brahmādayo devā bhayasaṃtrastamānasāḥ \|*  
*tadvighnārthamidaṃ procurmerumūrdhānamāśritāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on coming to know the greatness of a mansion (shrine) raised for Candra, Brahmā and other Devas became frightened in their minds. They resorted to the top of Meru and said thus in order to put obstacles in its erection:

## \|\| 1.87.14-18 \|\|

*saumyarkṣe somavāreṇa saumye māsi ca saṃsthite \|*  
*tithau ca somadevatye prāpte somagrahe tathā \|*  
*sakāraiḥ paṃcabhiryukte kāle somasya maṃdiram \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ya ekāhena saṃpādya prāsādaṃ sthāpayiṣyati \|*  
*caṃdraṃ sa sarvadevotthaharmyasyāpnoti satphalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sahasraguṇitaṃ samyakchraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*anyathā yastu caṃdrasya prāsādaṃ prakariṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vaṃśocchedaṃ samāsādya narakaṃ sa prayāsyati \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādbhītā na kurvaṃti narā bhuvi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*prāsādaṃ rātrināthasya supuṇyamapi saddvijāḥ \|*  
*ya eṣa rātrināthasya kṣetre'traiva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. “All the following (astrological) events beginning with Sa should coincide on a single day: (1) Saumya-Ṛkṣa i.e. Mṛgaśīras, (2)Somavāra (Monday), (3) Saumyatithi (?full-moon day) and (5) Somagraha (lunar eclipse). One who erects a palace on that (juncture) in a single day and installs Candra shall obtain the excellent benefit of erecting palaces (temples) for all the deities.

If the mind is sanctified by perfect faith, the benefit shall be thousand-fold. If one erects the palace of Candra otherwise he meets with the ruin of his family and falls into Naraka.

It is for this reason, that, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, men are afraid and so do not construct a shrine of the Lord of the night, though it is highly meritorious.

## \|\| 1.87.19 \|\|

*prāsādastvaṃbarīṣeṇa bhūbhujā sa vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃcitsamayaṃ prāpya yathoktaṃ śāstraciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A mansion of the Lord of the night that has been erected here in this holy place was raised by Aṃbarīṣa, the king who somehow found such a time as has been enjoined by those who ponder over scriptural topics.

## \|\| 1.87.20 \|\|

*tasyaivottaradigbhāge dvitīyo'nyaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*candramā dhaṃdhumāreṇa tadvatso'pi pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. To the northern direction thereof, a second Candramas was installed by Dhundhumāra. Like the other one he too is well established.

## \|\| 1.87.21 \|\|

*tataśca tau mahīpālau tatprabhāvādubhau dvijāḥ \|*  
*gatau ca paramāṃ siddhiṃ janmamṛtyuvivarjitām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Therefore, O Brāhmaṇas, both the kings attained the greatest Siddhi, by his power unaffected by birth and death.

## \|\| 1.87.22 \|\|

*prāsādo'nyastṛtīyastu kṣetre prābhāsike tathā \|*  
*ikṣvākuṇā nareṃdreṇa śraddhāyuktena nirmitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Another palatial shrine, the third one, is in the holy place of Prabhāsa. It was erected by the great king Ikṣvāku endowed with faith.

## \|\| 1.87.23 \|\|

*prāsādatrayametaddhi muktvātra dharaṇītale \|*  
*aparo nāsti candrasya satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*eko'sti narmadātīre puṇye revorisaṃgame \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Excepting these three palaces there is no other palace on the earth pertaining to Candra. What I have uttered is the truth. There is however one on the banks of Narmadā on the meritorious confluence of Revā and Ūri.

## \|\| 1.87.24 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ candramāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ cāpi sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus everything connected with the excellent greatness of Candra has been narrated to you completely. It is destructive of all sins of those who read and those who listen.

## Chapter 88 - Greatness of Aṃbāvṛddhā

## \|\| 1.88.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yāstvayā devatāḥ proktāścatasraḥ sūtanaṃdana \|*  
*camatkārī mahitthā ca mahālakṣmīstathā'parā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aṃbāvṛddhā caturthī ca tāsāṃ tisraḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vistareṇa caturthī ca aṃbāvṛddhā na kīrtitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etasyāḥ sarvamācakṣva prabhāvaṃ sūtasaṃbhava \|*  
*kenaiṣā nirmitā yātrā sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. O son of Sūta, four deities were enumerated by you, viz. Camatkārī, Mahitthā, Mahālakṣmī and another deity, the fourth one Aṃbāvrddhā.

Of them, three have been described in detail. The fourth one Aṃbāvrddhā has not been described. O son of Sūta, state the power of this deity. Who instituted her Yātrā (religious procession). Mention everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.88.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*eṣā tapomayī śaktirambāvṛddhā sureśvarī \|*  
*yathātra saṃsthitā pūrvaṃ tatsarvaṃ śrūyatāṃ mama \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. This goddess of Suras, namely Aṃbāvṛddhā is the divine power of austerity. May it be listened from me how she came to be established here formerly.

## \|\| 1.88.5 \|\|

*camatkāramahīpena purametadyadā kṛtam \|*  
*tadā tadrakṣaṇārthāya nirmitā bhāvitātmanā \|*  
*catasro devatā hyetāḥ saṃmatena dvijanmanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When this city was built by King Camatkāra, a man of meritorious soul, he installed these four deities in consultation with and advice of Brāhmaṇas for the protection of the city.

## \|\| 1.88.6 \|\|

*atha tasya mahīpasya aṃbānāmābhavatsutā \|*  
*tathānyā vṛddhasaṃjñā ca rūpaudāryaguṇānvite \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This king had two daughters, one by the name Aṃbā and the other named Vṛddhā. Both of them were endowed with beauty and excellent virtues.

## \|\| 1.88.7 \|\|

*ubhe te kāśirājena pariṇīte dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*gṛhyoktena vidhānena devaviprāgnisaṃnidhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Both of them were married to the king of Kāśī, in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Gṛhyasūtras and in the presence of Devas, Brāhmaṇas and the holy Fire, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.88.8 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya kāśirājasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*taiḥ kālayavanaiḥ sārdhamabhavatsaṃgaro mahān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once upon a time the king of Kāśī had to fight a great battle with the Kālayavanas (dark-complexioned Barbarians).

## \|\| 1.88.9 \|\|

*atha tairnihataḥ saṃkhye sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ \|*  
*haralabdhavarai raudraiḥ kāśirājaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Though the king of Kāśī was endowed with great prowess, he was killed in the battle along with his servants, armies and vehicles by those terrible ones who had obtained boons from Hara.

## \|\| 1.88.10-11 \|\|

*athāṃbā caiva vṛddhā ca vaidhavyaṃ prāpya duḥkhadam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ gatvā te vāṃchitapradam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*devyā ārādhane yatnaṃ kṛtavatyau tataḥ param \|*  
*nāśārthaṃ patiśatrūṇāṃ dhṛtavatyau śubhavratam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Aṃbā and Vṛddhā were reduced to the miserable state of widowhood. They went to the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara, the bestower of all desired things. They endeavoured to propitiate the goddess. They observed auspicious Vratas for the destruction of the enemies of their husband.

## \|\| 1.88.12 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ na ca tuṣṭā sureśvarī \|*  
*tato vairāgyamāsādya vāṃchaṃtyau svatanukṣayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For more than a hundred years, the goddess of Suras did not become pleased. They got disgusted and detached from the world. They wished to destroy their bodies.

## \|\| 1.88.13-14 \|\|

*maṃtrairātharvaṇairviprāḥ kṣurikāsūktasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*chittvācchittvā svamāṃsāni maṃtrapūtāni bhaktitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṛtavatyau tato homaṃ susamiddhe hutāśane \|*  
*agnikuṇḍāttatastasmāścaturhastā śubhānanā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. O Brāhmaṇas, they recited the Mantras of the Kṣurikā Sūkta of the Ātharvaṇa Veda. They cut off their flesh devoutly inspiring and sanctifying them with the Mantras and performed Homa in the well-kindled holy fire.

Thereupon a deity with four arms and splendid countenance rose up from the fire-pit.

## \|\| 1.88.15 \|\|

*śvetavastrā viniṣkrāṃtā nārī bālārkasavribhā \|*  
*tathānyā ca sunetrāsyā taptahāṭakasannibhā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lady was clad in white garments and she resembled the early morning sun in lustre. Another lady of excellent eyes and countenance also rose up. She resembled molten gold in lustre.

## \|\| 1.88.16 \|\|

*tasmātkuṇḍādviniṣkrāṃtā dhṛtakhaḍgā bhayāvahā \|*  
*sā'parāpi tathārūpā śaktiḥ paramadāruṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She rose up from the fire-pit holding a sword. She was terrifying. This other lady too was a highly frightening Śakti.

## \|\| 1.88.17 \|\|

*procatuste varaṃ hṛtsthaṃ prārthyatāmiti durlabham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. They said, “Let the boon cherished in the heart be requested for, even if it be very difficult to attain.”

## \|\| 1.88.18 \|\|

*te ūcatuḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ dayito bharttā kāśirājaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*nihataḥ saṃgare kruddhairyavanaiḥ kālapūrvakaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

The two (queens) said:

18\. Our beloved husband, the valorous king of Kāśī, has been killed in battle by the ferocious Kālayavanas.

## \|\| 1.88.19 \|\|

*yuṣmadīya prasādena yathā teṣāṃ parikṣayaḥ \|*  
*sañjāyate mahādevyau tathā kāryamasaṃśayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O great goddesses, something should be done so that their destruction can be effected undoubtedly with your favour.

## \|\| 1.88.20 \|\|

*sthātavyaṃ ca tathātraiva ubhābhyāmapi sādaram \|*  
*svapurasya prarakṣārthametatkṛtyaṃ mataṃ hi nau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Further, both of you should eagerly stay here for the protection of your own city. This is the task (boon) thought of by us.

## \|\| 1.88.21 \|\|

*tayostadvacanaṃ śrutvā ubhe te devate tataḥ \|*  
*saṃprocya bāḍhamityevaṃ tasminkuṇḍe vyavasthite \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing their words, both the deities said “So be it” and merged into that pit.

## \|\| 1.88.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasmātkuṇḍācchatasahasraśaḥ \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtāḥ saṃkhyayā hīnā mātaro naikarūpikāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime, innumerable mothers (goddesses), thousands of them of many forms, rose up from that Kuṇḍa.

(The different kinds of beings that arose from that fire-pit are described below:)

## \|\| 1.88.23 \|\|

*ekā gajamukhī tatra tathānyā turagānanā \|*  
*sārameya mukhāścānyāḥ pakṣicchāgamukhāḥ parāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. One set had the faces of elephants and another had those of horses. Others had the faces of dogs and still others those of birds and goats.

## \|\| 1.88.24 \|\|

*tiryañca vapuṣaścānyā vaktrairmānuṣasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*triśīrṣāḥ pañcaśīrṣāśca daśaśīrṣāstathā parāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Others had human faces but the bodies were those of lower animals. Some had three heads, some five heads and others even ten heads.

## \|\| 1.88.25 \|\|

*guhya sthānasthitairvaktrairekāścānyā hṛdisthitaiḥ \|*  
*pārśvasaṃsthaiḥ sthitāścānyā anyāḥ pṛṣṭhigatairmukhaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The faces of some of these beings were in different parts of the bodies. Some had faces in their privy parts; others in their breasts; yet others stood with faces at the sides; a few others had faces on the back.

## \|\| 1.88.26 \|\|

*ekahastā dvihastāśca pañcahastāstathāparāḥ \|*  
*anyā viṃśatihastāśca vihastāśca tathāparāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Some had only a single hand; others two hands; still others had five hands; a few others had even twenty hands; others were devoid of hands.

## \|\| 1.88.27 \|\|

*bahupādā vipādāśca ekapādāstathāparāḥ \|*  
*tathānyāścārdhapādāśca adhovaktrā vibhīṣaṇāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There were beings with many feet as well as those devoid of feet; there were single-footed and half-footed ones; some were terribly hideous with faces down.

## \|\| 1.88.28 \|\|

*ekanetrā dvinetrāśca trinetrāśca tathāparāḥ \|*  
*kāścidgajasamārūḍhā hayārūḍhāstathāparāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. There were single-eyed ones, two-eyed and others manyeyed. Some of them rode on elephants and others on horses.

## \|\| 1.88.29 \|\|

*vṛṣavānarasiṃhājavyāghrasarpāsthitāḥ parāḥ \|*  
*godhāśvarāsabhārūḍhāstathā ca vihagāśritāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Still others were riding on bulls, monkeys, lions, goats, tigers and pythons. Similarly some were seated on alligators, horses, donkeys etc. There were some seated on birds.

## \|\| 1.88.30 \|\|

*kūrmakukkuṭasarpādisamārūḍhāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*prakurvaṃtyo rudantyaśca gāyantyaśca tathā parāḥ \|*  
*nṛtyaṃtyaśca hasaṃtyaśca krīḍāsaktāḥ parasparam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. There were thousands seated on tortoises, cocks, serpents etc. They were gesticulating, howling and singing. Laughing, dancing and sporting about mutually, they proceeded ahead.

## \|\| 1.88.31 \|\|

*ūrdhvakeśā vikeśāśca gātrakeśāśca bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*laṃbakeśā vikeśāśca vājikeśāstathaiva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. There were many beings with hairs raised up, hairs covering the bodies and some having no hair at all. Others had long hairs, some with hairs like those of hordes and a few with various peculiar types of hairs.

## \|\| 1.88.32 \|\|

*hrasvadantyo vidaṃtyaśca dīrghadantyo vibhīṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*gajadaṃtyastathaivānyā lohadaṃtyobhayāvahāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There were terribly hideous beings with short teeth, long teeth and peculiar types of teeth. Others were frightening with elephant teeth and teeth like steel.

## \|\| 1.88.33 \|\|

*laṃbakarṇyo vikarṇyaśca śūrpakarṇyastathā parāḥ \|*  
*śaṃkukarṇyaḥ kukarṇyaśca bahukarṇyaḥ sukarṇikāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. There were many beings with ears hanging loosely down; others with peculiar ears; still others with ears like a winnowing basket. There were spike-eared, many-eared, ugly-eared and excellent-eared beings.

## \|\| 1.88.34 \|\|

*ekavastrā vivastrāśca bahuvastrāstathā parāḥ \|*  
*carmaprāvaraṇāścaiva kathāprāvaraṇānvitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There were single-clothed and many-clothed beings; others were without clothes; still others had hides as coverings or rags used to cover nakedness.

## \|\| 1.88.35 \|\|

*khaṅgahastāḥ śarāhastāḥ kuṃtahastāśca bhīṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*pāśahastāstathaivānyāḥ prāsacāpakarāḥ parāḥ \|*  
*śūlamudgarahastāśca bhuśuṃḍikarabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There were terrible beings with swords, arrows and javelins in their hands. Others had nooses in their hands and a few others with spears and bows in their hands, beings with tridents, mallets and Bhuśuṇḍīs adorning their hands.

## \|\| 1.88.36 \|\|

*atha tābhyāṃ tathā'karṇya tāḥ sarvā harṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*prasthitāstatra tā yatra te kālayavanāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then these beings heard the commands of the two goddesses and were highly delighted. They proceeded towards the place where dark-complexioned ones were staying.

## \|\| 1.88.37-38 \|\|

*tataste tatsamālokya balaṃ devīsamudravam \|*  
*raudra rūpadharaṃ tīvraṃ vikṛtaṃ vikṛtairmukhaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve bhayabhītā samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*dhāvato bhakṣitāstābhirdevatābhiḥ sunirdayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. On seeing the army of the goddesses with hideous forms and ugly countenances (advancing) all those (Kālayavanas) became afraid with gloomy faces. While they fled here and there, they were ruthlessly swallowed by those deities.

## \|\| 1.88.39 \|\|

*bālavṛddhasamopetaṃ teṣāṃ rāṣṭraṃ durātmanām \|*  
*strībhiśca sahitaṃ tābhirdevatābhiḥ prabhakṣitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The entire kingdom of those wicked-souled ones including children and old people as well as women were quickly swallowed by those deities.

## \|\| 1.88.40 \|\|

*evaṃ nirvāsya tadrāṣṭraṃ sarvāstā harṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*bhūya eva nijaṃ sthānaṃ saṃprāptā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After de-populating and exterminating the entire territory, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all of them joyously returned to their original abodes.

## \|\| 1.88.41-42 \|\|

*tataḥ procuḥ praṇamyoccaistābhyāṃ vinayapūrvakam \|*  
*hatāste yavanāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ saputrapaśubāṃdhavāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*udvāsitastathā sarvo deśasteṣāṃ sa vai mahān \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ dīyatāṃ kaścidāhārastṛptihetave \|*  
*nivāsāya tataḥ sthānaṃ kiṃciccāvedyatāṃ hi naḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Then they bowed down with humility to those two deities and requested loudly: “All those Kālayavanas have been killed along with their sons, kinsmen and cattle. The entire realm though vast has been rendered waste. Now some food may be given to us for our satisfaction. Similarly some place may be assigned to us for residence.

## \|\| 1.88.43 \|\|

*devyāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*martyaloke'tra yā nāryo garbhavatyaḥ svapaṃti ca \|*  
*saṃdhyākālaprakāśe ca tāsāṃ garbho'stu vo drutam \|\| 43 \|\|*

The Devīs said:

43\. The foetus of those pregnant women in the mortal world who go to sleep in dim light at the time of dusk may be taken by you quickly as your prey.

## \|\| 1.88.44 \|\|

*rudaṃtyo yā viniryāṃti catvareṣu trikeṣu ca \|*  
*tāsāṃ garbhastu yuṣmākaṃ saṃpradattaḥ prabhujyatām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The foetus of these women too have been given to you all: Those who cry and lament and rush to places where three roads and four roads meet. Let it be eaten by you.

## \|\| 1.88.45 \|\|

*ucchiṣṭā yāḥ prasarpaṃti ramante ca svapaṃti ca \|*  
*tāsāṃ garbhaḥ samastānāṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhoja nāya vai \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If women move about, sport about or sleep after being Ucchiṣṭa (i.e. without washing the mouth after taking food), the foetus of all those women have been assigned as food unto you all.

## \|\| 1.88.46 \|\|

*sūtikābhavane yasminnucchiṣṭaṃ copajāyate \|*  
*sa bālakastu yuṣmākaṃ bhojanāya prakalpitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If there is a case of Ucchiṣṭa (rennants \[remnants?\] of food etc.) in the lying-in-chamber, that child has been assigned to you as food.

## \|\| 1.88.47 \|\|

*na ṣaṣṭhījāgaro yasya bālakasya bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sa bhaviṣyati bhojyāya yuṣmākaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If Ṣaṣṭhījāgara (i.e. worship of Durgā and remaining awake on the sixth day after nativity) is not performed for any child, that child is undoubtedly given to you as food.

## \|\| 1.88.48 \|\|

*nāśaṃ yāsyati vā yatra pāvakaḥ sūtikāgṛhe \|*  
*sa bhaviṣyati bhojyāya yuṣmākaṃ bālarūpadhṛk \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If the fire kept in the lying-in-chamber becomes extinguished, the child therein shall be assigned to you as your meal.

## \|\| 1.88.49 \|\|

*māṃgalyaiḥ saṃparityaktaṃ yadbhavetsūtikāgṛham \|*  
*tasminyastiṣṭhate bālaḥ sa yuṣmākaṃ prakalpitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If the lying-in-chamber is left devoid of auspicious things, the boy who stays there is assigned to you for your meal.

## \|\| 1.88.50 \|\|

*saṃdhyāyāṃ bālakā ye vā svapaṃtyākāśadeśagāḥ \|*  
*te sarve bhojanārthāya yuṣmākaṃ saṃniveditāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. All the children who sleep under the open sky at dusk are given over to you as prey.

## \|\| 1.88.51 \|\|

*yasya janmadine prāpte varṣāṃte kriyate na ca \|*  
*māṃgalyaṃ tasya yadgātraṃ tadyuṣmākaṃ prakalpitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If at the end of a year when the birthday falls no auspicious rites are performed, the body of that child has been assigned to you.

## \|\| 1.88.52 \|\|

*tailābhyaṃgaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā yaśca snānaṃ karoti na \|*  
*sa datto bhojanārthāya yuṣmākaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If after anointing the body with oil a man does not take bath, he is undoubtedly given over to you as food.

## \|\| 1.88.53 \|\|

*ucchiṣṭo yaḥ pumāṃstiṣṭhedyo vā catvaramadhyagaḥ \|*  
*bhakṣaṇīyaḥ sa sarvābhirnirvikalpena cetasā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. If a man is Ucchiṣṭa (polluted by remainings of food) and he stands in the centre of the quadrangle, he should be eaten by you all unhesitatingly.

## \|\| 1.88.54 \|\|

*rajasvalāṃ vrajedyo vā puruṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ \|*  
*nagnaḥ śete tathā snāti bhakṣaṇīyaḥ sa satvaram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A man who is deluded by lust and cohabits with a woman in her monthly course, one who goes to bed naked or takes bath in the nude, should be eaten quickly.

## \|\| 1.88.55 \|\|

*dakṣiṇābhimukho rātrau yaśca snāti vimūḍhadhīḥ \|*  
*śete ca śayane so'pi bhakṣaṇīyaśca satvaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A man of deluded intellect who takes his bath at night facing the South and one who lies down on the bed thus should also be eaten quickly.

## \|\| 1.88.56 \|\|

*udaṅmukhaśca yo rātrau divā vā dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ \|*  
*mūtrotsargaṃ purīṣa vā prakuryādbhakṣya eva saḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One who urinates or defecates with face towards the North at night and towards the South during the day should be eaten.

## \|\| 1.88.57 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryādrajanīvaktre dadhisaktuprabhakṣaṇam \|*  
*aṃtyajābhigamaṃ cātha bhakṣaṇīyo drutaṃ hi saḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One who eats fried flour mixed with curds at the beginning of night or carnally approaches a low caste woman should be eaten quickly.

## \|\| 1.88.58 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tābhyāṃ tadā proktā devatāstāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*parivārya tadā tasthuḥ saṃprahṛṣṭena cetasā \|\| 58 \|\|*

Sūta said:

58\. On being told thus by the two goddesses those beings surrounded them with delighted minds and stood thus.

## \|\| 1.88.59 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare rājā camatkāraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*prāsādaṃ nirmame tābhyāṃ kailāsaśikharopamam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the meantime the valorous king Camatkāra built for them a palatial mansion similar to the Kailāsa peak.

## \|\| 1.88.60 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te khyāte kṣetre tatra mahodaye \|*  
*aṃbāvṛddhābhidhāne ca purarakṣāpare sadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Ever since then those two holy deities of great prosperity, known as Aṃbā and Vṛddhā are always alert in guarding the city.

## \|\| 1.88.61 \|\|

*yaḥ pumānprātarutthāya tābhyāṃ paśyati cānanam \|*  
*tasya saṃvatsaraṃyāvanna ca cchidraṃ prajāyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A man who gets up early in the morning and sees their countenances does not meet with misfortunes for the period of a whole year.

## \|\| 1.88.62 \|\|

*vṛddhyādau vātha cāṃte vā tābhyāṃ pūjāṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*na tasya jāyate cchidraṃ kathaṃcidapi bhūtale \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On happy occasions and festivities, a devotee should worship them at the beginning or at the close of the same. He never faces misfortune on the earth.

## \|\| 1.88.63 \|\|

*yātrākāle pumānyaśca tābhyāṃ pūjāṃ samācaret \|*  
*sa vāṃchitaphalaṃ prāpya śīghraṃ svagṛhamāpnuyāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. During pilgrimages, a man should perform the rite of adoration for those two. He attains the desired benefit and returns home quickly.

## \|\| 1.88.64-65 \|\|

*sadāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ yastābhyāṃ balimāharet \|*  
*sa kāmānāpnuyādiṣṭāniha pretya ca sadgatim \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yo mahānavamīsaṃjñe divase śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ samācaretpūjāṃ sa sadā syādakaṇṭakī \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. One who always offers oblation on the eighth or fourteenth lunar day to them, shall attain the desired things here and good goal hereafter.

One who is endowed with faith and worships them on the Mahānavamī day shall be free from risks and difficulties.

## Chapter 89 - Greatness of the Pādukās of Śrīmātā

## \|\| 1.89.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tatra sthite nityaṃ tasminmātṛgaṇe dvijāḥ \|*  
*bālakānāṃ kṣayo jajñe brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhegṛhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Thus when the group of mother-goddesses stayed there, the incidence of child-mortality took place in every household.

## \|\| 1.89.2 \|\|

*taruṇānāṃ viśeṣeṇa camatkārapurottare \|*  
*chidramanveṣamāṇāstā bhramaṃtyakhiladevatāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. All those goddesses roamed about in the city of Camatkārapura, in search of lapses and flaws in (the conduct) particularly of young men.

## \|\| 1.89.3 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve jñātvā chidrasamudbhavam \|*  
*vighātaṃ bālakānāṃ ca devatābhirvinirmitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. All those Brāhmaṇas came to know that the child-mortality (or destruction of children) was due to the blemishes and lapses and that it was created (caused) by those goddesses.

## \|\| 1.89.4 \|\|

*ambāvṛddhe samāsādya pūjayitvā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*procuśca duḥkhasantaptā vinayāvanatāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They approached Aṃbā and Vṛddhā, worshipped them assiduously and approached them humbly in the height of their misery:

## \|\| 1.89.5 \|\|

*rakṣārthaṃ sarvaviprāṇāṃ camatkāreṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*bhavadbhyāṃ nirmitaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prāsādo'yaṃ manoharaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This excellent and charming palatial shrine has been built by King Camatkāra unto you two, for the sake of according protection to all the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.89.6-7 \|\|

*hriyaṃte bālakā rātrau chidraṃ prāpya sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmadīyābhiretābhirdevatābhiḥ samantataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ tasmādbrāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*no cetpuraṃ parityajya yāsyāmo'nyatra bhūtale \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. But thousands of children are being carried away at night by these deities and beings belonging to you two after detecting some blemish or other everywhere.

Favour may be shown, therefore, to the noble-souled Brāhmaṇas. Otherwise we shall leave the city and go elsewhere on the earth.”

## \|\| 1.89.8 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tatoṃ'bā kṛpayānvitā \|*  
*hatvā pādaprahāreṇa bhūmiṃ cakre guhāṃ tataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing their words, Aṃbā became compassionate. She kicked the ground with her foot and created a cave.

## \|\| 1.89.9 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sve pāduke nyasya tataḥ provāca devatāḥ \|*  
*sarvāstā natasarvāṃgīrvinayena samanvitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She placed her sandals in the cave and spoke to the deities, the beings who were standing there humbly with their bodies stooping law:

## \|\| 1.89.10-11 \|\|

*ime matpāduke divye guhāmadhyagate sadā \|*  
*sarvābhiḥ sevanīye ca na gantavyaṃ bahiḥ kvacit \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yā kācillaulyamāsthāya niṣkramiṣyati mohataḥ \|*  
*sā divyabhāvanirmuktā śṛgālī saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. ‘These two divine sandals of mine kept in the interior of the cave should be served always by all of you. None should go out anywhere. One who, out of covetousness and delusion, goes out, shall be stripped of her divine nature. She will become a vixen.”

## \|\| 1.89.12 \|\|

*devatā ūcuḥ \|*  
*atra sthāne mahādevi ko'smākaṃ prakariṣyati \|*  
*pūjāṃ ko vātra cāhārastasmādbrūhi sureśvari \|\| 12 \|\|*

The Devatās said:

12\. O great goddess, who will perform our adoration in this spot? What shall be our food? Hence speak out, O goddess of Suras.

## \|\| 1.89.13 \|\|

*ambovāca \|*  
*atrāgatya vinirmuktā yogino dhyānacintakāḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ samyakkariṣyaṃti sarvāsāṃ bhaktisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Aṃbā said:

13\. Liberated Yogins devoted to meditation and contemplation shall come here and perform your worship with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.89.14 \|\|

*pāduke me prapūjyādau māṃsa madyādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*avāpsyaṃti ca saṃsiddhiṃ durlabhāmamarairapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At the outset they will worship my sandals with flesh, liquor etc., in due order. They will attain great Siddhi inaccessible even to immortals.

## \|\| 1.89.15 \|\|

*tatastatheti tāḥ procya guhāmadhye vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*parivārya śubhe tasyāḥ pāduke mokṣadāyike \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All of them said, “So be it” and remained in the interior of the cave surrounding those excellent sandals that yield salvation.

## \|\| 1.89.16 \|\|

*tatastatra samāgatya puruṣā api dūrataḥ \|*  
*prapūjya pāduke samyaṅmātṝstāśca tataḥ param \|*  
*prayāṃti ca parāṃ siddhiṃ janma mṛtyuvivarjitām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, men from even far-off places came there, duly worshipped the sandals and then the Mātṛs (Mother-deities) and attained the highest Siddhi (i.e. salvation) devoid of birth and death.

## \|\| 1.89.17 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare naṣṭā agniṣṭomādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāvratānyeva saṃyamā niyamāśca ye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the meantime Agniṣṭoma and other rites became defunct. So also pilgrimages, holy vows, mental control, restraint etc., came to a standstill.

## \|\| 1.89.18-19 \|\|

*ye cāpi brāhmaṇāḥ śāṃtāḥ sadā madyasya dūṣaṇam \|*  
*prakurvaṃti svahastena te'pi madyaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tarpayaṃti tathā māṃsaistyaktāśeṣamakhakriyāḥ \|*  
*pāduke mātṛbhirjuṣṭe tathā dhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Even those quiescent Brāhmaṇas who used to decry liquor began to offer libation of liquors of various kinds with their own hands. They eschewed all sacrificial rites. They propitiated the sandals with meat, wine and unguents in the company of the Mātṛs (Mother-deities).

## \|\| 1.89.20 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare bhītāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā yajñakriyocchedaṃ kṣutpipāsā samākulāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20 In the meantime, all the Devas including Vāsava noticed, to their utter dismay, the destruction of Yajña rites They became agitated with hunger and thirst.

## \|\| 1.89.21 \|\|

*procurmaheśvaraṃ gatvā vinayāvanatāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*stutvā pṛthagvidhaiḥ sūktairvedoktaiḥ śatarudriyaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They approached Maheśvara and stood before him humbly. After eulogizing Maheśvara by means of different kinds of Sūktas from the Vedas and the Śatarudriya passages they said:

## \|\| 1.89.22 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre pāduke tatra saṃsthite \|*  
*aṃbāyā mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ guhāmadhye suguptake \|\| 22 \|\|*

The Devas said:

22\. The sandals of Aṃbā are kept in the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara. They are well-guarded by the Mātṛs collectively in the centre of a cave.

## \|\| 1.89.23 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā apideveśa madyamāṃsena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ pūjāṃ prakurvaṃti prayāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even Brāhmaṇas, O Lord of Devas, perform the adoration thereof with liquor and meat. They attain the highest Siddhi too.

## \|\| 1.89.24 \|\|

*naṣṭā dharmakriyā sarvā martyaloketra sāṃpratam \|*  
*asmākaṃ saṃkṣayo jāto yajñabhāgaṃ vinā prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All religious rites in the human world have become defunct now. O Lord, by the absence of our share in the Yajñas, we have been doomed.

## \|\| 1.89.25 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ kuru deveśa yathā syātpādukākṣayaḥ \|*  
*prabhavaṃti makhā bhūmāvasmākaṃ syuḥ parā mudaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*
