25\. Hence, O Lord of Devas, kindly do something to bring about the decline of the sandals. Let the Makhas (sacrifices) flourish on the earth. May we attain the greatest joy.

## \|\| 1.89.26 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yā sā aṃbeti vikhyātā śaktiḥ sā parameśvarī \|*  
*jaganmātā'kṣayā sākṣānmamā pi jananī ca sā \|\| 26 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

26\. She who is well-known as Aṃbā is the Śakti of the great Lord. She is the everlasting mother of the universe. She is my direct mother too.

## \|\| 1.89.27 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ saṃkṣayastasyāḥ kartuṃ kenāpi śakyate \|*  
*manasāpi mahābhāgāḥ pādukānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. So how can her decline be brought about by anyone even mentally. So also is the special case of the sandals.

## \|\| 1.89.28 \|\|

*paraṃ tatra kariṣyāmi sukhopāyaṃ sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmabhyaṃ pādukāyāṃ ca mahattvaṃ yena jāyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. But, O great Suras, in this respect I shall employ an easier means whereby the greatness of the sandals is not impaired and that of yours is maintained.

## \|\| 1.89.29 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato dhyānaṃ cakre devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vyāvṛtyakamalaṃ hṛtsthamaṣṭapatraṃ sakarṇikam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After saying thus, Lord Maheśvara began his meditation opening up the eight-petalled lotus within the heart along with its pericarp.

## \|\| 1.89.30 \|\|

*tasyāṃtargatamāsīnamaṃguṣṭhāgramitaṃ śubham \|*  
*dvādaśārkaprabhaṃ sūkṣmaṃ svamātmānaṃ vyalokayat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He then looked at the subtle and splendid being seated within. It has the size of the top of the thumb and the lustre of twelve suns. It was his own soul.

## \|\| 1.89.31 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ dhyāyamānasya tṛtīyanayanāttataḥ \|*  
*śvetāṃbaradharā śubhrā nirgatā kanyakā śubhā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Even as he meditated thus, a pure and splendid girl clad in white clothes emerged from (his) third eye.

## \|\| 1.89.32 \|\|

*atha sā prāha taṃ devaṃ praṇipatya maheśvaram \|*  
*kimarthaṃ deva sṛṣṭāsmi mamādeśaḥ pradīyatām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then she bowed down to Lord Maheśvara and said, “O Lord, why have I been created? May the relevant command be given.”

## \|\| 1.89.33 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre pāduke saṃsthite śubhe \|*  
*śrīmāturjagatāṃ mukhye tābhyāṃ pūjāṃ tvamācara \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

33\. The splendid sandals of Śrī Mātā of the worlds are present in the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara. They are very important, important ones of the worlds! Do perform their worship.

## \|\| 1.89.34 \|\|

*kanyakāṃ saṃparityajya tavānvayavivarddhitām \|*  
*yaḥ kariṣyati tatpūjāmāhāraḥ syātsa mātṛṣu \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If anyone performs her adoration except a virgin brought up and nurtured in your family, he shall be the food unto the Mātrs.

## \|\| 1.89.35 \|\|

*kaumārabrahmacaryyeṇa tvayāpi ca subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ pūjā prakartavyā no cennāśamavāpsyasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Their adoration should be performed by you maintaining celibacy from girlhood onwards. If not, you will be ruined too.

## \|\| 1.89.36 \|\|

*tava pūjā kariṣyanti ye narā bhaktitatparāḥ \|*  
*mātṝṇāṃ saṃmatāste syuḥ sarvadaiva sukhānvitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those men who worship you with great devotion, shall be the persons getting the approbation of the Mātṛs. They shall always be happy.

## \|\| 1.89.37 \|\|

*evamuktvā tatastasyā maṃtramārgaṃ yathocitam \|*  
*pūjāmārgaṃ viśeṣeṇa kathayāmāsa vistarāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After saying thus he explained to her the procedures of the utterance of the Mantras as well as the details of the procedure of adoration in particular.

## \|\| 1.89.38 \|\|

*tato visarjayāmāsa dattvā chatrādibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*pratipattiṃ mahādevastāṃśca sarvānsureśvarān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then, Maheśvara gave her the umbrella and other ornaments as well as right knowledge and sent her off along with all the leading Suras.

## \|\| 1.89.39-40 \|\|

*kumāryuvāca \|*  
*tvayetatkathitaṃ deva tvadanvayasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*kanyakāḥ pūjayiṣyaṃti pāduke te suśobhane \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kaumārabrahmacaryyeṇa bhaviṣyatyanvayaḥ katham \|*  
*etanme vistarātsarvaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Kumārī (virgin) said:

39-40. O Lord, this was mentioned by you that the girls hailing from my family would be adoring those splendid sandals. How can a family come into existence if one resorts to celibacy ever since childhood? It behoves you to explain all this in detail.

## \|\| 1.89.41-42 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yasyāyasyāḥ prasannā tvaṃ kanyakāyā vadiṣyasi \|*  
*maṃtragrāmamimaṃ samyaktvadbhāvā sā bhaviṣyati \|\| 41 \|\|*

*evaṃ cānyā mahābhāge pāraṃparyeṇa kanyakāḥ \|*  
*tava vaṃśodbhavāḥ sarvāḥ prabhaviṣyaṃti maṃtrataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

41-42. If you are pleased with any virgin and if you impart this series of Mantras properly to her, she will be emotionally linked with you. O highly blessed one, in this manner other girls also can be trained successively. They will be considered as girls hailing from your family on the basis of the Mantras.

## \|\| 1.89.43 \|\|

*tataḥ sā tāṃ samāsādya pādukāsaṃbhavāṃ guhām \|*  
*pūjāṃ cakre yathānyāyaṃ yathoktaṃ tripurāriṇā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thereafter she went to the cave containing the sandals and performed the adoration duly as explained by the slayer of the Tripuras.

## \|\| 1.89.44 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tadanvayasamutthāyāḥ kanyakāyāḥ kareṇa yaḥ \|*  
*pādukābhyāṃ naraḥ pūjāṃ prakaroti samāhitaḥ \|*  
*iha loke sukhaṃ prāpya sa syātpretya sukhānvitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Sūta said:

44\. A man who with purity and mental concentration performs the adoration of the sandals through the hands of a virgin hailing from her family, shall attain happiness in this world as well as in the other

## \|\| 1.89.45 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kanyāhastena pāduke \|*  
*pūjanīye viśeṣeṇa pūjyā sā cāpi kanyakā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence by all means the sandals should be worshipped through the hands of a virgin. That worshipping virgin too should be duly worshipped.

## \|\| 1.89.46 \|\|

*vāṃchadbhiḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyamiha loke paratra ca \|*  
*mānavairbhaktisaṃyuktairityuvāca maheśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This worship should be carried out by those men who desire perpetual happiness in this world as well as in the other. They should be endowed with devotion, so said Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.89.47 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ pādukodbhavam \|*  
*śrīmāturanuṣaṃgeṇa aṃbādevyā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus the greatness pertaining to the sandals of Śrīmātā has been narrated to you completely. Incidentally, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Aṃbādevī too has been narrated.

## \|\| 1.89.48 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyādbhaktyā caturdaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tathāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣeṇa sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. One who devoutly listens to this with mental concentration and purity on the fourteenth lunar day as well as on the eighth day in particular attains the greatest region.

## Chapter 90 - Greatness of Vasordhārā

## \|\| 1.90.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*agnitīrthaṃ tvayā proktaṃ brahmatīrthaṃ ca yatpurā \|*  
*na tayoḥ kathitotpattirmāhātmyaṃ ca mahāmate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasmādvistarato brūhi ekaikasya pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*na vayaṃ tṛptimāpannāḥ śṛṇvataste vaco'mṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O highly intelligent one, Agnitīrtha and Brahmatīrtha have been mentioned by you earlier, but their origin and greatness have not been told. Hence describe each one separately and in detail. We are not fully satiated by listening to your nectar-like words.

## \|\| 1.90.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm \|*  
*agnitīrthasamudbhūtāṃ sarvasaukhyāvahāṃ śubhām \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. In this context I shall relate to you a story that is destructive of sins. It refers to Agnitīrtha. It is auspicious and contributes to the happiness of everyone.

## \|\| 1.90.4 \|\|

*somavaṃśasamudbhūtaḥ pratīpo nāma bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*purāsīcchauryasaṃpanno brahmajñānavicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly there was a king named Pratīpa. He hailed from the lunar race. He was endowed with heroism and was expert in the knowledge of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.90.5 \|\|

*tasya putradvayaṃ jajñe sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*devāpiḥ prathamastatra dvitīyaḥ śaṃtanurdvijāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He had two sons having all (good) features. Of them, O Brāhmaṇas, the first was Devāpi and the second was Śantanu.

## \|\| 1.90.6 \|\|

*atho śivapadaṃ prāpte pratīpe nṛpasattame \|*  
*tapo'rthaṃ rājyamutsṛjya devāpirniyaryau vanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When the excellent king Pratīpa went to the region of Śiva, Devāpi abandoned the kingdom and went to forest for performing penance.

## \|\| 1.90.7 \|\|

*tataśca maṃtribhiḥ sarvaiḥ śaṃtanustasya cānujaḥ \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahe rājye satvaraṃ sanniyojitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereupon Śantanu, his younger brother, was immediately installed in the hereditary kingdom by all the ministers.

## \|\| 1.90.8 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śakro na vavarṣa kruddhā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*yāvaddvādaśavarṣāṇi tasmi nrājyaṃ praśāsati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the meantime, while he was ruling the kingdom, Śakra who had become angry, did not shower rain for a period of twelve years.

## \|\| 1.90.9 \|\|

*ataḥ kṛcchraṃ gataḥ sarvo lokaḥ kṣutparipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*cāmuṃḍāsadṛśo jāto yo na mṛtyuvaśaṃgataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. So the entire world was afflicted by hunger and experienced great difficulties and sufferings. One who did not meet with death was like Cāmuṇḍā (ferocious).

## \|\| 1.90.10 \|\|

*saṃtyaktāḥ patibhirnāryaḥ putrāśca pitṛbhirnijaiḥ \|*  
*mātaraśca tathā putrairlokeṣvanyeṣu kā kathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Women were abandoned by their husbands; sons by their own fathers: mothers were abandoned by their sons. Others need not be mentioned.

## \|\| 1.90.11 \|\|

*daivayogātkvacitkiṃcitkasyacidyadi dṛśyate \|*  
*sasyaṃ siddhamasiddhaṃ vā hriyate vīryataḥ paraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By good luck or by chance, if at all any vestige of vegetation could be seen at any one’s place, be it raw or cooked, it was carried away forcibly by others.

## \|\| 1.90.12 \|\|

*śuṣkā mahīruhāḥ sarve tathā ye ca jalāśayāḥ \|*  
*nadyaśca svalpatoyāśca gaṃgādyā api saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All the trees became parched and all the water reservoirs became dried up. Even Gaṅgā and other rivers contained only very little water.

## \|\| 1.90.13-14 \|\|

*evaṃ vṛṣṭeḥ kṣaye jāte naṣṭe dharmapathe tathā \|*  
*loke'sminnasthisaṃghātaiḥ pūrite bhasmanā vṛte \|\| 13 \|\|*

*na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre na svādhyāyaṃ na ca vratam \|*  
*evamālokyate vyoma vṛṣṭyarthaṃ kṣutsamākulaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. When there was the absence of rain thus and religious observances vanished, the entire world was filled with heaps of bones and columns of ashes. No one performed Yajña, Svādhyāya (self-study of the Vedas) and Vrata. Those who were agitated through hunger simply gazed at the sky for rain.

## \|\| 1.90.15-16 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*carmāsthiśeṣasarvāṃgo bubhukṣārta itastataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paribhramaṃstataḥ prāpya kaṃcidgrāmaṃ nirudvasam \|*  
*mṛtamartyodbhavaivyāptamasthisaṃghaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. At that time the great sage Viśvāmitra became so distressed with hunger that only skin and bone remained in his body. Wandering here and there he reached a certain village from which everything had been completely drained and extracted. All round the entire region was covered with heap \[heaps?\] of bones of dead men.

## \|\| 1.90.17 \|\|

*atha tatra bhramanprāptaścaṃḍālasya niveśanam \|*  
*śūnye go'sthisamākīrṇe durgaṃdhena samāvṛte \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Wandering about in the desolate region filled with stinking small and covered with bones of cows he reached the hut of a Cāṇḍāla.

## \|\| 1.90.18 \|\|

*athāpaśyanmṛtaṃ tatra sārameyaṃ ciroṣitam \|*  
*saṃśuṣkaṃ gandhanirmuktaṃ gṛhaprāṃte vyavasthitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There he saw near the residence a dog long dead, dry and rigid and odourless.

## \|\| 1.90.19 \|\|

*samādāya tatastaṃ ca āpaddharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*prakṣālya salile paścātpracakarta tadā muniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sage resorted to a practice only befitting an occasion of excessive calamity and gathered it. He washed the dead animal with water and cut it up later.

## \|\| 1.90.20-22 \|\|

*tataśca śrapayāmāsa susamiddhe hutāśane \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmo bhojanārthāya tataḥ pākāgrameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*samādāya pitṝṃstarpya yāvadagnau juhoti saḥ \|*  
*tāvadvahniḥ parityajya samastamapi bhūtalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gataścādarśanaṃ sadyaḥ sarveṣāṃ kṣitivāsinām \|*  
*citte kopaṃ samādhāya śakrasyopari bhūriśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Overwhelmed with hunger he cooked it over a well-kindled fire for the purpose of eating. He took a bit of the cooked meat, propitiated the Pitṛs and consigned it to the sacred fire. Instantly the fire left the entire earth and vanished from the view of all the inhabitants of the earth with a great anger in the mind against Śakra.

## \|\| 1.90.23 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vahnau martyalokādvinirgate \|*  
*viśeṣātpīḍitā lokā ye'vaśiṣṭā dharātale \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime, when fire went out of the mortal world, those who remained on the earth were all the more troubled.

## \|\| 1.90.24 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devā brahmaviṣṇupuraḥ sarāḥ \|*  
*vahneranveṣaṇārthāya vabhramurdharaṇītale \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the meanwhile Devas with Brahmā and Viṣṇu as their leaders wandered all over the earth in their search for the Fire-god.

## \|\| 1.90.25 \|\|

*atha tairbhramamāṇaiśca pradṛṣṭo'bhūdgajo mahān \|*  
*niśvasanpatito bhūmau vahnitāpaprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. While they were wandering thus, a great elephant was seen by them. Scorched and distressed by Vahni (Fire) he fell on the ground and breathed heavily.

## \|\| 1.90.26 \|\|

*atha devā gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā papracchustvarayā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*kaccittvayā sa dṛṣṭo'tra kānane pāvako gaja \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing the elephant, the Devas hurriedly asked it, “O elephant, we hope Fire-god was seen by you in the forest.”

## \|\| 1.90.27 \|\|

*gaja uvāca \|*  
*vaṃśastaṃbe'tra saṃkīrṇe saṃpraviṣṭo hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ tena nirdagdhaḥ kṛcchrādatrāhamāgataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

The elephant said:

27\. The Fire has entered this thickly grown cluster of bamboos now. I have been almost burnt by him. With some difficulty I have come out of it.

## \|\| 1.90.28 \|\|

*atha tairveṣṭitastasminvaṃśastaṃbe hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*devairdattvā gajeṃdrasya śāpaṃ paścādvinirgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hutāśana (Fire) was thereupon surrounded by the Devas in the cluster of bamboos. He cursed the lordly elephant and came out of it later.

## \|\| 1.90.29 \|\|

*yasmāttvayāhamādiṣṭo devānāṃ vāraṇādhama \|*  
*tasmāttava mukhe jihvā viparītā bhaviṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O base elephant, since you pointed me out to the Devas, the tongue in your mouth will be inverted.”

## \|\| 1.90.30 \|\|

*evaṃ śaptvā gajaṃ śīghraṃ naṣṭo vaiśvānaraḥ punaḥ \|*  
*devāścāpi tathā pṛṣṭhe saṃlagnāstaddidṛkṣayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After cursing the elephant thus, Vaiśvānara (Fire) vanished instantly. The Devas closely followed him to find him out.

## \|\| 1.90.31 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭaḥ śukastaiśca bhramamāṇairmahāvane \|*  
*bhobhoḥ śuka tvayā vahniryadi dṛṣṭo nivedyatām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then a parrot was seen by them as they were wandering further in the great forest. They asked, “O parrot, if Vahni is seen by you, do tell us”

## \|\| 1.90.32 \|\|

*śuka uvāca \|*  
*yo'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate dūrācchamīgarbhe ca pippalaḥ \|*  
*etasmiṃstiṣṭhate vahniraśvatthe surasattamāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

The parrot said:

32\. Yonder is seen a Pippala tree, O excellent Suras, in the midst of the Śamī grove. Vahni is present within this Aśvattha.

## \|\| 1.90.33 \|\|

*atrastho yaḥ kulāyo ma āsīcchiśusamanvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃdagdhastatpratāpena ahaṃkṛcchrādvinirgataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. My nest was amongst its branches. It has been completely burnt along with my young ones. I was able to escape with great difficulty.

## \|\| 1.90.34 \|\|

*tacchrutvā taiḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ śamīgarbhaḥ sa tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*veṣṭitaḥ pāvako'pyāśu śukaṃ śaptvā vinirgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On hearing it Pāvaka (Fire-god) stationed within Śamī was immediately surrounded by all the Suras. He cursed the parrot and went away:

## \|\| 1.90.35 \|\|

*ahaṃ yasmāttvayā pāpa devānāṃ saṃniveditaḥ \|*  
*tasmācchuka na te vāṇī vispaṣṭā saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “O sinner, my presence was divulged to the Devas (by you). Hence, O Śuka (parrot), your voice will never be clear.”

## \|\| 1.90.36-37 \|\|

*evamuktvā jātavedā devādarśanavāṃchayā \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jalāśayaṃ sugambhīraṃ pūrvottaradiksaṃsthitam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tatra praviṣṭastu nibhṛtaṃ ca samāśritaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. After saying this Jātavedas (Fire) desired that he should not be seen by the Devas. He saw a deep water pond situated on the north-eastern side of the holy spot Hāṭakeśvara of lord Parameṣṭhin. He entered it and remained there quietly.

## \|\| 1.90.38 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra matsyakacchapadardurāḥ \|*  
*vahnipratāpanirdagdhā dṛśyaṃte śataśo mṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the meantime the fishes, turtles and frogs thereof were scorched by the heat of Vahni. Hundreds of them were found dead.

## \|\| 1.90.39 \|\|

*atha caiko'rdhanirdagdha āyuḥśeṣeṇa darduraḥ \|*  
*tasmājjalādviniṣkrāṃto dṛṣṭo devaiśca dūrataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One of the frogs partially burnt because he was destined to survive, came out of the water and it was seen by the Devas from afar.

## \|\| 1.90.40 \|\|

*pṛṣṭaśca brūhi cedbheka tvayā dṛṣṭo hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*tadarthamiha saṃprāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “O Bheka (frog), tell us whether you have seen Hutāśana. It is for that purpose that all the Devas including Vāsava have come here.”

## \|\| 1.90.41 \|\|

*bheka uvāca \|*  
*asmiñjalāśaye vahniḥ sāṃprataṃ paryavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tasyaite jalamadhyasthā mṛtā bhūrijalodbhavāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

The frog said:

41\. Now Vahni is staying in this water pond. On account of him many aquatic animals are dead under water itself.

## \|\| 1.90.42 \|\|

*asmākaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptaṃ kuṭumbaṃ surasattamāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ kṛcchreṇa niṣkrāṃta etasmājjalasaṃśrayāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O excellent Suras, our families have been destroyed. It was with very difficulty that I was able to escape from this watery expanse.

## \|\| 1.90.43 \|\|

*tacchrutvā te surāḥ sarve sarvatastaṃ jalāśayam \|*  
*veṣṭayitvā sthitāstatra vahnirbhekaṃ śaśāpa ha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing it, all the Suras surrounded that water pond. Thereupon Vahni cursed the frog:

“Since, O foolish frog, I was pointed out by you to the Devas, you shall become one without a tongue on this earth”

## \|\| 1.90.45 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sthānāttato vahnirvinirgataḥ \|*  
*tāvatsa brahmaṇā proktaḥ svayameva mahātmanā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. After saying thus Vahni came out of that spot. He was then addressed by the noble-souled Brahmā himself:

## \|\| 1.90.46-51 \|\|

*bhobho vahne kimarthaṃ tvaṃ devāndṛṣṭvā pragacchasi \|*  
*tvamādyaścaiva sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ saṃsthito mukham \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tvayyāhutirhutā samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate \|*  
*ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmāddhātā vidhātā ca tvameva jagataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭe dhāryate viśvaṃ tvayi ruṣṭe vinaṃkṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

*agniṣṭomādikā yajñāstvayi sarve pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*atha sarvāṇi bhūtāni jīvaṃti tava saṃśrayāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tvamagne sarvabhūtānāmantaścarasi sarvadā \|*  
*tenaivānnaṃ ca pānaṃ ca jaṭharasthaṃ pacatyalama \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ tvaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām \|*  
*kopasya kāraṇaṃ brūhi yatastyaktvā pragacchasi \|\| 51 \|\|*

46-51. “O Vahni, why do you run away on seeing the Devas. Originally you have been their very mouth. If an Āhuti is duly offered to you it goes to Āditya (Sun). From Āditya is born rain, from that the food-grain and from it subjects arise. Hence you have become Dhātā (creator) and Vidhātā (dispenser) of the universe. If you are pleased the universe is sustained. If you are angry it will perish.

All the Yajñas beginning with Agniṣṭoma are established in you. Then all the living beings sustain themselves through your support.

O Agni, you move about always within all living beings. Thereby the food and beverage taken is become digested.

Hence be pleased with all the Heaven-dwellers. Speak out the reason for your anger whereby you leave them and move out.”

## \|\| 1.90.52 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*provāca praṇayātkopaṃ kṛtvā natvā ca padmajam \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sūta said:

52\. On hearing those words of Lord Parameṣṭhin, Agni pretended to be angry because of his love, bowed down to the Lotus-born One and said:

## \|\| 1.90.53 \|\|

*agniruvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ kopaṃ samādhāya śakrasyopari padmaja \|*  
*praṇaṣṭo jagadutsṛjya yasmāttatkāraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 53 \|\|*

Agni said:

53\. I was angry with Śakra, O Lotus-born One, and so left the universe and vanished. Listen to the reason thereof.

## \|\| 1.90.54 \|\|

*anāvṛṣṭyā mahendrasya saṃjātaścauṣadhīkṣayaḥ \|*  
*tato'smyahaṃ śvamāṃsena viśvāmitreṇa yojitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Since Mahendra held back the downpour of rain, it resulted in damage to vegetation and medicinal herbs. As a result thereof I was offered the flesh of a dog by Viśvāmitra.

## \|\| 1.90.55 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇānnaṣṭo na kāmānna ca saṃbhramāt \|*  
*abhakṣyabhakṣaṇādbhītaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. For this reason I vanished, not out of capriciousness or because of any mistake. I was afraid of eating the forbidden stuff. The truth has been told by me.

## \|\| 1.90.56 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sa caturvaktraḥ śakramāha tataḥ param \|*  
*yuktameva śikhī prāha kimarthaṃ na ca varṣasi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On hearing it the Four-faced One said to Śakra “What Śikhin (Fire) says in cogent? Why don’t you send down rain?”

## \|\| 1.90.57 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramullaṃghya śaṃtanuḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahe rājye sa niviṣṭaḥ pitāmaha \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śakra said:

57\. O Pitāmaha, Śantanu has been installed in the hereditary kingdom out of turn by transgressing his elder brother (Devāpi).

## \|\| 1.90.58 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādvṛṣṭiḥ saṃniruddhā mayā prabho \|*  
*tadbrūhi kiṃ karomyadya tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ pitāmaha \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It is for this reason, O Lord, that the rain has been held back by me. Do tell me what shall I do now? O Pitāmaha you are the ultimate authority.

## \|\| 1.90.59 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca \|*  
*tasyākramasya saṃprāptaṃ pāpaṃ tena mahībhujā \|*  
*upabhuktamavṛṣṭyādya tasmādvṛṣṭiṃ kuru drutam \|\| 59 \|\|*

Pitāmaha said:

59\. The sin of that irregularity has been already incurred and the result experienced by that king by way of the drougḥt. Now do shower the rain quickly.

## \|\| 1.90.60 \|\|

*madvākyādyāti no nāśaṃ yāvadetajjagattrayam \|*  
*akālenāpi devendra sasyābhāvādbubhukṣayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Do everything at my behest, O Devendra, lest the three worlds perish ultimately through the want of vegetation and the attack of hunger.

## \|\| 1.90.61 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śakra ādideśa tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*puṣkarāvartakānmeghānvṛṣṭyarthaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In the meantime Śakra hurriedly ordered the Puṣkarāvartaka clouds to pour down rain on the earth.

## \|\| 1.90.62 \|\|

*te'pi śakrasamādeśātsamastadharaṇītalam \|*  
*tatkṣaṇātpūrayāmāsurgarjanto vidyudanvitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. At the bidding of Śakra they began to rumble and display lightning. In an instant, they filled the entire earth with water.

## \|\| 1.90.63 \|\|

*athābravītpunarbrahmā devaiḥ sārdhaṃ hutāśanam \|*  
*agnihotreṣu viprāṇāṃ pratyakṣo bhava pāvaka \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ tvaṃ varaṃ mattaḥ prārthayasvābhivāṃchitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then Brahmā along with the Devas spoke again to Hutāśana: “O Pāvaka, be visible to the Brāhmaṇas in the course of the Agnihotras. Now, do request me for any desired boon.”

## \|\| 1.90.64 \|\|

*agniruvāca \|*  
*ayaṃ jalāśayaḥ puṇyo mannāmnā pṛthivītale \|*  
*khyātiṃ yātu caturvaktra vahnitīrthamiti smṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

Agni said:

64\. O Four-faced One, may this watery expanse become meritorious and well-known all over the earth as Vahnitīrtha after my name.

## \|\| 1.90.65 \|\|

*atra yaḥ prātarutthāya snātvā śraddhā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*agnisūktaṃ japitvā ca tvāṃ prapaśyati sādaram \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭistvayā kāryā drutaṃ madvākyataḥ prabho \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If any devotee endowed with faith gets up early in morning, takes his holy bath, recites Agnisūkta and sees you respectfully, O Lord, you should be pleased with him. Do this kindly at my instance.

## \|\| 1.90.66-67 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*atra yaḥ prātarutthāya snātvā vai vedaviddvijaḥ \|*  
*agnisūktaṃ japitvā ca vīkṣayiṣyati māṃ tataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*agniṣṭomasya yajñasya sakalaṃ lapsyate phalam \|*  
*anekajanmajaṃ pāpaṃ nāśameṣyati pāvaka \|\| 67 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

66-67. If a Brāhmaṇa, conversant with the Vedas, gets up early in morning, takes his holy bath, recites Agnisūkta and then sees me, he will obtain the entire benefit of Agniṣṭoma Yajña. O Pāvaka, sins originating from many births will perish.

## \|\| 1.90.68 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa bhagavānvirarāma pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*pāvako'pi ca viprāṇāmagnihotreṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Sūta said:

68\. After saying thus, Lord Pitāmaha stopped, Pāvaka too stationed himself in the Agnihotras of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.90.69 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samudbhūtaṃ vahnitīrthaṃ mahādbhutam \|*  
*tatra snāto naraḥ prātaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thus the highly miraculous Vahnitīrtha originated there. A man who takes his holy bath (therein) in morning is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.90.70 \|\|

*agniruvāca \|\| mamātṛptasya lokeśa tāvaddvādaśavatsarān \|*  
*kṣutpīḍāsaṃvṛte martye na prāptaṃ kutraciddhaviḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Agni said:

70\. O Lord of the worlds, I remained unpropitiated for twelve years. As the mortal world was afflicted by hunger, I never got Havis anywhere.

## \|\| 1.90.71 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃti tathā yajñā kālena mahatā vibho \|*  
*saṃjātaiḥ paśubhirbhūyaḥ sasyādairaparairbhuvi \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Of course, Yajñas will be performed in future, O lord, in the course of a long time with herbivorous and other types of animals which afterwards will be born on the earth.

## \|\| 1.90.72-73 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*atra ye brāhmaṇāḥ kecinnivasaṃti hutāśana \|*  
*vasorddhārāpradānena te tvāṃ naktaṃdinaṃ sadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tarpayiṣyaṃti sadbhaktyā tataḥ puṣṭimavāpsyasi \|*  
*te'pi kāmyairmano'bhīṣṭairbhaviṣyaṃti samanvitāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

72-73. O Hutāśana, the few Brāhmaṇas who reside here will offer Vasordhārā (continuous flow of Havis etc., into the fire) day and night for ever. They will propitiate you and you will get nourished. They too will be requitted with all desirable things when their wishes are realized.

## \|\| 1.90.74-75 \|\|

*saṃkrāṃti samaye yeṣāṃ vasordhārāpradāyinām \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kṣutaṃ vahne hūyamāne tavānala \|\| 74 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ pāpaṃ ca yatkiṃcijjñānato'jñānataḥ kṛtam \|*  
*tadyāsyati kṣayaṃ sarvamājanmamaraṇāṃtikam \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. O Anala (Fire-god), when Homa is being performed at the time of Saṅkrānti (transit of the Sun), those who offer Vasordhārā may be sneezing. The sins of such persons committed knowingly or unknowingly ever since their birth and until the death, will be destroyed.

## \|\| 1.90.76 \|\|

*tvayi tuṣṭiṃ gate paścādbhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*śibirnāma suvikhyāta uśīnarasamudravaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. When you are satisfied all this will take place. Later on a well-known king named Śibi will be born in the land of Uśīnara.

## \|\| 1.90.77 \|\|

*sa kṛtvā śraddhayā yuktaḥ satraṃ dvādaśavārṣikam \|*  
*vasorddhārāpradānena varṣaṃ tvāṃ tarpayiṣyati \|*  
*kalaśasya ca vaktreṇāvicchinnena divāniśam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He will be endowed with perfect faith. He will be performing a Sattra lasting for twelve years. He will offer you Vasordhārā day and night through the mouth of a water-pot with continuous flow of the current.

## \|\| 1.90.78 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭiṃ parāṃ prāpya parāṃ puṣṭimavāpsyasi \|*  
*pūjyamāno dharāpṛṣṭhe sarvairvedavidāṃ varaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thereby you will be fully satisfied and get completely nourished. You will be worshipped on the surface of the world by all the most excellent of those conversant with the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.90.79 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti yatkiṃcitkarma cātra bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ vāpi vasorddhārāsamanvitam \|*  
*saṃbhaviṣyati tatsarvaṃ tava tṛptikaraṃ param \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. From now onwards, whatever holy rite may take place either Śāntika (contributory to peace) or Pauṣṭika (nourishing) should be accompanied by Vasordhārā. All those will cause great satisfaction unto you.

## \|\| 1.90.80 \|\|

*api yadvaiśvadevīyaṃ karma kiṃciddvijanmanām \|*  
*vasorddhārāvihīnaṃ ca niṣphalaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The Vaiśvadevīya holy rite of the Brāhmaṇas will be futile if it is devoid of Vasordhārā.

## \|\| 1.90.81 \|\|

*yasmādbhavati saṃpūrṇaṃ karma yajñādikaṃ hi tat \|*  
*śāṃtikaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca pūrṇāhutirihocyate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Since Yajña and other rites, the Śāntika, Pauṣṭika and Vaiśvadevīya become perfect and complete it is called Pūrṇāhuti.

## \|\| 1.90.82 \|\|

*yaḥ samyakchraddhayā yukto vasorddhārāṃ pradāsyati \|*  
*sa kāmaṃ manasā dhyātaṃ samavāpsyati kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. One who is endowed with faith and offers Vasordhārā shall entirely attain his desire mentally cherished.

## Chapter 91 - Creation of Agni Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.91.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa bhagavānvirarāma pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*saṃtoṣya pāvakaṃ kruddhaṃ svayameva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ sarvaiḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ śakraviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ \|*  
*jagāma brahmalokaṃ ca devāste ca nijaṃ padam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pāvako'pi dvijeṃdrāṇāmagnihotreṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*havirjagrāha vidhivadvasorddhārodbhavaṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: The story of Agni cursing the animals detailed in vv. 25-45 of the last chapter is found in Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana 85.28-40.

Sūta said:

1-3. After saying thus and consoling Fire-god who was angry, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Lord Pitāmaha stopped.

Then he went to Brahmaloka along with all the Suras including Śakra, Viṣṇu and Śiva. The Devas went to their region.

Pāvaka stationed himself in the Agnihotras of leading Brāhmaṇas. He duly accepted the Havis issuing from Vasordhārā.

## \|\| 1.91.4 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samudbhūtamagnitīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra snāto naraḥ prātarmucyate dinajādaghāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was thus that the excellent Agnitīrtha originated there. A man who takes his holy bath there in morning is rid of the sins accrued that day.

## \|\| 1.91.5 \|\|

*atha saṃprasthitāndṛṣṭvā tāndevānsvāśramaṃ prati \|*  
*gajeṃdraśukamaṇḍūkāste procurduḥkhasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing those Devas set off to their abodes, those leading elephant, parrot and frog spoke in their great misery:

## \|\| 1.91.6 \|\|

*yuṣmatkṛte vayaṃ śaptāḥ pāvakena sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*tasmājjihvākṛte'smākamupāyaściṃtyatāmapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “O leading Suras, was have been cursed by Pāvaka because of you. Hence think about the means for restoring our tongues.”

## \|\| 1.91.7 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*viparītāpi te jihvā yathānyeṣāṃ gajottama \|*  
*kāryakṣamā na saṃdeho bhaviṣyati viśeṣataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

The Devas said:

7\. O excellent elephant, though your tongue as in the case of others is inverted, it shall be especially efficient in its work. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.91.8 \|\|

*tathā yūyaṃ narendrāṇāṃ maṃdireṣu vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*bahu mānasamāyuktā mṛṣṭānnaṃ bhakṣayiṣyatha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Further, all of you residing in the palaces of leading kings will be honoured duly and you will eat sweet food in plenty.

## \|\| 1.91.9 \|\|

*yathā ca śuka te jihvā kṛtā maṃdā havirbhujā \|*  
*tathāpi bhūmipālānāṃ śaṃsanīyā bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O parrot, though your tongue has been made dull by Havirbhuj (Fire-god), still it shall be worthy of the praise of kings.

## \|\| 1.91.10 \|\|

*śrīmatāṃ ca tathānyeṣāmasmadīyaprasādataḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ ca maṃḍūka yattena vijihvo vahninā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadbhaviṣyati te śabdo vijihvasyāpi dīrghagaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Further, with our favour, you shall be worthy of the praise of other rich and glorious persons too.

O frog, though you have been rendered devoid of a tongue by Vahni, your croaking voice shall be long and loud.

## \|\| 1.91.11 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha te devāḥ svasthānaṃ prasthitāstataḥ \|*  
*teṣāmanugrahaṃ kṛtvā kṛpayā parayā yutā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After saying thus and blessing them sympathetically the Devas proceeded to their abode.

## Chapter 92 - Greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa (Importance of Bhīṣma-pañcaka Vrata)

## \|\| 1.92.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*agnitīrthasya māhātmyametadvaḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*brahmakuṃḍasamutpattiradhunā śrūyatāṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadā saṃsthāpito brahmā mārkaṃḍena mahātmanā \|*  
*tadā vinirmitaṃ tatra kuṇḍaṃ śucijalānvitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*proktaṃ ca kārtike māsi kṛttikāsthe niśākare \|*  
*samyagbhīṣmavrataṃ kṛtvā snātvātra salile śubhe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūjayiṣyati yo devaṃ padmayoniṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*sa śūdro'pi tanuṃ tyaktvā brahmayonau prayāsyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇo'pi yadi snānaṃ tatra kuṇḍe kariṣyati \|*  
*kṛtvā bhīṣmavrataṃ samyagbrahmalokaṃ prayāsyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-5. Thus the greatness of Agnitīrtha has been narrated to you. Now the origin of Brahmakuṇḍa may be listened to, O Brāhmaṇas.

When Brahmā was installed by the noble-souled Mārkaṇḍa, a Kuṇḍa was also created there with crystal-clear water.

This was also proclaimed that in the month of Kārttika, when the Moon is in the constellation Kṛttikā a devotee should observe the Bhīṣmavrata properly, take his holy bath here in the auspicious waters and worship the Lotus-born Lord thereafter. Even if he is a Śūdra, he will attain Brāhmaṇa womb (i.e. will be reborn as a Brāhmaṇa) after casting off this body. A Brāhmaṇa who, after properly observing the Bhīṣmavrata, takes his holy bath there in the Kuṇḍa, will go to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.92.6 \|\|

*evaṃ pravadatastasya mārkaṃḍeyasya sanmuneḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ tatsakalaṃ vākyaṃ paśupālena kenacit \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even as the excellent sage Mārkaṇḍeya was narrating thus, the entire speech was heard by a certain cowherd.

## \|\| 1.92.7 \|\|

*tataḥ śraddhāprayuktena tena tadbhīṣmapaṃcakam \|*  
*yathāvadvihitaṃ samyakkārtike māsi saṃsthite \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then the Bhīṣmapañcaka Vrata was dully observed by him with great ardour and faith in the Month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 1.92.8 \|\|

*tataśca kṛttikāyoge pūrṇimāyāṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*saṃpūjya padmajaṃ paścātpūjitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter on the full-Moon day when the Moon was in conjunction with Kṛttikā, he adored (at first) the Lotus-born Lord and afterwards Puruṣottama.

## \|\| 1.92.9 \|\|

*tataḥ kālavipākena sa paṃcatvamupāgataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya gṛhe jātaḥ pure'traiva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*jātismaraḥ prabhāyuktaḥ pitṛmātṛpratuṣṭidaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, as time passed on, he died, O Brāhmaṇas and he was reborn in this city itself in the house of a Brāhmaṇa. Endowed with great lustre, he gave his father and mother great pleasure. Further he could remember the previous birth too.

## \|\| 1.92.10-12 \|\|

*evaṃ pragacchatastasya vṛddhiṃ tatra purottame \|*  
*pitṛmātṛsamudbhūto yādṛksneho vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*anyadehodbhave vāpi tasya śūdreparisthitaḥ \|*  
*sa tasya dhanasaṃpannaḥ sadaiva kurute dvijaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*upakārapradānaṃ ca yatkiṃcittasya saṃmatam \|*  
*anyasmindivase śūdraḥ sa pitā pūrvajanmanaḥ \|*  
*tasya pañcatvamāpannaḥ saṃprāpte cāyuṣaḥ kṣaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. He grew prosperous thus in that excellent city. He entertained the same affection towards the father of the (previous) Śūdra birth as he had towards the parents (of this birth). The reborn Brāhmaṇa who was rich rendered all help to him and did everything approved by him. One day, as the span of life came to a close, the Śūdra father of the previous birth died.

## \|\| 1.92.13 \|\|

*atha tasya mahāśokaṃ sa kṛtvā tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*cakāra pretakāryāṇi niḥśeṣāṇi prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Brāhmaṇa son lamented much over this and performed all the rites due to the departed one without omitting anything. He had such a great devotion.

## \|\| 1.92.14 \|\|

*atha tasya samālokya tādṛśaṃ tadviceṣṭitam \|*  
*pṛṣṭaḥ sa kautukāviṣṭaiḥ pitṛmātṛsutādibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On noticing such an act on his part, he was asked by his father, mother, son and others (of this birth) out of curiosity:

## \|\| 1.92.15-16 \|\|

*kasmāttvamasya nīcasya paśupālasya sarvadā \|*  
*atisnehasamāyukto niḥspṛhasyāpi śaṃsa naḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tasyāpi pretakāryāṇi mṛtasyāpi karoṣi kim \|*  
*etannaḥ sarvamācakṣva na cedguhyaṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. “Why are you always extremely friendly to this lowborn cowherd although he seemed to expect nothing? Do tell us. Why did you perform the obsequies when he passed away? Kindly explain this entirely if it is not a great secret.”

## \|\| 1.92.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kiṃcillajjāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tānabravīcchṛṇudhvaṃ ca kathayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing their words he became slightly abashed. He told them, “Listen. I shall certainly narrate it.

## \|\| 1.92.18 \|\|

*ahamasyānyadehatve putra āsaṃ susaṃmataḥ \|*  
*paśupālanakarmajñaḥ prāṇebhyo vallabhaḥ sadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the previous birth, I was his duly honoured son dearer to him than his own life. I was well-versed in the art and craft of cattle-breeding.

## \|\| 1.92.19 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya mārkaṃḍasya mahāmuneḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ pravadato vākyaṃ brahmakuṇḍasamudbhavam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Once, even as the great sage Mārkaṇḍa was speaking, I heard his statement referring to Brahmakuṇḍa:

## \|\| 1.92.20-21 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge bhīṣmapañcakakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*samyakchraddhāsamutpanno yo'tra snānaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaṃ devaṃ pūjayitvā janārdanam \|*  
*sa bhaviṣyati śūdro'pi brāhmaṇaścānyajanmani \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. ‘A man endowed with perfect faith, who observes the Bhīṣmapañcakavrata on the full-moon day in the month of Kārttika when the Moon is in conjunction with the Kṛttikā constellation, takes his holy bath here, visits Lord Pitāmaha and worships Janārdana shall become a Brāhmaṇa in the next birth even if he happens to be a Śūdra.’

## \|\| 1.92.22 \|\|

*tanmayā vihitaṃ samyaksnātvā tatra śubhāvahe \|*  
*sukuṇḍe kārtike māsi tena jāto'smi saddvijaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. That observance was done by me after taking the holy bath in the sacred Kuṇḍa in the month of Kārttika. Hence I was reborn as an excellent Brāhamaṇa.

## \|\| 1.92.23 \|\|

*candrodayasya viprarṣeranvaye bhuvi viśrute \|*  
*saṃsmaranpūrvikāṃ jāti tena sneho mama sthitaḥ \|*  
*tasyopari mahānnityaṃ śūdrasyāpi nirargalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I was born in the well-known family of Candrodaya, a Brāhmaṇa-sage. I could recollect the previous birth. Hence I became excessively affectionate towards that Śūdra too without \[?any?\] inhibition.

## \|\| 1.92.24 \|\|

*ato'haṃ kṛttikāyoge kārtikyāṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā karomi bhīṣmasya paṃcakaṃ vratamuttamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Therefore (even now) I fully realize and devoutly perform the excellent Bhīṣmapañcaka Vrata on the full-moon day in the month of Kārttika when there is the conjunction of the full-Moon with the Kṛttikā constellation.

## \|\| 1.92.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā te cānye ca dvijottamāḥ \|\| \|*  
*bhīṣmasya pañcakaṃ cakruḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sūta said:

25\. On hearing his words, they and other excellent Brāhmaṇas observed the Bhīṣmapañcaka Vrata with perfect ardour and faith.

## \|\| 1.92.26 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tatkuṇḍaṃ vikhyātaṃ dharaṇītale \|*  
*sthitamuttaradigbhāge brahmakuṇḍamiti smṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Ever since then that Kuṇḍa became well-known as Brahmakuṇḍa all over the earth. It is situated on the northern side.

## \|\| 1.92.27 \|\|

*yaḥ snānaṃ sarvadā tatra brāhmaṇaḥ prakaroti vai \|*  
*sa saṃbhavati vipreṃdro jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A Brāhmaṇa who always takes his holy bath there, is reborn as a leading Brāhmaṇa frequently.

## Chapter 93 - Greatness of Gomukha Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.93.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athānyadapi tatrāsti gomukhākhyaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*yadgovaktrātpurā labdhaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*purāsīdatra gopālaḥ kaścitkuṣṭhasamāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ vipra atīva kṣāmatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tena mārgeṇa gokulam \|*  
*madhyāhnasamaye prāptaṃ caṃdre citrāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Then, there is another excellent Tīrtha named Gomukha. It is destructive of all sins. The name was obtained on account of (its resemblance to) the face of a cow.

Formerly there was a Brāhmaṇa cowherd in Camatkārapura. He was afflicted with leprosy and was utterly emaciated.

Once upon a time, a herd of cows came that way at midday when the Moon was in conjunction with the Citrā constellation.

## \|\| 1.93.4 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ tṛṣārttaṃ ca bhāskare vṛṣasaṃsthite \|*  
*ekayāpi tato dhenvā tṛṇastambamatīva hi \|*  
*nīlamālokitaṃ tatra dūrādetya praharṣitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was the eleventh lunar day. The Sun was in the zodiac of Taurus. The herd was extremely thirsty. One of the cows saw from a distance a blue spot excessively dark in colour. She was highly delighted.

## \|\| 1.93.5 \|\|

*dantairdrutaṃ samutpāṭya yāvadākarṣati dvijāḥ \|*  
*tāvattajjaḍamārgeṇa toyadhārā vinirgatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She dug it up with her teeth, O Brāhmaṇas, and pulled it (the grass) quickly. A current of water flowed through the passage of the roots.

## \|\| 1.93.6 \|\|

*athāsvādya tṛṇaṃ tasmāttṛṣārtā ca śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*papau toyaṃ suviśrabdhā susvādu kṣīrasaṃnibham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The cow grazed the grass and confidently drank the tasty water that was like milk.

## \|\| 1.93.7 \|\|

*tasyā vegena tattoyaṃ pibantyāstatrabhūtale \|*  
*gartā jātā suvistīrṇā salilena samāvṛtā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Even as the cow drank the water rapidly, a deep and wide pit took shape on the. ground. It was filled with water.

## \|\| 1.93.8 \|\|

*tato'nyāḥ śataśo gāvaḥ papustoyaṃ munirmalam \|*  
*tṛṣārttāstaddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ pīyūṣarasasaṃnibham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, hundreds of other cows also drank the pure nectar-like water as she did when distressed with thirst.

## \|\| 1.93.9 \|\|

*yathāyathā gatā gāvastatra toyaṃ pibaṃti tāḥ \|*  
*sā gartā vaktrasaṃsparśādvṛddhiṃ yāti tathā tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. As the cows went on drinking the water, the pit grew in size due to the contact with the mouths of the cows.

## \|\| 1.93.10 \|\|

*tataśca gokule kṛtsne jāte tṛṣṇāvivarjite \|*  
*gopālo'pi tṛṣārtastu tasmiṃstoye viveśa ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. As the entire herd of the cows quenched their thirst, the thirsty cowherd too entered the water-pond.

## \|\| 1.93.11 \|\|

*aṃgaṃ prakṣālya pītvāpo yāvanniṣkrāmati drutam \|*  
*tāvatpaśyati gātraṃ svaṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He washed his body, drank the water and quickly came out of the water. He then saw his body as lustrous as a group of twelve Suns.

## \|\| 1.93.12 \|\|

*tato vismayamāpanno gatvā svīyaṃ niketanam \|*  
*vṛtāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa lokānāṃ purato'khilam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He was wonder-struck. After going to his abode he mentioned the incident fully to all the people.

## \|\| 1.93.13 \|\|

*tṛṇastambaṃ yathā dhenvā tatrotpāṭya praśaktitaḥ \|*  
*yathā vinirgataṃ toyaṃ yathā tenāvagāhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He told them how the clump of grass was pulled out by the cow with force, how the water gushed out and how he plunged therein.

## \|\| 1.93.14 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā mānavāḥ sarve gatvā divyaṃ jalaṃ ca tat \|*  
*vyādhigrastā viśeṣeṇa snānaṃ cakruḥ samāhitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing the divine water-pond, all men, especially those who were diseased, took their holy bath with great mental concentration and purity.

## \|\| 1.93.15 \|\|

*bhavaṃti ca vinirmuktā rogaiḥ pāpaiśca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*apāpāśca punaryāṃti tatkṣaṇāttridivālayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They were rid of their ailments and sins instantly. Freed from sins, they went to heaven at the same moment.

## \|\| 1.93.16 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tatkhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ gomukhasaṃjñitam \|*  
*gomukhādbhūtale jātaṃ yataścaivaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ever since then that Tīrtha became well-known by the name Gomukha, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, because it originated through the mouth of a cow.

## \|\| 1.93.17 \|\|

*atha bhītaḥ sahasrākṣastaddṛṣṭvā svargadāyakam \|*  
*akleśena manuṣyāṇāṃ pūrayāmāsa pāṃsubhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter, the Thousand-eyed One observed that it yielded heavenly pleasures to men without any pain or exertion on their part. He became afraid thereby and filled it with dust particles.

## \|\| 1.93.18 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tatkāraṇamādiṣṭaṃ yena tattādṛśaṃ jalam \|*  
*tasmātsthānādviniṣkrāṃtaṃ sūtaputra vadasva naḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

The sages said:

18\. What was the cause of such a flow of water from that place? O son of Sūta, do narrate it to us.

## \|\| 1.93.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra pūrvaṃ tapastaptamambarīṣeṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*putra śokābhibhūtena toṣito garuḍadhvajaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. Here king Aṃbarīṣa had performed a penance. Formerly when he was overwhelmed by the bereavement of his son, the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord was propitiated by him.

## \|\| 1.93.20 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ suvikhyātaḥ suvarcā iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*eko babhūva vṛddhatve kathaṃciddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, somehow he begot a son during his old age. This son was very well-known as Suvarcas.

## \|\| 1.93.21 \|\|

*pūrvakarmavipākena sa bālo'pi ca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhisamākrāṃtaḥ pitṛmātṛsuduḥkhadaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even as a child that son was afflicted with the foul disease of leprosy as a result of his previous Karinas. He caused much distress to his father and mother.

## \|\| 1.93.22 \|\|

*atha tatkāmikaṃ kṣetraṃ sa gatvā pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*cakāra roganāśāya svaputrārthaṃ mahattapaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereupon, the king went to that holy spot that yielded desired benefits. On behalf of his son, he performed a great penance to get rid of his ailment.

## \|\| 1.93.23 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭiṃ gatastasya svayameva janārdanaḥ \|*  
*pradāya darśanaṃ vākyaṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Janārdana became pleased. He himself granted his vision and spoke graciously these words:

## \|\| 1.93.24 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa tasmāccitte'bhivāṃchitam \|*  
*prārthayasva prayacchāmi varaṃ putra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “O dear one, I am very much pleased with you. Request for whatever is desired by you in your heart. Dear son, undoubtedly I shall grant you the boon.”

## \|\| 1.93.25 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*mamāyaṃ saṃmataḥ putro grastaḥ kuṣṭhena keśava \|*  
*bālo'pi tatkuruṣvāsya kuṣṭhavyādhiparikṣayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

The king said:

25\. O Keśava, this well-esteemed son of mine has become afflicted with leprosy, though he is still a young boy. Do get his leprosy cured completely.

## \|\| 1.93.26 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*eṣa āsītpurā rājā meghavāhanasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇyaśca kṛtajñaśca sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

26\. He was formerly a king named Meghavāhana. He was a person who esteemed Brāhmaṇas. He was grateful. He had mastered all the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.93.27 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya brāhmaṇo'nena ghātitaḥ \|*  
*aṃtaḥpure niśākāle praviṣṭo jārakarmakṛta \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Once a Brāhmaṇa entered his female apartment for adultery. He was therefore killed (by the king).

## \|\| 1.93.28 \|\|

*atha paśyati yāvatsa prabhāte'bhyudite ravau \|*  
*yajñopavītasaṃyuktastāvatsa dvijarūpadhṛk \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When he saw him in the morning after the sunrise, with a sacred thread, he realized that he was a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.93.29 \|\|

*atha taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ matvā ghṛṇāviṣṭaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*gatvā kāśīpurīṃ paścāttapaścakre samāhitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He was certain that he was a Brāhmaṇa. He got distressed and became disgusted with his own action. He went to the city of Kāśī later and performed a penance with great concentration and mental purity.

## \|\| 1.93.30 \|\|

*rājye putraṃ samādhāya vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*niyato niyatāhāro bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He installed his son in the kingdom. After becoming utterly disgusted with worldly life, he observed all restraints and restricted his diet to the alms he received by begging.

## \|\| 1.93.31-32 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena saṃprāpto yamasya sadanaṃ prati \|*  
*vipāpmāpi ca cihnena yukto'yaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*brahmaghātodbhavenaiva bālabhāve'pi saṃsthite \|*  
*ye'tra kuṣṭhasamāyuktā dṛśyaṃte mānavā bhuvi \|*  
*tairnūnaṃ brāhmaṇāghāto vihitaścānyajanmani \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. In due course of time he reached Yama’s abode. Though he was otherwise sinless, he had all the signs of having committed Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. So the king in his rebirth became a leper even in his childhood. In the case of men who appear in the world suffering from leprosy, it is certain that Brāhmaṇa’s slaughter was committed by them in the previous birth.

## \|\| 1.93.33 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yo gatvā śrāddhamācaret \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāmanṛṇaḥ sa prajāyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One who goes to the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara and performs Śrāddha unto all the Pitṛs shall be free from indebtedness to them.

## \|\| 1.93.34 \|\|

*na brāhmaṇavadhādbāhyaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*etatsatyaṃ vijānīhi vadato mama bhūpate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The fell disease of leprosy afflicts none except’those who committed the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa. Even as I say this, O king, know that this is the truth.

## \|\| 1.93.35 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*etadarthaṃ surādhīśa mayā tvaṃ pūjitaḥ prabho \|*  
*prasanne tvayi deveśa nāsādhyaṃ vidyate bhuvi \|\| 35 \|\|*

Aṃbamrīṣa said:

35\. It is for this, O Lord of Suras, that you have been worshipped by me. If you are pleased, O Lord of Devas, there is nothing which cannot be achieved on the earth.

## \|\| 1.93.36 \|\|

*evamuktastatastena bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*pātālajāhnavītoyaṃ sa sasmāra samādhinā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On being told thus by him, Lord Madhusūdana remembered through his mental absorption the water of the Jāhnavī of nether-worlds.

## \|\| 1.93.37 \|\|

*sā dhyātā sahasā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*kṛtvā tu vivaraṃ sūkṣmaṃ viniṣkrāṃtā'tha tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On being meditated upon thus by the powerful Viṣṇu, she suddenly made a subtle crevice and gushed through it instantly.

## \|\| 1.93.38-39 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca vacanamaṃbarīṣaṃ caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*nimajjatu sutaste'tra supuṇye jāhnavījale \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yena kuṣṭhavinirmuktastatkṣaṇādeva jāyate \|*  
*tathā brahmavadhodbhūtaiḥ pātakairupapātakaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Then the Four-armed Lord spoke these words to Aṃbarīṣa: “Let your son dive into this extremely meritorious water of the Jāhnavī. Thereby he shall instantly be rid of the leprosy as well as the major and minor sins of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.”

## \|\| 1.93.40 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu samānīya sutaṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*snāpayāmāsa tattoyaiḥ pratyakṣaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. At the same time, the king brought his son and made him bath in the waters thereof in the very presence of the Lord having Śārṅga as his bow.

## \|\| 1.93.41 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bālakaḥ sadyaḥ snātamātro dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhivinirmukto jāto bālārkasaṃnibhaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, immediately after his bath, the boy was rid of the fell disease of leprosy. He attained the refulgence of the morning Sun.

## \|\| 1.93.42 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ devaṃ harṣeṇa mahatā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*pitrā samaṃ jagāmātha svakīyaṃ bhavanaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereafter, O Brāhmaṇas, he bowed down to the Lord with great joy. Then he went to his abode along with his son.

## \|\| 1.93.43 \|\|

*tasmingate mahīpāle saputre tatkṣaṇāddhariḥ \|*  
*tadraṃdhraṃ pūrayāmāsa yathā no vetti kaścana \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When the king went away along with his son Hari instantly filled up that hole lest anyone should see it.

## \|\| 1.93.44 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇātpūrvaṃ tattoyaṃ sarvapāpahṛt \|*  
*yadgomukhena bhūyo'pi bhūtale prakaṭīkṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It is for this reason that the water that had formerly dispelled all sins became manifest once again through the mouth of the cow.

## \|\| 1.93.45 \|\|

*adyāpi tajjalasparśātsupavitro dharātale \|*  
*yaḥ snānaṃ sūryavāreṇa kurute'rkodayaṃ prati \|*  
*tasya nāśaṃ drutaṃ yāṃti galagaṃḍādikā iha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Even today, if anyone on the earth gets himself sanctified by touching that water and takes the holy ablution on a Sunday at the time of sunrise, all ailments of his such as goitre (enlargement of the thyroid etc.) become destroyed.

## \|\| 1.93.46 \|\|

*vyādhayopi mahāraudrā dadrupāmā samudbhavāḥ \|*  
*upasargodbhavāścaiva visphoṭakavicarcikā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Other ailments of very terrible symptoms, such as scabies, itches etc., swellings etc., arising from contact etc., become destroyed.

## \|\| 1.93.47 \|\|

*niṣkāmastu punarmartyo yaḥ snānaṃ tatra bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*kurute yāti lokaṃ sa devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A man having no desire, who takes his holy bath devoutly there shall go to the world of the Discus-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.93.48-50 \|\|

*yasmindine samānītā sā gaṃgā tatra viṣṇunā \|*  
*tasmindine vṛṣe sūryaḥ sthitaścitrāsu caṃdramāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tithiścaikādaśī caiva devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|*  
*govaktreṇa tṛṇastaṃbaṃ yasmiṃścaiva tu vāsare \|*  
*samākṛṣṭaṃ ca tatraiva yoga evaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tathānye'pi dine tasminyadi toyamavāpya ca \|*  
*snānaṃ karoti sadbhaktyā tatphalaṃ so'pi cāpnuyāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. The day on which Gaṅgā was brought by Viṣṇu coincided with the transit of the Sun to the zodiac of Taurus; the Moon was in the Citrā constellation. It was the eleventh lunar day, that of the Sārṅga-bowed Lord of Devas. On the day (i.e. eleventh day in the bright half of Vaiśākha) when the clump of grasses was pulled out by the cow’s mouth, the Yoga (combination) of the Planets etc.., was the same.

Hence, anyone who takes his holy bath there on any similar day with great devotion shall obtain the benefit thereof.

## Chapter 94 - Greatness of Lohayaṣṭi

## \|\| 1.94.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*tathānyā lohayaṣṭistu tasminkṣetre'tiśobhanā \|*  
*muktā paraśurāmeṇa bhaṃktvā nijakuṭhārakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ samyagupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*mucyate hi svakātpāpāttatkṣaṇādvijasattamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. There is another holy object in that holy spot, namely the splendid Lohayaṣṭi (iron staff), which was abandoned by Paraśurāma after breaking his Kuṭhāra (axe). O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a man who perfectly observes fast and sees it, is rid of his sins at the very instant.

## \|\| 1.94.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kutaḥ paraśurāmeṇa bhaṃktvā nijakuṭhārakam \|*  
*nirmitā lohayaṣṭiḥ sā tatrotsṛṣṭā ca sā kutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. Why was his axe broken by Paraśurāma? Why was the iron staff made? Why was it left there?

## \|\| 1.94.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā rāmo hradaṃ kṛtvā tarpayitvā nijānpitṝn \|*  
*gatāmarṣo dvijendrāṇāṃ dattvā yajñe vasundharām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃprasthito hṛṣṭo dhṛtvā manasi sāgaram \|*  
*snānārthaṃ taṃ samādāya kuṭhāraṃ bhāskaraprabham \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4-5. Rāma made the Hrada (whirlpool of blood) and offered oblations to his Pitṛs. Thereby his anger vanished. Then he donated the entire earth to leading Brāhmaṇas in the course of a Yajña.

He was extremely delighted in his mind. He started towards the ocean for his holy bath. At that time he held his axe too that had the lustre of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.94.6-8 \|\|

*tadā sa munibhiḥ proktaḥ sarvaistatkṣetravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*vāṃchadbhistu hitaṃ tasya sadā śamaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rāmarāma mahābhāga yaddhārayasi pāṇinā \|*  
*śastraṃ pūrṇe pratijño'pi tanna yuktaṃ bhavettava \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anena karasaṃsthena tava kopaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*na yāsyati śarīrasthastasmādenaṃ parityaja \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Then he was told by all the sages of very quiescent nature, who were the inhabitants of that holy spot and always desired his welfare:

“O Rāma, O highly esteemed Rāma, it is not proper on your part to retain the weapon in your hand even when you have completed that task for which you had taken a vow. With this (weapon) held in your hand, the anger lurking in your physical frame will never go. Hence leave this off.”

## \|\| 1.94.9 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tato rāmaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*provāca vinayopetaḥ prahasaṃstāndvijottamān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing their words, Rāma joined his palms in reverence and humility. He spoke laughingly to those excellent Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.94.10-14 \|\|

*kuṭhāraścaiva vipreṃdrā rudratejodbhavena ca \|*  
*lohena nirmitaḥ pūrvamakṣayo viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ saṃparityajya kathamenaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kṣattradharmaparo'pyevaṃ pragacchāmi digaṃtaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yadi cainaṃ mayā muktaṃ kuṭhāraṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*grahīṣyati paraḥ kaścinmama vadhyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nāparādhamimaṃ śaktaḥ soḍha़ुṃ cāhaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*api brāhmaṇamukhyasya janasyānyasya kā kathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tathāpi nāsti te śāṃtirmukte'pyasmindvijottamāḥ \|*  
*gṛhīte'pi ca yuṣmābhistasmādrakṣyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

10-14. “O leading Brāhmaṇas, this axe was formerly made by Viśvakarman out of the steel arising from Rudra's splendour and is indestructible. Therefore, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, how can I abondon it and go elsewhere since I have been doing the duties of a Kṣatriya?

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if any one else lays his hand on this axe left by me, he shall deserve to be killed by me. I shall be unable to brook this offence even if it be that of a Brāhmaṇa chief, to say nothing of another (non-Brāhmaṇa) man.

So, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall have no peace even if it is left or taken by me. Therefore it should be guarded assiduously by you all.”

## \|\| 1.94.15-16 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadyevaṃ tvaṃ mahābhāga rakṣārthaṃ saṃprayacchasi \|*  
*asmākaṃ tatra bhaṃktvāśu piṃḍaṃ kṛtvā samarpaya \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yena rakṣāmahe sarve paramaṃ yavamāśritāḥ \|*  
*na ca gṛhṇāti vā kaścidgate kālāṃtare'pi ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

15-16. O highly esteemed one, if it is decided that you will hand it over to us for preservation, do break it and make a lump of it before giving it to us so that all of us can carefully guard it. Even after lapse of time, no one will seize it.

## \|\| 1.94.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*cakre lohamayīṃ yaṣṭiṃ taṃ bhaṃktvā sa kuṭhārakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing their words, Rāma, the foremost among wielders of weapons, broke the axe and made it a staff of steel.

## \|\| 1.94.18 \|\|

*tataḥ sa brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāmarpayāmāsa sādaram \|*  
*rakṣārthaṃ bhārgavaśreṣṭho vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then the most excellent one among the scions of Bhṛgu’s family handed it over to the leading Brāhmaṇas eagerly and stood aside bowing down humby \[humbly?\].

## \|\| 1.94.19 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*lohayaṣṭimimāṃ rāma tvatkuṭhārasamudbhavām \|*  
*vayaṃ saṃrakṣayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāma eva hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

19\. O Rāma, we shall guard this steel staff fashioned out of the axe, or rather we shall worship it.

## \|\| 1.94.20 \|\|

*yathā śaktimayī kīrtiḥ skandasyātra pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*lohayaṣṭimayī tadvattava rāma bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Just as the glory of Skanda has been established here in the form of his Śakti, O Rama, so also your glory will be established here in the form of this steel staff.

## \|\| 1.94.21 \|\|

*bhraṣṭarājyastu yo rājā enāmārādhayiṣyati \|*  
*svaṃ rājyamacirātprāpya sa pratāpī bhaviṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A king ousted from kingdom who propitiates this shall become extremely valorous and shall ere long regain his kingdom.

## \|\| 1.94.22 \|\|

*vidyākṛte dvijo vā yaḥ sadaināṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*sa vidyāṃ paramāṃ prāpya sarvajñatvaṃ prapatsyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A Brāhmaṇa who worships this always for the sake of the acquisition of learning shall attain the greatest lore and become omniscient.

## \|\| 1.94.23 \|\|

*aputro vā naro yo'tha nārī vā pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*etāṃ yaṣṭiṃ tvadīyāṃ ca putravānsa bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A man or a woman without a son, who adores this steel staff of yours shall get sons.

## \|\| 1.94.24 \|\|

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā yaścaināṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*āśvinasyāsite pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sa prāpsyati sadā kāmānabhīṣṭānmanasi sthitān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who observes fast and worships this particularly on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Āśvina, will always acquire the desired objectives cherished in the mind always.

## \|\| 1.94.25 \|\|

*evaṃ śrutvā tato rāmasteṣāmeva dvijanmanām \|*  
*praṇamya prayayau tūrṇaṃ samudrasadanaṃ prati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After listening to the words of those Brāhmaṇas Rāma bowed to them and went quickly to the abode at the ocean.

## \|\| 1.94.26 \|\|

*te'pi viprāstatastasyāścakruḥ prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*tatra saṃsthāya tāṃ cakrustataḥ pūjāsamāhitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Those Brāhmaṇas erected an excellent palatial shrine for that steel staff, installed it therein and performed the adoration with mental concentration and purity.

## \|\| 1.94.27 \|\|

*prāpnuvaṃti ca tatpārśvātkāmāneva hṛdi sthitān \|*  
*sustokenā'pi kālena durlabhāstridaśairapi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They obtained from it within a very short period, all the desires cherished in their hearts and rarely available even to Devas.

## Chapter 95 - Greatness of Ajāpāleśvarī (Ajāpāla-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.95.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athānyāpi ca tatrāsti deśakāmapradā nṛṇām \|*  
*ajāpālena bhūpena sthāpitā pāpanāśanī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tāṃ ca śuklacaturdaśyāmajāpāleśvarīṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yo vai pūjayate bhaktyā dhūpapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnotīpsitānkāmāndurlabhā sarvamānavaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 95-105 gives the version of Rāmāyaṇa. The author has skilfully welded the incidents (may be imaginary) in the Rāma story around the sacred spots (deities and Tīrthas) in Camatkārapura.—Ajāpāla in this chapter is Aja, Daśaratha’s father. He transformed all the ailments into goats and kept them locked up for preservation of the health of his subjects (vv 42-45). He propitiated the Devī who became known after his name (Aja). After the complaint from Yama, Śiva assumed the form of a deer and began to eat the goals. The king fought unarmed with that tiger and Śiva manifested himself and look him and his queen with him without giving him any time to crown Daśaratha.—Rāmāyaṇa does not know this. Kālidāsa describes how he fought for the sake of Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha’s cow.

Sūta said:

1-2. Further, there is another goddess also there who bestows desired things on men. She was installed by King Ajāpāla and is destructive of all sins.

A man who worships Ajāpāleśvarī on the fourteenth lunar day in a bright half (Śukla Pakṣa) with devotion by means of incense, flowers and unguents shall obtain all desired things inaccessible to all other men.

## \|\| 1.95.3 \|\|

*tasyā devyāḥ prasādena satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*ajāpālo mahīpālaḥ purā'sītsaṃmataḥ satām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He acquires (everything) with that favour of that goddess. It is the truth that has been uttered by me. Formerly there was a king named Ajāpāla, greatly honoured by good people.

## \|\| 1.95.4-5 \|\|

*hitakṛtsarvalokasya yathā mātā yathā pitā \|*  
*tena rājyaṃ samāsādya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ śubham \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ciṃtitaṃ manasā paścātsvayameva mahātmanā \|*  
*mayā tatkarma kartavyaṃ yadanyairiha bhūmipaiḥ \|*  
*na kṛtaṃ na kariṣyaṃti ye bhaviṣyantyataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He was one who did what is beneficial to all the people like their mother and like their father. After acquiring the splendid kingdom from his father and grandfather the noble-souled king mentally thought to himself thus: ‘Such work should be done by me as has not been done by other kings and will not be done by those who are to be born later.’

## \|\| 1.95.6 \|\|

*eṣa eva paro dharmo bhūpatīnāmudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*yatprajāpālanaṃ śaśvattāsāṃ ca sukhasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Perpetual protection of the subjects and safeguarding their all-round happiness alone has been cited as the greatest virtue of kings.

## \|\| 1.95.7 \|\|

*yathāyathā karaṃ bhūpāstā māṃ gṛhṇaṃti lolupāḥ \|*  
*tathātathā manaḥkṣobho hṛdaye saṃprajāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The more greedy kings levy taxes and tributes on their subjects, inevitably, the more agitation is provoked in their hearts.

## \|\| 1.95.8 \|\|

*na kareṇa vinā bhūpā hastyaśvādibalaṃ ca yat \|*  
*śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ pādātaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Without taxation kings will not be able to maintain an army consisting of elephants, horses etc. and also infantry in particular.

## \|\| 1.95.9 \|\|

*vinā tena sa gamyaḥ syānnīcānāmapi satvaram \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādbhūpāḥ karaṃ gṛhṇaṃti lokataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Without levying taxes a king is likely to be overcome easily and quickly by base (enemies). It is for this reason, that kings levy taxes on the people.

## \|\| 1.95.10-11 \|\|

*tasmānmayā vināpyāśu nāgaiścaiva naraistathā \|*  
*tapaḥ śaktyā prakartavyaṃ rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*karānagṛhṇatā tena lokānraṃjayatā sadā \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ viśeṣeṇa mahātmanām \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Hence my kingdom should be rendered free from thorn-like enemies by me solely through the power of penance, without having recourse to elephants and human beings (infantry), without levying taxes, but always keeping the public in good humour. That will keep me distinct from other noble-souled kings.

## \|\| 1.95.12 \|\|

*evaṃ citte samādhāya vasiṣṭhaṃ munipuṃgavam \|*  
*purodhasaṃ samāhūya tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After deciding thus in mind, he sent for the leading sage Vasiṣṭha, his priest, and then said to him respectfully:

## \|\| 1.95.13-14 \|\|

*atra bhūmitale vipra sarveṣāṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*alpakālena santuṣṭiṃ yatra yāti maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo'thavā brahmā hyetacchīghraṃ vadasva me \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yenāhaṃ sarvalokasya hitārthaṃ tapa ādade \|*  
*na svārthaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. “O Brāhmaṇa, tell me quickly, which is the most excellent of all the Tīrthas on this earth? It should be a place where Maheśvara, Vāsudeva or Brahmā may be pleased within a short time.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I solely pledge myself that I am not after selfish interests. I will perform a penance for the sake of the welfare of all the world.”

## \|\| 1.95.15 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*tisraḥ koṭyordhakoṭī ca tīrthānāmiha bhūtale \|*  
*saṃti pārthivaśārdūla prabhāvasahitāni ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

15\. O tiger among kings, there are thirty-five million Tīrthas on the earth. All of them are highly powerful.

## \|\| 1.95.16 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭistathā rājankṣetrāṇāmasti bhūtale \|*  
*yeṣāṃ sāṃnidhyamabhyeti sarvadaiva maheśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There are sixty-eight holy places on the earth where Maheśvara is always present.

## \|\| 1.95.17-19 \|\|

*tathā sarve surāstuṣṭā brahmaviṣṇu śivādayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ siddhipradaṃ śīghraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ mahīpate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*hāṭakeśvaradevasya kṣetraṃ pātakanāśanam \|*  
*devānāmapi sarveṣāṃ tuṣṭiṃ gacchati caṃḍikā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śīghramārādhitā samyakchraddhāyuktairnarairbhuvi \|*  
*tasmāttatkṣetramāsādya tāṃ devīṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*ārādhaya mahābhāga drutaṃ siddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Further, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and all the Suras are pleased with them.

But, O king, the holy place of Lord Hāṭakeśvara yields Siddhi very quickly to men. It is destructive of the sins of all the Devas too.

Caṇḍikā becomes pleased quickly if propitiated by men endowed with perfect ardour and faith on the earth.

Hence, O highly esteemed one, go to that holy place and propitiate that goddess with perfect faith. You will attain Siddhi within a short time.

## \|\| 1.95.20 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa tenātha gatvā tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya ca devīṃ tāṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On being told thus by him (Vasiṣṭha) he went to that excellent holy spot, installed that goddess and worshipped with devotion.

## \|\| 1.95.21 \|\|

*brahmacaryaparo bhūtvā śucirvrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*niyato niyatāhārastrikālaṃ snānamācaran \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He strictly adhered to the vow of celibacy. He observed all vows. He remained pure. He observed restraints in everything and particularly in the matter of the intake of food. He took holy bath thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.95.22 \|\|

*evamārādhyatastatra gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjāparasya sā devī tasya tuṣṭiṃ tato gatā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. While he continued the propitiation thus with sweet scents, flowers and unguents and performed the adoration, the goddess became pleased with him.

## \|\| 1.95.23 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭāsmi te vatsa vratenānena nityathaḥ \|*  
*balipūjāvidhānena vihitenāmunā svayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

The Devī said:

23\. O dear one, I am well pleased with your continued Vratas and the performance of adorations and oblations in this manner.

## \|\| 1.95.24 \|\|

*tadbrūhi yena te sarvaṃ prakaromi hṛdi sthitam \|*  
*sadya eva mahīpāla tridaśairapi durlabham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hence, O king, tell me so that I can grant you what you have in your heart, immediately, be it very difficult of obtaining even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.95.25 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*lokānāṃ hitakāmena mayaitadvratamāhṛtam \|*  
*yena teṣāṃ bhavetsaukhyaṃ matprasādādanuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

The king said:

25\. This Vrata has been eagerly taken up by me with a desire for the welfare of the worlds so that, with my favour, they will attain excellent happiness.

## \|\| 1.95.26 \|\|

*tasmāddehi mahābhāge jñānayuktāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*mamāstrāṇi vicitrāṇi svairagāṇi samantataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hence, O highly esteemed goddess, grant me missiles along with perfect knowledge. They must be able to move all round unimpeded. They should be of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.95.27 \|\|

*yāni jānaṃti bhūpṛṣṭhe mama pārśve sthitānyapi \|*  
*aparādhaṃ sadā loke paradārādi yatkṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Though they may be staying at my side, they should be aware of all crimes such as ravishing other people’s wives etc., wherever they are committed on the earth or anywhere in the world.

## \|\| 1.95.28 \|\|

*anurūpaṃ tatastasya pātakasya vinigraham \|*  
*prakurvaṃti mitho yena na teṣāṃ saṃkaro bhavet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. They must be able to mete out befitting punishment for the said sins so that there will not be inter-mixture of castes.

## \|\| 1.95.29 \|\|

*maṃtragrāmaṃ tathā devi mama dehi pṛthagvidham \|*  
*nigrahaṃ vyādhisattvānāṃ yena śīghraṃ karomyaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Further, O goddess, grant me different kinds of Mantras whereby I can immediately restrain and control ailments and beings that cause them.

## \|\| 1.95.30 \|\|

*yena syurmanujāḥ sarve mama rājye sukhānvitāḥ \|*  
*nīrogāḥ puṣṭisaṃpannā bhayaśokavivarjitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereby all men in my kingdom shall be happy, well nourished, free from ailments and also devoid of fright and grief.

## \|\| 1.95.31 \|\|

*nāhaṃ devi kariṣyāmi hastyaśvarathasaṃgraham \|*  
*yatasteṣāṃ bhavetpuṣṭirvittairvittaṃ karairbhavet \|*  
*gṛhītaiḥ sarvalokānāṃ tasmāttanna mamepsitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O goddess, I am not gathering together elephants, horses and chariots because they can be sustained only through money and money can be collected through taxes levied on all the people. So I do not like this.

## \|\| 1.95.32 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*atyadbhutataraṃ karma tvayaitatpṛthivīpate \|*  
*prārabdhaṃ yanna kenāpi kṛtaṃ na ca kariṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

32\. O king, highly wonderful is your undertaking which has not been practised by anyone else nor anyone is likely to undertake.

## \|\| 1.95.33 \|\|

*tathāpyevaṃ kariṣyāmi tava dāsyāmi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*jñānayuktāni śastrāṇi maṃtragrāmaṃ ca tādṛśam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Still I shall do this. I shall grant you weapons and missiles along with perfect knowledge and the requisite Mantras too.

## \|\| 1.95.34 \|\|

*gṛhyante yena te sarve vyādhayo'pi sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ sadaiva te rakṣyā manmantrairapi saṃyutāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By these all terrible ailments can be curbed. But, they should be well preserved always along with my Mantras.

## \|\| 1.95.35 \|\|

*yadi dṛṣṭipathāttubhyaṃ kvacidyāsyaṃti dūrataḥ \|*  
*mānavānpīḍayiṣyaṃti cirātprāpyādhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If perchance they stray away from the range of your vision, they will be afflicting men who may get more of the calamities.

## \|\| 1.95.36 \|\|

*yadā tvaṃ pṛthivīpāla svargaṃ yāsyasi bhūtalāt \|*  
*tadātra salile sthāpyā madagre yadvyavasthitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When you ascend to heaven from the earth, they should be deposited in the watery expanse existing before me.

## \|\| 1.95.37 \|\|

*sarve maṃtrāstathā'strāṇi mamavākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*yena syātpūrvavatsarvo vyavahāro nṛpodbhavaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. All the Mantras and the missiles should, at this bidding of mine, be undoubtedly deposited in the Tīrtha so that all the activities of kings shall be carried on as before.

## \|\| 1.95.38 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva tenokte tatkṣaṇāddvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*prādurbhūtāni divyāni tasyāstrāṇi bahūni ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sūta said:

38\. When the king said “So it shall be”, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, many divine missiles manifested themselves.

## \|\| 1.95.39 \|\|

*jñānasaṃpatprayuktāni yādṛśāni mahātmanā \|*  
*tena saṃyācitānyeva vyādhimaṃtrāstathaiva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. All of them were appended with the full complement of perfect knowledge (of Mantras) in the manner requested for by that noble-souled king. So also there were the Mantras for ailments.

## \|\| 1.95.40 \|\|

*vyādhayo yaiśca gṛhyaṃte mucyaṃte svecchayā sadā \|*  
*sukhena paripālyaṃte dṛṣṭigocarasaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By these, the ailments can (could) be curbed and released always as one pleased. Kept within the range of vision they can (could) be easily maintained.

## \|\| 1.95.41 \|\|

*tatastaṃ sakalaṃ prāpya prasādaṃ caṃḍikodbhavam \|*  
*tacca hastyādikaṃ sarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dadau nṛpa \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereupon, after acquiring the favour of Caṇḍikā, he gave away to Brāhmaṇas everything including elephants etc.

## \|\| 1.95.42-45 \|\|

*ekāṃ muktvā nijāṃ bhāryāmekaṃ daśarathaṃ sutam \|*  
*tāṃścāpi sakalānvyādhīnmaṃtraiḥ saṃyamya yatnataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ajārūpānsvayaṃ paścādyaṣṭimādāya rakṣati \|*  
*evaṃ tasya narendrasya vartamānasya bhūtale \|\| 43 \|\|*

*gupto'pi nāparādhaḥ syātkasyacitprakaṭaḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*pramādādyadi bhūloke kaścitpāpaṃ samācaret \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tadrūpo nigrahastasya tatkṣaṇādeva jāyate \|*  
*vadhaṃ vā yadi vā baṃdhaṃ kleśaṃ cā'rātisaṃbhavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. He gave away everything excepting his wife and his only son Daśaratha.

After assiduously controlling all the ailments in the form of goats through the Mantras himself pursuing them with a staff in his hand, he protected the land (This is the significance of his name Ajāpāla).

As the king maintained all these things on the earth here was no offence or crime stealthily perpetrated. How could there be open offence?

If anyone perpetrated any sin on the earth, a befitting punishment followed instantly, in the form of death, bondage or sufferings at the hands of enemies.

## \|\| 1.95.46 \|\|

*adṛṣṭānyapi śastrāṇi tāni kurvaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ca mahīpānāṃ rājye guptānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kurvanti manujāsteṣāṃ cakre vaivasvato graham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. These invisible missiles did everything instantly. Of course in the dominions of other kings men committed many secret crimes. In those places Vaivasvata (Yama) carried on the task of restraining and punishing.

## \|\| 1.95.47 \|\|

*na tatra bhayasaṃtrastastataḥ pāpasamācaret \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ vā viśeṣeṇa jñātvā śastrabhayaṃ ca tat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. There the people were too frightened to perpetrate crimes openly, especially due to the fear of the weapons.

## \|\| 1.95.48 \|\|

*tataste pāpanirmuktā lokāḥ saṃśuddhagātrakāḥ \|*  
*rogeṣu nigṛhīteṣu prāptāḥ sukhamanuttamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, the people devoid of sins became sanctified in their bodies. When the ailments were curbed, they attained excellent happiness.

## \|\| 1.95.49 \|\|

*evaṃ sthiteṣu lokeṣu gatapāpāmayeṣu ca \|*  
*prayātāḥ śūnyatāṃ sarve narakā ye yamālaye \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When the worlds thus became rid of sins and ailments, all the Narakas in the abode of Yama became empty.

## \|\| 1.95.50 \|\|

*na kaścinnarakaṃ yāti na ca mṛtyupathaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yathā kṛtayugaṃ tādṛktretāyāmapi saṃsthitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. No one fell into Naraka. No man traversed the path of death. Even in Tretā Yuga everything was a though in Kṛtayuga.

## \|\| 1.95.51 \|\|

*vyavahāre tato naṣṭe yamalokasamudbhave \|*  
*svargeṇa tulyatāṃ prāpte prāṇibhirmṛtyuvarjitaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. All the activities of Yama’s world came to a standstill. All living beings free from death, attained happiness on a par with Svarga.

## \|\| 1.95.52 \|\|

*tato vaivasvato gatvā brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ prati \|*  
*provāca duḥkhasaṃpannaḥ praṇipatya pitāmaham \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Vaivasvata went to the abode of Brahmā in great distress. He bowed down to Pitāmaha and said:

## \|\| 1.95.53-56 \|\|

*ahaṃ purā tvayā deva dharmādharmadidṛkṣayā \|*  
*mānuṣāṇāṃ samādiṣṭo nigrahānugrahaṃ prati \|\| 033 \|\|*

*ajāpālena bhūpena tatsarvaṃ viphalīkṛtam \|*  
*tapaḥśaktyā suraśreṣṭha devīmārādhya caṃḍikām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*nādhayo vyādhayastatra na pāpāni mahītale \|*  
*kasyaciddeva jāyaṃte yathā kṛtayuge tathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru suraśreṣṭha punareva yathā purā \|*  
*madīyabhavane kṛtsno vyavahāraḥ prajāyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. “Formerly, O Lord, I was entrusted by you with the task of punishing and blessing for the purpose of keeping watch on Dharma (virtue) and Adharma (vice).

Everything has been nullified by King Ajāpāla, O most excellent one among the Suras, through the power of his penance, acquired by propitiating Goddess Caṇḍikā.

As in Kṛtayuga, no one commits sins and no one falls sick or feels mental anguish.

Hence, of excellent one among the Suras, do something so that all the activities in my abode can be revived as before.”

## \|\| 1.95.57 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*samīpa upaviṣṭasya śivasyā'syaṃ vyalokayat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On hearing those words of his, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, glanced at the face of Śiva who was sitting by his side.

## \|\| 1.95.58 \|\|

*athābravītprahasyoccaistrinetraścaturānanam \|*  
*atyadbhutatamāṃ śrutvā tāṃ vārtāṃ yamasaṃbhavām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On hearing the highly mysterious news conveyed by Yama, Three-eyed Lord laughed and said to the Four-faced One.

## \|\| 1.95.59 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*dharmamārgapravṛttasya sadācārasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ nivāraṇaṃ tatra kriyate kaśca nigrahaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

Maheśvara said:

59\. How can one restrain or punish a king of excellent conduct pursuing the path of righteousness?

## \|\| 1.95.60-61 \|\|

*tasmāttena mahīpena yasmānmārgaḥ pradarśitaḥ \|*  
*apūrvo dharmasaṃbhūtaḥ kṛtaḥ samyaṅmahātmanā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tanmayāpi yathā cāsya prasādaḥ surasattama \|*  
*apūrvaḥ karaṇīyaśca yathā dharmo na duṣyati \|\| 61 \|\|*
