60-61. Since an unusual and unprecedented path has been shown and perfect righteousness has been established by that noble-souled one, O most excellent one among the Suras, an unusual and unprecedented favour should be shown by me, lest righteousness might be defiled.

## \|\| 1.95.62 \|\|

*evamuktvā caturvaktraṃ yamaṃ prāha tataḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*vadāyuṣo'sya yaccheṣamajāpālasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*yena tatsamaye prāpte taṃ nayāmi nijālayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After saying thus to the Four-faced One Śiva said to Yama: ‘Tell me how much of the span of life of King Ajāpāla yet remains so that when the time arrives I can take him to my abode.”

## \|\| 1.95.63-64 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi tasyātītāni cāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti pañcapañcāśatpratīkṣye'haṃ tataḥ katham \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yāvatkālaṃ suraśreṣṭha śūnye jāte sva āśraye \|*  
*tasmātkuru drutaṃ kaṃcidupāyaṃ tadvināśane \|\| 64 \|\|*

Yama said:

63-64. Five thousand years of his life have passed. Fifty-five thousand years yet remain. How can I wait till then? By that time my abode itself will become a void. So undertake some means immediately to destroy him.

## \|\| 1.95.65 \|\|

*evamukte yamenātha taṃ visṛjya gṛhaṃ prati \|*  
*vyāghrarūpaṃ samāsthāya svayaṃ tatsaṃnidhau yayau \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. When this was stated by Yama, Śiva sent him off to his abode. He assumed the form of a tiger and went near the king himself.

## \|\| 1.95.66 \|\|

*yatra saṃstho mahīpaḥ sa prajāpālanatatparaḥ \|*  
*meghagambhīranirghoṣaṃ garjamāno muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The king was stationed there engaged in his duty of according protection to the subjects. He (Śiva in the form of tiger) roared repeatedly in the loud rumbling sound of clouds.

## \|\| 1.95.67 \|\|

*ajāstāstaṃ ca saṃvīkṣya vyāghraṃ raudravapurddharam \|*  
*ajāpālaṃ samuddiśya saṃtrastāḥ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The goats saw the tiger’s aweful form and became frightened. They sought refuge in Ajāpāla.

## \|\| 1.95.68 \|\|

*tasya yatnaparasyāpi rakṣamāṇasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*ajāstā vyāghrarūpeṇa śaṃkareṇa prabhakṣitāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Notwithstanding the carefulness of the king in guarding them, those goats were devoured by Śaṅkara in the form of a tiger.

## \|\| 1.95.69 \|\|

*ajānāṃ kadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*svahastādyaṣṭimutsṛjya jagrāha niśitāyudham \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On seeing the destruction of the goats, the king threw away the staff from his hand and took up a sharp weapon.

## \|\| 1.95.70 \|\|

*yattasya tuṣṭayā dattaṃ caṃḍaṃ caṃḍārciṣā samam \|*  
*tacchastraṃ ca tathānyāni devīdattāni śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*śanaiḥśanaiḥ prajagrāha svavaktreṇa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. That fierce weapon had the lustre of the hot-rayed sun and was given to him by the goddess who was pleased with him. Śaṅkara, the great Lord, slowly grasped with his mouth that weapon as well as the other missiles given by the goddess.

## \|\| 1.95.71 \|\|

*astrābhāvāttatastūrṇaṃ dhriyamāṇe'pi kāṃtayā \|*  
*dvaṃdvayuddhena taṃ vyāghraṃ yodhayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The king had no weapon left with him. Though he was held back by his beloved, the king fought a duel with the tiger.

## \|\| 1.95.72 \|\|

*tatastasyāṃgasaṃsparśānmuktvā vyāghratanuṃ ca tām \|*  
*dadhāra bhasmasaṃdigdhāṃ tanuṃ candravibhūṣitām \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. At the contact with the body of the king, the Lord cast away the form of the tiger and resumed his own form embellished with the moon and smeared over with holy ash.

## \|\| 1.95.73 \|\|

*ruṃḍamālāvarāṃ divyāṃ sakhaṭvāṃgāṃ sapannagām \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa mahīpālaḥ sabhāryaḥ praṇatastataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The divine form had a garland of headless trunks (skulls?) along with serpents. It had the Khaṭvāṅga weapon. On seeing it the king and his wife bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.95.74 \|\|

*provācātha stutiṃ kṛtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ānaṃdāśrupariklinno harṣagadgadayā girā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He stood humbly drenched with tears of joy. After eulogizing the Lord, he spoke with words choked with great joy:

## \|\| 1.95.75 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*ajñānādyanmayā deva prahārāstava nirmitāḥ \|*  
*tiraskārastathā dattastatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ vibho \|\| 75 \|\|*

The king said:

75\. O Lord, I have hit you out of ignorance. I have insulted you. O Lord, may this be forgiven by you.

## \|\| 1.95.76 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*kṣāṃta eṣa mayā putra tava sarvaḥ parābhavaḥ \|*  
*parituṣṭena te karma dṛṣṭvā caivātimānuṣam \|\| 76 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

76\. O dear son, all your misdemeanour has been pardoned by me for I have witnessed with delight your superhuman exploit.

## \|\| 1.95.77 \|\|

*yathā kṛtaṃ tvayā rājyaṃ prajāḥ saṃrakṣitā nṛpa \|*  
*tathānyo bhūpatiḥ kaścinna kartā na kariṣyati \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. No other king administers the kingdom nor will ever do so in the manner done by you. The subjects have been protected by you very well.

## \|\| 1.95.78 \|\|

*tasmādgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ pātāle pārthivottama \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa dharmapatnyānayā saha \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Hence, O excellent king, accompany me to the nether world in this very body along with your virtuous wife.

## \|\| 1.95.79 \|\|

*nātaḥ paraṃ tvayā stheyaṃ martyaloke kathaṃcana \|*  
*viruddhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ yataḥ karma tvadudbhavam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Henceforth you shall never stay in the mortal world, since your activities are against the interests of all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.95.80 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*evaṃ deva kariṣyāmi gatvā'yodhyāṃ mahāpurīm \|*  
*putraṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpya maṃtriṇāṃ saṃnivedya ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

The king said:

80\. O Lord, I shall do so after going to the great city of Ayodhyā, informing the ministers and installing my son as king in the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.95.81 \|\|

*tathāhaṃ deva devyā ca proktaḥ saṃtuṣṭayā purā \|*  
*mantragrāmo yayā dattaḥ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Further I was particularly instructed thus by the delighted goddess who granted the series of Mantras and diverse kinds of weapons:

## \|\| 1.95.82 \|\|

*yadā tvaṃ tyajasi prājña martyalokaṃ sudustyajam \|*  
*tadātra māmake kuṇḍe prakṣeptavyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. “O highly intelligent one, when you leave the mortal world ordinarily very difficult to get rid of, all these (Mantras and missiles) should be thrown into my holy Kuṇḍa.”

## \|\| 1.95.83 \|\|

*tāni cārpaya me bhūyo yenānṛṇyaṃ vrajāmyaham \|*  
*tasyā devyāḥ surādhīśa tvatprasādena sāṃpratam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O Lord of Suras, do hand over them again (to the goddess) so that, with your favour I shall be free from indebtedness to the goddess now.

## \|\| 1.95.84 \|\|

*evamuktastatastena bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*ājñāpya tāni sarvāṇi dadau tatra drutaṃ gataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On being told thus by the king, Lord Tripurānataka commanded them (weapons etc.) and gave them (to the goddess) quickly after going there.

## \|\| 1.95.85-89 \|\|

*abravīcca sutastatra svayaṃ rājā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vīryaudāryasamopeto vaṃśasyoddharaṇakṣamaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tvaṃ cāgaccha mayā sārdhamadyaiva mama maṃdire \|*  
*praviśyātra jale puṇye devīkuṇḍasamudbhave \|\| 86 \|\|*

*adya māghacaturdaśyāṃ śuklāyāmaparo'pi yaḥ \|*  
*devīmimāṃ ca saṃpūjya jale'sminbhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*kariṣyati praveśena prāṇatyāgaṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*sa ca yāsyati yatrāste pātāle hāṭakeśvaraḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*snānaṃ vā pārthivaśreṣṭha yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ tasya vyādhīnāṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 89 \|\|*

85-89. The Lord said this also: “Your son shall himself be the king. He is endowed with heroism and exaltedness. He is capable of uplifting the race.

Do come to my palace this day itself after diving into the meritorious waters of Devīkuṇḍa.

O excellent king, on this day, i.e. the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha, if anyone else worships this goddess with great devotion, enters this water and casts off his life, he will go to the place in Pātāla where Hāṭakeśvara is present.

O excellent one among kings, a man who regularly takes his holy bath there will never contract hundred and eight kinds of ailments.”

## \|\| 1.95.90 \|\|

*evamuktvā tamādāya nṛpaṃ bhāryāsamanvitam \|*  
*ajābhistābhirastraiśca taiścāpi parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*praviveśa jale tasmindevīkuṇḍasamudbhave \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. After saying thus Parameśvara took the king along with his wife, the goats and the weapons. He entered the waters of Devīkuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.95.91 \|\|

*tataśca maṃdiraṃ nītaḥ svakīyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tenaiva naradehena sa kalatrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, with the same human body and his wife the king was led to his (Lord’s) own palace.

## \|\| 1.95.92 \|\|

*adyāpi tiṣṭhate tatra jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayānaśca taṃ devaṃ pātāle hāṭakeśvaram \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Even today he stays there without old age and death. He continues to worship Lord Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.95.93 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samudbhūtā sā devī parameśvarī \|*  
*sthāpitā tena bhūpena śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. It was thus that Goddess Parameśvarī was installed by that king with his mind sanctified with faith.

## Chapter 96 - Dialogue between Daśaratha and Śanaiścara

## \|\| 1.96.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasmingate bhūpe hyajāpāle rasātalam \|*  
*tatputraścābhavadrājā maṃtribhistu puraskṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yo nityamagamatsvarge vāsavaṃ ramate sadā \|*  
*śanaiścaro jito yena rohiṇīṃ paribhedayan \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gṛhe yasya svayaṃ viṣṇurbhūtvā caiva caturvidhaḥ \|*  
*rāvaṇasya vināśārthaṃ janma cakre praharṣitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: This chapter and the next (97) record events in Daśaratha’s life not known to Vālmīki. In this chapter, Daśaratha confronted Śani (Saturn) as Śani’s attempt to cross the Rohiṇī Śakaṭa would have resulted in a long famine. Vālmīki tells us about Putrakāmeṣṭi performed by Ṛṣyaśṛṅga whereby he got four sons. Our Purāṇa cells that Daśaratha performed penance at Hāṭakeśvara and created a Tīrtha called Rājavāpī. Due to his penance Daśaratha got the sons.

Sūta said:

1-3. When King Ajāpāla went to Rasātala thus his son being honoured by the ministers became the king.

It was he who later regularly visited Svarga and enabled Vāsava to enjoy himself always. Śanaiścara who was about to cross the orbit of Rohiṇī was conquered by that king.

It was in his abode that Viṣṇu joyously incarnated in four forms for the purpose of killing Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.96.4 \|\|

*tenāgatyātra satkṣetre toṣito madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ śobhanaṃ kṛtvā tataścaiva pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He came to this excellent holy place and propitiated Madhusūdana. After erecting a (a palace-like temple) of splendid features, he installed Madhusūdana therein.

## \|\| 1.96.5 \|\|

*tasyāpi viśrutā vāpī svayaṃ tena vinirmitā \|*  
*rājavāpīti loke'sminvikhyātiṃ paramāṃ gatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A famous tank was dug by him. It became well-known all over the world as Rājavāpī.

## \|\| 1.96.6 \|\|

*tasyāṃ yaḥ kurute śrāddhaṃ saṃprāpte pañcamīdine \|*  
*pretapakṣe viśeṣeṇa sa naraḥ syātsatāṃ priyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One who performs Śrāddha on the fifth lunar day particularly in the Pretapakṣa (dark half of Bhādrapada) shall become a favourite of good people.

## \|\| 1.96.7 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tena jitaḥ saurī rohiṇīśakaṭaṃ ca yat \|*  
*bhiṃdānastoṣitastena kathaṃ nārāyaṇo vada \|\| 7 \|\|*

The sages said:

7\. How did the son of the Sun (Saturn) break the cart-like Figure or Rohiṇī, conquered by him? How was Nārayāṇa propitiated by him? Tell us.

## \|\| 1.96.8 \|\|

*\|sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasmiñchāsati dharmajñe svadharmeṇa vasundharām \|*  
*atisaukhyānvito lokaḥ sarvadaiva vyajāyata \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

8\. When that king, a knower of Dharma, was ruling over the earth righteously, the entire world was always very happy.

## \|\| 1.96.9 \|\|

*bahukṣīrapradā gāvaḥ sasyāni guṇavaṃti ca \|*  
*kāmavarṣī ca parjanyo yatharttuphalitā drumāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Cows yielded milk profusely. Vegetation (food-grains) was luxurious and of good quality. Parjanya (god of rain, cloud) showered as much as desired. Trees bore fruits befitting the seasons.

## \|\| 1.96.10-11 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya daivajñaistasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ rohiṇībhedaṃ raviputraḥ kariṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasyānaṃtaramevāśu durbhikṣaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭiśca bhavitā raudrā dvādaśa vārṣikī \|*  
*yayā saṃpatsyate sarvaṃ bhūtalaṃ gatamānavam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Once Daivajñas (Astrologers) told that king: “The son of Ravi (Saturn) will cross the orbit of Rohiṇī. Immediately thereafter there will be a great famine. A terrible drought will come lasting for twelve years whereby the entire earth will become devoid of men.”

## \|\| 1.96.12 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa rājā kupito'bhyagāt \|*  
*śanaiścaraṃ samuddiśya vimānamadhiruhya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing their words, the king became very angry. He got into an aerial chariot and marched against Śanaiścara.

## \|\| 1.96.13 \|\|

*tasya tuṣṭena saṃdattaṃ vimānaṃ kāmagaṃ purā \|*  
*śakreṇa tatra saṃtiṣṭhañchanaiścaramupādravat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Formerly, Indra who was pleased with that king had given him that chariot that could go anywhere one wished.

## \|\| 1.96.14-15 \|\|

*tataḥ sūryapathaṃ muktvā tataścaṃdrasya pārthivaḥ \|*  
*nakṣatrasaraṇiṃ prāpya sajyaṃ kṛtvā mahaddhanuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatra bāṇaṃ samāropya śanaiścaramupādravat \|*  
*provāca purataḥ sthitvā sūryaputramadhomukham \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. He left the path of the Sun and then that of the Moon. After reaching the path of the stars and stringing the great bow, the king fitted an arrow therein and attacked Śanaiścara. He stood in front of Saturn (the son of the Sun) who stood with his face stooped down, and said:

## \|\| 1.96.16-17 \|\|

*tyajainaṃ rohiṇīmārgaṃ sāṃprataṃ tvaṃ śanaiścara \|*  
*madvākyādanyathā'haṃ tvāṃ nayiṣyāmi yamakṣayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*etena niśitāgrega śareṇā nataparvaṇā \|*  
*divyāstramaṃtrayuktena satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. “At my bidding, O Śanaiścara, leave the orbit of Rohiṇī now. Otherwise I will despatch you to the abode of Yama with this sharp-pointed arrow with flat joints and charged with divine Mantras. I am speaking the truth.”

## \|\| 1.96.18 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tādṛgraudratamaṃ mahat \|*  
*mando vismayamāpannastataścedamabhāṣata \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing his words of extremely terrible import, Manda (Saturn) was stunned with wonder and spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.96.19 \|\|

*kastvaṃ brūhi mahābhāga mama mārgaṃ ruṇatsi yaḥ \|*  
*agamyaṃ kenacilloke sarvairapi surāsuraiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O esteemed one, who are you? Why do you obstruct my path which is very difficult to approach even to all the Suras and Asuras of the world?”

The king spoke:

## \|\| 1.96.20 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ daśaratho nāma sūryavaṃśodbhavo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ajasya tanayaḥ prāptaḥ kāmaṃ vārayituṃ krudhā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I am a king named Daśaratha, hailing from the Solar race. I am Aja’s son. I have come here in anger to restrain you adequately.

## \|\| 1.96.21 \|\|

*maṃda uvāca \|*  
*na tvayā saha saṃbaṃdhaḥ kaścidasti mahīpate \|*  
*mama yattvaṃ prakopāḍhyo manmārgaṃ haṃtumicchasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

Manda (Saturn) said:

21\. O king, I have no relation at all with you that necessitates your wrathful obstruction of my path.

## \|\| 1.96.22-23 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*rohiṇīsaṃbhavaṃ tvaṃ hi śakaṭaṃ bhedayiṣyasi \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ mama daivajñairvākyametadudāhṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasminmanda tvayā bhinne na varṣati śatakratuḥ \|*  
*etadvadati daivajñā jyotiḥśāstravicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

The king said:

22-23. Daivajñas (Astrologers) have mentioned this to me that now you will break the cart-like figure of the constellation Rohiṇī. O Manda, when it is broken by you, Śatakratu (Indra) will not shower rains. Thus say the Daivajñas (expert in the science of Astrology).

## \|\| 1.96.24 \|\|

*jāte vṛṣṭinirodhe'tha jāyaṃte'nnāni na kṣitau \|*  
*annābhāvātkṣayaṃ yāṃti tato bhūbhitale janāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When rainfall is stopped food crops will not grow on the earth. Due to the absence of food the whole population on the earth will be ruined.

## \|\| 1.96.25 \|\|

*janocchede tato jāte agniṣṭomādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*na bhavaṃti dharā pṛṣṭhe tataḥ syādeva saṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When people are ruined, such rites as Agniṣṭoma etc. will never be performed on the earth. That will result in complete destruction.

## \|\| 1.96.26 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādruddho mārgaste sūryasaṃbhava \|*  
*rohiṇīṃ gaṃtukāmasya satyametanmayoditam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is for this reason, O Saturn born of the Sun, that your path has been obstructed as you were desirous of proceeding against Rohiṇī. The truth has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.96.27-28 \|\|

*śaniruvāca \|*  
*gaccha putra nijaṃ gehaṃ mamāpi tvaṃ ca rocase \|*  
*tuṣṭo'haṃ tava vīryeṇa na tvanyena mahīpate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*na kenacitkṛtaṃ karma yadetadbhavatā kṛtam \|*  
*na kariṣyati caivānyo devo vā mānavo'tha vā \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śani said:

27-28. O dear son, go home. You do appeal to me. O king, I am pleased with your heroism. No one else has done anything which you have done. Nor will anyone do so, be he a Deva or a human being.

## \|\| 1.96.29 \|\|

*nāhaṃ paśyāmi bhūpāla kathaṃcidapi tūrdhvataḥ \|*  
*yato dṛṣṭivinirdagdhaṃ bhasmasājjāyate'khilam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I do not see anything at all with my eyes raised up, O king, since everything will be reduced to ashes after being burned by my eyes.

## \|\| 1.96.30 \|\|

*jātamātreṇa bālena mayā pādau nirīkṣitau \|*  
*tātasya sahasā dagdhau tato'haṃ vāritoṃ'bayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. As an infant, soon after the birth, my father’s feet were looked at by me. Suddenly they were burnt. Thereupon, I was prevented by my mother (to look up):

## \|\| 1.96.31 \|\|

*na tvayā putra draṣṭavyaṃ kiṃcideva kathaṃcana \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ yadi te dharmo mātṛvākyasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “If the virtue of obeying your mother’s words of advice in considered valid by you, nothing at all should be looked at by you, dear son.”

## \|\| 1.96.32 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā mahatkarma kṛtamīdṛksuduṣkaram \|*  
*prajānāṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha tyaktvā dūrādbhayaṃ mama \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O most excellent one among kings, a great deed like this, very difficult to be carried out, has been done by you. You have warded off from afar the fear (evil consequences) of mine from your subjects.

## \|\| 1.96.33 \|\|

*tasmā ttava kṛte nāhaṃ bhedayiṣyāmi rohiṇīm \|*  
*kathaṃcidapi bhūpāla yugāṃtararaśateṣvapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence, out of deference to you, I will not break the cart-like figure of Rohiṇī at any cost even for hundreds of Yugas.

## \|\| 1.96.34 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya cāsmākaṃ tasmādadya bhaviṣyati \|*  
*hṛtatsthitaṃ durlabhaṃ bhūpa sarveṣāmiha dehinām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. So choose a boon from me, O king. Today the desire cherished in the heart by all embodied beings will be realized.

## \|\| 1.96.35 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tava yo vāsare prāpte tailābhyaṃgaṃ karoti vai \|*  
*tasyā'nyadivasaṃ yāvatpīḍā kāryā na ca tvayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

The king said:

35\. One who offers you oil bath on Saturday will not be troubled by you till the next Saturday.

## \|\| 1.96.36-39 \|\|

*tiladānaṃ karotyevaṃ lohadānaṃ ca yastava \|*  
*karoti divase śaktyā yāvadvarṣaṃ tvayā hi saḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*rakṣaṇīyaḥ sukṛcchreṣu saṃkaṭeṣu sadaiva hi \|*  
*tvayi gocarapīḍāyāṃ saṃsthite cārkasaṃbhava \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yaḥ kuryācchāṃtikaṃ samyaktilahomaṃ ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*vāsare tava saṃprāpte samidbhiśca tathā'kṣataiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasya sārdhāni varṣāṇi sapta kāryā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tvayā rakṣā mahābhāga varaṃ cenmama yacchasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. If anyone makes the gift of gingelly seeds or iron on your day (Saturday) in accordance with his capacity, he should be protected by you in the course of difficulties and great sufferings for the period of a year.

O highly esteemed one born of Arka (Sun-god), should you deem it proper to grant me a boon, you should accord full protection to a person for the period of your term of influence for seven years and half of your transit, if the person with devotion performs Śāntika (pacificatory) rites and Homa with gingelly seeds along with sacrificial twigs and raw rice grains on Saturday.

## \|\| 1.96.40 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamityeva saṃprocya virarāma tataḥ param \|*  
*śanaiścaro mahīpālavacanāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sūta said:

40\. Then Śanaiścara said: “Let it be so” and stopped, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. He granted everything in accordance with the request of the king.

## \|\| 1.96.41 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ suvistarāt \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ sūryaputrasya rājñā daśarathena hi \|*  
*saṃvādaṃ rohiṇībhede sañjātaṃ samupasthite \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus, everything has been told by me in detail about which I was asked by you, viz. the dialogue between Śanaiścara and Daśaratha, which happened when the breaking of the figure of Rohiṇī was imminent.

## \|\| 1.96.42 \|\|

*yaścaitatpaṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādyo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śanaiścarakṛtā pīḍā tasya nāśaṃ pragacchati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If anyone reads this everyday and listens to this in particular, the affliction brought about by Śanaiścara disappears.

## Chapter 97 - Daśaratha’s Penance

## \|\| 1.97.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti no mando rohiṇīśakaṭaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*bhinatti vacanāttasya rājño daśarathasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tadvṛttāṃtaṃ samākarṇya tasya śakraḥ praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhūpālaṃ taṃ samabhyetya tataścovāca sādaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Ever since then, O Brāhmaṇas, Saturn never broke the cart-like figure of Rohiṇī due to the deference for the words of King Daśaratha.

on getting the news of the incident, Śakra became delighted. Approaching that king, he spoke to him respectfully:

## \|\| 1.97.3-4 \|\|

*atyadbhutataraṃ karma tvayaitatpṛthivīpate \|*  
*saṃsādhitaṃ yadanyena manasāpi na cintyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ata eva hi saṃtuṣṭiḥ sañjātādya tavopari \|*  
*varaṃ matto gṛhāṇādya tadabhīṣṭaṃ hṛdi sthitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. “O king, a wonderful act has been done by you. It is what cannot be even mentally conceived by any other man. For this reason, I am highly pleased with you. Receive from me the desired boon, cherished in your heart.”

## \|\| 1.97.5 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tvayā saha suraśreṣṭha maitrī saṃprārthayāmyaham \|*  
*śāśvatī sarvakṛtyeṣu paramāṃ lokasaṃsthitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

The king said:

5\. O most excellent one among Suras, I solicit absolute and permanent friendship with you in respect of all tasks to be accomplished in the world.

## \|\| 1.97.6 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu rājeṃdra tvayā saha sadā mama \|*  
*saṃpatsyate sadā maitrī vasoriva ca śāśvatī \|\| 6 \|\|*

Indra said:

6\. O leading king, let it be so, A friendship, permanent like that of Vasu will always be maintained with you.

## \|\| 1.97.7 \|\|

*tvayā sadaiva me pārśve sabhāyāṃ devasaṃnidhau \|*  
*āgantavyaṃ viśeṣeṇa yena maitrī pravardhate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You must always come to the presence of the Devas and remain at my side, so that the friendship can flourish.

## \|\| 1.97.8 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrākṣo jagāma tridivālayam \|*  
*rājāpi cāgato harmye svakīye harṣasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After saying thus, the Thousand-eyed One went to heaven. The king too joyously went to his own palace.

## \|\| 1.97.9 \|\|

*rakṣayitvā jagatsarvaṃ śanaiścara kṛtādbhayāt \|*  
*aprāpyāṃ prāpya saṃkīrtiṃ stūyamānastu bandibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He had saved the entire universe from the fear of Saturn. He earned excellent glory not usually obtained by others. He was eulogized by bards.

## \|\| 1.97.10 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti nityaṃ sa sandhyākāla upasthite \|*  
*sāyāhnaṃ saṃvidhāyātha yāti śakrasya maṃdire \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Ever since then everyday he concluded his evening rites when the time of dusk arrived and then went to the palace of Śakra.

## \|\| 1.97.11-12 \|\|

*tatra sthitvā ciraṃ śrutvā gaṃdharvāṇāṃ manoharam \|*  
*gītaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca nṛtyaṃ ca tānādivihitaṃ śubham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vicitrārthāḥ kathāḥ śrutvā devarṣīṇāṃ mukhāccyutāḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ ca kīrtayitvātha prayāti nijamaṃdiram \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. He used to stay there for a long time listening to the sweet songs of Gandharvas, seeing the charming dances of splendid quality, hearing the stories of diverse import and themes uttered by divine sages and glorifying them himself. He then used to return to his abode.

## \|\| 1.97.13 \|\|

*vimānavaramāruhya haṃsabarhiṇanāditam \|*  
*manoharapatākābhiḥ samaṃtācca vibhūṣitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. While proceeding to and fro, he used to ride in an excellent chariot reverberating with the sounds of swans and peacocks and well-adorned with charming banners.

## \|\| 1.97.14 \|\|

*yadāyadā sa niryāti śakrasthānānnijālayam \|*  
*tadātadā'sane tasya kriyate'bhyukṣaṇaṃ sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Whenever he left the place of Śakra for his own abode, his seat was regularly sprinkled with water.

## \|\| 1.97.15 \|\|

*śakrādeśāttadā vetti na sa bhūpaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*anyasmindivase tasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvamabhyukṣaṇasamudbhavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It was at the bidding of Śakra and the king was not at all made aware of it. On another day, Nārada, the excellent sage, told him about this sprinkling of his seat.

## \|\| 1.97.16 \|\|

*vṛttāṃtaṃ tasya rājarṣestasyaiva gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrā prasaṃgena vidveṣaparivṛddhaye \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The matter was communicated to the saintly king by the sage who had come to his abode in the course of his pilgrimage. The sage had the ulterior motive of provoking hatred of the king.

## \|\| 1.97.17 \|\|

*tacchrutvā nāradenoktaṃ śraddheyamapi bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*na cakre hṛdaye'dharmamātmānaṃ pariciṃtayan \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing the words of Nārada, the king did not take them to heart although the utterance of the sage was considered trustworthy. The king thought that it was unrighteous of him to do so.

## \|\| 1.97.18-19 \|\|

*tathāpi kautukāviṣṭo gatvā śakraniveśanam \|*  
*anyasmindivase sthitvā ciraṃ tatra samutthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*alakṣyaṃ vīkṣayāmāsa svāsanaṃ dūramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃcitsadmāṃtaraṃ prāpya kautūhalasamanvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. But he was moved by curiosity. On another day he went of Śakra’s abode as usual, stayed there for a long time and then rose to leave. In his curiosity he went to another building and observed his seat from afar. He took care in particular that this was not directly perceived by anyone else.

## \|\| 1.97.20 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrasamādeśādutthāya surakiṃkaraḥ \|*  
*prokṣayāmāsa toyena pārthivasya tadāsanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. As usual, at the bidding of Śakra, the celestial attendant stood up and sprinkled the seat occupied by the king, with water.

## \|\| 1.97.21 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā kopasaṃpannaḥ sa rājā'bhyetya vāsavam \|*  
*provāca kimidaṃ śakra prokṣyate yanmamāsanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing it the king got angry. Approaching Vāsava he said: O Śakra, why is my seat sprinkled with water?

## \|\| 1.97.22 \|\|

*kiṃ mayā nihatā viprāḥ kiṃ vā viprasamudbhavam \|*  
*śāsanaṃ lopitaṃ kiṃcitkiṃ vā viprā viniṃditāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Were Brāhmaṇas killed by me? Were they censured by me? Was any charter or document connected with any Brāhmaṇa annulled by me?

## \|\| 1.97.23 \|\|

*kiṃ vā naṣṭo'smi saṃgrāme dṛṣṭvā śatrūnsamāgatān \|*  
*dainyaṃ vā jalpitaṃ teṣāṃ bhayatrastena cetasā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Did I run away from a battlefield on seeing the enemies arrive? Did I cry wretchedly and piteously before them with great fright in my mind?

## \|\| 1.97.24 \|\|

*mama rājye'thavā śakra durbalo balavattaraiḥ \|*  
*pīḍa़्yate vātha caurādyairmuṣyate vaṃcakaistathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Or, O Śakra, is any weak subject in my kingdom oppressed by more powerful persons. Is anyone robbed by thieves and others, or defrauded by cheats?

## \|\| 1.97.25 \|\|

*kiṃ vā rājye madīye ca jāyate yoniviplavaḥ \|*  
*saṃkaro vātha varṇānāṃ parityaktavidhikramaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Does a rape take place in my kingdom? Is there any mixture of castes and utter disorderliness due to the abandonment of holy rites?

## \|\| 1.97.26 \|\|

*kiṃ vā durjanavākyena dūṣito doṣavarjitaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍyate mama rājye ca kenacittridaśeśvara \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Or, O Lord of Devas, is any innocent person abused at the instance of wicked persons? Is he punished by anyone in my kingdom?

## \|\| 1.97.27 \|\|

*kiṃ vā cauro'tha pāpo vā gṛhīto doṣavānsvayam \|*  
*mucyate dravyalobhena tathānyo vā jugupsitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Or, is any thief, sinner or criminal who has been caught, or anyone else of contemptible conduct released (by a responsible officer) due to greed for money?

## \|\| 1.97.28 \|\|

*kiṃsvinmayā parityaktaḥ ko'pyatra śaraṇāgataḥ \|*  
*bhayatrastaḥ subhītena prāṇānāṃ tridaśādhipa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Or, O Lord of Devas, was anyone afraid for his very life, who had sought refuge in me abandoned by me, because I too was frightened for my very life?

## \|\| 1.97.29 \|\|

*kasya vā pṛṣṭhamāṃsāni bhakṣitāni mayā kvacit \|*  
*kaccicca tridaśādhīṣa brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Lord of Devas, was the flesh of anyone's back eaten by me? (Was anyone slandered and calumniated by me behind his back.) Did I act as a backbiter of any Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 1.97.30 \|\|

*kiṃ vā dānaṃ mayā dattvā brāhmaṇāya mahātmane \|\| paścāttāpaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaḥ paścāddattaṃ copekṣitaṃ ca vā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Did I regret at any time after making any gift to a noble-souled Brāhmaṇa? Did I neglect any of my good duties.

## \|\| 1.97.31 \|\|

*kiṃ vā rājye madīye ca dīnānāṃ prapataṃti ca \|*  
*aśrupātā divārātraṃ duḥkhitānāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Do the tears of wretched people in great distress continuously fall in my kingdom whether at night or during the day?

## \|\| 1.97.32 \|\|

*daivaṃ vā paitṛkaṃ vāpi kiṃ vā karma gṛhe mama \|*  
*lopaṃ gacchati devendra kriyate vā vidhicyutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Devendra, does any rite pertaining to the Devas or the Pitṛs suffer from omission or negligence in my abode? Is any rite performed disregarding the injunctions thereof?

## \|\| 1.97.33 \|\|

*yattvayā kriyate nityaṃ toyairabhyukṣaṇaṃ mama \|*  
*āsanasya drutaṃ brūyā yatpāpaṃ vihitaṃ mayā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Tell me quickly whether any sin has been committed by me for which my seat is being sprinkled with water on every occasion.

## \|\| 1.97.34 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*na vidyate mahārāja śarīre tava pātakam \|*  
*na rāṣṭre ca kule gehe bhṛtyavarge viśeṣataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Indra said:

34\. O great king, there is no sin (at all) in your physical form, abode, family, group of attendants or in the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.97.35 \|\|

*paraṃ śṛṇu pravakṣyāmi yatte pāpaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tena saṃprokṣyate caiva āsanaṃ sarvadaiva tu \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. But listen, I shall explain. A sin is likely to occur, for which your seat is always sprinkled.

## \|\| 1.97.36-41 \|\|

*aputrasya gatirnāsti na ca svargaṃ prapadyate \|*  
*paitṛkeṇa naro grasto ya ṛṇena sadā nṛpa \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dveṣyatāṃ yāti devānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yadā paśyati putrasya vadanaṃ puruṣo nṛpa \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ānṛṇyaṃ samavāpnoti pitṝṇāṃ sa tadā dhruvam \|*  
*sa tvaṃ naiva gato rājannānṛṇyaṃ yanmayoditam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pitṝṇāṃ tena te nityamāsane'bhyukṣaṇaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tasmādyatasva putrārthaṃ yadīcchasi parāṃ gatim \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ narakāttrātuṃ puṃsaṃjñācca tathā nṛpa \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa śakreṇa rājā daśarathastadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*duḥkhena mahatā yukto lajjayā'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*āmaṃtryātha sahasrākṣaṃ gatvā'yodhyāṃ nijāṃ purīm \|*  
*amātyānāṃ nijaṃ rājyamarpayāmāsa satvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

36-41. One without a son has no salvation. He does hot go to Svarga. O king, a man who has not paid off the debt due to the Pitṛs becomes reprehensible to Devas and Pitrs in particular.

When a man sees the face of a son, O king, he certainly becomes free from the indebtedness to the Pitṛs.

O king, you have never been free from the indebtedness I refer to. You are not free from the indebtedness to the Pitrs. Hence the seat is always being sprinkled.

If you wish for salvation, make efforts to get a son in order to save yourself from the Naraka named Put, O king.

On being told thus by Śakra, King Daśaratha became overwhelmed with excess of shame. He stood facing down.

He took leave of the Thousand-eyed One and went to his city of Ayodhyā. Immediately he handed over his kingdom to the ministers.

## \|\| 1.97.42-43 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānsarvāṃstapaḥ kāryaṃ mayā'dhunā \|*  
*yāvatputrasya saṃprāptistāvadeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*etadrājyaṃ prayatnena rakṣaṇīyaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*yuṣmābhirmama vākyena yāvadāgamanaṃ mama \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Then he spoke to them all: “Penance has to be performed by me now. Undoubtedly the penance has to be continued until I get a son. At my bidding this kingdom has to be duly guarded by you all assiduously till I come back.”

## \|\| 1.97.46 \|\|

*kārtikeyapuraṃ gatvā yatra pitrā purā tava \|*  
*tapastaptaṃ yathā labdhā siddhiśca manasepsitā \|\| 46 \|\|*

The ministers said:

46\. O great king, this endeavour for the sake of a son is proper indeed. Of what avail is the kingdom or wealth for a man without a son?

## \|\| 1.97.45-46 \|\|

*vayaṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmastava rājye samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*nirvṛtiṃ tvaṃ samāsthāya kuru putrakṛte tapaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kārtikeyapuraṃ gatvā yatra pitrā purā tava \|*  
*tapastaptaṃ yathā labdhā siddhiśca manasepsitā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. We shall protect your kingdom. Be free from worry and perform the penance for the sake of a son. It shall be more or less in the same manner as in the case of your father who went to Kārttikeyapura formerly, performed a penance and attained the Siddhi desired by him mentally.

## Chapter 98 - Greatness of Rājavāpī

## \|\| 1.98.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato daśaratho rājā maṃtribhistairvisarjitaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ saṃprāpto harṣasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatrāgatya tato devīṃ pitrā saṃsthāpitā purā \|*  
*pūjayitvā'tha sadbhaktyā snātvā kuṇḍe śubhodake \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tato'nyāni ca mukhyāni dṛṣṭvā cāyatanāni saḥ \|*  
*snātvā tīrtheṣvanekeṣu dattvā dānānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra saṃsthāpayāmāsa pratimāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ śubhām \|\| 4 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 98 (Rājavāpī), 99 (Sage Durvāsā’s Curse) sum up Rāma’s life upto the death of Lakṣmaṇa. Then instead of returning to Ayodhyā, Rāma asks his ministers to crown Kuśa. Rāma goes to Sugrīva and ihen to Vibhīṣaṇa. He install three Liṅgas on the Setu, but at Vibhīṣaṇa’s request he breaks Setu in the middle.—Chapters 100-101. He returns with Vānaras and Rākṣasas to Ayodhyā but on the ways his aerial chariot Puṣpaka stops at Hāṭakeśvara. He builds Śiva temples in the name of his brother and Sītā (Chapter 102). Monkeys and Rākṣasas install their Liṅgas.

Sūta said:

1-4. Then bidding farewell to his ministers, King Daśaratha joyously went to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara.

After his arrival, he worshipped the goddess installed earlier by his father. With great devotion he had already had his bath in the holy Kuṇḍa of splendid waters.

Thereafter, he had his holy ablutions in many Tīrthas. He visited all important shrines and made gifts of many kinds. He constructed a palace-like temple of the Discus-bearing Lord of Devas and installed the splendid icon of Viṣṇu there.

## \|\| 1.98.5 \|\|

*tasyāgre kārayāmāsa vāpīṃ svacchodakānvitām \|*  
*sopānapaṃktibhiryuktāṃ sādhubhiḥ saṃpraśaṃsitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In front of it, he got a big tank full of clear water made with rows of flights of steps. All good men praised it duly.

## \|\| 1.98.6 \|\|

*udakena tatastasyā devārādhanatatparaḥ \|*  
*prakārairbahubhistīvraṃ cakāra sumahattapaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The water thereof was respectfully made use of by him in the regular propitiation of the Lord. He performed severe penances of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.98.7 \|\|

*tato varṣaśate'tīte tasya tuṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vilokya ca tapastīvraṃ vihitaṃ tena bhūbhujā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Seeing the severe penance performed by that king, Lord Janārdana was pleased with him after the lapse of a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.98.8 \|\|

*provāca darśanaṃ gatvā pakṣirājaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*meghagambhīrayāvācā bahudevagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Seated on the King of Birds (Garuḍa) and surrounded by many groups of Devas, the Lord appeared before the king and spoke in a majestic voice like the rumbling of a cloud.

## \|\| 1.98.9 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*api te durlabhaṃ kāmamahaṃ dāsyāmi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

9\. O dear one, I am pleased with you. O king of excellent holy vows, choose your boon. Even if your desire is very difficult to be fulfilled, I shall grant it entirely.

## \|\| 1.98.10 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*putrārtho'yaṃ samāraṃbho mayā deva kṛto'khilaḥ \|*  
*tapaso dehi me putrāṃstasmādvaṃśavivṛddhidān \|\| 10 \|\|*

The king said:

10\. The whole of this undertaking of the penance by me is for the sake of sons. Grant me sons who will perpetuate my family.

## \|\| 1.98.11 \|\|

*anyatsarvaṃ surādhīśa dhruvamasti gṛhe sthitam \|*  
*prasādāttava yatkiṃcidvaibhavaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Overlord of Suras, everything else if of course present in the house. Thanks to your favour, I have some power and glory.

## \|\| 1.98.12 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tava gṛhe rājansvayameva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*avatāraṃ kariṣyāmi kṛtvā rūpacatuṣṭayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

12\. Undoubtedly, O king, I shall assume four forms and take incarnation in your abode.

## \|\| 1.98.13 \|\|

*devakāryāya tasmāttvaṃ gṛhaṃ gatvā mahīpate \|*  
*kuru rājyaṃ yathānyāyaṃ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the sake of Devas, I shall undertake this task. Hence, O king, do go home and rule over your great hereditary kingdom duly.

## \|\| 1.98.14 \|\|

*tatheyaṃ yā tvayā vāpī nirmitā vimalodakā \|*  
*rājavāpīti vikhyātā loke seyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The tank got dug by you that is full of pure water shall become well-known in the world as Rājavāpī (Royal Tank).

## \|\| 1.98.15-16 \|\|

*asyāṃ snātvā naro bhaktyā ya enāṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yuktaḥ saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tataḥ kariṣyati śrāddhaṃ yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ nṛpa \|*  
*aputraḥ prāpsyate putrānvaṃśavṛddhikarānsa hi \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. A man of great devotion should take his holy bath in this tank and worship this goddess with great ardour and faith on the fifth lunar day.

Thereafter, O king, he should perform Śrāddha for a year. If he has no sons he will beget sons who will perpetuate the family.

## \|\| 1.98.17 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭavadano bhūtvā so'pi rājā yayau gṛham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After saying thus, the Lord vanished. With his face beaming with delight the king too went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.98.18 \|\|

*tataḥ stokena kālena tasya putracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*saṃjātaṃ loke vikhyātaṃ kalatratritayasya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Within a short time thereafter, he begot of his three wives four sons who became well-known in the world.

## \|\| 1.98.19 \|\|

*kauśalyānāma vikhyātā tasya bhāryā suśobhanā \|*  
*jyeṣṭhā tasyāṃ suto jajñe rāmākhyaḥ prathamaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. His splendid eldest queen was well-known by the name Kauśalyā. His first son named Rāma was born of her.

## \|\| 1.98.20 \|\|

*tathānyā kaikayī nāma tasya bhāryā kaniṣṭhikā \|*  
*bharato nāma vikhyātastasyāḥ putro'bhavattvasau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The youngest of his wives was Kaikeyī by name. Her son was famous by the name Bharata.

## \|\| 1.98.21 \|\|

*sumitrākhyā tathā cānyā patnī yā madhyamā sthitā \|*  
*śatrughnalakṣmaṇau putrau tasyāṃ jātau mahābalau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Another wife of his, the middle one, was Sumitrā by name. Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa were her very powerful sons.

## \|\| 1.98.22 \|\|

*tathānyā kanyakā caikā babhūva varavarṇinī \|*  
*dadau yāṃ putrahīnasya lomapādasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He had a daughter of excellent complexion. She was given as the adopted daughter of King Lomapāda who had no sons.

## \|\| 1.98.23 \|\|

*ānṛṇyaṃ bhūpatiḥ prāpya evaṃ daśarathastadā \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ prayayau svargaṃ kṛtakṛtyastathā dvijāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. King Daśaratha thus attained freedom from the indebtedness to the Pitṛs, O Brāhmaṇas. With contentment, he went to Svarga.

## \|\| 1.98.24 \|\|

*atha rājā'bhavadrāmaḥ sārvabhaumastataḥ param \|*  
*rāvaṇo yena durdharṣo nihato devakaṃṭakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Rāma became the king and an emperor later. Rāvaṇa, the unassailable thorn of Devas, was killed by him.

## \|\| 1.98.25 \|\|

*yena rāmeśvaraścātra nirmito lakṣmaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*sītādevī tathā mūrtā yena cātra pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Rāmeśvara, Lakṣṃaṇeśvara and Sītā the goddess in a visible image—all these deities were installed by him.

## Chapter 99 - Sage Durvāsa Visits Rāma

## \|\| 1.99.1-5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tatra rāmeṇa nirmitaḥ \|*  
*rāmeśvarastathā sītā tena tatra vinirmitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathā ca lakṣmaṇārthāya nirmitastena saṃśrayaḥ \|*  
*etanmahadviruddhaṃ te pratibhāti vaco'khilam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tvayā sūta purā proktaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sītayā sahitaḥ prāptaḥ kṣetre'tra prasthito vane \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā gayāśīrṣe lakṣmaṇena viruddhya ca \|*  
*punaḥ saṃprasthito'raṇyaṃ krodhāviṣṭaśca taṃ prati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yattvayoktaṃ tadā tena nirmito'tra maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*etacca sarvamācakṣva saṃdehaṃ sūtanandana \|\| 5 \|\|*

Note: The episode of Durvāsā’s interference in the Devadūta’s conference with Rāma is based on Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, VII sages 103-105.

The sages said:

1-5. O Sūta, you say that by Rāma the deity Rāmeśvara was installed there; similarly, that Sītā was also installed and further that a resort was made by him for the sake of Lakṣmaṇa. These words of yours entirely appear to be contradictory.

O Sūta, earlier you said thus: “Accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, Rāma who was travelling through forests reached this holy spot. After performing Śrāddha in Gayāśīrṣa he had some dispute with Lakṣmaṇa. Angry with him, he went again to the forest.” There was mentioned by you, “Maheśvara was installed by him.” There is a doubt in this, O Sūtanandana, kindly clarify it fully.

## \|\| 1.99.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra me nāsti saṃdeho yuṣmākaṃ ca punaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tato vakṣyāmyaśeṣeṇa śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*etatkṣetraṃ punaścādyaṃ na kṣayaṃ yāti kutracit \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. In this regard I have no doubt; but you have. Hence I shall explain everything completely. May it be heard, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. This is the primordial holy spot. It does not perish at all.

## \|\| 1.99.7 \|\|

*anyasmindivase prāpte sa tadā raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*yadā virodhamāpannaḥ sārdhaṃ saumitriṇā saha \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It was on a different day that Raghunandana got into dispute with the son of Sumitrā.

## \|\| 1.99.8 \|\|

*etatpunardinaṃ cānyadyatra tena pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*rāmeśvaraḥ svayaṃ bhaktyā duḥkhitena mahātmanā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. But this day when Rāmeśvara was installed by him was a different day altogether. The noble-souled one in a miserable state of mind installed Rāmeśvara himself devoutly.

## \|\| 1.99.9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*anyasmindivase tatra kasminkāle raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptastasya kiṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃjātaṃ tatprakīrtaya \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:

9\. At what time did Raghūttama come there on a certain day? What was the misery he was in? Do narrate this.

## \|\| 1.99.10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kṛtvā sītāparityāgaṃ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ \|*  
*lokāpavādasaṃtrastastato rājyaṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

10\. Afraid of the popular (scandalous) talk against him, the lotus-eyed Rāma abandoned Sītā, but continued to rule the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.99.11 \|\|

*kṛtvā svarṇamayīṃ sītāṃ patnīṃ yajñaprasiddhaye \|*  
*na sa cakre mahābhāgo bhāryāmanyāṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The highly esteemed one did not take another wife. For the proper performance of the Yajña, he made a gold icon of Sītā and placed it in the position of his wife.

## \|\| 1.99.12 \|\|

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*brahmacaryeṇa cakre sa rājyaṃ nihatakaṃṭakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Uprooting all enemies like thorns he ruled for eleven thousand years, observing full celibacy.

## \|\| 1.99.13 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte prāpte caikādaśe dvijāḥ \|*  
*devadūtaḥ samāyāto rāmasya sadanaṃ prati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the close of the eleven-thousandth year, O Brāhmaṇas, a messenger from the Devas come to Rāma’s abode.

## \|\| 1.99.14 \|\|

*tenoktaṃ devarājena preṣito'haṃ tavāṃtikam \|*  
*tasmātkuru samālokaṃ vijane tvaṃ mayā saha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He said: “I have been deputed to you by the king of the Devas. Hence do meet me in an isolated place.”

## \|\| 1.99.15 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena dūtena raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ rahaḥ samāsādya mantraṃ cakre tataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On being told thus by the messenger, Raghunandana came to a very secret place and then took counsel with him.

## \|\| 1.99.16 \|\|

*tasyaivamupaviṣṭasya maṃtrasthāne mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*bahutvādiṣṭalokasya na rahasyaṃ prajāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Although he came and sat in the place of discussion, there was still no privacy because there were too many close relatives.

## \|\| 1.99.17 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā dūtaḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*vihasya janasaṃsargaṃ dṛṣṭvaikāṃte'pi saṃsthite \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Seeing the throng of people in what was expected to be a secluded spot, the messenger (of Indra) laughed a little at the outset. But immediately he became very angry and spoke thus vehemently:

## \|\| 1.99.18-19 \|\|

*yathā daṃṣṭrācyutaḥ sarpo nāgo vā madavarjitaḥ \|*  
*ājñāhīnastathā rājā mānavaiḥ paribhūyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*seyaṃ tava raghuśreṣṭha nājñāsti prativedmyaham \|*  
*śakrālāpamapi tvaṃ ca naikāṃte śrotumarhasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. “Like a serpent with the poisonous fangs extracted or an elephant devoid of ichor, a king who cannot implement his own command, is treated with contempt by men. O most excellent one among the scions of Raghu, I have understood that you have ceased to exert your ability to command. It has come to this that you cannot listen even to the message of Śakra in adequate privacy.”

## \|\| 1.99.20 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*triśākhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ sa prāha lakṣmaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing his words, Rāma’s eyes turned red due to anger. With knitted eyebrows he said to Lakṣmaṇa:

## \|\| 1.99.21-23 \|\|

*mamātra saṃniviṣṭasya sahānena prajalpataḥ \|*  
*yadi kaścinnaro mohādāgamiṣyati lakṣmaṇa \|*  
*svahastena na saṃdehaḥ sūdayiṣyāmi taṃ drutam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*na hanmi yadi taṃ prāptamatra me dṛṣṭigocaram \|*  
*tanmā bhūnme gatiḥ śreṣṭhā dharmiṇāṃ yā prapadyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā prayatnena tvayā bhāvyamasaṃśayam \|*  
*rājadvāri yathā kaścinna mayā vadhyate'dhunā \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. “While I am seated here in conference with this gentleman, O Lakṣmaṇa, If any man becomes so deluded as to interrupt, I will slay him soon with my own hand undoubtedly. Should I fail to slay him even when he comes here and falls within the range of my vision, let me not attain the excellent goal of a virtuous one.

After realizing this you should be alert yourself at the royal entrance, without hesitation or doubt. Let there not be an occasion when someone is slain by me now at the royal entrance itself.”

## \|\| 1.99.24 \|\|

*tamomityeva saṃprocya lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rājadvāraṃ samāsādya cakāra vijanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Lakṣmaṇa said “om” (Yes) by way of assent. Marked with all excellent features, Lakṣmaṇa came to the royal entrance and turned away all the people therefrom.

## \|\| 1.99.25 \|\|

*devadūto'pi rāmeṇa samaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|*  
*maṃtraṃ śakrasamādiṣṭaṃ tathānyaiḥ svargavāsibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The messenger of the Devas held the discussion with Rāma as ordered by Śakra and other inhabitants of Svarga.

## \|\| 1.99.26 \|\|

*devadūta uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ rāvaṇavināśārthamavatīrṇo dharātale \|*  
*sa ca vyāpādito duṣṭaḥ pāpastrailokyakaṃṭakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Devadūta said:

26\. It is for the annihilation of Rāvaṇa that you have taken the incarnation on the earth. That wicked one, the sinful thorn of the three worlds, has been slain.

## \|\| 1.99.27 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ mahābhāga deva kṛtyaṃ tvayā'dhunā \|*  
*tasmātsaṃtu sanāthāste devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Everything connected with the task of Devas has been concluded by you, O highly esteemed one. So let the Devas with Śakra as their leader get their Nātha (Lord) (i.e. yourself) once again

## \|\| 1.99.28 \|\|

*yadi te rocate citte noparodhena sāṃpratam \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru devānāṃ tasmādāgaccha satvaram \|*  
*svargalokaṃ parityajya martyalokaṃ suniṃditam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Do this favour unto Devas if you like. It is not proper on our part to press our importunity. Leave this highly despised mortal world and come quickly to the heavenly world.

## \|\| 1.99.29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāpto durvāsā munisattamaḥ \|*  
*provācātha kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ kvāsau kvāsau raghūttamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

29\. In the meantime Durvāsas, the excellent sage, reached the place. Assailed by hunger he asked loudly: “Where is he? Where is the most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu?”

## \|\| 1.99.30 \|\|

*lakṣmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*vyagraḥ sa pārthivaśreṣṭho devakāryeṇa kenacit \|*  
*tasmādatraiva vipreṃdra muhūrtaṃ paripālaya \|\| 30 \|\|*

Lakṣmaṇa said:

30\. O leading Brāhmaṇa, kindly wait here for a short while. Our excellent king is engaged in some task of Devas.

## \|\| 1.99.31 \|\|

*yāvatsāṃtvayate rāmo dūtaṃ śakrasamudbhavam \|*  
*mamopari dayāṃ kṛtvā vinayāvanatasya hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I humbly bow down and beseech you. Take pity on me. Please wait till Rāma satisfies the messenger of Śakra.

## \|\| 1.99.32 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*yadi yāsyati no dṛṣṭiṃ mama drāksa raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*śāpaṃ dattvā kulaṃ sarvaṃ taddhakṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

32\. If Raghūttama does not grant me audience (lit. come within the range of my sight) immediately I shall no doubt reduce the entire family to ashes by burning.

## \|\| 1.99.33 \|\|

*mamāpi darśanādanyanna kiṃcidvidyate guru \|*  
*kṛtyaṃ lakṣmaṇa yāvattvamanyanmūḍha़ prakatthase \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. There is no other task weightier than meeting me. O foolish Lakṣmaṇa, why do you prattle something else?

## \|\| 1.99.34 \|\|

*tacchrutvā lakṣmaṇaścitte ciṃtayāmāsa duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ me mṛtyurekasya mā bhūyātkulasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On hearing it, Lakṣmaṇa thought within his mind rather miserably. ‘Better that I alone die. Let not the whole family be ruined.’

## \|\| 1.99.35 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā tato rāmamupādravat \|*  
*uvāca daṃḍavadbhūmau praṇipatya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After resolving thus, he rushed to Rāma and feel at his feet on the ground like a log of wood. He then said with palms joined in reverence with a humble bow:

## \|\| 1.99.36 \|\|

*durvāsā muniśārdūlo deva te dvāri tiṣṭhati \|*  
*darśanārthī kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “O Lord, Durvāsas, the tiger among sages, stands at the entrance. He is hungry and wishes to see you. What shall I do, please command me.”

## \|\| 1.99.37 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tato dūtamuvāca tam \|*  
*gatvemaṃ brūhi deveśaṃ mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*ahaṃ saṃvatsarasyāṃta āgamiṣyāmi teṃ'tike \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing his words Rāma said to the messenger: “At my instance go back to the Lord of Devas and tell him unhesitatingly that I will come to him by the end of a year.”

## \|\| 1.99.38 \|\|

*evamuktvā visṛjyātha taṃ dūtaṃ prāha lakṣmaṇam \|*  
*praveśaya drutaṃ vatsa taṃ tvaṃ durvāsasaṃ munim \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After saying thus he despatched the messenger. Then he said to Lakṣmaṇa, “Dear one, do usher in Sage Durvāsas immediately.”

## \|\| 1.99.39 \|\|

*tataścārghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca gṛhītvā sammukho yayau \|*  
*rāmadevaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā sacivaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Rāma, the Lord then happily took Arghya and Pādya and proceeded welcome the sage joyously. He was accompanied by the ministers.

## \|\| 1.99.40-42 \|\|

*dattvārghyaṃ vidhivattasya praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*provāca rāmadevo'tha harṣagadgadayā girā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha bhūyaḥ susvāgataṃ ca te \|*  
*etadrājyamamī putrā vibhavaśca tava prabho \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṛtvā mama prasādaṃ ca gṛhāṇa munisattama \|*  
*dhanyo'smyanugṛhīto'smi yattvaṃ me gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*pūjyo lokatrayasyāpi niḥśeṣatapasāṃnidhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. After duly offering the Arghya and bowing down repeatedly Rāma, the Lord, spoke with words choked due to delight: “Welcome, O excellent sage. Welcome unto you. This kingdom, these sons, and the riches are yours, O holy Sir.

Do this favour unto me, O excellent sage. Accept this. I am blessed and contented that you came to my abode. You are worthy of being worshipped by the three worlds. You are the storehouse of all austerities.”

## \|\| 1.99.43-46 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*cāturmāsyavrataṃ kṛtvā nirāhāro raghūttama \|*  
*adya te bhavanaṃ prāpya āhārārthaṃ bubhukṣitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ yaccha me śīghraṃ bhojanaṃ raghunaṃdana \|*  
*nānyena kāraṇaṃ kiṃcitsaṃnyastasya dhanādinā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatastaṃ bhojayāmāsa śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*svayamevāgrataḥ sthitvā mṛṣṭānnairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*lehyaiścoṣyaistathā carvyaiḥ khādyaireva pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*yāvadicchā munestasya tathānnairvividhairapi \|\| 46 \|\|*

The sage said:

43-46. O Raghūttama, I have been fasting after concluding my Cāturmāsya Vrata. In my hunger I have now come to your abode for food. O Raghunandana, feed me quickly. I am a recluse. I have nothing to do with anything else such as ready cash etc.

Rāma stood in from and faithfully caused him to be fed with excellent dishes of various kinds of lambatives, chewables, and other types of foods to be swallowed and licked up till the sage was fully satisfied. Foodstuffs of various kinds were also served.

## Chapter 100 - Śrīrāma Goes to the City of Sugrīva

## \|\| 1.100.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhuktvā sa viprarṣirvāṃchayā rāmamaṃdire \|*  
*dattāśīrnirgataḥ paścādāmaṃtrya raghunaṃdanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Thus the saintly Brāhmaṇa eagerly took food in Rāma’s palace. Then he showered benedictions on Raghunandana and taking leave of him, departed thence.

## \|\| 1.100.2 \|\|

*atha yāte munau tasmindurvāsasi tadaṃtikāt \|*  
*lakṣmaṇaḥ khaṅgamādāya rāmadevamuvāca ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Sage Durvāsas had gone from the vicinity of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa took the sword and spoke to Rāma:

## \|\| 1.100.3 \|\|

*etatkhaṅgaṃ gṛhītvāśu māṃ prabho vinipātaya \|*  
*yena te syādṛtaṃ vākyaṃ pratijñātaṃ ca yatpurā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “O my Lord, take this sword and slay me quickly so that your earlier vow may be fulfilled.”

## \|\| 1.100.4 \|\|

*tato rāmaścirātsmṛtvā tāṃ pratijñāṃ svayaṃ kṛtām \|*  
*vadhārthaṃ saṃpraviṣṭasya samīpe puruṣasya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Rāma later recollected the vow he himself had taken earlier that a person who interrupted would be killed.

## \|\| 1.100.5 \|\|

*tato'ticiṃtayāmāsa vyākulenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*bāṣpavyākulanetraśca niḥṣvasanpannago yathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. His mind became agitated as he began pondering. His eyes became dim with tears. Like a serpent he began to heave sighs.

## \|\| 1.100.6 \|\|

*taṃ dīnavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā niḥṣvasaṃtaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*bhūyaḥ provāca saumitrirvinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing him sad-faced and heaving repeated sighs, the Son of Sumitrā who was politely standing by spoke again:

## \|\| 1.100.7-10 \|\|

*eṣa eva paro dharmo bhūpatīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yathātmīyaṃ vacastathyaṃ kriyate nirvikalpitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmāttvayā prabho proktaṃ svayameva mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva devadūtasya tāranādena kopataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yo'trāgacchati saumitre mama dūtasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*taṃ ceddhanmi svahastena nāhaṃ tasmātsupāpakṛt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ cāgatastāta bhayāddurvāsaso muneḥ \|*  
*niṣiddho'pi tvayātīva tasmācchīghraṃ tu ghātaya \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. “This alone is the greatest virtue, especially in the case of kings, that words are unhesitatingly kept true. O Lord, in front of me as well as of the messenger of Devas, you had uttered thus angrily and loudly: ‘O son of Sumitrā, if I do not myself kill a person who comes near me and the messenger. I will be a greater sinner than he.’ O dear brother, I came in because I was afraid of Sage Durvāsas, though you had expressly prohibited it. Hence kill me soon.”

## \|\| 1.100.11 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃmaṃtrya suciraṃ maṃtribhiḥ sahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇairdharmaśāstrajñaistathānyairvedapāragaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The king then consulted his ministers for a long time along with the Brāhmaṇas well-conversant with Dharmaśāstras and others who had mastered the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.100.12 \|\|

*provāca lakṣmaṇaṃ paścādvinayāvanataṃ sthitam \|*  
*vāṣpaklinnamukho rāmo gadgadaṃ niḥśvasanmuhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Afterwards he spoke to Lakṣmaṇa who was standing by humbly. Rāma was then heaving sighs repeatedly. His face was drenched with tears. While he spoke, he faltered in his speech:

## \|\| 1.100.13-14 \|\|

*vraja lakṣmaṇa muktastvaṃ mayā deśātaraṃ drutam \|*  
*tyāgo vātha vadho vātha sādhūnāmubhayaṃ samam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*na mayā darśanaṃ bhūyastava kāryaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*na sthātavyaṃ ca deśe'pi yadi me vāṃchasi priyam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. “O Lakṣmaṇa, you have been abandoned by me, go to another land immediately. In the case of good persons banishment and killing both are equal. I should not see you again on any account. If you wish to do what pleases me, you shall not stay in this land any more.”

## \|\| 1.100.15 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā praṇipatya tataḥ param \|*  
*niryayau nagarāttasmāttatkṣaṇādeva lakṣmaṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On hearing his words, Lakṣmaṇa bowed down to him and went out of that city instantly.

## \|\| 1.100.16 \|\|

*akṛtvāpi samālāpaṃ kenacinnijamaṃdire \|*  
*mātrā vā bhāryayā vātha sutena suhṛdāthavā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He did not talk to anyone in the palace, either with mother, wife, son or friend.

## \|\| 1.100.17 \|\|

*tato'sau sarayūṃ gatvā'vagāhyātha ca tajjalam \|*  
*śucirbhūtvā niviṣṭotha tattīre vijane śubhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then he went to River Sarayū and entered the waters thereof. After purifying himself, he sat on the banks in a secluded but very splendid spot.

## \|\| 1.100.18 \|\|

*padmāsanaṃ vidhāyātha nyasyātmānaṃ tathātmani \|*  
*brahmadvāreṇa taṃ paścāttejorūpaṃ vyasarjayat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He adopted the posture of Padmāsana; concentrated the soul within the supreme Ātman. Thereafter he discharged (himself in) the form of Tejas (splendour) through the Brahmadvāra (cerebral aperture).

## \|\| 1.100.19 \|\|

*atha tadrāghavo dṛṣṭvā mahattejo viyadgatam \|*  
*vismayena samāyukto'cintayatkimidaṃ tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Rāghava saw that great Tejas going up into the sky. He was surprised and thought: ‘What could be this?’.

## \|\| 1.100.20 \|\|

*atha martye parityakte tejasā tena tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*vaiṣṇavena turīyeṇa bhāgena dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that fourth part of Viṣṇu, the Tejas, abandoned the mortal sphere.

## \|\| 1.100.21 \|\|

*papāta bhūtale kāyaṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭopamaṃ drutam \|*  
*lakṣmaṇasya gataśrīkaṃ sarayvāḥ puline śubhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At the very instant, Lakṣmaṇa’s physical body fell down on the ground on the splendid banks of Sarayū, devoid of all glory, like a piece of wood or a lump of clay.

## \|\| 1.100.22 \|\|

*tatastu rāghavaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaṃ gatajīvitam \|*  
*patitaṃ saritastīre vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On hearing that Lakṣmaṇa had ceased to live and his body had fallen on the river bank, Rāghava lamented miserably.

## \|\| 1.100.23 \|\|

*svayaṃ gatvā tamuddeśaṃ sāmātyaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmaṇaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā karuṇaṃ paryadevayat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Along with his ministers and friends, he himself went to that place. Seeing Lakṣmaṇa fallen he lamented piteously:

## \|\| 1.100.24-30 \|\|

*hā vatsa māṃ parityajya kiṃ tvaṃ saṃprasthito divam \|*  
*prāṇeṣṭaṃ bhrātaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sadā tava mate sthitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasminnapi mahāraṇye gacchamānaḥ purādaham \|\|\| \|*  
*api saṃdhāryamāṇena anuyātastvayā tadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saṃprāpte'pi kabaṃdhākhye rākṣase balavattare \|*  
*tvayā rātrimukhe ghore sabhāryo'haṃ prarakṣitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yenendrajiddhato yuddhe tādṛgrūpo niśācaraḥ \|*  
*sa eṣa patitaḥ śete gatāsurdharaṇītale \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yena śūrpaṇakhā dhvastā rākṣasī sā ca dāruṇā \|*  
*līlayāpi mamādeśātsoyamevaṃvidhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yadbāhubalamāśritya mayā dhvastā niśācarāḥ \|*  
*so'yaṃ nipatitaḥ śete mama bhrātā hyanāthavat \|\|\| \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hā vatsa kva gato māṃ tvaṃ vimucya bhrātaraṃ nijam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ prāṇasamaṃ kiṃ te sneho'dya vigataḥ kvacit \|\| 30 \|\|*

24-30. “Alas! My dear one, why have you proceeded to heaven forsaking me, your dearest and most excellent brother who always abided by your suggestions?

When I proceeded to the great forest from the city I was followed by you who upheld me.

When the highly powerful Rākṣasa named Kabandha attacked at night, my wife and I were protected by you from the terrible plight.

Here he lies fallen lifeless on the ground—he by whom a Rākṣasa of such a terrible form, namely Indrajit, had been killed in battle.

He by whom the terrible demoness Śūrpaṇakhā was assailed as if for sport, at my order, has come to this state.

My brother whose might helped me to destroy demons, has fallen down here as though helpless.

Alas! My dear one, where have you gone leaving your own eldest brother who has been like your very vital airs? Has your love and affection strayed away elsewhere?”

## \|\| 1.100.31 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bahuvidhānkṛtvā pralāpānraghunandanaḥ \|*  
*mātṛbhiḥ sahito dīnaḥ śokena mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sūta said:

31\. Thus in the company of his mothers, Raghunandana, being afflicted with great grief, lamented much.

## \|\| 1.100.32 \|\|

*tataste maṃtriṇastasya procustaṃ vīkṣya duḥkhitam \|\| \|*  
*vilapaṃtaṃ raghuśreṣṭhaṃ strījanena samanvitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On seeing the most excellent one among the scions of Raghu’s family thus lamenting in the company of the womenfolk, the ministers spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.100.33 \|\|

*maṃtriṇa ūcuḥ \|*  
*mā śokaṃ kuru rājendra yathānyaḥ prākṛtaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*kuruṣva ca yathedaṃ syātsāṃprataṃ caurdhvadaihikam \|\| 33 \|\|*

The ministers said:

33\. O great king, do not be grief-stricken like an unenlightened one. Make arrangements so that the obsequial rites may be performed.

## \|\| 1.100.34 \|\|

*naṣṭaṃ mṛtamatītaṃ ca ye śocanti kubuddhayaḥ \|*  
*dhīrāṇāṃ tu purā rājannaṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ mṛtaṃ mṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those who bewail what is lost, dead or past are foolish and silly. Bold and intelligent men treat what is lost as lost and what is dead as dead.

## \|\| 1.100.35-37 \|\|

*evaṃ te mantriṇaḥ procya tatastasya kalevaram \|*  
*lakṣmaṇasya vilapyauccaiścandanośīrakuṃkumaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*karpūrāgurumiśraiśca tathānyaiḥ susugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*pariveṣṭya śubhairvastraiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃbhūṣya śobhanaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*candanāgurukāṣṭhaiśca citiṃ kṛtvā suvistarām \|*  
*nyadadhustasya tadgātraṃ tatra dakṣiṇadiṅmukham \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. After saying thus the ministers got the dead body of Lakṣmaṇa smeared with sandal, Uśīra (Khus, ta frgrant root) and saffron. These were mixed with camphor, Aguru (Agallochum) and other sweet scents. The dead body was then decorated in excellent cloths and embellished with splendid flowers. A broad pyre was then made with sandal and Aguru wood. They then placed the body on it facing the South.

## \|\| 1.100.38 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jātaṃ tatrāścaryaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tanme nigadataḥ sarvaṃ śṛṇvaṃtu sakalaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the meantime, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, something miraculous and mysterious took place. Do listen to it even as I narrate.

## \|\| 1.100.39 \|\|

*yāvatteṃ'taḥ samāropya citāṃ tasya kalevaram \|*  
*prayacchaṃti havirvāhaṃ tāvannaṣṭaṃ kalevaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. While they placed the body on the pyre and were about to kindle the fire, the body vanished.

## \|\| 1.100.40 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vāṇī nirgatā gaganāṃgaṇāt \|*  
*nādayaṃtī diśaḥ sarvāḥ puṣpavarṣādanaṃtaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the meantime a voice rose up in the firmament after a shower of flowers. All the quarters reverberated with the sound:

## \|\| 1.100.41-43 \|\|

*rāmarāma mahābāho mā tvaṃ śokaparo bhava \|*  
*na cāsya yujyate vahnirdātuṃ caiva kathaṃcana \|\| 41 \|\|*

*brahmajñānaprayuktasya saṃnyastasya viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*agnidānaṃ na yuktaṃ syātsarveṣāmapi yoginām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tavāyaṃ bāṃdhavo rāma brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*brahmadvāreṇa cātmānaṃ niṣkramya sumahāyaśāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. “O Rāma, O Rāma, O mighty-armed one, do not be distressed. It is not at all proper to apply fire to him (Lakṣmaṇa).

Cremation by the application of fire is not proper in regard to one endowed with the knowledge of Brahman, particularly in the case of one who has renounced the world. Burning the bodies of all Yogins is improper.

O Rāma, your brother has gone to the abode of Brahman. The highly renowned one has released his soul through the cerebral aperture.”

## \|\| 1.100.44-45 \|\|

*atha te maṃtriṇaḥ procustacchrutvā'kāśagaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*aśocyo yaṃ mahārāja saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*lakṣmaṇo gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ tasmātsvabhavane vibho \|\| 44 \|\|*

*cintyantāṃ rājakāryāṇi tathā yaccaurdhvadaihikam \|*  
*kuru snehocitaṃ tasya pṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇasattamān \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. On hearing the aerial voice, those ministers said: “O great king, Lakṣmaṇa has attained the greatest Siddhi. He should not be grieved over. Hence, O Lord, hurry homewards.

The affairs of the state should be attended to, consult the excellent Brāhmaṇas and discuss the procedure of the obsequial rites. Do everything befitting your love for him.”

## \|\| 1.100.46 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ gṛhaṃ gamiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇena vinā'dhunā \|*  
*prāṇānatra vihāsyāmi yathā tena mahātmanā \|\| 46 \|\|*

Rāma said:

46\. I will not go home now without Lakṣmaṇa. I will give up my life here in the manner it had been done by that noble-souled one.

## \|\| 1.100.47 \|\|

*eṣa putro mayā dattaḥ kuśākhyo mama saṃmataḥ \|*  
*yuṣmabhyaṃ kriyatāṃ rājye madīye yadi rocate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This honoured son of mine named Kuśa has been entrusted to you all. If you like, he may be crowned as king of the state.

## \|\| 1.100.48 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato rāmo gantukāmo divālayam \|*  
*cintayāmāsa bhūyo'pi smṛtvā mitraṃ vibhīṣaṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After saying thus, Rāma felt the desire to go to heaven. But, on remembering his friend Vibhīṣaṇa he reconsidered it.

## \|\| 1.100.49-56 \|\|

*mayā tasya tadā dattaṃ laṃkāyāṃ rājyamakṣayam \|*  
*bahubhaktipratuṣṭena yāvaccandrārkatārakāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*atikrūratarā jātī rākṣasānāṃ yataḥ smṛtā \|*  
*viśeṣādvarapuṣṭānāṃ jāyate'tra dharātale \|\| 50 \|\|*

*taccedrākṣasabhāvena sa mahātmā vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati suraiḥ sārdhaṃ virodhaṃ rāvaṇo yathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*taṃ devāḥ sūdayiṣyaṃti upāyaiḥ sāmapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*trailokyakaṇṭako yadvattasya bhrātā daśānanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tato me syānmṛṣā vāṇī tasmādgatvā tadaṃtikam \|*  
*śikṣāṃ dadāmi tasyāhaṃ yathā devānna dūṣayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tathā me paramaṃ mitraṃ dvitīyaṃ vānaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sugrīvākhyo mahābhāgo jāṃbavāṃśca tathā'paraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sabhṛtyo vāyuputraśca vāliputrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*kumudākhyaśca tāraśca tathānye'pi ca vānarāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tasmāttānapi saṃbhāṣya sarvānsaṃmaṃtrya sādaram \|*  
*tato gacchāmi devānāṃ kṛtakṛtyo gṛhaṃ prati \|\| 56 \|\|*

49-56. ‘I was exceedingly pleased with his great devotion. So I gave him eternal rulership over Laṅkā lasting as long as the sun, moon and stars shine.

It is generally remembered that the community of the Rākṣasas is exceedingly cruel, especially of those richly endowed with boons on the earth.

It is possible that even the noble-souled Vibhīṣaṇa may, like Rāvaṇa, antagonize Suras, as a result of his inborn Rākṣasa nature.

As in the case of his Ten-headed Brother who verily was a thorn unto all the three worlds, Devas may bring about his death through Sāma and other expedients. In that case my words will be futile and untrue. So I shall go to him and advise him that he should not offend Devas.

Further there is a second great friend, the monkey named Sugrīva. Another one is the highly esteemed Jāṃbavān. Then there is that attendant, the son of Vāyu along with the son of key named Kumuda, then Tāra. There are other

So I will have eager dialogues and consultations with them too. Thereafter, I shall go home fully satisfied that the task of Devas has been completed.’

## \|\| 1.100.57 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃcintya suciraṃ samāhūya ca puṣpakam \|*  
*tatrāruhya yayau tūrṇaṃ kiṣkindhākhyāṃ purīṃ prati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After reflecting thus for a long time, he summoned Puṣpaka, the aerial chariot, got into it and hurried to the city named Kiṣkindhā.

## \|\| 1.100.58 \|\|

*atha te vānarā dṛṣṭvā proddyotaṃ puṣpakodbhavam \|*  
*vijñāya rāghavaṃ prāptaṃ satvaraṃ sammukhā yayuḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The monkeys saw the remarkable splendour of Puṣpaka and knew that Rāghava had arrived. They came face to face with him.

## \|\| 1.100.59 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya te dūrājjānubhyāmavaniṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*jayeti śabdamādāya muhurmuhuritastataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. From a long distance they bowed down to him and knelt before him on the ground. Then they repeatedly shouted “Be victorious.”

## \|\| 1.100.60 \|\|

*tatastenaiva saṃyuktāḥ kiṣkindhāṃ tāṃ mahāpurīm \|*  
*viviśuḥ satpatākābhiḥ samaṃtātsamalaṃkṛtām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Accompanying him they entered the great city of Kiṣkindhā that had been embellished all round with excellent banners.

## \|\| 1.100.61 \|\|

*athottīrya vimānāgryātsugrīvabhavane śubhe \|*  
*praviveśa drutaṃ rāmaḥ sarvataḥ suvibhūṣite \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Rāma alighted from the excellent aerial chariot and hastily entered the splendid and well embellished abode of Sugrīva.

## \|\| 1.100.62 \|\|

*tatra rāmaṃ niviṣṭaṃ te viśrāṃtaṃ vīkṣya vānarāḥ \|*  
*arghyādibhiśca saṃpūjya papracchustadanantaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Seeing that Rāma was seated calmly, the monkeys duly honoured him with Arghya etc; and later asked him:

## \|\| 1.100.63 \|\|

*vānarā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tejasā tvaṃ vinirmukto dṛśyase raghunandana \|*  
*kṛśo'syatīva codvignaḥ kaccitkṣemaṃ gṛhe tava \|\| 63 \|\|*

The monkeys said:

63\. O Raghunandana, you appear devoid of all your remarkable splendour! You are very lean and you seem to be distressed. Wh\[?\] hope, everything is all right there in your abode.

## \|\| 1.100.64 \|\|

*kāye vā'nugato nityaṃ tathā te lakṣmaṇo'nujaḥ \|*  
*na dṛśyate samīpasthaḥ kimadya tava rāghava \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. We hope, you are physically all right. Lakṣmaṇa, your borther, who used to follow you closely is not seen near you now? What has happened to you, O Rāghava?

## \|\| 1.100.65 \|\|

*tathā prāṇasamā'bhīṣṭā sītā tava prabho \|*  
*dṛśyate kiṃ na pārśvasthā etannaḥ kautukaṃ param \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Further, your favourite wife, as dear to you as your very vital air, is not seen at your side? We are very much anxious.

## \|\| 1.100.66 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ niḥśvasya rāghavaḥ \|*  
*vāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇo bhūtvā sarvaṃ teṣāṃ nyavedayat \|\| 66 \|\|*

Sūta said:

66\. On hearing their words, Rāghava heaved a long and heavy sigh. With tears in his eyes he told them everything:

## \|\| 1.100.67 \|\|

*atha sītā parityaktā tathā bhrātā sa lakṣmaṇaḥ \|*  
*yadarthaṃ tatra saṃprāptaḥ svayameva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he told them why Sītā was banished and brother Lakṣmaṇa abandoned. He told them why he himself had come.

## \|\| 1.100.68 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vānarāḥ sarve sugrīvapramukhāstataḥ \|*  
*ruruduste suduḥkhārtāḥ samāliṃgya tataḥ param \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On hearing it, all the monkeys with Sugrīva as the chief became highly miserable and they cried. They embraced each other for consolation.

## \|\| 1.100.69-70 \|\|

*evaṃ ciraṃ pralapyoccaistataḥ procū raghūttamam \|*  
*ādeśo dīyatāṃ rājanyo'smābhiriha sidhyati \|\| 69 \|\|*

*dhanyā vayaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe yeṣāṃ tvaṃ raghusattama \|*  
*īdṛksnehasamāyuktaḥ samāgacchasi maṃdire \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. After lamenting loudly thus for a long time, they said to Raghūttama: “O king, let us be commanded. What shall be done by us?

All over the earth we are the most blessed ones, O most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu, since you have come to our abode so full of affection!”

## \|\| 1.100.71 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*uṣitvā rajanīmekāṃ sugrīva tava maṃdire \|*  
*prātarlaṃkāṃ gamiṣyāmi yatrāste sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

Rāma said:

71\. O Sugrīva, I will stay in your place for a night. In the morning I will be going to Laṅkā where Vibhīṣaṇa stays.

## \|\| 1.100.72 \|\|

*pradhānāmātyayuktena tvayāpi kapisattama \|*  
*āgaṃtavyaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ vibhīṣaṇagṛhaṃ prati \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O most excellent one among monkeys, you should also come with me to the abode of Vibhīṣaṇa. Take the chief minister also with you.

## Chapter 101 - Installation of Rāmeśvara in the Middle of the Setu

## \|\| 1.101.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra sa uṣitvā raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*upāsyamānaḥ sarvaistaiḥ sadbhaktyā vānarottamaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṇḍale \|*  
*kṛtvā prābhātikaṃ karma samāhūyātha puṣpakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sugrīveṇa suṣeṇena tāreṇa kumudena ca \|*  
*aṃgadenātha kuṇḍena vāyuputreṇa dhīmatā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gavākṣeṇa naleneva tathā jāṃbavatāpi ca \|*  
*daśabhirvānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ samārūḍhaḥ sa puṣpake \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Thus Raghūttama spent that night there after being duly attended upon with great devotion by all the excellent monkeys.

When the day dawned and the solar disc rose up in all its splendour, he concluded his religious rites of the morning and summoned Puṣpaka. He got into Puṣpaka along with the ten monkeys, viz. Sugrīva, Suṣeṇa, Tāra, Kumuda, Aṅgada, Kunda, the intelligent son of Vāyu, Gavākṣa, Nala and Jāṃbavān.

## \|\| 1.101.5 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃprasthitaḥ kāle laṃkāmuddiśya rāghavaḥ \|*  
*manojavena tenaiva vimānena suvarcasā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then at the proper time, Rāma started towards Laṅkā in that highly resplendent aerial chariot having the velocity of mind.

## \|\| 1.101.6 \|\|

*saṃprāptastatkṣaṇādeva laṃkākhyāṃ ca mahāpurīm \|*  
*vīkṣayaṃstānpradeśāṃśca yatra yuddhaṃ purā'bhavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Instantly he reached the great city named Laṅkā and saw all those places where the battle had taken place before.

## \|\| 1.101.7 \|\|

*tato vibhīṣaṇo dṛṣṭvā proddyotaṃ puṣpakodbhavam \|*  
*rāmaṃ vijñāya saṃprāptaṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ sammukho yayau \|*  
*maṃtribhiḥ sakalaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā bhṛtyaiḥ sutairapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing the remarkable splendour of Puṣpaka, Vibhīṣaṇa knew that Rāma had arrived. He joyously came to receive him along with all the ministers, servants, and sons.

## \|\| 1.101.8 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā sudūrāttaṃ rāmadevaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau jayaśabdamudīrayan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Even as he saw Lord Rāma from a great distance, Vibhīṣaṇa prostrated on the ground like a log of wood and uttered the words “Be victorious.”

## \|\| 1.101.9 \|\|

*tathāgataṃ pariṣvajya sādaraṃ sa vibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*tenaiva sahitaḥ paścāllaṃkāṃ tāṃ praviveśa ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He (Rāma) closely embraced Vibhīṣaṇa with great eagerness even as he arrived. Later accompanied by him, he entered Laṅkā.

## \|\| 1.101.10 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇagṛhaṃ prāpya tatra siṃhāsane śubhe \|*  
*niviṣṭo vānaraistaiśca samantātparivāritaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After entering the abode of Vibhīṣaṇa, he sat on the splendid throne with the monkeys surrounding him.

## \|\| 1.101.11 \|\|

*tato nivedayāmāsa tasmai sarvaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ putrakalatrādi yaccānyadapi kiṃcana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then Vibhīṣaṇa dedicated unto him everything—the kingdom, his sons, wives etc., and everything else.

## \|\| 1.101.12-13 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca vinayātkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ādeśo dīyatāṃ deva brūhi kṛtyaṃ karomi kim \|\| 12 \|\|*

*akasmādeva saṃprāptaḥ kimarthaṃ vada me prabho \|*  
*kiṃ nāyātaḥ sa saumitristvayā sārdha ca jānakī \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Then he stood with palms joined in reverence and humility and said: “O Lord, let the command be given. Tell me, what work I shall carry out. O Lord, say why you came all of a sudden. Why did the son of Sumitrā not come with you? Nor Jānakī?

## \|\| 1.101.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nivedya rāghavastasmai sarvaṃ gadgadayā girā \|*  
*vāṣpapūrapraticchannavaktro bhūyo viniḥśvasan \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. Rāghava heaved a sigh with his face covered by tears and told everything to him in faltering words.

## \|\| 1.101.15 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca satyārthaṃ vibhīṣaṇakṛte hitam \|*  
*taṃ cāpi śokasaṃtaptaṃ saṃbodhya raghunaṃdanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Raghunandana addressed Vibhīṣaṇa who was also highly distressed and spoke to him truthful words conducive to his good:

## \|\| 1.101.16 \|\|

*ahaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sāṃprataṃ rākṣasottama \|*  
*yāsyāmi tridivaṃ tūrṇaṃ lakṣmaṇo yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O most excellent one of the Rākṣasas, soon I will also leave the kingdom and go to heaven where Lakṣmaṇa has already gone.

## \|\| 1.101.17 \|\|

*na tena rahito martye muhūrtamapi cotsahe \|*  
*sthātuṃ rākṣasaśārdūla bāṃdhavena mahātmanā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O tiger among the Rākṣasas, I am not eager to stay behind even for a short while in the mortal world without my noble-souled brother.

## \|\| 1.101.18 \|\|

*ahaṃ śikṣāpaṇārthāya tava prāpto vibhīṣaṇa \|*  
*tasmādavyagracittena saṃśṛṇuṣva kuruṣva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is with the intention of advising you that I have come to you, O Vibhīṣaṇa. Hence listen without excitement in the mind and carry it out.

## \|\| 1.101.19 \|\|

*eṣā rājyodbhavā lakṣmīrmadaṃ saṃjanayennṛṇām \|*  
*madyavatsvalpabuddhīnāṃ tasmātkāryo na sa tvayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This prosperity and power arising from the rulership of the kingdom may generate arrogance in men of meagre intellect like liquor. So it shall not be adopted by you.

## \|\| 1.101.20 \|\|

*śakrādyā amarāḥ sarve tvayā pūjyāḥ sadaiva hi \|*  
*mānyāśca yena te rājyaṃ jāyate śāśvataṃ sadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. All the immortal ones including Śakra are worthy of being honoured and venerated by you always, so that your own kingdom will be always intact.

## \|\| 1.101.21-23 \|\|

*mama satyaṃ bhavedvākya metasmādahamāgataḥ \|*  
*prāptarājyapratiṣṭho'pi tava bhrātā mahābalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vināśaṃ sahasā prāptastasmānmānyāḥ surāḥ sadā \|*  
*yadi kaścitsamāyāti mānuṣo'tra kathaṃcana \|*  
*matkāya eva draṣṭavyaḥ sarvaireva niśācaraiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tathā niśācarāḥ sarve tvayā vāryā vibhīṣaṇa \|*  
*mama setuṃ samullaṃghya na gaṃtavyaṃ dharātale \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. My statement should remain true. Therefore, I have come. Although your exceedingly mighty brother was well entrenched in his kingdom, he suddenly met with destruction. Hence Suras should always be honoured. If somehow a human being comes over here, he should be seen as one with my physical form by all the night-stalkers (Rākṣasas). O Vibhīṣaṇa, all the demons should be kept restrained by you. No one should proceed to the mainland transgressing my bridge.”

## \|\| 1.101.24 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vibho kariṣyāmi tavādeśamasaṃśayam \|*
