*paraṃ tvayā parityakte martye me jīvitaṃ vrajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

Vibhīṣaṇa said:

24\. Undoubtedly, I shall carry out your directions, O Lord. But when the mortal world is abandoned by you my very life may depart.

## \|\| 1.101.25 \|\|

*tasmānmāmapi tatraiva tvaṃ vibho netumarhasi \|*  
*ātmanā saha yatrāste prāggato lakṣmaṇastava \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. So, it behoves you, O Lord, to take me too along with you where Lakṣmaṇa having departed earlier is present.

## \|\| 1.101.26 \|\|

*śrīrāma uvāca \|*  
*mayā te'kṣayamādiṣṭaṃ rājyaṃ rākṣasasattama \|*  
*tasmānnārhasi māṃ kartuṃ mithyācāraṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 26 \|\|*

Śrī Rāma said:

26\. O most excellent one among Rākṣasas, an everlasting kingdom has been already promised for you by me. Hence it does not behove you to make me one with false conduct (untrue utterance).

## \|\| 1.101.27 \|\|

*ahamasminsvake setau śaṃkaratritayaṃ śubham \|*  
*sthāpayiṣyāmi kīrtyarthaṃ tatpūjyaṃ bhavatā sadā \|*  
*bhaktimānpratisaṃdhāya yāvaccaṃdrārkatārakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. For the sake of my lasting reputation, I will install three idols (or Liṅgas) of splendid features on my own Setu (Bridge). They should be worshipped by you always with great devotion and determination as long as the moon, the sun and the stars shine.

## \|\| 1.101.28 \|\|

*evamuktvā raghuśreṣṭho rākṣasendraṃ vibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*daśarātraṃ tatra tasthau laṃkāyāṃ vānaraiḥ saha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After saying thus to Vibhīṣaṇa, the Lord of the Rākṣasas, the most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu stayed there in Laṅkā for ten days along with the monkeys.

## \|\| 1.101.29 \|\|

*kurvanyuddhakathāścitrā yāḥ kṛtāḥ pūrvameva hi \|*  
*paśyanyuddhasya sarvāṇi sthānāni vividhāni ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He spoke about the diverse incidents of the battle that had been fought already and visited the different sites of the battle.

SO. He praised those heroic Rākṣasas of superior strength such as Kuṃbhakarṇa, Indrajit and others who met him face to face in the, battle.

## \|\| 1.101.31 \|\|

*tataścaikādaśe prāpte divase raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*puṣpakaṃ tatsamāruhya prasthitaḥ svapurīṃ prati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On the, eleventh days, Raghunandana got into that Puṣpaka and proceeded towards his city.

## \|\| 1.101.32 \|\|

*vānaraistaiḥ samopeto vibhīṣaṇapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃsthāpayāmāsa setuprāṃte maheśvaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He was accompanied by those monkeys and Vibhīṣaṇa went ahead. Then he installed Maheśvara on the Setu at the end.

## \|\| 1.101.33-34 \|\|

*madhye caiva tathādau ca śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*rāmeśvaratrayaṃ rāma evaṃ tatra vidhāya saḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*setubaṃdhaṃ tathāsādya prasthitaḥ svagṛhaṃ prati \|*  
*tāvadvibhīṣaṇenoktaḥ praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. With the mind sanctified by faith, he installed the deity in the middle and in the beginning too. Thus he came actually to the site of the Setubandha and then proceeded towards his own home. Then Vibhīṣaṇa bowed down to him repeatedly and said:

## \|\| 1.101.35 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*anena setumārgeṇa rāmeśvaradidṛkṣayā \|*  
*mānavā āgamiṣyaṃti kautukācchraddhayāvitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vibhīṣaṇa said:

35\. Men will be coining along this Setu with a desire to visit Rāmeśvara either out of curiosity or keenly endowed with faith.

## \|\| 1.101.36 \|\|

*rākṣasānāṃ mahārāja jātiḥ krūratamā matā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā mānuṣamāyāṃtaṃ māṃsasyecchā prajāyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The community of the Rākṣasas is considered cruel, O great king. On seeing a man coming, they may feel a desire for human flesh.

## \|\| 1.101.37 \|\|

*yadā kaścijjanaṃ kaścidrākṣaso bhakṣayiṣyati \|*  
*ājñābhaṃgo dhruvaṃ bhāvī mama bhaktiratasya ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If any Rākṣasa begins to eat any human being it will necessarily be disobedience and breaking of the command on my part, although I continue my devotion.

## \|\| 1.101.38-40 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃti kalau kāle daridrā nṛpamānavāḥ \|*  
*te'tra svarṇasya lobhena devatādarśanāya ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nityaṃ caivāgamiṣyanti tyaktvā rakṣaḥkṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*teṣāṃ yadi vadhaṃ kaścidrākṣasātprāpayiṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati ca me doṣaḥ prabhudrohodbhavaḥ prabho \|*  
*tasmātkaṃcidupāyaṃ tvaṃ cintayasva yathā mama \|*  
*ājñābhaṃgakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ jāyate na guro kvacit \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. In Kali age, mankind in general may be poor. They will be coming here everyday under the pretext of visiting the deity but really motivated by the greed of gold. They may not be afraid of the Rākṣasas.

If any one among the Rākṣasas were to kill him it will be an act of disloyalty to my Lord on my part, O Lord. Hence think of some way out, lest I should incur the sin of disobedience.

## \|\| 1.101.41 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ sa raghusattamaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva coktvātha cāpaṃ sajjīcakāra saḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On hearing his words, the most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu said: “Of course, it may be so.” Then he got his bow ready with string.

## \|\| 1.101.42 \|\|

*tatastaṃ kīrtirūpaṃ ca madhyadeśe raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*acchinanniśitairbāṇairdaśayojanavistṛtam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then Raghūttama cut off with sharp arrows the monumental form of his renown in the middle region extending to ten Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.101.43 \|\|

*tena saṃsthāpito yatra śikhare śaṃkaraḥ svayam \|\| \|*  
*śikharaṃ tatsaliṃgaṃ ca patitaṃ vāridherjale \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thereby the peak where Śaṅkara had been installed by himself fell into the waters of the ocean along with the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.101.44 \|\|

*evaṃ mārgamagamyaṃ taṃ kṛtvā setusamudbhavam \|*  
*vānarai rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ tataḥ saṃprasthito gṛham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In this manner the pathway over the Setu was rendered impassable. He then went home along with the monkeys and Rākṣasas.

## Chapter 102 - Erection of Five Palatial Shrines for Lakṣmaṇa and Others

## \|\| 1.102.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*saṃprasthitasya rāmasya svakīyaṃ sadanaṃ prati \|*  
*yadāścaryamabhūnmārge śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, listen to the mysterious incident that occurred on the way as Rāma set out towards his abode.

## \|\| 1.102.2 \|\|

*nabhomārgeṇa gacchattadvimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*akasmādeva sañjātaṃ niścalaṃ citrakṛnnṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The aerial chariot Puṣpaka that was moving along the path of the firmament stood still unaccountably all of a sudden mystifying the men.

## \|\| 1.102.3 \|\|

*atha tanniścalaṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpakaṃ gaganāṃgaṇe \|*  
*rāmo vāyusutasyedaṃ vacanaṃ prāha vismayāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing Puṣpaka motionless in the sky Rāma who was surprised spoke to the son of Vāyu:

## \|\| 1.102.4-5 \|\|

*tvaṃ gatvā mārute śīghraṃ bhūmiṃ jānīhi kāraṇam \|*  
*kimetatpuṣpakaṃ vyomni niścalatvamupāgatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kadāciddhāryate nāsya gatiḥ kutrāpi kenacit \|*  
*brahmadṛṣṭiprasūtasya puṣpakasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. “O Māruti, go to the ground below quickly and find out the cause of this Puṣpaka having come to a standstill in the middle of the sky. This huge-bodied Puṣpaka created by the eyes of Brahmā has never been restrained in its movement by anyone at any place.”

## \|\| 1.102.6 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa procya hanūmāndharaṇītalam \|*  
*gatvā śīghraṃ punaḥ prāha praṇipatya raghūttamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “So it shall be”, said Hanumān and went to the ground quickly coming back. He bowed down to Raghūttama and said:

## \|\| 1.102.7-9 \|\|

*atrāsyādhaḥ śubhaṃ kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvara saṃjñitam \|*  
*yatra sākṣājjagatkartā svayaṃ brahmā vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ādityā vasavo rudrā devavaidyau tathāśvinau \|*  
*tatra tiṣṭhanti te sarve tathānye siddhakinnarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*etasmātkāraṇānnaitadatikrāmati puṣpakam \|*  
*tatkṣetraṃ niścalībhūtaṃ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. “Beneath here is the holy spot named Hāṭakeśvara where Brahmā, the creator of the universe, himself abides.

Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Aśvins who are the physicians of Devas as well as other Siddhas and Kinnaras—all these stay there.

It is for this reason that Puṣpaka does not go beyond that holy spot. It has become motionless. The truth has been spoken by me.”

## \|\| 1.102.10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kautūhalasamavitaḥ \|*  
*puṣpakaṃ prerayāmāsa tatkṣetraṃ prati rāghavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

10\. O hearing his words, Rāghava became curious. He directed Puṣpaka towards that holy place.

## \|\| 1.102.11 \|\|

*sarvaistairvānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣasaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*avatīrya tato hṛṣṭastasminkṣetre samantataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He got down along with all the monkeys and Rākṣasas of various types. He joyously moved about in the holy place all round.

## \|\| 1.102.12 \|\|

*tīrthamālokayāmāsa puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tato vilokayāmāsa pitāmahavinirmitām \|*  
*cāmuṇḍāṃ tatra ca snātvā kuṇḍe kāmapradāyini \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He saw the Tīrtha and visited the holy shrines. Thereafter he visited Cāmuṇḍā installed by Pitāmaha. Then he took his holy bath is the Kuṇḍa that bestows all desired things.

## \|\| 1.102.13 \|\|

*tato vilokayāmāsa pitrā tasya vinirmitam \|*  
*rāmaḥ svamiva deveśaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then Rāma saw the Lord of Devas installed by his father. He then visited the Four-armed Lord who was he himself.

## \|\| 1.102.14-16 \|\|

*rājavāpyāṃ śucirbhūtvā snātvā tarpya nijānpitṝn \|*  
*tataśca cintayāmāsa kṣetre tra bahupuṇyade \|\| 14 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmyeva yadvattātena keśavaḥ \|*  
*tathā me dayito bhrātā lakṣmaṇo divamāśritaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yastasya nāmanirdiṣṭaṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmyaham \|*  
*taṃ cāpi mūrtimaṃtaṃ ca sītayā sahitaṃ śubham \|*  
*kṣetre medhyatame cātra tathātmānaṃ dṛṣanmayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. He took his bath in the Rājavāpī and became pure. He then offered libations to the Pitṛs. Thereafter he thought thus: ‘In this holy spot here that yields much merit, I shall install a Liṅga in the same manner as Keśava was installed by my father. Further, my dear brother has resorted to heaven. I shall instal a Liṅga named after him. I shall also install an image of him along with a splendid image of Sītā. In this highly sacred and pure holy spot, I shall install myself in the form of a stone idol.’

## \|\| 1.102.17 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā prāsādānāṃ ca paṃcakam \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa sadbhaktyā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After deciding thus, Rāma the foremost among those who wield weapons, erected five palatial temples with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.102.18 \|\|

*tataste vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*liṃgāni sthāpayāmāsuḥ svānisvāni pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then all those monkeys and Rākṣasas in particular installed severally their own Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.102.19 \|\|

*tatraiva suciraṃ kālaṃ sthitāste śraddhayā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*tato jagmurayodhyāyāṃ vimānavaramāśritāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. They all stayed there itself for a long time with great faith. Then they went to Ayodhyā riding on the excellent aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.102.20 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā rāmeśvaro mahān \|*  
*lakṣmaṇeśvarasaṃyuktastasmiṃstīrthe suśobhane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus everything has been narrated to you all about how the great deity of Rāmeśvara along with Lakṣmaṇeśvara was installed in that highly splendid Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.102.21 \|\|

*yastau prātaḥ samutthāya sadā paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnoti śrute rāmāyaṇe'tra yat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A man who always gets up early in the morning and visits both of them shall attain the entire benefit which one gets when Rāmāyaṇa is listened to.

## \|\| 1.102.22 \|\|

*athāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ yo rāmacaritaṃ paṭhet \|*  
*tadagre vājimedhasya sa kṛtsnaṃ labhate phalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Further, one who reads Rāmāyaṇa before those two deities on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days shall attain the entire benefit of Vājimedha (horse-sacrifice).

## Chapter 103 - Greatness of Ānartaka Tīrtha Kūpikā

## \|\| 1.103.1 \|\|

*\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*āścaryaṃ sūtaputraitadyattvayā parikīrtitam \|*  
*yatsthāpitāni liṃgāni rākṣasairapi vānaraiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūtaputra, you have said that Liṅgas were installed by the Rākṣasas as well as the monkeys. This is indeed surprising.

## \|\| 1.103.2 \|\|

*tasmādvistarato brūhi yatrayatra yathāyathā \|*  
*taiḥ sthāpitāni liṃgāni yeṣu sthāneṣu sūtaja \|\| 2 \|\|*

2- Hence do narrate it in detail where and how the (particular) Liṅgas were installed by them. What were the holy spots where they installed these?

## \|\| 1.103.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*sugrīvaḥ saṃbhramitvātha kṣetraṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*bālamaṃḍanakaṃ prāpya tatra snātvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. Sugrīva wandered over the entire holy spot and reached Bālamaṇḍanaka. There he took his holy bath with great mental concentration and purity. He installed the Mukhaliṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord there.

## \|\| 1.103.4 \|\|

*mukhaliṃgaṃ tatastatra sthāpayāmāsa śūlinaḥ \|\| \|*  
*tathānyairvānaraiḥ sarvaimukhaliṃgāni śūlinaḥ \|*  
*svasaṃjñārthaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sthāpitāni yathecchayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Similarly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Mukhaliṅgas of the Trident-bearing Lord were installed by all the other monkeys as they wished, as their respective tokens.

## \|\| 1.103.5 \|\|

*yasteṣāṃ mukhaliṃgānāṃ karoti ghṛtakaṃbalam \|\| \|*  
*makarasthena sūryeṇa śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One who applies Ghṛtakaṃbala (coating the Liṅga with ghee) to those Mukhaliṅgas with the Sun in the zodiac Capricorn, goes to Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.103.6 \|\|

*tataḥ paścimadigbhāge tasya kṣetrasya rākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpitāni liṅgāni caturvaktrāṇi ca dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, in the western area of that holy place four-faced Liṅgas were installed by the Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.103.7 \|\|

*rāmeṇa pūrvadigbhāge prāsādānāṃ ca paṃcakam \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ bhaktiyuktena sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the eastern area, five palaces (temples) were erected with great devotion by Rāma. They are destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.103.8 \|\|

*tathādakṣiṇadigbhāge kūpikā tena nirmitā \|\| \|*  
*ānarttīyataḍāgasya samīpe pāpanāśanī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly a Kūpikā (small well) was dug by him in the southern area near the Ānartīya lake. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.103.9 \|\|

*yastasyāṃ kurute śrāddhaṃ saṃprāpte dakṣiṇāyane \|*  
*so'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya pitṛloke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who performs Śrāddha there in the course of Dakṣiṇāyana (southern transit of the Sun) obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice and is honoured in the world of Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.103.10 \|\|

*yastatra dīpakaṃ dadyātkārtike māsi ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*na sa paśyati raudrāṃstānnarakānekaviṃśatim \|*  
*na cāṃdho jāyate kvāpi yatrayatra prajāyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Brāhmaṇas, one who offers oil-lamps there in the month of Kārttika never sees the twenty-one dreadful Narakas. Wherever he is reborn, he never becomes blind.

## \|\| 1.103.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ānarttīyataḍāgaṃ tatkena tatra vinirmitam \|*  
*kiṃprabhāvaṃ ca kārtsnyena sūtaputra prakīrtaya \|\| 11 \|\|*

The sages said:

11\. By whom was that Ānartīya lake made there? what is its power? O Sūtaputra, narrate this completely.

## \|\| 1.103.12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*ānarttīyataḍāgasya mahimā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*ekavaktreṇa no śakyo vaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Ānartiya \[Ānartīya?\] lake cannot be described adequately by means of a single mouth even in the course of hundreds of years.

## \|\| 1.103.13 \|\|

*āśvinasya site pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*snātvā devānpitṝṃścaiva tarpayedvidhipūrvakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. With great mental concentration and purity, one should lake his holy bath on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Āśvina and duly offer libations to Devas and Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.103.14 \|\|

*tato dīpotsavadine śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*dāmodaraṃ yamaṃ pūjya dīpaṃ dadyātsvabhaktitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then on the day of the Festivities of Lamps, he should perform Śrāddha with concentration, worship Dāmodara and Yama and then devoutly offer the lamp.

## \|\| 1.103.15 \|\|

*saṃpūjyo dharmarājastu gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*māṣāstilāśca dātavyā goviṃdaḥ prīyatāmiti \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Dharmarāja should be worshipped with sweet scents, flowers and unguents. Pulses and gingelly seeds should be offered saying “May Govinda be pleased.”

## \|\| 1.103.16 \|\|

*tilamāṣapradānena dvijānāṃ tarpaṇena ca \|*  
*yamena sahito devaḥ prīyate puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By the offering of gingelly seeds and pulses and by the propitiation of Brāhmaṇas, Lord Puruṣottama along with Yama is pleased.

## \|\| 1.103.17 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kurute viprāstīrtha ānarta saṃjñite \|*  
*so'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpyabrahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Brāhmaṇas, one who does like this at the Tīrtha named Ānarta obtains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice and is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.103.18 \|\|

*yasmindine samāyāto rāmastatra praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*tasmindvijottamaiḥ sarvaiḥ proktaḥ so'bhyetya sādaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On the day when Rāma very joyously reached that place, excellent Brāhmaṇas approached him. All of them respectfully said to him:

## \|\| 1.103.19 \|\|

*atrāgastyo muniśreṣṭhastiṣṭhate raghunaṃdana \|*  
*taṃ gatvā paśya viprendra mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O Raghunandana, the excellent Sage Agastya stays here. Do go and see that leading Brāhmaṇa born of Mitra and Varuṇa.”

## \|\| 1.103.20 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ \|*  
*vānarai rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ satvaraṃ yayau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing their words, the lotus-eyed Rāma joyously went there immediately along with the monkeys and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.103.21 \|\|

*aṣṭāṃgapraṇipātena taṃ praṇamya raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*pariṣyakto dṛḍhaṃ tena sānandena mahātmanā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Raghūttama bowed down to him and made Aṣṭāṅga (prostrating with eight limbs touching the ground) obeisance to him. The delighted noble-souled sage embraced him closely.

## \|\| 1.103.22 \|\|

*nātidūre tatastasya vinayena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭo dharāpṛṣṭhe kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With palms joined in reverence, he sat on the ground humbly, not far from him.

## \|\| 1.103.23 \|\|

*tataḥ pṛṣṭastu muninā kathayāmāsa vistarāt \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvamātmīyaṃ svargasya gamanaṃ prati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On being asked by the sage, Rāma narrated in detail all the events connected with himself and his departure to heaven.

## \|\| 1.103.24 \|\|

*yathā sītā parityaktā yathā saumitriṇā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*parityāgaḥ svakīyasya saṃtyaktena mahātmanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He narrated everything about how Sītā was banished by

himself, how Lakṣmaṇa gave up his life on being exiled by himself.

## \|\| 1.103.25 \|\|

*tathā sugrīvamāsādya tathaiva ca vibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*saṃbhāṣya cāgamastvatra tataḥ puṣpakasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He told him how he went to Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa; how he conversed with them; how they arrived there and how Puṣpaka became motionless.

## \|\| 1.103.26 \|\|

*tato'gastyaḥ kathāścitrāścakre tasya purastadā \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ dṛṣṭāṃtairbahubhirmuniḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Sage Agastya told him diverse wonderful stories of ancient saintly kings (who ruled) before him; citing many examples.

## \|\| 1.103.27 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāvasāne ca calacittaṃ raghūttamam \|*  
*vilokya pradadau tasmai ratnābharaṇamuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At the end of the narration, the sage observed that Raghūttama was emotionally upset. He then gave him an excellent ornament studded with jewels.

## \|\| 1.103.28 \|\|

*yanna deveṣu yakṣeṣu siddhavidyādhareṣu ca \|*  
*nāgeṣu rākṣasendreṣu mānuṣeṣu ca kā kathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Such a jewel was never in the possession of even Devas, Yakṣas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Nāgas and leading Rākṣasas. No question of its being with humans arises.

## \|\| 1.103.29 \|\|

*yasyendrāyudhasaṃghāśca niṣkrāmaṃti sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*rātrau tamisrapakṣe'pi lakṣyate'rkopamatviṣaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. From that ornament rainbow-like clusters of refulgence emerged in the thousands. Even during the night of the dark half its lustre resembling the solar light could be seen.

## \|\| 1.103.30-31 \|\|

*tadrāmastu gṛhītvā'tha vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*papraccha kautukāviṣṭaḥ kutastvetanmune tava \|\| 30 \|\|*

*atyadbhutakaraṃ ratnairnirmitaṃ timirāpaham \|*  
*kaṇṭhābharaṇamākhyāhi nedamasti jagattraye \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Rāma took it and gazed at it with eyes wide open with wonder. Out of curiosity he asked: “Where did you get this from, O sage? This necklace made of very wonderful jewels dispels darkness. There is no similar thing anywhere in all the three worlds. Tell me where you got this from.”

## \|\| 1.103.32 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*yatpaśyasi raghuśreṣṭha taḍāgamidamuttamam \|*  
*mamāśramasamīpasthaṃ taddevadevanirmitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

Agastya said:

32\. O most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu, this excellent lake which you see near my hermitage is created by the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.103.33 \|\|

*tasya tīre mayā dṛṣṭaṃ yadāścaryamanuttamam \|*  
*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva raghu nandana \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I shall tell you, O Raghunandana, a mysterious thing seen by me on its banks. Listen.

## \|\| 1.103.34 \|\|

*kadācidrāghavaśreṣṭha niśīthe'haṃ samutthitaḥ \|*  
*paśyāmi vyomamārgeṇa pradyotaṃ bhāskaropamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Once, O Rāghavaśreṣṭha, I got up at midnight and saw a sun-like refulgence passing through the sky.

## \|\| 1.103.35 \|\|

*yāvattāvadvimānaṃ tadapsarogaṇarājitam \|*  
*tasya madhyagataścaikaḥ puruṣastaruṇastathā \|*  
*andhastatra samārūḍhaḥ stūyate kinnarairnṛpaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It was an aerial chariot shining with groups of celestial damsels. There was a young main in the centre thereof. A blind king it was, riding therein. He was being eulogized by Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.103.36 \|\|

*ratnābharaṇametacca bibhratkaṇṭhe sunirmalam \|*  
*dvādaśārkapratīkāśaṃ kāmadeva ivāparaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In physical charm he was like another Kāmadeva. He was wearing this pure jewel-studded ornament shining like twelve suns.

## \|\| 1.103.37 \|\|

*athottīrya vimānāgryātskaṃdhalagno raghūdvaha \|*  
*ekasya devadūtasya salilāṃtamupāgataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Getting down from the excellent aerial chariot, O Raghūdvaha, with the support of the shoulders of a divine messenger, he fame down to the water level.

## \|\| 1.103.38 \|\|

*tataśca salilāttasmādākṛṣya ca kalevaram \|*  
*mṛtakasya tato daṃtairbhakṣayāmāsa satvaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He pulled up from the water a corpse of a man and immediately began to chew it with his teeth.

## \|\| 1.103.39 \|\|

*yathāyathā mahāmāṃsaṃ sa bhakṣayati rāghava \|*  
*tathātathā punaḥ kāyaṃ tadrūpaṃ tatprajāyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Rāghava, even as he continued to eat the human flesh the body regained its original form once again.

## \|\| 1.103.40 \|\|

*tatastṛptiṃ cirātprāpya śucirbhūtvā praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*niṣkamya salilādyāvadvimānamadhirohati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After a long time, he became satisfied. Gladly he purified himself, got out of the water and was about to get into the Vimāna (aerial chariot).

## \|\| 1.103.41 \|\|

*tāvanmayā drutaṃ gatvā sa pṛṣṭaḥ kautukānnṛpaḥ \|*  
*sevyamāno'pi gandharvaiḥ samaṃtādbuddhitatparaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By that time, I hastened to him out of curiosity. Even as he continued to be attended upon by the Gandharvas with keen intellect all round, I asked him:

## \|\| 1.103.42 \|\|

*bhobho vaimānikaśreṣṭha muhūrtaṃ pratipālaya \|*  
*agastirnāma vipro'haṃ mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “O excellent one among the travellers of aerial chariot, wait for a while. I am a Brāhmaṇa named Agastya, the son of Mitra and Varuṇa.”

## \|\| 1.103.43 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sammukho bhūtvā praṇāmamakarottataḥ \|*  
*taiśca vaimānikaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvaistaiḥ kinnarādibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing it he faced me and bowed down to me along with all those attendants in the aerial chariot, Kinnaras and others.

## \|\| 1.103.44-45 \|\|

*so'yaṃ rājā mayā pṛṣṭaḥ kṛtānatiḥ puraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*kastvamīdṛgvapuḥ śrīmānvimānavaramāśritaḥ \|*  
*sevyamāno'psarobhiśca gandharvaiḥ kinnaraistathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*atrā'gatya taḍāgāṃte mahāmāṃsaprabhakṣaṇam \|*  
*kṛtavānasi vaikalyaṃ kasmātte dṛṣṭisaṃbhavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. The king bowed down and stood before me when I asked: “Who are you with such a glorious body, seated in an excellent aerial chariot? You are being attended upon by the celestial damsels, Gandharvas and Kinnaras. You have come to this lake and have eaten the human flesh! How did you get blind in the eyes?

## \|\| 1.103.46 \|\|

*vaimānika uvāca \|*  
*sādhu sādhu muniśreṣṭha yattvaṃ prāpto mamāntikam \|*  
*avaśyaṃ sānukūlo me vidhiryattvaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

The Vaimānika (Aerial Passenger) said:

46\. Weill Well! O excellent sage. It is good that you have come to me. indeed Vidhi (Fate) is favourable to me as you have come.

## \|\| 1.103.47 \|\|

*sādhūnāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ tīrthabhūtā hi sādhavaḥ \|*  
*kālena phalate tīrthaṃ sadyaḥ sādhusamāgamaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The sight of saintly men (meeting with good men) is meritorious. Good men are indeed better than Tīrthas. The benefit of a Tīrtha is achieved in due course, but a contact with good men yields the fruit instantly.

## \|\| 1.103.48 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaṃ tavākhyānaṃ kathayāmi mahāmune \|*  
*yena me garhitaṃ bhojyaṃ vibhavaśca tathedṛśaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, O great sage, I shall narrate my story, how my diet came to be a despised thing despite such affluence and splendid riches.

## \|\| 1.103.49 \|\|

*ahamāsaṃ purā rājā śvetonāma mahāmune \|*  
*ānartādhipatiḥ pāpaḥ sarvalokanipīḍakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O great sage, I was formerly a king named Sveta, the ruler of Ānarta. The sinner that I was, I harassed all the people.

## \|\| 1.103.50 \|\|

*na kiṃcitprāṅmayā dattaṃ na hutaṃ jātavedasi \|*  
*na ca rakṣā kṛtā loke na trātāḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Nothing was given as religious gift by me earlier. I never performed Homa in the sacred fire. Nor did I accord protection to people. Those who sought refuge in me were not saved by me.

## \|\| 1.103.51 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvā mayā ratnaṃ yatkiṃciddharaṇītale \|\| \|*  
*tadvai balāddhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sarveṣāmiha dehinām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Whenever I saw any jewel on the earth, I took possession

thereof forcefully. I took away everything belonging to any embodied person. 9

## \|\| 1.103.52 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena dīrgheṇa jarāgrastasya me balāt \|*  
*hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ svaputreṇa māṃ nirvāsya vigarhitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After a long time I became overwhelmed with old age. My kingdom was seized with force by my own son. I became despised and was banished.

## \|\| 1.103.53 \|\|

*tato'haṃ jarayā grasto vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*samāyāto'tra vipreṃdra bhramamāṇa itastataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Overwhelmed with old age, I became disgusted with the world. O leading Brāhmaṇa, I wandered here and there and ultimately reached this place.

## \|\| 1.103.54 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭho'haṃ snātvā'tra salile śubhe \|*  
*mṛtaśca saṃniviṣṭohaṃ kṣudhayā paripīḍitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Parched in my throat with hunger and thirst, I took my bath in the auspicious water here. Afflicted with hunger I died as soon as I entered the water.

## \|\| 1.103.55 \|\|

*prāviśyā'tra jale puṇye paṃcatvaṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*tataśca tatkṣaṇādeva vimānaṃ samupasthitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Since I entered the holy, meritorious water and died, an aerial chariot came there at the very instant.

## \|\| 1.103.56 \|\|

*māmanyena śarīreṇa samādāya ca kiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*tatrāropya tataḥ prāptā brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ prati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The divine servants took me with them investing me with another body in the aerial chariot. They then proceeded towards the abode of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.103.57 \|\|

*divyamālyāvaradharaṃdivyagandhānulepanam \|*  
*divyābharaṇasaṃjuṣṭaṃ stūyamānaṃ ca kinnaraiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I wore divine garlands and clothes. I was smeared with divine scents and unguents. I had divine ornaments and I was eulogized by Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.103.58 \|\|

*tato brahmasabhāmadhye hyahaṃ tairdevakiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*tādṛgrūpo vicakṣuśca dhārito brahmaṇaḥ puraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereafter, blind as I was, I was presented in front of Brahmā by those attendants of Devas in the centre of the assembly of Brahmā, without eyes, in the same form as before.

## \|\| 1.103.59 \|\|

*sarvaiḥ sabhāgatairdṛṣṭā vismitāsyaiḥ parasparam \|*  
*anyaiśca nindamānaiśca dhikchabdasya prajalpakaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I was looked at with evident surprise on their faces by all those who were in the assembly. They looked at one another too. A few others censured me and uttered the word Dhik (“Fie upon youl”).

## \|\| 1.103.60 \|\|

*kiṃkarā ūcuḥ \|*  
*eṣa devaścaturvaktraḥ sabheyaṃ tasya sambhavā \|*  
*sarvairdevagaṇairjuṣṭā praṇāmaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 60 \|\|*

The Kinnaras said:

60\. This is Lord Brahmā of four faces. This is his assembly. All the groups of Devas are here. Let him be bowed down to.

## \|\| 1.103.61 \|\|

*tato'haṃ praṇipatyoccaistaṃ devaṃ devasaṃyutam \|*  
*upaviṣṭaḥ sabhāmadhye vrīḍayā'vanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then I made an humble bow to that Lord accompanied by Devas. I set in the middle of the assembly with the head lowered due to shame.

## \|\| 1.103.62-63 \|\|

*yathāyathā kathāstatra prajāyante sabhātale \|*  
*devadvijanarendrāṇāṃ dharmākhyānāni kuṃbhaja \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tathātathā mamātīva kṣudvṛddhiṃ saṃpragacchati \|*  
*jāne kiṃ bhakṣayāmyāśu dṛṣadaḥ kāṣṭhameva vā \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. O Pot-born One, as the discourses of the Devas, Brāhmaṇas and kings on Dharma (righteousness) continued on the floor of the hall of the assembly, my hunger too kept on increasing. I knew I was even ready to gobble up stone or wood.

## \|\| 1.103.64 \|\|

*tato mayā praṇamyoccairvijñaptaḥ prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*prāṇipatya muniśreṣṭha lajjāṃ tyaktvā sudūrataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I gave up the feeling of shame, O excellent sage. After bowing down repeatedly, I said aloud to Prapitāmaha:

## \|\| 1.103.65-66 \|\|

*kṣudhā māṃ bādhate atīva sāṃprataṃ prapitāmaha \|*  
*tathā paśyāmi no kiṃcittādṛgbhojyaṃ prayaccha me \|\| 65 \|\|*

*kṣutpipāsādayo doṣā na vidyaṃte'tra te kila \|*  
*svarge sthitasya yaccaitattatkimevaṃvidhaṃ mama \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. “O Prapitāmaha, hunger overwhelms me now. I am unable to see anything. Hence give me something to eat. There are no weaknesses like hunger and thirst felt by you here. How then do they harass me though I am stationed in Svarga?”

## \|\| 1.103.67 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca \|*  
*tvayā nānnaṃ kvaciddattaṃ kasyacitpṛthivītale \|*  
*tenātrāpi bubhukṣā te vṛddhiṃ gacchati durmate \|\| 67 \|\|*

Pitāmaha said:

67\. O evil-minded one, you never gave anyone any bit of food down there on the earth. Therefore you hunger goes on increasing here too.

## \|\| 1.103.68 \|\|

*tathā hṛtāni ratnāni yāni dṛṣṭigatāni te \|*  
*cakṣurhīnastato jāto mama loke gato'pi ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Further, whatever gem or jewel you set your eyes on, you used to seize it. Hence you have become blind, though you have come to my world.

## \|\| 1.103.69 \|\|

*yastvaṃ pātakayukto'pi saṃprāpto mama maṃdiram \|*  
*tadvakṣyāmyakhilaṃ te'haṃ śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Listen to it attentively. I shall explain how you could come to my palace despite being very sinful.

## \|\| 1.103.70 \|\|

*yasmiñjale tvayā muktāḥ prāṇāḥ pāpā tmanāpica \|*  
*śvetadvīpapatistatra kalikālabhayāturaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The Lord of Śvetadvīpa is present in the water where you cast off your life. O sinner, The Lord abides there because he is afraid of Kali.

## \|\| 1.103.71 \|\|

*tato'sya sparśanātsadyo vimuktaḥ sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*annādānātparā pīḍā jāyate kṣutsamu dbhavā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Since you touched that water, you are rid of all your sins. But one not giving food (to the hungry) gets afflicted with hunger.

## \|\| 1.103.72 \|\|

*tathā ratnāpahāreṇa sañjātā cāṃdhatā tava \|*  
*naivānyatkāraṇaṃ kiṃcitsatyametanmayoditam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Further due to the seizure of gems and jewels you incurred blindness. There is no other cause thereof. The truth has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.103.73 \|\|

*tato mayā vidhiḥ proktaḥ punareva dvijottama \|*  
*eṣo'pi brahmalokaste narakādatiricyate \|*  
*tasmāttatraiva māṃ deva preṣayasva kimatra vai \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. Brahmā was again addressed by me: “This Brahmaloka is no better than Naraka. Hence, O Lord send me there. What is here in this Brahmaloka?”

## \|\| 1.103.74 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasmāttatraiva gaccha tvaṃ preṣi to'si kimatra vai \|*  
*narake tava vāso na śvetadvīpasamudbhavam \|\| 74 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

74\. So you should have gone there! Why were you sent here? You cannot have a stay in Naraka even because of this Śvetadvīpa (where your sin is removed).

## \|\| 1.103.75 \|\|

*māhātmyaṃ nāśamāyāti śāstraṃ syātsatyavarjitam \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ nityamārūḍho vimā ne traivasundare \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The greatness of the Śvetadvīpa would have perished. The scripture would have become untrue. Hence you remain here itself in the beautiful aerial car.

## \|\| 1.103.76 \|\|

*gatvā jalāśaye tasminyatra prāṇāḥ samujjhitāḥ \|*  
*tameva nijadehaṃ ca bhakṣayasva yathecchayā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. From here you go to that water tank riding in the aerial chariot—to the water tank where you had cast off your life. Then eat as you please your own body.

## \|\| 1.103.77 \|\|

*tadbhaviṣyati madvākyā dakṣayaṃ jalamadhyagam \|*  
*tāvatkālaṃ ca dṛṣṭiste bhojyakāle bhaviṣyati \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. At my bidding that body within the water shall be

everlasting. You will gain vision (visual ability) as long as you continue to eat.

## \|\| 1.103.78 \|\|

*tato'haṃ tasya vākyena dīpotsavadine sadā \|*  
*niśīthe'tra samā gatya bhakṣayāmi nijāṃ tanum \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Ever since then, at his instance, I regularly come here at midnight on the day of the Festivity of Lights and eat my own body.

## \|\| 1.103.79 \|\|

*tatastṛptiṃ pragacchāmi yāvaddaivaṃ dinaṃ sthitam \|*  
*mānuṣaṃ ca tathā varṣamīdṛgrūpo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then, remaining in this form, I feel satisfied for a divine day, that is to say for a human year.

## \|\| 1.103.80 \|\|

*nāstyasādhyaṃ muniśreṣṭha tava kiṃcijjagattraye \|*  
*yenaikaṃ culukaṃ kṛtvā nipītaḥ payasāṃnidhiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O excellent sage, the storehouse of waters, the ocean, was turned into a handful of water and was drunk by you. There is nothing in all the three worlds, which cannot be accomplished by you.

## \|\| 1.103.81 \|\|

*tasmānmune dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari mahattarām \|*  
*akṛtyā drakṣa māmasmātsarvalokavigarhitāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Hence, O sage, take great pity on me and save me from this misdemeanour despised by all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.103.82 \|\|

*tathā dṛṣṭipradānaṃ me kuruṣva munisattama \|*  
*nirviṇṇo'smyaṃdhabhāvena nānyā tvatto'sti me gatiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. So, O excellent sage, grant me the gift of vision. I am disgusted with the state of blindness. I have no other place of refuge than you.

## \|\| 1.103.83 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kṛpayā mama mānasam \|*  
*dravībhūtaṃ tadā vākyamavocaṃ taṃ raghūttama \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O Raghūttama, on hearing his words my mind melted with pity. Then I spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.103.84 \|\|

*tvamannaniṣkrayaṃ dehi kaṇṭhasthamiha bhūṣaṇam \|*  
*yena nāśaṃ prayātyeṣā bubhukṣā jaṭharodbhavā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. “You give me this necklace in exchange for food. Thereby the hunger in your stomach will disappear.

## \|\| 1.103.85 \|\|

*tathā'dyaprabhṛti prājña ratnadīpānsunirmalān \|*  
*atraiva sarasastīre dehi dāmodarāya ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Further, O wise one, from now onwards give the lamps of jewels of pure rays to Dāmodara on the banks of this very lake.

## \|\| 1.103.86 \|\|

*ddhasa yena saṃjāyate dṛṣṭiḥ śāśvatī tava nirmalā \|*  
*mama vākyādasaṃdigdhaṃ satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Thereby, at my instance, your vision shall be free from defects and permanent undoubtedly. I promise this solemnly on oath.

## \|\| 1.103.87 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*mamopari dayāṃ kṛtvā tvameva munisattama \|*  
*gṛhāṇa ratnasaṃbhūtaṃ kaṇṭhābharaṇamuttamam \|\| 87 \|\|*

The king said:

87\. O excellent sage, take pity on me and receive this excellent necklace studded with jewels.

## \|\| 1.103.88 \|\|

*tato dayābhibhūtena mayā tasya pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*niḥspṛheṇāpi saṃcīrṇo muninā raṇyavāsinā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Therefore, though I am a sage devoid of desire and I reside in the forest I accepted his gift because I was moved with pity.

## \|\| 1.103.89 \|\|

*tataḥ prakṣālya me pādau yāvattenānnaniṣkraye \|*  
*vibhūṣaṇamidaṃ dattaṃ sadbhaktyā bhāvitātmane \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Then he washed my feet and gave me this jewel in exchange for food, with great devotion. His soul became purified by good thought.

## \|\| 1.103.90 \|\|

*tatastasya praṇaṣṭā sā bubhukṣā tatkṣaṇānnṛpa \|*  
*saṃjātā paramā tṛptirdevapīyūṣasaṃbhavā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then, O king, his hunger disappeared instantly. A satisfaction as though resulting from the divine nectar occurred within him.

## \|\| 1.103.91 \|\|

*tasya naṣṭaṃ mṛtaṃ kāyaṃ tacca jīrṇaṃ purodbhavam \|*  
*yadāsīdakṣayaṃ nityaṃ tasmiṃstoye vyavasthitam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. His earlier body which became old and dried and later became everlastingly renewed in the water, disappeared forever.

## \|\| 1.103.92 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃsthāpitastena tasminsthāne subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*dāmodaro raghuśreṣṭha kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Then, O most excellent one among the descendants of Raghu, he erected an excellent palace with great devotion, and installed Dāmodara at that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.103.93 \|\|

*tasyāgre śraddhayā yukto dīpaṃ dayādyathāyathā \|*  
*tathātathā bhaveddṛṣṭistasya nityaṃ sunirmalām \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. With great faith, he offered regularly oil-lamps and his eyesight became clearer day by day.

## \|\| 1.103.94 \|\|

*tato māsātsamāsādya divyacakṣurmahīpatiḥ \|*  
*sa babhūva nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ spṛhaṇīyatamaḥ satām \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Then within a month the king regained divine eyes. He became the most excellent king and the most likable one to good ones.

## \|\| 1.103.95 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca māṃ hṛṣṭaḥ praṇipatya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*harṣagadgadayā vācā prasthitastridivaṃ prati \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Then joyously he started towards heaven. He bowed down to me and with palms joined in reverence he spoke words choked with delight:

## \|\| 1.103.96-97 \|\|

*tvatprasādātpraṇaṣṭā me bubhukṣā'tisudāruṇā \|*  
*tathā dṛṣṭiśca saṃjātā divyā brāhmaṇasattama \|\| 96 \|\|*

*anujñāṃ dehi me tasmādyena gacchāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ muniśreṣṭha tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, with your favour the dreadful insatiable hunger of mine has vanished and I have regained divine vision. Permit me, O excellent sage, so that I can go to Brahmaloka, thanks to the power of this Tīrtha.”

## \|\| 1.103.98 \|\|

*tato mayā vinirmuktaḥ praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*sa jagāma prahṛṣṭātmā brahmalokaṃ sanātanam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Then he was sent away by me. After repeatedly bowing down to me he joyously went to the eternal Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.103.99 \|\|

*evaṃ me bhūṣaṇamidaṃ jātaṃ hastagataṃ purā \|*  
*tava yogyamidaṃ jñātvā tubhyaṃ tena niveditam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. It was thus that his ornament came into my hands earlier. Realizing that this is worthy of you in every respect it has been given to you.

## \|\| 1.103.100 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti rājeṃdra samāgatyātra mānavāḥ \|*  
*ratnadīpānpradāyoccaiḥ snātvā'tra salile śubhe \|*  
*kārtike māsi niryāṃti dehāṃte tridivālayam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Ever since then, O great king, men regularly come here, take their holy bath here in the splendid waters in the month of Kārttika, offer lamps studded with jewels generously and go to the abode of Devas after death.

## \|\| 1.103.101 \|\|

*ye punaḥ prāṇasaṃtyāgaṃ prakurvaṃti samāhitāḥ \|*  
*pāpātmāno'pi te yāṃti brahmalokaṃ raghūttama \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. O Raghūttama, those with mental concentration and purity, who discard their life herein, go to Brahmaloka although they may be sinful.

## \|\| 1.103.102 \|\|

*tato dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaḥ prabhāvaṃ tajjalodbhavam \|*  
*pāṃsubhiḥ pūrayāmāsa samaṃtādbhayasaṃkulam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. On seeing the power of the holy water there the Thousand-eyed One (Indra) became agitated with fear and got it filled with dust particles.

## \|\| 1.103.103 \|\|

*tadadya divasaḥ prāpto dīpotsavasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*supuṇyo'tra mamādeśāttvaṃ kuruṣva sukūpikām \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Today happens to be the day of the Festivities of Oil Lamps. It is highly meritorious. At my bidding dig an excellent Kūpikā (well) here.

## \|\| 1.103.104 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snānaṃ vidhāyātha pitṝṃstarpaya rāghava \|*  
*devasyāsya puro dehi ratnadīpamanuttamam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. O Rāghava, take your holy bath therein and offer libations to the Pitṛs. Give excellent Ratnadīpas (jewel-studded oil-lamps) in front of the deity.

## \|\| 1.103.105 \|\|

*yena saṃjāyate siddhirbrahmalokasamudbhavā \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa satyametanmayoditam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Thereby you will attain the Siddhi of reaching Brahmaloka with this very body. The truth has been told by me.

## \|\| 1.103.106 \|\|

*tataste rāghavādeśā tsarve rākṣasavānarāḥ \|*  
*tasmindeśe vinidadhuḥ kūpikāṃ vimalodakām \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Then at the bidding of Rāghava all those Rākṣasas and monkeys dug Kūpikās containing waters devoid of impurities in that region.

## \|\| 1.103.107 \|\|

*tatra snātvā pitṝṃstarpya ratnadīpaṃ pradāya ca \|*  
*samastaṃ kārtikaṃ yāvadayodhyāṃ prasthitāstataḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. They spent the entire month of Kārttikā there, taking holy baths, offering libations to the Pitṛs and placing Ratnadīpas. Then they started back to Ayodhyā.

## \|\| 1.103.108 \|\|

*tato vibhīṣaṇaṃ muktvā hanūmaṃtaṃ ca vānaram \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gatāḥ sarve tattīrthasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then by the power of that Tīrtha all of them except Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanumān, the monkey, went to Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 104 - Installation of Kuśeśvara and Laveśvara

## \|\| 1.104.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*rākṣasaistatra liṃgāni yāni bhaktyā samanvitaiḥ \|*  
*sthāpitāni ca māhātmyaṃ teṣāṃ sūta prakīrtaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[Full title: Installation of Kuśeśvara (Kuśa-īśvara) and Laveśvara (Lava-īśvara)\]

Note: According to Rāmāyaṇa VII.108.4, Kuśa’s capital was Kuśāvatī; no son of Rāma ruled at Ayodhyā.

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta, describe the greatness of those Liṅgas which were installed there by Rākṣasas endowed with devotion.

## \|\| 1.104.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ pūjākṛte raudrā rākṣasā balavattarāḥ \|*  
*laṃkāpuryāḥ samāyāṃti sadaiva śataśaḥ purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. The terrible Rākṣasas of extraordinary might used to come formerly from the city of Laṅkā in hundreds always for the sake of worshipping them.

## \|\| 1.104.3 \|\|

*āgacchanto vrajantaste mārge kṣetre ca tatra ca \|*  
*bhakṣayanti janaughāṃśca bālavṛddhāñjanānapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. While coming and going back, they used to devour many people including children and old ones both in the holy spot and on the way.

## \|\| 1.104.4 \|\|

*tataste mānavāḥ sarve pradravaṃtaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*itaścetaśca dhāvanti prāṇarakṣaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. All the human beings in their eagerness to save their lives used to run about here and there.

## \|\| 1.104.5 \|\|

*tathānye bahavo gatvā hyayodhyākhyāṃ mahāpurīm \|*  
*rāmaputraṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ kuśaṃ procuḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then many of them went to the great city of Ayodhyā. Exceedingly grief-stricken, they spoke thus to the excellent king Kuśa, the son of Rāma:

## \|\| 1.104.6-11 \|\|

*tava pitrā samaṃ prāptāḥ pūrvaṃ ye rākṣasā nṛpa \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre vibhīṣaṇapuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saṃsthāpitāni liṃgāni caturvaktrāṇi tatra vai \|*  
*rākṣaseṃdraiḥ svamantraistaistasya kṣetrasya paścime \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tenaiva cānuṣaṃgeṇa samāgacchaṃti nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tasminkṣetre prakurvaṃti tathā lokasya bhakṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yadi vā tāni liṃgāni kaścitsaṃpūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*sadyo vināśamāyāti so'pyanartho mahānabhūt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmādyadi na rakṣā naḥ kariṣyasi mahīpate \|*  
*tacchanairyāsyate lokaḥ sarvo'yaṃ saṃkṣayaṃ dhruvam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tacca kṣetraṃ viśeṣeṇa yatrāgacchaṃti te sadā \|*  
*rākṣasāḥ krūrakarmāṇo mahāmāṃsasya lolupāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. “Formerly, the Rākṣasas with Vibhīṣaṇa as their leader had accompanied your father to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara. Four-faced Liṅgas were installed by those leading Rākṣasas with their own sets of Mantras, in the western zone of that holy spot. In this connection, everyday many of them come to the holy spot and devour people.

If at all any human being were to worship those Liṅgas, he is doomed immediately. This too has become another terrible calamity. Hence, O king, if you do not save us, certainly the entire world will gradually come to ruin. Particularly, that holy spot is going to be doomed, for the Rākṣasas of ruthless activities and covetous of human flesh, frequent it.”

## \|\| 1.104.12 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sa nṛpastūrṇaṃ svāmātyānāṃ nyavedayat \|*  
*rājyabhāraṃ tatastatra balena sahito yayau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing it, the king immediately entrusted the ministers with the governance of the kingdom.

Then he went to the holy spot along with his army.

## \|\| 1.104.13 \|\|

*atha prāptaṃ kuśaṃ dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*procustaṃ bhartsayitvā tu vacanaiḥ paruṣākṣaraiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing that Kuśa had arrived there, the survivors of the excellent Brāhmaṇas upbraided him with harsh words and said thus:

## \|\| 1.104.14-18 \|\|

*kimevaṃ kriyate rājyaṃ yathā tvaṃ kṣatriyādhamaḥ \|*  
*karoṣi yatra vidhvaṃsaṃ rākṣasai rnīyate janaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nūnaṃ jāto na rāmeṇa bhavānrāvaṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*yenopekṣasi sarvānno rākṣasaiḥ paripīḍitān \|\| 15 \|\|*

*satyametatpurā proktaṃ nītiśāstravicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yasya varṇasya yo rājā sa varṇaḥ sukhamedhate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ rākṣasodbhūto rākṣasairdvijasattamān \|*  
*upekṣase tataḥ sarvānbhakṣyamāṇāṃstathāparān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ārtānāṃ yatra lokānāṃ doṣaiḥ pārthivasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*pataṃtyaśrūṇi bhūpṛṣṭhe tatra rājā sa doṣabhāk \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. “O base Kṣatriya, why do you govern the kingdom in such a manner as to let the people be destroyed by Rākṣasas? You are not born of Rāma; you are born of Rāvaṇa. Hence you are indifferent to us tormented by the Rākṣasas.

Indeed, this fact has already been expressed by the people who are expert in the science of ethics and morality. That caste from which the king hails, enjoys flourishing happiness.

Hence you, begot by a Rākṣasa, neglect all the excellent Brāhmaṇas and others who are being devoured by the Rākṣasas. That king is blameworthy, on account of whose defaults, tears of the distressed people fall on the ground.”

## \|\| 1.104.19 \|\|

*kuśa uvāca \|*  
*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ viprā na mayā jñātamīdṛśam \|*  
*rākṣasebhyaḥ samutpanno brāhmaṇānāṃ parābhavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Kuśa said:

19\. O Brāhmaṇas, be consoled. I was not aware of such a thing as this happening, that the Brāhmaṇas have been subjected to harassment by the Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.104.20 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti yaḥ kaścidvināśaṃ nīyate kvacit \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vā'thavā'nyo'pi tadbhavenmama pātakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. From now onwards, if any Brāhmaṇa or anyone else is destroyed or ruined, it shall be my sin.

## \|\| 1.104.21 \|\|

*evamuktvā tatastūrṇaṃ preṣayāmāsa rāghavaḥ \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇāya saṃkruddho dūtaṃ bhayavivarjitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After saying thus, the irate scion of the family of Raghu despatched a fearless messenger to Vibhīṣaṇa:

## \|\| 1.104.22-28 \|\|

*gaccha dūta drutaṃ gatvā tvayā vācyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rāmocitastvayā sneho mayā saha kṛto mahān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yadrākṣasagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ mama bhūmiṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ kleśayasi durbuddhe māṃ viśvāsya subhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mama pitrā kṛteyaṃ te pratiṣṭhā rākṣasādhama \|*  
*tena no hanmi te bhrātā yathā tātena śātitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*viṣavṛkṣo'pi yo vṛddhiṃ svayameva praṇīyate \|*  
*kathaṃ saṃchidyate so'tra svayameva manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasmādadya dinādūrdhvaṃ yadi kaścinniśācaraḥ \|*  
*samudrasyottaraṃ pāraṃ kathaṃcidāgamiṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ satvaraṃ prāpya laṃkāṃ tava purīmimām \|*  
*sasainyo dhvaṃsayiṣyāmi tathā sarvānniśācarān \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tvāṃ ca baddhvā dṛḍhaiḥ pāśairnigaḍaiśca susaṃyatam \|*  
*kārāsaṃsthaṃ kariṣyāmi sadya eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

22-28. "Do go at once, O messenger, and tell Vibhīṣaṇa: ‘The deep affection of Rāma that you have enjoyed, has been very amply requited in my case!

O evil-minded one, with excellent words you made me trust in you, but you are now harassing my realm with your hosts of Rākṣasas.

O base Rākṣasa, it was my father who made you settle down in this prestigious position. Hence, I do not kill you in the way in which your brother was killed by my father.

Even if it be a poisonous tree, how can sensible men cut it off, after once nurturing it with great care!

Hence, after this day, if any demon somehow comes to the northern shore of the ocean, I will immediately invade this city Laṅkā of yours along with my army and destroy it. Further, I will bind you and all the Rākṣasas firmly with fetters. Undoubtedly I will put you in prison.”

## \|\| 1.104.29-30 \|\|

*evamuktastato dūto gatvā setuṃ drutaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rāmeśvaraṃ devaṃ yāvadagre vyava sthitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tāvatpṛṣṭo janaiḥ kaiścitkastvaṃ vatsa ihāgataḥ \|*  
*kena kāryeṇa no brūhi nātra gacchaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. On being ordered thus, the messenger went to the Setu quickly. After visiting the deity Rāmeśvara, he was about to proceed further when he was asked by some people: “O dear one, who are you? What is the purpose for which you have come here? Tell us. Usually human beings do not come here’.”

## \|\| 1.104.31 \|\|

*dūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ kuśena bhūpena vibhīṣaṇagṛhaṃ prati \|*  
*preṣitaḥ kāryamuddiśya tatra yāsyāmyahaṃ katham \|\| 31 \|\|*

The messenger said:

31\. I have been deputed by King Kuśa to the abode of Vibhīṣaṇa on a certain errand. How shall I go there?

## \|\| 1.104.32 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*nātaḥ paraṃ naraḥ kaścidgantuṃ śaktaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*bhagnaḥ seturyato madhye rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|\| 32 \|\|*

The people said:

32\. Beyond this no human being can go at all because the Setu was broken in the middle by Rāma of indefatigable actions.

## \|\| 1.104.33 \|\|

*tasmādatraiva te kāryaṃ siddhiṃ dūta prayāsyati \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇakṛtaṃ sarvaṃ darśanāttasya rakṣasaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence, O messenger, all your work with Vibhīṣaṇa can be concluded here by meeting that Rākṣasa.

## \|\| 1.104.34 \|\|

*sarvadā rākṣasendro'sau śubhaṃ rāmeśvaratrayam \|*  
*trikālaṃ pūjayatyeva niyamaṃ samupāśritaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. This leading Rākṣasa has adopted this regular practice of worshipping the three deities of Rāmeśvara three times everyday.

## \|\| 1.104.35 \|\|

*laṃkādvāre sthito yo vai setukhaṇḍe maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*prabhāte kurute tasya svayaṃ pūjāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the morning Vibhīṣaṇa performs the worship of Maheśvara in the portion of the setu near the gateway of Laṅkā.

## \|\| 1.104.36 \|\|

*jalamadhyagataṃ yacca setukhaṃḍaṃ dvitīyakam \|*  
*tatra rāmeśvaro yaśca madhyāhne taṃ prapūjayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He worships at noon the deity Rāmeśvara installed in the second portion of the Setu submerged in the water.

## \|\| 1.104.37 \|\|

*enaṃ deva niśīthe ca sarvadāgatya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjayenna sandehaḥ satyametatprakīrtitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Always at midnight he comes here with great devotion and worships this deity. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that has been uttered (by us).

## \|\| 1.104.38 \|\|

*tasmāttiṣṭha tvamavyagraḥ sthāne'traiva samāhitaḥ \|*  
*yāvadāgamanaṃ tasya rākṣasasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. So, wait here unruffled in this very spot with mental concentration, till that noble-souled Rākṣasa comes here.

## \|\| 1.104.39 \|\|

*tenaiva sahitaḥ paścātsvecchayā tasya mandiram \|*  
*prayāsyasi gṛhaṃ vāpi svakīyaṃ tadvisarjitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Later you can freely go to his palace in his company or to your own abode if he dismisses you.

## \|\| 1.104.40 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ tadākarṇya sa dūto harṣasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva coktvātha tatra caiva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On hearing their words, the messenger became delighted. “So it shall be”, he said and waited there.

## \|\| 1.104.41 \|\|

*atha prāpte niśārdhe sa rākṣasaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇaḥ samāyātastasminnāyatane śubhe \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. As midnight approached, Vibhīṣaṇa came to that splendid shrine surrounded by Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.104.42 \|\|

*vimānavaramārūḍhaḥ stūyamānaḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*rākṣasairbaṃdirūpaistairgīyamānastathā paraiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He was riding iṇ an excellent aerial chariot. He was eulogized all round by the Rākṣasas in the form of bards. Others sang songs.

## \|\| 1.104.43 \|\|

*uttīrya ca vimānāgryātkṛtvā'tha triḥ pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*rāmeśvaraṃ praṇamyoccaiḥ stotrametaccakāra saḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Coming out of the excellent aerial chariot, he circumambulated the deity Rāmeśvara three times. After bowing down to the deity, he recited the following prayer loudly:

\[Vibhīṣaṇa’s prayer\]

## \|\| 1.104.44 \|\|

*namaste devadeveśa bhaktānāmabhayaprada \|*  
*sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ te sarvatokṣiśiromukham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. "Obeisance to you, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, O bestower of freedom from fear on your devotees. You are endowed with hands and feet all round. You have eyes, heads and faces everywhere.

## \|\| 1.104.45 \|\|

*tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvaṃ caṃdrastvaṃ prabhākaraḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ caturvaktraḥ śakrastvaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You are Yajña; you are the Vaṣaṭkāra. You are Candra; you are Prabhākara (Sun). You are Viṣṇu; you are the Fourfaced One. You are Śakra. You are the great Īśvara.

## \|\| 1.104.46 \|\|

*yathā tilagataṃ tailaṃ gūḍhaṃ tiṣṭhati sarvadā \|*  
*tathā tvaṃ sarva lokeṣu gūḍhastiṣṭhasi śaṃkara \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Just as oil is always concealed in gingelly seeds, so also, O Śaṅkara, you stay hidden in all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.104.47 \|\|

*yathā kāṣṭhagato vahniḥ saṃsthito'pi na lakṣyate \|*  
*mūḍhaiḥ sarvatrasaṃsthopi tathā tvaṃ naiva lakṣyase \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Just as fire, latent in wood, is not perceived though it is present in it, similarly you are not perceived by the deluded ones, though you are present everywhere.

## \|\| 1.104.48 \|\|

*yathā dadhigataṃ sarpirnigūḍhatvena saṃsthitam \|*  
*carācareṣu bhūteṣu tathā tvaṃ deva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Just as ghee lies hidden in curd, so also, O Lord, you are stationed (unseen) in all living beings mobile and immobile.

## \|\| 1.104.49 \|\|

*yathā jalaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhātkhanannāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*tathā tvāṃ pūjayannityaṃ mokṣamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Just as a man digging the ground obtains water therefrom, so also one who always worships you attains salvation undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.104.50 \|\|

*tāvacca durlabhaḥ svargastāvacchūrāśca śatravaḥ \|*  
*yāvadeva na santoṣaṃ tvaṃ karoṣi śarīriṇām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. As long as you are not pleased with embodied ones, Svarga continues to be difficult of access and the brave are hostile (to them).

## \|\| 1.104.51 \|\|

*tāvallakṣmīścalā nṝṇāṃ tāvadrogāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ \|*  
*na yāvaddevadeva tvaṃ santoṣaṃ saṃprayāsyasi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Lord of Devas, as long as you are not propitiated and pleased, prosperity remains unsteady and ailments of different kinds begin to assail.

## \|\| 1.104.52 \|\|

*tāvatputrodbhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathā priyasamu dbhavam \|*  
*yāvattvaṃ deva nāyāsi santoṣaṃ dehināmiha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Lord, as long as your are not pleased with embodied beings, so long there is misery arising from one’s sons and one’s wife.”

## \|\| 1.104.53 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā tato liṃgaṃ snāpayitvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*gandhānulepanaidivyairmardayāmāsa vai tataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After eulogizing thus he duly bathed the Liṅga and then applied sweet scents and divine unguents.

## \|\| 1.104.54-55 \|\|

*pārijātakapuṣpaiśca tathā santānasambhavaiḥ \|*  
*kalpapādapasaṃbhūtaistathā mandārajairapi \|\| 54 \|\|*

*pūjāṃ cakre suvistīrṇā śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*divyairābharaṇairbhūṣya divyavastraistataḥ param \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. With great ardour and faith, he performed an elaborate adoration with the flowers of Pārijāta, Santāna, Mandāra and Kalpa trees. Thereafter, he adorned the Lord with divine ornaments and garments.

## \|\| 1.104.56-58 \|\|

*sa ca gītaṃ svayaṃ cakre tālamādāya pāṇinā \|*  
*mūrchātālakṛtaṃ ramyaṃ saptasvaravirājitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tānayuktyā samopetaṃ grāmai rāgaiḥ svalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā sa śuśrūṣā tasya devasya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yāvatsaṃprasthito bhūyo laṃkāṃ prati vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tāvaddūto'grataḥ sthitvā kuśavākyamuvāca ha \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. He himself sang, beating time with his hands, where the seven notes of the gamut were remarkable and pleasing with proper intonation and regular fall and rise of the notes. It was characterized by proper Tanas (key notes), Rāgas and Grāmas. Thus, he served the Lord devoutly.

As Vibhīṣaṇa was about to leave for Laṅkā, the messenger came before him and repeated the message of Kuśa.

## \|\| 1.104.59 \|\|

*viśeṣatastu tenoktaṃ yattasya purataḥ purā \|*  
*atikopābhibhūtena praraktanayanena ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In particular, he repeated the words which Kuśa had uttered in front of him with reddened eyes and great anger.

## \|\| 1.104.60 \|\|

*tacchrutvātha praṇamyoccairdūtaṃ prāha vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On hearing it, Vibhīṣaṇa stood humbly with palms joined in reverence and spoke to the messenger loudly:

## \|\| 1.104.61-62 \|\|

*yadyevaṃ vihitaṃ rājye rāmaputrasya rākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*tannūnaṃ tanmayā sarvaṃ vihitaṃ dūtasattama \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tasmānmahāprasādo me kṛtastena mahātmanā \|*  
*kuśena preṣito yastvaṃ mama mūrkhasya saṃnidhau \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. “O excellent Dūta (Messenger), if the Rākṣasas had behaved thus in the kingdom of Rāma’s son, it amounts to this that I too have behaved so (i.e. I accept the responsibility for it). It is indeed a great favour of that noble-souled one, Kuśa, that he sent you to me who have so long been an ignorant fool.”

## \|\| 1.104.63-64 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa tānsarvāñchodhayāmāsa rākṣasān \|*  
*ye gatvā bhūtale martyāndhvaṃsayaṃti sadaiva hi \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tatastatraiva cānīya tasya dūtasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*pratyekaṃ tānuvācedaṃ kopādaśrūṇi cotsṛjan \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. After saying this, he found out all the Rākṣasas who usually went to the mainland and always caused destruction.

He brought them to the presence of the messenger and shedding tears angrily, sternly warned each one of them.

## \|\| 1.104.65-67 \|\|

*yaiḥ kṛto janavidhvaṃso rākṣasaiḥ sudurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*rājye kuśasya saṃprāptaiḥ prabhormama mahātmanaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*te sarve vyaṃtarā raudrāḥ prabhavaṃtu suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*laṃkādvāragatā nityaṃ kṣutpipāsānipīḍitāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sarvabhogaparityaktāḥ śītātapasahi ṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*śleṣmamūtrakṛtāhārā nindyāḥ sarvajanasya ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. “Kuśa is my noble-souled overlord. All those Rākṣasas of wicked soul who went to his kingdom and perpetrated the destruction of the people shall become hideous ghosts and spirits in great misery. (Being banished) they will be lurking at the gates of Laṅkā always overwhelmed with hunger and thirst. They will be censured by all the people. They will be deprived of all pleasures and enjoyments. They will have to endure the chill of blizzards and the heat of the scorching sun. Phlegm and urine shall constitute their food intake.”

## \|\| 1.104.68 \|\|

*evaṃ dattvātha teṣāṃ sa śāpaṃ rākṣasasattamaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prāha ca taṃ dūtaṃ punareva kṛtāṃ jaliḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. After heaping this curse on them, the excellent Rākṣasas said again to the messenger with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.104.69-71 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti no kaścidrākṣasaḥ saṃprayāsyati \|*  
*tasmādvācyo raghuśreṣṭho madvākyātsa kuśastvayā \|*  
*kṣamyatāmaparādho me yadajñānā dayaṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*rākṣasairduṣṭajātīyairmahāmāṃsasyalolupaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtaśca nigrahasteṣāṃ pratyakṣaṃ tava dūta yaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yadanyadapi kṛtyaṃ syāddaivaṃ vā mānuṣaṃ ca vā \|*  
*mama bhṛtyasya tatsarvaṃ kathanīyamaśaṃkitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. “From now onwards no Rākṣasa will go there. Hence go and tell Kuśa, the excellent one among the descendants of Raghu, in my words: ‘May this crime be condoned because this has been perpetrated due to ignorance.’

Rākṣasas as a class are wicked and very greedy for human flesh. They have been punished in your presence, O messenger.

Whatever other duty there may be concerning Devas or human beings can be unhesitatingly communicated to me ever at your service.”

## \|\| 1.104.72 \|\|

*dūta uvāca \|*  
*yāni tatra ca liṃgāni rākṣasairnirmitāni ca \|*  
*tāni gatvā svayaṃ śīghraṃ tvamutpāṭaya rākṣasa \|\| 72 \|\|*

The messenger said:

72\. O Rākṣasa, go there yourself quickly and uproot all those Liṅgas installed by the Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.104.73-75 \|\|

*etadeva paraṃ kṛtyaṃ sarvalokasukhāvaham \|*  
*sthāpitāni ca yānyeva maṃtrai rākṣasasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*saṃpūjitāni rakṣobhiścaturvaktrāṇi rākṣasa \|*  
*ajānanmānavaḥ kaścidyadi pūjāṃ samācaret \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇānnāśamāyāti etaddṛṣṭaṃ mayā svayam \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādvacmi tvāmahaṃ rākṣasādhipa \|*  
*taiḥ sthitairbhūtale liṃgaiḥ sthitāḥ sarve niśācarāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-74a. This alone is the greatest task. It will be conducive to the happiness of all people.

These Liṅgas with four faces were installed with the Mantras specially pertaining to the Rākṣasas and worshipped by those Rākṣasas.

74b-75. If a person (being ignorant of the Rākṣasa way of worship) inadvertently worships them, he instantly falls down dead. That is why I request you this, O king of Rākṣasas. The presence of Liṅgas there on the earth (human world) is as good as the continued presence of all the Niśācaras there.

## \|\| 1.104.76 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*mayā pūrvaṃ pratijñātaṃ rāmasya purataḥ kila \|*  
*rāmeśvaramatikramya na gatavyaṃ dharātale \|\| 76 \|\|*

Vibhūṣaṇa said:

76\. Earlier, in the presence of Rāma it was promised by roe that none would go to the mainland beyond Rāmeśvara.

## \|\| 1.104.77 \|\|

*anyacca kāraṇaṃ dūta proktamatra manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*duḥsthitaṃ susthitaṃ vāpi śivaliṃgaṃ na cālayet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. There is another reason also for this, O messenger, as stated by learned men. One shall not dislodge a Śivaliṅga installed whether duly or unduly.

## \|\| 1.104.78 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ tatra gatvā'tha liṃgabhedaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*svayaṃ māheśvaro bhūtvā pratijñāya ca vai svayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Being a devotee of Maheśvara myself and having undertaken a solemn pledge, how can I go there and break the Liṅga myself?

## \|\| 1.104.79 \|\|

*tasmātprasādanīyaste madvākyātsa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*yadyuktaṃ mayā proktaṃ tattvaṃ kuru vinigraham \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. So, that king should be pacified with these words of mine: “If anything improper or irrelevant has been uttered by me do punish me.”

## \|\| 1.104.80 \|\|

*evamuktvātha taṃ dūtaṃ ratnaiḥ sāgarasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*prabhūtairbhūṣayitvā'tha visasarja nṛpaṃ prati \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. After saying so, he adorned the messenger with many jewels taken from the ocean and sent him off to the king.

## \|\| 1.104.81 \|\|

*atha te rākṣasāstena śaptāḥ procuḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*kuru śāpasya mokṣaṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ rākṣaseśvara \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then the Rākṣasas who had been imprecated by him said to him in great grief, “O Lord of Rākṣasas, grant us all relief from the curse.”

## \|\| 1.104.82 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ karomi bhūyo'pi yuṣmākaṃ rākṣasādhamāḥ \|\|*  
*anugrahaṃ praśaptānāṃ vaṃcakānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

Vibhīṣaṇa said:

82\. O base Rākṣasas, I shall not extend favour to you after you have been cursed, particularly because you are cheats.

## \|\| 1.104.83 \|\|

*tasmātso'pi raghuśreṣṭhaḥ prasādaṃ vaḥ kariṣyati \|*  
*mama vākyāda saṃdigdhaṃ kālaḥ kaścitpratīkṣyatām \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The most excellent one among the scions of Raghu’s family may be favourably disposed towards you undoubtedly by my request. Till then as per my order wait for some time.

## \|\| 1.104.84 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha rakṣendraḥ preṣayāmāsa satvaram \|*  
*dūtaṃ kuśamahīpasya mānuṣaṃ devapūjakam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. After saying so, the leading Rākṣasa sent off king Kuśa’s messenger, a human being worshipping the deity (with these words):

## \|\| 1.104.85 \|\|

*gatvā brūhi kuśaṃ bhūpaṃ satvaraṃ vacanānmama \|*  
*eteṣāṃ matpraśaptānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ durātmanām \|*  
*anugrahaṃ kuru vibho dīnānāṃ bhojanāya vai \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. “After going there, tell King Kuśa immediately my message. ‘O Lord, bless these Rākṣasas of wicked souls, who have been cursed by me. Let the wretched ones have their food.”

## \|\| 1.104.86 \|\|

*evamuktastatastena ito dūtena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kuśastena viniryātaḥ satvaraṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on being told by Vibhīṣaṇa thus, the messenger of Kuśā accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa’s messenger to Kuśa left the place immediately.

## \|\| 1.104.87 \|\|

*tato gatvā drutaṃ dūtaḥ kuśaṃ provāca sādaram \|*  
*praṇipatya yathā nyāyaṃ vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The messenger went speedily and respectfully reported to Kuśa, after bowing down to him and standing by with humility:

## \|\| 1.104.88 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇo mayā dṛṣṭo deve rāmeśvare vibho \|*  
*pūjārthaṃ tatra cāyāto rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. “O Lord, Vibhīṣaṇa was seen by me at the shrine of Rāmeśvara where he had come accompanied by many Rākṣasas for the purpose of adoration.

## \|\| 1.104.89 \|\|

*prokto mayā bhavadvākyamaśeṣaṃ raghunandana \|*  
*śrutaṃ tenāpi tatsarvaṃ vinayāvanatena ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O Raghunandana, he was told me all that you wanted me to say. Everything he listened to with great humility.

## \|\| 1.104.90 \|\|

*ajānataḥ prabho tasya rākṣasaiḥ sudurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*prajaivaṃ pīḍitā bhūmau mahāmāṃsasya lolupaiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. O Lord, the subjects were harrassed by his wicked Rākṣasas greedy of human flesh, without his knowledge.

## \|\| 1.104.91 \|\|

*tacchrutvā manmukhāttena sarveṣāṃ nigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*yaiḥ kṛtaṃ kadanaṃ bhūmau tava pārthiva sattama \|*  
*kṛtāste vyantarā sarve pāpāhāravihāriṇaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On hearing about it from me, he punished them all. O excellent king, those of them who committed brutality in the mainland were all turned into ghosts and spirits of defiled activities and diet.

## \|\| 1.104.92-96 \|\|

*bhaviṣyatha tathā yūyaṃ kṣutpipāsānipīḍitāḥ \|*  
*taiḥ sarvaiḥ prārthitaḥ so'pi bhūyobhūyaḥ praṇamya tam \|\| 92 \|\|*

*śaptāḥ sarve vayaṃ tāvatprasādaṃ kuru tadvibho \|*  
*te tenātha tataḥ proktā nāhaṃ vo rākṣasādhamāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*anugrahaṃ kariṣyāmi na dāsyāmi ca bhojanam \|*  
*kuśādeśānmayā sarve yūyaṃ pāpasamanvitāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*nigṛhītāḥ sa yuṣmākaṃ prasādaṃ prakariṣyati \|*  
*tadarthaṃ preṣito dūtastvatsakāśaṃ mahīpate \|\| 95 \|\|*

*rakṣasā tena yadyuktamakhilaṃ tattvamācara \|*  
*kiṃ vā te bahunoktena nāsti bhaktastathā vidhaḥ \|*  
*bhaktiśaktisamopeto yathā te sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

92-96. He told them further, ‘You will become afflicted with hunger and thirst.’

He was then requested by all of them after bowing down to him repeatedly, ‘O Lord, all of us have been cursed. Do this favour to us (by condoning our crime).’ On being asked by them thus, he said, ‘O base Rākṣasas, I will not condone and bless you. Nor will I give you food. It was at the bidding of Kuśa that ye sinners have been restrained and punished by me. He may be favourably disposed towards you.’

O King, for that purpose a messenger too has been sent to you by that Rākṣasa (i.e. Vibhīṣaṇa). What is proper may be entirely pursued by you. To be sure, there is no need to tell much. There cannot be any other devotee fully endowed with devotion and power like this Vibhīṣaṇa who is your devotee.

## \|\| 1.104.97 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti no bhūmau vicariṣyaṃti rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*tasya vākyādasaṃdehaṃ tvaṃ rājansukha bhāgbhava \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. From now onwards the Rākṣasas will never roam about on the mainland. They will desist from it undoubtedly at the bidding of his. O king, be at ease.

## \|\| 1.104.98-99 \|\|

*liṃgānāṃ ca kṛte rājanvijñaptaṃ tena rakṣasā \|*  
*na mayā cātra rājeṃdra āgantavyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*rāmadevasya vākyena jaṃbudvīpe na me gatiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*atra sthitasya yatkṛtyaṃ daivaṃ vā mānuṣaṃ ca vā \|*  
*tavādeśaṃ kariṣyāmi yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. With regard to the Liṅgas, O king, the Rākṣasa submits: ‘O great king, I should not at all come here. At the instance of Lord Rāma, I have no power to step into Jaṃbūdvīpa. Whatever duty I may have to perform, whether divine or human, I shall do it staying here alone even if it be very difficult.’

## \|\| 1.104.100 \|\|

*tasmāttena mahārāja rāmeśvaraprapūjakaḥ \|*  
*manuṣyaḥ preṣito dūto yastaṃ paśya mahīpate \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. For that purpose, O great king, a human being, a worshipper of the deity Rāmeśvara, has been sent as his messenger. Do meet him.”

## \|\| 1.104.101 \|\|

*atha tasya samādeśāḍḍhaukanīyaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*sahitaḥ sa samāyāto dūto rakṣeṃdranoditaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then at his bidding, the messenger sent by the leader of the Rākṣasas came there along with tributes and presents of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.104.102 \|\|

*dhātrīphalapramāṇānāṃ tena prasthāstrayodaśa \|*  
*mauktikānāṃ samānītāḥ kṛte tasya mahīpateḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. For the king thirteen Prastha-fuls of pearls each of the size of a Dhātrī (Indian gooseberry) fruit were brought by him.

## \|\| 1.104.103 \|\|

*vaiḍūryāṇāṃ marakatānāṃ maṇīnāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*jātyānāṃ ṣoḍaśa droṇāḥ samānītāḥ sunirmalāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, sixteen Droṇas of lapis lazuli, emerald and other jewels of excellent quality and devoid of blemishes were also brought.

## \|\| 1.104.104 \|\|

*agniśaucāni vastrāṇi tathā devamayāni ca \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāni vai hema jātyaṃ saṃkhyāvivarjitam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. There were numerous garments of divine quality brought which were pure like fire, and gold of the finest purity without any limit.

## \|\| 1.104.105 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ darśayitvātha kuśāya sumahātmane \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ paścātpraṇāmamakaroddvijāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The messenger displayed all these to the noble-souled Kuśa, O Brāhmaṇas. He circumambulated him and then bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.104.106 \|\|

*eṣa pārthivaśārdūla rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*praṇāmaṃ kurute bhaktyā manmukhenedamabravīt \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. “O tiger among kings, Vibhīṣaṇa, the eminent Rākṣasa bows down to you with devotion. He speaks to you through my mouth:

## \|\| 1.104.107-109 \|\|

*prasādātte pituḥ kṣemaṃ mama rājye mahī pate \|*  
*eṣa tiṣṭhāmyahaṃ nityaṃ pūjayaṃste piturharam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*mama rājannavijñātairyadi taiḥ sudurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*mahītale kṛtaṃ kiṃcidviruddhaṃ kṣamyatāṃ mama \|\| 108 \|\|*

*ete ye rākṣasāḥ śaptāstavārthāya mayā prabho \|*  
*eteṣāṃ pretarūpāṇāṃ tvamāhāraṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 109 \|\|*

107-109. ‘O king, thanks to your father, everything is quite all right in my kingdom. I abide here worshipping every day the deity Hara installed by your father.

O king, whatever has been committed atrociously on the earth (i.e. the mainland) by those wicked-souled ones unknown to me, may be excused.

On account of you, O Lord, these Rākṣasas have been cursed by me. Assign the diet unto them who are in the form ghosts and spirits.”

## \|\| 1.104.110 \|\|

*kuśa uvāca \|*  
*mamādeśātsamāgatya te'tra liṃgāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*pūrayaṃtu prayatnena pāṃsubhiḥ sarvatodiśam \|\| 110 \|\|*

Kuśa said:

110\. At my bidding let them (ghosts and spirits) come here and fill all the Liṅgas assiduously with dust particles all round.

## \|\| 1.104.111 \|\|

*tatastu bhojanaṃ teṣāṃ yadbhaviṣyati bhūtale \|*  
*tadvakṣyāmi sthiro bhūtvā śṛṇu devaprapūjaka \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Thereafter, I shall tell you what could be their food on the earth (mainland). Listen carefully, O worshipper of the deity (priest).

## \|\| 1.104.112 \|\|

*tulāgate sadāditye tairāgatya dharātale \|*  
*vihartavyaṃ prayatnena yāvadvṛścikadarśanam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Always, when the Sun enters Libra, they must come over to the earth (mainland) and divert themselves earnestly until the Sun is seen to enter Scorpio.

## \|\| 1.104.113-114 \|\|

*tatra yairna kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ pretapakṣe narādhamaiḥ \|*  
*kanyāsthe vā ravau yāvanna tulāṃtagatirbhavet \|\| 113 \|\|*

*jvararūpaistadaṃgasthairbhakṣyamannaṃ pṛthagvidham \|*  
*mamādeśādasaṃdigdhaṃ māsamekaṃ niśācaraiḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. If during the Pretapakṣa (dark half of Bhādrapada) or during the period of Sun’s transit in Virgo as well as Libra, it is my command that those Rākṣasas should assume the form of fever and infest their bodies. Undoubtedly they can feed on them in diverse ways for the period of a month.

## \|\| 1.104.115 \|\|

*vidhihīnaṃ ca yairdattaṃ bhuktaṃ ca vidhivarjitam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ vā mānuṣaiḥ sevyā jvararūpaiśca te sadā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. If people offer anything without resorting to the proper procedure, or if they eat anything in that manner or if Śrāddha is offered and partaken of in this manner, the Rākṣasas should always infest them in the form of Jvara (fever).

## \|\| 1.104.116 \|\|

*evaṃ vācyāstvayā sarve pretāste madvaco'khilam \|*  
*tasmādāgatya kurvaṃtu kārtike māsi madvacaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. All the ghosts and spirits should be told of my words entirely. Let them come here in the month of Kārttika and do as per my words.

## \|\| 1.104.117-119 \|\|

*tathā dūta tvayā vācyo mama vākyādvibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*pramādādyanmayā proktaṃ paruṣaṃ vacanaṃ tava \|\| 117 \|\|*

*jānāmyahaṃ mahābhāga na te'sti vikṛtiḥ kvacit \|*  
*parikliṣṭaṃ janaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayaitadvyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*rākṣasendre sthite bhūmau tvayi jānāmyahaṃ sadā \|*  
*tiṣṭhate janako mahyaṃ rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

117-119. Further, O messenger, Vibhīṣaṇa should be told by you these words of mine: ‘Inadvertently I spoke very harsh words to you. O highly esteemed one, I know (hope) that you are unperturbed thereby. On seeing the people suffer those words were blurted out by me.

Since you, the king of Rākṣasas, continue to stay on the earth I feel that my father Rāma, the foremost among those who wield weapons, also continues to live.’

## \|\| 1.104.120 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato dūtaṃ pūjayā māsa rāghavaḥ \|*  
*vastrairbahuvidhai ratnairnadyutthaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. After saying thus the descendant of Raghu honoured the messenger with various kinds of clothes and different kinds of jewels taken from fivers.

## \|\| 1.104.121 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇakṛte paścātpreṣayāmāsa rāghavaḥ \|*  
*ḍhaukanīyānyanekāni yāni saṃti ca tatra vai \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. For Vibhīṣaṇa also, Rāghava sent many things which were ready at hand there as presents.

## \|\| 1.104.122 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa sukhasaṃyuktānkṛtvā sarvāndvijottamān \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ dadau paścāttebhyo muktādikaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

Sūta said:

122\. Similarly, the king made all excellent Brāhmaṇas happy and comfortable and gave them all those pearls etc.

## \|\| 1.104.123-124 \|\|

*ḍhaukanīyaṃ tathā'yātaṃ tallaṃkāyāḥ pṛthagvidham \|*  
*śāsanāni tathānyāni gajāśvasahitāni ca \|\| 123 \|\|*

*pattanāni vicitrāṇi grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca \|*  
*yaccānyadvāṃchitaṃ yena taddattaṃ tena tasya vai \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. Whatever came as present from Laṅkā was given to them. Documentary charters etc. were presented along with elephants and horses. Towns of wonderful features, villages and cities were gifted away. Whoever asked for anything was given the same immediately.

## \|\| 1.104.125-126 \|\|

*tataḥ kuśeśvaraṃ devaṃ vidhāya ca laveśvaram \|*  
*svāṃ tanuṃ ca mahābhāgau bhrātarau tau raghūttamau \|\| 125 \|\|*

*nivedya brāhmaṇendrāṇāṃ kṛtvā vṛttiṃ yathocitām \|*  
*ayodhyāṃ nagarīṃ tūrṇaṃ kṛtakṛtyau vinirgatau \|\| 126 \|\|*

125-126. The deities of Kuśeśvara and Laveśvara were installed. Those two brothers hailing from the family of Raghu dedicated themselves to the leading Brāhmaṇas and made provision for their proper subsistence. With full satisfaction they (both) returned to the city of Ayodhyā.

## Chapter 105 - Removal of the Rākṣasa Liṅgas

## \|\| 1.105.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha prāpte dinādhīśe tulāyāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*pretā liṃgodbhavāṃ bhūmiṃ pūrayāmāsureva hi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as the Lord of the day (Sun) entered the zodiac of Libra, the ghosts filled the ground where the Liṅgas had been installed.

## \|\| 1.105.2 \|\|

*yatkiṃcittatra saṃsthaṃ tu ādyatīrthaṃ surālayam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vyantaraistaiśca pāṃsubhiḥ paripūritam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Whatever was there, namely the original Tīrtha, the shrine etc. was completely filled with dust particles by those ghosts and spirits.

## \|\| 1.105.3 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣemaṃ samutpannaṃ kṣetre tatra dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*anyeṣāmapi lokānāṃ liṃgaistairluptimāgataiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. As those Liṅgas disappeared, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there was peace and welfare everywhere in the holy spot and also to other people.

## \|\| 1.105.4 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya bṛhadaśvo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*śālvadeśātsamāyātaḥ kasmiścidyugaparyaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once upon a time, when there was change of the Yuga, King Bṛhadaśva came there from the Śālva land (south of Kurukṣetra).

## \|\| 1.105.5 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā vipulāṃ bhūmiṃ prāsādaiḥ parivarjitām \|*  
*prāsādārthaṃ matiṃ cakre tatra kṣetre dvijottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing the extensive ground, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, devoid of palaces, shrines, he became inclined to erect palaces.

## \|\| 1.105.6 \|\|

*śilpinaśca samāhūyānekāṃstatra sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*śodhayāmāsa tāṃ bhūmimadhastādbahuvistṛtām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He summoned many thousands of artisans and craftsmen. He dug up to explore that extensive plot of land from below.

## \|\| 1.105.7 \|\|

*bhūmau nikhanyamānāyāṃ tato liṃgāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*caturvaktrāṇi tānyeva yāṃti dṛṣṭeśca gocaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. As the ground was being dug up, all those numerous four-faced Liṅgas come into view.

## \|\| 1.105.8 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivastaiśca liṃgairdṛṣṭvā vṛtāṃ bhuvam \|*  
*tatkṣaṇānmṛtyumāpannaḥ śilpibhiśca samanvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereupon, after seeing the ground fully covered with the Liṅgas, the king as well as the artisans met with their death instantly.

## \|\| 1.105.9 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti no tatra kaścinmartyo mahītale \|*  
*prāsādaṃ kurute bhītyā taḍāgaṃ kūpameva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Ever since then, out of fear, no man erects palaces or digs lake or well there.

## Chapter 106 - Greatness of the Vanished Tīrthas

## \|\| 1.106.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhūpṛṣṭhe pāṃsubhistasminpretaistaiḥ paripūrite \|*  
*yāni tīrthāni luptāni liṅgāni ca vadasva naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāni tīrthāni tathā liṃgāni ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*lopaṃ gatāni vakṣyāmi prādhānyena prabodhata \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. Do tell us what those Liṅgas (Tīrthas) were that vanished when the ground was filled with dust-particles by those spirits and ghosts.

## \|\| 1.106.3 \|\|
