*tatra lopaṃ gataṃ tīrthaṃ cakratīrthamiti smṛtam \|*  
*yatra cakraṃ purā nyastaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

Innumerable Tīrthas and Liṅgas got vanished there, O Brāhmaṇas. I shall describe them in the order of their importance. Listen and understand.

3\. What is remembered as Cakra Tīrtha vanished. It was there that the discus was placed formerly by Viṣṇu, the all-powerful god.

## \|\| 1.106.4 \|\|

*mātṛtīrthaṃ tathaivānyatsarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*yatra tā mātaro divyāḥ kārtikeyapratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Another Tīrtha that got lost was Mātṛ Tīrtha that bestows all desired things on men. It was there that the Divine Mothers were established by Kārttikeya.

## \|\| 1.106.5 \|\|

*mucukundasya rājarṣestathānyalliṃga muttamam \|*  
*tatra lopaṃ gataṃ viprāḥ sagarasya tu bhūpateḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There was another excellent Liṅga of the saintly king Mucukunda that got vanished there as well as that of King Sagara.

## \|\| 1.106.6-8 \|\|

*ikṣvākorvasuṣeṇasya kakutsthasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ailasya candradevasya kāśirājasya sanmateḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*agniveśasya raibhyasya cyavanasya bhṛgostathā \|*  
*āśramo yājñavalkyasya tatra lopaṃ samāyayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*hārītasya maharṣeśca haryaśvasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kutsasya ca vasiṣṭhasya nāradasya tritasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-7a. (Liṅgas installed by the following persons were lost:) Liṅgas of (i.e. installed by) Ikṣvāku, Vasuṣeṇa, the noble-souled Kakutstha, Aila (Purūravas), Moon-god (Candradeva), the pious-minded Kāśīrāja, Agniveśa, Raibhya, Cyavana and Bhṛgu.

7b-8. The hermitage of Yājñavalkya got submerged (buried); so also the penance-groves of the great sage Hārīta, the noble-souled Haryaśva, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada and Trita.

## \|\| 1.106.9-11 \|\|

*tathaiva ṛṣipatnīnāṃ tatra liṃgāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*kātyāyanyāśca śāṃḍilyā maitreyyāśca tathā purā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*anyāsāṃ munipatnīnāṃ yāsāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*tatrāścaryamabhūdanyatpūryamāṇe mahītale \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pāṃsubhī rākṣasairyaistaiḥ pretairbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*tadvo'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śrotavyaṃ susamāhitaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-10a. The Liṅgas installed by many of the wives of these sages got vanished, such as those installed by Kātyāyanī, Śāṇḍilī, and Maitreyī and many other saintly wives whose number cannot be reckoned.

10b-11. When the ground was being filled with dust particles by those Rākṣasas who became ghosts and spirits, a miracle occurred there. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall narrate it to you. You must listen with concentration.

## \|\| 1.106.12 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā pāṃsumayīṃ vṛṣṭiṃ muktāṃ pretaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*mātṛvargeṇa tenātha pramuktaḥ pracuro'nilaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing the shower of dust particles let down by the spirits all round, gusts of winds were let loose by the group of Mātṛs (Mother-goddesses).

## \|\| 1.106.13 \|\|

*tena pāṃsukṛtā vṛṣṭiḥ samaṃtānmathitā bahiḥ \|*  
*tasyā bhūmeḥ patatyeva na kiṃcittatra pūryate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The shower of dust particles was suppressed (blown away) all round externally by the wind and the shower of dust never reached the ground nor was anything buried.

## \|\| 1.106.14 \|\|

*tataste vyaṃtarāḥ khinnā nirāśāstasya pūraṇe \|*  
*bhūtāstasya puro gatvā cukruśuḥ kuśabhūpateḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The spirits and ghosts became dejected. They lost their hopes for filling up. So they went to King Kuśa and lamented:

## \|\| 1.106.15-16 \|\|

*asmābhirvihitā tatra pāṃsuvṛṣṭirmahīpate \|*  
*nīyate śatadhā'nyatra mātṛmuktena vāyunā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sa tvaṃ tāsāṃ vighātārthamupāyaṃ bhūpa ciṃtaya \|*  
*yena tāṃ pāṃsubhirbhūmiṃ pūrayāmaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. “O king, we created a downpour of dust particles there but it is being blown away in a hundred ways by the gusts of wind let loose by the Mātṛs.

O king, you should consider the means of restraining them, so that we can fill the ground all round with dust particles.”

## \|\| 1.106.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ kuśamahīpatiḥ \|*  
*rudramārādhayāmāsa tatkṣetraṃ prāpya saddvijāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing their words, King Kuśa went to that holy spot, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and propitiated Rudra.

## \|\| 1.106.18 \|\|

*tatastasya gatastuṣṭiṃ varṣāṃte bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*provāca prārthayābhīṣṭaṃ yatte manasi vāṃchitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At the end of a year thereafter, Lord Hara became pleased with him and said, “Request for anything that has been desired in your mind.”

## \|\| 1.106.19 \|\|

*kuśa uvāca \|*  
*yathā saṃpūryate cāśu pāṃsubhirbhūmimaṃḍalam \|*  
*etatpretapramuktaiśca prasādātte tathā kuru \|\| 19 \|\|*

Kuśa said:

19\. Kindly see that, with your favour, the plot of land is covered soon by the dust particles poured by these ghosts.

## \|\| 1.106.20 \|\|

*mayā pretagaṇādeva nirdiṣṭāstasya pūraṇe \|*  
*mātṛsaṃrakṣyamāṇaṃ tacchakyaṃ caitanna pūritum \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Lord, the group of ghosts was directed by me to fill it up. Since it is being guarded by the Mātṛs it cannot be filled.

## \|\| 1.106.21 \|\|

*tatra rākṣasajairmaṃtraiḥ saṃti liṃgāni ca prabho \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitāni tatsparśāddarśanātsyājjanakṣayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Further, O Lord, there are Liṅgas there installed with the Mantras of the Rākṣasas. By the contact or sight (i.e. by touching or seeing them) thereof, destruction of the people may take place.

## \|\| 1.106.22 \|\|

*acalatvāttathā deva liṃgānāṃ śāstrasadbhayāt \|*  
*anyadutpāṭanādyaṃ ca naiva kurmaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There is the just fear as laid down in the scriptures that Liṅgas should not be moved. We do not have recourse to anything else at all such as uprooting them (Liṅgas) etc.

## \|\| 1.106.23 \|\|

*tasmālliṃgakṛto nāśo brāhmaṇānāṃ tapasvinām \|*  
*yathā na syātsuraśreṣṭha tathā nītirvidhīyatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence, O excellent one among Suras, let a way be adopted to ensure that there is no destruction of the Brāhmaṇas and the sages brought about by the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.106.24-25 \|\|

*tataśca bhagavānrudrastāḥ samāhūya mātaraḥ \|*  
*provāca tyajyatāṃ sthānaṃ bhavatyo yatra saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatra pāṃsubhiravyagrāḥ kariṣyaṃti divāniśam \|*  
*pretāḥ kuśasamādeśādvṛṣṭiṃ lokahitāya ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Then Lord Rudra summoned the Mātṛs and said: “Let the spot where you all are stationed be vacated. There, at the bidding of Kuśa and for the benefit of all the worlds, the ghosts and spirits free from worry will shower dust particles day and night.”

## \|\| 1.106.26 \|\|

*mātara ūcuḥ \|*  
*tyakṣyāmaśca tavādeśāttatsthānaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*paraṃ darśaya cāsmākaṃ kiṃcidanyattathāvidham \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Mātṛs said:

26\. O Bull-emblemed One, at your bidding we shall vacate this spot. But show us some other similar spot (to stay).

## \|\| 1.106.27 \|\|

*kṣetre'traiva nivatsyāmo yena skandakṛte vayam \|*  
*tena saṃsthāpitāścātra proktāḥ stheyaṃ sadā tataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. We would rather stay in this same holy spot created by Skanda by whom we have been installed and directed, “You must all stay here always.”

## \|\| 1.106.28-30 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca bhagavāṃstasmātsthānānmahattaram \|*  
*sthānaṃ dāsyāmi sarvāsāṃ pṛthaktvena śubhāvaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭistu kṣetrāṇāṃ madīyānāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*saṃsthitāsti mahābhāgā yeṣu matsaṃsthitiḥ sadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭivibhāgena bhūtvā sarvāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*teṣu tiṣṭhatha madvākyātpūjāmagryāmavāpsyatha \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Then the Lord said: “I shall grant you all severally a spot more auspicious and greater than this spot. O highly esteemed ones, I have already in my possession sixty-eight holy spots where I am always present. All of you, at my bidding, shall divide yourselves into sixty-eight separate groups and stay there. You will all get honoured adoration.”

## \|\| 1.106.31-32 \|\|

*tasya devasya tacchrutvā vākyaṃ tā mātarastadā \|*  
*prahṛṣṭāstatparityajya sthānaṃ skandavinirmitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭivibhāgena bhūtvā rūpaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu kṣetreṣu tasya tāḥ saṃsthitāḥ sadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. On hearing the words of that Lord the Mātṛs were delighted. They left the spot established by Skanda. They divided themselves into sixty-eight separate groups and settled in the sixty-eight holy spots forever.

## \|\| 1.106.33 \|\|

*tatastābhirvinirmuktaṃ tatsarvaṃ bhūmimaṇḍalam \|*  
*pāṃsubhiḥ pūritaṃ pretairdivārātramataṃdritaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The entire terrestrial region abandoned by them was filled with dust-particles by the spirits and ghosts working energetically day and night.

## \|\| 1.106.34 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya varaṃ dattvā bhagavānvṛṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ paścātsārdhaṃ savargaiṇairdvijāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After granting him the boon thus, the Bull-vehicled Lord left, O Brāhmaṇas, along with all the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 1.106.35 \|\|

*kuto'pi brāhmaṇaiḥ sarvestāpasaiśca praśaṃsitaḥ \|*  
*labdhāśī prayayau tasmādayodhyānagarīṃ prati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Praised by all the Brāhmaṇas and ascetics Kuśa accepted their benedictions and went from there to the city of Ayodhyā.

## Chapter 107 - Installation of Citraśarma Liṅga

## \|\| 1.107.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiriyaṃ proktā yā tvayā sūtanandana \|*  
*kṣetrāṇāṃ devadevasya kathaṃ sā tatra saṃsthitā \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*praśnabhāro mahāneṣa yo bhavadbhiḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi kīrtayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā pinākinam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtanandana, it has been mentioned by you that sixty-eight holy spots of the Lord of Devas were established there. How were they installed? Do describe them completely. We are greatly interested therein.

## \|\| 1.107.3 \|\|

*camatkārapure'vāsītpūrvaṃ brāhmaṇasattamaḥ \|*  
*vatsasyānvayasaṃbhūtaścitraśarmā mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

It is a very difficult question that you have put to me. Still I shall describe it after duly bowing down to the Pināka-bearing Lord.

3\. Formerly, there was an excellent Brāhmaṇa in the city of Camatkāra here. He hailed from the family (Gotra) of Vatsa. The name of this highly renowned one was Citraśarmā.

## \|\| 1.107.4 \|\|

*tasya buddhiriyaṃ jātā pātāle hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*atrānīya tato bhaktyā pūjayāmi divāniśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He thought: ‘There is Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla. I shall bring it here and devoutly worship it day and night.’

## \|\| 1.107.5 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā tapaścake tataḥ param \|*  
*niyato niyatāhāraḥ parāṃ niṣṭhāṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After resolving thus, he began to perform a penance later. Controlling himself and restricting his diet he reached the highest point of the penance.

## \|\| 1.107.6 \|\|

*tasyāpi bhagavāñchaṃbhuḥ kālena mahatā tataḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭo brāhmaṇa śreṣṭhāstataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Only after a long time, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Lord Śaṃbhu was pleased with him. He spoke to him courteously:

## \|\| 1.107.7-8 \|\|

*varaṃ prārthaya viprendra yatte manasi vartate \|*  
*api trailokyarājyaṃ te tuṣṭo dāsyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmātprārthaya te nityaṃ yatra citte vyavasthitam \|*  
*durlabhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. “O eminent Brāhmaṇa, request for a boon—whatever may be in your mind. Undoubtedly I shall gladly grant you (even) the kingdom of the three worlds. Hence, request for that which has been always lurking in your mind, even if it be very difficult to be obtained by all the human beings and all the Devas in particular.”

## \|\| 1.107.9 \|\|

*citraśarmovāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭosi me deva varaṃ cenme prayacchasi \|*  
*tadatrāgaccha pātālālliṃgarūpī sureśvara \|\| 9 \|\|*

Citraśarman said:

9\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if you wish to grant me a boon, O Lord of Suras, come here from Pātāla in the form of Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.107.10 \|\|

*yatpātāle sthitaṃ liṃgaṃ brahmaṇā saṃpratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu tadihāyātu satva ram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. May that Liṅga named Hāṭakeśvara which was installed by Brahmā and is stationed in Pātāla, come here quickly.

## \|\| 1.107.11 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*acalaṃ sarvaliṃgaṃ syātsarvatrāpi dvijottama \|*  
*ki punaḥ prathamaṃ yacca brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ svayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

11\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, all the Liṅgas in all the places are never to be shifted and disturbed. It is all the more so in the case of the primordial one installed by Brahmā himself.

## \|\| 1.107.12 \|\|

*tasmātthāpaya liṃgaṃ taddhāṭakena dvijottama \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu loke khyātaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, install that Liṅga of gold thereof. It will become well-known in the world by the name Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.107.13-14 \|\|

*somavāre catudaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*yastadbhaktisamāyuktaḥ pūjayiṣyati mānavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ādyaliṃgodbhavaṃ śreyaḥ pūjayā lapsyate dvija \|*  
*evamuktvā'tha bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. A man endowed with devotion who worships it on a Monday or on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half, O Brāhmaṇa, shall obtain through that adoration the benefit of worshipping the primordial Liṅga as well.

After saying thus, the Lord vanished from there.

## \|\| 1.107.15 \|\|

*citraśarmā'pi kṛtvātha prāsādaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*tatra hemamayaṃ liṃgaṃ sthāpayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Citraśarman erected a very charming palace-like shrine and devoutly installed a gold Liṅga there.

## \|\| 1.107.16 \|\|

*śāstroktena vidhānena pūjāṃ cakre ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tatastrailokya vikhyātaṃ talliṃgaṃ tatra vai dvijāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He performed its worship everyday in the manner enjoined in the scriptures. Thereupon, O Brāhmaṇas, that Liṅga there became well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.107.17-24 \|\|

*dūrādabhyetya lokāśca pūjayaṃti tataḥ param \|*  
*atha tatra dvijā ye'nye saṃsthitā guṇavattarāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ spardhā tato jātā dṛṣṭvā tasya viceṣṭitam \|*  
*ekasthānaprasūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ guṇaśālinām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ayaṃ guṇavihīno'pi prakhyāto bhuvanatraye \|*  
*harārādhanamāsādya yasmāttasmādvayaṃ haram \|*  
*tadarthe toṣayiṣyāmaḥ sāmyaṃ yena prajāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ smṛtā loke kṣetrāṇāṃ śūlapāṇinaḥ \|*  
*yatra sānnidhyamabhyeti trikālaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiśca gotrāṇāmasmākaṃ cātra saṃsthitā \|*  
*etena mūḍhamanasā sārdhaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasmādanena cārādhya bhagavantaṃ trilocanam \|*  
*tacca liṃgaṃ samānītamatra pātālasaṃsthitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tathā sarvaiśca sarvāṇi kṣetraliṃgāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*ānetavyāni cārādhya tapaḥśaktyā maheśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ sarvagotrāṇāmāneṣyati ca śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*yadgotraṃ kṣetrasaṃyuktaṃ yaccānyadvā bhaviṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

17-18a. Thereafter, people from far-off places came there and began to worship it. A great rivalry born of jealousy arose in those Brāhmaṇas of better qualities who were present there. On noticing the activities of Citraśarman, they thought:

18b-24. ‘All of us are endowed with good qualities and are born in this same place. But (this Brāhmaṇa) though devoid of good qualities has become famous in all the three worlds by propitiating Hara. Therefore, we shall also propitiate Hara for that purpose so that we may have equality with him.

The holy spots of the Trident-bearing Lord in the world are remembered to be sixty-eight in number and Parameśvara shows his presence there thrice a day.

The number of our Gotras staying here is also sixty-eight having common characteristics with this man of foolish mind.

After propitiating the Three-eyed Lord, the Liṅga stationed in Pātāla has been brought by him.

In the same manner, all of us should propitiate Maheśvara by the power of penance and bring all the Liṅgas of the holy spots.

Śaṅkara will bring them unto the people of all the Gotras and decide which Gotra should be connected with which holy spot. Other things also shall occur as he pleases.’

## \|\| 1.107.25 \|\|

*tataste śarmasaṃyuktāḥ sarva eva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*cakrustapaḥkriyāṃ sarve duṣkarāṃ sarvajantubhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then all the excellent Brāhmaṇas happily performed penance difficult to be performed by all the creatures.

## \|\| 1.107.26 \|\|

*japairhomopavāsaiśca niyamaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*balipūjopahāraiśca snānadānādibhistathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. They performed the penance along with Japa, Homa, observance of fast and restraints of different kinds, oblations, adorations, offerings of presents, holy ablution, Dāna, and other things.

## \|\| 1.107.27 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya devasya nāmnā khyātaṃ dvijeśvaram \|*  
*manoharatare procce prāsāde parvatopame \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They installed a Liṅga of the Lord which became well-known by the name Dvijeśvara in a lofty palace comparable to a mountain.

## \|\| 1.107.28 \|\|

*tyaktvā gṛhakriyāḥ sarvāstathā yajñasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*anyāśca lokayātrotthāstoṣayaṃti maheśvaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. They abandoned all their domestic activities and even sacrificial rites as well as everyday duties for the sake of mundane existence and continued to propitiate Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.107.29 \|\|

*evamārādhyamāno'pi santoṣaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*nābhyagacchatparāṃ tuṣṭiṃ kathaṃcidapi sa dvijāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Although he was propitiated thus, O Brāhmaṇas, Parameśvara did not become pleased. He never attained the highest satisfaction.

## \|\| 1.107.30 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte samārādhya maheśvaram \|*  
*na ca kiñcitphalaṃ prāptā yāvatkruddhāstato'khilāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When they never got any benefit even at the end of a thousand years of their propitiation of Maheśvara, all of them became angry.

## \|\| 1.107.31-33 \|\|

*asya mūrkhatamasyā'pi tvaṃ śūliṃścitraśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*sustokenā'pi kālena santoṣaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vayaṃ vārdhakyamāpannā bālyātprabhṛti śaṃkaram \|*  
*pūjayanto'pi no dṛṣṭastathā'pi parameśvara \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasmātsarve prakartavyaṃ havyavāhapraveśanam \|*  
*asmābhirniścayo hyeṣa tavāgre sāṃprataṃ kṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. “O Trident-bearing One, you became very pleased in a very short time with this utter fool Citraśarman. Still, O Parameśvara, we have not been taken into account though we have been worshipping Śaṅkara ever since our childhood and we have grown very old now. Hence all of us should enter fire and immolate ourselves. This is the conclusion we have arrived at. We will do it in front of you.”

## \|\| 1.107.34 \|\|

*tataścāhṛtya kāṣṭhāni sarve te dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*īśvaraṃ manasi dhyātvā citāścakruḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then all those excellent Brāhmaṇas brought fuel. Meditating upon Īśvara they prepared many funeral pyres.

## \|\| 1.107.35-36 \|\|

*tathā sarvaṃ kriyākalpaṃ snānadānādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*kṛtvā te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve susamiddhahutāśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yāvatkṛtvā sutaiḥ sārdhaṃ praviśaṃti samāhitāḥ \|*  
*tāvatsa bhagavāṃstuṣṭasteṣāṃ saṃdarśanaṃ yayau \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. They performed all the rites in accordance with the scriptural injunctions such as holy bath, Dāna etc., and kindled the holy fire. Thereafter, all those Brāhmaṇas were about to jump into the fire along with their sons, when the Lord who was pleased, granted them his vision.

## \|\| 1.107.37 \|\|

*abravīcca vihasyoccairmeghagambhīrayā girā \|*  
*sarvāṃstānbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhānmṛtānsaṃjīvayanniva \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He laughed boisterously and told all those excellent Brāhmaṇas in a tone as majestic as that of a rumbling cloud. Thereby he seemed to resuscitate them from death:

## \|\| 1.107.38-39 \|\|

*bho bho brāhmaṇaśārdūlā mā maivaṃ sāhasaṃ mahat \|*  
*yūyaṃ kuruta madvākyātsaṃtuṣṭasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmādvadata yaccitte yuṣmākaṃ caiva saṃsthitam \|*  
*yena dattvā pragacchāmi svameva bhuvanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. “O tigers among Brāhmaṇas, do not commit this rash act. I am particularly pleased. At my instance, you ought not to do so. Tell me what has been cherished within your heart so that I can grant it and go back to my own world.”

## \|\| 1.107.40 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*asminkṣetre suraśreṣṭha purasyāsya ca saṃnidhau \|*  
*kṣetrāṇāmaṣṭaṣaṣṭiryā dhanyā saṃkīrtyate janaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

40\. O most excellent one among Suras, the sixty-eight holy spots in this sacred region near this city are glorified by people as the most blessed.

## \|\| 1.107.41 \|\|

*sadābhyaitu samaṃ liṃgaistairādyaiḥ surasattama \|*  
*yenāmarṣapraśāṃtirnaḥ sarveṣāmiha jāyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O excellent one among Suras, let those primordial Liṅgas be in contact with this holy spot, so that all our indignation may become quelled.

## \|\| 1.107.42 \|\|

*eṣa saṃspardhate'smābhiḥ sarvairguṇavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*tvalliṃgasya prabhāvena tasmādetatsamācara \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Though this fellow is devoid of good qualities he vies with all of us, thanks to the power of your Liṅga. Hence do like this.

## \|\| 1.107.43 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare vipro jñātvā taṃ varadaṃ haram \|*  
*uvāca spardhayā yuktaścitraśarmā maheśvaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sūta said:

43\. In the meantime, the Brāhmaṇa Citraśarman came to know that Maheśvara was about to grant the boon. Therefore, he said to Maheśvara out of envious rivalry:

## \|\| 1.107.44-46 \|\|

*citraśarmovāca \|*  
*etaiḥ prāṇaparityāgamārabhya tadanataram \|*  
*tuṣṭiṃ nīto'si devaśa kṛtvā ca sumahattapaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mayā sparddhamānaiśca kevalaṃ guṇagarvitaiḥ \|*  
*tasmādeṣo na dātavyatvaṃ tvayā kiṃcitsureśvara \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yadi tvaṃ māmatikramya saṃpradāsyasi vāṃchitam \|*  
*etaiḥ putrakalatraiśca sārdhaṃ pratyakṣatastava \|*  
*pāvakaṃ sādhayiṣyāmi tasmādyuktaṃ samācara \|\| 46 \|\|*

Citraśarman said:

44-46. These Brāhmaṇas are arrogant due to their good qualities alone, O Lord of Devas. After performing a great penance they became inclined to abandon their life. Thus, you are propitiated by them. They want only to vie with me. So, O Lord of Suras, nothing should be given to them. If you set me aside and grant them their desire, I will fall into the fire along with these sons and wife, within your sight (presence). So do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.107.47-52 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa cittena kimatra sukṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ete brāhmaṇaśārdūlā vināśaṃ yāṃti matkṛte \|*  
*eṣo'pi sarvasaṃsiddho gaṇatulyo dvijottamaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tasmāddvābhyāṃ mayā kāryaṃ kṣetre saukhyaṃ yathā bhavet \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣeṇa tathā cātra nivāsinām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mamāpi sarvadā citte kṛtyametaddhi vartate \|*  
*eka sthāne karomyeva sarvakṣetrāṇi yāni me \|\| 50 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati tathā kālo raudraḥ kalisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tatra kṣetrāṇi tīrthāni nāśaṃ yāsyaṃti bhūtale \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sattīrthaistadbhayātsarvaiḥ kṣetrametatsamāśritam \|*  
*ānayiṣyāmyahamapi svāni kṣetrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sūta said:

47-52. On hearing his words the Moon-crested Lord thought thus in his mind: ‘What shall be the proper thing to do here? These tigers among Brāhmaṇas will perish on my account. This excellent Brāhmaṇa also who is on a par with the Gaṇas and who has achieved everything (may perish). Hence happiness should be provided to both by me, particularly to these Brāhmaṇas who reside here. I have always been thinking that all my holy spots should be brought by me in one place. The period of Kali age will be very terrible when holy spots and Tīrthas on the earth will perish. All the good Tīrthas have resorted to this holy spot out of the fear thereof. I shall bring all my Kṣetras also here.’

## \|\| 1.107.53 \|\|

*tatastaṃ citraśarmāṇaṃ prāha cedaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu madvacanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kuruṣva tadanaṃtaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then Maheśvara said to Citraśarman: “Listen to my words and later act accordingly.

## \|\| 1.107.54 \|\|

*atra kṣetrāṇi sarvāṇi madīyāni dvijottama \|*  
*samāgacchaṃtu viprāśca prabhavaṃtu praharṣitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, let all my holy spots come here and let the Brāhmaṇas become delighted.

## \|\| 1.107.55 \|\|

*tavāpi yogyatāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ kariṣyāmi mahāmate \|*  
*yadi me vartase vākye muktvā sparddhāṃ dvijodbhavām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If you abide by my advice and abandon your rivalry with the other Brāhmaṇas, O highly intelligent one, I shall make your efficiency too very excellent.

## \|\| 1.107.56 \|\|

*turīyamapi te gotraṃ vedoktena krameṇa ca \|*  
*ādyatāṃ cāpi te sarve kīrtayiṣyaṃti te dvijāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Although the order of your Gotra as mentioned in the Vedas is the fourth, yet all those Brāhmaṇas will proclaim it as the first.

## \|\| 1.107.57 \|\|

*tathānyadapi sanmānaṃ tava yacchāmi ca dvija \|*  
*ācandrārkamasaṃdigdhaṃ putrapautrādikaṃ ca yat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Further, O Brāhmaṇas, I shall bestow another honour on you. Undoubtedly you shall have sons, grandsons etc. as long as the moon and the sun shine.

## \|\| 1.107.58-59 \|\|

*tvadanvaye bhaviṣyaṃti putrapautrāstathā pare \|*  
*kṛtye śrāddhe tarpaṇe vā kriyamāṇe vidhānataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ādyasya vatsasaṃjñasya nāma uccārya gotrajam \|*  
*tato nāmāni cāpyevaṃ kīrtayiṣyaṃti bhaktitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. There will be sons and grandsons and others in your family. When the rites of Śrāddha or Tarpaṇa are performed in accordance with the injunctions, the names of the members of the Gotra of the first one named Vatsa and later those of others will he remembered with devotion.

## \|\| 1.107.60 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃtarpayiṣyaṃti pitṝnatha pitāmahān \|*  
*tathānyānapi baṃdhūṃśca suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibāṃdhavān \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then only they will offer the libations to the Pitṛs and the grandfathers and others, including relatives, friends and allies.

## \|\| 1.107.61 \|\|

*tvadanvaye vinā nāmnā tvadīyena vimohitāḥ \|*  
*ye pitṝṃstarpayiṣyaṃti teṣāṃ vyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In your family, if the members are deluded and offer libations without (uttering) your name, to the Pitṛs, those libations will be fruitless.

## \|\| 1.107.62 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ vā yadi vā dānaṃ tarpaṇaṃ vā tvadudbhavam \|*  
*tasmādahaṃkṛtiṃ muktvā māmārādhaya kevalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. That will be the case in regard to Śrāddha, Dāna and Tarpaṇa performed by you. So give up your arrogance and simply propitiate me.”

## \|\| 1.107.63-64 \|\|

*yena siddho'pi saṃsiddhiṃ parāmāpnoṣi śāśvatīm \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbodhya taṃ vipraṃ kṛtvādyamapi paścimam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tatastānbrāhmaṇānāha prāsādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|*  
*gotraṃgotraṃ puraskṛtya sthāpyaṃ liṃgamanuttamam \|*  
*yena saṃkramaṇaṃ teṣu mama saṃjāyatedvijāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Though, he was already a Siddha, Śiva informed him that he would attain the highest Siddhi of a permanent nature.

After saying thus to the Brāhmaṇas and making him first though he was as yet last, the Lord said to those Brāhmaṇas: “May the palace (shrine of Śiva) be built now. With each of the Gotras kept in view, the excellent Liṅga has to be installed, O Brāhmaṇas, so that my passing into them shall take place.”

## \|\| 1.107.65 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇāstatra bhūmibhāgānmanoharān \|*  
*dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvā pracakruśca prāsādānharṣasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then those Brāhmaṇas carefully chose the portions of the ground pleasing to the mind and joyously erected the palaces.

## \|\| 1.107.66 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭimitāndivyānkailāsaśikharopamān \|*  
*teṣu saṃsthāpayāmāsu liṅgāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*kṣetrekṣatre ca yannāma tattatsaṃjñāṃ pracakrire \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The palaces numbering sixty-eight were comparable to the peaks of Kailāsa. They installed different kinds of Liṅgas in them. They named them the same as before in the different holy spots.

## \|\| 1.107.67 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ punardṛṣṭiṃ gatvā devastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ kasmiṃścitkālaparyaye \|*  
*ārādhitastapaḥśaktyā liṃgasaṃsthāpanādanu \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After a lapse of some time, the Three-eyed Lord was propitiated after the installation of the Liṅgas by means of the power of penance. After some time, the Three-eyed Lord granted them vision and spoke these sweet words:

## \|\| 1.107.68 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi vipreṃdrā yuṣmākamahamadya vai \|*  
*etanmama kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ bhavadbhirakhilaṃ tataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

68\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, I am much pleased with you all today. Everything that has to be done in regard to me has been done by you.

## \|\| 1.107.69 \|\|

*asmadīyāni liṃgāni kṣetrāṇi ca kalerbhayāt \|*  
*tato mānyāśca me yūyaṃ nānyairetadbhaviṣyati \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Our Liṅgas and holy spots (have been changed) due to the fear of Kali age. So you are worthy of my commendation. This would not have been possible through others.

## \|\| 1.107.70 \|\|

*tasmāccittasthitaṃ śīghraṃ prārthayaṃtu dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*saṃprayacchāmi yenāśu yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, let the excellent Brāhmaṇas request for whatever has been cherished in the mind quickly so that I can immediately grant them even if they happen to be rare.

## \|\| 1.107.71-72 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi deva prasannastvamasmākaṃ ca sureśvara \|*  
*paścimaścitraśarmā ca yathādyo bhavatā kṛtaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*asmadīyaṃ sadā nāma kīrtanīyamasaṃśayam \|*  
*śrāddhakṛtyeṣu sarveṣu yathā tena samā vayam \|*  
*bhavāmastvatprasādena sāṃprataṃ citraśarmaṇā \|\| 72 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

71-72. O Lord, if you are pleased with us, O Lord of Suras, our names should always be uttered in all the Śrāddha rites in the same way as in the case of Citraśarman who has been made first though he was the last before. This may be done so that we can be on a par with that Citraśarman.

## \|\| 1.107.73 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yuṣmākamapi ye kecidvaśaṃ yāsyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*yuvānaḥ śāstrasaṃyuktā vedavidyāviśāradāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

73.74. If some young men endowed with the knowledge of scriptures were to come under your control, if they are masters of the Vedic lore, bring them up with the title of “Āmuṣyāyaṇa” (descendant of an illustrious family). They will be the permanent residents of the holy spot and they will perform the Śrāddha perpetually.

## \|\| 1.107.75 \|\|

*evamuktvātha deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*te'pi viprāḥ susaṃtuṣṭāstatra sthāne vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. After saying this, the Lord of Devas vanished. Those Brāhmaṇas were very highly pleased and established themselves in that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.107.76 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samastāni kṣetrāṇyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*kalibhītāni vipreṃdrā nivasaṃti sadaiva hi \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus, O leading Brāhmaṇas, all the holy spots and shrines which were afraid of (i.e. in danger of the influence of) Kali age live there permanently.

## \|\| 1.107.77 \|\|

*evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ prāpya siddhiṃ ceśvarapūjanāt \|*  
*khyātāḥ sarvatra bhuvane śrāddhasyākṣayyakārakāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Thus those Brāhmaṇas attained Siddhi by the adoration of Īśvara. They became well-known in all the worlds as the perpetual performers of Śrāddha.

## Chapter 108 - The Aṣṭaṣaṣṭi Tīrthas

## \|\| 1.108.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭipramāṇāni yāni kṣetrāṇi sūtaja \|*  
*tvayoktāni ca tānyeva nāmato naḥ prakīrtaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathānyāni ca tīrthāni yāni saṃti dharātale \|*  
*tāni kīrtaya kārtsnyena paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 108-110 enumerate the 68 Tīrthas, their locations and names of Śiva associated with them. Hāṭakeśvara is the best Tīrtha.

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaja, you said that the holy spots numbered sixty-eight. Do narrate and enumerate them mentioning their names. Further, you do describe all the other holy spots and Tīrthas situated on the earth. We are very much eager to listen about them.

## \|\| 1.108.3-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yāni proktāni tīrthāni bhavadbhirdvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭipramāṇāni tathā kṣetrāṇi bhūtale \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tāni sarvāṇi bhītāni praviṣṭāni rasātalam \|*  
*tīrthāni muniśārdūlāḥ pāpe hyatra kalau yuge \|\| 4 \|\|*

*etadeva purā pṛṣṭaḥ pārvatyā parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*yadbhavadbhirahaṃ pṛṣṭastīrthayātrākṛte dvijāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3-5. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Tīrthas that you asked me about and which number sixty-eight, and other holy spots that are situated on the earth were afraid of Kali age and had entered Rasātala.

O tigers among sages, this Kali yuga is so very sinful. This very same question was put to Parameśvara by Pārvatī formerly. O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of pilgrimage, you are now asking me about them.

## \|\| 1.108.6 \|\|

*kailāsaśikharāsīnaḥ purā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarvairgaṇagaṇaiḥ sārdhamupaviṣṭo varāsane \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Formerly, Lord Maheśvara was seated on the peak of Kailāsa along with all the groups of the Gaṇas. He was occupying an excellent seat.

## \|\| 1.108.7 \|\|

*praṇāma karaṇārthāya hyāgateṣvamareṣu ca \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu vipreṃdrā sarveṣu tridivālayam \|*  
*ardhāsanagatā devī vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Amaras (Devas) had come for making obeisance to the Lord, O leading Brāhmaṇas, and when all of them had gone back to heaven, the goddess who had occupied half the seat, spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.108.8 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva gaṃgākṣālitaśekhara \|*  
*vada me tīrthamāhātmyaṃ yadyahaṃ vallabhā tava \|\| 8 \|\|*

The Devī said:

8\. O Mahādeva, O Lord of Devas whose crest-jewel has been washed by Gaṅgā, do tell me the greatness of the Tīrthas if you consider me your beloved.

## \|\| 1.108.9 \|\|

*tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭī ca tīrthānāmiha bhūtale \|*  
*saṃkhyayā nāmato deva mahyaṃ kīrtaya sāṃpratam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The number of the Tīrthas on the earth is thirty-five million. Do enumerate them along with their names now:

## \|\| 1.108.10 \|\|

*yāni tīrthānyanekāni kṣetrāṇi caiva me prabho \|*  
*tāni kīrtaya deveśa sugamyaṃ caiva dehinām \|*  
*kīrtanācca samagrāṇāṃ tīrthānāṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Lord, O Lord of Devas, do describe the many Tīrthas and holy places to me in a manner easily understood by embodied beings. By glorifying all the Tīrthas great merit is obtained.

## \|\| 1.108.11 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tīrthaśabdo varārohe dharmakṛtyeṣu vartate \|*  
*dharmasthāneṣu sarveṣu tattvaṃ śṛṇu samāhitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

11\. O beautiful lady, the word Tīrtha refers to all the righteous rites and all the virtuous holy spots. Do listen with mental concentration.

## \|\| 1.108.12 \|\|

*mātā tīrthaṃ pitā tīrthaṃ tīrtha sādhusamāgamaḥ \|*  
*dharmānuciṃtanaṃ caiva tathaiva niyamo yamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Mother is a Tīrtha; father is a Tīrtha; association with good men is Tīrtha; so is thinking of doing righteous things and also observing restraints and abstentions.

## \|\| 1.108.13 \|\|

*puṇyāḥ kathā varārohe devarṣīṇāṃ kṛtāstathā \|*  
*āśrayāḥ sanmunīṃdrāṇāṃ devānāṃ ca tathā priye \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. So also are the meritorious stories of the celestial sages, the place of resort of excellent sages and Devas too, O My beloved beautiful lady.

## \|\| 1.108.14 \|\|

*bhūmibhāgāḥ pavitrāḥ syuḥ kīrtyate tīrthamityuta \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃdarśanādeva smaraṇāccāvagāhanāt \|*  
*mucyaṃte jantavaḥ pāpairapi janmaśatodbhavaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If parts of lands are holy, they are glorified as Tīrtha. By seeing them, by remembering them and by taking bath in them, all the creatures are liberated from sins arising from hundreds of births.

## \|\| 1.108.15 \|\|

*tathā pātakino ye ca ye ca viśvāsaghātakāḥ \|*  
*te'pi sarve tathā muktāsteṣāṃ caivāvagāhanāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Further, all sinners, all those who commit breach of trust, shall become rid of them by bathing in the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.108.16 \|\|

*evaṃ pāpāni saṃyāṃti nāśaṃ sarvāṃgasundari \|*  
*api brahmavadhātpāpaṃ yadbhavediha dehinām \|*  
*taccāpi tīrthasaṃsargātpralayaṃ yātyasaṃśayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. So also, O lady beautiful in every limb, all the sins perish. Even if the embodied beings incur sins by slaying a Brāhmaṇa, those sins undoubtedly get destroyed by the contact of the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.108.17 \|\|

*mamāpi karasaṃlagnaṃ kapālaṃ brahmaṇaḥ purā \|*  
*patitaṃ tīrthasaṃsargātteṣāṃ caivāvagāhanāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Formerly, the skull of Brahmā got stuck up to my hand. By contact with Tīrthas and by taking bath in them it dropped off.

## \|\| 1.108.18 \|\|

*evaṃ sarveṣu tīrtheṣu tathā hyāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*snātavyaṃ bhaktiyuktena cetasā nānyagāminā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In view of this, all should take their holy bath in all the Tīrthas and shrines with the mind fully endowed with devotion, without being diverted to other things.

## \|\| 1.108.19 \|\|

*yatra snātairnaraiḥ samyaksarveṣāṃ labhyate phalam \|*  
*mamāśrayaṃ viśālākṣi sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*kāmadaṃ ca tathā nṝṇāṃ nārīṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By means of this holy bath, all men attain the benefit thereof. O large-eyed one, my place of resort is destructive of all sins. It bestows all cherished things equally on men and women.

## \|\| 1.108.20 \|\|

*etadguhyatamaṃ devi mama nityavyavasthitam \|*  
*na kasyā'pi mayākhyātaṃ deveṃdrasyāpi pṛcchataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O goddess, this has always been maintained as the greatest secret. It has not been mentioned to anyone by me, not even to Devendra who had enquired about it.

## \|\| 1.108.21 \|\|

*vāllabhyāttava me bhadre kathitaṃ vai varānane \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ pragamyāni bhaktyā tīrthāni mānavaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O fair lady of excellent countenance, it is being mentioned to you because of your being my beloved. The sixty-eight Tīrthas should be frequented by men with adequate devotion.

## \|\| 1.108.22 \|\|

*mamāśrayāṇi tānyeva sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|*  
*kāmadāni varārohe matprabhāvādasaṃśayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All these are my resorts and they destroy sins. O beautiful lady, by my power they bestow desired things undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.108.23-24 \|\|

*yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ samādhāya tatra tīrthe pumānyadi \|*  
*kṛtvā snānaṃ tato devamarcayecca maheśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sukṛtaṃ manasi dhyātvā yairnaraiḥ pūjito hariḥ \|*  
*āstāṃ teṣāṃ varārohe darśanaṃ sparśanaṃ tathā \|*  
*smaraṇādapi mucyaṃte narāḥ pāpaiḥ purākṛtaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Whatever may be the desire cherished in the heart, a man shall take his holy bath in the Tīrtha and then worship Maheśvara. If Hari is worshipped by men while thinking of one’s meritorious deeds, O excellent lady, men are rid of their sins incurred earlier merely by remembering them, let alone their direct sight and touch.

## \|\| 1.108.25 \|\|

*ete śakrādayo devāsteṣu tīrtheṣu sundari \|*  
*māṃ pūjya tridivaṃ prāptāstathānye nāradādayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O beautiful lady, these Devas beginning with Śakra, and Nārada and others have attained heaven by worshipping me.

## \|\| 1.108.26 \|\|

*tānyahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi vistareṇa pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*nāmataḥ śṛṇu deveśi samāhitamanāḥ sthitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I shall mention them severally and in detail. With the mind in concentration, O goddess of Devas, listen to them by their names:

List of Tīrthas:

## \|\| 1.108.27 \|\|

*vārāṇasī prayāgaṃ ca naimiṣaṃ cāparaṃ tathā \|*  
*gayāśiraḥ supuṇyaṃ ca pavitraṃ kurujāṃgalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Vārāṇasī, Prayāga, Naimiṣa the next one, the highly meritorious Gayāśiras, the sacred Kurujāṅgala,

## \|\| 1.108.28 \|\|

*prabhāsaṃ puṣkaraṃ caiva viśveśvaramathāparama \|*  
*aṭṭahāsaṃ mahendraṃ ca tathaivojjayanī ca yā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, Viśveśvara, Aṭṭhāsa, Mahendra, Ujjayinī,

## \|\| 1.108.29 \|\|

*marukoṭiḥ śaṃkukarṇaṃ gokarṇaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*rudrakoṭiḥ sthaleśaṃ ca harṣitaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Marukoṭi, Śāṅkukarṇa\[2\], Gokarṇa the excellent holy spot, Rudrakoṭi, Sthaleśa, Harṣita and Vṛṣabhadhvaja,

## \|\| 1.108.30 \|\|

*kedāraṃ ca tathā kṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ madhyamakeśvaram \|*  
*sahasrākṣaṃ tathā kṣetraṃ tathānyatkārtikeśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The holy spot Kedāra, the holy spot Madhyamakeśvara, the holy spot Sahasrākṣa and the other one Kārttikeśvara,

## \|\| 1.108.31 \|\|

*tathaiva vastramārgaṃ ca tathā kanakhalaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*bhadrakarṇaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ daṇḍakākhyaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the same way, Vastramārga, Kanakhala, Bhadrakarṇa, the famous holy spot named Daṇḍaka,

## \|\| 1.108.32 \|\|

*tridaṇḍākhyaṃ tathā kṣetraṃ tathaiva kṛmijāṃgalam \|*  
*ekāmraṃ ca tathā kṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ chāgalakaṃ tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The holy spot called Tridaṇḍa and also Kṛmijāṅgala, the holy spot Ekāmra, the holy spot Chāgalaka,

## \|\| 1.108.33 \|\|

*kāliṃjaraṃ ca deveśi tathānyanmaṇḍaleśvaram \|*  
*kāśmīraṃ marukeśaṃ ca hariścaṃdraṃ suśobhanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O goddess of Devas, then the holy spot Kāliñjara and the other one Maṇḍaleśvara, Kāśmīra, Marukeśa, the splendid Hariścandra,

## \|\| 1.108.34 \|\|

*puraścaṃdraṃ ca vāmeśaṃ kukuṭeśvarameva ca \|*  
*bhasmagātramathokāraṃ trisaṃdhyā virajā tathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Puraścandra, Vāmeśa, Kukkuṭeśvara, Bhasmagātra, Oṃkāra, Trisandhyā and Virajā,

## \|\| 1.108.35 \|\|

*arkeśvaraṃ ca nepālaṃ duṣkarṇaṃ karavīrakam \|*  
*jāgeśvaraṃ tathā devi śrīśailaṃ parvatottamam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Arkeśvara, Nepāla, Duṣkarṇa, Karavīraka, Jāgeśvara and then, O goddess, the excellent mountain Śrīśaila,

## \|\| 1.108.36 \|\|

*ayodhyā caiva pātālaṃ tathā kārohaṇaṃ mahat \|*  
*devikā ca nadī puṇyā bhairavaṃ pūrvasāgaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Ayodhyā, Pātāla, the great Kārohaṇa\[9\], the meritorious river Devikā, Bhairava and Pūrvasāgara (eastern ocean in Bay of Bengal),

## \|\| 1.108.37 \|\|

*saptagodāvarītīrthaṃ tathaiva samudāhṛtam \|*  
*nirmaleśaṃ tathānyacca karṇikāraṃ suśobhanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Saptagodāvarī Tīrtha (seven mouths of Godāvarī joining the sea) is also cited, then Nirmaleśa, the splendid Karṇikāra,

## \|\| 1.108.38 \|\|

*kailāsaṃ jāhnavītīraṃ jalaliṃgaṃ ca vāḍavam \|*  
*badarītīrthavaryaṃ ca koṭitīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Kailāsa, Jāhnavītīra, Jalalīṅga, Vāḍava, Badarī, Tīrthavarya and also Kotitīrtha \[Koṭitīrtha?\],

## \|\| 1.108.39 \|\|

*viṃdhyācalo hemakūṭaṃ gandhamādanameva ca \|*  
*liṃgeśvaraṃ tathā kṣetraṃ laṃkādvāraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Vīndhyācala, Hemakūṭa, Gandhamādana, the holy spot Liṅgeśvara, and then Laṅkādvāra,

## \|\| 1.108.40 \|\|

*naleśvaraṃ tu madhyeśaṃ kedāraṃ rudrajālakam \|*  
*suvarṇākhyaṃ ca vāmoru tathānyatṣaṣṭikāpatham \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Naleśvara, Madhyeśa, Kedāra, Rudrajālaka, what is named Suvarṇa and the other one, O lady of beautiful thighs, Ṣaṣṭikāpatha.

## Chapter 109 - Greatness of Aṣṭaṣaṣṭi Tīrthas

## \|\| 1.109.1 \|\|

*\| īśvara uvāca \|*  
*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi varānane \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ sāraṃ tīrthasamuccayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. O lady of excellent countenance, thus everything that I have been asked, has been narrated to you. This group of Tīrthas is the essence of all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.109.2 \|\|

*eteṣvahaṃ varārohe sarveṣveva vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā cānyeṣu tīrtheṣu tridaśānāṃ hitārthataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lady of great beauty, I abide in all these Tīrthas by my name. So also in the other Tīrthas for the benefit of Devas.

## \|\| 1.109.3 \|\|

*yo māmeteṣu tīrtheṣu snātvā paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*kīrtayetkīrtanānnāmnā sa nūnaṃ mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A man who takes his holy bath in all these Tīrthas, visits me, and glorifies me with eulogies addressed to me by name shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.109.4 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*yeṣu tīrtheṣu yannāma kīrtanīyaṃ tava prabho \|*  
*tatkārtsyena mama brūhi yaccahaṃ tava vallabhā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

4\. O Lord, what is the name whereby you should be glorified in a specific holy spot? If I am your beloved, O Lord, say this holly.

\[List of Kṣetras and Names of Śiva associated with each—After giving the list of 68 Tīrthas, this chapter gives the different names of Śīva \[Śiva?\] associated with each.\]

## \|\| 1.109.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevaṃ prayāge ca maheśvaram \|*  
*naimiṣe devadevaṃ ca gayāyāṃ prapitāmaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. Mahādeva (is the name) in Vārāṇasī; Maheśvara in Prayāga; Devadeva in Naimiṣa; and Prapitāmaha in Gayā.

## \|\| 1.109.6 \|\|

*kurukṣetre viduḥ sthāṇuṃ prabhāse śaśiśekharam \|*  
*puṣkare tu hyajāgandhiṃ viśvaṃ viśveśvare tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They know that it is Sthāṇu in Kurukṣetra; Śaśiśekhara in Prabhāsa; Ajagandhi in Puṣkara, and Viśva in Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.109.7-8 \|\|

*aṭṭahāse mahānādaṃ mahendre ca mahāvratam \|*  
*ujjayinyāṃ mahākālaṃ marukoṭe mahotkaṭam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śaṃkukarṇe mahātejaṃ gokarṇe ca mahābalam \|*  
*rudrakoṭyāṃ mahāyogaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ sthaleśvare \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Mahānāda in Aṭṭahāsa; Mahāvrata in Mahendra; Mahākāla in Ujjayinī; Mahotkaṭa in Marukoṭa; Mahāteja in Śaṅkukarṇa; Mahābala in Gokarṇa; Mahāyoga in Rudrakoṭi and Mahāliṅga in Sthaleśvara.

## \|\| 1.109.9 \|\|

*harṣite ca tathā harṣaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaje \|*  
*kedāre caiva īśānaṃ śarvaṃ madhyamakeśvare \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Harṣa in Harṣita; Vṛṣabha in Vṛṣabhadhvaja; Īśāna in Kedāra; and Śarva in Madhyamakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.109.10 \|\|

*suparṇākṣaṃ sahasrākṣe susūkṣmaṃ kārtikeśvare \|*  
*bhavaṃ vastrāpathe devi hyugraṃ kanakhale tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Suparṇākṣa in Sahasrākṣa; Susūkṣma in Kārttikeśvara; Bhava in Vastrāpatha, O goddess; and Ugra in Kanakhala.

## \|\| 1.109.11 \|\|

*bhadrakarṇe śivaṃ caiva daṇḍake daṇḍinaṃ tathā \|*  
*ūrdhvaretaṃ tridaṇḍāyāṃ caṇḍīśaṃ kṛmijāṃgale \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Śiva in Bhadrakarṇa; Daṇḍin in Daṇḍaka; Ūrdhvareta in Tridaṇḍa; Caṇḍīśa in Kṛmijāṅgala.

## \|\| 1.109.12 \|\|

*kṛttivāsaṃ tathaikāmre chāgaleye kapardinam \|*  
*kāliñjare nīlakaṇṭhaṃ śrīkaṇṭhaṃ maṇḍaleśvare \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Kṛttivāsa in Ekāmra and Kapardin in Chāgaleya. Nīlakaṇṭha in Kāliñjara and Śrīkaṇṭha in Maṇḍaleśvara.

## \|\| 1.109.13 \|\|

*vijayaṃ caiva kāśmīre jayantaṃ marukeśvare \|*  
*hariścandre haraṃ caiva puraścandre ca śaṃkaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vijaya in Kāśmīra; Jayanta in Marukeśvara; Hara in Hariścandra and Śaṅkara in Puraścandra.

## \|\| 1.109.14 \|\|

*jaṭiṃ vāmeśvare vindyātsaumyaṃ vai kukkuṭeśvare \|*  
*bhūteśvaraṃ bhasmagātre oṃkāre'marakaṇṭakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It should be known that Jaṭī is the name in Vāmeśvara and Saumya in Kukkuṭeśvara; Bhūteśvara in Bhasmagātra and Amarakaṇṭaka in Oṃkāra.

## \|\| 1.109.15 \|\|

*tryaṃbakaṃ ca trisaṃdhyāyāṃ virajāyāṃ trilocanam \|*  
*dīptamarkeśvare jñeyaṃ nepāle paśupālakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Tryaṃbaka in Trisandhyā; Trilocana in Virajā; Dīpta should be known as the name in Arkeśvara; and Paśupālaka in Nepāla.

## \|\| 1.109.16 \|\|

*yamaliṃgaṃ ca duṣkarṇe kapālī karavīrake \|*  
*jāgeśvare triśūlī ca śrīśaile tripurāṃtakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Yamaliṅga in Duṣkarṇa; Kapālin in Karavīraka; Triśūlin in Jāgeśvara; and Tripurāntaka in Śrīśaila.

## \|\| 1.109.17 \|\|

*rohaṇaṃ tu ayodhyāyāṃ pātāle hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*kārohaṇe nakulīśaṃ devikāyāmumāpatim \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Rohaṇa in Ayodhyā; and Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla; Nakulīśa in Kārohaṇa; and Umāpati in Devikā.

## \|\| 1.109.18 \|\|

*bhairave bhairavākāramamaraṃ pūrvasāgare \|*  
*saptagodāvare bhīmaṃ svayaṃbhūrnirmaleśvare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Bhairavākāra in Bhairava; Amara in Pūrvasāgara; Bhīma in Saptagodāvara and Svayaṃbhū in Nirmaleśvara;

## \|\| 1.109.19 \|\|

*karṇikāre gaṇādhyakṣaṃ kailāse tu gaṇādhipam \|*  
*gaṃgādvāre himasthānaṃ jala liṃge jalapriyam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Gaṇādhyakṣa in Karṇikāra; Gaṇādhipa in Kailāsa; Himasthāna in Gaṅgādvāra; and Jalapriya in Jalaliṅga.

## \|\| 1.109.20 \|\|

*analaṃ vāḍave'gnau ca bhīmaṃ badarikāśrame \|*  
*śreṣṭhe koṭīśvaraṃ caiva vārāhaṃ vindhyaparvate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Anala in Vāḍava Agni; and Bhīma in Badarikāśrama; Koṭīśvara in Śreṣṭha and Vārāha in Vindhya Parvata.

## \|\| 1.109.21 \|\|

*hemakūṭe virūpākṣaṃ bhūrbhuvaṃ gandhamādane \|*  
*liṃgeśvare ca varadaṃ laṃkāyāṃ ca narāṃtakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Virūpākṣa in Hemakūṭa; Bhūrbhuva in Gandhamādana; Varada in Liṅgeśvara and Narāntaka in Laṅkā.

## \|\| 1.109.22 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiriyaṃ devi tavākhyātā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ vāpi sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thus, O goddess, the sixty-eight of them have been specifically enumerated to you. It is destructive of all the sins in the case of those who read or listen to them.

## \|\| 1.109.23 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kīrtanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kālatraye'pi śucibhirviśeṣācchivadīkṣitaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence, all clever (sensible) persons should assiduously glorify these names three times a day. They should remain pure. Especially those with the initiation in Śaiva doctrines should recite these.

## \|\| 1.109.24 \|\|

*likhitāpi varārohe yasyaiṣā tiṣṭhate gṛhe \|*  
*na tatra jāyate doṣo bhūtapretasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O excellent lady, if these names are kept written in the house, no defect arising from spirits and ghosts can happen in that house.

## \|\| 1.109.25 \|\|

*na vyādherna ca sarpāṇāṃ na caurāṇāṃ varānane \|*  
*nānyeṣāṃ bhūbhujādīnāṃ kadācidapi kutracit \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O lady of excellent countenance, there shall be no fear of ailments, serpents, thieves or others such as kings at any time or any place.

## Chapter 110 - Greatness of Sixty-eight Tīrthas

## \|\| 1.110.1-2 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*naiteṣvapi suraśreṣṭha sarveṣu bhuvi mānavāḥ \|*  
*api dīrghāyuṣo bhūtvā snātuṃ śaktāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*eteṣāmapi sārāṇi mama tīrthāni kīrtaya \|*  
*yeṣu snāto naraḥ samyaksarveṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

1-2. O most excellent one among Suras, men on the earth are not able at all to take their baths in these Tīrthas even if they be long-lived. Hence tell me the most important ones out of these Tīrthas so that a man taking his holy bath in them perfectly can attain the benefit of all of them.

## \|\| 1.110.3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*eteṣāṃ madhyato devi tīrthāṣṭakamanuttamam \|*  
*asti snātairnaraistatra sarveṣāṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3\. O fair lady, among these, eight Tīrthas are the most excellent ones. If people take their bath in them, they will attain the benefit of all.

## \|\| 1.110.4 \|\|

*naimiṣaṃ caiva kedāraṃ puṣkaraṃ kṛmijāṃgalam \|*  
*vārāṇasī kurukṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ hāṭakeśvaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They are: Naimiṣa, Kedāra, Puṣkara, Kṛmi (Kuru?)-Jāṅgala, Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa and Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.110.5 \|\|

*aṣṭāsveteṣu yaḥ snātaḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu satyametanmayoditam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One who takes his holy bath in all these eight perfectly and faithfully gets the benefit of taking the holy bath in all the sixty-eight Tīrthas. The truth has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.110.6 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*kalikāle mahādeva bhaviṣyati kathaṃcana \|*  
*snānaṃ tasmānmama brūhi yatsāraṃ tīrthameva hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

6\. O Mahādeva, holy bath in Kali age will take place with very great difficulty. Hence tell me the most important Tīrtha from among these.

## \|\| 1.110.7 \|\|

*aṣṭānāmapi caiteṣāṃ devadeva trilocana \|*  
*yadyahaṃ vallabhā bhaktā tathā cittānuvartinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Three-eyed Lord of Devas, if I am your favourite, devout beloved behaving in accordance with your mental inclination, mention the most important of all these eight.

## \|\| 1.110.8 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*aṣṭānāmapi deveśi kṣetrāṇāmasti cottamam \|*  
*eteṣāmapi tatkṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

8\. O goddess of Devas, that holy spot named Hāṭakeśvara is the most excellent of all these eight Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.110.9 \|\|

*yatra sarvāṇi kṣetrāṇi saṃsthitāni mamājñayā \|*  
*tathānyāni ca tīrthāni kalikāle'pi saṃsthite \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At my bidding, all the holy places are present here. So also the other Tīrthas even when Kali age has arrived.

## \|\| 1.110.10 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatkṣetraṃ sevyameva hi \|*  
*mānuṣairmokṣamicchadbhiḥ satyametanma yoditam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence, with all efforts that holy spot should be resorted to by men who wish for salvation. The truth has been said by me.

## \|\| 1.110.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātamaṣṭaṣaṣṭisamudbhavam \|*  
*samuccayaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā nāmadevasamanvitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything connected with the sixty-eight Kṣetras along with the names and the deities has been narrated to you.

## \|\| 1.110.12-13 \|\|

*yathā devena cākhyātaṃ pārvatyā guhyamuttamam \|*  
*prasannena mayā kṛtsnaṃ yuṣmākaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yaścaitatpaṭhate bhaktyā hyaṣṭaṣaṣṭisamudbhavam \|*  
*snānajaṃ labhate puṇyaṃ śṛṇvānaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. This is the secret narrated to Pārvatī by the Lord. I have joyously detailed them to you entirely. He who reads this and listens to this with devotion regarding the sixty-eight Kṣetras attains the merit of bath therein.

## Chapter 111 - Lamentation of the King of Ānarta

## \|\| 1.111.1-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śivakṣetrāṇi yairvipraiḥ samānītāni tatra ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ sarvāṇi gotrāṇi vada sūtaja vistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kasya gotrodbhavairvipraiḥ kiṃ kṣetraṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*śaṃkarasya prasādena tasminkāla upasthite \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kiyatyapi ca gotrāṇi camatkārapurottame \|*  
*sthāpitāni subhaktena tenānartena sūtaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tvayā proktaṃ purā dattaṃ puraṃ kṛtvā dvijanmanām \|*  
*na ca teṣāṃ kṛtā saṃkhyā tasmāttāṃ parikīrtaya \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-4. O Sūtaja, mention in detail all the Gotras of those Brāhmaṇas by whom the Śivakṣetras were brought and which holy spot was brought by which Brāhmaṇa of which Gotra, thanks to the favour of Śaṅkara, at the advent of that Kali age. How many Gotras were established in the excellent city of Camatkāra by the highly devout (King as) Ānarta? Earlier, you had mentioned that the city was built and bequeathed to Brāhmaṇas; but you had not mentioned their number. So do tell us now.

## \|\| 1.111.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*upadeśaḥ purā datto dvisaptatimunīśvaraiḥ \|*  
*ānartādhipatiḥ pūrvaṃ kuṣṭharoga prapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhatīrthaṃ samāgatya snānaṃ cakre tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. Advice was imparted earlier by seventy-two leading sages. Formerly, the Lord of Ānarta was afflicted by the disease of leprosy. He hurriedly went to the Śaṅkha Tīrtha and had his holy bath.

## \|\| 1.111.6 \|\|

*tena nāśaṃ gataḥ kuṣṭho bhūpatestasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*tasya tīrthasya māhātmyānnirvi ṇṇasya tanuṃ prati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereby, the leprosy of the king was instantly cured and disappeared, thanks to the greatness of that Tīrtha, though he had been dejected with the condition of his body at first.

## \|\| 1.111.7 \|\|

*tataḥ sa nīrujo bhūtvā toṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*tānuvāca muniśreṣṭhān praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When he was rid of the disease, he became extremely delighted. He bowed down to the excellent sages repeatedly and said:

## \|\| 1.111.8-9 \|\|

*suvarṇaṃ vā gajāśvaṃ vā rājyaṃ sakalameva vā \|*  
*bhavadbhyaḥ saṃpradāsyāmi tasmādabrūta dvijottamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yadyasya rocate yāvanmātramanyadapi dvijāḥ \|*  
*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mahyaṃ dīnasya praṇatasya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. “O excellent Brāhmaṇas tell me what appeals to you and how much thereof. Is it gold? Or an elephant? Or a horse? Or my entire kingdom? Or any other thing? I shall give them unto you. I am in a wretched plight. I am bowing down to you. May I be favoured.”

## \|\| 1.111.10 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*niṣparigrahadharmāṇo vānaprasthā vayaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥprakṣālakāḥ kiṃ no rājyena vibhavena ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

10\. We are Brāhmaṇas of the third stage (Vānaprastha) of life with non-acceptance of gifts as our virtue. We are those who wash off immediately (i.e. who spend money on sacred rites without hoarding it). Of what avail to us are riches and kingdom?

## \|\| 1.111.11 \|\|

*rājovāca \|\|*  
*upakāraṃ samāsādya yaḥ karoti na pāpakṛt \|*  
*upakāraṃ punastasya sa kṛtaghna udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The king said:

11\. One who does not help others in return after being helped by them is a sinner. He is called ungrateful.

## \|\| 1.111.12 \|\|

*brahmaghnaṃ ca surāpe ca caure bhagnava te śaṭhe \|*  
*niṣkṛtirvihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Expiation has been enjoined by learned men for a Brāhmaṇa-slayer, an imbiber of liquor, a thief, a rogue who violates solemn vows etc. But there is no rite of atonement for an ungrateful one.

## \|\| 1.111.13 \|\|

*tasmātkṛtvā prasādaṃ me kiṃcidbrūt dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yenānṛṇyaṃ pragacchāmi yadyapi syātsujīvitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, be pleased with me and tell me something whereby I shall be free from indebtedness and my life will be a good one.

## \|\| 1.111.14 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāga kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|*  
*paraṃ tatra bhaveddoṣo yatra dātā tu saspṛhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

The sages said:

14\. O highly esteemed one, it is indeed true that there is no rite of atonement for the ungrateful. But the defect is only there where the donor is one having some desire.

## \|\| 1.111.15 \|\|

*niḥspṛho yatra rājendra hyupakāraparo bhavet \|*  
*na tatra jāyate doṣaḥ svalpo'pi ca kathaṃcana \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O leading king, if one who has no desire is the person who renders help, there is not the slighest defect.

## \|\| 1.111.16 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha rājyaṃ svaṃ svadharmeṇa prapālaya \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva yena saukhyaṃ prajāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hence, do go and protect your kingdom according to Dharma, whereby there shall be happiness in this world as well as in the other world.

## \|\| 1.111.17 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhūmipo viprairniṣiddhaḥ sa sahasradhā \|*  
*kṛcchreṇa tānpraṇamyoccairjagāma svagṛhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus a thousand times the Brāhmaṇas refused to accept anything from the king. He bowed down to them repeatedly and went to his abode with great difficulty.

## \|\| 1.111.18 \|\|

*tatra gatvā prahṛṣṭā tmākṛtvā ramyaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*gītanṛtyasavādyaiśca rātrijāgaraṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*cakāra pūrvavadrājyaṃ samaṃtāddhatakaṃṭakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With great delight, he installed a fascinating idol of Maheśvara after reaching his place. He performed adoration along with observance of Jāgaraṇa (keeping awake at night) with songs, dances and instrumental music. After duly destroying the enemies, he ruled the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.111.19 \|\|

*ciṃtayāno divānaktaṃ brāhmaṇānprati tatsadā \|*  
*kathaṃ teṣāṃ dvijeṃdrāṇāmupakāro bhaviṣyati \|*  
*madīyo mama yairdattaṃ gātrametatpunarnavam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Day and night, he used to think about those Brāhmaṇas: ‘How can I help in return those Brāhmaṇas who gave me this new, fresh body (free from illness)?’

## \|\| 1.111.20 \|\|

*te'pi sarve muniśreṣṭhāḥ khecaratva samanvitāḥ \|*  
*tapaḥśaktyā yāṃti nānātīrtheṣu bhaktitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. All those excellent sages were endowed with the power of moving through the sky, due to their penance. They used to go to different Tīrthas with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.111.21 \|\|

*teṣu snānaṃ japaṃ kṛtvā tathaiva pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*prāṇayātrāṃ punaścakrustatrāgatya sva āśrame \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They used to perform the rites of holy bath, Japa and Tarpaṇa (libation unto the Pitṛs) in those places and later they came back to their hermitages and continued their earthly sustenance.

## \|\| 1.111.22-24 \|\|

*anye tatraiva kurvaṃti nityakṛtyāni ye dvijāḥ \|*  
*tathānye dūramāsādya tīrthaṃ dṛṣṭvā manoharam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*uṣitvā rajanīṃ tatra dvirātraṃ vā punargṛham \|*  
*samāgacchaṃti cānye tu trirātreṇa samāyayuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vārāṇasyāṃ prayāge vā puṣkare vātha naimiṣe \|*  
*prabhāse vā'tha kedāre hyanyasminnahi vāṃchyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. A few of those Brāhmaṇas carried on their daily rites there itself. Others went to far-off Tīrthas. After visiting those charming places and spending there a night or two they used to return home. A few others returned within three days.

(They visited) Vārāṇasi, Prayāga, Puṣkara, Naimiṣa, Prabhāsa and Kedāra. They never desired to stay in any other holy place.

## \|\| 1.111.25-26 \|\|

*kadācidatha te sarve kārtikyāṃ puṣkaratraye \|*  
*gatā viniścayaṃ kṛtvā snānārthaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*paṃcarātraṃ vasiṣyāmo vayaṃ tatra samāhitāḥ \|*  
*tasmādvahniṣu dāreṣu rakṣā kāryā svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Once all those excellent Brāhmaṇas resolved to take their holy bath in the three Puṣkaras at the time of the Kārttikī festival day. They decided: “We shall stay there for five nights with mental concentration and purity. The protection of our wives shall be done by the sacred fires within our homes.”

## \|\| 1.111.27 \|\|

*evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā gatā yāvaddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tāvaddha patinā jñātā na kaścittatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When those excellent Brāhmaṇas went thus with such a decision, the king came to know that no one stayed behind.

## \|\| 1.111.28-34 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye munīṃdrāṇāṃ sutīrthāśramavāsinām \|*  
*damayaṃtīti vikhyātā caṃdrabiṃbasamānanā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tāmuvāca rahasyevaṃ vraja tvaṃ cāruhāsini \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre mamādeśo'dhunā dhruvam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatra tiṣṭhaṃti yāḥ patnyo munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni vicitrāṇi tāsāṃ yaccha yathecchayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*na tāsāṃ patayo'smākaṃ prakurvaṃti pratigraham \|*  
*kathaṃcidapi suśroṇi lobhyamānāpi bhūriśaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*strīṇāṃ bhūṣaṇajā cintā sadā caivādhikā bhavet \|*  
*laulyaṃ ca kautukaṃ caiva sadā bhūṣaṇajaṃ bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*api mṛnmayakaṃ kiṃcitkāṣṭhasūtramayaṃ ca vā \|*  
*jatukācamayaṃ vāpi nārī dhatte vibhūṣaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*eṣa eva bhavetteṣāmupakārasyasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*upāyaḥ padmapatrākṣi na cānyo'sti kathaṃcana \|\| 34 \|\|*

28-34. The king came to know that no one among those leading sages, the residents of the hermitages in the excellent Tīrtha, stayed behind.

There was a lady with the countenance resembling the disc of the moon. She was well-known as Damayantī (one of his queens evidently). He said to her thus in secret: “O lady of charming smiles, do go now at my bidding to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara. The wives of the sages of purified souls live there. Give them different kinds of ornaments as per their desire (and liking). O lady of excellent hips, though I attempted to tempt them many times, their husbands never accepted presents from us. Women always think much of the ornaments. They always cherish a fancy and temptation for ornaments. Even if an ornament is made of clay, wood, thread, wax or glass a woman eagerly wears it. This alone affords a possibility of helping them. O lady of eyes like the petals of a lotus, there is no other means at all.”

## \|\| 1.111.35 \|\|

*sā tatheti pratijñāya vicitrābharaṇāni ca \|*  
*gṛhītvā harṣasaṃyukā tatastatkṣetramāyayau \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. She said “So be it” and joyously went to that holy place, taking with her different kinds of ornaments.

## \|\| 1.111.36-38 \|\|

*maṇimuktāmayānyeva kuṇḍalāni śubhāni ca \|*  
*tathā candrojjvalāhārānnūpurāṇi bṛhaṃti ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*indranīlamahānīlavaiḍūryakhacitāni ca \|*  
*padmarāgaistathā vajrairmāṇikyaiśca manoramaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*keśaiḥ kaṃkaṇairdivyaiḥ śakracāpanibhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*hemasūtraiśca jātyaiśca mekhalābhistathaiva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. There were splendid earrings made of jewels and pearls; necklaces shining like the moon and big anklets studded with Indranīla and Mahānīla (blue sapphires) and lapis lazuli, rubies, diamonds etc., of great charm. There were bracelets, bangles of divine exquisiteness resembling splendid rainbows. There were gold threads and girdles of excellent quality.

## \|\| 1.111.39 \|\|

*atha sā bodhane viṣṇoḥ saṃprāpte divase śubhe \|*  
*upavāsaparā snātā ekasminsalilāśaye \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On the auspicious day of Viṣṇu’s waking up (i.e. eleventh day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika) she took her holy bath in a tank and observed fast.

## \|\| 1.111.40 \|\|

*tīradeśe niveśyaiva mahābhūṣaṇaparvatam \|*  
*yasya prabhābhirugrābhirvyāptaṃ gaganamaṃḍalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The huge mountain-like heap of the great ornaments was placed on the bank. The lustre of those ornaments illuminated the entire firmament.

## \|\| 1.111.41 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāstāpasyaḥ kautukānvitāḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśā rājapatnī sā kiṃrūpā kiṃvibhūṣaṇā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the meantime wives of the sages came there in their eagerness to know how the queen looked like and what ornaments she wore.

## \|\| 1.111.42 \|\|

*atha tāstāṃ samālokya divyabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām \|*  
*surūpāṃgīṃ samādhisthāṃ citte cintāṃ pracakrire \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. They saw the beautiful queen adorned with divine ornaments engaged in meditation. They thought thus:

## \|\| 1.111.43 \|\|

*dhanyeyaṃ bhūpaterbhāryā yaivaṃ bhūṣaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*damayaṃtī surūpāḍhyā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. ‘This queen is blessed. She is adorned with ornaments thus. She is Damayantī of excellent beauty, marked with all characteristic features.’

## \|\| 1.111.44 \|\|

*samādhyaṃtaṃ samāsādya tāpasīrvīkṣya sā'pi ca \|*  
*damayaṃtī namaścakre tāḥ sarvā vidhipūrvakam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After concluding her meditation, Damayantī looked at the saintly ladies (women-sages) and duly bowed down to them.

## \|\| 1.111.45-46 \|\|

*tāḥ kṛtāṃjalinā prāha valguvākyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*mayāyaṃ bhūṣaṇastoma uddiśya garuḍadhvajam \|*  
*kalpito'dya dine snātvā samupoṣya dine hareḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasmādgṛhṇaṃtu tāpasyo mayā dattāni vāṃchayā \|\| \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni vicitrāṇi prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mama \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. She spoke these charming, sweet words with palms joined in reverence: “On this day of Hari, I have taken the holy bath and observed fast with the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord in view. I have set apart this collection of ornaments.

O saintly ladies, these ornaments of various kinds have been given to you joyously by me. May you be pleased to accept them. Let me be favoured thus.”

## \|\| 1.111.47 \|\|

*tataścaikā'bravīttāsāmeṣā muktāvalī mama \|*  
*imāṃ dehi na me vāṃchā vidyate'nyā nṛpapriye \|\| 47 \|\|*

Then one of those ladies said:

47\. This pearl necklace is mine. Give this to me. O beloved wife of the king, I have no other desire.

## \|\| 1.111.48 \|\|

*tatastayā vihasyoccaiḥ prakṣālya caraṇau svayam \|*  
*dattā muktāvalī tasyā vastrairdivyaiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*yasyāḥ ṣaṇmāṣatulyāni mauktikānyamalāni ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The queen laughed loudly and washed her feet and gave her the pearl necklace along with divine garments. The pure pearls themselves weighed six Māṣas.

## \|\| 1.111.49 \|\|

*śaratkāle yathā vyomni nakṣatrāṇi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tathānyā sparddhayā yuktā yayāce'malavarcasam \|*  
*hāraṃ nirmūlyatāyuktaṃ cittāhlādakaraṃ param \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the pearls shone like stars in autumn.

Another Tāpasī lady urged by rivalry requested for a pure necklace of inestimable value and blameless lustre. It was highly pleasing to the mind.

## \|\| 1.111.50 \|\|

*atha sā taṃ kare kṛtvā tasyā hāraṃ prayacchati \|*  
*tāvadanyā prajagrāha hāraṃ śṛṃgāralālasā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The queen took the necklace in the hand and gave it to her. By that time, another lady eagerly longing for elegant embellishments caught hold of the necklace.

## \|\| 1.111.51 \|\|

*tataḥ śeṣāśca tāpasyo bhūṣaṇārthaṃ samutsukāḥ \|*  
*sasparddhā jagṛhustāni bhūṣaṇāni svayaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, the remaining Tāpasīs too became eager to seize the ornaments. They vied with one another in seizing the ornaments themselves.

## \|\| 1.111.52 \|\|

*anyāścānyākare kṛtvā bhūṣaṇaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*balādākṛṣya jagrāha dharṣayitvā tataḥ param \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. One lady seized the beautiful ornament in the hand of another with force and attacked her.

## \|\| 1.111.53 \|\|

*yathāyathā pragṛhṇaṃti tāpasyo bhūṣaṇārcitāḥ \|*  
*tathātathāsyāḥ saṃjajñe damayaṃtyā mudā hṛdi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. As the Tāpasīs were continuously honoured with ornaments, Damayantī’s joy rose in her heart.

## \|\| 1.111.54 \|\|

*anyāni ca pracikṣepa śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*na tṛptirjāyate tāsāṃ tathāpi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. She threw at them hundreds and thousands of ornaments. Still, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they were not satisfied.

## \|\| 1.111.55-56 \|\|

*bhūṣaṇābhāvamāsādya tataḥ sā pārthivapriyā \|*  
*hṛṣṭā provāca tāḥ sarvāḥ saṃtoṣaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 55 \|\|*

*punaścaivānayiṣyāmi prabhāte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anyāni ca vicitrāṇi yasyā rocaṃti yāni ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. The beloved queen of the king found the ornaments exhausted. She told all of them: “Be satisfied with this much today. I shall undoubtedly bring other ornaments of wonderful features and give them to you as you like.”

## \|\| 1.111.57 \|\|

*tatastāḥ sakalāḥ procurgaccha tvaṃ pārthivapriye \|*  
*āgaṃtavyaṃ ca bhūyo'pi pragṛhyābharaṇāni ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then all of them said: “O beloved wife of the king, do go. Come again taking more ornaments.”

## \|\| 1.111.58 \|\|

*evamuktā tatastābhiḥ praṇipatya nṛpapriyā \|*  
*prahṛṣṭā prayayau tūrṇaṃ svapuraṃ prati saddvijāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On being told thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the beloved wife of the king bowed down to them and joyously went to her city quickly.

## \|\| 1.111.59 \|\|

*tāpasyopi gṛhaṃ gatvā vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni ca gātreṣu sasparddhā nidadhustadā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The Tāpasīs too went to their abodes and vied with one another in openly displaying and wearing the different kinds of clothes and ornaments on their bodies.

## \|\| 1.111.60 \|\|

*tāpasīnāṃ catuṣkaṃ ca parityajya yatavratam \|*  
*śeṣābhiḥ pragṛhītāni maṇḍanāni yathecchayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. With the exception of four Tāpasīs of solemn vows and restraints, all the others accepted these embellishments and ornaments as they pleased.

## \|\| 1.111.61-63 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṇḍale \|*  
*bhūyopi rājapatnī sā bhūṣaṇānyaṃbarāṇi ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tathaiva pradadau tāsāṃ jagṛhuśca tathaiva tāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tasyāḥ prayacchaṃtyā ahanyahani bhaktitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*paṃcarātramatikrāṃtaṃ tṛptāstāstāpasapriyāḥ \|*  
*na rājñī tṛptimāyāti prayacchaṃtī prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. Then the day dawned and the pure disc of the sun rose up. The queen brought further collections of ornaments and garments. She gave them to the Tāpasīs and they accepted them as before. Thus with great devotion she continued to offer the gifts daily for five days. The beloved wives of the sages became satisfied. Making the gifts with sincere devotion, the queen did not rest satisfied.

## \|\| 1.111.64 \|\|

*tataḥ śuśrāva tāpasyaścatasro'tra suniḥspṛhāḥ \|*  
*valkalājinadhāriṇyo na tasyāḥ pārśvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*na cānyā bhūṣitā dṛṣṭvā cakrurīrṣyāṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then she heard that four lady sages (Tāpasīs) still continued to wear bark garments or antelope skins. They were without any desire and they did not come to her (for any sort of present). Nor did they appear to be jealous of the other Tāpasīs who were well-adorned.

## \|\| 1.111.65-66 \|\|

*atha sā tvaritaṃ gatvā tāsāṃ pārśvamaniṃditā \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni mahārhāṇi gṛhītvā paṃcamīdine \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tataḥ provāca tāḥ sarvāḥ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|*  
*imāni bhūṣaṇārthāya bhūṣaṇāni pragṛhyatām \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Thereupon, the queen of blameless qualities took with her very valuable ornaments on the Pañcamī (fifth) day and hurriedly went to them. She said to them all: “May you be pleased. May these ornaments be received for the sake of adorning yourselves.”

## \|\| 1.111.67 \|\|

*tāpasya ūcuḥ \|*  
*nāsmākaṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ kāryaṃ bhūṣitā valkalairvayam \|*  
*tasmādgaccha nijaṃ harmyamarthibhyaḥ saṃpradīyatām \|\| 67 \|\|*

The Tāpasīs said:

67\. We have nothing to do with the ornaments. We consider ourselves well adorned with our own bark garments. You may go back to your own mansion. Let everything be given to those who seek.

## \|\| 1.111.68 \|\|

*vadantīnāṃ tayā sārdhamevaṃ tāsāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*catvāraḥ patayaḥ prāptā ekaikasyāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Even as they were talking to her thus, the excellent Brāhmaṇas, the four husbands, came there.

## \|\| 1.111.69 \|\|

*śunaḥśepo'tha śākreyo bauddho dāntaścaturthakaḥ \|*  
*viyanmārgaṃ hi catvāraḥ svāśramamāyayuḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They were Śunaḥśepa, Śākreya, Bauddha and the fourth one Dānta. All these four came to their hermitage by the aerial path.

## \|\| 1.111.70-71 \|\|

*śeṣāḥ sarve gatibhraṃśaṃ prāpya bhūmārgamāśritāḥ \|*  
*atha te svāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtākārabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*kimidaṃkimidaṃ procuryattāpasyo viḍaṃbitāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*kenaivaṃ pāpmanā'smākamāśramo'yaṃ viḍaṃbitaḥ \|*  
*pradattvā tāpasīnāṃ ca bhūṣaṇānyaṃbarāṇi ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. All the rest (of the sages) lost their capacity to move through the air and had to resort to the paths on the ground.

They found their hermitages were a mockery of their former ones, desecrated due to ornaments.

## \|\| 1.111.72 \|\|

*tatpatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*camatkārasya bhūpasya yaiṣā bhāryā vyavasthitā \|*  
*anayā saṃpradattāni sarvāsāṃ bhūṣaṇāni vai \|\| 72 \|\|*

They said: “What is this? What is this? Our saintly wives have been deceived by the offer of garments and ornaments. Who is that sinner by whom this hermitage of ours has been made a mockery by offering ornaments and garments to the saintly wives?”

Their wives said:

72\. That woman who is the wife of King Camatkāra was present here. Ornaments were given to everyone by her.

## \|\| 1.111.73 \|\|

*asmākamapi saṃprāptā gṛhe vai nṛpavallabhā \|*  
*dātuṃ vibhūṣaṇānyeva niṣiddhā'smābhiradya sā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The beloved queen of the king was here in our houses also in order to give ornaments thus. But that was rejected by us.

## \|\| 1.111.74 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataste kopa mūrcchitāḥ \|*  
*ūcustāṃ nṛpaterbhāryāṃ śāpaṃ dātuṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

Sūta said:

74\. On hearing those words, all of them became extremely angry. By way of giving curses to the King’s wife, they said thus repeatedly:

## \|\| 1.111.75-77 \|\|

*dvisaptatirvayaṃ pāpe snānārthaṃ puṣkare gatāḥ \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ vyomamārgeṇa manomārutaraṃhasā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*catvārasta ime prāptā yeṣāṃ dāraiḥ pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*na kṛtastasya bhūpasya kubhāryāyāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tasmādviḍaṃbito yasmādāśramo'yaṃ tapasvinām \|*  
*śilārūpā ca bhavatī tasmādbhavatu kutsitā \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. “O sinful woman, seventy-two of us went to Puṣkara for taking the holy bath on the Kārttikī day with the speed of mind and wind, by the aerial path.”

Only four have come back, those whose wives did not accept the gifts at all, of the silly woman, the wife of the king.

Since this hermitage of the sages has beeen deceitfully desecrated you shall be transformed into the ugly shape of a rock.”

## \|\| 1.111.78 \|\|

*atha sā tatkṣaṇādeva śilārūpā babhūva ha \|*  
*niśceṣṭā tatkṣaṇādeva munivākyādanaṃtaram \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. At the very instant, she was turned into a rock. Immediately, after the utterance of the sages, she became motionless.

## \|\| 1.111.79 \|\|

*tataḥ sa parivāro'syāstadduḥkhena samākulaḥ \|*  
*vāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇo dīnaḥ prasthitaḥ svapuraṃ prati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thereupon all her attendants became extremely distressed. With their eyes filled with tears in their wretched state, they set off towards their city.

## \|\| 1.111.80 \|\|

*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ damayaṃtyāḥ samudbhavam \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāstasyāḥ śāpasamudbhavam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they told the king the entire report about the curse of Queen Damayantī.

## \|\| 1.111.81 \|\|

*śrutvā sa pārthivastūrṇaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ śāpajaṃ tadā \|*  
*prasādanāya viprāṇāṃ duḥkhitaḥ sa vanaṃ yayau \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. On hearing the details of the curse the king hurriedly went to the forest to pacify the Brāhmaṇas. He was in great distress.

## \|\| 1.111.82-83 \|\|

*tataste munayastūrṇaṃ catvāro'pi mahīpatim \|*  
*jñātvā prasādanārthāya bhāryārthaṃ samupasthitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*agrihotrāṇi dārāṃśca samādāya tataḥ param \|*  
*kurukṣetraṃ samājagmuḥ khamārgeṇa drutaṃ tadā \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. On coming to know that the king had arrived there in order to pacify them in the matter concerning his wife, all those four sages quickly went to Kurukṣetra by the aerial path taking their wives and the Agnihotra requisites with them.

## \|\| 1.111.84 \|\|

*pārthivo'pi samanveṣya yatnāttānsarvato munīn \|*  
*nirviṇṇaḥ śramārtaśca bhāryāvyasanaduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The king assiduously searched for the sages everywhere. He became tired and dejected in addition to his grief at the plight of his wife.

## \|\| 1.111.85 \|\|

*tato jagāma taṃ deśaṃ yatra bhāryā śilāmayī \|*  
*sā sthitā tāpasīvṛndaiḥ sarvato'pi samanvitā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thereafter he went to that place where his queen was present in the form of a rock. She was surrounded by the groups of the Tāpasīs.

## \|\| 1.111.86 \|\|

*atha tāṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā sevakaiḥ sakalairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*hāheti sa muhuḥ procya mūrcchitaḥ prāpatatkṣitau \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. On seeing her in such a state, the king who had been attended upon by all the servants repeatedly uttered “Alas! Alas!” Ultimately, he fell down on the ground and swooned.

## \|\| 1.111.87 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchrātsamāsādya saṃjñāṃ toyasamukṣitaḥ \|*  
*pralāpamakarotpaścātsmṛtvāsmṛtvā priyānguṇān \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Water was sprinkled on him. With very great difficulty he regained consciousness. Later he recollected the various good qualities of his beloved and began to lament.

## \|\| 1.111.88-90 \|\|

*hā priye mṛgaśāvākṣi mama prāṇavināśini \|*  
*māṃ muktvā'dya priyaṃ kāṃtaṃ kva gatāsi śubhānane \|\| 88 \|\|*

*nābhukte mayi bhuktāsi nidrāṃ nā'nidrite gatā \|*  
*na saubhāgyasya garveṇa mamājñā laṃghitā kvacit \|\| 89 \|\|*

*na smarāmi tvayā proktaṃ kadācidvi kṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*rahasyapi viśālākṣi kimu bhojanasaṃsadi \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. “Alas! my beloved with eyes resembling those of a fawn! O lady of splendid countenance, by abandoning me, your dear lover, you have put an end to my very life. Where have you gone?

Hitherto you never took food until I had taken mine. You never went to sleep until I did. You have never transgressed my behests with misplaced haughtiness due to your conjugal felicity.

I don’t remember that any evil utterance was made by you even in private, O lady of large eye. There is no question of your doing so publicly during dinner or in the assembly?”

## \|\| 1.111.91 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ pralapatastasya bhūpateḥ karuṇaṃ bahu \|*  
*āyātā maṃtriṇastasya śrutvā bhūpaṃ tathāvidham \|\| 91 \|\|*

Sūta said:

91\. In the meantime the ministers of the king heard that he was in such a plight. They came to the place where the king was piteously lamenting.

## \|\| 1.111.92 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃbodhya taṃ kṛcchāddṛṣṭāntairvahuvistaraiḥ \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ mahadvyasanasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. They enlightened and consoled him with detailed accounts of ancient saintly kings facing calamities.

## \|\| 1.111.93 \|\|

*ninyustaṃ bhūpatiṃ dīnaṃ vāṣpavyākulalocanam \|*  
*niśvasaṃtaṃ yathānāgaṃ tejasā parivarjitam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. As the king heaved sighs like an elephant (or serpent) bereft of its splendour in an utterly wretched state with tears turning his eyes turbid, they took the king away.

## \|\| 1.111.94 \|\|

*so'pi kṛtvā'layaṃ tasyāḥ samaṃtātsumanoharam \|*  
*karpūrāgarudhūpādyairvastrakuṃkumacandanaiḥ \|*  
*yojayāmāsa tāṃ bhāryāṃ śilārūpāmapi sthitām \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. He created a beautiful shrine for her all round. He embellished his wife in the form of a rock with camphor, agallochum incense, garments, saffron, sandal-paste etc.

## Chapter 112 - The Creation of Barren Land

## \|\| 1.112.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ katipayāhasya gate tasminmahīpatau \|*  
*svagṛhaṃ prati duḥkhārte parivārasamanvite \|\| 1 \|\|*

*padbhyāmeva samāyātā hyaṣṭaṣaṣṭirdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pariśrāṃtāḥ kṛśāṃgāśca dhūlidhūsaritānanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Suta said:
