1-2. After the distressed and dejected king accompanied by his attendants had gone back to his abode, a few days elapsed. Then the sixty-eight excellent Brāhmaṇas reached the place utterly exhausted. They were emaciated in their limbs and had their faces turned greyish with dust. They had to come on foot.

## \|\| 1.112.3 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyati dārāḥ svā divyābharaṇa bhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*divyavastraiḥ susaṃvītā rājapatnya ivāparāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They saw their wives bedecked in divine ornaments and dressed in divine garments as though they were queens.

## \|\| 1.112.4-6 \|\|

*tataśca vismayāviṣṭāḥ papracchuste kṣudhānvitāḥ \|*  
*kimidaṃ kimidaṃ pāpā viruddhaṃ vihitaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kathaṃ prāptāni vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca \|*  
*nūnamasmadgaterbhraṃśaḥ khe jāto nā'nyathā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vikāramenaṃ saṃtyaktvā yuṣmadīyaṃ sugarhitāḥ \|*  
*atha tāḥ sarvavṛttāṃtamūcustāpasayoṣitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. They were very hungry. They asked them in great surprise, “O sinful ladies, what is this? What is this? Your bodies are rendered incongruous (as wives of asceties)?

How did you receive these costly ornaments and garments? Certainly, the loss of our ability of aerial movement could not have been caused by anything else.

O despicable women, excepting this aberration of yours, there can not be any other cause.”

Thereupon the wives of those sages narrated all the events.

## \|\| 1.112.7 \|\|

*yathā rājñī samāyātā damayantī nṛpapriyā \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni ca dattāni tayā caiva yathā dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They told them how Damayantī, the beloved wife and queen of the king, came there. O Brāhmaṇas, they told them how the ornaments were distributed by her.

## \|\| 1.112.8 \|\|

*yathā śāpaśca sañjāto brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*atha te munayaḥ kruddhāstacchrutvā garhitaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*rājapratigraho niṃdyastāpasānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They told them how the noble-souled (four) Brāhmaṇas cursed her.

On hearing those censurable words, the sages became angry. The acceptance of the gift from the king was blameworthy especially to the sages.

## \|\| 1.112.9 \|\|

*tato bhūpasya rāṣṭrasya nāśārthaṃ jagṛhurjalam \|*  
*krodhena mahatāviṣṭā vepamānā nirargalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. With great anger they began to shake uncontrollably. They took up water to destroy the king and his kingdom.

## \|\| 1.112.10 \|\|

*anena pāpmanā'smākaṃ kubhūpena praṇāśitā \|*  
*khe gatirlobhayitvā tu patnyo'smākamakṛtrimāḥ \|*  
*saralāstadgaṇāḥ sarve yenedṛgvyasanaṃ sthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Our aerial movement has been destroyed by this evil king of sinful nature. He has tempted our simple and straight forward wives and brought his ornaments to them and therefore this adverse situation has occurred.”

## \|\| 1.112.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te munayo yāvacchāpaṃ tasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*prayacchaṃti ca tāstāvadūcurbhāryā ruṣānvitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. While those sages were about to curse the king, the wives spoke to them angrily:

## \|\| 1.112.12 \|\|

*na deyo bhūpatestasya śāpo brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*asmadīyaṃ vacastāvacchrotavyamaviśaṃkitaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O excellent Brāhmaṇas, no curse should be uttered against the king. Our words should be listened to unreservedly.

## \|\| 1.112.13 \|\|

*vayaṃ sarvā narendrasya bhāryayā samalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*suvastrairbhūṣaṇairdivyaiḥ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All of us were adorned by the wife of the leading king by means of excellent garments and divine ornaments with her mind sanctified with faith.

## \|\| 1.112.14 \|\|

*vayaṃ daridradoṣeṇa sadā yuṣmadgṛhe sthitāḥ \|*  
*karśitā na ca saṃprāptaṃ sukhaṃ martyasamu dbhavam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All along we have been staying in your houses along with the defect of poverty. We are emaciated and feeble. We never had any pleasure possible in human life.

## \|\| 1.112.15 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ paraloko'tra vidyate ye taporatāḥ \|*  
*na ca martyaphalaṃ kiṃcidapi svalpataraṃ bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To those who are engaged in penance there exists only the other world. They will not have even the slightest of human pleasure and benefit.

## \|\| 1.112.16 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ viṣayasthānāmiha lokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*bhogaprasaktacittānāṃ nīcānāṃ sudurātmanām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This world has been proclaimed for those others who are engrossed in worldly pleasures. They are base and wicked with their minds solely attached to the pleasures here.

## \|\| 1.112.17 \|\|

*gṛhasthāśramiṇāṃ caiva svadharmaratacetasām \|*  
*iha lokaḥ paraścaiva jāyate nā'tra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the case of those householders with the minds turned towards their duties this world as well as the other world are both assured. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.112.18 \|\|

*tā vayaṃ nātra sandeho gṛhasthāśramamuttamam \|*  
*saṃsevya sādhayiṣyāmo lokadvayamanuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. We shall undoubtedly resort to the excellent stage of the householders and thereby achieve the best of both the worlds.

## \|\| 1.112.19-20 \|\|

*tasmādgṛhāṇi ramyāṇi pravadaṃti samāhitāḥ \|*  
*bhūpālādbhūmimādāya vṛttiṃ caivābhivāṃchitām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tataścaivātha vīkṣadhvaṃ putrapautrasamudbhavam \|*  
*saukhyaṃ cāpi kumārīṇāṃ bāṃdhavānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. That is why persons with cogent reasoning say that the household (i.e. householder’s stage) is very beautiful.

As for you, do accept the gift of the plots of land from the king as well as all desired means of sustenance. Then look after your sons and grandsons and their welfare. See to the happiness of your daughters and kinsmen in particular.

## \|\| 1.112.21 \|\|

*na kariṣyatha cedvākyametadasmadudīritam \|*  
*sarvāḥ prāṇaparityāgaṃ kariṣyāmo na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If you are not inclined to do as we have suggested, we shall all give up our lives unhesitatingly.

## \|\| 1.112.22 \|\|

*yūyaṃ strīvadhapāpena yuktāḥ santastataḥ param \|*  
*narakaṃ rauravaṃ durgaṃ gamiṣyatha suniścitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Afflicted by the sin of murdering your wives you will fall into the grave hell of Raurva certainly.”

## \|\| 1.112.23 \|\|

*evaṃ te munayaḥ śrutvā tāsāṃ vākyāni tāni vai \|*  
*bhūpṛṣṭhe tatyajustoyaṃ śāpārthaṃ yatkarairdhṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On hearing their words, the sages let fall the water they had held in their hands for the purpose of cursing the king.

## \|\| 1.112.24 \|\|

*tatastattoyanirdagdhaṃ tadvibhāgaṃ kṣitestadā \|*  
*ūṣaratvamanuprāptamadyāpi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that portion of the ground became burnt by that water. It became an arid land. It is visible even today.

## \|\| 1.112.25 \|\|

*āstāmannādikaṃ tatra yadutpaṃ na prarohati \|*  
*na janma cāpnuyādbhūyaḥ pakṣī vā kīṭa eva vā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Seeds sown there do not grow at all. Further, a bird or worm that dies there is not reborn.

## \|\| 1.112.26-27 \|\|

*tṛṇaṃ vātha mṛgastatra kiṃ punarbhaktimānnaraḥ \|*  
*yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ śraddhayā phālgune naraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*paurṇamāsyāṃ ravairvāre sa pitṝnuddharennijān \|*  
*api svakarmaṇā prāptānnarake dāruṇākṛtau \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Not even grass nor an animal survives there. All the more so in the case of a devout man! One who faithfully performs a Śrāddha in the month of Phālguna on the Full-Moon day and on a Sunday will redeem his Pitṛs even if they had fallen into a terrible Naraka due to their own action.

## Chapter 113 - Greatness of Agnikuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.113.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve gatakopā dadhurmatim \|*  
*yajñakarmasu gārhasthye putrapautrasamudbhave \|\| 1 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare rājā sa tānprāptāndvijottamān \|*  
*śrutvā bhakti samāyuktaḥ praṇāmārthamupāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śrutvā kopagatāṃ vārtāmupaśāmakṛtāṃ tathā \|*  
*gārhasthyāpratipannānāṃ vākyairbhāryāsamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Then all those Brāhmaṇas shed their anger and directed their minds to the sacrificial rites and householder’s duties pertaining to sons and grandsons.

In the meantime, the king heard that the Brāhmaṇas had returned. On hearing it, he went to them for the purpose of making obeisance to them with devotion.

He also heard that they were angry at first but later became calmed down on hearing the words of their wives. Further they had accepted the life of householders as well.

## \|\| 1.113.4 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya tānsarvānsāṣṭāṃgaṃ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ provāca vinataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He prostrated before them with eight parts of the body touching the ground. The king then stood humbly with palms joined in reverence and said:

## \|\| 1.113.5 \|\|

*yuṣmadīyaprasādena saṃprāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam \|*  
*mayā rogavināśena tasmādbrūta karomi kim \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “Thanks to the favour of you all, my ailments perished and I have attained the fruit of life. Tell me what I should do.”

## \|\| 1.113.6 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā tava rājeṃdra vayaṃ sarvatra vāsinaḥ \|*  
*nītāḥ kṛtārthatāṃ dattvā ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

6\. By giving different kinds of jewels, O leading king, all of us, the residents of this place, have been rendered happy by your wife.

## \|\| 1.113.7 \|\|

*tasmātpuravaraṃ kṛtvā kṣetre'traiva suśobhane \|*  
*asmākaṃ dehi gārhasthyaṃ yena samyakprajāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence build an excellent city here itself, in this splendid holy place and grant us the wherewithals of domestic life, whereby everything can become perfect.

## \|\| 1.113.8 \|\|

*yajāmo vividhairyajñaiḥ sadā saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*imaṃ lokaṃ paraṃ caiva sādhayāmaḥ sadāsthitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. We shall perform various kinds of Yajñas always with full complement of monetary gifts. Stationed here always, we shall achieve the benefits of this world as well as those of the other one.

## \|\| 1.113.9 \|\|

*tacchrutvā pārthivo hṛṣṭastathetyuktvā tataḥ param \|*  
*anukūladine prāpte śilpānāhūya bhūriśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing it, the king became delighted. He said, “So be it.” On an auspicious day, he summoned many craftsmen.

## \|\| 1.113.10 \|\|

*puraṃ prakalpayāmāsa bahuprākārasaṃkulam \|*  
*prākāraparikhāyuktaṃ gopuraiḥ samalaṃkṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He got a very great city built. It had many ramparts. There was a moat all round and ornamental gateways embellished it.

## \|\| 1.113.11 \|\|

*athāṣṭaṣaṣṭiviprāṇāṃ tatra madhye nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭigṛhāṇyeva cakāra subṛhaṃti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The excellent king built sixty-eight big mansions in the middle for the sake of the sixty-eight Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.113.12 \|\|

*mattavāraṇajuṣṭāni dīrghikāsahitāni ca \|*  
*gṛhodyānaiḥ sametāni yathā rājagṛhāṇi ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There were many ponds and parks all round as in the case of royal palaces. The houses had turrets and upper apartments.

## \|\| 1.113.13 \|\|

*tathā kṛtvā'tha ratnaughaiḥ pūrayitvā tathā paraiḥ \|*  
*dadau tebhyo aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṃ ca grāmāṇāṃ tadanaṃtaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After building them, he filled them with heaps of jewels and other things. Then he gifted them sixty-eight villages.

## \|\| 1.113.14 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvānsamāhūya putrapautrāṃstadagrataḥ \|*  
*provāca tāranādena śrūyatāṃ jalpato mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He called all of them and their sons and grandsons. In a loud voice he proclaimed thus before them:

## \|\| 1.113.15-19 \|\|

*etatpuraṃ mayā dattamebhirgrāmaiḥ samanvitam \|*  
*etebhyo brāhmaṇeṃdrebhyaḥ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tasmādrakṣā prakartavyā yathā na syātkṣatiḥ kvacit \|*  
*kaṣṭaṃ vā brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ tathā caiva parābhavam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*asmadvaṃśasamudbhūto yastvetāṃstoṣayiṣyati \|*  
*anyo vā bhūpatirvṛddhimagryāṃ nūnaṃ sa yāsyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yaścāparādhasaṃyuktānetānkhedaṃ nayiṣyati \|*  
*yojayiṣyati vā kleśairvividhairvā parābhavaiḥ \|*  
*sa śatrubhiḥ parābhūto veṣṭito vividhairgadaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*iha loke viyogādīnprāpya kleśānsudāruṇān \|*  
*rauravādiṣu raudreṣu narakeṣu prayāsyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. ‘'What I say may be listened to: This city has been given to these Brāhmaṇas with a mind sanctified by faith.

Hence protection should be accorded to them so that no loss, no pain, no discomfiture is caused to these leading Brāhmaṇas.

If anyone born of our race or any other king propitiates these, he will certainly attain the highest prosperity.

One who subjects them to criminal offence, leads them to distress, makes them suffer on various ways or adds to their discomfiture will be overwhelmed by enemies or oppressed by various kinds of ailments.

In this world, he will meet with terrible sufferings like bereavements and then will fall into horrible hells beginning with Raurava.”

## \|\| 1.113.20 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sarvaṃ teṣāṃ kṛtyaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*svayamevākaronnityaṃ divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying thus, the king engaged himself day and night untiringly in carrying out their tasks himself.

## \|\| 1.113.21 \|\|

*atha tā brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ bhāryāḥ sarvāḥ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*damayaṃtyāḥ samāsādya prāsādaṃ snehavatsalāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all the wives of the leading Brāhmaṇas lovingly went to the palace (shrine) of Damayantī.

## \|\| 1.113.22 \|\|

*kuṃkumāgarukarpūraiḥ puṣpairgaṃdhaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*tadarccā pūjayāmāsuḥ sa ca rājā dinedine \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They adored her image with saffron, agallochum and camphor as well as various kinds of flowers and scents everyday. The king also did likewise.

## \|\| 1.113.23 \|\|

*atha tāḥ procuranyonyaṃ tāpasyastatpuraḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*tasyabhūpasya saṃtoṣaṃ janayaṃtyo dvijottamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Standing before the image and creating great delight in the mind of the king, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, those Tāpasīs spoke to one another:

## \|\| 1.113.24-26 \|\|

*yadāsmākaṃ gṛhe vṛddhiḥ kadācitsaṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*tadagrataśca paścācca damayaṃtyāḥ prapūjanam \|*  
*kariṣyāmo na saṃdehaḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*enāṃ dṛṣṭvā kumārī yā vedimadhyaṃ gamiṣyati \|*  
*sā bhaviṣyatyasaṃdehaḥ patyuḥ prāṇasamā sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kanyāyajña upasthite \|*  
*damayaṃtī pradraṣṭavyā pūjanīyā prayatnataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. “Whenever there is an auspicious occasion in our house for the celebration of any prosperous event we shall adore Damayantī both before and after such an event. There is no doubt about it. In fact we shall do so always in the case of all holy rites.

A bride who sees her and then enters the marriage-pavilion shall undoubtedly be very dear to her husband like his very life breath.

Hence, when the Yajña-like sacred ceremony of a marriage is about to be performed, Damayantī should be visited and worshipped assiduously.”

## \|\| 1.113.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tatra pure tena bhūbhujā sumahātmanā \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṃ ca saṃsthāpya gotrāṇāṃ nirvṛtiḥ kṛtā \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. Thus, in that city the sixty-eight Gotras (of Brāhmaṇas) were established and rendered delighted by that noble-souled king.

## \|\| 1.113.28 \|\|

*teṣāmapi ca catvāri gotrāṇyura gajādbhayāt \|*  
*gatāni tatra yatra syustāni pūrvodbhavāni ca \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ sthitā tatra pure śeṣā dvijanmanām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Of them four Gotras went away due to the fear of serpents to that place where the previous races were present so that only sixty-four Gotras of the Brāhmaṇas remained in the city.

## \|\| 1.113.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kīdṛṅanāgabhayaṃ teṣāṃ yena te vigatā vibho \|*  
*parityajya nijaṃ sthānametanno vistarādvada \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:

29\. O holy Sir, of what nature was that fear from serpents whereby they had to go away forsaking their own original position? Describe this to us in detail.

## \|\| 1.113.30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ānarttādhipatiḥ pūrvamāsīnnāmnā prabhaṃjanaḥ \|*  
*dharmajñaḥ supratāpī ca parapakṣakṣayāvahaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sūta said:

30\. There was, formerly, a king of Ānarta named Prabhañjana. He was conversant with Dharma and sacred rites. He was valorous and capable of destroying hosts of his enemies.

## \|\| 1.113.31 \|\|

*tatastasya suto jajñe prāpte vayasi paścime \|*  
*aniṣṭasthānasaṃstheṣu graheṣu dvija sattamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a son was born to him when he was very advanced in age. At that time the planets were in unfavourable positions.

## \|\| 1.113.32 \|\|

*tatastena samāhūya daivajñāñchāstrapaṃḍitān \|*  
*teṣāṃ niveditaṃ sarvaṃ kālaṃ tasya samudbhavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He called together astrologers fully conversant with the scriptures and told them the time of the son’s birth.

## \|\| 1.113.33 \|\|

*daivajñā ūcuḥ \|*  
*eṣa te pṛthivīpāla jātaḥ putraḥ sugarhita \|*  
*kāle 'niṣṭaprade raudre gaṃḍāṃta tritayodbhave \|\| 33 \|\|*

The Daivajñas said:

33\. O king, this son of yours is born during an unfavourable and censurable hour. It is a terrible period when there are three Gaṇḍāntas (inauspicious positions of planets).

## \|\| 1.113.34 \|\|

*kathaṃcidapi yadyeṣa jīvayiṣyati pārthiva \|*  
*pitṛmātṛpurārthe ca deśānutsādayiṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If somehow this boy survives, O king, he will destroy the country and the assets of the city of his parents.

## \|\| 1.113.35 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*asti kaścidupāyo'tra daivo vā mānuṣo'pi vā \|*  
*yena saṃjāyate kṣemaṃ putrasya viṣayasya ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

The king said:

35\. Is there any remedy here, divine or human, whereby there shall be all-round welfare of the son as well as the kingdom?

## \|\| 1.113.36 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yathā samutthitaṃ yaṃtraṃ yaṃtreṇa pratihanyate \|*  
*yathā bāṇaprahārāṇāṃ kavacaṃ vāraṇaṃ bhaveta \|*  
*tathā grahavikārāṇāṃ śāṃtirbhavati vāraṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

36\. Just as a mechanical device coming up is checked by another mechanical device, just as armour acts as a protection from the attack of arrows, so also the Śānti rite (pacificatory rite conducive to peace and prosperity) can be a check against the evil effects of the planets.

## \|\| 1.113.37-38 \|\|

*tasmānnityamanudvignaḥ śāṃtikaṃ kuru bhūpate \|*  
*yena sarve grahāḥ saumyā jāyaṃte ca śubhāvahāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aniṣṭasthānasaṃstheṣu graheṣu viṣameṣu ca \|*  
*tataḥ sa satvaṃ gatvā camatkārapuraṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38a. Hence, O king, give up your dejection and perform Śānti (pacificatory) rites always. Thereby all the planets will become mild and auspicious. This is the remedy when planets become malefic and they are stationed in unfavourable houses.

38b. Thereupon, the king hurried to the city of Camatkāra.

## \|\| 1.113.39-42 \|\|

*tatra viprānsamāveśya sarvānprovāca sādaram \|*  
*vayaṃ yuṣmatprasādena rājyaṃ kurmaḥ sadaiva hi \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ye 'tītā ye bhaviṣyaṃti vaṃśe 'smākaṃ nṛpottamāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃto 'tra gatisteṣāṃ sasyānāṃ nīrado yathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yadatra matsuto jāto duṣṭasthānasthitairgrahaiḥ \|*  
*daivajñaiḥ śāṃtikaṃ proktaṃ tasyāniṣṭasya śāṃtidam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasmātkuruta vipreṃdrā yathoktaṃ śāṃtikaṃ mama \|*  
*na putraśca rāṣṭraṃ ca vibhavaśca vivardhate \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. There he summoned together the Brāhmaṇas and said to them respectfully: “It is with your favour that we always rule the kingdom. Just as rain-bearing cloud is the basis and support unto the crops so you are the redeemer to all the excellent kings who were born in our family and who are yet to be born.

My son was born when the planets were stationed in evil houses. Śāntika rites for (their) pacification have been recommended by Daivajñas.

Hence, O leading Brāhmaṇas perform the Śāntika rites as enjoined in the scriptures so that my son, kingdom and the royal prosperity may prosper.”

## \|\| 1.113.43-45 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ procuḥ saṃmaṃtryā'tha parasparam \|*  
*kṣemāya tava bhūnātha kariṣyāmo'tra śāṃtikam \|\| \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sadeva niyatāḥ saṃtaḥ śāṃtāḥ ṣoḍaśa te dvijāḥ \|*  
*upahārāḥ sadā preṣyāstvayā bhaktyā mahīpate \|*  
*māsāṃte cābhiṣekaśca grāhyo rudraghaṭodbhavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*evaṃ prakurvatastubhyaṃ putro vṛddhiṃ prayāsyati \|*  
*tathā rāṣṭraṃ ca kośaśca yaccānyadapi kiṃcana \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Then those Brāhmaṇas consulted one another and said: “O King, we shall perform Śānti rites for your welfare. Sixteen of us, good, quiescent Brāhmaṇas of great restraint, shall perform them always. O king; presents should always be sent by you with great devotion. At the end of every month, the Abhiṣeka (water for ablution) should be received from the Rudraghatas (waterpots pertaining to the deity Rudra). If you continue to do thus your son will prosper, so also the kingdom, the treasury and everything else.”

## \|\| 1.113.46 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya tānhṛṣṭo gatvā nijaniveśanam \|*  
*utsavaṃ putrajanmotthaṃ cakre taiḥ preritaḥ sadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then he bowed down to them and happily went to his abode. Urged by them he always celebrated the festival of the birth of his son.

## \|\| 1.113.47 \|\|

*saṃbhārānpreṣayāmāsa camatkārapure tataḥ \|*  
*māsāṃte cābhiṣekaśca grāhyo vai vidhipūrvakam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then he sent all the requisite things to the city of Camatkāra. At the end of every month, he duly received the water for ablution.

## \|\| 1.113.48 \|\|

*te'pi brāhmaṇaśārdūlāścātuścaraṇasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*krameṇa śāṃtikaṃ cakrurbrahmacaryaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Those tiger-like Brāhmaṇas too strictly adhered to the practice of celibacy and performed the Śāntika rites in due order in groups (or units) of four.

## \|\| 1.113.49 \|\|

*māsaṃ māsaṃ prati sadā śāṃtā dāṃtā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*tato māsā vasāne'nye cakrustacchāṃtikaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Every month they did thus quiescently and with the sense-organs fully under control. At the end of the month another set of Brāhmaṇas performed the Śāntika rites.

## \|\| 1.113.50 \|\|

*so'pi rājā'tha māsāṃte samāgatya subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*abhiṣekaṃ samādāya pūjayitvā dvijottamān \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The king came there at the end of every month with great devotion, honoured the excellent Brāhmaṇas and accepted the Abhiṣeka water.

## \|\| 1.113.51 \|\|

*vāsobhirmukuṭaiścaiva gobhūdānena kevalam \|*  
*saṃtarpyānyāṃstathā viprānsvasthānaṃ yāti bhūmipaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He then used to propitiate them with garments, coronets and gifts of cows and plots of land. Similarly, the king propitiated the other Brāhmaṇas also and went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.113.52 \|\|

*evaṃ pravartamāne ca śāṃtike tatra bhūpateḥ \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālaḥ kṣemārogyadhanāgamaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. As these Śānti rites continued to be performed on behalf of the king, a great deal of time elapsed according welfare, health and wealth.

## \|\| 1.113.53 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya māsādāvapi bhūpateḥ \|*  
*prārabdhe śāṃtike tasminmahāvyādhirajāyata \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After some time, once at the beginning itself of a month, when the Śāntika rites were to be begun, a major disease afflicted the king.

## \|\| 1.113.54 \|\|

*tatputrasya viśeṣeṇa tathaivāṃtaḥpurasya ca \|*  
*rāṣṭrasya ca samagrasya vāhanānāṃ tathā kṣayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. There was decline in health of his son in particular, of his women, of the entire kingdom and the vehicles.

## \|\| 1.113.55 \|\|

*sa tataḥ preṣayāmāsa śāṃtyarthaṃ tatra satpure \|*  
*susaṃbhārānviśeṣeṇa dakṣiṇāśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereupon the king sent extra requisites for the Śānti rites to the city and also special monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.113.56 \|\|

*yathāyathā dvijāstatra homaṃ kurvaṃti pāvake \|*  
*tathā sarve viśeṣeṇa rogā vardhaṃti sarvaśaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As the Brāhmaṇas went on performing the rite of Homa in the fire, all types of diseases particularly went on spreading everywhere.

## \|\| 1.113.57 \|\|

*mriyante vājinastasya bṛhanto vāraṇāstathā \|*  
*śatravaḥ sarvakāṣṭhāsu vigrahārthamupasthitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Horses began to die. So also elephants. Enemies appeared from all the quarters for waging war.

## \|\| 1.113.58 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vyākulībhūto rogagrasto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ prāpya sarvānviprānuvāca ha \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The king himself fell ill. In great excitement, he hastened to the city of Camatkārapura and said to all the Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.113.59-60 \|\|

*yuṣmābhiḥ svāmibhiḥ saṃsthairāpado'bhibhavaṃti mām \|*  
*tatkimetanmahābhāgāḥ kṣīyante mama saṃpadaḥ \|*  
*rogāścaiva vivardhaṃte śatrusaṃghaiḥ samanvitāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasmādviśeṣato homaḥ kāryo rogapraśāṃtaye \|*  
*dānāni ca viśiṣṭāni pradāsyāmi dvijanmanām \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. “O highly esteemed ones, even as you all remain in charge of these rites adversities assail me. Why? Why do my assets dwindle? The ailments increase along with groups of enemies. Hence some special Homa may be performed for suppressing the ailments. I shall make special gifts unto the Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 1.113.61 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve pratyakṣaṃ tasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*cakruḥ samāhitā bhūtvā śāṃtikaṃ taddhitāya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then all those Brāhmaṇas performed the Śāntika rites with great mental concentration for the welfare and in the very presence of the king.

## \|\| 1.113.62 \|\|

*yathāyathā prayuñjīranhomāṃte susamā hitāḥ \|*  
*tathātathāsya bhūpasya vṛddhiṃ rogaḥ pragacchati \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. As at the conclusion of the Homas the ascetic Brāhmaṇas pronounced (blessings) with great concentration, the ailment of the king became all the more serious.

## \|\| 1.113.63 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kruddhāste sarve dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*grahānuddiśya sūryādīñchāpāya kṛtaniścayāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. In the meantime, all those excellent Brāhmaṇas became greatly enraged. They decided to curse the Planets including the Sun.

## \|\| 1.113.64 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*pūjitā api sadbhaktyā vidhānena tathā grahāḥ \|*  
*pīḍayaṃti puraṃ rājñaḥ saputrapaśubāṃdhavam \|\| 64 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

64\. Although they have been worshipped with very good devotion and also in accordance with the injunctions, these Planets harass the city of the king along with his sons, kinsmen and wealth of cattle!

## \|\| 1.113.65 \|\|

*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā śucībhūya samāhitāḥ \|*  
*yāvadyacchaṃti tacchāpaṃ grahebhyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thus they decided. They remained pure with mental concentration. They were about to curse the Planets in their fit of anger.

## \|\| 1.113.66-71 \|\|

*tāvadvahniruvācedaṃ mūrto bhūtvā dvijottamān \|*  
*mā prayacchata vipreṃdrāḥ śāpaṃ kopātkathaṃcana \|\| 66 \|\|*

*grahebhyo doṣamuktebhyaḥ śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama \|*  
*māsimāsi prakurvaṃti homaṃ te ṣoḍaśa dvijāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ madhyasthitaścaikastrijāto brāhmaṇādhamaḥ \|*  
*tena taddūṣitaṃ dravyaṃ samagraṃ homasaṃbhavam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*mayā dattaṃ na gṛhṇaṃti te grahā bhāskarādayaḥ \|*  
*tena kurvaṃti bhūpasya pīḍāmapyadhikāmimām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tasmādenaṃ parityajya homaṃ kuruta mā ciram \|*  
*yena prītiṃ parāṃ yāṃti grahāḥ sarve'rkapūrvakāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ārogyaśca bhavedrājā gataśatruḥ sutānvitaḥ \|*  
*satataṃ sukhamabhyeti macchāṃtikaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

66-71. By then the Fire-god assumed a personal form and spoke to the excellent Brāhmaṇas: “O leading Brāhmaṇas, do not curse at any cost. Do not curse the Planets that are free from blemish. May my words be listened to. Sixteen Brāhmaṇas perform Homa every month. In their midst there is one Trijāta. All the articles pertaining to the Homa have been defiled by him. The Planets including the Sun do not accept what is offered by me. Therefore, they cause greater harassment to the king. Hence exclude him and begin the Homa without delay so that all the Planets including the Sun will have the greatest happiness. The king will become free from ailment along with his son. His enemies will go away. Thanks to the power of my Śāntika rites, he will attain perpetual happiness.”

## \|\| 1.113.72 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavānvahniścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*te'pi viprā viṣaṇṇāsyā lajjayā parayā vṛtāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After saying thus, Lord Vahni disappeared. Those Brāhmaṇas became dejected in appearance indicating how deeply they felt the sense of shame.

## \|\| 1.113.73-74 \|\|

*tatastaṃ pāvakaṃ bhūyaḥ stuvaṃtastatra ca sthitāḥ \|*  
*procurvaiśvānaraṃ brūhi trijāto yo'tra ca dvijaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yena taṃ saṃparityajya kurmaḥ karma praśāṃtaye \|*  
*niḥśeṣameva doṣāṇāṃ bhūpasyāsya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Thereupon they stayed on there and eulogized Pāvaka (Fire-god) again. They spoke to Vaiśvānara: “Tell us who is the Trijāta Brāhmaṇa here?

Thereat we can exclude him completely and resume our rite for the purpose of peace and suppression of the defects of the noble-souled king.”

## \|\| 1.113.75 \|\|

*vahniruvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ doṣaṃ dvijedrāṇāṃ jānannapi kathaṃcana \|*  
*bravīmi brāhmaṇā vandyā mama sarve dharātale \|\| 75 \|\|*

Vahni said:

75\. I will never speak out the defect of the leading Brāhmaṇas even though I know. All the Brāhmaṇas on the earth are worthy of my veneration.

## \|\| 1.113.76 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vahne nāsmākaṃ kīrtayiṣyasi \|*  
*tatte śāpaṃ pradāsyāmastasmācchīghraṃ vadasva naḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

76\. O Vahni (Fire-god), if you do not proclaim to us who that Brāhmaṇa is, we will curse you. Hence hurry up and tell us.

## \|\| 1.113.77-79 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vahnirbhayasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃ viciṃtayāmāsa kurve'taḥ kiṃ śubhāvaham \|\| 77 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ dūṣayiṣyāmi yadi tāvacca pātakam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdehaḥ śāpaścāpi tadudbhavaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kīrtayiṣyāmi vā naiva vidyamānaṃ dvijottamam \|*  
*śapiṣyati na saṃdehaḥ kruddhā āśīviṣopamāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

Sūta said:

77-79. On hearing their words, Vahni became afraid and thought thus for a long time: 'What is the best thing I should do here? If I reveal the defect of the Brāhmaṇa, I shall incur that much of sin undoubtedly. There will also be a curse coming from him. If I don’t proclaim the truth about the excellent Brāhmaṇa, these Brāhmaṇas comparable to serpents (in fury) will undoubtedly curse me.’

## \|\| 1.113.80 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya gātre svedo'bhavanmahān \|*  
*yena tatpūritaṃ kuṇḍaṃ homārthaṃ yatprakalpitam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Even as he pondered thus, there was profuse perspiration on his physical form and that holy Kuṇḍa which was specially prepared for the purpose of Homa was filled with it (sweat).

## \|\| 1.113.81 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānviprānkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vepamāno bhayatrastaḥkuṇḍānniṣkramya pāvakaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then the Fire-god came out of the Kuṇḍa. He was trembling with fear. He stood there with palms joined in reverence and said to the Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.113.82-84 \|\|

*nāhaṃ svajihvayā doṣaṃ brāhmaṇasya samudbhavam \|*  
*kathañcitkīrtayiṣyāmi tasmācchṛṇvantu bho dvijāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*atra sveda jale viprā ye sthitāḥ ṣoḍaśa dvijāḥ \|*  
*te snānamadya kurvaṃtu praviśuddhyarthamātmanaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ madhyago yaśca trijātaḥ sa bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasya visphoṭakairyuktaṃ snātasyāṃgaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

82-84. “O Brāhmaṇas, I will never utter the defects of a Brāhmaṇa by means of my own tongue at any cost. Hence listen: All the sixteen Brāhmaṇas who are present here should take their bath in the pit of sweat drops for the sake of purifying themselves. When the person who is Trijāta takes his bath his body will have tumours and boils.”

## \|\| 1.113.85 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve kramāttatra nimajjanam \|*  
*cakruḥ śuddhiṃ gatāścāpi muktvaikaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tadā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then all those took their bath there in due order. All except one Brāhmaṇa attained purity.

## \|\| 1.113.86 \|\|

*hāhākārastato jajñe mahāṃstatra janodbhavaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā visphoṭakairyuktamakasmāttaṃ dvijottamam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. On seeing that excellent Brāhmaṇa with tumours and boils all of a sudden, there was a great hue and cry among the people there.

\`

## \|\| 1.113.87 \|\|

*so'pi lajjānvito vipraḥ kṛtvā'dho vadanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*niṣkrāṃto'tha sabhāmadhyātsthānādviprasamudbhavāt \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. That Brahmaṇa became filled with shame. With the face hanging down he went out of the assembly of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.113.88 \|\|

*vahniruvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sādhitaṃ kṛtyaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tasmādyāsye nijaṃ sthānaṃ bhavadbhiḥ pāramāpitaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

Vahni said:

88\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, your (unprecedented) task has been accomplished by me. So I shall go to my abode with your permission.

## \|\| 1.113.89 \|\|

*na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syādapi svapre dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsamprārthyatāṃ kiṃcidabhīṣṭaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. But, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, viewing me even in a dream shall not go in vain. Hence the desire cherished in the heart may be requested for.

## \|\| 1.113.90 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*etattava jalaṃ vahne svedajaṃ sarvadaiva tu \|*  
*sthiraṃ bhavatu cātraiva viśuddhyarthaṃ dvijanmanām \|\| 90 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

90\. O Vahni, may this water reservoir of your sweat drops be permanent here for the sake of the purification of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.113.91 \|\|

*anyajāto naro yo'tra prakaroti nimajjanam \|*  
*tasya cihnaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ visphoṭakasamudbhavam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. If a person born of illegal father takes his plunge here, you must mark his body with tumours and boils.

## \|\| 1.113.92 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa procyā gatoṃ'tardhānameva hi \|*  
*pāvakaste dvijāḥ sarve maṃtraṃ cakruḥ parasparam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Saying “So it shall be" Pāvaka vanished from there and all the Brāhmaṇas held consultation together.

## \|\| 1.113.93 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ samudbhavam \|*  
*śuddhiratra prakartavyā pitṛmātṛsamuddbhavā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. From today onwards the test of purity of all the Brāhmaṇas in regard to their fathers and mothers shall be conducted here.

## \|\| 1.113.94 \|\|

*camatkārapurottho yaḥ kaścidvipraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*so'tra snāto viśuddhaśca vijñeyaḥ kulaputrakaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. A Brāhmaṇa said to be hailing from Camatkārapura should take his bath here. On being found pure, he will be considered a noble son.

## \|\| 1.113.95 \|\|

*tasmai kanyā pradātavyā sa śrāddhārho bhaviṣyati \|\|*  
*dharmakṛtyeṣu sarveṣu yojanīyaḥ sa eva hi \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. A virgin should be given to him alone. He should be one deserving invitation to a Śrāddha rite. Only he should be entertained in all sacred rites.

## \|\| 1.113.96 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu gotreṣu militeṣu yathākramam \|*  
*tatpratyakṣaṃ viśuddho yaḥ sa śuddhaḥ paṃktipāvanaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. All the members of the sixty-eight Gotras should gather together. He who proves to be pure in their presence should be regarded as deserving a place in the row of Brāhmaṇas for meals.

## \|\| 1.113.97-98 \|\|

*apavādāśca ye kecidbrahmahatyādikāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*anye'pi durjanaiḥ proktā dharmasandehakārakāḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*te sarve'tra viśuddhāḥ syurvijñeyāḥ kulaputrakāḥ \|*  
*apavādāstathā cānye nāśaṃ yāsyaṃti cākhilāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. If any scandalous rumour spreads, if there is any suspicion as to the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter or if there is any accusation from evil-minded persons casting aspersions on virtue—all these should be tested here and the purity established. All the calumny shall automatically drop down.

## \|\| 1.113.99 \|\|

*yāvannātra kṛtaṃ snānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ ca dvijanmanām \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ tāvadevā'tra na sa vipro bhavetsphuṭam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. No one shall be clearly pronounced as a Brāhmaṇa until this bath is taken in the presence of all the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.113.100 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā camatkārapurodbhavāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ śāṃtikaṃ cakrurhitārthaṃ tasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

Sūta said:

100\. Thus all the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura performed the Śāntika rites for the welfare of the king.

## \|\| 1.113.101 \|\|

*tasminkuṇḍe tataḥ snānaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvairmahātmabhiḥ \|*  
*bhayatrastairviśuddhyarthaṃ śeṣairapi mahātmabhiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then bath was taken by all the remaining noble-souled Brāhmaṇas also for the sake of purity, though at the outset they were afraid (naturally).

## \|\| 1.113.102-103 \|\|

*tato nīrogatāṃ prāptaḥ sa bhūpastatkṣaṇādvijāḥ \|*  
*yastatra kurute snānamadyāpi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*kārtikyāṃ paradārotthaiḥ sa vimucyeta pātakaiḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ yugatraye śuddhirāsīttatra dvijanmanām \|\| 103 \|\|*

102a. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, the king became rid of all his ailments instantly.

102b-103a. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, even today one who takes his bath there on the Kārttikī day becomes rid of the sins of having intercourse with other men’s wives.

103b. In three yugas the Brāhmaṇas had purity.

## \|\| 1.113.104 \|\|

*kulaśīlavihīnānāmanyeṣāmapi pāpmanām \|*  
*matvā kaliyugaṃ ghoraṃ paradārasuraṃjitam \|*  
*tatra śuddhistataḥ sarvaiḥ kṛtā vipraiśca vācikā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Of other sinners, even though they were devoid of nobility of birth and behaviour, in view of Kaliyuga as highly terrible with carnal connection with other men’s wives in abundance the purity was proclaimed by Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.113.105 \|\|

*purato devadevasya brahmaṇo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*pitṛmātṛjavaṃśasya viśuddhyarthamataṃdritaiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The declaration was made in front of Brahmā, the Lord of Devas, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in order to proclaim the purity of the families of the fathers and the mothers. They were scrupulous in regard to this.

## \|\| 1.113.106 \|\|

*adyāpi kurute tatra yaḥ snānaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*trijāto dahyate tatra vahninā sa na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Even today, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if a Trijāta takes his bath there he is scorched by fire undoubtedly.

## Chapter 114 - The Term ‘Nāgara’

## \|\| 1.114.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*so'pi vipro dvijaśreṣṭhā visphoṭakapariplutaḥ \|*  
*lajjayā parayā yukto gatvā kiṃcidvanāṃtaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato vairāgyamāpanno raudre tapasi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā gṛhādikaṃ sarvaṃ snehaṃ dārasutodbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*niyamaiḥ saṃyamaiścaiva śoṣayannātmanastanum \|*  
*kiṃcijjalāśrayaṃ gatvā sthāpayitvā maheśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Brāhmaṇa who had boils all over the body was utterly ashamed. He went to a dense forest with utter disgust and engaged himself in a severe penance. He had renounced his house etc., and all affection for his wife and sons.

With all controls and restraints he dried up his body. He went near a water reservoir (a lake or a pond) and installed Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.114.4 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tuṣṭastasya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*provāca darśanaṃ gatvā prārthayasva yathepsitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After a long time, Maheśvara was pleased with him. Appearing before him he said: “Request for anything you like.”

## \|\| 1.114.5 \|\|

*trijāta uvāca \|*  
*mātṛdoṣādahaṃ deva vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*madhye brāhmaṇamukhyānāmānarttādhipatestathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

Trijāta said:

5\. On account of the default of my mother, O Lord, I have become extremely embarrassed in the midst of the chiefs of Brāhmaṇas and the king of Anarta.

## \|\| 1.114.6 \|\|

*ahaṃ śaknomi no vaktuṃ kasyaciddarśituṃ vibho \|*  
*trijāto'smīti vijñāya bhūrividyānvito'pi ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Though I am endowed with great learning, O Lord, I am unable to show my face to any one after knowing that I am ‘thrice-born.’

## \|\| 1.114.7 \|\|

*tasmātsarvottamasteṣāmahaṃ caiva dvijanmanām \|*  
*yathā bhavāmi deveśa tathā nītirvidhīyatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Lord of Devas, do something so as to enable me to become the best of all those Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.114.8 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*camatkārapure viprā ye vasaṃti dvijottama \|*  
*teṣāṃ sarvottamo nūnaṃ matprasādādbhaviṣyasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

8\. Certainly you will become the best of all the Brāhmaṇas who stay in Camatkārapura, with my favour, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.114.9 \|\|

*tasmātkālaṃ pratīkṣasva kañcittvaṃ brāhmaṇottama \|*  
*samaye samanuprāpte tvāṃ ca neṣyāmi tatra vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, wait for some time. When the proper time arrives ī shall take you there.

## \|\| 1.114.10 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇo'pi tapastepe tathā saṃpūjayanharam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After saying thus, the Lord of Devas vanished from there. The Brāhmaṇa continued his penance, worshipping Hara.

## \|\| 1.114.11 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya matkārapure dvijāḥ \|*  
*maudgalyānvayasaṃbhūto devarāto'bhavaddvijaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Brāhmaṇas, once thereafter a Brāhmaṇa named Devarāta was born of the family of Maudgalya in Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.114.12 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ krathonāma yauvanoddhatavigrahaḥ \|*  
*sadā garvasamāyuktaḥ pauruṣe ca vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. His son named Kratha was very haughty when he was in the prime of youth. He was very manly but was always very proud.

## \|\| 1.114.13 \|\|

*sa kadācidyayau vipro nāgatīrthaṃ prati dvijāḥ \|*  
*śrāvaṇasyāsite pakṣe paṃcamyāṃ paryaṭanvane \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Once, on the fifth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Śrāvaṇa that Brāhmaṇa went to Nāgatīrtha, O Brāhmaṇas, and was roaming in the forest.

## \|\| 1.114.14 \|\|

*athāpaśyatsa nāgendratanayaṃ bhūrivarccasam \|*  
*rudramālamiti khyātaṃ jananyā saha saṃgatam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He saw the highly refulgent son of the leading serpent. He was well-known as Rudramāla. He was accompanied by his mother.

## \|\| 1.114.15 \|\|

*athā'sau taṃ samālokya sulaghuṃ sarpa putrakam \|*  
*jalasarpamiti jñātvā laguḍena vyapothayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The serpent child was very small. On seeing it he thought it was a water-snake and thrashed it with a stick.

## \|\| 1.114.16 \|\|

*hanyamānena tenātha pramuktaḥ sumahānsvanaḥ \|*  
*hā mātastāta tāteti vipanno'smi nirāgasaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On being hit by him he shouted very loudly: “Alas mother! Alas father! I am blameless yet I am in trouble.”

## \|\| 1.114.17 \|\|

*so'pi śrutvā'tha taṃ śabdaṃ brāhmaṇo mānuṣodbhavam \|*  
*sarpasya bhayasaṃtrastaḥ satvaraṃ svagṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing a human voice from a serpent, the Brāhmaṇa became afraid and went home hurriedly.

## \|\| 1.114.18 \|\|

*atha sā jananī tasya niṣkrāṃtā salilāśrayāt \|*  
*yāvatpaśyati tīrasthaṃ tāvatputraṃ nipātitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Its mother came out of the water reservoir and saw her son felled down on the bank.

## \|\| 1.114.19 \|\|

*tato mūrcchāmanuprāptā dṛṣṭvā putraṃ tathāvidham \|*  
*yaṣṭiprahāranirbhinnaṃ sarvāṃgarudhirokṣitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On seeing the son in such a plight with blood splashed all over his limbs shattered on being struck by a stick, she fell into a swoon.

## \|\| 1.114.20 \|\|

*atha labdhvā punaḥ saṃjñāṃ pralāpānakarodbahūn \|*  
*karuṇaṃ śokasaṃtaptā vāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After regaining consciousness, she began to lament piteously in various ways. Her eyes were filled with tears and she was tormented in the height of her grief.

## \|\| 1.114.21-27 \|\|

*hāhā putra parityaktvā māṃ ca kvāsi vinirgataḥ \|*  
*anāvṛttikaraṃ sthānaṃ kiṃ sneho nāsti te mayi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kena tvaṃ nihataḥ putra pāpena ca durātmanā \|*  
*niṣpāpo'pi ca putra tvaṃ kasya kruddho'dyavai yamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sapurasya sarāṣṭrasya sakuṭuṃbasya durmateḥ \|*  
*yena tvaṃ nihato'dyāpi paṃcamyāṃ pūjito na ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rajasā krīḍayitvā'dya samāgatya cirādatha \|*  
*kāmenotsaṃgamāgatya glāniṃ naiṣyati cāṃbaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gadgadāni manojñāni janahāsyakarāṇi ca \|*  
*tvayā vinā'dya vākyāni ko vadiṣyati me puraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*piturutsaṃgamāśritya kūrcākarṣaṇapūrvakam \|*  
*kaḥ kariṣyati putrā'dya satoṣaṃ bhavatā vinā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*niṣiddho'si mayā vatsa tvamāyāto'nupṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*martyalokamimaṃ tāta bahudoṣasamākulam \|\| 27 \|\|*

21-27. “Alas! My son, where have you gone forsaking me? why have you gone to a place from where there is no return? Don't you have any affection for me?

By which sinful and wicked-minded one have you been killed? Though you are sinless, you have been slain. With whom is Yama angry today?

On this fifth lunar day, you have been killed and not adored and honoured. Hence, Yama shall be angry with that wicked-minded one along with his city, family and land of birth.

Today my clothes will not become soiled as before when you used to come back to me after playing in dust for a long time and sit on my lap as you pleased.

Excepting you who will be lisping faltering but delightful words that make people laugh, in front of me?

You being not present, O my son, who will accept the lap of your father and cause merriment by pulling your father’s beard?

You were forbidden, O dear one, yet you closely followed me to this mortal world which is full of many defects!"

## \|\| 1.114.28 \|\|

*evaṃ vilapya nāgī sā saṃkruddhā śokakarṣitā \|*  
*taṃ mṛtaṃ sutamādāya jagāmānaṃtasaṃnidhau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After lamenting thus that Nāga woman who had been angry as well as pained with grief took the dead son and went to the presence of Ananta.

## \|\| 1.114.29 \|\|

*tatastadagrataḥ kṣiptvā taṃ mṛtaṃ nijabālakam \|*  
*pralāpānakaroddīnā viyuktā kurarī yathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then she placed her dead child in front of him and began to lament like the female osprey wretched in her separation.

## \|\| 1.114.30 \|\|

*nāgarājo'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā svaputraṃ vinipātitam \|*  
*jagāma so'pi mūrcchāṃ ca putraśokena pīḍitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even the king of serpents fell into a swoon on seeing the son thrown down. He was afflicted by the grief for his son.

## \|\| 1.114.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sikto jalaiḥ śītaiḥ saṃjñāṃ labdhvā sa kṛcchrataḥ \|*  
*pralāpānkṛpaṇāṃścakre prākṛtaḥ puruṣo yathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On being sprinkled with cool water, he regained consciousness with great difficulty. Like an ordinary man, he began piteous lamentations,

## \|\| 1.114.32 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare nāgāḥ sarve tatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*rurudurduḥkhitāḥ saṃto bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the meantime, all serpents assembled there. They cried miserably with the eyes bedimmed with tears.

## \|\| 1.114.33-35 \|\|

*vāsukiḥ padmajaḥ śaṃkhastakṣakaśca mahāviṣaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍaḥ sacūḍaśca puṃḍarīkaśca dāruṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*añjano vāmanaścaiva kumudaśca tathā paraḥ \|*  
*kambalāśvatarau nāgau nāgaḥ karkoṭakastathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*puṣpadaṃtaḥ sudaṃtaśca mūṣako mūṣakādanaḥ \|*  
*elāpatraḥ supatraśca dīrghāsyaḥ puṣpavāhanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. The following Nāgas were present there: Vāsuki, Padmaja, Śaṅkha, the highly poisonous Takṣaka, Śaṅkhacūḍa with the diadem on the head, the terrible Puṇḍarīka, Añjana, Vāmana, the great Kumuda, Kaṃbala, Aśvatara, the serpent Karkoṭaka, Puṣpadanta, Mūṣaka the devourer of mice, Elāpatra, Supatra, Dīrghāsya and Puṣpavāhana.

## \|\| 1.114.36 \|\|

*ete cānye tathā nāgāstatrā'yātāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*putraśokābhisataptaṃ jñātvā taṃ pannagādhipam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On coming to know that the king of serpents was struck with grief for the son, these and thousands of other serpents came there.

## \|\| 1.114.37 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃbodhya te sarve tamīśaṃ pavanāśanam \|*  
*pūrvavṛttaiḥ kathodbhedairdṛṣṭāṃtairvividhairapi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Quoting earlier incidents and different kinds of similar instances, they consoled their Lord, the chief serpent.

## \|\| 1.114.38 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbodhitastaistu cirātpannagasattamaḥ \|*  
*agnidāhyaṃ tataścakre tasya putrasya duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The excellent serpent in his misery got consoled after a long time. Then he performed the cremation rites for his son.

## \|\| 1.114.39 \|\|

*jaladānasya kāle ca sarpānsarvānuvāca saḥ \|*  
*sarvānnāgānpradānārthaṃ toyasya samupasthitān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When, at the time of offering water libation, all the serpents had assembled for the offering of libation, he spoke to them:

## \|\| 1.114.40-41 \|\|

*nāhaṃ toyaṃ pradāsyāmi svaputrasya kathaṃcana \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ prerito'pyevaṃ tathānyairapi bāṃdhavaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yāvattasya na duṣṭasya mama putrāṃtakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sadāraputrabhṛtyasya vihito na parikṣayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. “Unless and until the utter annihilation of that wicked

slayer of my son is brought about along with his wife, servants and sons, I will not at any cost offer the libation to my son, though urged by you all as well as other kinsmen.”

## \|\| 1.114.42 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ śeṣaḥ śodhayāmāsa taṃ dvijam \|*  
*yena saṃsūditaḥ putro daṃḍakāṣṭhena pāpmanā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After saying this Śeṣa formally proclaimed his retaliation against the sinful Brāhmaṇa who killed his son with a heavy wooden stick.

## \|\| 1.114.43-45 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānnāgānpārśvasthānpannagādhipaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yāṃtu me suhṛduttamāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*putraghnaṃ taṃ nihatyā'śu sakuṭumbaparigraham \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ sarvaṃ bhakṣaṇīyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatraiva vasatiḥ kāryā samastaiḥ pannagottamaiḥ \|*  
*yathā bhūyo vasennaiva tathā kāryaṃ ca tatpuram \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45 Then the Lord of serpents spoke to all those serpents who were near: “O my excellent friends, all of you, do go to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara.

After quickly killing the slayer of my son along with his attendants and members of the family the entire city of Camatkāra should be devoured by you all.

All the excellent serpents should put up their residence there. Manage in such a manner as to make the resettlement of that city impossible.”

## \|\| 1.114.46 \|\|

*evamuktāstatastena nāgāḥ prādhānyataḥ śrutāḥ \|*  
*gatvātha satvaraṃ tatra prathamaṃ taṃ dvijottamam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On being told thus by him, those of the serpents renowned as the most important ones hurriedly went to that excellent Brāhmaṇa at the outset.

## \|\| 1.114.47 \|\|

*devarātasutaṃ suptaṃ bhakṣayitvā tataḥ param \|*  
*tatkuṭuṃbaṃ samagraṃ ca krodhena mahatānvitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After eating the sleeping son of Devarāta they ate the entire family with great fury.

## \|\| 1.114.48 \|\|

*tato'nyānapi saṃkruddhā bālānvṛddhānkumārakān \|*  
*bhakṣayāmāsuḥ sarve te tiryagyonigatā api \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. All of them devoured furiously the others also, children, old people and youth and even the creatures and brutes there.

## \|\| 1.114.49 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jātaḥ pure tatra sudāruṇaḥ \|*  
*ākraṃdo brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ sarpabhakṣaṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In the meantime, a terribly loud lamentation of the leading Brāhmaṇas rose up there on account of the devouring spree of the serpents.

## \|\| 1.114.50 \|\|

*tatra bhūmau tathā'nyacca yatkiṃcidapi dṛśyate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ pannagairvyāptaṃ raudraiḥ kṛṣṇavapurdharaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Whatever else was seen on the ground was covered by the terrible serpents of dark-coloured bodies.

## \|\| 1.114.51 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ kecinmṛtyuvaśaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*viṣasaṃ ghūrṇitāḥ kecitpatitā dharaṇītale \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In the meantime, some who came there were subjected to death. Some who were trembling with the effects of poison fell on the ground.

## \|\| 1.114.52 \|\|

*anye gṛhādikaṃ sarvaṃ parityajya sutādi ca \|*  
*vitrastāḥ paridhāvaṃti vanamuddiśya dūrataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. A few others abandoned their children, houses and other things. Greatly afraid they ran far and wide towards the forest.

## \|\| 1.114.53 \|\|

*anye maṃtravido viprāḥ prayataṃte samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*maṃdaṃ dhāvaṃti saṃtrastā gṛhītvauṣadhayaḥ pare \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Other Brāhmaṇas conversant with the Mantras endeavoured (to cure the people) all round. Others accepting the medicinal herbs ran about in great fear.

## \|\| 1.114.54 \|\|

*evaṃ tatpuramuddiśya sarve te pannagottamāḥ \|*  
*pracaraṃti yathā kaścinna tatra brāhmaṇo vaset \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus all the excellent serpents continued to proceed towards the city so that no Brāhmaṇa stayed behind there.

## \|\| 1.114.55 \|\|

*atha śūnyaṃ puraṃ kṛtvā sarve te pannagottamāḥ \|*  
*vyacaransvecchayā tatra tīrtheṣvāyataneṣu ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then all those excellent serpents rendered that city desolate and freely roamed about in the Tīrthas and the shrines.

## \|\| 1.114.56 \|\|

*na kaścitpannagaḥ kṣetrāttyaktvā niryāti bāhyataḥ \|*  
*praviśenna paraḥ kaścittatra kṣetre ca mānavaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. No serpent left the holy spot and went out. No other man dared to enter the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.114.57 \|\|

*vyavasthaivaṃ samudbhūtā sarpāṇāṃ mānuṣaiḥ saha \|*  
*vadhabhakṣaṇajā nyonyaṃ bāhyābhyaṃtarasaṃbhavā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus as a result of murder and devouring a kind of adjustment between the serpents and the human beings occurred based on the exterior and interior (of the holy spot).

## \|\| 1.114.58 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śeṣo muktvā duḥkhaṃ sutodbhavam \|*  
*prahṛṣṭaḥ pradadau toyaṃ tasya jātibhiranvitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In the meantime, Śeṣa set aside his grief for the son. In great delight, he offered the water libations along with the others of his class.

## \|\| 1.114.59-60 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇāḥ kecitsarpebhyo bhayavihvalāḥ \|*  
*saśokā diṅmukhānyāśu te sarve saṃgatā mithaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tato vanaṃ samājagmustrijāto yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*haralabdhavaro hṛṣṭaḥ sumahattapasi sthitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Some of those Brāhmaṇas who were grief-stricken and terribly afraid of the serpents collected together from all the quarters and came to that forest where Trijāta was present. He had been delightfully performing a great penance and had received boons from Hara.

## \|\| 1.114.61-62 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā tāñjanānsarvāṃstathā duḥkhapariplutān \|*  
*putradārādikaṃ smṛtvā rudataḥ karuṇaṃ bahu \|\| 61 \|\|*

*so'pi duḥkhasamāyukto dṛṣṭvā tānsvapurodbhavān \|*  
*brāhmaṇeṃdrāṃstataḥ prāha bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. On seeing all those people overwhelmed with grief on remembering their sons, wives etc., and crying piteously in various ways, he too became agitated. On seeing the persons, the leading Brāhmaṇas hailing from his own city, he also became miserable. He spoke to them with eyes turned turbid with tears:

## \|\| 1.114.63-65 \|\|

*śṛṇvaṃtu brāhmaṇāḥ sarve vacanaṃ mama sāṃpratam \|*  
*mayā vinirgatenaiva tatpurāttoṣito haraḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tena mahyaṃ varo datto vāṃchito dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*gṛhīto na mayādyāpi prārthayiṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yathā syātsaṃkṣayasteṣāṃ nāgānāṃ sudurātmanām \|*  
*yaiḥ kṛtaṃ naḥ puraṃ kṛtsnamudrasaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65 “May all the Brāhmaṇas hear my statement now. As soon as I came out of that city, Hara was propitiated by me.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I have been granted the boon of accepting anything desired by me. Till today I have not accepted it. I shall now request for it.

I shall request for a boon whereby all the wicked-souled serpents will be destroyed. Those Nāgas of sinful activities have well nigh made our city utterly desolate.”

## \|\| 1.114.66 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha vipraḥ sa trijātaḥ parameśvaram \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa me deva taṃ varaṃ yaccha sāṃpratam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After saying thus, the Brāhmaṇa Trijāta requested Parameśvara: “O Lord grant me that boon now.”

## \|\| 1.114.67 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca deveśaḥ prārthayasva drutaṃ dvija \|*  
*yenābhīṣṭaṃ prayacchāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then the Lord of Devas said: “O Brāhmaṇa request for it; even if what is desired by you is very rare I shall grant it.”

## \|\| 1.114.68-69 \|\|

*trijāta uvāca \|*  
*nāgairasmatpuraṃ kṛtsnaṃ kṛtaṃ janavivarjitam \|*  
*tattasmātte kṣayaṃ yāṃtu sarve vṛṣabhavāhana \|\| 68 \|\|*

*yena tatpūryate viprairbhūyo'pi surasattama \|*  
*mamāpi jāyate kīrtiḥ svasthānoddharaṇodbhavā \|\| 69 \|\|*

Trijāta said:

68-69. O Bull-vehicled One, the entire city of ours has become bereft of people due to the Nāgas. Hence, let them all be destroyed.

Thereby, O most excellent one among Suras, the city can once again be filled with Brāhmaṇas. I too can have the credit of having redeemed my own native land.”

## \|\| 1.114.70 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*nāyuktaṃ vihitaṃ vipra pannagaistairmahātmabhiḥ \|*  
*nirdoṣaścāpi putro'tra yeṣāṃ vipreṇa sūditaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

70\. O Brāhmaṇa nothing improper has been committed by those noble-souled serpents whose son free from any defect or crime, was killed by the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.114.71 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa dvijaśreṣṭha saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|*  
*tatrā'pi śrāvaṇe māsi pūjyaṃte yatra pannagāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the murder was committed on the fifth lunar day in particular and that in the month of Śrāvaṇa when serpents are honoured.

## \|\| 1.114.72 \|\|

*tasmātte'haṃ pravakṣyāmi siddhamaṃtramanuttamam \|*  
*yasyoccāraṇamātreṇa sarppāṇāṃ naśyate viṣam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Hence I shall tell you an excellent Siddha-Mantra at the mere utterance of which the poison of serpents is destroyed.

## \|\| 1.114.73 \|\|

*taṃ maṃtraṃ tatra gatvā tvaṃ tadviprairakhilairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*śrāvayasva mahābhāga tāraśabdena sarvaśaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. After going there accompanied by all those Brāhmaṇas, O highly esteemed one, do utter that Mantra in a loud voice that can be heard everywhere.

## \|\| 1.114.74 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā ye na yāsyaṃti pātālaṃ pannagādhamāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmadvākyādbhaviṣyaṃti nirviṣāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. If the base serpents do not go to Pātāla after hearing it, they shall undoubtedly become poisonless at your instance.

## \|\| 1.114.75 \|\|

*trijāta uvāca \|*  
*brūhi taṃ me mahāmaṃtraṃ sarvatīkṣṇavināśanam \|*  
*yena gatvā nijaṃ sthānaṃ sarpānutsādayāmyaham \|\| 75 \|\|*

Trijāta said:

75\. O Śarva, tell me that great Mantra that destroys poison, so that I can go to my native land and eliminate the serpents.

## \|\| 1.114.76-77 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*garaṃ viṣamiti proktaṃ na tatrāsti ca sāṃpratam \|*  
*matprasādāttvayā hyetaduccāryaṃ brāhmaṇottama \|\| 76 \|\|*

*na garaṃ na garaṃ caitacchrutvā ye pannagādhamāḥ \|*  
*tatra sthāsyaṃti te vadhyā bhaviṣyaṃti yathāsukham \|\| 77 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

76-77. Gara means poison. That is not present there now. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, you utter “Nagaram, Nagaram” and you will have my favour. Nagaram Na-garam (there is no poison there is no poison). Nagaram is the Mantra. On hearing this if the base serpents still remain there they will be worthy of being killed easily.

## \|\| 1.114.78 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti tatsthānaṃ nagarākhyaṃ dharātale \|*  
*bhaviṣyati suvikhyātaṃ tava kīrtivivardhanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. From now onwards that spot shall be well-known all over the earth by the name “Nagara” and it will increase your reputation.

## \|\| 1.114.79-80 \|\|

*tathānyopi ca yo vipro nāgaraḥ śuddhavaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*nagarākhyena maṃtreṇa abhimaṃtrya tridhā jalam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*prāṇinaṃ kāla saṃdaṣṭamapi mṛtyuvaśaṃgatam \|*  
*prakariṣyati jīvāḍhyaṃ prakṣipya vadane svayam \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. If any other Brāhmaṇa of pure race hailing from Nagara and called Nāgara repeats the Mantra named ‘Nagara’ and charges water thrice with it and pours that water into the mouth of any creature bitten by a black serpent and killed thereby, he can be restored to life.

## \|\| 1.114.81 \|\|

*anyatrāpi sthito martyo maṃtrametaṃ trirakṣaram \|*  
*yaḥ smariṣyati saṃsupto na hiṃsyaḥ syādaherhi saḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. A man staying elsewhere and remembering this three-syllabled Mantra (na-ga-ra) at the time of going to sleep cannot be harmed by a serpent.

## \|\| 1.114.82 \|\|

*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ vā garaṃ hi tat \|*  
*tadanena ca maṃtreṇa saṃspṛṣṭaṃ tvamṛtāyitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. If the poison comes from an immobile thing, or a mobile one or if it is artificial it becomes nectar-like when touched after uttering this Mantra.

## \|\| 1.114.83 \|\|

*ajīrṇaprabhavā rogā ye cānye jaṭharodbhavāḥ \|*  
*maṃtrasyāsya prabhāvena sarve yāṃti drutaṃ kṣayam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Other stomach ailments caused by indigestion are entirely eradicated by the power of this Mantra.

## \|\| 1.114.84 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha taṃ vipraṃ bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ paścādyathā dīpo vitailakaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. After saying thus to that Brāhmaṇa the Bull-emblemed Lord went out of sight like a lamp without oil.

## \|\| 1.114.85 \|\|

*trijāto'pi samaṃ viprairhataśeṣaistu tairdrutam \|*  
*jagāma saṃprahṛṣṭātmā camatkārapuraṃ prati \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Along with the other Brāhmaṇas who survived the murderous attack Trijāta quickly and joyously went to the city of Camatkāra.

## \|\| 1.114.86 \|\|

*evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve trijātena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*na garaṃ na garaṃ proccairuccaraṃtaḥ samāyayuḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Thus all those Brāhmaṇas accompanied by Trijāta arrived there uttering loudly “Nagaram Nagaram”.

## \|\| 1.114.87 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ yattadvyāptaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*raudrairāśīviṣaiḥ krūraiḥ śeṣasyādeśamāśriteḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. They came to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara which was pervaded all round by the ruthless and terrible serpents obeying the command of Śeṣa.

## \|\| 1.114.88 \|\|

*atha te pannagāḥ śrutvā siddhamaṃtra śivodbhavam \|*  
*nirviṣāstejasā hīnāḥ samantātte pradudravuḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. On hearing the Siddha Mantra given by Siva the serpents were deprived of their poison. Bereft of their vigour, they ran all round.

## \|\| 1.114.89 \|\|

*valmīkānkecidāsādya citraraṃdhrāṃtarodbhavān \|*  
*anye cāpi prajagmuśca pātālaṃ daṃdaśūkakāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Some of the serpents took shelter in the anthills with diverse kinds of holes and others went to Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.114.90-91 \|\|

*ye kecidbhayasaṃtrastā vārddhakyena nipīḍitāḥ \|*  
*vālatvena tathā cānye śaknuvaṃti na sarpitum \|\| 90 \|\|*

*te sarve brāhmaṇendraistaiḥ kṛtasya pratikārakaiḥ \|*  
*nihatāḥ pannagāstatra daṃḍakāṣṭhaiḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

90-91. Thousands of those serpents who were extremely terrified, who could not even crawl, who were overwhelmed by old age or who were in their infancy were struck with heavy sticks by the Brāhmaṇas who wanted to take revenge.

## \|\| 1.114.92 \|\|

*evamutsādya tānsarvānbrāhmaṇāste gatavyathāḥ \|*  
*taṃ trijātaṃ puraskṛtya sthānakṛtyāni cakrire \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. After exterminating all of them, the Brāhmaṇas were rid of their anguish. With that Trijāta at their head they performed the essential things for the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.114.93 \|\|

*evaṃ tannagaraṃ jātamasmātkālādanaṃtaram \|*  
*devadevasya bhargasya prasādena dvijottamāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, with the favour of Bharga, the Lord of Devas, (the name of) that place became known as ‘Nagara’ thereafter.

## \|\| 1.114.94 \|\|

*etadyaḥ paṭhate nityamākhyānaṃ nagarodbhavam \|*  
*na tasya sarpajaṃ kvāpi kathaṃcijjāyate bhayam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. If one reads this narrative concerning the ‘Nagara’ always (everyday) he will never have any fear from serpents anywhere.

## Chapter 115 - Gotras of Sages

## \|\| 1.115.1-2 \|\|

*trijāto brāhmaṇastatra kinnāmā kasya sambhavaḥ \|*  
*kiṃgotraścaiva kiṃsaṃjñaḥ kīrtayasva mahāmate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kiṃ kulīnairguṇāḍhyairvā tejovidyāvicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*trijāto'pi varaṃ so'pi svaṃ sthānaṃ yena coddhṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O highly intelligent one, do proclaim to us the name of that Brāhmaṇa Trijāta. Whose son was he? What is his Gotra? What is his appellation? How is he, though a Trijāta, greater than those people of noble birth, having good qualities and radiant due to their brilliance and learning? It was by him that his land of nativity was lifted up (rehabilitated).

## \|\| 1.115.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| sāṃkṛtyasya munervaṃśe sa saṃbhūto dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*prabhāva iti vikhyāto dattasaṃjño nimeḥ sutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. That excellent Brāhmaṇa was born of the race of Sage Sāṅkṛtya. He was well known as Prabhāva. His appellation was Datta and he was son of Nimi.

## \|\| 1.115.4 \|\|

*sa evaṃ sthānamuddhṛtya cakārāyatanaṃ śubham \|*  
*trijāteśvaranāmnā ca devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After redeeming the native place he built an auspicious shrine of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas by the name Trijāteśvara.

## \|\| 1.115.5 \|\|

*tamārādhya divā naktaṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*saśarīro gataḥ svargaṃ tataḥ kālena kenacit \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then some time, thereafter, he propitiated that Lord day and night with great faith and went to heaven along with his physical body.

## \|\| 1.115.6 \|\|

*yastaṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā snāpayedviṣuve sadā \|*  
*na trijātaḥ kule tasya kathañcidapi jāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If one visits that Lord with true devotion and bathes him always on the Viṣuva (Equinox) day, never shall a Trijāta be born in his family.

## \|\| 1.115.7 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yāni gotrāṇi naṣṭāni yāni saṃsthāpitāni ca \|*  
*nāmatastāni no brūhi tatpuraṃ sūta nandana \|\| 7 \|\|*

The sages said:

7\. O Sūtanandana, recount to us the names of those Gotras that became extinct and those that were re-established in that city.

## \|\| 1.115.8-9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatropamanyugotrā ye krauṃcagotrasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*kaiśoryaṃ gotrasaṃbhūtāstraivaṇeyā dvijottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*te bhūyo'pi na saṃprāptā yathā gotracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*tatpūrvakaṃ śukādīnāṃ yannaṣṭaṃ nāgajādbhayāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:

8-9. Like the four Gotras of those beginning with Śuka who disappeared (left permanently) due to the fear of serpents, the following excellent Brāhmaṇas did not come back: those of Upamanyu Gotra, those born of Krauñca Gotra, those hailing from Kaiśorya Gotra and also those of Traivaṇeya Gotra.

## \|\| 1.115.10 \|\|

*śeṣānvaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi brāhmaṇāngotrasaṃbhavān \|*  
*kauśikānvayasaṃ bhūtāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiśca te smṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I shall mention to you the remaining Brāhmaṇas of different Gotras. Twenty-six are remembered as born of Kauśika family.

## \|\| 1.115.11 \|\|

*kaśyapānvayasaṃbhūtāḥ saptāśītirdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*lakṣmaṇānvayasaṃbhūtā ekaviṃśatirāgatāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, eighty-seven were born of Kaśyapa family; twenty-one families born of Lakṣmaṇa’s family came back to that city.

## \|\| 1.115.12 \|\|

*tatra naṣṭāḥ punaḥ prāptāstasminsthāne suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*bhāradvājāstrayaḥ prāptāḥ kauṃḍanīyāścaturdaśa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Those who had vanished earlier came back again in great misery. Three of the Bhāradvāja family and fourteen of the Kauṇḍanīya family came back.

## \|\| 1.115.13 \|\|

*raitikānāṃ tathā viṃśatpārāśaryāṣṭakaṃ tathā \|*  
*gargāṇāṃ ca dviviṃśaṃ ca hārītānāṃ viviṃśatiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Raitikas were twenty and Pārāśaryas eight; Gargas twenty-two and Hārītas twenty-three.

## \|\| 1.115.14 \|\|

*aurvabhārgavagotrāṇāṃ pañcaviṃśadudāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*gautamānāṃ ca ṣaḍviṃśamālūbhāyanaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The families of Aurvas and of Bhārgavas were cited as twenty-five; those of Gautamas twenty-six and those of Ālūbhāyanas (v.l. Ālūtāyana) were twenty.

## \|\| 1.115.15 \|\|

*māṃḍavyānāṃ triviṃśacca bahvṛcānāṃ triviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*sāṃkṛtyānāṃ viśiṣṭānāṃ pṛthaktvena daśaiva tu \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The families of Māṇḍavyas were twenty-three, those of Bahvṛcas twenty-three, those of Sāṃkṛtyas and Viśiṣṭas (? splendid) (or those of distinguished Sāṅkṛtyas) were severally ten in number.

## \|\| 1.115.16 \|\|

*tathaivāṃgirasānāṃ ca paṃca caiva prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ātreyā daśa saṃkhyātāḥ śuklātreyāstathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Further, Āṅgirasas were proclaimed as five in number; Ātreyas numbered ten and the same in the case of Śuklātreyas.

## \|\| 1.115.17 \|\|

*vātsyāḥ pañca samākhyātāḥ kautsāśca nava sapta vai \|*  
*śāṃḍilyā bhārgavāḥ pañca maudgalyā viṃśatiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Vātsyas are reckoned as five and Kautsas sixteen (nine and seven). Śāṇḍilya sub-division of Bhārgavas are five and Mudgalyas are remembered as twenty.

## \|\| 1.115.18 \|\|

*baudhāyanāḥ kauśalāśca triṃśanmātrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*atharvāḥ paṃcapaṃcāśanmaunasāḥ saptasaptatiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Baudhāyanas and Kauśalas are proclaimed as thirty; Atharvas fifty-five and Maunasas seventy-seven.

## \|\| 1.115.19 \|\|

*yājuṣāstriṃśatiḥ khyātāścyāvanāḥ sapta viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*āgastyāśca trayastriṃśajjaimineyā daśaiva tu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Yājuṣas were thirty and the well known Cyāvanas were twenty-seven; Āgastyas thirty-three and Jaimineyas only ten.

## \|\| 1.115.20 \|\|

*naivṛtāḥ paṃcapaṃcāśatpāṭhīnāḥ saptatirdvijāḥ \|*  
*gobhilāścāpi kākvāśca paṃcapaṃca dvijāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Naivṛta Brāhmaṇas were fifty-five and Pāṭhīnas seventy. Gobhila Brāhmaṇas and Kākva Brāhmaṇas are remembered as five each.

## \|\| 1.115.21 \|\|

*auśanasāśca dāśārhāstrayastraya udāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*lokākhyānāṃ tathā ṣaṣṭiraiṇiśānāṃ dvisaptatiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Auśanasas and Dāśārhas are cited as three each. Further, there were sixty families of Lokākhyas and those of the Aiṇiśas seventy-two.

## \|\| 1.115.22 \|\|

*kāpiṣṭhalāḥ śārkarākhyā dattākhyāḥ saptasaptatiḥ \|*  
*śārkavānāṃ śataṃ proktaṃ dārjyānāṃ saptasaptatiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Kāpiṣṭhalas, those designated as Śārkaras and Dattas were seventy-seven, Śārkavas are mentioned as one hundred and Dārjyas seventy-seven.

## \|\| 1.115.23 \|\|

*kātyāyanyāstrayo'dhiṣṭhā vaidiśāśca trayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇātreyāstathā paṃca dattātreyā stathaiva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kātyāyanyas were three; Adhiṣṭhas and Vaidiśas are remembered as three. Kṛṣṇātreyas and Dattātreyas were five (each).

## \|\| 1.115.24 \|\|

*nārāyaṇāḥ śaunakeyā jābālāḥ śatasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*gopālā jāmadanyāśca śālihotrāśca karṇikāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Nārāyaṇas, Śaunakeyas and Jābālas were one hundred in number. So also were Gopālas, Jāmadagnyas, Śālihotras and Karṇikas.

## \|\| 1.115.25 \|\|

*bhāgurāyaṇakāścaiva mātṛkāstraiṇavāstathā \|*  
*sarve te brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ krameṇa dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Further Bhāgurāyaṇakas, Mātṛkas and Traiṇavas were also similar.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all these were excellent Brāhmaṇas in due serial order.

## \|\| 1.115.26 \|\|

*eteṣāmeva sarveṣāṃ satkārāya dvijotamāḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśattathāṣṭau ca purā proktāḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It was for the consecration of all these that forty-eight excellent Brāhmaṇas were announced formerly by the Self-born Lord.

## \|\| 1.115.27 \|\|

*te sarve ca pṛthaktvena nirdiṣṭāḥ padmayoninā \|*  
*saṃdhyātarpaṇakṛtyāni vaiśvadevodbhavāni ca \|*  
*śrāddhāni pakṣakṛtyāni pitṛpiṃḍāṃstathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All of them were separately directed by the Lotus-born Lord. The enjoined rites were Sandhyā prayers, libations (Tarpaṇa to Pitṛs) and other things connected with Vaiśvadeva, Śrāddhas, the rites in the different Pakṣas (fortnights), balls of rice to be offered to the Pitṛs etc.

## \|\| 1.115.28 \|\|

*yajñopavītasaṃyuktāḥ pravarāścaiva kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*tathā mauṃjīviśeṣāśca śikhābhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All the Pravaras connected with the rite of investing with the sacred threads, the particularly significant Mauñjis as well as the various styles of keeping hair-tuft were announced.

## \|\| 1.115.29 \|\|

*trijātena samārādhya devadevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*teṣāṃ kṛtvā dvijedrāṇāmātmakīrtikṛte tadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It was done by Trijāta after propitiating Pitāmaha, the Lord of Devas, for the sake of those leading Brāhmaṇas and for his own reputation.

## \|\| 1.115.30 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ santoṣito brahmā trijātena mahātmanā \|*  
*karmakāṃḍaṃ kathaṃ bhinnaṃ kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

The sages said:

30\. How was Brahmā pleased by the noble-souled Trijāta? How was the Karmakāṇḍa (procedure of performing different religious rites) differentiated by that noble-souled one? Do mention everything. We are very much eager to know.

## \|\| 1.115.31-33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyārthe brāhmaṇaiḥ sarvaistoṣitaḥ prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*anenaivoddhṛtaṃ sthānamasmākaṃ sakalaṃ vibho \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmādasya vibho yaccha vedajñānamanutamam \|*  
*yena karmaviśeṣāśca jāyate'tra purottame \|\| 32 \|\|*

*etasya ca gurutvaṃ ca prasādāttava padmaja \|*  
*yathā bhavati deveśa tayā nītirvidhīyatām \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sūta said:

31-33. For his sake, Prapitāmaha was propitiated by all the Brāhmaṇas: “O Lord, our native land was entirely redeemed (and rehabilitated) by this one alone.

Hence, O Lord, grant him the excellent knowledge of the Vedas so that the different special rites can function here, in this excellent city.

O Lotus-born One, do manage everything with due expedients so that he can have the status of preceptor with your favour, O Lord of Devas.”

## \|\| 1.115.34 \|\|

*brahmā dadau tatastasya maṃtragrāmamanuttamam \|*  
*yena vijñāyate sarvaṃ vedārtho yajñakarma ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then Brahmā granted to him the excellent collection of the Mantras whereby the meanings of the Vedas and (the procedure of) the Yajña rites were entirely understood.

## \|\| 1.115.35-39 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānsarvānprahaṣṭenātarātmanā \|*  
*eṣa vedārthasaṃpanno bhaviṣyati mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bhartṛyajña iti khyāto yajñakarmavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*yadeva vakti yuṣmākaṃ kriyākāṃḍamaśaṃkitaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tatkāryaṃ svargamokṣāya mama vākyātprabodhitaiḥ \|*  
*vedārthāneṣa sarveṣāṃ yuṣmākaṃ yojayiṣyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ye cānyeṣu ca deśeṣu sthāneṣu ca gatāḥ kvacit \|*  
*etatsthānaṃ parityajya satyametadvijottamāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vedasthāne ca buddhyaiṣa yatkarma pracariṣyati \|*  
*nānṛte vātha pāpe ca vāṇī cāsya cariṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Then with a highly delighted mind, he told them all: “This one will become richly endowed with the knowledge of the meaning of the Vedas. He will become famous.

He will become well-known as Bhartṛyajña and will be an expert in the rites of Yajña. Whatever he tells you in the matter of Karmakāṇḍa should be unhesitatingly carried out by you for the sake of heaven and salvation. As enlightened by my statements, he will explain the meanings of the Vedic passages to you.

It shall be due (applicable)to you all who had abandoned this land and gone to other lands and holy spots. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this is the truth.

Whatever act he performs shall be with his intellect keenly rooted in the Vedas. His speech shall never be directed towards falsehood or sin.”

## \|\| 1.115.40 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa deveśo virarāma pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*bhartṛyajño'pi tāḥ sarvāścakre yajñakriyāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After saying thus, Pitāmaha, the Lord of Devas, stopped. Bhartṛyajña performed all those auspicious Yajña rites.

## \|\| 1.115.41 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ hitārthāya śrutyarthaṃ tasya kevalam \|*  
*daśapramāṇāḥ saṃproktāḥ sarve te brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. For the sake of the welfare of the Brāhmaṇas alone he expounded the meaning of Śruti. All those excellent Brāhmaṇas were mentioned as having ten valid authorities (or extended to ten).

## \|\| 1.115.42 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭiṣu gotreṣu hyevaṃ te brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*tena tatra samānītāstrijātena mahātmanā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In this manner, excellent Brāhmaṇas belonging to all the sixty-four Gotras were brought together by the noble-souled Trijāta.

## \|\| 1.115.43 \|\|

*teṣāmekatra jātāni daśapaṃcaśatāni ca \|*  
*sāmānya bhogamokṣāṇi tāni tena kṛtāni ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus, one thousand five hundred families collected there together in one place. Trijāta made them enjoy pleasures in common and attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.115.44 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭivibhāgena pūrvamāyuvyayodbhavam \|*  
*tatrāsīdatha gotre ca puruṣāṇāṃ prasaṃkhyayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Formerly, the income and expenditure were reckoned in the Gotra in sixty-eight divisions or groups on the basis of the numbers of the men (i.e. members) thereof.

## \|\| 1.115.45-46 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti sarveṣāṃ sāmānyena vyavasthitam \|*  
*trijātasya ca vākyena yena dūrādapi drutam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*samāgacchaṃti viprendrāḥ puravṛddhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*na kaścidyāti saṃtyaktvā dausthyādanyatra ca dvijāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. But ever since then, at the instance of Trijāta the matter became established in common pool.

Thereby, leading Brāhmaṇas used to come there from far-off lands and the city flourished. No one abandoned the city on account of sufferings or penury to go elsewhere, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.115.47 \|\|

*tatasteṣāṃ sutaiḥ pautrairnaptṛbhiśca sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*dauhitrairbhāgineyaiśca bhūyo bhūri prapūritam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then it became filled up with thousands of their sons, grandsons, great-grandsons, daughters' son, nephews etc. to a great deal.

## \|\| 1.115.48 \|\|

*tatpuraṃ vṛddhimāyāti dūrvāṃkurairiva dvijāḥ \|*  
*kāṃḍātkāṃḍātprarohadbhiḥ saṃkhyāhīnairanekadhā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. That city is flourishing, O Brāhmaṇas, with innumerable citizens like the growth of the sprouts of Dūrvā grass, that grow from stem to stem.

## \|\| 1.115.49 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ gotrasaṃkhyānakaṃ śubham \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ kīrtanaṃ cāpi sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sūta said:

49\. Thus the auspicious reckoning of the Gotras of the sages has been narrated to you all. The recital thereof is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.115.50 \|\|

*yaścaitatpaṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādvā prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*na syāttasya kulacchedaḥ kadācidapi bhūtale \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If anyone reads this daily or listens to it devoutly, he shall never have extinction of his family on the earth any time.

## \|\| 1.115.51 \|\|

*tathā vimucyate pāpairājanmamaraṇodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*na paśyati viyogaṃ ca kadācitpriyasaṃbhavam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He is liberated from sins committed ever since his birth upto death. He never suffers separation from people near and dear.

## Chapter 116 - Greatness of Ambā-Revatī Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.116.1-3 \|\|

*sūtauvāca \|*  
*tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti suvikhyātāmbarevatī \|*  
*devī kāmapradā puṃsāṃ bālakānāṃ sukhapradā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yāṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayitvā'tha caitrāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śuklāyāṃ nāpnuyānmartyaḥ kuṭumbavyasanaṃ kvacit \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kena vā sthāpitā tatra sā devī cāmbarevatī \|*  
*kiṃprabhāvā kiṃsvarūpā sūtaputra vadasva naḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Further, there is another well-known deity Ambārevatī. The goddess fulfills cherished desires of men and accords happiness to children.

By visiting and worshipping her especially on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra, a men will seldom face calamity in the whole family anywhere.

## \|\| 1.116.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā śeṣeṇa saṃdiṣṭā nānānāgā viṣolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*purasyāsya vināśāya krodhasaṃraktalocanāḥ \|*  
*tadā tasya priyā sā ca putraśokenapīḍitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*svayamevāgrato gatvā bhakṣayāmāsa taṃ dvijam \|*  
*kuṭumbena samāyuktaṃ yena putro nipātitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

O Sūtaputra, do narrate to us everything. By whom was that goddess Ambārevatī installed there? What is her nature? What is her power?

Sūta said:

4-5. When the different varieties of highly poisonous Nāgas, with eyes reddened through anger, were directed by Śeṣa for the destruction of the city, his beloved wife who was afflicted on account of her dead son, herself went ahead and swallowed along with the entire family that Brāhmaṇa by whom her son had been struck down.

## \|\| 1.116.6 \|\|

*atha tasya dvijendrasya bālavaidhavyasaṃyutā \|*  
*anujā'sīttapoyuktā brahmacaryakṛtakṣaṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Incidentally, there was a younger sister of the leading Brāhmaṇa. She was a child-widow but richly endowed with the power of penance. She strictly adhered to the practice of celibacy.

## \|\| 1.116.7 \|\|

*sā dṛṣṭvā bhakṣitaṃ sarvaṃ bhaṭṭikākhyā kuṭumbakam \|*  
*nāga patnyā tataḥ prāha jalamādāya pāṇinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Her name was Bhaṭṭikā. On seeing that the entire family had been swallowed by the wife of the Nāga, she took some water in the hand and said:

## \|\| 1.116.8-10 \|\|

*yasmāttvayā kuṭumbaṃ me nāśaṃ nītaṃ dvijihvake \|*  
*darśitaṃ ca mahadduḥkhaṃ mama bandhujanodbhavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathā tvamapi saṃprāpya mānuṣatvaṃ sugarhitam \|*  
*mānuṣaṃ patimāsādya putrapautrānavāpya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ vināśajaṃ duḥkhaṃ mā nuṣe tvamavāpsyasi \|*  
*nāgatve vartamānāyāḥ śāpaṃ te'muṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 10 \|\|*
