8-10. “O two-tongued one, you have bröught about the ruin of my family. You have caused much suffering to my kinsmen. Hence you will get the despicable human birth, you will marry a man and beget sons and grandsons. In that mortal life you will experience grief due to the death of those near and dear. I am uttering this curse to you even as you still continue to be a Nāga woman.”

## \|\| 1.116.11 \|\|

*sā'pi śrutvā'tha taṃ śāpaṃ revatī bhaṭṭikodbhavam \|*  
*krodhena mahatāviṣṭā hyadaśattāṃ drutaṃ tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing that imprecatory utterance of Bhaṭṭikā, Revatī (Nāga lady) was overwhelmed with anger and bit her quickly.

## \|\| 1.116.12 \|\|

*atha tasyāstanuṃ prāpya nāgīdaṃṣṭrā viṣolbaṇā \|*  
*jagāma śatadhā nāśaṃ bibhide na tvacaṃ kvacit \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. As soon as the poisonous fangs of the female Nāga came in contact with her (Bhaṭṭikā’s) body they were shattered into hundred pieces and penetrated at no place on her body.

## \|\| 1.116.13 \|\|

*tataḥ sā lajjayāviṣṭā svaraktaplāvitānanā \|*  
*viṣaṇṇā niṣasādātha saṃniviṣṭā dharātale \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereupon, she became overcome with shame. Her own blood splashed her mouth (face). In her utter bewilderment, she sat quietly on the ground.

## \|\| 1.116.14-15 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare nāgāstathānye ye samāgatāḥ \|*  
*revatīṃ te samālokya tathārūpāṃ bhayānvitām \|*  
*procuśca kimidaṃ devi tava vaktre rujāspadam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*athavā kiṃ prabhāvo'yaṃ kasyacidraktasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. In the meanwhile, the Nāgas and others who had come there saw her frightened and in that condition. They asked: “O queen, what is this painful thing in your mouth? Or is this the power of a peculiar type of blood?"

## \|\| 1.116.16 \|\|

*revatyuvāca \|*  
*yeyaṃ duṣṭatamā kāciddṛśyate duṣṭatāpasī \|*  
*asyā jāto vikāro'yaṃ mamāsye nāgasattamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Revatī said:

16\. O excellent Nāgas, you see here a wicked woman-sage. This strange change (ailment) in my mouth has taken place due to her.

## \|\| 1.116.17 \|\|

*tasmādenāṃ mahā duṣṭāṃ bhaginīṃ tasya durmateḥ \|*  
*yena me nihataḥ putro dvijaputreṇa sāṃpratam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This is the wicked sister of that evil-minded one, the son of a Brāhmaṇa, by whom my son was killed.

## \|\| 1.116.18 \|\|

*bhakṣyatāṃ bhakṣyatāṃ śīghraṃ mama nāśāya saṃsthitām \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ manmukhe tenaṃ rudhiraṃ pannagottamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Let her be eaten. Let her be swallowed. She is out for destroying me. O excellent serpents that is why there is blood in my mouth.

## \|\| 1.116.19 \|\|

*atha te pannagāḥ kruddhā dadaṃśustāṃ tapasvinīm \|*  
*samaṃ sarveṣu gātreṣu yathānyā prākṛtā striyam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Those serpents became infuriated. All of them collectively bit that saintly woman all over her body as though she was an ordinary woman.

## \|\| 1.116.20 \|\|

*tatasteṣāmapi tathā mukhāddaṃṣṭrā vinirgatāḥ \|*  
*rudhiraṃ ca tato jajñe śeṣapatnyā yathā tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereupon, their fangs too fell down from their mouths and blood flowed out therefrom as in the case of the wife of the Nāga.

## \|\| 1.116.21 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ prabhāvaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā te nāgasattamāḥ \|*  
*śeṣā bhaya paritrastāḥ prajagmuśca diśo daśa \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On becoming aware of the power of that saintly woman, the remaining Nāgas became terrified and they fled in all directions.

## \|\| 1.116.22 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikāpi jagāmāśu svāśramaṃ prati duḥkhitā \|*  
*bhayatrastaiḥ samaṃtācca vīkṣyamāṇā mahoragaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Bhaṭṭikā too was miserable. She hurried to her own hermitage even as the utterly terrified great serpents looked at her from all round.

## \|\| 1.116.23-24 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvaṃ samālokya tāpyamānaṃ mahoragaiḥ \|*  
*tatsthānaṃ svajanairmuktaṃ duḥkhena mahatānvitaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jagāmānyatra sā sādhvī samyagvrataparāyaṇā \|*  
*tīrtha yātrāṃ prakurvāṇā paribabhrāma medinīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. That chaste lady perfectly engaged in the observance of holy vows became very sad on seeing the holy spot being scorched and harassed by the great serpents and therefore abandoned by her own people utterly miserable themselves. She, therefore, wandered all over the earth performing a pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.116.25 \|\|

*evamudvāsite sthāne tasminsā revatī tadā \|*  
*smṛtvā taṃ bhaṭṭikāśāpaṃ duḥkhena mahatā'nvitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the place became deserted in this manner in that spot, Revatī became more miserable on recollecting the curse of Bhaṭṭikā.

## \|\| 1.116.26-29 \|\|

*kathaṃ me mānuṣīgarbhe śāpādvāso bhaviṣyati \|*  
*mānuṣyeṇa ca kāṃtena prabhaviṣyati saṃgamaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*naitatputrodbhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathā māṃ bādhate hradi \|*  
*yathedaṃ mānuṣe garbhe saṃvāso mānuṣaṃ prati \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tathā daśanasaṃtyaktā kathaṃ bhartuḥ svamānanam \|*  
*darśayiṣyāmi bhūyo'pi kṣate kṣāro'tra me sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasmātparicariṣyāmi kṣetre'traiva vyavasthitā \|*  
*kiṃ kariṣyāmi saṃprāpya gṛhaṃ putraṃ vinākṛtā \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. ‘What will be the nature of my stay within the womb of a human female as a result of the curse? How will the intercourse with a human lover take place?

The misery due to the death of my son does not give me so much pain in my heart as the thought of stay in a human womb and co-habitation with a human being.

Further, bereft of my fangs, how can I show my face to my husband. This is somewhat like sprinkling salt in a wound.

Hence I shall continue to worship in this holy spot itself restricting my movements to it. What will I do after reaching home, now that I have been rendered bereft of my son?’

## \|\| 1.116.30 \|\|

*tataścārādhayāmāsa samyakchraddhāsamanvitā \|*  
*aṃbikāṃ sā tadā devīṃ sthāpayitvā sureśvarīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then she installed goddess Sureśvarī (Deity of the Suras). With perfect faith she propitiated the goddess Aṃbikā.

## \|\| 1.116.31 \|\|

*gandhapuṣpopahāreṇa naivedyairvividhairapi \|*  
*gītanṛtyaistathā vādyairmanohāribhireva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. She adored the deity with offerings of scents and flowers, different kinds of food offerings and with charming songs, dances and instrumental music.

## \|\| 1.116.32 \|\|

*tataḥ katipayāhasya tastāstuṣṭā sureśvarī \|*  
*provāca varadā'smīti prārthayasva hṛdi sthitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After a few days, Sureśvarī became pleased with her and said: “I shall grant the boon. Request for whatever is cherished in your heart.”

## \|\| 1.116.33-34 \|\|

*revatyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ śaptā purā devi brāhmaṇyā kāraṇāṃtare \|*  
*yattvaṃ mānuṣamāsādya svayaṃ bhūtvā ca mānuṣī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃprāpsyasi phalaṃ teṣāṃ nāśasamudravam \|*  
*mahadduḥkhaṃ svaputrotthaṃ mama śāpena pīḍitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

Revatī said:

33-34. O goddess, formerly, for another reson I was cursed by a Brāhmaṇa lady: “You will become a human female and will associate with a human male. Then you will have sons and face the sad consequence of their destruction.” I am already greatly miserable due to the death of the son. In addition, I have been cursed.

## \|\| 1.116.35 \|\|

*tathā mama mukhāddaṃṣṭrā saṃnītāśca sureśvari \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca saṃbhavastāvatkathaṃ syāttvatprabhāvataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Moreover, O Sureśvarī, the fangs have been smashed in my mouth. How can they grow up again by your power?

## \|\| 1.116.36 \|\|

*bhavaṃtu tanayā naśca tathā vaṃśavivardhanāḥ \|*  
*etanme vāṃchitaṃ devi nānyatsaṃprārthayāmyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Let sons be born to me making our family flourish. O goddess, this is desired by me. I do not wish to get anything else.

## \|\| 1.116.37 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|\| \|*  
*nātra vāsastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcidapi śobhane \|*  
*manuṣyagarbhasaṃvāso bharttā ca bhavitā naraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

The goddess said:

37\. O splendid lady, no fear need be entertained by you in this that you will have to stay in a human womb and that a man will be your husband.

## \|\| 1.116.38 \|\|

*tasmācchṛṇuṣva me vākyaṃ yattvāṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*duḥkhanāśakaraṃ tubhyaṃ satyaṃ ca varavarṇini \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Hence, O Jady of excellent complexion, listen to my words which I shall utter now. In truth it is destructive of your misery.

## \|\| 1.116.39 \|\|

*utpatsyati na saṃdeho devakāryaprasiddhaye \|*  
*tava bharttā triloke'sminkṛtvā mānuṣavigraham \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There is no doubt that, for the sake of the fulfilment of the task of Devas, your husband will assume a human form and be born in these three worlds.

## \|\| 1.116.40 \|\|

*takṣakākhyastathā nāgo dvijaśāpa vaśācchubhe \|*  
*saurāṣṭraviṣaye rājā raivatākhyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O splendid lady, the serpent named Takṣaka will be born in Saurāṣṭra due to the curse of a Brāhmaṇa. He will have the name Raivata.

## \|\| 1.116.41 \|\|

*tasya kṣemakarī bhāryā nāmavaṃśasamudbhavā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdeho viśiṣṭā vipraśāpataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Undoubtedly due to the curse of a Brāhmaṇa an excellent lady born of a noble Nāga family, named Kṣemakarī (‘Causing welfare’) shall be his wife.

## \|\| 1.116.42 \|\|

*tasyā garbhaṃ samāsādya tvaṃ janma samavāpsyasi \|*  
*rāmarūpasya śeṣasya punarbhāryā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You will be in her womb and will be born thereof. You will be the wife of Śeṣa again, who will be in the form of Rāma.

## \|\| 1.116.43 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ devi mā śokaṃ kārye'sminkuru śobhane \|*  
*tena mānuṣaje garbhe saṃbhūtiḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hence, O fair lady, O splendid one, do not have any grief in this matter Therefore, your birth will take place in human womb.

## \|\| 1.116.44 \|\|

*tatra paśyasi yannāśaṃ svakuṭumbasamudbhavam \|*  
*hitāya tadavasthāyāstadbhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The fact that you will see the destruction of your family there shall undoubtedly be for your good in that plight then.

## \|\| 1.116.45 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ yugaṃ pāpaṃ yato bhīru bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tadūrdhvaṃ martyadharmāṇo mlecchāḥ sthāsyaṃti sarvataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Since thereafter there will be the advent of the sinful Kali Age, so all persons staying everywhere will be Mlecchas with the characteristics of human beings.

## \|\| 1.116.46 \|\|

*tataḥ svarganivāsārthaṃ bhagavāndevakīsutaḥ \|*  
*saṃhartā svakulaṃ sarvaṃ svayameva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then, for the purpose of stay in heaven, the Lord, the son of Devakī will destroy his own family entirely. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.116.47 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃti punardaṃṣṭrāstava vaktre manoramāḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha pātālaṃ svabharttā yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Beautiful fangs will again grow in your mouth. So do go to Pātāla where your husband stays now.

## \|\| 1.116.48 \|\|

*anyaccāpi yadiṣṭaṃ te kiṃciccitte vyavasthitam \|*  
*tatkīrtayasva kalyāṇi mahāṃstoṣo mama sthitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O auspicious lady, do say if you have any other desire lurking in your mind. I have great pleasure.

## \|\| 1.116.49 \|\|

*revatyu vāca \|*  
*sthāne stheyaṃ sadā'traiva mama nāmnā sureśvari \|*  
*yena me jāyate kīrtistrailokye sacarācare \|\| 49 \|\|*

Revatī said:

49\. O Sureśvarī, you should stay here in this spot for ever by my name so that my reputation shall spread everywhere in the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile creatures.

## \|\| 1.116.50-51 \|\|

*tathā'haṃ nāgalokācca caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca \|*  
*sadā tvāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi viśeṣānnavamīdine \|\| 50 \|\|*

*āśvinasya site pakṣe sarvairnāgaiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*prapūjāṃ te vidhāsyāmi śraddhayā parayā yutā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Further, on the eighth, ninth and especially on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Āśvina I shall come from the Nāga world accompanied by all the Nāgas and worship you. I shall perform the excellent worship with great faith.

## \|\| 1.116.52 \|\|

*tasminnahani ye'nye'pi pūjāṃ dāsyaṃti te narāḥ \|*  
*mā paśyaṃtu prasādātte narāste vallabhakṣayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If other men too perform your worship on that day, let them not witness the destruction of their beloved ones. Grant this favour.

## \|\| 1.116.53 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhadre kariṣyāmi vāso me'tra bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tvannāmnā pūjakānāṃ ca śreyo dāsyāmi te sadā \|*  
*mahānavamije cāhni viśeṣeṇa śucismite \|\| 53 \|\|*

The Devī said:

53\. O fair lady, I shall thus stay here by your name. I shall always bestow welfare on the worshippers always, O lady of pure smiles, particularly so on the day of Mahānavamī.

## \|\| 1.116.54 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tayā sā'tha revatī śeṣavallabhā \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ paścāddharṣeṇa mahatānvitā \|\| 54 \|\|*

Sūta said:

54\. On being told thus by her (the goddess) Ravatī, the beloved of Śeṣa, went to her abode later with great delight.

## \|\| 1.116.55 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti sā devī tasminkṣetre vyavasthitā \|*  
*tannāmnā kāmadā nṛṇāṃ sarvavyasananāśinī \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Ever since then, that goddess became well established in that holy spot by her name. She bestows desired things on men and destroys all distresses.

## \|\| 1.116.56 \|\|

*aṃbā sā kīrtyate durgā revatī soragapriyā \|*  
*tataḥ saṃkīrtyate loke bhūtale cāṃbarevatī \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Goddess Durgā is glorified as Aṃbā and that beloved wife of the serpent was Revatī. Hence the deity is glorified in the world as Aṃbārevatī.

## \|\| 1.116.57 \|\|

*yastāṃ śraddhāsamopetaḥ śucirbhūtvā prapūjayet \|*  
*navamyāmāśvine māsi śuklapakṣe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*na sa saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadvyasanaṃ svakulo dbhavam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One who remains pure and worships her with great faith on the ninth day in the bright half of the month of Āśvina will never witness any disaster in his family for the whole of that year.

## \|\| 1.116.58 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvāgre chidrakaṃ vyālayuktaṃ doṣairvimucyate \|*  
*grahabhūtapiśācotthaistathānyairapi cāpadaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By seeing a hole in front infested by a serpent one is rid of all evil arising from malefic planets, ghosts and spirits and also gets free from other troubles.

## Chapter 117 - Emergence of Bhaṭṭikātīrtha (Bhaṭṭikā Tīrtha)

## \|\| 1.117.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhaṭṭikākhyā purā proktā yā tvayā sūtanandana \|*  
*kasmāttasyāḥ śarīrāntāddaṃṣṭrā nāgasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viśīrṇāḥ kiṃ prabhāvaśca tapasaḥ sūtanandana \|*  
*kiṃ vā maṃtraprabhāvaśca etannaḥ kautukaṃ param \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yanmānuṣaśarīre'pi viśīrṇāstā viṣolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*nāgānāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa tasmātsarvaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. O Sūtanandana, the lady named Bhaṭṭikā was described by you earlier. How did the fangs of the Nāgas get broken when they came into contact with her body? O Sūtanandana, is it the power of her penance? Is it the power of magic spells? We are highly curious about this. How even in the body of a hūman being got shattered those poisonous fangs of the serpents in particular. Do describe everything.

## \|\| 1.117.4 \|\|

*\|sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā purā brāhmaṇī bālye vartamānā piturgṛhe \|*  
*vaidhavyena samāyuktā jātā karmavipākataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. That Brāhmaṇa lady became a widow even when she was in her father’s house during her childhood. That was a result of her previous Karmas.

## \|\| 1.117.5 \|\|

*tato bālye'pi śuśrāva śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*devayātrāṃ pracakre'tha tīrthe snāti samāhitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even in her childhood, she had the opportunity to listen to the various scriptural texts. She took part in religious pilgrimages. With great mental concentration and purity, she used to take holy bath in Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.117.6 \|\|

*tatra kedāradevaṃ ca gatvā nityaṃ samāhitā \|*  
*prātarutthāya gītaṃ ca bhaktyā cakre tadagrataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She used to go to the temple of Lord Kedāra with great mental concentration everyday. She used to get up early in the morning and sing devoutly before the deity.

## \|\| 1.117.7 \|\|

*tatastadgītalaulyena pātālātsamupetya ca \|*  
*takṣako vāsukiścaiva dvija rūpadharāvubhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Urged by the temptation to listen to her songs Takṣaka and Vāsuki assumed the form of two Brāhmaṇas and came there from Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.117.8-10 \|\|

*sā'pi tatra mahadgītaṃ tānaiḥ sarvairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*mūrcchanābhiḥ samopetaṃ saptasvaravirājitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yatibhiśca tathā grāmairvarṇagrāmaiḥ pṛtha gvidhaiḥ \|*  
*tataṃ ca vitataṃ caiva ghanaṃ suṣirameva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tālakālakriyāmānavardhamānādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*avidagdhāpi sā teṣāṃ gītāṃgānāṃ dvijāṃganā \|*  
*kevalaṃ kaṃṭhasaṃśuddhyā tābhyāṃ toṣaṃ samādadhe \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Her songs were exquisite with the Tānas and Mūrcchanās in the proper order. All the seven notes of the gamut embellished her songs. The Yatis, Gramas and Varṇagrāmas were of different kinds. The four types of musical instruments viz. Tata (stringed ones), Vitata (drums etc.,), Ghana (cymbals etc.), Suṣira (flutes etc.) have their own Tālas (beating of the time), Kālakriyā (the process of timing) etc. The Brāhmaṇa lady was of course not an expert in those different aspects of music. Merely by the purity of the mellifluous voice of her throat, she delighted those two.

## \|\| 1.117.11 \|\|

*tatastadgītalobhena sarve tatpuravāsinaḥ \|*  
*prātarutthāya kedāraṃ samāgacchaṃti kautukāt \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Getting up early in the morning with avidity (great attraction) for her music, all the citizens of that town eagerly assembled in the Kedāra shrine.

## \|\| 1.117.12 \|\|

*kasya cittvatha kālasya nāgau tau svapuraṃ prati \|*  
*ninyurbalātsamudyamya sarvalokasya paśyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Once those two Nāgas forcibly took her to their city even as all the people were watching.

## \|\| 1.117.13 \|\|

*nāgarūpaṃ samādhāya raudraṃ janavibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*bhogāgryeṇa ca saṃveṣṭya pātālatalamabhyayuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They had resumed their serpent form of terrible nature, causing great fright to the people and coiled their bodies around her. They then took her to Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.117.14 \|\|

*atha tāṃ svagṛhaṃ nītvā procatuḥ kāmapīḍitau \|*  
*bhavāvābhyāṃ viśālākṣi bhāryā dharmaparāyaṇā \|*  
*etadarthaṃ samānītā tvaṃ pātāle mahītalāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After taking her to their abode, those two serpents afflicted by lasciviousness said to her: “O lady of large eyes, become our faithful wife. It is for this that you have been brought here to Pātāla from the surface of the earth.”

## \|\| 1.117.15-16 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikovāca \|*  
*yattvaṃ takṣaka māṃ śāṃtāmanapekṣāṃ ratotsave \|*  
*ānaiṣīrapahṛtyāśu brāhmaṇānvaya saṃbhavām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mānuṣaṃ rūpamāsthāya purā māṃ tvaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*kāmopahṛtacittātmā tasmānmartyo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 16 \|\|*

Bhaṭṭikā said:

15-16. O Takṣaka, I am a quiet woman born of the family of a Brāhmaṇa. I am indifferent to the gaiety of sexual activity. Still you had assumed the form of a Brāhmaṇa and abducted me. You have further touched me with your mind and soul swayed by lust. In view of these things you will become a human being.

## \|\| 1.117.17 \|\|

*yadi māṃ tvaṃ durācāra dharṣayiṣyasi vīryataḥ \|*  
*śatadhā tava mūrdhā'yaṃ sadya eva bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O wicked one, if you ravish me per force your head will immediately shatter into a hundred pieces.

## \|\| 1.117.18 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā sumahāśāpaṃ tasyāḥ sa bhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing her terrible curse, he became extremely terrified and bewildered. He stood with palms joined in reverence and tried to pacify her:

## \|\| 1.117.19 \|\|

*mayā tvaṃ kāmasaktena samānītā sumohataḥ \|*  
*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me śāpasyāṃto yathā bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “I admit that out of delusion you have been brought here by me overcome by passion. So be pleased to bring about the end of the curse.”

## \|\| 1.117.20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ prasāditā tena takṣakeṇa dvijātmajā \|*  
*tataḥ provāca taṃ nāgaṃ bāṣpavyākulalocanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sūta said:

20\. Thus the daughter of the Brāhmaṇa was propitiated by that Takṣaka. Then she said to him with her eyes dimmed with tears:

## \|\| 1.117.21 \|\|

*yadi māṃ martyaloke tvaṃ bhūyo na yasi takṣaka \|*  
*tatra śāpasya paryaṃtaṃ kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O Takṣaka, if you take me again to the human world I shall undoubtedly bring about an end to the curse there.”

## \|\| 1.117.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jñātvā mānuṣīṃ svagṛhāgatām \|*  
*takṣakeṇa samānītāṃ kāmopahatace tasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime Takṣaka’s wives came to know that a human female had come to the abode; in fact she had been brought there by Takṣaka whose mind had been overcome by lust.

## \|\| 1.117.23 \|\|

*tatastasya kalatrāṇi maherṣyāsaṃśritāni ca \|*  
*tasyā nāśārthamājagmuḥ koparaktekṣaṇāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Overwhelmed with great jealousy, she came there apparently to destroy her. Her eyes were red due to anger.

## \|\| 1.117.24 \|\|

*atha tāsāṃ parijñāya takṣakaḥ sa viceṣṭitam \|*  
*vāñchañchāpasya paryaṃtaṃ tatpārśvādbhayasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Takṣaka understood her intention very well. Moreover, he was already frightened and he keenly desired the final dissolution of the curse from the lady (Brāhmaṇa).

## \|\| 1.117.25 \|\|

*vajrāṃ nāmāsmaradvidyāṃ tasyā gātraṃ tatastayā \|*  
*yojayāmāsa rakṣārthaṃ prāptā cātha bhujaṃgamī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He recollected the magical spell named Vajra and in order to protect her body cast the spell on her body. Presently, the serpent lady too came upon the scene.

## \|\| 1.117.26 \|\|

*adaśattāṃ tataḥ kruddhā brāhmaṇasya sutāṃ satīm \|*  
*sapatnīṃ manyamānoccaiḥ śīrṇadaṃṣṭrā vyajāyata \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. She took the chaste daughter of the Brāhmaṇa for her co-wife and consequently became highly infuriated. She at once bit her only to get her fangs shattered thereby.

## \|\| 1.117.27 \|\|

*atha tāmapi sā kruddhā śaśāpa dvijasaṃbhavā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sāpatnyajairbhāvairvartamānāṃ saherṣyayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing the serpent lady vitiated by jealousy and the feelings of animosity the daughter of the Brāhmaṇa became angry and cursed her also:

## \|\| 1.117.28 \|\|

*yasmāttvaṃ doṣahīnāṃ māṃ sadoṣāmiva manyase \|*  
*tasmādbhava drutaṃ pāpe mānuṣī duḥkhabhāginī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “I am without any fault. Still you consider me as full of defects. So, O sinful one, be born a human female experiencing misery.”

## \|\| 1.117.29 \|\|

*atha tāṃ saṃgṛhītvā sa takṣako nāgasattamaḥ \|*  
*kedārāyatane tasminnardharātre mumoca ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then Takṣaka, the most excellent one among Nāgas, carried her off and left her at the Kedāra shrine at midnight.

## \|\| 1.117.30 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tāṃ devīṃ kṛtāṃ jalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*śāpāṃtaṃ kuru me sādhvi svagṛhaṃ yena yāmyaham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Standing there with his palms joined together in reverence, he spoke to that fair lady: “O chaste lady, bring about an end to my curse so that I can go to my abode.”

## \|\| 1.117.31 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikovāca \|*  
*saurāṣṭraviṣaye rājā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi pannaga \|*  
*bhūmau raivatako nāma bhogānāṃ bhājanaṃ sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Bhaṭṭikā said:

31\. O serpent, you will become a king named Raivataka in the land of Saurāṣṭra on the earth. You will always enjoy worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 1.117.32 \|\|

*tataścaiva tanuṃ tyaktvā kṣetreṣvāśramamadhyataḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpsyasi nijaṃ sthānaṃ tatkṣetrasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then, by abandoning your body in the holy shrine in the middle of the hermitage in the holy place, you will regain your own original position by the power of the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.117.33 \|\|

*takṣaka uvāca \|*  
*eṣā mama priyā kāṃtā tvayā śāpena yojitā \|*  
*yā sā bhavatu me bhāryā mānuṣatve'pi vartite \|\| 33 \|\|*

Takṣaka said:

33\. Let this beloved wife of mine whom also you have cursed be my wife even during the human life.

## \|\| 1.117.34 \|\|

*eta tkuru prasādaṃ me dīnasya pariyācataḥ \|*  
*mā'syā bhavatu cānyena puruṣeṇa samāgamaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At least do this favour to this distressed soul of mine earnestly requesting you. Let there be no contact of another male person with her.

## \|\| 1.117.35 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikovāca \|*  
*ānartādhipatereṣā bhavitrī duhitā śubhā \|*  
*tataḥ pāṇigrahaṃ prāpya bhāryā tava bhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

Bhaṭṭikā said:

35\. She will be born as the splendid daughter of King Ānarta. Then after the marriage, she will become your wife.

## \|\| 1.117.36 \|\|

*kṣemaṃkarīti vikhyātā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|*  
*tvayā sārdhaṃ bahūnbhogānbhuktvā'tha pṛthivītale \|*  
*paraloke punastvāṃ vai cānuyāsyati śobhanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She will be well-known as Kṣemaṃkarī. She will be equipped with beauty of form and prime of youth. After enjoying many pleasures on the surface of the earth, the splendid lady will follow you to the other world too.

## \|\| 1.117.37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ ca sa tayā proktaḥ kṣamyatāmiti sādaram \|*  
*praṇipatya jagāmā'tha nijaṃ sthānaṃ praharṣitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sūta said:

37\. On being told thus by her, he became delighted. After respectfully bowing down to her and saying, “May you be pleased to forgive”, he went to his own abode.

## \|\| 1.117.38 \|\|

*sā'pi prāpte niśāśeṣe kedārasya puraḥ sthitā \|*  
*punaścakre ca tadgītaṃ śrutisaukhyakaraṃ param \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even as a part of the night still remained, she stood before Lord Kedāra and began her songs highly delightful to the ears.

## \|\| 1.117.39 \|\|

*atha tasya samāyātāḥ kedārasya didṛkṣavaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ kedārabhaktyāḍhyā brāhmaṇāḥ śataśaḥ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thereafter, many hundreds of Brāhmaṇas endowed with devotion to Kedāra deity came there with a desire to see the deity.

## \|\| 1.117.40 \|\|

*te tāṃ dṛṣṭvā samāyātāṃ bhaṭṭiṃkāṃ tāṃ dvijodbhavām \|*  
*vismayena samāyuktāḥ papracchustadanaṃta ram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing the daughter of the Brāhmaṇa, the lady Bhaṭṭikā who had returned there, they were surprised and they began to question her:

## \|\| 1.117.41 \|\|

*ko'sau brāhmaṇarūpeṇa nāgaḥ prāptaḥ suśobhane \|*  
*tena tvaṃ kutra nītāsi kimarthaṃ ca vadasva naḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “O highly splendid lady, who was this serpent who had come in the form of a Brāhmaṇa? Where were you taken to by him? Why? Do tell us.”

## \|\| 1.117.42 \|\|

*kasmātpunaḥ pramuktā'si sarvaṃ vada yathātatham \|*  
*atra naḥ kautukaṃ jātaṃ sumahattava kāraṇāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Why were you set free again? Do mention everything in the manner it had occurred. A great curiosity has heen generated in us on account of you.

## \|\| 1.117.43 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sā kathayāmāsa sarvaṃ takṣakasaṃbhavam \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ nāgasaṃbhūtaṃ śāpānugrahajaṃ tathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sūta said:

43\. She narrated everything concerning the story of Takṣaka, the curse and the subsequent pacification.

## \|\| 1.117.44 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptaṃ sarvaṃ tasyāḥ kuṭumbakam \|*  
*rorūyamāṇaṃ duḥkhārtaṃ śrutvā tāṃ tatra cāgatām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In the meantime all the members of her family came there. On hearing that she had returned, their misery increased and they were crying loudly.

## \|\| 1.117.45 \|\|

*atha sā jananī tasyā vāṣpa paryākulekṣaṇā \|*  
*sasvaje tāṃ tathā cānyāḥ sakhyaḥ snigdhena cetasā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. With her eyes turned turbid, her mother embraced her. Her companions too with affectionate mind closely clasped her.

## \|\| 1.117.46 \|\|

*tato ninyurgṛhaṃ svaṃ ca śṛṇvaṃtaśca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*nāgalokodbhavāṃ vārtāṃ visya yāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. They took her to their abode listening to the narration of the events that happened in Nāgaloka. They were extremely surprised in their minds.

## \|\| 1.117.47-49 \|\|

*atha tatra pure paurāḥ sarve procuḥ parasparam \|*  
*ayuktaṃ kṛtametena brāhmaṇena durātmanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yadānītā sutaruṇī paraharmyoṣitā tayā \|*  
*anyeṣāmapi viprāṇāṃ saṃti nāryo hyanekaśaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*taruṇyo rūpavatyaśca vaidhavyena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*tāsāmapi ca sarvāsāmeṣa nyāyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yonisaṃkarajo nūnaṃ tasmānnirvāsyatāmiti \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. The citizens of the city met together and said to one another: “An improper act has been committed by this wicked-minded Brāhmaṇa. His youthful daughter who had stayed in the mansion of others has been brought back. Other Brāhmaṇas too here have many women to take care of, who are young, beautiful and unfortunately overtaken by the state of widowhood. This may set a bad precedent unto all of them resulting in promiscuous sexual relationships and mixture of castes. Hence she should be banished.”

## \|\| 1.117.50 \|\|

*ekībhūya tataḥ sarve brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sāmapūrvamidaṃ vākyaṃ procuḥ śāstra samudbhavam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. All those excellent Brāhmaṇas gathered together and spoke to him these words in a gentle manner conforming to scriptural texts:

## \|\| 1.117.51-53 \|\|

*eṣā tava sutā vipra taruṇī rūpasaṃyutā \|*  
*sānurāgeṇa nāgeṇa pātāle ca samāhṛtā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tadvakṣyati pramuktāhaṃ nirdoṣā tena rāgiṇā \|*  
*na śraddhāṃ yāti loko'yaṃ śuddhaiṣā samudāhṛtā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tasmācchuddhiṃ dvijedrāṇāṃ prayacchatu dvijottama \|*  
*yenānyeṣāmapi prājña vinaśyaṃti na yoṣitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. “O Brāhmaṇa, this beautiful and youthful daughter of yours was carried off to Pātāla by a lustful Nāga.

Yet on being released by that lustful one she says, ‘I am blemishless and pure’. People do not believe that she can be considered pure.

Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, let her pass through a Divya (ordeal) to prove her purity to leading Brāhmaṇas. In this way, O wise one, the downfall of other young women can be prevented.”

## \|\| 1.117.54-55 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā tatastāṃ vijane sutām \|*  
*papraccha yadi te doṣaḥ kaścidasti prakīrtaya \|\| 54 \|\|*

*no cetprayaccha saṃśuddhiṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ pratuṣṭaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. “So it shall be”, he said and he asked his daughter privately away from the people: “If you have any blemish confess it out. Otherwise undergo the ordeal to satisfy the Brāhmaṇas and demonstrate your purity.”

## \|\| 1.117.56 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikovāca \|*  
*yuktamuktaṃ tvayā tāta tathānyairapi ca dvijaiḥ \|*  
*yuktā syādyoṣitaḥ śuddhirdvārātikramaṇādapi \|\| 56 \|\|*

Bhatṭikā said:

56\. Dear father, what is proper has been said by you as well as the other Brāhmaṇas. The purity of a woman can be called into question even on stepping out of the door.

## \|\| 1.117.57 \|\|

*kiṃ punaḥ paradeśaṃ ca gatāyā rāgiṇā saha \|*  
*tasmādahaṃ na saṃdehaḥ prātaḥ snātā hutāśanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All the more so in my case, who had been to an alien land with a lustful person. Hence, I shall take the holy bath in the morning and (enter) fire.

## \|\| 1.117.58 \|\|

*praviśya sarvaviprāṇāṃ śuddhiṃ dāsyāmya saṃśayam \|*  
*ahamatra ca pānaṃ ca yaccānyadapi kiṃcana \|*  
*prāśayiṣyāmi saṃprāpya śuddhiṃ caiva hutāśanāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By entering fire I shall demonstrate my purity to all the Brāhmaṇas undoubtedly. Food or beverage whatever I have to take in, I shall take in only after getting the clearance through the fire-ordeal.

## \|\| 1.117.59 \|\|

*evamuktastayā so'tha harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*prātarutthāya dārūṇi purabāhye nyayojayat \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On being told thus by her, he was extremely pleased. Getting up early in the morning, he piled up logs of wood at the outskirts of the city.

## \|\| 1.117.60-61 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikā'pi tataḥ snātvā śuklāṃbaradharā śuciḥ \|*  
*sarvaiḥ parijanaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā nija kuṭuṃbakaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*prasannavadanā hṛṣṭā viṣṇudhyānaparāyaṇā \|*  
*jagāma tatra yatrāste sumahāndāruparvataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Bhaṭṭikā took her bath and made herself pure. She wore white clothes and was accompanied by members of her family as well as by friends and attendants. With the face beaming with pleasure, she meditated upon Viṣṇu and went to that place where the huge pile of logs was made.

## \|\| 1.117.62 \|\|

*tato vahniṃ samādhāya svayaṃ tatra dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kṛtvā prāha caiva kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, she set it on fire herself. After circumambulating it three times, she said with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.117.63-64 \|\|

*yadi me'sti kvaciddoṣaḥ kāmajo'lpo'pi gātrake \|*  
*kṛto vā'pi balāttena takṣakeṇa durātmanā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*anyenāpi ca kenāpi bhaviṣyatyathavā paraḥ \|*  
*tasmātpradahatu kṣipraṃ samiddho'yaṃ hutāśanaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. “If there is an iota of blemish arising from lust in my body forcefully caused by that wicked-minded Takṣaka or by anyone else, or if such a blemish may arise later, let this well-kindled fire burn me quickly.”

## \|\| 1.117.65 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha sā sādhvī praviṣṭā nijaharmyavat \|*  
*susamiddho huto vahnirjāto jalamayaḥ kṣaṇāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. After saying thus, that chaste lady entered the burning fire as if it were her own mansion. The well-kindled fire turned into cool water.

## \|\| 1.117.66 \|\|

*sā ca paśyati cātmānaṃ jalamadhyagatāṃ śubhā \|*  
*papātā'tha mahāvṛṣṭiḥ kusumānāṃ nabhastalāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. She saw herself moving about in the middle of water. The splendid lady felt the coolness everywhere. A great shower of flowers fell from the sky.

## \|\| 1.117.67-72 \|\|

*devadūto vimānastha idaṃ vākyamuvāca ha \|*  
*śuddhāsi tvaṃ mahābhāge cāritrai rnijagātrajaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*na tvayā sadṛśī cānyā kācinnārī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tisraḥ koṭyordhakoṭī ca yāni lomāni mānuṣe \|*  
*prabhavaṃti mahābhāge sarvagātreṣu sarvadā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ madhye na te sādhvi pāpamekamapi kvacit \|*  
*tasmācchīghraṃ grahaṃ gaccha nijaṃ bāṃdhavasaṃyutā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kuru kṛtyāni puṇyāni samārādhaya keśavam \|*  
*etaccaiva citeḥ sthānaṃ tvadīyaṃ jalapūritam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tava nāmnā suvikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ loke bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti śayane bodhane hareḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*te yāsyaṃti parāṃ siddhiṃ duṣprāpyā yā'marairapi \|*  
*uktvaivaṃ viratā vāṇī devadūtasamudbhavā \|\| 72 \|\|*

67-72. A messenger of gods seated in an aerial chariot spoke these words: “O highly esteemed one, you are pure due to the chastity of the limbs.

No other woman will ever be equal to you. O highly esteemed one, in all the limbs together in a human body, there are altogether thirty-five million hairs.

Among them, O chaste lady, not a single one is sinful. Hence hasten back to your abode along with your kinsmen.

Do meritorious acts. Propitiate Keśava. This spot of the fire orderal filled now with water shall become a Tīrtha well-known after your name. Those who take their holy bath here at the time of Śayana and Bodhan of Hari (eleventh day in Āṣāḍha and Kārttika) will attain great Siddhis which even the immortal ones cannot.”

After saying this, the messenger of gods stopped.

## \|\| 1.117.73-75 \|\|

*bhaṭṭikā tu tato hṛṣṭā praṇamya janakaṃ nijam \|*  
*nāhaṃ gṛhaṃ gamiṣyāmi kiṃ kariṣyāmyahaṃ gṛhe \|\| 73 \|\|*

*atraivārādhayiṣyāmi nijatīrthe sadā'cyu tam \|*  
*tathā tapaḥ kariṣyāmi bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tasmāttāta gṛhaṃ gaccha sthitā'haṃ cāgra saṃśraye \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. Bhaṭṭikā became highly delighted. She bowed down to her father and said: “I will not go home. What will I do in the house?

Here itself in my own Tīrtha I shall propitiate Acyuta always. Further I shall perform penance with the food received as alms as my sustenance.

Hence, O dear father, I shall stay here in this place of resort.”

## \|\| 1.117.76 \|\|

*tataḥ sa janakastasyāste vā'pi puravāsinaḥ \|*  
*saṃprahṛṣṭā gṛhaṃ jagmuḥ śaṃsatastāṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Then her father and those citizens went home with great delight, praising her individually.

## \|\| 1.117.77 \|\|

*tayā traivikramī tatra pratimā prāgvinirmitā \|*  
*paścānmāheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Earlier an idol of Trivikrama was installed by her and later the Liṅga of Maheśvara after building the excellent palatial shrine.

## \|\| 1.117.78 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ tapaścakre bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanā \|*  
*śasyamānā janaiḥ sarvaiścamatkārapurodbhavaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Then she performed a great penance taking the alms received as her food. She was praised by all the people of Camatkāra city.

## \|\| 1.117.79-80 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yathā tasyā dṛḍhaṃ kāyamabhedyaṃ saṃsthitaṃ sadā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sarpāṇāṃ ca tathā'nyeṣāṃ śastrādīnāmapi dvijāḥ \|*  
*yaścaitatpaṭhate nityaṃ bhaṭṭikākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*nāpavādo bhavettasya kukṛto dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

Sūta said:

79-80. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything whatever I was asked, has been narrated to you by me, I have told you how her body remained firm and unbreakable always to serpents and others such as weapons etc. One who reads this excellent narrative of Bhaṭṭikā, O execellent Brāhmaṇas, will never meet with calumny caused by wicked people.

## Chapter 118 - Installation of Raivatakeśvara (Raivataka-īśvara) and Kṣemaṃkarī

## \|\| 1.118.1-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yattvayā sūtaja proktaṃ takṣakaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*saurāṣṭraviṣaye rājā raivatākhyo mahābalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathā tasya priyā bhāryo nāmnā kṣemaṃkarīti yā \|*  
*ānartādhipaterharmye saṃbhaviṣyati bhāminī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ sarvaṃ samācakṣva vṛttāṃtaṃ sūtanaṃdana \|*  
*atra naḥ kautukaṃ jātaṃ vicitraṃ jalpatastava \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kedāraśca śruto'smābhiḥ sūtaputra himācale \|*  
*sa kathaṃ tatra saṃjātaḥ sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-4. O Sūtaja, it was mentioned by you that Takṣaka would be born in the land of Saurāṣṭra as a highly powerful king named Raivata and further that his beloved wife would be born as a beautiful lady in the palace of the overlord of Ānarta by the name Kṣemaṃkarī. O Sūtanandana, give a fully detailed information about those two. In this matter, we are rather curious since what you tell is wonderful.

Moreover, O Sūtaputra, we have heard that Kedāra is in Himācala. How did it happen to be there? Describe everything in full.

## \|\| 1.118.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*yathā mayā śrutaṃ pūrvaṃ nijatātamukhāddvijāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. In this connection, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall speak unto you in the manner heard earlier by me from by own father.

## \|\| 1.118.6 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ tacchāpadoṣeṇa takṣako dharaṇītale \|*  
*saurāṣṭrādhipaterharmye raivatākhyo babhūva ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Due to his earlier default and the curse thereof, Takṣaka was born in the mansion of the Lord of Saurāṣṭra by the name Raivata.

## \|\| 1.118.7-8 \|\|

*ānarttādhipateścāpi saṃjātā tanayā gṛhe \|*  
*tasyāścāpi suvikhyātaṃ nāma jātaṃ dharātale \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṣemaṃkarīti viprendrāḥ karmaṇā prakaṭīkṛtam \|*  
*ānartādhipatiḥ pūrvamāsīdrājā prabhaṃjanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. A daughter was born in the house of the Lord of Ānarta. Her name became well-known all over the earth as Kṣemaṃkarī. O leading Brāhmaṇas, (the significance of the name) became manifest through her activity.

Formerly the Lord of Ānarta was Prabhañjana.

## \|\| 1.118.9 \|\|

*tasya vairaṃ samutpannaṃ bahubhiḥ saha bhūmipaiḥ \|*  
*tato nirvāsyate deśo nīyate paśavo balāt \|*  
*śatrubhirjāyate yuddhaṃ divā naktaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. His enmity with many kings cropped up. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the land began to be rid of its citizens (due to exodus). Cattle were carried off forcibly. There was a battle with the enemies (which continued) during day and night.

## \|\| 1.118.10 \|\|

*tataḥ katipayāhasya tasya bhāryā priyaṃvadā \|*  
*ṛtusnātā dadhārātha garbhaṃ puṇyaṃ nijodare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After a few days his wife Priyaṃvadā who had her menstrual cycle, duly conceived a meritorious foetus in her womb.

## \|\| 1.118.11 \|\|

*yataḥ prabhṛti tasyāḥ sa garbho'bhūdudarāśrayaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti rāṣṭrasya kṣemaṃ jātaṃ tathā pure \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Ever since the conception of the foetus in her womb, there was an overall state of welfare in the city as well as in the country.

## \|\| 1.118.12 \|\|

*eke saṃkhye jitā stena śatravo'pi sudurjayāḥ \|*  
*nihatāśca tathaivānye mitrabhāvaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A few invincible enemies were conquered by him in a battle. Others were killed and a few were taken over as allies.

## \|\| 1.118.13 \|\|

*tato jajñe śubhā kanyā tasyāḥ padmāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*aṃdhakāre'pi yadrātryāṃ dyotitaṃ sūtikāgṛham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A splendid girl with wide eyes resembling lotus-petals was born to her, when the lying-in-chamber shone even in darkness.

## \|\| 1.118.14 \|\|

*athā'sau pārthivaścakre sutavatsumahotsavam \|*  
*tasyāstoṣasamāyukto gītavādyādinisvanaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The king was highly delighted at her birth. He celebrated the birth with great festivities as though at the birth of a son, with the singing of songs and playing of musical instruments.

## \|\| 1.118.15 \|\|

*dine trayodaśe prāpte nāma tasyā yathocitam \|*  
*vihitaṃ bhūbhujā tena viprāṇāṃ purato dvijāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On the thirteenth day, O Brāhmaṇas, a befitting name was given to her by the king in the presence of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.118.16 \|\|

*yasmātkṣemaṃ samutpannaṃ garbhavāse'pi saṃsthayā \|*  
*anayā kṣemaṃkarīnāma tasmādeṣābhave ddvijāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O Brāhmaṇas, since there was Kṣema (welfare) even while she was in the womb, she shall be called Kṣemaṃkarī.”

## \|\| 1.118.17 \|\|

*evaṃ suvihitā khyātā vṛddhiṃ yāti dinedine \|*  
*śuklapakṣe kalā cendoryathaiva gaganāṃgaṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus duly consecrated and well reputed she grew up day by day like the digit of the moon in the firmament.

## \|\| 1.118.18 \|\|

*tatastāṃ yauvanopetāṃ raivatāya mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*dadau saurāṣṭranāthāya kāle vaivāhike śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then when she became one endowed with the prime of youth, the king, gave her to Raivata, the Lord of Saurāṣṭra, at a time very auspicious for marriage.

## \|\| 1.118.19-20 \|\|

*atha tābhyāṃ sutā jātā revatīnāma viśrutā \|*  
*bhaṭṭikāśāpadoṣeṇa śeṣapatnī yaśasvinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yā tūḍhā rāmarūpeṇa nāgarājena dhīmatā \|*  
*putrapautravatī jātā saubhāgyamadagarvitā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The celebrated wife of Śeṣa who had been wedded to the intelligent king of Nāgas in the form of Rāma and who had (was to have) sons and grandsons, became haughty on account of conjugal felicity. She was born as their daughter and was well-known as Revatī.

## \|\| 1.118.21 \|\|

*na ca tābhyāṃ suto jātaḥ kathaṃcidapi vaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*vayasoṃ'te'pi vipreṃdrāstato duḥkhaṃ vyajāyata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even when the two had grown old, O leading Brāhmaṇas, no son was born of them to perpetuate their line. Therefore they suffered great misery.

## \|\| 1.118.22 \|\|

*atha tau maṃtrivargasya rājyaṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*arpayitvā tu putrārthaṃ tapo'rthamiha cāgatau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then they entrusted the group of ministers with the whole kingdom and came here for practising a penance to get a son.

## \|\| 1.118.23 \|\|

*tataḥ svamāśramaṃ gatvā sthitau tatra samāhitau \|*  
*devīṃ kātyāyanīṃ sthāpya tadārādhanatatparau \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They went to their hermitage and stayed there with great mental concentration. They installed goddess Kātyāyanī and engaged themselves in propitiating her.

## \|\| 1.118.24 \|\|

*yayā vinihato raudro mahiṣākhyo mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*kaumāravratadhāriṇyā tasminvindhye mahācale \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. (You may remember) that it was this goddess engaged in Kaumāravrata (vow of celibacy) on the Vindhya mountain who had killed the terrible Asura named Mahiṣa.

## \|\| 1.118.25 \|\|

*tatastābhyāṃ dadau tuṣṭā sā putraṃ vaṃśavardhanam \|*  
*nāmnā kṣemajitaṃ khyātaṃ parapakṣakṣayā vaham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The goddess who was pleased granted them a son destined to perpetuate the line. He became well-known by the name Kṣemajit. He was a powerful warrior capable of destroying hosts of enemies.

## \|\| 1.118.26 \|\|

*tataḥ svaṃ rājyamāsādya bhūyo'pi sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*svaputraṃ vardhayāmāsa harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The king went back to his kingdom with great delight and brought up his son with great pleasure.

## \|\| 1.118.27 \|\|

*yadā sa yauvanopetaḥ sañjātaḥ kṣemajitsutaḥ \|*  
*taṃ ca rājye niyojyā'tha svasthānaṃ sa punaryayau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When this son Kṣemajit became a young man, the elderly king crowned him (as king of) the kingdom and went back to his original holy spot.

## \|\| 1.118.28 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tadetaddvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā sahitastyaktvā śeṣamanyaṃ paricchadam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. That holy spot is this Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. He left all his attendants and came to this holy spot along with his wife.

## \|\| 1.118.29 \|\|

*tatra saṃsthāpayāmāsa liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ ca manohāri tataścakre samāhitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. There he installed the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord. Then he constructed with great concentration a beautiful palace.

## \|\| 1.118.30 \|\|

*raivateśvaramityuktaṃ sarvapātaka nāśanam \|*  
*darśanādeva sarveṣāṃ dehināṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The deity is called Raivateśvara. It was simply through paying a visit to the Lord that it destroyed all the sins of all embodied beings, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.118.31 \|\|

*yā pūrvaṃ sthāpitā durgā tasminkṣetre mahībhujā \|*  
*tasyāḥ kṣemaṃkarī cakre prāsādaṃ śraddha yānvitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With great faith Kṣemaṃkarī constructed the palace of the deity Durgā that had been earlier installed by the king in that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.118.32 \|\|

*sāpi kṣemaṃkarīnāma tataḥ prabhṛti kīrtyate \|*  
*kātyāyanyapi yā proktā mahiṣāsuramardinī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Ever since then she is glorifed by the name Kṣemaṃkarī, the deity who was earlier called Kātyāyanī and Mahiṣāsuramardinī (suppressor of the demon Mahiṣa).

## \|\| 1.118.33 \|\|

*yastāṃ caitrasite pakṣe saṃpa śyedaṣṭamīdine \|*  
*tasyābhīṣṭā bhavetsiddhiḥ sarvadaiva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if a person visits her on the eighth day in the bright half on the month of Caitra, all his desires will allways be realized.

## \|\| 1.118.34 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ raivateśvaravarṇanam \|*  
*kṣemaṃkaryāḥ prabhāvaṃ ca sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus everything regarding Raivateśvara and the sin-destroying power of Kṣemaṃkarī has been narrated to you.

## Chapter 119 - Defeat of the Army of Gods

## \|\| 1.119.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yatvayā sūtaja proktaṃ devī kātyāyanī ca sā \|*  
*mahiṣāṃtakarī jātā kathaṃ sā me prakīrtaya \|\| \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kīdṛgdānavavaryaḥ sa māhiṣaṃ rūpamāśritaḥ \|*  
*kasmātsa sūdito devyā tanme vistarato vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 119-121 deal with the story of the creation of Kātyāyanī and killing of Mahiṣāsura. Mahābhārata, Vana 231-92 states that Skanda killed him.

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaja, it has been mentioned by you that Goddess Kātyāyanī destroyed Mahiṣa. How was it? Narrate it to us. Of what nature was that heroic Dānava who had assumed the form of a buffalo? Why was he slain by the goddess. Tell it to us in detail.

## \|\| 1.119.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi devyā māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*śrutamātre'pi martyānāṃ yena śatrukṣayo bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. In this context I shall expound to you the excellent greatness of the goddess completely. Even if it is merely listened to, there shall be the destruction of the enemies of all mankind.

## \|\| 1.119.4 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣasutaḥ pūrvaṃ mahiṣonāma dānavaḥ \|*  
*āsīnmahiṣarūpeṇa yena bhuktaṃ jagattrayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly, there was a Dānava named Mahiṣa. He was son of Hiraṇyākṣa. Assuming the form of a buffalo, he enjoyed the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.119.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*māhiṣeṇa svarūpeṇa kiṃjātaḥ sūtanaṃdana \|*  
*athavā śāpadoṣeṇa sañjātaḥ kenacidvada \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. O Sūtanandāna, was he born along with the form of a buffalo? Or did he become so due to a curse as a result of a crime? Tell us.

## \|\| 1.119.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*saṃjāto hi surūpāḍhyaḥ śatapatranibhānanaḥ \|*  
*dīrghabāhuḥ pṛthugrīvaḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā citrasamaḥ proktastejovīryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. Indeed he was born with a fine form and features. His face resembled a lotus. His arms were long and his neck was thick. He was characterised by all excellent features. He was endowed with brilliance and vigour. He was called by the name Citrasama.

## \|\| 1.119.7 \|\|

*sabālyātprabhṛti prāyo mahiṣāṇāṃ prabodhanam \|*  
*karoti saṃparityajya sarvamaśvādivāhanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ever since his childhood he generally avoided other vehicles like horses etc., and used to rouse the buffaloes (for the purpose of riding).

## \|\| 1.119.8 \|\|

*kadācinmahiṣārūḍhaḥ sa pratasthe danoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*jāhnavītīramāsādya vinighnañjalapakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once that son of Danu was seated on a buffalo and moved about near the banks of Gaṅgā killing aquatic birds.

## \|\| 1.119.9 \|\|

*athāsītsusamādhistho durvāsā munisattamaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgātīre vidhāyoccaiḥ padmā sanamanuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It happened that the excellent sage Durvāsā was seated in the lotus pose on the bank of Gaṅgā, practising excellent meditation.

## \|\| 1.119.10 \|\|

*vihaṃgāsaktacittena śūnyena sa munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭo na mahiṣakṣuṇṇaḥ khurairvegavaśāddvijaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Since the Dānava was keenly looking for birds, his mind was no better than absent in regard to the leading sage. He was not at all noticed by him and the Brāhmaṇa was trampled upon by the buffalo under his hoofs in its mad rush.

## \|\| 1.119.11 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣatajadigdhāṃgaḥ sa dṛṣṭvā dānavaṃ puraḥ \|*  
*atha dṛṣṭvā praṇāmena rahitaṃ kopamāviśat \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Smeared with the blood from his wounds, the sage saw the Dānava before him. Further, the fellow did not bow down to him. This enraged him.

## \|\| 1.119.12-13 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca taṃ kruddhastoyamādāya pāṇinā \|*  
*yasmātpāpa mama kṣuṇṇaṃ gātraṃ mahiṣajaiḥ khuraiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*samādheśca kṛto bhaṃgastasmāttvaṃ mahiṣo bhava \|*  
*yāvajjīvasi durbuddhe samyagjñānasamanvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The sage then took up water in his hand and said angrily: “O sinful one, my body was trampled upon by the hoofs of your buffalo and you have caused disturbance to my meditation, so you shall become a buffalo. O evil-minded one, you will be aware of this perfectly as long as you live.”

## \|\| 1.119.14 \|\|

*athā'sau mahiṣo jātaḥ kṛṣṇagātradharo mahān \|*  
*atidīrghaviṣāṇaśca aṃjanādririvāparaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereupon, he became a huge buffalo of dark complexion. He was like another mountain of collyrium. His horns were very long.

## \|\| 1.119.15 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa taṃ muniṃ vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*śāpātaṃ kuru me vipra bālyabhāvādajānataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With great humility he pacified the sage: “O Brāhmaṇa, I was too childish to observe things. Do put an end to the curse.”

## \|\| 1.119.16-17 \|\|

*atha taṃ sa muniḥ prāha na me syādvacanaṃ vṛthā \|*  
*tasmādyāvatsthitāḥ prāṇāstāvaditthaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mahiṣasya svarūpeṇa ninditasya sudurmate \|*  
*evaṃ sa taṃ parityajya gaṃgātīraṃ munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*jagāmā'nyatra so'pyāśu gatvā śukramuvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Then the sage said to him: “My words cannot go in vain. As long as you live, this will be like that. O highly evil-minded one, you will have this despicable form of a buffalo.”

After saying so, the leading sage left the banks of Gaṅgā and went elsewhere. The demon went to Śukra and said thus:

## \|\| 1.119.18-19 \|\|

*ahaṃ durvāsasā śaptaḥ kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare \|*  
*mahiṣatvaṃ samānītastasmāttvaṃ me gatirbhava \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yathā syātpūrvajaṃ dehaṃ tiryaktvaṃ naśyate yathā \|*  
*prasādāttava vipreṃdra tathā nītirvidhīyatām \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. “I have been cursed by Durvāsas for some reason and have been turned into a buffalo. Hence you should be my refuge. O leading Brāhmaṇa, do employ some means so that with your favour, the brutish form vanishes and I regain my original physical form.”

## \|\| 1.119.20 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*tasya śāpo'nyathā kartuṃ naiva śakyaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*kenāpi saṃparityajya devamekaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

Śukra said:

20\. Excepting Lord Maheśvara, this curse cannot be altered by anyone else.

## \|\| 1.119.21 \|\|

*tasmādārādhayā'śu tvaṃ gatvā liṃgamanuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvasiddhipradāyake \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence hasten to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara that bestows all Siddhis and propitiate the excellent Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.119.22 \|\|

*tatra sañjāyate siddhiḥ śīghraṃ dānavasattama \|*  
*api pāpayuge prāpte kiṃ punaḥ prathame yuge \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O excellent Dānava, acquisition of perfection is very quick even in the sinful age of Kali. All the more so in the first yuga (called Kṛta).

## \|\| 1.119.23 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa śukreṇa dānavaḥ satvaraṃ yayau \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tapastepe tataḥ param \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On being told thus by Śukra, the Dānava immediately went to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara and performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.119.24 \|\|

*sthāpayitvā mahalligaṃ bhaktyā devasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ ca tataścakre kailāsaśikharopamam \|\| 094 \|\|*

24\. With great devotion, he installed a great Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord and thereafter erected a palace comparable to a peak of Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.119.25 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya tapaḥsthasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālaḥ kṛcchre tapasi vartataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The large-hearted Dānava continued the strenuous ordeal of the penance for a long period.

## \|\| 1.119.26 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevo gatvā taddṛṣṭigocaram \|*  
*provāca parituṣṭo'smi varaṃ varaya dānava \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Mahādeva became pleased. He appeared before him and said: “O Dānava, I am pleased with you. Choose a boon.”

## \|\| 1.119.27 \|\|

*mahiṣa uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ durvāsasā śapto mahiṣatve niyojitaḥ \|*  
*tiryaktvaṃ nāśamāyātu tasmānme tvatprasādataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Mahiṣa said:

27\. I have been cursed by Durvāsas and have been turned into a buffalo. Hence with your favour, let this brutish form vanish.

## \|\| 1.119.28 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*nānyathā śakyate kartuṃ tasya vākyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*tasmāttava kariṣyāmi sukhopāyaṃ śṛṇuṣva tam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

28\. His utterance (curse) cannot be altered at any rate. Hence I shall suggest an easy means to you. Listen to it.

## \|\| 1.119.29 \|\|

*ye kecinmānavā bhogā daivikā ye tathā'surāḥ \|*  
*te sarve tava gātre'tra samprayāsyaṃti saṃśrayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. All types of sensual pleasures, human, divine and demoniac, will resort to your physical form.

## \|\| 1.119.30 \|\|

*bhogārthamiṣyate kāyaṃ yato martyaṃ surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*samavāpsyasi tānsarvāṃstasmāttava kalevaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. It is for the sake of sensual pleasures that a human form is sought after by Suras and Asuras. Hence this body of yours will obtain all those pleasures.

## \|\| 1.119.31 \|\|

*mahiṣa uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ devadeveśa bhogaprāptirbhavenmama \|*  
*tasmādavadhyamevāstu gātrametanmama prabho \|\| 31 \|\|*

Mahiṣa said:

31\. If thus, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, I will obtain sensual pleasures, let this physical form of mine be indestructible.

## \|\| 1.119.32 \|\|

*daśānāṃ devayonīnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tiryañcānāṃ ca nāgānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ surasattama \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. It may not be killed by the ten categories of divine beings and, all human beings, brutes, Nāgas and birds, O most excellent one among Suras.

## \|\| 1.119.33 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*nāvadhyo'sti dharāpṛṣṭhe kaściddehī ca dānava \|*  
*tasmādekaṃ parityaktvā śeṣānprārthaya daityapa \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

33\. O Dānava, no embodied being can be indestructible on the surface of the earth. Hence, O leader of Daityas, except this one, seek other ones (boons).

## \|\| 1.119.34-36 \|\|

*tataḥ sa suciraṃ dhyātvā provāca vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*striyamekāṃ parityaktvā nānyebhyastu vadho mama \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tathātra māmake tīrthe yaḥ kaścicchraddhayā naraḥ \|*  
*karoti snānamavyagrastvāṃ paśyati tataḥ param \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasya syāttvatprasādena saṃsiddhiḥ sārvakāmikī \|*  
*sarvopadravanāśaśca tejovṛddhiśca śaṃkara \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Then he thought for a long time and spoke to the Bull-emblembed One: “Leaving womankind alone let there not be my destruction by others.

Further, O Śaṅkara, if a man takes his holy bath in my Tīrtha with great faith and unperturbedly visits you thereafter, let him have the fulfilment of all desires with your favour. May all calamities end in his case and may his splendour increase.

## \|\| 1.119.37-38 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*mārgaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ tīrthe snātvā'tra tāvake \|*  
*vilokayiṣyati prītyā mama liṃgaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhūtapretapiśācādi saṃbhavāstasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*doṣā nāśaṃ prayāsyaṃti tathā rogā jvarādayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavan said:

37-38. If a person takes his holy bath in your Tīrtha on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa and lovingly visits my Liṅga thereafter, all troubles arising from ghosts, spirits, vampires etc. and all ailments like fever will finish.

## \|\| 1.119.39 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*mahiṣo'pi nijaṃ sthānaṃ prajagāma tataḥ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After saying this the Lord of Devas vanished. Thereafter Mahiṣa went to his own abode.

## \|\| 1.119.40 \|\|

*sa gatvā dānavānsarvānsamāhūya tataḥ param \|*  
*provācāmarṣasaṃyuktaḥ sabhāmadhye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After going there, he seated himself in the middle of the assembly and full of rage and vehemence of intolerance, summoned all the Dānavas and spoke to them:

## \|\| 1.119.41-42 \|\|

*pitā mama pitṛvyaśca ye cānye mama pūrvajāḥ \|*  
*dānavā nihatā devairvāsudevapurogamaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasmāttānnāśayiṣyāmi devānapi mahāhave \|*  
*ahaṃ trailokyarājyaṃ hi grahīṣyāmi tataḥ param \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. “All the Dānavas such as my father, paternal uncle and other ancestors were killed by Devas with Vāsudeva as their leader. Hence, I will exterminate all those Devas in a great battle. Then I will seize the kingdom of all the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.119.43-44 \|\|

*atha te dānavāḥ procuryuktametadanuttamam \|*  
*asmadīyamidaṃ rājyaṃ yacchakraḥ kurute divi \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasmādadyaiva gatvā'śu hatvendraṃ raṇamūrdhani \|*  
*divyānbhogānprabhuñjānāḥ sthāsyāmaḥ sukhino divi \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Then those Dānavas said: “This is proper. This is excellent. The kingdom ruled by Śakra in heaven is our own realm. Therefore we shall go there now itself and immediately kill Indra in battlefield. We shall then stay happily in heaven enjoying divine pleasures.”

## \|\| 1.119.45 \|\|

*evaṃ te dānavāḥ sarve kṛtvā maṃtraviniścayam \|*  
*meruśṛṃgaṃ tato jagmuḥ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. After taking the general counsel thus, all the Dānavas went to the peak of Meru along with their servants, armies and vehicles.

## \|\| 1.119.46 \|\|

*atha śakrādayo devā dṛṣṭvā taddānavodbhavam \|*  
*akasmādeva saṃprāptaṃ balaṃ śastrāstrasaṃyutam \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ svapuradvāri niryayustadanaṃtaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing the army of the Dānavas equipped with weapons and missiles descending upon them all of a sudden at the very threshold of their city for the purpose of fighting, Śakra and the other Devas too came out.

## \|\| 1.119.47 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrā nāsatyau ca bhiṣagvarau \|*  
*viśvedevāstathā sādhyāḥ siddhā vidyādharāśca ye \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. All these came out: Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, the expert physicians Nāsatyas, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Siddhas and Vidyādharas.

## \|\| 1.119.48 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ saha dānavaiḥ \|*  
*mithaḥ prabhartsyamānānāṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereupon, a battle ensued between the Devas and Dānavas who reviled one another and dared death bravely.

## \|\| 1.119.49 \|\|

*evaṃ samabhavadyuddhaṃ yāvadvarṣatrayaṃ divi \|*  
*raktanadyotivipulāstatrātīva prasusruvuḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thus the battle dragged on for three years in heaven. Vast rivers of blood overflowed.

## \|\| 1.119.50 \|\|

*anyasmindivase śakraṃ dṛṣṭaivārāvaṇasaṃsthitam \|*  
*taṃ śuklenātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani \|*  
*devaiḥ parivṛtaṃ divyaśastrapāṇibhireva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One day, he saw Śakra seated on Airāvata. A white umbrella was held above his head and he was surrounded by the Devas with divine missiles and weapons in their hands.

## \|\| 1.119.51 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā mahiṣo dānavādhipaḥ \|*  
*mahāvegaṃ samāsādya tasyaivābhimukho yayau \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereupon, the infuriated Lord of the Dānavas, Mahiṣa, rushed against him with great speed.

## \|\| 1.119.52 \|\|

*śṛṃgābhyāṃ ca sutīkṣṇābhyāṃ tataścairāvaṇaṃ gajam \|*  
*vivyādha hṛdaye so'tha cakre rāvaṃ sudāruṇam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. With his sharp horns, he hit the elephant Airāvata in his chest. The elephant made a terribly tumultous trumpeting sound.

## \|\| 1.119.53 \|\|

*tataḥ parāṅmukho bhūtvā palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*abhidudrāva vegena purī yatrāmarāvatī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then he reverted his face and began to flee. He ran speedly towards the city of Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 1.119.54 \|\|

*aṃkuśotthaprahāraiśca kṣatakuṃbho'pi bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*mahāmātraniruddho'pi na sa tasthau kathaṃcana \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The elephant driver pierced his forehead by hitting it with the goad. Though he was checked thus, he never stopped at all.

## \|\| 1.119.55 \|\|

*athābravītsahasrākṣo mahiṣaṃ vīkṣya garvitam \|*  
*garjamānāṃstathā daityānkṣveḍanāsphoṭanādibhiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On seeing very haughty Mahiṣa and the Daityas roaring gruffly and striking their arms and chest as wrestlers do with their hands, the Thousand-eyed One spoke:

## \|\| 1.119.56-57 \|\|

*mā daitya pravijānīhi yannaṣṭastridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*eṣa nāgo raṇaṃ hitvā vivaśo yāti me balāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tasmāttiṣṭha muhūrtaṃ tvaṃ yāvadāsthāya sadratham \|*  
*nāśayāmi ca te darpaṃ nihatya niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. “Of course, this elephant of mine is going away from the battlefield helplessly. But, O Daitya, do not think that the Lord of heaven has fled away. Hence wait for a while. Let me get into my excellent chariot. I shall hit you with my sharp arrows and destroy your arrogance.”

## \|\| 1.119.58 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ \|*  
*sahasraidarśabhiryuktaṃ vājināṃ vātaraṃhasām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In the meantime, Mātali, the charioteer of Śakra, came there with the chariot fitted with ten thousand horses with the speed of the wind.

## \|\| 1.119.59 \|\|

*te 'tha mātalinā aśvāḥ pratodena samāhatāḥ \|*  
*utpataṃta ivākāśe satvaṃ saṃpradudruvuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Struck with the whip by Mātali, those horses ran speedily as though they were flying up into the sky.

## \|\| 1.119.60 \|\|

*atha cāpaṃ samāropya satvaraṃ pākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*śarairāśīviṣākāraiśchādayāmāsa dānavam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then Pākaśāsana (Indra) lifted up his bow and covered the Dānava with the arrows having serpentine shapes.

## \|\| 1.119.61 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vegamāsthāya bhūyo'pi krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*abhidudrāva vegena sa yatra tridaśādhipaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thereupon, he became all the more infuriated and rushed with great speed to the place where the Lord of heaven was present.

## \|\| 1.119.62 \|\|

*tatastānsuhayāṃstasya śṛṃgābhyāṃ vegamāśritaḥ \|*  
*dārayāmāsa saṃkruddha āvidhyāvidhya cāsakṛt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He then furiously hit and pierced the excellent horses with his horns and tore them violently again and again.

## \|\| 1.119.63 \|\|

*tataste vājinastrastāḥ saṃjagmuḥ kṣatavakṣasaḥ \|*  
*raktaplāvitasarvāṃgā mārgamairāvaṇasya ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The excellent horses with their chests wounded and bodies drenched and smeared with blood, followed the path of Airāvata.

## \|\| 1.119.64 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimukhaṃ surasattamāḥ \|*  
*sarve pradudruvurbhītāstasya mārgamupāśritāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The excellent Suras observed the chariot of Śakra turning away. They were all frightened and they too fled following its path.

## \|\| 1.119.65 \|\|

*tatastu dānavāḥ sarve bhagnāndṛṣṭvā raṇe surān \|*  
*śastravṛṣṭiṃ pramuṃcaṃto garjamānā yathā ghanāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On seeing all the Suras shattered in the battle, all those Dānavas roared like rumbling clouds and showered volleys of missiles.

## \|\| 1.119.66 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā rajanī tamasāvṛtā \|*  
*na kiṃcittatra saṃyāti kasyaciddṛṣṭigocare \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In the meantime, night overtook them enveloping everything in darkness. Nothing became visible to the eyes of anyone.

## \|\| 1.119.67 \|\|

*tatastu dānavāḥ sarve yuddhānnirvṛtya sarvataḥ \|*  
*meruśṛṃgaṃ samāśritya ramyaṃ vāsaṃ pracakramuḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. All the Dānavas then retired from fighting. They resorted to the beautiful peak of Meru and decided to camp there.

## \|\| 1.119.68 \|\|

*vijayena samāyuktāstuṣṭiṃ ca paramāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*kathāścakruśca yuddhotthā yuddhaṃ tasya yathā bhavat \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Crowned with success in the battle, they became highly delighted. They recapitulated the incidents of the battle and began extolling how it took place.

## \|\| 1.119.69 \|\|

*devāścāpi hatotsāhāḥ prahāraiḥ kṣatavikṣatāḥ \|*  
*maṃtraṃ cakrurmitho bhūtvā bṛhaspatipuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The Devas lost all their enthusiasm on being utterly hit and wounded. They held discussion together in secret with Bṛhaspati as their leader:

## \|\| 1.119.70-71 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ dānavaiḥ sainyamasmākaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*vidhvastaṃ sunirutsāhamakṣamaṃ yuddhakarmaṇi \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tasmāttyaktvā pravekṣyāmaḥ purīṃ caivāmarāvatīm \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ yatra na syāddānavajaṃ bhayam \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. “Now our army has been turned away (defeated) by the Dānavas. It has been annihilated and rendered demoralised and incapable of fighting further. No vestige of enthusiasm for fighting remains in it now. Hence we shall abandon the city of Amarāvatī and enter the abode of Brahmā where there is no fear from the Dānavas.”

## \|\| 1.119.72 \|\|

*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā brahmalokaṃ tato gatāḥ \|*  
*śūnyāṃ śakrapurīṃ kṛtvā sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. All the Devas including Vāsava decided thus, evacuated the city of Śakra and went to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.119.73 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya dānavāste praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*śūnyāṃ śakrapurīṃ dṛṣṭvā viviśustadanaṃtaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The Dānavas got up in the morning and seeing the city of Śakra vacant entered it gladly.

## \|\| 1.119.74 \|\|

*atha śākre pade daityaṃ mahiṣaṃ saṃnidhāya ca \|*  
*praṇemustuṣṭisaṃyuktāścakruścaiva mahotsavam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. They installed the Daitya Mahiṣa in the post of Śakra. With great delight they bowed down to him and celebrated a great festival.

## \|\| 1.119.75 \|\|

*jagṛhuryajñabhāgāṃśca sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*devasthāneṣu sarveṣu devatā'bhimatāśca ye \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They partook of all the shares in the Yajñas that belonged to the heaven-dwellers. They occupied all the spots endearing to the Devas.

## Chapter 120 - The Origination of Kātyāyanī

## \|\| 1.120.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śakrādayo devā jitāste tu raṇājire \|*  
*mahiṣeṇa tato rājyaṃ trailokye'pi cakāra saḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatkiñcittriṣu lokeṣu sārabhūtaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*gajavājirathāśvādi sarvaṃ gṛhṇāti so'suraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*evaṃ pravartamānasya tasya devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*vadhārthaṃ militāścakruḥ kathā duḥkhasama nvitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Thus Śakra and the Devas were defeated in the battle by Mahiṣa. Then he ruled all over the three worlds. Whatever he saw in all the three worlds as important and substantially good, such as elephants, horses, chariots etc., that Asura appropriated for himself.

Even as he went on doing so, the Devas including Vāsava became all the more miserable. Meeting together they began to discuss ways and means for bringing about his death.

## \|\| 1.120.4 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ māhiṣaṃ sarvaṃ vyavahāraṃ mahotkaṭam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the meantime the excellent sage Nārada who had seen all the outrageous activities of Mahiṣa came there.

## \|\| 1.120.5 \|\|

*tataśca kathayāmāsa sarvaṃ teṣāṃ savista ram \|*  
*tasya saṃceṣṭitaṃ bhūri lokatrayaprapīḍanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He described in all details to them all the acts of harassment of the three worlds on his part.

## \|\| 1.120.6 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ mahākopo bhūya evābhyavardhata \|*  
*nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā tādṛglokakathodbhavam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing the words of Nārada regarding such atrocities of Mahiṣa inflicted on a universal scale, their anger which was already intense increased all the more.

## \|\| 1.120.7 \|\|

*teṣāṃ kopodbhavo gharmo vaktradvāreṇa niryayau \|*  
*yena diṅmaṃḍalaṃ sarvaṃ tatkṣaṇātkaluṣīkṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The heat generated by their cumulative anger issued forth through their mouths and the quarters became defiled (darkened) instantly.

## \|\| 1.120.8 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra kārtikeyaḥ samabhyayāt \|*  
*papraccha ca kimetaddhi devānāṃ kopakāraṇam \|*  
*yena kāluṣyatāṃ prāptaṃ dikcakraṃ sakalaṃ mune \|\| ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the meantime Kārttikeya came there and asked: “O sage, what is the cause of the anger of the Devas? The entire range of the quarters has become dark and foul.”

## \|\| 1.120.9 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*eteṣāṃ sāṃprataṃ skanda mayā vārtā niveditā \|*  
*trailokyaṃ dānavaiḥ sarvairyathā nītaṃ madotkaṭaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Nārada said:

9\. O Skanda, I have just now conveyed to these the news how everything was carried off by the arrogant Dānavas in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.120.10 \|\|

*strīratnamaśvaratnaṃ vā na kiṃcitkasyacidgṛhe \|*  
*te dṛṣṭvā mokṣayaṃti sma durnivāryā madotkaṭāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The demons are haughty and unthwartable. A jewel of a woman, a splendid house or anything fine in anyone’s house falling within their vision is never left alone.11

## \|\| 1.120.11 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kārtikeyasya viśeṣātsaṃprajāyata \|*  
*vaktradvāreṇa devānāṃ yathā kopaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11.On hearng this, a spasm of rage issued forth from the mouth of Kārttikeya just as the fury of the Devas did.

## \|\| 1.120.12 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jātā tatkopāṃte kumārikā \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā divyatejo'nvitā śubhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the meantime, from within that mass of rage a splendid virgin endowed with divine splendour and marked with all auspicious characteristic features arose.

## \|\| 1.120.13 \|\|

*kārtikeyasya kopena kope miśre divaukasām \|*  
*yasmājjātātra sā kanyā tasmātkātyāyanī smṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Since this virgin was evolved out of the rage of Kārttikeya getting mingled with that of the heaven-dwellers, she was remembered as Kātyāyanī.

## \|\| 1.120.14 \|\|

*tatastasyā dadau vajramāyudhaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*śaktiṃ skandaḥ sutīkṣṇāgrāṃ cāpaṃ devo janārdanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the Lord of the Devas gave her his weapon Vajra (thunderbolt), Skanda gave her the sharp pointed Śakti, and Lord Janārdana, the bow.

## \|\| 1.120.15 \|\|

*triśūlaṃ ca mahādevaḥ pāśaṃ ca varuṇaḥ svayam \|*  
*ādityaśca sitānbāṇāṃścaṃdramāścarma cottamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Mahādeva gave her the Triśūla (trident). Varuṇa gave his Pāśa (noose), Āditya sharp arrows and the Moon an excellent shield.

## \|\| 1.120.16 \|\|

*nistriṃśaṃ nirṛtistuṣṭa ulmukaṃ ca hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*vāyuśca cchurikāṃ tīkṣṇāṃ dhanadaḥ parighaṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The delighted Nirṛti gave the Nistriṃśa (sword) and Hutāśana (Fire-god) gave the firebrand. Vāyu gave the sharp Churikā (dagger) and Dhanada gave the Parigha (iron club).

## \|\| 1.120.17 \|\|

*daṇḍaṃ pretādhipo raudraṃ vadhāya suravidviṣām \|*  
*dvādaśaivaṃ samālokya sā'yudhāni dvijottamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Lord of Pretas (departed souls i.e. Yama) gave the Daṇḍa (baton) of terrific nature for the destruction of the enemies of the Suras. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the virgin saw these twelve weapons.

## \|\| 1.120.18 \|\|

*kātyāyanī tataścakre bhujadvādaśakaṃ tadā \|*  
*jagrāha ca drutaṃ tāni surāstrāṇi divaukasām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Kātyāyanī saw these twelve excellent weapons of the heaven-dwellers and assumed twelve hands and grasped them immediately.

## \|\| 1.120.19-20 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānsarvānsaṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhā \|*  
*yadarthaṃ vibudhaśreṣṭhāḥ sṛṣṭā tadbrūta mā ciram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ kāryaṃ kariṣyāmi yuṣmākaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mahiṣo dānavo raudraḥ samutpanno'tra sāṃpratam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then with evident delight as indicated by the rising hair, she spoke to them all: “O excellent Devas, tell me quickly why I have been created? I shall carry out all your tasks. There is no doubt about this.”

## \|\| 1.120.21 \|\|

*avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*muktvaikāṃ yoṣitaṃ tena tvamasmābhirvinirmitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

The Devas said:

The terrifying Dānava named Mahiṣa has come up (born) now.

21\. He cannot be killed by any living being and never indeed by human beings. Excepting a woman, none can kill him. Therefore, you have been created by us.

## \|\| 1.120.22 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ sāṃprataṃ gaccha viṃdhyākhyaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*tapastatra kuruṣvogra tejo yenābhivardhate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hence do go to the excellent mountain named Vindhya and perform a severe penance there whereby your refulgence can increase.

## \|\| 1.120.23 \|\|

*tatastu tejaḥsaṃyuktāṃ tvāṃ jñātvā vayameva hi \|*  
*agre dhṛtvā kariṣyāmo yuddhaṃ tena durātmanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After coming to know that you have become fully equipped with brilliance, we shall ourselves keep you in front and fight with that wicked-souled one.

## \|\| 1.120.24 \|\|

*tatastvacchastranirdagdhaḥ paṃcatvaṃ sa prayāsyati \|*  
*vayaṃ ca tridaśaiśvaryaṃ labhiṣyāmo hatadviṣaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then, consumed by the fire of your weapons, he will meet his death. With the enemies killed we will regain the lost prosperity and glory of Devas.

## Chapter 121 - Mahisāṣura Defeated

## \|\| 1.121.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*devānāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā tataḥ sā parameśvarī \|*  
*provāca vāhanaṃ kiṃciddevā yacchatu me drutam \|\| \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ siṃhaṃ dadau gaurī yānārthaṃ vikṛtānanam \|*  
*tamāruhya pratasthe sā tato viṃdhyaṃ nagaṃ prati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On hearing the words of the Devas, that great goddess said: “May the Devas give me a vehicle immediately.”

Thereupon, Gaurī gave her a hideous-faced lion as her vehicle. Then, riding on it she set off towards the Vindhya mountain.

## \|\| 1.121.3 \|\|

*tasyaikaṃ śṛṃgamāsthāya ramyaṃ śreṣṭhadrumānvitam \|*  
*phalapuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ latāmaṃḍapamaṃḍitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. She settled on one of its peaks. It was beautiful. It had excellent trees full of fruits and flowers. It appeared as though the peak was embellished with a pavilion of creepers.

## \|\| 1.121.4 \|\|

*tatastapo'karotsādhvī tīvravrataparāyaṇā \|*  
*saṃyamyendriyavargaṃ svaṃ dhyāyamānā maheśvaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the chaste lady observed severe vows and performed a penance. She controlled the group of her sense-organs and meditated upon Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.121.5 \|\|

*yathāyathā tapovṛddhistasyāḥ sañjāyate dvijāḥ \|*  
*tathā rūpaṃ ca kāṃtiśca śarīre prativardhate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. As and when her penance grew steadily, O Brāhmaṇas, the beauty and refulgence of her body went on increasing.

## \|\| 1.121.6 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāstatra daityeśakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*te tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vratopetāmatyadbhutavapurdha rām \|*  
*gatvā procuḥ svanāthasya mahiṣasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the meantime, the servants of the Lord of Daityas came there. On seeing a lady of wonderfully refulgent physical form engaged in the observance of Vratas, they went and reported it to their Lord, the wicked-souled Mahiṣa.

## \|\| 1.121.7 \|\|

*cārā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhramamāṇairdharāpṛṣṭhe dṛṣṭā'pūrvā kumārikā \|*  
*vindhyācale'dya cāsmābhirbhujairdvādaśabhiryutā \|*  
*nānāśastradharairdīptaiścarmacchāditagātrakā \|\| 7 \|\|*

The spies said:

7\. As we were roaming about on the surface of the earth we saw an extraordinary girl on the Vindhya mountain. She had twelve brilliant hands holding different kinds of weapons. She had covered her body with a hide.

## \|\| 1.121.8 \|\|

*na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī nāgakanyakā \|*  
*tādṛgrūpā purā'smābhiḥ kāciddṛṣṭā nitambinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. No lady of (such) beautiful buttocks like hers having such an exquisite form has been seen by us before. She does not belong to the category of Devas, Gandharvas, Asuras, or Nāgas.

## \|\| 1.121.9 \|\|

*na vidmo yannimittaṃ sā tapaścakre yaśasvinī \|*  
*svargakāmā'rthakāmā vā patikāmātha vā vibho \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. We do not know what she was performing the penance for. The lady of great reputation may be desirous of heaven, or she may be covetous of wealth or she may be desirous of a befitting husband, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.121.10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā mahiṣo dānavādhipaḥ \|*  
*kāmadeva vaśaṃ prāptaḥ śravaṇādapi tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

10\. On hearing their words, Mahiṣa, the Lord of Dānavas, was overwhelmed by Kāmadeva (god of Love) at the very moment he heard them.

## \|\| 1.121.11 \|\|

*tatastānagrataḥ kṛtvā sainyena mahatā nvitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma kautukāviṣṭo yatrāste sā tu kanyakā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then, keeping them in front and accompanied by a great army he went to the place where the girl was present. He was very much swayed with eagerness.

## \|\| 1.121.12 \|\|

*yathā mṛtyukṛte mandaḥ śṛgālaḥ siṃhavallabhām \|*  
*vane suptāṃ suviśvastāṃ sarvathāpya kutobhayām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It was as though for the sake of meeting sure death, a dull-witted jackal was approaching the beloved of a lion sleeping without any fear from any quarter quite complacently in a forest.

## \|\| 1.121.13 \|\|

*tasyāḥ saṃdarśanādeva tataḥ kāmaśarairhataḥ \|*  
*sa dānavapradhānaśca tatkṣaṇādeva saddvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Merely at the very sight of that goddess the leader of Dānavas was struck with the arrows of Kāma instantaneously, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.121.14 \|\|

*atha prāha priyaṃ vākyamekākī tatpuraḥsthitaḥ \|*  
*dhṛtvā dūrataresainyaṃ tasyā rūpeṇa mohitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the demon who had become infatuated by her beauty and utterly deluded, kept the army at a distance and stood alone before her. He spoke to her sweetly:

## \|\| 1.121.15-19 \|\|

*viruddhaṃ yauvanasyaitadvrataṃ te cāruhāsini \|*  
*tasmādetatparityaktvā trailokyasvāminī bhava \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ahaṃ hi mahiṣo nāma dānavendro yadi śrutaḥ \|*  
*mayā yena sahasrākṣo dvandvayuddhe vinirjitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*trelokyaṃ sakalaṃ mahyaṃ sāṃprataṃ ca vaśe sthitam \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ bhava suśroṇi bhāryā mama suvallabhā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sahasraṃ mama bhāryāṇāmanyadasti suśobhanam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ te'dya bhṛtyatvaṃ sāṃprataṃ praka riṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ahaṃ cāpi tavātyaṃtaṃ dāsabhāvaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*vartayiṣyāmi suśroṇi pradattvā'śeṣasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. “O lady of sweet smiles, this Vrata of yours is inconsistent with your youth. Hence, give this up and become the mistress of the three worlds.

I do not know whether you have heard about me. I am the Lord of Dānavas named Mahiṣa. It was by me that the thousand-eyed Lord Indra was defeated in a duel.

The entire area of the three worlds stays under my control now. Hence, O lady of excellent buttocks, become my extremely favourite wife..

I have already a thousand wives who are very splendid. All of them shall render menial service unto you now.

O lady of excellent lips, I shall hand over to you all my riches and shall behave like your very humble servant.”

## \|\| 1.121.20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ sā parameśvarī \|*  
*provāca bhartsamānā taṃ kopasaṃraktalocanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sūta said:

20\. On hearing his words the great goddess rebuked him and spoke thus with her eyes red due to anger:

## \|\| 1.121.21-22 \|\|

*dhigdhikpāpasamācāra kumāravratadhāriṇīm \|*
