*kāmopahatacittātmā kiṃ māmitthaṃ prabhā ṣase \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tava vadhārthāya nirmitā vibudhottamaiḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvāṃ nāśayiṣyāmi smareṣṭaṃ yaddhṛdi sthitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. “Fie upon you, fie upon you, O demon of sinful activities! Your mind is assailed by lust. Why do you speak like this to me observing the vow of virginity?

I have been created by the excellent Devas for the purpose of killing you. I shall hence destroy you. Remember the ardent desire lurking in your heart.”

## \|\| 1.121.23 \|\|

*mahiṣa uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ tadvarārohe yuktā syācca kumārikā \|*  
*prārthanīyā bhavedatra sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ yataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Mahiṣa said:

23\. If it is so, O beautiful lady, it is but proper that a virgin should be sought after by all living beings.

## \|\| 1.121.24 \|\|

*svargārthaṃ kriyate dharmastapaśca varavarṇini \|*  
*yena bhogāḥ prabhuñjaṃti ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lady of excellent complexion, virtuous rites and penances are performed for the sake of heavenly pleasures, whereby people enjoy human as well as divine pleasures.

## \|\| 1.121.25 \|\|

*tasmāddehi mamātmānaṃ gāṃdharveṇa suśobhane \|*  
*vivāhena yato'nyeṣāṃ sa pradhānaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Therefore, O highly splendid one, surrender yourself to me through the Gāndharva form of marital alliance because it has been glorified as more important than other types of marriage alliance.

## \|\| 1.121.26 \|\|

*evaṃ pravadatastasya sā devī krodhamūrchitā \|*  
*tadvaktrāṃtaṃ samuddiśya śaraṃ cikṣepa sa kṣaṇāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even as he was saying thus the goddess became very furious and in an instant discharged an arrow aiming at his mouth.

## \|\| 1.121.27-30 \|\|

*viveśa vadanaṃ tasya valmīkaṃ pannago yathā \|*  
*atha tairmārgagaṇairviddhaḥ sa vaktrāṃtānnadaṃstataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*susrāva rudhiraṃ bhūri gairikaṃ parvato yathā \|*  
*tataḥ kopaparītātmā nivṛttyātha śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*svasainyaṃ tvarito bheje kāmena ca vaśī kṛtaḥ \|*  
*provāca sainikānsarvānduṣṭā strīyaṃ pragṛhyatām \|*  
*yathā na tyajati prāṇānprahārairjarjarīkṛtā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*eṣā mama na sandehaḥ priyā bhāryā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yadi no śastrapātena paṃcatvamupayāsyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. In the manner of a serpent that enters an anthill the arrow pierced his mouth. On being hit with the arrows he cried aloud. Much blood flowed out of his mouth like the red chalk that flows from a mountain in liquid form. With anger overpowering him, he slowly receded and hurriedly resorted to the presence of his vast army. Completely under the control of Kāma he ordered thus to his soldiers: “May this wicked woman be captured. Although she may be shattered with blows see that the life does not leave her. If she does not fall dead due to the shower of arrows, she will certainly became my dear wife. There is no doubt about it.”

## \|\| 1.121.31 \|\|

*evamuktāstadā tena dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*dudruvuḥ sammukhāstasyā muñcanto niśitāñcharān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On being told thus by him the Dānavas, foolishly arrogant of their ability to fight, rushed at her discharging sharp arrows.

## \|\| 1.121.32-33 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devī sā dṛṣṭvā tānupasthitān \|*  
*yuddhāya kṛtasaṃkalpāṃstarjataśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tatastu līlayā devī muktā tīkṣṇānmahāśarān \|*  
*tānsarvāṃstāḍayāmāsa sarvamarmasu tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In the meantime the goddess observed that they had arrived with a firm determination to fight. Consequently they were threatening and taunting her again and again. Thereupon the goddess discharged sharp arrows and struck them instantly in all their vulnerable joints.

## \|\| 1.121.34 \|\|

*atha tīkṣṇaiḥ śarairdaityā nihatā dānavāstathā \|*  
*eke paṃcatvamāpannā gatāścānya itastataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hit by those sharp arrows some of those Daityas and Dānavas died and others were made to flee in different directions.

## \|\| 1.121.35 \|\|

*tataḥ sainyaṃ samālokya tadbhagnaṃ ca tayā raṇe \|*  
*kopāviṣṭastato daityaḥ svayaṃ tāṃ samupādravat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On observing that his army has been shattered by her in the battle the Daitya became furious and himself rushed at her.

## \|\| 1.121.36 \|\|

*yacchañchṛṃgaprahārāṃśca tasyāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ \|*  
*garjitaṃ vidadhaccograṃ śāradābhrasamaṃ muhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Rumbling and roaring frequently like and autumnal cloud he hit her hundreds and thousands of times with his horns.

## \|\| 1.121.37 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devī sāṭṭahāsakṛtasvanā \|*  
*trailokyavivaraṃ sarvaṃ yacchabdena prapūritam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the meantime the goddess laughed boisterously making the entire space of the three worlds filled therewith.

## \|\| 1.121.38 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyā hasaṃtyāśca vaktrāntādatha niryayuḥ \|*  
*puliṃdāḥ śabarā mlechāstathānye'raṇyavāsinaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus, when she laughed, Pulindas, Śabaras, Mlecchas and other forest-dwellers issued forth from her mouth.

## \|\| 1.121.39 \|\|

*śakāśca yavanāścaiva śataśaśtu vapurdharā \|*  
*varma sthagitagātrāśca yamadūtā ivāpare \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Śakas and Yavanas too came out thus in their hundreds of physical forms (bodies) covered with armour. They appeared like messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 1.121.40 \|\|

*te procurdevi no brūhi yena sṛṣṭā vayaṃ kṣitau \|*  
*kāryeṇa kriyate kṛtsnaṃ yena śīghraṃ varānane \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. They spoke: “O fair lady, for what purpose have we been created? Do tell us, O lady of excellent countenance, so that it can be carried out quickly.”

## \|\| 1.121.41 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*etānasya suduṣṭasya sainikānbalagarvitān \|*  
*sūdayadhvaṃ drutaṃ vākyādasmadīyādyathecchayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

Devī said:

41\. At our instance slay, as you please, these soldiers of this evil fellow. They are foolishly proud due to their inordinate strength. Slay them quickly.

## \|\| 1.121.42 \|\|

*atha te tadvacaḥ śrutvā valgaṃto'sidhanurddharāḥ \|*  
*daiteyabalamuddiśya dudruvurvegamāśritāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing her words, they danced and pranced holding their bows and swords. With great speed they rushed at the army of the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.121.43 \|\|

*tatasteṣāṃ mahadyuddhaṃ mitho jajñe sudāruṇam \|*  
*nātmīyaṃ na paraṃ tatra kenacijjñā yate kvacit \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then a great and very terrible battle ensued between the two armies wherein the soldiers of the same side could not be distinguished from those of the others.

## \|\| 1.121.44 \|\|

*atha te dānavāḥ sarve yodhairdevīsamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*bhagnā vyāpāditāścānye prahārairjarjarīkṛtāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then all those Dānavas were shattered and annihilated by the soldiers originating from the goddess. Others were wounded and disabled by their blows.

## \|\| 1.121.45 \|\|

*tato bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahiṣaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*tāmuvāca krudhā devīṃ vacanaiḥ paruṣākṣaraiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing his army broken up, the infuriated Mahiṣa spoke angrily to the goddess these harsh words:

## \|\| 1.121.46 \|\|

*āḥ pāpe strīti matvādya na hatāsi mayā yudhi \|*  
*tasmātpaśya prahāraṃ me tattvaṃ budhyasi nānyathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “O sinful woman, you were not killed by me in the battle solely on the consideration that you are a woman. So, see how I can strike. Otherwise you will not understand the reality.”

## \|\| 1.121.47 \|\|

*evamuktvā viśeṣeṇa prahārānsa vicikṣipe \|*  
*viṣāṇābhyāṃ mahāvego bhartsayāno muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After saying thus and reviling her frequently, he butted against her with special force with his horns.

## \|\| 1.121.48 \|\|

*tato'bhyāśagataṃ dṛṣṭvā sā devī dānavaṃ ca tam \|*  
*ārurohātha vegena pṛṣṭhideśena kopataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On seeing the Dānava close by, the goddess rode on him from behind furiously.

## \|\| 1.121.49 \|\|

*tataścukrośa daityo'sau vyomamārgaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhyāstalena nirbhinno rudhiraughapariplutaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Shattered at the hind quarters the Daitya was fully drenched with blood. He rose up into the sky and roared loudly.

## \|\| 1.121.50 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare siṃhaḥ sa tasyā jyotisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha paścime bhāge daṃṣṭrāgrairniśitaiḥ krudhā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In the meantime, a lion came out from her refulgence and seized the hind part (of his body) angrily with his curved fangs.

## \|\| 1.121.51 \|\|

*tato niścalatāṃ prāptaḥ pādākrāṃtaśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*akarodbhairavānnādānna śaktaścalituṃ padam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Dānava became motionless as he was caught under the feet (of the lion). He could not even take a step ahead. He gave out terrific roars.

## \|\| 1.121.52 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*vyomasthāstāṃ tadā procurdevīṃ harṣasamanvitāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the meantime, all the Devas, including Vāsava came there and stood in the sky. Joyously they spoke to the goddess:

## \|\| 1.121.53 \|\|

*etasya śirasaśchedaṃ śīghraṃ kuru sureśvari \|*  
*khaṅgenānena tīkṣṇena yāvanno yāti cānyataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “O goddess of Suras, cut off the head (of this demon) with this sharp-edged sword so that he cannot go elsewhere.”

## \|\| 1.121.54 \|\|

*sā śrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ devī kopasamanvitā \|*  
*khaḍgaṃ vyāpārayāmāsa kaṃṭhe tasyātipīvare \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On hearing their words, the goddess became very angry. She wielded the sword and hit his stout neck.

## \|\| 1.121.55 \|\|

*sa tena khaḍgaghātena kaṃṭhaḥ pīno'pi niṣṭhuraḥ \|*  
*dvidhā jajñe'tha daityasya dadhattuṣṭiṃ divaukasām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On being struck with the sword the neck of the Daitya though stout and tough split into two causing the delight of the heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.121.56 \|\|

*dvādaśārkapratīkāśo vaktrāṃtaścarmakhaḍgadhṛk \|*  
*bhartsayaṃstāṃ mahādevīṃ khaḍgodyatakarāṃ tadā \|*  
*khaḍgaṃ vyāpārayangātre tasyā bālārkasannibham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It had the splendour of twelve suns. The mouth held within it the shield as well as the sword. (The demon) began to revile the great goddess who had lifted up her hand with the sword. He then made the sword resembling the morning sun strike her body.

## \|\| 1.121.57 \|\|

*tataḥ keśeṣu cādhāya yāvattasyāpi cikṣipe \|*  
*prahāraṃ gātranāśāya tāvadūce sa dānavaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then (the goddess) caught hold of his hair and was about to strike him to destroy his body. Then the Dānava said:

## \|\| 1.121.58 \|\|

*dānava uvāca \|*  
*jaya devi jayāciṃtye jaya sarvasureśvari \|*  
*jaya sarvagate devi jaya sarvajanapriye \|\| 58 \|\|*

The Danava said:

58\. Be victorious, O goddess; be victorious, O omnipresent goddess of Suras, be victorious. Be victorious, O omnipresent goddess. Be victorious, O goddess, O favourite of all the people.

## \|\| 1.121.59 \|\|

*jaya kāmaprade nityaṃ jaya trailokyasundari \|*  
*jaya trailokya rakṣārthamudyate hyakutobhaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O bestower of desired things, be always victorious. Be victorious, O most beautiful lady in all the three worlds. Be victorious, O goddess endeavouring to protect all the three worlds. Be victorious, O goddess who have no fear from anywhere.

## \|\| 1.121.60 \|\|

*jaya devi kṛtānaṃde jaya daityavināśini \|*  
*jaya kleśacchide kāṃte jayābhaktavimohade \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Be victorious, O goddess who cause delight. Be victorious, O destroyer of the Daityas. Be victorious, O lustrous one who destroy sufferings. Be victorious, O bestower of delusion on the non-devotees.

## \|\| 1.121.61 \|\|

*tvaṃ sṛṣṭistvaṃ varā devī tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ sarasvatī \|*  
*tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You are the creation. You are the excellent goddess. You are the goddess of fortune. You are Sarasvatī. You are Svāhā; you are Svadhā, Tuṣṭi (satisfaction), Puṣṭi (nourishment). You are Medhā (intellect). You are Dhṛti (fortitude). You are Kṣamā (forgiveness).

## \|\| 1.121.62 \|\|

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me prāṇānrakṣa dayāṃ kuru \|*  
*praṇatasya sudīnasya hīnasya ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Hence accord favour unto me. Protect my life. Take pity on me as I have bowed down, as I am bereft of everything and extremely wretched too.

## \|\| 1.121.63 \|\|

*ahaṃ durvāsasā śapto hiraṇyākṣasuto balī \|*  
*mahiṣatvaṃ samānītastvayā devī vimokṣitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. I am the powerful son of Hiraṇyākṣa. I have been cursed by Durvāsas and turned into a Mahiṣa (buffalo). But, O goddess, I have been liberated by you.

## \|\| 1.121.64 \|\|

*tasmāddarpaḥ pramukto'dya mayā dānavasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*kiṃkaratvaṃ prayāsyāmi sāṃprataṃ te sureśvari \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Hence the haughtiness due to being a Dānava has been got rid of today. I shall be your servant now, O goddess of Suras.

## \|\| 1.121.65 \|\|

*jaya sarvagate devi sarvaduṣṭavināśini \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Be victorious, O goddess present in all, O destroyer of all wicked ones.

## \|\| 1.121.66 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kṛpaṇaṃ sā sureśvarī \|*  
*kṛpāviṣṭā'bravīdvākyaṃ tato vyomasthitānsurān \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On hearing these piteous words of the Daitya, the goddess of Suras was overcome with compassion. She then addressed these words to the Suras who stood in the firmament:

## \|\| 1.121.67-68 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi dayā jātā mamainaṃ prati he surāḥ \|*  
*tasmānnāhaṃ haniṣyāmi dānavaṃ dīnajalpakam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*vimukhaṃ khaḍgaśastraṃ ca tavāsmīti pravādinam \|*  
*api me pitṛhaṃtāraṃ na hanyāṃ ripumāhave \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. “What shall I do, O Suras? I have been moved with pity for him. Hence I will not kill the Dānava who is prattling piteously. I will not kill an enemy in the battle even if he be the murderer of my father, should he turn his face (back), leave off swords and weapons and aver ‘I am yours.’”

## \|\| 1.121.69 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|\| \|*  
*na cedasi ca deveśi tvamenaṃ dānavādhamam \|*  
*nāśayiṣyati tatkṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 69 \|\|*

The Devas said:

69\. O goddess of Devas, if you do not kill this base Dānava, he will surely destroy all the three worlds consisting of the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 1.121.70 \|\|

*eṣa vyarthaḥśramaḥ sarvastathāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tava saṃbhūtisaṃbhūtastava kleśastathā'khilaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. In that case all our efforts regarding your creation would be in vain. So also will be all your painful efforts.

## \|\| 1.121.71 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*nāhamenaṃ haniṣyāmi tyajiṣyāmi tathā'marāḥ \|*  
*enaṃ kacagrahaṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyāmi sarvadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

Devī said:

71\. O immortal ones, I will neither kill this one nor will I leave him off. I will catch hold of his hair and hold him always.

## \|\| 1.121.72 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābhāge yuktamuktaṃ tvayā vacaḥ \|*  
*etaddhi yujyate kartuṃ kāle'smiṃstridaśeśvari \|\| 72 \|\|*

The Devas said:

72\. O highly esteemed one! Excellent! Excellent! The proper word (decision) has been uttered by you. O goddess of Devas, indeed this alone is the proper thing to do on this occasion.

## \|\| 1.121.73 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ martyaloke tvaṃ rūpametatsamāśritā \|*  
*śastrodyatakarā raudrā mahiṣopari saṃsthitā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Do be in the mortal world now resorting to this terrible form with the weapons lifted up in the hands and seated on the buffalo. You will receive here highest adoration.

## \|\| 1.121.74 \|\|

*avāpsyasi parāṃ pūjāṃ durlabhā mamarairapi \|*  
*yastvāmetena rūpeṇa saṃsthitāṃ pūjayiṣyati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. One who propitiates you present here in this form (will attain) fruits rarely achieved even by the immortals.

## \|\| 1.121.75 \|\|

*tvamasya saṃgato bhāvi vikhyātā viṃdhyavāsinī \|*  
*kiṃ te vā bahunoktena śṛṇu saṃkṣepato vacaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. You shall be well-known as Vindhyavāsinī in association with this Demon. Of what avail is speaking too much! Listen to the words in brief.

## \|\| 1.121.76 \|\|

*asmadīyaṃ paraṃ tathyaṃ sarvalokahitāvaham \|*  
*pārthivānāṃ tvadāyattaṃ balaṃ devi bhaviṣyati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Our words will be the truth and beneficial unto all the worlds. O goddess, the strength of kings shall depend on you.

## \|\| 1.121.77-78 \|\|

*yuddhakāle samutpanne bhaktānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*prasthānaṃ vā praveśaṃ ca yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tvāṃ smṛtvā praṇipatyātha pūjayitvā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃpatsyate siddhiḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*iha kāpuruṣasyāpi kiṃ punaḥ subhaṭasya ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Especially when a time of war comes, the kings who are your devotees shall gain strength through you. There is no doubt about this.

If any man undertakes any compaign or enters into any undertaking after recollecting you, bowing down to you and offering you special worship, he will always achieve success in every activity. Even a coward will have success. All the more so in the case of an excellent warrior.

## \|\| 1.121.79-80 \|\|

*āśvinasya site pakṣe navamyāṃ cāṣṭamīdine \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati yo marttyastvāṃ sadbhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tasya saṃvatsaraṃ yāvatsamagraṃ surasundari \|*  
*na bhaviṣyati vai rogo na bhayaṃ na parābhavaḥ \|*  
*nāpamṛtyurna caurādi samudbhūta upadravaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. If any man worships you on the eighth or ninth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Āśvina with excellent devotional fervour, O most beautiful lady of Suras, he will never meet defeat, fear or ailment for a full year thereafter. He will never have premature or accidental death nor the harassment and torment due to thefts.

## \|\| 1.121.81 \|\|

*\|sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha te devāstāṃ devīṃ harṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*anujñātāstayā jagmuḥ svāṃ purīmamarāvatīm \|\| 81 \|\|*

Sūta said:

81\. After saying thus to the goddess, those delighted Devas went to their city Amarāvatī on being permitted by her.

## \|\| 1.121.82 \|\|

*tatra gatvā cirātprāpya svaṃ rājyaṃ pākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*pālayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭastrailokyaṃ hatakaṭakam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. After going there and having regained his realm after a long time, Pākaśāsana joyously protected the three worlds after the eradication of all thorns (obstacles).

## \|\| 1.121.83 \|\|

*lokāśca sukhasaṃpannāḥ sarve jātā stataḥ param \|*  
*yajñabhāgabhujo devā bhūyo jātā jagattraye \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. All the worlds were blessed with happiness thereafter. Devas once again became regular partakers of their shares in Yajñas in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.121.84 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ ca sā devī trailokye khyātimāgatā \|*  
*sarvakṣetreṣu tīrtheṣu sthāneṣu ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thereafter, that goddess became well-known in all the three worlds, in all the holy spots and Tīrthas in particular.

## \|\| 1.121.85 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jātaḥ surathonāma bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*ānartastena sadbhaktyā kṣetre'traiva vinirmitā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. In the meantime, Suratha, a king of Ānarta, was born. She was installed by him in this holy spot with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.121.86 \|\|

*yastāṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā caitrāṣṭamyāṃ site'hani \|*  
*sa pumānvatsaraṃ yāvatkṛtārthaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A person who devoutly visits her on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra shall undoubtedly be blessed for the period of a full year.

## Chapter 122 - Creation of Kedāra

## \|\| 1.122.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yathā sa nihato devyā mahiṣākhyo danūttamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sāṃprataṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm \|*  
*kedārasaṃbhavāṃ puṇyāṃ tāṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\| \|*  
*kedāraḥ śrūyate sūta gaṃgādvāre himācale \|*  
*sa kathaṃ ceha saṃprāptaḥ sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

Suta said:

1-3. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything I was asked has been narrated to you all, as to how that excellent Dānava named Mahiṣa was killed by the goddess.

Now I shall tell the sin-destroying story concerning the meritorious Kedāra. Listen to it with great concentration and mental purity.

## \|\| 1.122.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etatsatyaṃ girau tasminsvayaṃbhūḥ saṃsthitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*paraṃ tatra vaseddevo yāvanmāsāṣṭakaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

O Sūta, it is heard that Kedāra is in Gaṅgādvāra on the Himālaya mountain. How did it come to be here? Narrate everything in detail.

Sūta said:

4\. It is true that the Self-born Lord is present on that mountain. But, O Brāhmaṇas, the Lord stays there only for eight months.

## \|\| 1.122.5 \|\|

*yāvadgharmaśca varṣā ca tāvattatra vasetprabhuḥ \|*  
*śītakāle punaścātra kṣetre saṃtiṣṭhate sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. During summer and rainy season, the Lord stays there. But during winter, he is always stationed in this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.122.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tatkāryaṃ vasedyena kṣetre māsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*himācale yathaivāṣṭau sūtaputra vadasva naḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:

6\. O Sūtaputra, what is that purpose for which the Lord stays in this holy spot for four months and on Himācala for eight months? Do tell us.

## \|\| 1.122.7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuvasyādau manordaityo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣo mahātejāstapovīryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7\. Formerly, in the beginning of the Manvantara of the first Manu named Svāyaṃbhuva, there was Hiraṇyākṣa, a Daitya of inordinate strength. He was of great lustre and possessed the power of penance.

## \|\| 1.122.8 \|\|

*tairvyāptaṃ jagadetaddhi nirasya tridaśādhipam \|*  
*yajña bhāgāścadevānāṃ hṛtā vīryaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He (and his associates) encompassed the whole world. After ousting the overlord of Devas they appropriated the shares of Devas in Yajñas by means of their valour.

## \|\| 1.122.9 \|\|

*atha śakraḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ gaṃgādvāraṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*tapastepe suduḥkhārto rājyaśrīparivarjitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereupon, Śakra took refuge in Gaṅgādvāra along with the Suras. In his excessive distress due to the loss of royal glory, he performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.122.10-11 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya tapastīvraṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*māhiṣaṃ rūpamāsthāya niścakrāma dharātalāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*svayameva mahādevastataḥ śakramuvāca ha \|*  
*kedārayāmi me śīghraṃ brūhi sarvaṃ surottama \|*  
*daityānāmatha sarveṣāṃ rūpeṇānena vāsava \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Even as the noble-souled one performed the severe penance thus, Mahādeva himself assumed the form of a buffalo and came out of the surface of the earth. He then said to Śakra: “Whom should I tear off (ke=kān, dārayāmi) from the entire hosts of the Daityas by means of this form? O Vāsava, O most excellent one among Suras, tell me quickly.”

## \|\| 1.122.12 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣo mahādaityaḥ subāhurvakra kandharaḥ \|*  
*triśṛṃgo lohitākṣaśca paṃcaitāndāraya prabho \|*  
*hatairetairhataṃ sarvaṃ dānavānāmasaṃśayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Indra said:

12\. O Lord, tear asunder these five Dānavas, namely Hiraṇyākṣa the great Daitya, Subāhu, Vakrakandhara, Triśṛṅga and Lohitākṣa. If these are killed, undoubtedly all the Dānavas are annihilated.

## \|\| 1.122.13 \|\|

*kimanyaiḥ kṛpaṇairdhvastairyaiḥ kiṃcinnātra sidhyati \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaśrutvā bhagavāṃstūrṇamabhyagāt \|*  
*yatra dānavamukhyo'sau hiraṇyākṣo mahābalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Of what use is the destruction of the other men and wretched ones? Nothing can be achieved thereby.

On hearing those words, the Lord hastened to that place where the important Dānava, the extremely powerful Hiraṇyākṣa, was present.

## \|\| 1.122.14 \|\|

*atha taṃ dūrato dṛṣṭvā mahiṣaṃ parvatopamam \|*  
*āyātaṃ raudrarūpeṇa dānavāḥ sarvataśca te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All those Dānavas saw from a distance the buffalo comparable to a mountain coming on in a frightening form.

## \|\| 1.122.15 \|\|

*tato jaghnuśca pāṣāṇairlaguḍaiśca tathāpare \|*  
*kṣveḍitāsphoṭitāṃścakrustathānye balagarvitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Some of them hit him with stones and others with sticks. Still others in the arrogance of their strength slapped and clapped their arms shouting battle cries.

## \|\| 1.122.16 \|\|

*athavamanya tāndevaḥ prahāraṃ līlayā dadau \|*  
*yatrāste dānavendro'sau caturbhiḥ sacivaiḥ saha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Lord disregarded them all. He sportingly advanced to that place where the leading Dānava was present along with his four ministers.

## \|\| 1.122.17 \|\|

*tataḥ śastraṃ samudyamya yāvaddhāvati sammukhaḥ \|*  
*tāvacchṛṃgaprahāreṇa sonayadyamasādanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even as he lifted up the weapon and rushed against him, the Lord despatched him to the abode of Yama hitting him with his horns.

## \|\| 1.122.18 \|\|

*hatvā taṃ sacivānpaścātsubāhupramukhāṃśca tān \|*  
*jaghāna hanyamāno'pi samantāddānavaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After killing him, the Lord killed the ministers, the most important one among whom was Subāhu. Of course the other Dānavas struck him from all sides.

## \|\| 1.122.19 \|\|

*na tasya lagate kvāpi śastraṃ gātre kathaṃcana \|*  
*yatnato'pi visṛṣṭaṃ ca labdhalakṣaiḥ prahāribhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Dānavas struck with great effort and their aim was perfect. Yet none of the weapons had any serious effect at all on the body of the Lord.

## \|\| 1.122.20 \|\|

*evaṃ paṃca pradhānāstānhatvā daityānmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhūyo jagāma taṃ deśaṃ yatra śakro vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*abravīcca prahaṣṭātmā tataḥ śakraṃ taponvitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After killing the five important Daityas thus, Maheśvara once again went to the place where Śakra was waiting. With great delight in his mind, he spoke to Śakra fully equipped with the power of penance:

## \|\| 1.122.21-22 \|\|

*mayā te nihatāḥ paṃca dānavā ye tvayeritāḥ \|*  
*tasmāttrailokyarājyaṃ svaṃ bhūya eva samācara \|\| 21 \|\|*

*matto'nyadapi deveśa varaṃ prārthaya vāṃchitam \|*  
*kailāsaśikharaṃ yena gacchāmi tvarayā'nvitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. “Those five Dānavas mentioned by you have been killed by me. Hence enjoy once again the kingdom of the three worlds. O Lord of Devas, do choose from me another boon too that is desired by you so that I can hurry back to the peak of Kailāsa.”

## \|\| 1.122.23 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*anenaiva hi rūpeṇa tiṣṭha tvaṃ cātra śaṃkara \|*  
*trailokyarakṣaṇārthāya dharmāya ca śivāya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

Indra said:

23\. O Śaṅkara, do stay here in this very form to accomplish protection to the three worlds and preservation of virtue and welfare.

## \|\| 1.122.24 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*etadrūpaṃ mayā śakra kṛtaṃ tasya vadhāya vai \|*  
*avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yatonyeṣāṃ mayā hataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

24\. O Śakra, this form was assumed by me in order to slay him (Hiraṇyākṣa) since he could not be killed by other living beings. He has now been killed by me.

## \|\| 1.122.25 \|\|

*tasmādatraiva te vākyātsthāsyāmi sura sattama \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa mokṣadaḥ sarvadehinām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hence, at your instance, O most excellent one among Suras, I shall stay here along with this very form accordingly, for giving salvation unto all embodied ones.

## \|\| 1.122.26 \|\|

*evamuktvā virūpākṣaścakre kuṃḍaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ susvādukṣīravatpriyam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After saying thus, Lord Virūpākṣa (Śiva) made a great Kuṇḍa with water resembling pure crystal and pleasing and tasty like milk.

## \|\| 1.122.27 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca devendraṃ meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ bhagavāṃstripurātakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then Lord Tripurāntaka spoke to Devendra in a voice majestic like the rumbling sound of cloud, even as all the Devas were listening:

## \|\| 1.122.28-30 \|\|

*yo māṃ dṛṣṭvā śucirbhūtvā kuṃḍametatprapaśyati \|*  
*triḥ pītvā vāmasavyena dvābhyāṃ caiva tato jalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*karābhyāṃ sa pumānnūnaṃ tārayecca kulatrayam \|*  
*api pāpasamācāraṃ narake'pi vyava sthitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vāmena mātṛkaṃ pakṣaṃ dakṣiṇenātha paitṛkam \|*  
*ubhābhyāmatha cātmānaṃ karābhyāṃ madvaco yathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. “A person should remain pure and visit me and this Kuṇḍa. He should drink the water thereof first by the left hand, then by the right hand and again with both the hands. That man shall certainly redeem the entire family even if it be sinful in its activities or even if it has fallen into hell. He shall redeem the members of his mother’s family by the act of drinking the water with the left hand, his father’s family with the right and himself with both the hands. Everything shall be in accordance with my words.”

## \|\| 1.122.31 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*ahamāgatya nityaṃ tvāṃ svargādvṛṣabhavāhana \|*  
*atrasthaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi pāsyāmi ca tathodakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

Indra said:

31\. O Bull-vehicled One, always (everyday) I shall come from heaven and worship you stationed here. I shall also drink the holy water.

## \|\| 1.122.32 \|\|

*ke dārayāmi yatproktaṃ tvayā mahiṣarūpiṇā \|*  
*kedāra iti nāmnā tvaṃ tataḥ khyāto bhaviṣyasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Since you said when you were in the form of a buffalo, “ke dārayāmī” (vv 10, 11), you shall become well-known by the name Kedāra.

## \|\| 1.122.33 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ kuruṣe śakra tato daityabhayaṃ na te \|*  
*bhaviṣyati paraṃ tejo gātre saṃpatsyate'khilam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

33\. O Śakra, if you do so, you will never have any fear from Daityas. A great lustre will envelop your body.

## \|\| 1.122.34 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sahasrākṣastataḥ prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*tadarthaṃ nirmayāmāsa sādhvālokaṃ manoharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On being told thus, the Thousand-eyed One caused an excellent mansion to be built there. It was extremely beautiful to see and pleasing to the mind.

## \|\| 1.122.35 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ devamanumantrya tataḥ param \|*  
*jagāma nijamāvāsaṃ meruśṛṃgāgrasaṃsthitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he bowed down to that Lord, took leave of him and went to his own abode stationed on the top of a peak of Meru.

## \|\| 1.122.36 \|\|

*tataścāgatya nityaṃ sa svargāddevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*kedārasya subhaktyāḍhyāṃ pūjāṃ cakre samāhitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then he used to come there everyday from heaven. Endowed with great devotion to Kedāra he performed the adoration of the Trident-bearing Lord with great mental concentration.

## \|\| 1.122.37 \|\|

*mantrodakaṃ ca triḥ pītvā yayau brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya yāvattatra samāyayau \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He drank the holy water thrice and went away, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. After some time, he returned to the place.

## \|\| 1.122.38 \|\|

*tāvaddhimena tatsarvaṃ gireḥ śṛṃgaṃ prapūritam \|*  
*tacca kuṇḍaṃ sa devaśca prāsādena samanvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. At that time he saw the entire peak of the mountain covered with snow. The holy Kuṇḍa, the Lord and the entire palace too was covered with snow.

## \|\| 1.122.39 \|\|

*tato duḥkhaparītātmā bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ diśaṃ praṇipatyoccairjagāma nijamaṃdiram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He was miserable. With great devotion, he simply bowed down (uttering salutation) in loud voice in that direction and went back to his abode.

## \|\| 1.122.40 \|\|

*evamāgacchatastasya gataṃ māsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*apaśyato mahādevaṃ didṛkṣāgatacetasaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40 Four months elapsed thus since his return. All along, his mind was eager with the desire to see, but he could not see (the Lord).

## \|\| 1.122.41 \|\|

*tataḥ prāpte punarviprā gharmakāle himālaye \|*  
*saṃyāto dṛkpathaṃ devaḥ sa tathārūpasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, there was the advent of summer on Himācala. Then the Lord appeared again in the same form as before.

## \|\| 1.122.42 \|\|

*tataḥ pūjāṃ vidhāyoccaiścāturmāsyasamudbhavām \|*  
*gītavādyādikaṃ cakre tatpuraḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then he performed the adoration with great eclat that had been held up for four months. He sang and played the musical instruments before the Lord with great faith.

## \|\| 1.122.43 \|\|

*atha devaḥ samālokya tāṃ śraddhāṃ tasya gopateḥ \|*  
*provāca darśanaṃ gatvā bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The Lord noted the faith of the Lord of heaven. Lord Tripurāntaka appeared before him and said:

## \|\| 1.122.44 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi deveśa bhaktyā cānanyayā'nayā \|*  
*tasmātprārthaya dāsyāmi yaṃ kāmaṃ hṛdisaṃsthitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “O Lord of Devas, I am pleased with your exclusive devotion. Hence request for any desire lurking in your heart.”

## \|\| 1.122.45 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*tava prasādātsaṃjātaṃ mamaiśvaryamanuttamam \|*  
*yatkiṃcittriṣu lokeṣu tatsarvaṃ gṛhasaṃsthitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Śakra said:

45\. With your favour, I already possess an excellent and prosperous glory. Whatever (valuable) is in the three worlds is present in my abode too.

## \|\| 1.122.46 \|\|

*tasmādyadi prasādaṃ me karoṣi vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*varaṃ vā yacchasi prītastatkuruṣva vaco mama \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hence, O Bull-emblemed One, if you are favourable to me, if you are pleased and willing to grant me a boon, then kindly do as I say.

## \|\| 1.122.47 \|\|

*parvato'yaṃ bhavedgamyo māsānaṣṭau sureśvara \|*  
*yāvanmīnasthito bhānuḥ pragacchati śrutaṃ mayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Lord of Suras, I have heard that this mountain is accessible for eight months when the Sun occupies the zodiac of Pisces and proceeds ahead.

## \|\| 1.122.48 \|\|

*tataḥ paramagamyaśca himapūreṇa saṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yadā syāccaturo māsānyāvatkumbhagato raviḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereafter, it becomes inaccessible because it will be covered with snow i.e. for four months till the Sun comes to Aquarius.

## \|\| 1.122.49 \|\|

*saṃjāyate'pyagamyaśca mamāpi tripurāṃtaka \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ svalpasattvānāṃ narādīnāṃ sureśvara \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Lord of Suras, O Tripurāntaka, if it becomes inaccessible even to me, then in the case of human beings and others of inferior power it is all the more so.

## \|\| 1.122.50 \|\|

*tasmātsvarge'tha pātāle martye vā tridaśeśvara \|*  
*kuruṣvānenarūpeṇa sthitiṃ māsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*yena na syātpratijñāyā hānirmama sureśvara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Hence, O Lord of Tridaśas, do stay in this form for four months either in Svarga or in Pātāla or in the mortal world, so that my vow need not be broken.

## \|\| 1.122.51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato devaściraṃ dhyātvā provāca balasūdanam \|*  
*paraṃ saṃtoṣamāpanno meghanirghoṣaniḥsvanam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

51\. Then the Lord thought for a long time and with great delight said to Balasūdana (Indra) in a voice like the rumbling of a cloud:

## \|\| 1.122.52-54 \|\|

*ānartaviṣaye kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*asmadīyaṃ sahasrākṣa vidyate dharaṇītale \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tatrāhaṃ vṛścikasthe'rke sadā sthāsyāmi vāsava \|*  
*yāvatkumbhasya paryaṃtaṃ tava vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gatvā kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*mama rūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kurupūjā yathocitām \|*  
*yena tatra nijaṃ tejo dhārayāmi tavārthataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. “O Thousand-eyed One, on the earth there is our holy spot named Hāṭakeśvara in the land of Ānarta.

At your instance I shall undoubtedly be present there, O Vāsava, during the period beginning with when the Sun is in Scorpio until when he is in Aquarius.

Hence, go there quickly, erect an excellent palace, install my form (image or Liṅga) and perform the suitable adoration so that I can invest my own refulgence there for your sake.”

## \|\| 1.122.55 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā sahasrākṣo devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*gatvā tatra tataścakre yaddeveneritaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Sūta said:

55\. On hearing these words the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas, the Thousand-eyed One went there and did everything as told by the Lord.

## \|\| 1.122.56 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ nirmayitvātha rūpaṃ saṃsthāpya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍaṃ cakre ca tadrūpaṃ svacchodakasamāvṛtam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He built a palace, installed a form (Liṅga) of the Trident-bearing Lord and made a holy Kuṇḍa of the same form filled with clear water.

## \|\| 1.122.57 \|\|

*tataścārādhayāmāsa puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*snātvā kuṇḍe'pibattoyaṃ triḥkṛtvā ca yathāpurā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then he propitiated the Lord with flowers, incense and unguents. He took his bath in the Kuṇḍa and drank water thrice as before.

## \|\| 1.122.58 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstatra śakreṇārādhitaḥ purā \|*  
*samāyāto'tra vipreṃdrāḥ suramyāttu himācalāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus propitiated by Śakra, O leading Brāhmaṇas, the Lord came there from the beautiful Himācala.

## \|\| 1.122.59 \|\|

*yastamārādhayetsamyaksadā māsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*himapātodbhave martyaḥ sa śivāya prapadyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A man who perfectly propitiates him for the period of the four months when there is snowfall, shall attain welfare.

## \|\| 1.122.60 \|\|

*śeṣakāle'pi yaḥ pūjāṃ karotyeva subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa pāpaṃ kṣālayetprājña ājanmamaraṇāṃtikam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A sensible man who worships with great devotion during the remaining period too shall wash off his sin acquired ever since birth and upto death (i.e. throughout his life):

## \|\| 1.122.61 \|\|

*tatra gītaṃ praśaṃsaṃti nṛtyaṃ caiva pṛthagvidham \|*  
*devasya purataḥ prājñāḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Wise men conversant with all the scriptural texts speak in praise of music and dances of various kinds before the Lord.

## \|\| 1.122.62 \|\|

*atra ślokaḥ purā gīto nāradena surarṣiṇā \|*  
*tadvo'haṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. In this connection there is a Śloka sung by Nārada, the celestial sage. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall proclaim it for you. May it be heard:

## \|\| 1.122.63 \|\|

*kedāre salilaṃ pītvā gayāpiḍaṃ pradāya ca \|*  
*brahmajñānamathāsādya punarjanma na vidyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “By drinking the holy water in Kedāra, by offering balls of rice in Gayā and by gaining the knowledge of Brahman, there cannot be rebirth.”

## \|\| 1.122.64 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ kedārasya ca saṃbhavam \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus, everything connected with Kedāra has been narrated to you. This narration is destructive of all sins, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.122.65 \|\|

*yaścaitatchṛṇuyātsamyakpaṭhedvā tasya cāgrataḥ \|*  
*śrāvayedvāpi vā viprāḥ sarvapātakanānam \|*  
*kedārasya sa pāpaughairmucyate tatkṣaṇānnaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Brāhmaṇas, a man who listens to it perfectly, or reads before the deity or expounds to others, this sin-destroying description of Kedāra becomes liberated from clusters of sins instantly.

## Chapter 123 - Glory of Śukla Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.123.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti śuklatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*darbhaiḥ saṃsūcitaṃ śvetairyadadyāpi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*camatkārapure pūrvamāsītkaścitsuśalyavit \|*  
*rajakaḥ śuddhakonāma putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sa sarvarajakānāṃ ca prādhānyena vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*pradhānabrāhmaṇānāṃ ca karotyaṃbaraśodhanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: The Tīrtha (that is water in it) turned everything placed inside it white and hence is called ‘Śukla Tīrtha’.

Sūta said:

1-3. Further, there is another excellent Tīrtha there named Śuklatīrtha. It is known even today by means of the white Darbha grass, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

Formerly, there was a washerman named Śuddhaka in Camatkārapura. He was an expert in the use of darts. He was accompanied by his sons and grandsons. He was chief of all washermen. He used to wash the garments of important Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.123.4 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya nīlīkuṇḍyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*prākṣipadbrāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ vāso vijñātavāṃścirāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once upon a time though he had mental concentration he put the garments of the leading Brāhmaṇas in the cauldron of indigo and became aware of it only later.

## \|\| 1.123.5 \|\|

*athāsau mandacittaśca svāmāhūyakuṭumbinīm \|*  
*putrāṃśca vacanaṃ prāha rahasye bhayavihvalaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Moody in mind, the terrified washerman called his wife and sons and spoke to them in secret:

## \|\| 1.123.6-7 \|\|

*nirmūlyāni suvastrāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*nīlīmadhye vimohena prakṣiptāni bahūni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vadhabandhādikaṃ karma te kariṣyaṃtyasaṃśayam \|*  
*tasmādanyatra gacchāmo gṛhītvā rajanīmimām \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. “Many costly garments of noble-souled Brāhmaṇas were put in the indigo cauldron by mistake. Undoubtedly, they may imprison or even kill us. Hence, we shall go elsewhere tonight itself.”

## \|\| 1.123.8 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā sāramādāya maṃdirāt \|*  
*prasthito bhāryayā sārddhaṃ kāṃdiśīko dvijottamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After deciding thus, he took all essential things from the house, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and prepared to set off along with his wife like fugitive.

## \|\| 1.123.9-10 \|\|

*tāvattasya sutā gatvā svāṃ sakhīṃ dāśasaṃbhavām \|*  
*uvāca kṣamyatāṃ bhadre yanmayā kukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ajñānājjñānato vāpi prakrīḍaṃtyā tvayā saha \|*  
*praṇayādbālyabhāvācca krodhādvātha maherṣyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. In the meanwhile, his daughter went to a fisherman’s daughter who was her friend and said: “O fair lady, if any misdemeanour has been committed by me, let it be excused. While playing with you I might have committed some mistake knowingly or unknowingly. It might have been due to my childishness or over-friendliness. Or perhaps due to anger or keen jealousy.”

## \|\| 1.123.11 \|\|

*atha sā sahasā śrutvā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā \|*  
*uvāca kimidaṃ bhadre yanmāmitthaṃ prabhāṣase \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing these words all of a sudden, her eyes became dimmed with tears. She said: “What is this, O fair lady? Why do you tell me like this?”

## \|\| 1.123.12 \|\|

*sakhyuvāca \|*  
*mama tātena nīlāyāṃ prakṣiptānyaṃbarāṇi ca \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ mahārhāṇi vibhrameṇa sulocane \|\| 12 \|\|*

The friend said:

12\. O lady of excellent eyes, very costly garments of Brāhmaṇas were put in the indigo solution by my father by mistake.

## \|\| 1.123.13 \|\|

*tatprabhāte parijñāya daṃḍaṃ dhāsyaṃti dāruṇam \|*  
*evaṃ citte samāsthāya tātaḥ saṃprasthito'dhunā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On coming to know of this in the morning, they are sure to fine him or give him some other terrible punishment.

Thinking about this, my father has set off now.

## \|\| 1.123.14 \|\|

*ahaṃ tavātikaṃ prāptā darśanārthamanindite \|*  
*anujñātā prayāsyāmi tvayā tasmātpramucyatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O uncensured (praise-worthy) one, I have come to you to meet you. I shall go away on being permitted by you. Hence I may be allowed to go.

## \|\| 1.123.15 \|\|

*atha sā tadvacaḥ śrutvā prasannavadanā'bravīt \|*  
*yadyevaṃ mā sarojākṣi kutracitsaṃprayāsyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On hearing her words, she spoke with a pleasant face: “If this is the case, O lotus-eyed one, you need not go anywhere.

## \|\| 1.123.16 \|\|

*nivāraya drutaṃ gatvā tātaṃ no gamyatāmiti \|*  
*asti pūrvottare bhāge sthānādasmājjalāśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hurry up and prevent your father from going away. Tell him not to go. To the north-east of this place, there is a water-pond.

## \|\| 1.123.17 \|\|

*tatraikadā vinikṣiptaṃ mama tātena jālakam \|*  
*atīvakṛṣṇakeśotthaṃ tāvacchuklatvamāgatam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Once a net of very dark fibres and hair was cast into it by my father. Immediately it turned white.

## \|\| 1.123.18 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sasnau kutūhalāt \|*  
*yāvacchuklatvamāpannastādṛkkṛṣṇavapurdharaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He was surprised. Out of curiosity, he himself took his bath there. He was dark-complexioned before. He turned into a white-complexioned one.

## \|\| 1.123.19 \|\|

*suśvetamūrdhajaḥ sadyaḥ strīṇāṃ vairāgyakārakaḥ \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛti no jñātvā kaścittatra pragacchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. His hairs too suddenly became white causing disgust to women onlookers. Ever since then no one consciously goes there.

## \|\| 1.123.20 \|\|

*tasmāttatraiva vastrāṇi prakṣālayatu satvaram \|*  
*tātaḥ sa tava yāsyaṃti viśuddhiṃ paramāṃ śubhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. So, let your father wash those clothes there itself soon. O splendid girḥ they will become quite pure (white).”

## \|\| 1.123.21 \|\|

*atha sā satvaraṃ gatvā nijatātasya tadvacaḥ \|*  
*satvaraṃ kathayāmāsa prahṛṣṭavadanā satī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The girl thereupon hurried back to her father and with the face beaming with pleasure and eagerness repeated those words:

## \|\| 1.123.22-23 \|\|

*mama sakhyā samādiṣṭaṃ nātidūre jalāśayaḥ \|*  
*tatra śvetatvamāyāti sarvaṃ kṣiptaṃ sitetaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasmātprakṣālaya prātastatra gatvā jalāśaye \|*  
*vastrāṇyamūni śuklatvaṃ saṃprayāsyaṃtyasaṃśayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. “I have been informed by my friend that there is a water-pond not far off. Whatever is nonwhite and put therein becomes white. So go to that pond in the morning and wash these clothes, there. They will undoubtedly become white.”

## \|\| 1.123.24 \|\|

*rajaka uvāca \|*  
*naitatsaṃpatsyate putri yannīlasya parikṣayaḥ \|*  
*vastralagnasya jāyeta yataḥ proktaṃ purātanaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

The washerman said:

24\. Dear daughter, this is simply impossible that the indigo-colour of a cloth can disappear. It has been said by old people.

## \|\| 1.123.25 \|\|

*vajralepasya mūrkhasya nārīṇāṃ karkaṭasya ca \|*  
*eko grahastu mīnānāṃ nīlīmadyapayostathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “There is only one tenacious grip: that of Vajralepa (hard cement-like adhesive), of a fool, of women, of a crab, of a fish, of blue indigo and of a drunkard."

## \|\| 1.123.26 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*tatra hyāgamyatāṃ tāvadvastraṇayādāya yatnataḥ \|*  
*toyācchuddhiṃ prayāsyaṃti tadā'gaṃtavyameva hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

The girl said:

26\. Go there taking all the clothes with you. If they turn white come back.

## \|\| 1.123.27 \|\|

*bhūyo'pi maṃdire vā'tha tasmātsthānāddigaṃtaram \|*  
*gaṃtavyaṃ sakalaireva mamaitaddhṛdi saṃsthitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You can come back home or go away to distant quarters from that place along with all of us. This is what I think.

## \|\| 1.123.28 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sādhusādhviti te'sakṛt \|*  
*procya bāṃdhavabhṛtyāśca rātrāveva prajagmire \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing her words, the kinsmen and servants repeatedly said: “Well said!" All of them went away during the night itself.

## \|\| 1.123.29 \|\|

*dāśakanyāṃ puraḥ kṛtvā saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vibhavena samāyuktā nijena dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they still had a great doubt. Hence, they went away with all their valuables and possessions. They kept the fisherman’s daughter in front of them as their guide.

## \|\| 1.123.30 \|\|

*tataḥ sā darśayāmāsa dāśakanyā jalāśayam \|*  
*bahuvīrudhasaṃchannaṃ duṣpraveśaṃ ca dehinām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The fisherman’s girl showed them the water pond overgrown and densely covered with many creepers. It was impenetrable to all embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.123.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sa rajakastatra vastrāṇyādāya sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ salile tasminkṣālayāmāsa vai dvijāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The washerman entered the pond with all the garments, O Brāhmaṇas and washed them.

## \|\| 1.123.32 \|\|

*atha tāni suvastrāṇi mecakābhāni tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*jātāni sphaṭikābhāni tatkṣaṇādeva kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All those excellent garments originally dark-coloured turned entirely crystal-white instantly.

## \|\| 1.123.33 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭisamāyuktaḥ sādhusādhviti cā'bravīt \|*  
*samāliṃgya sutāṃ prāha dāśakanyāṃ ca sādaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then he became glad and exclaimed, “Excellent!” He embraced his daughter and respectfully said to the daughter:

## \|\| 1.123.34 \|\|

*suvastrāṇi dvijeṃdrāṇāmarpayāmo yathākramam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “We shall return all the excellent garments to the leading Brāhmaṇas in due order.”

## \|\| 1.123.35 \|\|

*tataḥ sa svagṛhaṃ gatvā tāni vastrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*yathākrameṇa saṃhṛṣṭaḥ pradadau dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he went back to his abode joyously and gave back all those garments (to the respective Brāhmaṇas).

## \|\| 1.123.36 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇā dṛṣṭvā tāṃ śuddhiṃ vastrasaṃbhavām \|*  
*taṃ ca śvetīkṛtaṃ cedṛgrajakaṃ vismayānvitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On seeing the whiteness of the garments and on finding that the washerman himself had been turned all white, the Brāhmaṇas became surprised.

## \|\| 1.123.37 \|\|

*papracchuḥ kimidaṃ citraṃ vastramūrdhajasaṃbhavam \|*  
*anaupamyaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ vadasva yadi manyase \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. They asked him, “What is this wonderful unprecedented change? What has happened to the garments and also (to you)? Speak out if you think (you know the cause).”

## \|\| 1.123.38 \|\|

*rajaka uvāca \|*  
*etāni viprā vastrāṇi mayā kṣiptāni mohataḥ \|*  
*nīlīmadhye suvastrāṇi vinaṣṭāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

The washerman said:

38\. O Brāhmaṇas, these garments were put in indigo solution by me by mistake. All the excellent garments were rendered useless.

## \|\| 1.123.39 \|\|

*tato bhayaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ kuṭumbena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*calito rajanīvaktre digaṃte brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a great fear caught hold of me. As soon as night fell, I moved out into the wide world along with my family.

## \|\| 1.123.40 \|\|

*athaiṣā tanayā'smākaṃ gatā nijasakhīṃ prati \|*  
*dāśātmajāṃ suduḥkhārtā punardarśanalālasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then this daughter of ours went to her friend, the fisherman’s daughter. She was extremely miserable and was eager to see her again.

## \|\| 1.123.41 \|\|

*tayā sarvamabhiprāyaṃ jñātvā me duḥkhahetukam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃdarśayāmāsa sthitāgre svajalāśayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She understood everything that caused sorrow (panic) to me. She stood as a guide and showed us the water-pond.

## \|\| 1.123.42 \|\|

*tasminprakṣiptamātrāṇi vastrāṇīmāni tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*īdṛgvarṇāni jātāni vismayasya hi kāraṇam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. As soon as these garments were put in it, they turned into these bright colours causing surprise (to us).

## \|\| 1.123.43 \|\|

*tathā me mūrdhajāḥ kṛṣṇāstatra snātasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*paraṃ śuklatvamāpannā etatproktaṃ mayā sphuṭam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Further my dark hair became white as soon as I took bath. Everything has thus been clearly explained by me.

## \|\| 1.123.44-45 \|\|

*evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ śrutvā kautūhalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*tatra jagmuḥ parīkṣārthaṃ vikṣipya tadanaṃtaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇadravyāṇi bhūrīṇi keśādīni sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ tacchuklatāṃ yāti tyaktvā varṇaṃ malīmasam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. On hearing this, the Brāhmaṇas became curious. They went there in order to test it themselves. Thousands of dark-coloured objects like hair etc. were put in it. Everything turned white losing its (original) dirty colour.

## \|\| 1.123.46 \|\|

*tato vṛddhatayā ye ca viśeṣācchvetamūrdhajāḥ \|*  
*te sasnuḥ śraddhayā yuktāstaruṇāścāpi dharmiṇaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then those who had their hair particularly white due to old age took bath with perfect faith. Young men of righteous behaviour too (took bath).

## \|\| 1.123.47 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklatvamāpannāstejovīryasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti tatprabhāvena prayāṃti ca parāṃ gatim \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then they attained purity and were equipped with refulgence and vigour. Thanks to its power, they attained the great goal.

## \|\| 1.123.48 \|\|

*atha tadvāsavo dṛṣṭvā śuklatīrthaṃ pramuktidam \|*  
*pūrayāmāsa rajasā mānuṣotthabhayena ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then Vāsava observed that the Śuklatīrtha was the bestower of salvation. Afraid of (its misuse by) human beings, he filled it up with dust particles.

## \|\| 1.123.49 \|\|

*adyāpi tatra yatkiṃcijjāyate'tha tṛṇādikam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ śuklatāmeti tattoyasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even today whatever grows there like grass etc. becomes bright (white), thanks to the power of that water.

## \|\| 1.123.50 \|\|

*tatrotthairyaḥ kuśaiḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*śvaitaistaistārayetsarvānpitṝnnarakagānapi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One who is endowed with faith and performs Śrāddha with the white Kuśa grasses growing there, redeems all the Pitṛs even though they have fallen into Naraka.

## \|\| 1.123.51 \|\|

*tattīrthotthāṃ mṛdaṃ gātre yojayitvā narottamaḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ karoti tīrthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. An excellent man who applies over his body the mud taken out of the Tīrtha and takes the holy bath attains the benefit of all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.123.52 \|\|

*yastairdarbhairnaro bhaktyā tilaiścāraṇyasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*karoti tarpaṇaṃ viprāḥ sa prīṇāti pitāmahān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Brāhmaṇas, a man who offers libation devoutly by means of those Darbhas and gingelly seeds grown naturally in the forest propitiates grandfathers.

## \|\| 1.123.53 \|\|

*athāśvamedhātsaṃprāpyaṃ gayāśrāddhena yatphalam \|*  
*nīlasaṃjñagavotsarge tathātrāpi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, what could be attained by a horse-sacrifice, through Gayā Śrāddha or by loosening a blue bull is attained here also.

## \|\| 1.123.54 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\| \|*  
*śuklatīrthaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ tatra tvaṃ sūtanaṃdana \|*  
*vistareṇa samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

The sages said:

54\. How did this Śuklatīrtha come into being here, O Sūtanandana? Explain it in detail. We are very eager.

## \|\| 1.123.55-56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śvetadvīpaḥ samānīto viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tatkṣetre kalibhītena yathā śauklyaṃ na saṃtyajet \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kalikālena saṃspṛṣṭaḥ śvetadvīpo'pi śyāmatām \|*  
*na prayāti dvijaśreṣṭhāstatastatra niveśitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Sūta said:

55-56. Śvetadvīpa was brought here by the powerful Viṣṇu. He was afraid of Kali and thought it would lose its whiteness. Śvetadvīpa will not attain dark colour though contacted by Kali Kāla. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, it was for that purpose that it was placed here.

## Chapter 124 - Creation of Mukhāra Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.124.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athānyadapi tatrāsti mukhāraṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*yatra te munayaḥ śreṣṭhā viprāścaureṇa saṃgatāḥ \|\| \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra siddhiṃ samāpannaḥ sa caurastatprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*vālmīkiriti vikhyāto rāmāyaṇanibaṃdhakṛt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Vālmīki was originally a highwayman Nārada reformed him with Rāma Mantra and he became the author of Rāmāyaṇa. Herein Saptarṣis reform him with a Sāma-mantra

Sūta said.:

1-2. Then there is another excellent Tīrtha named Mukhāra where excellent Brāhmaṇa-sages had contact with a thief.

That thief attained Siddhi, thanks to their power. Later he composed the epic Rāmāyaṇa and became well-known as Vālmīki.

## \|\| 1.124.3 \|\|

*camatkārapure pūrvaṃ māṃḍavyānvaya saṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*lohajaṃgho dvijo hyāsītpitṛmātṛparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly, there was a Brāhmaṇa named Lohajaṅgha in Camatkārapura. He hailed from the family of Māṇḍavya. He was devoted to his father and mother.

## \|\| 1.124.4 \|\|

*tasyaikā cābhavatpatnī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*pativratā patiprāṇā patipriyahite ratā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He had a wife who was dearer to him than his own life. The chaste lady considered her husband as her very life. She was always engaged in what was pleasing and beneficial to her husband.

## \|\| 1.124.5 \|\|

*atha tasya sthitasyātra brahmavṛttyābhivartataḥ \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālaḥ pitṛmātṛratasya ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A great deal of time elapsed as he continued to pursue the profession fit for a Brāhmaṇa and be devoted to his father and mother.

## \|\| 1.124.6 \|\|

*ekadā bhagavāñchakro na vavarṣa dharātale \|*  
*ānartaviṣaye kṛtsne yāvadvādaśavatsarāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once Lord Śakra did not shower rain in the entire land of Ānarta on the earth for twelve years.

## \|\| 1.124.7 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kaṣṭamāpanno lohajaṃgho dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*na prāpnoti kvacidbhikṣāṃ na ca kiṃcitpratigraham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Lohajaṅgha underwent great sufferings. He did not get any alms or monetary gift.

## \|\| 1.124.8 \|\|

*tatastau pitarau dvau tu dṛṣṭvā kṣutparipīḍitau \|*  
*bhāryāṃ ca ciṃtayāmāsa duḥkhena mahatānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing his parents and wife afflicted with hunger, he was overcome by great sorrow and he thought thus:

## \|\| 1.124.9 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ syāddarśanaṃ mama \|*  
*etābhyāmapi vṛddhābhyāṃ patnyāścaiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. ‘What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I continue to see these elderly people and particularly my wife in this miserable plight?’

## \|\| 1.124.10 \|\|

*tataḥ sa duḥkhasaṃyuktaḥ phalārthaṃ prayayau vane \|*  
*na ca kiṃcidavāpnoti sarve śuṣkā mahīruhāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In his great grief he went to a forest for the sake of (gathering) fruits. He could not get any. All the trees were dry and parched.

## \|\| 1.124.11 \|\|

*athāpaśyatsa vṛddhāṃ strīṃ stokasasyasamanvitām \|*  
*gacchamānāṃ tathā tena śrameṇa mahatānvitām \|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he saw an old lady going along with some quantity of vegetables. She was extremely tired thereby.

## \|\| 1.124.12 \|\|

*tatastatsasyamādāya vastrāṇi ca sa nirdayaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pitṛbhyāṃ ca nyavedayat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The merciless wretch snatched her vegetables and clothes and joyously went to his abode and offered the same to his parents.

## \|\| 1.124.13 \|\|

*sa evaṃ labdhalakṣo'pi dasyukarmaṇi nityaśaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā cauryaṃ pupoṣātha nijameva kuṭumbakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Achieving his purpose thus, everyday by the acts of a thief, he maintained his family through thievery.

## \|\| 1.124.14 \|\|

*subhikṣe cāpi saṃprāpte nānyatkarma karoti saḥ \|*  
*brāhmīṃ vṛttiṃ parityaktvā cauryakarma samācarat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the famine passed off and the time of plenty arrived, he never did any personal work. Forsaking his Brāhmaṇical pursuits, he continued the practice of a thief.

## \|\| 1.124.15 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tīrthayātrāprasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*tatra saptarṣayaḥ prāptā marīcipramukhā dvijāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Once, O Brāhmaṇas, the seven sages, the chief of whom was Maria, came there in the course of their pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.124.16 \|\|

*tatastānvijane dṛṣṭvā drohakopasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*yaṣṭimudyamya vegena tiṣṭhadhvamiti cābravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing them in an isolated place, he became, furious and inimical. Raising forcibly his stick, he ordered: “Stop there.”

## \|\| 1.124.17 \|\|

*triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā satvaraṃ samupādravat \|*  
*bhartsamānaḥ sa paruṣairvākyaistāṃstāḍayanniva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He knitted his eyebrows and rushed at them. He rebuked them with harsh words as if he was about to beat them.

## \|\| 1.124.18 \|\|

*tataste munayo dṛṣṭvā yamadūtopamaṃ ca tam \|*  
*yajñopavītasaṃyuktaṃ procuste kṛpayānvitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The sages saw him as one comparable to the messenger of Yama. They noticed that he had a sacred thread. Then they said to him with compassion:

## \|\| 1.124.19 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*aho tvaṃ brāhmaṇo'sīti tatkasmādatigarhitam \|*  
*karoṣi karma caitaddhi mlecchakṛtyaṃ tu bāliśa \|\| 19 \|\|*

The sages said:

19\. Alas, you appear to be a Brāhmaṇa. How childish you are in pursuing this barbarous practice! Why do you carry on this despicable activity?

## \|\| 1.124.20 \|\|

*vayaṃ ca munayaḥ śāṃtāstyaktā'śeṣaparigrahāḥ \|*  
*nāsmākamapi pārśvasthaṃ kiṃcidgṛhṇāti yadbhavanān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. We are quiet and quiescent sages. We have given all our belongings. We have nothing with us which you can take away.

## \|\| 1.124.21 \|\|

*lohajaṃgha uvāca \|*  
*etāni śubhracīrāṇi valkalānyajināni ca \|*  
*upānahasametāni śīghraṃ yacchaṃtu me dvijāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Lohajaṅgha said:

21\. O Brāhmaṇas, hurry up and give me these white bark garments and antelope skins along with your shoes.

## \|\| 1.124.22 \|\|

*no ceddhatvāprahāreṇa yaṣṭyā vajropamena ca \|*  
*prāpayiṣyasyasaṃdigdhaṃ dharmarājaniveśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If not I will kill you all with my stick comparable to the thunderbolt. Undoubtedly, I will despatch you to the abode of Dharmarāja.

## \|\| 1.124.23 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ dāsyāmahe tubhyaṃ vayaṃ tāvanmalimluca \|*  
*kiṃvadantīṃ vadāsmākaṃ yāṃ pṛcchāmaḥ kutūhalāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

The sages said:

23\. O robber, we shall give away everything to you but we would like to ask you something in general out of curiosity. Tell us.

## \|\| 1.124.24 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ kuruṣe cauryaṃ tvaṃ vipro'si sunirghṛṇaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ jito vyasanai raudraiḥ kiṃ vā vyādhadvijo bhavān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are a Brāhmaṇa. Why do you mercilessly commit theft? Have you became enslaved to terrible vices? Are you a hunter in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 1.124.25 \|\|

*lohajaṃgha uvāca \|*  
*vyasanārthaṃ na me kṛtyametaccauryasamudbhavam \|*  
*kuṭumbārthaṃ vijānītha dharmametanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Lohajaṅgha said:

25\. This act of thievery on my part is not an indulgence in vice. It is for the sake of the maintenance of the family. Hence it is undoubtedly righteous.

## \|\| 1.124.26 \|\|

*pitarau mama vārddhakye vartamānau vyavasthitau \|*  
*tathā pativratā patnī gṛhadharmavicakṣaṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. My parents are in their advanced state of senility. My chaste wife is an adept in household chores.

## \|\| 1.124.27 \|\|

*upārjjayāmi yatkiñcidahametena karmaṇā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ tatkṛte nūnaṃ satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. What little I earn by means of this activity is entirely for their sake. I state this on a solemn oath.

## \|\| 1.124.28 \|\|

*tasmānmuṃcatha prāksarvaṃ vibhavaṃ kiṃ vṛthoktibhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtābhiḥ sphurate hasto mamāyaṃ hantumeva hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence at the very outset, out with all your possessions. Why indulge in vain talk? My hands throb to hit you all.

## \|\| 1.124.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadyevaṃ caura tadgatvā tvaṃ pṛcchasva kuṭumbakam \|*  
*mamapāpāṃśabhāgī tvaṃ kiṃ bhaviṣyasi kiṃ na vā \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:

29\. If it is so, O thief, go home and ask everyone, “Are you willing to share a portion of my sins or not?”

## \|\| 1.124.30 \|\|

*yadi te saṃvibhāgena pāpasyāṃśo'pi gacchati \|*  
*tatkuruṣvāthavā pāpa durvahaṃ te bhaviṣyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If by their sharing, a part of your sin goes away, you do as you please; otherwise the sin will become unbearable (to you).

## \|\| 1.124.31 \|\|

*sakalaṃ raurave raudre patitasya sudurmate \|*  
*vayaṃ tvā brāhmaṇaṃ matvā brūma etadasaṃśayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O extremely wicked one, you will fall into Raurava Naraka. We are saying this only out of the consideration that you are a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.124.32 \|\|

*kṛpāviṣṭāḥ sahāsmābhiḥ sañjāte'pi sudarśane \|*  
*munīnāṃ yatacittānāṃ darśanāddhi śubhaṃ bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. We are feeling compassionate towards you. It is good that you have met us. Auspicious indeed is the result of seeing sages of controlled minds.

## \|\| 1.124.33 \|\|

*ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṃkte mahājanaḥ \|*  
*bhoktāro vipramucyaṃte kartā doṣeṇa lipyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One commits the sin. The other man enjoys the benefit. Those who enjoy escape punishment. It is the doer who is affected by the adverse result.

## \|\| 1.124.34-36 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa teṣāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā cauraḥ kiṃcidbhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*satyametanna saṃdeho yadetairvyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmātpṛcchāmi tadgatvā nijameva kuṭumbakam \|*  
*yadi syātsaṃvibhāgo me pāpāṃśasya karomi vai \|\| 35 \|\|*

*etatkarma na gṛhṇaṃti yadi vā saṃtyajāmyaham \|*  
*mahadbhayaṃ samutpannaṃ mama cetasi sāṃpratam \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sūta said:

34-36. On Hearing their words the thief became slightly afraid. He thought: ‘There is no doubt about this that what these people say is true. So I shall go home and ask all the members of the family. If they are amenable to partake of a share in my sin I shall continue to do like this. If they do not take a share therein, I shall abandon this thievish activity. Now a great terror has entered my mind.’ (Then he said to them:)

## \|\| 1.124.37-39 \|\|

*yadi yūyaṃ na cānyatra prayāsyatha munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*palāyanaparā bhūtvā tadgatvā nijamaṃdiram \|\| 37 \|\|*

*pṛcchāmi poṣyavargaṃ ca yuṣmadvākyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yadi tatpātakāṃśaṃ me grahīṣyati kuṭumbakam \|*  
*tadyuṣmākaṃ grahīṣyāmi yatkiṃcitpārśvasaṃsthitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*athavā pratiṣedhaṃ me pāpasyāsya kariṣyati \|*  
*tattyajiṣyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ sarvānvaḥ saparicchadān \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. “O great sages, if you do not go elsewhere and flee from me I shall go home. I shall ask all my dependents what you said in particular. If the family acceptṣ a share in my sin, I will take away whatever you possess. If they refuse to have anything to do with my sin, I shall undoubtedly let you (go) along with all your possessions."

## \|\| 1.124.40 \|\|

*tataste śapathānkṛtvā tasya pratyayakāraṇāt \|*  
*tasyopari dayāṃ kṛtvā mumucustaṃ gṛhaṃ prati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Taking pity on him, they promised (not to leave the place) in order to make him believe and then sent him homewards.

## \|\| 1.124.41-43 \|\|

*so'pi gatvā'tha papraccha pragatvā pitaraṃ nijam \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta vaco'smākaṃ tataḥ pratyuttaraṃ kuru \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yatkṛtvāhamakṛtyāni cauryādīni sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*puṣṭiṃ karomi te nityas tadbhāgaste'sti vā na vā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pāpasya mama prabrūhi pṛcchato'tra yathātatham \|*  
*atra me saṃśayo jātastasmācchīghraṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. After going home, he first asked his father: “Dear father, listen to my words and then reply:

Thousands of forbidden acts like thievery I do everyday and nourish you. Do you partake of any share (of sins) therein or not?

In this I entertain my own doubt. Tell me even as I ask “are you prepared to share the sin duly? Tell me quickly.”

## \|\| 1.124.44 \|\|

*pitovāca \|*  
*bālye putra mayā nītastvaṃ puṣṭiṃ vyākulātmanā \|*  
*śubhā'śubhāni kṛtyāni kṛtvā snigdhena cetasā \|\| 44 \|\|*

The father said:

44\. Dear son, during your childhood I went through many worries and sufferings, committed many things good and bad with an affectionate heart and nursed you.

## \|\| 1.124.45 \|\|

*etadarthaṃ punaryena vārdhakye samupasthite \|\| \|*  
*gāṃ pālayasi bhūyo'pi kṛtvā karma śubhā'śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In view of this, when I am in advanced (old) age, you commit things good and bad and protect me.

## \|\| 1.124.46 \|\|

*na tasya vidyate bhāgastava svalpo'pi putraka \|*  
*śubhasya vā'tha pāpasya sāṃprataṃ ca tathā mama \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O child, just as you had not the slightest share in the auspicious or sinful acts then committed, the same is the case with me now.

## \|\| 1.124.47 \|\|

*ātmanaiva kṛtaṃ karma svayamevopabhujyate \|*  
*śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ bhoktāronyajanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The (fruit) of Karma committed by a person, whether meritorious or sinful, has to be experienced by him only. But the partakers of the beneficial results are others (not responsible for the Karmas).

## \|\| 1.124.48 \|\|

*sādhutvenātha cauryeṇa kṛṣyā vā vāṇijena vā \|*  
*tvamupānayase bhojyaṃ na me cintā prajāyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I am not worried whether you bring me food by honest means or thievery. Nor do I care to think whether you cultivate the land or engage yourself in trading or commerce.

## \|\| 1.124.49 \|\|

*tasmānnaitaddhṛdi sthāpyaṃ karmaniṃdyaṃ kariṣyasi \|*  
*yattasyāṃśaṃ prabhoktā tvaṃ vayaṃ sarve prabhuṃjakāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Hence this should not be entertained in the heart that we are all the partakers of shares in the despicable thing you commit (we are only the enjoyers). You alone are the person who have to share.

## \|\| 1.124.50 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa etadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyākulenānttarātmanā \|*  
*papraccha mātaraṃ gatvā tamevārthaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Sūta said:

50\. On hearing these words he became greatly agitated in his mind. He then went to his mother and asked the same assiduously.

## \|\| 1.124.51 \|\|

*tatastayāpi taccoktaṃ yatpitrā tasya jalpitam \|*  
*asāmānyaṃ śubhe pāpe kṛtye tasya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, what was said by the father was repeated by her too, namely non-participation in his activity whether good or bad.

## \|\| 1.124.52 \|\|

*tataḥ papraccha tāṃ bhāryāṃ gatvā duḥkhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sā'pyuvāca tatastādṛkpāpaṃ gurujanodbhavam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then he went to his wife and asked the same. She too had the same stand in regard to the sin as the elders had.

## \|\| 1.124.53 \|\|

*tataḥ sa śokasaṃtaptaḥ paścāttāpena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*garhayanneva cātmānaṃ yayau te yatra tāpasāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thereupon he got extremely distressed with regret. He despised himself; he went back to the place where the sages were present.

## \|\| 1.124.54 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya tānsarvānkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*gamyatāṃ gamyatāṃ viprāḥ kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāṃ mama \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He bowed down to all of them standing there with palms joined in reverance. He said: “You all may go, O Brāhmaṇas. May my crime be forgiven.

## \|\| 1.124.55 \|\|

*yanmayā maurkhyamāsthāya yuṣmannirbhartsanā kṛtā \|*  
*supāpmanā vimūḍhena tasmātkāryā kṣamādya me \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I have been sinful and deluded. So I foolishly rebuked and threatened you. So you should forgive me.

## \|\| 1.124.56 \|\|

*yuṣmadīyaṃ vacaḥ kṛtsnaṃ madgurubhyāṃ prajalpitam \|*  
*bhāryayā ca dvijaśreṣṭhāstena me duḥkhamāgatam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, your words came true in the utterance of my parents and wife. Hence I feel regret.

## \|\| 1.124.57 \|\|

*tasmātkurvaṃtu me sarve prasādaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*upadeśapradānena yena pāpaṃ kṣapāmyaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence, O excellent sages, be pleased ye all to impart some sound instruction to me so that I can eradicate my sins.

## \|\| 1.124.58 \|\|

*mayā karma kṛtaṃ niṃdyaṃ sadaiva dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*striyo'pi ca dvijeṃdrāśca tāpasāśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I have always been doing these despicable things. Women, eminent Brāhmaṇas and sages in particular (were attacked by me).

## \|\| 1.124.59 \|\|

*ye ye dīnatarā lokā na samarthāḥ prayodhitum \|*  
*te mayā muṣitāḥ sarve na samarthāḥ kadācana \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All those persons of weak nature, those who are incapable of fighting, have been robbed by me, never those who could fight.

## \|\| 1.124.60 \|\|

*kuṭumbārthaṃ vimūḍhena sādhusaṃgavivarjinā \|*  
*yathaiva paṭhatā śāstraṃ tanme'dya patitaṃ hṛdi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. All this I did for the sake of the family, deluded that I was, not having associated with good people (before). But something has entered my heart today as though I have been reading the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.124.61 \|\|

*yadi na syādbhavadbhirme darśanaṃ cādya sattamāḥ \|*  
*tadanyānyapi pāpāni kartāhaṃ syāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O excellent persons, if I had not met you all today, I would have continued to perform other sinful acts too. There is no doubt about it.”

## \|\| 1.124.62 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhyagataścāsītpulaho nāma sanmuniḥ \|*  
*hāsyaśīlaḥ sa taṃ prāha viplavārthaṃ dvijottamam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There was a good sage among them named Pulaha, one of a jovial nature. He said to the excellent Brāhmaṇa just to bewilder him:

## \|\| 1.124.63-65 \|\|

*ahaṃ te kīrtayiṣyāmi mantramekaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*yaṃ dhyāyañjapyamānastvaṃ siddhiṃ yāsyasi śāśvatīm \|\| 63 \|\|*

*jāṭaghoṭetimantro'yaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakaḥ \|\|*  
*tamenaṃ japa vipra tvaṃ divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tato yāsyasi saṃsiddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. “I shall tell you a splendid Mantra. By repeating it and meditating you will attain permanent Siddhi. This Mantra namely Jāṭaghoṭa is the bestower of all Siddhis. O Brāhmaṇa, repeat this Mantra day and night untiringly. Thereby you will attain perfection rare in the case of even Devas.”

## \|\| 1.124.66 \|\|

*evamuktvātha te viprāstīrthayātrāṃ tato yayuḥ \|*  
*so'pi tatraiva caurastu sthito japaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After saying thus those Brāhmaṇas went on their pilgrimage. The thief on his part stayed there completely engrossed in the Japa.

## \|\| 1.124.67 \|\|

*ananyamanasā tena prārabdhaḥ sa tadā japaḥ \|*  
*yathā'bhavatsamādhistho yenāvasthāṃ parāṃ gataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The Japa was begun by him in all earnestness with his mind not turning to anything else. He maintained the mental absorption. He reached the climax thereof.

## \|\| 1.124.68 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ smaramāṇasya taṃ mantraṃ brāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*niścalatvaṃ gataḥ kāyaḥ kārye ca niścalaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. As the Brāhmaṇa continued the recitation of the Mantra, his body remained motionless and he was steady in the Japa.

## \|\| 1.124.69 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā valmīkena samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*samaṃtādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā dhyānasthasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. After a great deal of time had elapsed an anthill enveloped the noble-souled one engaged in meditation, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.124.70 \|\|

*tau mātāpitarau tasya sā ca bhāryā manasvinī \|*  
*yātā mṛtyuvaśaṃ sarve tamanveṣya prayatnataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. His parents and his wife of lofty mind made a fruitless search for him and ultimately they died themselves.

## \|\| 1.124.71 \|\|

*na vijñātaśca tatrasthaḥ saṃnyastaḥ sa mahāvrataḥ \|*  
*saṃsārabhāvanirmuktastasmānmunisamāgamāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The man engaged in the great Vrata had renounced everything. He was liberated from all worldly feelings, thanks to the association with those sages. He could not be found out even as he was there itself.

## \|\| 1.124.72 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tena mārgeṇa te punaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena munayaḥ samupasthitāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After some time, those sages came the same way in the course of their pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.124.73 \|\|

*procuścaitaddvijāḥ sthānaṃ yatra caureṇa saṃgamaḥ \|*  
*āsīdvastena raudreṇa brāhmaṇacchadmadhāriṇā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. They said thus, O Brāhmaṇas: “This is the place where you had come into contact with that terrible thief who was in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa.”

## \|\| 1.124.74 \|\|

*tato valmīkamadhyasthaṃ śuśruvurnisvanaṃ ca te \|*  
*jāṭaghoṭetimaṃtrasya tasyaiva ca mahātmanaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. They heard from within an anthill the sound of the Mantra Jāṭaghoṭa from the same noble soul.

## \|\| 1.124.75 \|\|

*atha bhūmyāṃ prahārāste sasvanuḥ sarvatodiśam \|*  
*te valmīkaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā taṃ cauraṃ tasya madhyagam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They heard the vibrations on the ground from all sides. They saw the anthill all round and the thief seated in the midst.

## \|\| 1.124.76 \|\|

*japamānaṃ tu taṃ mantraṃ pulahena niveditaḥ \|*  
*hāsyarūpeṇa yastasya siddhiṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They saw that he had been repeating the Mantra jocularly imparted to him by Pulaha. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they found out the Siddhi yielded by that Mantra.

## \|\| 1.124.77 \|\|

*yadvā satyamidaṃ proktamācāryaiḥ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*stokaṃ siddhikṛte tasya yasmātsiddhirupasthitā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. What the preceptors whose eye is the scripture, say is true. Very little indeed is enough for the achievement of perfection (Siddhi). Hence the Siddhi was attained by him.

## \|\| 1.124.78 \|\|

*mantre tīrthe dvije deve daivajñe bheṣaje gurau \|*  
*yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhirbhavati tādṛśī \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The Siddhi in the case of Mantra, Tīrtha, Brāhmaṇa, deity, astrologer, medicine and preceptor is always in proportion to the mental fervour and faith one has.

## \|\| 1.124.79 \|\|

*atha taṃ vīkṣya saṃsiddhaṃ kumantreṇāpi taskaram \|*  
*te viprā vismayāviṣṭāḥ kṛpāviṣṭā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. They were surprised to observe that the thief had become a great Siddha even through an insignificant sham Mantra. The Brāhmaṇas were overcome with compassion too all the more.

## \|\| 1.124.80-81 \|\|

*samādhyarhaistato dravyaistailaistadbheṣajairapi \|\| 80 \|\|*

*mamardustasya tadgātraṃ samādhisthaṃ ciraṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa cetanāṃ labdhā ālokya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*provāca vismayāviṣṭastānmunīnprakṛtāniti \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. They massaged his body with things specific for recovering from Samādhi, such as oils and medicines. O Brāhmaṇas, you know that he had been in meditation for a long time. After regaining consciousness he stared at them frequently and said to them in utter surprise:

## \|\| 1.124.82 \|\|

*lohajaṃgha uvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ na gatā yūyaṃ mayā muktā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*nāhaṃ kiṃcidgrahīṣyāmi yuṣmadīyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*kuṭuṃbārthaṃ yatastasmādvrajadhvaṃ svecchayā'dhunā \|\| 82 \|\|*

Lohajaṅgha said:

82\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, why did you not go away? I will not take anything belonging to you. You were let off by me. Since I do not want anything for the sake of the family, you can go away as you please.

## \|\| 1.124.83 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*cirakālādvayaṃ prāptāḥ punarbhrāṃtvā'tra kānane \|*  
*samādhisthena na jñātaḥ kālo'tītastvayā bahu \|\| 83 \|\|*

The sages said:

83\. We have been wandering in the forest. We have come here after a long time. The long period of time that has elapsed has not been noticed by you because you were in meditation.

## \|\| 1.124.84 \|\|

*tau mātāpitarau vṛddhau tvayā muktau kṣayaṃ gatau \|*  
*tvaṃ ca saṃsiddhimāpannaḥ parāmasmatprasādataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Your aged parents whom you left have all died. With our favour, you have achieved great Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.124.85 \|\|

*valmīkāṃtaḥ sthito yasmātsaṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*valmīkirnāma vikhyātastasmālloke bhaviṣyasi \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Since you achieved great Siddhi seated within a Valmīka (an anthill), you will become well-known in the world as Vālmīki.

## \|\| 1.124.86 \|\|

*atrasthena yato muṣṭāstvayā lokāḥ purā dvija \|*  
*mukhārākhyaṃ tatastīrthametatkhyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O Brāhmaṇa, you stayed here and robbed (muṣṭa \[muṣṭaḥ\]) the world earlier. Hence this will become famous as a Tīrtha named Mukhāra.

## \|\| 1.124.87 \|\|

*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti śrāvaṇyāṃ śraddhayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*kṣālayiṣyaṃti te pāpaṃ caurya karmasamudbhavam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Those who faithfully take their holy bath here on Śrāvaṇī day, O Brāhmaṇas, will wash off their sin due to thievery.

## \|\| 1.124.88-91 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha te viprāstamāmaṃtrya muniṃ tataḥ \|*  
*praṇatāstena saṃjagmurvāṃchitāśāṃ tataḥ param \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tapaḥsthaḥ so'pi tatraiva vālmīkiriti yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*munīnāṃ pravaraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃjātaśca tataḥ param \|*  
*adyāpi tiṣṭhate mūrtaḥ sa tatrastho munīśvaraḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*yastaṃ prapūjayedbhaktyā sa kavirjāyate bhuvam \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

Sūta said:

88-91. After saying thus, those Brāhmaṇas took leave of the sage. They were duly bowed down to by him and they went in the direction they desired. Engaged in his penance he was later remembered as Vālmīki. He became a leading sage. Even today that leading sage is present there in the form of an idol. One who worships him with great faith and devotion especially on the eighth lunar day will certainly become a poet.

## Chapter 125 - The Story of King Satyasandha

## \|\| 1.125.1-2 \|\|

*\|sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ karṇotpalātīrthaṃ vikhyātaṃ cāsti śobhanam \|*  
*yatra snāto naraḥ samyaṅna viyogamavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kathaṃcidapi ceṣṭena dhanenālijanena ca \|*  
*parākrameṇa dharmeṇa kalatreṇa viśeṣataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: This king Satyasandha is different from the three Satyasandhas mentioned in Mahābhārata.

Sūta said:

1-2. Beyond it there is the well-known splendid Tīrtha named Karṇotpalā. A man who takes his bath duly therein, will never get separated from his desired object, wealth or servant-folk. Nor will he be devoid of valour, virtue and a splendid wife.

## \|\| 1.125.3 \|\|

*satyasaṃdha iti khyātaḥ purāsītpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākukulasaṃbhūtaḥ sarvarūpaguṇairyutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly, there was a king well-known as Satyasandha. He was born of the Ikṣvāku race and was endowed with handsome features and all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.125.4 \|\|

*tasya karṇotpalānāma jātā kanyā suśobhanā \|*  
*bahuputrasya caikā sā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He had many sons but only one daughter named Karṇotpalā. She was very splendid and endowed with all good features.

## \|\| 1.125.5 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ pitā nāma cakre dvādaśame dine \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhṛtyāmātyairmuhurmuhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*
