5\. After repeated consultations with Brāhmaṇas, servants and ministers, her father gave her the name on the twelfth day.

## \|\| 1.125.6-7 \|\|

*yasmātkarṇotpalā ceyaṃ jātā mama kumārikā \|*  
*tasmātkarṇotpalānāma jātā kanyā suśobhanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bahu putrasya caikā sā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|*  
*tasmātkarṇotpalānāma jāyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. “My daughter resembles a lotus-like ear-ornament. Hence the splendid girl shall be named Karṇotpalā.”

She is the only daughter among many sons. She is marked with all good features. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, let her be Karṇotpalā by name.

## \|\| 1.125.8 \|\|

*kṛtanāmā'tha sā bālā vṛddhiṃ yāti dinedine \|*  
*āhlādakāriṇī nityaṃ kalā cāṃdramasī yathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After the naming ceremony, the girl grew up day by day delighting everyone like the digit of the moon (in the bright half of a month).

## \|\| 1.125.9 \|\|

*atha sā kramaśaḥ prāptā yauvanaṃ baṃdhulālitā \|*  
*hastāddhastaṃ pragacchaṃtī sarveṣāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as a child she went from hand to hand and was fondled by all the kinsmen. She grew up and attained youth.

## \|\| 1.125.10-11 \|\|

*atha tāṃ yauvanopetāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa cittena kasyemāṃ pradadāmyaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*na tasyāḥ sadṛśaḥ kaścidvaro'tra dharaṇītale \|*  
*na svarge na ca pātāle kiṃ kṛtyaṃ me'dhunā bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. On noticing that she had become endowed with the prime of youth, the king considered in his mind, “To whom shall I give her? Neither on the earth, nor in Svarga, nor in Pātāla, is there a bridegroom suitable to her. What should be done by me now?”

## \|\| 1.125.12-13 \|\|

*sa evaṃ bahudhā dhyātvā tadarthaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*niścayaṃ prākaroccitte praṣṭavyo'tra pitāmahaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mayādya viṣaye cāsminsa devaḥ prerayiṣyati \|*  
*tasmai putrīṃ pradāsyāmi nānyasmai vai kathaṃcana \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. That king thought thus in various ways on her behalf and ultimately decided thus: “In this connection, Pitāmaha (Brahmā) should be asked. In this matter that Lord is to be consulted. He will guide me. I shall give my daughter to him, not at all to anyone else."

## \|\| 1.125.14 \|\|

*sa evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā tāmādāya tataḥ param \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ jagāmātha praṣṭuṃ tasyāḥ kṛte varam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After deciding thus, he took her to the world of Brahmā in order to consult him about a bridegroom for her.

## \|\| 1.125.15 \|\|

*atha yāvatsa saṃprāpto brahmalokaṃ nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*tāvatsaṃdhyā samutpannā brāhmī brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, by the time the king reached Brahmaloka, the Brāhmī Sandhyā (the twilight of Brahmā) had set in.

## \|\| 1.125.16 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare brahmā sāyaṃtanakriyotsukaḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭaḥ samādhisthastatkālaṃ samapadyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the meantime, Brahmā was eager to perform the evening rites. At that time, he was engaged in meditation.

## \|\| 1.125.17 \|\|

*satyasaṃdho'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā samādhisthaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*samādhyaṃtaṃ pratīkṣansa upaviṣṭaḥ samīpataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On observing that Pitāmaha was engaged in meditation, Satyasandha sat near him waiting for the conclusion of the meditation.

## \|\| 1.125.18 \|\|

*tato vilokya cātmānamātmani prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*padme pravartite samyagaṣṭapatre hṛdi sthite \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the eight-petailed lotus situated in the heart, that was blooming perfectly, Prapitāmaha saw the Ātman within the (higher) Ātman.

## \|\| 1.125.19 \|\|

*karṇikāmadhyagaṃ dīptaṃ bahuvarṇamatisthiram \|*  
*ānaṃdāśrupariklinnavadanaḥ pulakāṃkitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It was refulgent in the centre of the pericarp. On seeing the Ātman, Brahmā experienced horripilation and tears of joy drenched his face.

## \|\| 1.125.20 \|\|

*tata ācamya prakṣālya caraṇau sarvatodiśam \|*  
*apaśyatpraṇataḥ sarvairbrahmalokanivāsibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He then washed his feet and performed the Ācamana (ritualistic sipping of water) rite. Then he looked all round, when he was bowed to by all the residents of Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.125.21 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare rājā tāmādāya śubhānanām \|*  
*namaskṛtya tayā sārdhaṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the meantime the king together with the splendid-faced girl bowed down and spoke respectfully:

## \|\| 1.125.22-24 \|\|

*ahaṃ deva samāyāto martyalokāttavāṃtikam \|*  
*satyasaṃdho mahīpāla ānarta bhuvi viśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*iyaṃ karṇotpalānāma mama kanyā suśobhanā \|*  
*asyā bhuvi mayā labdho na samo'tra patiḥ kvacit \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sadṛśastena cāyātastava pārśve surottama \|*  
*tasmānme brūhi bharttāramasyā yena dadāmyaham \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. “O Lord, I am King Satyasandha well-known in the land of Ānarta. I have come to you from the human world. This is my splendid daughter named Karṇotpalā. A husband suitable to her was not found by me anywhere on the earth.

Therefore, O excellent one among Suras, I have come to you. Hence, tell me who her husband should be, so that I can give her unto him.”

## \|\| 1.125.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ provāca padmajaḥ \|*  
*vihasya sarvadevānāṃ samāje dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing his words, the Lotus-born One laughed, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and spoke to him in the assembly of all the Devas:

## \|\| 1.125.26-33 \|\|

*yadi pṛcchasi me bhūpa kanyādharmapatiṃ prati \|*  
*tannaiṣā kasyaciddeyā sāṃprataṃ śṛṇu kāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ātmaśreṇiprasūtāya vayojyeṣṭhāya bhūpate \|*  
*kanyā deyā ca dharmāya yaśase kulavṛddhaye \|\| 27 \|\|*

*seyaṃ tava sutā martye jyeṣṭhabhāvaṃ samāśritā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ yattattvaṃ kāraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mamāṃtikaṃ prapannasya tava jātaṃ yugatrayam \|*  
*atītā bhūtale martyā ye dṛṣṭāḥ prāktvayā nṛpa \|\| 29 \|\|*

*anyā sṛṣṭiḥ samutpannā sāṃprataṃ dharaṇītale \|*  
*na tvaṃ jānāsi māhātmyānmama lokasamudbhavāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*na devā mānuṣīṃ bhāryāṃ kurvanti ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ saṃsthānaṃ yā vigarhitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmādatraiva tiṣṭha tvaṃ sutayā sahito nṛpa \|*  
*hastyaśvādi ca yatkiṃcittatsarvaṃ te kṣayaṃ gatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*putrāḥ pautrāstathā bhṛtyā ye cānye bāṃdhavāstava \|*  
*te sarve nidhanaṃ prāptā ye cānye bhavatekṣitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

26-33. “If you ask me concerning a righteous husband for this girl, O king, then she should not be given to anyone now. Listen to the reason.

For the purpose of virtue, fame and prosperous increase of the family, a girl should be given, O king, to one who is older than her in age and belongs to the same caste as oneself. This daughter of yours has attained very great seniority in the mortal world to all the kings. You do listen to the reason.

Since your arrival here in my presence, three yugas have passed off. Those men who were seen by you are not aware of these things (on the earth).

Devas do not take mortal women as their wives because they being the receptacles of phlegm, urine and faeces are despicable to them. Hence, O king, stay here itself along with your daughter. Whatever you had, elephants, horses etc. have perished. The sons, grandsons, servants and all your kinsmen have died. So also, all the others seen by you (earlier).”

## \|\| 1.125.34 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya sthitaḥ pārthivasattamaḥ \|*  
*yāvattāvatsuduḥkhārtā rudatīsā'bravītsutā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “So it shall be", said the excellent king and stayed back But his extremely distressed daughter wept and said:

## \|\| 1.125.35-37 \|\|

*nāhaṃ tāta vasiṣyāmi sthānesminbrahmasaṃbhave \|*  
*sakhījanaparityaktā baṃdhuvargavinākṛtā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasmādyāsyāmi tatraiva yatra sā jananī mama \|*  
*tāśca sakhyaḥ kṛtānaṃdā yābhiḥ saṃkrīḍitaṃ mayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhartrā vinākṛtā nāhaṃ nayiṣye kālasaṃsthitim \|*  
*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha yatra me jananī sthitā \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. “O father, I will not stay here in the region of Brahmā, bereft of my girl companions and away from the groups of kinsmen. Hence I will go there where my mother is present as also my friends who delighted me and with whom I had played. I am not going to continue endlessly in time without a husband. So go quickly to that place where my mother is present.”

## \|\| 1.125.38 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā snehārdreṇa sa cetasā \|*  
*tāmādāya tataḥ prāptaḥ svaṃ deśaṃ pārthivottamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing her words, the excellent king had his heart filled with affectionate compassion. Taking her with him he reached his land.

## \|\| 1.125.39 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyati tāvatsa sthalasthāne jalāśayān \|*  
*jalasthāneṣu saṃjātāḥ sthalasaṃghāḥ sudurgamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He saw water-ponds in the place of dry lands. Impassable land regions had risen up in (former) water ponds.

## \|\| 1.125.40 \|\|

*anye lokāstathā dharmāsteṣāṃ madhye vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*pṛcchannapi na jānāti saṃbaṃdhaṃ kenacitsaha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Those areas were inhabited by different people with different customs and rites. Although he asked many, he could not come to know of any relationship with anyone.

## \|\| 1.125.41 \|\|

*tathā martyānilaspṛṣṭandyatattkaṇātsa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*sā ca kanyā jarāgrastā saṃjātā śvetamūrddhajā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The moment they came into contact with human atmosphere (touched by winds of the mortal world) the king and the girl were overcome with old age. Their hair turned grey.

## \|\| 1.125.42 \|\|

*valibhiḥ pūrṇitāṃgī ca śīrṇadaṃtā kucacyutā \|*  
*amanojñā virūpāṃgī cipiṭākṣī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all her limbs were covered with wrinkles. Her teeth dropped down and her breasts hung loose. With deformed limbs and flattened eyes, she became utterly ugly.

## \|\| 1.125.43 \|\|

*sopi rājā tathābhūto vepamānaḥ padepade \|*  
*papraccha bhūpatiḥ kotra deśaḥ koyaṃ puraṃ ca kim \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The king also became like that and faltered at every step. He asked the people, “Who is the king here? What is this land (called)? What is the name of this city?"

## \|\| 1.125.44-46 \|\|

*atha procurjanāstasya deśa ānarta ityayam \|*  
*ayaṃ bhūpotra vikhyātaḥ sudharmajño bṛhadbalaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*etatprāptipuraṃnāma eṣā sābhramatī nadī \|*  
*gartātīrthamidaṃ puṇyametasyāḥ parikīrtitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yatraite munayaḥ śāṃtā dāṃtāścāṣṭaguṇe ratāḥ \|*  
*taparatā mahābhāgāḥ snānajapyayaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. Then the people said: “This is the land of Ānarta. The king here is the well-known Bṛhadbala excellently conversant with virtue. This city is called Prāptipura. This is the river Sābhramatī. The Tīrtha here is meritorious and is glorified as Gartātīrtha. It is the place where these highly esteemed quiescent sages are engaged in penance. They possess the eight qualities and they are devoted to holy bath and Japa."

## \|\| 1.125.47 \|\|

*tataḥ sa tu samākarṇya ruroda kṛtaniḥsvanaḥ \|*  
*svasutāṃ tāṃ samāliṃgya duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing this, the king embraced his daughter with great sorrow. He lamented loudly.

## \|\| 1.125.48 \|\|

*tau ca vṛddhatamau dṛṣṭvā rudatau kṛpayānvitāḥ \|*  
*sarve lokāḥ samājagmuḥ papracchuśca suduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On seeing these two old people cry all those persons felt sorry. They came near them and asked sympathetically:

## \|\| 1.125.49-51 \|\|

*kiṃ tvaṃ vṛddha suduḥkhārtaḥ prarodiṣi nirargalam \|*  
*anayā vṛddhayā sārdhaṃ tasmānnaḥ kāraṇaṃ vada \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kiṃ te naṣṭaḥ priyaḥ kaścitkiṃ vā jāto dhanakṣayaḥ \|*  
*parābhūtosi vā kiṃ tvaṃ kenāpi vada mā ciram \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dharmajño duṣṭahaṃtā ca sādhūnāṃ pālane rataḥ \|*  
*rājā bṛhadbalosmākaṃ yena te kurute sukham \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. “O old man, why are you miserable? Why do you cry continuously along with this old woman? Tell us the reason thereof. Is anyone dear to you lost or dead? Have you incurred loss of wealth? Or have you been humiliated by anyone? Tell us quickly. Our king Bṛhadbala is the destroyer of the wicked and is engaged in protecting the good. He is fully conversant with virtue and righteous conduct. He will accord happiness to you.”

## \|\| 1.125.52 \|\|

*satyasaṃdha uvāca \|*  
*ānarttādhipatiścāhaṃ satyasaṃdha iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*mama karṇotpalānāma suteyaṃ dayitā sadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

Satyasandha said:

52\. I too was a Lord of Ānarta. I am remembered as Satyasandha. This is my daughter named Karṇotpalā who has always been my darling. She is dear to me always.

## \|\| 1.125.53 \|\|

*sohamasyāḥ pradānārthaṃ brahmalokamito gataḥ \|*  
*praṣṭuṃ pitāmahaṃ devaṃ sthitastatra muhūrtavat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I had gone to Brahmaloka from here in connection with giving her in marriage. I wanted to consult Lord Pitāmaha and stayed there only for a short while.

## \|\| 1.125.54 \|\|

*tato bhūyaḥ samāyāto yāvatpaśyāmi bhūtalam \|*  
*tāvadvilomatāṃ prāptaṃ sarvaṃ no vedmi kiñcana \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then immediately, I returned to the earth. What do I see? Everything has changed the wrong way. I do not know anything.

## \|\| 1.125.55 \|\|

*tacchrutvā te janā gatvā vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*bṛhadbalāya tatsarvamācakhyustuṣṭisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On hearing it, all the persons were surprised with eyes raised up and beaming with great delight they reported everything to Bṛhadbala.

## \|\| 1.125.56 \|\|

*so'pi tatsarvamākarṇya tataḥ śīghrataraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*padbhyāmeva sthito yatra satyasandho mahīpatiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On hearing everything, Bṛhadbala hurried on foot and reached the place where King Satyasandha was present.

## \|\| 1.125.57-58 \|\|

*tatastaṃ praṇipatyoccaiḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*svāgataṃ te mahīpāla bhūyaḥ susvāgataṃ ca te \|\| 57 \|\|*

*idaṃ rājyaṃ nijaṃ bhūyo mayā bhṛtyena sādaram \|*  
*kuruṣva svecchayā dehi dānāni vividhāni ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. He made obeisance with deep reverence to him and stood there with palms joined in veneration. He said: “Welcome unto you, O king, hearty welcome unto you again. Take back this kingdom of yours once again along with me as your respectful servant. Rule over it as you please, giving religious gifts of various kinds.”

## \|\| 1.125.59 \|\|

*tatastaṃ ca samāliṃgya śirasyādhāya cāsakṛt \|*  
*uvācāśrupariklinnavadano gadgadākṣaram \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thereupon, the other king embraced him and smelt the crown of his head frequently. With tears drenching his face, he said with words choked with emotions:

## \|\| 1.125.60-61 \|\|

*vatsa cīrṇaṃ mayā rājyaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ pṛthagvidham \|*  
*vājimedhamukhairyajñairiṣṭaṃ saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tasmāttapaścariṣyāmi sutayā cānayā saha \|*  
*yathaiṣā labhate bhūyastāruṇyaṃ prāktanaṃ śubham \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. “Dear One, I have amply held sway over the kingdom. Different kinds of gifts had been made. I have also performed many Yajñas like house-sacrifices with the full complement of monetary gifts. So I shall perform penance along with this daughter of mine, so that she can regain her earlier splendid youth.”

## \|\| 1.125.62 \|\|

*bṛhadbala uvāca \|*  
*pāraṃparyeṇa rājeṃdra mayaitatsakalaṃ śrutam \|*  
*satyasaṃdho mahīpālaḥ kanyāmādāya nirgataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

Bṛhadbala said:

62\. O great king, this has been heard by me traditionally that King Satyasandha went away taking his daughter.

## \|\| 1.125.63 \|\|

*kutracinna samāyātaḥ sa bhūyo'pi purottame \|*  
*tatastatsacivai rājyaṃ pratipālya ciraṃ nṛpa \|*  
*abhiṣiktastataḥ putraḥ suhayonāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He had gone somewhere and never returned to his excellent city. O king, his (your) ministers waited for a long time and crowned his son well-known by the name Suhaya.

## \|\| 1.125.64 \|\|

*tasyāhaṃ kramaśo jātaḥ saptasaptatimo vibho \|*  
*puruṣastava vaṃśasya samudbhūto mahāpatiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I am the seventy-seventh successor in your family. I have now become the king.

## \|\| 1.125.65 \|\|

*tasmādatraiva kalyāṇe sthāne'sminmedhyatāṃ gate \|*  
*gartātīrthe kuru vibho tapastvamanayā saha \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Hence in this meritorious spot in the sacred Gartā Tīrtha, O Lord, do perform the rites of your penance along with this lady.

## \|\| 1.125.66 \|\|

*yena te caraṇau nityaṃ praṇipatya trisaṃdhijam \|*  
*śreyaḥ prāpnomyasaṃdigdhaṃ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. May this favour be done to me, so that I can bow down at your feet thrice a day and attain the welfare doubtlessly.

## \|\| 1.125.67 \|\|

*satyasaṃdha uvāca \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre mayāsītsthāpitaṃ purā \|*  
*liṃgaṃ vṛṣabhanāthasya tāvadasti suputraka \|\| 67 \|\|*

Satyasandha said:

67\. Formerly there, in Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra, a Liṅga of the Lord of the bull (Vṛṣabhanātha) had been installed by me. O good son, I hope it is still there.

## \|\| 1.125.68 \|\|

*tattasyārādhanaṃ nityaṃ kariṣyāmi divāniśam \|*  
*tasmātprāpaya māṃ tatra anayā sutayā saha \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Hence I shall propitiate it day and night. So do take me there along with this daughter of mine.

## \|\| 1.125.69 \|\|

*evaṃ tayoḥ pravadatoranyonyaṃ bhūmipālayoḥ \|*  
*garttātīrthātsamāyātā brāhmaṇāḥ kautukānvitāḥ \|*  
*śrutvā bhūmipatiṃ prāptaṃ ciraṃtanaguruṃ śubham \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Even as the two kings were conversing together thus, Brāhmaṇas from Gartātīrtha who had heard that the age-old splendid king had come, came out of curiosity.

## \|\| 1.125.70 \|\|

*tataḥ sa pārthivasteṣāṃ dattvārghaṃ prāṃjaliḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*provāca svargavṛttāṃtamāsyatāmiti sādaram \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then the king offered them Argha and stood with palms joined in reverence. He said respectfully, “Be seated” and narrated to them the events of Svarga.

## \|\| 1.125.71-72 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*upaviṣṭā nareṃdrasya caturdikṣu suvismitāḥ \|*  
*papracchustaṃ ca bhūpālaṃ vārtāṃ brahmagṛhodbhavām \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yathā sa tatra niryāta āgataśca yathā purā \|*  
*ālāpāḥ padmayoneśca yathā jātāstvanekaśaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71 -72. Then all those Brāhmaṇas who were wonder-struck sat comfortably all round the great king in the order of their seniority. They asked the king for detailed news about the abode of Brahmā as to how he went there earlier and came back from there and the way the various talks were held with the Lotus-born One.

## \|\| 1.125.73 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāṃtamāsādya satyasaṃdho mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*kiṃcidāsādya taṃ prāha samīpasthaṃ bṛhadbalam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then at the close of the dialogue King Satyasandha came and told Brahadbala:

## \|\| 1.125.74 \|\|

*mayā iṣṭaṃ makhaiścitrairanekairbhūridakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*dānāni ca vicitrāṇi yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “I have performed various kinds of sacrifices with plenty of monetary gifts. Innumerable gifts were made by me.

## \|\| 1.125.75 \|\|

*ekadāhaṃ gataḥ putra camatkārapurottame \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ mayā puraṃ tacca samaṃtādbrāhmaṇaivṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Once, dear son, I went to the excellent city of Camatkāra. The entire city was full of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.125.76 \|\|

*japasvādhyāyasaṃpannairagnihotraparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*gṛhasthadharmasaṃpannairlokadvayaphalānvitaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Those Brāhmaṇas were always engaged in regular practice of Japa and self-study of the Vedas. They were devoted to Agnihotra rites. They regularly performed all the rites of householders and they were fortunate enough to enjoy the benefit of the two (this and other) worlds.

## \|\| 1.125.77-78 \|\|

*tataśca ciṃtitaṃ citte sa vanyo mama pūrvajaḥ \|*  
*yenaiṣopārjitā kīrtiḥ śāśvatī kṣayavarjitā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tasmādahamapi sthāpya puramīdṛksamucchritam \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradāsyāmi tatkīrtiparivṛddhaye \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Thereupon, I thought in my mind, ‘That ancestor of mine is blessed. He has earned everlasting fame. Hence, I shall also create a great city like this and I shall give it over to Brāhmaṇas for increasing the reputation thereof.’

## \|\| 1.125.79-80 \|\|

*evaṃ citayamānasya mama nityaṃ mahīpate \|*  
*avāṃtareṇa saṃjātaṃ brahmalokaprayāṇakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*etadekaṃ hi me citte paścāttāpakaraṃ sthitam \|*  
*nānyatkiṃcinmahīpāla kṛtakṛtyasya sarvataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Even as I was always thinking thus, O king, the trip to Brahmaloka took place incidentally. This is the only matter and nothing else that causes regret to my mind. O king, I have fulfilled all my duties.

## \|\| 1.125.81 \|\|

*tasmātprārthaya vipreṃdrānkāṃścideṣāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*yena yacchāmi susthānaṃ kṛtvā tebhyastavājñayā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Hence, ask some of the leading Brāhmaṇas from among these noble-souled ones so that, with your permission, I shall make a good place for living and give it over to them.’

## \|\| 1.125.82-83 \|\|

*tataḥ sa prārthayāmāsa tadarthaṃ brāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*mamopari dayāṃ kṛtvā kriyatāṃ bhoḥ parigrahaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*asya bhūpasya sadbhaktyā yacchataḥ puramuttamam \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ pālayiṣyāmi sarve madvaṃśajāśca te \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Thereafter, he requested the excellent Brāhmaṇas: “Have compassion on me and let this be accepted. Thanks to the good devotion of this king who has given an excellent city. I shall protect you all. So also all the persons born of my family.”

## \|\| 1.125.84 \|\|

*tataḥ kāṃścitsukṛcchreṇa samānīya bṛhadbalaḥ \|*  
*rājñe nivedayāmāsa etebhyo dīyatāmiti \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Then Bṛhadbala brought some persons with great difficulty and submitted to the king, “Let it (the township) be given to these.”

## \|\| 1.125.85 \|\|

*tataḥ prakṣālya sarveṣāṃ pādānsa pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*satyasaṃdho dadau tebhyaḥ purārthaṃ bhūmimuttamām \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then Satyasandha, the king, washed their feet and gave them excellent plot of land for the construction of the city.

## \|\| 1.125.86 \|\|

*bṛhadbalasya cādeśaṃ dadau saṃprasthitaḥ svayam \|*  
*tvayaitadyogyatāṃ neyaṃ puraṃ parapuraṃjaya \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. He gave directions to Bṛhadbala: “O destroyer of the cities of enemies, this city should be made fit by you.” Then he started.

## \|\| 1.125.87 \|\|

*gatvā ca sa tayā sārdhaṃ tatkṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*talliṃgaṃ prāpya saṃhṛṣṭaściraṃ tepe tapastataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Along with her (his daughter) he went to the holy place Hāṭakeśvara. Approaching that Liṅga he became delighted and then performed penance for a long time.

## \|\| 1.125.88 \|\|

*sāpi karṇotpalā prāpya kiṃcitpuṇyaṃ jalāśayam \|*  
*tapastepe pratiṣṭhāpya gaurīṃ śraddhāsamanvitā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Karṇotpalā went to a sacred water-pond and installed Gaurī there with great faith. Then she too performed penance.

## \|\| 1.125.89 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare rājā kāladharmamupāgataḥ \|*  
*ānartādhipatiryuddhe hataḥ putraiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. In the meantime, the king of Ānarta (i.e.Bṛhadbala) was killed in battle along with his sons.

## \|\| 1.125.90 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve gartātīrthasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*satyasaṃdhaṃ samabhyetya procurduḥkhasamanvitāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then all those Brāhmaṇas hailing form Gartātīrtha approached Satyasandha and told him with deep sorrow:

## \|\| 1.125.91-93 \|\|

*parigrahaḥ kṛto'smābhiḥ kevalaṃ pṛthivīpate \|*  
*na ca kiṃcitphalaṃ jātaṃ vṛttijaṃ naḥ purodbhavam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru sthitiṃ tvaṃ ca svadharmaparivṛddhaye \|\| \|*  
*yena tadvartanopāyo hyasmākaṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 92 \|\|*

*rājā bṛhadbalo yuddhe kāladharmamupāgataḥ \|*  
*yastvayā darśito'smākaṃ vṛttyarthaṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 93 \|\|*

91-93. “O Lord of the earth, only we have formally accepted the gifts. But nothing has been done in regard to the city and our means of sustenance.

Hence, O excellent king, do the things necessary to augment your virtue by making arrangements for our sustenance. King Bṛhadbala who was pointed out to us by you for the purpose of our sustenance, has been killed in battle.”

## \|\| 1.125.94 \|\|

*satyasandha uvāca \|*  
*saṃnyasto'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā vṛttiṃ kartuṃ na ca kṣamaḥ \|*  
*yadi me syātpumānkaścidanvaye'pi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

Satyasandha said:

94\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I am a recluse. I have renounced the world. Hence I am not competent to create means of sustenance (for you). There could have been no doubt about it if there was a man in our family.

## \|\| 1.125.95 \|\|

*tasmādvrajatha harmyaṃ svaṃ prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mama \|*  
*abhāgyairbhavadīyaiśca hato rājā bṛhadbalaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Hence be pleased to go home. Since you are unlucky, king Bṛhadbala has been killed.

## \|\| 1.125.96 \|\|

*evamuktāśca te viprā matvā tathyaṃ ca tadvacaḥ \|*  
*svasthānaṃ tvaritā jagmuḥ so'pi cakre tapaściram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. On being told thus, those Brāhmaṇas thought it true. They considered his words based on facts. Then they went to their abode and the king continued his penance for a long time.

## Chapter 126 - Greatness of Satyasandheśvara (Satyasandha-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.126.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya tapasthasya putryā saha dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ājagmurbrāhmaṇāḥ sarve camatkārapurodbhavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, while he was engaged in penance along with his daughter (Karṇotpalā) all the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura came there.

## \|\| 1.126.2 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*sandeheṣu ca sarveṣu vivādeṣu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*abhāvātpārthivendrasya saṃjātaśca parābhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

2\. Loss (of justice) and confusion has arisen due to the absence of a leading king who could take decision in all doubtful cases, particularly in disputes.

## \|\| 1.126.3 \|\|

*tataśca dvijavaryaiḥ sa saṃnyastaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭaśca prārthitaścaiva nijarājyasya rakṣaṇe \|*  
*anyasmindivase prāha kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then the king who had renounced was requested by the excellent Brāhmaṇas for the protection of their kingdom. On another day, he stood with palms joined in reverence and asked:

## \|\| 1.126.4 \|\|

*rājovāca \|\| \|*  
*anarho'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ saṃdehaṃ hartumeva vaḥ \|*  
*rakṣāṃ kartuṃ viśeṣeṇa tyaktaśastro'smi cādhunā \|\| 4 \|\|*

The king said:

4\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I am not competent to remove your doubts. I am particularly incapable of according protection as I have set aside all weapons now.

## \|\| 1.126.5-6 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*sarve vayaṃ mahārāja bhūpasyāpyadhikā yataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃkāreṇa darpeṇa nijaṃ sthānaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*na kasyacinmahārāja kadāpi ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*vartanāyāśca sandehaḥ sthānakṛtye'pi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

5-6. O great king, since all of us are considered to be superior to king, since we have resorted to our place with selfishness and arrogance, no one has any doubt at any time in regard to the duty regarding rites to be performed at the holy spot and also sustenance.

## \|\| 1.126.7 \|\|

*asaṃkhyātā kṛtā vṛttiḥ purā'smākaṃ mahātmanā \|*  
*tataḥ sā vṛddhimānītā tatparaiḥ pārthivottamaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly, innumerable means of sustenance were assigned to us by the noble-souled one. Then increase was done in it by the later excellent kings.

## \|\| 1.126.8-9 \|\|

*tvayā caiva viśeṣeṇa yāvadrājā bṛhadbalaḥ \|*  
*ānartaviṣaye rājā yo yaḥ syātsa prayacchati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvāṃ vṛttiṃ gṛhasthānāṃ yathāyogyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tavāgre kiṃ vayaṃ brūmastvaṃ vetsi sakalaṃ yataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Especially this has been said by you: “As long as King Bṛhadbala continues to be in Ānarta land and later whoever happens to be the king, he will assiduously offer sustenance to the householders.” Now what can we say before you? For you know everything.

## \|\| 1.126.10 \|\|

*yathā vṛttiḥ purā dattā yathā saṃrakṣitā tvayā \|*  
*tasmāccintaya rājendra sthānaṃ vartanasaṃbhavam \|*  
*upāyaṃ yena maryādā vṛttistasmātsukhena tu \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. You know how sustenance was offered earlier and how it was maintained by you. Hence, O leading king, think about the spot and also the means of sustenance whereby there shall be happiness and comfort. Everything shall be within bounds.

## \|\| 1.126.11 \|\|

*tataḥ sa suciraṃ dhyātvā gartātīrthasamudbhavān \|*  
*ākāryopamanyuvaṃśasya saṃbhavānvedapāragān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon, he thought for a long time and summoned those masters of the Vedas born of the family of Upamanyu, hailing from Gartātīrtha.

## \|\| 1.126.12-16 \|\|

*praṇipātaṃ prakṛtvātha tataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*madīyasthāna saṃsthānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvakṛtyāni kāryāṇi bhṛtyavadvinayānvitaiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ rakṣā vidhātavyā yuṣmadīyaṃ vacokhilam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ete saṃpālayiṣyanti maryādākāramuttamam \|*  
*sandeheṣu ca sarveṣu vivādeṣu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*rājakāryeṣu cānyeṣu ete dāsyanti nirṇayam \|*  
*yuṣmadīyaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ete pālyāḥ prasādena puṣṭiṃ neyāśca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*īrṣyāṃ sarvāṃ parityajya madīyasthānavṛddhaye \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. After making obeisance he respectfully told: “All the duties should be carried out humbly like servants, in regard to all the people residing in my holy spot particularly the Brāhmaṇas. Protection should always be accorded (to them).

They will strictly observe the bounds and limits of decorum in cases of doubts and especially in cases of all disputes (But the following is to be noted).

In administrative matters and other cases also these people will ultimately decide after listening to your words, good or bad.

These should be protected with favour. They should be nourished in accordance with your capacity. Jealousy should be eschewed. Everything should be done for the prosperity of my holy spot.”

## \|\| 1.126.17 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva taiḥ proktaḥ sa rājā brāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*camatkāpurodbhūtānbhūyaḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On being told by them, “So it shall be” the king once again respectfully said to the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura:

## \|\| 1.126.18-20 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ vartanārthāya sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*ete viprā mayā dattā gartātīrthasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ vacanātsarvaṃ yuṣmadīyaṃ prajāyatām \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā jāyate nūnaṃ cātuścaraṇasūcitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nānyathā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu \|*  
*proktaṃ lakṣamitairanyairyuṣmadīyapurodbhavaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. “For your sustenance in regard to all matters for ever, these Brāhmaṇas hailing from Gartātīrtha have been appointed by me. Everything concerning you shall be at the instance of these. The establishment of everything shall duly result as indicated by the four Vedas. Not otherwise, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, whether little or much is expressed by others hailing from your city numbering one hundred thousand."

## \|\| 1.126.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataste brāhmaṇā hṛṣṭāstānādāya dvijottamān \|*  
*teṣāṃ matena cakruśca sarvakṛtyāni sarvadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sūta said:

21\. Thereupon, those Brāhmaṇas joyously took those excellent Brāhmaṇas and did everything forever in accordance with their advice.

## \|\| 1.126.22 \|\|

*tatastatra pure jātā maryādā dharmavarddhinī \|*  
*sarvakṛtyeṣu sarveṣāṃ tathā vṛddhiḥ purasya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereupon, there arose bounds of morality (Dharma) causing the increase of virtue in that city. In every affair everyone in the city flourished.

## \|\| 1.126.23 \|\|

*te'pi teṣāṃ prasādena garttātīrthabhavā dvijāḥ \|*  
*parāṃ vibhūtimāsthāya modante sukhasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With their favour those Brāhmaṇas hailing from Gartātīrtha attained great riches and rejoiced happily.

## \|\| 1.126.24 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya sa rājā tatpurottamam \|*  
*samabhyetya dvijānsarvāṃstataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Once thereafter that king arrived at the city and spoke respectfully to all those Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.126.25-27 \|\|

*yuṣmadīyaprasādena kṣetre'tra sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaṃ svargaṃ prayāsyāmi sāṃprataṃ tu dvijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nāsmākamanvaye kaścitsāṃprataṃ vartate nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ liṃgametadvai darśayāmi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūjārthaṃ cāpi vṛttyarthaṃ bhogārthaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tasmādyuṣmābhirevāsya pūjā kāryā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*rathayātrā viśeṣeṇa dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. “With your favour, a severe penance has been performed by me in the holy spot here. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall now go to Svarga.

Now there is no king belonging to our family, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, to whom I can show this Liṅga, who could have used this for the purpose of adoration, livelihood or for enjoyment of pleasures. Hence this worship should be assiduously carried out by you alone. Taking pity on me, do these things and particularly the Rathayātrā (religious procession with the deity in a chariot).”

## \|\| 1.126.28 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*sapta viṃśatiliṃgāni yatheṣṭāni mahītale \|*  
*camatkārasutānāṃ ca pūjyaṃte sarvadaiva tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

28\. Already twenty-seven Liṅgas are dear to the sons of Camatkārapura and are always worshipped by them.

## \|\| 1.126.29 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśatimaṃ tadvadetalliṃgaṃ tavodbhavam \|*  
*sarvadā pūjayiṣyāmo niścinto bhava pārthiva \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Similarly your Liṅga shall be the twenty-eighth one. We shall worship it always. O king, be free from any anxiety (about it).

## \|\| 1.126.30 \|\|

*asya yātrāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ kārtike māsi sarvadā \|*  
*balipūjopahārāṃśca gītavādyāni śaktitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. We shall perform the Yātrā always in the month of Kārttika and offer oblations, presents, adorations, songs and instrumental music within our capacity.

## \|\| 1.126.31 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa tairhṛṣṭo gatvātmīyaṃ tadāśramam \|*  
*snāpayitvātha talliṃgaṃ pūjāṃ cakre prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On being told thus, he became delighted. After going to the hermitage, he bathed the Liṅga and performed the worship with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.126.32 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ samarpitaṃ liṃgaṃ tena taddharasaṃbhavam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ vaṃśocchede sthite dvijāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Sūta said:

32\. Thus, the Liṅga of Hara was dedicated to all those leading Brāhmaṇas, O Brāhmaṇas, when the extinction of the family was about to happen.

## \|\| 1.126.33 \|\|

*sakalaṃ kārtikaṃ martyo yastacchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*snāpayetpūjayeccāpi sa nūnaṃ muktimāpnuyāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A man who is endowed with perfect faith and who bathes and worships it during the whole of the month of Kārttika shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.126.34 \|\|

*somasya divase prāpte varṣaṃ yāvatkṛtakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tasya pūjāṃ karotyevaṃ snāpayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*so'pi muktiṃ vrajenmartya etattātānmayā śrutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A devotee should wait patiently for a year and on a Monday the worship should be performed after duly bathing it. He also will attain salvation. I have heard this from my father.

## Chapter 127 - Greatness of Karṇotpalā Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.127.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yā sā karṇotpalānāma tvayāsmākaṃ prakīrtitā \|*  
*kiñcijjalāśrayaṃ prāpya tapastapati saṃsthitā \|*  
*tasyāḥ sarvaṃ samācakṣva yathā tapasi sā sthitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. The lady named Karṇotpalā was mentioned by you. She had gone to some water-pond and engaged herself in penance. Do tell us everything connected with her and also the details of her penance.

## \|\| 1.127.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gaurīpādakṛtasthānā śraddhayā parayā yutā \|*  
*tāvattuṣṭiṃ gatā devī girijā śaṃkarapriyā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. She resorted to the feet of Gaurī and was endowed with great faith. Girijā, the beloved wife of Śaṅkara, became pleased.

## \|\| 1.127.3 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca te putri tuṣṭāhaṃ vāṃchitaṃ vada \|*  
*yena yacchāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then she said: “Dear daughter, I have become pleased with you. Say what is desired by you, so that I can grant it to you even if it is extremely difficult to get.”

## \|\| 1.127.4 \|\|

*karṇotpalovāca \|*  
*mama patyuḥ kṛte devi mama tātaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*rājyādbhraṣṭaḥ sukhāccāpi kuṭuṃbena vivarjitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Karṇotpalā said:

4\. O goddess, my father had been very miserable in seeking a husband for me. He ceased to be a king, lost his happiness and had no kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.127.5 \|\|

*tataścaiva tapastepe vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ vārddhakyamāpannā kaumārye'pi ca saṃsthitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He became disgusted and detached, so performed a penance. I have become old, yet I continue to be a confirmed virgin.

## \|\| 1.127.6 \|\|

*tasmādbhavatu me bharttā kaścidrūpotkaṭaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ devamartyānāṃ tvatprasādātsureśvari \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Hence, O goddess of Suras, with your favour, let someone be my husbanḍ—someone who is most handsome among all the Devas and human beings.

## \|\| 1.127.7 \|\|

*tathā syātparamaṃ rūpaṃ tāruṇyaṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|*  
*yathāsya jāyate saukhyaṃ tāpasasyāpi me pituḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Further, let me regain youth and beauty, with your favour, so that even as a sage my father should be happy.

## \|\| 1.127.8 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*māghamāsatṛtīyāyāṃ śanaiścaradine śubhe \|*  
*nakṣatre vasudaivatye rūpaṃ dhyātvātha yauvanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

The Devī said:

8\. On the third lunar day in the month of Māgha, when the splendid day of Saturn coincides with the constellation Dhaniṣṭhā, you shall meditate upon beauty and youthful form.

## \|\| 1.127.9 \|\|

*tvayā snānaṃ prakartavyaṃ supuṇye'tra jalāśaye \|*  
*tato divya vapurbhūtvā yauvanena samanvitā \|*  
*bhaviṣyasi na saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then you should take your holy bath in this meritorious water-pond. Thereby you will attain a divine physical form as well as the prime of youth. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that is spoken by me.

## \|\| 1.127.10 \|\|

*anyāpi yā mahābhāge nārī snānaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*tasminnahani sāpyevaṃ rūpayuktā bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O highly esteemed lady, any other woman who takes her bath on that day, shall also become endowed with beauty.

## \|\| 1.127.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha sā devī gatā cādarśanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*sāpi cānveṣayāmāsa tṛtīyāṃ śaninā saha \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After saying thus, the goddess disappeared. She too began her quest for the third lunar day coinciding with a Saturday.

## \|\| 1.127.12 \|\|

*vasudevātmakenaiva nakṣatreṇa prayatnataḥ \|*  
*dhyāyamānā ca tāṃ devīṃ sarvakāmapradāyinīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. She wanted eagerly that day to coincide with the constellation Dhaniṣṭhā. She continued her meditation on the goddess, the bestower of all desires.

## \|\| 1.127.13 \|\|

*tataḥ katipayāhasya jātā sā yogasaṃyutā \|*  
*tṛtīyā yā yathoktā ca tayā devyā purā dvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After a few days the third lunar day had such a combination as mentioned by the goddess earlier, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.127.14 \|\|

*tataḥ sā rūpasaubhāgyaṃ yauvanaṃ vāṃchitaṃ patim \|*  
*dhyāyamānā jale tasminnarddharātre viveśa ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then she meditated upon exquisite beauty, prime of youth and a desirable husband. She entered the pond at midnight.

## \|\| 1.127.15 \|\|

*tato divyavapurbhūtvā yauvanena samanvitā \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtā salilāttasmājjanavismayakāriṇī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereby she attained the prime of youth as well as a divine physical form. She came out of water causing surprise unto all the people.

## \|\| 1.127.16-18 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto gaurīvākyaprabodhitaḥ \|*  
*tadarthaṃ bhagavānkāmaḥ patnyarthaṃ prītisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*abravīcca mahābhāge kāmohaṃ svayamāgataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pārvatyādeśitā bhāryā tasmānme bhava mā ciram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yasmātprītyā samāyātastavāṃtikamahaṃ śubhe \|*  
*tasmātprītiriti khyātā mama bhāryā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. In the meantime, Lord Kāma who was enlightened in this respect by the words of Gaurī came there joyously to claim her as his wife. He said: “O highly esteemed lady, I am Kāma himself present before you. Hence, as commanded by Pārvatī, be my wife. Do not delay. O Lady of splendid nature, since I came near you with great Prīti (pleasure), you shall become my wife well-known by the name Prīti.”

## \|\| 1.127.19 \|\|

*karṇotpalovāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ smara mattātaṃ taṃ gatvā prārthaya svayam \|*  
*svacchaṃdā syādyataḥ kanyā na kathaṃcitpravartitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

Karṇotpalā said:

19\. If this be so, O Smara, go to my father and request him yourself since no girl can act independently as she pleases.

## \|\| 1.127.20 \|\|

*ya eṣa dṛśyate ramyaḥ prāsādo nāti dūrataḥ \|*  
*asyāṃte tiṣṭhate'smākaṃ tātastapasi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Yonder, not very far away, is seen a beautiful palace. My father is engaged in penance within it.

## \|\| 1.127.21 \|\|

*atrāhaṃ pūrvato gatvā tasya tiṣṭhāmi cāṃtike \|*  
*bhavānāgatya paścācca prārthayiṣyati māṃ tataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I shall go there before you and stand by my father. You will come there later and request him for me.

## \|\| 1.127.22-24 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva kāmokte gatā sā tatsamīpataḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya tataḥ prāha diṣṭyā tāta mayā punaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saṃprāptaṃ yauvanaṃ kāṃtaṃ samārādhya harapriyām \|*  
*tasmātkuru vivāhaṃ me hṛtsthaṃ sukhamavāpnuhi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*madarthe preṣito bharttā tayā devyā'tisundaraḥ \|*  
*puṣpa cāpaḥ svayaṃ prāptaḥ so'pi tāta tavāṃtikam \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. When Kāma said “So be it”, she went (ahead) near her father. After bowing down to him, she said: “Dear father, fortunately exquisite prime of youth has been regained by me after propitiating the beloved of Hara. So perform my marriage and be satisfied in your heart. A very handsome husband has been sent by the goddess for my sake. The Flower-bowed One (god of Love) himself has come to you, dear father."

## \|\| 1.127.25-26 \|\|

*atha tāṃ sa samālokya svāṃ sutāṃ yauvanānvitām \|*  
*harṣeṇa mahatā yuktāṃ kāṃtayuktāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*abravīdadya me putri saṃjātaṃ tapasaḥ phalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*jīvitasya ca kalyāṇi yatvaṃ prāptā navaṃ vayaḥ \|*  
*bhartāraṃ ca tathābhīṣṭaṃ devyā dattaṃ manobhavam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. On seeing his daughter blessed with youthful form, extremely pleased in the company of her lover, he said: “Dear daughter, now my penance has become fruitful. O splendid lady, my life is blessed, since you have regained prime of youth and a covetable husband, the mind-born Kāma himself, bestowed, by the goddess.”

## \|\| 1.127.27-28 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kāmastasyāṃtikamupādravat \|*  
*abravīddehi me bhūpa svāṃ kanyāṃ cāruhāsinīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

*asyā arthe'hamādiṣṭaḥ svayaṃ gauryā nṛpottama \|*  
*kāmadeva iti khyātastrailokyaṃ yena mohitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In the meantime, Kāma came quickly to his presence and said: “O king, give me your daughter of beautiful smiles. O excellent king, I have been ordered by Gaurī herself in regard to this lady. I am well known as Kāmadeva by whom the three worlds have been enchanted.”

## \|\| 1.127.29 \|\|

*tatastāmarpayāmāsa tāṃ kanyāṃ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāgniṃ sākṣiṇaṃ vākyādbrāhmaṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, at the instance of Brāhmaṇas, the king offered his daughter to him keeping the Fire-god as witness.

## \|\| 1.127.30 \|\|

*sā cāsya cābhavatprītisthānaṃ yasmātsulocanā \|*  
*rateranaṃtarā tasmātprītināmā'bhavacchubhā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Since the splendid-eyed lady became the object of his love, being second only to Rati, the auspicious fair lady became Prīti by name.

## \|\| 1.127.31 \|\|

*evaṃ tayā tapastaptaṃ tasmāttatra jalāśaye \|*  
*tannāmnā khyātimāyātaṃ samaste'tra mahītale \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Since the lady had performed her penance in that holy pond, it became well-known all over the earth after her name.

## \|\| 1.127.32 \|\|

*sakalaṃ māghamāsaṃ ca yā strī snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*pumānvā prātarutthāya sa prayāgaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A woman who performs holy ablution during the whole of the month of Māgha, or a man who gets up early in the morning and takes his bath, shall attain the benefit of (bath in) Prayāga.

## \|\| 1.127.33 \|\|

*rūpavāñjāyate dakṣaḥ sadā janmani janmani \|*  
*na viyogamavāpnoti kadātridbāṃdhavaiḥ saha \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In every birth he will be handsome and expert and efficient in everyting. Never will he be separated from his kinsmen.

## Chapter 128 - Origin of Aṭeśvara (Aṭa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.128.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*satyasandhopi hṛṣṭātmā satāṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhānvitām \|*  
*abhīṣṭapatinā yuktāṃ kṛtakṛtyo babhūva ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatastasyaiva liṃgasya dakṣiṇāṃ mūrtimāśritaḥ \|*  
*dṛḍhaṃ padmāsanaṃ kṛtvā samyagdhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ātmānamātmanaivātha brahmadvāreṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tato niḥsārayāmāsa pulakena samanvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. On seeing his daughter happy after being united with her desired husband, Satyasandha became highly pleased in his heart and felt that he had done his duty.

He resorted to the southern phase (side?) of the same Liṅga and seated himself in lotus posture firmly. He began the meditation properly thereafter. He saw the Atman within himself. With a sensation of horripilation, he released it through Brahmadvāra (cerebral aperture).

## \|\| 1.128.4 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇāstasya camatkārapurodbhavāḥ \|*  
*devatā darśanārthāya prāptā dṛṣṭvā kalevaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura came there for viewing the deity but saw his dead body.

## \|\| 1.128.5 \|\|

*apriyaṃ tejasā hīnaṃ mṛtamaspṛśyatāṃ gatam \|*  
*liṃgasya nātidūrasthaṃ dāhyārthaṃ yatnamāsthitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It was dead, displeasing and lacking in lustre. It was not worthy of being touched. It was found not far from the Liṅga. They then prepared for the cremation thereof.

## \|\| 1.128.6 \|\|

*yāvadgurvīṃ citāṃ kṛtvā tamanveṣṭuṃ samudyatāḥ \|*  
*tāvannaṣṭaṃ śavaṃ tacca jñāyate naiva kutracit \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They prepared a large pyre and came in to take him out. Then they saw the corpse missing. It could not be seen anywhere.

## \|\| 1.128.7 \|\|

*tataśca vismayāviṣṭāstaṃ praśaṃsāsamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*vacanairbahuśo bhūyo vikathya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They were overwhelmed with surprise. They repeatedly spoke about him in highly laudatory terms.

## \|\| 1.128.8 \|\|

*tatastasyotthaliṃgasya sarvaṃ pūjādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*sarve nirūpayāmāsuḥ saptaviṃśatimadhyataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then all of them reviewed the mode of worship of the Liṅga pertaining to him, in the middle of the twenty-seven (other Liṅgas).

## \|\| 1.128.9 \|\|

*liṃgānāṃ tadbhavennityaṃ satyasaṃdhasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*kāmadaṃ bhaktajaṃtūnāṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Of all the Liṅgas, that Liṅga happened to be the bestower of desired things upon all devout creatures and the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 1.128.10 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*camatkāranareṃdrasya vaṃśe kṣīṇe mahāmate \|*  
*ānarttādhipatiḥ ko'nyastatra rājā babhūva ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

The sages said:

10\. O highly intelligent one, when the line of the king of Camatkāra (pura) became extinct which other king became the overlord of Ānarta?

## \|\| 1.128.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bṛhadbale hate bhūpe saṃgrāme dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*putrabaṃdhusamāyuktāḥ sarva lokāḥ samāyayuḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when king Bṛhadbala was killed in battle, all the people accompanied by their sons and kinsmen came there.

## \|\| 1.128.12 \|\|

*yatrasthaḥ sa mahīpālaḥ satyasaṃdhastaponvitaḥ \|*  
*śokodvignāstataḥ prāhustaṃ bhūpaṃ rahasi sthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They came to the place where King Satyasandha was engaged in penance. With great distress and sorrow they spoke to the King in his secret resort:

## \|\| 1.128.13-16 \|\|

*kṣīṇo'yaṃ tāvako vaṃśo na kaścidvidyate yataḥ \|*  
*dāyādo'pi kathaṃ pṛthvī saṃpratīyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*arājake nṛpaśreṣṭha mātsyo nyāyaḥ pravartate \|*  
*rāṣṭre caiva pure caiva grāme caiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*paradāraratā ye ca ye ca taskaravṛttayaḥ \|*  
*sarve rājabhayādrājanmaryādāṃ pālayaṃti vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ tapa utsṛjya rājyaṃ pūrvakramāgatam \|*  
*kuru rājyaṃ tathā dārānputrārthaṃ prāpya mā ciram \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. “This line of yours is extinct since none of your cousins and successors is present (alive). How shall the earth be sustained now?

In the state of anarchy, O excellent king, Mātsya Nyāya will prevail (i.e. a powerful one will prey upon weaker ones). Whether it is the whole country or a city or, more particularly, a village the same rule will hold good (everywhere).

Those who are enamoured of other men’s wives, those who adopt thievery as the means of sustenance—all these keep to the bounds of morality and decorum only because they are afraid of the king.

Hence, do stop your penance and rule over the kingdom that has come to you by succession. Take a wife for the sake of begetting a son.”

## \|\| 1.128.17 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*saṃnyasto'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā na rājyaṃ kartumutsahe \|*  
*na sutānāṃ na dārāṇāṃ saṃgrahaṃ ca kathaṃcana \|\| 17 \|\|*

The king said:

17\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I have renounced the world. I am not eager to rule over a kingdom. Nor do I want to marry or beget sons.

## \|\| 1.128.18 \|\|

*tatputrārthaṃ pravakṣyāmi yuṣmākaṃ svāminaḥ kṛte \|*  
*upāyaṃ yena rājā syādānartto lokapālakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Therefore, I shall tell the means of getting a leader of you all and his son. Thereby, a king of Ānarta ruling over the people shall be obtained.

## \|\| 1.128.19-20 \|\|

*jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa yadā kṣatraṃ nipātitam \|*  
*garbhasthamapi kārtsnyena kopopahatacetasā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣatriyabhāryāḥ prāgṛtusnānātsamāyayuḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānputrajanmārthaṃ na kāmārthaṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. When the entire Kṣatriya race, even those in the womb, was exterminated by the furious son of Jamadagni, Paraśurāma, in his furious onslaught, the wives of those Kṣatriyas, before their menstrual bath, approached Brāhmaṇas for begetting sons and not out of lust.

## \|\| 1.128.21 \|\|

*tataḥ putrāḥ samutpannāstejovīryasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*kṣetrajā bhūmipālānāṃ saṃjātāśca mahīkṣitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sons were born who were full of refulgence and virility. Being Kṣetrajas (born of the wives) of kings they duly became kings.

## \|\| 1.128.22-23 \|\|

*tasmādbṛhadbalasyaitā bhāryāstiṣṭhaṃti yā janāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇāṃstā upāgamya ṛtusnātā yathocitān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*labhiṣyaṃti ca putrāṃstāstebhyaḥ kṣatriyapuṃgavān \|*  
*ye bhūmiṃ pālayiṣyaṃti pālayiṣyaṃti ca prajāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Hence, O people, there are the wives of Bṛhadbala. Let Brāhmaṇas approach them after their menstrual bath and get befitting sons, leading Kṣatriyas. They will rule over the earth and protect the people.

## \|\| 1.128.24 \|\|

*tathā'trāsti śubhaṃ kuṇḍaṃ vāsiṣṭhaṃ putrajanmadam \|*  
*yatra snātā ṛtau nārī sadyo garbhavatī bhavet \|*  
*amogharetāḥ kāṃtā ca snānādatra prajāyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Further, here there is the splendid Kuṇḍa of Vasiṣṭha, which bestows sons. A woman in her menstrual cycle who takes her bath there, becomes pregnant immediately. The beautiful one becomes Amogha-retā (one in whose womb semen never becomes futile) by taking bath here.

## \|\| 1.128.25 \|\|

*ye pūrvaṃ kṣatriyā jātā brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriṇīṣu ca \|*  
*te sarve tatprabhāvena saṃjātā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those Kṣatriyas who were earlier born to Brāhmaṇas from Kṣatriya women, were born by its power undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.128.26 \|\|

*yayāyayā dvijo yaśca kṣatriṇyā'bhūdvṛtaḥ purā \|*  
*tayā saha samāgatya snātaṃ mantrapuraskṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On being wooed by a Kṣatriya woman the Brāhmaṇa had his bath with due utterance of the Mantras, and then had union with her.

## \|\| 1.128.27 \|\|

*sakṛnmaidhunasaṃsargāttatastīrthaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ yatsutā jātā duhitā na kathaṃcana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It was, due to the efficacy of the Tīrtha that by a single sexual contact male issues (sons) were born to all (those Kṣatriya women) and no daughter at all.

## \|\| 1.128.28 \|\|

*ye kecitputradā maṃtrāścātuścaraṇāsaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*te sarve'tra vasiṣṭhena prayuktāḥ kṣattramicchatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All Mantras possessing the power of bestowing sons, which were found (incorporated) in the Vedas were utilized by Vasiṣṭha who was desirous of (the continuity of) Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 1.128.29 \|\|

*daṃpatyoḥ snānamātreṇa jāte'tra syātsuputrakaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsuputradaṃnāma kuṇḍametannigadyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If the bath is taken by a wedded pair, a good son will be born. Hence this Kuṇḍa is called Suputrada (‘Granter of a good son’).

## \|\| 1.128.30 \|\|

*tasmādbhāryāḥ samastāstā bṛhadbalasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*atra snānaṃ prakurvaṃtu yathoktavidhinā janāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Hence, O people, all the wives of Bṛhadbala should take their bath here in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.128.31 \|\|

*naiva kiṃcidasatyaṃ syānna ca niṃdākaraṃ tathā \|*  
*śrūyate ca yataḥ ślokaḥ pūrvācāryairudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. There is no untruth in this nor is it blameworthy. For, there is this Śloka cited by earlier Ācāryas (preceptors):

## \|\| 1.128.32 \|\|

*adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣattramaśmano lohamucchritam \|*  
*teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “Fire is produced from water, Kṣatriyas from Brāhmaṇas and steel from rocks. Their refulgence spreads everywhere and gets dissolved in their original causes.”

## \|\| 1.128.33 \|\|

*tacchrutvā janāḥ sarve sacivānāṃ vacokhilam \|*  
*tadācakhyurdrutaṃ gatvā satyasaṃdhasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On hearing those words of King Satyasandha the people informed the ministers about it.

## \|\| 1.128.34 \|\|

*tatastāḥ sarvaśo dārā brāhmaṇānatisundarān \|*  
*ṛtusnātāḥ samājagmurnṛpapatnyaḥ suharṣitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All those wives of the king after their menstrual bath joyously courted and contacted very beautiful Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.128.35 \|\|

*yatra tatputradaṃ tīrthaṃ vasiṣṭhena vinirmitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā sakṛtsaṃgaṃ samāsādya dvijodbhavam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. They went to the Putrada Tīrtha created by Vasiṣṭha, had their bath therein and had intimate contact once only with Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.128.36 \|\|

*sarvāstāḥ putravatyaśca saṃjātā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*āsīttasya nareṃdrasya śataṃ paṃcabhiranvitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all of them gave birth to sons. The great king had one hundred five wives.

## \|\| 1.128.37 \|\|

*tāsāṃ samabhavadviprāḥ śataṃ paṃcādhikaṃ tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Brāhmaṇas, one hundred five Brāhmaṇas had their sexual union with them.

## \|\| 1.128.38 \|\|

*pratyekaṃ varaputrāṇāṃ vaṃśavṛddhikaraṃ param \|*  
*ānaṃdajananaṃ samyaksarveṣāṃ rāṣṭravāsinām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Everyone of them begot excellent sons and increased the family. They caused prefect bliss to all the residents of the country.

## \|\| 1.128.39 \|\|

*tatra śreṣṭho'bhavatputro ya ānartapatirbhuvi \|*  
*aṭonāma suvikhyātaḥ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The most excellent of those sons was well known all over the world by the name Aṭa and he became the Lord of Ānarta. He destroyed all enemies.

## \|\| 1.128.40 \|\|

*aṭeśvaraiti khyāto yena devo'tra nirmitaḥ \|*  
*subhaktyā yena dṛṣṭena vaṃśocchittirna jāyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It was by him that the deity well-known as Aṭeśvara was installed with great devotion. If the deity is visited, the extinction of the family can be averted.

## \|\| 1.128.41-42 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmāttasya kṛtaṃ nāma etaccā'ṭa iti smṛtam \|*  
*anvayena parityaktaṃ tasmātkīrtaya sūtaja \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sacivairbrāhmaṇairvāpi tasyaitannāma nirmitam \|*  
*mātrā vā tatsamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

The sages said:

41-42. Why was he given this name Aṭa? This has been abandoned by the family. Do explain this, O Sūtaja. Was this name given by the ministers or Brāhmaṇas? Or by the mother? Tell this as we are very eager to hear it.

## \|\| 1.128.43 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*na mātrā tatkṛtaṃ nāma na vipraiḥ sacivairnṛpa \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ devadūtena vyomasthena dvijottamāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sūta said:

43\. That name was given neither by the mother, nor by the Brāhmaṇas nor by the ministers. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, it was given by the messenger of Devas stationed in the firmament.

## \|\| 1.128.44 \|\|

*yathā tathā pravakṣyāmi śrotavyaṃ susamāhitaiḥ \|*  
*yayā sa bhūpatirjāto daśārṇādhipateḥ sutā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. How it was given, I shall explain. Listen with attention. It was the daughter of the king of Daśārṇa who gave birth to that king.

## \|\| 1.128.45-46 \|\|

*sā rūpayauvanopetā rūpāḍhyaṃ prāpya saddvijam \|*  
*prasthitā snātukāmātha putratīrthe mṛgekṣaṇā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sahitā tena vipreṇa kaṃdarpapratimena ca \|*  
*atha tābhyāṃ mahānrāmo mithaḥ saṃdarśanātsthitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. The fawn-eyed lady blessed with beauty and prime of youth obtained an excellent Brāhmaṇa. Desirous of the holy bath in the Putra Tīrtha she set off along with the Brāhmaṇa resembling Kandarpa. At the (first) sight of each other, their love became very intense.

## \|\| 1.128.47 \|\|

*tādṛṅmātraṃ sukṛcchreṇa prāptaṃ tīrthaṃ sutapradam \|*  
*tataḥ snātvā jale tasminniṣkrāṃtau tau sukāmukau \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Their mutual attraction was so much that they reached Sutaprada Tīrtha with very great difficulty. (They were so eager for union that they felt the journey to the Tīrtha very long and difficult.)

## \|\| 1.128.48 \|\|

*vrajamānau ca mārge'pi kāmadharmamupāgatau \|*  
*atyautsukyātsusaṃhṛṣṭau lajjāṃ tyaktvā sudūrataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. While going along the path, they indulged in sexual intercourse. They were very delighted due to ardent desire. So they cast aside shame.

## \|\| 1.128.49 \|\|

*niṃdamānasya lokasya vicchedavacanaistadā \|*  
*vīryotsarge'tha saṃjāte yāvaduttiṣṭhate dvijaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The people censured them with words urging them to separate. By that time the semen had been discharged and the Brāhmaṇa tried to get up.

## \|\| 1.128.50-52 \|\|

*tāvadākāśagā vāṇī sahasā devanirmitā \|*  
*aṭatārājamārgeṇa vipreṇānena vai yataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*utpāditastu putro'yamautsukyādbrāhmaṇena tu \|*  
*aṭākhyo bhūpatistasmālloke khyāto bhaviṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dīrghāyurbahuputraśca śatruṃpakṣakṣayāvahaḥ \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādviprā aṭākhyaḥ sa babhūva ha \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. By that time an aerial voice caused by Devas announced: “Since this son was eagerly begot by the Brāhmaṇa while going along the Highway, he will become a king well known by the name Aṭa. He will be long-lived. He will have many sons and he will conquer the enemies.”

It was for this reason, O Brāhmaṇas, that he was called Aṭa.

## \|\| 1.128.53 \|\|

*svavaṃśoddharacaṃdro'tra vāṃchitārthaprado'rthinām \|*  
*tenaitatkṣetramāsādya sthāpitaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|*  
*svanāmnā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvadeṣṭapradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He was a person who lifted up his family arising from it like the Moon. He gifted wealth to all suppliants. He came to this holy spot and installed an excellent Liṅga after his own name. O excellent Brāhmaṇas this Liṅga is the bestower of all desires of men.

## \|\| 1.128.54 \|\|

*yastanmāghacaturdaśyāṃ pūjayecchraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*na tasya jāyate kiṃcidduḥkhaṃ saṃtānasaṃbhavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One who worships it with great faith on the fourteenth lunar day in the month of Māgha will never have any sorrow regarding the continuity of his race.

## \|\| 1.128.55-56 \|\|

*api varṣaśatānārī snātvā kuṇḍe sutaprade \|*  
*aṭeśvaraṃ tataḥ paśyecchivabhaktiparāyaṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sadyaḥ putramavāpnoti vaṃśavṛddhikaraṃ param \|\| tatprasādānna saṃdehaḥ kārtikeya vaco yathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. A woman may be hundred years old but if she has great devotion to Śiva and takes her bath in Sutaprada Kuṇḍa and then visits Aṭeśvara, she will immediately attain a son who will increase the prosperity of the family. This is undoubtedly due to the favour of the deity. So says Kārttikeya.

## Chapter 129 - Greatness of the Hermitage of Yājñavalkya

## \|\| 1.129.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti yājñavalkyasamudravaḥ \|*  
*āśramo loka vikhyāto mūrkhāṇāmapi siddhidaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra taptvā tapastīvraṃ yājñavalkyena dhīmatā \|*  
*saṃprāptā nikhilā vedā guruṇā'pahṛtāśca ye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko'sau gururabhūttasya yājñavalkyasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*pāṭhayitvā punaryena hṛtā vedā mahātmanā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ ca samācakṣva sūtaputrātra vistarāt \|*  
*kautukaṃ paramaṃ jātaṃ sarveṣāṃ no dvijanmanām \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Further, there is an Āśrama belonging to Yājñavalkya. It is well-known all over the world. It accords Siddhi even to dullards.

It was here that the intelligent Yājñavalkya performed a severe penance and regained all the Vedas that had been taken away by his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.129.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsīdbrāhmaṇaśārdūlaḥ śākalya iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavānvayasaṃbhūto veda vedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. There was a tiger among Brāhmaṇas well-known as Śākalya. He hailed from the family of Bhārgavas. He was master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.129.6 \|\|

*bṛhatkalpe purā viprā vardhamāne purottame \|*  
*bahuśiṣyasamāyukto vedādhyayanatatparaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Formerly, in the Bṛhat-kalpa, O Brāhmaṇas, he lived in the excellent city of Vardhamāna with a great number of disciples. He was eagerly engrossed in the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.129.7 \|\|

*sa sadā prātarutthāya vidyādānaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*śiṣyebhyaścānurūpebhyaḥ prasādādvijasattamāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he always got up in the morning and imparted instructions to deserving disciples with great pleasure.

## \|\| 1.129.8 \|\|

*cakāra sa tadā viprāḥ paurohityaṃ mahīpateḥ \|*  
*sūryavaṃśaprasūtasya supriyasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At that time, he was the royal priest of the noble-souled king Supriya born of the solar race, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.129.9 \|\|

*sa tasya dharmakṛtyāni sarvāṇyeva dinedine \|*  
*kṛtvā svagṛhamabhyeti pūjitastena bhūbhujā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After performing all the holy rites (of the day), he used to return home everyday, honoured duly by the king.

## \|\| 1.129.10 \|\|

*ekaṃ śiṣyaṃ samāropya śāṃtyarthaṃ tasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*kathayitvā pramāṇaṃ ca vidhānaṃ homasaṃbhavam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. For the performance of the Śānti rites of the king, he used to leave one disciple thereafter telling him the scope and procedure of the Homas.

## \|\| 1.129.11 \|\|

*śiṣyo'pi sakalaṃ kṛtvā tatkarma susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*āśīrvādaṃ pradattvā ca bhūpatergṛhameti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The disciple used to perform all the rites with great concentration. After offering the blessings to the king, he used to return home.

## \|\| 1.129.12 \|\|

*evaṃ prakurvatastasya śākalyasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*paurohityaṃ gataḥ kālaḥ kiyanmātro dvijottamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the noble-souled Śākalya performed the priestly duties for a long time.

## \|\| 1.129.13-14 \|\|

*tadā vaivāhike kāle śapto yaḥ śaṃbhunā svayam \|*  
*suniṃdyāṃ vikṛtiṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya vedyāṃ gatasya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*atha taṃ yojayāmāsa śāṃtyarthaṃ nṛpamaṃdire \|*  
*yājñavalkyaṃ sa śākalyaḥ pratipadyāgataṃ tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. After seeing his (of Brahmā) aberration on the altar at the time of marriage, Śaṃbhu cursed him. He was then born as Yājñvalkya. Śākalya engaged Yājñavalkya in the royal palace for the performance of the Śānti rites.

## \|\| 1.129.15 \|\|

*so'pi tāruṇyagarveṇa veśyākarajavikṣataḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃgeṣu sunirlajjaḥ prakaṭāṃgo jagāma vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the pride of youth he also went shamelessly exposing his body marked all over by the nails of courtesans without covering it.

## \|\| 1.129.16 \|\|

*tataśca śāṃtikaṃ kṛtvā japāṃte bhūpatiṃ ca tam \|*  
*śāṃtodakapradānāya hasyamāno janairyayau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then he performed the Śānti rites. At the end of the Japa, he went to the king to offer the holy water of the Śānti rite. While going there, he was laughed at by the people.

## \|\| 1.129.17 \|\|

*pārthivo'pi ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛgrūpaṃ viṭaṃ dvijam \|*  
*nāśīrjagrāha tenoktāṃ vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing the Brāhmaṇa in such a vicious form of a Vita (lustful person), the king did not accept the blessings uttered by him. He then spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.129.18 \|\|

*ucchiṣṭo'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śayyārūḍho vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*atra śālodbhave staṃbhe tasmādetajjalaṃ kṣipa \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “I am Ucchiṣṭa (impure), O excellent Brāhmaṇa. Hence I am still in the bed. So pour this water on the pillar in the hall.”

## \|\| 1.129.19 \|\|

*so'pi sāvajñamājñāya taṃ bhūpaṃ kupitānanaḥ \|*  
*taṃ ca staṃbhaṃ samuddiśya dhyātvā tadbrahma śāśvatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Yājñavalkya understood that the king showed contempt. Hence he became angry. With the pillar in view, he meditated upon the eternal Brahman.

## \|\| 1.129.20 \|\|

*dyāṃ tvamālikhya ityeva proktvā maṃtraṃ ca yājuṣam \|\|*  
*prākṣipacchāṃtikaṃ toyaṃ tasya mūrdhani satvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He recited the Yajurveda Mantra beginning with dyām tāmālikhya etc., and poured the holy water of Śāntika rite quickly on its top.

## \|\| 1.129.21 \|\|

*tataḥ sa patite toye staṃbhaḥ pallavaśobhitaḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādeva saṃjajñe phala puṣpairvirājitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As soon as the water fell on it, the pillar instantly became splendid with sprouts and was embellished with flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 1.129.22 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthivaḥ so'tha vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*paścāttāpaṃ vidhāyātha vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing this, the eyes of the king beamed with wonder. He repented for his conduct and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.129.23 \|\|

*abhiṣekaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha mamāpi tvaṃ prayaccha bhoḥ \|*  
*anenaiva tu mantreṇa śucitvaṃ me vyavasthitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, give me this holy water of ablution with (uttering) the same Mantra. I am not impure.”

## \|\| 1.129.24 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*mamābhiṣekadānasya tvamanarho'si pārthiva \|*  
*tasmādyāsyāmyahaṃ sadyo yatrasthaḥ sa gururmama \|\| 24 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

24\. O king, you are unworthy to receive the offer of the holy water of ablution from me. So I shall go immediately to the place where my preceptor is present.

## \|\| 1.129.25 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tava dāsyāmi vastrāṇi vāhanāni vasūni ca \|*  
*tasmādyacchābhiṣekaṃ me mantreṇā'nena sāṃpratam \|\| 25 \|\|*

The king said:

25\. I shall give you ample wealth, vehicles and garments. Offer me this holy water of ablution now with the same Mantra.

## \|\| 1.129.26 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*na homāṃtaṃ vinā mantraḥ sphurate pārthivottama \|*  
*abhiṣekavidhau prokto yaḥ pūrvaṃ padmayoninā \|*  
*tasmānnāhaṃ kariṣyāmi tava yadvai hṛdi sthitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Yājñvalkya said:

26\. Before the conclusion of the Homa, O excellent king, the Mantra cannot manifest (and function) the Mantra that was earlier uttered by the Lotus-born One in connection with the procedure of ablution. Hence I will not carry out what is present in your heart.

## \|\| 1.129.27 \|\|

*ityuktvā vacanaṃ bhūpaṃ yājñavalkyaḥ sa vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ tūrṇaṃ nispṛhatvaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After saying thus to the king, Yājñavalkya, the Brāhmaṇa who strictly adhered to the principle of non-covetousness, went home immediately.

## \|\| 1.129.28 \|\|

*apare'hni samāyātaṃ śākalyamatha bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*provāca prāṃjalirbhūtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When śākalya came (to the palace) next day, the king said to him humbly with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.129.29 \|\|

*yastvayā preṣitaḥ kalya śiṣyo brāhmaṇasattamaḥ \|*  
*śāṃtyarthaṃ preṣaṇīyaśca bhūyo'pyevaṃ gṛhe mama \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “The excellent Brāhmaṇa, your disciple who was deputed by you yesterday, should be sent to my abode again for the purpose of Śānti rites."

## \|\| 1.129.30 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā tato gatvā nijālayam \|*  
*yājñavalkyaṃ samāhūya tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He said, “So be it" and went to his abode. He called Yājñavalkya and told him earnestly:

## \|\| 1.129.31 \|\|

*adyāpi tvaṃ nareṃdrasya śāṃtyarthaṃ bhavane vraja \|*  
*viśeṣātpārthiveṃdreṇa samāhūto'si putraka \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “Today also you should go to the abode of the king for the Śānti rites. Dear son, you have been specially invited by the great king.”

## \|\| 1.129.32 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ tāta gamiṣyāmi śāṃtyarthaṃ tasya maṃdire \|*  
*avalepena yuktasya śuddhyā virahitasya ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

32\. Father, I will not go to his mansion for Śānti rites, because he is very arrogant and devoid of cleanliness.

## \|\| 1.129.33 \|\|

*mayā tasyābhiṣekārthaṃ salilaṃ codyataṃ ca yat \|*  
*salilaṃ tena tatkāṣṭhe samādiṣṭaṃ kubuddhinā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sacred water I proffered to him for the purpose of holy ablution was directed by that evil-minded one to be poured over the wood (i.e. pillar).

## \|\| 1.129.34 \|\|

*tato mayāpi tatraiva tatkṣaṇātsalilaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tasminkāṣṭhe parikṣiptaṃ nītaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At the very instant the water was poured over the wood and it flourished instantly.

## \|\| 1.129.35 \|\|

*śākalya uvāca \|*  
*ata eva viśeṣeṇa samāhūto'si putraka \|*  
*tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha nāvajñeyā mahībhujaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Śākalya said:

35\. That is why, dear son, you have been specially summoned. So go there quickly. Kings should not be treated with contempt.

## \|\| 1.129.36 \|\|

*apamānādbhavenmānaṃ pārthivānāmasaṃśayam \|*  
*yaḥ karoti punastatra mānaṃ na sa bhavetpriyaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On being disrespected kings may become angry doubtlessly. One who makes them angry may not become a favourite.

## \|\| 1.129.37 \|\|

*kopaprasāda vastūni vicinvaṃtīha ye sadā \|*  
*ārohaṃti śanairbhṛtyā dhunvaṃtamapi pārthivam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The servants who piece together the matters of anger and favour, get the upper hand over the king who always tries to repulse them.

## \|\| 1.129.38 \|\|

*samau mānāpamānau ca cittajñaḥ kālavittathā \|*  
*sarvaṃsahaḥ kṣamī vijñaḥ sa bhavedrājavallabhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One who takes respect and disrespect equanimously, one who knows the mind (of the king), one who understands the opportune time, one who endures everything and remains patient is wise. He shall be a favourite of the king.

## \|\| 1.129.39 \|\|

*apamānamanādṛtya tasmādgaccha nṛpālayam \|*  
*mamājñāpi na laṃghyā ta eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Ignore the disrespect shown to you and go to the abode of the king. Further, you must not transgress my command. This is the eternal right conduct.

## \|\| 1.129.40 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*ājñābhaṃgo dhruvaṃ bhāvī paripāṭīvyatikramāt \|*  
*karoṣi yadi śiṣyāṇāṃ ye tvayā tatra yojitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

40\. If the convention is violated transgression of the command will surely follow. Should you alter the arrangement of your disciples who have been employed there by you?

## \|\| 1.129.41 \|\|

*tasmādyadi balānmāṃ tvaṃ yojayiṣyasi taṃ prati \|*  
*tvāṃ tyaktvā'nyatra yāsyāmi yataḥ proktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence, if you forcibly employ me there, I will leave you and go elsewhere, since it has been said by great sages:

## \|\| 1.129.42 \|\|

*gurorapyavaliptasya kāryākāryamajānataḥ \|*  
*utpathe vartamānasya parityāgo vidhīyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “Desertion is enjoined in the case of even a preceptor who is overbearing and arrogant, who does not discriminate between what should be done and what should not be done and who adhers to wrong path.”

## \|\| 1.129.43 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śākalyaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ provāca taṃ bhūyo bhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sūta said:

43\. On hearing his words Śākalya became farious. He said rebuking him repeatedly:

## \|\| 1.129.44-45 \|\|

*ekamapyakṣaraṃ yatra guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā hyanṛṇī bhavet \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmādgaccha drutaṃ dattvā madadhyayanamālayam \|*  
*tyaktvā vidyāṃ mayā dattāṃ no cecchapsyāmyahaṃ tava \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. If a preceptor teaches but one syllable to a disciple, no sufficient wealth exists on the earth (is available) for giving it to the Guru and to get oneself free from debt.

Hence go to your abode after returning the lore received from me. Renounce the learning imparted by me. Otherwise I will curse you.”

## \|\| 1.129.46 \|\|

*evamuktvābhimaṃtryātha nādabiṃdusamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtrairātharvaṇaistoyaṃ pānārthaṃ cārpayattataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying thus, he charged the water by means of the Ātharvaṇic Mantras evolved from Nādabindu (Eternal Sound and Oṃkāra) and gave it to him to drink.

## \|\| 1.129.47 \|\|

*so'pibattatkṣaṇāttoyaṃ tatpītvā vyākuleṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*udgiradvāṃtidharmeṇa tattvavidyāvimiśritam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Instantly, he drank the water after which he experienced excessive exhaustion in all the sense-organs. He vomited all the contents of the bowels mixed with the spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 1.129.48-49 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca taṃ bhūyaḥ śākalyaṃ kupitānanaḥ \|*  
*ekamapyakṣaraṃ nāsti tāvakīyaṃ mamodare \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tasmācchiṣyo'smi te nāhaṃ na ca me tvaṃ guruḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ svecchayā'nyatra prayāsyāmi karoṣi kim \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Then he spoke to Śākalya with extreme anger manifest in his face: “There is not even a single syllable taught by you in my stomach. Hence I am no longer your disciple, nor are you my preceptor. I will now go elsewhere as I please. What can you do?”

## \|\| 1.129.50 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha nirgatya tasmātsthānācciraṃtanāt \|*  
*papraccha mānavānbhūyaḥ siddhikṣetrāṇi cāsakṛt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After saying thus he went out of that age-old holy spot according Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.129.51 \|\|

*tatastasya samādiṣṭaṃ kṣetrametanmanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*siddhidaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ na vṛthā syātkathaṃcana \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then this holy spot was mentioned to him by learned men. It bestows Siddhi on all creatures. It cannot be fruitless at all.

## \|\| 1.129.52-53 \|\|

*āstāṃ tāvattapastaptvā vrataṃ niyamameva vā \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre siddhiḥ saṃvasato'pi ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yenayena ca bhāvena tatra kṣetre vasejjanaḥ \|*  
*tasyānurūpiṇī siddhiḥ śubhā syādyadi vā'śubhā \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “Leave aside Siddhi acquired by performing penance or observing Vratas and restraints. Siddhi is acquired by one who simply stays in the Hāṭakeśvara kṣetra.

The Siddhi of people shall be splendid or otherwise (auspicious or inauspicious) in accordance with the mental fervour and feeling of the people with which they stay there.”

## \|\| 1.129.54-55 \|\|

*tacchrutvā ca drutaṃ prāpya kṣetrametaddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhānumārādhayāmāsa sthāpayitvā tataḥ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

*niyato niyatāhāro brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*gāyatraṃ nyāsamāsādya nirvikalpena cetasā \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. On hearing it, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he hurried to this holy spot, installed an image of Bhānu and propitiated it. He observed celibacy. He assigned Gāyatrī Mantra to the various limbs (ritualistically as Nyāsa) and meditated with a mind cleared of all doubts.

## \|\| 1.129.56 \|\|

*tataśca bhagavāṃstuṣṭo varṣāṃte tamuvāca saḥ \|*  
*darśane tasya saṃsthitvā tejaḥ saṃyamya dāruṇam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. At the end of a year, the Lord was pleased with him, restrained his terrifying refulgence, appeared before him and spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.129.57 \|\|

*yājñavalkya varaṃ brūhi yatte manasi rocate \|*  
*sarvameva pradāsyāmi nādeyaṃ vidyate tvayi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. “O Yājñavalkya, speak out whatever is in your mind. Take it as my boon. I will grant you everything. There is nothing that cannot be given to you."

## \|\| 1.129.58 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭaḥ suraśreṣṭha vedādhyayanasaṃbhave \|*  
*gururbhava mamādyaiva mamaitadvāṃchitaṃ hṛdi \|\| 58 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

58\. If you are pleased, O excellent one among Suras, be my preceptor in regard to the study of the Vedas. This is the desire of my heart.

## \|\| 1.129.59 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tava kṛpāviṣṭastejaḥ saṃhṛtya tatparam \|*  
*tataścātra samāyātastena no dahyase dvija \|\| 59 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

59\. O Brāhmaṇa, out of compassion for you I have restrained my excessive refulgence and come here. Hence you are not burned.

## \|\| 1.129.60 \|\|

*tasmādatraiva kuṃḍe ca maṃtrānsārasvatāñchubhān \|*  
*vedoktānkṣepayiṣyāmi svayameva dvijottama \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Now I shall deposit here in this holy Kuṇḍa all the splendid Sārasvata Mantras mentioned in the Vedas myself, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.129.61 \|\|

*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā yatkiṃcidvedasaṃbhavam \|*  
*paṭhiṣyasi sakṛttatte kaṃṭhasthaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Take your holy bath and be pure and clean. Whatever Vedic Mantra you may utter then once, it shall remain with you permanently.

## \|\| 1.129.62 \|\|

*tattvārthaṃ prakaṭaṃ kṛtsnaṃ viditaṃ te bhaviṣyati \|*  
*matprasādānna saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The entire meaning and principles will be manifest to you with my favour. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that has been spoken by me.

## \|\| 1.129.63 \|\|

*adyādi mānavaḥ prātaḥ snātvā tvatra hrade ca yaḥ \|*  
*sāvitreṇa ca sūktena māṃ dṛṣṭvā prapaṭhiṣyati \|*  
*tasmai tatsyādasaṃdigdhaṃ yattavoktaṃ mayā dvija \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. From now onwards, if a man takes his holy bath in the pool here in the morning and recites Sāvitra Sūkta facing me, O Brāhmaṇa, he shall undoubtedly have everything that has been mentioned in your case by me.

## \|\| 1.129.64 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu deveśa yattvayoktaṃ vaco'khilam \|*  
*paraṃ mama vaco'nyacca tacchṛṇuṣva bravīmi te \|\| 64 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

64\. Let it be so, O Lord of Devas; may all the words uttered by you be true. But what I wish to say is another thing. Listen.

## \|\| 1.129.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti yājñavalkyasamudravaḥ \|*  
*āśramo loka vikhyāto mūrkhāṇāmapi siddhidaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1 shall tell you.

## \|\| 1.129.65 \|\|

*nāhaṃ manuṣyadharmāṇamupādhyāyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*kariṣyāmi jagannātha kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Lord of the universe, be merciful to me. I will never have a human being as my preceptor.

## \|\| 1.129.66 \|\|

*tatastasyā dadau sūryo laghimā nāma śobhanām \|*  
*vidyāṃ hi tatprabhāvāya sutuṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then with his inner self fully pleased Sūrya granted him the splendid Vidyā named Laghimā for augmenting his prowess.

## \|\| 1.129.67-68 \|\|

*tatastaṃ prāha karṇāṃte mamāśvānāṃ praviśya vai \|*  
*abhyāsaṃ kuru vidyānāṃ vedādhyayanamācara \|\| 67 \|\|*

*manmukhādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭha yadyetattava vāṃchitam \|*  
*na te syādyena doṣo'yaṃ mama raśmisamudbhavaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. He said to him: “Enter the ear of my horses and practise the recitation of the Vedic Mantras.

Learn the Vedas direct from my mouth, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, if that be your desire. You will not have any harm from my rays.”

## \|\| 1.129.69 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa tenātha vājikarṇaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*laghurbhūtvā'paṭhadvedānbhāskarasya mukhāttataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On being told thus by him (i.e. Sun) Yājñavalkya became very small and weightless. He resorted to the ear of the horse and learned the Vedas from the mouth of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.129.70 \|\|

*evaṃ siddhiṃ samāpanno yājñavalkyo dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvopaniṣadaṃ cāru vedārthaiḥ sakalairyutam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thus the excellent Brāhmaṇa Yājñavalkya attained Siddhi. He composed the Upaniṣad (Bṛhadāraṇyaka) in a fascinating manner incorporating all the meanings of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.129.71 \|\|

*janakāya nareṃdrāya vyākhyāya ca tataḥ param \|*  
*kātyāyanaṃ sutaṃ prāpya vedasūtrasya kārakam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He explained it to king Janaka. He begot a son named Kātyāyana who composed the Vedic Sūtras (Śrauta Sūtras).

## \|\| 1.129.72 \|\|

*tyaktvā kalevaraṃ tatra brahmadvāri vinirmite \|*  
*tattejo brahmaṇo gātre yojayāmāsa śaktitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He cast off his body in the holy water made by Brahmā. He united his refulgence with the body of Brahmā in accordance with his capacity.

## \|\| 1.129.73 \|\|
