*tasya tīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca divākaram \|*  
*nādabiṃduṃ paṭhitvā ca tadagre muktimāpnuyāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. A man who takes his holy bath in the Tīrtha, visits the deity Divākara (Sun) and utters Nāda-bindu Mantra before him, shall attain salvation.

## Chapter 130 - Creation of Pañcapiṇḍā Cow

## \|\| 1.130.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyasutaḥ sūta yastvayā parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*katamā tasya mātābhūtsarvaṃ no brūhi vistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta, you have said about a son of Yājñavalkya. Who was his mother? Do speak everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.130.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya bhāryādvayaṃ śreṣṭhamāsītsarvaguṇānvitam \|*  
*ekā guṇavatī tasya maitreyīti prakīrtitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhā cānyātha kalyāṇī khyātā kātyāyanīti ca \|*  
*yasyāḥ kātyāyanaḥ putro vedārthānāṃ prajalpakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2-3. He (Yājñavalkya) had two excellent wives endowed with all good qualities. One is gloriously mentioned as Maitreyī who had good qualities. She was the senior. The other one of good features (Kalyāṇī) was well known as Kātyāyanī Kātyāyana, the expounder of the meaning of the Vedas, was her son.

## \|\| 1.130.4 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ kuṇḍadvayaṃ tatra saṃtiṣṭhati suśobhanam \|*  
*yatra snātā narā yāṃti lokāṃstāṃśca mahodayān \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There are two holy pits of splendid features pertaining to them there. Men who take their holy baths therein, attain those worlds of great glory.

## \|\| 1.130.5 \|\|

*kātyāyanyāśca tīrthasya śāṃḍilyāstīrthamuttamam \|*  
*pativratātvayuktāyāstathānyattatra saṃsthitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The excellent Tīrtha of the chaste lady Śāṇḍilī is another Tīrtha near Kātyāyanī Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.130.6 \|\|

*yatra kātyāyanī prāptā śāṃḍilyā pratibodhitā \|*  
*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ prāptā sapatnīduḥkhaduḥkhitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Kātyāyanī who was distressed due to the (rivalry) of her co-wife, had great detachment and she became enlightened by Śāṇḍilī at that place.

## \|\| 1.130.7 \|\|

*tatra yā kurute snānaṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ samāhitā \|*  
*nārī mārgasite pakṣe sā saubhāgyavatī bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A woman who takes her holy bath there on the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa shall enjoy conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.130.8 \|\|

*atha daurbhāgyasaṃpannā kāṇā vṛddhā'tha vāmanā \|*  
*abhīṣṭā jāyate sā ca tatprabhāvāddvijottamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a one-eyed woman, an aged woman, a dwarfish woman, and one overcome by misfortune becomes a desirable one by its power.

## \|\| 1.130.9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kīdṛksapatnijaṃ duḥkhaṃ kātyāyanyā upasthitam \|*  
*upadeśaḥ kathaṃ labdhaḥ śāṃḍilyāḥ sūta kīdṛśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:

9\. What sort of distress due to her co-wife assailed Kātyāyanī? O Sūta, how did she get spiritual instructions from Śāṇḍilī? What was it?

## \|\| 1.130.10 \|\|

*kātyāyanyā samācakṣva kautukaṃ no vyavasthitam \|*  
*sāmānyo bhavitā naiṣa upadeśastayeritaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Do mention how Kātyāyanī obtained the instruction, which couldn’t have been ordinary as (it was) uttered by her (Śāṇḍilī).

## \|\| 1.130.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*maitreyyā saha saṃsaktaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ vilokya sā \|*  
*kātyāyanī suduḥkhārtā saṃjātā cerṣyayā tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. Once Kātyāyanī saw Yājñavalkya enamoured of and united with Maitreyī. Due to jealousy, she became very miserable and distressed.

## \|\| 1.130.12 \|\|

*sā na snāti na bhuṃkte ca na hāsyaṃ kurute kvacit \|*  
*kevalaṃ bāṣpapūrṇākṣī niḥśvāsāḍhyā babhūva ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. She stopped taking bath and eating food. She never indulged in jokes and fun. She always heaved sighs and kept her eyes filled with tears.

## \|\| 1.130.13-14 \|\|

*tataḥ kadācidevātha phalārthaṃ nirgatā bahiḥ \|*  
*apaśyacchāṃḍilīnāma patipārśve vyavasthitām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭāṃ sādhvī vinayāvanatā sthitām \|*  
*so'pi tasyā mukhāsaktaḥ sānurāgaḥ prasannadṛk \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Once she chanced to go out for gathering fruit. Then she saw Śāṇḍilī standing by the side of her husband. The chaste lady was standing very humbly with palms joined in reverence. The husband was lovingly looking at her face with eyes displaying pleasure.

## \|\| 1.130.15-16 \|\|

*guṇadoṣodbhavāṃ vārtāmāpṛcchyākathayattathā \|*  
*sā ca tau daṃpatī dṛṣṭvā saṃhṛṣṭāvitaretaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*citte sve ciṃtayāmāsa sudhanyeyaṃ tapasvinī \|*  
*yasyāḥ patirmukhāsakto guṇadoṣaprajalpakaḥ \|*  
*sānurāgaśca susnigdho nānyāṃ nārīṃ bibhartti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He was eliciting facts regarding good and bad things and explaining them. On seeing the couple pleased with each other, she thought within herself, ‘This saintly lady is blessed. Her husband always looks up to her and expounds matters good and bad. He is full of love. He never has anything to do with other women.’

## \|\| 1.130.17 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃcitya sā sādhvī bhūyobhūyo dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*jagāma svāśramaṃ paścānniṃdyamānā svakaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Brooding over it frequently, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, she went back to her hermitage censuring her own physical form.

## \|\| 1.130.18-22 \|\|

*tataḥ kadācidekāṃte sthitāṃ tāṃ śāṃḍilīṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*bahirgate bhartari ca tasyāḥ kāryeṇa kenacit \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kātyāyanī samāgamya tataḥ papraccha sādaram \|*  
*vada kalyāṇi me kaṃcidupadeśaṃ mahodayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mukhaprekṣaḥ sadā bharttā yena strīṇāṃ prajāyate \|*  
*nāpamānaṃ karotyeva duruktavacanaiḥ kvacit \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nānyāṃ saṃgacchate nārīṃ cittenāpi kathaṃcana \|*  
*ahaṃ bhartuḥ kṛtairduḥkhairatīva paripīḍitā \|*  
*sapatnījairviśeṣeṇa tasmānme tvaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yathā te vaśago bharttā saṃjātaḥ kāmadaḥ sadā \|*  
*manasāpi na saṃdadhyānnārīmeṣa kathaṃcana \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. Then once, O Brāhmaṇas, when Śāṇḍilī was sitting alone as her husband had gone out on some business Kātyāyanī approached her and respectfully asked her: “O fair lady! Can I have some instruction from you, which will lead to great prosperity? Please tell me.

I am extremely afflicted by the miseries caused by my husband, especially those caused through the co-wife. So do tell me how a husband can be turned into one always looking at the face of his wife. He should not disrespect her by means of offensive words, nor associate with other women even mentally.

Do tell me how your husband has come to be under your control and how he always accords you what you desire, not thinking of another women even mentally."

## \|\| 1.130.23 \|\|

*śāṃḍilyuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sādhvi pravakṣyāmi tavāhaṃ guhyamuttamam \|*  
*yathā mamābhavadvaśyo mukhaprekṣastathā patiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Śāṇḍilī said:

23\. Listen, O chaste lady, I shall tell you an excellent secret as to how my husband looks only at me and is subject to my control.

## \|\| 1.130.24-25 \|\|

*mama tātaḥ kurukṣetre śāṃḍilyo munisattamaḥ \|*  
*vānaprasthāśrame'tiṣṭhatpūrve vayasi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatraikāhaṃ samutpannā kanyā tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhiṃ gatā krameṇātha tasminneva tapovane \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Śāṇḍilya, the excellent sage of Kurukṣetra, is my father. He was in the stage of Vānaprastha when I was born as the sole child and daughter of that noble-souled one. I grew up gradually in that very hermitage.

## \|\| 1.130.26 \|\|

*karomi tatra śuśrūṣāṃ homakāle yathocitām \|*  
*nīvārādīni dhānyāni nityaṃ caivānayāmyaham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I used to render him befitting service at the time of Homa. I used to fetch Nīvāra (wild rice) and other grain everyday.

## \|\| 1.130.27 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*āśrame mama tātasya suśrāṃtaḥ samupāgataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Once the excellent Sage Nārada came to my father’s hermitage utterly tired.

## \|\| 1.130.28 \|\|

*tātādeśāttatastatra mayā sa viśramaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*pādaśaucādibhiḥ kṛtyaiḥ snānādyaiśca tathāparaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the behest of my father, I gave relief to him from weariness by fetching water for washing feet, toilet, bath etc., and by other services.

## \|\| 1.130.29 \|\|

*tato bhuktāvasāne'tha niviṣṭaḥ mukhasaṃsthita \|*  
*mama mātrā paripṛṣṭo vinayādvaravarṇini \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At the conclusion of meal, the sage was relaxing. Then, O lady of excellent complexion, he was asked politely by my mother.

## \|\| 1.130.30-32 \|\|

*ekeyaṃ kanyakāsmākaṃ jāte vayasi saṃsthite \|*  
*saṃjātā muniśārdūla prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tadasyāḥ kīrtaya kṣipraṃ sukhopāyaṃ sukhodayam \|*  
*vrataṃ vā niyamaṃ vā tvaṃ homaṃ vā mantrameva vā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yena cīrṇena bharttā syātsusaumyaḥ sadguṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*priyaṃvado mukhaprekṣaḥ paranārīparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. “O tiger among sages, this is our only daughter born in our advanced age. She is dearer to us than our own very vital breath.

Therefore, quickly explain some easy means leading to her happy future, be it an observance (Vrata), regulation, Homa or some Mantra.

By resorting to that means, she should attain a husband of gentle manners and good features. He should speak pleasing words and always look at her only. He should be averse to other men’s wives.”

## \|\| 1.130.33 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa munistadanaṃtaram \|*  
*ciraṃ dhyātvā vacaḥ prāha prasannavadanastataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On hearing her words, the sage thought for a long time and spoke thus with a pleasant face:

## \|\| 1.130.34 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre pañcapiṃḍā vyavasthitā \|*  
*gaurī gauryā svayaṃ tatra sthāpitā parameśvarī \|\| 34 \|\|*

Nārada said:

34\. In the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, Gaurī has been installed as Pañcapiṇḍā (five lumps). The great goddess has been installed by Gaurī herself.

## \|\| 1.130.35 \|\|

*tāmeṣā vatsaraṃ yāvacchraddhayā parayā yutā \|*  
*sadā pūjayatu prītyā tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Let this (daughter of yours) worship her with great faith and devotion for a period of one year, particularly on the third lunar day.

## \|\| 1.130.36 \|\|

*tato varṣāṃtamāsādya saṃprāpsyati yathocitam \|*  
*bharttāraṃ nātra saṃdeho yādṛgrūpaṃ yathocitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At the conclusion of a year, she will attain a befitting husband. There is no doubt about it. He will be as handsome as she is beautiful.

## \|\| 1.130.37 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ gatā gaurī parityajya maheśvaram \|*  
*gaṃgerṣyayā mahābhāge jñātvā kṣetraṃ susiddhidam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O highly esteemed lady, formerly Gaurī had resorted to that place which, she knew, bestows success, after having been distressed due to her jealousy of Gaṅgā and having deserted Maheśvara (for that reason).

## \|\| 1.130.38-39 \|\|

*tataḥ sā ciṃtayāmāsa kāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmyaham \|*  
*saubhāgyārthaṃ yato'nyā māṃ pūjayaṃti surastriyaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmādahaṃ prabhaktyāḍhyā svayamātmānameva ca \|*  
*ātmanaiva kṛtotsāhā pūjayiṣyāmi siddhaye \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Then she had thought, ‘Which goddess should I worship? Other women of Suras worship me for the sake of conjugal felicity. Therefore, with great devotion and excessive enthusiasm I shall worship myself through my own self for achieving success.’

## \|\| 1.130.40 \|\|

*tataḥ prāṇāgnihotrotthairmaṃtrairātharvaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*mṛtpiṃḍānpaṃca saṃyojya hyekasthāne samāhitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. With great concentration, she joined together in one place five lumps of earth uttering the auspicious Atharvaveda Mantras referring to Prāṇāgnihotra.

## \|\| 1.130.41 \|\|

*pṛthvīmapaśca tejaśca vāyumākāśameva ca \|*  
*teṣu saṃyojayāmāsa mṛtpiṃḍeṣu nidhāya sā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She deposited in those lumps of earth the elements of Pṛthvī, Apaḥ, Tejas, Vāyu and Ākāśa.

## \|\| 1.130.42 \|\|

*mahadbhūtāni caitāni pañca devī yatavratā \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsa puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then the goddess observed the holy vow and worshipped these five elements with flowers, incense and unguents.

## \|\| 1.130.43 \|\|

*atha tāṃ tatra vijñāya tapaḥsthāṃ girajāṃ bhavaḥ \|*  
*tanmaṃtrākṛṣṭacittaśca satvaraṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On coming to know that Girijā was engaged in penance there and his mind having been attracted by those Mantras, Bhava (Śiva) came there hurriedly.

## \|\| 1.130.44-45 \|\|

*provāca ca prahṛṣṭātmā kasmāttvamiha cāgatā \|*  
*māṃ muktvā doṣanirmuktaṃ mukhaprekṣaṃ sadā ratam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmādāgaccha kailāsaṃ vṛṣārūḍhā mayā saha \|*  
*athavā kāraṇaṃ brūhi yadi doṣo'sti me kvacit \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. He joyously said to her: “Why have you come here forsaking me, though I am free from faults and despite my being always devoted to you? I have been looking up at you always. Now be seated on the bull along with me and come to Kailāsa. Otherwise, if at all I have any fault tell me the reason for your coming away.”

## \|\| 1.130.46 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ mūrdhnā jāhnavīṃ dhatse mūrtāṃ padajalātmikām \|*  
*tasmānnāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi maṃdiraṃ te kathaṃcana \|\| 46 \|\|*

Devī said:

46\. You are holding on your head Jāhnavī, the personified form of the water from the feet (of Viṣṇu). Hence I will never go to your place at all.

## \|\| 1.130.47-49 \|\|

*yāvanna tyajasi vyaktaṃ mama sāpatnyatāṃ gatām \|*  
*tathā nityaṃ praṇāmaṃ tvaṃ karoṣi vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pratyakṣamapi me nityaṃ saṃdhyāyāśca na lajjase \|*  
*tasmādetatparityajya karma lajjākaraṃ param \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ākārayasi māṃ deva tatsyādyadi mataṃ mama \|*  
*anyathāhaṃ na yāsyāmi tava harmye kathaṃcana \|*  
*etacchrutvā yadiṣṭaṃ te kuruṣva vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. I am not inclined to return unless you clearly repudiate her occupying the position of my co-wife. Further, O Bull-emblemed One, even while I look on you bow down to Sandhyā everyday. You are not ashamed of it, hence give up these shameful acts. Thereafter, if you call me, I will respond approvingly. Otherwise, I will not come to your place at all. After hearing this, O Bull-emblemed One, do what pleases you.

## \|\| 1.130.50 \|\|

*deva uvāca \|\|*  
*nāhaṃ saukhyena tāṃ gaṃgāṃ dhārayāmi sureśvari \|\| 50 \|\|*

The Lord said:

50\. O goddess of Suras, it is not for my pleasure that I hold Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.130.51 \|\|

*bhagīrathena bhūpena prārthito jñāti kāraṇāt \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu tapastaptvā sudāruṇam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After performing severe penance for a period of a thousand years according to the divine reckoning I had been requested by King Bhagīratha on behalf of his ancestors:

## \|\| 1.130.52 \|\|

*yena no yāti pātālaṃ gaṃgā svargaparicyutā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ deva madvākyātsvamūrdhnā vaha jāhnavīm \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “O Lord, do hold on your head Jāhnavī, so that after falling from Svarga she may not flow towards Pātāla. Do this at my request.”

## \|\| 1.130.53 \|\|

*mayā tasya pratijñātaṃ dhārayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|*  
*ākāśājjāhnavīvegaṃ pataṃtaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I had promised to him, “I shall undoubtedly hold the rapid current of Jāhnavī falling on the earth from the firmament.”

## \|\| 1.130.54 \|\|

*no cedvrajeta pātālaṃ yadatra viṣayesthim \|*  
*tato'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Otherwise, she would have gone to Pātāla which is the matter of concern here. So I shall mention something important in this connection which you do listen with attention.

## \|\| 1.130.55 \|\|

*eṣā gaṃgā varārohe mama mūrdhno vinirgatā \|*  
*himavaṃtaṃ nagaṃ bhittvā dvidhā jātā tataḥ param \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O lady of exquisite features, this Gaṅgā came out of my head (tresses of hair) and breaking on the Himalaya mountain she split into two.

## \|\| 1.130.56 \|\|

*tataḥ siṃdhvabhidhānā sā paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ gatā \|*  
*śatāni nava saṃgṛhya nadīnāṃ parameśvari \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The part named Sindhu flowed into the western ocean, O Parameśvarī, taking nine hundred rivers along with her.

## \|\| 1.130.57 \|\|

*tathā gaṃgābhidhānā ca saiva prāksāgaraṃ gatā \|*  
*tāvatīśca samādāya nadīḥ parvatanandini \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The other part named Gaṅgā flowed into the eastern ocean, O Daughter of the Mountain, taking as many rivers with her.

## \|\| 1.130.58 \|\|

*evamaṣṭādaśaitāni nadīnāṃ parvatātmaje \|*  
*śatāni sāgare yāṃti tena nityaṃ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus, O Daughter of the Mountain, these eithteen hundred rivers flow into the ocean everyday. Thereby it stands sustained.

## \|\| 1.130.59-60 \|\|

*satataṃ śoṣyamāṇo'pi vāḍavena divāniśam \|*  
*samudrasalilaṃ meghāḥ samādāya tataḥ param \|\| 59 \|\|*

*martyaloke pravarṣaṃti tataḥ sasyaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*sasyena jīvate lokaḥ prabhavanti makhāstathā \|*  
*makhāṃśena surāḥ sarve tṛptiṃ yāṃti tataḥ param \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Though the Vāḍava fire (submarine fire) dries it up (evaporates it) day and night, it is never exhausted.

Clouds take up the waters of the ocean and shower them on the world of mortals (i.e. earth). Thereby vegetation grows up. The world is sustained by the vegetation. This enables the performance of Makhas (sacrifices). Through getting their share in the Makhas all the Suras become satisfied.

## \|\| 1.130.61 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇānmūrdhni devi gaṃgāṃ dadhāmyaham \|*  
*na snehātkāmato naiva jagadyena pravartate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. It is for this reason, O fair lady, that I hold Gaṅgā and not through affection or lust. On account of this the world goes on.

## \|\| 1.130.62 \|\|

*athavā santyajāmyenāṃ yadi mūrdhnaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*taddūraṃ vegato bhittvā pṛthvīṃ yāti rasātalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. If for any reason I were to let her off from my head, it would pierce, through the earth in full force and flow into Rasātala.

## \|\| 1.130.63 \|\|

*tataḥ śoṣaṃ vrajedāśu samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*aurveṇa pīyamāno'tra tato vṛṣṭirna jāyate \|*  
*vṛṣṭyabhāvājjagannāśaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then the Ocean, the Lord of Rivers, would get dried up on being drunk by Aurva (submarine fire). There will no longer be any shower. Absence of rain will lead to the ruin of the world. It is the truth that is uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.130.64 \|\|

*evaṃ gaṃgākṛte proktaṃ mayā tava sureśvari \|*  
*śṛṇu sandhyākṛte'nyacca yena tāṃ praṇamāmyaham \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus, O goddess of Suras, everything has been (explained) to you in regard to Gaṅgā. Listen to another explanation of mine as to why I bow down to Sandhyā.

## Chapter 131 - Kātyāyanī’s Distress

## \|\| 1.131.1-3 \|\|

*deva uvāca \|*  
*eṣā rātriḥ samādiṣṭā dānavānāṃ sureśvari \|*  
*piśācānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatkiṃcitkriyate karma tatra snānādikaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ jāyate teṣāṃ purā dattaṃ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*maryādā taiḥ samaṃ yena devānāṃ ca yadā kṛtā \|*  
*arhāṇāṃ yajñabhāgasya kāśyapānāmathāgrajām \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1-3. O goddess of Suras, this night has been assigned to Dānavas, Piśācas, Bhūtas and Rākṣasas in particular.

It has been granted by the Self-born Lord that whatever auspicious rite, such as ablution etc., is performed then, the benefit thereof accrues to them.

This agreement was made by Devas with them because being the sons of Kaśyapa, both of them deserved share in the Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.131.4 \|\|

*tadarthaṃ daśasāhasrā dānavā yuddha durmadāḥ \|*  
*kuṃtaprāsakarā bhānuṃ ruṃdhantyudgatakārmukāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. For this purpose ten thousand Dānavas assail Bhānu with raised bows. They are very irrepressible in battles and hold javelins and spears in their hands.

## \|\| 1.131.5 \|\|

*tamuddiśya sahasrāṃśuṃ yajjalaṃ parikṣipyate \|*  
*sāvitreṇa ca mantreṇa teṣāṃ tajjāyate phalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When water is poured down with the thousand-rayed Sun in view, uttering the Sāvitra Mantra, the result is manifest in them.

## \|\| 1.131.6 \|\|

*te hatāstena toyena vajratulyena tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*pramuṃcaṃti sahasrāṃśuṃ nityameva sureśvari \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They are killed at the same instant by that water powerful like thunderbolt. Hence, O goddess of Suras, the Thousand-rayed One is let off everyday.

## \|\| 1.131.7 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāttoyamastrarūpaṃ kṣipāmyaham \|*  
*saṃdhyā kālaṃ samuddiśya bhānuṃ saṃdhyāṃ na pārvati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is for this purpose that I pour down water in the form of a missile at the time of twilight with Bhānu in view and not Sandhyā.

## \|\| 1.131.8-9 \|\|

*yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattaduttarataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*udayārthaṃ raviṃ yāntaṃ nirundhanti ca dāruṇāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*te'pi saṃdhyājalairdevi nihatā brāhmaṇottamaiḥ \|*  
*mayā ca taṃ vimuñcaṃti mūrcchitā nipatanti ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Whatever the best and leading ones do, persists subsequently. The terrible ones restrain Ravi who proceeds to rise up. But, O goddess, they are killed through the water offerings during Sandhyā by me and also by excellent Brāhmaṇas. They swoon and fall down and let off the Sun.

## \|\| 1.131.10 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddevi sandhyayorubhayorapi \|*  
*ahaṃ cānye ca viprā ye te namaṃti divākaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It is for this reason, O goddess, that I and other Brāhmaṇas bow down to Divākara (Sun) during the two Sandhyās (dawn and dusk).

## \|\| 1.131.11 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gṛhamāgaccha tyaktverṣyāṃ parvatātmaje \|*  
*praśasyāṃ tvāṃ parityaktvā nānyāsti hṛdaye mama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hence eschew your jealousy, O daughter of the Mountain, and come home. Excepting you, the praiseworthy one there is no other woman in my heart.

## \|\| 1.131.12 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*niṣkāmo vā sakāmo vā saṃdhyāṃ strīsaṃjñitāmimām \|*  
*yattvaṃ namasi deveśa tanme duḥkhaṃ prajāyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

Devī said:

12\. O Lord, whether you are interested or disinterested (in Sandhyā), it causes to shower rain when you bow down to Sandhyā who has (even grammatically) feminine appellation.

## \|\| 1.131.13 \|\|

*tasmādgaṅgāparityāgaṃ sandhyāyāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yāvanna kuruṣe deva tāvattuṣṭirna me bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, O Lord, I will not be satisfied unless and until you abandon Gaṅgā and Sandhyā in particular.

## \|\| 1.131.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha sā devī viśeṣavratamāsthitā \|*  
*avamanya mahādevaṃ prārthayānamapi svayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus the goddess refused to comply with the request made by Mahādeva himself and resorted to a special vow.

## \|\| 1.131.15-16 \|\|

*tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa kimetatkāraṇaṃ sthitam \|*  
*viraktā'pi mamotkaṇṭhāṃ yenaiṣā prakaroti na \|\| 15 \|\|*

*na ca sāmnā vrajettuṣṭiṃ kathaṃcidapi pārvatī \|*  
*mṛṣerṣyāṃdhāriṇī devī naitatsvalpaṃ hi kāraṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Then he thought: ‘What is the reason hereof? Though she is unattached, she does not destroy (eliminate) my eagerness about her.

The goddess is adopting the pretence of jealousy. Pārvatī will never be satisfied and agreeable with peaceful overtures. And this is an insignificant cause.’

## \|\| 1.131.17 \|\|

*tato mantraprabhāvaṃ taṃ vijñāya parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*dhyānaṃ dhṛtvā susūkṣmeṇa jñānenātha svayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Parameśvara knew the potency of Mantra. He meditated with this subtle realization on himself.

## \|\| 1.131.18 \|\|

*tameva mantraṃ mantreṇa nyāsena ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*samyagārādhayāmāsa saṃpūjyātmānamātmanā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He worshipped his own self through himself. He uttered the selfsame Mantra along with ritualistic touching of the limbs (Nyāsa) in particular and perfected his propitiation.

## \|\| 1.131.19 \|\|

*yathā devyātmabhūtāni pṛthakkṛtvā ca paṃca ca \|*  
*pūjitāni tathā devaḥ sarveṣāmaṃtare gataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the manner, in which the goddess separated the Ārman from the five dements and worshipped them, the Lord also did so by being immanent in all of them.

## \|\| 1.131.20 \|\|

*tānyeva pūjayāmāsa pṛthakkṛtvā samādhitaḥ \|*  
*niyojya ca punarbāhye tataḥ pūjāṃ samācarat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By means of Samādhi, he separated them and worshipped them. Again he united them externally and performed the rite of adoration.

## \|\| 1.131.21 \|\|

*tasmānnāsti paraḥ kaścitpūjyapūjyaḥ sa eva ca \|*  
*aiśvaryātsarvadevānāmīśānastena nirmitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There is no one greater than he. He alone is worthy of the worship of those who themselves should be worshipped, Īśāna was thus created by him through the Aiśvarya (potency and glory) of all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.131.22 \|\|

*evaṃ yāvatsa īśānaḥ samārādhayati prabhuḥ \|*  
*tāvaddevī samāyātā mantrākṛṣṭā ca yatra saḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even as the Lord propitiated Īśāna the goddess who had been drawn by means of the Mantras came to the place where he was present.

## \|\| 1.131.23-24 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca taṃ devaṃ praṇipatyakṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*jñātaṃ mayā vibho sarvaṃ na māṃ tyaja tava priyām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tasmādāgaccha gacchāvo yatra tvaṃ vāñchasi prabho \|*  
*kṣamyatāṃ deva me sarvaṃ na kṛtaṃ yadvacastava \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Then she bowed down to the Lord with palms joined in reverence. She spoke to him: “O Lord, everything has been understood by me. Do not forsake me, your beloved one. Hence, do come. O Lord, let us go wherever you wish to go. The fact that I had not complied with your words may kindly be excused.”

## \|\| 1.131.25 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevastāmāliṅgya śucismitām \|*  
*idamūce vihasyoccairmeghagambhīrayā girā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Mahādeva who was pleased, embraced her even as he smiled pleasantly. Then he said thus laughingly in words majestic like the rumble of clouds:

## \|\| 1.131.26 \|\|

*yaiṣā tvayā'tmabhūtotthā nirmitā paramā tanuḥ \|*  
*etāṃ yā kāminī kācitpūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva vidhānena tasyā bhartā bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “A great physical form arising from the Ātman and the five elements has been created by you. If a woman in love devoutly worships this form in accordance with this procedure, she will get a husband.

## \|\| 1.131.27 \|\|

*tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhe \|*  
*sā labhiṣyati satkāntaṃ putradaṃ sarvakāmadam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Particularly, if she worships it on the third lunar day and continues it for a year, O splendid one, she will get a good husband who will accord her everything she desires and will bless her with sons.

## \|\| 1.131.28 \|\|

*tathaitāṃ māmakīṃ mūrtimīśānākhyāṃ ca ye narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ duṣṭāpi yā kāntā saumyā caiva bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Similarly, those men who worship my idol named Īśāna can make even their wicked (disobedient) beloved gentle.

## \|\| 1.131.29 \|\|

*ye punaḥ kanyakāhetoḥ pūjayiṣyaṃti bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*yāṃ kanyāṃ manasi sthāpya tāṃ labhiṣyantyasaṃśayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Those who devoutly worship for the sake of a daughter, shall undoubtedly obtain a daughter of their mental choice.

## \|\| 1.131.30 \|\|

*niṣkāmāścāpi ye martyā pūjayiṣyaṃti sarvadā \|*  
*te yāsyaṃti parāṃ siddhiṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Those men who are free from all desires and worship it always, will attain the greatest Siddhi devoid of old age and death.”

## \|\| 1.131.31 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahādevo vṛṣamāropya tāṃ priyām \|*  
*svayamāruhya paścācca kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After saying thus, Mahādeva made his beloved mount the Bull and then he himself mounted it. Afterwards, he went to the mountain Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.131.32 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|\|*  
*tasmāttava suteyaṃ yā tāmārādhayatu drutam \|*  
*pañcapiṇḍamayā gaurīṃ yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhām \|\| 32 \|\|*

Nārada said:

32\. Hence, let this daughter of yours propitiate splendid Gaurī consisting of the five lumps for a year.

## \|\| 1.131.33 \|\|

*tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa tataḥ prāpsyati satpatim \|*  
*mukhaprekṣamatiprītaṃ rūpādibhirguṇairyutam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She should worship particularly on the third lunar day. Then she will get a good husband who will look up to her, will be very loving and will be endowed with handsome features and other good qualities.

## \|\| 1.131.34 \|\|

*śāṃḍilyuvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā muniśreṣṭho nāradaḥ prayayau tataḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāṃ prati prītyā mama mātrā visarjitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Śāṇḍilī said:

34\. After saying thus, Nārada, the excellent sage, proceeded ahead, in his pilgrimage. My mother lovingly bade farewell to him.

## \|\| 1.131.35 \|\|

*mayāpi ca tadādeśātkaumāryepi ca saṃsthayā \|*  
*pūjayā vatsaraṃ yāvatpūjitā patikāmyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At his behest, I remained steadfast in the vow of virginity and worshipped the deity for a period of one year with a desire for husband.

## \|\| 1.131.36 \|\|

*tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa mārgamāsāditaḥ śubhe \|*  
*naivedyairvividhairdānairgaṃdhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I worshipped especially on the third lunar day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa with various kinds of food offerings, gifts, scents, garlands and unguents, O splendid lady.

## \|\| 1.131.37 \|\|

*tatprabhāvādayaṃ prāpto jaiminirnāma saddvijaḥ \|*  
*kātyāyani yathā dṛṣṭastvayā kiṃ kīrtitaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By its power, O Kātyāyanī, this excellent Brāhmaṇa named Jaimini was obtained by me. As you have seen him, why should there be further glorification?

## \|\| 1.131.38 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi kalyāṇi pūjayaināṃ samāhitā \|*  
*saṃprāpsyasi susaubhāgyaṃ maitreyyā sadṛśaṃ śubhe \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Hence, O fair lady, worship the goddess with great concentration. You will attain good conjugal felicity, O splendid lady, on par with that of Maitreyī.

## \|\| 1.131.39-40 \|\|

*tvayā na pūjitā ceyaṃ kaumārye vartamānayā \|*  
*yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ gaurī tṛtīyāyāṃ na cādhikam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sāpatnyaṃ tena saṃjātaṃ saubhāgyepi nirargale \|*  
*yathoktavidhinā devī satyametanmayoditam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Earlier, the goddess was not worshipped by you in the prescribed way. You did not resort to the vow of celibacy. You did not continue it for a year. You did not make special adoration on the third lunar day. Hence, the pain due to a co-wife, although good fortune should have been unrestricted. The truth has been said by me.

## \|\| 1.131.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā kātyāyanī sarvaṃ śāṃḍilyā yatprakīrtitam \|*  
*tataḥ praṇamya tāṃ pṛṣṭvā svameva bhavanaṃ yayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

41\. After hearing everything said by Śāṇḍilī Kātyāyanī bowed down to her. Then taking leave of her she went to her own house.

## \|\| 1.131.42 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe'tha saṃprāpte tṛtīyādivase site \|*  
*tāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmāsa varṣaṃ yāvakṛtakṣaṇā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, she propitiated the goddess. She continued the same on the same (third day) for a year.

## \|\| 1.131.43 \|\|

*gauriṇīrbhojayāmāsa mṛṣṭānnairbhojanai rasaiḥ \|*  
*tailakṣāraparityaktairgandhaiḥ kuṃkumapūrvakaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. She fed virgins with sweet food and tasty juices avoiding oil and salt. She offered them sweet scents and substances like saffron.

## \|\| 1.131.44-45 \|\|

*tatastu vatsare pūrṇe yājñavalkyastadantikam \|*  
*gatvā provāca kiṃ kaṣṭaṃ tvaṃ karoṣi śucismite \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mayā kāṃtena raktena kāmadena sadaiva tu \|*  
*tasmādāgaccha gacchāva svameva bhavanaṃ śubhe \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. When the year was complete, Yājñavalkya went near her and said: “O lady of pure smiles, why do you undertake such a trouble? While I, your affectionate lover, am ready to give whatever you desire always, why should you worry? O splendid lady, come, let us go to our own house.”

## \|\| 1.131.46 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu tāṃ hṛṣṭāṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare \|*  
*jagāma bhavanaṃ paścātpulakāṃkitagātrajām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying thus to her, he grasped her right hand even as she experienced horripilation all over her body and went home.

## \|\| 1.131.47 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ tayā sārdhaṃ vartate harṣitānanaḥ \|*  
*maitreyyā sahito yadvadaviśeṣeṇa sarvadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thereafter, he was as much delighted with her as with Maitreyī. He was always a smiling face without any change.

## \|\| 1.131.48 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃjanayāmāsa tasyāṃ putraṃ guṇānvitam \|*  
*kātyāyanābhidhānaṃ ca yajña vidyāvicakṣaṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He begot of her a son of good qualities named Kātyāyana, an expert in the lore of Yajñas (as the author of a Śrautasūtra).

## \|\| 1.131.49 \|\|

*putro vararuciryasya babhūva guṇasāgaraḥ \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. His son was Vararuci, an ocean of good qualities. He wās omniscient and expert in all rites. He was a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.131.50-54 \|\|

*sthāpito'tra śubhe kṣetre yena vidyārthināṃ kṛte \|*  
*samārādhya viśeṣeṇa caturthyāṃ śuklavāsare \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mahāgaṇapatirbhaktyā sarvavidyāpradāyakaḥ \|*  
*yastasya purato viprāḥ śāṃtipāṭhavidhānataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gṛhṇāti puṣpamālāṃ yaḥ paṭhecchaktyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vedāṃtakṛtsa vipraḥ syātsadā janmanijanmani \|\| 52 \|\|*

*aśaktyā cātha pāṭhasya yo gṛhṇāti dhanena ca \|*  
*sa viśeṣādbhavedvipro vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*viduṣāṃ sa gṛhe janma yājñikānāṃ sadā labhet \|*  
*na kadācittu mūrkhārṇāṃ ninditānāṃ kathañcana \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. For the good of pupils he installed Mahāgaṇapati the bestower of all lores, with great devotion, after duly worshipping him on the fourth lunar day on a Friday.

One who takes a flower garland and recites the Vedas in accordance with the injunctions, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, shall be an expounder of Vedanta in the course of every birth.

One who is incapable of reciting himself but makes others recite by offering cash reward shall become a Brāhmaṇa who masters the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

He will always be born in the houses of Yājñikas (performers of Yajñas). He will never be born in the houses of fools or censured ones.

## Chapter 132 - Creation of Vāstupada

## \|\| 1.132.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\|*  
*tvayā sūtaja tatrasthaṃ yājñavalkyasya kīrtitam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ vararuceścaiva vaināyakyaṃ pravidyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kātyāyanasya na proktaṃ kiñcittatra mahāmate \|*  
*kiṃ vā tena kṛtaṃ naiva kiṃ vā te vismṛtiṃ gatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasmādācakṣva naḥ śīghraṃ yadi kiṃcinmahātmanā \|*  
*kṣetretra nirmitaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. O Sūtaja, you mentioned the Tīrtha of Yājñavalkya as situated there. The Tīrtha of Vararuci known as Vaināyakya is also there.

O highly intelligent one, no Tīrtha of Kātyāyana has been mentioned. Is it because no such Tīrtha was made by him or has it escaped your memory?

Now tell us quickly if any Tīrtha bestowing all the Siddhis was created in the holy spot here by the noble-souled one.

## \|\| 1.132.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tena vāstupadaṃnāma tatra tīrthavinirmitam \|*  
*kātyāyanena vipreṇa sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. A Tīrtha named Vāstupada was made by that Brāhmaṇa Kātyāyana. It gives all desired things unto men.

## \|\| 1.132.5 \|\|

*catvāriṃśattribhiryuktā devatā yatra paṃca ca \|*  
*pūjyaṃte pūjitāścāpi siddhiṃ yacchaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At that place forty-eight deities are worshipped. On being worshipped, they bestow Siddhi instantly.

## \|\| 1.132.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmāttā devatāḥ sūta pūjyaṃte tatra saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*nāmataśca vibhāgena kīrtayasva pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:

6\. Why are those deities stationed there worshipped, O Sūta? Describe them by names separately.

## \|\| 1.132.7-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pūrvaṃ kiṃcinmahadbhūtaṃ nirgataṃ dharaṇītalāt \|*  
*apūrvaṃ raudramatyugraṃ kṛṣṇa daṃtaṃ bhayānakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śaṃkukarṇaṃ kṛśāsyaṃ ca ūrdhvakeśaṃ bhayānakam \|*  
*devānāṃ nāśanārthāya mānuṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7-8. Formerly, a great Bhūta (Spirit) came out of the surface of the earth. It was unprecedented, highly frightening and formidable and had black teeth. It was spike-eared, leanfaced and had upraised hairs. It came out terrifyingly for destroying Devas and human beings in particular.

## \|\| 1.132.9 \|\|

*ākṛṣṭaṃ dānaveṃdreṇa maṃtraiḥ śukrapradarśitaiḥ \|*  
*avadhyaṃ sarvaśastrāṇāmastrāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It was attracted and activated by the leading Dānava by means of Mantras indicated by Śukra. It could not be killed by any weapon or even missiles.

## \|\| 1.132.10 \|\|

*atha devāḥ samālokya tattādṛksubhayāvaham \|*  
*jaghnuḥ śastraiḥ śitaiścitraiḥ kopena mahatānvitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing such a highly terrifying spirit, the Devas provoked by great anger struck it with sharp weapons of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.132.11 \|\|

*naiva śekustadaṃgeṣu prahartuṃ yatnamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyaṃte kevalaṃ tena śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In spite of their effort, they were unable to strike its limbs. Hundreds and thousands were simply gobbled up by it.

## \|\| 1.132.12 \|\|

*atha te yatnamāsthāya sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā tadbhūtamabhidudruvuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With great effort then all the Devas including Vāsava, kept Brahmā at their head and rushed against that Bhūta.

## \|\| 1.132.13 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃgṛhya yatnena sarvagātreṣu sarvataḥ \|*  
*tacca paṃcaguṇairdevaiḥ pātitaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereafter, they caught hold of it with great effort. They bound all his limbs five times with a rope (of five strands?) and felled it on the ground.

## \|\| 1.132.14 \|\|

*upaviṣṭāstatastasya sarve bhūtvā samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*prahārānsaṃprayacchaṃti na lagaṃti ca tasya te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then all of them sat around it and began to strike it but no blow had any effect on it.

## \|\| 1.132.15 \|\|

*ātharvaṇena sūktena jātaṃ cāmṛtabiṃdunā \|*  
*tadbhūtaṃ preṣitaṃ daityairmuṃḍena ca tadaṃtikam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then a Bhūta originating from the Ātharvaṇa Sūkta named Amṛtabindu was hurled by the Daityas near it along with a shaven head (Muṇḍa Sūkta?)

## \|\| 1.132.16 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃtaṃ tattathaiva vyavasthitam \|*  
*na muṃcaṃti bhayātte tu na haṃtuṃ śaknuvaṃti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus for a thousand years it remained there in that condition. They could not leave it due to fear nor could they strike it.

## \|\| 1.132.17 \|\|

*tasyodare sthito brahmā śakrādyā amarāśca ye \|*  
*caturdikṣu sthitāḥ kruddhā mahadyatnena saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*tataste dānavāḥ sarve maṃtraṃ cakruḥ parasparam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Brahmā stood on its belly and the furious Immortals beginning with Śakra stood in the four directions with great effort. Thereupon all the Dānavas began to have consultations together.

## \|\| 1.132.18 \|\|

*asya bhūtasya raudrasya śukrasṛṣṭasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*eka evātra nirdiṣṭa upāyo devasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The destruction of the Devas was suggested as the sole aim of this formidable Bhūta created by Sukra instantly.

## \|\| 1.132.19 \|\|

*tataḥ śastrāṇi tīkṣṇāni dānavāste mahābalāḥ \|*  
*muṃcaṃto vividhānnādānsamājagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then those mighty Dānavas discharged sharp weapons and shouted loudly. Thus they came there in thousands.

## \|\| 1.132.20 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurāgatastatra tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*āha bhūtaṃ tadā viṣṇurvacasā hlādayanniva \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the meantime, Viṣṇu came there at the same instant. Then Viṣṇu spoke to the Bhūta delighting it as it were by means of his words:

## \|\| 1.132.21-22 \|\|

*yo yasminsaṃsthito gātre devastava samudbhave \|*  
*tatra pūjāṃ samādāya tasmāttvāṃ tarpayiṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

*naivaṃvidhā tu loke'sminpūjā devasya saṃsthitā \|*  
*kasyacidyādṛśī te'dya mayā saṃpratipāditā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. “Each of the Devas will propitiate you after getting the adoration in the respective limb pertaining to you wherein he is present. The type of worship mentioned by me in your case has never been adopted in the case of a Deva in the whole world.”

## \|\| 1.132.23-24 \|\|

*tatastena pratijñātamavikalpena cetasā \|*  
*evaṃ te'haṃ kariṣyāmi paraṃ me vacanaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yadi kaścinna me pūjāṃ kariṣyati kadācana \|*  
*kathaṃcinmānavaḥ kaścitsa me bhakṣyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Thereupon, the Bhūta promised with an unhesitating mind: “I shall carry out your words thus. But listen to my words: If any human being at any time does not adore me in any manner, he shall be my prey.”

## \|\| 1.132.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva ca prokte tato devena cakriṇā \|*  
*tadbhūtaṃ niścalaṃ jātaṃ harṣeṇa mahatānvitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sūta said:

25\. The Discus-bearing Lord said, “Of course.” Then the Bhūta became motionless with great delight.

## \|\| 1.132.26 \|\|

*tato devāḥ samutthāya tattyaktvā śastrapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*jaghnuśca niśitaiḥ śastraiḥ palāyanasamutsukān \|*  
*lajjāhīnāngatāmarṣāndīnavākyaprajalpakān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then the weapon-wielding Devas left it and got up. With their sharp arrows they struck down (the Dānavas) who were eager to flee and shameless. With the disappearance of their ire they began to utter piteous words:

## \|\| 1.132.27 \|\|

*tataḥ svasthaḥ sa bhūtvā tu harirdaityairnipātitaiḥ \|*  
*provāca padmajaṃ nāma bhūtasyāsya kuruṣva bhoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With the Daityas struck down, Hari felt relieved. He spoke to the Lotus-born One: “Oh, give a name to this Bhūta.”

## \|\| 1.132.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| \|*  
*anena tava vākyasya proktaṃ vākyaṃ hare yataḥ \|*  
*vāstvetaditi yasmācca tasmādvāstu bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

28\. In reply to your statement the words uttered by this (Bhūta), O Hari, were “vā astu etad” (“Or this may be so”). Hence, its name shall be “Vāstu.”

## \|\| 1.132.29 \|\|

*evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśa āhūya viśvakarmaṇe \|*  
*vidhānaṃ kathayāmāsa pūjārthaṃ vistarānvitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On being told thus, Hṛṣīkeśa summoned Viśvakarman and told him the detailed procedure of the adoration.

## \|\| 1.132.30-32 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāha yājñavalkyasutaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmāṇamāhūya prathamaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre mamāśramapadaṃ kuru \|*  
*anenaiva vidhānena proktena tu mahāmate \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatohaṃ sakalaṃ buddhvā vṛddhiṃ neṣyāmi bhūtale \|*  
*bālāvabodhanārthāya tasmādāgaccha satvaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. In the mean time, the intelligent son of Yājñvalkya summoned Viśvakarman, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and said: “First make my hermitage at the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, O highly intelligent one, in accordance with this procedure now explained. Thereafter, I shall understand everything and make it flourish on the earth so that children (ignorant persons) may learn and understand the same. Hence come quickly.”

## \|\| 1.132.33 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa taṃ brahmāpi tadaṃtikam \|*  
*viśvakarmāṇamāhūya svasutasya hite sthitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then Brahmā, inclined to abide by what was beneficial to his son (Yājñavalkya being Brahmā’s own incarnation) summoned Viśvakarman and sent him to him (son of Kātyāyanī).

## \|\| 1.132.34 \|\|

*viśvakarmāpi tatraitya vāstupūjāṃ yathoditām \|*  
*cakāra brahmaṇā proktāṃ yādṛśīṃ sakalāṃ tataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Viśvakarman came there and fully performed the Vāstu adoration in the manner explained by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.132.35 \|\|

*kātyāyano'pi tāṃ sarvāṃ dṛṣṭvā cakre sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tadā viśvahitārthāya śālākarmādi pūrvikām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Kātyāyana observed everything and rendered it a thousand-fold for the benefit of the universe including Śālākarman etc. (method of building the hall).

## \|\| 1.132.36 \|\|

*evaṃ vāstupadaṃ jātaṃ tasminkṣetre dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*asminkṣetre naraḥ pāpātspṛṣṭo mucyeta karmaṇā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It was thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that the site of abode (Vāstupada) came to be in that holy spot. A man overwhelmed by sins will become released therefrom by means of holy rites performed in this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.132.37 \|\|

*tathā na prāpnuyāddoṣaṃ gṛhajātaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*śilpotthaṃ kupadotthaṃ ca kuvāstujamathāpi ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He will not incur any sin due to any house, architecture, bad site or irregular activity of the site (rite).

## \|\| 1.132.38 \|\|

*vaiśākhasya tṛtīyāyāṃ śuklāyāṃ rohiṇīṣu ca \|*  
*tatpadaṃ nihitaṃ tatra vāstostena mahātmanā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It was on the third lunar day in the bright half of Vaiśākha, coinciding with Rohiṇī star, that the Vāstupada was placed there by that noble-souled one.

## \|\| 1.132.39 \|\|

*tasminnapi ca yaḥ pūjāṃ tenaiva vidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*tasya yaḥ kurute samyaksa bhūpatvamavāpnuyāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A man who performs its adoration on that day in accordance with the injunction shall attain the status of king.

## \|\| 1.132.40 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ doṣānvitaṃ prāpya śilpādibhirupadrutam \|*  
*tasyopasaṃgamaṃ prāpya samṛddhiṃ yāti taddine \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A house may be defective or it may have structural slips but due to this association (with the Vāstu-adoration) it flourishes day by day.

## Chapter 133 - Origin of Ajāgṛhā

## \|\| 1.133.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā'nyāpi ca tatrāsti devatā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*ajāgṛheti vikhyātā sarvarogakṣayāvahā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: For protecting his subjects against diseases, Aja converted them as goats and kept them confined in a fold. Once a Brāhmaṇa-pilgrim ignorantly slept there and contracted leprosy. King Aja performed penance and propitiated the Kṣetra Devatā. The Devatā advised the Brāhmaṇa to take a bath in the Candra Kūpikā nearby which cured his disease. Hence the Devatā came to be known as Ajāgṛhā.

Sūta said:

1\. Further, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there is another deity there well-known as Ajāgṛhā. It is destructive of all ailments.

## \|\| 1.133.2 \|\|

*ajāpālo yadā rājā sarvalokahite rataḥ \|*  
*ajārūpāḥ prayāṃti sma vyādhayaḥ sakalā dvijāḥ \|*  
*tadā rātrau samānīya tasminsthāne dadhāti saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Ajāpāla who was engaged in what is beneficial to all the worlds, was the king, O Brāhmaṇas, all the ailments used to go away in the form of goats. He used to bring them back during the night and place them at that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.133.3 \|\|

*tatastadāśrayātsthānamajāgṛhamiti smṛtam \|*  
*sarvairjanairdharā pṛṣṭhedarśanādvyādhināśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The place being their (of the ailments) resort came to be remembered as Ajāgṛha. By visiting it once, people residing on the surface of the earth, get (their) ailments destroyed.

## \|\| 1.133.4 \|\|

*tatraiśvaryamabhūtpūrvaṃ yattadbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi śrotavyaṃ susamāhitaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I shall recount unto you all, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Aiśvarya (lordly glory) that existed there formerly. It should be listened to with great concentration.

## \|\| 1.133.5 \|\|

*tatrāgato dvijaḥ kaścitkṣetre tāpasarūpadhṛk \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena rātrau prāptaḥ śramānvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A certain Brāhmaṇa in the guise of a sage came to that holy spot in the course of his pilgrimage. He came there at night and he was awfully tired.

## \|\| 1.133.6 \|\|

*ajāvṛṃdamathālokya niviṣṭaṃ susukhānvitam \|*  
*romaṃtha karmasaṃyuktaṃ viśvastamakutobhayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He saw that a flock of goats was kept there comfortably. They were chewing the cud in a carefree manner without any fear from aṇy quarter.

## \|\| 1.133.7-9 \|\|

*sa jñātvā mānuṣeṇātra bhavitavyamasaṃśayam \|*  
*na śūnyāḥ paśavo rātrau sthāsyaṃti vijane vane \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tataḥ phūtkṛtya phūkṛtya divaṃ yāvanna saṃdadhe \|*  
*kaścidvācaṃ prasuptaśca tāvattatraiva ciṃtayan \|\| 8 \|\|*

*avaśyaṃ mānuṣeṇātra paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca \|*  
*āgaṃtavyaṃ kuto'pyāśu tasmāttiṣṭhāmi nirbhayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. He knew that undoubtedly some person must be present there. Cattle or beasts are not kept at night in a desolate forest. He repeatedly shouted at the sky but there was no response. He went to sleep thinking: ‘Certainly for the protection of these animals some man should soon come from somewhere. So I shall stay here fearlessly.’

## \|\| 1.133.10 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya prasuptasya gatā sā rajanī tataḥ \|*  
*tatastvaritavattasya suśrāṃtasya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. While he was asleep thus in utter exhaustion, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the night passed off quickly.

## \|\| 1.133.11 \|\|

*atha yāvatprabhāte sa prapaśyati nijāṃ tanum \|*  
*tāvatkuṣṭhādibhī rogaiḥ samaṃtātparivāritām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In the morning when he looked all over his body, he found it covered by leprosy and other ailments.

## \|\| 1.133.12-13 \|\|

*aśaktaścalituṃ sthānādapi caikaṃ padaṃ kvacit \|*  
*tejo hīno'pi raudreṇa cintayāmāsa vai tataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kimidaṃ kāraṇaṃ yena mamaiṣā saṃsthitā tanuḥ \|*  
*akasmādeva rogo'yaṃ calituṃ naiva ca kṣamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. He was unable to move even a step from that place. He became lustreless on account of the terrible ailments. He began to think: ‘What is the cause? My body has become like this suddenly with this ailment. I am unable to move.’

## \|\| 1.133.14 \|\|

*evaṃ cintayamānasya tasya viprasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*dvādaśārkapratīkāśaḥ puruṣaḥ samupāgataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Even as that Brāhmaṇa was thinking thus, a person resembling twelve suns in lustre came there instantly.

## \|\| 1.133.15 \|\|

*taṃ yūthaṃ kālayāmāsa tataḥ saṃjñābhirāhvayan \|*  
*pṛthaktvena samādāya yaṣṭiṃ savyena pāṇinā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He called and grouped that flock naming them specifically. He had a stick in his left hand and he was separating them.

## \|\| 1.133.16 \|\|

*athāpaśyatsa taṃ vipraṃ vyādhibhiḥ sarvato vṛtam \|*  
*aśaktaṃ calituṃ kvāpi tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then he saw that Brāhmaṇa completely overpowered by ailment and unable to move anywhere. Then he spoke to him respectfully.

## \|\| 1.133.17-19 \|\|

*kastvamevaṃvidhaḥ prāptaḥ sthāne cātra dvijottama \|*  
*nāsti rājye mama vyādhiḥ kasyacitkutracitsphuṭam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ajonāma narendro'haṃ yadi te śrotramāgataḥ \|*  
*vyādhīṃśca cchāgarūpeṇa rakṣāmi janakāraṇāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tasmādbrūhi śarīrastho yaste vyādhirvyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yenā'haṃ nigrahaṃ tasya karomi dvijasattama \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, who are you and whence have you come to this spot in such a plight? In my kingdom clearly no one suffers from any disease anywhere. I am a king named Aja. Perhaps you have heard about me. For the sake of the people, I segregate the ailments in the form of goats. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, tell me what is the sickness that has overcome your body? Tell me so that I can control it.”

## \|\| 1.133.20 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparo'haṃ ca bhramāmi kṣitimaṃḍale \|*  
*krameṇā'tra samāyātaḥ kṣetre'sminhāṭakeśvare \|\| 20 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

20\. I am engaged in pilgrimage. I am wandering all over the earth. In due course, I have come to this holy place of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.133.21-22 \|\|

*niśāvaktre nṛpaśreṣṭha vāsaḥ saṃciṃtito mayā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā'mūṃśca paśūnbhūpa mānuṣaṃ bhāvyameva hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tataścātra prasupto'haṃ paśūnāmaṃtike nṛpa \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. O excellent king, I came here at nightfall. On seeing these animals, O King, I thought there should be human beings around and decided to stay here. O king, I went to sleep by the side of these animals.

## \|\| 1.133.23 \|\|

*atha yāvatprabhāte'haṃ prapaśyāmi nijāṃ tanum \|*  
*tāvatkuṣṭhādirogaiśca samaṃtātparivāritām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When it dawned, I saw my body completely covered with leprosy and other ailments.

## \|\| 1.133.24 \|\|

*nānyatkiṃcinnṛpaśreṣṭha kāraṇaṃ vedmi tattvataḥ \|*  
*kimetena nṛpaśreṣṭha bhūyobhūyaḥ prajalpatā \|*  
*bahutvātkuru tasmānme yathā syānnīrujā tanuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In fact I do not know of any other cause. Let it go, O excellent king. Why should we talk much? Do something so that my body shall be free from disease.

## \|\| 1.133.25 \|\|

*tataste vyādhayaḥ proktā ajāpālena bhūbhujā \|*  
*kenājñā khaṃḍitā me'dya ko vadhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ mama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Ailments were told by King Ajāpāla: “By whom was my command broken? Who should be killled by me?”

## \|\| 1.133.26 \|\|

*vyādhaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*mā kopaṃ kuru bhūpāla kṛtye'smiṃstvaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*yasmādeṣa dvijo viṣṭaḥ sāṃprataṃ vyādhibhistribhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Ailments said:

26\. O king, do not be angry at all in this matter wherein this Brāhmaṇa has now been assailed by three Ailments.

## \|\| 1.133.27 \|\|

*rājayakṣmā ca kuṣṭhaṃ ca pāmā ca dvijasattama \|*  
*ete saṃsargajā doṣāstrayo'dyāpi prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The three Ailments, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, are consumptive disease, leprosy and scabies. All these three defects (diseases) are proclaimed till today as contagious.

## \|\| 1.133.28 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ prathamau yau dvau nivṛttirahitau smṛtau \|*  
*auṣadhaiścaiva maṃtraiśca śeṣā nāśaṃ vrajaṃti ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The first two of these Ailments are remembered as irremediable either through medicines or through Mantras. The others can be destroyed.

## \|\| 1.133.29 \|\|

*ābhyāṃ ca brahmaśāposti yena nāsti nivartanam \|*  
*tasmādatra nṛpaśreṣṭha kuru yatte kṣamaṃ bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. There is curse of Brahmā on these two. Hence there is no question of their removal. O excellent king, do whatever is within your power in this matter.

## \|\| 1.133.30 \|\|

*etena brāhmaṇenaite spṛṣṭā rājaṃstrayopi ca \|*  
*tasmāttāvattanuṃ cāsyāviśatāṃ tāvasaṃśayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O king, all these three have been touched by this Brāhmaṇa. Hence undoubtedly these have entered his body.

## \|\| 1.133.31 \|\|

*aparaṃ śṛṇu bhūpāla vacanaṃ no mukhāccyutam \|*  
*hitāya sarvajaṃtūnāṃ tava śreyovivṛddhaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Further, O king, listen these words issuing from our mouths for the benefit of all creatures and for increasing your glory.

## \|\| 1.133.32 \|\|

*yatra sthānaṃ ciraṃ tatra medinyāṃ vihitaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*purīṣaṃ ca samāviddhā tenaiṣā medinī drutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O king, a permanent spot had been made there on the ground where excreta have been dropped (by the goats). Therefore, the ground has been broken down and rendered uneven immediately.

## \|\| 1.133.33 \|\|

*kālāṃtarepi ye martyā bhūmyāmasyāṃ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*bhūmeḥ sparśaṃ kariṣyaṃti te bhaviṣyaṃti cedṛśāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Even on later occasions, those men who come to this region and touch the ground will become like this.

## \|\| 1.133.34-35 \|\|

*vayaṃ śeṣā mahārāja vyādhayo ye vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*tvayā muktvā bhaviṣyāmo mantrauṣadhavaśānugāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*naitau punastu durgrāhyau brahmaśāpa samudbhavau \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. We, the remaining ailments, O great king, are amenable to Mantras and medicinal herbs. We should be set free by you, not these two uncontrollable ones cursed by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.133.36-37 \|\|

*tacchrutvā pārthivaḥ so'pi tasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ punaḥ prāha na bhetavyaṃ tvayā dvija \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tvāṃ rakṣayiṣyāmi vyādherasmātsudāruṇāt \|*  
*atra tasmātpratīkṣasva kañcitkālaṃ mamājñayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. On hearing it the king too settled down in that place. He told the Brāhmaṇa again: “O Brāhmaṇa, you should not be afraid. I will protect you from this gruesome disease. At my behest, therefore, wait here for some time.”

## \|\| 1.133.38 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataścakre tadarthaṃ sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*ārādhayanprabhaktyā ca samyaktāṃ kṣetradevatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After saying thus he performed very great penance for that purpose, propitiating the presiding deity of the holy spot perfectly with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.133.39 \|\|

*muṃḍenātharvaśīrṣeṇa divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*kṣetrapālotthasūktena vāstusūktena ca dvijāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Brāhmaṇas, he untiringly recited the various Sūktas of Atharvaśīrṣa such as Muṇḍa, Kṣetrapālottha and Vāstusūkta.

## \|\| 1.133.40 \|\|

*siddhārthai raktapuṣpaiśca guggulena sudhūpitaiḥ \|*  
*homaṃ kurvannṛpaḥ paścānnīlarudrānviśeṣataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The king performed Homa with white mustard and red flowers rendered well fragrant with incense. Then he (recited) the Nīlarudra Sūktas particularly.

## \|\| 1.133.41-42 \|\|

*atha naktāvasānena tasya homasya cotthitā \|*  
*bhittvā dharātalaṃ devī mantrākṛṣṭā vinirgatā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*devatā tasya kṣetrasya tataḥ provāca taṃ nṛpam \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The presiding deity of that holy spot, the goddess attracted by the Mantras, pierced the earth towards the close of the night at the conclusion of the Homa and came out. She spoke to the king:

## \|\| 1.133.43-44 \|\|

*ekāhaṃ tava bhūpāla homasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*vinirgatā dharāpṛṣṭhātkṣetrasyāsyādhipā smṛtā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasmādvada mahābhāga yatte kṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*parāṃ tuṣṭimanuprāptā tasmādbrūhi yadīpsitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. “O king, by the power of this Homa of yours, I have risen up from the surface of the earth. I am the only one remembered as the presiding deity of this holy spot. Hence, O highly esteemed one, tell me. What task of yours shall I carry out? I have attained the greatest pleasure. Hence, speak out what is desired by you.”

## \|\| 1.133.45 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*atra sthāne sadā stheyaṃ tvayā devi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vyādhisaṃsargajo doṣo bhūmerasyā yathā vrajet \|\| 45 \|\|*

The king said:

45\. O goddess, you must stay particularly in this holy spot forever so that the defects of this land arising from the contact of the ailments, may disappear.

## \|\| 1.133.46-47 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti deveśi tathā nītirvidhīyatām \|*  
*no cedasyāḥ prasaṃgena prabhaviṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vyādhigrastā yathā vipro yo'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate puraḥ \|*  
*mayātra vyādhayaḥ kālaṃ ciraṃ saṃsthāpitā yataḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati ca me doṣo no ceddevi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. From now onwards, O goddess of Devas, let this policy be adopted. Otherwise men will become afflicted with diseases due to contagion, like this Brāhmaṇa seen in front. For a long time these diseases were contained by me here. Otherwise it would undoubtedly be a fault of mine.

## \|\| 1.133.48 \|\|

*tathāyaṃ brāhmaṇo rogāttvatprasādātsureśvari \|*  
*mukto bhavatu medinyāmatra stheyaṃ sadā tvayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Further, O goddess of Suras, let this Brāhmaṇa be rid of this disease, with your favour. You must stay in this place forever.

## \|\| 1.133.49 \|\|

*kṣetradevatovāca \|*  
*etatsthānaṃ mayā sarvaṃ vyādhidoṣavivarjitam \|*  
*vihitaṃ sarvadaivātra sthāsye'hamiha sarvadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

The Kṣetra Devatā said:

49\. The entire spot has been rendered free from the blemish of disease by me. I shall stay here forever.

## \|\| 1.133.50 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ yo'tra me sthāne vyādhigrastaḥ sameṣyati \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati māṃ bhaktyā nīrogaḥ sa bhaviṣyati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Whoever comes here afflicted with sickness and worships me devoutly, will become free from sickness.

## \|\| 1.133.51 \|\|

*tasmādadya dvijeṃdro'yaṃ māṃ pūjayatu sādaram \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Hence, let this leading Brāhmaṇa respectfully worship me today. He must possess great devotion. He must be clean. He must have great concentration and mental purity.

## \|\| 1.133.52 \|\|

*atra kṣetre parā'nyāsti vikhyātā caṃdrakūpikā \|\|*  
*tasyāṃ snātu yathānyāyaṃ nityameva mahīpate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There is another quite well-known well in this holy spot named Candrakūpikā. O king, let him duly take his holy bath therein everyday.

## \|\| 1.133.53 \|\|

*dakṣaśāpapraśaptena yā caṃdreṇa purā kṛtā \|*  
*svasnānārthaṃ kṣayavyādhipragrastena mahātmanā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. It was formerly dug up by Candra cursed by Dakṣa. The noble-souled one afflicted with the consumptive disease wanted this for the sake of his own holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.133.54 \|\|

*tathā khaṇḍaśilānāma devatā cātra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*saubhāgyakūpikāsnānaṃ kṛtvā tāṃ ca prapaśyatu \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. There is another deity stationed there named Khaṇḍaśilā. Let the Brāhmaṇa take the holy bath in the Saubhāgyakūpikā and then visit the deity.

## \|\| 1.133.55 \|\|

*yā kṛtā kāmadevena kuṣṭhagrastena vai purā \|*  
*snapanārthaṃ ca kuṣṭhasya vināśāya ca sādaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. This well was dug formerly be Kāmadeva who was afflicted with leprosy. He did it with great respect for his own ablution as well as for the destruction of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.133.56 \|\|

*tathā cāpsarasāṃ kuṇḍamatrāsti nṛpasattama \|*  
*tatra snātvā raverahni tataḥ pāmā praśāmyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O excellent king, there is a Kuṇḍa (holy pit) of Apsarās also here. One who bathes therein on a Sunday gets rid of scabies.

## \|\| 1.133.57 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ prāpya supuṇyāṃ candrakūpikām \|*  
*snānaṃ kṛtvā ca tāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*yāvanmāsaṃ tato muktaḥ satvaraṃ rājayakṣmaṇā \|\| 57 \|\|*

Sūta said:

57\. Then the Brāhmaṇa went to the very sacred Candrakūpikā, took his bath and worshipped that goddess with devotion for a period of one month. Then he was immediately relieved of the consumptive disease.

## \|\| 1.133.58 \|\|

*tataḥ saubhāgyakūpīṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmavinirmitām \|*  
*tathā snānaṃ vidhāyātha paśyankhaṃḍaśilāṃ ca tām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then he visited Saubhāgyakūpikā made by Kāma. After taking his holy bath, he visited Khaṇḍaśilā.

## \|\| 1.133.59 \|\|

*tadvanmāsena nirmuktaḥ kuṣṭhena dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tasyā devyāḥ prabhāvena kūpikāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. As before, he did this for a month and was rid of leprosy, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, by the power of the goddess as well as of the Kūpikā in particular.

## \|\| 1.133.60 \|\|

*tataścāpsarasāṃ kuṃḍe snātvaikaṃ ravivāsaram \|*  
*pāmayā saṃparityakto buddhyeva viṣayātmakaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then on a Sunday, he took bath in the Kuṇḍa of Apasrās. He was rid of scabies like one immersed in worldly pleasures (but) who is rid of them by means of knowledge and good sense.

## \|\| 1.133.61 \|\|

*tataḥ sa brāhmaṇo jāto dvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*toṣeṇa mahatā yukto dattāśīstasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then that Brāhmaṇa gained a lustre like that of twelve suns. He became extremely pleased. He gave a blessing to the king.

## \|\| 1.133.62 \|\|

*prayayau vāṃchitaṃ deśamanujñātaśca bhūbhujā \|*  
*devatāyāṃ praṇāmaṃ ca tābhyāṃ kṛtvā punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He bowed repeatedly to those two deities. On being permitted by the king, he went to the land of his choice.

## \|\| 1.133.63 \|\|

*sopi rājā sadoṣāṃstānajārūpānvilokya ca \|*  
*svasyaiva brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ tathā saṃpraharṣitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The king realized the defect of the diseases in the form of the goats. On seeing the Brāhmaṇa healthy he became glad.

## \|\| 1.133.64 \|\|

*svayaṃ ca prayayau tatra yatrastho hāṭakeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tenaiva ca śarīreṇa nijakāṃtāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He himself went to the place where the Lord of Hāṭakeśvara was present in his own body accompanied by his beloved.

## \|\| 1.133.65 \|\|

*ajāgṛhe sthitā yasmātsā devī kṣetradevatā \|*  
*ajāgṛhā tataḥ khyātā sarvatraiva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Since the presiding deity of the holy spot was stationed in Ajāgṛha, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, she became well known everywhere as Ajāgṛhā.

## \|\| 1.133.66 \|\|

*adyāpi yakṣmaṇā grasto yastāṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*tainaiva vidhinā samyaksa nīrogo drutaṃ bhavet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Even today a consumptive patient who worships well that goddess in accordance with the injunction shall quickly become rid of the sickness.

## Chapter 134 - Origin of Tīrthas like Saubhāgyakūpikā

## \|\| 1.134.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadā dakṣeṇa kruddhena purā śapto himadyutiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ bhavatā proktaṃ somanāthakathānakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sāṃprataṃ vada kāmasya yathā kuṣṭho'bhavatpurā \|*  
*yena doṣeṇa śāpaśca kena tasya niyojitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śilākhaṃḍā ca yā devī tathā saubhāgyakūpikā \|*  
*yathā tatra samutpannā tathā'smākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. You have narrated the story of Somanātha as to how the Snow-rayed One was cursed by the furious Dakṣa.

Now tell us how Kāma suffered from leprosy and what was his fault. By whom was he cursed? Recount to us how goddess Śilākhaṇḍa (Khaṇḍaśila) and Saubhāgyakūpikā originated there.

## \|\| 1.134.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāsīdbrāhmaṇo nāma hārīta iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*sa tapastatra saṃtepe vānaprasthāśrame vasan \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. Formerly there was a Brāhmaṇa well-known by the name Hārīta. He performed his penance there in his Vānaprastha

stage.

## \|\| 1.134.5 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī rūpaudāryasamanvitā \|*  
*trailokyasundarī sākṣāllakṣmīriva madhudviṣaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He had a chaste lady as his wife. She possessed beauty and other exquisite qualities. Like Lakṣmī, the wife of the enemy of Madhu (Viṣṇu) she was the most beautiful lady in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.134.6 \|\|

*khyātā pūṇakalānāma sarvaiḥ samuditāguṇaiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā padmajo'pyāśu kāmasya vaśago'bhavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She was well-known by the name Pūrṇakalā. She had well-developed good qualities. On seeing her even the Lotus-born One fell victim to the influence of Kāma.

## \|\| 1.134.7 \|\|

*kadācidapi sa prāptastasminkṣetre manobhavaḥ \|*  
*saha ratyā tathā prītyā kāmeśvaradidṛkṣayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Once, with a desire to see Kāmeśvara (i.e. Lord Śiva), Manobhava (Kāma) too came there along with (his wives) Rati and Prīti.

## \|\| 1.134.8 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare sāpi snānārthaṃ tatra cāgatā \|*  
*kṛtvā vastraparityāgaṃ viveśa jalāśayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the meantime, she too came there for her bath. She stripped herself of all her garments and entered the water-pond.

## \|\| 1.134.9 \|\|

*atha tāṃ kāmadevopi samālokya śubhānanām \|*  
*ātmīyairapi nirviddho hṛdaye puṣpasāyakaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then on seeing the lady of splendid countenance, Kāmadeva too was hit in his heart by his own flowery arrows.

## \|\| 1.134.10 \|\|

*tato ratiṃ parityaktvā prītiṃ ca śarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*vijanaṃ kaṃcidāsādya prasuptaḥ sa taroradhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Wounded by his own arrows, he left Rati and Prīti, reached a lonely spot beneath a tree and slept there.

## \|\| 1.134.11 \|\|

*gātraiḥ pulakitaiḥ sarvairniḥśvāsānniḥśvasanmuhuḥ \|*  
*agnivarṇānsudīrghāṃśca bāṣpa pūrṇavilocanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All his limbs experienced horripilation. He repeatedly heaved hot sighs with fiery colour (agni-varṇa) and long puffs, his eyes were filled with tears.

## \|\| 1.134.12 \|\|

*tiṣṭhansa darśane tasyā ekadṛṣṭyā vyalokayat \|*  
*yogīva susamādhistho dhyāyaṃstadbrahma saṃsthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He then stood in the range of her vision and looked at her with fixed stare like a Yogin in the midst of his mental absortion meditating on the steady established Brahman.

## \|\| 1.134.13 \|\|

*sāpi kāmaṃ samālokya sānurāgaṃ puraḥ sthitam \|*  
*jṛṃbhābhaṃgakṛtāsyaṃ ca vepamānaśarīrakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She too stared at Kama who was standing lovingly in front of her, yawning and having various facial contortions. His whole body was trembling.

## \|\| 1.134.14 \|\|

*sāpi tadbāṇanirbhinnā sābhilāṣā babhūva ha \|*  
*kāmaṃ prati viśeṣeṇa tasya rūpeṇa mohitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She was attracted by Kāma. She was fascinated by his extraordinary features. Her heart was pierced by the arrows of Kāma.

## \|\| 1.134.15 \|\|

*atha tasmājjalātkṛcchrādviniṣkramya śucismitā \|*  
*tīropāṃtaṃ samāsādya sthitā taddṛṣṭigocare \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With great difficulty the lady of pure smiles came out of water and reached the bank. Then she stood within his view.

## \|\| 1.134.16 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmaḥ samutthāya śanaistadaṃtikaṃ yayau \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Kāma got up and came near her very slowly. With palms joined in reverence, he spoke to her respectfully:

## \|\| 1.134.17 \|\|

*kā tvamatra viśālākṣi prāptā snātuṃ jalāśaye \|*  
*mama nāśāya cārvaṃgi tasmācchṛṇu vaco mama \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Who are you, O lady of large eyes? You have come to the water pond for bathing. But, O lady of beautiful limbs, you are out to ruin me. So listen to my word

## \|\| 1.134.18 \|\|

*ahaṃ puṣpaśaro loke prasiddhaścāruhāsini \|*  
*viḍaṃbanāṃ mayā nītā devā api nijaiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lady of beautiful smiles, I am famous in the world as the Flower-arrowed One. Even Devas have been subjected to mortification by me through my arrows.

## \|\| 1.134.19 \|\|

*madbāṇenāhato rudraḥ svaśarīre nitaṃbinīm \|*  
*arddhena dhārayāmāsa tyaktvā lajjāṃ sudūrataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On being struck down by my arrows, Rudra held his wife by means of half of his body, thereby casting off all shame.

## \|\| 1.134.20 \|\|

*brahmā maccharanirbhinnaḥ svasutāṃ cakame tataḥ \|*  
*janayāmāsa tānviprānvālakhilyāṃstathāvidhān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Pierced by my arrows, Brahmā entertained lust for his own daughter and begot of her the Brāhmaṇas Vālakhilyas of such peculiar features.

## \|\| 1.134.21 \|\|

*ahilyāṃ cakame śakro gautamasya priyāṃ satīm \|*  
*madbāṇaiḥ pīḍito'tīva svargādetya dharātalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Śakra was enamoured of Ahalyā, the beloved wife of Gautama. Because he was tormented by my arrows, he came down to the earth from heaven.

## \|\| 1.134.22 \|\|

*evaṃ devā api kṣuṇṇā maccharairye mahattarāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punarmānavāḥ subhrūḥ kṛmiprāyāḥ sucaṃcalāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thus, O lady of excellent eyebrows, even the Devas of superior status have been assailed by my arrows. What then about human beings, very fickle and almost like worms!

## \|\| 1.134.23 \|\|

*ākīṭāṃtaṃ jagatsarvamābrahmāṃtaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*viḍaṃbanāṃ parāṃ prāptaṃ maccharaiścāruhāsini \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O lady of sweet smiles, the entire universe beginning with an insect and ending with Brahmā, has become mortified on account of my arrows.

## \|\| 1.134.24 \|\|

*ahaṃ punastvayā bhīru nīto'vasthāmimāṃ śubhe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Despite all those things, O splendid lady, O timid one, I have been reduced to this plight by you.

## \|\| 1.134.25 \|\|

*tasmāddehi mahābhāge mamādya ratadakṣiṇām \|*  
*yāvanna yāṃti saṃtyajya mama prāṇāḥ kalevarāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hence, O highly esteemed one, give me the grand gift of sexual intimacy today lest my vital breaths should forsake my body.

## \|\| 1.134.26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sāpi tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pativrataparāyaṇā \|*  
*hanyamānā viśeṣeṇa tadbāṇairhṛdaye bhṛśam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sūta said:

26\. On hearing his words, she was in a great dilemma. On the one hand she was devoted to the vow of fidelity to her husband, but on the other hand, she was excessively assailed in the heart by his (Kāma’s) arrows.

## \|\| 1.134.27 \|\|

*anabhijñā ca sā sādhvī kāmadharmasya kevalam \|*  
*tāpasaiḥ saha saṃvṛddhā nānyaṃ jānāti kiṃcana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The poor chaste lady was stranger to the perversity of love-lorn activity. She had grown up in the midst of hermits. She knew none else, nothing else.

## \|\| 1.134.28 \|\|

*vaktuṃ tadviṣaye yacca procyate kāmapīḍitaiḥ \|*  
*adhomukhā'likhadbhūmimaṃguṣṭhena sthitā ciram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. She did not know what to speak and how to speak as is usually the case with those who are tormented by Kāma. She stood thus for a long time looking down and scratching the ground with the big toe of her foot.

## \|\| 1.134.29-31 \|\|

*etasminnantare bhānuḥ prāptaścāstaṃ giriṃ prati \|*  
*vihārasamaye prāpta āhitāgnirniveśane \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hārīto'pi ciraṃ vīkṣya tanmārgaṃ cākṛtāśanaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa kasmātsā cātra nāgatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*snātvā tīrthavare tasmindṛṣṭvā tāṃ candrakūpikām \|*  
*kāmeśvaraṃ ca deveśaṃ kāmadaṃ sukhadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. In the meantime, the sun arrived on the setting mountain (the western quarter). Hermit Hārīta who maintained the sacred fires came back at the time of the elaborate rituals. He waited for her for a long time without taking food. He began to worry: ‘Why has she not come back? After taking her bath in the excellent Tīrtha, viewing that Candrakūpikā and visiting Kāmeśvara, the Lord of the Devas, the bestower of desired happiness on men (she should have come back by this time).’

## \|\| 1.134.32 \|\|

*tataḥ śiṣyasamāyukto vīkṣamāṇa itastataḥ \|*  
*taṃ deśaṃ samanuprāpto yatra tau dvāvapi sthitau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then in the company of his disciples, he looked for her here and there. Ultimately, he came to that place where both of them had been standing.

## \|\| 1.134.33 \|\|

*ālapanbahudhā kāmo hanyamāno nijaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*sāpi caiva viśeṣeṇa vrīḍayā'dhomukhī sthitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Being struck by his own arrows, Kāma was uttering many (overtures of love), but she was standing looking down with excessive bashfulness.

## \|\| 1.134.34 \|\|

*sa gulmāṃtaritaḥ sarvaṃ tacchrutvā kāmajalpitam \|*  
*tasyāśca tadgataṃ bhāvaṃ tataḥ kopāduvāca saḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Concealed behind a hedge, he heard whatever was prattled by Kāma. He noticed her emotional fervour. Thereupon, he became furious and said:

## \|\| 1.134.35-37 \|\|

*yasmātpāpa tvayā patnī mamaivaṃ śarapīḍitā \|*  
*anabhijñā tathā sādhvī patidharmaparāyaṇā \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktastasmādvipriyadarśanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi pāpātmanmukto dāraiḥ svakairapi \|*  
*sā'pi caiva viśeṣeṇa vrīḍayā'dhomukhī sthitā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*eṣāpi ca śilāprāyā bhaviṣyati vicetanā \|*  
*tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā yā sarāgā'bhūnnijadharmabahiṣkṛtā \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. “O sinner, you have afflicted my wife thus with the arrows. She has been an innocent chaste lady devoted loyally to her husband. She has been hit by you and made to stand with face down with excessive bashfulness. Hence you will be overcome with the fell disease of leprosy. You will be unpleasant to see. Even your wives will forsake you. On seeing you, she became enamoured of you. Thereby she transgressed her duty. She shall become senseless resembling a rock.”

## \|\| 1.134.38 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa taṃ kāmaḥ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*na jñāteyaṃ mayā vipra tava bhāryeti sundarī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereupon, Kāma prostrated down to him and pacified him: “O Brāhmaṇa, this beautiful lady was not known to me as your wife.

## \|\| 1.134.39 \|\|

*tena proktā viruddhāni vākyāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*etasyā nāsti doṣo'tra madbāṇaiḥ pīḍitā bhṛśam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Therefore, she was told by me various kinds of words not suited to her. It is not her fault that she was acutely afflicted by my arrows.

## \|\| 1.134.40 \|\|

*sānurāgā paraṃ jātā noktaṃ kiṃcidvaco mune \|*  
*tasmānnārhasi śāpaṃ tvaṃ dātumasyāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Very well, she became infatuated, O sage, but no word was uttered by her. Hence, it does not behove you to curse her at all.

## \|\| 1.134.41 \|\|

*mamāstyeṣo 'parādho'tra tasmānme nigrahaṃ kuru \|*  
*bhūyo'pi brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha asyāḥ śāpasamudbhavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Herein it is my fault. Hence do chastise me. But, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the curse against her is unbearable.

## \|\| 1.134.42 \|\|

*api rudrādayo devā madbāṇebhyo dvijottama \|*  
*soḍhuṃ śaktā na te yasmāttatkathaṃ syādiyaṃ śilā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, even Devas beginning with Rudra are unable to bear my arrows. Hence could she have borne? Why should she be turned into a rock?

## \|\| 1.134.43 \|\|

*tathātra trividhaṃ pāpaṃ pravadaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*mānasaṃ vācikaṃ caiva karmajaṃ ca tṛtīyakam \|*  
*tadasmākaṃ dvidhā jātamekaṃ cāsyā munīśvara \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Further, learned men say that sin is of three kinds, mental, verbal and the third one, physical. O leading sage, I am guilty of two types of sins, whereas she is guilty of only one type.

## \|\| 1.134.44 \|\|

*bhāryāyāste surūpāyāstasmātsaṃpūrṇanigraham \|*  
*kariṣyasi na te bhītiḥ kācidasti paratrajā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Your beautiful wife may have committed only one sin, but you want to mete out the full punishment. Are you not afraid of the future world?

## \|\| 1.134.45 \|\|

*manastāpādvrajetpāpaṃ mānasaṃ vācikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tasya prasādanenaiva yasyopari vijalpitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A mental sin can be wiped off by mental anguish and regret. A verbal sin can be eradicated by pacifying him against whom something foul has been uttered.

## \|\| 1.134.46 \|\|

*prāyaścittairyathoktaiśca karmajaṃ pātakaṃ vrajet \|*  
*dharmaśāstraiḥ pariproktaṃ yataḥ sarvairmahāmune \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A physical sin will disappear through atonement as mentioned in the scriptures on ethical conduct. O great sage, all those scriptures do lay down these.”

## \|\| 1.134.47 \|\|

*hārīta uvāca \|*  
*anyatra viṣaye tasyāḥ pātakaṃ kāmadevate \|*  
*etasya tava dharmasya prādhānyaṃ manasaḥ smṛtam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Hārīta said:

47\. O Kāmadeva, her sin may be as you say if it refers to other matters. But in regard to your sphere of activity, the importance is that of the mind.

## \|\| 1.134.48-50 \|\|

*tasmādevaṃvidhā ceyaṃ sadā sthāsyati cādhama \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ kuru yatkṛtyaṃ nāhaṃ vakṣyāmi kiṃcana \|\| 48 \|\|*

*prathamaṃ manasā sarvaṃ ciṃtyate tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*tataḥ prajalpate vācā kriyate karmaṇā tataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pramāṇaṃ hi manastasmātsarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇātpūrṇo mayā'syā nigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. At the outset everything is mentally conceived. Then it is uttered by means of words. Then the physical act takes place. Hence it is the mind that is more important in regard to all matters always. For this reason I had to mete out a full punishment to her. Hence she will stay in this manner always, O mean fellow. You may do what constitutes your duty. I will not say anything.

## \|\| 1.134.51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā muniśreṣṭho hārītaḥ svāśramaṃ yayau \|*  
*sāpi pūrṇakalā jātā śilārūpā ca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

51\. After saying thus, Hārīta, the excellent sage, went to his hermitage. Pūrṇakalā was turned into a rock at the same instant.

## \|\| 1.134.52 \|\|

*kāmadevo'pi kuṣṭhena grasto raudreṇa ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*śīrṇanāsāṃghripāṇiśca netrāṇāmapriyo'bhavat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Brāhmaṇas, Kāmadeva was seized by leprosy of terrible proportions. His nose, hands and legs became withered and he became repulsive to the eyes of onlookers.

## \|\| 1.134.53 \|\|

*atha kāme nirutsāhe saṃjāte dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*vyādhigraste jagatyasminsṛṣṭirodho vyajāyata \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when Kāma was afflicted with the disease and consequently lost interest in his routine activities, the process of creation in the whole universe stopped.

## \|\| 1.134.54 \|\|

*kevalaṃ kṣīyate loko naiva vṛddhiṃ pragacchati \|*  
*svedajā ye'pi jīvāḥ syustepi yātāḥ parikṣayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The whole world dwindled and deteriorated. There was no growth at all. Even the sweat-born living organisms faced ruin and destruction.

## \|\| 1.134.55-56 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāḥ sarve ciṃtāsamākulāḥ \|*  
*kimidaṃ kṣīyate loko jalasthaiḥ sthalajaiḥ saha \|\| 55 \|\|*

*na dṛśyate kvacidbālaḥ ko'pi kaścitkathaṃcana \|*  
*na ca garbhavatī nārī kaccitkṣemaṃ smarasya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. In the meantime, all the Devas were agitated with anxiety: ‘Why does the world including all aquatic and ground-born living beings decay? No child is seen at all anywhere. Nor is a pregnant lady visible. We hope Smara is all right.’

## \|\| 1.134.57 \|\|

*tatastaṃ vyādhinā grastaṃ jñātvātra kṣetrasaṃśrayam \|*  
*ājagmustvaritāḥ sarve vyākulenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On coming to know that he was afflicted with a disease and had resorted to this holy spot all of them hurried to the place with mental agitation and worry.

## \|\| 1.134.58 \|\|

*kāmeśvarapurasthaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā kusumāyudham \|*  
*atyaṃtavikṛtākāraṃ ciṃtayānaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. They saw the Flower-weaponed One staying in Kāmeśvarapura meditating on Maheśvara. His features were hideous and ugly.

## \|\| 1.134.59 \|\|

*tataḥ procuḥ suduḥkhārtāḥ kimidaṃ kusumāyudha \|*  
*nirutsāhaḥ samutpannaḥ kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In their great distress, they said: “O Flower-weaponed One, what is this? You have become afflicted with the fell disease of leprosy! You have lost all enthusiasm.”

## \|\| 1.134.60 \|\|

*tataścādhomukho jāto lajjayā parayā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*provāca śāpajaṃ sarvaṃ hārītasya viceṣṭitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Overcome with excessive shame, he stood with face turned downwards. He narrated the entire account regarding Hārīta’s action and his curse.

## \|\| 1.134.61 \|\|

*tataste vibudhāḥ procuḥ pātakaṃ yadgirā kṛtam \|*  
*tattasyārādhanātsarvaṃ saṃkṣayaṃ yātyasaṃśayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then the Devas said: “The sin perpetrated verbally shall undoubtedly perish in full by propitiating her.

## \|\| 1.134.62 \|\|

*tasmādetāṃ śilārūpāṃ tvamārādhaya cittaja \|*
