*yena kuṣṭhaḥ kṣayaṃ yāti tatastejo'bhivardhate \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. So, Mind-born One, propitiate her in the form of a rock. Thereby your leprosy will perish and your refulgence will increase.

## \|\| 1.134.63 \|\|

*jagati syānmahāsṛṣṭirdevakṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*na te'sti kāyajaṃ pāpaṃ yato muktvā pravācikam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Since you have not incurred any sin except the verbal one (this atonement will be enough). Let there be the great activity of creation. Let the divine task be fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.134.64-65 \|\|

*atra kuṇḍe tvadīye'nyo yaḥ snātvā śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*enāṃ pāpavinirmuktāṃ śilāṃ vai mānavaḥ spṛśet \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kuṣṭhavyādhisamopetaḥ kāyotthenāpi karmaṇā \|*  
*so'pi vyādhivinirmukto bhaviṣyati gatajvaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. If any other man afflicted with the disease of leprosy, though it may be a result of a sinful action of the body, takes his bath in your Kuṇḍa with great faith and touches this rock freed from sin, he will also be relieved from his sickness and the distress thereof.

## \|\| 1.134.66 \|\|

*etatsaubhāgyakūpaṃ ca loke khyātaṃ jalāśayam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdehaḥ sarvarogakṣayāvaham \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This water pond shall become well-known in the world by the name Saubhāgyakūpa. It shall be destructive of all ailments. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.134.67 \|\|

*dadrūṇi durvibhūtāni tathānyāśca vicarcikāḥ \|*  
*atra snātasya yāsyaṃti dṛṣṭvaitāṃ sadya eva hi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Itches of excessively putrid nature and scabies of the person taking bath here will disappear afrter \[after?\] viewing this rock.”

## \|\| 1.134.68 \|\|

*evamuktvātha te devāḥ prajagmustridaśālayam \|*  
*kāmadevo'pi tatrasthastasyāḥ pūjāmatha vyadhāt \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. After saying this, the Devas went to the heavenly adode. Kāmadeva stayed there and performed the adoration.

## \|\| 1.134.69 \|\|

*tataśca samatikrāṃte māsamātre dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tādṛgrūpaḥ sa saṃjāto yādṛgāsītpurā smaraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Then, even when only a month elapsed, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Smara regained that form which he originally had.

## \|\| 1.134.70 \|\|

*tataścāyatanaṃ tasyāḥ kṛtvā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma vāṃchitaṃ deśaṃ sṛṣṭyarthaṃ yatnamāsthitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then he made a temple for her with great faith and went to the place of his choice in his endeavour for creation.

## \|\| 1.134.71 \|\|

*sāpi namramukhī tādṛktena śaptā tathaiva ca \|*  
*saṃjātā khaṇḍakākārā tena khaṇḍaśilā smṛtā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The lady who had been standing with face lowered down when being cursed, became a fragment of rock. Hence, she is remembered as Khaṇḍaśilā.

## \|\| 1.134.72 \|\|

*yastāṃ pūjayate bhaktyā trayodaśyāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*nāpavādo bhavettasya paradārasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. If anyone devoutly worships her on the thirteenth lunar day, he will never face scandals arising from association with other men’s wives.

## \|\| 1.134.73 \|\|

*kāminyāśca viśeṣeṇa prāhaitacchaṃkarātmajaḥ \|*  
*kārtikeyo dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Kārttikeya, the son of Śaṅkara, has prescribed this rite in particular to a lustful woman. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, what has been said by me is the truth.

## \|\| 1.134.74 \|\|

*tathā kāmeśvaraṃ devaṃ kāmadevapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*trayodaśyāṃ samārādhya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. By propitiating the deity called Kāmeśvara installed by Kāmadeva, on the thirteenth lunar day, one shall attain all desired things.

## \|\| 1.134.75 \|\|

*ratiprītisamāyuktaḥ sthitastatra smarastathā \|*  
*mūrto brāhmaṇaśārdūlāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ prāsādamāśritaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Smara is in a personified form there along with Rati and Prīti, O tigers among Brāhmaṇas. He has an excellent palatial shrine as his resort.

## \|\| 1.134.76-79 \|\|

*virūpo durbhago yo vā trayodaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*yastaṃ kuṃkumajaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjayati mānavaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sa saubhāgyasamāyukto rūpavāṃśca prajāyate \|*  
*yā nārī patinā tyaktā sapatnījanasaṃvṛtā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*taṃ devaṃ sukalatrāḍhyaṃ tathaiva paripūjayet \|*  
*trayodaśyāṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kesaraiḥ kuṃkumodbhavaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*sā saubhāgyavatī viprā jāyate ca prajāvatī \|*  
*dhanadhānyasamṛddhā ca duḥkhaśokavivarjitā \|*  
*doṣaiḥ sarvairvinirmuktā śaṃsitā dharaṇītale \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-79. One ugly in form and unlucky in his plight should worship him with flowers and saffron with great mental concentratrion on the thirteenth lunar day. That man is reborn as a handsome person endowed with conjugal felicity.

A woman abandoned by her husband and surrounded by co-wives should worship that deity along with excellent wives on the thirteenth lunar day with filaments of lotuses and saffron, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. She will enjoy conjugal felicity, O Brāhmaṇas. She will beget sons. She will have flourishing wealth and food-grain. She will be free from misery and grief. She will have no blemishes at all. She will be one praised all over the earth.

## Chapter 135 - Boon to a Chaste Lady: Dīrghikā

## \|\| 1.135.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti dīrghikākhyā suśobhanā \|*  
*sarasī lokavikhyātā sarvapātakanāśanī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yasyāṃ snāto naraḥ samyagbhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: The main object of this chapter is to describe the spiritual power of a chaste lady.—The object of Chapters 135 to 138 is to glorify the Dīghikā Tīrtha. Dīghikā, an old lady, marries an old leper. She carries him on her head to make him perform the pilgrimage of 68 Tīrthas. She reached Hāṭakeśvara at night. In the darkness she inadvertently dashed against sage Māṇḍavya who was impaled there. Due to excruciating pain, he cursed that her husband? ground and a spring of water appeared where they quenched their thirst. The next morning the Sun did not rise. Devas approached her. She allowed the Sun to rise. The Devas made her husband who died due to Māṇḍavya’s curse, live again. They made both of them young. The spring of water created Dīrghikā became known as Dīrghika-Tīrtha and is still efficacious.

Sūta said:

1-2. Further, there is another very splendid lake there named Dīrghikā. It is well-known all over the world and is destructive of all sins.

A man who takes his holy ablution there properly at the time of sunrise on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.135.3 \|\|

*āsītpūrvaṃ dvijo vīraśarmanāmātiviśrutaḥ \|*  
*vedavidyāvratasnāto vardhamāne purottame \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly, in the excellent city of Vardhamāna there was a well-renowned Brāhmaṇa named Vīraśarman. He was a very efficient scholar of the Vedic lore and holy vows connected therewith.

## \|\| 1.135.4 \|\|

*tasya kanyā samutpannā kadācillakṣaṇāccyutā \|*  
*atidīrghā pramāṇena janahāsyavivarddhinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once he had a daughter without good features. She was too tall, beyond the normal size. Thereby she caused popular derision.

## \|\| 1.135.5 \|\|

*tataḥ sā yauvanaṃ prāptā tadrūpāpi kumārikā \|*  
*na kaścidvarayāmāsa śāstravākyamanusmaran \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the same form, the girl attained youth. Remembering the scriptural injunction, no one came forward to marry her:

## \|\| 1.135.6-7 \|\|

*atisaṃkṣiptakeśā yā atidīrghātivāmanā \|*  
*udvāhayati yaḥ kanyāṃ puruṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuṃ sa prāpnoti naro dhruvam \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇātsarve tāṃ tyajaṃti kumārikām \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. “A man who deluded by lust, marries a girl who is too tall, too short or with very short tresses of hairs, shall certainly meet death within six months.” Such was the scriptural passage and for this reason, everyone avoided that girl.

## \|\| 1.135.8 \|\|

*puruṣā atidīrghatvayuktāṃ vīkṣya samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tato vairāgyamāpannā tapastepe'tidāruṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All men avoided her on seeing her excessive height. Thereupon, she became dejected and performed a very severe penance.

## \|\| 1.135.9 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tayā cīrṇānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*pārākāṇi yathoktāni tathā sāṃtapanāni ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She performed the expiations named Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, Parāka and Sāntapana as laid down in the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.135.10 \|\|

*vrataṃ yadvidyate kiṃcinniyamaḥ saṃyamastathā \|*  
*anyaccāpi śubhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tatsarvaṃ ca tayā kṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Whatever Vrata there was, she observed it. So also Niyama, Saṃyama (control) and all other meritorious rites.

## \|\| 1.135.11 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyā vratasthāyā jarā samyagupasthitā \|*  
*tathāpi tejaso vṛddhirvavṛdhe tapasā kṛtā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Even as she observed all these Vratas, old age overtook her. Still there was augmentation of refulgence caused by her penance.

## \|\| 1.135.12 \|\|

*sā ca nityaṃ mahendrasya sabhāṃ yātyatikautukāt \|*  
*devarṣīṇāṃ mataṃ śrotuṃ devatānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Due to excessive curiosity, she always used to attend the court of Mahendra in order to listen to the opinions of the celestial sages and Devas in particular.

## \|\| 1.135.13 \|\|

*yadā sā svāsanaṃ tyaktvā prayāti svagṛhonmukhī \|*  
*tadaivābhyukṣaṇaṃ cakrustatra śakrasya kiṃkarāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Whenever she vacated her seat and went homewards, Śakra’s servants used to sprinkle it with water.

## \|\| 1.135.14 \|\|

*tathānyadivase dṛṣṭaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tayā hi tat \|*  
*abhyukṣaṇaṃ svakīye ca āsane dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on a certain day she herself saw the seat being sprinkled upon.

## \|\| 1.135.15 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītāṃgī dīrghikā sā kumārikā \|*  
*triśākhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ prāha puraṃdaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereupon, the aged virgin Dīrghikā became furious. Knitting her eyebrows, she said to Indra:

## \|\| 1.135.16-17 \|\|

*kiṃ doṣaṃ vīkṣya me śakra prokṣitaṃ cāsanaṃ tvayā \|*  
*paradvā rakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ kiṃ mayaitatkṛtaṃ kvacit \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmānme pātakaṃ brūhi no cecchāpaṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*tvayi dāsyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ satye nātmānamālabhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. “What fault did you notice, O Śakrā? Why was the seat sprinkled with water? Is it a defect caused by another or is it mine? Hence tell me my sin. Otherwise, I will pronounce a terrible curse. There is no doubt about it. On this solemn truth, I vouch myself.”

## \|\| 1.135.18 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*na te dīrghe'stidoṣotra kaścidekaṃ vinā śubhe \|*  
*tenātha kriyate caitadāsanasyābhiṣecanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Indra said:

18\. O splendid lady Dīrghikā, except a single one you have no other fault. It is for this reason that the seat is sprinkled with water.

## \|\| 1.135.19 \|\|

*tvaṃ kumāryapi saṃprāptā ṛtukālaṃ vigarhitā \|*  
*tena doṣaṃ tvamāpannā nānyadastīha kāraṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Though you are a virgin, you do experience the despicable monthly menstrual cycle. Hence, you incur the defect. There is no other reason.

## \|\| 1.135.20 \|\|

*tasmādadyāpi tvāṃ kaścidudvāhayati tāpasaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ taṃ varaya bharttāraṃ yena gacchasi medhyatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Hence even now, if any sage is prepared to marry you take him on as your husband so that you will acquire purity.

## \|\| 1.135.21 \|\|

*tataśca lajjayā yuktā sā tadā dīrghakanyakā \|*  
*gatvā bhūmitale tūrṇaṃ vardhamāne purottame \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That aged virgin Dīrghikā became ashamed thereby and hurriedly went to the excellent city Vardhamāna on the earth.

## \|\| 1.135.22 \|\|

*tataḥ phūtkartumārabdhā catvareṣu trikeṣu ca \|*  
*ucchritya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ bhramamāṇā itastataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Wandering here and there, in places where four roads or three roads meet, with her right hand lifted up, she began to proclaim with a loud cry:

## \|\| 1.135.23 \|\|

*yadi kaściddvijo jātyā karoti mama sāṃpratam \|*  
*pāṇigrāhaṃ tapo'rddhasya śreyo yacchāmi tasya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “If anyone, Brāhmaṇa by birth, comes forward to grasp my hand in marriage, I shall give a moiety of the accumulated benefits of my penance.”

## \|\| 1.135.24 \|\|

*evaṃ tāṃ pravijalpantīṃ śrutvā lokā divāniśam \|*  
*unmattāmiti manvānā hāsyaṃ cakruḥ parasparam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing her blurting out thus day and night, the people thought her to be mad and cut jokes about her among themselves.

## \|\| 1.135.25 \|\|

*tataḥ katipayāhasya prakurvaṃtī ca dīrghikā \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhigṛhītena brāhmaṇena pariśrutā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus Dīrghikā carried on for many days when a Brāhmaṇa afflicted with leprosy heard her.

## \|\| 1.135.26 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca mandaṃ sa samāhūya suduḥkhitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He called the distressed woman and spoke to her slowly:

## \|\| 1.135.27 \|\|

*ahaṃ tvāmudvahāmyadya kṛtvā pāṇigrahaṃ tava \|*  
*yadi madvacanaṃ sarvaṃ sarvadaivānutiṣṭhasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “If you carry out all my behests I shall grasp your hand and marry you.”

## \|\| 1.135.28 \|\|

*kumārikovāca \|*  
*kariṣyāmi na saṃdehastava vākyaṃ dvijādhipa \|*  
*kuru pāṇigrahaṃ me'dya vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

The virgin said:

28\. I shall carry out your instructions, O leading Brāhmaṇa. There is no doubt about it. Grasp my hand duly in accordance with the scriptural injunctions.

## \|\| 1.135.29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatastasyāḥ kumāryāḥ sa pāṇiṃ jagrāha dakṣiṇam \|*  
*gṛhyoktena vidhānena devāgnigurusaṃnidhau \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

29\. Then he grasped the right hand of the virgin in the presence of Devas, fire and preceptor in accordance with the scriptural injunctions laid down in the Gṛhya Sūtras.

## \|\| 1.135.30 \|\|

*atha sā prāha bhūyo'pi vivāhakṛtamaṃgalā \|*  
*ādeśaṃ dehi me nātha yaṃ karomi tavādhunā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After the auspicious rite of marriage, she spoke again: “O my lord, command me, I shall carry it out now."

## \|\| 1.135.31 \|\|

*patiruvāca \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu snātumicchāmi sundari \|*  
*sāhāyyena tvadīyena yadi śaknoṣi tatkuru \|\| 31 \|\|*

The husband said:

31\. O beautiful lady, I wish to take the holy ablution in sixty-eight Tīrthas with your help. If you can, kindly do so.

## \|\| 1.135.32-33 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sā procya tatastūrṇaṃ pativratā \|*  
*tatpramāṇaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā ramyaṃ vaṃśakuṭīrakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*mṛdu tūlasamāyuktaṃ tataḥ prāha nijaṃ patim \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭā bhūtvā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. She said, “So it shall be”. Then the chaste lady made a beautiful small hut of bamboos befitting his size. She placed soft cotton pieces therein and then spoke to her husband with great delight, standing with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.135.34 \|\|

*etattava kṛte ramyaṃ kṛtaṃ vaṃśakuṭīrakam \|*  
*mama nāthāruhāśu tvaṃ yena kṛtvātha mūrdhani \|*  
*nayāmi sarvatīrtheṣu kṣetreṣu suśubheṣu ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “For your sake this beautiful hut of bamboos has been made ready, O my lord. Get into it quickly. I shall carry it on my head and take you to all splendid holy spots.”

## \|\| 1.135.35 \|\|

*tataḥ kuṣṭhī prahṛṣṭātmā śanairutthāya bhūtalāt \|*  
*tayā coddhṛtadehaḥ sansupto vaṃśakuṭīrake \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The leper was pleased in his heart. As she lifted him up, he slowly got up from the ground, went into the bamboo-structure and slept there.

## \|\| 1.135.36 \|\|

*tatastaṃ mastake kṛtvā sarvatīrthe yathāsukham \|*  
*sarvakṣetreṣu babhrāma snāpayantī nijaṃ patim \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She carried him comfortably on her head. She wandered over all the holy spots and made her husband bathe in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.135.37 \|\|

*yathā yathā sa cakre'tha snānaṃ tīrtheṣu kuṣṭhabhāk \|*  
*tathātathāsya gātreṣu tejo vṛddhiṃ pragacchati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. As the leper performed the holy ablution in the Tīrthas, the refulgence in his limbs went on increasing.

## \|\| 1.135.38 \|\|

*tataḥ krameṇa sā sādhvī bhramamāṇā mahītale \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃprāptā rajanī mukhe \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the course of her slow wandering over the earth, the chaste lady reached Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra at nightfall.

## \|\| 1.135.39 \|\|

*klāntā vaiklavyamāpannā bhārākrāntā pativratā \|*  
*nidrāndhā niśvasantī ca praskhalantī padepade \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Burdened with the weight the chaste lady became weak and tired. Overcome with blinding sleep and heaving deep sighs, she faltered at every step.

## \|\| 1.135.40 \|\|

*atha tatra pradeśe tu māṇḍavyo munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*śūlāropitagātrastu saṃtiṣṭhati suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It was at that spot that the leading sage Māṇḍavya was kept pinned down to the spike in a miserable state.

## \|\| 1.135.41 \|\|

*atha sā taṃ samāsādya śūlaṃ rātrau pativratā \|*  
*nijagātreṇa bhārārttā gacchamānā mahāsatī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The great chaste lady groaning under a heavy burden, was passing by the spike at night.

## \|\| 1.135.42 \|\|

*tayā saṃcālitaḥ so'tha māṃḍavyo munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*parāṃ pīḍāṃ samāsādya tataḥ prāha suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. She dashed against the leading sage shaking him slightly. Experiencing great pain, the miserable sage said:

## \|\| 1.135.43 \|\|

*kenedaṃ pāpmanā śalyaṃ mamāṃtaḥ paricālitam \|*  
*yenāhaṃ duḥkhayukto'pi bhūyo duḥkhāspadīkṛtaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “Who is that sinful one by whom the spike within me is shaken? Already miserable, I have been forced to bear greater pain!"

## \|\| 1.135.44 \|\|

*dīrghikovāca \|*  
*na mayā tvaṃ mahābhāga nidropahatayā dṛśā \|*  
*dṛṣṭastena parispṛṣṭo hyaspṛśyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Dīrghikā said:

44\. O highly esteemed one, my eyes have been blinded by overwhelming slumber. Hence you were not noticed. You are the most sinful one and so cannot be even touched. But you were touched.

## \|\| 1.135.45 \|\|

*na tvayā sadṛśaścānyaḥ pāpātmāsti dharātale \|*  
*śirasyudbhūtaśūlo'pi yo mṛtyuṃ nādhigacchati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. There is no other single soul on the earth like you. Though the stake has pierced through your head, you have not met death!

## \|\| 1.135.46 \|\|

*ahaṃ pativratā mūḍha vahāmi śirasā dhṛtam \|*  
*tīrthayātrākṛte kāṃtaṃ vikalāṃgaṃ suvallabham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I am a chaste lady, O deluded one, I bear my beloved husband on my head for the sake of pilgrimage as he is disabled.

## \|\| 1.135.47 \|\|

*kasmāttasyāstiraskāraṃ mama yacchasi niṣṭhuram \|*  
*ajñātāṃ mūḍhabuddhiḥ sanviśeṣānmānuṣodbhavām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In spite of all these, you despise me cruelly. Human beings are likely to err unwittingly. Still you were foolish to despise me.

## \|\| 1.135.48-49 \|\|

*māṇḍavya uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ yādṛktvayā proktastādṛgeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*pāpātmā mūḍhabuddhiśca aspṛśyaḥ sarvadehinām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yadi prātastavāyaṃ ca bharttā jīvati niṣṭhure \|*  
*yena me janitā pīḍā prāṇāṃtakaraṇī dṛḍhā \|\| 49 \|\|*

Māṇḍavya said:

48-49. O cruel lady, your husband caused me acute pain, very nearly killing me. If that husband of yours continues to live in the morning, then undoubtedly I am, what you say, a sinful soul, one of deluded intellect and unworthy of being touched by all embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.135.50 \|\|

*tasmādeṣa tavābhīṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ \|*  
*mayā śaptaḥ parityāgaṃ jīvitasya kariṣyati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Hence this lover of yours has been cursed by me. On being touched by the rays of the Sun, he will give up his life.

## \|\| 1.135.51 \|\|

*dīrghikovāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ maraṇaṃ patyuḥ prabhāte saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*madīyasya tataḥ prātarnodgamiṣyati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Dīrghikā said:

51\. If thus the death of my husband should take place in the morning, then the Sun will not rise at all.

## \|\| 1.135.52 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sātha niṣasāda dharātale \|*  
*bhūmau tadbhartṛsaṃyuktaṃ muktvā vaṃśakuṭīrakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After saying thus, she placed the bamboo structure along with her husband on the ground and sat there.

## \|\| 1.135.53 \|\|

*atha tāṃ prāha kuṣṭhī sa pipāsā saṃpravartate \|*  
*tasmāttoyaṃ samānehi pānārthamatiśītalam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then the leper said to her: “I am thirsty. Fetch me cool water to drink."

## \|\| 1.135.54-55 \|\|

*tathaiva sā samākarṇya bharturādeśamutsukā \|*  
*itastataśca babhrāma jalārthaṃ na prapaśyati \|*  
*na ca niryāti dūraṃ sā tyaktvāraṇye tathāvidham \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhartāraṃ śvāpadotthaṃ ca bhayaṃ hṛdi vitanvatī \|*  
*upaviśya tato bhūmau spṛṣṭvā pādau patestadā \|*  
*provāca dīrghikā vākyaṃ tāravākyena duḥkhitā \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. On hearing the command of her husband, she eagerly moved about for water, but could not see. Nor did she go very far because she did not want to leave her husband in that plight in the forest, because she was afraid of the beasts of prey. She, therefore, sat on the ground. Touching the feet of her husband the distressed Dīrghikā spoke these words in high pitch:

## \|\| 1.135.56 \|\|

*pativratā tvamācīrṇaṃ yadi samyaṅmayā sphuṭam \|*  
*tena satyena bhūpṛṣṭhānnirgacchatu jalaṃ śubham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “If I am perfect in my adherence to chastity and fidelity to my husband, let splendid water come out from the ground on the basis of this truth.”

## \|\| 1.135.57 \|\|

*evamuktvā jaghānātha pādāghātena medinīm \|*  
*kāntabhaktiṃ puraskṛtya tasya jīvitavāṃchayā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After saying thus she stamped her foot on the ground, remembering her devotion to her husband and desiring his life.

## \|\| 1.135.58 \|\|

*etasminnantare toyaṃ pādāghātādanantataram \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtaṃ nirmalaṃ svādu māṇḍavyasya ca paśyataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In the meantime, even as Māṇḍavya was watching, pure and tasty water sprang up after stamping the foot.

## \|\| 1.135.59 \|\|

*tatastaṃ snāpayāmāsa tasmiṃstoye śramāturam \|*  
*apāyayattataḥ paścātsvayaṃ snātvā papau jalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then she made her weary and sick husband bathe in the water. Thereafter, she made him drink the water. She herself had her bath and drank the water.

## \|\| 1.135.60 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare sūryaḥ pativratakṛtādbhayāt \|*  
*nābhyudeti samutpannastataḥ kālātyayo mahān \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the meantime, due to the fear of the chaste lady’s vow of fidelity, the Sun did not rise up. Much time elapsed then.

## \|\| 1.135.61 \|\|

*atha rātriṃ samālokya dīrghāṃ ye kāmukā janāḥ \|*  
*te sarve tuṣṭimāpannāstathā ca kula striyaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On noticing the prolongation of the night, all lascivious men and immoral unchaste women became delighted.

## \|\| 1.135.62 \|\|

*kauśikā rākṣasāścāpi corā jārāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*te sarve procuḥ saṃhṛṣṭāḥ samāliṃgya parasparam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The owls, Rākṣasas, thieves and paramours embraced one another joyously and said:

## \|\| 1.135.63 \|\|

*adyāsmākaṃ vidhistuṣṭo bhagavānmanmathastathā \|*  
*yena dīrghā kṛtā rātrirnāśaṃ nītaśca bhāskaraḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “Today the fate is pleased with us. So also Manmatha, for the night has been prolonged and the Sun is made to vanish.”

## \|\| 1.135.64 \|\|

*ye punarbrāhmaṇāḥ śāṃtā yajñakarmasamudyatāḥ \|*  
*te sarve duḥkhamāpannāḥ sūryodayavinākṛtāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. But in the case of Brāhmaṇas, quiescent and devoted to the rites of Yajñas, all of them became miserable due to the absence of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.135.65 \|\|

*na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre yājanaṃ na ca saddvijaḥ \|*  
*na śrāddhaṃ na ca saṃkalpaṃ na svādhyāyaṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. No excellent Brāhmaṇa performed Yajña himself or made others perform a Yajña. None of them performed Śrāddha rite, Saṅkalpa (ritualistic proclamation of intended rite) or Svādhyāya (self-study of the Vedas).

## \|\| 1.135.66 \|\|

*na snānaṃ na ca dānaṃ ca lokayātrāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vyavahāraṃ na kṛtyaṃ ca kiṃciddharmasamudbhavam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. None took the holy ablution, none made a gift; no one got engaged especially in worldly business or dealings with others. None carried out virtuous and sacred rites.

## \|\| 1.135.67 \|\|

*etasminnantare devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ dauḥsthyaṃ samāpannā yajñabhāgavivarjitāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. In the meantime, all the Devas with śakra at their head experienced great inconvenience and misery, because they were deprived of their shares of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.135.68-70 \|\|

*tato bhāskaramāsādya ūcurduḥkhasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*kasmānnodgamanaṃ deva prakaroṣi divākara \|\| 68 \|\|*

*etattvayā vinā sarvaṃ jagadvyākulatāṃ gatam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tasmāllokahitārthāya tvamudgaccha yathāpurā \|*  
*agniṣṭomādikā yajñā vartaṃte yena bhūtale \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. Then they approached Bhāskara and said in great sorrow: “O Divākara, why don't you rise, O Lord? without you all this universe has become agitated. Hence, for the benefit of all the worlds rise up as usual, so that Yajñas including Agniṣṭoma can be performed on the earth.”

## \|\| 1.135.71 \|\|

*sūrya uvāca \|\|*  
*pativratāsamādeśāttyaktaścābhyudayo mayā \|*  
*tasmādgatvā surāḥ sarve tāṃ vadaṃtu kṛte mama \|\| 71 \|\|*

Sūrya (Sun) said:

71\. ī have cancelled rising at the bidding of a chaste lady. Hence may all the Devas go to her and plead on my behalf.

## \|\| 1.135.72 \|\|

*yena tadvākyamāsādya pravarttāmi yathāsukham \|*  
*anyathā māṃ śapetkruddhā nūnaṃ sā hi pativratā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Then at her behest I can resume my activity comfortably. Otherwise, the infuriated lady may curse me. Indeed she is a chaste lady loyal to her husband.

## \|\| 1.135.73 \|\|

*evaṃ sā tapasā yuktā protkṛṣṭaṃ hi surottamāḥ \|*  
*pativratātvamādhatte tathānyadaparaṃ mahat \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O excellent Suras, endowed with the power of penance, she possesses the great and extraordinary power of chastity.

## \|\| 1.135.74 \|\|

*kastasyā vacanaṃ śaktaḥ kartumevamato'nyathā \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādbhīto nodgacchāmi kathaṃcana \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. So who is powerful enough to transgress her behest. I am afraid to rise up at all.

## \|\| 1.135.75 \|\|

*na tatkratusahasreṇa yajaṃtaḥ prāpnuyuḥ phalam \|*  
*pativratātvamāpannā yatstrī viṃdati kevalam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those who worship by means of a thousand Kratus cannot even aspire to attain that merit which naturally accrues to a lady equipped with the power of chastity.

## \|\| 1.135.76 \|\|

*tataste vibudhāḥ sarve gatvā tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*procustāṃ dīrghikāṃ vākyairmṛdubhiḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Then all those Devas went to that excellent holy spot, stood before the chaste lady Dīrghikā and spoke these soft words:

## \|\| 1.135.77-78 \|\|

*tvayā pativrate sūryo yanniṣiddho na tatkṛtam \|*  
*śubhaṃ yato hatāḥ sarvā bhūtale śobhanāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tasmādudgacchatu prājñe tvadvākyāttīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*yajñakriyā viśeṣeṇa yena vartaṃti bhūtale \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. “O chaste lady, in forbidding the Sun to rise, you have not done anything auspicious, since all the splendid holy rites are doomed. Hence, O sensible lady, let the Fierce-rayed One rise at your behest whereby the rites of Yajñas can earnestly be carried out on the earth.”

## \|\| 1.135.79 \|\|

*pativratovāca \|*  
*ayaṃ ca me patiḥ sadyaḥ prāṇebhyo'pi ca yaḥ priyaḥ \|*  
*so'bhyeti nidhanaṃ devāḥ prodgate ravimaṃḍale \|\| 79 \|\|*

The chaste lady Dīrghikā said:

79\. If the solar disc comes up, immediately my husband who is dearer to me than my own life, will meet his death, O Devas.

## \|\| 1.135.80 \|\|

*śaptaścānena duṣṭena māṃḍavyena supāpmanā \|*  
*kāryaṃ vināpi nirdiṣṭastadbrūyāṃ bhāskaraṃ katham \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. He (my husband) has been cursed by this wicked and sinful Māṇḍavya. He (my husband) has been unnecessarily pointed out for this dire end (death). So how can I tell Bhāskara (to rise)?

## \|\| 1.135.81 \|\|

*udayārthaṃ na me yajñaiḥ kāryaṃ kiṃcinna cāparaiḥ \|*  
*śrāddhadānādikaiḥ kṛtyaiḥ saṃjātairdaryitaṃ vinā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. How can I urge Bhāskara to rise. Without my husband, I have nothing to do with Yajñas or other rites such as Śrāddha, Dāna etc.

## \|\| 1.135.82 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataste vibudhāḥ sarve samālokya parasparam \|*  
*cirakālaṃ suduḥkhārtāstāmūcurvinayānvitāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

Sūta said:

82\. Thereupon all the Devas looked at one another for a long time with great sorrow. Then they said to her humbly:

## \|\| 1.135.83 \|\|

*udgacchatu ravirbhadre tavāyaṃ dayitaḥ patiḥ \|*  
*prayātu nidhanaṃ sadyo bhūyādeṣa munīśvaraḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. “O fair lady, may Ravi (Sun) come up. Let your beloved husband meet his death. This leading sage shall be revived again.

## \|\| 1.135.84 \|\|

*punarjīvāpayiṣyāmo vayamenamapi drutam \|*  
*mṛtyumārgamanuprāptaṃ tvatkṛte pativatsale \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Even if he meets death, we shall resuscitate him for your sake, O lady endearing to your husband.

## \|\| 1.135.85 \|\|

*pañcaviṃśativarṣīyaṃ kāmadevamivāparam \|*  
*tvaṃ drakṣyasi sudīptāṃgaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. You will see him as a young man of twenty-five years, another veritable Kāmadeva. His limbs will be shining. He will be marked with all good features.

## \|\| 1.135.86 \|\|

*bhūtvā paṃcadaśābdīyā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*martyaloke sukhaṃ samyaktvecchayā sādhayiṣyasi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. You will become a lady with large eyes resembling the petals of a lotus. You will be one aged fifteen years. You will enjoy all worldly pleasures as you please.

## \|\| 1.135.87 \|\|

*eṣo'pi muniśārdūlo vipāpmā sāṃprataṃ śubhe \|*  
*śūlavedhena nirmuktaḥ sukhabhāgī bhavatklama \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. O splendid lady, let this tiger among sages be freed from his sins. Let him be released from the torture at the stake. Let him be reasonably happy.”

## \|\| 1.135.88 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva ca prokte tayā sa dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*udgato bhagavānsūryastatkṣaṇādeva vegataḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

Sūta said:

88\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas as soon as she said, “So be it", Lord Sun rose up speedily at the moment.

## \|\| 1.135.89 \|\|

*tataḥ sūryāṃśusaṃspṛṣṭaḥ sa mṛtaśca sukuṣṭhabhāk \|*  
*vibudhānāṃ karaiḥ spṛṣṭaḥ punareva samutthitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Touched by the rays of the Sun, the leper died. Touched by the hands of the Devas, he rose up alive.

## \|\| 1.135.90 \|\|

*paṃcaviṃśativarṣīyaḥ kāmadeva ivāparaḥ \|*  
*saṃsmaranpūrvikāṃ jātiṃ sarvā harṣa samanvitaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He was a young man of twenty-five years. He stood like another Kāmadeva. He joyously remembered the previous birth entirely.

## \|\| 1.135.91 \|\|

*dīrghikāpi parispṛṣṭā svayaṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*saṃjātā yauvanopetā divyalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Touched by Lord Śaṃbhu himself, Dīrghikā became endowed with youth and divine features.

## \|\| 1.135.92 \|\|

*padmapatrekṣaṇā ramyā candrabimbasamānanā \|*  
*madhye kṣāmā sugaurāṃgī pīnonnatapayodharā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. She was beautiful with eyes resembling petals of a lotus. She was slender at the waist. Her limbs were fair-complexioned. Her breasts were thick and protruding.

## \|\| 1.135.93 \|\|

*tatastaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ śūlāgrādavatārya ca \|*  
*procuśca vibudhaśreṣṭhāḥ sādaraṃ harṣasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The excellent Devas got that tiger among sages down from the top of the stake and spoke to him with respect and great delight:

## \|\| 1.135.94-96 \|\|

*etatsatyaṃ kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mune tava yathoditam \|*  
*mṛto'pi brāhmaṇaḥ kuṣṭhī saṃspṛṣṭo raviraśmibhiḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*punarutthāpito'smābhiḥ kṛtaśca taruṇaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*anayā bhāryayā sārdhaṃ tasmāttvaṃ svāśramaṃ vraja \|\| 95 \|\|*

*nāsmākaṃ darśanaṃ vyarthaṃ kathaṃcidapi jāyate \|*  
*tasmātprārthaya yaccitte tava nityaṃ samāśritam \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. “O sage, the words uttered by you were made true. The leper, the Brāhmaṇa, died on being touched by the rays of the Sun. Of course, he was resuscitated by us and made a young man again along with his wife. So, go back to your hermitage. (The act of) seeing us cannot become fruitless at any cost. Hence, ask for whatever you have cherished in your heart always.”

## Chapter 136 - Origin of Dīrghikā

## \|\| 1.136.1 \|\|

*\| māṃḍavya uvāca \|*  
*grahīṣyāmi suraśreṣṭhā varaṃ yuṣmatsamudravam \|*  
*paraṃ me nirṇayaṃ caikaṃ dharmarājaḥ pracakṣatu \|\| 1 \|\|*

Māṇḍavya said:

1\. O excellent Suras, I shall surely accept the boon granted by you. But let Dharmarāja make a decisive statement in my case.

## \|\| 1.136.2 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ loke kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*upatiṣṭhati nānyatra satyametatsurottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O excellent Suras, this is also true that it is only the virtuous and non-virtuous acts that always follow all living beings and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.136.3 \|\|

*mayāpyatra pare cāpi kiṃ kṛtaṃ pātakaṃ ca yat \|*  
*īdṛśīṃ vedanāṃ prāpto na ca mṛtyuṃ kathacana \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (Then) what is that sin committed by me in this world or in the other, wherefore I am experiencing such a torture not leading to death at all.

## \|\| 1.136.4 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca \|*  
*anyadehe tvayā vipra bālabhāvena vartatā \|*  
*śūlāgreṇa sutīkṣṇena kāye viddho bakaḥ kṣitau \|\| 4 \|\|*

Dharmarāja said:

4\. In another body (birth), O Brāhmaṇa, while you were yet a boy, a crane was pierced by you with the tip of a spear on the ground.

## \|\| 1.136.5 \|\|

*nānyatkṛtamapi svalpaṃ pātakaṃ kiṃcideva hi \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādeṣā vyathā saṃsevitā dvija \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You did not commit any other sin even in the least. Hence, O Brāhmaṇa, this pain had to be experienced.

## \|\| 1.136.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ krodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tatastaṃ prāha māṃḍavyo dharmarājaṃ puraḥ sthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Stūa said:

6\. On hearing his words, Māṇḍavya was excessively angry. He spoke to Dharmarāja standing before him:

## \|\| 1.136.7-9 \|\|

*asya svalpāparādhasya yasmādbhūyānvinigrahaḥ \|*  
*kṛtastvayā sudurbuddhe tasmācchāpaṃ gṛhāṇa me \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tvaṃ prāpya mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ śūdrayonau vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*jātikṣayakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prabhūtaṃ sevayiṣyasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathā kṛtā mayaiṣādya vyavasthā sarvadehinām \|*  
*aṣṭamādvatsarādūrdhyaṃ karmaṇā garhitena ca \|*  
*pragrahīṣyati vai jaṃtuḥ puruṣo yoṣideva vā \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. “For this slight offence, O highly wicked one of defiled intellect, you have meted out a disproportionately severe punishments So take this curse from me.

You will be born as a human being in the womb of a Śūdra woman. Then you will have ample experience of sorrow due to the loss of your kinsmen.

Further, this declaration is being made by me now in regard to all the embodied beings. A man or a woman will be adversely affected by a despicable deed only if it is committed after the eighth year.”

## \|\| 1.136.10 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa māṃḍavyo dharmarājaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*prasthito roṣanirmukto vāṃchitāśāṃ prati dvijāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After saying thus to Dharmarāja, Māṇḍavya got rid of his anger, O Brāhmaṇas, and he went to the place of his choice.

## \|\| 1.136.11 \|\|

*atha taṃ prasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā procuḥ sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*dharmarājakṛte vyagrāḥ śrutvā śāpaṃ tathāvidham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing him preparing to leave the place, all the Heaven-dwellers who were worried about the fate of Dharmarāja after hearing such a curse, said to him:

## \|\| 1.136.12 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavanpāpasaktasya dharmarājasya kevalam \|*  
*na tvamarhasi śāpena śūdraṃ kartuṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 12 \|\|*

Devas said:

12\. O holy Sir, although Dharmarāja was guilty of a sinful deed, it does not behove you to make him a Śūdra by means of the curse.

## \|\| 1.136.13 \|\|

*prasādaṃ kuru tasmāttvamasya dharmapaterdvija \|*  
*asmākaṃ vacanātsadyaḥ prārthayasva tathā varam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇa, be pleased with this Dharmapati at our instance, and immediately request for a boon.

## \|\| 1.136.14 \|\|

*māṃḍavya uvāca \|*  
*nānyathā jāyate vāṇī yā mayoktā surottamāḥ \|*  
*avaśyaṃ dharmarājo'yaṃ śūdrayonau prayāsyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

Māṇḍavya said:

14\. O excellent Suras, my speech uttered once cannot be altered. Certainly this Dharmarāja will be born of a Śūdra womb.

## \|\| 1.136.15 \|\|

*paraṃ naivāsya saṃtānaṃ tasyāṃ yonau bhaviṣyati \|*  
*saṃprāpsyati ca bhūyo'pi dharmarājatvamuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. But in that birth he will not beget any child. He will regain the excellent status of Dharmarāja.

## \|\| 1.136.16 \|\|

*ārādhayatu cāvyagraḥ kṣetre'traiva trilocanam \|*  
*prasādāttasya devasya śīghraṃ mṛtyumavāpsyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Unperturbed, let him propitiate the Three-eyed One in this holy spot itself here. With the favour of that Lord, he will meet with an early death.

## \|\| 1.136.17 \|\|

*tathā deyo varo mahyaṃ bhavadbhiryadi svargapāḥ \|*  
*tadeṣā śūlikā'smākaṃ sparśādbhūyātsudharmadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Further, O rulers of heaven, if a boon has to be granted by you all to me, then let this spear (the stake) of course be one that accords excellent merit merely on being touched.

## \|\| 1.136.18 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*enāṃ yaḥ prātarutthāya sparśayiṣyati śūlikām \|*  
*pātakātsa vimukto vā iha loke bhaviṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

Devas said:

18\. One who gets up early in the morning and touches this Śūla (stake) shall become rid of sins in this world.

## \|\| 1.136.19 \|\|

*evamuktvā muniṃ taṃ te devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*tatastāṃ sādaraṃ prāhuḥ saha bhartrā pativratām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After speaking thus to the sage, those Devas with Śakra as their leader told the chaste lady and her husband:

## \|\| 1.136.20 \|\|

*tvamapi prārthayābhīṣṭamasmatto varavarṇini \|*  
*yatte citte sthitaṃ nityaṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate'tra naḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “O fair-complexioned lady, you too do request for anything desired from us. You may ask for whatever is in your mind. In your case, there is nothing that cannot be given by us.”

## \|\| 1.136.21 \|\|

*pativratovāca \|*  
*yeyaṃ mayākṛtā gartā sthāne'tra tridaśeśvarāḥ \|*  
*mannāmnā khyātimāyātu dīrghiketi jagattraye \|\| 21 \|\|*

The Pativratā said:

21\. O Lord of Devas, let the holy pit made in this holy spot by me be well-known in all the three worlds as Dīrghikā after my name.

## \|\| 1.136.22 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti loke'tra gartteyaṃ tava śobhane \|*  
*dīrghiketi suvikhyātā bhaviṣyati jagattraye \|\| 22 \|\|*

Devas said:

22\. O splendid lady, from now onwards this holy pit shall become well known in all the three worlds as Dīrghikā.

## \|\| 1.136.23 \|\|

*ye'syāṃ snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti prātarutthāya mānavāḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktāste bhaviṣyaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those men who get up early in the morning and take their holy bath in this will be rid of all their sins at the very instant.

## \|\| 1.136.24-25 \|\|

*kanyārāśigate sūrye saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti śraddhayā sahitā narāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aputrāste bhaviṣyaṃti saputrā vaṃśavardhanāḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā'tha tāṃ devā jagmuḥ svargaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. On the fifth lunar day, when the Sun is in the Zodiac Virgo, men with great faith shall take their holy bath here. If they have no sons they will beget sons and augment their family.

After saying thus to her, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, those Devas went to heaven.

## \|\| 1.136.26 \|\|

*pativratāpi tenaiva saha kāṃtena sundarī \|*  
*sevayāmāsa kalyāṇī smarasaukhyamanuttamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The beautiful chaste lady enjoyed the pleasure of love along with her lover (husband).

## \|\| 1.136.27 \|\|

*parvateṣu suramyeṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca \|*  
*udyāneṣu vicitreṣu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They roamed about in beautiful mountains, banks of rivers, wonderful parks, forests and gardens.

## \|\| 1.136.28 \|\|

*tato vayasi saṃprāpte paścime kālaparyayāt \|*  
*tadevātmīyasattīrthaṃ sevayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After the efflux of time in their later advancing age, they eagerly resorted to their own excellent Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.136.29 \|\|

*tato dehaṃ parityaktvā svakāṃtaṃ vīkṣya taṃ mṛtam \|*  
*tatra toye jagāmātha brahmalokaṃ pativratā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing her husband dead, the chaste lady cast off her body in the waters thereof and went to the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.136.30 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ dīrghikākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*yasya saṃśravaṇādeva naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus the excellent story of Dīrghikā has been narrated to you all. By listening to this alone, a man becomes rid of sins.

## Chapter 137 - Māṇḍavya Impaled

## \|\| 1.137.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kenāsau muniśārdūlo māṃḍavyaḥ sumahātapāḥ \|*  
*śūlāyāṃ sthāpitaḥ kena kāraṇena ca no vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa māṃḍavyo muniḥ pūrvaṃ tīrthayātrāṃ samācaran \|*  
*asminkṣetre samāyātaḥ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viśvāmitrīyamāsādya sattīrthaṃ pāvanaṃ mahat \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ cakre bhāskaraṃ prati sa vratī \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. By whom was this tiger among sages, Māṇḍavya of excellent penance, placed on the stake? For what reason? Do tell us.

## \|\| 1.137.4-6 \|\|

*japanvibhrāḍiti śreṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ bhāskaravallabham \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare cauro loptramādāya kasyacit \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kopi tatra samāyātaḥ pṛṣṭhe lagnairjanairdvijāḥ \|*  
*tataścauro'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā maunasthaṃ munisattamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*loptraṃ muktvā tadagre'tha praviveśa guhāṃtare \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāptāste janā loptrahetave \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

That sage Māṇḍavya was performing his pilgrimage with great faith. He came to this holy spot. That sage of great vows came to the great and excellent Tīrtha of Viśvāmitra and offered libation to the ancestors and also to the Sun.

4-6. He repeated the excellent Sūkta beginning with “vibhrāṭ”, a great favourite of Bhāskara. In the meantime a thief who carried the stolen booty of some person came there, O Brāhmaṇas, along with the people closely pursuing him. On seeing the excellent sage in the vow of silence, the thief dropped down the booty in front of him and entered a cave. In the meantime, those persons reached that place for taking away the booty.

## \|\| 1.137.7-8 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā loptraṃ tadagrasthaṃ tamūcurmunipuṃgavam \|*  
*mārgeṇānena cāyāto loptrahasto malimlucaḥ \|*  
*brūhi śīghraṃ mahābhāga kena mārgeṇa nirgataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sa ca jānannapi prājño guhāsaṃsthaṃ malimlucam \|*  
*na kiṃcidapi covāca maunavrata parāyaṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The sage was strictly adhering to the vow of silence. The wise sage knew that the thief was in the cave. Yet he did not say anything. Seeing the booty in front of him, they said to the leading sage: “A thief with the booty in his hand has come this way. O esteemed one, say quickly which way did he go out.”

## \|\| 1.137.9-10 \|\|

*asakṛtprocyamāno'pi paraciṃtāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*yadā provāca no kiṃcitsa rakṣaṃścaurajīvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatastairmaṃtritaṃ sarvaireṣa nūnaṃ malimlucaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaḥ pṛṣṭhato'smābhirmunirūpo babhūva ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He was repeatedly asked. But he was thinking about the Supreme Being (or consideration for others). He saved the life of the thief. Thereupon they whispered: “Indeed this man is the thief. Closely pursued by us, he has taken the guise of a sage.”

## \|\| 1.137.11 \|\|

*avicārya tataḥ sarvairābhīraistairdurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*śūlīmāropitaḥ sadyo nītvā kiṃcidvanāṃtaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Without thinking anything further, those tribal people of wicked intention took him to a dense forest and staked him on the spike.

## \|\| 1.137.12 \|\|

*evaṃ prāptā tadā śūlī muninā tena dāruṇā \|*  
*pūrvakarmavipākena doṣahīnena dhīmatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It was thus that the sage was staked on the spear, as a result of the terrible Karma of the previous birth, though he was wise and faultless.

## Chapter 138 - Origin of Dharmarājeśvara

## \|\| 1.138.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ dharmarājena tapodhyānādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*māṃḍavyaśāpanāśāya tadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. What penance, meditation etc. was performed by Dharmarāja in order to wipe out completely the curse of Māṇḍavya? Narrate it to us.

## \|\| 1.138.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*māṃḍavya śāpamāsādya dharmarājaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*tapastepe dvijaśreṣṭhāstasminkṣetre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. On getting the curse of Māṇḍavya, Dharmarāja was extremely miserable. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he settled in the same holy spot and performed a penance.

## \|\| 1.138.3 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ devadevasya saṃvidhāya kapardinaḥ \|*  
*avyagraṃ pūjayāmāsa puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He constructed a palace unto Kapardin (Śiva), the Lord of Devas, and worshipped him unperturbedly with flowers, incense and unguents.

## \|\| 1.138.4 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tuṣṭastasya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*provāca varado'smīti prārthayasva yadīpsitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After the lapse of a great deal of time Maheśvara was pleased with him. He said, “I am the bestower of boons. Request for whatever is desired.”

## \|\| 1.138.5 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ deva purā śapto māṃḍavyena mahātmanā \|*  
*svadharme vartamāno'pi sarvadoṣavivarjitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Dharmarāja said:

5\. O Lord, earlier I was cursed by the noble-souled Māṇḍavya although I was faultless and strictly adhering to my duty.

## \|\| 1.138.6-7 \|\|

*kupitena ca tenoktaṃ śūdrayonau bhaviṣyasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tatrāpi ca mahadduḥkhaṃ jñātināśasamudravam \|*  
*macchāpajanitaṃ sadyo jātijaṃ samavāpsyasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He had told me angrily, “You will be born of the womb of a Śūdra woman. There too you will experience great sorrow due to the death of kinsmen. As a result of my curse, you will soon attain the adverse effects due to your caste.”

## \|\| 1.138.8 \|\|

*tasmāttrāhi suraśreṣṭha tasyā yoneḥ sakāśataḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ caitadvidho bhūtvā tasyāṃ janma karomyaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Hence, O excellent one among Suras, save me from that (Śūdra) womb. How can I be born of that womb after being like this all along?

## \|\| 1.138.9 \|\|

*tatrāpi ca mahaduḥkhaṃ jñātināśasamudbhavam \|*  
*etadarthe suraśreṣṭha mayā cārādhito bhavān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There too, the great misery of the death of kinsmen is to be borne. It was for this purpose that you have been propitiated by me.

## \|\| 1.138.10 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*na tasya sanmunervākyaṃ śakyate kartumanyathā \|*  
*tasmācchūdro'pi bhūtvā tvaṃ na saṃtānamavāpsyasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

10\. The utterance of that sage cannot be altered or invalidated. Yet, although you will be born a Śūdra, you will not beget a son.

## \|\| 1.138.11 \|\|

*jñātikṣayaṃ pradṛṣṭvāpi naiva duḥkhamavāpsyasi \|*  
*yato niṣidhyamānāpi na kariṣyaṃti te vacaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Although you will witness complete destruction of kinsmen, you will not become miserable. Although you may forbid them, they will not pay heed to your words.

## \|\| 1.138.12 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāccitte na te duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*jñātijaṃ dharmarājaitatsatyameva mayoditam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For this reason, O Dharmarāja, you will not suffer the sorrow arising from the kinsmen. The truth alone has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.138.13 \|\|

*sthitvā varṣaśataṃ prājña tvaṃ śūdro dharmavatsalaḥ \|*  
*upadeśānbahūndattvā jñātibhyo hitakāmyayā \|*  
*api śraddhā vihīneṣu pāpātmasu sadaiva hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O wise one, you will live for a hundred years as a pious Śūdra. With a desire for the benefit of the kinsmen, you will offer them many instructions, although they may not have credence therein and they may be always sinful.

## \|\| 1.138.14 \|\|

*tato varṣaśate pūrṇe brahmadvāreṇa kevalam \|*  
*ātmānaṃ samyagutsṛjya mokṣameva prayāsyasi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When hundred years are completed, you will take out your soul through Brahmadvāra (cerebral aperture) and attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.138.15 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāngataścādarśanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*dharmarājo'pi taṃ śāpaṃ bheje māṃḍavyasaṃbhavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After speaking thus, the Lord vanished. Dharmarāja had to bear the effect of the curse of Māṇḍavya.

## \|\| 1.138.16 \|\|

*tadā vidurarūpeṇa hyavatīrya dharātale \|*  
*māṃḍavyasya vacaḥ satyaṃ sa cakāra mahāmatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He took incarnation on the earth in the form of Vidura. The highly intelligent one made the statement of Māṇḍavya true.

## \|\| 1.138.17 \|\|

*jāto bhagavatā sākṣādvyāsenāmitatejasā \|*  
*pārāśaryeṇa vipreṇa dāsīgarbhasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He was born of Vyāsa, the holy sage of unmeasurable refulgence, the son of Parāśara. He was born from the womb of a woman-slave.

## \|\| 1.138.18 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ dharmarājasamudbhavam \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ yadahaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus everything connected with the story of Dharmarāja has been told to you all as I was requested for. This story is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 139 - Greatness of Dharmarājeśvara (Dharmarāja-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.139.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dharmarājeśvarotthaṃ ca māhātmyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*yanmayā praśrutaṃ puṇyaṃ sakāśātsvapituḥ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|*  
*trailokye'pi suvikhyātaṃ sarva pātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 138-140 tell that Māṇḍavya cursed Yamadharma to be a sonless Śūdra for the disproportionate punishment given by him. Yamadharma became Vidura, Dharmarājeśvara blessed him with a son (Yudhiṣṭhira) from Pāṇḍu’s wife.

Sūta said:

1-2. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I shall narrate unto you all the greatness of Dharmarājeśvara that was heard by me earlier from my father. Listen to that meritorious narrative with great concentration. It is well known in all the three worlds. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.139.3 \|\|

*tatra kṣetre purā vipraḥ kaśyapānvayasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*upādhyāya iti khyāto vedavidyāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly, there was a Brāhmaṇa hailing from the family of Kaśyapa in that holy spot. He was well-known as Upādhyāya. He was devoted to the Vedic lore.

## \|\| 1.139.4 \|\|

*paścime vayasi prāpte tasya putro babhūva ha \|*  
*svādhyāyaniyamasthasya prabhūtavibhavasya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He begot a son later in his advancing age even as he strictly adhered to regular study of the Vedas. He acquired ample wealth.

## \|\| 1.139.5 \|\|

*pañcavarṣakamātrastu yadā jajñe ca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*tadā mṛtyuvaśaṃ prāptaḥ pitṛmātṛsuduḥkhakṛt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When only five years old that son expired causing great sorrow to his father and mother.

## \|\| 1.139.6 \|\|

*tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ kopaṃ cakre vaivasvatopari \|*  
*dharmarājagṛhaṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā nijakumārakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On knowing that his son had gone to the abode of Dharmarāja, the Brāhmaṇa became angry with Vaivasvata (Dharmarāja).

## \|\| 1.139.7 \|\|

*ādāya salilaṃ haste śucirbhūtvāsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*pradadau dāruṇaṃ śāpaṃ dharmarājāya duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In his height of grief, he took some water in his hand. With mental concentration and personal cleanliness, he then pronounced a terrible curse on Dharmarāja.

## \|\| 1.139.8-10 \|\|

*aputro'dya kṛto yasmādahaṃ tena durātmanā \|*  
*ataḥ so'pi ca duṣṭātmā yamo'putro bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathāsya bhūtale loko naiva pūjāṃ vidhāsyati \|*  
*kīrtayiṣyati no nāma yathānyeṣāṃ divaukasām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yaḥ kaścitprātarutthāya nāma cāsya grahī ṣyati \|*  
*maṃgalyakaraṇe cātha vighnaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. “Since I have been made a sonless person by that wicked-souled one, Yama, of defiled soul, he will also become sonless.

Further people in this world will not perform worship to him nor glorify his name as in the case of other heaven-dwellers.

If anyone gets up early in the morning and recalls his name, there shall be obstacle in his auspicious activity.”

## \|\| 1.139.11 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā tasya viprasya yamaḥ śāpaṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*svadharme vartamānastu tato duḥkhā nvito'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing the highly terrible curse of the Brāhmaṇa, though he had been abiding by his duties, Yama became grief-stricken.

## \|\| 1.139.12 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare gatvā brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ prati \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā yamaḥ prāha pitāmaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the meantime Yama went to the abode of Brahmā. With palms joined in reverence, Yama said to Pitāmaha:

## \|\| 1.139.13-15 \|\|

*paśya deveśa śapto'haṃ nirdoṣopi dvijanmanā \|*  
*svadharme vartamānastu yathānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmādahaṃ tyajiṣyāmi niyogaṃ te pitāmaha \|*  
*brahmaśāpabhayā dbhītaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*purā māṃḍavyaśāpena śūdrayonyavatāritaḥ \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ putrarahitaḥ kṛto'pūjyaśca sattama \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. “See, O Lord of Devas, although I am faultless and I have been abiding by my duty, I have been cursed by the twice-born one as though I am like any other vulgar person.

I have been frightened by the curse of the Brāhmaṇa, O Pitāmaha. I shall give up your assignment. I have told you the truth.

Formerly, O excellent one, I was made to be born in a Śūdra womb by the curse of Māṇḍavya. Now I have been rendered devoid of adoration and of any son!”

## \|\| 1.139.16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dīnaṃ vaivasvatasya ca \|*  
*tatkālocitamāhedaṃ svayameva śatakratuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sūta said:

16\. On hearing these pitiable words of Vaivasvata, Śatakratu himself said these words befitting that occasion:

## \|\| 1.139.17-20 \|\|

*yuktamuktamanenaitaddharmarājena padmaja \|*  
*niyoge vartamānena tāvakīye sureśvara \|\| 17 \|\|*

*avaśyameva martye ca manuṣyāḥ samaye sthitāḥ \|*  
*bālye vā yauvane vātha vārdhakye vā pitāmaha \|*  
*saṃhartavyā na saṃdeho nākāle ca kathaṃcana \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etadeva kṛtaṃ nāma dharmarājākhyamuttamam \|*  
*tvayā ca samamitrasya samaśastrormahātmanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmādadya samālokya kaścideva viciṃtyatām \|*  
*upāyo yena nirdoṣo niyogaṃ kurute tava \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. “O Lotus-born One, O Lord of Suras, quite reasonable word (appeal) has been uttered by this Dharmarāja who is working as per your command.

O Pitāmaha, there is no doubt about this that in the mortal world, men as per rule should be withdrawn in childhood, youth or old age, but never prematurely (when not due).

This excellent name Dharmarāja has been given by you to that noble-souled one who sees friends and foes alike.

Therefore, after due consideration let some means be resorted to whereby a person who carries out your order should be immune from fault or sin.”

## \|\| 1.139.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*brahmaśāpaṃ na śakto'ha manyathākartumevaca \|*  
*upāyaṃ ca kariṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tridaśādhipa \|\| 21 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

21\. O Lord of Devas, I cannot alter the curse of a Brāhmaṇa. I shall employ some other remedy.

## \|\| 1.139.22 \|\|

*tato dhyānaṃ pracakre sa brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tadarthaṃ sarvadevānāṃ purataḥ susa māhitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then, for that purpose, in front of all the Devas, Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds, began to meditate.

## \|\| 1.139.23 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ dhyānasaktasya prādurbhūtāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*mūrtā rogāḥ suraudrāste vātagulmakaphātmakāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataprāyāḥ procustaṃ ca kṛtādarāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even as he was engaged in meditation the personified forms of one hundred eight ailments with Vāta (Wind), Pitta (Bile) and Kapha (phlegm) as their causes appeared before him and respectfully said to him:

## \|\| 1.139.24 \|\|

*rogā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ devadeveśa tvayā sṛṣṭā vayaṃ vibho \|*  
*ādeśo dīyatāṃ śīghraṃ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 24 \|\|*

The Ailments said:

24\. O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, why have we been created? Let the order be given quickly. May this favour be done.

## \|\| 1.139.25 \|\|

*vrahmovāca \|*  
*vrajadhvaṃ bhūtale śīghraṃ mamādeśādasaṃśayam \|*  
*yamādeśānmanuṣyeṣu gantavyamavikalpitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

25\. At my behest, go quickly to the earth. At the behest of Yama, You must move about unhesitatingly among human beings.

## \|\| 1.139.26 \|\|

*evamukttvā tu tānrogāṃstataḥ prāha pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*dharmarājaṃ samīpasthaṃ bhṛśaṃ dīnamadhomukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After saying thus to those Ailments, Pitāmaha spoke to Dharmarāja who was standing nearby with downcast face in his great distress:

## \|\| 1.139.27-30 \|\|

*ete te vyādhayaḥ sarve mayā yama niyojitāḥ \|*  
*sāhāyyaṃ ca kariṣyaṃti sarvakṛ tyeṣu sarvadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yaḥ kaścidadhunā martyo gatāyuḥ saṃprapadyate \|*  
*vadhāya tasya yatnena tvayā preṣyāḥ sadaiva tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ jāyate tena jananāśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*apavādo dharāpṛṣṭhe na ca saṃjāyate tava \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tasmādgatvā nijaṃ sthānaṃ svādhikāraparo bhava \|*  
*mamādeśādasaṃdigdhaṃ naivaṃ doṣamavāpsyasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. “O Yama, all these Ailments have been employed by me. They will always render help to you in all matters. Now if anyone reaches the end of his life-span these should be sent always by you to take his life. Thereby, the ignominy arising from the death of people shall devolve upon these alone on the earth and not on you. Therefore, at my behest, go to your own abode and be engaged in your duty. Undoubtedly, you will never incur a fault (sin).”

## \|\| 1.139.31 \|\|

*tatastānsakalānvyādhīngṛhītvā ravinaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*yamalokaṃ samāsādya tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the Son of Ravi took all those Ailments to his world and spoke to them respectfully:

## \|\| 1.139.32-34 \|\|

*pṛṣṭvāpṛṣṭvā ca gaṃtavyaṃ citraguptaṃ dharātale \|*  
*gaṃtavyaṃ jananāśāya samaye samupasthite \|\| 32 \|\|*

*paramasti mayā tatra sthāpitaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajekṣetre sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yastaṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa yuṣmābhiḥ sadā tyājyo dūrato vacanānmama \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. “You shall regularly ask Citragupta and go to the earth for taking away the life of people when the proper time arrives.

But there is an excellent Liṅga installed by me there in Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra. It is destructive of all sins.

A man who gets up early in the morning and visits it with good devotion, shall always be avoided by you from afar, at my behest:”

## \|\| 1.139.35 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa tānvyādhīṃstato vaivasvataḥ svayam \|*  
*tasya viprasya taṃ putraṃ gṛhītvā satvaraṃ yayau \|*  
*tasyaiva maṃdire ramye kṛtvā rūpaṃ dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After saying thus to those Ailments, Vaivasvata assumed the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, took the (recently dead) son of the Brāhmaṇa and went to his beautiful abode.

## \|\| 1.139.36-37 \|\|

*athāsau brāhmaṇo dṛṣṭvā svaṃ putraṃ gṛhamāgatam \|*  
*sahitaṃ viprarūpeṇa dharmarājena dhīmatā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tataḥ prahṛṣṭacittena satvaraṃ sammukho yayau \|*  
*putraputreti jalpansa nijabhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. On seeing his own son coming to the house along with the wise Dharmarāja in the form of a Brāhmaṇa he went to them face-to face with a delighted heart accompanied by his wife, saying “My son! My son!”

## \|\| 1.139.38 \|\|

*pariṣvajya tato bhūyo vāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*āghrāya ca tato mūrdhni vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He embraced him repeatedly and sniffed at his head. With tears agitating his eyes he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.139.39 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ putra samāyātastvaṃ tasmā dyamamaṃdirāt \|*  
*na kaścitpunarāyāti yatra gatvā'pi vīryavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

39\. O my son, how have you come back from that abode of Yama, from where not even a powerful person can return after going?

## \|\| 1.139.40 \|\|

*kiṃ vā caitatsamutpannamindrajālaṃ mamāṃtikam \|*  
*kiṃ vā svapnamidaṃ kiṃ vā mamāyaṃ dṛṣṭivibhramaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Is this some sort of jugglery happening near me? Is this a dream? Is this a perversion of my vision?

## \|\| 1.139.41 \|\|

*kaścāyaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ pārśve tava saṃtiṣṭhate suta \|*  
*divyena tejasā yuktastaṃ namāmyahamātmaja \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Who is this Brāhmaṇa standing by your side, dear son. He is endowed with divine refulgence. O my son, bow down to him.

## \|\| 1.139.42 \|\|

*putra uvāca \|*  
*eṣa brāhmaṇarūpeṇa samāyāto yamaḥ svayam \|*  
*māmādāya kṛpāviṣṭo jñātvā tvāṃ duḥkhasaṃyutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

The son said:

42\. This is Yama himself who has come in the form of a Brāhmaṇa. Knowing that you are grief-stricken, he has become sympathetic and he has come for taking me with him.

## \|\| 1.139.43 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ kuru tātāsya śāpānugrahamadya vai \|*  
*gṛhaprāptasya susnehādyadyahaṃ tava vallabhaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hence, father, let him withdraw the curse of you consider me your darling. He has come to your house with great friendliness.

## \|\| 1.139.44 \|\|

*tatastasya praṇāmaṃ sa kṛtvā brāhmaṇasattamaḥ \|*  
*vrīḍayā'dhomukho bhūtvā tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then the excellent Brāhmaṇa bowed down to him and remained with face turned downwards due to shame. Then he spoke respectfully:

## \|\| 1.139.45 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam \|*  
*yatputrasya mama prāptirgatasya yamasādanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

45\. Today my life has become fruitful. My life has become excellent, since I have regained my son who had gone to the abode of Yama.

## \|\| 1.139.46 \|\|

*tvaṃ ca putrakṛte tāta santoṣaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tasmātputreṇa saṃyukto yathāyaṃ syāttathā kuru \|\| 46 \|\|*

The son said:

46\. O father, you have become extremely glad on account of your son. Hence see that he also has a son.

## \|\| 1.139.47 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*na me syādanṛtaṃ vākyaṃ kadā cidapi putraka \|*  
*api svaireṇa yatproktaṃ kiṃ punarduḥkhitena ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

47\. O my son, my utterance can never be untrue even if it is jokingly made. It is all the more so if uttered by a grief-stricken one.

## \|\| 1.139.48 \|\|

*tasmāttasya bhavetputro daivayonisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*na kathaṃcidapi prājña mama śāpavaśāddhruvam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, O wise one, he will not get a son from the divine womb due to my curse.

## \|\| 1.139.49 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati sutaścānyo mānuṣīyonisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ yaścainaṃ tārayiṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He will have another son born of the womb of a human female by means of Rājasūya and Aśvamedha. He will redeem him.

## \|\| 1.139.50 \|\|

*ko'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na saṃtāraṇakṣamaḥ \|*  
*pitṛpakṣaṃ śubhaṃ karma kṛtvā sarvottamaṃ bhuvi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Of what avail is a son born to one if he is not capable of redeeming the members of his father’s family by performing excellent rites on the earth?

## \|\| 1.139.51 \|\|

*tathā pūjākṛte yo'sya śāpo dattaśca vai purā \|*  
*tatrāpi śṛṇu me vākyaṃ tasya putraka jalpataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. As regards the curse uttered by me in regard to his worship earlier, O dear son, listen to what I say:

## \|\| 1.139.52 \|\|

*vedoktairvividhairmantrairyā pūjā cāsya saṃsthitā \|*  
*na bhaviṣyati sā loke kathaṃcidapi putraka \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. His worship with various kinds of Mantras mentioned in the Vedas will not find a place on the earth at all, dear son.

## \|\| 1.139.53 \|\|

*asya mānuṣasaṃbhūtairmantraiḥ pūjā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*viśiṣṭā sarvadevebhyaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. His worship shall be with Mantras composed by humans. It will be different from that of the other Devas. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.139.54 \|\|

*putra uvāca \|*  
*ahamenaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya drijaśreṣṭha mahītale \|*  
*samyagārādhayiṣyāmi kimanyairvibudhairmama \|\| 54 \|\|*

The son said:

54\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I shall install him on the earth and propitiate him perfectly. Of what avail are the other Devas to me?

## \|\| 1.139.55 \|\|

*tasmātsaṃkīrtayiṣyāmi maṃtrānmānuṣasaṃbhavān \|*  
*tathā pūjāvidhānaṃ ca tvatprasādena pūrvaja \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Hence, O my ancestor (father), I shall adopt human Mantras and procedure for worship, with your favour.

## \|\| 1.139.56 \|\|

*tataḥ sugaṃ naḥ pantheti tasya maṃtraṃ vidhāya saḥ \|*  
*samācaratprahṛṣṭātmā dharmarājasya śṛṇvataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then he composed the Mantra beginning with “sugaṃ naḥ panthāḥ” and performed the worship even as Dharmarāja was listening.

## \|\| 1.139.57 \|\|

*tacchrutvātha yamaḥ proccaiḥ suprasannena cetasā \|*  
*taṃ brāhmaṇa muvācedaṃ harṣagadgadayāgirā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On hearing it, Yama was pleased in his mind. He spoke loudly to the Brāhmaṇa in words choked with delight:

## \|\| 1.139.58 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃcidapi vipredra na me syāddarśanaṃ vṛthā \|*  
*anyeṣāmapi devānāṃ tasmātprārthaya vāṃchi tam \|\| 58 \|\|*

Yama said:

58\. O leading Brāhmaṇa, my vision (Darśana) can never be in vain like that of Devas. So request for what is desired.

## \|\| 1.139.59-60 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*tavārcāṃ mama putro'yaṃ sthāpayiṣyati yāmiha \|*  
*tāmanenaiva maṃtreṇa yaḥ kaścitpūjayeddvijaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*bhavetsaṃvatsaraṃ yāvatsaṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|*  
*mā tasya putraśoko hi iha loke kathañcana \|\| 60 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

59-60. If any Brāhmaṇa worships uttering this Mantra, the idol of yours which this son of mine has installed on the fifth lunar day, let him have the benefit for the period of a year. Let him not have the grief due to the loss of a son in this world on any account.

## \|\| 1.139.61 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya saṃprahṛṣṭamanā yamaḥ \|*  
*yamalokaṃ jagāmātha svādhikāraparo'bhavat \|\| 61 \|\|*

Sūta said:

61\. He promised “Let it be so.” Then Yama joyously went to his world and resumed his duty.

## \|\| 1.139.62 \|\|

*so'pi brāhmaṇadāyādaḥ kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*yamamārādhayāmāsa madhye saṃsthāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*pitrā coktena mantreṇa tenaiva vidhipūrvakam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. That son of the Brāhmaṇa erected an excellent palace. In the centre, he installed the idol with great devotion by means of the Mantra uttered by his father and duly propitiated Yama.

## \|\| 1.139.63 \|\|

*tataśca kramaśaḥ prāpya putrapautrānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kāladharmamanuprāptaściraṃ sthitvā mahītale \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He begot sons and grandsons in plenty. He lived on the earth for a long time and then passed away.

## \|\| 1.139.64 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ purāṇeyatpurā śrutam \|*  
*yaścaitatkīrtayedbhaktyā saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|*  
*nāpamṛtyurbhavettasya na ca śokaḥ sutodbhavaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus what was heard by me from the Purāṇa has been narrated to you. One who recites this on the fifth lunar day with devotion shall never die prematurely. He will never suffer grief due to the loss of a son.

## Chapter 140 - The Son of Dharmarāja

## \|\| 1.140.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ putro mānuṣavigrahaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati yamasyātra kaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ sa sūtaja \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya putraḥ samutpannaḥ pāṃḍoḥ kṣetre mahītale \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhira iti khyātaḥ sarvakṣatriyapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaja, it has been mentioned by you that Yama would beget a son in human form. Who was born so?

## \|\| 1.140.3 \|\|

*rājasūyo makho yena iṣṭaḥ sampūrṇadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvānbhūmipatīnvīryātsaṃvidhāya karapradān \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

A son was born to him in the wife of Pāṇḍu on the earth. He was well-known all over the world as Yudhiṣṭhira. He was a leader of all the Kṣatriyas.

3\. After rendering all the kings as the payers of tribute (to him) by means of his valour, he performed Rājasūya Makha with the full complement of monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.140.4 \|\|

*aśvamedhāḥ kṛtāḥ paṃca tathā sampūrṇadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*bhrāmayitvā hayaṃ bhūmau paścātprāpa sa sadgatim \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Further, he made a horse wander all over the earth and performed five Aśvamedhas with the full complement of monetary gifts. Afterwards he attained the highest goal.

## \|\| 1.140.5 \|\|

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyekopi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*yajeta vā'śvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Ṃany sons should be sought after so that at least one of them may go to Gayā. Or one should perform Aśvamedha Yajña or release a blue bull ritualistically.

## \|\| 1.140.6 \|\|

*yadanena vṛtaṃ mattaḥ putritvaṃ sumahātmanā \|*  
*hayamedhānmahāyajñānkartā syādasya vai sutaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This noble-souled one requested of me that he should be one having a son who will perform great Aśvamedha sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.140.7 \|\|

*manyeta kṛtakṛtyatvaṃ yena putreṇa dharmapaḥ \|*  
*anyaiḥ putraśataiḥ kiṃ vā vaṃśānuddhārakārakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thanks to that son, the Lord of Dharma can consider himself contented as having fulfilled his tasks. Of what avail are hundreds of other sons who never redeem the race?

## Chapter 141 - Greatness of Miṣṭānnadeśvara (Miṣṭānnada-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.141.1-3 \|\|

*sūtauvāca \|*  
*tathānyo'pi hi tatrāsti devo miṣṭānnadāyakaḥ \|*  
*yasya saṃdarśanādeva miṣṭānnaṃ labhate naraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āsītpūrvaṃ nṛpo nāmnā vasusena iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ānarttādhipatiḥ khyāto bṛhatkalpe dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*atyaiśvaryasamāyukto gajavājirathānvitaḥ \|*  
*jitāripakṣastejasvī dātā bhogī jiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Further, there is a deity that bestows sweet food. By visiting that deity, a man obtains sweet food.

Formerly, there was a king remembered as Vasusena. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in Bṛhatkalpa he was well known as the over-lord of Ānarta.

He possessed a large amount of wealth. He was equipped with elephants, horses and chariots. As highly refulgent one, he conquered all the hosts of his enemies. He was a liberal donor. He enjoyed pleasures and had full control over his sense-organs.

## \|\| 1.141.4-5 \|\|

*sa saṃkrāṃtau vyatīpāte grahaṇe ravi somayoḥ \|*  
*parvakāleṣu cānyeṣu vividheṣu subhaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prayacchati dvijātibhyo ratnāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*iṃdranīlamahānīlavidrumasphaṭikādi ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. During Saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta, eclipses of the Sun and the Moon and other auspicious occasions, with great devotion he used to make to Brāhmaṇas, gifts of various kinds of gems such as lapis lazuli, sapphire, coral, diamonds etc.

## \|\| 1.141.6 \|\|

*māṇikyamauktikānyeva vidrumāṇi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*hastyaśvarathayānāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He made gifts of rubies, pearls, very fine corals, horses, elephants, chariots and vehicles and garments of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.141.7 \|\|

*na kasyacitpradadyātsa sasyaṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*atīva sulabhaṃ matvā tathā toyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thinking it to be very cheap and easily accessible, he did not give anyone food-grains and vegetables and water.

## \|\| 1.141.8 \|\|

*tato rājyaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā dṛṣṭvā putrodbhavānsutān \|*  
*kāladharmamanuprāptaḥ kasmiṃścitkālaparyaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He ruled over the kingdom for a long time and saw sons born to his sons. After the lapse of some time he passed away.

## \|\| 1.141.9 \|\|

*tataśca maṃtribhistasya satyasena iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*abhiṣiktaḥ suto rājye vīryodāryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereupon, his son remembered as Satyasena who was endowed with heroism and nobility and generosity, was crowned in the kingdom by his ministers.

## \|\| 1.141.10 \|\|

*vasuseno'pi saṃprāpya svargaṃ dānaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*divyāṃbaradharo bhūtvā divyaratnairvibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By the power of his liberal-mindedness and readiness to give, Vasusena attained heaven. He was adorned with divine robes.

## \|\| 1.141.11 \|\|

*sevyamāno'psarobhiśca vimānavaramāśritaḥ \|*  
*babhrāma sarvalokeṣu svecchayā kṣutsamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was attended upon by Apsarās. He rode in excellent aerial chariots. He could move about in all the worlds as he pleased. But he was always hungry.

## \|\| 1.141.12 \|\|

*pipāsākulacittaśca mukhena pariśuṣyatā \|*  
*na kaṃciddadṛśe tatra bhuṃjānamaparaṃ divi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. His mouth was always dry. He was agitated with thirst. But he could not see anyone else in heaven taking food.

## \|\| 1.141.13 \|\|

*na ca pānasamāsaktaṃ na sasyaṃ salilaṃ na ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He could not see anyone eagerly drinking. In fact there was neither water nor any type of vegetation or foodgrain.

## \|\| 1.141.14 \|\|

*tato gatvā sahasrākṣamuvāca dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*kṣuttṛṣāvṛtadehastu lajjayā'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In this state of hunger and thirst, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he went to the Thousand-eyed One. He stood near him with the face turned downwards and said to him:

## \|\| 1.141.15-18 \|\|

*naivātra dṛśyate kaścitkṣuttṛṣāparipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*māṃ muktvā vibudhaśreṣṭha tatkimetadvadasvame \|\| 15 \|\|*

*eṣa me svargarūpeṇa narakaḥ samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*kimetairbhūṣaṇairvastrairvimānādibhireva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṣudhā saṃpīḍyamānasya svargametacchacīpate \|*  
*agnitulyaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ mama citte'pi vartate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yathā kṣunna prabādhate \|*  
*nocetkṣipa suraśreṣṭha raurave narake drutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. “O most excellent one among Devas, excepting me, no one is seen here afflicted with hunger and thirst. Why is this so? Do tell me.

This has come to me like veritable Naraka though it has the form of Svarga. Of what avail are these ornaments, robes, aerial chariots and other things?

To a person like me afflicted with hunger, O Consort of Śacī, this Svarga is projected before my mind like fire.

Hence do me this favour. See that hunger does not bother me. If not, O excellent one among Suras, cast me quickly into Raurava Naraka.”

## \|\| 1.141.19 \|\|

*iṃdrauvāca \|*  
*anarhosi mahīpāla narakasya tvameva hi \|*  
*tvayā dānāni dattāni saṃkhyāhīnāni sarvadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

Indra said:

19\. O king, you don’t deserve being thrown into Naraka. Numerous gifts have always been made by you.

## \|\| 1.141.20 \|\|

*paraṃ kiṃ tu kvacinnānnaṃ dattaṃ rājanna codakam \|*  
*na kiṃcidapi saṃciṃtya yataḥ sulabhameva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. But, O king, nothing like water or cooked food was given by you at any place thinking that this was easily accessible.

## \|\| 1.141.21 \|\|

*toyaṃ sānnaṃ sadā dadyādannaṃ caiva sadakṣiṇam \|*  
*ya icchecchāśvatīṃ tṛptimiha loke paratra ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. But, one who wishes for permanent contentment here in this world as well as in the other world, should make gift of water and food or of food with monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.141.22 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ hi kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ svarge caiva mahīpate \|*  
*bhūṣito bhūṣaṇaiḥ śreṣṭhairvimānavaramāśritaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hence, O king, you are afflicted with hunger in heaven, though you are adorned with ornaments and moving about in the excellent aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.141.23 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*asti kaścidupāyo'tra devau vā mānuṣo'pi vā \|*  
*kṣutpipāse'titīvre me vināśaṃ yena gacchataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

The king said:

23\. Is there any remedy here, divine or human, whereby my hunger and thirst can be quenched?

## \|\| 1.141.24-25 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*yadi kaścitsutastubhyaṃ viprebhyaḥ satataṃ jalam \|*  
*dadāti ca sadā sasyaṃ tatte tṛptiḥ prajāyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nānyathā pārthivaśreṣṭha ekasminnapi vāsare \|*  
*adattasya tava prāptiḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Indra said:

24-25. If any son of yours offers always water and vegetable dish to Brāhmaṇas, it shall be to your contentment, not otherwise, O excellent king. Even if it is not offered a single day, you will not be contented. The truth has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.141.26 \|\|

*so'pi bhūmipateḥ putrastava yacchati nodakam \|*  
*na ca sasyaṃ dvijātibhyastvanmārgamanusaṃcaran \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. That son of yours follows your path in not offering water to you and not gifting vegetable or food dish to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.141.27 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*brahmalokātsthitau yatra tau bhūmipasureśvarau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the meantime, Nārada, the excellent sage, came from the world of Brahmā to the place where the king and Indra were present.

## \|\| 1.141.28 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraḥ samutthāya tasmai tuṣṭisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*arghaṃ dattvā vidhānena sādaraṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then Śakra joyously got up, duly offered him Arghya and spoke thus respectfully:

## \|\| 1.141.29 \|\|

*kutaḥ prāpto'si vipreṃdra prasthitaḥ kva ca sāṃpratam \|*  
*kena kāryeṇa cedguhyaṃ na te'sti vada sāṃpratam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O great Brāhmaṇa, whence have you come here? Where do you intend to go now? What is your mission? If it is no secret, do tell us now”

## \|\| 1.141.30 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmalokādahaṃ prāptaḥ prasthitastu dharātale \|*  
*tīrthayātrākṛte śakra nānyadastīha kāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nārada said:

30\. O Śakra, I have come here from the world of Brahmā. I am proceeding towards the earth for pilgrimage. There is no other purpose.

## \|\| 1.141.31-34 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa nṛpo hṛṣṭastamuvāca munīśvaram \|*  
*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mahyaṃ dīnasya munipuṃgava \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tvayā bhūmitale vācyo mama putro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*ānarttādhipatiḥ khyātaḥ satyasena iti prabho \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tava tāto mayā dṛṣṭaḥ śakrasya sadanaṃ prati \|*  
*kṣutpipāsāparītāṃgo dīnātmā devamadhyagaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tasmātputro'si cenmahyaṃ tvaṃ satyaṃ parirakṣasi \|*  
*tanmannāmnā prayacchoccaiḥ sasyāni salilāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sūta said:

31-34. On hearing it that king became delighted. He spoke to the great sage: “O great sage, I am in a wretched plight. A favour may be done to me. O holy sage, my son is a king on the earth. He is the overlord of Ānarta and is well known as Satyasena. He should be told by you: ‘Your father was seen by me at the abode of Śakra. In the midst of the Devas, he remains a wretched one because he is oppressed by hunger and thirst. If you are my son, if you wish to safeguard Satya (Truth), make in my name loudly, gifts of waters and vegetable dishes.’”

## \|\| 1.141.35 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*anujñāpya sahasrākṣaṃ prasthito bhūtalaṃ prati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Having promised “It shall be so”, Nārada, the great sage, took permission of the Thousand-eyed One (Indra) and started towards the earth.

## \|\| 1.141.36 \|\|

*tataḥ krameṇa tīrthāni bhramamāṇaḥ sa saddvijaḥ \|*  
*ānarttaviṣayaṃ prāpya satyasenamupādravat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Wandering over the Tīrthas one by one, the excellent Brāhmaṇa came to the land of Ānarta and approached Satyasena.

## \|\| 1.141.37 \|\|

*atha saṃpūjitastena samyagbhūpatinā muniḥ \|*  
*pituḥ saṃdeśamācakhyau vijane tasya sādaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. That sage was properly honoured by the king. He conveyed the message from his father while there was no one around.

## \|\| 1.141.38 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śokasaṃtaptaḥ satyaseno mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*taṃ visṛjya muniśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing it, King Satyasena became distressed with grief. He made farewell to the excellent sage after honouring him duly.

## \|\| 1.141.39 \|\|

*tato janakamuddiśya miṣṭānnena subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ bhojayāmāsa nityaśaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then with his father in view, he duly fed a thousand leading Brāhmaṇas devoutly with dainty sweet food.

## \|\| 1.141.40 \|\|

*prapādānaṃ tathā cakre grīṣmakāle viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tyaktvānyāḥ sakalā yāśca kriyā dharmasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He made provision for watersheds (on the wayside) particularly during summer season. He suspended all other virtuous sacred rites.

## \|\| 1.141.41 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya mahīpasya vartamānasya ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭirabhūdraudrā sarvasasyakṣayāvahā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Brāhmaṇas, as the king proceeded thus, a terrific drought-situation befell the land causing destruction to all types of vegetation.

## \|\| 1.141.42 \|\|

*yāvaddvādaśavarṣāṇi na jalaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*mumoca dharaṇīpṛṣṭhe sarve lokāḥ kṣudhārditāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The Lord of Devas did not let down showers of water on the earth for twelve years. All the people were distressed due to hunger.

## \|\| 1.141.43 \|\|

*atrābhāvāttato bhūyo na sasyaṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samuddiśya pitaraṃ svaṃ yathā purā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Due to want of food, there was distress. Hence he did not give vegetable dishes to Brāhmaṇas with his father in view as before.

## \|\| 1.141.44 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kṣutparītāṃgaḥ pitā tasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*svapne provāca taṃ putramatīva malināṃbaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Therefore the father of the king became overcome with hunger. He appeared before him in dream clad in very dirty robes and spoke to the son:

## \|\| 1.141.45 \|\|

*tvayā putreṇa putrāhaṃ kṣutpipāsāsamākulaḥ \|*
