*svargastho'pi hi tiṣṭhāmi tasmādannaṃ prayaccha vai \|*  
*mannāmnā toyasaṃyuktaṃ yadi tvaṃ matsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O son, thanks that you are my son. I am distressed with hunger and thirst even though I stay in heaven. Hence make gifts of food along with water in my name. Do this if you are born of me.”

## \|\| 1.141.46 \|\|

*tataḥ śokasamāyuktaḥ sa nṛpaḥ svapnadarśanāt \|*  
*annābhāvātsamaṃ maṃtraṃ maṃtribhiḥ sa tadākarot \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In view of the dream the king became grief-stricken. On account of absence of food, he consulted his ministers. He spoke to them thus:

## \|\| 1.141.47 \|\|

*ahamārādhayiṣyāmi sasyārthe vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*rājye rakṣā vidhātavyā bhavadbhiḥ sādaraṃ sadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “I shall propitiate the Bull-bannered Lord (Śiva) for the sake of vegetation and crops of food-grain. All of you shall accord all round protection in the kingdom with devotion to duty.”

## \|\| 1.141.48 \|\|

*tato'traiva samāgatya sthāpayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*samyagārādhayāmāsa vrataiśca niyamaistathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then he came here itself, installed Maheśvara and perfectly propitiated him duly observing Vratas and restraints.

## \|\| 1.141.49 \|\|

*atha tasya gatastuṣṭiṃ varṣāṃte bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*abravīdvarado'smīti prārthayasva yathepsitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then, at the end of a year, Lord Śiva became pleased with him and said: “I am the bestower of boons. Request for whatever is desired.”

## \|\| 1.141.50 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*annārthaṃ devadeveśa mayāyaṃ vihito vidhiḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ yaccha me śīghramasaṃkhyaṃ vṛṣavāhana \|\| 50 \|\|*

The king said:

50\. O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, this procedure (of penance) has been undertaken by me for the sake of food. Hence, O Bull-vehicled One, give unto me plenty of it quickly.

## \|\| 1.141.51 \|\|

*tathā saṃjāyatā vṛṣṭiḥ samaste dharaṇītale \|*  
*yena sasyāni jāyaṃte salilāni ca sāṃpratam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Let there be rainfall all over the earth so that plants can grow with plenty of water now.

## \|\| 1.141.52 \|\|

*jāyatāṃ mama tātasya svargasthasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*prasādāttava saṃtṛptirakṣayā surasattama \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O most excellent one among Suras, thanks to your favour, let my noble-souled father in heaven have everlasting contentment.

## \|\| 1.141.53 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*bhavitā na cirādvṛṣṭiḥ prabhūtā dharaṇītale \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti tathānnāni yāni kāni mahītale \|\| 53 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

53\. Ere long there shall be plenty of rainfall all over the earth. Different kinds of food-crops will grow on the earth.

## \|\| 1.141.54 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha rājeṃdra svagṛhaṃ prati sāṃpratam \|*  
*mama vākyādasaṃdigdhametadeva bhaviṣyati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. At my bidding this shall undoubtedly take place. Therefore, O leading king, do go back to your abode now.

## \|\| 1.141.55-56 \|\|

*taccaitanmāmakaṃ liṃgaṃ yattvayā sthāpitaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*prātarutthāya yaḥ kaścitsamyaktadvīkṣayiṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

*miṣṭānnamamṛtasvādu sa hi nūnamavāpsyati \|*  
*mama vākyānnṛpaśreṣṭha sadā janmanijanmani \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. O king, one who gets up in the morning and properly (with devotion) visits my Liṅga installed by you shall certainly get dainty food as sweet as nectar. O excellent king, this shall be in (his) every birth at my instance.

## \|\| 1.141.57 \|\|

*sa evaṃ bhagavānuktvā tataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*so'pi rājā nijaṃ sthānaṃ harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma cakārātha rājyaṃ nihatakaṃṭakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After saying thus the Lord vanished. The king came to his abode with great joy and ruled over the realm destroying all thorns (enemies).

## \|\| 1.141.58-59 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*adyāpi kalikāle'tra saṃprāpte dāruṇe yuge \|*  
*yastaṃ miṣṭānnadaṃ paśyetprātarutthāya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sa miṣṭānnamavāpnoti yadi kāmayate dvijāḥ \|*  
*niṣkāmo vā samabhyeti sthānaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

Sūta said:

58-59. O Brāhmaṇas, even now when the terrible Kali Age has come, one who gets up early in the morning and with devotion visits Lord Miṣṭānnada shall obtain dainty food, if he so desires. If he is without desire he attains the abode of the Trident-bearing Lord.

## Chapter 142 - Greatness of the Trio of Gaṇapatis

## \|\| 1.142.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti puṇyaṃ gaṇapatitrayam \|*  
*svargadaṃ martyadaṃ puṇyaṃ tathānyannarakāpaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*haṃtṛ vai sarvavighnānāṃ pūjitaṃ suradānavaiḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ caiva vidyākīrtivivardhanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Further there is the trio of Gaṇapati deities, that accords heavenly and worldly pleasures. It is meritorious and keeps off Naraka.

It destroys all obstacles. It is worshipped by Suras and Dānavas. It bestows all cherished things and increases learning and reputation.

## \|\| 1.142.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*trividhāḥ puruṣāḥ sūta jāyaṃtetra mahītale \|*  
*uttamā madhyamāścānye tathā cānye'dhamāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. O Sūta, three types of people are born on the earth. They are: the best, the middling and the worst or basest.

## \|\| 1.142.4 \|\|

*uttamāḥ prārthayaṃti sma mokṣameva hi kevalam \|*  
*gatā yatra nivartaṃte na kathaṃciddharātale \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The best ones seek only salvation, after attaining which they never return to the earth.

## \|\| 1.142.5 \|\|

*madhyamāḥ svargamārgaṃ ca divyānbhogānmanoramān \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ samaṃ krīḍāṃ yajñādyaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṛtām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The middling seek the path to heaven and enjoyment of divine pleasures. They seek to sport with Apsarās caused (attained) by Yajñas and other rites.

## \|\| 1.142.6 \|\|

*adhamā martyaloketra ramaṃte viṣayātmakāḥ \|*  
*viṣakīṭakavattatra ratiṃ kṛtvā garīyasīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The base ones divert themselves in the mortal world identifying themselves with the objects of the senses, it is as though they take great pleasure therein like a worm in poisonous fluid.

## \|\| 1.142.7 \|\|

*svargamokṣau parityajya tatkasmānmartya iṣyate \|*  
*yenāsau prārthyate martyairmartyado gaṇanāyakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. How does a mortal wish for that after discarding heavenly pleasures and salvation? And why is this Martyada (one that bestows human pleasures) Gaṇanāyaka prayed to by human beings?

## \|\| 1.142.8 \|\|

*kena saṃsthāpitāste ca tasminkṣetre gajānanāḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle ca draṣṭavyāḥ sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By whom have those Gajānanas installed in that holy spot? At what time should they be visited? Explain everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.142.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pūrvaṃ taptvā tapastīvraṃ martyaloke dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tato gacchaṃti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ svecchayā tridivaṃ prati \|*  
*mokṣamārgaṃ tathaivānye dhyānāviṣkṛtamānasāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9\. Formerly in the mortal world, excellent Brāhmaṇas performed severe penance and went joyously to heaven as they pleased. Similarly others whose minds become open through meditation, take to the path of Mokṣa (liberation from Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 1.142.10 \|\|

*tataḥ svarge samākīrṇe kadācinmanujottamaiḥ \|*  
*deveṣu kṣipyamāṇeṣu samaṃtāttatprabhāvataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, Svarga was completely filled by excellent men once. Thanks to their power, the Devas were ousted all round.

## \|\| 1.142.11 \|\|

*gatvā svayaṃ sahasrākṣaḥ sarvairdevagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*provāca śaṃkaraṃ gauryā sārdhamekāsanasthitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then, accompanied by all the groups of Devas, the Thousand-eyed One himself went to Śaṅkara who was seated along with Gaurī occupying the same seat and said to them:

## \|\| 1.142.12 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*tapaḥprabhāvasaṃsiddhairmānavaiḥ parameśvara \|*  
*asmākaṃ vyāpyate sarvaṃ mahimānaṃ gṛhādikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Indra said:

12\. O supreme Lord, everything connected with our glory such as (the possession of) abodes etc. is pervaded by human beings who have attained perfection, thanks to the power of penance.

## \|\| 1.142.13 \|\|

*tasmātkṛtvā prasādaṃ naḥ kaṃcicciṃtaya sāṃpratam \|*  
*upāyaṃ yena tiṣṭhāmaḥ saukhyenātra śivālaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence do this favour to us now. Think about some means whereby we can stay happily here in Śivālaya (abode of śiva).

## \|\| 1.142.14 \|\|

*atha śrutvā virūpākṣasteṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*pārvatyāḥ pārśvasaṃsthāyā mukhacandraṃ samaikṣayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brāhmaṇas, on hearing their words, Virūpākṣa (Śiva) glanced at the moon-like face of Pārvatī sitting by his side.

## \|\| 1.142.15 \|\|

*nijagātraṃ tato devī susaṃmardya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*malamāhṛtya taṃ kṛtsnaṃ cakre nāgamukhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereupon, the goddess massaged her own body very well repeatedly and gathered the dirt thereof entirely. She made an elephant-faced one out of that lump of body-dirt.

## \|\| 1.142.16 \|\|

*caturhastaṃ mahākāyaṃ laṃbodarasamanvitam \|*  
*sukautukakaraṃ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It had a huge body with four hands and protruding belly. It excited the curiosity and fancy of all the Heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.142.17-18 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vinayādāha devīṃ śikharavāsinīm \|*  
*yadarthamaṃba sṛṣṭo'haṃ tatkāryaṃ vada mā ciram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*trailokye tvatprasādena nāsādhyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The newly created one spoke humbly to the goddess staying on the peak (of the mount): “O mother, tell me the job for which I have been created. Do not delay. With your favour, there is nothing which I cannot accomplish in all the three worlds."

## \|\| 1.142.19 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*martyaloke narā ye ca svargamokṣaparāḥ sadā \|*  
*teṣāṃ vighnaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ śubhakṛtyeṣu caiva hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

The goddess said:

19\. Obstacles should be created by you in the auspicious rites of those men in the mortal world, who are desirous of the attainment of Svarga and Mokṣa (liberation).

## \|\| 1.142.20-21 \|\|

*saritāṃ patayastriṃśacchaṃkavaḥ saptasaptatiḥ \|*  
*mahāsarojaṣaṣṭiśca nikharvāṇāṃ ca viṃśatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*arbudāyutasaṃyuktāḥ koṭyo navatipañca ca \|*  
*lakṣāśca paṃcapaṃcāśatsahasrāḥ paṃcaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*śatāni navaṣaṣṭiśca gaṇāścānye'tra saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The Lords of rivers are thirty Śaṅkus (ten billions) and seventy-seven. There are eighty Nikharvas (billions) of the Mahāsarojas. There are various other Gaṇas numbering one hundred million ten thousand ninety-five crore fifty-five lakh twenty-five thousand sixty-nine hundred.

## \|\| 1.142.22 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ nadī smṛtaḥ pūrvo mahākālastathā paraḥ \|*  
*te sarve vaśagāstubhyaṃ prabhavaṃtu gaṇottamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Of these Nandin is proclaimed as the foremost and Mahākāla as the next. May all those excellent Gaṇas function under your control.

## \|\| 1.142.23 \|\|

*ādhipatyaṃ mayā dattaṃ tava vatsa kuruṣva tat \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ gaṇavṛṃdānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O dear one, the overlorḍship thereof has been given to you by me. Be established in the overlordship of all these groups of Gaṇas and administer them.

## \|\| 1.142.24-25 \|\|

*evamuktvātha sā devī samānīyauṣadhībhṛtān \|*  
*hemakuṃbhānsutīrthāṃbhaḥ paripūrṇānmahodayān \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasyābhiṣecanaṃ cakre svayameva sureśvarī \|*  
*gītavādyavinodena nṛtyamaṃgalajaiḥ svanaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. After saying thus, the goddess fetched highly auspicious gold pots filled with waters from excellent Tīrthas and containing medicinal herbs as well. The goddess of Suras sprinkled the sacred water over him to the accompaniment of music, playing of musical instruments and auspicious chantings of the Mantras along with dances.

## \|\| 1.142.26 \|\|

*trayastriṃśatsmṛtāḥ koṭayo devānāṃ yāḥ sthitā divi \|*  
*tāḥ sarvāstatra cāgatya tasya cakruśca maṃgalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There are thirty-three crores of Devas stationed in heaven. All of them came there and celebrated that auspicious rite for him.

## \|\| 1.142.27 \|\|

*atha tasya dadau tuṣṭo bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*kuṭhāraṃ niśitaṃ haste sadā vai śreṣṭhamāyudham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Bull-emblemed Lord who was pleased with him, gave him a sharp axe as his permanent excellent weapon.

## \|\| 1.142.28 \|\|

*pātraṃ modakasaṃpūrṇamakṣayaṃ caiva pārvatī \|*  
*bhojanārthe mahābhāgā mātṛsnehaparāyaṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O highly esteemed ones, Pārvatī was full of motherly love for him and gave him a vessel filled with perennial supply of Modakas (round-shaped sweets) for his food.

## \|\| 1.142.29 \|\|

*mūṣakaṃ kārtikeyastu vāhanārthaṃ praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhrātaraṃ manyamānastu bandhusnehena saṃyutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Kārttikeya joyously considered him his brother. Endowed with the affection of a kinsman he gave him a mouse as his vehicle.

## \|\| 1.142.30 \|\|

*jñānaṃ divyaṃ dadau brahmā tasmai hṛṣṭena cetasā \|*  
*atītānāgataṃ caiva vartamānaṃ ca yadbhavet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With a delighted mind, Brahmā bestowed divine knowledge on him comprising everything past, present and future.

## \|\| 1.142.31 \|\|

*prajñāṃ viṣṇuḥ sahasrākṣaḥ saubhāgyaṃ cottamaṃ mahat \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ kāmadevastu kubero vibhavādikam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Viṣṇu granted him intellect. The Thousand-eyed One gave him the great and excellent fortune. Kāmadeva gave him conjugal felicity. Kubera gave him riches etc.

## \|\| 1.142.32 \|\|

*pratāpaṃ bhagavānsūryaḥ kāṃtimagryāṃ niśākaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Lord Sūrya granted him valour. Moon granted him excellent lustre.

## \|\| 1.142.33 \|\|

*tathānye vibudhāḥ sarve daduriṣṭāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*ātmīyāni pratuṣṭyarthaṃ devyā devasya ca prabhoḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In the same way, in order to please the goddess and the Lord, all the other Devas gave him various things belonging to them, and desired by him.

## \|\| 1.142.34 \|\|

*evaṃ labdhavaraḥ so'tha gaṇanātho dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*devakṛtyaparo nityaṃ cakre vighnāni bhūtale \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, having obtained excellent things by way of boon thus Gaṇanātha became interested in the work of Devas and therefore worked out obstacles on the earth.

## \|\| 1.142.35 \|\|

*dharmārthaṃ yatamānānāṃ mokṣāya sukṛtāya ca \|*  
*tato bhūmitale'bhyetya gaṇeśastatra yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He produced the obstacles in the way of those who endeavoured for piety, salvation and meritorious acts. Then he came down to the earth and was remembered there as Gaṇeśa.

## \|\| 1.142.36 \|\|

*vaimānikaiḥ samabhyetya sthāpitastatra sa dvijāḥ \|*  
*yena svargārthino lokāḥ pūjāṃ tasya pracakrire \|*  
*prathamaṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu vighnanāśāya tatparāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Brāhmaṇas, Vaimānikas (persons moving about in aerial chariots) came there and installed him so that people seeking Svarga adored him as the first in all the sacred rites, because they were desirous of extermination of obstacles.

## \|\| 1.142.37 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle ca camatkārapurodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇairbrahmavijñānatatparairmokṣahetubhiḥ \|*  
*īśānaḥ sthāpitastatra mokṣado ya udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. At that very time, Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura, who had great interest in the knowledge of Brahman with salvation as their aim, installed Īśāna there. He was cited as Mokṣada (‘bestower of salvation’).

## \|\| 1.142.38 \|\|

*svargaṃ vāñchadbhirevānyaiḥ svargadvārapradastathā \|*  
*heraṃbaḥ sthāpitastatra satyanāmā yathoditaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Heramba, Svargadvāraprada (the bestower of the portals of Svarga), was installed there by those who desired heavenly pleasures. He was true to his name given.

## \|\| 1.142.39 \|\|

*tathānyairmartyado nāma gaṇaiśastatra yaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*yena svargāccyutā yāṃti na kadā narakādikam \|*  
*tiryaktvaṃ vā kṛmitvaṃ vā sthāvaratvamathāpi vā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Gaṇeśa named Martyada was installed by others. Thanks to him, even those who slip down from Svarga never go to Naraka etc., or attain the state of a brute, worm or immobile being.

## \|\| 1.142.40 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāttatra kṣetre puṇye dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*herambo martyado jātaḥ svargiṇāṃ martyadaḥ sadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. For this reason, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Heraṃba (Gaṇeśa) became martyada in that meritorious holy spot. He was always martyada unto heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.142.41 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ puṇyaṃ heraṃbasaṃbhavam \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ sarvavighnāni yannihanti śrutaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus the meritorious story of Heraṃba has been completely narrated to you all. On being listened to, this story destroys all obstacles.

## \|\| 1.142.42 \|\|

*etanmāghacaturthāṃ yaḥ śuklāyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*na tasya vatsaraṃ yāvadvighnaṃ sañjāyate kvacit \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If a man worships this deity on the fourth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha, he will never meet with any obstacle for the period of a year.

## Chapter 143 - Provocation of Jābāli

## \|\| 1.143.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti devaścitreśvaro dvijāḥ \|*  
*citrapīṭhasya madhyasthaścitrasaukhyaprado nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 143-146 describe the greatness of Amareśvara Liṅga and the Kuṇḍa in front of it.—Jābāli beats his daughter practically to death for her immoral act. She does not die due to the power of Amareśvara Liṅga before which she was beaten. Śiva elevated her to Yogiṇī-ship.—The spirited dialogue between Jābāli and his daughter, a feminist of that age, is worth reading in original (in Chapter 144).

Sūta said:

1\. Further, O Brāhmanas, there is another deity there named Citreśvara. It is situated in the middle of Citrapītha and grants diverse kinds of pleasures unto men.

## \|\| 1.143.2 \|\|

*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayitvā ca snāpayitvāthavā naraḥ \|*  
*mucyate paradārotthaiḥ pātakaiścopapātakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By visiting that deity, adoring it or bathing it a man is rid of major and minor sins arising from close intimacy with other men’s wives.

## \|\| 1.143.3 \|\|

*dharṣayitvā guroḥ patnīṃ kanyāṃ vā nijavaṃśajām \|*  
*nīcāṃ vā vratayuktāṃ vā kāmāsaktena cetasā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. One who ravishes the wife of the preceptor or a girl of one’s own family, a girl of a low family or a woman who has adopted Vratas, with the mind overpowered by lust, gets rid of the sin.

## \|\| 1.143.4 \|\|

*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*sa tatpāpaṃ nihatyāśu svargalokaṃ tato vrajet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A man who worships that deity on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra eradicates the sin thereof and goes to Svarga quickly.

## \|\| 1.143.5-6 \|\|

*tathā citrāṃgadastatra jābālisahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*kumāryā sahitaḥ sārddhaṃ nagnayā tatsamutthayā \|*  
*santiṣṭhate tadagre tu śapto jābālinā purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*trayāṇāmapi yasteṣāṃ tasminnahani nirvapet \|*  
*sa iṣṭāṃ labhate nārīṃ siddhiṃ ca manasi sthitām \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Further there is King Citraṅgada accompanied by Sage Jābāli. He is also accompanied by a girl born of the sage, a naked girl who has not yet attained the age of menstruation (Nagnikā). He stands before him having been cursed by Jābāli already. One who offers libations to all the three (on that day) obtains a woman loved by him as well as Siddhi sought by him.

## \|\| 1.143.7-8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmājjābālinā śaptaḥ pūrvaṃ citrāṃgado yuvā \|*  
*sā ca tattanayā kasmātkumārī vastravarjitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*adyāpi tiṣṭhate tatra viruddhaṃ rūpamāśritā \|*  
*janahāsya karaṃ nityaṃ tasmātsūta vadasva naḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

The sages said:

7-8. Why was the youth Citrāṅgada cursed formerly by Jābāli? Why does his daughter stand stripped of her clothes? Why has she adopted this contrary form causing derision of the people? O Sūta, describe this to us.

## \|\| 1.143.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ārsotpūrvaṃ munirnāmnā jābāliriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*kaumārabrahmacaryeṇa yena cīrṇaṃ tapaḥ sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9\. Formerly there was a well-known sage named Jābāli. He performed penances always with celibacy, ever since his child-hood.

## \|\| 1.143.10 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ samāsādya sa saddvijāḥ \|*  
*bālye'pi vayasi prāpte samārebhe mahattapaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, even in his childhood he came to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara and began a great penance.

## \|\| 1.143.11 \|\|

*kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni pārākāṇi śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*kurvatā tena te devāḥ saṃnītā bhayagocaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was gradually performing Paraka, Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa and other rites. Thereby he made Devas highly frightened.

## \|\| 1.143.12 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrādayo devāḥ saṃtrastā merumūrdhani \|*  
*militvā cakrire maṃtraṃ tasya vighnakṛte mithaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Śakra and other Devas who were afraid met together on the peak of Meru and consulted one another for the purpose of causing obstacles to him.

## \|\| 1.143.13-15 \|\|

*yadyasya tapaso vṛddhirevaṃ yāsyati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*cyāvayiṣyati tannūnaṃ svargarājyācchatakratum \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmādgacchatu raṃbhākhyā tatpārśve 'psarasāṃ varā \|*  
*brahmacaryavighātāya tasyarṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brahmacaryaṃ tapomūlaṃ yataḥ saṃkīrtitaṃ dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tasyābhāvātparikleśaḥ kevalaṃ na phalaṃ vrate \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. “If there is to be increase of his penance everyday thus, he will certainly destabilize Śatakratu and make him fall from his heavenly kingdom. Therefore let the foremost among the Apsarās named Raṃbhā go to him to cause destruction of the celibacy of that sage of sanctified soul.

Celibacy is the root cause of penance. It has been glorified thus by Brāhmaṇas. The loss of it causes great difficulty. Simply there will not be any fruit resulting from the Vrata.”

## \|\| 1.143.16 \|\|

*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā samāhūya tataḥ param \|*  
*raṃbhāmūcurmaheṃdreṇa sarve devāstadādarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After deciding thus all the Devas together with Mahendra summoned Raṃbhā and spoke to her respectfully:

## \|\| 1.143.17-18 \|\|

*gaccha śīghraṃ mahābhāge jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tapovighnāya tasya vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

*te te bhāvāḥ prayoktavyāḥ kathāstāstā manoharāḥ \|*  
*vardhayaṃtī tathā citte tasya kāmaṃ nirargalam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. “O highly esteemed lady, go quickly to the place where Jābāli is present in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara for the purpose of disturbing his penance. All emotional coquetries and charmingly eloquent speechess and tales should be employed by you exciting unrestricted lust in his mind.”

## \|\| 1.143.19 \|\|

*raṃbhovāca \|*  
*sa munirna vijānāti kāmadharmaṃ sureśvara \|*  
*arasajñaṃ kathaṃ deva kariṣyāmi smarānvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

Raṃbhā said:

19\. O Lord of Suras, that sage does not know the art of love-play. O Lord, how can I convert a man devoid of fascination and charm into one of lascivious proclivity?

## \|\| 1.143.20 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*eṣa yāsyati madvākyādvasaṃtastasya sannidhau \|*  
*asya saṃdarśanādeva bhaviṣyati sa sasmaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Indra said:

20\. At my bidding this Vasanta shall go near him. Merely by his sight, he will become swayed by love.

## \|\| 1.143.21 \|\|

*tasmādgaccha drutaṃ tatra sahānena varānane \|*  
*saṃsiddhirjāyate yena devakṛtyaṃ bhaveddrutam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence, O lady of excellent countenance, go there quickly along with him so that there shall be quick accomplishment of the tasks of Devas.

## \|\| 1.143.22 \|\|

*atha sā taṃ praṇamyoccaiḥ prasthitā dharaṇītalam \|*  
*vasaṃtena samāyuktā jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereupon, she bowed down to him elaborately and went along with Vasanta to the place where Jābāli was staying.

## \|\| 1.143.23 \|\|

*athākasmādaśokasya saṃjātaḥ puṣpasaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*tilakasya ca cūtasya maṃjaryaḥ samupasthitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then, all of a sudden, Aśoka became fully blossomed; bunches of flowers appeared on Tilaka and mango trees.

## \|\| 1.143.24 \|\|

*śiśire ca sarojāni vikāsaṃ prāpureva hi \|*  
*vavau ca surabhirvāyurdākṣiṇātyaḥ sukāmadaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Even in the winter lotuses bloomed. A fragrant southern wind blew satisfying all desires.

## \|\| 1.143.25 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā raṃbhā tatra varāpsarāḥ \|*  
*salilāśayatīrastho jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meantime, Raṃbhā, the excellent Apsarā, reached the bank of the water-pond where Jābāli was present.

## \|\| 1.143.26 \|\|

*akṣamālādhṛtakaro japanmaṃtramanekadhā \|*  
*abhīṣṭaṃ śraddhayā yukto vidhāya pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After offering the desired (i.e. requisite) oblation to Pitṛs with faith, he was uttering Mantras many times with the rosary of beads held in his hand.

## \|\| 1.143.27 \|\|

*atha saṃpaśyatastasya muktvā vastraparigraham \|*  
*snānārthaṃ tajjalaṃ sā'tha praviveśa varāpsarāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then even as he was looking on, the excellent Apsarā stripped herself of all garments and entered the water for taking bath.

## \|\| 1.143.28 \|\|

*vivastrāṃ tāṃ samālokya so'pi yauvanaśālinīm \|*  
*yāmyānilena ca spṛṣṭaḥ kāmasya vaśago 'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Seeing her in the prime of youth but stripped of her garments, and being swayed by the southern wind, he became a victim of Kāma, under his full control.

## \|\| 1.143.29 \|\|

*tatastasyābhavatkaṃpastatkṣaṇādeva sanmune \|*  
*akṣamālā karāgrācca papāta dharaṇītale \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The excellent sage experienced a tremor at the instant. The rosary fell down on the ground from his hand.

## \|\| 1.143.30 \|\|

*pulakaḥ sarvagātreṣu saṃjajñe'tīva dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*aśrupātāḥ pataṃti sma koṣṇāḥ plāvitabhūtalāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. There was horripilation in all his limbs. It had terrific result. Slightly warm tears fell down drenching the ground.

## \|\| 1.143.31 \|\|

*atha taṃ kṣubhitaṃ jñātvā cittajñā sā varāpsarāḥ \|*  
*nirgatya salilāttasmāccakre vastraparigraham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On knowing that he had become excited the excellent Apsarā conversant with the mental predilection came out of water and wore the garments again.

## \|\| 1.143.32 \|\|

*tatastasyāṃtike gatvā praṇipatya kṛtādarā \|*  
*provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ varddhaṃtī tasya tanmatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. She went near him, bowed down with great respect and spoke these sweet words increasing his lovelorn state:

## \|\| 1.143.33 \|\|

*āśrame sakalaṃ brahmankaccitte kuśalaṃ mune \|*  
*svādhyāye tapasi prājña śiṣyeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “O holy Sir, I hope everytinhg is quite good in your hermitage. O wise Sage, I hope your study of the Vedas goes on smoothly; O Sage, I hope your disciples and the birds and animals here are also quite all right.”

## \|\| 1.143.34 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*kuśalaṃ me varārohe sarvatraivādhunā sthitam \|*  
*viśeṣeṇātra saṃprāptā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

The sage said:

34\. O beautiful lady, everything everywhere is quite all right in regard to me. Particularly, since you have come—you who are marked with all the characteristics.

## \|\| 1.143.35 \|\|

*kā tvaṃ vada mahābhāge mama manmathavardhanī \|*  
*kiṃ devī vāsurī vā kiṃ pannagī kiṃ tu mānuṣī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O highly esteemed one, tell me who you are. You enhance love in me. Are you a Devī or an Asura lady, a serpent lady or a human one?

## \|\| 1.143.36 \|\|

*nivedaya śarīre me kiṃ na paśyasi vepathum \|*  
*nirargalaśca romāṃco bāṣpapūraśca netrajaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Tell me, don’t you notice a tremor in my body? There is unrestricted flow of tears from the eyes, and the bristling of the bairs \[hairs\] all over the body.

## \|\| 1.143.37 \|\|

*raṃbhovāca \|*  
*kiṃ te gātrasvabhāvo'yam kiṃ vānyo vyādhisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*kaccideva na te svāsthyaṃ prapaśyāmi śarīrajam \|\| 37 \|\|*

Raṃbhā said:

37\. I don't see any normalcy in the state of your body. Are these aberrations in your body natural to it? Or are they caused by ailments?

## \|\| 1.143.38 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*na me gātrasvabhāvo na vyādhibhiśca sulocane \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva kāraṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yenedṛksaṃsthitaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

The sage said:

38\. O lady of excellent eyes, this is neither natural to my body, nor is it caused by ailments. Listen to the whole cause whereby the body has come to this plight.

## \|\| 1.143.39 \|\|

*yāvatī vartate velā tava darśanasaṃbhavā \|*  
*tāvatkālamidaṃ rūpaṃ mama gātrasamudbhavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. As long as I continue to set my eyes on you, this state of the body persists.

## \|\| 1.143.40 \|\|

*tadahaṃ manmathāviṣṭo darśanāttava śobhane \|*  
*brahmacaryaparopītthaṃ mahāvratadharo'pi ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. That means, O splendid lady, I have been overwhelmed with love (passion) on seeing you. Though I am devoted to celibacy, though I have adopted great vows, this is my present condition.

## \|\| 1.143.41 \|\|

*raṃbhovāca \|\|*  
*yadyevaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha māṃ bhajasva yathāsukham \|*  
*nātra kaścidbhaveddoṣaḥ paṇyanārī yato'smyaham \|\| 41 \|\|*

Raṃbhā said:

41\. If that is so, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, do comfortably resort to me. No harm can result from it because I am only a common courtesan.

## \|\| 1.143.42 \|\|

*sādhāraṇā vayaṃ vipra yataḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva lokānāṃ viśeṣeṇa dvijanmanām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Brāhmaṇa, we have been created by the Self-born Lord as common for all the people especially for twice-born ones.

## \|\| 1.143.43 \|\|

*ahaṃ cāpi samālokya tvāṃ mune manmathopamam \|*  
*hatā kāmaśaraistīkṣṇairna ca gaṃtuṃ samutsahe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On seeing you, O sage, I too have been struck by the sharp arrows of Kāma, since you are on a par with Kāma. I don't feel inclined to go elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.143.44 \|\|

*mayā dṛṣṭāḥ surāḥ pūrvaṃ yakṣā vidyādharāstathā \|*  
*siddhāśca kiṃnarā nāgā guhyakāḥ kimu mānuṣāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Earlier Suras, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, Siddhas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, Guhyakas and even human beings have been seen by me.

## \|\| 1.143.45 \|\|

*nedṛgrūpaṃ vapusteṣāmekasyāpi vilokitam \|*  
*madhye brāhmaṇaśārdūla tasmādbhaktāṃ bhajasva mām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. But, O tiger among Brāhmaṇas, such an exquisite form as this has never been seen amongst them, Hence do resort to me, your devotee.

## \|\| 1.143.46 \|\|

*yo nārīṃ kāmasaṃtaptāṃ svayaṃ prāptāṃ parityajet \|*  
*sa mūrkhaḥ pacyate ghore narake śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A foolish person who avoids a woman distressed by love, who herself approaches him, is cooked in terrible Naraka for all years to come (i.e. a pretty long period).

## \|\| 1.143.47 \|\|

*evamuktvā tayā so'tha pariṣvakto mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*anicchannapi vākyena hṛdayena ca saspṛhaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After saying thus, she embraced the great sage. He showed unwillingness in speech, though he was desirous of it in his heart.

## \|\| 1.143.48 \|\|

*tato latāni kuṃje taṃ samānīya munīśvaram \|*  
*kāmaśāstroditairbhāvai rarāma kṛtrimairmunim \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. She then took the sage to the bower of creepers and made him sport about with artificial and coquetish behaviour as laid down in erotic science.

## \|\| 1.143.49 \|\|

*evaṃ tayā samaṃ tatra sthito yāvaddinakṣayam \|*  
*kāmadharmasamāsaktaḥ saṃtyaktāśeṣakarmakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thus till the end of the day, he remained with her eagerly engaged in erotic activities. He discarded all other holy rites.

## \|\| 1.143.50 \|\|

*tato niṣkāmatāṃ prāpto lajjayā parivāritaḥ \|*  
*visasarja ca tāṃ raṃbhāṃ śaucaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thereby he satisfied his lustful desire (but) became ashamed thereafter. He dismissed Raṃbhā and then washed himself clean.

## \|\| 1.143.51 \|\|

*sāpi tena vinirmuktā kṛtakṛtyā vilāsinī \|*  
*prahṛṣṭā prayayau tatra yatra devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On being dismissed by him the contented lady of graceful charms became glad. She joyously went to the place where Devas including Vāsava were present.

## Chapter 144 - The Story of Citrāṅgadeśvara, Phalavatī and Jābāli

## \|\| 1.144.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā gatvā tridivaṃ paścātsahasrākṣaṃ surairyutam \|*  
*provāca bhagavandiṣṭyā kṣobhito'sau mahāmuniḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tapastasya hataṃ kṛtsnaṃ yatkṛcchreṇa samācitam \|*  
*tathā nistejasatvaṃ ca nītastvaṃ sukhabhāgbhava \|\| 2 \|\|*

\[Full title: The Story of Citrāṅgadeśvara (Citrāṅgada-īśvara), Phalavatī and Jābāli\]

Sūta said:

1-2. She went to heaven and later told the Lotus-eyed One (Indra) along with the Devas: “Fortunately, O Lord, the great sage has been rendered agitated. The penance that he had accumulated with great difficulty has been entirely shattered. He has become deprived of refulgence. Hence relax and be happy.”

## \|\| 1.144.3 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha sā raṃbhā śaṃsitā nikhilaiḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*amogharetasastasya dadhre garbhaṃ nijodare \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On uttering these words, Raṃbhā was congratulated by all the Suras.

Since the sage was Amogharetas (‘one whose semen never goes in vain’) she conceived the foetus in her womb.

## \|\| 1.144.4 \|\|

*jābālirapi kṛtvā ca paścāttāpamanekadhā \|*  
*bhūyastu tapasi sthitvā sthitastatraiva cāśrame \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. As for sage Jābāli, he regretted very much for what he did. But he resumed his penance once again in the hermitage where he stayed.

## \|\| 1.144.5 \|\|

*tatastu daśame māsi saṃprāpte suṣuve śubhām \|*  
*kanyāṃ sarojapatrākṣīṃ divyalakṣaṇalakṣitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Ten months later, the Apsarā delivered a splendid daughter marked with divine characteristics with eyes like the petals of a lotus.

## \|\| 1.144.6 \|\|

*atha tāṃ mānuṣodbhūtāṃ matvā tasyaiva cāśramam \|*  
*gatvā mumoca pratyakṣaṃ tasyarṣeścedamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In view of the fact that she had origin from a human being, the mother of the girl went to his hermitage and left her there. She then told him directly:

## \|\| 1.144.7-8 \|\|

*tava vīryasamudbhūtāmenāṃ majjaṭharoṣitām \|*  
*kanyakāṃ muniśārdūla tasmātpālaya sāṃpratam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*na svarge vidyate vāso mānuṣāṇāṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇāttubhyaṃ mayā brahmansamarpitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. “O tiger among sages, nurse and bring up this girl born from your semen, and conceived in my womb. Human beings cannot have a permanent stay in Svarga. For this reason, O Brāhmaṇa, she is being entrusted to you.”

## \|\| 1.144.9 \|\|

*evamuktvā yayau raṃbhā satvaraṃ tridaśālayam \|*  
*jābālirapi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyakāṃ snehamāviśat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying this, Raṃbhā hastened back to the abode of Devas. On seeing his own daughter Jābāli was drawn to her by great affection.

## \|\| 1.144.10 \|\|

*tatastāṃ kanyakāṃ kṛtvā suṣṭhu gupte latāgṛhe \|*  
*rasairmiṣṭaphalodbhūtaiḥ pupoṣa ca divāniśam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He kept his child well-guarded in a creeper-hut and nurtured her day and night with the juice of sweet fruits.

## \|\| 1.144.11 \|\|

*sāpi kanyā parāṃ vṛddhiṃ śanairyāti dinedine \|*  
*śuklapakṣaṃ samāsādya yathā candrakalā divi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Like the digit of the moon in the sky in the bright half of a month, the girl slowly grew up day by day.

## \|\| 1.144.12 \|\|

*yathāyathātha sā yāti vṛddhiṃ kamalalocanā \|*  
*tathātathāsya susneho jābālerapyavardhata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. As the lotus-eyed girl grew up, the filial affection of Jābāli too increased steadily.

## \|\| 1.144.13 \|\|

*sā śiśutve mṛgaiḥ sārddhaṃ pakṣibhiśca suśobhanā \|*  
*krīḍāṃ cakre suviśrabdhairvardhayaṃtī munermudam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In her childhood the splendid girl played with the deer and birds that remained calm and carefree. Thereby she enhanced the delight of the sage.

## \|\| 1.144.14 \|\|

*tato bālyaṃ parityaktvā valkalāvṛtagātrikā \|*  
*tasyarṣeḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sāhāyyaṃ prakaroti ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She grew up form the childish stage into a young maiden regularly clad in bark garments. She always helped the sage in all his holy rites.

## \|\| 1.144.15 \|\|

*samitkuśādi yatkiṃcitphalapuṣpasamanvitam \|*  
*vanāttadānayāmāsa tasya prītimavardhayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. She brought sacrificial twigs, Darbha grass etc. along with fruits and flowers from the forest and thereby heightened his pleasure.

## \|\| 1.144.16 \|\|

*tataḥ katipayāhasya phalārthaṃ sā mṛgekṣaṇā \|*  
*nidāghasamaye dūraṃ svāśramātprajagāma ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After a few days, once, in the heat of summer, the fawn-eyed girl went far into the forest from her hermitage to collect fruits.

## \|\| 1.144.17 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra vimānavaramāśritaḥ \|*  
*prāptaścitrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the meantime Citrāṅgada, a Gandharva out of the celestial beings, came there riding in his aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.144.18 \|\|

*tena sā vijane bālā pūrṇacandranibhānanā \|*  
*dṛṣṭā cāṃdramasī lekhā patiteva dharātale \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the desolate forest, the girl with the countenance resembling the full moon was seen by him, like the digit of the moon fallen on the ground.

## \|\| 1.144.19 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmaparītāṃgaḥ sovatīrya dharātalam \|*  
*vimānānmadhurairvākyaistāmuvāca kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He experienced the pangs of love all over the body. He descended to the earth from his aerial chariot. With palms joined in veneration, he spoke these sweet words:

## \|\| 1.144.20 \|\|

*kā tvaṃ kamalagarbhābhā nirjane'tha mahāvane \|*  
*bhramasyekākinī bāle vanamadhye sulocane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Who are you, O bright-eyed girl roaming about in the great desolate forest? Your complexion is like the tender inside of a lotus. Yet you move about alone.”

## \|\| 1.144.21 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ phalavatīnāma jābālerduhitā mune \|*  
*phalapuṣpārthamāyātā tadarthamiha kānane \|\| 21 \|\|*

The girl said:

21\. I am the daughter of Sage Jābāli, named Phalavatī. I have come to this forest to gather fruits for him.

## \|\| 1.144.22 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|*  
*kumārabrahmacārī sa śrūyate munisattamaḥ \|*  
*tatkathaṃ tasya vāmoru tvaṃ jātā bhāryayā vinā \|\| 22 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

22\. O lady of beautiful thighs, it is reported that the excellent sage is a life-long celibate. How were you then born without a wife of his?

## \|\| 1.144.23 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāga nāsti dāraparigrahaḥ \|*  
*tasyarṣeḥ kiṃ tu saṃjātā yathā tanme'vadhāraya \|\| 23 \|\|*

The girl said:

23\. O highly esteemed one, it is true that the sage has not taken a wife unto himself. Listen then how I came to be born.

## \|\| 1.144.24 \|\|

*raṃbhā nāmāpsarāstena purā dṛṣṭā surāṃganā \|*  
*tataḥ kāmaparītena sevitā ca yathāsukham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Formerly an Apsarā named Raṃbhā was seen by him. As he was overcome by love then the celestial lady was resorted to by him for pleasure.

## \|\| 1.144.25 \|\|

*tatastadudarājjātā devaloke mahattare \|*  
*tayāpi ceha tasyarṣerbhūya eva niyojitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I was born out of her womb in the exalted Devaloka. I was then entrusted to the sage by her.

## \|\| 1.144.26 \|\|

*evaṃ sa me pitā jāto jābālirmunisattamaḥ \|*  
*poṣitā'haṃ tatastena nānāphalasamudravaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It was in this manner that the excellent sage Jābāli came to be my father. Thereafter, I was brought up by him by means of juice extracted from various kinds of fruits.

## \|\| 1.144.27 \|\|

*tataḥ phalavatī nāma kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā \|*  
*mamānurūpametaddhi yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then I was given the name Phalavatī by that noble-souled one. Indeed this befits me. This is the story about which you have asked.

## \|\| 1.144.28 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|*  
*tava rūpaṃ samālokya kāmasyāhaṃ vaśaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhajasva māṃ bhīru no cedyāsyāmi saṃkṣayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

28\. O timid lady, after seeing your beautiful form I have become a slave unto Kāma. Hence do resort to me. Otherwise I shall be doomed (die).

## \|\| 1.144.29 \|\|

*ahaṃ citrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām \|*  
*tīrthayātrākṛte prāptaḥ kṣetre'smiñchraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I am a Gandharva out of the heaven-dwellers named Citrāṅgada. I have come to this holy spot with great faith, in the course of my pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.144.30 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*kumāradharmiṇī cāhamadyāpi vaśagā pituḥ \|*  
*kāmadharmaṃ na jānāmi citrāṃgada kathaṃcana \|\| 30 \|\|*

The girl said:

30\. I am still virgin and under the control of my father. O Citrāṅgada, I am not conversant with the nuances of love play.

## \|\| 1.144.31 \|\|

*tasmātprārthaya me tātaṃ sa māṃ tubhyaṃ pradāsyati \|*  
*anurūpāya yogyāya taruṇāya manasvinīm \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Hence request my father. He will give me unto you. You are a young man fully qualified and so suitable to me, a girl of exalted mind.

## \|\| 1.144.32 \|\|

*mamāpi rucitaṃ citte tava vākyamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*dhanyāhaṃ yadi te kaṇṭhamāliṃgāmi yathecchayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Your excellent words appeal to me too. I will consider myself blessed if I can embrace your neck as I please.

## \|\| 1.144.33 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|*  
*na śaknomi mahābhāge tāvatkālaṃ pratīkṣitum \|*  
*māṃ dahatyeṣa gātrotthaḥ sumahānkāmapāvakaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

33\. O highly esteemed maiden, I cannot wait so much time. The great fire of love arising out of my body burns me.

## \|\| 1.144.34 \|\|

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me ratidānena śobhane \|*  
*ko jānāti hi taccittaṃ kīdṛgrūpaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence, O splendid maiden, do me the favour of the gift of sexual intimacy. Who knows how his mind will react?

## \|\| 1.144.35 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*evaṃ te vartamānasya mama tātaḥ prakopataḥ \|*  
*dahiṣyati na saṃdehaḥ śāpaṃ dattvā sudāruṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

The girl said:

35\. If you behave thus, there is no doubt about it that my father, out of anger, will bum you down giving you a terrible curse.

## \|\| 1.144.36 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|*  
*tava tātaḥ sa kālena māṃ dahiṣyati mānade \|*  
*kāmānalaḥ punaḥ sadya eṣa bhasma kariṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

36\. O honour-bestowing maiden, your father will bum only after the lapse of some time. But this fire of love will reduce me to ashes immediately.

## \|\| 1.144.37 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha tāṃ bālāṃ vepamānāṃ trapāvatīm \|*  
*gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe pāṇau praviveśa surālayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After saying thus to the timid, bashfully trembling maiden, he caught her right hand and entered the temple.

## \|\| 1.144.38 \|\|

*tatra tāṃ ramayāmāsa tadā kāmaprapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*tatkālajātarāgāṃdhāṃ nirlajjatvamupāgatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There the Gandharva being afflicted with love, sported with her who had become shameless at that time with her passion rendering her blind.

## \|\| 1.144.39 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyāḥ samaṃ tena sthitāyā divaso gataḥ \|*  
*nimeṣavanmuniśreṣṭhāstataścāstaṃ gato raviḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O excellent sages, even as she remained thus along with him, the day passed off like a minute. Then the day came to a close. The sun set.

## \|\| 1.144.40 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vipro jābālirduḥkha saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*anāyātāṃ sutāṃ jñātvā paribabhrāma sarvataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the meantime, the Brāhmaṇa Jābāli became extremely miserable, after having noticed that his daughter had not returned. He wandered here and there.

## \|\| 1.144.41-42 \|\|

*aho sā duhitā mahyaṃ kimu vyālaiḥ prabhakṣitā \|*  
*vṛkṣaṃ kaṃcitsamārūḍhā patitā dharaṇī tale \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kiṃ vā jalāśayaṃ kaṃcitprāpya gādhamajānatī \|*  
*nimagnā tatra sā bālā saṃpraviṣṭā jalārthinī \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. ‘Alas, has my daughter been devoured by tigers? Has she fallen on the ground after climbing up a tree? Or did she enter some pond and get drowned because she could not gauge the depth? She might have entered it seeking water.’

## \|\| 1.144.43 \|\|

*evaṃ sa pralapanvipro babhrāma gahane vane \|*  
*kuśakaṇṭakaviddhāṃgaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamākulaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Lamenting thus the Brāhmaṇa roamed about in the dense forest. He was himself agitated due to hunger and thirst. Thorns and Kuśa grass wounded his limbs.

## \|\| 1.144.44 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ śṛṇoti śabdaṃ sa mṛgapakṣisamudbhavam \|*  
*rajanyāṃ tatra niryāti matvā phalavatīṃ ca tām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. At night whenever he heard some sound of a bird or animal, he became startled thinking that it was Phalavatī.

## \|\| 1.144.45 \|\|

*atha kramātsamāyāto haraharmyaṃ sa sanmuniḥ \|*  
*yatra citrāṃgadopetā sā saṃtiṣṭhati kanyakā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Slowly the excellent sage came to the temple of Hara where his daughter was present in close intimacy with Citrāṅgada.

## \|\| 1.144.46 \|\|

*niḥśaṃkā jalpamānā ca rāgavākyānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*anarhāṇi kumārīṇāṃ brahmajānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. She was speaking many words expressing love unhesitatingly but improper in the case of virgins especially if they hail from a Brāhmaṇa family.

## \|\| 1.144.47 \|\|

*tataḥ sa suciraṃ śrutvā dūrastho vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*kumāryāśceṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even from afar he had been hearing those words for a long time and was astonished. On seeing the activity of the girl, he became angry with reddened eyes.

## \|\| 1.144.48 \|\|

*atha dudrāva vegena gṛhya kāṣṭhasamuccayam \|*  
*dvābhyāmeva vināśāya bhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He gathered together a bundle of sticks and rushed against them with the intention of killing both. He rebuked them repeatedly:

## \|\| 1.144.49-50 \|\|

*dhigdhikpāpasamācāre kaumāryaṃ dūṣitaṃ tvayā \|*  
*lāṃchanaṃ ca samānītaṃ mama lokatraye'pi ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nitarāṃ patimāsādya karmaṇānena cādhame \|*  
*tasmādanena pāpena yuktāṃ tvāṃ nāśayāmyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. “Fie upon you, O girl of sinful behaviour! You have defiled your own virginity. A stigma has been brought on me. It is bound to be known in all the three worlds.

Certainly, O base girl, you have obtained a husband by means of this misdeed. I shall destroy you already defiled by this sin.”

## \|\| 1.144.51 \|\|

*evamuktvā prahāraṃ sa yāvatkṣipati sanmuniḥ \|*  
*tāvaccitrāṃgado naṣṭo vyomamārgeṇa satvaram \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After saying thus the excellent sage was about to hurl the stick to strike when Citrāṅgada disappeared quickly through the path of the sky.

## \|\| 1.144.52 \|\|

*vivastrā sāpi tatraiva khinnāṃgī kāmasevayā \|*  
*na śaśāka kvacidgaṃtuṃ samutthāya tataḥ kṣitau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Stripped of her clothes and fatigued by love play (Phalavatī) could not get up from the ground and go somewhere else.

## \|\| 1.144.53 \|\|

*tataḥ kāṣṭhaprahāroghairhatvā tāṃ patitāṃ kṣitau \|*  
*mṛtāmiti parijñāya sa krodhaparivāritaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With a number of strokes of the stick he continuously thrashed the fallen maiden on the ground with excessive anger. He thought her dead (and ceased to beat).

## \|\| 1.144.54 \|\|

*tataścitrāṃgadasyāpi dadau śāpaṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā'kāśamārgeṇa gacchamānaṃ bhayāturam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On seeing the frightened Citrāṅgada passing through the sky, he uttered a curse on him:

## \|\| 1.144.55-56 \|\|

*ya eṣa kanyakāṃ mahyaṃ dharṣayitvā samutpatet \|*  
*sa patatvacirātpāpaśchinnapakṣa ivāṃḍajaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktaścalituṃ naiva ca kṣamaḥ \|*  
*etasminnantare bhūmau sa papāta nabhastalāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. “Let this sinful fellow who has ravished my daughter

and who tries to flee fall down immediately like a bird whose wings have been clipped. Let him be afflicted with leprosy and be incapable of even moving.” In the meantime, he did fall on the ground from the sky.

## \|\| 1.144.57 \|\|

*kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktaḥ sa ca citrāṃgado yuvā \|*  
*tatastaṃ sa muniḥ prāha kāṣṭhodyatakaraḥ krudhā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The young man Citrāṅgada was overtaken by the disease of leprosy. With a piece of wood raised up in his hand with anger, the sage said to him:

## \|\| 1.144.58 \|\|

*kastvaṃ pāpasamācāra yena me dharṣitā balāt \|*  
*kumārī tannayāmyeṣa tvāmadya yama śāsanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. “Who are you, O fellow of sinful activities? Who are you by whom the virgin had been ravished? Hence I shall send you to the abode of Yama.”

## \|\| 1.144.59 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ citrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena kṣetre'sminsamupāgataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

59\. I am a Gandharva, one of the (categories of) Heaven-dwellers. I am Citrāṅgada by name, I came to this holy spot in the course of my pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.144.60 \|\|

*tatastu kanyakāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmadevavaśaṃ gataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On seeing this girl, I wsas overcome by Kāma (sexual desire).

## \|\| 1.144.61 \|\|

*tataḥ sevitavānatra latāharmye janacyute \|*  
*tasmātkuru kṣamāṃ mahyaṃ dīnasya praṇatasya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Therefore I resorted to her in this bower of creepers isolated from people. So do forgive me. I am distressed myself and I readily bow down to you.

## \|\| 1.144.62 \|\|

*yathā vyādherbhavennāśo yathā syādgagane gatiḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'pi tvatprasādena svalpaḥ kopo hi sādhuṣu \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. With your favour, let this disease be eradicated. Let me have the freedom of movement in the sky. Indeed the anger in good men is meagre and short-lived.

## \|\| 1.144.63-65 \|\|

*jābāliruvāca \|*  
*īdṛgrūpadharastvaṃ hi mama vākyādbhaviṣyasi \|*  
*eṣāpi matsutā pāpā vastrahīnā sadedṛśī \|\| 63 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati na saṃdeho jīvayiṣyati cetkvacit \|*  
*yadyeṣā dhāsyati kvāpi vastraṃ gātre nije kvacit \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tannūnaṃ ca śiro'pyasyāḥ phaliṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā vikopaśca sa jagāma nijāśramam \|\| 65 \|\|*

Jābāli said:

63-65. Indeed, as per my utterance you will be in this form alone. This my sinful daughter shall always be nude like this. There is no doubt about it. If at all she comes back to life and if she were to wear any cloth, her head will burst undoubtedly.

After saying thus he got rid of his anger and went back to his hermitage.

## \|\| 1.144.66-67 \|\|

*citrāṃgado'pi tatraiva tayā sārdhaṃ tathā sthitaḥ \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya tatra kṣetre samāyayau \|\| 66 \|\|*

*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*gantuṃ citreśvare pīṭhe gaṇai raudraiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yoginībhiḥ pracaṇḍābhiḥ sārdhaṃ prāpte niśāmukhe \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Cirtāṅgada continued to be there along with her in that plight.

Once thereafter, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, the Moon-crested Lord came to that holy spot in order to sport about in the Citreśvara Pīṭha. He was surrounded by his terrible attendants and the fierce Yoginīs. It was at nightfall that he came.

## \|\| 1.144.68 \|\|

*atha prāpte niśārdhe tu yoginyastāḥ sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*mahāmāṃsaṃ mahāmāṃsamityūcurbhakṣaṇāya vai \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. When it was midnight the extremely terrible Yoginīs began to clamour for food saying, “The great (human) meat! The great meat (of humans)!”

## \|\| 1.144.69 \|\|

*nṛtyamānāḥ purastasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*saspardhā gaṇamukhyaistairnartamānaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They began to dance before the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas. In their devilish dances they vied with the chiefs of the Gaṇas dancing all round.

## \|\| 1.144.70 \|\|

*yastatra samaye tāsāṃ mahāmāṃsaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*maṃtrapūtaṃ sa saṃsiddhiṃ samavāpnoti vāṃchitām \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He who at that time offers to them the great meat (human flesh) sanctified by Mantras shall attain desired Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.144.71 \|\|

*madyaṃ māṃsaṃ tathā cānyannaivedyaṃ vā phalādikam \|*  
*tasya siddhiḥ samādiṣṭā yathā svahṛdaye sthitā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. If one offers liquor, meat or other food offering such as fruits etc., his Siddhi has been mentioned as anything cherished in his own heart.

## \|\| 1.144.72 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kanyā sā jābālisamudbhavā \|*  
*sa ca citrāṃgadastatra gatvā provāca sādaram \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. In the meantime the daughter of Jābāli and Citrāṅgada went there and spoke respectfully.”

## \|\| 1.144.73 \|\|

*asmadīyamidaṃ māṃsaṃ yoginyo harṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣayantu yathāsaukhyaṃ svayameva prakalpitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. “May the delighted Yoginīs eat comfortably our flesh that we offer ourselves voluntarily.”

## \|\| 1.144.74 \|\|

*atha taṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kuṣṭhavyādhisamāvṛtam \|*  
*vivastrāṃ kanyakāṃ tāṃ ca sarvāstā vismayānvitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On seeing the male being afflicted with leprosy and the girl stripped of her clothes, all of them were surprised.

## \|\| 1.144.75 \|\|

*te ca sarve gaṇā raudrāḥ sa ca devastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*papraccha kautukāviṣṭastatra citrāṃgadaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. All the Gaṇas of Rudra and the three-eyed Lord were surprised. The Lord prompted by curiosity asked Citrāṅgada:

## \|\| 1.144.76-77 \|\|

*kastvaṃ dhairyasamāyukto mahatsattve vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ prayacchasi jīvaṃ tvaṃ kīṭasyāpi suvallabham \|\| 76 \|\|*

*keyaṃ ca vasanaiṃrhīnā tvayā sārdhaṃ gatavyathā \|*  
*prayacchati nijaṃ dehaṃ yaddeyaṃ naiva kasyacit \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. “Who ṇre you, O bold one having great courage and strength? You are offering your very life which is endearing even to an insect.

Who is this maiden without clothes, without anguish, who offers along with you her own body that should not be given to anyone else?”

## \|\| 1.144.78 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa sarvamātmaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*yathā kanyāsamaṃ saṃgaḥ kṛtaḥ śāpaśca sanmuneḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

Sūta said:

78\. Then he recounted everything regarding his own act, how he had intercourse with the girl and how the good sage cursed.

## \|\| 1.144.79 \|\|

*tataścitrāṃgadaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa gandharvaṃ divaukasām \|*  
*tathārūpaṃ kṛpāviṣṭastataḥ provāca śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. On seeing Citrāṅgada, the Gandharva (one) among the Heaven-dwellers, in that form, Śaṅkara became sympathetic and said to him:

## \|\| 1.144.80 \|\|

*mama saṃdarśanaṃ prāpya na mṛtyurjāyate kvacit \|*  
*na vṛthā darśanaṃ caitattasmātprārthaya sādaram \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. “After seeing me no one meets death. Nor can my vision be futile. Hence request (for a boon) respectfully.”

## \|\| 1.144.81 \|\|

*citrāṃgada uvāca \|\| \|*  
*vyādhinā'haṃ sunirviṇṇastena devātra cāgataḥ \|*  
*yena vyādhikṣayo bhāvī dehanāśena śaṃkara \|\| 81 \|\|*

Citrāṅgada said:

81\. O Śaṅkara, I have become greatly affected due to this ailment. Hence, O Lord, I came here so that along with the destruction of the body there can be the eradication of the ailment too.

## \|\| 1.144.82 \|\|

*tasmātkuru kṣayaṃ vyādheryadi yacchasi me varam \|*  
*khecaratvaṃ punardehi yena svargaṃ vrajāmyaham \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Hence do destroy the disease. If you grant me any boon, give me back my ability to go freely through the sky so that I can go to Svarga.

## \|\| 1.144.83 \|\|

*śrīśaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ sthāpayātra malliṃgaṃ pīṭhe gandharvasattama \|*  
*tataścārādhaya prītyā yāvadvarṣamupasthitam \|\| 83 \|\|*

Śrī Śaṅkara said:

83\. Install my Liṅga on the sacred pedestal (Pīṭha) here, O most excellent one among Gandharvas. Then propitiate it with love and devotion for the period of a year.

## \|\| 1.144.84 \|\|

*yathāyathā supūjāṃ tvaṃ malliṃgasya kariṣyasi \|*  
*dinedine tathā vyādhestava nāśo bhaviṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. As you go on performing the excellent adoration of my Liṅga everyday, so your ailment will be getting eradicated.

## \|\| 1.144.85 \|\|

*tatastu khe gatiṃ prāpya punaḥ svargaṃ prayāsyasi \|*  
*matprasādānna sandehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then you will attain the ability to go through the sky and will go to Svarga with my favour. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that I have uttered.

## \|\| 1.144.86 \|\|

*eṣāpi kanyakā yasmātpraviṣṭā pīṭhamadhyataḥ \|*  
*tasmātphalavatīnāma yoginī sambhaviṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Since this maiden entered the area of the pedestal, she will become a Yoginī named Phalavatī.

## \|\| 1.144.87 \|\|

*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa nagnatvena vyavasthitā \|*  
*mukhyāmavāpsyate pūjāṃ vāṃchitaṃ ca pradāsyati \|*  
*pūjakānāṃ sthitaṃ citte śatasaṃkhyaguṇaṃ tadā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. She will become installed in this same naked form. She will be the chief object of worship. She will grant things cherished in the heart of those who worship. She will even grant the same a hundred-fold.

## \|\| 1.144.88 \|\|

*etāṃ saṃpūjayenmartyaḥ pīṭhametattataḥ param \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati tasyeṣṭā siddhirevaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. A man should worship her and thereafter the pedestal. If he worships so, he will attain the desired Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.144.89 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sā'tha harṣeṇa mahatā'nvitā \|*  
*yoginīvṛṃdamadhyasthā nṛtyaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. On being told thus she became extremely delighted. Standing in the centre of the group of Yoginīs, she began to dance.

## \|\| 1.144.90 \|\|

*evaṃ babhūva sā tatra yoginī ca varāṃganā \|*  
*tathā cakre paraṃ nṛtyaṃ yathā tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. It was thus that the excellent maiden became a Yoginī. She danced well and Maheśvara was pleased with it.

## \|\| 1.144.91-93 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tāṃ hṛṣṭaḥ sarvayoginisaṃnidhau \|*  
*anena tava nṛtyena gītena ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*parituṣṭosmi te vatse tasmācchṛṇu vaco mama \|*  
*niśīthe'dya dine prāpte yaste pūjāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 92 \|\|*

*surā māṃsānnasatkārairmaṃtrairāgamasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*sa bhaviṣyati tatkālaṃ śāpānugrahaśaktimān \|\| 93 \|\|*

91-93. On being delighted the Lord said to her in the presence of all the Yoginīs: “O dear maiden, I am pleased with this dance of yours as well as with the song sung. Hence listen to my words. On this day at mid-night, if a devotee worships you with the offerings of liquor, meat and cooked food uttering the Mantras taken from Āgamas, he will become at that very time one having the power to curse and bless.”

## \|\| 1.144.94 \|\|

*baṃdhanaṃ mohanaṃ cāpi śatroruccāṭanaṃ tathā \|*  
*kariṣyati na sandeho vaśīkaraṇameva ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. There is no doubt about it that he will have the following powers against his enemies: Bandhana (bondage), Mohana (fascination, enchanting), Uccāṭana (exorcising) and Vaśīkanaṇa (keeping under one’s control).

## \|\| 1.144.95 \|\|

*trikoṇaṃ kuṇḍamāsthāya diśāṃ pālānprapūjayet \|*  
*kṣetrapālaṃ ca sarvāstā devatā gamanodbhavāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Occupying the triangular Kuṇḍa, he shall adore the Guardians of the Quarters, the Kṣetrapāla and all those deities of the firmament.

## \|\| 1.144.96-97 \|\|

*tathā catvarapūjāṃ ca prakṛtvā vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*paścāttvāṃ pūjayitvā ca homaṃ yaśca kariṣyati \|\| 96 \|\|*

*śatruvāmapadotthena spṛṣṭena rajasā'thavā \|*  
*guggulena sahasrāṃtaṃ staṃbhanaṃ ca kariṣyati \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. He should then duly perform the worship of Catvara (the levelled ground kept ready for Yajña); then he should worship you and perform Homa with Guggula (fragrant gum resin) mixed with the dust of the left foot of the enemy. The devotee thereby attains the power of Staṃbhana (benumbing, stupefying) of a thousand (persons).

## \|\| 1.144.98 \|\|

*yaśca śatruṃ hṛdi sthāpya śatrūdvartanasaṃbhavam \|*  
*malaṃ dhātrīphalaiḥ sārdhaṃ mohanaṃ sa kariṣyati \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The devotee thinks about the enemy in his heart and mixes the unguents, the bodily dirt and Dhātrī fruits (embylic myrobalan) (for the Homa). He will be able to enchant people or the enemy (Mohana).

## \|\| 1.144.99-100 \|\|

*yaḥ śatroḥ snānajaṃ toyaṃ gṛhītvā cātha kardamam \|*  
*śivanirmālyasaṃyuktaṃ juhvayiṣyati pāvake \|\| 99 \|\|*

*tavāgre sa naro nūnaṃ śatrumuccāṭayiṣyati \|*  
*eṣopi tava saṃgena tava citrāṃgadaḥ priyaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpsyati ca satpūjāmanuṣaṃgāttvadudbhavāt \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Further, the devotee should collect the water wherein the enemy has bathed. It is then to be mixed with mud and Śivanirmālya (Remnants of the worship of Śiva) to be consigned to the sacred fire by way of Homa. The entire worship is to be performed before you and certainly the man outwits the enemy. This lover of yours, Citrāṅgada will get due worship by virtue of your contact.

## \|\| 1.144.101-104 \|\|

*phalavatyuvāca \|*  
*yadi deva prasanno me tathānyamapi sadvaram \|\| 101 \|\|*

*hṛdisthaṃ dehi me saukhyaṃ yena saṃjāyate'khilam \|*  
*pitā mamaiṣa jābālirnirmukto vasanaiḥ sadā \|\| 102 \|\|*

*ahaṃ yathā tathātraiva saṃtiṣṭhatu divāniśam \|*  
*yena saṃtāpamāyāti paśyanmama virodhinīm \|\| 103 \|\|*

*krīḍāṃ brāhmaṇavaṃśasya madyamāṃsasamudbhavām \|*  
*madyagandhaṃ samāghrāti māṃsaṃ paśyati saṃskṛtam \|*  
*māṃ svacchaṃdaratāṃ nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ yāti dinedine \|\| 104 \|\|*

Phalavatī said:

101-104. If, O Lord, you are pleased with me, do grant me another excellent boon whereby the pleasure cherished in my heart can be realized fully. Let this father of mine, Jābāli, also be stripped of his clothes always. Let him stand day and night in the manner that I stand.

Let him thereby become more distressed on seeing my acts involving use of liquor and meat contrary to the conventions of Brāhmaṇa families.

He should smell the (odour) of liquor and see meat consecrated. He shall also witness me engaged in free love play. Thereby he shall undergo misery day by day.

## \|\| 1.144.105 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhaviṣyati proktaṃ saṃjātaṃ cādhunā śubhe \|*  
*ahaṃ yāsyāmi kailāsaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭhātra yathoditā \|\| 105 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

105\. O splendid lady, this shall become as mentioned. It has already happened now. I shall go to Kailāsa. Do remain here as you are told.

## \|\| 1.144.106 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa bhagavānproktvā gataścādarśanaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*yoginyaścaiva tāḥ sarvāḥ svesve sthāne vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

Sūta said:

106\. After saying thus, Lord Hara vanished. All those Yoginīs remained settled in their respective abodes.

## \|\| 1.144.107 \|\|

*citrāṃgadopi tatraiva kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Citrāṅgada made an excellent palace there and installed the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.144.108 \|\|

*tataścārādhayāmāsa divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then he propitiated it alertly without lassitude day and night.

## \|\| 1.144.109 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte vyādhimuktaḥ surūpadhṛk \|*  
*vimānavaramārūḍho jagāma tridaśālayam \|*  
*so'pi jābālināmātha vivastra samapadyata \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Then at the end of a year he was rid of his disease and he regained excellent form. Riding on an excellent aerial chariot, he went to the abode of Devas. The sage named Jābāli remained naked.

## \|\| 1.144.110 \|\|

*janahāsyakaro loke sthitastatraiva sarvadā \|*  
*paśyamāno vikārāṃstānduḥkhitaḥ svasutodbhavān \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. He caused derisive laughter among the people and remained thus always ruefully observing the aberrations of his daughter.

## \|\| 1.144.111 \|\|

*tataśca garhayāmāsa strīṇāṃ janma mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tasminpīṭhe samāsādya duḥkhena mahatā'nvitaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The great sage having come near the Pīṭha (pedestal) became extremely distressed and censured the life and activities of women.

## \|\| 1.144.112-114 \|\|

*aho pāpātmanāṃ puṃsāṃ saṃbhaviṣyaṃti yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*yāsāmīdṛksamācāro dvijavaṃśodbhavāsvapi \|\| 112 \|\|*

*sakṛdeva mayā saṃgaḥ kṛto nāryā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*ājanmamaraṇaṃ yāvatpāpaṃ prāptaṃ yathedṛśam \|\| 113 \|\|*

*ye punastāsu saṃsaktāḥ sadaiva puruṣādhamāḥ \|*  
*kā teṣāṃ jāyate loke gatirvedmi na ciṃtayan \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. “Alas, such women come across sinful men, as have conduct like this although they are born of Brāhmaṇa families!

Only for once did I have close intimacy with a woman, but a sin like this extending from birth till death has been incurred.

On the other hand, there are base men who are enamoured of them always. What will be their destiny? Although I ponder over it, I do not understand.”

## \|\| 1.144.115 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya bruvāṇasya yoginyastāḥ krudhānvitāḥ \|*  
*tamūcurbrāhmaṇaṃ tatra ghṛṇayā parivāritam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Even as he was prattling thus, the infuriated Yoginīs surrounded the Brāhmaṇa with contempt and spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.144.116 \|\|

*yoginya ūcuḥ \|*  
*mā niṃdāṃ kuru mūḍhātmaṃstvaṃ strīṇāṃ yogamāśritaḥ \|*  
*etaccarācaraṃ viśvaṃ strībhiḥ saṃdhāryate yataḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

Yoginīs said:

116\. O deluded soul, you may have practiced yoga but do not censure women because this entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is sustained by women.

## \|\| 1.144.117 \|\|

*yābhiḥ saṃjanitaḥ śeṣaḥ kūrmaśca tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*yābhyāṃ saṃdhāryate pṛthvī yasyāṃ viśvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. It is by them that Śeṣa and Kūrma were given birth to. These two, Śeṣa and Kūrma, sustain and stabilize the earth and it is the earth whereon the universe is established.

## \|\| 1.144.118 \|\|

*dhanyeyaṃ te sutā mūḍha yā prāptā yogamuttamam \|*  
*prāptā ca paramaṃ sthānaṃ stokairevātra vāsaraiḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. O deluded fool, blessed indeed is your daughter who has acquired the excellent yoga in the course of a very few days.

## \|\| 1.144.119 \|\|

*tvaṃ punarmūrkhatāṃ prāptaśchāṃdasaṃ mārgamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*avidyayā samāyuktaḥ saṃsāre'tra bhramiṣyasi \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. You are foolish enough and cling to the path of the Chandas (Vedas). You are associated with Avidyā (ignorance) and roam about in the world.

## \|\| 1.144.120 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*striyo niṃdyatamāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāvasthāsu duḥkhadāḥ \|*  
*ihaloke pare caiva tābhyaḥ saukhyaṃ na labhyate \|\| 120 \|\|*

The sage said:

120\. All the women deserve to be censured in all conditions. They give only misery. Neither in this world nor in the other world can pleasure be derived from them.

## \|\| 1.144.121 \|\|

*yadarthaṃ nihataḥ śumbho niśumbhaśca mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*rāvaṇo daṇḍabhūpaśca tathānye'pi sahasraśaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. It is on account of them (women) that the great Asuras, Śuṃbha, Niśuṃbha, Rāvaṇa and Daṇḍabhūpa (King Daṇḍa) and thousands of others have been killed.

## \|\| 1.144.122 \|\|

*prāpya tādṛgdvijaṃ kāṃtaṃ gautamaṃ strīsvabhāvataḥ \|*  
*ahilyā śakramāsādya cakame śīlavarjitā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Despite the fact that she had such a brilliant husband as Brāhmaṇa Gautama, Ahalyā devoid of the conventional decorum, loved and resorted to Śakra.

## \|\| 1.144.123 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*yacca niṃdasi mūḍhātmansaṃti niṃdyāśca yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*tadvadasva mayā sārdhaṃ yena tvāṃ bodhayāmyaham \|\| 123 \|\|*

The girl said:

123\. O deluded one, you are going on censuring and trying to establish that young women are worthy of being censured. Well, speak with me so that I can make you sensible.

## \|\| 1.144.124 \|\|

*na te'sti hṛdaye buddhirna lajjā na dayā mune \|*  
*kimaṃtyajo'pi tatkarma kurute yattvayā kṛtam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. O sage, there is neither intellect nor shame nor mercy in your heart. Does even a base-born Śūdra commit the deed perpetrated by you?

## \|\| 1.144.125 \|\|

*ahaṃ tāvatprahāreṇa tvayā vyāpāditā'dhama \|*  
*strīhatyodbhavapāpasya na cintā vidhṛtā hṛdi \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. O base one, I was killed by you when you struck me with the piece of wood (stick). You never worried about the sin arising from the murder of a woman.

## \|\| 1.144.126 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa sutāyāśca kopāviṣṭena cetasā \|*  
*gacchaṃti pātakānyatra prāyaścittaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Your sin is all the more, because it was your own daughter that you murdered in the height of your anger. Of course, a few sins get dissolved through different kinds of expiation.

## \|\| 1.144.127 \|\|

*strīvadhotthaṃ punaryāti yadi tattvaṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*etanme na ca duḥkhaṃ syādyaddhatāsmi dvijādhama \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. But that arising from the murder of a woman? Say if there is any means whereby it will disappear. O mean Brāhmaṇa, I do not at all feel miserable for having been struck by you.

## \|\| 1.144.128 \|\|

*yacchaptā nagnasadbhāvaṃ nītā tatpātakaṃ ca te \|*  
*kalpāṃte'pi sudurbuddhe na saṃyāsyati kutracit \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. O highly evil-minded one, even at the end of a Kalpa, this sin of yours will not vanish—this sin caused by your curse whereby I was rendered nude forever.

## \|\| 1.144.129 \|\|

*tasmādbhuṃkṣva suduḥkhārtaḥ sthito'traiva mayā saha \|*  
*na bhūyo niṃdasi prāyo na ca vyāpādayiṣyasi \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Stay here itself along with me. Continue your misery and reap the fruit thereof. You will not dare to censure and you will not commit another murder.

## \|\| 1.144.130 \|\|

*aniṃdyā yoṣitaḥ sarvā naitā duṣyaṃti karhicit \|*  
*māsimāsi rajo hyāsāṃ duṣkṛtānyapakarṣati \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. All young maidens are not to be deemed censurable. They are not at all defiled. The monthly menstrual cycle takes away their sins.

## \|\| 1.144.131 \|\|

*muni ruvāca \|*  
*striyaḥ pāpasamācārā naitāḥ śudhyaṃti karhicit \|*  
*parakāṃte ratiryāsāmaṃtyajatvaṃ prayacchati \|\| 131 \|\|*

The sage said:

131\. Women are sinful in their conduct. They cannot be purified at all. Their attachment to another woman’s husband gives them the status of a Śūdra.

## \|\| 1.144.132 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*mā maivaṃ vada mūḍhātmannamedhyā iti yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*atra ślokaḥ purā gīto manunā taṃ nibodha me \|\| 132 \|\|*

The girl said:

132\. O deluded one, do not say that young midens are impure. In this connection there is a verse sung by Manu earlier. Know it from me.

## \|\| 1.144.133 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ pādato medhyā gāvo medhyāstu pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*ajāśvā mukhato medhyā striyo medhyāśca sarvataḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. “Brāhmaṇas are pure in their feet. Cows are pure in their hind parts. Goats and horses are pure in their mouths. Women are pure all over their person.”

## \|\| 1.144.134 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ sarvato medhyā gāvo medhyāśca sarvataḥ \|*  
*ajāśvā mukhato medhyā na medhyāśca striyaḥ kvacit \|\| 134 \|\|*

The sage said:

134\. Brāhmaṇas are pure everywhere. Cows are pure everywhere. Goats and horses are pure in their mouths. Women are not pure anywhere.

## \|\| 1.144.135 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*tasya ciṃtāmaṇirhaste tasya kalpadrumo gṛhe \|*  
*kuberaḥ kiṃkarastasya yasya syātkāminī gṛhe \|\| 135 \|\|*

The girl said:

135\. He who has a loving woman in his house has the Philosopher’s Stone (Cintāmaṇi) in his hand, and the wish-yielding Kalpa tree in his house. Kubera is a servant unto him.

## \|\| 1.144.136 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*tasyāpado'khilā duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tasyākhilaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*narakaḥ sarvatastasya yasya syātkāminīgṛhe \|\| 136 \|\|*

The sage said:

136\. He who has a lustful woman in his house has all the adversities. Everything in his house is miserable. Naraka is all round him.

## \|\| 1.144.137 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*yāni kānyatra saukhyāni bhogasthānāni yāni ca \|*  
*dharmārthakāmajātāni tāni strībhyo bhavaṃti hi \|\| 137 \|\|*

The girl said:

137\. It is from women that all these originate: wherever things are pleasurable, whatever things yield enjoyment, everything yielded by virtue, wealth and love.

## \|\| 1.144.138 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*yāni kāni suduḥkhāni kleśāni yāni dehinām \|\|*  
*yāni kaṣṭānyaniṣṭāni strībhyastāni bhavaṃti ca \|\| 138 \|\|*

The sage said:

138\. It is from women that all these originate: whatever yields misery and pain unto embodied beings, whatever is desagreeable and undesirable.

## \|\| 1.144.139 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣānstrī caturo'pi catasṛbhiḥ \|*  
*vahnipradakṣiṇābhistānvivāhe'pi pradarśayet \|\| 139 \|\|*

The girl said:

139\. Through the four circumambulations of fire at the time of marriage a woman displays the four Puruṣārthas (aims in life), viz. Dharma, wealth, love and salvation.

## \|\| 1.144.140 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*saṃsārabhramaṇaṃ nārī prathame'pi samāgame \|*  
*vahnipradakṣiṇānyāyavyājenaiva pradarśayet \|\| 140 \|\|*

The sage said:

140\. At the very first close contact under the pretext of the (religious rite of) circumambulations of fire, a woman makes the roaming (cycle of coming and going) in the worldly existence manifest.

## \|\| 1.144.141 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*ke nāma na virajyaṃti jñānāḍhyā api mānavāḥ \|*  
*karṇāṃtalagnanetrāṃtāṃ dṛṣṭvā pīna payodharām \|\| 141 \|\|*

The girl said:

141\. Who among even the wise men, becomes disinterested on seeing a woman of plump breasts and wide eyes extending upto the ears?

## \|\| 1.144.142 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*ke nāma na vinaśyaṃti mūḍhajñānā nitaṃbinīm \|*  
*ramyabuddhyopasarpaṃti ye jvālāḥ śalabhā iva \|\| 142 \|\|*

The sage said:

142\. What (that is all) people of deluded wisdom who approach a big-buttocked woman thinking her to be beautiful, do not get perished like fire-flies in flames? (All perish.)

## \|\| 1.144.143 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*nirmukhau ca kaṭhorau ca proddhatau ca manoramau \|*  
*strīstanau sevate dhanyo madhumāṃse viśeṣataḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

The girl said:

143\. Only a blessed man resorts to the breasts of a woman that are Nirmukha (having no face, no prominent nipple), Kaṭhora (hard), Proddhata (haughty, protruding) and manorama (charming to the mind) and specially one who also resorts to liquor and meat.

## \|\| 1.144.144 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*ābhoginau maṃḍalinau tatkṣaṇānmuktakaṃcukau \|*  
*varamāśīviṣau spṛṣṭau na tu patnyāḥ payodharau \|\| 144 \|\|*

The sage said:

144\. It is better to touch two serpents rather than the two breasts of the wife though both are Ābhogins (having big body and expanded hood yielding pleasures), Maṇḍalis (circular in coils), Muktakañcuka (have bodice stripped; having shed the slough) at that time.

## \|\| 1.144.145 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*na cāsāṃ racanāmātraṃ kevalaṃ ramyamaṃgibhiḥ \|*  
*pariṣvaṃgo'pi rāmāṇāṃ saukhyāya pulakāya ca \|\| 145 \|\|*

The girl said:

145\. Not only the structure of the limbs of women is beautiful but their embrace also gives pleasure and causes horripilation.

## \|\| 1.144.146 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*na cāsāṃ racanāmātraṃ ramyaṃ syātpāpadaṃ dṛśaḥ \|*  
*vapuḥ spṛṣṭaṃ vināśāya strīṇāṃ pretya narakāya ca \|\| 146 \|\|*

The sage said:

146\. The structure of the limbs of these is not merely beautiful but accords sin to the eyes. The body of women, if touched, is conducive to ruin and to Naraka after death.

## \|\| 1.144.147 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*ko nāma na sukhī loke ko nāma sukṛtī na ca \|*  
*spṛhaṇīyatamaḥ ko na strījano yasya rajyate \|\| 147 \|\|*

The girl said:

147\. If womenfolk begin to love one, who is not happy in the world, who is not meritorious and who is not covetable?

## \|\| 1.144.148 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*ko na muktiṃ vrajettatra ko na śasyataro bhavet \|*  
*ko na syātkṣemasaṃyuktaḥ strījane yo na rajyate \|\| 148 \|\|*

The sage said:

148\. If one does not take interest in womenfolk, who does not attain salvation, who is not praiseworthy, who is not happy and well-off.

## \|\| 1.144.149 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*saṃsārāṃtaḥ prasuptasya kīṭasyāpi prarocate \|*  
*strīśarīraṃ narasyātra kiṃ punarna vivekinaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

The girl said:

149\. The female body appeals exceedingly even to an insect sleeping in the world, and to a discriminating man still more so.

## \|\| 1.144.150 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*amedhyajā tasya yathā tathā tadrocanaṃ kṛmeḥ \|*  
*tathā saṃsārasūtasya strīśarīraṃ ca kāminaḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

The sage said:

150\. The appeal of the female body to a lustful man in the world is like that (appeal) to a worm arising from rubbish.

## \|\| 1.144.151 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*saukhyasthānaṃ nṛṇāṃ kiṃcidvedhasā 'nyadapaśyatā \|*  
*śāśvataṃ ciṃtayitvātha strīratnamidamāhṛtam \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. The creator was thinking of (creating) a permanent and pleasing spot unto men. Not being able to see anything else, Strīratna (jewel of a woman) was brought (created).

## \|\| 1.144.152 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*baṃdhanaṃ jagataḥ kiṃcidvedhasā'nyadapaśyatā \|*  
*strīrūpeṇa tataḥ kopi pāśo'yaṃ strīmayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

The sage said:

152\. A noose in the form of a woman was made by the creator who could not see anything else that could bind the world.

## \|\| 1.144.153 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa muniśārdūlastayātīva samāgame \|*  
*niruttarīkṛto yāvattataḥ prāha nijāṃ sutām \|\| 153 \|\|*

Sūta said:

153\. Thus the tiger among sages was rendered incapable of making any reply by her. Then he said to his daughter:

## \|\| 1.144.154 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*tvayā saha na saṃvādo mayā kāryo'dhunā kvacit \|*  
*yā tvaṃ bālāpi māmevaṃ niṣedhayasi sarvataḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

The sage said:

154\. Now I should not hold further conversation with you. Though a girl you have negated (refuted) me in every respect.

## \|\| 1.144.155 \|\|

*tasmāddhanyataraṃ manye ahamātmānamadya vai \|*  
*yasya me tvaṃ sutā īdṛgīdṛkchāstravicakṣaṇā \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. I consider myself highly blessed because I have a daughter like you, an able exponent of the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.144.156 \|\|

*tasmānna me mahābhāge kopaḥ svalpo'pi vidyate \|*  
*tasmādyathecchayā krīḍāṃ kuru yoginimadhyagā \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Hence, O highly esteemed woman, I have not even the vestige of anger in me. So engage yourself in sports as you please in the midst of the Yoginīs.

## \|\| 1.144.157 \|\|

*tataḥ sā lajjitā dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ snehavatsalam \|*  
*praṇipatya punaḥprāha yoginīmadhyasaṃsthitā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. On seeing her father so very affectionate she became bashful. Standing amongst the Yoginīs she bowed to him and spoke again:

## \|\| 1.144.158-159 \|\|

*ajñānādyadi vā jñānāttvaṃ niṣiddho mayā prabho \|*  
*kṣaṃtavyaṃ sakalaṃ me'dya vālikāyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

*atra pīṭhe samāgatya prathamaṃ te dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ sarve kariṣyaṃti mānavā bhaktitatparāḥ \|*  
*paścācca sarvapīṭhasya yāsyaṃti ca parāṃ gatim \|\| 159 \|\|*

158-159. “Whether through knowledge or ignorance, O holy Sir, if you have been negated by me, may it be forgiven especially because I am only a girl.

After coming to this Pīṭha, all the excellent Brāhmaṇas will perform your worship at the outset and only later the adoration of all the other deities in the Pīṭha. Devout men thus will attain the greatest goal.”

## \|\| 1.144.160 \|\|

*evaṃ sā tatra saṃjātā jābālimunisaṃbhavā \|*  
*jābāliśca muniśreṣṭhastathā citrāṃgadeśvaraḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. It was thus that the daughter of Jābāli, the sage, happen to be there. So also the excellent sage Jābāli and Citrāṅgadeśvara.

## \|\| 1.144.161-164 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi yasteṣāṃ pūjāṃ martyaḥ samācaret \|*  
*divasedivase tatra sa siddhiṃ samavāpnuyāt \|\| 161 \|\|*

*nāsādhyaṃ vidyate kiṃcittāvadatra dharātale \|*  
*pūjyate bhūmipālādyairbhogāndivyāṃstathā labhet \|\| 162 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena sa muniḥ sā ca kanyakā \|*  
*pūjanīyā viśeṣeṇa sa devo'tha maheśvaraḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātamākhyānaṃ sarvakāmadam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva ihaloke paratra ca \|\| 164 \|\|*

161-164. A man who performs the worship of all the three everyday shall attain Siddhi. There is nothing here on the earth which cannot be achieved. Thus the narrative that accords all cherished desires has been told to you. It yields all benefits to those who read and listen both in this world and in the other world.

## Chapter 145 - Greatness of Amarakeśvara Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.145.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yattvayā kathitaṃ sūta na mṛtā sā kumārikā \|*  
*hatā raudraprahāraiśca kautukaṃ tanmahattaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yato bhūyaḥ prasaṃjātā yoginī haratuṣṭidā \|*  
*yattvārthaṃ sarvamācakṣva kāraṇaṃ ca tadadbhutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

\[Full title: Greatness of Amarakeśvara (Amaraka-īśvara) Kṣetra\]

The sages said:

1-2. O sūta, it has been said by you that the girl did not die though she was killed with terrible blows. Here we have become very curious: How did she survive as the Yoginī giving delight to Hara? Describe the whole thing and the wonderful reason.

## \|\| 1.145.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā praviṣṭā samaṃ tena supuṇyamamareśvaram \|*  
*māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ na mṛtyuryatra vidyate \|\| 3 \|\| \|\| \|*  
*api caivāyuṣaḥ śeṣe kimutākālato dvijāḥ \|*  
*tena no nidhanaṃ prāptā hatāpi sudṛḍhaṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. Along with him (i.e. Citrāṅgada) she entered the highly meritorious Amareśvara on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of Māgha. There is no question of meeting death therein.

## \|\| 1.145.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā praviṣṭā samaṃ tena supuṇyamamareśvaram \|*  
*māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ na mṛtyuryatra vidyate \|\| 3 \|\| \|\| \|*  
*api caivāyuṣaḥ śeṣe kimutākālato dvijāḥ \|*  
*tena no nidhanaṃ prāptā hatāpi sudṛḍhaṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*
