4\. O Brāhmaṇas, there is no death even when there remain no span of life. There is no question of premature death. Therefore, although she was struck terribly, she did not meet death.

## \|\| 1.145.5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*amareśvara ityukto yo devo hyamaratvadaḥ \|*  
*kena saṃsthāpito hyatra kiṃprabhāvaśca kīrtaya \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

5\. You have mentioned a deity name Amareśvara, the bestower of immortality. By whom was the deity installed there? What is its power? Do narrate.

## \|\| 1.145.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*aditiśca ditiścaiva prajāpatisute śubhe \|*  
*kṛte purātirūpāḍhye kaśyapena mahātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. There were two splendid daughters of Prajāpati. They were extremely beautiful. They were Aditi and Diti. They were married to the noble-souled Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 1.145.7 \|\|

*adityāṃ vibudhā jātā diteścaiva tu daityapāḥ \|\| \|*  
*teṣāṃ sāpatnyabhāvena mahadvairamupasthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Devas were born of Aditi and Daityas of Diti. Being sons of rival cowives, they become great enemies.

## \|\| 1.145.8 \|\|

*atha daityaiḥ surā dhvastāḥ kṛtāścānye parāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*anye tu bhayasaṃtrastā diśo jagmuḥ kṣatāṃgakāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Some of the Suras were killed by the Daityas. Other were driven away with faces averted. Those who were frightened and those whose limbs were wounded fled to all the quarters.

## \|\| 1.145.9 \|\|

*tato duḥkhasamāyuktā devamātātra saṃsthitā \|*  
*tapaścakre divānaktaṃ śivadhyānaparāyaṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. So the mother of Devas settled here with great sorrow. Devoted to the meditation of Śiva, she performed penance day and night.

## \|\| 1.145.10 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyāstapaḥsthāyā gate yugacatuṣṭaye \|*  
*nirbhidya dharaṇīpṛṣṭhaṃ śivaliṃgaṃ samutthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Four Yugas passed by even as she was engaged in her austere penance. Then a Śivaliṅga pierced through the surface of the earth and rose up.

## \|\| 1.145.11 \|\|

*tatastasmai kṛtānandā stutvā stotraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭāṃgapraṇipātena namaścakre samāhitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The delighted lady eulogized the Lord with various kinds of prayers and made obeisance to him with great concentration falling at the feet with Aṣṭāṅgas (eight limbs) touching the ground.

## \|\| 1.145.12 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vāṇī saṃjātā gaganāṃgaṇe \|*  
*śarīrarahitā divyā meghagambhīraniḥsvanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the meantime a divine voice arose in the firmament without a body. It had the rumbling majestic sound of clouds.

## \|\| 1.145.13 \|\|

*varaṃ prārthaya kalyāṇi yaste hṛdi vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*prasanno'haṃ pradāsyāmi tavādya śaśiśekharaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “I am the Moon-crested Lord. I am pleased with you. Request for a boon cherished in the heart. I shall grant it to you.”

## \|\| 1.145.14 \|\|

*aditiruvāca \|*  
*mama putrāḥ suraśreṣṭha hanyante yudhi dānavaiḥ \|*  
*tatkuruṣva gatāyāsānavadhyānraṇamūrdhani \|\| 14 \|\|*

Aditi said:

14\. O most excellent one among Suras, my sons are being killed in battle by Dānavas. Render them free from sufferings. Let them not be killed in battle.

## \|\| 1.145.15 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*etalliṃgaṃ madīyaṃ ye spṛṣṭvā yāsyaṃti saṃyuge \|*  
*avadhyāste bhaviṣyanti yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhe \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

15\. O splendid lady, those who touch this Liṅga and go to the battle front cannot be killed in the course of a year.

## \|\| 1.145.16-18 \|\|

*anyo'pi mānavo yo'tra caturdaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*māghamāsasya kṛṣṇāyāṃ prakariṣyati jāgaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*so'pi saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadbhaviṣyati nirāmayaḥ \|*  
*api mṛtyudine prāpte yo'sminnāyatane śubhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

*āgamiṣyati taṃ mṛtyurdūrātparihariṣyati \|*  
*evamuktvātha sā vāṇī virarāma tataḥ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Any other man with great concentration who keeps awake in the night of the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Māgha, shall be free from ailments for the period of a year. If a man comes to this splendid shrine on the day he is destined to die, the god of Death will avoid him from afar.

After saying thus, the voice ceased.

## \|\| 1.145.19 \|\|

*aditiścāpi santuṣṭā hataśeṣānsutāṃstataḥ \|*  
*samānīyātha talliṃgaṃ teṣāmeva nyadarśayat \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ māhātmyaṃ yadvaroditam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Aditi too was pleased. She summoned the surviving sons and showed the Liṅga to them. She told them everything that the voice had said while granting the boon.

## \|\| 1.145.20 \|\|

*tataste vibudhāḥ sarve talliṃgaṃ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*pratijagmustuṣṭiyuktāḥ śastrāṇyādāya tānprati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then all the Devas bowed down to that Liṅga and taking all the weapons with them, joyously marched against them (Daityas).

## \|\| 1.145.21 \|\|

*yatra te dānavā hṛṣṭāḥ sthitāḥ śakrapade śubhe \|*  
*svargabhogasamāyuktā nandanāṃtarvyavasthitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They went to the place where the Dānavas were present in the auspicious region of Śakra stationing themselves in the Nandana garden. There they were enjoying the pleasures of Svarga.

## \|\| 1.145.22 \|\|

*atha te dānavā dṛṣṭvā saṃprāptāṃstridivaukasaḥ \|*  
*sahasā saṃgarārthāya nānāśastradharānbahūn \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Dānavas saw many Heaven-dwellers arriving suddenly with various kinds of weapons for the sake of fighting.

## \|\| 1.145.23 \|\|

*rathavaryānsamāruhya dhṛtaśastrāstravarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ sammukhā jagmurgarjamānā ghanā iva \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They equipped themselves with weapons and coats of mail and got into the excellent chariots. Like roaring and rumbling clouds, they marched ahead for the battle.

## \|\| 1.145.24 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*roṣapreritacittānāṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A big battle ensued between the Devas and the Dānavas. Incited by anger in their minds, they were not afraid of death (They made god of Death to recede).

## \|\| 1.145.25 \|\|

*tataste vibudhāḥ sarve haralabdhavarāstadā \|*  
*jaghnurdaityānasaṃkhyātācchitaiḥ śastrairanekadhā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then all those Devas who had obtained the boon from Hara killed innumerable Daityas with many sharp weapons.

## \|\| 1.145.26 \|\|

*hataśeṣāśca ye teṣāṃ te tyaktvā tridaśālayam \|*  
*palāyanakṛtotsāhāḥ praviṣṭā makarālayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Those who survived among them abandoned the abode of Devas. Fleeing with great effort they entered the sea.

## \|\| 1.145.27 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraḥ samāpede svarājyaṃ dānavairhṛtam \|*  
*yadāsītpūrvakāle tatsamagraṃ hatakaṇṭakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then Śakra regained his kingdom that had been taken by the Dānavas. He got the entire dominion intact. He ruled over it after destroying all the thorns (enemies).

## \|\| 1.145.28 \|\|

*tataste dānavāḥ śeṣā jñātvā talliṃgasaṃbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vṛṣanāthasya kṣetrasyāsyodbhavasya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The remaining Dānavas came to know of the greatness of that Liṅga and the origin of the holy shrine of the Bull-emblemed Lord.

## \|\| 1.145.29-31 \|\|

*śukreṇa kathitaṃ sarvaṃ māghakṛṣṇe niśāgame \|*  
*caturdaśyāṃ śucirbhūtvā yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*kālāghrāto'pi na prāṇaiḥ sa pumāṃstyajyate kvacit \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tasmādyūyaṃ samāsādya talliṃgaṃ taddine niśi \|*  
*pūjayadhvaṃ mahābhāgā yena syurmṛtyuvarjitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yāvatsaṃvatsarasyātaṃ satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*yathā te devasaṃghāśca tatprabhāvādasaṃśayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Everything was told by Śukra: “If any devotee remains pure on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of Māgha and worships that Liṅga, he shall never become bereft of his life even though grasped by Kāla.

Hence, O highly esteemed ones, ye all resort to that Liṅga at night on that day and worship duly. Thereby you shall be devoid of death.

Just like those groups of Devas you too do worship till the end of the year. By the power thereof, you shall be free from death. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that has been spoken by me.”

## \|\| 1.145.32 \|\|

*atha taṃ dānavendrāṇāṃ maṃtraṃ jñātvā sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*nāradādbrāhmaṇaḥ putrādbhayatrastamanāstataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. From Nārada, the son of Brahmā, the Lord of Suras came to know of the secret plan of the leading Dānavas. Thereby he became greatly frightened in his mind.

## \|\| 1.145.33 \|\|

*maṃtraṃ cakre samaṃ devaistatra devasya rakṣaṇe \|*  
*yathā syādudyamaḥ samyaktasminnahani sarvadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He had consultation with the Devas for devising the means of guarding the deity that day. Their endeavour (to protect) should be perfect for that purpose.

## \|\| 1.145.34 \|\|

*koṭayastu trayastriṃśaddevānāṃ sāyudhāstataḥ \|*  
*rakṣārthaṃ tasya liṃgasya tasminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ susaṃnaddhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All the thirty-three crores of Devas with their weapons settled in that holy spot for protecting that deity on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Māgha. They prepared themselves for the purpose of striking.

## \|\| 1.145.35 \|\|

*atha te dānavā dṛṣṭvā tāndevāṃstatra saṃsthitān \|*  
*bhayasaṃtrastamanaso dudruvuḥ sarvato diśam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing the Devas already established there the Dānavas became extremely frightened. They fled in all directions.

## \|\| 1.145.36 \|\|

*atha prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṇḍale \|*  
*bhūya eva surāḥ sarve maṃtraṃ cakruḥ parasparam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When the day dawned fully and the solar disc rose up, the Suras took counsel with one another again:

## \|\| 1.145.37-39 \|\|

*yadyetatkṣetramutsṛjya gamiṣyāmaḥ surālayam \|*  
*liṃgametatsamabhyetya pūjayiṣyaṃti dānavāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tato'vadhyā bhaviṣyaṃti te'pi sarve yathā vayam \|*  
*tasmādatraiva tiṣṭhāmastrayastriṃśatpranāyakāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*koṭīnāmeva sarveṣāṃ śeṣā gacchantu tatra ca \|*  
*sahasrākṣeṇa saṃyuktāḥ svarge svapararakṣakāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. “If we are to go to Svarga leaving the holy spot, the Dānavas will approach the Liṅga and worship it.

They will be free from being killed like us. Hence we all the thirty-three chiefs shall stay here. All the remaining ones of the crores of Devas may go back along with the Thousandeyed One and remain as the protectors of heaven from the enemies.”

## \|\| 1.145.40-41 \|\|

*tato'ṣṭau vasavastatra dvādaśārkāstathaiva ca \|*  
*ekādaśāpare rudrā nāsatyau dvau ca sundarau \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ete talliṃgarakṣārthaṃ tasminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*śeṣāḥ śakrasamāyuktāḥ prajagmustridaśālayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Thereupon, eight Vasus, twelve Arkas, eleven Rudras and the two handsome Nāsatyas (Aśvins) remained in the holy spot for protecting that Liṅga. The others went to the abode of Devas along with Śakra.

## \|\| 1.145.42 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ prabhāvaṃ liṃgaṃ tu devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ paripṛṣṭaṃ yadadityā sthāpitaṃ purā \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sūta said:

42\. The Liṅga of the trident-bearing Lord of Devas which had been installed formerly by Adith has such a power. It was about this that you have asked me.

## \|\| 1.145.43 \|\|

*yasmānna vidyate mṛtyustena dṛṣṭena dehinām \|*  
*amarākhyaṃ tato liṃgaṃ vikhyātaṃ bhuvanatraye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The Liṅga has become well known by the name of Amara in all the three worlds, because if it is visited, embodied beings will never meet death.

## \|\| 1.145.44-45 \|\|

*yasmindeśe'pi sā kanyā hatā tena dvijanmanā \|*  
*jābālinā sukruddhena tasya devasya maṃdire \|\| 44 \|\|*

*āsīttatra dine kṛṣṇā māghamāsa caturdaśī \|*  
*tena no nidhanaṃ prāptā suhatā'pi tapasvinī \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. It was on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of Māgha, that the girl was struck by the infuriated Brāhmaṇa Jābāli. The place was the same. Therefore the poor girl did not meet death though hit with force.

## \|\| 1.145.46 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ tasya liṃgasya sambhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the origin and greatness of that Liṅga has been narrated to you. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.145.47 \|\|

*yaścaitatpaṭhate bhaktyā tasya liṃgasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*apamṛtyubhayaṃ tasya kathaṃcinnaiva jāyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If a person reads this with devotion in the presence of that Liṅga, he will never have the danger of premature death at any cost.

## \|\| 1.145.48 \|\|

*tasyāgre'sti śubhaṃ kuṇḍaṃ pūritaṃ svacchavāriṇā \|*  
*adityā nirmitaṃ devyā snānārthaṃ cātmanaḥ kṛte \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In front of it, there is the splendid Kuṇḍa filled with clear water. It was made by the fair lady Aditi for the purpose of her own bath.

## \|\| 1.145.49 \|\|

*snānaṃ kṛtvā narastasminyastalliṃgaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*karoti jāgaraṃ rātrau tasminneva dinedine \|*  
*so'dyāpi vatsaraṃ yāvannāpamṛtyumavāpnuyāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even today the same effect continues. A man who takes his holy bath therein, visits that Liṅga and keeps awake there itself everyday, shall not have premature death for the period of a year.

## Chapter 146 - Greatness of Amareśvara Kuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.146.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ādityānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vasurudrādikāśvinām \|*  
*pratyekaśaḥ samācakṣva nāmāni tvaṃ mahāmate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vṛṣadhvajaśca śarvaśca mṛgavyādhastṛtīyakaḥ \|*  
*ajaikapādahirbudhnyaḥ pinākī ṣaṣṭha eva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dahanaśceśvaraścaiva kapālī navamastathā \|*  
*vṛṣākapistu daśamo rudrastryaṃbaka eva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

\[Full title: Greatness of Amareśvara (Amara-īśvara) Kuṇḍa\]

Note: This chapter enumerates (by names) the thirty-three Devas protecting the Kuṇḍa and mentions the days on which these should be propitiated.

The sages said:

1-3. O highly intelligent one, enumerate separately the names of all the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras and Aśvins.

## \|\| 1.146.4 \|\|

*dhuro dhruvaśca somaśca makhaścaivānilo'nalaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

The eleven Rudras are: Vṛṣadhvaja, Śarva, Mṛgavyādha (the third), Ajaikapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Pinākin (the sixth), Dahana, Īśvara, Kapālin (the ninth), Vṛṣākapi (the tenth) and Tryaṃbaka.

4\. The following are glorified as the eight Vasus: Dhura, Dhruva, Soma, Makha, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.146.5-6 \|\|

*varuṇaśca tathā sūryo bhānuḥ khyātaśca tāpanaḥ \|*  
*iṃdraścaivāryamā caiva dhātā caiva bhagastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gabhastirdharmarājaśca svarṇaretā divākaraḥ \|*  
*mitraśca vāsudevaśca dvādaśaite ca bhāskarāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The following twelve are Bhāskaras (Ādityas): Varuṇa Sūrya, Bhānu, Tāpana, Indra, Aryaman. Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Gabhasti, Dharmarāja, Svarṇaretas, Divākara, Mitra and Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.146.7 \|\|

*nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca khyātāvetau tathāśvinau \|*  
*devavaidyau mahābhāgau tvāṣṭrīgarbhasamudbhavau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Nāsatya and Dasra are the well known Aśvins. They are the highly esteemed physicians of Devas. They were born of the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ.

## \|\| 1.146.8 \|\|

*trayastriṃśatsamākhyātā ete ye suranāyakāḥ \|*  
*kṣetre'traivāsthitā nityaṃ dānavānāṃ vadhāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. These leaders of Suras are the thirty-three well-known ones settled in the holy spot for the purpose of destroying the Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.146.9 \|\|

*yastānsaṃpūjayedbhaktyā puruṣaḥ saṃyateṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*yathoktadivase prāpte nāpamṛtyuḥ prajāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A man with well-controlled sense-organs who devoutly worships them on the said day will not meet with premature death.

## \|\| 1.146.10 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ rudrāḥ pūjyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tasminkṣetre viśeṣeṇa vāṃchadbhiḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Rudras should be worshipped on the eighth and foruteenth lunar days by knowers who desire the greatest position. They shall perform special adorations in that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.146.11 \|\|

*daśamyāṃ vasavaḥ pūjyāstathāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*svargaṃ samīhamānaiśca vilāsairvividhaistathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Vasus should be worshipped on the eighth lunar day in particular and on the tenth lunar day by those who desire Svarga along with different kinds of graceful charms.

## \|\| 1.146.12 \|\|

*saptamyāmatha ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca pūjanīyā divākarāḥ \|*  
*ye vāṃchanti narāḥ sattvaṃ paripaṃthivivarjitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Ādityas should be worshipped on the sixth and seventh lunar days by men who desire strength (to be) devoid of enemies.

## \|\| 1.146.13 \|\|

*devavaidyau tathā pūjyau dvādaśyāṃ vyādhisaṃkṣayam \|*  
*ye vāṃchanti sadā martyā nīrujā sambhavaṃti te \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The physicians of Devas should be worshipped on the twelfth lunar day by those men who desire the destruction of ailments. They become rid of their ailments.

## Chapter 147 - Dialogue between Vyāsa and Śuka

## \|\| 1.147.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti devaḥ putraprado nṛṇām \|*  
*vaṭikeśvara nāmā ca sarvapāpaharo haraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Further there is another deity there who is the bestower of sons on men. It is Śiva named Vaṭikeśvara and he dispels all sins.

## \|\| 1.147.2 \|\|

*yasminvaṭikayā pūrvaṃ tapastaptaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*prāptā putraṃ śuke yāte vanaṃ vyāsātkapiṃjalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there Vaṭikā performed a penance formerly, and obtained from Vyāsa a son, Kapiñjala, when Śuka went to the forest.

## \|\| 1.147.3-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasyāsau vaṭikā tatra kathaṃ taptavatī tapaḥ \|*  
*kasmādgṛhaṃ parityaktvā śuko'pi vanamāśritaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kathaṃ kapijalaṃ putraṃ vyāsāllebhe śucismitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

3-4. Whose daughter was Vaṭikā? Why did she perform penance there? Why did Śuka abandon his father and seek refuge in the forest? How did the lady of pure smiles obtain Kapiñjala as son from Vyāsa?

## \|\| 1.147.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsīdvyāsasya vipreṃdrāḥ kalatrārthaṃ matiḥ kvacit \|*  
*niṣkāmasya praśāṃtasya sarvajñasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, once Vyāsa was inclined to take a wife unto himself though he was devoid of lust. The noble-souled one was omniscient and quiescent.

## \|\| 1.147.6-7 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣayamanuprāpte vaṃśe kurusamudbhave \|*  
*vicitravīryamāsādya pārthivaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*satyavatyāḥ samādeśāttasya kṣetre tataḥ param \|*  
*sa putrāñjanayāmāsa trīñchūrānpāṃḍupūrvakān \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Once the Kuru race became extinct ending with King Vicitravīrya, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

Thereupon, at the bidding of Satyavatī, he begot three heroic sons including Pāṇḍu in the wives of Vicitravīrya.

## \|\| 1.147.8 \|\|

*vānaprasthavrate tiṣṭhansakṛnmaithunatatparaḥ \|*  
*kṣetrajaistanayairvaṃśe kurostasmādupasthite \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus while he was in the stage of Vānaprastha, he had a desire for sexual intercourse once. Therefrom the race of Kuru was revived through the sons born of Kṣetra (wives of the dead king Vicitravīrya).

## \|\| 1.147.9 \|\|

*tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa bhāryāmadya karomyaham \|*  
*gārhasthyenātha dharmeṇa sādhayāmi śubhāṃ gatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then he thought thus, ‘I shall take a wife unto me. Through the rites of a householder, I shall attain excellent goal.’

## \|\| 1.147.10 \|\|

*tataḥ sa prārthayāmāsa jābāliṃ tu sutāṃ śubhām \|*  
*vaṭikākhyāṃ śubhāṃ kanyāṃ sa dadau tasya satvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then he requested Jābāli for his splendid daughter, he immediately gave him his splendid daughter named Vaṭikā.

## \|\| 1.147.11 \|\|

*tatastayā sametaḥ sa vanavāsaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*vānaprasthāśrame tiṣṭhankṛtamaithunatatparaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he began his residence in the forest in her company. Continuing to abide by the Vānaprastha stage, he became inclined to have sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 1.147.12 \|\|

*tato garbhavatī jajñe piṃjalā tasya pārśvataḥ \|*  
*ṛtau mohanamāsādya vyāsātsatyavatīsutāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then Piñjalā (Vaṭikā) became pregnant, thanks to him. During the prescribed days of the menstrual cycle, she received the semen from Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī.

## \|\| 1.147.13 \|\|

*atha yāti parāṃ vṛddhiṃ sa garbhastatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*udare vyāsabhāryāyāḥ śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The foetus developed gradually in the womb of Vyāsa’s wife like the moon in the bright half of month.

## \|\| 1.147.14 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃgacchatastasya vṛddhiṃ garbhasya nityaśaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśābdā atikrāṃtā na janma samavāpnuyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The foetus thus attained development and twelve years passed by. But no delivery took pace.

## \|\| 1.147.15 \|\|

*yatkiṃcicchṛṇute tatra garbhastho'hi vacaḥ kvacit \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ hṛdisaṃsthaṃ ca cakre prajñāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The child in the womb was endowed with great intellect. Staying there whatever word he happened to hear, he immediately committed to memory.

## \|\| 1.147.16 \|\|

*vedāḥ sāṃgāḥ samādhītā garbhavāse'pi tena ca \|*  
*smṛtayaśca purāṇāni mokṣaśāstrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even while staying in the womb, the Vedas, the Aṅgas, Smṛtis, Purāṇas and the scriptural texts on liberation were entirely burnt by him.

## \|\| 1.147.17 \|\|

*tatrastho'pi divā naktaṃ svādhyāyaṃ prakaroti saḥ \|*  
*na ca janmotthajāṃ buddhiṃ kathaṃcidapi ciṃtayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Stationed there in the womb itself, day and night he regularly recited Vedic texts but he never thought of coming out as a child.

## \|\| 1.147.18 \|\|

*sāpi mātā parā pīḍāṃ nityaṃ yāti tathākulā \|*  
*yathāyathā sa saṃyāti vṛddhiṃ jaṭharamāśritaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Even as he went on developing while staying there (in the womb), the mother experienced excruciating pain and was extremely agitated.

## \|\| 1.147.19-20 \|\|

*tataśca vismayāviṣṭo vyāso vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kastvaṃ madgṛhiṇīkukṣau praviṣṭo garbharūpadhṛk \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na niṣkrāmasi kasmāttvaṃ kimetāṃ sūdayiṣyasi \|*  
*garbha uvāca \|*  
*rākṣaso'haṃ piśācohaṃ devo'haṃ mānuṣastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Suprised thereat Vyāsa spoke these words: “Who are you that have entered the womb of my wife assuming the form of a foetus? Why do you not come out? Will you kill her?”

## \|\| 1.147.21 \|\|

*gajo'haṃ turagaścāpi kukkuṭaśchāga eva ca \|*  
*yonīnāṃ caturāśītisahasrāṇi ca saṃkhyayā \|\| 21 \|\|*

The foetus said:

I am a Rākṣasa. I am a Piśāca, I am a Deva. I am also a man.

21\. I am an elephant, a horse, a cock, a goat also. There are eighty-four thousand different types of species taking up nativity.

## \|\| 1.147.22 \|\|

*bhrāṃto'haṃ teṣu sarveṣu tatko'haṃ prabravīmi kim \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā jaṭharaṃ samupāśritaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I have wandered over all these forms. Hence how can I say I am this or that? Now I have become a human being and am settled in a womb.

## \|\| 1.147.23 \|\|

*mānuṣaṃ na kariṣyāmi niṣkāmaṃ ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*nirviṣṭo bhramamāṇo'tra saṃsāre dāruṇe tataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I will not at all come out as a human being in order to roam about in the terrible worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.147.24 \|\|

*atrastho bhavanirmukto yogābhyāsarataḥ sadā \|*  
*mokṣamārgaṃ prayāsyāmi sthānānmokṣamasaṃśayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Staying here itself, I will be perpetually engaged in the practice of Yoga and shall get rid of mundane existence. I will follow the path of salvation and undoubtedly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.147.25 \|\|

*tāvajjñānaṃ ca vairāgyaṃ pūrvajātismṛtiryathā \|*  
*yāvadgarbhasthito jantuḥ sarvo'pi dvijasattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Excellent Brāhmaṇa, all the creatures as long as they are in the womb, will have perfect knowledge, detachment and non-affection for all worldly objects and the memory of previous births.

## \|\| 1.147.26 \|\|

*yadā garbhādviniṣkrāṃtaḥ spṛśyate viṣṇumāyayā \|*  
*tadā nāśaṃ vrajatyāśu satyametadasaṃśayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. As soon as it comes out of the womb and is touched by Viṣṇumāyā all this stops undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.147.27 \|\|

*tasmānnāhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha niṣkramiṣye kathaṃcana \|*  
*garbhādasmātprayāsyāmi sthānānmokṣamasaṃśayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I will not at all come out of this womb. I shall attain salvation from this very spot.

## \|\| 1.147.28-29 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*na bhaviṣyati te māyā vaiṣṇavī sā kathaṃcana \|*  
*sughorānnarakādasmānniṣkramasva vigarhitāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

*garbhavāsāttato yogaṃ samāśritya śivaṃ vraja \|*  
*tasmāddarśaya me vaktraṃ svakīyaṃ yena me bhavet \|*  
*ānṛṇyaṃ pitṛlokasya tava vaktrasya darśanāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

28-29. The Vaiṣṇavī Māyā will not affect you at all. Come out of this extremely terrible and despicable Naraka in the form of the stay in the womb.

Practice Yoga thereafter and resort to Śiva. So, you do show me your face so that I shall get freedom from the indebtedness to the people of Pitṛloka.

## \|\| 1.147.30 \|\|

*garbha uvāca \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ pratibhuvaṃ yadi me tvaṃ prayacchasi \|*  
*idānīṃ yatsvayaṃ tanme janma syānnānyathā dvija \|\| 30 \|\|*

The foetus said:

30\. You must now itself offer Vāsudeva as the guarantor and surety. Then my birth may be possible. Not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.147.31 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato vyāso drutaṃ gatvā dvārakāṃ prati duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ vistarāccakrapāṇine \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sūta said:

31\. Then, Vyāsa in his great distress hastened to Dvārakā. He narrated everything to the Discus-bearing Lord in detail.

## \|\| 1.147.32 \|\|

*tenaiva sahitaḥ paścātsvagṛhaṃ punarāgataḥ \|*  
*vyāsaḥ pratibhuvaṃ tasmai dātuṃ viṣṇuṃ niraṃjanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Later he returned to his house along with him. Vyāsa wanted to offer Viṣṇu, the unsullied, as guarantor and surety.

## \|\| 1.147.33 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*pratibhūrasmi nāśāya māyāyāstava nirgame \|*  
*madvākyānniṣkramaṃ kṛtvā gaccha mokṣamanuttamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:

33\. I am the gurantor unto you for the destruction of Māyā when you come out. At my instance do come out and attain the excellent salvation.

## \|\| 1.147.34 \|\|

*tato drutaṃ viniṣkrāṃto viṣṇuvākyena sa dvijāḥ \|*  
*dvādaśābdapramāṇastu yauvanasya samīpagaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then at the instance of Viṣṇu, O Brāhmaṇas, he hurriedly came out as a person nearing youth, a person twelve years old.

## \|\| 1.147.35 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya daityāriṃ vyāsaṃ ca jananīṃ tathā \|*  
*prasthito vanavāsāya tatkṣaṇādvyāsanaṃdanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Instantly, the son of Vyāsa bowed down to Daityāri (Kṛṣṇa), Vyāsa and his mother started for residence in the forest.

## \|\| 1.147.36 \|\|

*atha taṃ sa muniḥ prāha tiṣṭha putrātmamaṃdire \|*  
*saṃskārāñjātakādyāṃśca yena te prakaromyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then the sage said to him: “Dear son, stay in your own abode so that I can perform the post-natal consecratory rites unto you.”

## \|\| 1.147.37 \|\|

*śiśuruvāca \|*  
*saṃskārāḥ śataśo jātā mama janmanijanmani \|*  
*bhavārṇave parikṣipto yairahaṃ bandhanātmakaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

The child said:

37\. Hundreds of consecratory rites have been performed on me in the course of the different births. These have worked as bonds whereby I have been thrown into the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.147.38 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*śukavajjalpate yasmāttavāyaṃ putrako mune \|*  
*tasmācchuko'yaṃ nāmnāstu yogavidyāvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

38\. O sage, this son of yours who is expert in the yogic lore is prattling like a Śuka (parrot). So let him be named Śuka.

## \|\| 1.147.39 \|\|

*nāyaṃ sthāsyati harmye sve mohamāyāvivarjitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādgacchatu mā snehaṃ tvaṃ kuruṣvāsya saṃbhavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He is bereft of delusion and ignorance. He will not stay in your abode. Let him go. Do not exhibit much of affection for him.

## \|\| 1.147.40 \|\|

*ahaṃ gṛhaṃ prayāsyāmi tvaṃ muktaḥ paitṛkādṛṇāt \|*  
*darśanādeva putrasya satyametanmayoditam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I shall go home. You are freed from the indebtedness to the Pitṛs merely by the perception of your son. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.147.41 \|\|

*evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśo vyāsamāmaṃtrya satvaram \|*  
*vihagādhipamārūḍhaḥ prayayau dvārakāṃ prati \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After saying thus, Hṛṣīkeśa took leave of Vyāsa. Riding on the King of Birds, he started for Dvārakā.

## \|\| 1.147.42 \|\|

*tato gate hṛṣīkeśe vyāsaḥ putramuvāca ha \|*  
*prasthitaṃ vanavāsāya niḥspṛhaṃ svagṛhaṃ prati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After Hṛṣīkeśa had gone, Vyāsa said to his son who was at the point of starting forestwards and who was devoid of any desire for his own home:

## \|\| 1.147.43 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*gṛhasthadharmariktānāṃ pitṛvākyaṃ praṇaśyati \|*  
*pitṛvākyaṃ tu yo mohānnaiva samyaksamācaret \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ tasmānmadvākyātputra mā vraja \|\| 43 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

43\. In the case of those who do not observe the householder’s rites, a statement of father comes to nought. He who does not, due to delusion, strictly abide by the statement of his father falls into Naraka. Hence, O son, do not go. Desist from going at my instance.

## \|\| 1.147.44 \|\|

*śuka uvāca \|*  
*yathādyāhaṃ tvayā jāto mayā tvaṃ cānyajanmani \|*  
*saṃjāto'si muniśreṣṭha tathāhamapi te pitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

Śuka said:

44\. Just as today I am born as your son so also in another birth you were born as my son, O excellent sage. Therefore, I am your father.

## \|\| 1.147.45 \|\|

*tasmādvākyaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ yadyeṣā dharmasaṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*nāhaṃ niṣedhanīyastu vrajamānastapovanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence you must carry out my order. If this is the position of Dharma, I should not be denied permission to go to penance grove.

## \|\| 1.147.46 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya gṛhe janma puṇyaiḥ saṃprāpyate nṛbhiḥ \|*  
*saṃskārānyatra saṃprāpya vedoktānmunirāpyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

46\. It is through merits that men attain birth in the family of a Brāhmaṇa. There as a Brāhmaṇa, he gets the Vedic con-secratory rites (and attains salvation).

## \|\| 1.147.47 \|\|

*śuka uvāca \|*  
*saṃskārairāpyate muktiryadi karma śubhaṃ vinā \|*  
*pākhaṃḍino'pi yāsyaṃti tanmuktiṃ vratadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Śuka said:

47\. If without auspicious Karmas, salvation is attained, then heretics too will attain salvation by merely observing vows.

## \|\| 1.147.48 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brahmacārī bhavetpūrvaṃ gṛhasthaśca tataḥ param \|*  
*vānaprastho yatiścaiva tato mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

48\. One shall at first be a celibate student. Then he shall be a householder. He then becomes a Vānaprastha and recluse. Thereafter one shall attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.147.49-51 \|\|

*śuka uvāca \|*  
*brahmacaryeṇa cenmokṣastatṣaṇḍhānāṃ sadā bhavet \|*  
*gṛhasthāśramiṇāṃ cetsyāttatsarvaṃ mucyate jagat \|\| 49 \|\|*

*athavā vanaraktānāṃ tanmṛgāṇāṃ prajāyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

*athavā yatidharmāṇāṃ yadi mokṣo bhavennṛṇām \|*  
*daridrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tanmuktiḥ prathamā bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

Śuka said:

49-51. If through celibacy salvation can be attained, then impotent eunuchs will always have it. If householders get it, then entire universe can get released. Or if the resident of forest were to get salvation, then (forest) animals can attain it. Or, if those having ascetic virtues attain salvation, all the poverty-stricken shall attain liberation at the first instance.

## \|\| 1.147.52 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*gṛhasthadharmaraktānāṃ nṛṇāṃ sanmārgagāminām \|*  
*iha lokaḥ paraścaiva manunā saṃprakīrtitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

52\. It has been gloriously proclaimed by Manu that this world and the next one can be attained by men devoted to the pious activities of the householder following the path of the righteous.

## \|\| 1.147.53 \|\|

*śrīśuka uvāca \|*  
*gṛhaguptau suguptānāṃ baṃdhānāṃ baṃdhubaṃdhanaiḥ \|*  
*moharāgasamāveśātsanmārga gamanaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Śrī Śuka said:

53\. Whence can those who are well-concealed in domestic protection, and are well bound by the bonds of kinship follow the path of the righteous, since delusion and passion have adverse effect on them?

## \|\| 1.147.54 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|\| \|*  
*kaṣṭaṃ vane nivasato'tra sadā narasya no kevalaṃ nijatanuprabhavaṃ bhavecca \|*  
*daivaṃ ca pitryamakhilaṃ na vibhāti kṛtyaṃ tasmādgṛhe nivasatātmahitaṃ pracintyam \|\| 54 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

54\. In the case of a man residing in forest always, suffering is not caused by his body alone but also by supernatural beings and ancestors, because he does not fulfill the duties towards the deity and ancestors. Hence welfare of the soul should be considered seriously by one staying in the householder’s stage.

## \|\| 1.147.55 \|\|

*śrīśukadeva uvāca \|*  
*bhāvena bhāvitamahātapasāṃ munīnāṃ tiṣṭhanti tāvadakhilāni tapaḥphalāni \|*  
*yatte nikāśaśaraṇāḥ puruṣā na jātu paśyaṃtyasajjanamukhāni sukhaṃ tadeva \|\| 55 \|\|*

Śrī Śuka said:

55\. All the benefits of penance abide in the case of sages with great austerities sanctified by mental purity. This itself is the height of happiness that persons who seek refuge in their close proximity never see faces of bad people.

## \|\| 1.147.56 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*gṛhaṃ parigrahaḥ puṃsāṃ gṛhasthāśramadharmiṇām \|*  
*ihaloke pare caiva sukhaṃ yacchati śāśvatam \|\| 56 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

56\. In the house, the spouse accords permanent happiness in this world as well as in the other world to men following the practices of the householder stage.

## \|\| 1.147.57 \|\|

*śrīśuka uvāca \|*  
*śītaṃ hutāśādapi daivayogātsañjāyate candramaso'pi tāpaḥ \|*  
*parigrahātsaukhyasamudbhavo'tra bhūto'bhavadbhāvi na martyaloke \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Śuka said:

57\. At the intercession of fate chillness may exude from fire and scorching heat from the moon. But the occurrence of happiness from a spouse is neither a thing of the past nor of the present nor of the future in the human world.

## \|\| 1.147.58 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*supuṇyairlabhyate kṛcchrānmānuṣyaṃ bhuvi durlabham \|*  
*tasmiṃllabdhe na kiṃ labdhaṃ yadi syādgṛhadharmavit \|\| 58 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

58\. Human birth is a rare thing. It is obtained with great difficulty through excellent merits. If that is acquired, what is it that has not been acquired if one is conversant with the practices and virtues of the householder’s stage?

## \|\| 1.147.59 \|\|

*śrīśukadeva uvāca \|*  
*yadi syājjñānasaṃyukto janmakāletra mānavaḥ \|*  
*nijāvasthāṃ samālokya tajjñānaṃ hi vilīyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

Śrī Śuka said:

59\. If a man is endowed with knowledge at the time of birth, that knowledge itself will get lost on perceiving one’s own plight.

## \|\| 1.147.60 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*muditasyāpi putrasya gardabhasyārbhakasya ca \|*  
*bhasmalolasya lokasya śabdo'pi raṭato mude \|\| 60 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

60\. To the world, as fickle as ashes, the sound of a delighted son and of the young one of a donkey is conducive to

## \|\| 1.147.61 \|\|

*śrīśuka uvāca \|*  
*rasatā sarpatā dhūli loke tvaśucinā ciram \|*  
*mune'tra śiśunā lokastuṣṭiṃ yāti sa bāliśaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

Śrī Śuka said:

61\. O sage, if the world gets satisfied and delighted with an impure child that cries and crawls in dust, then it is also childish.

## \|\| 1.147.62 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*puṃnāmāsti mahāraudro narako yamamandire \|*  
*putrahīno vrajettatra tena putraḥ praśasyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

62\. There is an exceedingly terrible Naraka named Pum in the palace of Yama. One not having a son goes there. Hence Putra (son) is honoured.

## \|\| 1.147.63 \|\|

*śrīśuka uvāca \|*  
*yadi syātputrataḥ svargaḥ sarveṣāṃ syānmahāmune \|*  
*śūkarāṇāṃ śunāṃ caiva śalabhānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O great sage, if heavenly pleasure is attained through a son then all including pigs, dogs and locusts too should attain it.

## \|\| 1.147.64 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*pitṝṇāmanṛṇo martyo jāyate putradarśanāt \|*  
*pautrasyāpi ca devānāṃ prapautrasya divāśrayaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

64\. By seeing a son a man becomes free from indebtedness to Pitṛs; by seeing a grandson he becomes free from indebtedness to Devas and by seeing a great-grandson a man becomes a heaven-dweller.

## \|\| 1.147.65 \|\|

*śuka uvāca \|*  
*cirāyurjjāyate gṛdhraḥ saṃtatiṃ paśyate nijām \|*  
*krameṇa saṃtataṃ kiṃ na sa mokṣaṃ pratipadyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

Śuka said:

65\. A vulture is long-lived and it sees a series of its generations (progeny). Why does it not attain salvation?

## \|\| 1.147.66 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā parityajya pitaraṃ sa vanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*mātaraṃ ca suduḥkhārtāṃ pralapantīmanekadhā \|\| 66 \|\|*

Sūta said:

66\. After saying thus, he went to the forest abandoning his father and the exceedingly miserable mother who lamented in various ways.

## \|\| 1.147.67 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhito vyāso nirāśaḥ putradarśane \|*  
*putraśokābhisaṃtapto bhāryayā sahito'bhavat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On seeing him Vyāsa lost hope of seeing his son further and so became miserable. He became distressed due to the separation from the son and he stayed in the company of his wife.

## Chapter 148 - Greatness of Vaṭikeśvara (Vaṭika-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.148.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ taṃ niḥspṛhaṃ jñātvā gṛhaṃ prati nijātmajam \|*  
*piṃgalā duḥkhasaṃyuktā vyāsametaduvāca ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tapaścariṣyāmi putrārthaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*anujñāṃ dehi me yena toṣayāmi maheśvaram \|*  
*putro yena bhavenmahyaṃ vaṃśavṛddhikaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On realizing that her son had no desire for householder’s life, Piṅgalā (i.e.Vaṭikā) became miserable and spoke to Vyāsa thus: “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I will perform a penance for the sake of a son. Do grant me permission so that I can propitiate Maheśvara. Thereby a son causing the family to flourish shall be born of me.”

## \|\| 1.148.3 \|\|

*evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā labdhvānujñāṃ munestataḥ \|*  
*kṣetrametatsamāsādya tapastepe pativratā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After deciding thus and getting the permission of the sage the chaste lady reached this holy spot and performed penance.

## \|\| 1.148.4 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya śaṃkaraṃ devaṃ tadagre nirmalodakam \|*  
*kṛtvā vāpīṃ suvistīrṇāṃ snānātpātakanāśanīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She installed Lord Śaṅkara and made a large tank of pure water. It was destructive of sins through bath.

## \|\| 1.148.5 \|\|

*tatastasyā gatastuṣṭiṃ bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*varado'smīti tāṃ prāha prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then Lord Tripurāntaka became pleased with her. With a delighted heart he spoke to her: “I am the bestower of boons.”

## \|\| 1.148.6 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te bhadre varaṃ varaya suvrate \|*  
*yaḥ sthito hṛdaye nityaṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Mahādeva said:

6\. O fair lady, I am pleased with you. O lady of excellent Vratas, choose your boon whatever may be cherished in the heart. There is nothing which cannot be given.

## \|\| 1.148.7 \|\|

*vaṭikovāca \|*  
*sutaṃ dehi suraśreṣṭha mama vaṃśavivardhanam \|*  
*cittāhlādakaraṃ nityaṃ suśīlaṃ vinayānvitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Vaṭikā said:

7\. O excellent one among Suras, give me a son who will make the family flourish, who will always delight my mind, is well-behaved and endowed with humility.

## \|\| 1.148.8 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdehastava putraḥ suśobhane \|*  
*yādṛktvayā mahābhāge prārthitastadviśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Śrī Mahādeva said:

8\. O splendid lady, O highly esteemed one, there is no doubt about it that a son will be born to you as requested. In fact, he will be better qualified.

## \|\| 1.148.9-11 \|\|

*anyāpi mānuṣī yā'tra vāpyāṃ snātvā samāhitā \|*  
*pañcamyāṃ vatsaraṃ yāvacchuklapakṣe hyupasthite \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati malliṃgaṃ yaccādya sthāpitaṃ tvayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sātha lapsyati satputraṃ dattvā phalamanuttamam \|*  
*yā ca daurbhāgyasaṃyuktā tṛtīyādivase'tra vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

*snātvā'tra salile paścānmalliṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*sā saubhāgya samopetā varṣāṃte ca bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Any other woman who with great concentration takes her bath in this tank on the fifth lunar day in the bright half for a year and also worships this Liṅga installed by you today, will attain a good son by offering an excellent fruit. If one who suffers due to ill-luck takes her bath on the third lunar day in this tank and afterwards worships my Liṅga, she will be blessed with conjugal felicity by the end of the year.

## \|\| 1.148.12-14 \|\|

*yaḥ punaḥ puruṣaścātra snātvā māṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*sakāmo lapsyate kāmānvikāmo mokṣameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*evamuktvā mahādevastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sā'pi lebhe sutaṃ vyāsātkapiṃjalamiti śrutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yādṛktena purā prokto devadevena śūlinā \|*  
*yenaiva sthāpitā cātra devī kelīvarī purā \|*  
*sarvasiddhipradā loke tatra yā'rādhitā purā \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. A man who bathes here and worships me shall obtain his desires if he has desires, or salvation if he has no desire.

After saying thus Mahādeva vanished. She also conceived a son from Vyāsa. He was well known as Kapīñjala as was said by the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas earlier. By him Goddess Kelīśvarī was installed here. On being propitiated she bestows all Siddhis in the world.

## Chapter 149 - Manifestation of Kelīśvarī (Keli-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.149.1-5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kelīśvarī ca yā devī śrūyate sūtanaṃdana \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vada nastasyā utpattiṃ ca suvistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kasminkāle samutpannā kimarthaṃ ca sureśvarī \|\| \|*  
*kiṃ tasyā jāyate śreyaḥ pūjayā namanena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tvayā kātyāyanī proktā cāmuṇḍā ca sureśvarī \|*  
*śrīmātā ca samutpannā kimarthaṃ ca sureśvarī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śrīmātā ca tathā tārā devī śatruvināśinī \|*  
*kelīśvarī na saṃproktā tasmāttāṃ vada sāṃpratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kautukaṃ naḥ samutpannamatrārthe sūtanaṃdana \|\| 5 \|\|*

Note: Chapters 149-150 describe how demon Andhaka defeated Devas. Lord Śiva created Goddess Kelīśvarī for killing Andhaka. Śukra also propitiated the same Devī by oblating his own flesh in the Homa.

The sages said:

1-5. O Sūtanandana, a goddess is heard about as Kelīśvarī. Tell us her origin and greatness in detail.

At what time did she originate? What benefit results from her adoration and obeisance?

Kātyāyanī was described by you and also Cāmuṇḍā, the goddess of Suras. Śrīmātā, is also born as goddess of Suras. Śrīmātā and goddess Tārā, the destroyer of enemies, have been described. Kelīśvarī was not described. Hence, extol her now.

Great curiosity and interest has been created in us, O Sūtanandana.

## \|\| 1.149.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ādyaikā devatā loke bahurūpā vyavasthitā \|*  
*devatānāṃ hitārthāya daityapakṣakṣayāya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. The primordial single goddess established herself in many forms for the welfare of Devas and destruction of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.149.7-11 \|\|

*yadāyadātra devānāṃ vyasanaṃ jāyate kvacit \|*  
*tadātadā parā śaktiryā sā vyāpya vyavasthitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sarvametajjagaddhātrī janma cakre dharātale \|*  
*mahiṣāsuranāśāya sā ca kātyāyanī bhuvi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*avatīrṇā parā mūrtirgatāsminbhuvanatraye \|*  
*yadā śuṃbhanikṣaṃbhau ca dānavau baladarpitau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*avatīrṇā tadā saiva cāmuṃḍā rūpamāśritā \|*  
*prodgate kālayavane sarvadevabhayāvahe \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śrīmātārūpiṇī devī saiva jātā mahītale \|*  
*aṃdhāsuravadhārthāya śaṃbhunā'krāṃtacetasā \|*  
*sṛṣṭā kelīvarī devī yayā vyāptamidaṃ jagat \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. Whenever any distress occurs anywhere unto Devas, that great Śakti which pervades the entire universe incarnates on the earth.

For the destrucion of Mahiṣāsura she descended to the earth as Kātyāyanī. The great form of the goddess extended all over the three worlds.

When the two Dānavas, Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha became haughty on account of their strength, she hereself incarnated assuming the form of Cāmuṇḍā.

When Kālayavana striking terror into the Devas rose up, she was born on the earth in the form of Śrīmātā.

For the destruction of Andhāsura, Goddess Kelīśvarī was created by Śaṃbhu who occupied her mind and the entire universe was pervaded by her.

## \|\| 1.149.12 \|\|

*tatastasyāḥ prabhāvena hatvā daityānaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*andhako nihataḥ paścāttrailokyavyasanapradaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then by her power, all the Daityas were killed entirely. Afterwards, Andhaka who caused great distress to all the three worlds was killed.

## \|\| 1.149.13 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*andhakaḥ kasya putro'yaṃ kiṃprabhāvaḥ kathaṃ hataḥ \|*  
*kasmāddhatastu saṃgrāme sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 13 \|\|*

The sages said:

13\. Whose son was Andhaka? What was his power? How was he killed? Why. was he killed in battle? Do narrate everything in detail.

Sūta said.

## \|\| 1.149.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dakṣasya duhitā nāmnā ditiḥ sarvaguṇālayā \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurnāma tasyāḥ putro babhūva ha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There was a daughter of Dakṣa named Diti. She was the abode of all good qualities. She had a son named Hiraṇyakaśipu.

## \|\| 1.149.15 \|\|

*yena śakrādayo devā jitāḥ sarve raṇājire \|*  
*svarge rājyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhūri svayameva mahātmanā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śakra and other Devas were conquered by him in battle. The great soul ruled over the kingdom of Svarga himself.

## \|\| 1.149.16 \|\|

*yadbhayātsakalairdevairnānāśastrāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*nirmitānyatimukhyāni varmacarmayutāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Afraid of him, all the Devas made various kinds of weapons of great importance along with coats of mail and shields.

## \|\| 1.149.17 \|\|

*svayaṃ vidārito yaśca viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*karajairjānuni pṛṣṭhe vinidhāya prakopataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Viṣṇu, the powerful Lord, angrily placed him on his back on the knees and tore him up with his claws.

## \|\| 1.149.18 \|\|

*tasya putradvayaṃ jajña vīryaudāryaguṇānvitam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ prahlāda ityukto dvitīyaścāṃdhakastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Two sons of great vigour and exalted virtues were born to him. The elder one is called Prahlāda and the second one was Andhaka.

## \|\| 1.149.19 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipau prāpte mṛtyulokaṃ suhṛdgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*amātyaiśca tataḥ proktaḥ prahlādo vinayānvitaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When Hiraṇyakaśipu entered the world of the god of death, the groups of his friends and ministers humbly requested Prahlāda:

## \|\| 1.149.20 \|\|

*pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyametadācara sāṃpratam \|*  
*dhuraṃ vahasva rājyotthāṃ devānyuddhe nipātaya \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Take up this hereditary kingdom and rule. Bear the weight of administration of the dominion. Strike down Devas in battle.”

## \|\| 1.149.21 \|\|

*prahrāda uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ rājyaṃ kariṣyāmi kathaṃcidapi bhūtale \|*  
*yatastato nibodhadhvaṃ vacanaṃ mama sāṃpratam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

21\. I will not rule over the earth at any cost. Why? Listen to my words and understand now.

## \|\| 1.149.22 \|\|

*daityarājyaṃ na vāṃchaṃti devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ rakṣākaro nityaṃ viṣṇuḥ sa bhagavānsvayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Devas with Śakra as their leader never like the rule of Daityas. Viṣṇu, the Lord, is himself their protector always.

## \|\| 1.149.23 \|\|

*apyahaṃ santyaje prāṇānsarvasvaṃ vā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*hariṇā saha saṃgrāmaṃ nāhaṃ kartumaho kṣamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I would rather give up my life. I shall forsake all my possessions without any doubt. I am incapable of fighting with Hari.

## \|\| 1.149.24 \|\|

*yo mayā'bhyarcito nityaṃ praṇataśca sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*na tena sahito yuddhaṃ kariṣyāmi kathañcana \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This Lord of Suras has been bowed to and adored always by me. I will not engage myself in war against him on any account.

## \|\| 1.149.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*prahlādena ca saṃtyakte rājye pitṛsamudbhave \|*  
*andhakaḥ sthāpitastatra saṃmaṃtrya sacivairmithaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sūta said:

25\. When the kingship which was devolved on him from his father was refused by Prahlāda, Andhaka was established there by the ministers after having mutual consultation.

## \|\| 1.149.26-27 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putro devadānavadarpahā \|*  
*so'pi rājyamamātyebhyo nidhāya tadanantaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tapaścakre ciraṃ kālaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ pitāmaham \|*  
*tyaktvā kāmaṃ tathā krodhaṃ daṃbhaṃ matsarameva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. This son of Hiraṇyakaśipu could destroy the arrogance of Devas as well as of Dānavas. He entrusted the kingdom to the care of the ministers and performed penance for a long time meditating on Pitāmaha. He eschewed lust, anger, hypocrisy and rivalry.

## \|\| 1.149.28 \|\|

*jiteṃdriyaḥ suśāṃtātmā samaḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu \|*  
*vṛkṣamūlāśrayaḥ śāṃtaḥ saṃtuṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He kept his soul quiescent and the sense-organs well controlled. He was impartial to all the creatures. With a calm and delighted mind, he resorted to the root of a tree.

## \|\| 1.149.29 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ phalāhāro babhūva ha \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśanāhāro yāvadvarṣasahasrakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. For a period of a thousand years, his diet consisted of fruits alone. Then for another thousand years, he ate only withered and decayed leaves.

## \|\| 1.149.30 \|\|

*dhyāyamāno divānaktaṃ devadevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*vāyubhakṣastato jajñe tāvatkālaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Day and night he meditated on Pitāmaha, the Lord of Devas. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, his diet consisted of air only, for an equal time.

## \|\| 1.149.31 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte caturthe samupasthite \|*  
*tamuvāca svayaṃ brahmā svayamabhyetya harṣitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then at the close of the fourth set of thousand years, Brahmā himself joyously approached him and said:

## \|\| 1.149.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*tuṣṭo'haṃ te pradāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

32\. O dear one, I am pleased with you. O devotee of excellent Vratas, choose your boon. I am pleased. I shall grant you even the rarest of objects.

## \|\| 1.149.33 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*yadi yacchasi me brahmanvaraṃ manasi vāṃchitam \|*  
*jarāmaraṇanāśāya dīyatāṃ surasattama \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Brahmā, if you wish to give the boon cherished in the mind then, O most excellent one among Suras, grant me the cessation of old age and cause of death.

## \|\| 1.149.34 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*na kaścicca jarāhīno vidyate'tra dharātale \|*  
*maraṇena vinā naiva yasya janma bhavetkṣitau \|\| 34 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

34\. Nobody devoid of old age exists on the surface of the earth. There is no one who is born on the earth and is without death.

## \|\| 1.149.35 \|\|

*tathāpi tava dāsyāmi bahudharmaratasya ca \|*  
*tasmātkuru mahābhāga rājyaṃ gatvā nijaṃ gṛham \|\| 35 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

35\. Still, I shall grant it unto you devoted as you are to many pious rites. Hence, O highly fortunate one, go back to your abode and rule over the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.149.36 \|\|

*bhavedbahuphalaṃ rājyaṃ śmaśānaṃ bhavanaṃ yathā \|*  
*bahukaṇṭakasaṃkīrṇaṃ krūrakarmabhirāvṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The kingdom shall be rich with many good things even if it is like a cremation ground overgrown with thorns and persons of ruthless activities (it will turn out into a home of happiness).

## \|\| 1.149.37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā caturvaktrastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya preritaḥ kāladharmaṇā \|*  
*provāca sacivānso'tha piturvairamanusmaran \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sūta said:

37\. After saying thus the Four-faced One vanished. Once thereafter, urged as if by the activities of Kāla, he recollected the enmity of his father and spoke to the ministers:

## \|\| 1.149.38 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*pitāsmākaṃ hato devaiḥ pitṛvyaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kapaṭena na śauryeṇa tasmāttānsūdayāmyaham \|\| 38 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

38\. Our father as well as our mighty uncle were killed by Devas by fraud and not heroic fight. Hence I will kill them.

## \|\| 1.149.39 \|\|

*ko'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na kṛtyaiḥ suśaṃsitaiḥ \|*  
*prākaṭyaṃ yāti sarvatra vaṃśasyāgre dhvajo yathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Of what purpose is a son born, who does not show himself at the forefront everywhere by means of well-prised activities like the banner at the top of the flagstaff!

## \|\| 1.149.40 \|\|

*maṃtriṇa ūcuḥ \|*  
*yuktametanmahābhāga yattvayā vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*vadhyāḥsyurvibudhāḥ sarve ye'smākaṃ paripaṃthinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Misisters \[Ministers\] said:

40\. O highly esteemed one, what has been said by you is but proper. Devas who are our enemies should all be killed.

## \|\| 1.149.41 \|\|

*asmākaṃ khalvime lokāḥ ke devāḥ ke dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*yajñabhāgānhariṣyāmo hatvā śakramukhānsurān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All these worlds are ours. Who are these Devas? Who are the Brāhmaṇas? After killing Suras including Śakra, we shall take away our share in the Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.149.42 \|\|

*evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā sainyena mahatānvitāḥ \|*  
*prajagmustvaritāstatra yatra śakro vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After resolving thus, they, accompanied with a powerful army, hurried to the place where Śakra was present.

## \|\| 1.149.43 \|\|

*śakro'pi dānavānīkaṃ dṛṣṭvā tānsahasāgatān \|*  
*āruhyairāvaṇaṃ nāgaṃ yuddhārthaṃ niryayau tadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On seeing the army of the Dānavas and noticing that they had launched a surprise attack Śakra rode on the elephant Airāvata and set out for the battle.

## \|\| 1.149.44-47 \|\|

*saha devagaṇaiḥ sarvairvasurudrārkapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare śakro vajraṃ raudratamaṃ ca yat \|\| 44 \|\|*

*samuddiśyāṃdhakaṃ tasmai mumoca paravīrahā \|*  
*sa hatastena vajreṇa vihasya danujottamaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śakraṃ provāca saṃhṛṣṭastāranādena saṃyuge \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ bāhubalaṃ śakra tavādya sucirānmayā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*adhunā paśya cāsmākaṃ tvameva balasūdana \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. He was accompanied by all the groups of Devas including Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas. In the meantime Śakra, the destroyer of enemies, aimed at Andhaka and discharged his extremely terrible Vajra. On being struck by it, the excellent Danuja laughed and said to Śakra in a loud voice with great delight: “O Śakra, after a long time, the might of your arm has been seen by me in this battle. Now, O destroyer of Bala, you yourself see ours.”

## \|\| 1.149.48-49 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha cāvidhya gadāṃ gurvīṃ mumoca ha \|*  
*śataghaṃṭāmahārāvāṃ nirmitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sarvāyasamayīṃ gurvīṃ yamajihvābhivāparām \|*  
*śatahastāṃ pramāṇena prāṇināṃ bhayavarddhinīm \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sūta said:

48-49. After saying thus, he hurled with great force a huge mace that was made by Viśvakarman. It produced the loud sound of a hundred bells. It was fully made of iron and very huge as though it was another tongue of Yama. It ex-tenḍed to a hundred Hastas (hands) and increased the fright of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.149.50 \|\|

*tayā vinihataḥ śakro mūrchāvyākuliteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritya niviṣṭo gajamūrddhani \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On being struck by it Śakra fell into a swoon with all his sense-organs disorganized. With the support of the flagstaff, he fell on the head of the elephant.

## \|\| 1.149.51 \|\|

*atha saṃmūrchitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śakraṃ skandaḥ prakopitaḥ \|*  
*mumocātha nijāṃ śaktimamoghāṃ vajrasaṃnibhām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On seeing Śakra unconscious in a swoon, Skanda became furious. He discharged his Śakti that was never ineffective and resmebled the thunderbolt.

## \|\| 1.149.52 \|\|

*tāmāyāṃtīṃ samālokya dānavo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*pratilomāṃ tataścakre līlayaiva mahābalaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On seeing it coming, the Dānava made it turn back with sharp arrows. The mighty one did this sportingly.

## \|\| 1.149.53 \|\|

*tataḥ skando'pi saṃgṛhya cāpaṃ taṃ prati sāyakān \|*  
*mumocāśīviṣākārāllaṃghvastraṃ tasya darśayan \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then Skanda took up his bow and discharged arrows against him resembling furious serpents whose very breath was poisonous. By this he displayed how easily he could wield missiles.

## \|\| 1.149.54 \|\|

*etasminnantare devāḥ sarve śastrapravṛṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*samaṃtācchādayāmāsurdānavānāmanīkinīm \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the meantime, all the Devas showered volleys of weapons and covered the army of the Dānavas all round.

## \|\| 1.149.55 \|\|

*tatastu dānavāḥ sarve devatānāmanīkinīm \|*  
*prahāraiḥ pīḍayāmāsurdudruvuste divaukasaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. All the Dānavas thereafter inflicted pain on the army of the Devas by a series of blows. The Heaven-dwellers fled then.

## \|\| 1.149.56 \|\|

*tato bhagnānsurāndṛṣṭvā sagaṇo vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*darśayāmāsa cātmānaṃ devānāśvāsayanniva \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then the Bull-vehicled Lord with his Gaṇas saw the Suras shattered. So he revealed himself thereby consoling the Devas as it were:

## \|\| 1.149.57-58 \|\|

*mā bhaiṣṭa devatāḥ sarvāḥ paśyadhvaṃ madviceṣṭitam \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavāñchambhurmaṃtrairātharvaṇaistadā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*āhvayāmāsa viśveśāṃ parāṃ śaktimanuttamām \|*  
*āhūtā paramā śaktirjagāma harasaṃnidhim \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. “O ye Devas, do not be afraid. See my act.” Saying thus Lord Śaṃbhu invoked the excellent Parāśakti (the great power), the goddess of the universe, reciting Ātharvaṇa Mantras. On Being summoned thus, the greatest Śakti went near Hara.

## \|\| 1.149.59 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāmagrataḥ prāptāṃ sarvaidevaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|*  
*astāvītpraṇato bhūtvā stotreṇānena bhaktitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On seeing that she had come before him, Lord Śaṃbhu bowed down along with all the Devas and eulogized her devoutly by means of his prayer:

## \|\| 1.149.60 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*namaste devadeveśi namaste bhaktivallabhe \|*  
*sarvage sarvade devi namaste viśvadhāriṇi \|\| 60 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

60\. Obeisance unto you, O goddess of the chiefs of Devas. Obeisance to you, O goddess endeared by devotion. O omnipresent one, O bestower of everything, O goddess, O sustainer of the Universe, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.149.61 \|\|

*namaste śaktirūpeṇa sṛṣṭipralayakāriṇi \|*  
*namaste prabhayā yukte vidyujjvalitakuṇḍale \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Obeisance to you who are the cause of creation and dissolution in the form of Śakti. Obeisance to you, O refulgent one one with earrings shining like lightning.

## \|\| 1.149.62 \|\|

*tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā devi tvaṃ sṛṣṭistvaṃ śucirdhṛtiḥ \|*  
*aruṃdhatī tatheṃdrāṇī tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ ca pārvatī \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. You are Svāhā; you are Svadhā, O goddess; you are the creation. You are purity. You are fortitude (Dhṛti). You are Arundhatī and Indrāṇī. You are Lakṣmī. You are Pārvatī.

## \|\| 1.149.63 \|\|

*yatkiṃcitstrīsvarūpaṃ ca samastaṃ bhuvanatraye \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ tvatsvarūpaṃ syāditi śāstreṣu niścayaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. This is the conclusion of all the scriptures that all those things in all the three worlds which are in female form are your forms.

## \|\| 1.149.64-65 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ ca samāhūtā tvayāhaṃ vṛṣavāhana \|*  
*maṃtrairātharvaṇai raudraistatsarvaṃ me prakīrtaya \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yena te kṛtsnaśaḥ kṛtyaṃ prakaromi yathoditam \|\| 65 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

64-65. Explain to me: why did you invite me with terrible Mantras from the Atharvaveda, O Bull-vehicled One, so that I shall carry out that entirely as per what you say.

## \|\| 1.149.66 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ete śakrādayo devāḥ sarve svargādvivāsitāḥ \|*  
*aṃdhakena mahābhāge daityānāmadhipena ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

66\. All the Devas including Śakra have been expelled from Svarga, O highly esteemed one, by Andhaka, the overlord of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.149.67 \|\|

*tasmāttasya vadhārthāya gacchamānasya me śṛṇu \|*  
*sāhāyyaṃ kuru me cāśu sūdayāmi raṇājire \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Listen. I am proceeding ahead to kill him. Render assistance unto me. I shall kill him in the battle.

## \|\| 1.149.68 \|\|

*ete mātṛgaṇāḥ sarve mayā dattāstavādhunā \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmāḥ sūdayiṣyaṃti dānavānye puraḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. All these groups of Mothers are given unto you now. Emaciated with hunger, they will kill the Dānavas who are standing in front.

## \|\| 1.149.69 \|\|

*yasmātkelīmayaṃ rūpaṃ vidhāya tvaṃ sahasradhā \|*  
*anekairvikṛtai rūpaiḥ samāhūtāgnimadhyataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. You have assumed a sportive form with various hideous forms in thousands. You have been invoked in this from the middle of fire.

## \|\| 1.149.70 \|\|

*tasmātkelīśvarīnāma trailokye tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa yastvāṃ bhaktyā'rcayiṣyati \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, you will be known all over the three worlds by the name Kelīśvarī. A devotee should worship you in this form alone with devotion.

## \|\| 1.149.71 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tasyābhīṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yuddhakāle'tha saṃprāpte stotreṇānena te stutim \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He should worship you on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days. He shall attain what has been desired.

When the time of battle arrives, a devotee should eulogize you by means of his prayer.

## \|\| 1.149.72 \|\|

*yaḥ kariṣyati bhūpālo jayastasya bhaviṣyati \|*  
*api svalpasvasainyasya svalpāśvasya ca saṃgare \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A king who eulogizes with this hymn shall be victorious in battle even if this army is small and he has only a small cavalry.

## \|\| 1.149.73 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati jayo nūnaṃ tvatprasādādasaṃśayam \|*  
*evaṃ sā devadevena proktā kelīśvarī tadā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Undoubtedly, with your favour he will be certainly victorious.

Thus goddess Keliśvarī \[Kelīśvarī?\] was addressed by the Lord of Devas then.

## \|\| 1.149.74 \|\|

*prasthitā puratastasya bhavasainyasya harṣitā \|*  
*sarvairmātṛgaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ raudrārāvaiḥsubhīṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On being told thus by the Lord, the goddess Kelīśvarī went ahead of the army of Bhava joyously. She was accompanied by all the groups of Māṭrs whose shouts were extremely terrible.

## \|\| 1.149.75 \|\|

*yuddhotsāhaparai raudrairnānāśastraprahāribhiḥ \|*  
*atha te dānavā dṛṣṭvā strīsainyaṃ tatsamāgatam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They went along with the groups of Rudras keenly enthusiastic in fighting and striking with many kinds of weapons.

The Dānavas saw the army of women coming in this manner.

## \|\| 1.149.76 \|\|

*vikṛtaṃ vikṛtākāraṃ vikṛtākārarāvaṇam \|*  
*śastrodyatakaraṃ sarvayuddhavāṃchāparāyaṇam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They were hideous in forms and features. They cried hideously with weapons lifted up in their hands. They were eager for fighting.

## \|\| 1.149.77 \|\|

*jahasuḥ susvaraṃ kecitkecinnirbhartsayaṃti ca \|*  
*anye strīti parijñāya praharaṃti na dānavāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Some of the Dānavas laughed boisterously. Some rebuked them. Others knowing that they were women did not stoop to hit them.

## \|\| 1.149.78 \|\|

*vadhyamānāpi lajjaṃtaḥ pauruṣe sve vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāpto nārado munisattamaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. On being hit by them, in return they felt bashful as they were conscious of their manliness (and did not retaliate).

In the meantime Nārada, the excellent sage, came there.

## \|\| 1.149.79-84 \|\|

*andhakāya sa vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*naitāḥ striyo danuśreṣṭha yuddhārthaṃ samupasthitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*eṣā kṛtyā vadhārthāya tava rudreṇa nirmitā \|*  
*yaiṣā siṃhasamārūḍhā cakrāṃkitakarā sthitā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*eṣā kelīśvarīnāma vahnikuṇḍādvinirgatā \|*  
*etābhiḥ saha raudrābhiḥ strībhirmaṃtrabalāśrayāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

*svaraktena kṛte home devadevena śambhunā \|*  
*sa eṣa bhagavānkruddhaḥ svayamabhyeti teṃ'tikam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yuddhāya nijaharmye tānsthāpayitvā surottamān \|*  
*pratijñāya vadhaṃ tubhyaṃ purataḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*etajjñātvā mahābhāga yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 84 \|\|*

79-84. He told Andhaka the fact entirely: “O excellent Dānava these are not mere women. They have come for fighting.”

This woman who is seated on a lion and has notably a discus in hand is the Kṛtyā (ogress of black magic) created by Rudra for killing you. Her name is Kelīśvarī. She come out of the fire pit when Homa was performed by means of his own blood by Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas. By resorting to the efficacy of the Mantras, she came out along with these Rudras (terrible ones created by Rudra). Here comes the furious Lord himself near you.

In front of Parameṣṭhin he has declared that you will be killed. He has kept all the excellent Suras in his own palace for the purpose of battle. Understand this, O highly esteemed one, and do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.149.85 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ bibhemi rudrasya tathānyasyāpi kasyacit \|*  
*na strīṇāṃ prahariṣyāmi pālayanpuruṣavratam \|\| 85 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

85\. I am not afraid of Rudra or anyone else. But I will not strike a woman. I will maintain the vow of manliness.

## \|\| 1.149.86 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ pravadatastasya dānavasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ākraṃdaḥ sumahāñjajñe tasmindeśe samaṃtataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

Sūta said:

86\. Even as the noble-souled Dānava firmly said thus, there arose a loud cry all round in that place.

## \|\| 1.149.87 \|\|

*bhakṣyante dānavāḥ kecidvadhyante tvatha cāpare \|*  
*ardhabhakṣita gātrāśca praṇaśyaṃti tathā pare \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Some Dānavas were eaten. Others were killed. Others perished even as their bodies were partially eaten.

## \|\| 1.149.88 \|\|

*yudhyamānāstathaivānye śaktimaṃto'pi dānavāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyaṃte mātṛbhistatra sāyudhāśca savāhanāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Other fighting Dānavas though themselves powerful, were being eaten along with their weapons and vehicles by the Mātṛs.

## \|\| 1.149.89 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sa mahākraṃdamaṃdhakaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*ādāya khaḍgamuttasthau kimidaṃ kimidaṃ bruvan \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. On hearing that loud tumult, Andhaka became highly furious. He seized his sword and rose up saying, “What is this? What is this?”

## \|\| 1.149.90 \|\|

*atha paśyati vidhvastāndānavānbaladarpitān \|*  
*bhakṣyamāṇāstathaivānyānpalāyanaparāyaṇān \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He saw those Dānavas who were very proud on account of their might, killed. Others were being eaten and still others were bent on fleeing.

## \|\| 1.149.91 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ nihatānāṃ ca rudaṃtyo nikaṭasthitāḥ \|*  
*sa paśyati priyā bhāryāḥ pralapaṃtyo'tiduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He saw the beloved wives of others killed. They were standing near them and crying in the height of their misery.

## \|\| 1.149.92 \|\|

*atha tatkadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā aṃdhakaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*bhartsayāmāsa tāḥ sarvā yoginīḥ samarodyatāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. On seeing that havoc, Andhaka was at the zenith of his anger. He rebuked all those Yoginīs engaged in battle.

## \|\| 1.149.93 \|\|

*na ca tāstasya daityasya bhayaṃ cakruḥ kathaṃcana \|\| \|*  
*kevalaṃ sūdayaṃti sma bhakṣayaṃti ca dānavān \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. They were not at all afraid of that Daitya. They simply continued the slaughter and ate up the Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.149.94 \|\|

*tataḥ sa dānavastāsāṃ dṛṣṭvā tacceṣṭitaṃ ruṣā \|*  
*svasya gātrasya rakṣāṃ sa cakāra bhayasaṃkulaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. That Dānava noticed their activity angrily. Frightened much, he tried to guard his own body.

## \|\| 1.149.95 \|\|

*tamo'straṃ mumuce raudraṃ kṛtvā rāvaṃ sa tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare kṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ tamasā vṛtam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. He terrifically yelled and discharged the missile of Tamas (Darkness). In an instant in the meantime all the three worlds were enveloped in darkness.

## \|\| 1.149.96 \|\|

*na kiṃcijjñāyate tatra samaṃ viṣamameva ca \|*  
*kevalaṃ dānavendraśca sarvaṃ paśyati netaraḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Nothing similar or dissimilar was seen anywhere there. Only the leading Dānava could see everything. None else.

## \|\| 1.149.97 \|\|

*tataḥ sa sūdayāmāsa yoginīstāḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*yathāyathā parā nāryastādṛgrūpā bhavanti ca \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. With sharp arrows he killed those Yoginīs. Other women of the same form immediately cropped up.

## \|\| 1.149.98 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā parāṃ vṛddhiṃ yoginīnāṃ sa dānavaḥ \|*  
*saṃhāraṃ tasya cāstrasya cakāra bhayasaṃkulaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. On seeing the inordinate increase in the number of the Yoginīs, that Dānava withdrew that missile in great agitation due to fear.

## \|\| 1.149.99 \|\|

*tataḥ śukraṃ samāsādya dīnaḥ prāha kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*paśya me bhārgavaśreṣṭha strībhiryatkadanaṃ kṛtam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. He approached Śukra in a wretched condition with palms joined in reverence. He said: “O foremost one among the descendants of Bhṛgu, see the havoc perpetrated by the women in my case.

## \|\| 1.149.100 \|\|

*avadhyābhirmamāstrāṇāṃ maṃtraśaktyā suradviṣaḥ \|*  
*utpannābhiḥ prabhūtābhirhataṃ me sarvato balam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Though I am a Rākṣasa, these women cannot be killed by my weapons on account of the power of Mantras. They have cropped up in plenty and all my armies are killed.

## \|\| 1.149.101 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi tāṃ vidyāṃ prasādhaya mahāmate \|*  
*yadi me vāṃchasi śreyo nānyathāsti jayo raṇe \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Hence, O highly intelligent one, you also employ the same Vidyā if you wish my good; otherwise there is no hope of victory in the battle.”

## Chapter 150 - Greatness of Kelīśvarī (Keli-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.150.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śukrastasya vacaḥ śrutvā citte kṛtvā dayāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ gatvā siddhipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*cakāra vidhivaddhomaṃ svamāṃsena hutāśane \|*  
*maṃtrairātharvaṇai raudraiḥ kuṇḍaṃ kṛtvā trikoṇakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On hearing his words, Śukra took pity on him. He went to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara that yields Siddhis and duly performed the Homa in fire by means of his own flesh in the triangular Kuṇḍa made by himself. He recited the Ātharvaṇa and Rudra Mantras while performing the Homa.

## \|\| 1.150.3 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃjuhvatastasya tena vai vidhinā tadā \|*  
*yathā rudreṇa saṃtuṣṭā devī kelīśvarī tadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. While he performed the Homa with the same procedure as employed by Rudra, Goddess Kelīśvarī became pleased.

## \|\| 1.150.4-5 \|\|

*taṃ provāca sametyāśu śukraṃ daityapurohitam \|*  
*mā tvaṃ bhārgavaśārdūla kuru māṃsaparikṣayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhāvitā'haṃ trinetreṇa tatkiṃ brūhi karomi te \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. She quickly approached Śukra, the priest of Daityas, and said: “O tiger among the scions of the family of Bhṛgu, do not waste your flesh. I have been created and sanctified by the Three-eyed Lord. Tell me what I need do unto you.”

## \|\| 1.150.6 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*yathā rudrasya sāhāyyaṃ tvayātra vihitaṃ śubhe \|*  
*aṃdhakasyā'pi kartavyaṃ tathaivaiṣa varo mama \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śukra said:

6\. O auspicious goddess, just as you rendered assistance to Rudra in the battle, today extend the same assistance to Andhaka. That is the boon I seek.

## \|\| 1.150.7 \|\|

*ye keciddānavā yuddhe bhakṣitāśca vināśitāḥ \|*  
*asya sainyasya te sarve punarjīvaṃtu satvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Those Dānavas of his army who were killed or swallowed should become alive quickly.

## \|\| 1.150.8 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*jīvayiṣyāmi tānsarvāndānavānnihatānraṇe \|*  
*navasaṃbhakṣitānvipra praviṣṭānyoginīmukhe \|\| 8 \|\|*

The Devī said:

8\. O Brāhmaṇa, I shall resuscitate all those Dānavas killed in battle and recently swallowed, those who entered the mouths of the Yoginīs.

## \|\| 1.150.9 \|\|

*evamuktvā dadau tasmai sā devī harṣitānanā \|*  
*nāmnā'mṛtavatīṃ vidyāṃ yayā jīvaṃti te mṛtāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying thus the goddess delighted in her face gave him the Vidyā named Amṛtavatī by which the dead could regain life.

## \|\| 1.150.10-13 \|\|

*tataḥ śukraḥ prahṛṣṭātmā gatvāṃdhakamuvāca ha \|*  
*siddhā kelīśvarī devī yathā śambhostathā mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tayā dattā śubhā vidyā mama daityā mṛtāśca ye \|*  
*tānsarvāṃstatprabhāvena yojayiṣyāmi jīvite \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tvayā'syāḥ satataṃ bhaktiḥ kāryā dānava sattama \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa caturdaśyāṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*eṣā sā paramā śaktiryayā vyāptamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*kevalaṃ bhaktisādhyā sā na daṇḍena kathaṃcana \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Then, delighted within himself Śukra went to Andhaka and said: “Goddess Kelīśvarī has been won over by me as in the case of Śaṃbhu. An auspicious Vidyā has been granted to me by her. By its power, I shall resuscitate all those Daityas who died.

O most excellent one among the Dānavas, you must have devotion to this goddess always. On the eighth lunar day especially and on the fourteenth always she should be worshipped.

She is that great Śakti by whom this universe has been pervaded. She could be propitiated only through devotion and not at all by means of force.”

## \|\| 1.150.14 \|\|

*evamuktastu śukreṇa sa tadā dānavādhipaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmāsa bhāvabhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On being told thus by Śukra, the overlord of the Dānavas adored that goḍdess with devotion and emotional fervour.

## \|\| 1.150.15 \|\|

*stutvā ca vividhaiḥ stotraistataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*tathānyā mātaraḥ sarvā yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathākramam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After eulogizing her and all the Mātṛs by means of various kinds of prayers, he spoke to her paying respects to the Mothers in due order of seniority:

## \|\| 1.150.16 \|\|

*ajñānādyanmayā devi kṛtaḥ kopastavopari \|*  
*marṣaṇīyastathā so'dya dīnasya praṇatasya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O goddess, I was angry with you due to ignorance. That should be excused. I am wretched. I have bowed down to you.”

## \|\| 1.150.17 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭā'smi te vatsa prabhāvādbhārgavasya ca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya tasmāttvaṃ na vṛthā darśanaṃ mama \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

17\. O dear one, I am pleased with you and the power of Bhārgava. Hence choose your boon. My sight cannot go in vain.

## \|\| 1.150.18 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa ye tvāṃ dhyāyaṃti dehinaḥ \|*  
*pūjayaṃti ca sadbhaktyā saṃsthāpya pratimāṃ tava \|*  
*teṣāṃ siddhiḥ pradātavyā tvayā hṛdayavāṃchitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

18\. If embodied beings install your image in this form and meditate upon you with great devotion, a Siddhi desired by them in their heart should be granted by you.

## \|\| 1.150.19 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yo māmanena rūpeṇa sthāpayiṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tasya mokṣaṃ pradāsyāmi pāpasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The Devī said:

19\. If any man, even if he be a sinner, installs my image in this form, I shall grant him salvation. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.150.20 \|\|

*yo'ṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ mama pūjāṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*tasmai svargaṃ pradāsyāmi pāpasyāpi danūttama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O most excellent one among the Dānavas, if a man performs my adoration on the eighth or fourteenth lunar day, I will grant him Svarga even if he is a sinner.

## \|\| 1.150.21 \|\|

*kevalaṃ darśanaṃ yaśca dhyānaṃ vā me kariṣyati \|*  
*tasya rājyaṃ pradāsyāmi bhogānmānuṣasaṃbhavān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If anyone simply visits me or meditates on me, I will grant him kingdom and all human pleasures.

## \|\| 1.150.22 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha sā devī tataścādarśanaṃ gatā \|*  
*taiśca mātṛgaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ paśyatastasya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After saying thus, the goddess vanished along with the groups of the Mātṛs in an instant even as he remained watching.

## \|\| 1.150.23 \|\|

*śakro'pi dānavānsarvāṃstayā saṃsiddhayā tataḥ \|*  
*mṛtānsaṃjīvayāmāsa daiteyānnavabhakṣitān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By means of the Vidyā achieved by him, Śukra brought to life all the dead and the recently swallowed Dānavas and Daityas.

## \|\| 1.150.24 \|\|

*taiḥ sametya sa daityendraḥ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*tāṃ purīṃ prāpya śakrasya rājyaṃ cakre divāniśam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Joining them with delighted mind, the leader of the Daityas went to the city of Śakra and ruled the kingdom day and night.

## \|\| 1.150.25 \|\|

*tāṃ devīṃ dhyāyamānastu pūjayāno divāniśam \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa mahābalaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The highly powerful Dānava meditated on and adored the goddess day and night particularly on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days.

## \|\| 1.150.26 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ prabhāvaṃ taṃ jñātvā vyāsasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*sthāne'tra sthāpayāmāsa saṃsiddhiṃ pa parāṃ gataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Knowing the power of the goddess Vyāsa’s son (Kapiñjala) installed the goddess in this holy spot and attained perfection.

## \|\| 1.150.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\|*  
*evaṃ kelīśvara devī saṃjātā parameśvarī \|*  
*tasmātsthāpyā ca pūjyā ca dhyeyā caiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. Thus goddess Kelīśvarī, the great goddess, originated. Hence, she should be installed, worshipped and meditated upon.

## \|\| 1.150.28 \|\|

*evaṃ devyā naro yaśca paṭhate vā śṛṇoti vā \|*  
*vācyamānaṃ sa mucyeta vyasanena garīyasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A man who reads the story of the goddess or listens to it when it is read shall be rid of great distress.

## \|\| 1.150.29 \|\|

*bhraṣṭarājyo'thavā rājā yaḥ śṛṇotyaṣṭamīdine \|*  
*sa rājyaṃ labhate bhūyo nikhilaṃ hatakaṃṭakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If a king ousted from his kingdom, listens to this on the eighth (lunar) day he gets back the entire kingdom again with all the enemies destroyed.

## \|\| 1.150.30 \|\|

*yuddhakāle ca saṃprāpte yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*sa hatvā śatrusaṃghātaṃ vijayaṃ ca samāpnuyāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When war is imminent, if a man listens to this, he will kill all the enemies and attain victory.

## Chapter 151 - Greatness of Bhairava Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.151.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*andhako'pi parāṃ vidyāṃ jñātvā śukrārjitāṃ tadā \|*  
*kelīśvaryāḥ prasādaṃ ca bhaktijaṃ balavṛddhidam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*avadhyatāmātmanaśca pitāmahavarodbhavam \|*  
*maheśvaraṃ samuddiśya kopaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: The Purāṇa author used the Andhaka legend to glorify this Tīrtha. As against the version given here in Mahbāhārata, Anuśāsana 14.214-215 and Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa 6. 43.6 Śaṅkara killed Andhaka.

Sūta said:

1-2. On coming to know that the great Vidyā has been acquired by Śukra, that Kelīśvarī has been pleased with devotion, that the Vidyā bestowed increased strength, and recollecting that he had been rendered difficult to be killed as a result of the boon of Pitāmaha, Andhaka became furious with Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.151.3-5 \|\|

*dūtaṃ ca preṣayāmāsa kailāsaṃ parvataṃ prati \|*  
*gaccha dūta haraṃ brūhi mama vākyena sāṃpratam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śakramenaṃ parityajya sukhaṃ tiṣṭhātra parvate \|*  
*no ceddrutaṃ samāgatya sakailāsaṃ sabhāryakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sagaṇaṃ ca raṇe hatvā sukhī sthāsyāmi naṃdane \|*  
*tvāmahaṃ nāśayiṣyāmi satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. He sent a messenger to Kailāsa mountain instructing him: “O messenger, go and tell Hara these words of mine now:

‘Leave the side of Śakra and stay comfortably here on this mountain. Otherwise, I will come there quickly and kill you in battle along with your wife and Gaṇas. Then I will stay happily in the Nandana garden. I will destroy you. This is the solemn oath I take.’”

## \|\| 1.151.6 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa daityena dūto gatvā drutaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*provāca śaṃkaraṃ vākyaiḥ paruṣaiḥ sa viśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On being told thus by the Daitya, the messenger hurried there and told Śaṅkara those harsh words.

## \|\| 1.151.7 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*gaṇānsaṃpreṣayāmāsa vadhārthaṃ tasya durmateḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereupon, the Bull-emblemed Lord became very furious and he despatched the Gaṇas to kill that wicked fellow.

## \|\| 1.151.8-9 \|\|

*vīrabhadraṃ mahākālaṃ naṃdiṃ hastimukhaṃ tathā \|*  
*aghoraṃ ghoranādaṃ ca ghoraghaṃṭaṃ mahābalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*eteṣāmanugāścānye koṭirekā pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*sarvānsaṃpreṣayāmāsa vadhārthaṃ tasya durmateḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The leaders were Vīrabhadra, Mahākāla, Nandin, Hastimukha, Aghora, Ghoranāda and the mighty Ghoraghaṇṭa. Each of these had ten million followers under him. The Lord sent them all to kill that wicked one.

## \|\| 1.151.10 \|\|

*atha saṃpreṣitāstena gaṇāste vikṛtānanāḥ \|*  
*harṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭā garjamānā yathā ghanāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On being despatched thus by him, the Gaṇas of hideous faces became extremely delighted. They roared like rumbling clouds.

## \|\| 1.151.11 \|\|

*dhṛtāyudhā gatāḥ sarve yuddhārthaṃ yatra sā purī \|*  
*śakrasyāsāditā tena dānavena balīyasā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Holding up the weapons for the battle, all of them went to that city of Śakra which the powerful Dānava had occupied.

## \|\| 1.151.12 \|\|

*atha prāptāngaṇāndṛṣṭvā dānavāste dhṛtāyudhāḥ \|*
