*niścakramurvai sahasā yuddhārthamatigarvitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing that the Gaṇas had come, the Dānavas too seized their weapons arrogantly and rushed out at once with the intention of giving a tough fight.

## \|\| 1.151.13 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ gaṇānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*parasparaṃ mahāraudraṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then a battle ensued between the Gaṇas and the Dānavas. The mutual fight was extremely violent. They kept back death reversed (regarded retreat as death). They were not afraid of death.

## \|\| 1.151.14 \|\|

*tato haragaṇāḥ sarve dānavaistai raṇājire \|*  
*jitā jagmurdiśo bhītā haravīkṣaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then in the battle, all the Gaṇas of Hara were defeated by the Dānavas. They fled to the various quarters in their fright. They became eager to see Hara.

## \|\| 1.151.15 \|\|

*haro'pi tāngaṇānbhagnāndṛṣṭvā kopādviniryayau \|*  
*haraṃ dṛṣṭvā tato daityā duddruvuste diśo daśa \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing his Gaṇas shattered, Hara came out angrily. On seeing Hara, the Daityas fled in all the ten directions.

## \|\| 1.151.16 \|\|

*andhako'pi haraṃ dṛṣṭvā yuddhārthaṃ saṃmukho yayau \|*  
*tato yuddhaṃ samabhavadaṃdhakasya hareṇa tu \|*  
*vṛtravāsavayoḥ pūrvaṃ yathā yuddhamabhūnmahat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing Hara, Andhaka came face to face with him for the sake of fighting. Thereupon, the fight between Andhaka and Hara started even as the great battle between Vṛtra and Vāsava had occurred earlier.

## \|\| 1.151.17 \|\|

*cakranālīkanārācaistomaraiḥ khaḍgamudgaraiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ na śakyate haṃtuṃ dānavo vividhāyudhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (Hara fought with) various weapons like discus, shafts, arrows, Tomaras, swords and hammers. But that Dānava could not be killed by these various weapons.

## \|\| 1.151.18 \|\|

*astrayuddhaṃ parityajya bāhu yuddhamupāgatau \|*  
*karaṃ kareṇa saṃgṛhya muṣṭipraharaṇau tadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then they ceased to fight with weapons. They resorted to (wrestling) a hand-to-hand fight. Each grasped the other by the hand and began to hit with fist.

## \|\| 1.151.19 \|\|

*dānavenātha deveśo baṃdhenākramya pīḍitaḥ \|*  
*niṣpaṃdabhāvamāpannastato mūrcchāmupāgataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Lord of Devas was kept bound by the Dānava and great pain was inflicted on him. He remained motionless and fell in a swoon.

## \|\| 1.151.20 \|\|

*mūrchāgataṃ tu tajjñātvā hyandhako niryayau gṛhāt \|*  
*tāvatsthāṇuḥ kṣaṇāllabdhvā cetanāmāttakārmukaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Coming to know that he had fallen in a swoon Andhaka went out of the abode (?) In an instant Sthāṇu (Śiva) regained consciousness and took up his bow.

## \|\| 1.151.21 \|\|

*āyasīṃ lakuṭīṃ gṛhya prabhurbhārasahasi kām \|*  
*dānavendraṃ tataḥ prāpya tāḍayāmāsa mūrdhani \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Lord then lifted an iron rod weighing a thousand Bhāras, approached the leader of the Dānavas and struck him on his head.

## \|\| 1.151.22 \|\|

*so'pi khaḍgena deveśaṃ tāḍayāmāsa vegataḥ \|*  
*atha devo'pi sasmāra kauberāstraṃ mahāhave \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He struck the Lord of the Devas quickly and forcibly with a sword. Then the Lord remembered the missile of Kubera in the great battle.

## \|\| 1.151.23 \|\|

*astreṇa tena hṛdaye tāḍayāmāsa dānavam \|*  
*tataḥ sa tāḍitastena rudhirodgāramudvaman \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With the missile he struck the Dānava in his chest. Being struck therewith he vomited blood.

## \|\| 1.151.24 \|\|

*patito'dhomukho bhūtvā tataḥ śūlena bheditaḥ \|*  
*śūlāgrasaṃsthitaḥ pāpaścakravadbhramate tataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. With the face turned downwards he fell down. Then he was pierced with the trident. Perched on the top of the trident, the sinful (Andhaka) began to whirl like a wheel.

## \|\| 1.151.25 \|\|

*andhako'pi tadātmānaṃ tathāvasthamavekṣya ca \|*  
*tato vāgbhiḥ supuṣṭābhirastauddevaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Finding himself in that plight, Andhaka eulogized Lord Maheśvara with richly worded prayer:

## \|\| 1.151.26 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*namaste jagatāṃ dhātre śarvāya triguṇātmane \|*  
*vṛṣabhāsanasaṃsthāya śaśāṃkakṛtabhūṣaṇa \|\| 26 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

26\. Obeisance to you, to Śarva, O creator of the worlds, having the three Guṇas within. O Lord with the moon (worn) as an ornament, obeisance to the Lord stationed on (riding) the bull.

## \|\| 1.151.27 \|\|

*namaḥ khaṭvāṃgahastāya namaḥ śūladharāya ca \|*  
*namo ḍamarukodaṇḍakapālānaladhāriṇe \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Obeisance to the Lord holding the Khaṭvāṅga in the hand, to the holder of the trident. Obeisance to the Lord holding Ḍamaru drum, Kodaṇḍa (bow), skull and fire.

## \|\| 1.151.28 \|\|

*smaradehavināśāya mūrtyaṣṭakamayātmane \|*  
*namaḥ svarūpadehāya hyarūpabahurū piṇe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Obeisance to the destroyer of the body of Smara, to the supreme soul with eight cosmic bodies. Obeisance to the Lord with his handsome body, to the Lord devoid of form, to the multi-formed one.

## \|\| 1.151.29 \|\|

*uttamāṃgavināśāya viriṃceḥ sṛṣṭikāriṇe \|*  
*smaśānavāsine nityaṃ namo bhairavarūpiṇe \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Obeisance to the destroyer of the head of Viriñci (Brahmā), to the cause of creation, to the permanent resident of cremation ground. Obeisance to the Lord of Bhairava (terrible) form.

## \|\| 1.151.30 \|\|

*sarvagaḥ sarvakartā ca tvaṃ hartā nānya eva hi \|*  
*tvaṃ bhūmistvaṃ rajaścaiva tvaṃ jyotistvaṃ tamastathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. You are present everywhere; you are the creator of all. You alone are the destroyer and none else. You are the earth; you are the Rajas; you are the light as well as the darkness.

## \|\| 1.151.31 \|\|

*tvaṃ vapuḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jīvabhūto maheśvara \|*  
*astaudevaṃ dānavendro devaśūlāgra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Maheśvara, you constitute the body of all living beings; you are the soul of every individual.

Thus the leading Dānava eulogized even as he was held perched on the tip of the trident.

## \|\| 1.151.32 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya stutiṃ śrutvā parituṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ provāca taṃ harṣācchūlāgrasthaṃ danūttamam \|\| 32 \|\|*

Sūta said:

32\. On hearing his eulogy thus, Maheśvara was delighted. He joyously told the excellent Danuja held on the tip of the trident:

## \|\| 1.151.33 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*nedaṃ vīravrataṃ daitya yacchatrukarapīḍanāt \|*  
*procyante sāmavākyāni viśeṣāddaityajanmanā \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

33\. O Daitya, this is not the established practice of heroes, especially of one born as a Daitya, to utter conciliatory words at the time of being afflicted at the hands of an enemy.

## \|\| 1.151.34 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*nirviṇṇo'smi suraśreṣṭha triśūlā'graṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsūdaya māṃ yena drutaṃ syānme vyathākṣayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

34\. O most excellent one among Suras, I have become disgusted and dejected on remaining held up on the tip of the trident. Hence do slay the quickly so that my pain can be reduced.

## \|\| 1.151.35 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*na te'sti maraṇaṃ daitya kathaṃcicciṃtitaṃ mayā \|*  
*tenetthaṃ vidhṛtaṃ vyomni bhittvā śūlena vakṣasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

35\. Your death has never been intended by me. Hence, you have been pierced in the chest by the trident and held thus.

## \|\| 1.151.36 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gaṇatāṃ gaccha sāṃprataṃ pāpavarjitaḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā dānavajaṃ bhāvaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Giving up your demoniac nature and behaviour you will be freed from sin. Attain the state of a Gaṇa and be equipped with great faith.

## \|\| 1.151.37 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*gato me dānavo bhāvaḥ sāṃprataṃ tava kiṃkaraḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi na sandehaḥ satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 37 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

37\. My Dānava state has disappeared. Now I shall be your servant undoubtedly. I solemnly take this oath.

## \|\| 1.151.38 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa brūhi yatte'bhivāṃchitam \|*  
*prārthayasva prayacchāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

38\. O dear one, I am pleased with you. Tell me what is desired by you. Request. I shall grant it even if it is difficult to obtain.

## \|\| 1.151.39-40 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa śṛlāgrasthitamattanum \|*  
*yo martyorccāṃ prakṛtvā te sthāpayiṣyati bhūtale \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tasya mokṣastvayā deyo madvākyātsurasattama \|*  
*tathetyuktvā maheśastaṃ śūlāgrātpramumoca ha \|*  
*asthiśeṣaṃ kṛśāṃgaṃ ca cāmuṇḍāsadṛśaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

39-40. If a man makes an image of yours with my body as it is now fixed at the tip of the trident, and places it on the ground, O most excellent one among Suras, salvation should be granted to him by you at my instance.

Saying “So it shall be” Maheśa freed him from the tip of the trident. O Brāhmaṇas, he was a skeleton of bones, very lean and resembling Cāmuṇḍā.

## \|\| 1.151.41 \|\|

*tataḥ sa gaṇatāṃ prāpto gītaṃ cakre manoharam \|*  
*purato devadevasya pārvatyāśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then he attained the status of a Gaṇa. He sang a melodious song before the Lord of Devas and Pārvatī too.

## \|\| 1.151.42 \|\|

*bhṛṃgavadraṭanaṃ yasmāttasya śrotrasukhā vaham \|*  
*bhṛṃgīriṭi iti proktastataḥ sa tripurāriṇā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. His Raṭana (voice) was pleasing to. the ears like the humming sound of a black bee. So he was called Bhṛṅgīrīṭa by the Slayer of the Tripuras.

## \|\| 1.151.43 \|\|

*evaṃ sa gaṇatāṃ prāpto devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*viśvāsyaḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu tatparaṃ samapadyata \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. It was thus that he attained the status of a Gaṇa of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas. Later on, he became highly trustworthy and prompt in all his duties.

## \|\| 1.151.44 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti loke'tra devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tādṛśenaiva rūpeṇa sthāpyate bhūtale janaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Ever since then, Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, is installed by people on the earth in such a form.

## \|\| 1.151.45-46 \|\|

*prāpyate'tra parā siddhistatprasādādalau kikī \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya rājyādbhraṣṭo mahīpatiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*surathākhyaḥ prasiddho'tra sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tato vasiṣṭhamāsādya sa cātmīyaṃ puro hitam \|*  
*provāca praṇato bhūtvā bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Great Siddhi of super-worldly nature is obtained here with his favour.

Once upon a time, a famous king named Suratha hailing from the solar race, had been ousted from his kingdom. He approached Vasiṣṭha, his own preceptor and he bowed down to him and spoke with eyes dimmed by tears:

## \|\| 1.151.47-48 \|\|

*tvayā nāthena me brahmansaṃsthitenā'pi śatrubhiḥ \|*  
*balācca yaddhṛtaṃ rājyaṃ manda bhāgyasya sāṃpratam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yena me rājyasaṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'pi tvatprasādena nānyā me vidyate gatiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. “O holy Sir, in spite of the fact that you were staying as my guide and master, the enemies have taken away my realm now. I am really unfortunate.

Hence do me this favour so that I may regain my dominion. I have none else to turn to.”

## \|\| 1.151.49 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ te mahārāja madvākyātsatvaraṃ vraja \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 49 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

49\. O great king, if it is so, hurry up and go at my bidding to the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara that accorḍs all Siddhis.

## \|\| 1.151.50 \|\|

*tatra bhairavarūpeṇa sthāpayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*bhujodyatograśūlāgraviddhāndhakakalevaram \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. There you shall install Maheśvara in the form of Bhairava with the boby of Andhaka that is pieced with the tip of trident and raised up in his arms.

## \|\| 1.151.51 \|\|

*nārasiṃhena maṃtreṇa tataḥ pūjaya taṃ nṛpa \|*  
*raktapuṣpaistathā dhūpai raktaiścaivānulepanaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then, O king, worship it uttering the Narasiṃha Mantra and offering red flowers, incense and red unguents.

## \|\| 1.151.52 \|\|

*tataḥ sadvīrya māsādya tejovīryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*haniṣyasyakhilāñchatrūṃstatprasādādasaṃśayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then after attaining excellent virility and becoming equipped with refulgence and heroism undoubtedly, thanks to his favour, you will kill all the enemies.

## \|\| 1.151.53 \|\|

*paraṃ śaucasametena saṃpūjyo bhagavāṃstvayā \|*  
*anyathā prāpsyase vighnānsatyametanmayoditam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Lord should be worshipped by you with great purity; otherwise you will meet with obstacles. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.151.54 \|\|

*atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā satvaraṃ yayau \|*  
*tatra kṣetre tato devaṃ sthāpayāmāsa bhairavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On hearing his words, the king hurried quickly to the holy place and installed Lord Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.151.55 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsa nārasiṃhena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*mantreṇa prayato bhūtvā brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then reciting the Narasiṃha Mantra with devotion, he maintained purity and celibacy and worshipped the Lord.

## \|\| 1.151.56 \|\|

*tato daśasahasrāṃte tasya maṃtrasya saṃkhyayā \|*  
*bhairavastuṣṭimāpannaḥ provā ca tadanantaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. When the Mantra had been repeated ten thousand times, Bhairava became pleased and spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.151.57 \|\|

*śrībhairava uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te rājanmaṃtreṇānena pūjitaḥ \|*  
*tasmātprārthaya yacceṣṭaṃ yena sarvaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Bhairava said:

57\. O king, by being worshipped with this Mantra I am pleased with you. Hence do request for what is desired, so that I can grant you everything.

## \|\| 1.151.58 \|\|

*suratha uvāca \|*  
*śatrubhirme hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tvatprasādātsureśvara \|*  
*tanme bhavatu bhūyo'pi śatrubhiḥ parivarjjitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

Suratha said:

58\. My kingdom has been captured by enemies. May it be mine again, thanks to your grace. It should be free from enemies.

## \|\| 1.151.59-60 \|\|

*anyo'pi yaḥ pumānitthaṃ tvāmihāgatya pūjayet \|*  
*anenaiva tu maṃtreṇa tasya siddhistvayā vibho \|\| 59 \|\|*

*deyā deva sahasrāṃte yathā mama sureśvara \|*  
*tatheti taṃ pratijñāya gataścādarśanaṃ haraḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. If another man comes here and worships you with this Mantra, O Lord, you should grant him Siddhi at the end of a thousand recitations as in my case, O Sureśvara.

After promising him, “So it shall be,” Hara vanished thereafter.

## \|\| 1.151.61 \|\|

*suratho'pi nijaṃ rājyaṃ prāpa hatvā raṇe ripūn \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After killing the enemies in battle, Suratha regained his realm.

## Chapter 152 - Greatness of Cakrapāṇi

## \|\| 1.152.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāni tīrthāni tvayoktā nyatra sūtaja \|*  
*devamānuṣajātāni devatāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tathā vānarajātāni rākṣasasthāpitāni ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūtaputra vadāsmākaṃ yairdṛṣṭaiḥ sparśitairapi \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ labhyate pūrṇaṃ phalaṃ cepsitamatra ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtaputra, you have enumerated innumerable Tīrthas and shrines installed by Devas, human beings, monkeys and Rākṣasas.

Tell us what of all of those Tīrthas and shrines, when visited and touched, will facilitate the full acquisition of desired benefit.

## \|\| 1.152.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāgāstatra saṃkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ caiva liṃgānāmāśra māṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. O highly esteemed ones, it is true that there is no limit to the number of Tīrthas, Liṅgas and Āśramas (hermitages).

## \|\| 1.152.4 \|\|

*tatra yaḥ kurute snānaṃ śaṃkhatīrthe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One who takes his holy bath with great concentration in Śaṅkha Tīrtha especially on the eleventh lunar day, obtains the benefit of all.

## \|\| 1.152.5 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyati naro bhaktyā tatraikādaśarudrakam \|*  
*siddheśvarasamaṃ tena dṛṣṭāḥ sarve maheśvarāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If a man devoutly visits the eleven Rudras there including Siddheśvara, it is as good as all the Maheśvaras have been seen by him.

## \|\| 1.152.6 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyati vaṭādityaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ caitre viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*bhāskarākṛtsnaśo dṛṣṭāstena tatrahi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If anyone visits Vaṭāditya especially on the sixth lunar day in the month of Caitra, it is as though all the Bhāskaras stationed there have been seen by him.

## \|\| 1.152.7 \|\|

*māhitthāṃ paśyati tathā ye devīṃ śraddhayāvitāḥ \|*  
*tena durgāḥ samastāstā vīkṣitā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. If anyone endowed with perfect faith visits Goddess Māhitthā, it is undoubtedly as though all the Durgās have been seen.

## \|\| 1.152.8 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyati gaṇeśaṃ ca svargadvārapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*sarve vināyakāstena dṛṣṭāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If anyone visits Gaṇeśa, the bestower of the heavenly gate (Svargadvāra-prada) on men, it is undoubtedly as though all the Vināyakas have been seen by him.

## \|\| 1.152.9 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhāsthāpitāṃ gaurīṃ yo jyeṣṭhāṃ tatra paśyati \|*  
*tena gauryaḥ samastāstā vīkṣitā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if anyone visits Jyeṣṭhā Gaurī there, installed by Śarmiṣṭhā, it is as though all the Gaurīs have been seen by him.

## \|\| 1.152.10 \|\|

*cakrapāṇiṃ ca yaḥ paśyetprātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevā samastāśca tena tatra nirīkṣitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If a man gets up early in the morning and visits Cakrapāṇi, it is as though all the Vāsudevas have been seen by him.

## \|\| 1.152.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvayāsūta tathā'smākaṃ cakrapāṇiśca yaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*nākhyātaḥ sa kathaṃ tatra vismṛtaḥ kiṃ vadasva naḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle viśeṣeṇa sa draṣṭavyo manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The sages said:

11\. O Sūta, how is it that Cakrapāṇi who is stationed there has not been mentioned to us. Has he been forgotten? Do narrate to us. At what time is he to be seen particularly by learned men?

## \|\| 1.152.12-13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*arjunenaiṣa viprendrāḥ kṣetre'traiva pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*śayane bodhane caiva prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*snānaṃ kṛtvā subhaktyā ca yaḥ paśyeccakrapāṇinam \|*  
*brahmahatyādipāpāni tasya naśyaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12-13. O leading Brāhmaṇas, the Lord was installed here, in this holy spot, by Arjuna. He is to be visited by devotees after getting up early in the morning on Śayana (eleventh day of the bright half of Āṣāḍha) and Bodhana (eleventh day of the bright half of Kārttika) days after devoutly taking the holy bath. If he visits Cakrapāṇi, the sins of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and the like perish instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.152.14 \|\|

*bhūbhārottāraṇārthāya dharmasaṃsthāpanāya ca \|*  
*brahmaṇāvatāritau viprā naranārāyaṇāvubhau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brāhmaṇas, the two deities Nara and Nārāyaṇa were made to incarnate by Brahmā for the purpose of dispelling the burden of the earth and establishing virtue (Dharma).

## \|\| 1.152.15 \|\|

*kṛṣṇārjunau tadā martye dvāparāṃte dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe mithaḥ snehānugau tadā \|*  
*naranārāyaṇāvetau svayameva vyavasthitau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At the close of Dvāpara, these Nara-Nārāyaṇa took incarnation as Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. They took birth on the earth and they were mutually affectionate.

## \|\| 1.152.16 \|\|

*yathā rakṣovināśāya rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe tadvatkṛṣṇo'pi cāparaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Just as Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, took the incarnation on the earth for the destruction of Rākṣasas, so also Kṛṣṇa was another incarnation.

## \|\| 1.152.17-18 \|\|

*yadā pārthaḥ samāyātastīrthayātrāṃ prati dvijāḥ \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhirasamādeśācchakraprasthātpurottamāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*draupadyā sahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā rahasi bhrātaraṃ dvijam \|*  
*provāca praṇato bhūtvā vinayāvanato'rjunaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Arjuna installed the Lord during pilgrimage. When Arjuna happened to see his brother (Yudhiṣṭhira) in their (intimate) privacy with Draupadī, he undertook a pilgrimage from the excellent city of Śakraprastha (Indraprastha) at the instance of Yudhiṣṭhira. He bowed down and humbly submitted:

## \|\| 1.152.19 \|\|

*arjuna uvāca \|*  
*āyudhārthamahaṃ prāptaḥ sāṃprataṃ pārthivottama \|*  
*dvijadhenuvimokṣāya mamājñāṃ dehi pārthiva \|\| 19 \|\|*

Arjuna said:

19\. O excellent king, I have now come here for taking my weapons to get the cows of the Brāhmaṇa released. O king, grant me permission.

## \|\| 1.152.20 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*gacchārjuna drutaṃ tatra nīyante yatra taskaraiḥ \|*  
*dhenavo dvijavaryasya tā mokṣaya dhanaṃjaya \|\| 20 \|\|*

Yudhiṣṭhira said:

20\. O Arjuna, go there quickly to the place where the cows of the excellent Brāhmaṇa are being taken by the thieves. O Dhananjaya, get them released.

## \|\| 1.152.21 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāṃ tato gaccha yāvaddvādaśavatsarān \|*  
*tataḥ pāpavinirmuktaḥ sameṣyasi mamāṃtikam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter undertake a pilgrimage for twelve years. Then, rid of the sins, you will come back to me.

## \|\| 1.152.22 \|\|

*yaḥ sadāraṃ naraṃ paśyedekāṃtasthaṃ tu buddhimān \|*  
*api cātyaṃtapāpaḥ syātkiṃ punarnijabāṃdhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even a sensible man will become highly sinful if he looks at a man in union with his wife in a secluded spot. It is still more so, if the man happens to be one’s own brother.

## \|\| 1.152.23 \|\|

*tasmānna vīkṣayetkañcidekāṃtasthaṃ sabhāryakam \|*  
*bāṃdhavaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa ya icchecchubhamātmanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence one who wishes for his own welfare should not look at anyone in union with his wife in a secluded spot and particularly at a brother.

## \|\| 1.152.24 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya rathamāruhya satvaram \|*  
*dhanurādāya bāṇāṃśca jagāma tadanantaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter, he promised “So it shall be”, hurriedly got into his chariot seizing the bow and the arrows and went away.

## \|\| 1.152.25 \|\|

*yena mārgeṇa tā gāvo nīyante taskarairbalāt \|*  
*tiraskṛtya dvijānsarvāñchitaśastradharairdvijāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brāhmaṇas, he went on that path on which the cows were being taken forcibly by the thieves holding sharp weapons, after warding off all the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.152.26 \|\|

*atha hatvā kṣaṇāccaurāngāḥ sarvāḥ svayamāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*svāḥ svā nivedayāmāsa brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He quickly killed the thieves and brought back all the cows himself and returned them to the noble-souled Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.152.27 \|\|

*tatastīrthānyanekāni sa dṛṣṭvāyatanāni ca \|*  
*kṣetre'traiva samāyātaḥ snānārthaṃ pāṃḍunandanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the son of Pāṇḍu visited many Tīrthas and shrines and came here to this holy spot for the purpose of a holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.152.28 \|\|

*tena pūrvamapi prāyastatkṣetramavalokitam \|*  
*duryodhanasamāyukto yadā tatra samāgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. That holy spot had already been visited by him earlier when he was there in the company of Duryodhana.

## \|\| 1.152.29 \|\|

*atha saṃpūjayāmāsa yalliṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ purā \|*  
*arjuneśvara saṃjñaṃ tu puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then with flowers, incense and unguents he worshipped the Liṅga name Arjuneśvara which had been installed earlier (by him).

## \|\| 1.152.30 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ kauravendrāṇāṃ pāṃḍavānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Similarly (he worshipped) Liṅgas which had been installed by other Pāṇḍavas and leading Kauravas also.

## \|\| 1.152.31-33 \|\|

*atha saṃciṃtayāmāsa manasā pāṃḍunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ naraḥ svayaṃ sākṣātkṛṣṇo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmādatra kariṣyāmi cakrapāṇiṃ sureśvaram \|*  
*prāsādo mānavaścaiva yādṛṅnāsti dharātale \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kalpāṃte'pi na nāśaḥ syādasya kṣetrasya karhicit \|*  
*prāsādo'pi tathāpyevamatra kṣetre bhaviṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Then the son of Pāṇḍu began to think in his mind: ‘I am Nara himself. Hence I shall install here Cakrapāṇi, the Lord of Suras, and also build a palace a like of which no human being has as yet built on the earth.

Even at the close of the Kalpa, this holy spot will not perish at all. The palace too shall be so in this holy spot.’

## \|\| 1.152.34 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā svacitte pāṃḍavānujaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ nirmame paścādvaiṣṇavaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this holy spot will not perish at all. The palace too shall be so in this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.152.35 \|\|

*tato viprānsamāhūya camatkārapurodbhavān \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayāmāsa mataṃ teṣāṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he invited the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura and abiding by their views, he made them install the image.

## \|\| 1.152.36 \|\|

*dattvā dānānyanekāni śāsanāni bahūni ca \|*  
*anyacca pradadau paścātsa teṣāṃ tuṣṭidāyakam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He made various gifts to them and offered many grants of lands. He gave them later other things which gave them satisfaction.

## \|\| 1.152.37 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tānsarvānkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*naro'haṃ brāhmaṇājjātaḥ pāṇḍorbhūmiṃ prapedivān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then with palms joined in reverence, he spoke: “I am Nara (in that birth) born of Brāhmaṇa (but now) begot of the wife of Pāṇḍu.

## \|\| 1.152.38 \|\|

*mānuṣeṇaiva rūpeṇa tyaktvā tāṃ badarīṃ śubhām \|*  
*prasiddhyarthaṃ mayā cātra prāsādo'yaṃ vini rmitaḥ \|*  
*mannāmnā narasaṃjñaśca śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I left the auspicious Badarī and assumed a human form. This palace has been built by me here for the sake of reputation. I have built it with a mind sanctified by faith. The palace has been named after my name Nara.

## \|\| 1.152.39-40 \|\|

*tasmādeṣa bhavadbhiśca cakrapāṇiriti dvijāḥ \|*  
*kīrtanīyaḥ sadā yena mama nāma prakāśya tām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*viṣṇuloke dhvaniryāti yāvaccaṃdradivākarau \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Hence, O Brāhmaṇas, this deity should be glorified always as Cakrapāṇi so that my name could be echoed in the Viṣṇuloka as long as the Moon and the Sun shine.

## \|\| 1.152.41 \|\|

*tathā mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ śayane bodhane hareḥ \|*  
*caitramāse viśeṣeṇa saṃprāpte viṣṇuvāsare \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Further a grand festival should be held on days of Viṣṇu’s going to sleep (Śayana, on the eleventh day in the bright half of Āṣāḍha) and on that of waking up (Bodhana, eleventh day in the bright half of Kārttika) and in Caitra on the day of Viṣṇu (the eleventh lunar day in the bright half of Caitra).

## \|\| 1.152.42 \|\|

*eteṣu triṣu lokeṣu tyaktvemāṃ badarīmaham \|*  
*pūjāmasya kariṣyāmi svayaṃ viṣṇordvijottamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On these three days, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I leave Badarī and perform the worship of Viṣṇu personally.

## \|\| 1.152.43 \|\|

*yastatra divase martyaḥ pūjāmasya vidhā syati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa yāsyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A maṇ who worships this deity on that day shall be rid of all sins and go to Viṣṇuloka.

## \|\| 1.152.44 \|\|

*tathā ye vāsudevasya kṣetre kecidvyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ pradarśanaṃ śreyo nityaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca lapsyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Further all those who are settled in the holy spot of Vāsudeva should be seen by him and welfare will be acquired by him.”

## \|\| 1.152.45 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva tairukto dāśārhaḥ pāṃḍunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadbhāramāveśya praśāṃtenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*yayau tīrthāni cānyāni kṛtakṛtyastataḥ param \|\| 45 \|\|*

Sūta said:

45\. They said: “So it shall be”. The son of Pāṇḍu belonging to the family of Dāśārha (Yādava—from his mother’s side?) entrusted all the responsibility to them. With a calm and peaceful mind, he went to the other Tīrthas. He felt contented.

## \|\| 1.152.46 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra sthito devaścakrapāṇivapurddharaḥ \|*  
*svayameva hṛṣīkeśo jaṃtūnāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus, Hṛṣīkeśa himself, the destroyer of the sins of all the creatures, stationed himself there in the form of Cakrapāṇi.

## \|\| 1.152.47 \|\|

*adyā'pi ca kalā viṣṇoḥ prāpte caikādaśītraye \|*  
*pūrvoktena vidhānena tasmācchraddhāsamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*sadaiva pūjanīyaśca vandanīyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even today, on the three Ekādaśī days the Lord’s digit (part) thus manifests himself. Hence, he should be worshipped always by persons endowed with faith in accordance with the injunctions laid down before. He should be specially honoured and adored.

## Chapter 153 - Origin of Apsarā Kuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.153.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti rūpatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra snāto naraḥ samyagvirūpo rūpavānbhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ bhagavatā tena brahmaṇā loka kartṛṇā \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ kṛtvā ca vistīrṇāṃ yathoktaṃ ca caturvidhām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa rūpasaṃcayasaṃyutām \|*  
*ekāmapsarasaṃ divyāṃ devamāyāṃ sṛjāmyaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Further, there is another excellent Tīrtha there called Rūpatīrtha. A man who properly takes his holy bath there becomes handsome even if he is ugly.

Formerly, Lord Brahmā, the creator of the world, brought into being the vast creation of the four types as mentioned.

Thereafter he thought: ‘I shall create a divine Apsarā, Devamāyā, endowed with all the characteristics of beauty.’

## \|\| 1.153.4-5 \|\|

*tataśca sarvadevānāṃ samādāya tilaṃtilam \|*  
*rūpaṃ ca nirmame paścādatyāścaryamayīṃ ca tām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣobhamāpannaḥ svayameva pitāmahaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He took a Tila (a gingelly seed, minute part) from all the Devas and created a highly wonderful female being, on seeing whom Pitāmaha himself became excited.

## \|\| 1.153.6 \|\|

*tatastāṃ preṣayāmāsa kailāsaṃ prati padmajaḥ \|*  
*gaccha devi mahādevaṃ praṇamasva śucismite \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then, the Lotus-born One sent her to Kailāsa: “O fair lady of pure smiles, go and bow down to Mahādeva.”

## \|\| 1.153.7 \|\|

*tataḥ sā satvaraṃ gatvā kailāsaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*apaśyacchaṃkaraṃ tatra nirviṣṭaṃ pārvatīsamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then, she hurriedly went to the excellent mountain Kailāsa. There she saw Śaṅkara seated along with Pārvatī.

## \|\| 1.153.8 \|\|

*śaṃkaro'pi ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sudṛṣṭāṃ nākarodbhītyā pārśvasthāṃ vīkṣya pārvatīm \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing her, even Śaṅkara was extremely surprised. Seeing that Pārvatī was by his side, he did not openly look at her because he was afraid.

## \|\| 1.153.9 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ cakre sā praṇamya maheśvaram \|*  
*śraddhayā parayā yuktā kṛtāṃjalipuṭā sthitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Endowed with great faith and keeping the palms joined in reverence, she bowed down to Maheśvara and (began to) circumambulate him.

## \|\| 1.153.10 \|\|

*yāvaddakṣiṇapārśvasthā tāvadvaktraṃ sa dakṣiṇam \|*  
*pracakāra mahādevastadupākṛṣṭalocanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When she came to the southern side, Mahādeva whose eyes were attracted by her, created a southern face of his.

## \|\| 1.153.11 \|\|

*paścimāyāṃ yadā sā'bhūtpradakṣiṇavaśācchubhā \|*  
*paścimaṃ vadanaṃ tena tadarthaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As the splendid lady came to the west in the course of her circumambulation, the western face was created by him.

## \|\| 1.153.12 \|\|

*evamuttarasaṃsthāyāṃ tasyāṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*uttaraṃ vadanaṃ klṛptaṃ gaurībhītena cetasā \|*  
*na grīvāṃ cālayāmāsa kathaṃcidapi sa dvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In this manner, when she came to be in the north, the northern face was created by Lord Śaṃbhu who was afraid of Gaurī. (Hence) O Brāhmaṇas, he did not move his neck even a bit.

## \|\| 1.153.13 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra nārado munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*abravītpārvatīṃ paścātpraṇipatya maheśvaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the meantime, Nārada the leading sage (came there) and bowed down to Pārvatī and Maheśvara. Then he spoke to Pārvatī:

## \|\| 1.153.14 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*paśya pārvati te patyuśceṣṭitaṃ garhitaṃ yathā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rūpavatīṃ nārīṃ kṛtaṃ \|mukhacatuṣṭayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Nārada said:

14\. See the misdemeanour of your husband. On seeing a beautiful lady, four faces have been evolved by him.

## \|\| 1.153.15 \|\|

*ahametadvijānāmi na tvayā sadṛśī kvacit \|*  
*asti nārī tathā'nyopi vijānāti sureśvari \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O goddess of Suras, I know this. All men know this that there is no woman like you.

## \|\| 1.153.16 \|\|

*hāsyasya padavīmadya tvaṃ gamiṣyasi pārvati \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ devapatnīnāṃ jñātvānyāsaktamīśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. But, O Pārvatī, on their coming to know that Lord Śaṅkara is attached to another woman, you will be the object of derision of all the wives of all Devas.

## \|\| 1.153.17-18 \|\|

*etaddevi vijānāsi yādṛkcittaṃ śivodbhavam \|*  
*asyā upari veśyāyā niṃditāyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*samādāya nije harmya etāṃ saṃsthāpayiṣyati \|*  
*paraṃ lajjāsamopeto na bravīti vacaḥ śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. O goddess, do you know how Śiva’s mind works? He broods over this harlot censured by intelligent people. He will bring her and settle her in his own palace. But, O splendid lady, overwhelmed by shame, he does not express it in words.

## \|\| 1.153.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā kāṃtaṃ caturmukham \|*  
*krodhena mahatāviṣṭā vikṛtaṃ vīkṣya taṃ haram \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. On hearing the words of Nārada, she found that her dear Lord had four faces. Realizing that Hara had become deformed, she was overwhelmed with anger.

## \|\| 1.153.20 \|\|

*tato nirodhayā māsa drutaṃ sā parvatātmajā \|*  
*sarvanetrāṇi devasya mahiṣīdharmamāśritā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Adopting the practice of chief of queens, the Daughter of the Mountain quickly closed all the eyes of the Lord.

## \|\| 1.153.21 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śailā viśīryaṃti samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*maryādāṃ saṃtyajaṃti sma sarve ca makarālayāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the meantime, all the mountains all round began to shatter. All the oceans transgressed their limits.

## \|\| 1.153.22 \|\|

*pralayasya samutthānaṃ saṃjātaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tāvadbrahmadinaṃ prāptaṃ paramaṃ sṛṣṭilakṣaṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pralaya appeared there, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Then the next day of Brahmā dawned with the re-appearance of creation.

## \|\| 1.153.23 \|\|

*nimeṣeṇa punastasya pralayasya prajāpateḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ sā niśā proktā sarvaṃ toyamayaṃ bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Because of the closing (of the eyes) there was Pralaya. It is called the night of Brahmā, the Prajāpati. Everything becomes flooded with water.

## \|\| 1.153.24 \|\|

*atha tatra gaṇāḥ sarve bhṛginaṃdipuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*so'pi devamunirbhītastāmuvāca sureśvarīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then all the Gaṇas with Bhṛṅgī and Nandin as leaders came there. The celestial sage (Nārada) became afraid and he spoke to the Goddess of Suras:

## \|\| 1.153.25 \|\|

*muṃcamuṃca surajyeṣṭhe devanetrāṇi saṃprati \|*  
*nocennāśaḥ samastasya lokasyāsya bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O senior-most lady of Suras, leave off the eyes of the Lord. Otherwise there will be the utter annihilation of this world.”

## \|\| 1.153.26-27 \|\|

*evaṃ proktā'pi sā devī yāvacca na mumoca tam \|*  
*tāvaddevena lālāṭaṃ visṛṣṭaṃ locanaṃ param \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṛpāviṣṭena lokānāṃ yena rakṣā prajāyate \|*  
*na śakto vārituṃ devīṃ prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Though requested thus, the goddess did not take away her hands.

Then another eye in the forehead was created by the Lord who was moved with pity, so that the worlds could be preserved. He could not prevent the goddess dearer to his own life.

## \|\| 1.153.28 \|\|

*aṃbikāṃ vibudhāḥ prāhustryaṃbakāṇi yato dvijāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsaṃkīrtyate loke tryaṃbakaśca sureśvaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Devas said to Aṃbikā, O Brāhmaṇas: “Since he has three eyes, the Lord of Suras is glorified as Tryaṃbaka.”

## \|\| 1.153.29 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃtyajya taṃ devaṃ devī parvataputrikā \|*  
*provāca koparaktākṣī puraḥsthāṃ tāṃ tilottamām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the goddess, the Daughter of the Mountain, left the Lord. With the eyes turned red due to anger she spoke to Tilottamā who was standing in front:

## \|\| 1.153.30 \|\|

*yasmānme dayitaḥ pāpe tvayā rūpādviḍaṃbitaḥ \|*  
*caturvaktraḥ kṛtastasmāttvaṃ virūpā bhava drutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “O sinful woman, my lover has been deceived by you through your beauty and converted into one with four faces. So be hideous and ugly quickly.”

## \|\| 1.153.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sā sahasā bhūtvā tatkṣaṇādbhagnanāsikā \|*  
*śīrṇakeśā bṛhaddaṃtā cipiṭākṣī mahodarā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then instantaneously her nose became flattened, her hair withered and her teeth elongated. Her eyes were rendered sunken within and her belly protruding.

## \|\| 1.153.32 \|\|

*atha vīkṣya nijaṃ dehaṃ tathābhūtaṃ varāpsarāḥ \|*  
*provāca vepamānā sā kṛtāṃjalipuṭā sthitā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On observing her body transformed thus, the excellent Apsarā trembled. With palms joined together in veneration, she spoke:

## \|\| 1.153.33-34 \|\|

*ahaṃ saṃpreṣitā devi praṇāmārthaṃ triśūlinaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā tena cāyātā yuṣmākaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nirdoṣāyā virāgāyāstasmādyuktaṃ na te bhavet \|*  
*śāpaṃ dātuṃ prasādaṃ me tasmāttvaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “O goddess, I have been sent by Brahmā for the sake of paying obeisance to the Trident-bearing Lord and to you all as well. So I have come here. Hence, it does not behove you to curse me because I am not blameworthy. Nor am I attached. It behoves you to do a favour unto me.”

## \|\| 1.153.35 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā dīnaṃ satyaṃ ca pārvatī \|*  
*paścāttāpasamopetā tataḥ provāca supriyam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing her piteous but truthful words, Pārvatī regretted (her action) and said to her lovingly:

## \|\| 1.153.36-39 \|\|

*strīsvabhāvātsamāyātaḥ kopo'yaṃ tvāṃ prati drutam \|*  
*tasmādāgaccha gacchāvo mayā sārdhaṃ dharātale \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tatrāsti rūpadaṃ tīrthaṃ mayā cotpāditaṃ svayam \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ snānārthaṃ vimalodakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yā nārī prātarutthāya tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sā syādrūpavatī nūnamadṛṣṭe ravimaṃḍale \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sadā māghe tṛtīyāyāṃ tatra snānaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*adya sā tatra yāsyāmi snānāya kṛtaniścayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. “It is due to the innate nature of women that I got angry with you. Hence I got enraged with you all of a sudden. But now let us go to the earth. You do come with me.

There is a Tīrtha there created by me myself for the sake of holy ablution on the third lunar day in the bright half of the month on Māgha. Its waters are green from impurities and it bestows beauty. A woman who gets up early in the morning before the solar disc is visible and takes her holy bath (therein) shall certainly become beautiful.

I take my holy bath there on the third lunar day in the month of Māgha always. Today, it is the same day. I have decided to take my bath. I shall go there.”

## \|\| 1.153.40 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā samādāya sā devī tāṃ tilottamām \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre rūpatīrthaṃ jagāma ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sūta said:

40\. After saying thus, the goddess took Tilottamā to the Rūpa Tīrtha in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.153.41 \|\|

*tatra snānaṃ svayaṃ cakre vidhipūrvaṃ sureśvarī \|*  
*tasyā hyanantaraṃ sāpi bhaktiyuktā tilottamā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. There the goddess of Suras took her bath herself as per injunctions and after her, Tilottamā also bathed with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.153.42 \|\|

*tataḥ kāṃtimatī jātā tatkṣaṇādeva bhāminī \|*  
*pūrvamāsīyadthārūpā tathāsā'bhūdviśeṣataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereupon the lady became very lustrous, in fact more lustrous than what she was formerly in complexion.

## \|\| 1.153.43 \|\|

*atha tuṣṭisamāyuktā tāṃ praṇamya sureśvarīm \|*  
*provāca vismayāviṣṭā harṣagadgadayā girā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then she was highly satisfied. Overwhelmed with surprise, she bowed down to the goddess of Devas. She spoke in vioce choked with delight:

## \|\| 1.153.44 \|\|

*prāptaṃ rūpaṃ mahādevi tvatprasādāccirantanam \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyāmi māmanujñātumarhasi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “O great goddess, I have regained my beauty permanently with your favour. I shall now go to the world of Brahmā. It behoves you to permit me.”

## \|\| 1.153.45 \|\|

*gauryuvāca \|*  
*varaṃ yacchāmi te putri yatkiṃciddhṛdi saṃsthitam \|*  
*tasmātprārthaya viśrabdhā na vṛthā mama darśanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Gaurī said:

45\. O my daughter, your visit to me cannot be futile. I shall grant you a boon. Hence do pray for whatever is cherished in your heart without hesitation.

## \|\| 1.153.46 \|\|

*tilottamovāca \|*  
*ahamatra kariṣyāmi kṣetre tīrthaṃ nijaṃ śubhe \|*  
*tvatprasādena taddevi yātu khyātiṃ dharātale \|\| 46 \|\|*

Tilottamā said:

46\. O splendid goddess, I shall also make my own Tīrtha in this holy spot. Let it attain renown all over the earth with your favour.

## \|\| 1.153.47 \|\|

*tvayā tatrāpi kartavyaṃ varṣāṃte snānameva hi \|*  
*hitārthaṃ sarvanārīṇāṃ rūpasaubhāgyadāyakam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. At the end of every year, you too should take your holy bath there for the sake of the benefit of all women. It should bestows beauty and conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.153.48 \|\|

*gauryuvāca \|*  
*caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ sadāhaṃ tvatkṛte śubhe \|*  
*snānaṃ tatra kariṣyāmi madhyāhne samupasthite \|\| 48 \|\|*

Gaurī said:

48\. O splendid lady, for your sake, I will always take my ablution at the Tīrtha made by you, on the third day of the bright half of Caitra at mid-day.

## \|\| 1.153.49-50 \|\|

*hitārthaṃ sarvanārīṇāṃ tava vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*yā tatra divase nārī tasmiṃstīrthe kariṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

*snānaṃ sā saukhyasaṃyuktā bhaviṣyati sukhānvitā \|*  
*spṛhaṇīyā ca nārīṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Undoubtedly I do so at your instance and for the sake of the benefit of all women. A woman who takes her bath there on that day, will become happy. She will be one loved and liked by all the women on the earth.

## \|\| 1.153.51 \|\|

*puruṣo'pi subhaktyā yastatra snānaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*saptajanmāni rūpāḍhyaḥ sasaubhāgyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even a man who takes his bath there with great devotion will become very handsome for seven births and also enjoy conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.153.52 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tadā devyā sāpsarā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*cakre kuṇḍaṃ suvistīrṇaṃ vimalodaprapūritam \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sūta said:

52\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on being told thus by the goddess, the celestial damsel made a big Kuṇḍa filled with pure water.

## Chapter 154 - Greatness of Citreśvara Pīṭha

## \|\| 1.154.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yā nārī tatra satkuṇḍe snātvā tāṃ pārvatīṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā snāti tatastīrthe tasminrūpamaye śubhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*punaśca pārvatīṃ paśyecchraddhayā parayā yutā \|*  
*sadyaḥ sā mucyate kṛtsnairājanmamaraṇāṃtikaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. A woman who takes her bath in that excellent Kuṇḍa, sees Pārvatī, takes bath again in the splendid Rūpamaya Tīrtha and finally visits Pārvatī with great faith shall be immediately rid of all sins committed from birth till death.

## \|\| 1.154.3 \|\|

*tatraivāsti jayānāma pārvatyāḥ kiṃkarī dvijāḥ \|*  
*tayā tatra kṛtaṃ kuṇḍaṃ gaurīkuṇḍasamīpataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There itself, O Brāhmaṇas, near Gaurī Kuṇḍa is the Kuṇḍa made by the servant maid of Pārvatī named Jayā.

## \|\| 1.154.4 \|\|

*yā tatra kurute snānaṃ tṛtīyādivase'balā \|*  
*sutasaubhāgyasaṃpannā sā bhavetpativallabhā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A woman who takes her holy ablution there on the third lunar day shall become a great favourite of her husband and be richly endowed with conjugal felicity, and happiness due to birth of sons.

## \|\| 1.154.5 \|\|

*tathānyadapi tatrāsti vijayākuṇḍamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātā'pi vaṃdhyā strī jāyate putrasaṃyutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Further, there is another excellent Kuṇḍa named Vijayākuṇḍa there itself. A barren woman who takes her holy bath therein becomes blessed with sons.

## \|\| 1.154.6 \|\|

*na ca paśyati putrāṇāṃ kadācidvyasanaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*na viyogaṃ na duḥkhaṃ ca svapnāṃte ca kadācana \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She does not see even in dreams any calamity befalling her sons, nor separation from them nor any other type of grief.

## \|\| 1.154.7 \|\|

*kākavaṃdhyā'pi yā nārī tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sā putrānvividhāṃllabdhvā svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A Kākavandhyā (i.e. a woman with only one child) who takes her holy bath there shall beget many sons and become honoured in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 1.154.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ sūta tīrthānāṃ tīrthamasti susiddhidam \|*  
*kvacitkiṃñcidbhavetsiddhiryatra snānāccharīrajā \|\| 8 \|\|*

The sages said:

8\. O Sūta, among these Tīrthas, is there any Tīrtha that bestows excellent bodily Siddhi if the bath is taken there?

## \|\| 1.154.9-11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiliṃgāni yāni saṃti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye'bhavatsiddhirekasminnikhilā dvijāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ekasya sattvayuktasya vīravratayutasya ca \|*  
*āśvinasya caturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ardharātre vidhānena teṣāṃ pūjāṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*prāguktaṃ japanaṃ bhaktyā sa kramātsādhakottamaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9-10a. There are twenty-seven Liṅgas. Complete Siddhi will be obtained out of anyone of them by a devotee who is endowed with the Sattva quality and has adopted Vīravrata.

10b-11. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he who, at mid-night on the fourteenth day of the dark half of Āśvina, adores them (those Liṅgas) as per prescribed procedure and in due course devoutly mutters the previously mentioned Mantra is the best of the aspirants.

## \|\| 1.154.12-13 \|\|

*aṃganyāsaṃ vidhāyoccaiḥ kṣurikāsūktamuccarat \|*  
*teṣāmagre punaḥ samyakpūjayitvā ca śaṃkaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pṛthagekaikaśo bhaktyā pūjayeddikpatīṃśca vai \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. After performing Aṅganyāsa (ritualistic touching of the limbs) a devotee should loudly recite the Kṣurikā Sūkta. Then in front of them he should perfectly worship Śaṅkara and devoutly worship the Guardians of the quarters severally.

## \|\| 1.154.14-17 \|\|

*athā'gatya gaṇeśo vai vikarālo bhayānakaḥ \|*  
*laṃbodaro vai nagnaśca kṛṣṇadantasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*khaḍgahasto'bravīdyuddhaṃ prakuruṣva mayā samam \|*  
*muktvaitatkapaṭaṃ bhūmau yadi vīro'si sāttvikaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatastatkarṣaṇāccāpi yastenāśu pratāḍyate \|*  
*sa tenaiva śarīreṇa nīyate tena tatpadam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yatra sthāne jarāmṛtyurna śokaśca kadācana \|*  
*tathā citreśvarīpīṭhe siddhirekasya kīrtitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. (The text is obscure) It is possible that Vighneśa may put obstacles. He may assume hideous and terrific form with protruding belly. He may be nude and he may have black teeth. With the sword in his hand he may say. “Fight with me if you are a hero of Sāttvika type, leave off this (Kapaṭa) (Karpaṭa?) fraudulent practice on the ground.” The devotee may be dragged and beaten, but he is ultimately taken to the highest region along with his own body—the highest region where there is never death or grief. So this Siddhi of one is glorified in the Citreśvarī Pīṭha.

## \|\| 1.154.18-23 \|\|

*māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ yaḥ pīṭhaṃ tatra pūjayet \|*  
*āgamoktavidhānena samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*paścātkapālamādāya mahāmāṃsaprapūritam \|*  
*ahamasya karomyadya mahāmāṃsasya vikrayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*siddhimūlye na gṛhṇātu kaściccedasti sāttvikaḥ \|*  
*tataśca yācate yaśca pragṛhṇāti ca saddvijāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sa tamādāya niryāti yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ liṃgaṃ citraśarmapratiṣṭhitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasya sthānasya madhyastho yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*śivarātrau niśīthe ca puṣpalakṣaṇabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*susiddhimāpnuyāttūrṇaṃ sa śarīreṇa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*siddhisthānāni sarvāṇi tasminkṣetre sthitāni vai \|*  
*vīravrataprayuktānāṃ mānavānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

18-23. (The worship of the goddess in the way of the vulgar Tāmasa people). The Devotee should worship the Pīṭha on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Māgha in accordance with the injunctions in Āgamas. He shall have perfect faith.

Then he takes up a Kapāla (potsherd, skull?) filled with Mahāmāṃsa (human flesh) and declares: “I am selling this Mahāmāṃsa now with Siddhi as the price thereof. If there is any Sāttvika let him take it.”

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he who begs, takes it and goes out to the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra where Lord Maheśvara is present in the form of a Liṅga installed by Citraśarman.

The devotee should seat himself in the centre of that place and worship it on Śivarātri day at midnight with devotion by means of flowers. He shall attain Siddhi with the body at the same instant.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all the Siddhisthānas are present in that holy spot. They are for men who have adopted Vīravrata (the vow of the heroes).

## \|\| 1.154.24 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tāmaso yastvayā proktaḥ siddhimārgo mahāmate \|*  
*anarho brāhmaṇendrāṇāṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

The sages said:

24\. O highly intelligent one, this path of perfection is Tāmasa (that of barbarous and outlandish ones) that has been mentioned by you. This is not worthy of acceptance for great Brāhmaṇas and specially for those who are well-versed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.154.25-26 \|\|

*śuddhāntaḥ karaṇaiḥ sūta bhūtahiṃsāvivarjitaiḥ \|*  
*yathā saṃprāpyate mokṣo brāhmaṇaiḥ sucirādapi \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ brūhi mahābhāga mokṣopāyaṃ dvijanmanām \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O Sūta, O highly esteemed one, tell us the path of salvation for Brāhmaṇas, the way whereby salvation is attained by Brāhmaṇas of pure mental predilection, who eschew injury to all living beings even if it may be a delayed process.

## \|\| 1.154.27-29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*rudrairdaśabhiḥ saṃyuktamānaṃdeśvarakaṃ tathā \|*  
*snātvā tadagrataḥ kuṇḍe śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saṃsiddhimāpnuyānmartyo durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|*  
*māghamāse naraḥ snātvā viśvāmitrahrade naraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pratyūṣe tilapātraṃ ca brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahma loke mahīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27-28a. There is Ānandeśvaraka associated with ten Rudras. A devotee then should take his holy bath in the Kuṇḍa in front of him in accordance with the rules found in the scriptural texts.

28b-29. The man should take his holy bath in the Viśvāmitra Hrada in the month of Māgha. He should take the bath early in the morning and make the gift of a pot of gingelly seeds to a Brāhmaṇa. He shall be rid of all sins and be honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.154.30-31 \|\|

*yadyapi syāddurācāraḥ sarvāśī sarvavikrayī \|*  
*suparṇākhyasya devasya purataḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtvā hyupavāsaparo naraḥ \|*  
*yastyajenmānavaḥ prāṇānna sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. That shall be the result even if he be one with evil conduct, an indiscriminate eater and seller of anything and everything. A man endowed with faith should undertake fast and perform Prāyopaveśa (fast unto death) in front of the Lord named Suparṇa. One who forsakes his life thus is never reborn.

## \|\| 1.154.32 \|\|

*evaṃ siddhitrayaṃ proktaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ hitāvaham \|*  
*sāttvikaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ śaṃsitaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus three different methods of attaining Siddhi have been mentioned. They are beneficial to Brāhmaṇas. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, They are Sāttvika means praised even by Devas.

## \|\| 1.154.33 \|\|

*anyāni tatra tīrthāni devatāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tāni svargapradānyāhurmunayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. There are other Tīrthas and holy shrines. Sages of well praised holy vows say that they bestow heavenly pleasures.

## \|\| 1.154.34 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ kṣetramāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradevasya sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus the greatness of the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara has been fully narrated to you all. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.154.35 \|\|

*yo'tra sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snātvā paśyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sarvāṇyāyatanānyeva sa pāpo'pi vimucyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even a sinner who takes his holy bath in all the Tīrthas and devoutly visits all the shrines, becomes liberated.

## \|\| 1.154.36 \|\|

*etatkhaṃḍaṃ purāṇasya prathamaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*kārtikeyapraṇītasya sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This Khaṇḍa is declared as the first one of this Purāṇa composed by Kārttikeya. It is (both) auspicious and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.154.37 \|\|

*yaścaitatkīrtayedbhaktyā śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*iha bhuktvā suvipulānbhogānyāti triviṣṭapam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He who devoutly reads this or listens to this with concentration shall enjoy all pleasures here and go to heaven.

## \|\| 1.154.38 \|\|

*sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvadānaiśca yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti śṛṇvañchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One who listens with great faith (this Khaṇḍa) attains all the benefits obtained (by pilgrimage to) all Tīrthas and by giving all Dānas.

## \|\| 1.154.39 \|\|

*śrutvā purāṇametaddhi janmakoṭisamudbhavāt \|*  
*pātakādvipramucyeta kulānāmuddharecchatam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. By listening to this Purāṇa one is rid of all the sins arising from millions of births. One redeems a hundred members of his family.

## \|\| 1.154.40 \|\|

*tato vyāsaḥ pūjanīyo vastradānādibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*gobhūhiraṇyanirvāpairdānaiśca vividhairapi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then Vyāsa (the expounder of the Purāṇas) should be honoured by means of the gifts of garments, etc., cows, plots of lands, food offerings etc. of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.154.41 \|\|

*tena saṃpūjito vyāsaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ manuḥ \|*  
*sākṣātsatyavatīputro yena vyāsaḥ supūjitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If the expounder of the Purāṇas is duly honoured then the original Vyāsa Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, the son of Satyavatī, becomes honoured by him.

## \|\| 1.154.42 \|\|

*ekamapyakṣaraṃ yastu guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā hyanṛṇī bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The preceptor may impart to the disciple only a single syllable. Even then there is nothing on the earth by giving of which the disciple can be free from the indebtedness.

## \|\| 1.154.43 \|\|

*etatpavitramāyuṣyaṃ dhanyaṃ sva styayanaṃ mahat \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvaduḥkhebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. This is sacred. This is conducive to longevity and wealth. This results in and leads to welfare. On nearing this great text one is liberated from all miseries. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 155 - A Kṣatriya Addresses His Wife

## \|\| 1.155.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā'nye tatra tiṣṭhaṃti vasavo'ṣṭau dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sthānamekaṃ samāśritya sarvadaiva prapūjitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ekādaśa tathā rudrā ādityā dvādaśaiva tu \|*  
*devavaidyau tathā cānyāvaśvinau tatra saṃsthitau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*devatāstatra tiṣṭhaṃti koṭikoṭipranāyakāḥ \|*  
*ekaikā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ kalikālabhayākulāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yajñabhāgāptaye sadā \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ śuklapakṣe tu madhumāse vyavasthite \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yastānvasūñchucirbhūtvā snātvā dhautāṃbaro naraḥ \|*  
*tarpayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhānpaścātsaṃpūjayennaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Note: Though the printed text does not mention it, the Second Part (Khaṇḍa) begins here. There is duplication of many legends of the First Khaṇḍa in this (Second) Part.

Sūta said:

1-4a. Further, there are other deities also there, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, (such as) the eight Vasus who have resorted to one spot. They are always worshipped by all Devas.

There are also eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas and two Aśvins, the physicians of Devas.

The Devas who are leaders of crores and crores are stationed there, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Everyone of them is overcome with fear of the Kali age.

4b-5. A man (devotee) should take his holy bath on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra. He should wear newly washed clothes and remain pure. After propitiating excellent Brāhmaṇas, the devotee should begin his adoration (of Vasus).

## \|\| 1.155.6 \|\|

*vasavastvā kṛṇvanniti mantreṇānena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ ca tato dadyādvasavaśchaṃdasāviti \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He shall devoutly utter the Mantra, vasavas tvā kṛṇvan. Then he should make the food offering while reciting the Mantra, vasavaśchandasau.

## \|\| 1.155.7 \|\|

*tato dhūpaṃ sugandhaṃ ca yo yacchati samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vasavastvāṃ jetu tathā mantrametamudīrayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The devotee with great concentration should offer incense and sweet scents and utter this Mantra, vasavas tvāṃ jetu.

## \|\| 1.155.8 \|\|

*ārārtikaṃ tato bhūyo yaḥ karoti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vasavastvāṃ jetu tathā śrūyatāṃ yatphalaṃ hi tat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the devotee then offers Ārārtika (waving of lighted lamps) reciting the Mantra, vasavas tvāṃ jetu. Now let it be heard what the benefit that accrues, is:

## \|\| 1.155.9 \|\|

*kanyābhiḥ koṭibhiryacca pūjitābhirbhavetphalam \|*  
*vasūnāṃ caiva tatsarvamaṣṭabhistaiḥ prapūjitaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If the eight Vasus are adored, one gets the benefit of worshipping crores of virgins.

## \|\| 1.155.10 \|\|

*tathā ye dvādaśādityāstasminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*tānsthāpya pūjayitvā ca saptamyāmarkavāsare \|*  
*samyakchraddhāsamopetaḥ puṣpagandhānulepanaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the same manner, the devotee should install and worship those twelve Ādityas who are already settled in that holy place, on the day when the seventh lunar day coincides with a Sunday. He should worship them with flowers, sweet scents and unguents properly with full faith.

## \|\| 1.155.11 \|\|

*paścāttatpuratasteṣāṃ samastānyekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*ādityavrata saṃjñāni tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereafter, before them he performs twenty-one Vratas called Ādityavratas. Listen to the benefit thereof:

## \|\| 1.155.12 \|\|

*koṭidvādaśakaṃ yastu sūryāṇāṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ prāpnuyātkṛtsnaṃ pūjayannātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. One who worships here shall undoubtedly obtain the benefit of worshipping twelve crores of Ādityas.

## \|\| 1.155.13 \|\|

*tathaikādaśarudrā ye tatra kṣetre dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ekasthāne sthitāsteṣāṃ pūjayā śrūyatāṃ phalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Similarly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, listen to the benefit of the worship of the eleven Rudras stationed in one spot in this holy Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.155.14 \|\|

*yastānpūjayate bhaktyā sthāpayitvā sureśvarān \|*  
*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ japecca śatarudriyam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The devotee should install the gods of Suras and devoutly worship them on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra. He should repeat the Śatarudriya Mantra.

## \|\| 1.155.15 \|\|

*ekādaśapramāṇena koṭayastena pūjitāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti nātra saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Śatarudriya Mantra is to be recited eleven times. It will be as good as though eleven crore (Rudras) have been worshipped by him. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that has been stated by me.

## \|\| 1.155.16-17 \|\|

*yathā tāvaśvinau tatra devavaidyau vyavasthitau \|*  
*āśvine māsi cāśvinyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ tathā tithau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yastau saṃpūjayitvā tu hyaśvinīsūktamuccaret \|*  
*dvikoṭi guṇitaṃ puṇyaṃ samyaktena samāpyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Further, the Aśvins, the physicians of Devas, are also stationed there. The devotee should worship them on the full-moon day in the month of Āśvina with the constellation Aśvinī coinciding. He should recite the Aśvinī Sūkta: The benefit acquired thereby shall be twenty million times more.

## \|\| 1.155.18 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ vasusaṃbhavam \|*  
*ādityānāṃ ca rudrāṇāmaśvinordvijasattamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus the greatness of the Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras and Aśvins has been spoken to you all, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.155.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā'nyo'pi ca tatrāsti yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*puṣpāditya iti khyātaḥ sarvakāmaprado nṛṇām \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. Further, there is another deity there installed by Yājñavalkya. It is well-known by the name Puṣpāditya, the bestower of all cherished desires on men.

## \|\| 1.155.20 \|\|

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya taṃ pūjayati mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa taṃ kṛtsnamavāpnoti yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A man may think of any desired object before worshipping. He will obtain it completely even if it is difficult of access.

## \|\| 1.155.21 \|\|

*aputro labhate putrāndhanārthī dhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*bahuvairo'rināśaṃ ca vidyārthī śāstravidbhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One without a son gets sons; a seeker of wealth shall get wealth; one with many enemies will get the enemies destroyed, and a seeker of learning shall become an expert in the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.155.22 \|\|

*saptamyāmarkavāreṇa yastaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*mucyeddinodbhavātpāpānmahato'pidvijottamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a man who visits it on the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday shall be rid of the sins which are accrued on that day even if they happen to be great.

## \|\| 1.155.23 \|\|

*pūjayā hi praṇaśyeta pāpaṃ varṣasamudbhavam \|*  
*nāśaṃ yāti na saṃdehastamaḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By the adoration sins accumulated over a year will perish. There is no doubt about it that it will perish like darkness at the time of sunrise.

## \|\| 1.155.24 \|\|

*aṣṭottaraśataṃ caiva yaḥ karoti pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*phalahastaḥ sa mucyeta hyājanmamaraṇādaghāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He who circumambulates one hundred eight times with fruits in his hand, shall be rid of sins accrued from birth to death.

## \|\| 1.155.25 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇāṃ prakuvāṇo yo yaṃ kāmamabhīpsati \|*  
*sa tamāpnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ niṣkāmo mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person who circumambulates shall obtain whatever he desires undoubtedly. One without desires shall attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.155.26 \|\|

*saṃkrāṃtau sūryavāreṇa yaḥ kuryātsnāpanakriyām \|*  
*abhīṣṭaṃ sidhyate tasya meṣe vā yadi vā tule \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One who performs the rite of bathing (the deity) at the time of Meṣa (Aries) and Tulā (Libra) transit coinciding with a Sunday realizes (his) desires.

## \|\| 1.155.27 \|\|

*tasminsarvaprayatnena vāṃchadbhirīpsitaṃ phalam \|*  
*sa devo vīkṣaṇīyaśca pūjanīyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On that occasion, those who desire the benefit of their choice shall visit and adore the Lord with all efforts.

## \|\| 1.155.28 \|\|

*yaddevaiḥ sakalairdṛṣṭaiścamatkārapurodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*phalamāpnoti taddṛṣṭau tena tatphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The benefit obtained on the visit shall be on a par with the benefit accruing from the visit to all the Devas stationed in Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.155.29 \|\|

*\|ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyena devo'sau yadi tāvatpratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*puṣpādityaḥ kathaṃ prokta etanno vaktumarhasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:

29\. If, as you say, the Lord was installed by Yājñavalkya, why is the deity called Puṣpāditya? it behoves you to explain this.

## \|\| 1.155.30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi cetihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*puṣpādityo yathā jāto yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sūta said:

30\. In this connection I shall narrate an ancient legend as to how the deity installed by Yājñavalkya became Puṣpāditya.

## \|\| 1.155.31 \|\|

*astyatra medinīpṛṣṭhe supuraṃ vaidiśaṃ mahat \|*  
*nānāsaudha samākīrṇaṃ varaprākāraśobhitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Here on the earth there is an excellent great city named Vaidiśā. (Vidiśā). There are many mansions there. It is embellished with many excellent remparts \[ramparts?\] and wells.

## \|\| 1.155.32 \|\|

*udyānaśatasaṃkīrṇaṃ taḍāgairupaśobhitam \|*  
*tatrāsītpārthivaśreṣṭhaścitravarmeti viśrutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Hundreds of parks and lakes adorn it There was an excellent king there well known as Citravarmā.

## \|\| 1.155.33 \|\|

*na durbhikṣaṃ na ca vyādhirna ca caurakṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*tasmiñchāsati dharmajñe satataṃ dharmavatsale \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. While that king who was a knower of Dharma (piety) and who loved virtue always, was ruling over the kingdom, there was no fear from thieves, no ailment and no famine.

## \|\| 1.155.34 \|\|

*tatpure kṣatriyo jātyā maṇibhadra iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa vai dhanena saṃyuktaḥ pitṛpaitāmahena ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In that city there was a person, a Kṣatriya by caste. He is remembered by the name Maṇibhadra. He had plenty of wealth inherited from father and grandfather.

## \|\| 1.155.35 \|\|

*tatpuraṃ sakalaṃ caiva sa rājā maṃtribhiḥ saha \|*  
*kusīdāhṛtavittena vartate kārya utthite \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Whenever necessity arises, the king along with his ministers, nay the entire city, sustained itself through loan taken from him on interest.

## \|\| 1.155.36 \|\|

*sa ca kāyena kubjaḥ syājjarāvyāptastathaiva ca \|*  
*valīpalitagātraśca hyatyaṃtaṃ ca virūpadhṛk \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This Maṇibhadra was an old man of graying hair and wrinkled body (limbs). He was extremely ugly in appearance.

## \|\| 1.155.37 \|\|

*tathā caiva kukīnāśaḥ prabhūte'pi dhane sati \|*  
*na dadāti sa pāpātmā kasyacitkiñcideva hi \|*  
*na bhakṣayati tṛṣṇārtaḥ svayameva kathaṃcana \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He was miserly despite ample wealth. He was a sinner who never gave anything to anyone. He remained thirsty and hungry. He never ate anything (to his fill).

## \|\| 1.155.38-41 \|\|

*evaṃvidho'pi so'tīvavirūpo'pi sudurmatiḥ \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa vai kanyāṃ svajātyāṃ vīkṣya suṃdarīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

*biṃboṣṭhīṃ cārudehāṃ ca muṣṭigrāhyakṛśodarīm \|*  
*padmapatraviśālākṣīṃ gūḍhagulphāṃ sukeśikām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*raktāṃ saptasu gātreṣu trigaṃbhīrāṃ tathā punaḥ \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇāṃ jātīyāṃ sumanoramām \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kṣatriyāddvijaśārdūlā daridreṇa ca pīḍitāt \|*  
*tena tatsakalaṃ vṛttaṃ bhāryāyai saṃniveditam \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. Though that wicked man was like this, and ugly, he happended to see a beautiful girl of his caste. He wanted to marry the girl who had lips like a Biṃba fruit. Her body was beautiful and fascinating. She had a slender belly that could be grasped within one’s fist. Her eyes were large like the petals of a lotus. Her hair was glossy. Her ankles were not visible (because of ample flesh). She was red (in complexion)in seven limbs and deep in three. She was charming and endowed fully with all characteristics. But, O tigers among Brāhmaṇas, he requested for the girl from a Kṣatriya (her father) who was afflicted with dire poverty. He (the father) mentioned everything about this to his wife.

## \|\| 1.155.42 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sā ca duḥkhena mūrcchitā saṃbabhūva ha \|*  
*saṃbodhitā tatastena vākyairdṛṣṭāṃtasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing that she fell into a swoon due to sorrow. Thereafter, he enlightened her with suitable words with suitable (relevant) examples.

## \|\| 1.155.43 \|\|

*kṣatriya uvāca \|*  
*na sā vidyā na tacchilpaṃ na tatkāryaṃ na sā kalā \|*  
*arthārthibhirna tajjñānaṃ dhanināṃ yanna dīyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

The Kṣatriya said:

43\. There is no learning, no art or craft, and no object which is not given to rich people by persons seeking wealth.

## \|\| 1.155.44 \|\|

*iha loke ca dhanināṃ paro'pi svajanāyate \|*  
*svajano'pi daridrāṇāṃ kāryārthe durjanāyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In this world even a stranger becomes a kinsman in the case of rich people. In the case of poor people even a kinsman becomes wicked.

## \|\| 1.155.45 \|\|

*arthebhyo hi vivṛddhebhyaḥ saṃbhṛtebhyastatastataḥ \|*  
*pravartaṃte kriyāḥ sarvāḥ parvatebhyo yathāpagāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. From increased riches collected from here and there, all activities spring up like rivers from mountains.

## \|\| 1.155.46 \|\|

*pūjyate yadapūjyo'pi yadagamyo'pi gamyate \|*  
*vaṃdyate yadavandyo'pi hyanubaṃdho dhanasya saḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. One unworthy of being approached is approached and one not deserving to be saluted is bowed down to. It is the consequence of wealth.

## \|\| 1.155.47 \|\|

*aśanādiṃdriyā ṇīva syuḥ kāryāṇyakhilāniha \|*  
*sarvasmātkāraṇādvittaṃ sarvasādhanamucyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. As sense-organs get activised through eating (food), so all the functions through their causes. Wealth is called the cause of all.

## \|\| 1.155.48 \|\|

*arthārthī jīvaloko'yaṃ śmaśānamapi sevate \|*  
*janitāramapi tyaktvā niḥsvaḥ saṃyāti dūrataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. This world of living beings may resort to even the cremation ground while seeking wealth. A man without wealth abandons even his father and goes far away.

Probably karpaṭa, ‘old garment’, rag indicating old human body.

## Chapter 156 - Maṇibhadra Cheats a Brāhmaṇa Named Puṣpa

## \|\| 1.156.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sambodhitā tena sā bhāryā vijane gatā \|*  
*kanyāpradānasya ruciḥ saṃjātā tadanantaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa pādau prakṣālya maṇibhadrasya satvaram \|*  
*udakaṃ sākṣataṃ haste kanyādānakṛte dadau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*so'pi hastakṛte toye taṃ kṣatriyamuvāca ha \|*  
*adyaiva kuru me śīghraṃ vivāhaṃ kanyayā saha \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yasmādicchāmi saṃsthātuṃ tena te gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*kṣatriya uvāca \|*  
*nātra nakṣatramarhaṃ tu na kiṃcidbhagadaivatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4a. On being addressed thus by him in a secluded spot, the wife evinced her keenness for the offer of the virgin (daughter). Then he washed the feet of Maṇibhadra at once and offered water along with raw rice grain in his hand as a prelude to the offer of the virgin.

As soon as the water was offered in the hand, he insisted to the Kṣatriya: “Perform the rite of marriage with the virgin today itself. For, I wish to set up my household. Hence I have come to your house.”

The Kṣatriya said:

4b. The star is not favourable now. It is not Pūrvā Phalgunī.

## \|\| 1.156.5-6 \|\|

*vivāhasya na vārastu prasupte madhusūdane \|*  
*asminkāle tu saṃprāpte yā kanyā pariṇīyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sā ca saṃvatsarānmadhye dhruvaṃ vaidhavyamāpnuyāt \|*  
*evaṃ daivajñamukhyānāṃ śrutaṃ pravadatāṃ mayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. There is no auspicious time for marriage when Viṣṇu is asleep (i.e. between Āṣāḍha and Kārttika). The girl who is married during this period will certainly become a widow within a year. I have heard prominent astrologers say thus.

## \|\| 1.156.7 \|\|

*tasmācchubhe tu saṃprāpte nakṣatre bhagadaivate \|*  
*tvaṃ vivāhaya me kanyāṃ protthite madhusūdane \|*  
*yena kṣemaṃkarī te syāttathā putraprapautriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence, after the advent of the auspicious constellation of Pūrvā Phalgunī, when Lord Viṣṇu gets up from his sleep, do marry my daughter. She. will then bring welfare unto you and will be blessed with sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 1.156.8 \|\|

*maṇibhadra uvāca \|*  
*nakṣatraṃ vahnidaivatyaṃ prasupto madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Maṇibhadra said:

8\. The constellation is Kṛttikā and Viṣṇu is asleep.

## \|\| 1.156.9 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ vatsarāṃto'yaṃ vivāhe vihite sati \|*  
*kāmāgnirutthitaḥ kāye sāṃprataṃ māṃ prabādhate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Now it will take a year to celebrate the marriage, but the fire of love has risen up and torments me.

## \|\| 1.156.10 \|\|

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me kanyāvivahitena tu \|*  
*tava vittaṃ pradāsyāmi sukhī yena bhaviṣyasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence, do me the favour of giving the girl in marriage. I will give you ample wealth and you will be happy and comfortable.

## \|\| 1.156.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasmācca vittalobhena kṣatriyo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa tatkṣaṇādeva sa dvijāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. So, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Kṣatriya got the marriage celebrated at that very time due to his avariciousness for the money.

## \|\| 1.156.12 \|\|

*dadau kanyāṃ suduḥkhārtāmaśrupūrṇekṣaṇāṃ sthitām \|*  
*sannidhau vahniviprāṇāṃ tadā tena vivāhitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He gave the daughter in marriage, although her eyes were filled with tears and she was very unhappy. In the presence of the Brāhmaṇas and the holy fire, she was taken by him as his wife.

## \|\| 1.156.13 \|\|

*nītvā nijagṛhaṃ paścātkāmadharme niyojitā \|*  
*anicchaṃtīmapi satīṃ tāmatīva nirargalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Later, he took her to his house and engaged her in loveplay. Though she did not like it, he indulged in it unfettered.

## \|\| 1.156.14 \|\|

*so'pi niṣkāmatāṃ prāpya nirbhartsya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*bhāṣikābhiranekābhistāpayitvā ca bhāminīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After the lust got subsided, he began to rebuke her repeatedly. He used many threatening words and made the maiden sad and distressed.

## \|\| 1.156.15 \|\|

*śāṃtiṃ nītā tatastena pratyūṣe samupasthite \|*  
*bhṛtyavargaḥ samasto'pi tato niḥsārito gṛhāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When it was about the daybreak, she was pacified a little. All the servants were then dismissed by him from the house.

## \|\| 1.156.16 \|\|

*irṣyādharmaṃ samāsthāya paramaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*eka eva kṛtastena dvārapālo napuṃsakaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was a case of sheer jealousy, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Only a single servant, an eunuch, was retained as the gatekeeper.

## \|\| 1.156.17 \|\|

*proktaṃ na ca tvayā deyaḥ praveśo'tra gṛhe mama \|*  
*bhṛtyasya bhikṣukasyaiva vṛddhasya vratinastathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He told him: “You must not let into my house any servant or beggar, even an old man observing Vratas.”

## \|\| 1.156.18 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ tu tataścakre janaiḥ samam \|*  
*vyavahārakriyāḥ sarvā dravyalakṣaiḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After making all these arrangements, he began his daily business activities with thousands and hundred thousands in cash.

## \|\| 1.156.19 \|\|

*śvaśurasyāpi no dattaṃ kiṃcittena durātmanā \|*  
*bhāryāyāḥ śvetavastrāṇi muktvā'nyannaiva kiṃcana \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Nothing was given by that wicked fellow even to his father-in-law, and to his own wife nothing except white clothes.

## \|\| 1.156.20 \|\|

*yāmadvaye'pi saṃprāpte dinasya gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*mitamannaṃ tata stasyā bhojanārthaṃ prayacchati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When two Yāmas (six hours) of the day time passed off (after twelve noon) he came home. He then used to give her some measured quantity of foodstuff to eat.

## \|\| 1.156.21 \|\|

*yāvanmātraṃ ca sā bhuṃkta ekaviprānvitaḥ svayam \|*  
*bhuktvā caiva tato yāti vyavahārakṛte bahiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. She was given only enough for eating and while she took her food, he used to take his own food along with a single Brāhmaṇa. After taking food, he used to go out for his business activity.

## \|\| 1.156.22 \|\|

*āgacchati punarharmyaṃ saṃdhyākāla upasthite \|*  
*sā'pi tiṣṭhati harmyasthā patnī tasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then he used to return home at dusk. That wife of this wicked fellow remained throughout within the house.

## \|\| 1.156.23 \|\|

*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ prāptā duḥkhaśokasamanvitā \|\| \|*  
*matsīva patitā toyādanyasmiṃstu sthalāṃtike \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. She was invariably dejected and overcome with sorrow and misery. She was as miserable as a fish that had slipped onto the ground from the water.

## \|\| 1.156.24 \|\|

*cakravākī vimukteva saṃprāpte divasakṣaye \|*  
*haṃsī haṃsaviyukteva mṛgīva mṛgavarjitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. She could be compared to a female Cakravākī that is separated from her mate when the day comes to a close, or to a female swan separated from her mate and to a hind taken away from her deer.

## \|\| 1.156.25 \|\|

*so'pi nityaṃ dadau bhojyaṃ viprasyaikasya ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*procya taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ sāmapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brāhmaṇas, he used to give food to a single Brāhmaṇa everyday, but invariably, he stipulated in a conciliatory tone the following pre-condition beforehand:

## \|\| 1.156.26 \|\|

*adhovaktreṇa bhoktavyaṃ sadā vipra gṛhe mama \|\| \|*  
*yadi paśyasi me bhāryāṃ saṃprāpsyasi viḍaṃbanām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “O Brāhmaṇa, you must always keep your face down when you take your food. If you dare to look at my wife you will meet with mortification.”

## \|\| 1.156.27 \|\|

*evaṃ viḍaṃbitāstena hyūrdhvavaktrāvalokinaḥ \|*  
*ye cānye bhayasaṃtrastā na yāṃti ca tadālayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus many who dared to look up and stare had been subjected to mortification by him. Others who were quite frightened never came to his house.

## \|\| 1.156.28 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya puṣponāma dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena saṃprāptastatpuraṃ prati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Once thereafter an excellent Brāhmaṇa named Puṣpa came to that city in the course of his pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.156.29-30 \|\|

*pūrve vayasi saṃsthaśca darśanīyatamākṛtiḥ \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmaḥ supariśrāṃto madhyāhne samupasthite \|\| 29 \|\|*

*paribhramati vai nṛṇāṃ sa gṛhāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*maṇibhadraḥ samādiṣṭastasya kenāpi bhojyadaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. He was in the prime of his youth and was very handsome to look at. But on this occasion at midday, he was extremely hungry and weary. He wandered among the house of the people around. Someone told him that Maṇibhadra would give him food.

## \|\| 1.156.31 \|\|

*tatastaṃ prārthayāmāsa gatvā bhojyaṃ ca sa dvijāḥ \|*  
*tenāpi sa dvijaḥ proktastadāsau dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Brāhmaṇas, he (Puṣpa) went to him and begged for food. The Brāhmaṇa was told thus:

## \|\| 1.156.32-33 \|\|

*adhovaktreṇa bhoktavyaṃ tvayā vīkṣyā na me priyā \|*  
*no cedviḍaṃbanāṃ vipra saṃprāpsyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāga yatkṣemaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. “You must eat your food with the face kept down. My beloved should not be stared at by you. Otherwise, O Brāhmaṇa, you will undoubtedly meet with unpleasant vexation. Keeping this in mind, O highly esteemed one, do what is conducive to your welfare.”

## \|\| 1.156.34 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmasya na me kāryaṃ paradāravilokanaiḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanayuktasya tīrthayātrāratasya ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

34\. I am now hungry, emaciated with hunger. What do I gain by staring at other men’s wives? I am a student of the Vedas and am now engaged in pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.156.35 \|\|

*maṇibhadra uvāca \|*  
*tadāgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ sāṃprataṃ mama maṃdiram \|*  
*viśeṣāttava dāsyāmi bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇānvitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

Maṇibhadra said:

35\. Then come to my abode along with me now. I shall serve unto you a special food with a monetary gift.

## \|\| 1.156.36 \|\|

*evaṃ tau saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā yayaturbrāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*haṭṭamārge gatau tatra yatra ṣaṃḍho vyava sthitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they made this settlement and proceeded homewards along the market path. They came to the place where the eunuch was standing guard.

## \|\| 1.156.37 \|\|

*tatpārśve brāhmaṇaṃ dhṛtvā praviṣṭo gṛhamadhyataḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā śrapayāmāsa dhānyaṃ mānamitaṃ tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Asking the Brāhmaṇa to wait by his side (i.e. that of the eunuch) he entered the house. A measured quantity of cereal (was given to his wife and) she was asked to cook it.

## \|\| 1.156.38-40 \|\|

*tato devārcanaṃ kṛtvā vaiśvadevāṃta āgatam \|*  
*puṣpamāhūya tatpādau prakṣālya ca niveśya ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kṛtvārcanavidhiṃ tasya dattvānnaṃ ca susaṃskṛtam \|*  
*upaviśya tataḥ paścādbhojanārthaṃ tato dvijāḥ \|*  
*puṣpo'pi vīkṣate tasyāḥ pādau paṃkajasaṃnibhau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yathāyathā sa kautukyādvīkṣate yauvanāśritaḥ \|*  
*kautukyāttena ca tatastasyā vaktraṃ nirīkṣitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. At the close of the worship of the deity and Vaiśvadeva Yajña, Puṣpa was summoned and his feet were washed. He was made to sit and was duly honoured. Well-cooked food was served then, O Brāhmaṇas, Puṣpa sat down for his meal and (in front of him) he saw the lotus-like feet of the woman. The more the Brāhmaṇa in his youth gazed at the feet, the more out of curiosity he looked at her face.

## \|\| 1.156.41 \|\|

*tataścākārayāmāsa maṇibhadraḥ prakopataḥ \|*  
*taṃ ṣaṇḍhamuktavāñjāraṃ tvamenaṃ ca viḍaṃbaya \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This enraged Maṇibhadra. He immediately called the eunuch and said: “Punish this wretched adulterer.”

## \|\| 1.156.42 \|\|

*tatastena dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sa puṣpo mūrdhni tāḍitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Puṣpa was hit on his head by him.

## \|\| 1.156.43 \|\|

*adho nipatitaṃ bhūmau rudhireṇa pariplutam \|*  
*caraṇābhyāṃ samākṛṣya dūto mārgaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He fell down on the ground stained and smeared with blood. The servant caught hold of his feet, dragged him away and left him on the highway.

## \|\| 1.156.44 \|\|

*yāvaccatuṣpathaṃ nīto yatra saṃcarate janaḥ \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsīttasminpuravare tadā \|\| 44 \|\|*
