44\. When he was brought thus to the main thoroughfare where people moved up and down, there arose a long hue and cry in the excellent city.

## \|\| 1.156.45 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva paurāṇāṃ tadavasthaṃ vilokya tam \|*  
*tato'nyaiḥ śītatoyena sobhiṣikto dayānvitaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing him in that plight, all the citizens made a lot of noise. Some people compassionately sprinkled cold water over him.

## \|\| 1.156.46 \|\|

*kṛtvā vāyupradānaṃ ca gamitaścetanāṃ prati \|*  
*sa prāpya cetanāṃ kṛcchrāttattoyāttānathābravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The crowd was made to stand aside and there was open air. He was enabled to regain consciousness. After coming to consciousness with very great difficulty by the use of water, he spoke to them:

## \|\| 1.156.47-49 \|\|

*na mayā vihitaṃ cauryaṃ paradārā na sevitāḥ \|*  
*paśyadhvaṃ maṇibhadreṇa yathāhaṃ kleśito janāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tīrthayātrāparo vipro brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhojanārthaṃ samāmantrya nīto'vasthāmimāṃ tataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kiṃ nāsti vātra bhūpālo yenaitadasamaṃjasam \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa nirdoṣasya mahājanāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. “No theft, no adultery has been committed by me. See ye men, how Maṇibhadra has tortured me.

I am a Brāhmaṇa engaged in pilgrimage. I am under the vow of celibacy. I was invited for food but reduced to this plight.

O men, is there no king here? How is this bad treatment with an innocent Brāhmaṇa allowed to happen?”

## \|\| 1.156.50 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bahavastena pāpena viprāḥ pūrvaṃ viḍaṃbitāḥ \|*  
*rājaprasādayuktena cerṣyāṃ prāpya śarīriṇā \|\| 50 \|\|*

The people said:

50\. Many Brāhmaṇas have been tormented by him earlier. He is blessed with the favour of the king. He is always jealous of other embodied beings (persons).

## \|\| 1.156.51 \|\|

*ko'pi rājaprasādānna kiṃcidbrūte'sya sammukham \|*  
*tasmāduttiṣṭha gacchāmo dāsyāmaste'śanaṃ vayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In view of his favour at the king’s place, no one says anything directly to him. Now get up. We shall give you food.

## Chapter 157 - Boons to Puṣpa by the Sun-god

## \|\| 1.157.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbodhitastaistu lokaiḥ puṣpastadā dvijāḥ \|*  
*tānabravīttataḥ kuddho na kariṣyāmi bhojanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yāvanna cāsya pāpasya kariṣyāmi pratikriyām \|*  
*tadvadadhvaṃ mahābhāgā devo vā devatā'thavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tathānye siddhamantrā vā sadyaḥ pratyayakārakāḥ \|*  
*ārādhitā yathā sadyo mānuṣāṇāṃ varapradāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. O Brāhmaṇas! Though Puṣpa was thus enlightened (and invited for food) by the people, he who was enraged, replied to them: “I will not take food till I do not avenge myself of this sinful fellow. Hence tell me, O fortunate ones, if there is a god or a goddess or (persons who mastered) Mantras which have immediate effect. They should, on being propitiated, confer good boons on human beings immediately.”

## \|\| 1.157.4 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*eko devaḥ sthitaścātra sadyaḥpratyayakārakaḥ \|*  
*tathaikā devatā cātra śrūyate jagatī tale \|\| 4 \|\|*

The people said:

4\. There is one Lord stationed here who will immediately bring about credence. Further a goddess is also spoken about on the earth.

## \|\| 1.157.5 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*ko'sau devaḥ kiyaddūre kasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tathā ca devatā brūta dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 5 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

5\. Who is that Lord? How far away is he? At what spot is he stationed? So also tell me about the goddess.

## \|\| 1.157.6 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure sūryo yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*asti vipra śruto'smābhiḥ sadyaḥ pratyayakārakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The people said:

6\. O Brāhmaṇa, there is Lord Sūrya installed in Camatkārapura by Yājñavalkya. We have heard that he commands instant credence.

## \|\| 1.157.7-11 \|\|

*sūryavāreṇa saptamyāṃ phalahastaḥ pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*yaḥ karoti narastasya hyaṣṭottaraśataṃ dvija \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasya siddhipradaḥ samyaṅmanasā vāṃchitaṃ dadet \|*  
*tathānyā śāradā nāma devī kāśmīrasaṃsthitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*upavāsakṛtereva sāpi siddhipradāyinī \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ janānāṃ sa dvijottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*samuddiśya camatkāraṃ tasmātsthānāttataḥ param \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ prāpya saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tatrāgatya tataḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*gataḥ saṃti ṣṭhate yatra yājñavalkyakṛto raviḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-8a. O Brāhmaṇa! A person who, on the seventh lunar day coinciding with Sunday, circumambulated the deity one hundred eight times with a fruit in his hand, attains excellent Siddhī and obtains whatever he desires in his mind.

8b-9a There is also another deity called Śāradā, originally installed in Kaśmīr \[Kashmir\]. She bestows Siddhis on being adored when one is observing fast.

9b-11. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on hearing the words of those people, he proceeded towards Camatkārapura from that place. He reached Camatkārapura on the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday. He took his holy bath and remained clean. With mental concentration and purity, he reached the place where the Sun-god installed by Yājñavalkya was stationed.

## \|\| 1.157.12 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇāḥ kṛtvā aṣṭottaraśataṃ mitāḥ \|*  
*nālikerāṇi cādāya śraddhayā parayāḥ yutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Holding coconuts in his hand, he performed one hundred eight circumambulations with perfect faith.

## \|\| 1.157.13 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṃṭhaḥ sa pariśrāṃtastadagrataḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭo japaṃ kurvansūryeṣṭaiḥ stavanaistadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then braving hunger, parched throat and great weariness, he sat in front of the deity reciting the prayers liked by the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.157.14-15 \|\|

*maṃḍalabrāhmaṇādyaiśca tāraṃ svaramupāśritaḥ \|*  
*saptayuṃjara vādyaiśca agnireveti bhaktitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ādityavratasaṃjñādyaiḥ sāmabhirdṛḍhabhaktibhāk \|*  
*kṣurikāmaṃtrapūrvaiśca tathaivātharvaṇodbhavaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The Mantras were those beginning with yad etan maṇḍalam tapatī, sapta yuñjanti ratham ekacakram (RV.I. 164.2), agnireva etc. He recited them in high pitch with great devotion. With devout fervour he recited the Sāman verses called Ādityavrata and the Ātharvaṇa Mantras such as Kṣurikā Mantras etc.

## \|\| 1.157.16 \|\|

*yāvadanyorkavārastu naiva tuṣṭo divākaraḥ \|*  
*paurṇamāsīdine prāpte vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He continued this till the next Sunday. When Lord Sun did not become pleased even on the full-moon day, he became extremely dejected.

## \|\| 1.157.17 \|\|

*tataḥ puṣpo vidhāyātha snānaṃ dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*bhūnāmnā sādhya bhūmiṃ ca sthaṃḍilārthaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then Puṣpa took his bath and wore washed cloth. Remaining pure, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he consecrated a piece of land uttering the name of the earth, for the purpose of preparing a sacrificial altar.

## \|\| 1.157.18 \|\|

*sthaṃḍilaṃ hastamātraṃ ca sthaṃḍile pratyakalpayat \|*  
*agnimīḷetimaṃtreṇa tato'gniṃ sa nidhāya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The altar was made a Hasta (hand) high. He repeated the Mantra agnimīle (RV I.I.I) and placed the sacrificial fire there.

## \|\| 1.157.19 \|\|

*tṛṇaiḥ paristṛṇāmītikṛtvopastaraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*ābrahmanniti mantreṇa dattvā brahmāsanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He performed the Upastaraṇa (ritualistic covering) rite repeating the Mantra, tṛṇaiḥ paristṛnāmi. He offered seat unto Brahmā uttering “ā brahman” etc. (VS 22.22)

## \|\| 1.157.20 \|\|

*sutrāmāṇamiti procya samidhaḥsthāpanaṃ ca yat \|*  
*prokṣaṇīpātramāsādya prokṣaṇaṃ kṛtavāṃstataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Uttering the Mantra sutrāmāṇam (RV X. 63.10) he placed the Samit (sacrificial twigs). He went near the Prokṣaṇī vessel and sprinkled the water.

## \|\| 1.157.21 \|\|

*pātrāṇāmatha sarveṣāṃ sruvādīnāṃ yathākramam \|*  
*tataḥ prakalpayāmāsa haviḥsthāne nijāṃ tanum \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Sruvā (ladle) and other utensils were kept in the usual order. In the place of Havis (food offering) he kept his own body.

## \|\| 1.157.22 \|\|

*nyāyaṃ tu devatāsthāne sa ācāryavidhānataḥ \|*  
*grahaṇaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ caiva sūryāya tveti cottaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He placed Nyāya in the place of the deity and considered himself Ācārya (Preceptor) in accordance with the injunctions. Uttering the Mantras sūryāya tvā juṣṭam nirvapāmi sūryāya tvā juṣṭam prokṣāmi, he performed the rites of Grahaṇa (reception) and Prokṣaṇa (sprinkling).

## \|\| 1.157.23 \|\|

*ayaṃ ta idhma ātmeti japtvātha samidhaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*agnisometi mantrābhyāṃ hutvā cājyāhutī tataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Uttering the Mantra ayam ta idhma ātmā he placed the Samit uttering the Mantras agnaye svāhā somāya svāhā he performed two offerings of Ājya (Ghee).

## \|\| 1.157.24 \|\|

*kṛtvā vyāhṛtihomaṃ tu bhūrbhuvaḥ sveti bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*ye te śateti mantrādyairhutvātraiva ca dāruṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He performed the Vyāhṛti Homa by uttering bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Brāhmaṇas. He then performed Dāruṇa (terrible) Homa, with the Mantra beginning with yete śata etc.

## \|\| 1.157.25 \|\|

*āhvayāmāsa vahniṃ ca pratyakṣo bhava deva me \|*  
*evaṃ mantreṇa kṛtvā taṃ saṃmukhaṃ jvalanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He invoked the Fire-god saying “O Lord be visible to me.” Thus he made the fire appear in front.

## \|\| 1.157.26-27 \|\|

*kālīkarālikādyāśca saptajihvāśca yāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tāsāmāhvānakaṃ kṛtvā tato dīpte havirbhuji \|\| 26 \|\|*

*juhāva ca sa māṃsāni svāni cotkṛttya śastrataḥ \|*  
*lomabhyaḥ svāheti vidiśo digbhyo dattvā tataḥ param \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. He then invoked the seven tongues (flames of fire), Kālī, Karālikā etc. and when the fire blazed, he chopped off his flesh in pieces. He offered them to the quarters and interceding directions uttering the Mantra lomabhyaḥ svāhā.

## \|\| 1.157.28 \|\|

*agnaye sviṣṭakṛtaiti yāvadātmānamākṣipet \|*  
*tāvaddhṛtaḥ sa sūryeṇa svahastena samaṃtataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He was then about to offer himself uttering the Mantra agnaye sviṣṭakṛte (Tait. Br. 3.12.2.3.). Immediately he was stopped and held by the Sun-god with his own hand.

## \|\| 1.157.29-30 \|\|

*dhṛtaśca sādaraṃ tena mā vipra kuru sāhasam \|*  
*nedṛgghomaḥ kṛtaḥ kvāpi kadācitkenaciddvija \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tuṣṭo'haṃ ca mahābhāga brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te \|*  
*adeyamapi dāsyāmi yatte manasivartate \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. He was eagerly held and addressed thus: “O Brāhmaṇa, do not do anything rash and reckless. Such a Homa as this has never been performed by anyone anywhere.

O highly esteemed one, I am pleased. Tell me what shall I do? I shall give you whatever is in your mind even if it cannot be ordinarily given.”

## \|\| 1.157.31 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭosi deveśa yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*taddeyaṃ guṭikāyugmaṃ yadarthaṃ prārthayāmyaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

31\. O Lord of Devas, if you are pleased, if a boon has to be granted to me, then a pair of pills should be given. It is for this that I request.

## \|\| 1.157.32 \|\|

*vaidiśe nagare cāsti maṇibhadro mahādhanī \|*  
*kubjāṃgaḥ kṣatriyo deva jarāvalisamanvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Lord, in the city of Vaidiśā there is a great rich Kṣatriya named Maṇibhadra. He is short in his limbs, overcome by old age and wrinkles.

## \|\| 1.157.33-35 \|\|

*abrahmaṇyo mahānīcaḥ kīnāśo janadūṣitaḥ \|*  
*dvayorekāṃ yadā vaktre sadā caiva karomyaham \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tadā me tādṛśaṃ rūpamavikalpaṃ bhavatviti \|*  
*yadā punargṛhītvā tāṃ dvitīyāṃ prakṣipāmyaham \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tataśca sahajaṃ rūpaṃ mama bhūyātsureśvara \|*  
*vaidiśe nagare cāsti maṇibhadraḥ sureśvara \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. He is very mean and miserly. He is against Brāhmaṇas

and is always rebuked by the people. Of the two pills let one be of this nature. Whenever I put it in my mouth let my form be exactly like his. When I take the other one and put it in my mouth, O Lord of Suras, let me have the natural form. This Maṇibhadra is in the city of Vaidiśā.

## \|\| 1.157.36 \|\|

*aparaṃ tasya yatkiṃciddhanadhānyādikaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ viditaṃ me syāttathā deva prajāyatām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Another thing, whatever he possesses in his house, cash, grain etc., should be known to me.

## \|\| 1.157.37 \|\|

*kiṃ vānena bahūktena tasya mitrāṇi bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*vyavahārāstathā sarve prakaṭāḥ syuḥ sadaiva hi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Why should I say much? Let his friends, kinsmen and all business deals be clearly manifest unto me.

## \|\| 1.157.38 \|\|

*na kaścijjāyate tatra vikalpaḥ kasyacitkvacit \|*  
*mama tasyādhama syāpi sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In all my activities at all times, no one should find out any difference between me and that base fellow.

## \|\| 1.157.39 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mahābhāga guṭikādvitayaṃ śubham \|*  
*śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca vaktrasthaṃ vibheda jananaṃ mahat \|\| 39 \|\|*

Bhāskara said:

39\. O highly esteemed one, take these two excellent pills. They are black and white in colour. When kept in the mouth they cause a great deal of difference.

## \|\| 1.157.40 \|\|

*śuklayā tasya rūpaṃ ca tava nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*kṛṣṇayāpi punaḥ svaṃ ca saṃprāpsyasi mahādvija \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O great Brāhmaṇa, through the white pill your form will be certainly turned into his. Through the black one you will get back your own form.

## \|\| 1.157.41 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*aparaṃ vada me deva saṃdehaṃ hṛdaye sthitam \|*  
*yattvāṃ pṛcchāmi deveśa tava kīrtivivardhanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

41\. There is another query, O Lord. Clear the doubt in my mind. O Lord of Devas, I shall ask you. I shall be conducive to increase in your reputation.

## \|\| 1.157.42 \|\|

*mayā śrutaṃ suraśreṣṭha saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare \|*  
*yaste pradakṣiṇānāṃ ca kuryādaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva phalahastasya siddhidaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O most excellent one of Suras, I have heard this. If any one takes one hundred eight circumambulations around you with a fruit in his hand you bestow Siddhi on him instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.157.43-44 \|\|

*mūrkhasyāpi ca pāpasya sarvadoṣānvitasya ca \|*  
*caturvedasya me kasmāttīrthayātrāparasya ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*saptarātre gate tuṣṭo homa evaṃvidhe kṛte \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. This you are ready to grant even to a fool and a sinner and one with all defects. On the other hand, I have mastered all the four Vedas and am regularly engaged in pilgrimage. Still you became pleased only after seven days and after such a Homa was performed.

## \|\| 1.157.45 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*tāmasena tu bhāvena tvavā sarvamidaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tena sarvaṃ vṛthā jātaṃ tvayā sarvaṃ ca yatkṛtam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Śrī Sūrya said:

45\. You have performed all these with a Tāmasa (violent) feeling. So whatever has been performed by you has become useless.

## \|\| 1.157.46 \|\|

*yatkiṃcitkriyate vipra tāmasaṃ bhāvamāśritaiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ jāyate vyarthaṃ kiṃ na vetti bhavā nidam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Don’t you know this, O Brāhmaṇa, that whatever is done by people of Tāmasa feeling becomes futile?

## \|\| 1.157.47 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sūryastasya gātrāṇyupāspṛśat \|*  
*khaṃḍitāni svahastena nirvraṇāni kṛtāni ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After saying thus, Sūrya touched him with his own hand. All the wounds became healed.

## \|\| 1.157.48-50 \|\|

*abravīcca punaḥ puṣpaṃ prasanna vadanaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva vidhānena yaḥ karoti kuśaṃḍikām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*somyabhāvaṃ samāśritya samidbhiścārkasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*tilākṣatairviśeṣeṇa homaṃ yastu samācaret \|\| 49 \|\|*

*chandaṛṣisamopetamekaṃ yāvatsahasrakam \|*  
*tasya dāsyāmyahaṃ hṛtsthamadhikebhyo'dhikaṃ phalam \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. He said to Puṣpa once again with a pleased face: “If a person adopts gentleness and performs this Kuśaṇḍikā Homa in accordance with this same procedure, I will grant him much benefit. He shall use the sacrificial twigs made of Arka, tree or with gingelly seeds and raw rice grain. The Chanda and the sage invoked shall be the same. He shall offer a thousand Homas. I shall grant him more than what he wishes in his heart.”

## \|\| 1.157.51 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustatraivāṃ taradhīyata \|*  
*dīpavallakṣito naiva kena mārgeṇa nirgataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After saying thus the Thousand-rayed One vanished there itself like a lamp. It could not be seen which way he went away.

## Chapter 158 - Maṇibhadra’s Death

## \|\| 1.158.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*puṣpo'pi guṭike labdhvā bhāskarādvāritaskarāt \|*  
*cirādbhojanamāsādya prasthito vaidiśaṃ prati \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato vaidiśamāsādya sa puṣpo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*śuklā tāṃ guṭikāṃ vaktre cakāradvijasattamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*maṇibhadrasamo jātastatkṣaṇādeva sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*haṭṭamārgaṃ gate so'tha tasmingatvā'tha maṃdire \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ sahasā madhye prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Having received the two pills from the Sun, the stealer (evaporator) of waters, he took food after a long delay. Puṣpa then proceeded towards Vaidiśā.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Puṣpa was highly pleased in his mind when he reached Vaidiśā. He put the white pill in this mouth. Immediately, the Brāhmaṇa was transformed into one identical with Maṇibhadra.

With a highly delighted mind he entered his house which was on the main road leading to the market.

## \|\| 1.158.4 \|\|

*tataścākārayāmāsa taṃ ṣaṃḍhaṃ dvāramāśritam \|*  
*tasya dattvātha vastrāṇi paścātṣaṃḍhamuvāca saḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then he called the eunuch stationed at the threshold. After presenting him with garments, he spoke to the eunuch:

## \|\| 1.158.5-8 \|\|

*ṣaṃḍhakaścitpumānatra samyagveṣakaro hi saḥ \|*  
*mama veṣaṃ samādhāya bhramate sakale pure \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sāṃprataṃ madgṛhe so'tha lobhanāyāgamiṣyati \|*  
*sa ca kṛtrima veṣeṇa niṣeddhavyastvayā hi saḥ \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya dvāradeśaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*puṣpo'pi cābravīdbhāryāṃ māhikākhyāṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*māhikedya mayā dṛṣṭaḥ svatātaḥ svapuraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vīrabhadraḥ suduḥkhārto malināṃbarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*abravīcca tataḥ kopānmāmevaṃ paruṣākṣaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-6ab. “O Ṣaṇḍha (eunuch), an impostor, very clever in disguising himself, is moving about in the entire city in my guise. Now in his artificial guise, he is sure to come to our house to tempt the inmates. He should be refused entry.” He (Ṣaṇḍha) nodded assent saying, “It shall be so” and stood (alert) at the entrance.

7-8. Thereafter, Puṣpa spoke to his (Maṇibhadra’s) wife named Māhikā: “O Māhikā, today I saw my father Vīrabhadra standing before me clad in dirty rags and feeling highly distressed. He spoke in harsh words thus to me:

## \|\| 1.158.9-18 \|\|

*dhigdhikpāpa tvayā kanyātīva rūpavatī sadā \|*  
*vaṃcayitvā janetāramudūḍhā sā sumadhyamā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na dattaṃ tatpituḥ kiṃcinna tasyā atha putraka \|*  
*vidhavāṃ yādṛśīṃ tāṃ ca śvetāṃbaradharāṃ sadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*saṃdhārayasi pāpātmanneṣṭaṃ bhojyaṃ prayacchasi \|*  
*tasmāttasyāḥ piturdehi tvaṃ suvarṇāyutaṃ dhruvam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhūṣaṇaṃ vāṃchitaṃ tasyā yattadvai rucipūrvakam \|*  
*yena saṃdhārayedbhāryā sā'naṃdaṃ paramaṃ gatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nirānaṃdā yato nārī na garbhaṃ dhārayetsphuṭam \|*  
*niḥsaṃtāno yato vaṃśaḥ svargādapi kṣitiṃ vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sa patiṣyatyasaṃdigdhaṃ kulāṃgāreṇa ca tvayā \|*  
*sā tvamānaya vastrāṇi gṛhamadhyācchubhāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yāni dattāni bhūpena vyavahāraistadā mama \|*  
*pañcāṃgaśca prasādo yo mayā prāptaśca taiḥ saha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tvaṃ saṃdhāraya gātraiḥ svaiḥ śīghraṃ rasavatīṃ kuru \|*  
*bhojanāyaiva śīghraṃ tu tvayā sārdhaṃ karomyaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ekasminnapi pātre ca tadādeśādasaṃśayam \|*  
*sāpi sarvaṃ tathā cakre yaduktaṃ tena harṣitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhojanācchādanaṃ caiva nirvikalpena cetasā \|*  
*tataḥ kāmāturaḥ puṣpo maithunāyopacakrame \|\| 18 \|\|*

9-17a. ‘Fie upon you! Fie upon you! O sinful one, a very beautiful girl of excellent middle has been married by you after deceiving her father.

O my son, nothing has been given to her or to her father by you. You are keeping her like a widow always clad in white garments.

With sin lurking within you hold her back; you do not give her food to eat. So, give by all means ten thousand pieces of gold to her father.

Whatever ornament she likes, let your wife wear it and become highly delighted.

A woman without inner happiness, it is quite obvious, will not conceive. Since the line of family that is not perpetuated by a child will fall on the earth from heaven, our family will undoubtedly fall due to you, the cause of the ruin of the family.’ So he said.

Now bring those excellent clothes from within the house, given by the king and the five articles of present gained by my business deals and wear these yourself And cook our tasty dish quickly. I shall take food with you. We shall take food from the same pot. It is undoubtedly his command.”

17b-18. The girl was delighted by what he said. She also did everything accordingly. She prepared the food unhesitatingly and wore the excellent garments. Then the impatiently lustful Puṣpa began the preparation for sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 1.158.19-20 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto maṇibhadraḥ samutsukaḥ \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmaḥ sa pipāsārto vyavahārotthalipsayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*praveśaṃ kurute yāvadgṛhamadhye samutsukaḥ \|*  
*niṣiddhastena ṣaṇḍhena bhartsayitvā muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. In the meantime, Maṇibhadra came there with great earnestness. Due to his greediness and the consequent business engagement, he had become very hungry and thirsty. When he entered the house in all eagerness, he was stopped by the eunuch who repeatedly rebuked him.

## \|\| 1.158.21 \|\|

*haṭhādyāvatpraveśaṃ sa cakāra nijamaṃdire \|*  
*tāvacca daṇḍakāṣṭhena mastake tena tāḍitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When he forced his entry into his own house, he was hit on his head with a heavy srick.

## \|\| 1.158.22 \|\|

*atha saṃpatito bhūmau mūrchayā saṃpariplutaḥ \|*  
*kartavyaṃ naiva jānāti tatprahāraprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereupon, he fell on the ground and was overcome with unconsciousness. Afflicted by the hitting (blow) he did not know what to do.

## \|\| 1.158.23 \|\|

*tataḥ kolāhalo jātastasya dvāre gṛhasya ca \|*  
*janasya saṃprayātasya hāhākāraparasya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A great tumult arose at the gate of that house when people who flocked there also raised a hue and cry.

## \|\| 1.158.24-25 \|\|

*papracchustaṃ janāḥ keci ddhikpāpa kimidaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*vṛttibhaṃgaḥ kṛto'nena atha tvaṃ vyaṃtarārditaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*imāmavasthāṃ yannītaḥ saṃprāpto'si nṛpādvadham \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Some people asked him: “Fie upon you! O sinner, what have you done? By this action you have deprived yourself of the means of sustenance. Or have you been possessed by the devil? This fellow has been brought to this plight. Surely the king will hang you.

## \|\| 1.158.26 \|\|

*ṣaṃḍha uvāca \|*  
*na vṛttirgarhitā tena nāhaṃ vyaṃtarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*maṇibhadro na caiṣa syādeṣa veṣakaraḥ pumān \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Ṣaṇḍha said:

26\. I have not abused my means of sustenance by this action. Nor have I been possessed by the devil. This is not Maṇibhadra. He is an imposter, other man in his guise.

## \|\| 1.158.27 \|\|

*māṇibhadraṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā saṃprāpto yācituṃ dhanam \|*  
*haṭhātpraviśyamānastu sa mayā mūrdhni tāḍitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He poses himself as Maṇibhadra. He has come here to request for money. When he forced his entry he was struck on his head by me.

## \|\| 1.158.28 \|\|

*maṇibhadro gṛhasyāṃtarbhuktvā śayanamāśritaḥ \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhate na jānāti vṛttāṃtamidamā sthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Maṇibhadra is in fact within the house. He has taken food and is resting on his bed. He is not aware of this incident that has occurred.

## \|\| 1.158.29 \|\|

*tataḥ puṣpo'pi tacchrutvā taṃ ca kolāhalaṃ bahiḥ \|*  
*maṇibhadrasya rūpeṇa dvāradeśaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then Puṣpa also heard the tumultuons noise outside. He came to the door in the form of Maṇibhadra.

## \|\| 1.158.30-31 \|\|

*abravīnnityamabhyeti mama rūpeṇa cādhamaḥ \|*  
*eṣa veṣadharaḥ kaścidyācituṃ dhanameva hi \|\| 30 \|\|*

*etenāpi ca ṣaṃḍhena na ca bhadramanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*yatkubjo'yaṃ hato mūrdhni yācituṃ samu pasthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. “Some base fellow poses like myself and comes here everyday begging for money.

Of course, this Ṣaṇḍha has not done the right thing by having struck this crooked fellow on his head for having come here to beg for money.”

## \|\| 1.158.32-33 \|\|

*etasminnantare so'pi cetanāṃ prāpya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*vīkṣate purato yāvattāvadātmasamaḥ pumān \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sarvataḥ sa tamālokya tato vacanamabravīt \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In the meantime, the other fellow (real Maṇibhadra) regained complete consciousness. When he looked ahead he saw a man exactly like himself. After fully surveying him he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.158.34-35 \|\|

*kva coraḥ saṃpraviṣṭo me mama rūpeṇa maṃdire \|*  
*bhedayitvā tu ṣaṇḍākhyamevaṃ dattvā ca vāsasī \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yāvadbhūpagṛhaṃ gatvā tvāṃ ṣaṃḍhena samanvitam \|*  
*vadhāya yojayāmyeva tāvaddrutataraṃ vraja \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. “A thief has entered my house in my own form. He has bribed the eunuch with clothes to betray me. It is better you run away before I go to the king’s place and get you along with this eunuch executed.”

## \|\| 1.158.36 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*mama rūpaṃ samādhāya tvamāyāto gṛhe mama \|*  
*śūnyaṃ matvā tato jñātastvayā'haṃ gṛhasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

36\. You have come to my house in my guise thinking that the house is unoccupied. Then you come to know that I am in the house.

## \|\| 1.158.37 \|\|

*tato nṛpāya dāsyāmi vadhārthaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*no cedgaccha drutaṃ pāpa yadi jīvitumicchasi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, I shall take you to the king for getting you done to death without any doubt. Or, if you wish to live, O sinful man, run away.

## \|\| 1.158.38 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamukttvā tatastau ca bāhuyuddhena vai mithaḥ \|*  
*yudhyamānau narairanyaiḥ kṛcchreṇa tu nivāritau \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sūta said:

38\. After saying this to each other they began to fight dual. With great difficulty they were restrained by other people.

## \|\| 1.158.39 \|\|

*tataste svajanā ye tu maṇibha drasya cāgatāḥ \|*  
*parijānaṃti no dvābhyāṃ viśeṣaṃ māṇibhadrakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The kinsmen of Maṇibhadra who came there could not differentiate between the two and establish the identity of real Maṇibhadra.

## \|\| 1.158.40 \|\|

*vālisugrīvayoryuddhaṃ tārārthe yudhyamānayoḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vivadamānau tu krodhatāmrā yatekṣaṇau \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. With their large eyes blazing like heated copper due to anger, they argued and quarrelled like Bāli and Sugrīva who fought with each other over Tārā.

## \|\| 1.158.41 \|\|

*rājadvāraṃ samāsādya sthitau svajanasaṃvṛtau \|*  
*dvāḥsthena sūcitau rājñe sabhātalamupasthitau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. They went to the palace entrance and stood there in the midst of their own kinsmen. The king was informed by the doorman and they came to the Assembly Hall.

## \|\| 1.158.42 \|\|

*cauracaureti jalpantau para sparavadhaiṣiṇau \|*  
*bhūbhujā vīkṣitau tau ca dvijau tu dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they appeared to be eager to slay each other and they shouted, “Oh you thief! Oh you thief!" The king glanced at both the twice-borns.

## \|\| 1.158.43-44 \|\|

*na viśeṣo'sti viśleṣastayorekopikāyataḥ \|*  
*tataśca vyavahāreṣu samatī teṣu vai tadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭau guhyeṣu sarveṣu pratyakṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vadatastau yathāvṛttaṃ pṛthakpṛthagvyavasthitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. There was no bodily difference distinguishing between them. After the royal affairs at the court were over, they were asked in regard to all well-known and secret matters. They readily answered everything duly.

## \|\| 1.158.45 \|\|

*tatastu svajanaiḥ sarvaireko nītva tha cānyataḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭo gotrānvayaṃ sarvaṃ dvitīyastu tataḥ param \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then the kinsmen asked each of them away from the presence of the other, the details of the family and the lineage.

## \|\| 1.158.46 \|\|

*teṣāmapi tathā sarvaṃ yathāsamyaṅniveditam \|*  
*atha rājā bṛhatsenaḥ sarvāṃstāni damabravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. To these questions too, they gave the correct replies. Then king Bṛhatsena spoke to them all:

## \|\| 1.158.47 \|\|

*patnī cānīyatāṃ tasya maṇibhadrasya vai gṛhāt \|*  
*nijakāntasya vijñāne sā pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “Let the wife of Maṇibhadra be brought from his house. She shall be the real authority in identification of her husband.”

## \|\| 1.158.48 \|\|

*tato gatvā ca sā proktā puruṣairnṛpasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*āgaccha kāṃtaṃ jānīhi tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The officers of the king went and told her, “Come on please. Find out your husband. You alone shall be the deciding authority.”

## \|\| 1.158.49-50 \|\|

*tataḥ sā vrīḍayā yuktā pracchāditaśirāstataḥ \|*  
*nṛpāgre saṃsthitā proce viddhisamyaṅnijaṃ priyam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*na vayaṃ niścayaṃ vidmo na caite svajanāstava \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Bashfully she stood before the king with the head covered and was asked: “Identify your dear husband. We do not know decisively. Nor these kinsmen of yours”

## \|\| 1.158.51-54 \|\|

*tataḥ sā cintayāmāsa nijacitte varāṃganā \|*  
*maṇibhadreṇa dagdhāhamīrṣyāvahnigatā'niśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vaṃcayitvā tu pitaraṃ gṛhītāsmi tataḥ param \|*  
*na kiṃcitpāpmanā dattaṃ jalpayitvā dhanaṃ bahu \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dvitīyena tu me puṃsā martyaloke sukhaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*dattvā vastrāṇi citrāṇi tathaivābharaṇāni ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pradāsyati ca tātasya suvarṇaṃ kathitaṃ ca yat \|*  
*yadgṛhṇāmi svahastena maṇibhadraṃ dvitīyakam \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. Then the excellent lady thought in her mind: ‘I have been scorched continuously by this Maṇibhadra in the fire of his jealousy. He orally offered plenty of cash and deceived my father. Thus he took me away but nothing was given by the sinful fellow. But this second man presented me with diverse kinds of garments and ornaments. He gave me the worldly pleasure too. He will also give my father the gold promised. So I shall grasp the second Maṇibhadra with my hand.’

## \|\| 1.158.55 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya manasā dṛṣṭvā raktapariplutam \|*  
*prathamaṃ maṇibhadraṃ sā jagṛhe'tha dvitīyakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After deciding thus mentally, she saw that the first Maṇibhadra was fully smeared with blood. So she grasped the second one.

## \|\| 1.158.56-57 \|\|

*abravīcca tato vākyaṃ sarvalokasya śṛṇvataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tātena dattāsya vivāhe agnisaṃnidhau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dvitīyo'yaṃ durācāro veṣakartā samā gataḥ \|*  
*māṃ ca prārthayate guptāṃ nānācāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. She spoke these words when all the people listened to them: “In the presence of the sacred fire I was given in marriage to this man. This other one is an impostor of evil conduct. He has come here seeking me well-guarded by different kinds of conventions.”

## \|\| 1.158.58 \|\|

*tatastu pārthivaḥ kruddhastasya śākhāvalaṃbanam \|*  
*ādideśa dvijaśreṣṭhā maṇibhadrasya durmateḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the king became furious and commanded the hanging, from the branch of a tree, of the evil-minded Maṇibhadra.

## \|\| 1.158.59 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare so'tha vadhakānāṃ samarpitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ vṛkṣaṃ nīyamānastu ślokānetāṃstadāpaṭhat \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the meantime, he was handed over to the hangman. As he was being led to the tree he recited these verses:

## \|\| 1.158.60 \|\|

*nirdayatvaṃ tathā drohaṃ kuṭilatvaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*aśaucaṃ nirghṛṇatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ doṣāḥ svabhāvajāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. “These are the innate faults and defects of women: Want of mercy, hatred, crippledness, want of cleanliness and ruthlessness.

## \|\| 1.158.61 \|\|

*antarviṣamayā hyetā bahirbhāge manoramāḥ \|*  
*guñjāphalasamākārā yoṣitaḥ sarva daivahi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Women always resemble a Guñjāphala (red-black berry) poisonous within but having charming external features only.

## \|\| 1.158.62 \|\|

*uśanā veda yacchāstraṃ yacca veda bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*manvādayastathānye'pi strībuddhestatra kiṃca na \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The scriptural knowledge of Uśanas, the Vedic scholarship of Bṛhaspati and the wisdom of Manu and others are nothing in comparison to the wisdom of women.

## \|\| 1.158.63 \|\|

*pīyūṣamadhare vāsaṃ hṛdi hālāhalaṃ viṣam \|*  
*āsvādyate'dharastena hṛdayaṃ ca prapīḍyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Nectar resides in the lips of a woman and Halāhala poison in the heart. Hence the lips are kissed and tasted while the heart (chest) is pressed hard.

## \|\| 1.158.64 \|\|

*alaktako yathā rakto naraḥ kāmī tathaiva ca \|*  
*hṛtasārastathā so'pi pādamūle nipā tyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Lac juice is Rakta (red); so also a lustful man is Rakta (attached, loving). After the essence has been taken, he too is kept beneath the soles of the feet.

## \|\| 1.158.65 \|\|

*saṃsāraviṣavṛkṣasya kukarmakusumasya ca \|*  
*narakārtiphalasyoktā mūlameṣā nitaṃbinī \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The poisonous tree of worldly existence has evil actions as the blossom and distress in hell as the fruit. Its root however is a woman of ample buttocks.

## \|\| 1.158.66 \|\|

*kasya no jāyate trāso dṛṣṭvā dūrā dapi striyam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Who is not terribly frightened by seeing a woman from a distance?

## \|\| 1.158.67 \|\|

*saṃsārabhramaṇaṃ nārī prathame'pi samāgame \|*  
*vahnipradakṣiṇanyāyavyājenaiva pradarśayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Even at the first formal union, a woman makes the whirl of the mundane existence manifest under the pretext of the customary circumambulation of the sacred fire.

## \|\| 1.158.68 \|\|

*etāstu nirghṛṇatvena nirdaya tvena nityaśaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣājjāḍyakṛtyena dūṣayaṃti kulatrayam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. These women defile three generations of the family (or three families) through ruthlessness, want of mercy and a perpetual sluggishness in particular.

## \|\| 1.158.69 \|\|

*kulatrayagṛhaṃ kīrtyā nijayā dhavalīkṛtam \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ karotyakṛ tyena nārī dīpaśikheva tu \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The abode of the three families spotlessly clean due to its reputation, is blackened by a woman with her misdeeds, like the flame of a lamp.

## \|\| 1.158.70 \|\|

*dharmavṛkṣasya vātālī cittapadmaśaśiprabhā \|*  
*sṛṣṭā kāmārṇavagrāhī kena mokṣadṛḍhārgalā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. God Brahmā has created woman who upsets virtue and piety like a violent gust of wind uprooting a tree; who bedevils the minds like moonlight that destroys lotuses; who is like an alligator in the ocean of love and who is a bolt that closes the door to salvation.

## \|\| 1.158.71 \|\|

*kārā saṃtānakūṭasya saṃsāravanavāgurā \|*  
*svargamārgamahāgartā puṃsāṃ strī vedhasā kṛtā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Woman has been created by Brahmā in regard to men like a prison-house for a group of children, a net in the forest of worldly existence and an abysmal depth in the pathway to heaven.

## \|\| 1.158.72 \|\|

*vedhasā baṃdhanaṃ kiṃcinnṛṇāmanyadapaśyatā \|*  
*strīrūpeṇa tataḥ ko'pi pāśo'yaṃ sudṛḍhaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Vedhas (Brahmā) could not find any other means of binding men. Hence, he made the firm noose in the form of woman.”

## \|\| 1.158.73 \|\|

*ityevaṃ bahudhā so'pi vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*strīcintāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā ātmānaṃ cāpyagarhayat \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thus in the height of his sorrow he lamented much. Worried over his wife in various ways, he censured himself:

## \|\| 1.158.74 \|\|

*aho kubuddhinā naiva labdhaṃ saṃsārajaṃ phalam \|*  
*na kadācinmayā dattaṃ tṛṣṇāvyākulacetasā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “I have been evil-minded and unwise. No benefit has been obtained by me from the worldy life. Nothing was given as gift by me at any time, because my mind was agitated by Tṛṣṇā (greed, thirst).

## \|\| 1.158.75 \|\|

*aiśvarye'pi sthite bhūri na mayā sukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*kadācinnaiva japtaṃ ca na hutaṃ ca hutāśane \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Although I had adequte wealth and prosperity no meritorious action has been done by me. I never performed a Japa or a Homa in the sacred fire.

## \|\| 1.158.76 \|\|

*athavā satyamevoktaṃ kenāpi ca mahātmanā \|*  
*kṛpaṇena samo dātā na bhūto na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*aspṛṣṭvāpi ca vittaṃ svaṃ yaḥ parebhyaḥ prayacchati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. As it has been truly expressed by a certain noble-souled man, ‘Like a miser there never was a great donor nor will there ever be, because without even touching his own wealth himself, he gives it to others.’

## \|\| 1.158.77 \|\|

*śaraṇaṃ kiṃ prapannānāṃ viṣavanmārayaṃti kim \|*  
*na dīyate na bhujyaṃte kṛpaṇena dhanāni ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Riches do kill like a poison those who seek refuge therein. They are neither given away nor enjoyed by the miser.

## \|\| 1.158.78 \|\|

*dānaṃ bhogo nāśastisro gatayo bhavaṃti vittasya \|*  
*yo na dadāti na bhuṃkte tasya tṛtīyā gatirbhavati \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. There are three states (ways of being spent) to which wealth is destined: gift, enjoyment and ruin. That which is neither given nor enjoyed meets with the third (i.e.ruin).

## \|\| 1.158.79 \|\|

*dhaninopyadānavibhavā gaṇyaṃte dhuri daridrāṇām \|*  
*nahi haṃti yatpipāsāmataḥ samudro'pi marureva \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Even wealthy men also who do not give are considered as extreme type of the poor. Since the ocean does not quench the thirst, it is no better than a desert.

## \|\| 1.158.80 \|\|

*atyupayuktāḥ sadbhirgatāgatairaharahaḥ sunirviṇṇāḥ \|*  
*kṛpaṇajanasaṃnikāśaṃ saṃprāpyārthāḥ svapaṃtīha \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Riches are fully utilized by good people where they are at ease with to and fro movements. By coming near miserly persons, they go to sleep forever.

## \|\| 1.158.81 \|\|

*prāptānna labhaṃte te bhogānbhoktuṃ svakarmaṇā kṛpaṇāḥ \|*  
*mukhapākaḥ kila bhavati drākṣāpāke balibhujānām \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Miserly persons do not get the opportunity of enjoying pleasures because of their own Karinas. When it comes to the enjoyment of grapes, crows eating oblations suffer from inflammation of the mouth.

## \|\| 1.158.82 \|\|

*dātavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ sati vibhave saṃcayo na kartavyaḥ \|*  
*paśyeha madhukarīṇāṃ saṃcitamarthaṃ haraṃtyanye \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. When one has adequate wealth, one should make a gift of it or enjoy it fully. One shall not hoard it. Look here: Others take away what is stored by honey-bees.

## \|\| 1.158.83 \|\|

*yācitaṃ dvijavare na dīyate saṃcitaṃ kratuvare na yojyate \|*  
*tatkadaryaparirakṣitaṃ dhanaṃ caurapārthivagṛheṣu bhujyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The well-guarded wealth of the miser that has been begged for but not distributed to excellent Brāhmaṇas, that has been hoarded but not employed in an excellent Yajña, is (finally) used up in the abodes of thieves and kings.

## \|\| 1.158.84 \|\|

*tyāgo guṇo vittavatāṃ vittaṃ tyāgavatāṃ guṇaḥ \|*  
*parasparaviyuktau tu vitta tyāgau viḍambanam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Munificence is a virtue of the wealthy; wealthiness is a virtue of the munificent; separation of wealth and munificence is a mockery.

## \|\| 1.158.85 \|\|

*kiṃ tayā kriyate lakṣmyā yā vadhūriva kevalā \|*  
*yā na veśyeva sāmānyā pathikairapi bhujyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. What can be done with that wealth which is no exclusive possession like a bride nor a common property enjoyed even by travellers like a harlot?

## \|\| 1.158.86 \|\|

*arthoṣmaṇā bhavetprāṇo bhavedbhakṣyairvinā nṛṇām \|*  
*yataḥ saṃdhāryate bhūmiḥ kṛpaṇasyoṣmaṇā hi sā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Life is sustained by the warmth of wealth. Even without foodstuff man can have it. That by which the earth is sustained is the warmth from the miser.

## \|\| 1.158.87 \|\|

*kṛpaṇānāṃ prasādena śeṣo dhārayate mahīm \|*  
*yataste bhūgataṃ vittaṃ kurvate tasya coṣmaṇā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Śeṣa (the serpent) supports the earth, thanks to the favour of the misers, because they keep their wealth under the ground and the warmth therefrom (gives comfort to Śeṣa)”

## \|\| 1.158.88 \|\|

*evaṃ bahuvidhā vācaḥ pralapanmaṇibhadrakaḥ \|*  
*nītvā taiḥ pārthivoddiṣṭaiḥ puruṣaiḥ paruṣākṣaram \|*  
*bahudhā pralapaṃ ścaiva kṛtaḥ śākhāvalaṃbanaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Thus Maṇibhadra went on prattling much. Even as he continued the prattle thus he was scolded by the men of the king with harsh words and they hanged him.

## Chapter 159 - Puṣpa Acquires Prosperity

## \|\| 1.159.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*puṣpo'pi tāṃ samādāya māhikākhyāṃ varāṃganām \|*  
*sa tadā prayayau hṛṣṭo maṇibhadrasya maṃdiram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śaṃkhatūryaninādena sarvaistaiḥ svajanairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*na kasya tatra saṃbhūto vikalpastatsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhāskarasya prasādena tathaivānyasya karhicit \|*  
*so'pi maṃdiramāsādya yathātmapitṛsaṃbhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. Taking the excellent lady named Māhikā Puṣpa joyously went to the abode of Maṇibhadra together with all the kinsmen to the accompaniment of conches and other musical instruments.

None of them there had any doubt about him. Thanks to the favour of Bhāskara or others, he reached that abode as though it were his ancestral home.

## \|\| 1.159.4-6 \|\|

*upaviśya tato madhye bandhūnsarvānsamāhvayat \|*  
*adya tāvaddine mahyaṃ tulāgraṃ kamalā śritā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*calitāpi punaścāsyāḥ supatnyā vākyataḥ sthitā \|*  
*kiyaṃtaṃ caiva kālaṃ me kārpaṇyaṃ mahadāsthitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jñātamadya calā lakṣmīstena tyaktaṃ sudūrataḥ \|*  
*tasmādbaṃdhujanaiḥ sārdhaṃ devairvipraiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*saṃvibhaktāṃ kariṣyāmi satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. He sat in the centre and summoned all the kinsmen. He said: “Today my fortune has hung in the balance. Though it oscillated it stood steady by the words of this excellent wife. So long extreme miserliness had overpowered me.

Today I have become aware that fortune is unsteady. In fact I have abandoned it. Hence I shall share it entirely with kinsmen, Brāhmanas and deities. I take a solemn oath myself.”

## \|\| 1.159.7 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sarvānsamāhūya pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*sa nāmabhirdadau vastraṃ bhūṣaṇāni yathārhataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After saying thus he called them severally uttering their names and gave them clothes and ornaments befittingly.

## \|\| 1.159.8 \|\|

*tato vedavido viprānsamāhūya sa nāmabhiḥ \|*  
*ekaikasya dadau vittaṃ savastraṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then he invited Brāhmaṇas conversant with the Vedas individually by their names. With faith he gave each of them cash and clothes.

## \|\| 1.159.9 \|\|

*tatastu nartakebhyaśca dīnāṃdhebhyo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dadau bhojyaṃ sami ṣṭānnaṃ savastraṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, O excellent Brāhmanas, he gave good food with delicacies and clothes to dancers, blind beggars and wretched people.

## \|\| 1.159.10 \|\|

*tatastu svayamevānnaṃ bubhuje bhāryayā saha \|*  
*visṛjya tānsamāyātānsvajanānbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After dismissing the kinsmen along with the Brāhmaṇas, he himself took food in the company of his wife.

## \|\| 1.159.11 \|\|

*evaṃ tena tadā prāptaṃ vittaṃ ca parasaṃbhavam \|*  
*bubhuje svecchayā nityaṃ tadā bhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus another man’s wealth was acquired by him which he enjoyed for long as he pleased along with his wife.

## Chapter 160 - Brāhmaṇas Invited for Puraścaraṇa

## \|\| 1.160.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*anyasminnahani prāpte rahasyuktaḥ sa bhāryayā \|*  
*rātrau prasuptaḥ pārśve ca pādau saṃspṛśya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tvaṃ tāvanmama bharttāsi yāvajjīvamasaṃśayam \|*  
*tadvadasva vibho'smākaṃ tvadarthaṃ sa mayojjhitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*indrajālamidaṃ kiṃ te kiṃ vā maṃtraprasādhanam \|*  
*devānāṃ vā prasādo'yaṃ yattvaṃ caitādṛśaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mayā tvaṃ hi tadā jñātaḥ prathame'pi dine sthite \|*  
*yadā saṃbhūṣitā vastraistathā vastuvibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yadyahaṃ tava vārtāṃ ca sarvāṃ kapaṭasaṃbhavām \|*  
*kathayāmi dvitīyasya tatte pādau spṛśāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-5. On another day at night when he lay by her side, the wife massaged his feet and said to him in full confidence: “Undoubtedly you are my husband as long as I live. So, my Lord, do tell me. The other one has been forsaken by me for your sake. Is there any jugglery on your part? Or have you practised any sacred Mantra? Or is this the favour of the deities? How is it that you have come to be like this? Even on the very first day I had become aware of you when I was adorned and presented with clothes and ornaments. Oh! Were I to disclose your fraud entirely to the other one? No, no it shall not be. I touch your feet.”

## \|\| 1.160.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamukto vihasyoccaiḥ sa tadā brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*tāmāliṃgya tataḥ prāha vacanaṃ madhurākṣaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

6\. On being told thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he (Puṣpa) embraced her and spoke to her in sweet words:

## \|\| 1.160.7-8 \|\|

*sādhu priye tvayā jñātaṃ sarvaṃ mama viceṣṭitam \|*  
*ahaṃ sa vipraḥ subhage maṇibhadreṇa yaḥ purā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*viḍaṃbito mukhaṃ paśyaṃstvadīyaṃ caṃdrasannibham \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ gatvā mayā cārādhito raviḥ \|*  
*tena tuṣṭena me dattaṃ tadrūpaṃ jñānameva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. “Oh my beloved! You have correctly understood all my activities. Oh fair lady! I am that Brāhmaṇa who was made to suffer by Maṇibhadra for looking at your moon-like face. I went to Camatkārapura and propitiated Ravi (Sun-god). This form and knowledge (of the details of Maṇibhadra) was granted to me by the delighted Sun-god.”

## \|\| 1.160.9-11 \|\|

*māhikovāca \|*  
*tvadīyadarśanenāhaṃ kāmadevavaśaṃ gatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmādārādhayiṣyāmi taṃ gatvā dinanāyakam \|*  
*yena te tādṛśaṃ bhūyaḥ pratuṣṭo vidadhāti saḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kiṃ me caitena rūpeṇa tāruṇyenāpi ca prabho \|*  
*yatte tathāvidhaṃ rūpaṃ saṃbhajāmi divāniśam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Māhikā (the wife) said:

9-11. Merely at your sight, I was overwhelmed by Lord Kāma. Hence I shall also go and propitiate the Sun-god so that he will grant you joyously once again that original form of yours. O my Lord, of what use are my beauty and youth! I am worshipping your original form day and night.

## \|\| 1.160.12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā guṭikāṃ puṣpa samādāya mukhāntataḥ \|*  
*dadhāra tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ yādṛgdṛṣṭaṃ purā tayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12\. On hearing it, Puṣpa took out the other pill and placed it within his mouth. He regained that form in which she had seen him earlier.

## \|\| 1.160.13 \|\|

*tataḥ sā harṣitā māhī pulakena samanvitā \|*  
*tamāliṃgyābhajadgāḍhaṃ vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then the delighted Māhī (Māhikā) experienced horripilation. She embraced him closely and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.160.14-16 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ janma yauvanaṃ rūpameva ca \|*  
*yattvaṃ hṛdvāṃchitaḥ kāṃtaḥ pralabdho madanopamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etāvaṃti dinānyeva na mayā kāmajaṃ sukham \|*  
*api svalpataraṃ labdhaṃ kathaṃcidvṛddhasevayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*bhajasva svecchayā vipra dāsī te'haṃ vyavasthitā \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. “Today my birth, youth and beauty have become fruitful since you, fully comparable to Madana and desired heartily, have been obtained by me.

All these days I have been serving you in the form of the old fellow and hence only the least pleasure of love was attained by me. Now enjoy me fully, O Brāhmaṇa, to your heart’s content. I am at your service, your very slave.”

## \|\| 1.160.17 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*praviśāmi kimaṃgeṣu bhavantīṃ kiṃ milāmyaham \|*  
*priye cireṇa labdhāsi na jāne kara vāṇi kim \|\| 17 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

17\. Oh my beloved! I have obtained you after a long time. I do not know what to do. Shall 1 squeeze myself into you? Shall I merge my limbs into yours?

## \|\| 1.160.18 \|\|

*evamuktvā tatastau ca maithunāya kṛtakṣaṇau \|*  
*pravṛttau brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ kāmadevavaśaṃgatau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After this conversation, they indulged in close physical intimacy, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as they got the opportunity and were fully under the control of Lord Kāma.

## \|\| 1.160.19 \|\|

*atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāmudite sūryamaṇḍale \|*  
*vaktre tāṃ guṭikāṃ kṛtvā sa puṣpastādṛśo'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then, as the night came to a close and the Sun’s disc rose up, Puṣpa put the pill into the mouth and assumed the form similar to that of Maṇibhadra.

## \|\| 1.160.20 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya sthitasyātra mahānkālo vyajāyata \|*  
*putrāḥ pautrāstathā jātāḥ kanyakāśca tathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In this way, they spent a long time. Sons, daughters and grandsons were born.

## \|\| 1.160.21-23 \|\|

*sa vṛddhatvaṃ yadā prāpto jarāviplavatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tadā sa cintayāmāsa mayā pāpaṃ mahatkṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*maṇibhadro varāko'sau mithyācāreṇa ghātitaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryā hṛtā caiva prasūtiṃ ca niyojitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tasmādgatvā karomya ham \|*  
*puraścaraṇasaṃjñaṃ ca yena śuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. When he became old and rather feeble due to senility, he thought: ‘A great sin has been committed by me. The poor Maṇibhadra was treacherously made to meet his death. His wife was snatched away by me and forced to bear children. Hence I shall go to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara and perform the expiatory rite of Puraścaraṇa so that I can regain purity.’

## \|\| 1.160.24 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā puṣpaścitte nije tadā \|*  
*asaṃkhyaṃ vittamādāya camatkārapuraṃgataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After coming to this decision in his mind, Puṣpa took plenty of cash with him and went to Camtkārapura.

## \|\| 1.160.25 \|\|

*putrebhyo'pi yathāsaṃkhyaṃ dattvā caiva pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa tasya sūryasya śobhanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He gave to his sons severally the due share of their inheritance. Then he got a splendid palace of the Sun-god built.

## \|\| 1.160.26-27 \|\|

*yasminsiddhiṃ gataḥ so'tra yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhite \|*  
*tato madhyamamāhūya praṇipatyābhivādya ca \|*  
*so'bravīdbrāhmaṇānāṃ me cātuścaraṇamānaya \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yenāhamagrato bhūtvā prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*puraścaraṇasaṃjñaṃ tu prārthayāmi yathāvidhi \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The deity had been installed by Yājñavalkya and there he attained Siddhi.

## Chapter 161 - Greatness of Puṣpāditya

## \|\| 1.161.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha tena dvijāḥ sarve brahmasthāne niveśitāḥ \|*  
*cātuścaraṇasaṃjñāśca tatastasya niveśitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*so'pi keśānparityajya sarvagātrasamudbhavān \|*  
*nijapatnyā samopetaḥ praṇamya ca dvijottamān \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*bhāskarasyāsya vihitaḥ prāsādoyaṃ mayā dvijāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*puṣpāditya iti khyātiṃ prayātu bhuvanatraye \|*  
*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*na vayaṃ yājñavalkyasya kīrtiṃ neṣyāmahe kṣayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ pradāsyāmaścittasya hṛdayaṃgamam \|*  
*anye ca brāhmaṇāḥ procuḥ kecinmadhyasthavṛttayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4a. Then all the Brāhmaṇas were placed by him in the place allotted to Brahmā. Then those designated as Cātuścaraṇas were also placed.

Then Puṣpa shaved off hair all over his body. Accompanied by his wife, he bowed down to the excellent Brāhmaṇas. With palms joined in reverence, he spoke these words: “O Brāhmaṇas, this palace has been got built by me for the Sun-god. Let it be well-known in all the three worlds as Puṣpāditya.

The Brāhmaṇas said:

4b-5. We will not make the reputation of Yājñavalkya decrease and disappear. We shall grant you the expiation to your heart’s content.

## \|\| 1.161.6 \|\|

*vṛttyarthamasya devasya lakṣaṃ home'tra kalpyatām \|*  
*lakṣaṃ tu sarvaviprāṇāṃ prāyaścittaviśuddhaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

Some other Brāhmaṇas in the capacity of middlemen said:

6\. “In connection with the Homa here, let a hundred thousand (coins) be set apart for the maintenance of this deity and another hundred thousand for the Brāhmaṇas so that the expiatory rite can be rendered clean.”

## \|\| 1.161.7 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*tasmātsarve dvijaśreṣṭhā mannāmnā kīrtayaṃtvimam \|*  
*puṣpādityamiti khyātiṃ kīrtayaṃtu tathāniśam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Puṣp said:

7\. Let all the excellent Brāhmaṇas call this deity after my name and glorify this always.

## \|\| 1.161.8 \|\|

*anayā bhāryayā mahyaṃ mānyā yā sthāpitā purā \|*  
*durgā'syāścātra nāmnā vai bhūyātkhyātā'tra satpure \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Earlier, my wife had installed the honoured Durgā. Let it be well-known here in the excellent city after her name.

## \|\| 1.161.9 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*duḥśīlena purā'kāri prāsādo harasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*durvāsaḥsthāpitasyāpi bhavadbhistuṣṭa mānasaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

9\. Formerly, the palace of Hara was erected by Duśśīla. That of the deity installed by Durvāsas has been built by you with joyous minds.

## \|\| 1.161.10 \|\|

*tathāpyasya tu dīnasya prāsādaḥ kriyatāṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Yet, let this palace of this distressed one be erected, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.161.11 \|\|

*nāmamātreṇa devasya duḥśīlena yayā purā \|*  
*anenārādhitaḥ pūrvaṃ svamāṃsaireṣa bhāskaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Formerly Duśśīla propitiated the Lord merely by uttering the names. But by this (Puṣpa) the Sun-god Bhāskara had been propitiated earlier by means of his own flesh.

## \|\| 1.161.12 \|\|

*tasmānna kṣatirasyātha datte nāmni yathā purā \|*  
*nāmnā māhikayā nāma māhītyeva ca sā bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence there is no harm in giving the deity his name. What has been earlier installed by Māhikā shall be Māhī.

## \|\| 1.161.13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*puṣpeṇa dāne datte'tha saṃmatenāgrajanmanām \|*  
*madhyamena kṛtaṃ nāma puṣpāditya iti śrutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sūta said:

13\. When the requisite Dāna was made by Puṣpa with the approval of the Brāhmaṇas, the name well known as Puṣpāditya was given by the middle ones.

## \|\| 1.161.14 \|\|

*tatpatnyā cāpi yā tatra durgā devī dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*nāmnā māhikayā nāma māhītyeva ca sā'bhavat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Goddess Durgā who was formerly installed by his wife named Māhikā, came to be known as Māhī.

## \|\| 1.161.15 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*puṣpā dityo yathā jāto yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sūta said:

15\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything I was asked has been thus told, i.e. how the deity installed by Yājñavalkya became Puṣpāditya.

## \|\| 1.161.16 \|\|

*adyāpi kalikāle sa dṛṣṭo bhaktyā sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*nāśayeddinajaṃ pāpaṃ narāṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even now in Kali age, that Lord of Suras, if visited devoutly, shall destroy the sin of men caused that day. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.161.17 \|\|

*tathā ca saptamīyukte ravervāre dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃyāvatphalahastaḥ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāṃ ca sadbhaktyā sa labhedvāṃchitaṃ phalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Further, if a devotee holds a fruit and circumambulates one hundred eight times on a Sunday coinciding with the seventh lunar day, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he shall obtain the desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.161.18 \|\|

*māhīkāmapi yo durgāṃ nityameva prapaśyati \|*  
*na sa paśyati kaṣṭāni tasminnahani karhicit \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who visits Durgā Māhikā everyday, will never meet with difficulties at all on that day.

## \|\| 1.161.19 \|\|

*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ yastāṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃvatsaraṃyāvannāpatsaṃjāyate kvacit \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If a man worships her on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra, no disaster shall befall him for the whole of that year.

## Chapter 162 - Procedure of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī

## \|\| 1.162.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ nāmni kṛte tasya bhāskarasyāṃśumālinaḥ \|*  
*dvijānāṃ purataḥ puṣpaḥ kathayāmāsa ceṣṭitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ātmīyaṃ kutsitaṃ teṣāṃ maṇibhadravadho yathā \|*  
*vihito vihitā patnī tasya vyājena kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ procustacchrutvā kopasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*sītkārānpracurānkṛtvā dhiktvāṃ pāpa pragamyatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ātmīyaṃ hema cādāya na te śuddhirbhaviṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*brahmaghnastvaṃ yataḥ proktāstrayo varṇā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ smṛtiśāstraprapāṭhakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-5. When the name was thus assigned unto Bhāskara of many rays, Puṣpa confessed all his misdeeds before the Brāhmaṇas, such as how Maṇibhadra was got executed and how his wife was fraudulently made his own wife.

## \|\| 1.162.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatastu duḥkhitaḥ puṣpo bāṣpasaṃpūritekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmasthānādvinirgatya praruroda suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

On hearing it, the Brāhmaṇas became highly furious. Expressing strong protest they said: “O sinner, fie upon you! Go away with your gold and all; you cannot be sanctified. You are in fact a Brahmaghna (Brāhmaṇa-slayer) because all the three castes, Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas are Dvijottamas (excellent twice-borns) as declared by the writers of the Smṛtis and scriptural texts.”

Sūta said:

6\. Thereupon, Puṣpa was grief-stricken. His eyes were filled with tears. He came out of the space allotted to the Brāhmaṇas and cried in great sorrow.

## \|\| 1.162.7 \|\|

*rorūyamāṇamālokya tataste nāgarā dvijāḥ \|*  
*dayāṃ ca mahatīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ procuḥ parasparam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing him lamenting continuously, those Nāgara Brāhmaṇas felt compassion for him and spoke to one another.

## \|\| 1.162.8-11 \|\|

*nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇi smṛtayaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ \|*  
*purāṇāni samastāni vīkṣadhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kutracitkvacidevāsya kathaṃcicchuddhirasti cet \|*  
*na tacca vidyate śāstramasminsthāne na cāsti yat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na smṛtirna purāṇaṃ ca vedāṃtaṃ vā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*na cāsti brāhmaṇaḥ so'tra sarvajñapratimo na yaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasmāccintayata kṣipramasya śuddhipradaṃ hi yat \|*  
*tacca pramāṇatāṃ nītvā śuddhirasya pradīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. “The scriptural texts are of various kinds. The Smṛtis are diverse. With great concentration pore through all the Purāṇas. See whether some means of his purification somewhere (in some texts) is found. There cannot be any scriptural text that is not available in this holy spot.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the same is the case with Smṛti, Purāṇa and Vedānta. Further there is no Brāhmaṇa here who is not on a par with the ommiscient (Śiva). Hence, ponder over this quickly as to what can accord him purity. Taking that as an authority, the purificatory rite of this Puṣpa can be performed.”

## \|\| 1.162.12-14 \|\|

*athaiko brāhmaṇaḥ prāha caṃḍaśarmeti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*mayā skāṃdapurāṇe'sminpuraścaraṇasaṃśritā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*paṭhitā saptamī yā ca puraścaraṇasaṃjñitā \|*  
*puraścaraṇataḥ pāpaṃ vihitaṃ tu yathā vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*samyaktathāpi vipreṃdrāstato yāti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkarotu tāmeṣa puraścaraṇasaptamīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Then a Brāhmaṇa well known as Caṇḍa Śarman said: “In this Skanda Purāṇa, I have read about Puraścaraṇa Saptamī. A sin committed shall vanish through this Puraścaraṇa. O leading Brāhmaṇas, there is no doubt about it. Hence let him perform this rite of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī.”

## \|\| 1.162.15 \|\|

*aparaṃ bhūbhujādeśānmaṇibhadro nipātitaḥ \|*  
*vadhakaistasya tatpāpaṃ yadi pāpaṃ prajāyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Another thing: Maṇibhadra was executed by the hangmen at the behest of the king. If at all there is a sin, it is his (the king’s).

## \|\| 1.162.16 \|\|

*rājā bhūtvā na yaḥ samyagvicārayati vādinam \|*  
*tasya tatpātakaṃ ghoraṃ rājñaścaiva prajāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the capacity of judge, if the king does not carefully examine the plaintiff, the terrible sin devolves only on the king.

## \|\| 1.162.17 \|\|

*tathāsya patnyāstatpāpaṃ jānaṃtyā yattayoditam \|*  
*matpitrā brāhmaṇairdatto'yaṃ purā vahnisaṃnidhau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Now coming to the sin of his wife: She knowingly said, ‘Earlier, it was this (Puṣpa) to whom I was given by my father and the Brāhmaṇas in the presence of fire.’

## \|\| 1.162.18-19 \|\|

*viḍaṃbitena cānena kṛtapratikṛtaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tasmānna cāsya doṣaḥ syādyataḥ proktaṃ munīśvaraiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kṛte pratikṛtaṃ kuryāddhiṃsane pratihiṃsanam \|*  
*na tatra jāyate doṣo yo duṣṭe duṣṭamācaret \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Through this deceptive means what has been committed is tit for tat. Hence there is no fault because leading sages have said: ‘One should do in return what has been done to one. If one is injured one can injure in return. If one commits a michief \[mischief\] or wickedness towards a mischievous or wicked fellow there is no fault (sin)’.”

## \|\| 1.162.20 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadyevaṃ vada viprāsya puraścaraṇasaṃjñitām \|*  
*saptamīmadya vipreṃdra varākasya viśuddhaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

20\. O Brāhmaṇas, if it so, prescribe this procedure of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī for the sake of this poor Brāhmaṇa’s purity today.

## \|\| 1.162.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athāsya kathayāmāsa saptamīṃ tāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmābhidhānastu kṛtvā tasyopari kṛpām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Brāhmaṇa named Caṇḍa Śarman took pity on him and explained the Saptamī rite.

## \|\| 1.162.22 \|\|

*tenāpi vihitā samyagyathā tasya mukhācchrutā \|*  
*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte vipāpmā samapadyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The rite was performed by him in the manner it was heard from him directly (orally). Then at the close of the year, he became free from sins.

## \|\| 1.162.23 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*puraścaraṇasaṃjñāṃ tu saptamīṃ vada sūtaja \|*  
*vidhinā kena kartavyā kasminkāla upasthite \|\| 23 \|\|*

The sages said:

23\. O Sūtaja, expound the rite called Puraścaraṇa Saptamī. What is the procedure by which it should be carried out? What is the time? Where should it be performed?

## \|\| 1.162.24 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi rohitāśvasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*mārkaṃḍena purā proktā pṛcchayamānena bhaktitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Sūta said:

24\. I shall narrate to you all that was said to King Rohitāśva by Mārkaṇḍeya formerly, on being devoutly asked by him.

## \|\| 1.162.25 \|\|

*saptakalpasmaro viprā mārkaṃḍākhyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*rohitāśvena pṛṣṭaḥ sa hariścaṃdrātmajena ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brāhmaṇas, the great sage named Mārkaṇḍeya was one who could remember (the events of) seven Kalpas. He was asked by Rohitāśva, the son of Hariścandra:

## \|\| 1.162.26 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*ajñānājjñānato vāpi yatpāpaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*upāyaṃ tasya nāśāya kiṃcinme vada sanmune \|\| 26 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

26\. O excellent sage, tell me some means to get rid of a sin that a man commits knowingly or unknowingly.

## \|\| 1.162.27 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*mānasaṃ vācikaṃ caiva kāyikaṃ ca tṛtīyakam \|*  
*trividhaṃ pātakaṃ loke narāṇāmiha jāyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

27\. Sins of men occur in the world in three differentt ways viz. mental, verbal and physical.

## \|\| 1.162.28 \|\|

*tatropāyā vināśāya tasya saṃparikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tānahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva nṛpasattama \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Means for their eradication have been duly expounded. O excellent king, listen, I shall describe them.

## \|\| 1.162.29 \|\|

*mānasaṃ caiva yatpāpaṃ narāṇāmiha jāyate \|*  
*paścāttāpe kṛte tasya tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In regard to mental sin that men commit, it perishes instantly when they repent for it.

## \|\| 1.162.30 \|\|

*vācikaṃ caiva yatpāpaṃ nābhuktvā tatpraṇaśyati \|*  
*puraścaraṇabāhyaṃ tu satyametanmayoditam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A verbal sin does not perish before the fruit is reaped except in a case where Puraścaraṇa rite is performed. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.162.31 \|\|

*nivedya brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ taduktaṃ ca samācaret \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ yathoktaṃ tu tataḥ śuddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After confessing it to eminent Brāhmaṇas one should perform the expiatory rite as (may be) instructed by them. Then he shall regain purity.

## \|\| 1.162.32 \|\|

*athavā pārthivo jñātvā kurute tasya nigra ham \|*  
*tena śuddhimavāproti yadyapi syātsa kilviṣī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Or, if the king comes to know of it and he metes out the suitable punishment, then he regains purity even if he is sinful.

## \|\| 1.162.33 \|\|

*lajjayā brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ yo na brūte kathaṃcana \|*  
*na ca rājā vijānāti śarīrasthena yo mriyet \|*  
*tasya nigrahakartā ca svayaṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If out of shame, he does not at all confess before eminent Brāhmaṇas nor the king comes to know of it and the fellow dies even as the sin clings to his body, then Yama, the son of Vivasvān, will himself give him adequate punishment.

## \|\| 1.162.34 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kṛtvā pāpaṃ vijānatā \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ tu kartavyaṃ yathoktaṃ brāhmaṇo ditam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence, a person who commits a sin knowingly should assiduously perform the expiatory rite as instructed by the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.162.35 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva pāpānāṃ vihitānāṃ munīśvara \|*  
*kiṃcidvrataṃ samācakṣva dānaṃ vā homameva vā \|*  
*vipāpmā jāyate yena puraścaraṇavarjitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

35\. O great sage, mention some Vrata, Dāna or Homa for the eradication of all the sins committed so that the person can be rid of sins without Puraścaraṇa.

## \|\| 1.162.36 \|\|

*nityaṃ pāpāni kurute naraḥ sūkṣmāṇi sarvataḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittāni sarveṣāṃ kartuṃ śaktiḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A man commits very subtle sins everyday. How can he have the capacity to perform expiatory rite for all of them?

## \|\| 1.162.37 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*asti rājanvrataṃ puṇyaṃ puraścaraṇasaṃjñitam \|*  
*puraścaraṇasaṃjñā tu saptamī sūryavallabhā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

37\. O king, there is a pious Vrata called Puraścaraṇa. The rite of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī is a favourite with the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.162.38 \|\|

*yayā saṃcīrṇayā rāja nkāyastho yamasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*vicitro mārjayetpāpaṃ kṛtaṃ janmani saṃcitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O king, if this rite is performed, Yama’s personal clerk Vivitra (Citragupta) shall wipe off the sins committed and accumulated in the course of a birth.

## \|\| 1.162.39 \|\|

*tasmātkuru mahārāja tathāśu vacanaṃ mama \|*  
*yena vā mucyate pāpā tsarvasmātkāyasaṃbhavāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence, O great king, carry out my instruction immediately so that you can be rid of all the sins clinging to the body.

## \|\| 1.162.40 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*puraścaraṇasaṃjñā tu saptamī munisattama \|*  
*vidhinā kena kartavyā kasminkāle vada sva me \|\| 40 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

40\. O excellent sage, by what procedure and at what time should the rite of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī be performed? Tell me.

## \|\| 1.162.41 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*māghamāse site pakṣe makarasthe divākare \|*  
*sūryavāreṇa saptamyāṃ vratametatsamācaret \|\| 41 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

41\. One should perform this Vrata on the seventh lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha when the Sun is in Capricorn and it (the day) coincides with a Sunday.

## \|\| 1.162.42 \|\|

*pākhaṃḍaiḥ patitaiḥ sārdhaṃ tasminnahani nālapet \|*  
*bhakṣayitvā nṛpaśreṣṭha prabhāte dantadhāvanam \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena paścācca kartavyo niyamo nṛpa \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On that day a devotee should not talk with heretics and hypocritical persons, O excellent king. Early in the morning the devotee chews a twig for cleaning the teeth. Afterwards, the Niyama (restraint) is to be observed by uttering this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.162.43 \|\|

*puraścaraṇakṛtyāyāṃ saptamyāṃ divasādhipa \|*  
*upavāsaṃ kariṣyāmi adya tvaṃ śaraṇaṃ mama \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “O Lord of day, I shall observe fast as a part of the rite of Puraścaraṇa Saptamī. Today you are my refuge.”

## \|\| 1.162.44 \|\|

*tato'parāhṇasamaye snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*pratimāṃ pūjayedbhaktyā dinādhipasamudbhavām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then in the afternoon he takes bath and remains pure wearing washed clothes. He shall then worship with devotion the image of the Lord of Day.

## \|\| 1.162.45 \|\|

*raktaiḥ puṣpairmahāvīra pādādyaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|*  
*pataṃgāya namaḥ pādau mārtaṃḍāyeti jānunī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O great hero, the devotee worships the foot etc. with red flowers. The feet of the Sun-god are to be worshipped by saying “Obeisance to Pataṅga.” It is in this way that the different parts of the person of the Sun-god are to be worshipped with flowers. The knees (of the Sun-god) shall be worshipped with the Mantra "Obeisance to Mārtaṇḍa.”

## \|\| 1.162.46 \|\|

*guhyaṃ divasanāthāya nābhiṃ dvādaśa mūrtaye \|*  
*bāhū ca padmahastāya hṛdayaṃ tīkṣṇadīdhite \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “Obeisance to the Lord of Day" (privy). “Obeisance to one of twelve forms" (navel). “Obeisance to the Lord with lotus in hand" (arms). “O fiery-rayed one" (chest).

## \|\| 1.162.47 \|\|

*kaṃṭhaṃ padmadalābhāya śirastejomayāya ca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivaddhūpaṃ karpūramādadet \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “Obeisance to the one having the lustre of lotus petals" (the neck). “Obeisance to the resplendent one" (the head).”

After worshipping duly the form, one should offer camphor.

## \|\| 1.162.48 \|\|

*guḍaudanaṃ ca naivedyaṃ raktavastrābhiveṣṭitam \|*  
*raktasūtreṇa dīpaṃ ca tathaivārārtikaṃ nṛpa \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Cooked rice mixed with jaggery should be the food offering. It should be covered with a red cloth. O king, the Dīpa (lamp) and Ārārtika (waving of lights) shall be with red thread.

## \|\| 1.162.49 \|\|

*śaṃkhe toyaṃ samādāya raktacandanamiśritam \|*  
*saphalaṃ ca tataḥ kṛtvā arghyaṃ dadyāttataḥ param \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The devotee then takes water in a conch and puts red sandal-paste therein. After placing a fruit thereon he offers the

Arghya.

## \|\| 1.162.50 \|\|

*kukṛtaṃ yatkṛtaṃ kiṃcidajñānājjñānato'pi vā \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ kṛtaṃ deva mamārghyaśca pragṛhyatām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. (Mantra) “O Lord, expiatory rite has been performed for the misdeed that has been committed knowingly or unknowingly. Let my Arghya be received.”

## \|\| 1.162.51 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjayadvipraṃ gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*dattvā tu bhojanaṃ tasmai dakṣiṇāṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*prāśanaṃ kāyaśuddhyarthaṃ pañcagavyasya cācaret \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then the devotee honours the Brāhmaṇa with scents, flowers and unguents. After serving him food and giving him Dakṣīṇā according to one’s capacity the devotee should eat pañcagavya (five products of a cow) for the purification of the body.

## \|\| 1.162.52 \|\|

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā samudvīkṣya divākaram \|*  
*divākaraṃ gataścaiva mantrametaṃ samuccaret \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. With palms joined in reverence, looking up towards the Sun and meditating on the Sun the devotee should recite this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.162.53 \|\|

*idaṃ vrataṃ mayā deva gṛhītaṃ puratastava \|*  
*avighnaṃ siddhimāyātu prasādāttava bhāskara \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “O Lord Bhāskara, this Vrata is observed by me in front of you. With the favour of Your Lordship, let it reach perfection (completion) without obstacles.”

## \|\| 1.162.54 \|\|

*tataśca phālgune māsi saṃprāpte munisattama \|*  
*kundena pūjayeddevaṃ tenaiva vidhinā tataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then, at the advent of the month of Phālguna, O excellent sage, the devotee should worship the Lord with Kunda flowers in accordance with the same procedure (explained previously).

## \|\| 1.162.55 \|\|

*dhūpaṃ ca gugguluṃ dadyānnaivedyaṃ bhaktameva ca \|*  
*prāśanaṃ gomayaṃ proktaṃ sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. For the purpose of purification of all sins the devotee offers Guggulu incense and cooked food (rice) as Naivedya. Then he eats Gomaya (i.e. Pañcagavya).

## \|\| 1.162.56-57 \|\|

*caitre māsi tu saṃprāpte surabhyā pūjyeddharim \|*  
*naivedyaṃ guṇikāḥ proktā dhūpaṃ sarjarasodbhavam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kuśodakaṃ ca saṃprāśya kāyaśuddhimavāpnuyāt \|*  
*vaiśākhe kiṃśukaiḥ pūjāṃ yathāvacca ghṛtāśanaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57a. In the month of Caitra, the devotee worships Hari with Surabhi (fragrance). “Guṇikās” are cited as the food offering and the resin of Sarja constitutes the incense. The devotee gains the purity of the body by imbibing Kuśa water.

57b. In the month of Vaiśākha, the worship (of the Sun-god) is done with Kiṃśuka flowers and drinking of Ghee (for purification).

## \|\| 1.162.58 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ ca surāmāṃsaṃ dhūpaṃ ca vinivedayet \|*  
*dadhiprāśanamevātra kartavyaṃ kāyaśuddhaye \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The Naivedya is meat and liquor. Incense is to be offered. Drinking of curd should be done for the purification of the body.

## \|\| 1.162.59-61 \|\|

*puṣpapāṭalayā pūjā vidhātavyā ravernṛpa \|*  
*naivedye saktavaḥ proktāḥ prāśanaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ smṛtam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kapilāyā mahāvīra sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|*  
*āṣāḍhe munipuṣpaiśca pūjayedbhāskaraṃ nṛpa \|\| 60 \|\|*

*naivedye ghārikā proktā prāśanaṃ madhusarpiṣoḥ \|*  
*dhūpaṃ caivāgaruṃ dadyātparayā śraddhayā yutaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-60a. (In Jyeṣṭha) O king, the worship of Ravi is to be performed by means of Pāṭala flowers. Saktu (barley flour?) is recommended for food offering.

Ghee prepared from the milk of a tawny-coloured cow should be imbibed for the eradication of sins, O great hero.

60b-61. In the month of Āṣāḍha, O king, one should worship Bhāskara with Muni flowers. Ghārikās (small cakes of flour, jaggery and fruit boiled in ghee) are prescribed as the Naivedya (food offering to the deity).

## \|\| 1.162.62 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe tu kadaṃbena pūjanaṃ tīkṣṇadīdhiteḥ \|*  
*naivedye modakāścaiva tagaraṃ dhūpa mādadet \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The worship of the Fiery-rayed One (the Sun) in Śrāvaṇa is to be performed with Kadamba flowers. Modakas (sweetmeat) are offered as Naivedya and Tagara is to be used for incense.

## \|\| 1.162.63-65 \|\|

*gośṛṃgodakamādāya sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate \|*  
*jātyā bhādrapade pūjā kṣīranaivedyamādadet \|\| 63 \|\|*

*dhūpaṃ nakhasamudbhūtaṃ prāśanaṃ kṣīrameva ca \|*  
*āśvine kamalaiḥ pūjā naivedye ghṛtapūrikā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*dhūpaṃ kuṃkumajaṃ proktaṃ karpūraprāśanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-64a. By taking in the water from Gośṛṅga (cow’s horn) the devotee is rid of sins immediately.

The adoration in Bhādrapada is by means of Jāti flowers. Milk is offered as Naivedya.

The incense arises from claws (of certain animals). Milk is used for imbibing.

64b-65. In the month of Āśvina the worship is performed with lotus flowers. Ghṛtapūrikā (Puns fried in ghee) is to be offered as Naivedya.

The incense is from saffron and Karpūra water (flavoured with camphor) is to be imbibed.

## \|\| 1.162.66 \|\|

*tulasyā kārtike pūjā bhāskarasya prakīrtitā \|*  
*naivedye caiva khaṃḍākhyaṃ dhūpaṃ kausuṃbhikaṃ nṛpa \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O king, in the month of Kārttika the worship of Bhāskara is done by means of Tulasī. Khaṇḍa (sugar candy) is offered as Naivedya and the incense is from Kusuṃbha.

## \|\| 1.162.67 \|\|

*prāśanaṃ ca lavaṃgākhyaṃ sarvapāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*bhṛṃgarājena pūjā ca saumye māsi samācaret \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Laviṅga (clove) is to be taken in as destructive of all sins.

In the month of Saumya (Mārgaśīrṣa) one should perform the worship by means of Bhṛṅgarāja.

## \|\| 1.162.68 \|\|

*naivedye pheṇikā deyā dhūpaṃ guḍasamudbhavam \|*  
*kaṃkolaprāśanaṃ caiva bhāskarasya pratuṣṭaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Pheṇikā (a kind of sweetmeat) is to be offered as Naivedya. The incense comes from jaggery. For the satisfaction of Bhāskara, Kaṅkola should be ṭgken in.

## \|\| 1.162.69 \|\|

*śatapatrikayā pūjā pauṣe māsi raveḥ smṛtā \|*  
*sahajaṃ dhūpamādiṣṭaṃ naivedye śuṣkalī tathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. It is ordained in the Smṛti that the worship of Ravi in the month of Pauṣa should be done by means of Śatapatrikā (hundred-petalled lotus). Something natural (easily available) is offered as incense and Śaṣkuli (fried flour-coils) has to be offered as Naivedya.

## \|\| 1.162.70 \|\|

*prāśane pūrvamuktāni sarvāṇyeva samācaret \|*  
*samāptau ca tato dadyātṣaḍbhāgaṃ gṛhasaṃbhavam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. As for imbibing, one can have all the things mentioned before. At the conclusion of the adoration one-sixth of the income of the household is to be given as Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 1.162.71 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya nṛpaśreṣṭha sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|*  
*iṣṭabhojyaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ svaśaktyā pārthivottama \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O excellent one among kings, the above-mentioned Dakṣiṇā is to be given to a Brāhmaṇa for the eradication of all sins. Thereafter friends and persons of one’s choice are to be fed in accordance with one’s capacity.

## \|\| 1.162.72 \|\|

*evaṃ tu kurute yo'tra saptamīṃ bhāskarodbhavām \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto nirmalatvaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He who performs the Saptamī rite unto Bhāskara in this manner shall become pure after being rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.162.73 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*evaṃ purā vai kathitā rohitāśvāya dhīmate \|*  
*mārkaṃḍena mahābhāga tasmāttvamapi tāṃ kuru \|\| 73 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

73\. Thus the procedure was formerly described to the intelligent Rohitāśva by Mārkaṇḍeya. O highly esteemed one, do this yourself too.

## \|\| 1.162.74 \|\|

*yena saṃjāyate samyakpuraścaraṇameva te \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Thereby the Puraścaraṇa rite will be perfected in your case.

## \|\| 1.162.75 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā puṣpo'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tāṃ cakre saptamīṃ hṛṣṭo yathā tena niveditā \|\| 75 \|\|*

Sūta said:

75\. On hearing his words, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Puṣpa too joyously performed that Saptamī rite in the manner described by him.

## \|\| 1.162.76 \|\|

*ṣaḍbhāgaṃ pradadau tasmai brāhmaṇāya mahātmane \|*  
*svavittasya gṛhasthasya kupyākupyasya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. To that noble-souled Brāhmaṇa, he gave a sixth of all his wealth as a householder in the form of costly gems or ordinary metals.

## \|\| 1.162.77 \|\|

*so'pi jagrāha tadvittaṃ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*suvarṇamaṇi ratnāni saṃkhyayā parivarjitam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He too accepted with a delighted mind that wealth in the form of innumerable gifts of gold and gems.

## Chapter 163 - Creation of Brāhma Nāgara \[Community\]

## \|\| 1.163.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha te nāgarāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tadvittabhājanam \|*  
*na kenāpi grahītavyaṃ sarvānkāmānnirasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The legend in this chapter explains the formation of ‘Brāhma Nāgara’ as a subcommunity of Nāgaras (vide vv 35-37).

Sūta said:

1\. On seeing that pot of wealth, all the Nāgaras (citizens with that appellation) came to the agreement that the pot should not be accepted by anyone.

## \|\| 1.163.2 \|\|

*tataste samayaṃ kṛtvā samānīya ca madhyagam \|*  
*tasyāsyena tataḥ procurbrahmasthāne vyavasthi tāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. They abandoned all their desires (for money). They made an agreement (within themselves) and appointed a “middle-man” (umpire-like decision-maker). Stationed in the place assigned to Brahmā, they announced through the oral declaration of the middleman:

## \|\| 1.163.3-7 \|\|

*anena lobhayuktena tiraskṛtya dvijottamān \|*  
*puṣpavittamupādāya prāyaścittaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tathā caiva tu ṣaḍbhāgo gṛhīto vibhavasya ca \|*  
*tasmādeṣa samastānāṃ bāhyabhūto bhaviṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nāgarāṇāṃ dvijedrāṇāṃ yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adyaprabhṛti cānena yaḥ saṃbaṃdhaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*so'pi bāhyastu sarveṣāṃ nāgarāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhojanaṃ vātha pānīyaṃ yo'sya sadmani karhicit \|*  
*kariṣyati sa cā'pyevaṃ patitaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. “The greedy one (i.e. Caṇḍaśarman) has ignored and dishonoured excellent Brāhmaṇas, accepted cash from Puṣpa and performed the expiatory rite.

A sixth of his (Puṣpa’s) riches was received by him. So he will be excluded by all of us, the leading Brāhmaṇas of Nāgara (community). He will be on a par with a low-caste one. From now onwards, he who associates with this fellow shall also be excommunicated from the society of all the Nāgaras. He who accepts food or beverage from his house shall also become a fallen one in this manner.”

## \|\| 1.163.8 \|\|

*evamuktvā tatastena dattaṃ tālatrayaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*brahmasthāne dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kṛtvā puṣpasamaṃ ca tam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After saying this, he clapped thrice from the place (post) of Brahmā and made him (Caṇḍaśarman) like a stale flower (that is thrown away).

## \|\| 1.163.9 \|\|

*atha te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve jagmuḥ svaṃsvaṃ niveśanam \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmā sa codvignaḥ puṣpapārśvaṃ tadā gataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then all those Brāhmaṇas, went to their respective abodes. Caṇḍaśarman became highly distressed and went near Puṣpa.

## \|\| 1.163.10-11 \|\|

*eteṣāmeva sarveṣāṃ saṃmatena mayā tava \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ tadā dattaṃ tathā pi patitaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*
