*tasmādahaṃ patiṣyāmi susamiddhe hutāśane \|*  
*naiva jīvitumicchāmi svajanaiḥ parivarjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. (He said:) “It is with the consent of all these (Brāhmaṇas) that expiatory rite for you was performed by me. Still I have been declared as fallen from grace. I shall, therefore, fall into the well-kindled fire. I do not wish to remain alone after being forsaken by my people.”

## \|\| 1.163.12 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*na viṣādastvayā kāryaḥ kārye'smidvijasattama \|*  
*vittārthaṃ dūṣitastvaṃhi yato brāhmaṇasattamaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

12\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, do not be distressed in this matter, as you have been slighted by the excellent Brāhmaṇas for the sake of money.

## \|\| 1.163.13-14 \|\|

*nāgarāṃstoṣayiṣyāmi tānahaṃ vividhairdhanaiḥ \|*  
*yācayiṣyaṃti yanmātraṃ tava gātraviśuddhaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tāvanmātraṃ pradāsyāmi tebhyo hi tava kāraṇāt \|*  
*evamuktvā samāgatya brahmasthānaṃ tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. In order to get your person purified, I shall make those Nāgaras delighted by means of different kinds of wealth. I shall give them as much as they request for. For your sake I shall give them that much.

After saying this, he hurriedly came back to Brahmasthāna.

## \|\| 1.163.15-16 \|\|

*cātuścaraṇamānīya madhyagāsyena so'bravīt \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmā dvijo yaśca madarthe patitaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yuṣmābhirvittalobhena tadvittaṃ vo dadāmyaham \|*  
*samastaṃ madgṛhe yacca kriyatāṃ vacanaṃ dvijaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He caused the Cātuścaraṇa to be brought. Through the mouth of the middleman he said: “For my sake, the Brāhmaṇa Caṇḍaśarman has been rendered fallen from grace by you all due to your greed for money. I shall give you all the wealth that is in my house. Let this request be accepted by the Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 1.163.17 \|\|

*atha te kupitāḥ procuḥ sarva eva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sītkārānvividhānkṛtvā krodha saṃraktalocanāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then those angry Brāhmaṇas made different kinds of gruff sounds. With the eyes reddened due to anger they said:

## \|\| 1.163.18-22 \|\|

*dhigdhikpāpasamācāra jihvā te śatadhā tataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ na yāti yadevaṃ tvaṃ prajalpasi vigarhitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*patito'yaṃ kṛto 'smābhirnaiva vittasya kāraṇāt \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ yato dattamekenāpi durātmanā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*smṛtayo dūṣitāstena purāṇāni viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ caivāsma dīyaṃ ca karma caitatprakurvatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ pradātavyaṃ caturbhiraparaiḥ saha \|*  
*saṃmantrya manunā proktametadeva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvadīyaṃ pātakaṃ cāsya śarīre'dya vyavasthitam \|*  
*ekākinā yato dattaṃ tenāyaṃ patitaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. “Fie upon you! Fie upon you! Oh sinful one. How is it that your tongue does not get split into a hundred pieces though you prattle this despicable thing!

This Brāhmaṇa has not been excommunicated and rendered fallen from grace for the sake of money. It is because the expiatory rite was performed by this wicked soul single-handed.

By performing this rite thus, Smṛtis have been defiled (by transgressing them). Purāṇas have been slighted and further this holy spot of ours has been rendered unholy.

Expiatory rite is to be performed after consulations with four others. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this has been said by Manu.

Your sin has today dung to his body because the rite has been performed by him single-handedly. Therefore, he has fallen from grace.”

## \|\| 1.163.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā dvijāḥ sarve jagmuḥ svaṃsvaṃ niketanam \|*  
*puṣpopi ca samudvigno vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:

23\. After saying this, all the Brāhmaṇas went to their respective abodes. Puṣpa too was much distressed and utterly confused.

## \|\| 1.163.24 \|\|

*jagāmātha nijāvāsaṃ niḥśvasannurago yathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He returned to his residence heaving sighs like a hissing serpent.

## \|\| 1.163.25-27 \|\|

*tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa yāvanno sāhasaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tāvatsiddhirmanuṣyāṇāṃ na kathaṃcitprajāyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasmādahaṃ kariṣyāmi caṇḍaśarmakṛte mahat \|*  
*kṛtaghnatā yathā na syātproktaṃ caiva yato budhaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*brahmaghne ca surāpe ca caure bhagnavrate tathā \|*  
*niṣkṛtirvihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Then he thought, ‘Human beings cannot attain Siddhi unless they take risks. Therefore, I shall perform something great for the sake of Caṇḍaśarman lest there should be ungratefulness. Wise men have declared thus:

“Rites of redemption have been laid down by good people in the case of a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, an imbiber of liquor, a thief and one who breaks his vows. But there is no rite of redemption in the case of the ungrateful.”

## \|\| 1.163.28-29 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya manasā sūryavāreṇa saptamī \|*  
*yadā'yātā dvijaśreṣṭhāstadā cāṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇāḥ kṛtāstena puṣpādityasya dhīmatā \|*  
*tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ samādāya pūrvoktavidhinā tataḥ \|*  
*chittvāchittvā nijāṃgāni juhuyājjātavedasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. After resolving thus, O excellent Brāhmanas, when Sunday coincided with the seventh lunar day, he made one hundred eight circumambulations of Puṣpāditya. That sensible (Brāhmaṇa) took up a sharp weapon. As before he cut off pieces from his limbs and consigned them to the sacred fire.

## \|\| 1.163.30 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ yāvatkāyaśeṣeṇa yacchati \|*  
*tāvatpratyakṣatāṃ gatvā sa prokto bhāsvatā svayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When he wanted to offer the remaining part of his body as Pūrṇāhuti, the Sun-god himself appeared and said to him:

## \|\| 1.163.31 \|\|

*puṣpa mā sāhasaṃ kārṣīḥ parituṣṭo'smi te'nagha \|*  
*bhūya eva mahābhāga brūhi kiṃ te dadāmyaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “O Puṣpa, O sinless one, do not be rash. I am pleased with you again. O highly esteemed one, what shall I give you?”

## \|\| 1.163.32 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*caṇḍaśarmā dvijendro'yaṃ madarthe patitaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*samastairnāgarairdeva taṃ tairnaya samānatām \|\| 32 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

32\. O Lord, this leading Brāhmaṇa Caṇḍaśarman has been rendered fallen on account of me by all the Nāgaras. Do make him equal to them.

## \|\| 1.163.33 \|\|

*śāstraṃ dṛṣṭvā pradattaṃ me prāyaścittaṃ mahātmanā \|*  
*tathāpi dūṣitaḥ kṣudraiḥ samastairasahiṣṇubhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. It was after going through the scriptural texts that the noble-souled one performed the expiation rite. Still all the mean fellows who were intolerant (and jealous) censured (rendered fallen) him.

## \|\| 1.163.34 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ekasyāpi vaco naiva śakyate kartumanyathā \|*  
*nāgarasya dvijaśreṣṭha samastānāṃ ca kiṃ punaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

The Lord said:

34\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, it is impossible to alter the words of even a single Nāgara. Still more so the joint declaration of all the Nāgaras.

## \|\| 1.163.35 \|\|

*parameṣa dvijaḥ pūtaścaṃḍaśarmā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*brāhmo'yaṃ nāgaraḥ khyātaḥ samaste dharaṇītale \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. But this Caṇḍaśarman shall become purified. He will be well-known all over the earth as Brāhmanāgara.

## \|\| 1.163.36 \|\|

*etasya ye sutāścaiva bhaviṣyaṃti dharātale \|*  
*vikhyātiṃ te'pi yāsyaṃti mānyāḥ pūjyā mahībhṛtām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All his sons and descendants will become well-known all over the world. They will be honoured and esteemed by kings.

## \|\| 1.163.37 \|\|

*ye cāpi bāṃdhavā ścāsya suhṛdaśca samāgamam \|*  
*kariṣyaṃti samaṃ te'pi bhaviṣyaṃti suśobhanāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. All the kinsmen and friends who associate with him shall also become splendid.

## \|\| 1.163.38 \|\|

*tvaṃ cāpi matprasādena saṃpūrṇāṃgo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You too shall get back your entire physical body by my grace.

## \|\| 1.163.39 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*puṣpo'pi cākṣatāṃgatvaṃ tatkṣaṇātsamapadyata \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After saying this the Thousand-rayed One vanished. Puṣpa instantly regained his wounded limbs intact.

## Chapter 164 - Installation of Nāgeśvara (Nāga-īśvara) etc.

## \|\| 1.164.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare puṣpaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmagṛhaṃ gatvā diṣṭyādiṣṭyeti cābravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vivarṇavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇaṃ tadā \|*  
*bāndhavaiḥ sahitaṃ sarvairdārairbhṛtyaistathā sutaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. In the meantime, Puṣpa went to the abode of Caṇḍaśarman with a delighted heart. He saw him with pallid face and eyes filled with tears in the company of all kinsmen, wife, sons and servants. He exclaimed “Thank God! Thank God!” and said thus:

## \|\| 1.164.3 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*tavārthe ca mayā sūryaḥ kāyatyāgena toṣitaḥ \|*  
*patitattvaṃ na te kāye tatprasādādbhaviṣyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

3\. For your sake the Sun-god has been propitiated by me by sacrificing my own body. Due to his favour, the state of being a fallen fellow shall not befall you.

## \|\| 1.164.4 \|\|

*tava putrāśca pautrāśca ye bhaviṣyaṃti vaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*nāgarāṇāṃ ca te sarve bhaviṣyaṃti guṇādhikāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Your sons, grandsons and all your successors yet to be born shall surpass the Nāgaras in good qualities and features.

## \|\| 1.164.5 \|\|

*tasmāduttiṣṭha gacchāmo nadīṃ puṇyāṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*tasyāstaṭe nivāsāya kṛtvā caivāśramaṃ dvija \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hence get ready. We shall go to the holy river Sarasvatī in order to settle on her banks, O Brāhmaṇa, after building a hermitage there.

## \|\| 1.164.6-9 \|\|

*tvayā saha vasiṣyāmi ahameva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*asti me vipulaṃ vittaṃ ye cānye te'nuyāyinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tānsarvānpoṣayiṣyāmi tyajyatāṃ mānaso jvaraḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā caṇḍaśarmā tu putrairbaṃdhubhiranvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sarasvatīṃ samuddiśya niṣkrāṃto nagarāttataḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya namaskṛtya suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇo dīna uttarābhimukho yayau \|*  
*puṣpeṇa sahitaścaiva muhurmuhuḥ prabodhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. Definitely I too shall stay with you. There is no doubt about it. I have ample wealth. I shall maintain all your followers too. Leave all of your mental worries and anguish.

On hearing it, Caṇḍaśarman set off from Nagara towards Sarasvatī accompanied by his sons and kinsmen.

With great grief and tears filling the eyes, he bowed down and circumambulated the holy spot. Accompanied by Puṣpa and repeatedly enlightened by him, he went towards the North.

## \|\| 1.164.10 \|\|

*tataḥ sarasvatīṃ prāpya puṇyāṃ śītajalāṃ nadīm \|*  
*sevitāṃ munisaṃghaistāṃ lolakallolamālinīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They reached the meritorious river Sarasvatī of cool waters, tremulous with garland-like waves and ripples and served by groups of sages.

## \|\| 1.164.11 \|\|

*tasyā dakṣiṇakūle sa nivāsamakarottadā \|*  
*puṣpasya matimāsthāya bandhubhiḥ sakalairvṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Relying on the suggestion of Puṣpa, he then set up his residence on her southern banks along with all his kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.164.12 \|\|

*tasyāsīnnagarasthasya pratijñā caṇḍaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*saptaviṃśati bhirliṃgairdṛṣṭaibhokṣyāmyahaṃ sadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. While staying in Nagara, Caṇḍaśarman had taken the vow that he would take food only after visiting twenty-seven Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.164.13 \|\|

*tāṃ ca saṃsmaratastasya pratijñāṃ pūrvasaṃcitām \|*  
*hṛdayaṃ dahyate tasya divānaktaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Constantly remembering the vow taken earlier, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, his heart continued to burn day and night.

## \|\| 1.164.14 \|\|

*sa ca snātvā sarasvatyāṃ śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍakṣarasya mantrasya japaṃ cakre pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He took his bath in Sarasvatī with great concentration and regained cleanliness. Then he performed the Japa of the six-lettered Mantra severally (for every Liṅga).

## \|\| 1.164.15 \|\|

*nāma coccārya liṃgasya namaskārāntamādadhe \|*  
*kardamena dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ paṃcāṃgulaśatena ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He uttered the name of the particular Liṅga and made it end with namaḥ. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he made the Liṅgas five hundred Aṅgulas long out of mud.

## \|\| 1.164.16 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya pūjayedbhaktyā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*prāṇarudrāñjapanpaścācchraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After installing them he devoutly adored them with flowers, incense and unguents. Thereafter, with great faith he performed the japa of Prāṇa Rudra Mantras.

## \|\| 1.164.17 \|\|

*duḥsthitaṃ susthitaṃ vāpi śivaliṃgaṃ na cālayet \|*  
*iti matvā dvijendro'sau naiva tāni visarjayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One should not remove or dislodge a Liṅga whether it is firmly installed or remains unsteady. With this in view, the leading Brāhmaṇa did not perform the ritualistic Visarjana (dismissal).

## \|\| 1.164.18 \|\|

*uparyupari teṣāṃ ca kardamena dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*cakre liṃgāni nityaṃ sa saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Everyday he made twenty-seven Liṅgas out of mud and all these were heaped up, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.164.19 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā jātaḥ kardamaparvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the course of a long time a huge mountain of clay piled up there.

## \|\| 1.164.20 \|\|

*atha tuṣṭo mahādevastasya bhaktyatirekataḥ \|*  
*nirbhidya dharaṇīpṛṣṭhaṃ tasya liṃgamadarśayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Mahādeva became pleased with the excess of his devotion. Breaking open the surface of the earth he appeared and showed him a Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.164.21-23 \|\|

*abravītsādaraṃ taṃ ca meghagambhīrayā girā \|*  
*caṇḍaśarmanpratuṣṭosmi tava bhaktyā'nayā dvija \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasmālliṃgamidaṃ nityaṃ pūjayasva prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiliṃgānāṃ yataḥ phalamavāpsyasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

*anyopi ca naro bhaktyā yaścainaṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiliṃgānāṃ so'pi śreyo'bhilapsyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. He spoke courteously to him in words majestic like the rumbling of a cloud: “O Brāhmaṇa Caṇḍaśarman, I am pleased with this devotion of yours. So with great devotion do worship this Liṅga. Thereby you will get the benefit of worshipping twenty-seven Liṅgas. Another man too who happens to worship this will derive the benefit of worshipping all the twenty-seven Liṅgas.”

## \|\| 1.164.24 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmāpi taṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pūjayāmāsa tattvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After saying thus, the Lord vanished therefrom. Caṇḍaśarman joyously and truthfully as per prescribed procedure worshipped it.

## \|\| 1.164.25 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa tasya liṃgasya śobhanam \|*  
*nāma cakre tatastasya vicārya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He caused a splendid palace constructed for the Liṅga. He pondered over the matter frequently and arrived at a name to be given to it.

## \|\| 1.164.26 \|\|

*nagarasthita liṃgānāṃ yasmātsaṃsmaraṇātsthitaḥ \|*  
*nāgareśvarasaṃjñastu tasmādeṣa bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He happened to remember the Ungas stationed in Nagara. Hence he decided: “This shall be named Nāgareśvara.”

## \|\| 1.164.27 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃsthāpya talliṃgaṃ caṃḍaśarmā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ārādhayāmāsa tadā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sūta said:

27\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Caṇḍaśarman installed that Liṅga and propitiated it with flowers, incense and unguents.

## \|\| 1.164.28 \|\|

*saptaviṃśatiliṃgānāṃ prāpnoti ca tathā phalam \|*  
*pūjitānāṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā nagare yāni tāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he obtained the benefit of worshipping all the twenty-seven Liṅgas that were in Nagara.

## \|\| 1.164.29 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā nāgareśvaratuṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*śivalokaṃ gataḥ sākṣādyānamadhye niveśitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After a long time, Nāgareśvara having been gratified, he sitting in the centre of a vehicle went directly to Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.164.30 \|\|

*puṣpopi sthāpayāmāsa puṣpādityamathāparam \|*  
*puṇye sarasvatītīre tataḥ pūjāparo'bhavat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Puṣpa installed another Puṣpāditya on the banks of Sarasvatī and then became engaged in its worship.

## \|\| 1.164.31-32 \|\|

*tasyāpi darśanaṃ gatvā prītyā vacanamabravīt \|*  
*puṣpa tuṣṭosmi bhadraṃ te varaṃ prārthaya suvrata \|\| 31 \|\|*

*adeyamapi dāsyāmi tasmātprārthaya mā ciram \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. He (Śiva) appeared before him and spoke these words with pleasure: “O Puṣpa, welfare unto you. O devotee of good holy vows, I am pleased with you. Request for a boon. I shall grant it to you even if it happens to be one that should not be granted. Hence do not delay. Request for it.”

## \|\| 1.164.33 \|\|

*puṣpa uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*taddehi yācamānasya mama yaddhṛdi saṃsthitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Puṣpa said:

33\. If you are pleased, O Lord, with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, then even as I beg, grant to me what is in my heart.

## \|\| 1.164.34 \|\|

*camatkārapure deva tava yā mūrtayaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*dvādaśaiva pramāṇena pūjyāḥ sarvadivaukasām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Lord, you have twelve Mūrtis (forms) stationed in Camatkārapura. They are worthy of being worshipped by all the Heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.164.35 \|\|

*tāsāṃ pūjāphalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ saṃprāpnotu naro bhuvi \|*  
*yaḥ pūjayati mūrtiṃ te yaiṣā saṃsthāpitā mayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A man on the earth who worships your form that has been installed by me here, should get the entire benefit of all of them.

## \|\| 1.164.36 \|\|

*nāgarāditya ityeṣā khyātā bhavatu bhūtale \|*  
*yeyaṃ sarasvatītīre prāsāde sthāpitā mayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Let this form that has been installed on the banks of Sarasvatī in a palace be well-known all over the world as Nāgarāditya.

## \|\| 1.164.37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya gataścādarśanaṃ raviḥ \|*  
*dīpavadbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāstadadbhutamivā bhavat \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sūta said:

37\. Lord Ravi (Sun-god) promised, “Let it be so” and vanished like a lamp. It was all miraculous, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.164.38 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā puṣpopi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*sūryalokamanuprāpto vimānena suvarcasā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then after a long time, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Puṣpa attained the world of Sun-god by means of an aerial chariot of great refulgence.

## \|\| 1.164.39 \|\|

*śākambharīti vikhyātā bhāryā'sīccaṃḍaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*tayā saṃsthāpitā durgā sarasvatyāḥ śubhe taṭe \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Caṇḍaśarman had a wife well-known by the name Śākaṃbharī. Durgā was installed by her on the excellent banks of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.164.40 \|\|

*ārādhitā'tha sadbhaktyā divānaktaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tatastuṣṭā varaṃ tasyāḥ sā dadau dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, she was propitiated day and night with great devotion. Thereafter, she became pleased and granted her a boon:

## \|\| 1.164.41 \|\|

*putri tuṣṭāsmi bhadraṃ te śākaṃbhari pragṛhyatām \|*  
*varaṃ yatte sadābhīṣṭaṃ matprasādādasaṃśayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “O dear daughter, I am pleased with you. Welfare unto you, O Śākaṃbharī, let what has been always cherished by you in your heart be received as the boon, with my favour undoubtedly".

## \|\| 1.164.42-43 \|\|

*śākambharyuvāca \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭigaṇā devi mātṛṇāṃ ye vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*camatkārapure khyātā hāsyāttuṣṭiṃ vrajaṃti yāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yā rātrau balidānena jāte vṛddhau tataḥ param \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ jāyatāṃ puṇyaṃ yaste mūrtiṃ prapūjayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

Śākaṃbharī said:

42-43. O goddess, there are sixty-four groups of the Mothers settled in Camatkārapura. It is well-known that they become satisfied by laughter indulged in by one at night. The offer of oblations at the time of prosperity also satisfied them. Let all those merits accrue to one who worships your idol.

## \|\| 1.164.44 \|\|

*atrāgatya nadītīre yaiṣā saṃsthāpitā mayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The idol has been installed by me after coming to the banks of the river.

## \|\| 1.164.45-46 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*āśvinasya site pakṣe mahānavamisaṃjñite \|*  
*yo mamāgre samāgatya pūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasya kṛtsnaṃ phalaṃ sadyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nāgarasya viśeṣeṇa satyametanmayoditam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

45-46. In the bright half of Āśvina on the ninth day called Mahānavamī, if a devotee comes before me and worships devoutly, he will have the entire fruit immediately. There is no doubt about it. Particularly in the case of a Nāgara it is so. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.164.47 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu sā devī tataścādarśanaṃ gatā \|*  
*tasyā nāmnā ca sā devī proktā śākambharī bhuvi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After saying thus, the goddess vanished. That goddess is called on the earth after her name Śakaṃbharī.

## \|\| 1.164.48 \|\|

*vṛddheranaṃtaraṃ tasyā yaḥ pūjāṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*tasya vṛddherna vighnaḥ syātkadāciddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After Vṛddhi (prosperity) if a man worships her, there shall never be any impediment to his prosperity, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## Chapter 165 - Origin of Aśva Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.165.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛtipuṇye ca sarasvatyāstaṭeśubhe \|*  
*bāhyānāṃ nāgarāṇāṃ ca sthānaṃ jātaṃ mahattaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*putrapautrapravṛddhānāṃ dauhitrāṇāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*camatkārapurasyāgre yajjñātaṃ vidyayā dhanaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kasyacittvatha kālasya viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*śaptā sarasvatī kopātkṛtā rudhiravāhinī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃsevyate hṛṣṭai rākṣasaiḥ sā divāniśam \|*  
*gītanṛtyaparaiścānyairbhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ piśācakaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tataste nāgarā bāhyāstāṃ tyaktvā dūrataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*kāṃdiśīkāstato yātā bhakṣyamāṇāstu rākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*narmadāyāstaṭe puṇye mārkaṇḍāśramasaṃnidhau \|\| 5 \|\|*

Note: (vv. 7-8ff) The story of the curse of Sarasvatī is taken from Mahābhārata, Śalya. 42. 38-39. But it was not Prācī Sarasvatī but Sarasvatī in Kurukṣetra area which was cursed.

Sūta said:

1-5. Ever since then on the splendid and auspicious banks of Sarasvatī, a great holy spot of persons outside Nāgaras took shape, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

They flourished with sons, daughters and grandsons ahead of Camatkārapura and it became well-known through learning and riches.

Once upon a time Sarasvatī was angrily cursed by the intelligent Viśvāmitra and was made to flow with blood.

Thenceforth, it is resorted to by delighted Rākṣasas day and night, and also by Bhūtas, Pretas and Piśācas engaged in singing and dancing.

## \|\| 1.165.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmātsarasvatī śaptā viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*mahānadyā ko'parādhastayā tasya vinirmitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:

6\. Why was Sarasvatī cursed by the intelligent Viśvāmitra? What offence was committed against him by the great river?

## \|\| 1.165.7-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsītpurā mahadvairaṃ viśvāmitravasiṣṭhayoḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇyasya kṛte viprāḥ prāṇāntakaraṇaṃ mahat \|*  
*sa sarvairbrāhmaṇaiḥ prokto viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṣatriyo'pi puraskṛtya devadevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*na caikena vasiṣṭhena tenaitadvairamāhitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

7-8. Formerly, there arose a great enmity between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha for the sake of Brāhmaṇahood, O Brāhmaṇas. The great enmity was deadly.

Viśvāmitra, the great sage, was called a Brāhmaṇa by all though he was a Kṣatriya. This they did keeping Pitāmaha, the Lord of Devas, at the head. Vasiṣṭha alone did not do so. Hence this enmity grew up.

## \|\| 1.165.9-10 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyo'pi kathaṃ vipro viśvā mitro mahāmate \|*  
*vasiṣṭhena kathaṃ nokto yaḥ prokto brahmaṇā svayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*etannaḥ sarvamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ sthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

The sages said:

9-10. O highly intelligent one, how was Viśvāmitra a Bṛāhmaṇa, though he was really a Kṣatriya? How was it that he was not (called so by Vasiṣṭha, though he was called so by Brahmā himself?) Narrate this entirely to us. We have great curiosity.

## \|\| 1.165.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsītpurā ṛcīkākhyo bhṛguputro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*vratādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sutapasvī mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. Formerly, there was a great sage named Ṛcīka. He was son of Bhṛgu. He was a regular observer of holy vows and engaged in regular study of the Vedas. He was highly renowned as an excellent ascetic.

## \|\| 1.165.12 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena sa kadācinmunīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ bhojakaṭaṃ nāma prāpto gādhimahīpateḥ \|*  
*yatra sā kauśikīnāma nadī trailokyaviśrutā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By way of pilgrimage that leading sage once reached the holy spot named Bhojakaṭa. It was in the dominion of King Gādhi. It was there that the river named Kauśikī flowed. It is well known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.165.13 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snātvā dvijaśreṣṭho yāvattiṣṭhati tīragaḥ \|*  
*samādhistho japaṃ kurvansaṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The excellent Brāhmaṇa took his holy bath there. He offered oblations to the Pitṛs and Devatās. Then he stationed himself on its banks performing Japa and meditating.

## \|\| 1.165.14 \|\|

*tāvattatra samāyātā rājakanyā suśobhanā \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇā sarvaireva guṇairyutā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By that time the splendid princess came there. She was fully endowed with all characteristic features and all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.165.15 \|\|

*sa tāṃ saṃvīkṣate yāvatsarvāvayavaśobhanām \|*  
*tāvatkāmaśarairvyāptaḥ kartavyaṃ nābhyaviṃdata \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hardly had he espied that girl, splendid in every limb, when he was fully overwhelmed by the arrows of Kāma. He was at a loss to know what he should do.

## \|\| 1.165.16-17 \|\|

*tataḥ papraccha lokānsa labdhvā kṛcchreṇa cetanām \|*  
*kasyeyaṃ kanyakā sādhvī kimarthamiha cāgatā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kva yāsyati varārohā sarvaṃ me kathyatāṃ janāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Regaining his balance of mind with very great difficulty, he asked the people: “Whose daughter is this excellent maiden? Why has she come here? Where will this exquisite girl go? Let everything be told to me, O people.”

## \|\| 1.165.18 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*eṣā gādhisutānāma khyātā trailokyasundarī \|*  
*antaḥpurātsamāyātā gaurīpūjanalālasā \|\| 18 \|\|*

The people said:

18\. This is the daughter of Gādhi, well-known by the name Trailokyasundarī.{GL\_NOTE::} Desirous of performing the worship of Gaurī, she has come here from the palace.

## \|\| 1.165.19 \|\|

*vāṃchamānā subharttāraṃ sarvaiḥ samuditaṃguṇaiḥ \|*  
*prāsādo'yaṃ sthito yo'tra nadītīre bṛhattaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. She covets an excellent husband having the full complement of all good qualities. Yonder you see a very huge palace situated on the banks of the river.

## \|\| 1.165.20 \|\|

*umā saṃtiṣṭhate cātra sarvaiḥ saṃpūjitā suraiḥ \|*  
*etāṃ ca snāpayitveyaṃ pūjayitvā yathā kramam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Umā is present here and is adored by all the Suras. This maiden has bathed the image of the goddess and has concluded the adoration duly.

## \|\| 1.165.21 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ vividhaṃ dattvā kariṣyati tataḥ param \|*  
*vīṇāvinodamātraṃ ca śrutimārgasukhāvaham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After making different kinds of food offerings she will amuse herself of playing on the lute delighting the ears (of the listeners).

## \|\| 1.165.22 \|\|

*tato yāsyati harmyaṃ svaṃ mandībhūte ca bhāskare \|*  
*ṛcīkastu tadākarṇya lokānāṃ vacanaṃ ca yat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter, she will go back to the palace when the sun becomes less bright.

Ṛcīka was moved much on hearing the words of the people.

## \|\| 1.165.23 \|\|

*yayau gādhigṛhaṃ śīghraṃ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā prāptamṛcīkaṃ bhṛgu sattamam \|*  
*saṃmukhaḥ prayayau tūrṇaṃ gādhiḥ pārthivasattamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He was afflicted by the arrows of Kāma and so hastened to the abode of Gādhi. On noticing that Ṛcīka, the most excellent one among the descendants of Bhṛgu, had come all of a sudden, Gādhi, the most excellent one among kings, hurried to him to receive him directly.

## \|\| 1.165.24 \|\|

*gṛhyoktena vidhānena kṛtvā caivārhaṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After paying him obeisance in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Gṛhya Sūtras, he stood with palms joined in reverence and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.165.25 \|\|

*niḥspṛhasyāpi te vipra kimāgamanakāraṇam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva yena yacchāmi te'khilam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O Brāhmaṇa, it is certain that you are free from desires. What may be the purpose of your visit? Do tell me entirely so that I shall give you everything.”

## \|\| 1.165.26 \|\|

*ṛcīka uvāca \|*  
*tava kanyā'sti vipreṃdra varārhā varavarṇinī \|*  
*brāhmoktena vivāhena tāṃ me dehi mahīpate \|\| 26 \|\|*

Ṛcīka said:

26\. O eminent king, haven't you a daughter of excellent complexion, befitting a good bridegroom? O king, do give her to me in accordance with the Brahma mode of marriage.

## \|\| 1.165.27 \|\|

*etadarthamahaṃ prāpto gṛhe tava smarārditaḥ \|*  
*sā mayā vīkṣitā rājangaurīpūjārthamāgatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is for this purpose that I have come to your abode. I am tormented by Smara (god of Love). O king, I have already seen her when she came out for the sake of the adoration of Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.165.28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhayasaṃtrasto gādhiḥ pārthivasattamaḥ \|*  
*asavarṇaṃ ca taṃ matvā daridraṃ vṛddhamevaca \|*  
*adāne śāpabhītastu tato vyājamuvāca saḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sūta said:

28\. On hearing those words, the excellent king hesitated in view of his belonging to a different caste. Besides he was very old and poor. In openly refusing him he was afraid of being cursed by him and so spoke thus trying to make an excuse.

## \|\| 1.165.29 \|\|

*asmākaṃ kanyakādāne śulkamasti dvijottama \|*  
*taccedyacchasi kanyāṃ tāṃ tubhyaṃ dāsyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, among us there is the practice of offering a fee when asking for a girl in marriage. If you are able to offer the requisite fee I shall undoubtedly give her to you.”

## \|\| 1.165.30 \|\|

*ṛcīka uvāca \|*  
*brūhi pārthivaśārdūla kanyāśulkaṃ mama drutam \|*  
*yena yacchāmi te sarvaṃ yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 30 \|\|*

Ṛcīka said:

30\. O tiger among kings, tell me quickly what you intend to have, by way of the requisite dowry so that I can readily offer it to you even if it happens to be very rare.

## \|\| 1.165.31-32 \|\|

*gādhiruvāca \|*  
*ekataḥ śyāmakarṇānāmaśvānāṃ vātaraṃhasām \|*  
*śatāni sapta vipreṃdra śvetānāṃ caiva sarvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ya ānīya pradadyānme tasmai kanyāṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

Gādhi said:

31-32. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, I demand seven hundred horses having the speed of wind. They shall be white in colour but the ears on one side shall be black. Whoever brings them and gives them to me, I shall give the daughter unto him.

## \|\| 1.165.33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya ṛcīko munisattamaḥ \|*  
*kānyakubjaṃ samāsādya gaṃgātīre viveśa ha \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sūta said:

33\. The excellent sage Ṛcīka promised, “It shall be so". He went to Kānyakubja and settled on the banks of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.165.34 \|\|

*aśvo voḍheti yatsūktaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭisamudbhavam \|*  
*chaṃdaṛṣidevatāyuktaṃ japaṃ cakre tataḥ param \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thereafter he performed the Japa of the Sūkta among the famous sixty-four Sūktas beginning with aśvo voḍha (RV IX.112.4) proclaiming the Chandas, the names of the deities and the sages.

## \|\| 1.165.35 \|\|

*viniyogaṃ vājikṛtaṃ gādhinā yatprakīrtitam \|*  
*tataste vājinastasmānniṣkrāṃtāḥ salilāddvijāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The application was for the sake of horses as demanded by Gādhi. Thereupon, O Brāhmaṇas, those horses rose up from the water.

## \|\| 1.165.36 \|\|

*sarvaśvetāḥ suvegāśca śyāmaikaśravaṇāstathā \|*  
*śatāni saptasaṃkhyāni tāvatsaṃkhyai rnaraiyutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. They were completely white. They had great speed. One of the ears was black. There were seven hundred of them with as many men incharge of them.

## \|\| 1.165.37 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti vikhyātamaśvatīrthaṃ dharātale \|*  
*gaṃgātīre śubhe puṇye kānyakubjasamīpagam \|*  
*yasminsnāne kṛte martyo vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Ever since then it became well-known all over the world as Aśvatīrtha. It is on the sacred and splendid banks of Gaṅgā, very near Kānyakubja. A man who takes his holy bath there shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## Chapter 166 - Birth of Paraśurāma

## \|\| 1.166.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ṛcīko'pi samādāya puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ \|*  
*tānaśvānprajagāmātha yatra gādhirvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasmai nivedayāmāsa kanyārthaṃ tānhayottamān \|*  
*gādhistu tānpragṛhyātha yogyānvājimakhasya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ekaikaṃ paramaṃ teṣāṃ sa jagāmātha pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tatastāṃ pradadau tasmai kanyāṃ trailokyasundarīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

*viprāgnisākṣisaṃbhūtāṃ gṛhyoktavidhinā nvitaḥ \|*  
*tato vivāhe nirvṛtta ṛcīko munisattamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ saṃveśane caiva niṣkāmaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*athābravīnnijāṃ bhāryāṃ niṣkāmaḥ saṃsthito muniḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-5. Ṛcīka took those horses along with the obedient men incharge and went to the place where Gādhi was present.

He offered those excellent horses to the king for the sake of the maiden. Gādhi took them as they were worthy of horse-sacrifice. Each of them surpassed the other and the king derived great pleasure.

Thereupon, he gave his daughter Trailokyasundarī to him in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Gṛhyasūtras. He gave the daughter in marriage in which the Fire-god and Brāhmaṇas were the witnesses.

But after the formal rite of marriage had been concluded, Ṛcīka, the excellent sage, became uninterested in cohabitation with her.

The sage without passionate attachment spoke to his wife:

## \|\| 1.166.6 \|\|

*ahaṃ yāsyāmi suśroṇi kānanaṃ tapasaḥ kṛte \|*  
*tvaṃ prārthaya varaṃ kaṃcidyenābhīṣṭaṃ dadāmi te \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “O lady of excellent buttocks, I am going to the forest for performing penance. Do request for some boon, so that I can give you what is desired by you.”

## \|\| 1.166.7 \|\|

*sā śrutvā tasya tadvākyaṃ niṣkāmasya prajalpitam \|*  
*vāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā jagāma jananīṃ prati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing the words uttered without any sexual attachment, she became distressed. With eyes filled with tears, she went to her mother.

## \|\| 1.166.8 \|\|

*provāca vacanaṃ tasya sā niṣkāmapate stadā \|*  
*varadānaṃ tathā tena yathoktaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas! She told her about the words of her husband who had no sexual desire but who offered her a boon.

## \|\| 1.166.9 \|\|

*atha śrutvaiva sā mātā yathā tajjalpitaṃ tayā \|*  
*sutayā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāstato vacanamabravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on hearing the words uttered by her daughter, the mother spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.166.10-11 \|\|

*yadyayaṃ putri te bhartā varaṃ yacchati vāṃchitam \|*  
*tatprārthaya sutaṃ tasmādbrāhmaṇyena samanvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*madarthaṃ caikaputraṃ ca niḥśeṣakṣāttratejasā \|*  
*saṃyuktaṃ yācaya śubhe viputrā'haṃ yataḥ sthitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. “O my daughter, if this husband of yours is giving whatever is desired by you as boon unto you, then request for a son endowed with Brāhmaṇical virtues.

O splendid girl, on my behalf also request for a son full of the refulgence of a Kṣatriya, since I have been without a son so long.”

## \|\| 1.166.12 \|\|

*sā śrutvā jananīvākyamṛcīkaṃ prāpya suvratā \|*  
*abravījjananī vākyaṃ sarvaṃ vistarato dvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing the words of her mother, the maiden of excellent holy vows went to Ṛcīka and told him what had been mentioned by her mother in full details.

## \|\| 1.166.13 \|\|

*sa tasyāśca vacaḥ śrutvā cakārātha carudvayam \|*  
*putreṣṭiṃ vidhivatkṛtvā namaskṛtya svayaṃbhuvam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing her words, he duly performed Putreṣṭi sacrifice, bowed down to the Self-born Lord and prepared two Cams.

## \|\| 1.166.14 \|\|

*ekasminyojayāmāsa brāhmyaṃ tejo'khilaṃ ca saḥ \|*  
*kṣātraṃ tejastathānyasminsakalaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One of the Carus (Consecrated food offering) he charged with all Brāhmaṇical radiance in one and the other with the refulgence pertaining to Kṣatriyas, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.166.15-16 \|\|

*bhāryāyai pradadau pūrvaṃ brāhmyaṃ ca carumutta mam \|*  
*abravītprāśayitvainamaśvatthāliṃganaṃ kuru \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tataḥ prāpsyasi satputraṃ brāhmyatejaḥsamanvitam \|*  
*dvitīyaścaruko yaśca taṃ tvaṃ mātre nive daya \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He gave the former, the excellent Brāhmaṇical Caru, to his wife and told her, “Take this in and embrace an Aśvattha tree. Thereby you will get an excellent son endowed with Brāhmaṇical radiance. Give unto your mother this second Caru.”

## \|\| 1.166.17-18 \|\|

*abravīcca tatastāṃ tu ṛcīko munisattamaḥ \|*  
*tvamenaṃ carukaṃ prāśya nyagrodhāliṃganaṃ kuru \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tataḥ prāpsyasi satputraṃ saṃyuktaṃ kṣātratejasā \|*  
*niḥśeṣeṇa mahābhāge na me syādvacanaṃ vṛthā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Then the excellent sage Ṛcīka spoke to her (the mother): “Do eat this Caru and embrace a Nyagrodha tree. Thereby you will get an excellent son endowed with the entire radiance of Kṣatriya, O highly esteemed one, my words cannot be futile.”

## \|\| 1.166.19 \|\|

*evamuktvā ṛcīkastu sa visṛjya ca tejasī \|*  
*suhṛṣṭo brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaḥ svayaṃ ca mahito'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After saying thus, Ṛcīka joyously charged with two types of refulgence. The excellent Brāhmaṇa was in a happy (euphoric) mood.

## \|\| 1.166.20 \|\|

*te caiva tu gṛhe gatvā prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*ūcatuśca mithaste ca satyametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They returned home in a highly delighted mood. They spoke to each other, “It will certainly take place.”

## \|\| 1.166.21-24 \|\|

*tato mātā sutāṃ prāha ātmārthe sakalo janaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣaṃ kurute kṛtye sāmānye ca vyavasthite \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tattavārthaṃ kṛto'nena yaścaruścārulocane \|*  
*yastasminvihito'nena mantragrāmo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa mahābhāge satyametanmayoditam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasmācca carukaṃ mahyaṃ tvaṃ gṛhāṇa śucismite \|*  
*ātmīyaṃ mama yacchasva vṛkṣābhyāṃ ca viparyayaḥ \|*  
*kriyatāṃ ca mahābhāge yena me syātsutottamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rājyakarmaṇi dakṣaśca śūraḥ parabalārdanaḥ \|*  
*tvadīyo dvijamātro'pi tava tuṣṭiṃ kariṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. Then the mother said to the daughter: “When the work on hand is common, it is the practice of all people to do something special.

O lady of excellent eyes, he would have certainly charged a group of Mantras into the Caru that was prepared for you. O highly esteemed one, it is the truth that has been uttered by me.

Hence, O lady of splendid smiles, take my Caru and give yours to me. Let there be alteration in the matter of embracing the trees too. O highly esteemed lady, thereby an excellent son will be born to me.

He will be an expert in the administration of the kingdom. He will be a hero capable of suppressing the army of enemies. Your son shall certainly delight you though he may be only a Brāhmaṇa.”

## \|\| 1.166.25 \|\|

*atha sā vijane proktā tayā mātrā yaśasvinī \|*  
*akarodvyatyayaṃ vṛkṣe carau ca dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On being told thus in secret by her mother, the lady of great renown interchanged the Carus and the trees, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.166.26 \|\|

*tataḥ puṃsa vane snāte te śubhe cārulocane \|*  
*dadhāte garbhamevātha bhartuḥ saṃyogataḥ kṣaṇāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the course of the Puṃsavana rite both the ladies of charming eyes had their holy baths and conceived instantly by the intimate contact with the husband.

## \|\| 1.166.27 \|\|

*tatastu garbhamāsādya sā ca trailokyasundarī \|*  
*kṣāttreṇa tejasā yuktā tatkṣaṇātsamapadyata \|*  
*mano rājye tataścakre hastyaśvārohaṇodbhave \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After the conception Trailokyasundarī (Satyavatī) became instantly endowed with the refulgence special to Kṣatriyas. She began to think mentally of kingdoms, riding on elephants and horses and the like.

## \|\| 1.166.28 \|\|

*yuddhavārttāstathā cakre devāsuragaṇodbhavāḥ \|*  
*śṛṇoti ca tathā nityaṃ vilāseṣu mano dadhe \|*  
*anuṣṭhānaṃ tataścakre manorājyasamudbhavam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Stories regarding the battles between the hosts of Devas and Asuras were discussed and listened to and the mind was directed towards enjoyment. She put into practice many of her mental plans.

## \|\| 1.166.29 \|\|

*piturgṛhātsamānīya jātyānaśvāṃstathā gajān \|*  
*raktāni caiva vastrāṇi kāśmīrādyaṃ vilepanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. She caused excellent horses and elephants to be fetched from her father’s house. Red garments and (saffron) unguents from Kāśmīra and other things too were brought.

## \|\| 1.166.30 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā ceṣṭitaṃ tasyā rājyārhaṃ bahubhogadhṛk \|*  
*brāhmaṇārhaiḥ parityaktaṃ samācāraiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Ṛcīka noticed the various activities of his wife befitting regal status and the enjoyment of diverse kinds of pleasures. She totally eschewed activities and behaviour worthy of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.166.31-38 \|\|

*abravīcca tataḥ kruddho dhikpāpe kimidaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*vyatyayo vihito nūnaṃ carukasya nagasya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tvayā pāpe prapaśyāmi yenedṛktava ceṣṭitam \|*  
*kṣatriyārhaṃ dvijācāraiḥ sakalaiḥ parivarjitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*cīravalkalasaṃtyaktaṃ snānajāpyavivarjitam \|*  
*saṃyuktaṃ vividhairgandhairmṛganābhipuraḥsaraiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tava mātā śamasthā sā japahomaparāyaṇā \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparā caiva vedaśravaṇalālasā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmātte kṣatriyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mātuśca brāhmaṇaśreṣṭho brahmacaryakathāparaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sutaścihnairgarbhalakṣaṇasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yasmādudīritaḥ pūrvaṃ śloko'yaṃ śāstracintakaiḥ \|*  
*yādṛśā dohadāḥ santi sagarbhāṇāṃ ca yoṣitām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tādṛgeva svabhāvena tāsāṃ putro'tra jāyate \|*  
*saivamuktā bhayatrastā vepamānā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

31-38. Thereupon, he angrily spoke: “O sinful lady, fie upon you! What has been committed? Certainly interchange of the Carus and the trees has been committed by you.

O sinful lady, I do see that your activities are like these due to that. These activities suit Kṣatriyas. They are avoided in all the activities of Brāhmaṇas.

Bark garments are abandoned. You perform neither holy bath nor Japa. Various kinds of scents such as musk are used (by you). On the other hand your mother is tranquil and quiescent. She is devoted to Japa and Homa and is inclined towards pilgrimage and listening to Vedic Chants. Hence, there is no doubt about it that your son will be a Kṣatriya.

From the characteristic features of the pregnancy, it is certain that an excellent Brāhmaṇa devoted to propagation and practice of celibacy will be born to your mother.

Formerly this was said by the expounders of scriptural texts: ‘The innate quality of the sons of young women in pregnancy will be in conformity with their longings and inclinations (of the mother) at that time.’

On being told thus, she trembled much in her great fright. She remained standing with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.166.39-40 \|\|

*bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*satyametatprabho vākyaṃ yattvayā samudāhṛtam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*atītānāgataṃ vetti vinā liṃgairbhavāniha \|*  
*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yathā syādbrāhmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyasya tu putrasya bhavānnārhaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. With tears filling her eyes, the distressed maiden spoke these words: “O holy lord, the words spoken by you are true. Without the help of (telltale) signs, you can (directly) know the past and future. Hence, do me this favour of making my son a Brāhmaṇa. A Kṣatriya son does not befit you.”

## \|\| 1.166.41 \|\|

*ṛcīka uvāca \|*  
*yatkiṃcidbrahmatejaḥ syāttannyastaṃ te carau mayā \|*  
*kṣāttraṃ tejaśca te māturvyatyayaṃ ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*karomi vādhamo loke śāstra sya ca vyatikramam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Ṛcīka said:

41\. Whatever Brāhmaṇical refulgence there was had been deposited by me in the Caru intended for you and the regal refulgence in that intended for your mother. If I were to cause any change in this, I will be transgressing the scriptural injunction.

## \|\| 1.166.42-43 \|\|

*patnyuvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ bhṛguśārdūla mama pautro'tra yo bhavet \|*  
*kṣāttraṃ tejo'khilaṃ tasya gātre bhūyā ttvayā'hṛtam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*putrastu brāhmaṇaśreṣṭho bhūyādabhyadhikastava \|\| 43 \|\|*

The wife said:

42-43. If it is so, O tiger among the descendants of Bhṛgu, let there be the entire Kṣatriya refulgence caused by you manifested in my grandson to be. Let the son be an excellent Brāhmaṇa even excelling you.

## \|\| 1.166.44 \|\|

*ṛcīka uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu madvākyātputraste brāhmaṇaḥ śubhe \|*  
*pautraḥ sudurddharaḥ saṃkhye saṃyuktaḥ kṣāttratejasā \|\| 44 \|\|*

Ṛcīka said:

44\. O splendid lady, let it be so. At my instance, your son will be a Brāhmaṇa and the grandson, an irresistible one in battle. He will be equipped with the radiance special to Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 1.166.45 \|\|

*tataḥ satyaṃ varaṃ labdhvā prasannavadanā satī \|*  
*māturnivedayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ kāṃta jalpitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On obtaining the truthful boon, the chaste lady was delighted with the face beaming fully. She told her mother what was stated by her husband.

## \|\| 1.166.46 \|\|

*tataḥ sā daśame māsi saṃprāpte gurudaivate \|*  
*nakṣatre janayāmāsa putraṃ bālārkasannibham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then, in the tenth month, in the constellation Puṣya (the constellation with Brahspati \[Bṛhaspati?\] as the deity) she gave birth to a son on a par with the rising Sun.

## \|\| 1.166.47 \|\|

*brāhmyā lakṣmyā samopetaṃ nidhānaṃ tapasāṃ śuci \|*  
*jamadagniriti khyāto yo'sau trailokyaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya putrobhavatkhyāto rāmonāma mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He was endowed with the Brāhmaṇical glory. He was clean, a storehouse of austerities. He was well-known in all the three worlds as Jamadagni. His son became well known by the name Rāma.

## \|\| 1.166.48 \|\|

*ekaviṃśatidā yena dharā niḥkṣatriyā kṛtā \|*  
*kṣāttratejaḥprabhāvena pitāmahaprasādataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. It was by him that the earth was rid of Kṣatriyas twenty-one times, thanks to the favour of Pitāmaha and the power of the radiance pertaining to Kṣatriyas.

## Chapter 167 - Viśvāmitra Renounces Kingdom

## \|\| 1.167.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gādhestu yā'tha patnī ca prāśanāccaru kasya vai \|*  
*sāpi garbhaṃ dadhe tatra vāsare mantrataḥ śubhā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sā ca garbhasamopetā yadā jātā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparā sādhvī jātā vrataparāyaṇā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vedadhvanirbhavedyatra tatra harṣasamanvitā \|*  
*pulakāṃcitasarvāṃgī sā śuśrāva ca sarvadā \|*  
*tyaktvā rājyocitānsarvānalaṃkārānsukhāni ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. By taking in the Caru and as a result of the Mantras, Gādhi’s auspicious wife conceived during those days.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when the splendid lady became pregnant she became interested in pilgrimage. The chaste lady was highly devoted to holy Vratas.

Whereever the sound of Vedic chanting arose she became delighted and experienced horripilation in all her limbs. She always listened to it eagerly even ignoring all the ornaments and embellishments pertaining to the royal status and the happiness therefrom.

## \|\| 1.167.4 \|\|

*atha sāpi dvijaśreṣṭhā daśame māsi saṃsthite \|*  
*suṣuve suprabhaṃ putraṃ brāhmyā lakṣmyā samāvṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when the tenth month arrived she gave birth to a lustrous son endowed with Brāhmaṇical glory and radiance.

## \|\| 1.167.5 \|\|

*viśvāmitrastathā khyātastrailokye sacarā care \|*  
*vavṛdhe sa mahābhāgo nityamevādhikaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He became well-known as Viśvāmitra in all the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings. That highly esteemed one grew up day by day surpassing all men.

## \|\| 1.167.6 \|\|

*śuklapakṣaṃ samāsādya tārāpatirivāṃbare \|*  
*yadāsau yauvanopetaḥ saṃjāto dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He grew up like the moon in the bright half of a month in the sky and attained the prime of youth, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.167.7 \|\|

*rājyakṣamastadā rājye gādhinā sa niyojitaḥ \|*  
*anicchamānaḥ svaṃ rājyaṃ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was considered capable of looking after the kingdom and was appointed to rule over the realm of his ancestors but he was unwilling.

## \|\| 1.167.8 \|\|

*vedādhyayanasaṃpanno nityaṃ ca paṭhate hi saḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇocitamārgeṇa gacchamāno divāniśam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He proceeded ahead in the path that befitted Brāhmaṇas. He showed much inclination for Vedic study and he recited the Vedas everyday:

## \|\| 1.167.9 \|\|

*saṃsthāpyātha sutaṃ rājye babhūva vanagocaraḥ \|*  
*sakalatro mahābhāgo vānaprasthāśrame rataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Gādhi crowned his son in the kingdom and went to the forest. The highly esteemed one entered the stage of life of a forest-dweller along with his wife.

## \|\| 1.167.10 \|\|

*viśvāmitro'pi rājyastho dvijasaṃpūjane rataḥ \|*  
*dvijaiḥ sarvaiścacārātha snānajāpyaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Though crowned as king, Viśvāmitra was more devoted to the adoration of Brāhmaṇas. He moved about in the company of Brāhmaṇas and engaged himself in holy ablution and performance of Japas.

## \|\| 1.167.11 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya pāparddhiṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*praviveśa vanaṃ raudraṃ nānāmṛgasamākulam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Once he became inclined for Pāpardhi (hunting wild animals) and entered a terrible forest infested with different kinds of beasts.

## \|\| 1.167.12-13 \|\|

*jaghāna sa vane tatra varāhānsaṃbarāngajān \|*  
*tarakṣāṃśca rurūnkhaḍgānāraṇyānmahiṣāṃstathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*siṃhānvyāghrānmahāsarpāñcharabhāṃśca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mṛgayāsaktacittaḥ sa bhramamāṇo mahāvane \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. He was urged by a desire to chase, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in the course of his wandering in the great forest, and killed boars, Saṃbara deer, elephants, bears, Ruru deer, rhinoceros, wild buffalos, lions, tigers, huge pythons and Śarabhas.

## \|\| 1.167.14-15 \|\|

*madhyāhnasamaye prāpte vṛṣasthe ca divākare \|*  
*kṣutpipāsāpariśrāṃto viśvāmitro dvijottamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āsasādāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭho'pi samālokya viśvāmitraṃ nṛpo ttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The sun was in the zodiac Taurus and the time was mid-day, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Viśvāmitra became utterly weary due to hunger and thirst. He reached the sacred hermitage of the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha who received the excellent king Viśvāmitra.

## \|\| 1.167.16 \|\|

*nijāśrame tu saṃprāptaṃ sānandaṃ sammukho yayau \|*  
*dattvā tasmai tadārghyaṃ ca madhuparkaṃ ca bhūbhuje \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. With great joy, he met the king directly (lit. face to face). As he entered the hermitage the sage offered him Arghya and Madhuparka.

## \|\| 1.167.17 \|\|

*abravīcca tato vākyaṃ svāgataṃ te mahīpate \|*  
*vada kṛtyaṃ karomyeva gṛhāyātasya yacca te \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He spoke: “Welcome unto you, O king. Do tell me what I can do unto you who have come to my abode.”

## \|\| 1.167.18 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*mṛgayāyāṃ pariśrāṃtaḥ pipāsāvyākulendriyaḥ \|*  
*pānārthamiha saṃprāpta āśrame te munīśvara \|\| 18 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

18\. O great sage, I became too tired after hunting. All my sense-organs are upset due to thirst. I came to your hermitage for the sake of drinking water.

## \|\| 1.167.19 \|\|

*tatpītaṃ śītalaṃ toyaṃ vitṛṣṇo'haṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*anujñāṃ dehi me brahmanyena gacchāmi maṃdiram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Cool water has been drunk and I have quenched my thirst. O holy Brāhmaṇa, permit me to go back to the palace.

## \|\| 1.167.20 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*madhyāhna samayo raudraḥ sūryo'tīva sutāpadaḥ \|*  
*tatkṛtvā bhojanaṃ rājannaparāhṇe vyavasthite \|*  
*gantāsi nijamāvāsaṃ bhuktvānnaṃ mama cāśrame \|\| 20 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

20\. O king, this is the terrible time of midday. The sun is greatly scorching. Take your food and go back to your residence in the afternoon. Do take in food (cooked rice) in my hermitage.

## \|\| 1.167.21-23 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*caturaṃgeṇa sainyena mṛgayāmahamāgataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tavāśramasya dvārasthaṃ mama sainyaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*bubhukṣiteṣu bhṛtyeṣu yaḥ svāmī kurute'śanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tyajyate ca guṇairdrutam \|*  
*tasmādājñāpaya kṣipraṃ māṃ mune svagṛhāya bhoḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

The king said:

21-23. I have come for hunting with the full complement of the four divisions of my army. They are left at the entrance of your penance-grove. If the master takes food even as the servants are hungry, he soon falls into terrible hell bereft of all good qualities. Hence, O sage, allow me to go back home.

## \|\| 1.167.24 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*yadi te sevakāḥ saṃti dvāradeśe bubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*sarvānihānaya kṣipraṃ tṛptiṃ neṣyāmyahaṃ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

24\. If your attendants are at the gateway and are hungry, summon them all quickly hither. I shall make them satisfied.

## \|\| 1.167.25 \|\|

*asti me nandinīnāma kāmadhenuḥ suśobhanā \|*  
*vāṃchitaṃ yacchate sarvaṃ tapasā pārthivottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent king, I have a splendid cow named Nandinī acquired by means of my penance. It gives me whatever I desire.

## \|\| 1.167.26 \|\|

*tṛptiṃ neṣyati te sarvaṃ sainyaṃ pārthivasattama \|*  
*tasmādānīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ paśya me dhenujaṃ phalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O excellent King, it will satisfy the entire army of yours. Let them be fetched here and you can witness the gift of my cow.

## \|\| 1.167.27-28 \|\|

*tacchrutvā cānayāmāsa sarvaṃ sainyaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*snātaśca kṛtajapyaśca santarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānvācayitvā ca siṃhāsanasamāśritaḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare dhenuḥ samāhūtā ca naṃdinī \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. On hearing it, the king summoned the entire host. He took his bath and offered libations to the Pitṛs and Devatās. Then he performed Japa. After making the Brāhmaṇas chant the Vedic passages, he took his rest on a throne-like seat. In the meantime the cow Nandinī was called in.

## \|\| 1.167.29 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhena samāhūtā viśvāmitrapuraḥsthitā \|*  
*abravīcca tatā vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhamṛṣi sattamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On being summoned by Vasiṣṭha, she came and stood before Viśvāmitra. Then she spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha, the excellent sage.

## \|\| 1.167.30 \|\|

*ādeśo dīyatāṃ mahyaṃ kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “May I be commanded. What shall I do? Order me.”

## \|\| 1.167.31 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*pādaprakṣālanādyaṃ tu kuruṣva vacanānmama \|*  
*viśvāmitrasya rājarṣeryāvadbhojanasaṃsthitim \|\| 31 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

31\. At my instance carry out everything pertaining to the washing of the feet and the like in regard to the saintly king Viśvāmitra. Do manage everything including the preparation of the food.

## \|\| 1.167.32 \|\|

*khādyaiḥ sarvaistathā lehyaiścoṣyaiḥ peyaiḥ pṛthavidhaiḥ \|*  
*kuruṣva tṛptiparyantaṃ sasainyasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*aśvānāṃ ca gajānāṃ ca ghāsādibhiryathākramam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Fully satisfy the king and the army with all types of food—lambatives, drinks of diverse kinds and things that can be sucked. Let the horses and elephants be rendered satisfied with grass etc. duly.

## \|\| 1.167.33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva sāpyuktvā tatastatsasṛje kṣaṇāt \|*  
*yatproktaṃ tena muninā bhṛtyānāṃ cāyutaṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sūta said:

33\. “Yes as per your order”, said the cow and in a moment created whatever was called for by the sage to cater food to the ten thousand (soldiers of the king).

## \|\| 1.167.34 \|\|

*tataste sarvamādāya bhṛtyā bhojyaṃ dadustathā \|*  
*ekaikasya pṛthaktvena pratipattipuraḥsaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those attendants served the food to each of the guests severally, with great solicitude.

## \|\| 1.167.35 \|\|

*evaṃ tayā kṣaṇenaiva tṛptiṃ nīto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*sasainyaḥ saparīvāro gajoṣṭrāśvairvṛṣaiḥ saha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus the cow rendered the king and his attendants fully satisfied, along with the soldiers, elephants, camels, horses and bullocks.

## \|\| 1.167.36 \|\|

*tatastu kautukaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*sāmātyo visma yāviṣṭo mantrayāmāsa ca dvijāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On watching such goings-on creating wonder and curiosity. King Viśvāmitra and his ministers were surprised, O Brāhmaṇas. They whispered to one another:

## \|\| 1.167.37 \|\|

*aho citramaho citraṃ yayā'kasmādvarūthinī \|*  
*tṛptiṃ nīteyamasmākaṃ kṣutpipāsāsamākulā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “Oh, how wonderful it is! How marvellous! Our entire army was overwhelmed with hunger and thirst! Now every member of it has been rendered satisfied by this cow.

## \|\| 1.167.38 \|\|

*tasmātsaṃnīyatāmeṣā svagṛhaṃ dhenuruttamā \|*  
*kiṃ kariṣyati vipro'yaṃ nirbhṛtyo vanasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Hence let this excellent cow be taken to our hometown. What can this Brāhmaṇa do? He is isolated in the forest. He has no servants of his own.”

## \|\| 1.167.39-40 \|\|

*tato vasiṣṭhamāhūya vākyametaduvāca saḥ \|*  
*naṃdinī dīyatāṃ mahyaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi cānayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tvameko vanasaṃsthastu nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ \|*  
*athavā tava dāsyāmi vyayārthe munisattama \|*  
*varāngrāmāṃśca hastyaśvānanyāṃścāpi yathepsitān \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Then he called Vasiṣṭha and spoke these words: “Let this Nandinī be given no me. What will you do with her? You are alone. You stay in forest. You are free from the mutually opposed passions. You don't require any possessions. Or, O excellent sage, if you have any expenses of your own I shall hand over to you excellent villages, elephants, houses and other desired things.”

## \|\| 1.167.41-42 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*homadhenuriyaṃ rājannasmākaṃ kāmadohinī \|*  
*adeyā gaurmahārāja sāmānyāpi dvijanmanām \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kiṃ punarnaṃdinī yaiṣā sarvakāmapradāyinī \|*  
*aparaṃ śṛṇu rājeṃdra smṛtivākyamanuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

41-42. O king, this cow is an adjunct to the Homa rites. Whatever we desire can be milked out of her. Further, O great king, even an ordinary cow cannot be given away by the twice-born ones. It is all the more so in the case of Nandinī who accords to me all that I desire? Listen to one thing more, O great king. There is this excellent statement in the Smṛti text.

## \|\| 1.167.43-44 \|\|

*gavāṃ hi vikrayārthe ca yaduktaṃ manunā svayam \|*  
*gavāṃ vikrayajaṃ vittaṃ yo gṛhṇāti dvijottamaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*antyajaḥ sa parijñeyo mātṛvikrayakārakaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnāhaṃ pradāsyāmi nandinīṃ tāṃ mahīpate \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. It is laid down by Manu himself in the context of the sale of cows:

"An excellent Brāhmaṇa who accepts cash proceeding from the sale of cows, should be considered an Antyaja (Śūdra). He is no better than the seller of his own mother.”

Hence, O king, I will not give you the cow Nandinī.”

## \|\| 1.167.45 \|\|

*na sāmnā naiva bhedena na dānena kathaṃcana \|*  
*na daṇḍena mahārāja tasmādgaccha nijālayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Neither through conciliatory pleadings, nor by threats, neither as an exchange for some gift nor by the punishment (i.e. force) meted out, will I give you the cow. Hence, do go back to your own abode.

## \|\| 1.167.46 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*yatkiṃcidvidyate ratnaṃ pārthivasya kṣitau dvija \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ rājakīyaṃ syāditi vittavido viduḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

46\. O Brāhmaṇa, persons conversant with monetary transactions are of this view that every jewel, excellent and valuable, that is on the earth belongs to the king.

## \|\| 1.167.47 \|\|

*ratnabhūtā tato dhenurmameyaṃ naṃdinī sthitā \|*  
*daṇḍenāpi grahīṣyāmi sāmnā yacchasi no yadi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This cow Nandinī is present here as a jewel belonging to me. If you do not part with her at my earnest request I will seize her meting out punishment to you.

## \|\| 1.167.48 \|\|

*evamuktvā vasiṣṭhaṃ sa viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*ādideśa tato bhṛtyānnadinīyaṃ pragṛhyatām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After saying thus to Vasiṣṭha, King Viśvāmitra commanded his servants. “Let this Nandinī be seized.”

## \|\| 1.167.49 \|\|

*atha sā bhṛtyavargeṇa nīyamānā ca naṃdinī \|*  
*hanyamānā prahāraiśca pāṣāṇairlakuṭairapi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The group of servants led Nandinī away. They even hit her with stones and sticks.

## \|\| 1.167.50 \|\|

*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā prahārairjarjarīkṛtā \|*  
*kṛcchrādupetya taṃ prāha vasiṣṭhaṃ munisattamam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The blows shattered the poor cow. Tears filled her eyes. With great difficulty she rushed towards Vasiṣtha, the excellent sage and said:

## \|\| 1.167.51 \|\|

*kiṃ dattāsmi muniśreṣṭha tvayāhaṃ cāsya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*yena māṃ kālayaṃtyasya puruṣāḥ svāmino yathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. “O excellent sage, have I been transferred to this king? His men dare to handle me like my masters.”

## \|\| 1.167.52 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*na tvāṃ yacchāmyahaṃ dheno prāṇatyāge'pi saṃsthite \|*  
*tadrakṣasva svayaṃ dheno ātmānaṃ matprabhāvataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

52\. O my dear cow, I will not give you away even if my death is imminent. So protect yourself, by my own power.

## \|\| 1.167.53 \|\|

*evamuktā tadā dhenurvasiṣṭhena mahātmanā \|*  
*kopāviṣṭā tataścakre huṃkārāndāruṇāṃstathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On being told thus by the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha, the cow became furious. She made gruff and dreadful hissing sounds.

## \|\| 1.167.54 \|\|

*tasyā huṃkāraśabdaiśca niṣkrāṃtāḥ sāyudhā narāḥ \|*  
*śabarāśca puliṃdāśca mlecchāḥ saṃkhyāvivarjitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. At the gruffing sound of the cow innumerable men, Śabaras, Mlecchas, Pulindas all equipped with arms came out.

## \|\| 1.167.55 \|\|

*taiśca bhṛtyā hatāḥ sarve viśvāmitrasyabhūpateḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kopābhibhūto'sau viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. All the servants of King Viśvāmitra were killed by them. Thereupon King Viśvāmitra was overcome with anger.

## \|\| 1.167.56 \|\|

*sajjaṃ kṛtvā svasainyaṃ tu caturaṃgaṃ prakopataḥ \|*  
*yuddhaṃ cakre ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ maraṇe kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. With great fury he got his army of four divisions ready to fight with them. He resolved even to die if needed.

## \|\| 1.167.57 \|\|

*atha te sainikā stasya te gajāste ca vājinaḥ \|*  
*paśyato nihatāḥ sarve puruṣairdhenusaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Even as he kept on watching them his soldiers, elephants and horses were killed in no time by the men created by the cow.

## \|\| 1.167.58-60 \|\|

*viśvāmitraṃ parityajya śeṣaṃ sarvaṃ nipātitam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā veṣṭitaṃ mlecchairyu dhyamānaṃ mahīpatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kṛpāṃ kṛtvā vasiṣṭhastu nandinīmidamabravīt \|*  
*rakṣa naṃdini bhūpālaṃ mlecchairetaiḥ samāvṛtam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*rājā hi yatnato rakṣyo yatprasādādidaṃ jagat \|*  
*sanmārge vartate sarvaṃ na cāmārge pravartate \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Barring Viśvāmitra everything else was struck. On noticing that though the king continued to fight he was pretty well surrounded by Mlecchas, Vasiṣṭha took pity on him and spoke to Nandinī thus: “O Nandinī, save the king encircled by these Mlecchas. The king should be assiduously protected. It is due to his favour that these all (people) abide by the path of the good and all desist from following the wrong path.”

## \|\| 1.167.61 \|\|

*tatastu naṃdinīṃ yāvanniṣedhayitumāgatām \|*  
*viśvāmitro'simudyamya prahartumupacakrame \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thereupon, Nandinī came there to dissuade (the Mlecchas etc.) when Viśvāmitra raised his sword and tried to strike (Nandinī) with it.

## \|\| 1.167.62 \|\|

*vasiṣṭho'pi samālokya vadhyamānāṃ ca tāṃ tadā \|*  
*bāhuṃ saṃstaṃbhayāmāsa khaḍgaṃ tasya ca bhūpateḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On seeing the cow about to be killed, Vasiṣṭha rendered the hand and the sword of the king motionless and benumbed.

## \|\| 1.167.63 \|\|

*atha vailakṣyamāpanno viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*provāca vrīḍayā yukto vasiṣṭhaṃ munisattamam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thereat King Viśvāmitra found himself discomfited. Overcome with shame, he spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages:

## \|\| 1.167.64-66 \|\|

*rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ muniśreṣṭha vadhyamānaṃ sudāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*mlecchaiḥ kuruṣva me bāhuṃ stambhena tu vivarjitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*mamāparādhātsaṃnaṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ sainyamanantakam \|*  
*tasmādyāsyāmyahaṃ harmyaṃ na yuddhena prayojanam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*durvinītaḥ śriyaṃ prāpya vidyāmaiśvaryameva ca \|*  
*na tiṣṭhati ciraṃ yuddhe yathāhaṃ madagarvitaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. “O excellent sage, save me who am about to be killed by the dreaded Mlecchas. Render my hand free from the benumbed state.

It is my fault (offence) that caused the destruction of my vast army. Hence I go back to my place. I have nothing to do with the battle.

A rude and impolite fellow cannot stand the rigour of a battle for long, though he may have won glory, learning and prosperity like me who have become haughty and arrogant.”

## \|\| 1.167.67 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamukto vasiṣṭhastu viśvāmitreṇa bhūbhujā \|*  
*cakāra taṃ bhujaṃ tasya staṃbhadoṣavivarjitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

Sūta said:

67\. On being appealed to thus by King Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha relieved that hand from the defect of numbness.

## \|\| 1.167.68-69 \|\|

*abravītprahasanvākyaṃ vidhāya sa śubhaṃ karam \|*  
*gaccha rājanvimukto'si staṃbhadoṣeṇa vai mayā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*mākārśīrbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ virodhaṃ bhūya eva hi \|*  
*anujñātaḥ sa tenātha viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. After making the hand excellent (free) he laughingly spoke these words: “O king, go alone. I have rid you of the fault of stupefaction. Do not come into clash and rivalry again with Brāhmaṇas.” Thus Viśvāmitra, the king, was allowed to go by him.

## \|\| 1.167.70 \|\|

*savrīḍaṃ prayayau harmyaṃ padbhyāmeva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*svapuradvāramāsādya sugupte rajanīmukhe \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he went to the palace bashfully on foot alone and reached the gate of his capital at nightfall when everything was shrouded in darkness.

## \|\| 1.167.71-73 \|\|

*pralāpamakarottatra bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dhigbalaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca dhigvīryaṃ dhikprajīvitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*ślāghyaṃ brahmabalaṃ caikaṃ brāhmyaṃ tejaśca kevalam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*etatkarma mayā kāryaṃ yathā syādbrahmajaṃ balam \|*  
*tyaktvā caiva nijaṃ rājyaṃ cariṣyāmi mahattapaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

71 -73. There he lamented with the eyes dimmed with tears: “Fie upon the strength of Kṣatriyas! Fie upon their vigour! Fie upon their very life! Praiseworthy is the power of Brāhmaṇas alone, their radiance alone. I have to do that whereby I will have the Brāhmaṇical power. Abandoning my kingdom, I will perform great penance.”

## \|\| 1.167.74 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā rājye saṃsthāpya vai sutam \|*  
*nāmnā viśvasahaṃ khyātaṃ prajagāma tapovanam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. After resolving thus, he crowned his son named Viśvāsaha as the king and went to the penance grove.

## Chapter 168 - Greatness of the Source of Dhārotpatti

## \|\| 1.168.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya viśvāmitro dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*himavantaṃ nagaṃ prāpya tapaścakre sudāruṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*varṣāsvākāśaśāyī ca hemaṃte salilāśayaḥ \|*  
*pañcāgnisādhako grīṣme sthito varṣaśatatrayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*phalamūlakṛtāhārastato varṣaśatatrayam \|*  
*dhyāyamānaḥ paraṃ brahma sthito brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśanaḥ paścāttāvatkālaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataścaiva jalāhārastāvanmātraṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kālaṃ sa vāyubhakṣaśca tataścaivāyutaṃ samāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Thus abdicating kingdom, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Viśvāmitra went to the Himālaya mountain and performed a severe penance.

During rainy reason he lay under the open sky and during winter he lay in water. During summer he performed the austerity amidst five fires and continued thus for three hundred years.

Then for three hundred years, his diet was fruits and roots. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he remained meditating upon the supreme Absolute. Then for a long time he subsisted on scattered dry leaves thereafter.

Then for the same period, he remained on water alone for sustenance. Then for ten thousand years he remained with the sole intake of air.

## \|\| 1.168.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha dṛṣṭvā tapaḥśaktiṃ tasya tāṃ tridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*pātāyaṣyati māṃ nūnameṣa sthānānnṛpottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. On seeing the power of penance of Viśvāmitra, the Lord of Devas thought thus: ‘Certainly this excellent king will drag me down from my position.’

## \|\| 1.168.6 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca saṃgatya sāmnā paramavalgunā \|*  
*viśvāmitraṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ bhayena mahatā'nvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Actuated by great fright, he came to the excellent king Viśvāmitra and spoke to him these sweet words in conciliatory terms.

## \|\| 1.168.7 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*viśvāmitra pratuṣṭo'smi tapasānena pārthiva \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yadabhīṣṭaṃ hṛdisthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Indra said:

7\. O Viśvāmitra, I am very much pleased by this penance. Welfare unto you, O king, choose your boon, whatever may be the desire in your heart.

## \|\| 1.168.8 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ dehi me śakra yadi tuṣṭo'si sāṃpratam \|*  
*tadarthaṃ tapasaścaryāṃ jānīhi tvaṃ puraṃdara \|\| 8 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

8\. O Śakra, if you are pleased now, grant me Brāhmaṇical status. O Purandara, know that my austerity is aimed at this.

## \|\| 1.168.9 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa kṣatriyaḥ syātkathaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatisaṃskārairdviguṇairyaḥprajāyate \|*  
*tadanyatprārthaya kṣipraṃ yatte'bhīṣṭataraṃ sthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Indra said:

9\. How can a Kṣatriya become a Brāhmaṇa with the selfsame boby? A Brāhmaṇa is made by the performance of the double of twenty-four Saṃskāras (i.e. forty-eight rites). Hence request immediately for something else which is more covetable.

Viśvāmitra siad:

## \|\| 1.168.10 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*na brāhmaṇyātparaṃ kiṃcitprārthayāmi sureśvara \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Lord of Suras, I don’t wish to request for anything else than Brāhmaṇical status.

## \|\| 1.168.11 \|\|

*api trailokyarājyaṃ te vastuṣvanyeṣu kā kathā \|*  
*tasmādgaccha suraśreṣṭha svarājyaṃ paripālaya \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I don’t request even for your dominion of all the three worlds. Then, how can there be even the talk of other objectives! Hence, O most excellent one among Suras, do go away and rule over your realm.

## \|\| 1.168.12-13 \|\|

*parityakṣyāmyahaṃ dehaṃ yāsye vā'haṃ dvijanmatām \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya devarājo divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā sarvadevasamāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitro'pi tadrūpaṃ cakāra duścaraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12a. This is my resolve. Either I will attain Brāhmaṇical status or I will cast off my life.

12b-13a. On hearing his words and knowing his resolve, the king of Devas surrounded by gods went to heaven.

13b. Viśvāmitra then resumed the performance of the harsh penance as before.

## \|\| 1.168.14 \|\|

*atha varṣasahasre tu vyatikrānte dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*anyasminvāyubhakṣasya viśvāmitrasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, another period of a thousand years passed by, through which King Viśvāmitra continued his austerity sustaining himself only on intake of air.

## \|\| 1.168.15 \|\|

*ājagāma svayaṃ brahmā puṇyairdevarṣibhiḥ saha \|*  
*abravīttaṃ mahīpālaṃ tapasā dagdhakilbiṣam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Brahmā himself came there along with the holy celestial sages. He spoke to the king who had got all his sins burned by means of his penance.

## \|\| 1.168.16 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*viśvāmitra pratuṣṭo'smi tapasānena sattama \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te pradāsyāmyapi durlabham \|\| 16 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

16\. O Viśvāmitra, O most excellent one, I am very much pleased with this penance. Welfare unto you. Choose a boon. I shall grant it to you even if it is difficult to obtain.

## \|\| 1.168.17 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ dehi me deva nānyadiṣṭatamaṃ mahat \|\| 17 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

17\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, then grant Brāhmaṇical status to me. Nothing else is eagerly sought after by me.

## \|\| 1.168.18 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kṣatriyeṇa prajātasya dvijatvaṃ jāyate katham \|*  
*śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ hi kimevaṃ vadasīpsitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

18\. How can Brāhmaṇical status be granted to one begotten by a Kṣatriya? Why do you express such a desire as is opposed to the injunction of the Śruti and Smṛti?

## \|\| 1.168.19 \|\|

*yanna jātaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe na bhaviṣyati karhicit \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This is what has never occurred on the surface of the earth and will never occur at all.

## \|\| 1.168.20 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ devadeveśa brahmalokamanuttamam \|*  
*ahaṃ tyakṣyāmi vā prāṇānsaṃprāpsye vā dvijanmatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

20\. Go away, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, to the excellent Brahmaloka. I will either attain the Brāhmaṇical status or cast off my life.

## \|\| 1.168.21-24 \|\|

*atha devarṣimadhyastha ṛcīko vākyamabravīt \|*  
*asya janmakṛte deva brāhmyairmaṃtrairmayā caruḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*abhito brahmasarvasvaṃ tatra sayojitaṃ mayā \|*  
*tenaiva kṣatrajanmā'yaṃ brāhmaṇaścaturānana \|\| 22 \|\|*

*brahmarṣikīrtayasvainaṃ tasmāttvaṃ prapitāmaha \|*  
*rājyastho'pi dvijārhāṇi satkṛtyānya karodasau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*brāhmamantraprabhāvena tasmādbrahmarṣimāhvaya \|*  
*yena kīrtāmahe sarve viśvāmitraṃ dvijottamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. Then Ṛcīka who was in the middle of the celestial sages spoke these words: “O Lord, for the birth of this king Caru was prepared by me with Brāhmya Mantras. All round thereof, Brahma-Sarvasva (everything Brāhmaṇical) was used by me. So indeed, O Four-faced One, he is a Brāhmaṇa though born of a Kṣatriya.

Hence, O Pitāmaha, proclaim him a Brāhmaṇical sage; though he was in the administrative post of a realm, he used to perform excellent rites befittting a Brāhmaṇa.

It is the power of the Brāhma Mantras. Hence, call him a Brahmarṣi so that all of us can glorify Viśvāmitra as the most excellent Brāhmaṇa.”

## \|\| 1.168.25-27 \|\|

*atha brahmā ciraṃ dhyātvā brāhmyai rmaṃtraiśca tejasā \|*  
*samutpannaṃ tataḥ prāha brāhmaṇastvaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tyajedaṃ duṣkaraṃ ghoraṃ tapo madvacanāddrutam \|*  
*sa yadā brahmaṇā prokto brahmarṣi stvamasaṃśayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ṛcīkādyaistataḥ sarvaiḥ prokto devarṣibhistathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-26a. Then Brahmā meditated for a long time. He thought of him as born of Brāhmya Mantras and refulgence. He then said: “You have been transformed into a Brāhmaṇa by me. At my instance leave off this terrible penance very difficult to perform.”

26b-27. When he was proclaimed by Brahmā, “You are a Brahmarṣi”, he was proclaimed so by Ṛcīka and other celestial sages.

## \|\| 1.168.28-29 \|\|

*atha teṣāṃ madhyagato vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*so'bravītkopasaṃyukto nāhaṃ vakṣyāmi karhicit \|\| 28 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyājjātaṃ jānannapi pitāmaha \|*  
*ṛcīkasya ca dākṣiṇyāttathā tvaṃ vadasi prabho \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Vasiṣṭha, the excellent sage, was also among them. He angrily announced, “I will not at all proclaim him thus. Knowing (full well) that he was begotten by a Kṣatriya, O Grandfather, out of courtesy to Ṛcīka, you proclaim him to be so (a Brāhmaṇa).”

## \|\| 1.168.30 \|\|

*procyamāno 'pi bahudhā vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*pitāmahena munibhirnāradādyairanekadhā \|*  
*jagāmātha parityajya tānsarvāndvijasattamān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Though importuned in diverse ways by Pitāmaha, and the sages including Nārada, Vasiṣṭha, the excellent sage, did not relent. He left all those excellent Brāhmaṇas and went away.

## \|\| 1.168.31 \|\|

*sa cāgatya muni śreṣṭho deśaṃ cānartasaṃjñitam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre śaṃkhatīrthasamīpataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The excellent sage arrived in the land called Ānarta at Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra near Śaṅkha Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.168.32 \|\|

*yatra brahmaśilā puṇyā śvetadvīpasamanvitā \|*  
*sarasvatī sthitā yatra nadī pāpaharā śubhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The meritorious Brahmaśilā and the Śvetadvīpa are there. The splendid river Sarasvatī that dispels sins is also present there.

## \|\| 1.168.33 \|\|

*tatrāśramapadaṃ kṛtvā cakāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitro'pi sāmarṣastadvadhārthaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He built a penance-grove there and performed an elaborate penance. The revengeful Viśvāmitra also came there with an intention of killing him.

## \|\| 1.168.34 \|\|

*tasyāśramasya dūre sa yāmyāṃ diśi samāśritaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāśramapadaṃ tatra tasya cchidrāṇi cintayan \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Far from Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage in the southern quarter he set up his penance-grove and began to think about finding his vulnerable points.

## \|\| 1.168.35 \|\|

*saṃsthitaḥ suciraṃ kālaṃ na ca paśyati kiṃcana \|*  
*athābhicārikaṃ tena prārabdhaṃ tasya copari \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Though he waited thus for a long time, he could not discover any. Thereupon, black magic began to be practised by him against Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.168.36 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ sāmavidhinā sāmavede vadhātmakam \|*  
*tasya tairdāruṇairmaṃtrairjuhvato jātavedasam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. What has been laid down in the Sāmaveda as a means of killing by means of employing Sāman Mantras, he performed Homas in the sacred fire by uttering those deadly Mantras.

## \|\| 1.168.37 \|\|

*niṣkrāṃtā dāruṇā śaktirmuktakeśī bhayānakā \|*  
*vānaraskaṃdhamārūḍhā kurvāṇā kilkilādhvanim \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A terrible Śakti arose from the sacred fire. She was hideous-looking with hair dishevelled. She was riding on the shoulders of a monkey and making Kilkila (chattering) sounds.

## \|\| 1.168.38-39 \|\|

*nānāyudhasamopetā yamajihvā yathā parā \|*  
*sābravīdvada vipreṃdra kiṃ te kṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 38 \|\|*

*trailokyamapi kṛtsnaṃ ca saṃharāmi tavājñayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. She had various weapons. She appeared like another Yamajihvā (Yama’s tongue). She said: “Tell, O leading Brāhmaṇa, what job on your behalf shall I carry out? At your bidding I shall destroy the entire group of the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.168.40 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*mama śatrurmānyo tra vasiṣṭhaḥ kumuniḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ tvaṃ jahi drutaṃ gatvā tadarthaṃ ca mayā kṛtā \|\| 40 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

40\. I have a formidable foe here. He is a base sage named Vasiṣṭha. Do go there and kill him quickly. You have been created for that purpose.

## \|\| 1.168.41 \|\|

*evamuktā tu sā tena viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhāśramamuddiśya prasthitā cottarāmukhī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On being told thus by the intelligent Viśvāmitra, she set off facing the northern quarter towards the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.168.42 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu vasiṣṭhasyāśrame dvijāḥ \|*  
*durnimittāni jātāni prabhūtāni mahāṃti ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In the meantime, O Brāhmaṇas, there occurred many great evil omens in the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.168.43 \|\|

*papāta mahatī colkā nihatya ravimaṇḍalam \|*  
*tathā rudhiravṛṣṭiśca asthimiśrā vyajāyata \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A great comet fell down hitting against the solar disc. A shower of blood with bones mixed fell there.

## \|\| 1.168.44 \|\|

*dīptāṃ diśaṃ samāsādya ruroda ca tathā śivā \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sumahotpātānvasiṣṭho munipuṃgavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A vixen howled coming up to the illuminated spot. Vasiṣṭha, the great sage, saw her as well as the great ill omens.

## \|\| 1.168.45 \|\|

*yāvadālokate rūpaṃ jvālāmālāsamākulam \|*  
*tataḥ samyakparijñāya sarvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. When he closely scrutinized the form shrouded in wreaths of flames, he understood everything by means of the divine vision.

## \|\| 1.168.46 \|\|

*viśvāmitraprayukteyaṃ śaktirmama vadhāya ca \|*  
*kṛtyā rūpā sumaṃtraiśca sāmavedasamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. (He said to himself:) ‘This is the Śakti employed by Viśvāmitra for killing me. She is in the form of a Kṛtyā (Evil Spirit) caused by the excellent Mantras of the Sāmaveda.’

## \|\| 1.168.47 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti tenoktā tataḥ sā niścalābhavat \|*  
*nijamaṃtraiśca sā tena staṃbhitātharvaṇodbhavaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. She was addressed, “Stop! Stop!” by him (Vasiṣṭha). Suddenly she stood motionless. By means of his own Mantras taken from the Atharva Veda, she was rendered immobile and paralysed.

## \|\| 1.168.48-49 \|\|

*tataḥ strīrūpamādāya provāca munipuṃgavam \|*
