*sāmavedastu vedānāṃ prādhānyena vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vidhinā tena saṃsṛṣṭā viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*mā kurutvapramāṇaṃtu prahāraṃ saha me mune \|*  
*rakṣayiṣyāmi te \|*  
*prāṇānsvalpasparśena te mune \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. She then assumed the form of a woman and said to the great sage: “It is the Sāmaveda that is the most important of all the Vedas. The intelligent sage Viśvāmitra created me on the basis of the injunctions therein. Do not make my blow ineffective, O sage. Do endure it. Through a gentle touch I shall avoid death unto you.”

## \|\| 1.168.50 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ kuru me sparśaṃ na marma sparśanaṃ śubhe \|*  
*mayā cātharvaṇā maṃtrāḥ saṃhṛtāḥ kṛpayā tava \|\| 50 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

50\. If it be so, do not touch my vulnerable points. Make a gentle touch, O splendid one. Out of pity for you I have withdrawn the Atharva Mantras.

## \|\| 1.168.51 \|\|

*tataḥ sā dāruṇā śaktirviśvāmitraprayojitā \|*  
*tasyāṃgadeśaṃ spṛṣṭvātha nipapāta dharātale \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then the terrible Śakti employed by Viśvāmitra gently touched a part of his body and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 1.168.52-54 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo vasiṣṭhastu tāmāha madhuraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti te pūjāṃ kariṣyaṃti samāhitāḥ \|*  
*janāḥ sarve mahābhāge bhaktyā paramayā yutāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*caitramāse site pakṣe aṣṭamīdivase sthite \|*  
*ye te pūjāṃ kariṣyaṃti śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*te sarve vatsaraṃyāvadbhavi ṣyaṃti nirāmayāḥ \|*  
*tasmādatraiva sthātavyaṃ sadaiva mama vākyataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Vasiṣṭha who was pleased thereby spoke these sweet words to her: “From now onwards, people with great concentration will perform your adoration, O highly esteemed one. They will be endowed with great devotion. Those who have great faith and worship you on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, shall be free from ailments for a year thereafter! Hence at my instance you must stay here always.”

## \|\| 1.168.55-56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā ca sā tena vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā \|*  
*sthitā tatraiva sā devī tasya vākyena tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

*prāpnoti paramāṃ pūjāṃ viśeṣānnāgaraiḥ kṛtām \|*  
*dhārānāmeti vikhyātā bhaktalokasukha pradā \|\| 56 \|\|*

Sūta said:

55-56. On being told thus by the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha the goddess stays there itself at his instance from the same moment. She regularly gets the adoration performed specially by the Nāgaras. She is well known by the name Dhārā. She accords happiness unto the devoted folk.

## Chapter 169 - Greatness of Dhārā Devī

## \|\| 1.169.1-5 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmātsā tuṣṭidā proktā nāgarāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dhārānāmeti vikhyātā kasmātsā dharaṇītale \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*camatkārapure pūrvaṃ dhārānāmeti viśrutā \|*  
*āsīttapasvinī sādhvī nāgarī brāhmaṇottamā \|*  
*tasyāḥ sakhyamarundhatyā āsītpūrvaṃ sumedhayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*arundhatī yadā prāptā camatkārapure śubhe \|*  
*snānārthaṃ śaṃkhatīrthaṃ tu vasiṣṭhena samāgatā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tayā dṛṣṭātha sā tatra aṃguṣṭhāgreṇa saṃsthitā \|*  
*vāyubhakṣā nirāhārā divyena vapuṣānvitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tayā pṛṣṭā ca sā sādhvī kā tvaṃ kasya sutā śubhe \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tu sthitā cogre tapasi brūhi me śubhe \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-5. Why is she well-known all over the earth by the name Dhārā? Why is she said to be the deity specially delighting the Nāgaras?

## \|\| 1.169.6 \|\|

*dhārovāca \|*  
*devaśarmākhyaviprasya sutāhaṃ nāgarasya ca \|*  
*bālatve vartamānāyā vaidhavyaṃ me vyavasthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

Formerly, there was an ascetic woman well-known by the name Dhārā in Camatkārapura. She was an excellent Brāhmaṇa lady, a chaste Nāgara woman. Formerly, she was a close friend of the highly intelligent Arundhatī.

When she (Arundhatī) came at the outset to the splendid Camatkārapura along with Vasiṣṭha in order to take her holy bath in Śaṅkhatīrtha, she had met the lady who eschewing all food was performing a penance with the sole intake of air. The lady endowed with a divine physical form was standing on the tip of her big toe.

The chaste lady was asked by Arundhatī: “Who are you? O splendid lady, whose daughter are you? Why are you practising this severe penance? O splendid lady, do tell me.”

Dhārā said:

6\. I am daughter of a Nāgara Brāhmaṇa named Devaśarman. I became a widow during even childhood.

## \|\| 1.169.7 \|\|

*śaṃkhatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ śrutvā śaṃkheśvarasya ca \|*  
*tato'haṃ saṃsthitā hyatra tasyaivārādhane sthitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing the greatness of Śaṅkha Tīrtha and that of Śaṅkheśvara, I permanently settled here engaged in propitiating the same deity.

## \|\| 1.169.8 \|\|

*arundhatyuvāca \|*  
*tavopari mahānsneho darśanātte vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādāgaccha gacchāvo mamāśramapadaṃ śubham \|\| 8 \|\|*

Arundhatī said:

8\. Merely at your sight I am having a great affection for you. Hence, do come. Let us go to my splendid penance-grove.

## \|\| 1.169.9 \|\|

*sarasvatyā staṭe śubhre sarvapātakanāśane \|*  
*śāstragoṣṭhīratā nityaṃ tatra tiṣṭha mayā saha \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the splendid banks of Sarasvatī that is destructive of all sins, stay there with me devoted to the discussion of the scriptural topics.

## \|\| 1.169.10 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃprasthitā sā tu tayā sārdhaṃ tapasvinī \|*  
*anujñātā svapitrā tu jananyā bāṃdhavaistathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After taking the permission of her father, mother and kinsmen, the ascetic lady started along with her (Arundhatī).

## \|\| 1.169.11 \|\|

*tasyāḥ sakhyaṃ ciraṃ kālaṃ tayā saha babhūva ha \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya sā śaktistatra cāgatā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Their friendship continued for a long time. Once that Śakti too came there.

## \|\| 1.169.12 \|\|

*viśvāmitreṇa saṃsṛṣṭā vasiṣṭhasya vadhāya ca \|*  
*sā staṃbhitā vasiṣṭhena kṛtā devīsvarūpiṇī \|*  
*saṃpūjyā devamartyānāṃ sarvarakṣāpradā śubhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (You may remember that) she had been created by Viśvāmitra for killing Vasiṣṭha. She was rendered paralysed by

Vasiṣṭha and turned into a goddess worthy of being adored by Devas and human beings. The splendid deity accorded protection unto all.

## \|\| 1.169.13 \|\|

*tatastu dhārayā tasyāḥ kailāsaśikharopamaḥ \|*  
*prāsādo nirmito viprā nānāratnavicitritaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A palace (-like shrine) comparable to the peak of Kailāsa was built by Dhārā unto the deity, O Brāhmaṇas. It was wonderfully inlaid with different kinds of Jewels.

## \|\| 1.169.14 \|\|

*cakārātha tataḥ stotraṃ tasyāḥ sā ca tapasvinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the ascetic lady eulogized the goddess:

## \|\| 1.169.15 \|\|

*namaste parame brāhmi dhārayoge namonamaḥ \|*  
*ardhamātre pare śūnye tasyārdhārdhe namostu te \|\|\|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “O supreme Brāhmī, obeisance to you. O Dhārā Yoga (Yoga of continuous flow), obeisance, obeisance. O greatest void! O half of a Mātrā! O Supreme Śūnya! A moiety of half thereof! Obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.169.16 \|\|

*namaste jagadādhāre namaste bhūtadhāriṇi \|*  
*namaste padmapatrākṣi namaste kāṃcanadyute \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to you, O basic support of the universe. Obeisance to you, O support of all living beings. Obeisance to you, O deity with eyes resembling lotus petals Obeisance to you, O deity lustrous like gold.

## \|\| 1.169.17 \|\|

*namaste siṃhayānāḍhye namaste'stumahābhuje \|*  
*namaste devatābhīṣṭe namaste daityasūdini \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to you, O deity having the Leonine vehicle. Obeisance to you, O deity of great arms. Obeisance to you, O deity granting the desire of Devas. Obeisance to you, O destroyer of the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.169.18 \|\|

*namaste mahiṣākrāṃtaśarīracchinnamastake \|*  
*namaste viṃdhyanirate surāmāṃsabalipriye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Obeisance to you, O deity with a shattered head and a body assailed by Ṃahiṣa. Obeisance, O deity liking to stay in Vindhya to whom liquor and meat are the favourite oblations.

## \|\| 1.169.19 \|\|

*tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ śacī gaurī tvaṃ siddhistvaṃ vibhāvarī \|*  
*tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tuṣṭistvaṃ puṣṭistvaṃ sureśvarī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You are Lakṣmī; you are Śacī; you are Gaurī; you are Siddhi (perfect achievement). You are Vibhāvarī (night, excellent in lustre). You are Svāhā. Your are Svadhā. You are Tuṣṭi (Satisfaction) You are Puṣṭi (Nourishment). You are the goddess of Suras.

## \|\| 1.169.20 \|\|

*śaktirūpāsi devi tvaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakā riṇī \|*  
*tvayi dṛṣṭamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O goddess, you are in the from of Śakti. You are the cause of creation and dissolution. All these, the entire group of the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings, are seen in you.

## \|\| 1.169.21-22 \|\|

*yathā tilesthitaṃ tailaṃ dadhisaṃsthaṃ yathā ghṛtam \|*  
*havirbhujaśca kāṣṭhasthaḥ suguptaṃ labhyate na hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tathā tvamapi deveśi sarvagāpi na lakṣyase \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Just as oil latent in gingelly seed, ghee present in curd and fire present in wood are all well concealed and cannot be seen, so also, O goddess of Devas, you cannot be perceived though you are omnipresent.”

## \|\| 1.169.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etena stotramukhyena smṛtā sā parameśvarī \|*  
*bahūni varṣa pūgāni pūjayaṃtyā dinedine \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:

23\. She continued her adoration day after day for many years, remembering the great goddess through this important prayer.

## \|\| 1.169.24 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya caitraśuklāṣṭamī sitā \|*  
*tasminnahani devī sā nadyāṃ saṃsnāpya pūjitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Once, on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, the deity was bathed in the river and adored.

## \|\| 1.169.25 \|\|

*bali pūjāṃ tato dattvā stotreṇānena ca stutā \|*  
*tataḥ pratyakṣatāṃ gatvā tāmuvāca tapasvinīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After offering the oblations and performing the worship she eulogized the goddess by means of the prayer quoted above. Thereupon, the deity manifested herself and she spoke to the ascetic woman:

## \|\| 1.169.26 \|\|

*putri tuṣṭāsmi bhadraṃ te stotreṇānena cānaghe \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te tava dāsyāmi vāṃchitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Dear daughter, welfare unto you. I am pleased at this eulogy, O sinless one, choose a boon. I shall give you the desired thing.”

## \|\| 1.169.27 \|\|

*dhārovāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭāsi me devi yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*tanme nāma tavāpyastu prāsāde'tra hi kevalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

Dhārā said:

27\. O goddess, if you are pleased with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, then let my name be yours too only in this palace.

## \|\| 1.169.28-29 \|\|

*aparaṃ nāgaro yo'tra tvasminnahani saṃsthite \|*  
*pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kṛtvā tava dattvā phalatrayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*stotreṇānena bhavatīṃ stutvā ca kurute natim \|*  
*tasya saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadrogo rakṣyastvayā'khilaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Another thing: If a Nāgara devotee circumambulates you three times, offers you three fruits, eulogizes you with this prayer and bows to you on that particular day, then for the period of the whole of that year, all his ailments should be prevented by you.

## \|\| 1.169.30 \|\|

*yā ca vaṃdhyā bhavennārī sā bhūyātputrasaṃyutā \|*  
*durbhagā ca sasaubhāgyā kurūpā rūpasaṃbhavā \|*  
*rogiṇī roganirmuktā sarvasaukhyasamanvitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A barren woman-devotee should be blessed with sons. An unfortunate woman shall become a woman enjoying conjugal felicity; an ugly one should become beautiful; and a sick woman should be rid of her ailments. She must have every happiness.

## \|\| 1.169.31 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ dhāreti vikhyātā prāsāde'tra tvayā kṛte \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi na sandehastava kīrtikṛte sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

The Devī said:

31\. For the sake of enhancing your reputation I shall become well-known as Dhārā in the palace built by you. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.169.32-33 \|\|

*atra yo nāgaro bhaktyā samāgatya tapasvini \|*  
*pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kuryāddattvā mama phalatrayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*so'pi saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadbhavitā rogavarjitaḥ \|*  
*evamuktā tu sā devītataścādarśanaṃ gatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. O ascetic lady, if a Nāgara comes here, makes three circumambulations and offers me three fruits, he shall be rid of all ailments for the period of a year.

After saying thus the goddess vanished.

## \|\| 1.169.34 \|\|

*dhārāpi saṃsthitā tatra arundhatyā samanvitā \|*  
*adyāpi dṛśyate vyomni tasyāścāpi samīpagā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Dhārā stayed there permanently accompanied by Arundhatī. Even today she is visible in the sky very near her (Arundhatī).

## \|\| 1.169.35 \|\|

*etaddhārodbhavaṃ yo'tra vṛttāṃtaṃ kīrtayiṣyati \|*  
*śṛṇuyādvā dvijaśreṣṭhā mucyetpāpāddinodbhavāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, one who glorifies this story of the origin of Dhārā or listens to it shall be rid of the sins of that day.

## \|\| 1.169.36 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena paṭhanīyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śrotavyaṃ ca prabhaktyedaṃ nāgaraiśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hence, it should be read with all efforts and listened to with great devotion by every one, especially by the Nāgaras.

## Chapter 170 - Creation of Dhārā Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.170.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi saṃjātamāścaryaṃ yadabhūddvijāḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitreṇa sā śaktirvasiṣṭhāya visarjitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vadhārthaṃ tasya viprarṣervasiṣṭhena ca dhīmatā \|*  
*staṃbhitā'tharvaṇairmantraiḥ prasvedaḥ samajāyata \|\| 2 \|\|*

*svedātsamabhavattoyaṃ śītalaṃ tadajāyata \|*  
*pādābhyāṃ nirgataṃ toyamatra dṛśyamajāyata \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vidārya bhūmiṃ saṃjātā jaladhārā suśītalā \|*  
*nirmalaṃ pāvanaṃ svacchaṃ gaṃgāṃbha iva niḥsṛtam \|\| 4 \|\| \|\| gaṃ \|*  
*gā pratyakṣatāṃ yātā tīrthaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*pūritaṃ vāriṇā kuṇḍaṃ nirmalaṃ śītalaṃ śivam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Further, O Brāhmaṇas, another wonderful incident occurred there. That Śakti was discharged towards Vasiṣṭha by Viśvāmitra for the purpose of killing that saintly Brāhmaṇa. It was rendered motionless and steady by the intelligent Vasiṣṭha through the Atharvaṇa Mantras. Then he began to perspire profusely.

The sweat flowed down as cool water. When it flowed out of the feet it appeared visible like a cool stream of water that had broken through the ground. It was devoid of impurities. It flowed like the crystalline clean Gaṅgā water.

## \|\| 1.170.5 \|\|

*vidārya bhūmiṃ saṃjātā jaladhārā suśītalā \|*  
*nirmalaṃ pāvanaṃ svacchaṃ gaṃgāṃbha iva niḥsṛtam \|\| 4 \|\| \|\| gaṃ \|*  
*gā pratyakṣatāṃ yātā tīrthaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*pūritaṃ vāriṇā kuṇḍaṃ nirmalaṃ śītalaṃ śivam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Gaṅgā herself appeared accompanied by all the Tīrthas. The Kuṇḍa was filled with water. It was auspicious and cool.

## \|\| 1.170.6 \|\|

*tasyāṃ yā kurute snānaṃ nārī vaṃdhyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥ putravatī sā syādraudre kaliyuge dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even in the terrible Kaliyuga, O Brāhmaṇas, a barren woman who takes her holy bath therein shall immediately be blessed with a son.

## \|\| 1.170.7 \|\|

*anyo'pi kurute snānaṃ sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Anyone else who takes his bath there shall obtain the benefit of all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.170.8 \|\|

*snātvā tatra tu yo devīṃ paśyecca vidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā putrānrājyotthaṃ ca sukhaṃ labhet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A man who takes the bath and then duly visits the goddess, shall obtain wealth, food-grain, sons and the happiness arising from a kingdom.

## \|\| 1.170.9 \|\|

*yā nārī durbhagā vandhyā sā'pi putravatī bhavet \|*  
*caitre māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ bhaktiyogasamanvitā \|*  
*mahāniśāyāṃ tatraiva naivedyabalipiṃḍikām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even an unfortunate barren woman shall become endowed with sons. On the eighth lunar day in the bright half of Caitra she should offer a ball (Piṇḍikā) of oblations with great devotion at the time of Mahāniśā (between its second and third watches).

## \|\| 1.170.10 \|\|

*prasannayā kumāryā tu svayaṃ cā'tha karoti yā \|*  
*gṛhṇāti yā ca vai nārī piṃḍikāṃ balisaṃyutām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. She may offer it herself or through a joyous virgin. A woman who grasps the Piṇḍikā of oblations also gets the benefit.

## \|\| 1.170.11 \|\|

*śatavarṣā tu yā nārī piṃḍikāṃ bhakṣayeddvijāḥ \|*  
*sā'pi putravatī ca syādyadi vṛddhatamā bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If a woman of advanced age of even a hundred years eats the Piṇḍikā she shall become endowed with sons.

## \|\| 1.170.12 \|\|

*kiṃ punaryauvanopetā saubhāgyena samanvitā \|*  
*putrasaukhyavatī nārī devyā vai darśanena ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This is all the more so in the case of youthful women enjoying conjugal felicity? Any woman merely by means of the sight (Darśana) of the goddess gets the happiness of having sons.

## \|\| 1.170.13 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ nāgarāṇāṃ tu bhāvajā devatā smṛtā \|*  
*sā sārdhāṣṭadvipaṃcāśadgotrāṇāṃ kuladevatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She is the hereditary deity of the fifty-two and eight Gotras of all Nāgaras. She is the deity remembered through devotional fervour.

## \|\| 1.170.14 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādyātrā nāgaraiḥ sukṛtā bhavet \|*  
*na vinā nāgarairyātrāṃ tuṣṭiṃ yāti sureśvarī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. For this reason the religious procession (Yātrā) performed by Nāgaras is more effective. Without the Yātrā performed by Nāgaras, the goddess of Suras does not become pleased.

## Chapter 171 - Battle between Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra

## \|\| 1.171.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tāṃ śaktiṃ vyarthatāṃ prāptāṃ jñātvā kopasamanvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mumoca tadvadhārthāya brahmāstraṃ so'bhimaṃtritam \|*  
*tasya saṃhitamātrasya prasvanaḥ samajāyata \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataścolkāḥ prabhūtāśca prayāṃti ca nabhastalāt \|*  
*tataḥ kuntāḥ śaktayaśca tomarāḥ parighāstathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhiṃḍipālā gadāścaiva khaḍgāścaiva paraśvadhāḥ \|*  
*bāṇāḥ prāsāḥ śataghnyaśca śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Note: Vide Mahābhārata, Ādi ch. 174.

Sūta said:

1-4. In the meantime, the great sage Viśvāmitra came to know that the Śakti had become futile and hence was very angry thereby.

He then discharged Brahmāstra for killing him after invoking the requisite Mantras. Even when it was only combined (with the Ṃantra) its sound was very loud. Then a great number of meteors started to fall down from the sky. Various weapons like Kuntas, Śaktis, Tomaras, Parighas, Bhindipālas, clubs, swords, axes, arrows, spears and Śataghnīs came down in hundreds and thousands.

## \|\| 1.171.5-7 \|\|

*vasiṣṭho'pi parijñāya preṣitaṃ gādhisūnunā \|*  
*brahmāstraṃ mṛtyave tena śucirbhūtvā tataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*iṣīkāṃ ca samādāya brahmāstraṃ tatra yojayan \|*  
*abravīdgādhiputrāya svastyastu tava pārśvataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*hanyatāmastrametaddhimama vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*tatastena hataṃ tacca brahmāstraṃ tatsamudbhavam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Vasiṣṭha came to know that the Brahmāstra was discharged by the son of Gādhi to bring about his death. So he remained pure and clean, took an Iṣīkā reed and charged it with the power of Brahmāstra. Then he told Gādhi’s son, “May it be well unto you. Let this missile be hit at sides at my instance without doubt.” Then Vasiṣṭha struck down the Brahmāstra discharged by him.

## \|\| 1.171.8-9 \|\|

*vajrāstraṃ ca tato muktaṃ vajrāstreṇa vināśitam \|*  
*yadyadastraṃ kṣipatyeṣa viśvāmitraḥ prakopitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tattaddhaṃti vasiṣṭhastu maṃtrasya ca prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu kṣubhito makarālayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then Vajrāstra was discharged by Viśvāmitra and it was destroyed by another Vajrāstra (by Vasiṣṭha). Thanks to the power of his Mantras, Vasiṣṭha struck down every missile that the furious Viśvāmitra discharged. In the meantime, the ocean became agitated.

## \|\| 1.171.10 \|\|

*śīryaṃte giriśṛṃgāṇi raktavṛṣṭiḥ parā sthitā \|*  
*pralayasyeva cihnāni saṃjātāni dharātale \|*  
*kimakāle mahāneṣa pralayaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Peaks of mountains crumbled down. There was a tremendous shower of blood. Signs like those at the time of Pralaya (ultimate dissolution) were seen cropping up all over the earth. Devas wondered, “Why should there be an untimely Pralaya?”

## \|\| 1.171.11 \|\|

*tataḥ pitāmahaṃ jagmuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*procuḥ pralayacihnāni yāni saṃti dharātale \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All the Devas including Vāsava went to Pitāmaha and told him that the signs of Pralaya had been seen on the earth.

## \|\| 1.171.12-14 \|\|

*tato brahmā ciraṃ dhyātvā tānuvāca divaukasaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitra vasiṣṭhābhyāṃ yuddhametadvyavasthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*divyāstrasaṃbhavaṃ devāstenaitadvyākulaṃ jagat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmādgacchāmahe tatra yāvanno jāyate kṣayaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ divyāstrāṇāṃ prabhāvataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Thereupon, Brahmā meditated for some time and said to the Heaven-dwellers: “A fight between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha has ensued. O Devas, they are fighting with divine weapons. Hence, the entire universe is in throes (of this agitation). So we shall go there before all the living beings are destroyed due to the power of the divine missiles.”

## \|\| 1.171.15 \|\|

*tato'bhigamya te deśaṃ yatra tau munisattamau \|*  
*vicāmitravasiṣṭhau tau yudhyamānau parasparam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He then went to that place where the excellent sages Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha were fighting with each other.

## \|\| 1.171.16 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca tau brahmā sāmnā paramavalgunā \|*  
*nivartyatāmidaṃ yuddhametaddivyāstrasaṃbhavam \|*  
*yāvanna pralayo bhāvi samaste dharaṇītale \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Brahmā spoke to them in gentle and sweet tones: “May this fight with divine missiles be withdrawn lest there should be a wide-spread Pralaya on the entire earth.”

## \|\| 1.171.17 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*nāhamastraṃ prayuṃjāmi viśvāmitravadhecchayā \|*  
*ātmarakṣākṛte deva astramastreṇa śāmayan \|\| 17 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

17\. O Lord, I am not employing the missiles with a desire to kill Viśvāmitra. As a means of self-defence I am subduing his missiles by means of counter-missiles.

## \|\| 1.171.18 \|\|

*ayaṃ mama vināśāya kevalaṃ cāstramokṣaṇam \|*  
*kurute nirdayo brahmaṃstaṃ nivāraya sāṃpratam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. This ruthless fellow discharges the missiles solely with the intention of killing me. O Brahmā, restrain him now.

## \|\| 1.171.19-20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*viśvāmitra muniśreṣṭha vasiṣṭhaṃ brāhmaṇottamam \|*  
*tvaṃ rakṣa mama vākyena tathā sarvamidaṃ jagat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*astramokṣavirāmaṃ tvaṃ brahmarṣe kuru satvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

19-20. O Viśvāmitra, O most excellent one among the sages, protect (keep off from) Vasiṣṭha, the excellent Brāhmaṇa at my instance. So save the entire universe. O Brāhmaṇa-sage, quickly stop discharging the missiles.

## \|\| 1.171.21 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*na māmeṣa dvijaṃ brūte kathaṃcitprapitāmaha \|*  
*tasmādeṣa prakopo me saṃjāto'sya vadhopari \|\| 21 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

21\. O Prapitāmaha, he does not at all call (recognize) me a Brāhmaṇa. Hence my anger has been provoked with the intention of killing him.

## \|\| 1.171.22 \|\|

*tasmādvadatu deveśa māmeṣa brāhmaṇaṃ drutam \|*  
*nivārayāmi yenāstraṃ yadasyopari saṃdhitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hence, O Lord of Devas, let him presently call me a Brāhmaṇa, upon which I shall withdraw the missile aimed at him.

## \|\| 1.171.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tvaṃ vasiṣṭhādhunā brūhi viśvāmitraṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*brāhmaṇo jāyate tena tava jīvasya rakṣaṇam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

23\. O Vasiṣṭha, it is my behest that you now call Viśvāmitra a Brāhmaṇa. Thereby your life can be saved.

## \|\| 1.171.24 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ kṣatriyasaṃjātaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vacmi padmaja \|*  
*na vadhe mama śakto'yaṃ kathaṃcitkṣatriyodbhavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

24\. O Lotus-born One, I shall never call by the name Brāhmaṇa, someone begotten by a Kṣatriya. He, born of a Kṣatriya, is incapable to kill me at all.

## \|\| 1.171.25 \|\|

*brāhmyaṃ tejo na kṣā ttreṇa tejasā saṃpraṇaśyati \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā caturvaktra yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Brāhmaṇical radiance will not get destroyed through the Kṣatriya refulgence. Fully comprehending thus, O Fourfaced One, do what is befitting.

## \|\| 1.171.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*viśvāmitra dvijaśreṣṭha tyaktvā divyāstrasaṃbhavam \|*  
*kuru yuddhaṃ vasiṣṭhena no cecchapsyāmahaṃ ca te \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

26\. O Viśvāmitra, O most excellent one among the twice-borns, proceed ahead with your fight with Vasiṣṭha eschewing the use of divine missiles. Or I may have to curse you.

## \|\| 1.171.27 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*divyāstrāṇi ca saṃtyajya mayā vadhyaḥ sudurmatiḥ \|*  
*kiṃcicchidraṃ samāsādya tvaṃ gaccha nijasaṃśrayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

27\. Even after stopping the divine missiles, this evil-intentioned fellow can be done away with by attacking some vulnerable point. You may go to your abode.

## \|\| 1.171.28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityevamuktā ca brahmalokaṃ gato vidhiḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitravasiṣṭhau ca sarasvatyāstaṭe sthitau \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sūta said:

28\. “Of course”, said Vidhi (Brahmā) and went to Brahmaloka. Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha stayed behind on the banks of Sarasvatī.

## Chapter 172 - Sarasvatī Cursed

## \|\| 1.172.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛti cchidrāṇi viśvāmitro nirīkṣayan \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasya vadhārthāya saṃsthito dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ātmaśaktiprabhāvena maśakasya yathā gajaḥ \|*  
*anyasminnahani prāpte viśvāmitreṇa sā nadī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*samāhūtā samāyātā drutaṃ sā strīsvarūpiṇī \|*  
*abravītprāṃjalirbhūtvā ādeśo dīyatāṃ mama \|*  
*brahmarṣe yena kāryeṇa samāhūtāsmi sāṃpratam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: It was Sarasvatī in Kurukṣetra which was cursed in Mahābhārata, vide Mahābhārata, Śalya Parva ch. 42, 38-39 for the curse, or release from the curse Mahābhārata, Śalya 43.16. Here that episode is used in connection with Prācī Sarasvatī.

Sūta said:

1-3. Ever since then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Viśvāmitra stayed there looking for vulnerable points of Vasiṣṭha for the purpose of slaying him, thanks to the power, like a mosquito (would do) against an elephant.

## \|\| 1.172.4 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*yadā nimajjanaṃ kuryāttava toye mahānadi \|*  
*paramaṃ vegamāsthāya tadā'naya mamāṃtikam \|\| 4 \|\|*

On another day the river was summoned by Viśvāmitra. Immediately she assumed the form of a woman and appeared before him. With palms joined in reverence she said: “O saintly Brāhmaṇa, let the command be given as to the purpose for which I have been called now.”

Viśvāmitra said:

4\. O great river, when he (Vasiṣṭha) plunges (while bathing) into your waters, bring him near me with great rapidity.

## \|\| 1.172.5 \|\|

*pūrṇaśrotraṃ jale naiva vyākulāṃgaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*nihanmi yena śīghraṃ ca nānyacchidraṃ pralakṣaye \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Let his ears be filled with waters. Let his limbs be shaken and exhausted. This will enable me to kill him. I don’t see any other vulnerable point.

## \|\| 1.172.6 \|\|

*evamuktā tadā tena viśvāmitreṇa sā nadī \|*  
*vitrastā bhayasaṃyuktā śāpādvākyamuvāca sā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On being told thus by Viśvāmitra, that river became frightened. She was afraid of his curse and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.172.7-11 \|\|

*nāhaṃ drohaṃ kariṣyāmi vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmarṣe na ca te yuktaṃ kartuṃ vai brahmaṇo vadham \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yadi tvaṃ brahmaṇā prokto brahmarṣiḥ svayameva tu \|*  
*kāmānnāyaṃ vasiṣṭhastu tasmātkopaṃ parityaja \|\| 8 \|\|*

*manasāpi vadhaṃ yastu brāhmaṇasya viciṃtayet \|*  
*taptakṛcchreṇa mucyeta manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo'bravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vācayā pravadedyastu brāhmaṇasya vadhaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*cāṃdrāyaṇena śuddhiḥ syāttasya devo'bravīdidam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasmānnāhaṃ kariṣyāmi tava vākyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*vasiṣṭhārthaṃ tu yatproktaṃ kuru yattava rocate \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. “I will not do anything atrocious in regard to Vasiṣṭha, the noble-souled one. Nor, O Brahmarṣi, is it proper on your part to kill a Brāhmaṇa.

If you have been called a Brahmarṣi by Brahmā himself and it does not please Vasiṣṭha to do so, what is the harm? Hence give up your anger.

If someone even thinks of killing a Brāhmaṇa he can be rid of the sin by the rite of Taptakṛcchra. So says Manu, the son of the Self-born Lord.

The Lord has said that if a man says that he will kill a Brāhmaṇa, his purity can be brought about by Cāndrāyaṇa rite.

Hence, I will not carry out your bidding concerning Vasiṣṭha. You may do whatever you like.”

## \|\| 1.172.12 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kupitastasyā viśvāmitro dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*śaśāpa tāṃ nadīṃ śreṣṭhāṃ yattadvakṣyāmi śrūyatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing it, O Brāhmaṇas, Viśvāmitra got angry. He cursed that excellent river. I shall tell you. Let it be heard what that curse is:

## \|\| 1.172.13 \|\|

*yasmātpāpe vaco mahyaṃ na kṛtaṃ kunadi tvayā \|*  
*tasmādraktapravāhaste jalajo'yaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “O sinful bad river, since my behest has not been carried out, your watery stream shall become bloody.”

## \|\| 1.172.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā karāttoyaṃ saptavārābhimaṃtritam \|*  
*cikṣepātha jale tasyāḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After saying this with eyes turned red due to anger, he took some water in his hand. He charged it with Mantra seven times and poured it down into the water of the river.

## \|\| 1.172.15 \|\|

*tataśca tatkṣaṇājjātaṃ tattoyaṃ rudhiraṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*sārasvataṃ supuṇyaṃ ca yadāsīcchaṃkhasaṃnibham \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereupon, the highly meritorious water of River Sarasvatī which was formerly white like a conch, turned into blood that very moment.

## \|\| 1.172.16 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā bhūtapretaniśācarāḥ \|*  
*pītvāpītvā pranṛtyaṃti gāyaṃti ca hasaṃti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the meantime, ghosts, goblins and night-stalkers came there. Drinking the blood they began to laugh, sing and dance about.

## \|\| 1.172.17 \|\|

*ye tatra tāpasāḥ kecittaṭe tasyā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*te sarve'pi ca tāṃ tyaktā dūradeśaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A few sages who had settled on her banks abandoned her in a body and went to some far-off land.

## \|\| 1.172.18 \|\|

*bahirvāsāśca ye tatra nāgarāḥ samavasthitāḥ \|*  
*caṇḍaśarma prabhṛtayaste'pi yātāḥ sudūrataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Caṇḍaśarman and others, the Nāgaras, who had settled there as external residents, went away.

## \|\| 1.172.19 \|\|

*vasiṣṭho'pi muniśreṣṭho jagāmārbudaparvatam \|*  
*viśvāmitrastu viprarṣiścamatkārapuraṃ gataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Vasiṣṭha, the excellent sage, went to Arbuda (Abu) mountain. Viśvāmitra, the Brāhmaṇ-sage went to Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.172.20 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yatsthitaṃ viprasaṃkulam \|*  
*tatrāśramapadaṃ kṛtvā tapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There was a spot abounding in Brāhmaṇas at Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra. He built a hermitage there and performed a severe penance.

## \|\| 1.172.21-22 \|\|

*yena sṛṣṭikṣamo jātaḥ spardhate brahmaṇā saha \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā sārasvataṃ jalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rudhiratvamanuprāptaṃ viśvāmitrasya śāpataḥ \|*  
*caṃḍaśarmādayo viprā yathā deśāṃtaraṃ gatāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Thereby Viśvāmitra became capable of creating the world and (could) compete with god Brahmā (in the matter of world creation).

Thus everything has been narrated to you as to how the waters of Sarasvatī turned into blood as a result of the curse of Viśvāmitra and how Caṇḍaśarman and other Brāhmaṇas went a way to other lands.

## Chapter 173 - Sarasvatī Gets Rid of the Curse

## \|\| 1.173.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*aho bata mahāścaryaṃ viśvāmitrasya sanmuneḥ \|*  
*maṃtraprabhāvato yena tattoyaṃ rudhirīkṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥprabhṛti saṃprāptaṃ kathaṃ toyaṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*sarasvatyā mahābhāga sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. Oh, how miraculous and wonderful indeed is this! Thanks to the power of the Mantras of Viśvāmitra, the good sage, the waters thereof got turned into blood.

Now do narrate, O highly esteemed one, how the waters of Sarasvatī were re-established (on purity). Narrate everything in detail.

Sūta Said:

## \|\| 1.173.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bahukālaṃ pravāhaḥ sa sarasvatyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mahānraktamayo jāto bhūtarākṣasasevitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, for a pretty long time the stream of Sarasvatī was full of blood and it was resorted to by goblins, ghosts and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.173.4 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*arbudasthastayā prokto dīnayā duḥkhayuktayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once the excellent sage Vasiṣṭha who was staying in Arbuda was appealed by the River who was distressed and miserable:

## \|\| 1.173.5-7 \|\|

*tavārthāya mune śaptā viśvāmitreṇa kopataḥ \|*  
*rudhiraughavahājātā tapasvijanavarjitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yathā syātsalilaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*pravāhe mama viprendra prayāti rudhiraṃ kṣayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*trailokyakaraṇe vipra saṃkṣaye vā sthitau hi vā \|*  
*nāśaktirvidyate kācittava sarvamunīśvara \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. “O sage, it was for your sake that I have been cursed angrily by Viśvāmitra whereby blood began to flow in my bed and I was deserted by the community of sages.

Hence O great Brāhmaṇa, do me this favour. Let there be flow of water once again in my bed and let the blood then disappear.

O lord of all sages! You are not deficient in the ability of creation, sustenance or destruction of the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.173.8 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā syātsalilaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*pravāhe tava niryāti sarvaṃ raktaṃ parikṣayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

8\. O fair one, I shall do that whereby water will flow once again in your bed and the blood gets eliminated.

## \|\| 1.173.9 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa viprarṣiravatīrya dharātale \|*  
*gataḥ plakṣataruṃ yasmā davatīrṇā sarasvatī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying thus, the saintly Brāhmaṇa descended to the ground and went to the Plakṣa tree from which Sarasvatī flowed.

## \|\| 1.173.10 \|\|

*samādhiṃ tatra saṃdhāya niviṣṭo dharaṇītale \|*  
*saṃbhramaṃ paramaṃ gatvā viśvāmitrasya copari \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He went into Samādhi (trance) there and squattedon the ground. He was full of Saṃbhrama (fury) against Viśvāmitra.

## \|\| 1.173.11 \|\|

*vāruṇena tu mantreṇa vīkṣa yanvasudhātalam \|*  
*tato nirbhidya vasudhāṃ bhūritoyaṃ vinirgatam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Looking down at the ground he repeated the Varuṇa Mantra. Thereupon, a great stream burst open the earth and flowed out.

## \|\| 1.173.12 \|\|

*randhradvayena viprendrā locanābhyāṃ nirīkṣaṇāt \|*  
*ekasya salilaṃ kṣipraṃ yatra jātā sarasvatī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It flowed through two openings as Vasiṣṭha was looking at the ground with both of his eyes. From one flowed out water quickly which became the source of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.173.13 \|\|

*plakṣamūle tatastasya vegenāpahṛtaṃ balāt \|*  
*tadraktaṃ tena saṃpūrṇaṃ tatastena mahānadī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The blood which completely filled the great river was flushed out forcibly at (its very source at) the Plakṣa tree.

## \|\| 1.173.14 \|\|

*dvitīyastu pravāho yaḥ saṃbhramā ttasya nirgataḥ \|*  
*sā ca sābhramatī nāma nadī jātā dharātale \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The second current that had flowed out of his Saṃbhrama (fury) became river Sābhramatī (Sabaramati) on the earth.

## \|\| 1.173.15 \|\|

*evaṃ prakṛtimāpannā bhūya eva sarasvatī \|*  
*yatpṛṣṭo'smi mahābhāgāḥ sarasvatyāḥ kṛte dvijāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus Sarasvatī attained her normal state once agtain \[again\]. O highly esteemed ones, (this is what) I had been asked regarding Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.173.16 \|\|

*etatsārasvataṃ nāma vyākhyānamatibuddhidam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchraṇuyādvāpi matistasya vivarddhate \|*  
*sarasvatyāḥ prasādena satyametanma yoditam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This narrative called Sārasvata gives great intellect. One who reads or listens to it has his intellect bettered, thanks to the favour of Sarasvatī. It is the truth that I mentioned.

## Chapter 174 - Birth of Pippalāda

## \|\| 1.174.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi vo vacmi liṃgaṃ yattatra saṃsthitam \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ pippalādena kaṃsāreśvaramityaho \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: An ancient teacher, the editor of the Atharva Veda, is mentioned in Praśnopaniṣad. He subsisted on Pippala leaves and hence came to be known as Pippalāda. The derogatory Puranic account is untraceable in the Upaniṣad and in Mahābhārata.

Sūta said:

1\. Further I shall describe unto you another Liṅga established there. This Liṅga was installed by Pippalāda and is called Kaṃsāreśvara.

## \|\| 1.174.2 \|\|

*yasmindṛṣṭe tu lokānāṃ pāpaṃ yāti dinodbhavam \|*  
*nate ṣāṇmāsikaṃ caiva pūjite varṣasaṃbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. If it is visited sins of people committed on that day are dispelled; if it is bowed down to, sins of six months are eradicated and if it is adored, of the whole year (are destroyed).

The Ṛṣis Said:

## \|\| 1.174.3-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*pippalādena yalliṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ sūtanandana \|*  
*kaṃsāreśvaramityuktaṃ kasmāttacca bravīhi naḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ka eṣa pippalādastu kasya putro vadasva naḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ kṣetre tatra mahātmanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O Sūtanandana, you said that the Liṅga installed by Pippalāda is called Kaṃsāreśvara. Kindly tell us why it is so. Who is this Pippalāda? Whose son was he? Tell us for what purpose was the Liṅga installed there in that holy place by the noble-souled one.

## \|\| 1.174.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*praśnabhāro mahāneṣa bhavadbhiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi kathayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā svayaṃbhuvam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. A great burden of questions has been placed upon me by you all. I shall, however, answer after paying obeisance to the Self-born Lord.

## \|\| 1.174.6 \|\|

*yājñavalkyasyabhaginī kaṃsārīti ca viśrutā \|*  
*kumārabrahmacaryeṇa tapa stepe sudāruṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Yājñavalkya had a sister well-known as Kaṃsārī. Observing celibacy even in childhood, she performed a severe penance.

## \|\| 1.174.7-8 \|\|

*yājñavalkyāśrame puṇye bāṃdhavena samanvitā \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya yājñavalkyasya bho dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*caskanda retaḥ svapnāṃte dṛṣṭvā kāṃcidvarāpsarām \|*  
*tāruṇyabhāvasaṃsthasya tapoyuktasya saddvijāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. She stayed in the meritorious hermitage of Yājñavalkya in the company of kinsmen. Once, O Brāhmaṇas, Yājñavalkya had an emission of semen at the end of a dream when he saw an excellent Apsarā. Although he was endowed with the power of penance, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he was after all in the prime of his youth.

## \|\| 1.174.9 \|\|

*retasā tasya mahatā paridhānaṃ pariplutam \|*  
*tacca tena parityaktaṃ prabhāte samupasthite \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. His cloth got drenched with the powerful semen. Of course, at dawn he discarded that cloth.

## \|\| 1.174.10 \|\|

*kaṃsārikā'tha jagrāha snānārthaṃ vasanaṃ ca tat \|*  
*amogharetasā klinnamajānantī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. But, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Kaṃsārikā did not know that the cloth had been wetted by semen of never-failing efficacy. She took the cloth at the time of her bath.

## \|\| 1.174.11 \|\|

*kurvantyā yajanaṃ tasyā jalaṃ vīryasamanvitam \|*  
*praviṣṭaṃ bhagamadhye tu ṛtukāla upasthite \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It so happened that she was in her menstrual period then. While she was taking her plunge the water mingled with the semen entered her vagina.

## \|\| 1.174.12 \|\|

*tato garbhaḥ samabhavattasyāstūdaramadhyagaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhiṃ cāpyagamannityaṃ śuklapakṣe yathoḍurāṭ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. As a result of that she conceived a foetus in her womb. It grew up daily like the Moon in the bright half of a month.

## \|\| 1.174.13 \|\|

*sā'pi taṃ garbhamādāya svodarasthaṃ tapasvinī \|*  
*duḥkhena mahatā yuktā lajjayā'tha tadā'vṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Realizing that a child had been conceived in her womb the poor woman was extremely distressed and overcome by shame.

## \|\| 1.174.14 \|\|

*cintayāmāsa suciraṃ vismayena samanvitā \|*  
*gopāyantī tadā'tmānaṃ darśanaṃ yāti no nṛṇām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She pondered over this for a long time. She was perplexed and wondered how it had happened. Perforce she concealed herself from men and never came within their view.

## \|\| 1.174.15 \|\|

*vratacaryāmiṣaṃ kṛtvā sadā rahasi saṃsthitā \|*  
*saṃprāpte daśame māsi niśīthe samupasthite \|*  
*tasyāḥ kumārako jāto vālārkasadṛśadyutiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Under the pretext of the observance of holy vows, she always isolated herself. On the completion of ten months, at midnight, on a certain day, a boy was born to her. He had a lustre resembling that of the morning Sun.

## \|\| 1.174.16 \|\|

*atha sā taṃ samā dāya sūkṣmavastreṇa veṣṭitam \|*  
*kṛtvā jagāma cāraṇyaṃ manuṣyaparivarjitam \|*  
*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā rudantī guptameva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She covered the child with a nice cloth and took it to a forest devoid of human traffic. All the while, she was crying to herself in great wretchedness. Her eyes welled up with tears.

## \|\| 1.174.17 \|\|

*tato gatvā ca sā'śvatthaṃ vijane sumahattaram \|*  
*tasyādhastādvimucyātha vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the desolate region, she came to the foot of a great Aśvattha tree and left the child there speaking these words:

## \|\| 1.174.18-19 \|\|

*aśvattha viṣṇurūpo'si tvaṃ deveṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādrakṣasva me putraṃ sarvatastvaṃ vanaspate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*eṣa te śaraṇaṃ prāpto mama putrastu bālakaḥ \|*  
*pāpāyā nirdayāyāśca tasmādrakṣāṃ samācara \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. “O Aśvattha, you are Viṣṇu in visible form. You have a pre-eminent position among Devas. Hence, O Vanaspati (Tree), protect my son from all sides.

This child, my son, is seeking refuge in you, though I may seem to be ruthless and sinful. Do protect him.”

## \|\| 1.174.20 \|\|

*evamuktvā ruditvā ca suciraṃ sā tapasvinī \|*  
*jagāma svāśramaṃ paścādvāṣpavyākulalocanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying thus, the poor ascetic woman cried for a long time and later started towards her hermitage with her eyes dimmed by profuse tears.

## \|\| 1.174.21 \|\|

*yāvadroditi sā mātā tasyādhastādvanaspateḥ \|*  
*tāvadākāśajā vāṇī saṃjātā meghaniḥsvanā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. While the distressed mother was lamenting beneath that tree, an aerial voice arose resembling a rumbling cloud:

## \|\| 1.174.22-28 \|\|

*mā tvaṃ śokaṃ kuruṣvāsya bālakasya kṛte śubhe \|*  
*eṣa śāpādutathyasya jyeṣṭhabhrāturbṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe yogyatāṃ samavāpsyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

*eṣa cātharvaṇaṃ vedaṃ śatakalpaṃ suvistaram \|*  
*śatabhedaṃ ca navadhā paṃcakalpaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pippalasya taroreṣa rasaṃ saṃbhakṣayiṣyati \|*  
*pippalāda iti khyātastato loke bhaviṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yā tvaṃ vismayamāpannā puruṣeṇa vinā śiśuḥ \|*  
*saṃjāto'yaṃ mama prāṃśustatastatkāraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 25 \|\|*

*snānavastraṃ ca te bhrātū retasā yatpariplutam \|*  
*tattvayā ṛtukāle tu paridhānaṃ kṛtaṃ śubhe \|\| 26 \|\|*

*snānakāle tu toyāni retodakamathāspṛśan \|*  
*amogharetasā tena putro'yaṃ tava saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāge yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 28 \|\|*

22-28. “O splendid lady, do not grieve over this boy. He is the incarnation of Bṛhaspati who was cursed by his elder brother Utathya. He will occupy an honoured place on the earth. He will condense the Atharva Veda that has a hundred Śākhās and Kalpas into one of nine Śākhās and five Kalpas. He will imbibe the juice of Pippala tree and therefore will be well-known as Pippalāda.

You were wondering how a full-fledged child was born to you without (contact with) a man. Listen to the cause thereof.

The bath-towel of your brother which was drenched with his seminal discharge was worn by you during the menstrual period, O fair lady.

At the time of your bath the waters got mingled with the seminal fluid. This son of yours is the product of that never-failing seminal fluid. Now that you have understood everything, O highly esteemed lady, do what is proper in this respect.”

## \|\| 1.174.29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā devalokasyavajrapātopamaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*hāhākāraparā bhūtvā nipapāta dharātale \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

29\. On hearing the thunderbolt-like words originating from the divine region, she cried loudly and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 1.174.30 \|\|

*chinnavṛkṣalatā yadvatpatitā sā tapasvinī \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. That pitiable lady fell down like a creeper cut off from a tree.

## \|\| 1.174.31 \|\|

*cirāyantyāṃ tu tasyāṃ sa yājñavalkyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*śūnyaṃ tamāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā papracchānyānmunīśvarān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On coming to know that the hermitage was vacant and her sister was late in returning, Yājñavalkya, the great sage, asked the other sages:

## \|\| 1.174.32 \|\|

*kva ca me bhaginī yātā kaṃsārī sutapasvinī \|*  
*tayā vinā'dya me sarvaṃ śūnyamāśramamaṃḍalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “Where has my sister Kaṃsārī, the excellent ascetic woman, gone? Without her the entire penance grove has become void.”

## \|\| 1.174.33-34 \|\|

*ācakhyau tāpasaḥ kaścidbhaginī te yavīyasī \|*  
*niśceṣṭā patitā bhūmāvaśvatthasya samīpataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mayā dṛṣṭā muniśreṣṭha tāṃ tvaṃ bhāvaya mā ciram \|*  
*athāsau tvarayā yuktaḥ saṃbhrāṃtastu pradhāvitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. A certain sage announced: “Your younger sister has fallen down on the ground near the Aśvattha tree without any movement of the limbs. I saw her, O excellent sage. Save her. Do not delay.”

Thereupon he (Yājñavalkya) hastened there in bewilderment.

## \|\| 1.174.35 \|\|

*yatra sā kathitā tena tāpasena tapasvinī \|*  
*vīkṣate yāvattatrasthā śvasamānā vyavasthitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He went to the place where the ascetic had said she was lying. He saw her gasping for breath at that place.

## \|\| 1.174.36 \|\|

*atha toyena śītena secayitvā muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*dattvā bhūyo'pi vātaṃ ca yāvaccakre sacetanām \|*  
*tāvatkātyāyanī prāptā maitreyī ca sasaṃbhramam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He sprinkled her with cold water frequently and fanned her. By the time she regained consciousness Kātyāyanī and Maitreyī reached the place with great excitement.

## \|\| 1.174.37-38 \|\|

*kimidaṃ kimidaṃ jātaṃ nanāṃdarvada mā ciram \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kiṃ vā sarpeṇa daṣṭāsi sannipātena dūṣitā \|*  
*kiṃ vā bhūtagṛhītā'si māheṃdreṇa jvareṇa vā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. “What has befallen you, O sister-in-law? Tell us quickly. Were you bitten by a serpent or are you afflicted with the derangement of the three humours (Vāta, Pitta and Kapha)? Are you posessed by spirits? Or are you in the grip of the Māhendra fever?”

## \|\| 1.174.39 \|\|

*atha sā cetanāṃ labdhvā yājña valkyaṃ puraḥ sthitam \|*  
*bhāryayā sahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍayā'sūnmumoca ha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Though she had regained consciousness, she was overcome with bashfulness seeing Yājñavalkya standing in front in the company of his wives. She gave up her life.

## \|\| 1.174.40 \|\|

*atha tāṃ ca mṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā ruditvā ca ciraṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyaḥ sabhāryastu dattvā vahniṃ ca śokadhṛk \|*  
*jagāma svāśramaṃ paścāddattvā ca salilāñjalim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing her dead, O Brāhmaṇas, Yājñavalkya and his wives lamented much. They cremated her and offered libations. Eventually, they returned to their hermitage.

## \|\| 1.174.41 \|\|

*so'pi bālo'tha vavṛdhe pippalāsvādapuṣṭidhṛk \|*  
*aśvatthasya tale tasya vṛddhiṃ yāti śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. At the foot of the Aśvattha, the boy grew slowly sustaining himself by the tasty Pippala juice.

## \|\| 1.174.42 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena tena mārgeṇa cāgataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Once Nārada, the excellent sage, came that way in the course of his pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.174.43-45 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā bālakaṃ tatra dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|*  
*ekākinaṃ vane śūnye pippalāsvādatatparam \|*  
*papraccha vismayāviṣṭa ekākī ko bhavāniha \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vane śūnye mahāraudre siṃhavyāghrasamākule \|*  
*kva te mātā pitā caiva kimarthaṃ ceha tiṣṭhasi \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nivasasi kathaṃ caiva sarvaṃ me vistarādvada \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. On seeing the boy with the refulgence of twelve Suns engaged in regularly tasting the Pippala all by himself in that desolate forest, he asked in great surprise: ‘Who may you be, O lonely fellow? This is a extremely terrible desolate forest infested by lions and tigers. Why do you stay here alone? Where are your mother and father? How do you manage to live? Tell me in detail.’”

## \|\| 1.174.46 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca \|\| \|*  
*nāhaṃ jānāmi pitaraṃ mātaraṃ na ca bāṃdhavam \|*  
*nāpi tvāṃ ko'tra cā yāto mama pārśve tu sāṃpratam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Pippalāda said:

46\. I do not know my father and mother or any kinsman. Nor do I know you who came near me now.

## \|\| 1.174.47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatastaṃ prahasanprāha jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sūta said:

47\. On hearing his words the leading sage meditated for some time. When he understood everything by means of his divine vision, he laughingly said:

## \|\| 1.174.48 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*mayā jñāto'si vatsa tvaṃ yājñavalkyasya retasā \|*  
*daivayogātsamutpanno bhaginyā udare hyṛtau \|\| 48 \|\|*

Nārada said:

48\. O dear boy, I have understood who you are. The seminal fluid of Yājñavalkya gained entry into the womb of his sister entirely by chance at the time of the menstrual period. You are born thus.

## \|\| 1.174.49 \|\|

*utathyaśāpadoṣeṇa devācāryo bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*devakāryasya siddhyarthaṃ tasmāttacchṛṇu kāraṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You are the incarnation of Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of Devas (born), as a result of the curse of Utathya. It is for the accomplishment of a divine task. Listen to it.

## \|\| 1.174.50-51 \|\|

*atharvavedo yaścaiṣa śataśākho vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*śata kalpaśca gūḍhārtho bhūpānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

*navaśākhaḥ paṃcakalpastvayā kāryaḥ sukhāvahaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The Atharvaveda of a hundred Śākhās and a hundred Kalpas has been gcomposed for the accomplishment of various tasks of kings. Its meaning is incomprehensible. It should be condensed within nine Śākhās and five Kalpas so that there will be facility thereby.

## \|\| 1.174.52-54 \|\|

*tava mātrā mahābhāga retasā ca pariplutam \|*  
*yadvastraṃ yājñavalkyasya paridhānaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat \|\| 52 \|\|*

*bhaginyā sutapasvinyā snānārthaṃ na ca kāmyayā \|*  
*tadreto jalamiśraṃ tu bhagamadhye vinirgatam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*amoghaṃ tena saṃbhūtastvamatra jagatītale \|*  
*mātā vai mṛtyumāpannā jñātvaivaṃ lajjayā tayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. O highly esteemed one, your mother, the sister of Yājñavalkya, was a woman with geat \[great\] ascetic virtues. By mistake and due to no desire at all, she took the bath towel of Yājñavalkya and wore it. Earlier, that cloth had been drenched with his own seminal fluid which got mingled with water and gained entry into her vagina. It was never ineffective. You are born on the earth due to that. After realizing this, your mother became ashamed resulting in her ultimate death.

## \|\| 1.174.55 \|\|

*camatkārapure tubhyaṃ mātulo janakastathā \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhate mahābhāga tatpārśve tvamito vaja \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O highly esteemed one, your progenitor as well as maternal uncle is present at Camatkārapura now. Do go to him now.

## \|\| 1.174.56 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ vratakālaste varṣaṃ caivāṣṭamaṃ sthitam \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya lajjayā'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. This is your eighth year. It is time for religious Vratas and rites.

On hearing these words of Nārada, the boy bashfully stood with face turned down.

## \|\| 1.174.57-58 \|\|

*tataścireṇa dīnaṃ sa vākyametaduvāca tam \|*  
*kiṃ mayā pāpamākhyāhi pūrvadehāṃtare kṛtam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yenedaṃ garhitaṃ janma viyogo mātṛsaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*parityakṣyāmi jīvaṃ svaṃ duḥkhenānena sanmune \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-5 8. After a long time, he spoke to the sage these piteous words: “O excellent sage, tell me what sin was committed by me in my previous birth as a result of which this birth has been so deplorable. I am also separated from my mother. I will forsake my life on account of this misery.”

## \|\| 1.174.59 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*na tvayā duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcitpūrvadehāṃtare kṛtam \|*  
*paraṃ yena susaṃjātaṃ tavedaṃ vyasanaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 59 \|\|*

Nārada said:

59\. No sin was committed by you in the previous birth. Then why this mishap? Listen.

## \|\| 1.174.60 \|\|

*janmasthena bhavāñjātaḥ śaninā nā'tra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tenāvasthāmimāṃ prāpto nānyadasti hi kāraṇam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. You are born with Saturn in the house of nativity. There is no doubt about it. Hence you fell into this miserable plight. There is no other cause.

## \|\| 1.174.61 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvamālokayāmāsa samuddiśya śanaiścaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On hearing these words his eyes became red with anger. He looked up towards Śanaiścara (Saturn).

## \|\| 1.174.62 \|\|

*tasya dṛṣṭinipātena nyapatatsa tu tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*vimānātsvādraveḥ putro yayātiriva nāhuṣaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. As his glance fell on him, the son of Ravi (i.e. Saturn), fell down from his aerial chariot like Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa.

## \|\| 1.174.63 \|\|

*adhovaktro dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ piturādeśamāśritaḥ \|*  
*bālabhāve'pi tenaiva dagdhau pādau tadā raveḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He fell with face down, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as per the command of his father. (You may remember) in childhood the feet of Ravi had been burned by him.

## \|\| 1.174.64-65 \|\|

*atha taṃ nāradaḥ prāha patamānamadhomukham \|*  
*bālyabhāvādanena tvaṃ pātito'si śanaiścara \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tasmānmā vīkṣayasvainaṃ bhaviṣyati prakopabhāk \|*  
*mā patasva tathā bhūmau balānmadvākyasaṃbhavāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Then Nārada said to him as he fell with face down: “O Śanaiścara, it is due to the childishness of this boy that you have been made to fall down. Hence do not look at him. He will become very angry. Further, stop falling on the ground by the force of my utterance.”

## \|\| 1.174.66 \|\|

*staṃbhayitvā tathāpyevaṃ gaganasthaṃ śanaiścaram \|*  
*tataḥ provāca taṃ bālaṃ pippalādaṃ munīśvaraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After having rendered Śanaiścara stable even as he was in the sky, the leading sage spoke to the boy Pippalāda:

## \|\| 1.174.67-71 \|\|

*mā kopaṃ kuru bāla tvameṣa sūryasuto grahaḥ \|*  
*devānāmapi pīḍāṃ ca kurute'ṣṭamarāśigaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*janmasthastu viśeṣeṇa dvitīyastu tathāparaḥ \|*  
*yadyeṣa kupitastvāṃ tu vīkṣayiṣyati karhicit \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kariṣyati na saṃdeho bhasmarāśiṃ mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*anena vīkṣitau pādau jātamātreṇa sūryakau \|\| 69 \|\|*

*āyātasya tu tuṣṭasya putradarśanavāñchayā \|*  
*antardhānīkṛte vastre jñātvā taṃ raudracakṣuṣam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tato dagdhāvubhau cāpi tiṣṭhataścarma veṣṭitau \|*  
*dṛśyete'dyāpi mūrttau tau ghaṭitāyāṃ dharātale \|\| 71 \|\|*

67-71: “O boy, do not be angry. This is the Planet, son of Sun-god. When he is in the eighth house (zodiac) he inflicts pain on even the Devas.

He is all the more malific when he is in the house of nativity. Further he is so in the second house as well.

If he angrily looks at you at all, there is absolutely no doubt that he will reduce you to ash just in front of me.

Even at the time of his own birth, the feet of his father, Sun-god, were looked at by him. The father had joyously come to see his son. Knowing that he was hideous-eyed a cloth had been put over the feet: Still both of the feet were burnt. Even now they are seen covered with skin for a Ghaṭikā (short while, period of time) on the earth.”

## \|\| 1.174.72 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya nāradasya sa bālakaḥ \|*  
*bhayena mahatā yuktastataḥ papraccha taṃ munim \|\| 72 \|\|*

Sūta said:

72\. On hearing the words of Nārada, the boy was extremely frightened. He asked the sage:

## \|\| 1.174.73 \|\|

*kathaṃ yāsyati me tuṣṭiṃ vadaiṣa mama sanmune \|*  
*ajñānātpātito vyomnaḥ śaktiṃ cāsyāvijānatā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. “O excellent sage, tell me how he will be pleased with me. Unknowingly, I have caused him to fall down. I never knew his power too.”

## \|\| 1.174.74 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*grahā gāvo nareṃdrāśca brāhmaṇāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*pūjitāḥ pratipūjyaṃte nirdahaṃtyapamānitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

Nārada said:

74\. Planets, cows, kings and Brāhmaṇas in particular, honour (others) when they are honoured. If they are insulted, they burn them.

## \|\| 1.174.75 \|\|

*tasmātkuru stutiṃ cāsya svaśaktyā bhāskareḥ prabho \|*  
*prasādaṃ gacchate yena kopaṃ tyajati pātajam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Hence, O lordly boy, eulogize, according to your capacity, the son of Bhāskara, so that he will eschew the anger caused by his fall and become pleased.

## \|\| 1.174.76-77 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛtāṃjalirbhūtvā stutiṃ cakre sa bālakaḥ \|*  
*bhayena mahatā yuktastataḥ saṃpṛcchya taṃ munim \|\| 76 \|\|*

*pippalādo dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*namaste krodhasaṃsthāya piṃgalāya namo'stu te \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77a. Then the boy stood with palms joined in reverence. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this Pippalāda was extremely frightened. He took leave of the sage and bowed down to Sanaiścara repeatedly and eulogized:

77b. “Obeisance to you who are wrathful by nature. Obeisance to the Piṅgala (tawny-coloured one).

## \|\| 1.174.78 \|\|

*namaste vasurūpāya kṛṣṇāya ca namo'stu te \|*  
*namaste raudradehāya namaste cāṃtakāya ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Obeisance to the deity Babhru (deep brown) in colour. Obeisance to you, the dark-coloured one. Obeisance to you the deity with a terrible body. Obeisance to you, the destroyer.

## \|\| 1.174.79 \|\|

*namaste yamasaṃjñāya namaste sauraye vibho \|*  
*namaste mandasaṃjñāya śanaiścara namo'stu te \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Obeisance to you having the appellation ‘Yama’. Obeisance to you, O Lord, O son of Sūra (the Sun). Obeisance to you known by the appellation ‘Manda’ (slow). O Śanaiścara, I make obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.174.80 \|\|

*prasādaṃ kuru deveśa dīnasya praṇatasya ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O Lord of Devas, be pleased with this wretched (boy) who has bowed down to you.”

## \|\| 1.174.81 \|\|

*śanaiścara uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa stotreṇānena sāṃpratam \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yena yacchāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 81 \|\|*

Śanaiścara said:

81\. O dear boy, I am pleased with this eulogy of yours now. Welfare unto you. Choose your boon so that I can grant it to you.

## \|\| 1.174.82 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti no pīḍā bālānāṃ sūryanandana \|*  
*tvayā kāryā mahābhāga svakīyā ca kathaṃcana \|\| 82 \|\|*

Pippalāda said:

82\. O son of the Sun-god, from now onwards you should not inflict harassment on boys and girls,

## \|\| 1.174.83-86 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣāṣṭamaṃ jātaṃ mama vākyena sūryaja \|*  
*stotreṇānena yo'tra tvāṃ stūyātprātaḥ samutthitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*tasya pīḍā na kartavyā tvayā bhāskaranandana \|*  
*tava vāre ca saṃjāte tailābhyaṃgaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*dināṣṭakaṃ na kartavyā tasya pīḍā kathaṃcana \|*  
*yastvāṃ lohamayaṃ kṛtvā tailamadhye hyadhomukham \|\| 85 \|\|*

*dhārayettena tailena tataḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tasya pīḍā na kartavyā deyo lābho mahībhujaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

83-86. O Sūryaja, at my instance you must desist from troubling them till the eighth year.

If anyone gets up early in the morning and eulogizes you by means of this prayer, O Bhāskaranandana, you must not inflict harm to him.

If anyone takes oil bath on the day pertaining to you (i.e. Saturday), you must not afflict him for eight subsequent days.

If anyone makes an iron (metallic) image of yours, puts that image topsy-turvy into oil and then takes his bath with that oil, you must not afflict him. You must accord benefit unto kings.

## \|\| 1.174.87-90 \|\|

*adhyarddhāṣṭamikāyoge tāvake saṃsthite naraḥ \|*  
*tavavāre tu saṃprāpte yastilāṃllohasaṃyutān \|\| 87 \|\|*

*svaśaktyā rāti no tasya pīḍā kāryā tvayā vibho \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃ gāṃ yastu viprāya tavoddeśena yacchati \|\| 88 \|\|*

*adhyarddhāṣṭamajā pīḍā nā'sya kāryā tvayā vibho \|*  
*śamī samidbhiryo homaṃ tavoddeśena yacchati \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tathā kṛṣṇatilaiścaiva kṛṣṇapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ karoti yastubhyaṃ dhūpaṃ vai guggulaṃ dahet \|*  
*kṛṣṇavastreṇa saṃveṣṭya tyājyā tasya vyathā tvayā \|\| 90 \|\|*

87-90. During the seven and a half years of your malefic period, if someone tries to consume gingelly seeds with some metal on Saturdays, he should not be troubled by you, O Lord.

If anyone gives a black cow to a Brāhmaṇa with you in view, O Lord, you must desist from afflicting him during those seven and a half years.

If anyone performs Homa unto you with Śamī twigs, covers your image with black cloth, worships you with black gingelly seeds, black flowers and unguents and offers incense burning Guggulu, you must avoid harassing him.

## \|\| 1.174.91 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktaḥ śanistena bāḍhamityeva jalpya ca \|*  
*nāradaṃ samanujñāpya jagāma nijasaṃ śrayam \|\| 91 \|\|*

Sūta said:

91\. On being requested thus by him, Śani said (promised): “Of course, it will be done,” took leave of Nārada and went to his resort.

## \|\| 1.174.92 \|\|

*nārado'pi tamādāya vālakaṃ kṛpayānvitaḥ \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ gatvā yājñavalkyāya cārpayat \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Moved by compassion Nārada took that boy and went to Camatkārapura. He entrusted the boy to the care of Yājñavalkya.

## \|\| 1.174.93 \|\|

*kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ tasya saṃbhūti saṃbhavam \|*  
*yaddṛṣṭaṃ jñānadīpena tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He told him all the report concerning his birth and the like which had been seen by him with the lamp of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.174.94-95 \|\|

*eṣa te vīryasaṃbhūto bālako bhaginīsutaḥ \|*  
*mayā'śvatthatale labdhaḥ kānane'śvatthasaṃnidhau \|\| 94 \|\|*

*vratabaṃdha kuruṣvāsya sāṃprataṃ cāṣṭavārṣikaḥ \|*  
*nātra doṣosti vipreṃdra na bhaginyāstathā tava \|*  
*tasmādgṛhāṇa putraṃ svaṃ bhāgineyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. “This is your sister’s son born of your seminal fluid. I found him in the forest near an Aśvattha tree at its root.

Now he is eight years old. Perform the holy rites of Vratabandha (investiture with the sacred thread) unto him. In this affair, O great Brāhmaṇa, there is no fault of yours nor of your sister. Accept your own son who is also your nephew.”

## \|\| 1.174.96 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa devarṣistataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyo'pi tacchrutvā viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

Sūta said:

96\. After saying thus, the celestial sage vanished. On hearing all this Yājñavalkya experienced great distress and anguish.

## \|\| 1.174.97 \|\|

*pāpaṃ tacciṃtayanneva na śāṃtimadhigacchati \|*  
*ātmānaṃ garhayannityaṃ divānaktaṃ ca śocati \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Considering that a sinful incident, he had no peace of mind. He despised himself day and night and grieved over it.

## \|\| 1.174.98 \|\|

*taṃ ca putraṃ parijñāya taistaiścihnairnijaiḥ sthitaiḥ \|*  
*tatastu poṣayitvā taṃ vratena samayojayat \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Through various signs and similarities with him, he recognised him as his son. He brought him up and performed his thread ceremony.

## Chapter 175 - Gift of a Boon to Yājñavalkya

## \|\| 1.175.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃśocate yāvadātmānaṃ parigarhayan \|*  
*tatastu brahmaṇā proktaḥ svayamabhyetya bho dvijāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tvayā śaṃkā na kartavyā sutasyāsya kṛte dvija \|*  
*ajñānādeva te jāto daivayogena bālakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. O Brāhmaṇas, while he was thus denigrating himself and feeling grief-stricken, Brahmā himself came there and said: “O Brāhmaṇa, you need not feel suspicious about this boy. The boy’s birth was non-deliberate and purely accidental.”

## \|\| 1.175.3 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*tathāpi deva me śuddhirhṛdayasya na jāyate \|*  
*tasmādvada suraśreṣṭha prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

3\. Still, O Lord, my heart does not feel pacified. Hence, O most excellent one among Suras, prescribe the requisite expiatory rite.

## \|\| 1.175.4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi te cittaśuddhistu na kathaṃcitpravartate \|*  
*tatsthāpaya mahābhāga liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

4\. O highly esteemed one, if you feel that your conscience has not become clear (free from feeling of guilt) at all, install the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord.

## \|\| 1.175.5-6 \|\|

*ajñānājjñānatovāpi yatpāpaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyādikaṃ cāpi strīvadhādvāpi yadbhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*paṃceṣṭikāmayaṃ vāpi yaḥ kuryāddharamandiram \|*  
*tasya tannāśamāyāti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. When a man knowingly or unknowingly commits any sin, even if it is Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and the like or the murder of a woman, the sin can be wiped off like darkness at sunrise, if he builds a shrine of Hara though it may consist only of five bricks.

## \|\| 1.175.7 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa mahābhāga hāṭakeśvarasaṃbhave \|*  
*kṣetre tatra sumedhye tu sarvapātakanāśane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Especially, O highly esteemed one, in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, it is more effective, as it is sacred and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.175.8 \|\|

*kalikāle ca saṃprāpte yatra pāpaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*ahamapyatra vāṃchāmi yajñaṃ kartuṃ dvijottama \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Even at the advent of Kali age, there is no sin that vitiates it. I too wish to perform a Yajña here, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.175.9 \|\|

*ānayiṣyāmi tattīrthaṃ puṣkaraṃ cātmanaḥ priyam \|*  
*kalikālabhayāccaitadyāvanno vyarthatāṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I shall bring here that Puṣkara Tīrtha that is highly endearing to me, lest it should be made inefficacious due to the pernicious effect of Kali age.

## \|\| 1.175.10 \|\|

*kalikāle tu saṃprāpte tīrthāni sakalāni ca \|*  
*yāsyaṃti vyarthatāṃ vipra muktvedaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When Kali age sets in, O Brāhmaṇa, all Tīrthas except this excellent one, become inefficacious.

## \|\| 1.175.11-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā caturvaktrastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyo'pi tacchrutvā pitāmahavaco' khilam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa jñātvā kṣetramanuttamam \|*  
*abravīcca tato vākyaṃ meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11-12. Saying thus, the Four-faced One (Brahmā) vanished. After completely hearing the words of Pitāmaha Yājñavalkya was convinced that the holy spot was very excellent. So he installed the Liṅga. Thereafter, he declared thus in tone as majestic as the rumbling sound of a cloud:

## \|\| 1.175.13-14 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ yo liṃgaṃ māmakaṃ tvidam \|*  
*snāpayiṣyati sadbhaktyā tasya pāpaṃ prayāsyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paradārakṛtaṃ yacca mātrāpi ca samaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*kṣālayiṣyati tatpāpaṃ snāpitaṃ pūjitaṃ paraiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. “If anyone bathes this Liṅga of mine with great devotion on the eighth or fourteenth lunar day, his sin is destroyed.

The Liṅga that has been caused to be washed or adored by others, washes off that sin arising from habitation with other people’s wives or even with one’ own mother.

## \|\| 1.175.15 \|\|

*asminnahani saṃprāpte tasya pakṣasamudbhavam \|*  
*prayāsyati kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yadajñānādvinirmitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The adoration performed on this day wipes off the sin committed in the course of a fortnight, if it is perpetrated unknowingly.

## \|\| 1.175.16 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti vikhyāto yājñava lkyeśvaraḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*tasminkṣetre dvijaśreṣṭhā hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñake \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ever since then it is well known in that holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara as Yājñavalkyeśvara, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.”

## Chapter 176 - Origin of Kaṃsāreśvara (Kaṃsāra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.176.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṃgaṃ yājñavalkyena dhīmatā \|*  
*svamātuḥ śuddhihetoḥ sa tannāmnā liṃgamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthāpayāmāsa vipreṃdrāḥ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*tataścānīya vipreṃdraṃ madhyagaṃ nāgarodbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On seeing the Liṅga installed by the intelligent Yājñavalkya he (Pippalāda) installed a Liṅga named after his mother for the sake of her sanctification. O eminent Brāhmaṇas, he was fully endowed with perfect faith.

Thereafter, he bought an eminent Nāgara Brāhmaṇa of the middle region.

## \|\| 1.176.3-8 \|\|

*gartātīrthasamudbhūtamāhitāgniṃ prayājinam \|*  
*yathaitannagarasthānaṃ tathā tvamapi dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu gotrāṇāṃ nāyakatve vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tava vākyena sarvāṇi gotrāṇi dvijasattama \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vartayiṣyaṃti kṛtyeṣu yāvaccandrārkatārakāḥ \|*  
*govardhana tvayā ciṃtā kāryā cāsya samudbhavā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*liṃgasya pūjanārthāya preraṇīyāśca nāgarāḥ \|*  
*pūjayā tasya liṃgasya vṛddhiṃ yāsyati te'nvayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*apūjayā vināśaṃ ca yāsyatyatra na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tava vaṃśodbhavā ye ca pūjayitvā prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etalliṃgaṃ kariṣyaṃti kṛtyāni vividhānica \|*  
*tāni siddhiṃ prayāsyaṃti prasādādasya dīkṣita \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. He hailed from Gartātīrtha. He maintained the sacred fires and regularly performed Yajña. He said to him: “Just as this city is holy, so you also are initiated. You are established in the leadership of sixty-eight Gotras. (Brāhmaṇas of) all Gotras will abide by your decision (speech) in all (religious) rites till the sun, the moon and stars last.

O Govardhana, you must think about the ways and means of the worship of this Liṅga. Nāgaras should be encouraged to worship this. By the adoration of the Liṅga, your family will flourish.

By not adoring, there is no doubt about it that the family will meet with destruction. If your descendants adore this Liṅga with great devotion and then perform their various kinds of activities, O Dīkṣita, those activities will become successful, with the favour of this.”

## \|\| 1.176.9 \|\|

*govardhana uvāca \|*  
*ahamarcāṃ kariṣyāmi liṃgasyāsya sadā dvija \|*  
*bhaktiṃ ca prakariṣyāmi hetorasya hetorasya kṛte dvija \|*  
*pūjārthaṃ caiva ye cānye mama vaṃśasamudravāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Govardhana said:

9\. O Brāhmaṇa, I will always adore this Liṅga and for its sake I will extend my devout activities. So also all those born in my family (will ḍo so).

## \|\| 1.176.10 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca \|*  
*govardhana drutaṃ viprāṃstatra cānaya nāgarān \|*  
*teṣāṃ matena devasya nāmamātraṃ karomyaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

Pippalāda said:

10\. O Govardhana, bring those Nāgara Brāhmaṇas there quickly. With their permission I shall give merely the name to the deity.

## \|\| 1.176.11 \|\|

*tataścānāyayāmāsa viprāṃścaiva vicakṣaṇān \|*  
*śrutādhyayanasaṃpannānyajñakarmaparāyaṇān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He accordingly brought Brāhmaṇas expert in performing Yajña rites, rich in learning and devoted to regular recitation (of the Vedas).

## \|\| 1.176.12-14 \|\|

*tānabravītpraṇamyoccaiḥ pippalādo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*mama mātā mṛtā pūrvaṃ kaṃsārīti ca nāmataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasyā uddeśato liṃgaṃ mayaitatsaṃpratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*yuṣmadvākyātprasiddhiṃ ca prayātu dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ yaścaitatsnāpayiṣyati \|*  
*yājñavalkyeśvarotthaṃ ca sa vai śreyo hyavāpsyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. After bowing down to them, the great sage Pippalāda spoke to them loudly: “My mother named Kaṃsārī is already dead. With her in view, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this Liṅga has been installed by me. Let it become well-known by your proclamation.

He who bathes this as well as that of Yājñavalkyeśvara on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days shall attain Śreyas (spiritual perfection).”

## \|\| 1.176.15 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha tairbrāhmaṇaiḥ sarvaistasya nāma pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kaṃsārīśvara ityevaṃ gauravāttasya sanmu neḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sūta said:

15\. With due reference to that excellent sage, the name of that Liṅga was declared as Kaṃsārīśvara by all those Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.176.16 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭho'smi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kaṃsārīśvarasaṃjñastu yathā jātastu pāpahā \|*  
*sthāpitaḥ pippalādena svayaṃ caiva mahātmanā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus everything has been spoken to you, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in answer to what was asked regarding the origin of the deity named Kaṃsārīśvara and how this sin-destroying deity was installed by the noble-souled Pippalāda himself.

## \|\| 1.176.17-18 \|\|

*yaścaitatpuṇyamākhyānaṃ tasya devasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*saṃpaṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi samyakchaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*manasā ciṃtitaṃ pāpaṃ paradārakṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tasya tannāśamāyāti pippalāda vaco yathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. He who reads or listens to this meritorious narrative in the presence of that deity with great devotion, will find his mental sin of thinking erotically of other men’s wives destroyed. It is in accordance with the words of Pippalāda.

## \|\| 1.176.19-21 \|\|

*yastasya purato bhaktyā nīlarudrā nsadā japet \|*  
*prāṇarudrānviśeṣeṇa bhavarudrasamanvitān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*brahmahatyodbhavaṃ caiva api tasya praṇaśyati \|*  
*paracakrabhaye jāte hyanā vṛṣṭibhaye tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*atharvavede sādyaṃte paṭhite tasya cāgrataḥ \|*  
*śatrurvilayamabhyeti vṛṣṭiḥ sañjāyate drutam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. If a devotee recites in front of him Nīlarudra Mantras and Prāṇarudras along with Bhavarudra Mantras, even the sin arising from Brāhmaṇa-slaughter perishes. When there is danger from hostile kings as well as from severe drought, Atharva Veda shouild be recited from the beginning to the end. The enemy gets destroyed and it rains immediately in showers.

## \|\| 1.176.22 \|\|

*rājadauḥsthye samutpanne rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*sarvarogavinirmuktaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If a king happens to be in a difficult situation (or ill health) he should be righteous and should be devoted to the protection of the subjects. He shall then be rid of all his ailments.

## \|\| 1.176.23 \|\|

*upasargabhaye jāte tasya doṣaḥ praśāmyati \|*  
*śanaiḥ śanairasaṃdigdhaṃ pippalādavaco yathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If there occurs adverse effect of divine calamity, it shall disappear gradually as Pippalāda himself has said.

## \|\| 1.176.24-25 \|\|

*kiṃ vā te bahunoktena yatkiṃcidvyasanaṃ mahat \|*  
*tattasya vyasanaṃ kiṃcidatharvaṇaḥ prakī rtanāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

*asya devasya purato yāti nāśaṃ ca vai drutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Of what avail is much talk? Whatever great mishap occurs shall get quickly dissolved (removed) by reciting the Atharva Veda before this deity.

## Chapter 177 - Creation of Pañcapiṇḍikā

## \|\| 1.177.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti gaurī vai pañcapiṃḍikā \|*  
*lakṣmyā saṃsthāpitā caiva mānuṣatvaṃvyavasthayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasyā darśanamātreṇa nārī saubhāgyamāmuyāt \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe vṛṣasthe ca divākare \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasyā upari nārī yā jalayantraṃ dadhāti vai \|*  
*srāvyamāṇaṃ divānaktaṃ saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ labhet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2a. Further, there is the deity Gaurī called Pañcapiṇḍikā there itself. The image was installed by Lakṣmī who was in human form. Merely by visiting that deity, a woman attains conjugal felicity.

2b-3. A woman-devotee should place the Jalayantra (a pitcher with a hole at the bottom allowing water to trickle drop by drop on the deity below) above the deity in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha when the Sun is in the zodiac Taurus. It shall trickle day and night. The woman shall attain greatest conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.177.4 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ labhate nārī samastairvihitairvrataiḥ \|*  
*gaurīsamudbhavaiścaiva dānairdattaistadiṣṭajaiḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate sarvaṃ jalayantrasya kāraṇāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By offering Jalayantra, a woman obtains the whole of that benefit which she is likely to obtain through the performance of all the Vratas pertaining to Gaurī and making gifts of their choice.

## \|\| 1.177.5 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena strībhiḥ saubhāgyakāraṇāt \|*  
*jalayantraṃ vidhātavyaṃ jyeṣṭhe gauryāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hence in the month of Jyeṣṭha a Jalayantra should be offered assiduously to Gaurī by women for the sake of conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.177.6-7 \|\|

*kiṃ vratairniyamairvāpi strīṇāṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*japairhomaiḥ kṛtairanyairbahukleśakaraiśca taiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*strīṇāṃ brāhmaṇaśārdūlā jaleyantre dhṛte sati \|*  
*gauryā upari sadbhaktyā vṛṣasthe tīkṣṇadīdhitau \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, of what avail is the performance of other Vratas, Niyamas, Japas and Homas in the case of women? They are but causes of great pain and strain. At a time when the Fierce-rayed One (Sun) is in Taurus if a Jalayantra is placed over Gaurī’s (image) with excellent devotion, it is meritorious, O tigers among Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.177.8 \|\|

*naivaṃ saṃjāyate vaṃdhyā kākavandhyā na jāyate \|*  
*na daurbhāgyasamopetā saptajanmāṃtarāṇi sā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If that be done, no woman becomes barren or Kāka Vandhyā (having only one child) or one afflicted by misfortune (e.g. death of husband) all through seven births.

## \|\| 1.177.9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*gaurī caturbhujā proktā dṛśyate parameśvarī \|*  
*pañcapiṃḍā kathaṃ jātā hyetaṃ naḥ saṃśayaṃ vada \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:

9\. Gaurī, the great goddess, is said to be and is seen as four-armed. How did it happen that she is Pañcapiṇḍā too? Do clarify this doubt of ours.

## \|\| 1.177.10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā ca pralayo bhāvi tadā tmānaṃ karotyasau \|*  
*paścapiṃḍīmayaṃ viprāḥ kurute rūpamuttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

10\. O Brāhmaṇas, when Pralaya occurs she makes herself Pañcapiṇḍīmaya (consisting of five lumps); she assumes this excellent form.

## \|\| 1.177.11 \|\|

*eṣā sā paramā śaktiḥ sarvaṃ vyāpya sureśvarī \|*  
*tayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She is that great Śakti, the goddess of Suras; she pervades everything. The entire range of the three worlds including mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by her.

## \|\| 1.177.12 \|\|

*pṛthivyāpaśca tejaśca vāyurākāśameva ca \|*  
*sṛṣṭyarthaṃ rakṣayedeṣā tataḥ syātpaṃcapiṃḍikā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For the purpose of creation, she preserves the five elements viz. earth, water, fire, wind and ether. Hence, she is Pañcapiṇḍikā.

## \|\| 1.177.13 \|\|

*yadasyāṃ pūjitāyāṃ tu pratyakṣāyāṃ prajāyate \|*  
*sahasratriguṇaṃ tacca yatra syātpañcapiṇḍikā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If the Pañcapiṇḍikā is worshipped, the merit is three thousand times more than when she is directly worshipped.

## \|\| 1.177.14 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi viśeṣeṇa jalayaṃtrārcanena ca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi tviti hāsaṃ purātanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The worship is to be carried out in the month of Jyeṣṭha, especially with the use of a Jalayantra. In this connection, I shall narrate unto you an ancient legend.

## \|\| 1.177.15 \|\|

*yadvṛttaṃ kāśirājasya bhāryāyā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*yacca proktaṃ purā lakṣmyā viṣṇave paripṛṣṭayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this befell the wife of the king of Kāśā and this was earlier narrated by Lakṣmī to Viṣṇu on being asked.

## \|\| 1.177.16 \|\|

*lakṣmī ruvāca \|*  
*kāśirājaḥ purā hyāsījjayasena iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryāsahasraṃ tu hyāsīdrūpasamanvitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Lakṣmī said:

16\. Formerly, there was a king of Kāśī well-known by the name Jayasena. He had a thousand wives of excellent beauty.

## \|\| 1.177.17 \|\|

*atha cānyā priyā tena labdhā bhāryā suśobhanā \|*  
*manuṣyatvavyavasthāyā mama cāṃśakalā hi yā \|*  
*sutā madrādhirājasya viṣvaksenasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then he acquired another splendid beloved wife. She was a part of my Kalā, in the form of a human being. She was the daughter of Viṣvaksena, the intelligent king of Madra.

## \|\| 1.177.18 \|\|

*sā gatvā prātarutthāya śubhe gaṃgātaṭe tadā \|*  
*pañcapiṃḍātmikāṃ gaurīṃ kṛtvā karddamasaṃbhavām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She used to get up early in the morning and go to the splendid banks of Gaṅgā. She then made the image of Gaurī with five lumps of clay out of the mud from the river.

## \|\| 1.177.19-21 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsa mantraiḥ paṃcabhireva ca \|*  
*tato gandhaiḥ parairmālyairdhūpai rvastraiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*naivedyaiḥ paramānnaiśca gītairnṛtyaiḥ pravāditaiḥ \|*  
*tato visṛjya tāṃ devīṃ taduddeśena vai tataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dattvā dānāni bhūrīṇi gauriṇīnāṃ dvijanmanām \|*  
*tataśca gṛhamabhyeti bhūrivāditraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21.
