*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pulastyaḥ satvaraṃ yayau \|*  
*sāvitrī tiṣṭhate yatra gītanṛtyasamākulā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing his words Pulastya hastened to the place where Sāvitrī was present engrossed in songs and dances.

## \|\| 1.181.44-45 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca kiṃ devi tvaṃ tiṣṭhasi nirākulā \|*  
*yajñayānocitaḥ kālaḥ so'yaṃ śeṣastu tiṣṭhati \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmādāgaccha gacchāmastātaḥ kṛcchreṇa tiṣṭhati \|*  
*somabhārārdditaścordhvaṃ sarvairdevaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. He said then: “O goddess, why do you stand thus unmoved? Very little time is left for the Muhūrta proper for the procedure of Yajñayāna. Hence come (hurry up). We shall go. Father is excessively agitated and afflicted with the weight of the Soma kept over (his head). He is surrounded by all the Devas.”

## \|\| 1.181.46 \|\|

*sāvitryuvāca \|*  
*sarvadevavṛtastāta tava tāto vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*ekākinī kathaṃ tatra gacchāmyahamanāthavat \|\| 46 \|\|*

Sāvitrī said:

46\. Dear Son, your father being surrounded by all the Devas is settled well. How can I go there all by myself like a helpless person?

## \|\| 1.181.47 \|\|

*tadbrūhi pitaraṃ gatvā muhūrtaṃ paripālyatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Go and tell father to be patient for a short while.

## \|\| 1.181.48 \|\|

*yāvadabhyeti śakrāṇī gaurī lakṣmīstathā parāḥ \|*  
*devakanyāḥ samāje'tra tābhireṣyāmyaha8drutam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. (He may be pleased to wait) till Śakrāṇī, Gaurī, Lakṣmī and other celestial women gather together in our assembly. I shall come quickly along with them.

## \|\| 1.181.49 \|\|

*sarvāsāṃ preṣito vāyurnimatraṇakṛte mayā \|*  
*āgamiṣyanti tāḥ śīghramevaṃ vācyaḥ pitā tvayā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. May your father be informed that Vāyu has been sent by me to invite all of them. They will come presently.

## \|\| 1.181.50-51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*so'pi gatvā drutaṃ prāha somabhārārditaṃ vidhim \|*  
*naiṣābhyeti jagannātha prasaktā gṛhakarmaṇi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sā māṃ prāha ca devānāṃ patnībhiḥ sahitā makhe \|*  
*ahaṃ yāsyāmi tāsāṃ ca naikādyāpi pradṛśyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sūta said:

50-51. He hastened to Vidhi who was afflicted with the burden of Soma: “O Lord of the universe, she is engaged in her domestic chores. She is not coming. She tells me, ‘I will attend the Makha along with the wives of the Devas. But none of them is seen so far.’

## \|\| 1.181.52 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā suraśreṣṭha kuru yatte surocate \|*  
*atikrāmati kālo'yaṃ yajñayānasamudravaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhate ca gṛhavyagrā sāpi strī śithilātmikā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Know this, O most excellent one among Suras, and do what pleases you the most. It is rather getting very late for the procedure of the Yajña rite. That woman in her dilatoriness is busy with her domestic chores.”

## \|\| 1.181.53 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya pulastyasya pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*samīpasthaṃ tadā śakraṃ provāca vacanaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On hearing the words of Pulastya, Pitāmaha spoke to Śakra who was nearby, O Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.181.54 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śakra nāyāti sāvitrī sāpi strī śithilātmikā \|*  
*anayā bhāryayā yajño mayā kāryo'yameva tu \|\| 54 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

54\. O Śakra, Sāvitrī has not come. She is rather a dilatory woman. But, am I to perform this Yajña with such a wife?

## \|\| 1.181.55 \|\|

*gaccha śakra samānīhi kanyāṃ kāṃcittvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*yāvanna kramate kālo yajñayānasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O Śakra, go and fetch some other girl quickly so that the auspicious hour for Yajña does not slip away.

## \|\| 1.181.56 \|\|

*pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā tadarthaṃ kanyakā dvijāḥ \|*  
*śakreṇāsāditā śīghraṃ bhramamāṇā samīpataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On hearing the words of Pitāmaha, O Brāhmaṇas, (Śakra went in search) of such a girl. Soon she was met by him, as she wandered nearby.

## \|\| 1.181.57 \|\|

*atha takraghaṭavyagramastakā tena vīkṣitā \|*  
*kanyakā gopajā tanvī caṃdrāsyā padmalocanā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. She was a slim cowherd lass, lotus-eyed and moonfaced. A pot of curd was on her head and she was scrupulously taking care of it.

## \|\| 1.181.58-59 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā yauvanāraṃbhamāśritā \|*  
*sā śakreṇātha saṃpṛṣṭā kā tvaṃ kamalalocane \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kumārī vā sanāthā vā sutā kasya bravīhi naḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. She was at the threshold to the prime of youth. She was endowed with full complement of all auspicious features. She was asked by Śakra: “O lotus-eyed one, who may you be? Are you a virgin or a married one with a husband? Tell me, whose daughter are you?”

## \|\| 1.181.60 \|\|

*kanyo vāca \|*  
*gopakanyāsmi bhadraṃ te takraṃ vikretumāgatā \|*  
*yadi gṛhṇāsi me mūlyaṃ tacchīghraṃ dehi mā ciram \|\| 60 \|\|*

The girl said:

60\. I am daughter of a cowherd. Welfare unto you. I have come here to sell buttermilk. If you want it, pay me the cost thereof. Do not delay.

## \|\| 1.181.61 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tridivendro'pi matvā tāṃ gopakanyakām \|*  
*jagṛhe tvarayā yuktastakraṃ cotsṛjya bhūtale \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On hearing it, the Lord of Heaven came to know she was daughter of a cowherd. He seized her quickly and split all the buttermilk on the ground.

## \|\| 1.181.62 \|\|

*atha tāṃ rudatīṃ śakraḥ samādāya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*govaktreṇa praveśyātha guhyenākarṣayattataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Even as she went on crying Śakra seized her, forced her through the mouth of a cow and dragged her out of the anus.

## \|\| 1.181.63 \|\|

*evaṃ medhyatamāṃ kṛtvā saṃsnāpya salilaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhakuṇḍasya viprendrāḥ paridhāyya suvāsasī \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After sanctifying her thus, O leading Brāhmaṇas, he bathed her in the auspicious waters of the first Kuṇḍa and made her wear excellent garments.

## \|\| 1.181.64 \|\|

*tataśca harṣasaṃyuktaḥ provāca caturānanam \|*  
*drutaṃ gatvā puro dhṛtvā sarvadevasamāgame \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then he joyously spoke to the Four-faced One hastening to him and placing her in front in the assembly of all the Devas:

## \|\| 1.181.65-66 \|\|

*kanyakeyaṃ suraśreṣṭha samānītā mayā'dhunā \|*  
*tavārthāya surūpāṃgī sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*gopakanyā viditvemāṃ govaktreṇa praveśya ca \|*  
*ākarṣitā ca guhyena pāvanārthaṃ caturmukha \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. “O excellent one among Suras, this girl has been brought by me now for your sake. She is comely in her limbs and is marked by all the auspicious features.

Knowing that she is daughter of a cowherd, O Four-faced One, she was forced through the mouth of a cow and then dragged out through the anus for the purpose of sanctifying her.”

## \|\| 1.181.67 \|\|

*śrīvāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*gavāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kulamekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam \|*  
*ekatra maṃtrāstiṣṭhaṃti haviranyatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 67 \|\|*

Śrī Vāsudeva said:

67\. Cows and Brāhmaṇas belong to the same family. It is split into two, the Mantras abide in one, while the Havis abides in the other.

## \|\| 1.181.68 \|\|

*dhenūdarādviniṣkrāṃtā tajjāteyaṃ dvijanmanām \|*  
*asyāḥ pāṇigrahaṃ deva tvaṃ kuruṣva makhāptaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Coming out of the belly of a cow this girl has become a daughter of Brāhmaṇas. Grasp her hand, O Lord, for the fulfilment of the Makha.

## \|\| 1.181.69 \|\|

*yāvanna calate kālo yajñayānasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Let it be before the auspicious hour for the performance of the Yajña slips by.

## \|\| 1.181.70 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*praviṣṭā gomukhe yasmādapānena vinirgatā \|*  
*gāyatrīnāma te patnī tasmādeṣā bhaviṣyati \|\| 70 \|\|*

Rudra said:

70\. She entered the mouth of a cow and came out of the anus. Hence, she is named Gāyatrī. She shall become your wife.

## \|\| 1.181.71 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vadantu brāhmaṇāḥ sarve gopakanyāpyasau yadi \|*  
*saṃbhūya brāhmaṇīśreṣṭhā yathā patnī bhavenmama \|\| 71 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

71\. May all the Brāhmaṇas say collectively that though she is the daughter of a cowherd she has become an excellent Brāhmaṇa girl so that she can be my wife.

## \|\| 1.181.72 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*eṣā syādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā gopajātivivarjitā \|*  
*asmadvākyāccaturvaktra kuru pāṇigrahaṃ drutam \|\| 72 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

72\. She shall be an excellent Brāhmaṇa woman free from the nativity of a cowherd. At our instance, O Four-faced One, marry her quickly.

## \|\| 1.181.73 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ pāṇigrahaṃ cakre tasyā devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā somaṃ tato mūrdhni gṛhyoktavidhinā dvijāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Sūta said:

73\. Then Lord Pitāmaha married her. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, he held the Soma above the head in the manner it has been enjoined in the Gṛhya Sūtras.

## \|\| 1.181.74 \|\|

*saṃtiṣṭhati ca tatrasthā mahādevī supāvanī \|*  
*adyāpi loke vikhyātā dhanasaubhāgyadāyinī \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The sacred great goddess is standing there even today. She is well-known as the bestower of wealth and conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.181.75 \|\|

*yastasyāṃ kurute martyaḥ kanyādānaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*samastaṃ phalamāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A man who makes the gift of a virgin there with great concentration, shall derive the entire benefit of a Rājasūya and horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.181.76 \|\|

*kanyā hastagrahaṃ tatra yā'pnoti patinā saha \|*  
*sā syātputravatī sādhvī sukhasaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The girl who gets married there shall be blessed with sons, happiness and conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.181.77 \|\|

*piṃḍadānaṃ narastasyāṃ yaḥ karoti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pitarastasya saṃtuṣṭāstarpitāḥ pitṛtīrthavat \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, if a man offers balls of rice there the Pitṛs become pleased with him as though libations were offered in a Pitṛtīrtha.

## Chapter 182 - The Yajña of Brahmā: The First Day

## \|\| 1.182.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ patnīṃ samāsādya gāyatrīṃ caturānanaḥ \|*  
*saṃprahṛṣṭamanā bhūtvā prasthito yajñamaṇḍapam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. After having secured Gāyatrī as his wife, the Four-faced Lord became highly delighted in his mind. He started towards the pavilion of sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.182.2 \|\|

*gāyatryapi samādāya mūrdhni tāmaraṇiṃ mudā \|*  
*pratasthe saṃparityajya gopabhāvaṃ vigarhitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Gāyatrī eschewed the despicable state of a cowherdess and proceeded ahead joyously holding the Araṇi on the head.

## \|\| 1.182.3-4 \|\|

*vādyamāneṣu vādyeṣu brahmaghoṣe divaṃgate \|*  
*kalaṃ pragāyamāneṣu gandharveṣu samaṃtataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sarvadevadvijopetaḥ saṃprāpto yajñamaṇḍape \|*  
*gāyatryā sahito brahmā mānuṣaṃ bhāvamāśritaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Even as the musical instruments were played and the chanting of the Vedas reached the vaults of heaven and the Gandharvas were singing sweetly all round, Brahmā in the assumed form of a human being reached the Yajña Maṇḍapa accompanied by Gāyatrī and all the Devas and the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.182.5 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare cakre keśanirvapaṇaṃ vidheḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmā nakhānāṃ ca gāyatryāstadanaṃtaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the meantime, Viśvakarmā cut the hair of Vidhi and pared the nails of Gāyatrī after him.

## \|\| 1.182.6 \|\|

*audumbaraṃ tato daṇḍaṃ pulastyo'smai samādade \|*  
*eṇaśṛṃgānvitaṃ carma mantravadvijasattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Pulastya handed the Audumbara staff along with the Mantra-charged hide of a deer together with its horns.

## \|\| 1.182.7 \|\|

*patnīśālāṃ gṛhītvā ca gāyatrīṃ maunadhāriṇīm \|*  
*mekhalāṃ nidadhe cānyāṃ kaṭyāṃ mauṃjīmayīṃ śubhām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Gāyatrī was taken to the Patnīśālā even as she observed silence. A splendid girdle of the Muñja grass was tied round her waist.

## \|\| 1.182.8 \|\|

*tataścakre paraṃ karma yaduktaṃ yajñamaṃḍape \|*  
*ṛtvigbhiḥ sahito vedhā vedavākyasamādṛtaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Accompanied by the Ṛtviks, Vedhas (Brahmā) respectfully followed the instructions in the Vedas. He performed the later rites in the Yajña Maṇḍapa.

## \|\| 1.182.9-10 \|\|

*pravargye jāyamāne ca tatrāścaryamabhūnmahat \|*  
*jālmarūpadharaḥ kaściddigvāsā vikṛtānanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kapālapāṇirāyāto bhojanaṃ dīyatāmiti \|*  
*niṣedhyamāno'pi ca taiḥ praviṣṭo yājñikaṃ sadaḥ \|*  
*sa kṛtvā'ṭanamanyāyyaṃ tarjyamāno'pi tāpasaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. While Pravargya (a prelude to Soma Sacrifice) was begun a miracle took place there. A nude fellow with a hideous face appeared in his hand and requested, “Food may kindly be given.” He entered the sacrificial chamber though he was prevented. Though he was threatened by the sages, he wandered there freely and unjustifiably.

## \|\| 1.182.11 \|\|

*sadasyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmātpāpasametastvaṃ praviṣṭo yajñamaṇḍape \|*  
*kapālī nagnarūpo yo yajñakarmavivarjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The Sadasyas (members of the Assembly) said:

11\. “Why have you, O sinner, entered the Yajña pavilion nude in form, holding a skull and bereft of all experience in Yajña rite?

## \|\| 1.182.12 \|\|

*tasmādgaccha drutaṃ mūḍha yāvadbrahmā na kupyati \|*  
*tathā'nye brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāstathā devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O fool, go away quickly before Brahmā becomes angry. Others like the excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Devas including Vāsava also may be furious.”

## \|\| 1.182.13 \|\|

*jālma uvāca \|*  
*brahmayajñamimaṃ śrutvā dūrādatra samāgataḥ \|*  
*bubhukṣito dvijaśreṣṭhāstatkimarthaṃ vigarhatha \|\| 13 \|\|*

The Rogue said:

13\. I heard about the Yajña of Brahmā and have come here from very far. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I am hungry. Why should you censure me?

## \|\| 1.182.14 \|\|

*dīnāṃdhaiḥ kṛpaṇaiḥ savairstarpitaiḥ kraturucyate \|*  
*anyathā'sau vināśāya yaduktaṃ brāhmaṇairvacaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This rite is called Kratu when the wretched ones, the blind and the miserable ones are propitiated. If that is not the case, that should be conducive to destruction as per these words mentioned by Brāhmaṇas:

## \|\| 1.182.15 \|\|

*annahīno dahedrāṣṭaṃ mantrahīnastu ṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*yājñikaṃ dakṣiṇā hīno nāsti yajñasamo ripuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “There is no other enemy on a par with Yajña. If it is without food supply, it will burn the nation. If it is without Mantras, it will burn the Ṛtviks. If it is without monetary gifts, it will destroy the performer of the Yajña.”

## \|\| 1.182.16 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi tvaṃ bhoktukāmastu samāyāto vraja drutam \|*  
*etasyāṃ satraśālāyāṃ bhuñjate yatra tāpasāḥ \|*  
*dīnāndhāḥ kṛpaṇāścaiva tataḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṃṭhitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

16\. If you have come here with a desire to eat then go quickly to this Sattraśālā (Sacrificial hall) where the ascetics, the blind, the wretched and the miserable ones with parched throats due to hunger, are taking their food.

## \|\| 1.182.17 \|\|

*athavā dhanakāmastvaṃ vastrakāmo'tha tāpasa \|*  
*vraja vittapatiryatra dānaśālāṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Or, O sage, if you are desirous of money or garments go to the place in the Dānaśālā (chamber of gifts) where the Vittapati (Lord of wealth, Kubera) is present.

## \|\| 1.182.18 \|\|

*aniṃdyo'yaṃ mahāmūrkha yajñaḥ paitāmaho yataḥ \|*  
*arcitaḥ sarvataḥ puṇyaṃ tatkiṃ nindasi durmate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O great fool, this Yajña of Pitāmaha is uncensurable. It is venerated all round. O wicked-minded one, why do you censure this meritorious thing?

## \|\| 1.182.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktaḥ kapālaṃ sa parikṣipya dharātale \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ sadyo dīpavaddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, on being told thus, he threw down the skull on the ground and vanished immediately like a lamp.

## \|\| 1.182.20 \|\|

*ṛtvija ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ yajñakriyā kāryā kapāle sadasi sthite \|*  
*parikṣipatha tasmāttu evamūcurdvijottamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

The Ṛtviks said:

20\. How can the sacrificial rite proceed as long as the skull lies in the main Sadas (chamber)? Hence, throw it away, said the excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.182.21 \|\|

*athaiko bahudhā proktaḥ sadasyaiśca dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ samudyamya pracikṣepa bahistathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One of them who was repeatedly told thus by the excellent Brāhmana members of the assembly, lifted up a stick and pushed it out.

## \|\| 1.182.22 \|\|

*athānyattatra saṃjātaṃ kapālaṃ tādṛśaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tasminnapi tathā kṣipte bhūyo'nyatsamapadyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then another skull like this one cropped up there. When it was pushed away, another skull took its place.

## \|\| 1.182.23 \|\|

*evaṃ śatasahasrāṇi hyayutānyarbudāni ca \|*  
*tatra jātāni tairvyāpto yajñavāṭaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus hand reds, thousands, ten thousands and millions of skulls rose up there. The Yajñavāṭa (the premises of Yajña) was filled with them all round.

## \|\| 1.182.24 \|\|

*hāhākārastatau jajñe samaste yajñamaṇḍape \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kapālasaṃghāṃstānyajña karmapradūṣakān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A great hue and cry arose in the entire Yajña pavilion on seeing heaps on heaps of skulls that defiled the sacrificial rite.

## \|\| 1.182.25-26 \|\|

*atha saṃciṃtayāmāsa dhyānaṃ kṛtvā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*harāriṣṭaṃ samājñāya tatsarvaṃ hṛṣṭarūpadhṛk \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā tataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*maheśvaraṃ samāsādya yajñavāṭasamāśritam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Then Pitāmaha meditated and thought. He came to know that everything calamitous was thus caused by Hara. He joined his palms in veneration and spoke to Maheśvara joyously and respectfully. Maheśvara was then in the precincts of the Yajñavāṭa.

## \|\| 1.182.27-28 \|\|

*kimidaṃ yujyate deva yajñe'sminkarmaṇaḥ kṣatiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsaṃhara sarvāṇi kapālāni sureśvara \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yajñakarmavilopo'yaṃ mā bhūttvayi samāgate \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. “O Lord, is it proper that there should be deficiency in the rites concerning the Yajña? Hence, O Lord of Suras, withdraw all the skulls. Let there not be omissions in the Yajña rites even when you have arrived.”

## \|\| 1.182.29-33 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca saṃkruddho bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*tanmameṣṭatamaṃ pātraṃ bhojanāya sadā sthitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ete dvijādhamāḥ kasmādvidviṣaṃtipitāmaha \|*  
*tathā na māṃ samuddiśya juhuvurjātavedasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yathānyādevatā stadvanmantrapūtaṃ havirvidhe \|*  
*tasmādyadi vidhe kāryā samāptiryajñakarmaṇi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatkapālāśritaṃ havyaṃ kartavyaṃ sakalaṃ tvidam \|*  
*tathā ca māṃ samu ddiśya viśaṣājjātavedasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

*hotavyaṃ havirevātra samāptiṃ yāsyati kratuḥ \|*  
*nānyathā satyamevoktaṃ tavāgre caturānana \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. Thereupon, the Moon-crested Lord said angrily: “That is my favourite bowl of food. It has always been so. O Pitāmaha, why do these base Brāhmaṇas hate me? They did not offer oblations (saying Svāhā) into the fire with me in view.

O Vidhi (Drahmā), the Havis offering charged and sanctified with Mantras have not been made to me as (they have done) in the case of other deities. So do you wish that the Yajña rite should be concluded?

Then all the Havyas should be put in those skulls. Further with me in view, a special Homa should be offered in the sacred fire. Then the Kratu will be concluded; not otherwise. O Four-faced One, the truth has been spoken to you.”

## \|\| 1.182.34 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca \|*  
*rūpāṇi tava deveśa pṛthagbhūtānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*saṃkhyayā parihīnāni dhyeyāni sakalāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

Pitāmaha said:

34\. O Lord of Devas, your forms are myriad and different. There is no limit to their number and all of them are to be meditated upon.

## \|\| 1.182.35-36 \|\|

*etanmahāvrataṃ rūpamākhyātaṃ te trilocana \|*  
*naivaṃ ca makhakarma syāttatraiva ca na yujyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

*adyaitatkarma kartuṃ ca śrutibāhyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*tava vākyamapi tryakṣa nānyathā kartumu tsahe \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. O Three-eyed One, this is called your Mahāvrata. In this manner it shall not be a Makha rite and it is not proper to perform this rite as being outside the scope of the Vedic injunction. But, O three-eyed One, I do not intend to go against your behest.

## \|\| 1.182.37 \|\|

*mṛnmayeṣu kapāleṣu haviḥ śrāpyaṃ sureśvara \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti yajñeṣu puroḍāśātmikaṃ dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tavoddeśena deveśa hotavyaṃ śatarudri yam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. So, O Lord of Suras, the Havis may be cooked in a Kapāla of clay (potsherd). That is, the Puroḍāśa should be cooked in them from now onwards by the Brāhmaṇas. When it refers to the Yajña, O most excellent one among Suras, O Lord of Devas, with you in view the Śatarudriya should be chanted while performing Homa.

## \|\| 1.182.38-39 \|\|

*viśeṣātsarvayajñeṣu japyaṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kapālānāṃ tu dvāreṇa tvayā rūpaṃ nijaṃ kṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*prakaṭaṃ ca suraśreṣṭha kapāle śvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ bhavitā rudra kṣetre'smindvādaśo'paraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. In the course of all the Yajñas, it should be recited in particular. By means of these Kapālas (skulls), O most excellent one among Suras, your own real form has been revealed by you. Hence, O Rudra, you will be named Kapāleśvara in this holy spot, a twelfth among them.

## \|\| 1.182.40 \|\|

*atra yajñaṃ samārabhya yastvāṃ prākpūjayiṣyati \|*  
*avighnena makha stasya samāptiṃ pravrajiṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If anyone begins a Yajña here and worships you at the outset, his Ṃakha will be named Kapāleśvara.

## \|\| 1.182.41 \|\|

*evamukte tatastena kapālāni dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi naṣṭāni saṃkhyayā rahitāni ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. When this was spoken by him, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, all the skulls, unlimited in number, vanished.

## \|\| 1.182.42 \|\|

*tato hṛṣṭaścaturvaktraḥ sthāpayāmāsa tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*ligaṃ māheśvaraṃ tatra kapāleśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then, the delighted Four-faced God immediately installed the Liṅga of Maheśvara there, called Kapāleśvara.

## \|\| 1.182.43-44 \|\|

*abravīcca tato vākyaṃ yaścaitatpūjayiṣyati \|*  
*mama kuṇḍatraye snātvā sa yāsyati parāṃ gatim \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ kārtike jāgaraṃ tu yaḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati punaścāsya liṃgasya susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*ājanmaprabhavātpāpātsa vimuktimavāpsyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. And he said: “He who, after taking bath in my Kuṇḍas, worships this Liṅga, will attain the greatest goal. He who performs the Jāgara (keeping awake) rite on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika with great concentration in front of this Liṅga, will get rid of all the sins since his birth.”

## \|\| 1.182.45 \|\|

*evamukte'tha vidhinā prahṛṣṭastripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*yajñamaṇḍapamāsādya prasthito vedisaṃnidhau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. When this was spoken by Vidhi, the Slayer of the Tripuras became very delighted. Reaching the Yajña Ṃaṇḍapa he went near the Vedi (Altar).

## \|\| 1.182.46 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaiśca tataḥ karma prārabdhaṃ yajñasambhavam \|*  
*vismayotphullanayanairnamaskṛtya maheśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then, after duly bowing down to Maheśvara the Yajña rites were started by the Brāhmaṇas with their eyes beaming with pleasant surprise.

## \|\| 1.182.47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ ca yaja tastasya caturvaktrasya tatra ca \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ koṭirāyātā dakṣiṇāpathavāsinām \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sūta said:

47\. Even as the Four-faced One was performing the Yajña there in this manner, there came a crore of sages, the inhabitants of the southern region.

## \|\| 1.182.48-49 \|\|

*śrutvā paitāmahaṃ yajñaṃ kautukena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśo bhavitā yajño dīkṣito yatra padmajaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kīdṛkkṣetraṃ ca tatpuṇyaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*kīdṛśāste ca viprendrā ṛtvijastatra ye sthitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. On hearing about the Yajña of Pitāmaha they became inquisitive: “How will this Yajña be, where the Lotus-born Lord himself has become initiated? Of what nature is that meritorious holy place named Hāṭakeśvara? Of what nature are those leading Brāhmaṇas appointed there as the Ṛtviks?”

## \|\| 1.182.50-51 \|\|

*atha te supariśrāṃtā madhyaṃdinagate ravau \|*  
*ravivāreṇa saṃprāpte nakṣatre cāśvisaṃsthite \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vaivasvatyāṃ tithau caiva prāptā gharmapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*kaṃcijjalāśayaṃ prāpya praviṣṭāḥ salilaṃ śubham \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The ḍay was Sunday coinciding with the constellation Aśvinī. The Sun was in the middle of the day and the lunar day was Vaivasvatī (second day). The visitors were afflicted with the heat. They came to a certain water-pond and entered the splendid waters.

## \|\| 1.182.52-54 \|\|

*śaṃkukarṇā mahākarṇā vakanāsāstathāpare \|*  
*mahodarā bṛhaddantā dīrghoṣṭhāḥ sthūlamastakāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*cipiṭākṣāstathā cānye dīrghagrīvāstathā pare \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃgāḥ sphuṭitaiḥ pādairnakhairdīrghaiḥ samutthitaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tato yāvadviniṣkrāṃtāḥ prapaśyanti parasparam \|*  
*tāvadvairūpasyanirmuktāḥ saṃjātāḥ kāmasannibhāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. All the visitors were hideous and ugly. Some had large ears. Some were spike-eared. Others had crooked noses. There were some with huge bellies; a few with large teeth; many with hanging lips and large heads. Others were flateyed. Still others had long necks. Some were dark-complexioned. Some had split feet, long nails and some with nails lifted up. But when they came out and saw one another, they found themselves rid of all ugly features. All of them had become like Kāma.

## \|\| 1.182.55-60 \|\|

*tato vismayamāpannā mithaḥ procuḥ praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*rūpavyatyayamālokya jñātvā tīrthaṃ taduttamam \|*  
*atra snānādidaṃ rūpamasmābhiḥ prāptamuttamam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yasmāttasmādidaṃ tīrthaṃ rūpatīrthaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*trailokye sakale khyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyanti śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*surūpāste bhaviṣyaṃti sadā janmani janmani \|\| 57 \|\|*

*pitṝṃśca tarpayiṣyanti ya tra śraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|*  
*jalenāpi gayāśrāddhātte lapsyante dhikaṃ phalam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ye'tra ratnapradānaṃ ca prakariṣyanti mānavāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃdeho rājānaste bhavebhave \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sthāsyāmo vayamatraiva sāṃprataṃ kṛtaniścayāḥ \|*  
*na yāsyāmo vayaṃ tīrthaṃ yadyapi syātsuśobhanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

55-60. They were surprised and they spoke to one another joyously when they realized that the Tīrtha was excellent in view of the change in their forms: “This excellent form has been obtained by us by taking our bath here. Hence this Tīrtha will become well-known in the entire range of the three worlds as Rūpatīrtha. It shall be destructive of all sins.

Those who are endowed with great faith and take their holy bath here will become handsome in features in the course of every birth.

Those who have perfect faith and offer libations with the waters hereof unto the Pitṛs will attain more benefit than that from Gayā Śrāddha.

Those men who make gifts of jewels here will undoubtedly become kings in the course of every re-birth.

We have come to this decision that we will stay here now. We will not go to (another) Tīrtha even if it be very splendid.”

## \|\| 1.182.61 \|\|

*evamuktvā'tha vyabhajaṃstatsarvaṃ munayaśca te \|*  
*yajñopavītamātrāṇi svāni tīrthāni cakrire \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After saying thus, those sages divided the whole of the Tīrtha (among themselves). Each made his own Tīrtha of the extent of his Yajñopavīta (sacred thread).

## \|\| 1.182.62 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*adyāpi ca dvijaśreṣṭhāstatra tīrthe jagadguruḥ \|*  
*prathamaṃ spṛśate toyaṃ nityaṃ syāddayitaṃ śubham \|\| 62 \|\|*

Sūta said:

62\. Even today, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the Jagadguru (Preceptor of the universe) touches the water in the Tīrtha there at the outset. It shall be loveable and auspicious.

## \|\| 1.182.63 \|\|

*niṣkāmastu punarmartyo yaḥ snānaṃ tatra śraddhayā \|*  
*kurute sa paraṃ śreyaḥ prāpnuyātsiddhilakṣaṇam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A man who is bereft of desire and performs the holy bath with faith shall attain the greatest benefit characterized as Siddhi (perfection).

## \|\| 1.182.64 \|\|

*evaṃ te munayaḥ sarve vibhajya tanmahatsaraḥ \|*  
*sāyaṃtanaṃ ca tatraiva kṛtvā karma suvistaram \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus all those sages shared that great lake and carried out elaborately all the rites of the evening.

## \|\| 1.182.65 \|\|

*tato niśāmukhe prāptā yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*dīkṣitastvatha maunī ca yajñamaṇḍapasaṃśritaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. At the beginning of the nightfall they came to the place where Lord Pitāmaha was present in the Yajñamaṇḍapa, observing silence in the course of initiation.

## \|\| 1.182.66 \|\|

*taṃ praṇamya tataḥ sarve gatā yatrartvijaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭāḥ pariśrāntā divā yajñiyakarmaṇā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After bowing down to him, all of them went to the place where the Ṛtviks were present. They were seated there as they had become tired due to the day-long Yajña rites.

## \|\| 1.182.67 \|\|

*indrādikaiḥ surairbhaktyā mṛdyamānāṅghrayaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*abhivādyātha tānsarvānupaviṣṭāstato grataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. With great devotion, Indra and other Suras were massaging their feet. The visiting sages bowed down to all of them and seated themselves in front of them.

## \|\| 1.182.68 \|\|

*cakruścātha kathāścitrā yajñakarmasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*somapānasya saṃbandho vyatyayaṃ ca samudbhavam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. They held diverse discourses pertaining to the Yajña rites and the relationship with Soma-imbibing and also the change in origin.

## \|\| 1.182.69 \|\|

*udgātuḥ prabhavaṃ caiva tathādhvaryoḥ parasparam \|*  
*procuste tattvamāśritya tathānye dūṣayanti tat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They spoke among themselves about the origin of Udgātṛ and of Adhvaryu as based on principles. Others refuted this.

## \|\| 1.182.70 \|\|

*anye mīmāṃsakāstatra kopasaṃraktalocanāḥ \|*  
*hanyusteṣāṃ mataṃ vādamāśritā vāgvicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Other Mīmāṃsakas refuted the arguments of these with their eyes turned red due to anger. They were rather very clever and eloquent in their speech and they maintained their point in the argument.

## \|\| 1.182.71 \|\|

*pariśiṣṭavidaścānye madhyasthā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*procurvādaṃ parityajya sābhiprāyaṃ yathoditam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Others who were excellent Brāhmaṇas took up the central (neutral) position as they were aware of the Pariśiṣṭa (Appendix). They forsook arguments and revealed their opinion as mentioned.

## \|\| 1.182.72 \|\|

*mahāvīrapuroḍāśacayanapramukhāṃstathā \|*  
*vivādāṃścakrire cānye svaṃsvaṃ pakṣaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Others started discussions about the collection of Mahāvīrapuroḍāśa and other topics defending their own respective positions.

## \|\| 1.182.73 \|\|

*evaṃ sā rajanī teṣāmatikrāntā dvijanmanām \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thus the Brāhmaṇas passed that night.

## Chapter 183 - Creation of Nāga Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.183.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dvitīye divase prāpte yajñakarmasamudbhave \|*  
*dvādaśyāmabhavattatra śṛṇudhvaṃ taddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vṛttāntaṃ sarvadevānāṃ mahāvismayakārakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. It was on the twelfth lunar day that the second day of the Yajña rites was celebrated. Listen to the news about all the Devas. It can cause great wonder.

## \|\| 1.183.2-3 \|\|

*makhakarmaṇi prārabdha ṛtvigbhirvedapāragaiḥ \|*  
*jalasarpaṃ samādāya baṭuḥ kaścitsunarmakṛt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*praviśyātha sadastatra taṃ sarpaṃ brāhmaṇāntike \|*  
*cikṣepa prahasaṃścaiva sarvaduḥkhabhayaṃkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The rites of the Makha were begun by the Ṛtviks who were masters of the Vedas. A mischievously mirthful religious student took a water-snake, entered the assembly and hurled it near the Brāhmaṇas. All along he went on laughing. But it was a terrible act that caused panic unto all.

## \|\| 1.183.4-5 \|\|

*tatastu ḍuṇḍubhastūrṇaṃ bhramamāṇa itastataḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ sadasisthānāṃ saktānāṃ yajñakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*aho hotuḥ sthite praiṣe dīrghasatrasamudbhave \|*  
*sa sarpo veṣṭayāmāsa tasya gātraṃ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The Brāhmaṇas in the assembly were engrossed in their respective duties. The Hotṛ was afflicted due to the long drawn Sattra. Also the water-snake rambled here and there and ultimately coiled round the body of the Hotṛ.

## \|\| 1.183.6 \|\|

*na cacāla nijasthānātprāyaścittavibhīṣayā \|*  
*novāca vacanaṃ so'tra cayananyastalocanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He did not move away from his assigned post because he was afraid of the expiation, should it be the case. With his eyes fixed upon the Cayana (collection of sacrificial twigs) he did not speak a word.

## \|\| 1.183.7 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahāñjajñe etasminnaṃtare dvijāḥ \|*  
*tasminsadasi viprāṇāṃ viṣā ḍhyāhipraśaṃkayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the meantime, a great hue and cry ensued there in the assembly of the Brāhmaṇas because they suspected that it was a poisonous snake.

## \|\| 1.183.8-9 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsīttaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarpaveṣṭitam \|*  
*tasya putro vinītātmā maitrāvaruṇakarmaṇi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saṃsthitastena saṃdṛṣṭaḥ pitā sarpābhiveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā tu ceṣṭitaṃ tasya bhaye sarpasamudbhave \|*  
*śaśāpa krodhasaṃyuktastatastaṃ sa baṭuṃ muniḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. There was great wailing on seeing the Hotṛ encircled by the snake. His well-disciplined modest son engaged in the duty of Maitrāvaruṇa saw the father encircled by the snake. His activities were like those afraid of a serpent. Therefore, the sage became angry and he cursed the religious student.

## \|\| 1.183.10 \|\|

*yasmātpāpa tvayā sarpaḥ kṣiptaḥ sadasi durmate \|*  
*tasmādbhava drutaṃ sarpo mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O widcked-minded one, a snake has been hurled into the assembly by you, a sinner. Hence be yourself a serpent quickly at my instance undoubtedly.”

## \|\| 1.183.11 \|\|

*baṭuruvāca \|*  
*hāsyena jalasarpo'yaṃ mayā mukto'tra līlayā \|*  
*na te tātaṃ samuddiśya tatkiṃ māṃ śapasi dvija \|\| 11 \|\|*

The religious student said:

11\. It was for fun that this water-snake was playfully released by me here. I did not aim it at your father. So, O Brāhmaṇa, why do you curse me?

## \|\| 1.183.12 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare muktvā tasya gātraṃ sa pannagaḥ \|*  
*jagāmānyatra tasyāpi sarpatvaṃ samapadyata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the meantime, the water-snake slipped down from his body and went somewhere else but the religious student remained turned into a serpent.

## \|\| 1.183.13 \|\|

*so'pi sarpatvamāpannaḥ sanātanasuto baṭuḥ \|*  
*duḥkhaśokasamāpanno brāhmaṇaiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The religious student, the son of Sanātana, who got transformed into a serpent became miserable. He was surrounded by other Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.183.14 \|\|

*atha gatvā bhṛguṃ so'pi bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ \|*  
*provāca gadgadaṃ vākyaṃ praṇipatya puraḥsaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With eyes full of tears, he went to Bhṛgu, bowed down before him and spoke these words choked with tears:

## \|\| 1.183.15-16 \|\|

*sanātanasutaścāsmi pautrastu parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*śaptastava sutenāsmi cyavanena mahātmanā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nirdoṣo brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha tasmācchāpātprarakṣa mām \|*  
*tacchrutvā cyavanaṃ prāha kṛpāviṣṭo bhṛguḥ svayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. “I am the son of Sanātana and the grandson of Parameṣṭhin. I have been cursed by your noble-souled son Cyavana. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I am not guilty. So, save me from the curse.”

On hearing this, Bhṛgu became merciful. He spoke to Cyavana:

## \|\| 1.183.17-18 \|\|

*ayuktaṃ vihitaṃ tāta yacchapto'yaṃ baṭustvayā \|*  
*na māṃ dharṣayituṃ śakto viṣāḍhyo'pi bhujaṃgamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kiṃ punarjalasarpo'yaṃ nirviṣo rajjusaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*na māmuddiśya nirmuktaḥ sarpo'nena dvijanmanā \|*  
*śāpamokṣaṃ kuruṣvāsya tasmācchīghraṃ dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. “O dear one, it is an improper thing that has been committed by you, for this religious student has been cursed. Even a very poisonous serpent cannot harm me. How then can this water-snake, as free from poison as a rope, harm me? Further, this snake has not been hurled by this Brāhmaṇa aiming at me. Hence, quickly redeem this Brāhmaṇa from the curse.”

## \|\| 1.183.19 \|\|

*cyavana uvāca \|*  
*yadi tyajati maryādāmabdhiḥ śaityaṃ vrajedraviḥ \|*  
*uṣṇatvaṃ ca kṣapānāthastanme syādanṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Cyavana said:

19\. If the ocean transgresses its boundary, if the Sun becomes cool and if the Lord of the night (Moon) becomes hot, then my words shall be false.

## \|\| 1.183.20 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya svayameva pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tatrāyātaḥ sthito yatra sa pautraḥ sarparūpadhṛk \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing his words, Pitāmaha himself came there where his grandson was present in the form of a serpent.

## \|\| 1.183.21 \|\|

*provāca na viṣādaste putra kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*yatsarpatvamanuprāptaḥ śṛṇuṣvātra vaco mama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O my boy”, He said, “Do not feel aggrieved at all that you have been transformed into a serpent. In this connection, listen to my words:

## \|\| 1.183.22 \|\|

*purā saṃsraṣṭukāmo'haṃ nāgānāṃ navamaṃ kulam \|*  
*tadbhaviṣyati tvatpārśvātsamaryādaṃ dharātale \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Formerly, I was desirous of creating the ninth family of Nāgas. That shall be introduced on a limited scale on the earth through you.

## \|\| 1.183.23 \|\|

*mantrauṣadhiyujāṃ puṃsāṃ na pīḍāmācariṣyati \|*  
*saṃprāpsyati parāṃ pūjāṃ samaste jagatītale \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It will not afflict persons who are masters of Mantras and herbal medicines. It will receive excellent worship all over the earth.

## \|\| 1.183.24 \|\|

*atrā'sti suśubhaṃ toyaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñite \|*  
*kṣetre tatra samāvāsaḥ putra kāryastvayā sadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Here in the holy place named Hāṭakeśvara there is a pond with excellent water. My child, you must take up your residence there always.

## \|\| 1.183.25 \|\|

*tatrasthasya tapasthasya nāgaḥ karkoṭako nijam \|*  
*tava dāsyati satkanyāṃ tataḥ sṛṣṭirbhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. While you stay there and proceed ahead with your penance, Serpent Karkoṭaka will give his excellent daughter to you. Therefrom, the creation (of your family) will take place.

## \|\| 1.183.26-27 \|\|

*navamasya kulasyātra samaryādasya bhūtale \|*  
*śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapakṣe tu saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saṃprāpsyati parāṃ pūjāṃ pṛthivyāṃ navamaṃ kulam \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti tattoyaṃ nāgatīrthamiti smṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The creation of the new ninth family on a limited scale shall begin on the earth. On the fifth lunar day in the dark half(?) of the month of Śrāvaṇa, this ninth family shall receive the highest worship of the earth. From this day onwards the water pond shall be remembered as Nāga Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.183.28-31 \|\|

*khyātiṃ yāsyati bhūpṛṣṭhe sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti saṃprāpte paṃcamīdine \|\| 28 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ vatsaraṃyāvadbhaviṣyatyahijaṃ bhayam \|*  
*viṣārdditastu yo martyastatra snānaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇānnirviṣo bhūtvā saṃprāpsyati paraṃ sukham \|*  
*putrakāmā tu yā nārī paṃcamyāṃ bhāskarodaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kariṣyati tathā snānaṃ phalahastā prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati ca sā śīghraṃ vaṃdhyā'pi ca suputriṇī \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. It will be reputed all over the earth. It will be destructive of all sins. If devotees take their holy bath on the fifth lunar day here, they will have no fear from serpents till the end of the year. A man who is afflicted with the poison and who takes his holy bath here, shall be rid of the poison instantly and attain great happiness. A woman who is desirous of a son should take the holy bath on the fifth lunar day at sunrise with great devotion holding any fruit in the hands. Even if she is a barren woman, she will become one having excellent sons.”

## \|\| 1.183.32 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ pravadatastasya brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*anye nāgāḥ samāyātāstatra yajñe nimaṃtritāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Sīita said:

32\. Even as Brahmā, born of the Unmanifest One, was speaking thus, other serpents that had been invited for the Yajña came there.

## \|\| 1.183.33 \|\|

*vāsukistakṣakaścaiva puṇḍarīkaḥ kṛśodaraḥ \|*  
*kambalāśvatarau nāgau śeṣaḥ kāliya eva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. They were Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Puṇḍarīka, Kṛśodara, Kaṃbala, Aśvatara, Śeṣa and Kāliya.

## \|\| 1.183.34-35 \|\|

*te praṇamya vacaḥ procuḥ proccairdevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*tavādeśādvayaṃ prāptā yajñe'tra prapitāmaha \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sāhāyyārthaṃ tadādeśo dīyatāṃ prapitāmaha \|*  
*yena kurmo vayaṃ śīghraṃ nāgarājye hyadhiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. They bowed down to Lord Pitāmaha and spoke thus loudly: “O Prapitāmaha, we have come here at your behest.

O Prapitāmaha, we have come here to be of some assistance. We are well settled in the realm of Nāgas. We may be commanded. We shall carry out your behest quickly.”

## \|\| 1.183.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| sāhāyyametadasmākaṃ bhavadīyaṃ mahoragāḥ \|*  
*gatvānena samaṃ śīghraṃ nāgarājena tiṣṭhata \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

36\. O great serpents, this shall be your assistance to us. Go along with this king of serpents.

## \|\| 1.183.37 \|\|

*nāgatīrthe tataḥ stheyaṃ sarvaistatra samāsthitaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thereafter, all of you should stay there in the Nāgatīrtha well-settled.

## \|\| 1.183.38 \|\|

*yaḥ kaścinmama yajñe'tra duṣṭabhāvaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*samāgacchati vighnāya rakṣaṇīyaḥ sa satvaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If anyone with evil intention comes here to create obstacles in the Yajña, he should be quickly set aside.

## \|\| 1.183.39 \|\|

*rākṣaso vā piśāco vā bhūto vā mānuṣo'pi vā \|*  
*etatkṛtyatamaṃ nāgā mama yajñasya rakṣaṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It may be a Rākṣasa, Piśāca, Bhūta or human being. O Nāgas, this form of assistance is the best to be offered (by you all).

## \|\| 1.183.40 \|\|

*tathā yūyamapi prāpte māsi bhādrapade tathā \|*  
*paṃcamyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣasya tatra pūjāmavāpsyatha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then, on the fifth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Bhādrapada, you will all be duly worshipped.

## \|\| 1.183.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva te procya praṇipatya pitāmaham \|*  
*sanātanasutopetā nāgatīrthaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

41\. They said, “So it shall be” and bowed down to Pitāmaha. Accompanied by the son of Sanātana, they settled in Nāga Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.183.42 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ nāgatīrtha miti smṛtam \|*  
*kāmapradaṃ ca bhaktānāṃ narāṇāṃ snānakāriṇām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Ever since then that Tīrtha is remembered as Nāga Tīrtha. It fulfils all desires of devout men who take their holy bath.

## \|\| 1.183.43 \|\|

*yastatra kurute snānaṃ sakṛdbhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*nānvaye'pi bhayaṃ tasya jāya te sarpasaṃbhavam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. If anyone devoutly performs his holy ablution there even once, there shall be no danger from serpents to his family.

## \|\| 1.183.44 \|\|

*tatra yacchati miṣṭānnaṃ dvijānāṃ sajjanaiḥ saha \|*  
*pūjayitvā tu nāgeṃdrānsanātanapuraḥsarān \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After worshipping the leading Nāgas beginning with (the son of) Sanātana, a person should offer sweet food to Brāhmaṇas along with good people.

## \|\| 1.183.45 \|\|

*saptajanmāṃtaraṃ yāvanna sa dauḥsthyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ śākinīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*na cchidraṃ na ca rogāśca nādhayo na riporbhayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. For seven subsequent births, he will never meet with misery arising from Bhūtas, Pretas and Piśācas and Śākinīs in particular. He will never have sickness, anguish, defects, blemish or fear from enemies.

## \|\| 1.183.46 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyādbhaktyā vācyamānaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*so'pi saṃvatsaraṃ yāvatpannagairna ca pīḍyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he who listens to this being read will never be afflicted by serpents for the period of one year therefrom.

## \|\| 1.183.47 \|\|

*sarpadaṣṭasya yasyaitatpurataḥ paṭhyate bhṛśam \|*  
*nāgatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ kāla daṣṭo'pi jīvati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If this greatness of Nāga Tīrtha is duly read before one who is bitten by a serpent, he will survive even if he is bitten by Kāla (god of Death).

## \|\| 1.183.48 \|\|

*pustake likhitaṃ caitannāgatīrthasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ tiṣṭhate yatra na sarpastatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. No serpent stays in the place where the book in which this greatness of Nāga Tīrtha is written down is kept.

## Chapter 184 - The Yajña of Brahmā: The Third Day

## \|\| 1.184.1-2 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tṛtīye ca dine prāpte trayodaśyāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*prātaḥsavanamādāya ṛtvijaḥ sarva eva te \|*  
*svesve karmaṇi saṃlagnā yajñakṛtyasamudbhave \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ pravartate yajñastadā paitāmaho mahān \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhastu sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. The advent of the third day was on the thirteenth lunar day, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. All the Ṛtviks became engaged in their respective duties in connection with the Yajña rite beginning with Prātassavana. Then the great Yajña of Pitāmaha began, rich in all good qualities and desirable components.

## \|\| 1.184.3-5 \|\|

*dīyatāṃ dīyatāṃ tatra bhujyatāṃ bhujyatāmiti \|*  
*ekaḥ saṃśrūyate śabdo dvitīyo dvijasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nānyastatra tṛtīyastu yajñe paitāmahe śubhe \|*  
*yo yaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ hemaratnasamudbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sa tatprāpnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ vāṃchitācca caturguṇam \|*  
*pakvānnasya kṛtāstatra dṛśyaṃte parvatāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. The one word uttered by the Brāhmaṇas and heard theṛe was “dīyatām dīyatām” (Let this be given). The second word uttered and heard was “bhujyatām bhujyatām” (Let this be eaten). In that excellent Yajña of Pitāmaha no third word was heard. If anyone wished for anything, say gold or jewel, he undoubtedly got it, nay four times as much as he desired. Splendid mountains of cooked sweet food were seen heaped up there.

## \|\| 1.184.6 \|\|

*ghṛtakṣīra mahānadyo dānārthaṃ vittarāśayaḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāptaḥ kaścijjñānī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There were great rivers of ghee and milk (for eating) and heaps of coins for distribution were also seen.

In the meantime, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a wise philosopher also came there.

## \|\| 1.184.7 \|\|

*atītānāgatānvetti vartamānaṃ ca yaḥ sadā \|*  
*sa brahmāṇaṃ namaskṛtya niviṣṭaśca tadagrataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was one who could know the past, present, and future always. He bowed down to Brahmā and squātted in front of him.

## \|\| 1.184.8 \|\|

*karmāṃtareṣu viprāṇāṃ sa sarveṣāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa yadvṛttaṃ bālyātprabhṛti kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In between the various rites of all those Brāhmaṇas, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he narrated everything that had happened ever since childhood.

## \|\| 1.184.9 \|\|

*tatasta ṛtvijaḥ sarve kautukāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*papracchurjñāninaṃ taṃ ca vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The minds of all those Ṛtviks were overcome with fancy and curiosity. With their eyes beaming with wonder, they asked the philosopher:

## \|\| 1.184.10 \|\|

*vismṛtāni smaraṃtaste nijakṛtyāni vai tataḥ \|*  
*proktāni garhaṇīyāni hyasaṃkhyātāni sarvaśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “They (probably) recollected the fact that they had forgotten (or omitted) some of their duties and the innumerable censurable things uttered by them (unwittingly).”

## \|\| 1.184.11-14 \|\|

*tataste punarevātha papracchurjñāninaṃ ca tam \|*  
*lokottaramidaṃ jñānaṃ kathaṃ te saṃsthitaṃ dvija \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ko guruste samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|*  
*ahojñānamaho jñānaṃ naitaddṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ ca na \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yādṛśaṃ te dvijaśreṣṭha dṛśyate pārthasaṃsthitam \|*  
*kiṃ brahmaṇā svayaṃ vipra tvamevaṃ pratibodhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kiṃ vā hareṇa tuṣṭena kiṃ vā devena cakriṇā \|*  
*nānyaprabodhitasyaivaṃ jñānaṃ saṃjāyate sphuṭam \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Then they asked the philosopher once again: “O Brāhmaṇa, how did you attain this extraordinary wisdom?

Oh! Wonderful is your knowledge. Oh! Wonderful is your wisdom. Such a thing as this has neither been seen nor heard by us. Who is your preceptor? Tell us. We are very curious.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, such a thing as is seen by you has not been heard by us. O Brāhmaṇa, has Brahmā himself enlightened you?

Were you instructed by Hara who was pleased? Or by the Discus-bearing Lord? It is patent that such clear perception can never be had by one enlightened by anyone else.”

## \|\| 1.184.15 \|\|

*atithiruvāca \|*  
*piṃgalā kuraraḥ sarpaḥ sāraṃgaścaiva yo vane \|*  
*iṣukāraḥ kumārī ca ṣaḍete guravo mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

The guest said:

15\. These six are my preceptors: Piṅgalā (a queen), a Kurara (sparrow-like) bird, a serpent, a Sāraṅga (black bee) in the forest, an arrow-maker and a virgin.

## \|\| 1.184.16 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā jñānaṃ me samupasthitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I acquired wisdom by observing the activities of these:

## \|\| 1.184.17 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāga kathaṃ te guravaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ ca tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ teṣāṃ caiva viceṣṭitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

17\. O highly esteemed one, tell us, how these became your preceptors. What sort of activities of these was observed by you?

## \|\| 1.184.18 \|\|

*kasmindeśe tvamutpannaḥ kasminsthāne vadasva naḥ \|*  
*kiṃnāmā kiṃ nu gotraśca sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In which land and which area were you born? Tell us. What is your name? What is your Gotra? Say everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.184.19 \|\|

*atithiruvāca \|*  
*āsannava pure viprāścatvāro ye vivāsitāḥ \|*  
*śunaḥśepo'tha śākreyo bauddho dāṃtaścaturthakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The guest said:

19\. In this city, there were four Brāhmaṇas who had been banished, viz. Śunaḥśepa, Śākreya, Bauddha and Dānta the fourth one.

## \|\| 1.184.20 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye tu yo bauddhaḥ śāṃto dāṃta iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*chandogagotravikhyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Among them Dānta was remembered as enlightened and quiescent. He was well-known as hailing from Chāndoga Gotra. He was a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.184.21 \|\|

*nāgareṣu samutpannaḥ paścimevayasi sthitaḥ \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ prathamaḥ putraḥ prāṇebhyo'pi suhṛtpriyaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was born in the Nāgara community. He was in the state of advanced age. I am his eldest son, very dear to his heart, clearer than his own life.

## \|\| 1.184.22 \|\|

*tato'haṃ yauvanaṃ prāpto yadā dvijavarottama \|\|*  
*tadā me dayitastātaḥ paṃcatvaṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when I entered the prime of youth, my dear father passed away.

## \|\| 1.184.23 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare rājā hyānartādhipatirdvijāḥ \|*  
*sutapāstena nirdiṣṭo'haṃ tu kaṃcukikarmaṇi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime, O Brāhmaṇas, I (met) Sutapas, the King of Ānarta. I was employed as his Kañcukin (chamber-lain) by him.

## \|\| 1.184.24 \|\|

*śāṃtaṃ dāṃtaṃ samālokya viśvastena mahātmanā \|*  
*tasya cāṃtaḥpure hyāsītpiṃgalānāma nāyikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He saw me quiescent and having control over the sense-organs. Hence, the noble-minded one trusted me. There was a queen named Piṅgalā in his palace (Antaḥpura).

## \|\| 1.184.25 \|\|

*daurbhāgyeṇa samopetā rūpeṇāpi samanvitā \|*  
*athānyāḥ śataśastasya bhāryāścāṃtaḥpure sthitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. She was utterly unlucky, being denied conjugal felicity though richly endowed with beauty. Moreover, there were hundreds of other wives in his palace.

## \|\| 1.184.26 \|\|

*tāḥ sarvā rajanīvaktre vyākulatvaṃ prayāṃti ca \|*  
*āharaṃti parāngandhāndhūpāṃśca kusumāni ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All of them used to become excessively agitated and excited at nightfall. They used to gather together exquisite scents, incense and flowers.

## \|\| 1.184.27 \|\|

*vilepanāni mukhyāni surabhīṇi tathā puraḥ \|\| \|*  
*puṣpāṇi ca vicitrāṇi hyanyāḥ sūkṣmāṃbarāṇi ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The choicest of fragrant unguents were brought forward; other women gathered diverse kinds of flowers and fine fabrics.

## \|\| 1.184.28 \|\|

*tāvadyāvatsthitaḥ kālaḥ śayanīyasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*manmathotsāhasaṃ yuktāḥ pulakena samanvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This excitement goes on till the time of going to bed. They exhibited great enthusiasm in love-play and experienced horripilation.

## \|\| 1.184.29 \|\|

*ekā jānāti māṃ suptāṃ nūnamākārayiṣyati \|*  
*anyā jānāti māṃ caiva parasparamamarṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They used to vie with one another. One thinks “he” will certainly summon her to sleep. Another thinks the same about herself.

## \|\| 1.184.30 \|\|

*spardhayanti prayudhyanti virūpāṇi vadanti ca \|*  
*tāsāṃ madhyāttataścaikā prayāti nṛpasaṃnidhau \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They used to exhibit rivalry and jealousy, fight with one another and make adverse comments. Ultimately, one among them proceeds to the chamber of the king.

## \|\| 1.184.31 \|\|

*śeṣā vai lakṣyamāsādya niḥśvasya prasvapanti ca \|*  
*duḥkhārtā na labhanti sma tāśca nidrāṃ parābhavāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those left behind experience chagrin; they have sighs in their excess of sorrow and finally go to bed. In utter discomfiture, they never got even a wink of sleep.

## \|\| 1.184.32 \|\|

*kāmena pīḍitāṃgāśca bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Their eyes became filled with tears and they were excessively afflicted by the god of Love.

## \|\| 1.184.33 \|\|

*āśā hi paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ nirāśā paramaṃ sukham \|*  
*āśānirāśāṃ kṛtvā ca sukhaṃ svapiti piṃgalā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Āśā (eager expectation) is the greatest of misery. Absence of the same is the height of happiness. Making Āśā disappointed, Piṅgalā used to sleep soundly.

## \|\| 1.184.34 \|\|

*na karoti ca śṛṃgāraṃ na spardhāṃ ca kadācana \|*  
*na vyākulatvamāpede sukhaṃ svapiti piṃgalā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. She never indulged in coquettish make-up. She never exhibited rivalry. Hence, she never became distressed. Piṅgalā did sleep soundly.

## \|\| 1.184.35 \|\|

*tato mayāpi taddṛṣṭvā tasyāśceṣṭitamuttamam \|*  
*āśāḥ sarvāḥ parityaktāḥ svapimīha tataḥ sukhī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This excellent behaviour of the lady was closely observed by me and all Āśās (longings and expectations) were eschewed by me. So I too have a happy and sound sleep.

## \|\| 1.184.36 \|\|

*ye svapaṃti sukhaṃ rātrau teṣāṃ kāyāgniridhyate \|*  
*āhāraṃ pratigṛhṇāti tataḥ puṣṭikaraṃ param \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The gastric fire of those who sleep soundly gets ignited well. Thereby their food-intake becomes very nutritious.

## \|\| 1.184.37 \|\|

*tadetkāraṇaṃ jātaṃ mama tejo bhivṛddhaye \|*  
*gurutve piṃgalā jātā tena sā me dvijottamāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. This has, therefore, become the cause of the enhancement of my radiance. Therefore, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Piṅgalā has become my preceptor (preceptress).

## \|\| 1.184.38 \|\|

*āśāpāśaiḥ parītāṃgā ye bhavanti naro rditāḥ \|*  
*te rātrau śerate naiva tadaprāptivicintayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who are entangled within the noose of Āśā, men who are thus afflicted, never lie down at night brooding over the non-acquisition of the same.

## \|\| 1.184.39 \|\|

*naivāgnirdīpyate teṣāṃ jāṭharaśca tataḥ param \|*  
*āhāraṃ vāṃchate naiva tanna tejobhivardhanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Their abdominal fire never gets ignited thereafter. Nor do they have any appetite at all. Nor is their food-intake conducive to the enhancement of radiance.

## \|\| 1.184.40 \|\|

*sarvasya vidyate prāṃto na vāṃchāyāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There is a limit to everything except to yearning or craving.

## \|\| 1.184.41 \|\|

*yathāyathā bhavellābho vāṃcitasya nṛṇāmiha \|*  
*haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva vṛddhiṃ yāti tathātathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. As there is the fulfilment of desires in man so these go on increasing like fire through the addition of Havis offerings.

## \|\| 1.184.42 \|\|

*yathā śṛṃgaṃ ruroḥ kāye vardhamānasya vardhate \|*  
*evaṃ tṛṣṇāpi yatnena vardhamānena vardhate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Just as the horn of a Ruru deer goes on rising up as its body develops, so also desires of men get enhanced as their effort for the same increases.

## \|\| 1.184.43 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāgaḥ puruṣeṇa vijānatā \|*  
*divā tatkarma kartavyaṃ yena rātrau sukhaṃ svapet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O highly esteemed ones, after realizing this, a discerning person should be doing that during the day whereby he can sleep soundly during the night.

## Chapter 185 - Creation of Holy Places

## \|\| 1.185.1-4 \|\|

*\| atithiruvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā me piṃgalā guruḥ \|*  
*saṃjātā kuraro jāto yathā tatpravadānyaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mamāsīddraviṇaṃ bhūri pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ye'tha putrāśca dāyādā bāṃdhavā api \|*  
*te māṃ sarve prabādhante dravyasasyakṛte sadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yasyāhaṃ na prayacchāmi sa māṃ caiva prabādhate \|*  
*sīdamānastu subhṛśaṃ darśayanprāṇasaṃkṣayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

The guest said:

1-4. Thus everything has been narrated to you all as to how Piṅgalā became my Guru (teacher). How the Kurara bird (osprey) became so, I shall explain to you.

I had much wealth inherited from my father and grandfather. All the kinsmen, relatives, sons and grandsons began to pester me for money and food-grain.

If I deny anyone anything, he begins to torment me. He exhibits utter exhaustion to the point of extinction of the very life.

## \|\| 1.185.5 \|\|

*eka sāmnā prayācaṃte vittaṃ bhedena cāpare \|*  
*bhayadānena cānye'pi keciddaṃḍena ca dvijāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Brāhmaṇas, a few of them used to request me for wealth in conciliatory terms. Others thte atened me to give wealth. Others tempted me with bribes for having some share. Some actually meted out physical violence to me (to extort money by force). Thus, I could not find any means whereby I could get peace.

## \|\| 1.185.6 \|\|

*evaṃ nāhaṃ kvacitsaukhyaṃ teṣāṃ pārśvāllabhāmi bhoḥ \|*  
*cintayāno divānaktaṃ kleśasya pari saṃkṣayam \|*  
*upāyaṃ na ca paśyāmi yena śāṃtiḥ prajāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. So I never had any happiness on account of them. I was worried day and night about the means of bringing about the end to my troubles. I did not find out any means to get peace of mind.

## \|\| 1.185.7 \|\|

*anyasmindivase dṛṣṭaḥ kṛtamāṃsaparigrahaḥ \|*  
*kuraraścaṃcunā vyomni gacchamānastvarānvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On a certain day, a Kurara (osprey) was seen by me going hurriedly through the sky holding a piece of meat in its beak.

## \|\| 1.185.8 \|\|

*hanyamānaḥ samaṃtācca māṃsārthe vividhaiḥ khagaiḥ \|*  
*atha tena parikṣiptaṃ tanmāṃsaṃ pakṣijādbhayāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It was being hurt (pecked) and assailed by different kinds of birds all round for the sake of the piece of meat. Then afraid of the other birds, it let the piece of meat fall down.

## \|\| 1.185.9-10 \|\|

*yāvattāvatsukhī jātaste'pisarve samujjhitāḥ \|*  
*mayāpi kliśyamānena tadvacca nijabāṃdhavaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sāmiṣaṃ kuraraṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ nirāmiṣaiḥ \|*  
*āmiṣasya parityāgātkuraraḥ sukhamedhate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The moment it cast off the piece of meat it became happy. All the other birds abandoned it. Similarly, when I was being tormented by my kinsmen, I resolved thus after seeing the Kurara with meat being attacked by those without meat and that later after throwing away the meat it regained happiness.

## \|\| 1.185.11 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya manasā sarvānānīya bāṃdhavān \|*  
*putrānpautrāṃstataḥ sarvānpurasteṣāṃ niveditam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After coming to a decision I summoned all the kinsmen, sons, grandsons and all the others and told them:

## \|\| 1.185.12 \|\|

*triḥsatyaṃ śapathaṃ kṛtvā nānyadastīti me gṛhe \|*  
*vibhajyārthaṃ yathānyāyaṃ yūyaṃ gṛhṇīta bāndhavāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O my kinsmen, take and share this wealth judiciously. There is nothing else left in my house.” Thus I swore three times.

## \|\| 1.185.13 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tairmuktaḥ sukhaṃ tiṣṭhāmyahaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇājjāto mamāsau kuraro guruḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Ever since then, O Brāhmaṇas, I was left alone by them and I am happy. For this reason, the Kurara (osprey) became my Guru.

## \|\| 1.185.14 \|\|

*arthasaṃpadvimohāya vimoho narakāya ca \|*  
*tasmādarthamanarthaṃ taṃ mokṣārthī dūratastyajet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Wealth and riches give rise to delusion. Delusion leads to Naraka. Hence hoarded wealth is disastrous. One who seeks salvation should avoid it from afar.

## \|\| 1.185.15 \|\|

*yathāmiṣaṃ jale matsyairbhakṣyate śvāpadairbhuvi \|*  
*ākāśe pakṣibhiścaiva tathā sarvatra vittavān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Just as a piece of meat is swallowed by fish in water, by beasts of prey on the ground and by birds in the sky, so also a man of wealth (is preyed upon) everywhere.

## \|\| 1.185.16 \|\|

*doṣahīno'pi dhanavānbhūpādyaiḥ paritāpyate \|*  
*daridraḥ kṛtadoṣo'pi sarvatra nirupadravaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A rich man may be faultless. But he is tormented by kings and others. A poor man might have committed some crime but he is not harassed anywhere.

## \|\| 1.185.17 \|\|

*ālaṃbitāḥ parairyāṃti praskhalaṃti padepade \|*  
*gadgadāni ca jalpaṃte dhanino madyapā iva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Rich people are like drunkards. They move with the support of others. They falter at every step. They stutter and stammer.

## \|\| 1.185.18 \|\|

*bhakte dveṣo bahiḥ prītī rucitaṃ gurulaghvapi \|*  
*mukhe ca kaṭutā nityaṃ dhanināṃ jvariṇāmiva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. As in the case of one afflicted with fever, a rich man hates devoted ones, as a fever-stricken one dislikes cooked food. They show pleasure outwardly liking for heavy and light things but there is bitterness (inwardly) (bitter taste: bitter words) in the mouth.

## \|\| 1.185.19 \|\|

*arthānāmarjane duḥkhamarjitānāṃ ca rakṣaṇe \|*  
*nāśe duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhaṃ dhigartho duḥkhabhājanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There is trouble in earning money and misery in preserving what is earned. There is misery in loss of wealth or when it is spent. Fie upon wealth, the cause of misery!

## \|\| 1.185.20 \|\|

*arthārthī jīva loko'yaṃ smaśānamapi sevate \|*  
*janitāramapi tyaktvā niḥsvaṃ yāṃti sutā api \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. All the people in the world seek wealth and resort even to the cremation ground (for its sake). Even sons forsake their father and walk away if he is without wealth.

## \|\| 1.185.21 \|\|

*sutasya vallabhastāvatpitā putro'pi vai pituḥ \|*  
*yāvannārthasya saṃbandhastābhyāṃ bhāvī parasparam \|*  
*saṃbandhe vittaje jāte vairaṃ saṃjāyate mithaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A son is a favourite of the father and a father that of the son as long as there is no monetary relationship between the two. Once monetary relationship arises between them, mutual enmity also develops.

## \|\| 1.185.22 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādvittaṃ mayā tyaktaṃ tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*tena saukhyena tiṣṭhāmi kurarasyopadeśataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For this reason, O ascetics, money is abandoned by me. Therefore I stay happy, thanks to the instruction from the Kurara.

## \|\| 1.185.23 \|\|

*śṛṇudhvaṃ ca mahābhāgā yathā me'hirguruḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Listen, O highly esteemed ones, as to how a serpent became my Guru.

## \|\| 1.185.24 \|\|

*yathā mayā gṛhaṃ tyaktaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*gṛhāraṃbhaḥ suduḥkhāya sukhāya na kadācana \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Listen how the house was abandoned by me on seeing the activity of a serpent. Starting the construction of one’s own house leads to great misery. It never leads to happiness.

## \|\| 1.185.25 \|\|

*sarpaḥ parakṛtaṃ veśma praviśya sukhamedhate \|*  
*uṣitvā tatra saukhyena bhūyo'nyattādṛśaṃ vrajet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A serpent enters the abode made by others and enjoys. After living there comfortably, it passes on to another one like that.

## \|\| 1.185.26 \|\|

*mama tvaṃ kurute naiva mamedaṃ gṛhamityasau \|*  
*na gṛhaṃ jāyate tasya na svayaṃ hi kṛtaṃ yataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It does not have mamatva (sense of possession) feeling “This is my house”. That does not become its house, because it is not made by itself.

## \|\| 1.185.27 \|\|

*yaḥ punaḥ kurute harmyaṃ svayaṃ kleśaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*na tasya yāti tatpaścānmṛtyukāle'pi saṃsthite \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After undergoing different kinds of trouble and suffering if a man builds a mansion it does not go with him when the time of his death arrives.

## \|\| 1.185.28 \|\|

*gṛhātsaṃjāyate bhāryā tataḥ putraśca kanyakā \|*  
*teṣāmarthe karoti sma kṛtyākṛtyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After building a house one takes a wife. Then a son and a daughter are born. For the sake of these he begins to do all sorts of things that should be and should not be done later.

## \|\| 1.185.29 \|\|

*kośakāramivātmānaṃ veṣṭayannāvabudhyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Like a silk-worm in its cocoon he gets encircled himself and does not realize it.

## \|\| 1.185.30 \|\|

*putradāragṛhakṣetrasaktāḥ sīdaṃti jaṃtavaḥ \|*  
*lobhapaṃkārṇave magnā jīrṇā vanagajā iva \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Creatures attached to sons, wives, houses and fields meet with disaster. They get submerged in the mirish sweat of greed like aged wild elephants.

## \|\| 1.185.31 \|\|

*ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṃkte mahājanaḥ \|*  
*bhoktāro vipramucyaṃte kartā doṣeṇa lipyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One person commits sins but the common people taste fruit thereof; those who enjoy it go scot-free but the doer of it is tarnished with the fault.

## \|\| 1.185.32 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddharmyaṃ mayā tyaktaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mokṣamārgārgalā bhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. For this reason, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the mansion was left by me. It is an obstruction in the path of salvation. This was the result of my observation of the activities of the serpent.

## \|\| 1.185.33 \|\|

*ekarātraṃ vasedgrāme trirātraṃ pattane vaset \|*  
*yo yāti sa yatiḥ prokto yo'nyo yogaviḍaṃbakaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A true ascetic stays in a village for a single night’s rest and for three nights in a town. He who (thus continuously) goes (yāti) on is called a Yati, an ascetic. The other one is an impostor in the practice of Yoga.

## \|\| 1.185.34 \|\|

*vidhūme ca praśāṃtāgnau yastu mādhukarīṃ caret \|*  
*gṛhe ca vipramukhyānāṃ yatiḥ sa netaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who performs the Madhukarī Vṛtti (collecting alms like a bee that sucks honey) at the houses of leading Brāhmaṇas where the fire in the kitchen has calmed down and it does not emit smoke, is the (real) Yati, not anyone else.

## \|\| 1.185.35 \|\|

*daṇḍī bhikṣāṃ ca vā kuryāttadeva vyasanaṃ vinā \|*  
*yastiṣṭhati na vairāgyaṃ yāti naiva yatirhi saḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A Daṇḍin (Sannyāsin) may beg for alms but there should be no addiction to it. He who stays behind and does not become detached is not an ascetic at all.

## \|\| 1.185.36 \|\|

*divā svapnaṃ vṛthānnaṃ ca strīkathā'lokyameva ca \|*  
*śvetavastraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca yatīnāṃ patanāni ṣaṭ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The following six cause the downfall of ascetics: Sleeping during the day; eating in excess (i.e. more than what is absolutely essential for sustenance); talking about women; gazing at them intently; and (wearing) white cloth and gold (ornaments).

## \|\| 1.185.37 \|\|

*samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanaḥ \|*  
*suhṛtputra udāsīnaḥ sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. None else but he is proclaimed as a Yati (in Smṛtis) who is impartial towards enemy and friend; who looks at a lump of clay, stone and gold as equals; and who is free from affection for friends and sons.

## \|\| 1.185.38 \|\|

*samau mānāpamānau ca svadeśe parikepi vā \|*  
*yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He who meets honour and insult squarely whether in his own land or in an alien country, he who does not revel too much nor hates is a Yati, not anyone else.

## \|\| 1.185.39 \|\|

*yasmingṛhe viśeṣeṇa labhedbhikṣā ca vāśanam \|*  
*tatra no yāti yo bhūyaḥ sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If in a house special alms are received or food is distributed, a true Yati does not go there again. No one else is remembered to be so (i.e. a Yati).

## \|\| 1.185.40 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā mayā vipra dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*sarvasaṃgaparityāgo mokṣārthaṃ parikalpitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After observing the activities of a serpent and realizing thus eschewal of all associations was pursued by me for the sake of salvation.

## \|\| 1.185.41 \|\|

*evaṃ mamāhiḥ saṃjāto gururbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*tatprabhāvānmahattejaḥ saṃjātaṃ vigrahe mama \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the serpent became my Guru. By its power, a powerful radiance shone (shines) in my body.

## \|\| 1.185.42 \|\|

*yathā me bhramaro jāto gurustadvadvadāmi ca \|*  
*kasminvṛkṣe mayā dṛṣṭo bhramaraḥ ko'pi saṃgataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I shall tell you how the black-bee became my Guru. A certain black-bee was seen by me. It was closely associated with a tree.

## \|\| 1.185.43-45 \|\|

*śākhāya tu samāśritya kṛtapūrvanibaṃdhanam \|*  
*vasaṃtasamaye prāpte puṣpavaṃtaśca ye drumāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sugandhaphalapuṣpāśca sugandhadalasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmaṇuṃ samādāya śreṣṭhaśreṣṭhatamaṃ rasam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*niyojayati śākhāgre tarorasya sadaiva hi \|*  
*anirviṇṇatayā hṛṣṭastadā samyaṅnirīkṣitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. It resorted to the bit of a branch where it had built a hive before. During spring season the trees began to blossom. The flowers had fragrant petals. There were fruits as well. The bee collected excellent juice from them and deposited it (in the hive) at the tip of the branch. It was seen to be perfectly happy without any dejection.

## \|\| 1.185.46 \|\|

*madhujālaṃ tato jātaṃ kālena mahatā mahat \|*  
*yenānye madhunā tṛptiṃ prāptāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Vast quantity of honey was thus collected in the course of a long time. With that honey hundreds and thousands became satisfied.

## \|\| 1.185.47 \|\|

*tacceṣṭitaṃ mayā vīkṣya śāstrāṇyanyāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*tatasteṣāṃ samādāya sārabhūtaṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*kṛtāni bhūriśāstrāṇi vedāṃtāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I observed this activity of the bee. In the same manner, I extracted the essence from the several scriptural texts, Vedānta works etc., entirely.

## \|\| 1.185.48 \|\|

*upajīvaṃti yānyanye yathā bhṛṅgāstathā dvijāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Like the other bees, other Brāhmaṇas made use of my collection and excerpts.

## \|\| 1.185.49 \|\|

*evaṃ me madhupo jāto gurutve ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tenāhaṃ tejasā yukto nānyadastīha kāraṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the black-bee became my Guru. Therefore I am refulgent. There is no other cause (for my being so).

## \|\| 1.185.50 \|\|

*vedāṃtavādino ye'tra prabhavaṃti vratānvitāḥ \|*  
*nirlobhā gatatṛṣṇāśca te bhavaṃti sutejasaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The expounders of Vedānta who observe Vratas regularly become powerful. They are free from greed and they have cast off desires. They become highly refulgent.

## \|\| 1.185.51 \|\|

*ekenāpi vihīnā ye prabhavaṃti kubuddhayaḥ \|*  
*lobhamohānvitāḥ pāpā jāyaṃte te vicetasaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If they are devoid of even one of these (scriptures and Vratas) they become sinners and stupidly malevolent.

## \|\| 1.185.52 \|\|

*vedāṃtāni subhūrīṇi mayā dṛṣṭvā vicārya ca \|*  
*samarūpāḥ kṛtā granthā martyalokahitārthinā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Many Vedānta texts were pored over, studied and pondered over by me. With the intention of the welfare of human world books of the same level were written by me.

## \|\| 1.185.53 \|\|

*evaṃ me gurutāṃ prāpto madhupo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*iṣukāro yathā jātastathā caiva bravīmi vaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the black-bee became my Guru. How the arrow-maker became so, I shall tell you.

## \|\| 1.185.54 \|\|

*ātmāvalokanārthāya mayā dṛṣṭāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*yogino jñānasaṃpannāstaiḥ proktaṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. For the purpose of realizing the Ātman, thousands of Yogins were interviewed by me. They were richly endowed with wisdom and they expounded in accordance with their ability.

## \|\| 1.185.55-56 \|\|

*ātmāvalokanaṃ bhāvi suśiṣyāya yathā tathā \|*  
*sa samādhijadvāreṇa caturāśītikena ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*āsanaistatpramāṇaiśca padmāsanaprapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyaiḥ kāraṇaiścaiva hyadhyātmapaṭhanaistathā \|*  
*tatopi lakṣito naiva mayā'tmā ca kathaṃcana \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. They tried to explain how an excellent disciple succeeds in realizing the Ātman. That realization results from the practice of eithty-four different types of Samādhi (mental absorption) and Āsanas (postures) equal in number (eighty-four) including the lotus-posture. There are innumerble other factors too, such as recitation of spiritual texts. In spite of all these, Ātman could not be visualized at all by me.

## \|\| 1.185.57 \|\|

*tato vairāgyamāpannaḥ prabhramāmi dharātale \|*  
*gurvarthe na ca lebhe'haṃ gurumātmāvalokane \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence I became disgusted and wandered all over the earth for the sake of a preceptor and guide. I did not meet with a Guru for the purpose of self-realization.

## \|\| 1.185.58 \|\|

*anyasminnahani prāpte rājamārgeṇa gacchatā \|*  
*mayā dṛṣṭo mahīpālaḥ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On another day, I was going along the royal highway when I saw the king surrounded by a vast army.

## \|\| 1.185.59 \|\|

*tato'haṃ mārgamutsṛjya saṃmukhasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*uṭajadvāramāśritya kiṃcidūrdhvopi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. So I avoided the path taken by the king and came to the entrance of a hut. I stood at the door after going a short distance upwards.

## \|\| 1.185.60 \|\|

*tatrāpi ca sthitaḥ kaścitpuruṣaḥ kāṃḍakārakaḥ \|*  
*ṛjukarmaṇi saṃyuktaḥ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. There was an arrow-maker there engaged in the simple activity of shaping the arrows of crooked joints.

## \|\| 1.185.61 \|\|

*tasmindūragate bhūpe tathānyaḥ sevako'bhyagāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. When the king had gone far away,another servant came there.

## \|\| 1.185.62 \|\|

*taṃ papraccha tvarāyuktaḥ śṛṇvato'pi mama dvijāḥ \|*  
*kāṃḍakarmaṇi saṃsaktamṛjutvena sthitaṃ tadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He was in a hurry, O Brāhmaṇas. Even as I was within hearing, he asked the artisan staying upright, engaged in shaping the arrows:

## \|\| 1.185.63 \|\|

*kiyatī vartate velā gatasya pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*mārgeṇānena me brūhi yena gacchāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “How much time has elapsed after the king passed along this road? Tell me so that I can follow him.”

## \|\| 1.185.64-66 \|\|

*so'bravīttaṃ tadā viprā adhovaktraḥ sthito naraḥ \|*  
*anena rājamārgeṇa gacchamāno mahīpatiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*na mayā vīkṣitaḥ kaścididānīṃ rājasevaka \|*  
*tadanyaṃ pṛccha cetkāryaṃ tavānena bravītu saḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*śarakarmaṇi saṃsaktastvahamatra vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya svacitte cintitaṃ mayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66a. The man (artisan) who was sitting with the face bent down, O Brāhmaṇas, spoke then: “O royal attendant, no king going along this royal highway has been seen by me. If you have anything to do with him you may ask someone else. He is likely to tell you. I am sitting here deeply engaged in the work on the arrows.”

66b. On hearing his words I thought thus:

## \|\| 1.185.67 \|\|

*ekacittatayā yogo brahmajñānasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*nānyathā bhavitā me sa tataścittanirodhanam \|*  
*karomi brahmasaṃsiddhyai tato me'sau bhaviṣyati \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. ‘Practice of yoga with concentration of mind will be the means of the knowledge of Brahman. It cannot be gained by other means. Thereafter, I shall begin to curb the mind for the sake of the realization of Brahman. Thereby, it shall be attained by me.’

## \|\| 1.185.68 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti citte sve dhārayāmi sadaiva tu \|*  
*viśvarūpaṃ tathā sūryaṃ hṛtpaṃkajanivāsinam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Ever since then I am retaining in my mind always the Lord, the sun of universal form, forever present in the lotus of the heart.

## \|\| 1.185.69 \|\|

*tato dikṣu diganteṣu gagane dharaṇītale \|*  
*tamekaṃ caiva paśyāmi nānyatkiṃciddvijottamāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thereafter, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I see him solely in all the quarters, in the far end of the quarters, in the firmament and on the earth. (I could see) Nothing else.

## \|\| 1.185.70 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca tejasā yuktastatprabhāveṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. By its power, I am equipped with refulgence.

## \|\| 1.185.71 \|\|

*evaṃ me sa gururjātaḥ śarakāro dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ kanyakā jātā gurutve me yathā purā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that arrow-maker became my Guru. Listen How a Kanyakā (girl) became my Guru earlier.

## \|\| 1.185.72 \|\|

*sarvasaṃgaparityāgī yadāhaṃ nirgato gṛhāt \|*  
*mamānupṛṣṭhataścaiva tato bhāryā vinirgatā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Renouncing all associations, I came out of the house. At that time my wife also closely came behind me and came out.

## \|\| 1.185.73 \|\|

*śiśuṃ putraṃ samādāya kanyāmekāṃ ca śobhanām \|*  
*tato'haṃ bhāryayā prokto vānaprasthāśrame sthitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. She held the infant son and a splendid daughter. I was then in my Vānaprastha stage. I was thus addressed by my wife:

## \|\| 1.185.74 \|\|

*kuru me vacanaṃ muktiratraiva hi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*brahmacārī gṛhastho vā vānaprastho'thavā yatiḥ \|*  
*yadi syātsaṃyatātmā sa nūnaṃ muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “Follow my advice. You will have salvation here itself. A man may be a celibate religious student, a householder, a Vānaprastha or a recluse. If he has perfect restraint over himself, he shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.185.75 \|\|

*athavā māṃ parityajya yadi yāsyasi cānyataḥ \|*  
*tadahaṃ ca mariṣyāmi satyametadasaṃśayam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Otherwise, if you abandon me and go elsewhere. I shall undoubtedly die. This is true.

## \|\| 1.185.76 \|\|

*mṛtāyāṃ mayi te bālāvetāvanumariṣyataḥ \|*  
*kumārī ca kumāraśca tasmānnātha dayāṃ kuru \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. After my death these children of yours, the son and the daughter will die subsequently. Hence, O my lord, have mercy on me.

## \|\| 1.185.77 \|\|

*mā vrajasva paraṃ tīrthaṃ parijānannapi svayam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetrametatpuṇyataraṃ smṛtam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Do not go to any other Tīrtha. You know yourself that this holy place of Hāṭakeśvara is remembered as highly meritorious.

## \|\| 1.185.78 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ śrutametanmayā vibho \|*  
*vadatāṃ brāhmaṇendrāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ tapasvinām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. It is the greatest of all Tīrthas. O my Lord, this has been heard by me from eminent Brāhmaṇas and other ascetics who extolled it.

## \|\| 1.185.79 \|\|

*śloko'yaṃ bahudhā nātha kīrtyamāno mayā vibho \|*  
*viśvāmitrasya vaktreṇa sanmuneḥ satyavādinaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. O my Lord, this verse has been heard by me often repeated orally by Viśvāmitra, the great sage of truthful speech.

## \|\| 1.185.80 \|\|

*punaṃti sarvatīrthāni snānadānādasaṃśayam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ smaraṇādapi pāvayet \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. ‘All the (other) Tīrthas undoubtedly sanctify through holy ablution and monetary gifts. But the holy place Hāṭakeśvara shall sanctify even on being remembered.’”

## \|\| 1.185.81 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchrātpratijñātaṃ mayāśramaniṣevaṇam \|*  
*vānaprasthodbhavaṃ vā syāttato'haṃ tatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thereupon, with great difficulty, I vowed to resort to the Vānaprastha Āśrama (stage). So I stayed there itself.

## \|\| 1.185.82 \|\|

*tatrasthasya hi me kanyā krīḍate parataḥ sthitā \|*  
*valayāpūritābhyāṃ ca prakoṣṭhābhyāṃ tatastataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. While I remained there, my daughter in front of me began to play with her wrists full of bangles.

## \|\| 1.185.83 \|\|

*yathāyathā sā kurute kandamūlaphalāśanam \|*  
*tanutvaṃ yāti kāyena tathā caiva dinedine \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. As she went subsisting only on roots, fruits and bulbous roots, she became leaner and leaner day by day.

## \|\| 1.185.84 \|\|

*tato me jāyate duḥkhaṃ teṣāṃ patana saṃbhavam \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya saṃjātaṃ valayatrayam \|*  
*tasyā haste tatastābhyāṃ śabdaḥ saṃjāyate mithaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thereupon I became unhappy fearing that the bangles may fall down. Once it happened that only three bangles remained on her wrists. When they clashed with each other, a sound was produced.

## \|\| 1.185.85 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tābhyāmekaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*na saṃgharṣo na śabdaśca tatrasthasya ca jāyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. After a long time only one of them remained. There was no clash and no sound when it was on the wrist.

## \|\| 1.185.86 \|\|

*tadvicintya mayā so'pi hyāśramaḥ parivarjitaḥ \|*  
*cintitaṃ ca mayā citte kṛtvā caivaṃ suniścayam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Thinking deeply over this, the hermitage was forsaken by me. After deciding thus I thought as follow:

## \|\| 1.185.87 \|\|

*bahubhiḥ kalaho nityaṃ dvābhyāṃ saṃgharṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*
