## \|\| 1.196.10 \|\|

*tadā'nartādhipo hṛṣṭaḥ preṣayāmāsa taṃ prati \|*  
*vivāhārthaṃ suvijñāya vākya metaduvāca ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then, after a discreet enquiry the delighted king of Ānarta sent a messenger for the sake of matrimonial alliance instructing him thus:

## \|\| 1.196.11-12 \|\|

*gacchadhvaṃ mama vākyena daśārṇādhipatiṃ prati \|*  
*vācyaḥ sa vinayādgatvā vivāhārthaṃ mamāṃtikam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*samāgaccha nijāṃ kanyāṃ yena yacchāmyahaṃ tava \|*  
*nāmnā ratnavatīṃ khyātāṃ trailokyasyāpi sundarīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. “At my behest go to the Lord of Daśārṇa land. He should be told humbly: ‘Come to me so that I can give my daughter in marriage to you. Her name is Ratnavatī. She is well-known as the most beautiful lady in all the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.196.13-14 \|\|

*gatvā sa satvaraṃ tatra yatra rājā bṛhadbalaḥ \|*  
*provāca sakalaṃ vākyamānartādhipateḥ sphuṭam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*so'pi tatsahasā śrutvā teṣāṃ vākyamanuttamam \|*  
*paramāṃ tuṣṭimāsādya prasthitastatpuraṃ prati \|*  
*sainyena mahatā yuktaścaturaṃgeṇa pārthivaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The messenger quickly went to the place where king Bṛhadbala was present and told him clearly what the king of Ānarta had told. That king heard the excellent statement of those and was delighted very much. Accompanied by his vast army of four divisions, that king went to the city of Ānarta.

## Chapter 197 - The Expiation of Parāvasu

## \|\| 1.197.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu nāgaro dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*viśvāvasuriti khyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*paścime vayasi prāpte tasya putro babhūva ha \|*  
*parāvasuriti khyātastasya prāṇasamaḥ sadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sa vedādhyayanaṃ cakre yauvane samupasthite \|*  
*vayasyaiḥ saṃmataiḥ sārdhaṃ sadā hāsya parāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. In the meantime, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there was a Nāgara Brāhmaṇa who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. He was well-known as Viśvāvasu.

In his later years he had a son well-known as Parāvasu whom he considered on a par with his own vital air.

He concluded the study of the Vedas by the time he became a full-fledged youth. He spent most of his time along with his esteemed friends who always indulged in jokes, fun and gaiety.

## \|\| 1.197.4 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya māghamāsa upasthite \|*  
*rātrau so'dhyayanaṃ cakra upādhyāyagṛhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once in the month of Māgha he went to the house of his preceptor and began to chant the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.197.5 \|\|

*niśīthe sa samutthāya sarvairmi traiśca rakṣitaḥ \|*  
*veśyāgṛhaṃ samāsādya prasupto veśyayā saha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At midnight he got up and went to the house of a prostitute guarded by all his friends. He slept with the courtesan there.

## \|\| 1.197.6 \|\|

*jalapūrṇaṃ samādhāya jalapātraṃ samīpagam \|*  
*nijācamanayogyaṃ ca jalapānārthameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He kept near him a pot filled with water intended for Ācamana (ritualistic sipping) as well as for drinking purposes.

## \|\| 1.197.7 \|\|

*niśāśeṣe tu saṃprāpte sa pipāsāsamākulaḥ \|*  
*nidrālasyasamopetaḥ śayyāṃ tyaktvā samutthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Towards the close of the night, he became very thirsty. Though overcome by sleep and lethargy, he left the bed and got up.

## \|\| 1.197.8 \|\|

*veśyāyā madyapātraṃ tu hyadhastātsaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*tadādāya papau madyaṃ jalabhrāṃtyā yadaiva saḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The pot of liquor kept by the courtesan had been placed lower down. Mistaking it for water, he drank the liquor.

## \|\| 1.197.9 \|\|

*tadā madyaṃ parijñāya pātraṃ tyaktvā suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gatvā pralāpānakaro dbahūn \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Immediately, he came to know that it was liquor and he was distressed. He cast off the liquor-pot with great dejectedness. He lamented much.

## \|\| 1.197.10-11 \|\|

*aho nidrānvitenādya kiṃ mayā vikṛtaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*yadadya madyamāpītaṃ jalabhrāṃtyā vigarhitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ śuddhirbhavenmama \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ kariṣyāmi yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. “Alas, what a great misdeed has been committed by mer, Overcome by sleep, I have drunk the hated liquor mistaking it for water.

What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I get myself sanctified. I shall perform expiatory rite even if it be very difficult to do.”

## \|\| 1.197.12 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya manasā prabhāte samupasthite \|*  
*śaṃkhatīrthaṃ samāsādya kṛtvā snānaṃ tathā param \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After resolving thus mentally, he went to Śaṅkha Tīrtha. When the day dawned, he took his bath.

## \|\| 1.197.13-14 \|\|

*saśikhaṃ vapanaṃ paścātkārayitvā tvarāvitaḥ \|*  
*gataśca tiṣṭhate yatra brahmaghoṣaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*upādhyāyaḥ saśiṣyaśca brahmasthānaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*sa gatvā dūrataḥ sthitvā saṃniviṣṭo yathāntyajaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. He caused his tuft (and beard) to be shaved off in a hurry later and went to the place where his preceptor and his disciples were engaged in chanting the Vedas in the place assigned to it. Like a Śūdra, he sat in a place very far off.

## \|\| 1.197.15 \|\|

*śmaśrumūrdhajahīnastu yadā mitrairvilokitaḥ \|*  
*tadā hāsyāddhato mūrdhni hastāgraiśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When he was seen with hair and beard shaven off, by his friends, he was frequently stroked on the tonsured head by them with the tips of their hands.

## \|\| 1.197.16 \|\|

*upādhyāyastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā dīnaṃ bāṣpapariplutam \|*  
*śmaśrumūrdhajasaṃtyaktaṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing him bereft of hair and beard, utterly distressed and shedding tears, the preceptor spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.197.17 \|\|

*kimadya vatsa dūre tvamupaviṣṭastu dainyadhṛk \|*  
*ehi me saṃnidhau brūhi parābhūto'si kena vā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “O my dear one, why are you sitting very far off in a morose mood? Come near me and tell me. By whom have you been humiliated?”

## \|\| 1.197.18-19 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*ayogyo'haṃ guro jātaḥ sevāyāstava sāṃpratam \|*  
*veśyāyā maṃdirasthena jñātvā nijakamaṃḍalum \|\| 18 \|\|*

*veśyāyā madyapātraṃ tu madyapūrṇaṃ pragṛhya ca \|*  
*tasmāddehi vibho mahyaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

Parāvasu said:

18-19. O venerable Sir, I am now unfit for your service. I had been to the abode of a courtesan. I mistook the pot of liquor of the courtesan for my water-pot and I drank it off. Hence, O holy Lord, prescribe an expiatory rite for the sake of purifying myself.

## \|\| 1.197.20 \|\|

*dharmadroṇeṣu yatproktaṃ tatkariṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Undoubtedly, I shall perform whatever has been ordained in the Dharmaśāstra (religious) texts.

## \|\| 1.197.21 \|\|

*atha taṃ baṭavaḥ procurvayasyāstasya ye sthitāḥ \|*  
*hāsyaṃ kṛtvā prakāmāśca veśyā yā gurusaṃnidhau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereupon, his friends, the Brāhmaṇa boys, who stood around there made funny remarks in the presence of the courtesan and the preceptor:

## \|\| 1.197.22 \|\|

*yā eṣā nṛpateḥ kanyā khyātā ratnāvatī jane \|*  
*asyāḥ stanau gṛhītvā tvamadharaṃ pibasi drutam \|*  
*tataste syādviśuddhiśca nānyathā prabhaviṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “The daughter of the king is well-known to all the people by the name Ratnavatī. You must hold her breasts and quickly kiss her lips. Thereby you will become purified' not otherwise.”

## \|\| 1.197.23 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*na vayasyā narmakālo viṣame mama saṃsthite \|*  
*mamopari yadi sneho vālamitratvasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tadānīya dvijānanyānvadadhvaṃ niṣkṛtiṃ mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

Parāvasu said:

23\. O my friends, this is no time for fun or gaiety when I am in an odd position. If you have any love for me by virtue of my being your boyhood friend, gather together other Brāhmaṇas and find out a way for my redemption,

## \|\| 1.197.24 \|\|

*atha te narmamutsṛjya tadduḥkhena ca duḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*viśvāvasuṃ samāsādya tadvṛttāṃtamathābruvan \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereupon, they all became serious and stopped passing jocular remarks. They became distressed due to his grief. They went up to. Viśvāvasu and narrated the news concerning him (Parāvasu).

## \|\| 1.197.25 \|\|

*so'pi teṣāṃ samākarṇya tatkarṇakaṭukaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*sabhāryaḥ prayayau tatra yatra putro vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing their words extremely disagreeable and unpleasant to the ears, he went along with his wife to the place where his son was present.

## \|\| 1.197.26 \|\|

*duḥkhena mahatā yuktaḥ skhalamānaḥ padepade \|*  
*vṛddhabhāvāttathā śokātputrākṛtyasamudbhavāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was extremely distressed. He faltered at every step due equally to his old age and the grief arising from the misdemeanour of his son.

## \|\| 1.197.27-28 \|\|

*tatastau procatuḥ putraṃ bāṣpagadgadayā girā \|*  
*daṃpatī bahuśokārtau hā putra kimidaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*so'pi sarvaṃ samācakhyau tābhyāṃ vṛtāṃtamātmanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ kariṣyāmi tasmādātmaviśuddhaye \|*  
*tato viśvāvasurviprānsmārtāñchrutisamanvitān \|*  
*tadarthamānayāmāsa vedavidyāvicakṣaṇān \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. With words choked and faltering due to tears the grief-stricken couple spoke to their son: “Alas, dear son! What have you done?” He (Parāvasu) narrated all the details about his act to them and expressed his desire, saying: “Hence, I shall perform expiatory rite to sanctify myself.”

Thereupon, Viśvāvasu summoned for the purpose Brāhmaṇas expert in the Smṛtis and having great mastery over the Vedic lore.

## \|\| 1.197.29-30 \|\|

*tataḥ parāvasusteṣāṃ puraḥ sthitvā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*provāca svāditaṃ madyaṃ mayā rātrāvajānatā \|*  
*veśyā bhāṃḍaṃ samādāya jñātvā nijakamaṃḍalum \|\| 29 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā yadarhaṃ ca prāyaścittaṃ pradīyatām \|*  
*yena me jāyate śuddhiḥ prasādādvo dvijottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Parāvasu stood before them with palms joined in reverence and said: “I have unwittingly imbibed liquor at night having lifted up the pot of the courtesan mistaking it for my own waterpot. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, considering this, do give me the requisite expiation so that, with your favour, I can regain sanctity.”

## \|\| 1.197.31 \|\|

*evamuktāstatastena viprāste smṛtivādinaḥ \|*  
*dharmaśāstraṃ samālokya tataḥ procuśca taṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On being requested thus by him, those Brāhmaṇas, the expounders of the Smṛti texts, pored over the scriptural texts and spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.197.32-33 \|\|

*atimānādatikrodhātsnehādvā yadi vā bhayāt \|*  
*prāyaścittamanarhaṃ tu dadattatpāpamaśnute \|\| 32 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ pradāsyāmastasmādyuktaṃ vayaṃ tava \|*  
*yadi śaknoṣi tatkartuṃ tatkuruṣva samāhitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. “If anyone performs expiatory rite on behalf of one who does not deserve it due to excess of arrogance, anger, love or fear, he incurs the sin thereof. Hence, we shall give (advise) you the befitting expiatory rites. If you are capable of doing it, do so with great concentration of mind.”

## \|\| 1.197.34 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*karomi vo na cedvākyaṃ tatpṛcchāmi kuto dvijāḥ \|*  
*nāhaṃ kenāpi saṃdṛṣṭo madyapānaṃ samācaran \|\| 34 \|\|*

Parāvasu said:

34\. I have not been seen imbibing liquor by anyone, O Brāhmaṇas. Then why should I ask you, if I don’t intend to act accordingly at your instance?

## \|\| 1.197.35 \|\|

*tasmādbrūta yathārhaṃ me prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*api prāṇaharaṃ raudraṃ no cetpāpamavāpsyatha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hence, lay down the amends befitting me for the sake of purity even if it be terrible and destructive of life. Otherwise, you will incur sin.

## \|\| 1.197.36 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*budhyamāno dvijo yastu madyapānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tāvanmātraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca taptaṃ pītvā viśudhyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

36\. A Brāhmaṇa who knowingly and wantonly drinks liquor shall become pure by drinking molten gold of equal quantity.

## \|\| 1.197.37 \|\|

*ajñānato yadā pītaṃ madyaṃ vipreṇa karhicit \|*  
*agnitulyaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā tāvanmātraṃ viśudhyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If liquor has been drunk unwittingly by any Brāhmaṇa, he becomes pure by drinking heated clarified butter of the same quantity.

## \|\| 1.197.38 \|\|

*evaṃ te sarvamākhyātaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*yadi śaktoṣi cetkartuṃ kuruṣva tvaṃ dvijottama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus everything regarding the expiatory rite for the sake of purity has been mentioned to you. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, if you can do it, do carry it out.

## \|\| 1.197.39 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*gaṃḍūṣamekaṃ madyasya mayā pītaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tāvanmātraṃ pibāmyeva ghṛtaṃ vahnisamaṃ kṛtam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Parāvasu said:

39\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a mouthful of liquor was drunk by me. I shall drink an equal quantity of ghee made hot like fire.

## \|\| 1.197.40 \|\|

*yuṣmadādeśato'dyaiva svaśarīraviśuddhaye \|*  
*viśvāvasuśca tacchrutvā vajrapātopamaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. At your behest I shall do so today itself for the sake of the purity of my body.

Viśvāvasu (was stunned) on hearing those words comparable to the thunderbolt.

## \|\| 1.197.41 \|\|

*viprāṇāṃ cātha putrasya tadovāca suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāśrumokṣaṇaṃ bhūri bāṣpagadgadayā girā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The words of his son and those of the Brāhmaṇas were no less than a thunderbolt. He then became extremely distressed and said with faltering words after shedding profuse tears:

## \|\| 1.197.42-43 \|\|

*sarvasvamapi dāsyāmi putrasyāsya viśuddhaye \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ samācartuṃ na dāsyāmi kathaṃcana \|\| 42 \|\|*

*aśrāddheyo vipāṃkteyaḥ saputro vā bhavāmyaham \|*  
*sthānaṃ vā saṃtyajāmyetatputra maivaṃ samācara \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. “For the sake of the purity of my son, I will give away all my possessions. But I will not let him at any cost perform this expiatory rite.

Let me become Aśrāddheya (unworthy of being invited for Śrāddha) or Vipāṅkteya (unworthy of sitting in the row of Brāhmaṇas for meals) along with my son. I shall very well abandon this spot. Dear son, do not perform this.”

## \|\| 1.197.44 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya piturvighnakaraṃ param \|*  
*prāyaścittasya sasnehaṃ putro vacanamabravīt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing those words of his father causing obstacles to the expiatory rites, the son spoke words affectionately:

## \|\| 1.197.45 \|\|

*tyaja tāta mama snehaṃ mā vighnaṃ me samācara \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ kariṣyāmi niścayo'yaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Stop this excess of affection for me. Do not create obstacles. I will certainly carry out this expiatory rite. This decision has been taken by me.”

## \|\| 1.197.46 \|\|

*mātovāca \|*  
*yadi putra tvayā kāryaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*tadahaṃ patinā sārdhaṃ pravekṣyāmi puro'nalam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Mother said:

46\. If it is compulsory for you, dear son, to perform this expiatory rite for the sake of purity, then I will enter the burning fire before you, along with my husband.

## \|\| 1.197.47 \|\|

*tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ naiva śakromi pibaṃtamagnivadghṛtam \|*  
*paścātprāṇaparityaktaṃ satyenā tmānamālabhe \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I will not be able to endure seeing you drinking the fiery hot ghee and falling dead thereafter. I solemnly take this vow.

## \|\| 1.197.48 \|\|

*pitovāca \|*  
*yuktaṃ putrānayā proktaṃ mātrā tava hitaṃ tathā \|*  
*mamāpi saṃmataṃ hyetatkariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Father said:

48\. Dear son, your mother has said most pertinently and also for the sake of your own benefit. I approve of it and shall do so undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.197.49 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare sarve suhṛdastasya ye sthitāḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā taṃ samāyātā vṛttāṃtaṃ duḥkhasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sūta said:

49\. In the meantime, all those friends of his heard about him and came there in great distress.

## \|\| 1.197.50 \|\|

*procuśca vividhairvākyaiḥ sapatnīkaṃ vibhāvasum \|*  
*putraśokena saṃtaptaṃ maraṇe kṛtaniścayam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They spoke various words to Vibhāvasu (Viśvāvasu) distressed along with his wife over his son, having decided to commit suicide.

## \|\| 1.197.51 \|\|

*putraṃ prabodhayāmāsuḥ prāyaścittanivṛttaye \|*  
*tadā na śaknuvaṃti sma nivartayitumaṃ jasā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. They also persuaded the son to desist from the performance of the said expiatory rite, but they were not able to do so.

## \|\| 1.197.52 \|\|

*tāvubhau ca pitāputrau prāṇatyāgakṛtādarau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Both of them, the father as well as the son, were bent upon putting an end to their lives.

## \|\| 1.197.53 \|\|

*tato vāstupadaṃ jagmuḥ sarvajño yatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*bhartṛyajño mahābhāgaḥ sarvasaṃdeha vārakaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then they went to the Vāstupada (site of abode) where the omniscient Bhartṛyajña, the highly esteemed scholar who clarified all doubts, was present.

## \|\| 1.197.54-55 \|\|

*tasya sarvaṃ samācakhyuḥ parāvasusamudbhavam \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ madyapānotthaṃ yanmitraistasya kīrtitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ tu hāsyena yacca smārtaiḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*viśvāvasośca saṃkalpaṃ vahnisādhanasaṃbhavam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. To him they narrated everything concerning Parāvasu, how he imbibed liquor, the details of expiatory rites jokingly mentioned by his friends, that enjoined by the exponents of Smṛtis and ultimately the idea of self-immolation by Parāvasu in fire.

## \|\| 1.197.56 \|\|

*sapatnīkasya mitrāṇāṃ yacca duḥkhamupasthitam \|*  
*nivedya tattathā procurbhū yo'pivinayānvitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. They also reported how he, his wife and all the friends grieved over this. After narrating all this, they spoke again politely:

## \|\| 1.197.57-60 \|\|

*atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca bhaviṣyadvāpi yadbhavet \|*  
*na te'styaviditaṃ kiṃcitsarvaṃ jānīmahe vayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*etacca nagaraṃ sarvaṃ viśvāvasukṛte'dhunā \|*  
*saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāptaṃ tena prāptāstavāṃtikam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tasmādbrūhi mahābhāga yadyastyaparameva hi \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ dvijasyāsya madyapānaviśuddhaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

*na te hyaviditaṃ kiṃcittava vedasamudbhavam \|*  
*bhartṛyajño vihasyoccaistato vacanamabravīt \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. “We all know that there is nothing unknown to you whether past, present, or future. We know that this whole city is very much in doubt about Viśvāvasu. Hence, we have approached you.

O highly esteemed one, say whether there is any other expiatory rite for the purification of this Brāhmaṇa who has imbibed liquor. There is nothing in the Vedic lore that is not known to you.”

Thereupon, Bhartṛyajña laughed loudly and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.197.61 \|\|

*brāhmaṇasyāsya śuddhyarthamapyayupāyaḥ sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*vidyamāno'pi nāstyeva matireṣā sthitā mama \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. “There is a very pleasant and easy means of purification for this Brāhmaṇa. Though present (in existence, available) it is actually non-existent. This is my opinion.”

## \|\| 1.197.62 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|\| pūrvāparavirodhe navākyametanmahāmate \|*  
*kathamasti kathaṃ nāsti tasmāttvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|*  
*vismayo'yaṃ mahāñjātaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca dvijanmanām \|\| 62 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

62\. O highly intelligent one, these statements are contradictory to each other. How is the means present? How is it non-existent? It behoves you to explicate. All the Brāhmaṇas are extremely surprised thereby.

## \|\| 1.197.63 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*japacchidraṃ tapaśchidraṃ yacchidraṃ yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*sarvaṃ bhavati niśchidraṃ yasya cecchaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

63\. A flaw in the performance of Japa, penance, sacrifice etc. can be corrected if the Brāhmaṇas wish so.

## \|\| 1.197.64 \|\|

*acchidramiti yadvākyaṃ vadaṃti kṣitidevatāḥ \|*  
*viśeṣānnāgarodbhūtāstattathaiva na cānyathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If the Brāhmaṇas, especially those hailing from the Nāgara community, utter “Achidra” (free from flaw) it shall definitely be so.

## \|\| 1.197.65 \|\|

*tathā ca brahmaśālāyāṃ saṃsthitairyadudāhṛtam \|*  
*nānyathā tatparijñeyaṃ hāsyenāpi smṛtiṃ vinā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Similarly, whatever has been uttered by those stationed in Brahma-śālā (Yajña site), it should be known, shall not become otherwise even if uttered in fun without a basis in Smṛti texts.

## \|\| 1.197.66-67 \|\|

*sa eṣa hāsyabhāvena prokto mitraiḥ parāvasuḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ratnavatyāḥ stanau gṛhya yadyāsvādayate'dharam \|*  
*tadbhaviṣyati me śuddhirmadyapāna samudbhavā \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. This Parāvasu has been told jokingly by his friends: “Your purity from the adverse effects of imbibing liquor shall be effected if you hold the breasts of Ratnavatī and kiss her lips.”

## \|\| 1.197.68 \|\|

*tadupāyo mayā prokto viprasyāsya sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*parāśaramatenaiva karoti yadi śudhyati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. This has been mentioned by me as a pleasant and easy means of purification in the case of this Brāhmaṇa. If he performs this in accordance with the injunctions of Parāśara, he shall become purified.

## \|\| 1.197.69 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadyetacchuṇute rājā vākyamīrṣyāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatsarveṣāṃ vadhaṃ kuryādviprāṇāmanyathā bhavet \|\| 69 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

69\. If the king were to hear this statement, he will become extremely intolerant and may kill all the Brāhmaṇas. It will be contrary to what we want.

## \|\| 1.197.70 \|\|

*tasmātkarotu cābhīṣṭameṣa vipraḥ parāvasuḥ \|*  
*mātāpitṛsamopeto vayaṃ yāsyāmahe gṛham \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, let this Brāhmaṇa Parāvasu do whatever he likes in the company of his mother and father. We shall go home.

## \|\| 1.197.71 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*sa rājā nītimānvijñaḥ sarvadharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhakto devadvijānāṃ ca sarvaśāstra vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

71\. That king is just and wise. He is devoted to all types of pious activities. He is an adept in all scriptural texts and is a devotee of Devas and Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.197.72 \|\|

*tasmānmayā samaṃ sarve nāgarāyāṃtu tadgrahe \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Hence, let all the Nāgaras go to his abode along with me.

## \|\| 1.197.73 \|\|

*madhyagaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā tadvaktreṇa ca tatpuraḥ \|*  
*kathayaṃtu ca vṛttāṃtaṃ madyapāna samudbhavam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. We shall keep the Madhyaga in front of us. Through him let us narrate the incident concerning the imbibing of liquor.

## \|\| 1.197.74 \|\|

*parāvasośca yatproktaṃ vayasyairhāsyamāśritaiḥ \|*  
*parāśarasamutthaṃ ca yadvākyaṃ tatsmṛteḥ param \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. We shall also narrate what was said jokingly to Parāvasu by his friends. The statement of Parāśara is greater than any other Smṛti.

## \|\| 1.197.75 \|\|

*tacchrutvā yadi bhūpāla īrṣyā lobhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati tato'haṃ taṃ dhārayiṣyāmi satpathe \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On hearing it, if the king becomes furiously intolerant and over-covetous, I shall make him abide by the path of the good.

## \|\| 1.197.76-82 \|\|

*sūtauvāca \|*  
*tataste nāgarāḥ sarve santoṣaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*sādhuvādaiḥ samabhyarcya bhartṛyajñaṃ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tenaiva sahitaṃ tūrṇaṃ madhye kṛtvā ca madhyagam \|*  
*garttātīrthasamudbhūtaṃ vedavedāṃgapāragam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*smṛtijñaṃ lakṣaṇajñaṃ tamāhitāgniṃ yaśasvinam \|*  
*yaṣṭāraṃ bahuyajñānāṃ bhartṛyajñamate sthitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ānartenāpi bhūpena svargabhraṣṭena vai purā \|*  
*karṇotpalājanitreṇa yaśca pūrvaṃ cirantanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*camatkārapure nyastaḥ sthāne'sminvipragauravāt \|*  
*yena sidhyaṃti kāryāṇi sarveṣāṃ ca dvijanmanām \|\| 80 \|\|*

*tathā caiva tu cānyāni camatkārapurasya ca \|*  
*haribhadrābhidhānaṃ taṃ bhartṛyajñasamanvitam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kṛtvā te nāgarāḥ sarve rājadvāramupāgatāḥ \|*  
*parāvasuṃ samādāya mātāpitṛsamanvitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

Sūta said:

76-82. Then all those Nāgaras became extremely pleased. They congratulated Bhartṛyajña in different kinds of words of approbation.

The Madhyaga was placed in the centre along with him (Bhartṛyajña). This Madhyaga hailed from Gartā Tīrtha. He had fully mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. He was conversant with the Smṛtis and all characteristic omens. He was famous as a regular householder preserving the sacred fires. He regularly performed many Yajñas. He scrupulously abided by the opinion of Bhartṛyajña.

It was he who was settled in this holy spot in Camatkārapura by virtue of being a Brāhmaṇa, formerly by the father of Karṇotpalā, the king of Ānarta who had fallen from heaven. Due to his efforts all the tasks of all the Brāhmaṇas were accomplished. Other works of Camatkārapura also got completed through him.

His name was Haribhadra. All the Nāgaras took him along with Bhartṛyajña and came to the threshold of the royal palace. They also took with them Parāvasu and his parents.

## \|\| 1.197.83 \|\|

*atha dvāḥstho drutaṃ gatvā bhūpatestānnyavedayat \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhartṛyajñena haribhadreṇa saṃyutān \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The door-keeper hastened within and intimated to the king that the Brāhmaṇas had arrived accompanied by Haribhadra and Bhartṛyajña.

## \|\| 1.197.84 \|\|

*ānarto'pi ca tāñchrutvā rājadvārasamāgatān \|*  
*purodhasā samāyuktaḥ saṃmukhaṃ prayayau tadā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On hearing that they had all come to the royal threshold, Ānarta came to receive them directly accompanied by his own priest.

## \|\| 1.197.85 \|\|

*dattvārghaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca viṣṭaraṃ gāṃ tathā nṛpaḥ \|*  
*prathamaṃ bhartṛyajñāya haribhadrāya vai tataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The king offered Argha, Madhuparka, a cow and a seat first to Bhartṛyajña and then to Haribhadra.

## \|\| 1.197.86 \|\|

*caturṇāṃ mudgahastānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ dvijanmanām \|*  
*ādyaṛgyajuḥsāmnāṃ ca pragṛhyāśīrvacaḥ param \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The same was offered to four Brāhmaṇas with Mudga (kidney bean) in their hands and also to the other Brāhmaṇas. Then the first one (the king) accepted their benedictions through Ṛk, Yājus and Sāman hymns.

## \|\| 1.197.87 \|\|

*sabhāmaṃḍapamāsādya sarvānsamupaveśayat \|*  
*varāsaneṣu haimeṣu yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He came to the pavilion and made all of them sit on excellent seats of gold in due order.

## \|\| 1.197.88 \|\|

*tathā teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu sarveṣu pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*upaviśya dharāpṛṣṭhe kṛtāṃjalira bhāṣata \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. When all of them sat, the king sat on the ground. With palms joined in reverence he spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.197.89-91 \|\|

*dhanyo'smyanugṛhīto'smi yanme gṛhamupāgataḥ \|*  
*sarvo'yaṃ nāgaro loko bhartṛyajñasamanvitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tadādiśatu māṃ loko yatkṛtyaṃ prakaromi vaḥ \|*  
*adeyamapi yacchāmi gṛhāyātasya sāṃpratam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*agamyamapi yāsyāmi kariṣye'kṛtyameva ca \|*  
*tacchrutvā haribhadraḥ sa samutthāya tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. “Blessed indeed am I. I have been duly honoured since all the Nāgara folk have come to my abode along with Brartṛyajña \[Bhartṛyajña?\].

Hence, surely command me, ye all. What task shall I carry out? To one who has arrived at my abode now, I will give even that which cannot be (ordinarily) given. I will approach even him who should not be approached. I will do even that which cannot be done.”

On hearing this, Haribhadra hurriedly stood up.

## \|\| 1.197.92 \|\|

*papracchādyāṃstadarthaṃ ca bahvṛcāṃstadanaṃtaram \|*  
*adhvaryūṃścaiva chāṃdogyānanujñātaśca taistadā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. For that purpose (i.e. what should be done now) he asked the Ādyas (the first ones, the elders) and then the Bahvṛcas, Adhvaryus and Chāndogyas. Then he was permitted by them.

## \|\| 1.197.93-94 \|\|

*prāṇarudrānvadaṃtvādyā jīvasūktaṃ ca bahvṛcāḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ caiva pṛthivyādisavanaṃ yatpurā kṛtam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*paṭhantvadhvaryavaḥ sarve chāṃdogyāśca pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*madhucyutena saṃyuktaṃ prapaṭhantu ca siddhaye \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. “May the Ādyas recite Prāṇarudra Mantras and the Bahvṛcas the Jīvasūkta hymn. It was by these that the Savana (sacrifice) of Prṭhivī etc., was performed formerly. Let all the Adhvaryus and the Chāndogyas recite separately the hymns including Madhucyuta for the purpose of fulfillment.”

## \|\| 1.197.95 \|\|

*bhartṛyajñamatenaivaṃ tena proktā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*papracchuścaiva tatsarvaṃ yatproktaṃ tena dhīmatā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. When the excellent Brāhmaṇas were addressed thus with the concurrence of Bhartṛyajña, they recited everything as was said by that intelligent one.

## \|\| 1.197.96 \|\|

*tataḥ pāṭhāvasāne tu madhyagaḥ prāha sādaram \|*  
*parāvasusamudbhūtaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ tasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. At the conclusion of the chanting and recitation the Madhyaga duly narrated to the king the episode connected with Parāvasu.

## \|\| 1.197.97 \|\|

*yathā tenā'savaḥ pīto yathā mitraiḥ prajalpitam \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ samādiṣṭaṃ yathā smārtairghṛtodbhavam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. He narrated how Āsava (liquor) had been imbibed by him, how the friends prattled something by way of expiation and how the expounders of the Smṛti proclaimed the expiatory rite of drinking (hot) ghee.

## \|\| 1.197.98 \|\|

*bhartṛyajñena cānītā yathā sarve dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā pārthivo hṛṣṭaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭo'bravīt \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. He also mentioned how all the Brāhmaṇas were brought together by Bhartṛyajña.

On hearing his words the king became delighted. With palms joined in due deference he spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.197.99-100 \|\|

*dhanyohaṃ kṛtapuṇyo'smi yasya me nāgarairdvijaiḥ \|*  
*vipratrayaprarakṣārthaṃ prasādo'yaṃ mahānkṛtaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*dhanyā me kanyakā ceyaṃ rakṣayiṣyati ca svayam \|*  
*brāhmaṇatritayaṃ hyetanmaraṇe kṛtaniścayam \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. “I am blessed. I am meritorious because a great favour has been bestowed on me by the Nāgara Brāhmaṇas resulting in the saving of the lives of three Brāhmaṇas. Blessed indeed is my daughter who will herself save three Brāhmaṇas who had decided to end their lives.”

## \|\| 1.197.101 \|\|

*athā'sāvānayāmāsa tāṃ kanyāṃ tatkṣaṇāddvijāḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭaṃ sabhāmadhye brāhmaṇebhyo nyavedayat \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. O Brāhmaṇas, then the king brought his daughter there immediately. When she sat in the centre of the assembly he offered her to the Brāhmaṇas (and said):

## \|\| 1.197.102 \|\|

*eṣā kanyā mayānītā yuṣmadvākyāddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhartṛyajñena yatproktaṃ tatkarotu ca sa dvijaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. “O excellent Brāhmaṇas, at your instance this daughter of mine has been summoned by me. Let that Brāhmaṇa do what has been laid down by Bhartṛyajña.”

## \|\| 1.197.103 \|\|

*tatastatra samānīya brāhmaṇa taṃ parāvasum \|*  
*bhartṛyajña idaṃ vākyaṃ kanyāyāḥ purato'bravīt \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Thereupon, Bhartṛyajña summoned the Brāhmaṇa Parāvasu there and spoke these words in the presence of the girl:

## \|\| 1.197.104-107 \|\|

*imāṃ tvaṃ kanyakāṃ citte jananīṃ yadi manyase \|*  
*adharāsvādanaṃ kurvaṃstataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 104 \|\|*

*anurāgaparo bhūtvā yadyāsvādanatatparaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati tato raktaṃ tava vaktre parāvaso \|\| 105 \|\|*

*śuddhasya tvatha dugdhaṃ ca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*stanābhyāṃ tava hastābhyāṃ sparśātkṣīraṃ bhavedyadi \|*  
*tatte śuddhiḥ parijñeyā raktaṃ vā na bhaviṣyati \|\| 107 \|\|*

104-107. “Even as you kiss her on her lips if you consider this girl as your mother you will attain Siddhi. If you kiss her with passionate love, O Parāvasu, blood will come out of your mouth. If you are innocent and pure, undoubtedly milk will exude therefrom.

On coming into contact with your hands if blood does not flow out of the breasts but milk does flow out, it should be known that you have become purified.”

## \|\| 1.197.108-110 \|\|

*evamuktvātha taṃ kanyāṃ tataḥ provāca sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*enaṃ tvaṃ putravatpaśya putri brāhmaṇasattamam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*yena śuddhimavāpnoti tvadoṣṭhāsvādane kṛte \|*  
*sparśitābhyāṃ stanābhyāṃ ca prāyaścittaṃ yataḥ smṛtam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*etadasya dvijeṃdrasya vayasyairhāsyasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*yena śuddhimavāpnoti no cenmṛtyumavāpsyati \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. After saying thus to him the Brāhmaṇa said to the girl: “Dear daughter, consider this excellent Brāhmaṇa as though he is your son. Thereby, he will attain purity. In accordance with the Smṛti, the expiatory rite is the kissing of your lips and touching your breasts.

This expiatory rite has been jokingly suggested by the friends of this leading Brāhmaṇa. Thereby, he will attain purity. Otherwise he will meet with death.”

## \|\| 1.197.111-112 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā tatheti pratijñāya savrīḍaṃ tamuvāca ha \|*  
*ehi vatsa kuruṣva tvaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|\| 111 \|\|*

*mātṛbhāvaṃ samādhāya mayā tvaṃ kalpitaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*so'pi tāṃ mātṛvanmatvā tasyāḥ sāṃnidhyamāgataḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

Sūta said:

111-112. She assented saying, “So it shall be” and spoke to him (Parāvasu) shyly: “Do come dear child, perform the expiatory rite for the sake of purity.

I have adopted motherly attitude and you have been considered my son.”

He too considered her as his mother and came to her vicinity.

## \|\| 1.197.113-114 \|\|

*spṛṣṭavāṃśca stanau tasyāḥ sarvalokasya paśyataḥ \|*  
*spṛṣṭābhyāṃ ca stanābhyāṃ ca tatkṣaṇāddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*kṣīradhāre viniṣkrāṃte kundeṃduhimasaṃnibhe \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. Even as all the people were watching he touched her breasts. At the very same moment, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, two streams of milk flowed from those breasts touched by him. The streams resembled a jasmine flower, the moon and snow flakes.

## \|\| 1.197.115 \|\|

*athauṣṭhāsvādanaṃ yāvattasyāḥ sa kurute dvijaḥ \|*  
*tāvatkṣīraṃ viniṣkrāṃtaṃ tādṛgrūpaṃ tadānanāt \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Afterwards when the Brāhmaṇa kissed her lips, milk flowed out of her mouth as before.

## \|\| 1.197.116 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare sarvaistālā dattā dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*rājñā'yaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śuddho vadamānairmuhurmuhuḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. In the meantime hands were clapped by all the Brāhmaṇas as well as the king, even as they repeatedly said: “This Brāhmaṇa is pure now.”

## \|\| 1.197.117 \|\|

*so'pi pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tāṃ ca kanyāṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya kṣamasveti tvaṃ mātaḥ putravatsale \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He (Parāvasu) circumambulated the girl many times. After bowing down to her, he said: “Forgive me, O mother fond of your son.”

## \|\| 1.197.118 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryamānarto vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*śaśaṃsa bhatṛyajñaṃ taṃ prāyaścittapradāyakam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. On seeing this great wonderful incident the king was surprised. He praised Bhartṛyajña who had enjoined the expiatory rite.

## \|\| 1.197.119-121 \|\|

*aho'tīva subhā gyo'haṃ yasya me gṛhamāgatāḥ \|*  
*īdṛśā brāhmaṇāḥ sarve camatkārapurodbhavāḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

*tathā caitādṛśī kanyā hyasāmānyapravartinī \|*  
*ratnāvatī mahābhāgā satyaśaucasamanvitā \|\| 120 \|\|*

*tathā'yaṃ naiva sāmānyo brāhmaṇaśca parāvasuḥ \|*  
*yaścedṛśīṃ samāsādya kanyāṃ no vikṛtaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

119-121. “Oh! Wonderful! I am extremely fortunate, since such Brāhmaṇas hailing from Camatkārapura have come to my city.

A girl like this has carried out an unprecedented task. Ratnavatī is really highly praise-worthy and endowed with truthfulness and purity.

Similarly, this Brāhmaṇa Parāvasu is not an ordinary Brāhmaṇa. In spite of coming close to such a girl, he has not become excited.”

## \|\| 1.197.122 \|\|

*evamuktvā visṛjyātha tānviprānpārthivottamāḥ \|*  
*tāṃ ca kanyāṃ samādāya tataścāṃtaḥpuraṃ yayau \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. After saying thus and bidding farewell to those Brāhmaṇas, the excellent king went into the inner apartment taking his daughter with him.

## \|\| 1.197.123-125 \|\|

*atha te nāgarāḥ sarve maryādāṃ cakrire tataḥ \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti yā veśyā sthāne'sminvāsameṣyati \|\| 123 \|\|*

*tayā naiva gṛhe dhāryaṃ surāmāṃsaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*dūṣayaṃti sadā duṣṭā nāgarāṇāṃ sutāniha \|\| 124 \|\|*

*atha vyavasthāmutkramya yā hi taddhārayiṣyati \|*  
*sā daṇḍyāsmācca nirvāsyā pretya syātpāpabhāginī \|\| 125 \|\|*

123-125. Then all those Nāgaras stipulated the bounds of decency: “From now no courtesan staying here should keep liquor or meat in her abode. These defiled women will spoil the sons of Nāgaras.

One who transgresses this stipulation should be punished by us and banished from this holy spot. After death, she will incur sins.”

## \|\| 1.197.126 \|\|

*audumbaryā madhyagena dattaṃ tālatrayaṃ tadā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Then the Madhyaga clapped thrice with a shoot of Uduṃbara tree (in his hand).

## Chapter 198 - Śūdrī Brāhmaṇī Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.198.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu daśārṇādhipatistadā \|*  
*ratnavatyā vivāhārthaṃ tatra sthāne samāgataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sa śrutvā tatra vṛttāṃtaṃ ratnavatyāḥ samudbhavam \|*  
*viraktiṃ paramāṃ kṛtvā prasthitaḥ svapuraṃ prati \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ śrutvā prasthitaṃ bhūpamānartaḥ svapuraṃ prati \|*  
*pṛṣṭhato'nuyayau tasya vyāgho ṭanakṛte tadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. It was at this juncture that the Lord of Daśārṇa came to that spot for doing matrimonial alliance with Ratnavatī.

But on hearing the details of the incident pertaining to Ratnavatī, he became extremely disinterested and so returned to his own city.

On hearing that the visiting king Daśārṇa was going back to his own city, Ānarta followed closely behind him to make him turn back.

## \|\| 1.198.4 \|\|

*athābravīcca taṃ prāpya kasmāttvaṃ prasthito nṛpa \|*  
*pāṇigrahamakṛtvā tu mama kanyāsamudbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After coming near him, he said: “O king, why have you turned back without taking the hand of my daughter in marriage?”

## \|\| 1.198.5 \|\|

*daśārṇa uvāca \|*  
*dūṣiteyaṃ tava sutā kanyakātvavivarjitā \|*  
*yasyāḥ pīto'dharo'nyena marditau ca tathā stanau \|\| 5 \|\|*

Daśārṇa said:

5\. This daughter of yours has become defiled. Her virginity has been molested as her lips have been kissed and her breasts have been pressed.

## \|\| 1.198.6-9 \|\|

*punarbhūriti saṃjñā sā sañjātā duhitā tava \|*  
*punarbhūrjanayetputraṃ yaṃ kadācitkathaṃcana \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sa pātayatyasaṃdigdhaṃ daśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|*  
*ekaviṃśatimaṃ caiva tathaivātmānameva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*na variṣyāmyahaṃ tena sutāṃ te'haṃ narasipa \|*  
*nirdākṣiṇyamiti procya daśārṇādhipatistadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*chaṃdyamāno'pi vividhairhastyaśvarathapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*avajñāya mahīpālaṃ prasthitaḥ svapuraṃ prati \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-8a. Your daughter has now earned the appellation of Punarbhū (‘widow remarried’). If any son is somehow born to a Punarbhū at any time, he will undoubtedly cause the downfall of ten predecessors and ten successors in his family and he himself will be the twenty-first one. Therefore, I will not woo your daughter, O king.

8b-9. After saying this rudely, the Lord of Daśārṇa went back to his city. In spite of his offer of various things such as elephants, horses and chariots, and pressing pleadings, he insulted the other king.

## \|\| 1.198.10 \|\|

*athānartto gṛhaṃ prāpya mṛgāvatyāḥ samākulaḥ \|*  
*tadvṛttaṃ kathayāmāsa yaduktaṃ tena bhūbhujā \|*  
*svabhāryāyāḥ sutāyāśca mantriṇāṃ duḥkhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the distressed king of Ānarta returned to his abode and told Mṛgāvatī all that had happened and what had been spoken by the king. He thus shared the misery of his wife, daughter and the ministers.

## \|\| 1.198.11-12 \|\|

*te procuḥ saṃti bhūpālāḥ saṃkhyāhīnā mahītale \|*  
*rūpāḍhyā yauvanopetā hastyaśvarathasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*teṣāmekatamasya tvaṃ dehi kanyāṃ nijāṃ vibho \|*  
*mā viṣāde manaḥ kṛtvā duḥkhasya vaśago bhava \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. But they said: “There are innumerable kings on the earth. They are endowed with (good) features, prime of youth and possess elephants, horses and chariots. O Lord, give your daughter to one of them. Why should you be dejected and subject yourself to tormenting grief?”

## \|\| 1.198.13 \|\|

*ānarto'pi ca tacchrutvā teṣāṃ vākyaṃ suduḥkhitam \|*  
*tataḥ prāha prahṛṣṭātmā tānsarvānmantripūrvakān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing their words, albeit uttered in great grief, Ānarta became delighted and he addressed the ministers and others.

## \|\| 1.198.14-15 \|\|

*tāṃ ca kanyāṃ sthitāṃ tatra sāmnā paramavalgunā \|*  
*putri dṛṣṭā mahīpālāḥ sarve citragatāstvayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ madhyānnṛpaṃ cānyaṃ kañcidvaraya śobhane \|*  
*yaste cittasya santoṣaṃ kurute dṛkpathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. He used extremely conciliatory and sweet words to his daughter who was present there: “Dear daughter, all the kings have been seen by you in the portraits. O splendid girl, choose some other king from them, whoever is likely to satisfy you on being seen directly.”

## \|\| 1.198.16 \|\|

*ratnāvatyuvāca \|*  
*na cāhaṃ varayiṣyāmi patimanyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*daśārṇādhipatiṃ muktvā śrūyatāmatra kāraṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Ratnavatī said:

16\. At any cost I will not take another husband excepting the Lord of Daśārṇa. May the reason thereof be heard.

## \|\| 1.198.17 \|\|

*sakṛjjalpaṃti rājānaḥ sakṛjjalpaṃti ca dvijāḥ \|*  
*sakṛtkanyāḥ pradīyaṃte trīṇyetāni sakṛtsakṛt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Kings speak only once. They don’t change their words. Twice-borns speak only once. Virgins are given in marriage only once. All these three take place only once.

## \|\| 1.198.18 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā na māṃ tāta tvamanyasminmahīpatau \|*  
*dātumarhasi dharmo'yaṃ na bhavecchāśvato yataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After realizing this, dear father, desist from giving me to another king. It does not behove you to do so because the eternal Dharma cannot be sustained thereby.

## \|\| 1.198.19-20 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*vāṅmātreṇa pradattā tvaṃ daśārṇādhipatermayā \|*  
*na te hastagrahaṃ prāpto viprāgnigurusannidhau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tatkathaṃ sa patirjātastavaḥ putri vadasva me \|\| 20 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

19-20. You have been given to the Lord of Daśārṇa only orally. He has not grasped your hand in the presence of the holy fire, Brāhmaṇas and preceptor. Hence, tell me, dear daughter, how has be become your husband?

## \|\| 1.198.21 \|\|

*ratnāvatyuvāca \|*  
*manasā ciṃtyate kāryaṃ sakṛttātapurā yataḥ \|*  
*vācayā procyate paścāt karmaṇā kriyate tataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Ratnavatī said:

21\. At the outset, all acts are mentally thought of once. Later, it is uttered orally. Thereafter, it is carried out in practice.

## \|\| 1.198.22 \|\|

*tanmayā manasā dattastasyātmā'yaṃ purā kila \|*  
*tvayā ca vācayā cāsmai pradattāsmi tathā vibho \|*  
*tatkathaṃ na patirme syādbrūhi vā yadi manyase \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Indeed, the soul has been given over to him at the outset by me. Thereafter, O Lord, it was orally given to him by you. Then, how can he not be my husband? Tell me if you really think so.

## \|\| 1.198.23 \|\|

*sāhaṃ tapaścariṣyāmi kaumāravratadhāriṇī \|*  
*nānyaṃ patiṃ kariṣyāmi niścayo'yaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I will undertake penance adopting the vow of celibacy. I will not wed another husband. This decision has been made by me.

## \|\| 1.198.24 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ raudraṃ mātā tasyā mṛgāvatī \|*  
*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing those terrible words, her mother Mṛgāvatī spoke these words with tears filling her eyes in the state of dejection and distress:

## \|\| 1.198.25-29 \|\|

*mā putri sāhasaṃ kārṣīstapo'rthaṃ tvaṃ kathañcana \|*  
*bālā tvaṃ sukumārāṃgī sadaiva sukhabhāginī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kathaṃ tapaḥ samarthāsi vidhātuṃ tvamaniṃdite \|*  
*kandamūlaphalāhārā cīravalkaladhāriṇī \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmānmukhyasya bhūpasya kasyacitvāṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*eṣā te brāhmaṇīnāma sakhī paramasaṃmatā \|*  
*pratīkṣate vivāhaṃ te kaumāraṃ bhāvamāśritā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yasya bhūpasya tvaṃ harmye prayāsyasi vivāhi tā \|*  
*purodhāstasya yo rājño bhāryeyaṃ tasya bhāvinī \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. “Dear daughter, do not be rash enough to undertake a penance at any cost. You are a mere girl of delicate limbs and always accustomed to enjoy pleasures.

O blameless girl, how will you be able to perform a penance? Your diet should be confined to roots, fruits and bulbous roots. You will have to wear bark garments. Hence, I shall give you in marriage to some eminent king.

This your highly esteemed companion named Brāhmaṇī has herself adopted a life of celibacy and is awaiting your marriage. She is to become the wife of the priest of that king to whose mansion you will go after being wedded.”

## \|\| 1.198.30 \|\|

*ratnāvatyuvāca \|*  
*na ca bhūyastvayā vācyaṃ vākyamevaṃvidhaṃ kvacit \|*  
*madarthe yadi me prāṇāstvaṃ vāṃchasi sutaiṣiṇī \|\| 30 \|\|*

Ratnavatī said:

30\. You should never speak again words like these on my behalf, if you love your daughter and desire that I should be alive.

## \|\| 1.198.31-32 \|\|

*athavā tvaṃ haṭhārthaṃ ca tapovighnaṃ kariṣyasi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatastyakṣyāmyahaṃ dehaṃ bhakṣayitvā mahadviṣam \|*  
*khaṃḍayiṣyāmyahaṃ jihvāṃ pravekṣyāmi ca vā jalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. On the other hand, if you obstinately put obstacles in my penance, I will swallow some powerful poison and put an end to my life. Or, I will cut off my tongue or drown myself in water.

## \|\| 1.198.33-34 \|\|

*evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā procya tāṃ jananīṃ tadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tataḥ provāca tāṃ kanyāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ saṃmatāṃ sakhīm \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭā bhūtvā samāliṃgya ca sādaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. After taking such an ominous decision and telling her mother in so many words, she said thus to Brāhmaṇī, her esteemed girl companion. She embraced her respectfully and said with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.198.35-36 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ svapiturharmyaṃ preṣitāsi mayā śubhe \|*  
*yena te yacchati pitā nāgarāya mahātmane \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kṣamasva yanmayā proktā kadācitparuṣaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tvayāpi yanmama proktaṃ kṣāṃtaṃ caitanmayā dhruvam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. “O splendid girl, I have discharged you. Go to the mansion of your father so that your father can give you to a noble-souled Nāgara.

Forgive me if I have at my time spoken harshly to you. I have certainly forgiven whatever might have been uttered by you against me.”

## \|\| 1.198.37 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca \|*  
*aṣṭavarṣā bhavedgaurī navavarṣā tu rohiṇī \|*  
*daśavarṣā bhavetkanyā ata ūrdhvaṃ rajasvalā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brāhmaṇī said:

37\. A girl of eight years is called Gaurī. One of nine years is Rohiṇī. A girl of ten years shall be a Kanyā. Beyond this she is Rajasvalā (one with menses).

## \|\| 1.198.38 \|\|

*kaumāryaṃ ca praṇaṣṭaṃ me tvatsaṃparkādvarānane \|*  
*jātaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ varṣaṃ strīdharmeṇa samanvitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O lady of excellent countenance, my girlhood has ceased after coining in contact with you. I have come to the age of sixteen years with regular menses as befitting a woman.

## \|\| 1.198.39 \|\|

*na me pāṇigrahaṃ kaścinnāgaro'tra kariṣyati \|*  
*budhyamānastu smṛtyarthaṃ vakṣya māṇaṃ varānane \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. No Nāgara here will take my hand in marriage in view of his knowledge of the Smṛti dictum:

## \|\| 1.198.40-41 \|\|

*rajasvalāṃ ca yaḥ kanyāmudvāhayati nirghṛṇaḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ santānamāsādya pātayetpuruṣāndaśa \|\| 40 \|\|*

*rajasvalā tu yaḥ kanyāṃ pitā yacchati nirghṛṇaḥ \|*  
*sa pātayedasaṃdigdhaṃ daśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. “He who marries a Rajasvalā (a girl above ten years of age) without feeling aversion, will cause the downfall of ten generations through the child thereof.

A father who gives away in marriage a Rajasvalā girl without aversion shall undoubtedly cause the downfall of ten generations of predecessors as well as ten generations of successors.”

## \|\| 1.198.42 \|\|

*tasmādahaṃ kariṣyāmi tvayā sārdhaṃ tapaḥ śubhe \|*  
*pitrā naiva hi me kāryaṃ na ca mātrā kathaṃcana \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, O splendid girl, I shall perform penance along with you. I have nothing to do with my father. I have nothing to do at all with my mother.

## \|\| 1.198.43 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā kanyake dve dvijotamāḥ \|*  
*gate yatra sthitaḥ sākṣādbhartṛyajño mahāmuniḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sūta said:

43\. After resolving this, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, those two girls went to the place where the great sage Bhartṛyajña was staying personally.

## \|\| 1.198.44-46 \|\|

*sthito vāstupade ramye sarvatīrthamaye śubhe \|*  
*tasya tapaḥprabhāvena jātu kopo na dṛśyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kasyacitkvāpi martyasya tiryagyoniga tasya ca \|*  
*krīḍaṃti nakulāḥ sarpairmārjārāḥ saha mūṣakaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sāraṃgā dvīpibhiḥ sārdhaṃ kākāśca saha kauśikaiḥ \|*  
*bhartṛyajñaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ tatra gatvā tu te śubhe \|*  
*procaturvinayopete kṛtāṃjalipuṭe sthite \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. He was stationed in the beautiful Vāstupada consisting of all Tīrthas. By the power of his penance, no one, whether a human being or an ordinary base creature, had the feelings of anger. Mongooses played with serpents and cats with mice. Stags played with panthers and crows with owls.

The splendid girls approached Bhartṛyajña who was comfortably seated and spoke to ḥīm humbly with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 1.198.47-48 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ sakhyā samaṃ yātā hyanayā rājakanyayā \|*  
*tapo'rthe tava pādāṃte tadbrūhi tapaso vidhim \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vadasva yena tatkṛtsnaṃ prakaromi mahāmate \|\| 48 \|\|*

Brāhmaṇī said:

47-48. Accompanied by this friend of mine, a princess, I have come to your feet for the sake of performing penance. Hence do expound the procedure of penance. Do instruct me, O highly intelligent one, so that I can perform it completely.

## \|\| 1.198.49 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi tapaścaryāvidhiṃ pṛthak \|*  
*yena saṃprāpyate mokṣaḥ ki punastridaśālayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

49\. I shall expound to you the procedure of penance distinctly whereby even salvation can be obtained, why speak of heaven?

## \|\| 1.198.50-51 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tathā sāṃtapanāni ca \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhe kāle tathā bhojyaṃ dināṃtaritameva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*brahmakūrcaṃ trirātraṃ ca ekabhaktamayācitam \|*  
*tapodvārāṇi sarvāṇi kṛtānyetāni vedhasā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The following types of penance have been enjoined by Vedas: Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, Sāntapana, taking food once instead of six times (i.e. once in three days), taking food on alternate days, Brahmakūrca (drinking Pañcagavya on Full-moon day after fast), Trirātra (fasting for three days) and Ekabhakta (a single meal per day), Ayācita (without begging for food or an eatable).

## \|\| 1.198.52 \|\|

*svaśaktyā caiva kāryāṇi rāgadveṣavivarjitaiḥ \|*  
*vāṃchitavyaṃ phalaṃ caiva sarveṣāmeva putrike \|*  
*tataḥ siddhimavāpnoti yā sadā manasi sthitā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. These types of penance should be performed by persons without Rāga (attachment) and Dveṣa (aversion). They should be performed in accordance with one’s capacity. Dear daughter, the benefit of all of them is equally desirable. Thereby one attains the Siddhi that has been mentally conceived always.

## \|\| 1.198.53 \|\|

*samatvaṃ śatrumitrābhyāṃ tathā pā ṣāṇaratnayoḥ \|*  
*yadā saṃjāyate citte tadā mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When an attitude of impartiality arises in the mind for enemies and friends as well as a stone and a gem, one attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.198.54 \|\|

*yo liṃgagrahaṇaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kopaparo bhavet \|*  
*tasya vṛthā hi tatsarvaṃ yathā bhasmahutaṃ tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If after taking the sign (initiation in penance) one becomes angry, everything becomes futile, like Homa performed in ashes.

## \|\| 1.198.55 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sā tathetipratijñāya brāhmaṇī sahitā tayā \|*  
*ratnāvatyā jagāmātha kiṃciccaiva jalāśayam \|\| 55 \|\|*

Sūta said:

55\. Brāhmaṇī promised to do so by saying “So it shall be.” Accompanied by Ratnavatī, she went to a water-pond.

## \|\| 1.198.56 \|\|

*svacchodakena saṃpūrṇaṃ padminīṣaṃḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*tataścāṃdrāyaṇaṃ cakre tapasaḥ prathamaṃ vratam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It was full of clear water and was adorned by clusters of lotus-plants.

Then she performed the Cāndrāyaṇa rite, the first of the Vratas pertaining to her penance.

## \|\| 1.198.57 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchravrataṃ cakre tataḥ sāṃtapanaṃ ca sā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhānnakālabhojyā ca sā cābhūdvatsaratrayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then she performed the Kṛcchra expiation and the Sāntapana rite thereafter. Thereafter, for three years she took food only once in the course of six meal times.

## \|\| 1.198.58 \|\|

*trirātropoṣaṇaṃ paścādyāvadvarṣatrayaṃ tathā \|*  
*ekāntaropavāsaiśca sā'nayadvatsaratrayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Afterwards, for three years she performed the Vrata of observing Trirātra (fasting for three days). Then she passed three years observing Ekāntaropavāsas (fasting on alternate days).

## \|\| 1.198.59 \|\|

*hemaṃte jalamadhyasthā sā babhūva tapasvinī \|*  
*paṃcāgnisādhakā grīṣme sā babhūva yaśasvinī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The saintly lady remained in water during early winter and during summer she performed penance in the midst of five fires and earned fame.

## \|\| 1.198.60 \|\|

*nirāśrayā'bhavatsādhvī varṣākāla upasthite \|*  
*dhyāyamānā divānaktaṃ devadevaṃ janārdanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The chaste lady remained without a shelter during rainy season. She meditated on Janārdana, the Lord of Devas, throughout the days and nights.

## \|\| 1.198.61 \|\|

*yadyadvrataṃ purā cakre brāhmaṇī sā ca suvratā \|*  
*anyaṃ jalāśayaṃ prāpya sā taccakre nṛpātmajā \|*  
*prītyā paramayā yuktā tadā sā dvijasa ttamāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The king’s daughter went to another pond and performed whatever Vrata had been performed by Brāhmaṇī earlier. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that lady of good holy rites was then highly delighted.

## \|\| 1.198.62 \|\|

*tato varṣaśataṃ sārdhaṃ phalāhārā babhūva sā \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśanā paścāttāvanmātraṃ vyavasthitā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then she adopted a regular fruit-diet for a hundred and fifty years. Afterwards, she ate only withered leaves for an equal period of time.

## \|\| 1.198.63 \|\|

*tataścaiva jalāhārā yāvadvarṣaśatāni ṣaṭ \|*  
*vāyubhakṣā babhūvātha sahasraṃ parivatsarān \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then for a period of six hundred years, she took in only water. Thereafter, for the period of a thousand full years her only intake was air.

## \|\| 1.198.64 \|\|

*yathāyathā tapaścakre sā kumārī dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tathātathā'bhavattasyāstejovṛddhiranuttamā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as the virgin went on performing her penance, her excellent refulgence went on increasing.

## \|\| 1.198.65-66 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*gauryā saha prasannātmā tasyā gocaramāgataḥ \|*  
*meghagaṃbhīrayā vācā tatovacanamabravīt \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. In the meantime, the delighted Moon-crested Lord accompanied by Umā, came within her view. Thereafter, he spoke these words as majestically as the deep sound of a rumbling cloud:

## \|\| 1.198.67 \|\|

*vatse taponivṛttiṃ tvaṃ kuruṣva vacanānmama \|*  
*prārthayasva mano'bhīṣṭaṃ yena sarvaṃ dadāmi te \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “Dear child, conclude your penance at my instance and pray for anything mentally desired, so that I can grant it to you entirely.”

## \|\| 1.198.68 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca \|*  
*abhīṣṭametadevaṃ me yattvaṃ dṛṣṭo'si śaṃkara \|*  
*svapne'pi darśanaṃ deva durlabhaṃ te nṛṇāṃ yataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Brāhmaṇī said:

68\. This alone had been my wish, O Śaṅkara, that you may be seen, since, O Lord, your vision is very difficult to get even in a dream in the case of humans.

## \|\| 1.198.69 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*na me syāddarśanaṃ vyarthaṃ kathaṃcitsutapasvini \|*  
*tasmādvaraya bhadraṃ te varaṃ yena dadāmyaham \|\| 69 \|\|*

The Lord.said:

69\. O lady of excellent penance, my vision can never be futile. Welfare unto you. Therefore, choose your boon so that I can grant it unto you.

## \|\| 1.198.70 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca \|*  
*eṣā me susakhī sādhvī rājaputrī yaśasvinī \|*  
*khyātā ratnāvatīnāma prāṇebhyo'pigarīyasī \|\| 70 \|\|*

Brāhmaṇī said:

70\. This is my excellent companion, the chaste princess of great renown well-known by the name Ratnavatī. She is dearer to me than my own vital breath.

## \|\| 1.198.71 \|\|

*mama tulyaṃ tapaścakre śūdrayonāvapi sthitā \|*  
*nivartate tu yadyeṣā tapasastu nivartanam \|*  
*karomyadya jagannātha tadahaṃ saṃśayaṃ vinā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Though she is born of a Śūdra womb, she in respect of penance is on a par with me. If she ceases to perform penance I too shall cease. O Lord of the universe, there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.198.72 \|\|

*asyāḥ snehena saṃtyakto mayā bhartā sureśvara \|*  
*tasmāddeva varaṃ dehi tvamasyā manasi sthitam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Lord of Suras, due to the affection for her, I have forsaken my husband. Hence, O Lord, grant the boon that has been cherished in her mind.

## \|\| 1.198.73-74 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*abravīdrājaputrīṃ tāṃ meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|*  
*vatse madvacanādadya tapastvaṃ tyaktumarhasi \|\| 73 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya kalyāṇi nityaṃ manasi saṃsthitam \|*  
*adeyamapi dāsyāmi sāṃprataṃ tava bhāmini \|\| 74 \|\|*

Sūta said:

73-74. On hearing her words the Moon-crested Lord said to the princess in words as majestic as the rumbling of a cloud:

“Dear daughter, it behoves you to stop further penance at my instance. O fair lady, choose your boon that has been cherished in your mind always. I shall grant it now, O gentle lady, even if it is not to be given (ordinarily).”

## \|\| 1.198.75 \|\|

*ratnāvatyuvāca \|*  
*etajjalāśayaṃ puṇyaṃ padminīṣaṇḍa maṇḍitam \|\| 75 \|\|*

Ratnavatī said:

75\. This water-pond is meritorious and is adorned by clusters of lotus plants.

## \|\| 1.198.76 \|\|

*yatraiṣā brāhmaṇī sādhvī nityaṃ ca tapasi sthitā \|*  
*asyā nāmnā ca vikhyātiṃ tīrthametatprapadyatām \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. It is the place where this chaste Brāhmaṇī has been engaged in her penance always. Let this Tīrtha become well known after her name.

## \|\| 1.198.77 \|\|

*atra yaḥ kurute snānaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhūyātsadā vāso devadeva triviṣṭape au \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O Lord of Devas, if a person takes his holy bath here with great faith, let him have his perpetual residence in Heaven.

## \|\| 1.198.78 \|\|

*madīyaṃ mama nāmnā tu śūdrāsaṃjñaṃ tu jāyatām \|*  
*tasya tulyaprabhāvaṃ tu tīrthasya pratipadyatām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Let my pond be named Śūdra Tīrtha after my name. Let it have the same power as the previous one.

## \|\| 1.198.79 \|\|

*āvābhyāṃ nityaśaḥ kāryaṃ kumāratve mahattapaḥ \|*  
*ārādhyastvaṃ suraśreṣṭho vāṅmanaḥkarmabhistathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. In our virginity great penance should be performed everyday by us. You, the most excellent one of Suras, should be the one to be propitiated by us verbally, mentally and physically.

## \|\| 1.198.80 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu nirbhidya dharaṇītalam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ māheśvaraṃ viprā niṣkrāṃtaṃ sūryasaṃnibham \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. In the meantime, O Brāhmaṇas, the Liṅga of Maheśvara resembling the Sun pierced through the earth and came out.

## \|\| 1.198.81 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca te devaḥ svayameva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ sutapasā tuṣṭaḥ sādaraṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Lord Maheśvara who had became pleased by their excellent penance and who is fond of his devotees, spoke to them eagerly himself:

## \|\| 1.198.82-85 \|\|

*etattīrthadvayaṃ khyātaṃ trailokyepi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śūdrīnāma tvadīyaṃ tu brāhmaṇī ca sakhī tava \|\| 82 \|\|*

*tīrthadvaye'pi yaḥ snātvā etasmiñchraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*tvattaḥ padmāni saṃgṛhya asyāstoyaṃ ca nirmalam \|*  
*etacca māmakaṃ liṃgaṃ snāpayitvā'rcayiṣyati \|\| 83 \|\|*

*paścātpadmaiścaturdaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ somavāsare \|*  
*caitre māsi ca saṃprāpte cirāyuḥ sa bhaviṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto yadyapi syātsupāpakṛt \|\| 85 \|\|*

82-85. “The pair of these Tīrthas will become well-known in all the three worlds. Your Tīrtha shall be called Śūdri Tīrtha and that of your companion Brāhmaṇī Tīrtha.

A person should take his holy bath in both the Tīrthas with great faith. He should collect lotuses from your Tīrtha and pure water from her Tīrtha. Then he shall bathe my Liṅga and adore it.

Afterwards, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half coinciding with a Monday in the month of Caitra, he should adore it with lotus flowers. He will have long life.

Even if he has committed great sins, he shall become rid of all those sins.”

## \|\| 1.198.86 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tatra nityaṃ ca tapasi sthite sakhyāvubhāvapi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. After saying thus, the Lord vanished. The two lady companions stayed there and performed penance for ever.

## \|\| 1.198.87 \|\|

*yāvatkalpaśataṃ tāvajjarāmaraṇavarji te \|*  
*adyāpi gagane te ca dṛśyete tārakātmake \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. They continued the penance for a hundred Kalpas without old age and death. Even today they are seen in the firmament in the form of stars.

## \|\| 1.198.88-89 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tatkhyātaṃ tīrthayugmaṃ dharātale \|*  
*āgatyātha naro dūrāttābhyāṃ kṛtvā nimajjanam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā tu talliṃgaṃ tato yāti divālayam \|*  
*mahāpātakayukto'pi tatprabhāvādasaṃśayam \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Ever since then the pair of the Tīrthas became reputed all over the earth. People from far-away places came there and had their holy ablution in both of them. After adoring that Liṅga they went to Heaven even when they were overwhelmingly sinful. Undoubtedly, it was due to the power of the two Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.198.90 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare martye naṣṭā dharmasya ca kriyā \|*  
*yajñadānakṛtā yā ca devārcanasamudbhavā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. In the meanwhile all holy rites such as Yajña, Dāna (gifts) and adoration of deities ceased to be performed in the human world.

## \|\| 1.198.91 \|\|

*vyāptastathākhilaḥ svargo mānavaiḥ spardhayānvitaiḥ \|*  
*sārdhaṃ devairvimānasthairapsarogaṇasevitaiḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On the other hand, the entire heavenly region became overpopulated (full) with human beings vying with Devas and attended by groups of Apsarās.

## \|\| 1.198.92 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu dharmarājaḥ samāyayau \|*  
*yatra vedadhvanirbrahmā brahmalokaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. In the meantime, Dharmarāja came to the place where Brahmā was in Brahmaloka, chanting Vedic passages loudly.

## \|\| 1.198.93-100 \|\|

*abravīdduḥkhito dīnaḥ kṣiptvāgre patrakadvayam \|*  
*ekaṃ pāpasamudbhūtamanyaddharmasamudbhavam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*citreṇa likhitaṃ yacca vicitreṇa tathā param \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre devatīrthayugaṃ sthitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*śūdrākhyaṃ brāhmaṇīnāma tathānyatpadmamaṃḍitam \|*  
*tathā tatrāsti liṃgaṃ ca puṇyaṃ māheśvaraṃ mahat \|\| 95 \|\|*

*trayāṇāmatha teṣāṃ ca prabhāvātsarvamānavāḥ \|*  
*api pāpasamāyuktāḥ prayāṃti tridaśālayam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*śūnyā me narakā jātāḥ sarve te rauravādayaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre na dānaṃ na ca tarpaṇam \|*  
*devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tasmānmukto mayā sarvo yo'dhikārastavodbhavaḥ \|*  
*niyojayasva tatrānyaṃ kañcicchaktatamaṃ tataḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*apramāṇaṃ sthitaṃ sarvametatpatradvayaṃ mama \|*  
*tacchrutvā padmajaḥ prāha samānīya śatakratum \|\| 100 \|\|*

93-94a. He placed before Brahmā two sheets well illustrated with pictures, one intended for listing sinners and the other listing virtuous ones. With great sorrow and distress, he spoke thus:

94b-100. “O Lord, there are two Tīrthas in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara. There is a Tīrtha named Śūdrī Tīrtha and the other named Brāhmaṇī Tīrtha. It is adorned with clusters of lotuses. Further, there is the great Liṅga of Maheśvara. It is highly meritorious. By the power of these three, all men, even excessively sinful ones, go to heavenly abode. All Narakas of mine, Raurava etc.; have became empty.

No one has performed Yajñas, no one made over any religious gifts nor did anyone perform the rite of offering libation to deities and ancestors and guests.

Hence I have abdicated all my powers assigned by you. Do employ someone else there proving himself more competent than I. These two sheets prepared by me have become totally invalid.”

## \|\| 1.198.101-102 \|\|

*gatvā śīghratamaṃ martye tvaṃ śakra vacanānmama \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tīrthadvayamanuttamam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*śūdryākhyaṃ brāhmaṇītyeva yacca liṃgamanuttamam \|*  
*tatrasthaṃ nāśaya kṣipraṃ kṛtvā pāṃsupravarṣaṇam \|\| 102 \|\|*

On hearing these words the Lotus-born One summoned Śatakratu and said:

101-102. “At my behest, O Śakra, hasten to the human world. In the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara there are two excellent Tīrthas. One is called Śūdrī Tīrtha and the other Brāhmaṇī Tīrtha. There is another excellent thing, the Liṅga stationed there. Shower dust particles therein and destroy (bury) them quickly.”

## \|\| 1.198.103 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā satvaraṃ śakro gatvā bhūmitalaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pāṃsubhiḥ pūrayāmāsa te tīrthe liṃgameva ca \|\| 103 \|\|*

Sūta said:

103\. On hearing these words, Śakra hastened to the earth and filled the two Tīrthas and the Liṅga with dust particles.

## \|\| 1.198.104 \|\|

*adyāpi kalikāle'smindvābhyāṃ gṛhya sumṛttikām \|*  
*snātvā ca tilakaṃ kāryaṃ sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Even today in the Kali Age, men should take their holy bath, taking the holy dust thereof. They must apply it on the forehead as Tilaka for destroying all sins.

## \|\| 1.198.105 \|\|

*caturdaśīdine prāpte somavāre ca saṃsthite \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ yaḥ kurute śrāddhaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*gayāśrāddhena kiṃ tasya manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo'bravīt \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Manu, born of the Self-born Lord, has said thus: “On the fourteenth lunar day coinciding with Monday, a person should perform Śrāddha in both of them with great faith. Of what avail is Gayā Śrāddha unto him?”

## \|\| 1.198.106 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yathā sā brāhmaṇī jātā śūdrī cāpi tathāparā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, thus I have narrated everything that I was asked about in regard to that Brāhmaṇī and Śūdrī.

## \|\| 1.198.107 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyādbhaktyā paṭhedvā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*so'pi taddinajātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he who devoutly listens to this or reads this shall undoubtedly be relieved of the sins of the day.

## \|\| 1.198.108 \|\|

*evaṃ naro na kaḥ siddhastasya liṃgasya pūjanāt \|*  
*cirāyuśca tathā jāto yathānyo nātra vidyate \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Which man has not become a Siddha by adoring that Liṅga? Who has not become a long-lived one? there is none who has become so (by resorting to a Tīrtha) elsewhere.

## Chapter 199 - Greatness of Eight Nāgara Families

## \|\| 1.199.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tisraḥkoṭyordhakoṭī ca tīrthānāmiha bhūtale \|*  
*śrūyate sūta kārtsnyena kīrtyamānā munīśvaraiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kathaṃ labhyeta sarveṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ snānajaṃ phalam \|*  
*alpāyurbhirmahābhāga kalikāla upasthite \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2: O Sūta, thirty-five million Tīrthas are said by leading sages as existing all over the earth. O highly esteemed one, how can (man) of limited life span obtain the benefit of taking holy ablution in all those Tīrthas at the advent of the Kali Age?

## \|\| 1.199.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kṣetratrayamihākhyātaṃ tathāraṇyatrayaṃ mahat \|*  
*purītrayaṃ vanānyeva trīṇi grāmāstathātrayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tathā tīrthatrayaṃ cānyatparvatatritayānvitam \|*  
*mahānadītrayaṃ caiva sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3-4. O Brāhmaṇas, three sacred places (Kṣetras) have been extolled here. So also three great Araṇyas (forests), three Purīs (Cities), three Vanas (sylvan parks), three Grāmas (villages), three other Tīrthas along with three Parvatas (mountains) and three Mahānadīs (great rivers). These are all destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.199.5 \|\|

*martyalokesthitaṃ viprāḥ sarvatīrthaphalapradam \|*  
*sarveṣveteṣu yaḥ snāti sa sarveṣāṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They are situated in the mortal world and they accord the benefit of all the Tīrthas. He who takes his holy bath in all these, shall attain the benefit of all.

## \|\| 1.199.6 \|\|

*caturviṃśatisaṃkhyānāmidamāha prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*ya ekasmiṃstrike snāti sarva trikaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Prajāpati has said this that he who resorts to one set of three for holy bath out of the entire twenty-four (i.e. 8 Trikas) shall attain the benefit of all the Trikas.

## \|\| 1.199.7-8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\|*  
*trīṇi kṣetrāṇi kānīha tathāraṇyāni kāni ca \|*  
*puryastisro mahābhāga kāḥkhyātāśca vanāni ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ke grāmāḥ kāni tīrthāni ke nagāḥ saritaśca kāḥ \|*  
*nāmabhirvada naḥ sūta sarvāṇyetāni vistarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

The sages said:

7-8. O highly esteemed one, what are the three Kṣetras? What are the three Araṇyas? What are the three well-known Purīs? What are the three Vanas? What are the three Grāmas? What are the Tīrthas? What are the Nagas (mountains)? What are the Sarits (rivers)? O Sūta, describe all these in detail citing their names.

## \|\| 1.199.9-10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\|*  
*kurukṣetramiti khyātaṃ prathamaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ dvitīyaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prābhāsikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu kṣetraṃ hi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*etatkṣetratrayaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9-10. The first excellent Kṣetra is well-known as Kurukṣetra. Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra is glorified as the second one. Prabhāsika (Prabhāsa) is the third Kṣetra, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. All these three Kṣetras are meritorious and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.199.11-12 \|\|

*yathoktavidhinā dṛṣṭvā naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|*  
*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyankṣetreṣveteṣu bhaktitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*snānaṃ karoti tasyeṣṭaṃ manaso jāyate phalam \|*  
*caturviṃśatimāneṣu snāto bhavati sa dvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. By visiting these in accordance with the injunctions thereof, a man is rid of sins. If a devotee takes his holy bath in these Keṣetras with any cherished mental desire, the same is attained. O Brāhmaṇas, he becomes one having the ablution in all the twenty-four (cited before).

## \|\| 1.199.13 \|\|

*ekaṃ tu puṣkarāraṇyaṃ naimiṣāraṇyameva ca \|*  
*dharmāraṇyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu teṣāṃ saṃkīrtyate dvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One is the Puṣkara Araṇya. The other is Naimiṣāraṇya. O Brāhmaṇas, Dharmāraṇya is glorified as the third.

## \|\| 1.199.14 \|\|

*triṣveteṣu ca yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He who bathes in these three attains (the benefit of bath in all the twenty-four holy places).

## \|\| 1.199.15 \|\|

*vārāṇasī purītyekā dvitīyā dvārakāpurī \|*  
*avantyākhyā tṛtīyā ca viśrutā bhuvanatraye \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (Out of cities) one Puri is Vārāṇasī. The second is Dvārakāpurī. The city named Avantī is the third one. It is well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.199.16 \|\|

*etāsu yo naraḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A man who takes his holy bath in these Purīs gets the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.17 \|\|

*vṛndāvanaṃ vanaṃ caikaṃ dvitīyaṃ khāṃḍavaṃ vanam \|*  
*khyātaṃ dvaitavanaṃ cānyattṛtīyaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Vṛndāvana is one Vana (sylvan park). Khāṇḍava is the second Vana. Dvaitāvana is well-known all over the earth. It is the third Vana.

## \|\| 1.199.18 \|\|

*triṣveteṣu ca yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who takes his holy bath in these three Vanas, attains the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.19 \|\|

*kalpagrāmaḥ smṛtaścaikaḥ śāligrāmo dvitīyakaḥ \|*  
*naṃdigrāmastṛtīyastu viśruto dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kalpa (Kalāpa) Grāma is remembered as the first Grāma. Śāligrāma is remembered as the second. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Nandigrāma is well-known as the third.

## \|\| 1.199.20 \|\|

*triṣveteṣu ca yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He who takes his holy bath in these three Grāmas attains the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.21 \|\|

*agnitīrthaṃ smṛtaṃ caikaṃ śuklatīrthamathāparam \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ tu pitṝṇāmativallabham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Agnitīrtha is remembered as one Tīrtha. Another is Śuklatīrtha. The third one is Pitṛtīrtha. It is a great favourite of Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.199.22 \|\|

*triṣveteṣu ca yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He who takes his holy bath in these three Tīrthas has the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.23 \|\|

*śrīparvataḥ smṛtaścaiko dvitīyaścārbudastathā \|*  
*tṛtīyo raivatākhyo'tra vikhyātaḥ parvatottamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Śrīparvata is remembered as the first Parvata. The second is Arbuda (Mt. Abu). The third one is well-known by the name Raivata. It is an excellent Parvata.

## \|\| 1.199.24 \|\|

*triṣveteṣu ca yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He who takes his holy bath in these three, attains the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.25 \|\|

*gaṃgā nadī smṛtā pūrvā narmadākhyā tathā parā \|*  
*sarasvatī tṛtīyā tu nadī plakṣasamudbhavā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Gaṅgā is remembered as the foremost Nadī (river). Another one is Narmadā. Sarasvatī is the third river. It originates from Plakṣa (tree).

## \|\| 1.199.26 \|\|

*āsu sarvāsu yaḥ snāti caturviṃśatibhāgbhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He who takes his holy bath in all these attains the benefit of all the twenty-four.

## \|\| 1.199.27 \|\|

*eteṣveva hi sarveṣu yaḥ snānaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sārdhakoṭitrayasyātra sa kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A man who takes his holy bath in all these (twenty-four) shall attain the entire benefit of all the thirty-five million (sacred places),

## \|\| 1.199.28 \|\|

*yaścaikasminnaraḥ snāti sa trikasya phalaṃ labhet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A man who bathes in one of a set of three, attains the benefit of the entire Trika.

## \|\| 1.199.29 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*saṃkṣepāttīrthajaṃ puṇyaṃ labhyate yannarairbhuvi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, everything that I was asked, i,e. about the benefit from the Tīrtha that is obtained by men on the earth, has been told succinctly.

## \|\| 1.199.30 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ kiṃ nu vo vacmi yattadvadata mā ciram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Now what should I tell you? Tel! me without delay.

## \|\| 1.199.31 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yāni tīrthāni sūtaja \|*  
*tāni proktāni sarvāṇi tvayā'smākaṃ suvistarāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

The sages said:

31\. O Sūtaja, all the Tīrthas situated in Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra have been described by you to us in full detail.

## \|\| 1.199.32 \|\|

*tathā cāyatanānyeva saṃkhyayā rahitāni ca \|*  
*api varṣaśatenātra snānaṃ kartuṃ na śakyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. So also the innumerable Āyatanas (shrines). It is not possible to take holy bath in all these even in the course of a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.199.33 \|\|

*teṣu sarveṣu martyena yathoktavidhinā sphuṭam \|*  
*devatāyatanānyeva tathā draṣṭuṃ mahā mate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. No man can take bath in accordance with the injunctions. It is clear. O highly intelligent one, it is equally not possible to visit all the shrines.

## \|\| 1.199.34-35 \|\|

*yasminsnāto dine caiva tasya vyuṣṭiḥ prakīrtitā \|*  
*alpāyuṣastadā martyāḥ kṛte'pi parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tretāyāṃ dvāpare cāpi kimu prāpte kalau yuge \|*  
*evamalpāyuṣo jñātvā mānavānsūtanaṃdana \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The benefit one derives is only for the day on which he takes the bath. Even in Kṛta Yuga, men are said to be short- lived. So also in Tretā and Dvāpara. There is hardly any need to say about Kali Age. O Sūtanandana, know that men are short-lived (in all Yugas).

## \|\| 1.199.36 \|\|

*labheraṃśca kathaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ snānajaṃ phalam \|*  
*devadarśanajaṃ vāpi viśeṣānnirdhanāśca ye \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. How can they, therefore, obtain the benefit of the holy ablution in all the Tīrthas? How can they obtain the benefit of viewing the deity (everywhere)—especially if they are poor?

## \|\| 1.199.57 \|\|

*viśvāmitreśvaraṃ nāma sarveṣāṃ sa phalaṃ labhet \|*  
*nabhasyasya sitāṣṭamyāṃ sarveṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Is there any remedy in this respect. Human or divine, whereby merit can be acquired by all easily.

## \|\| 1.199.38 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*asminnarthe purā pṛṣṭo viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*samupetyāśramaṃ tasya ānartena mahībhujā \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sūta said:

38\. In this matter, Viśvāmitra, the great sage, was formerly asked by king Ānarta who had gone to his hermitage.

## \|\| 1.199.39 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*bhagavannatra tīrthāni saṃkhyayā rahitāni ca \|*  
*teṣu snānavidhiḥ proktaḥ sarveṣveva pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 39 \|\|*

The king said:

39\. O holy Sir, there are innumerable Tīrthas here. Procedures enjoined in the case of the holy ablution in all those are distinct and separate.

## \|\| 1.199.40 \|\|

*māse vāre dine caiva kutracinmunisattamaiḥ \|*  
*dānāni ca tathoktāni yathā snāna vidhistathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The difference is in respect of month, day of the week or lunar day in different Tīrthas as explained by excellent sages. Rules regarding Dāna are also mentioned differently as in the case of holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.199.41 \|\|

*devānāṃ darśanaṃ cāpi pṛthaktena prakīrtitam \|*  
*na śakyate phalaṃ prāptuṃ sarveṣāṃ kenacinmune \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A visit to the deities has also been proclaimed separately. O sage, it is not possible to obtain the benefits of all of them by any one person, O sage.

## \|\| 1.199.42 \|\|

*api varṣaśatenāpi kiṃ punaḥ stokavāsaraiḥ \|*  
*tasmādvada mahābhāga sukhopāyaṃ ca dehinām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is impossible to achieve (this) even in the course of a hundred years. It is all the more so in the course of a few days. Hence, O highly esteemed one, do mention an easy means for all embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.199.43 \|\|

*ekasminnapi ca snātastīrthe prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ snānajaṃ sakalaṃ phalam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Can any man taking his holy ablution even in one Tīrtha obtain the benefit arising from the holy ablution in all the Tīrthas?

## \|\| 1.199.44 \|\|

*tathaikasminsure dṛṣṭe sarvadevasamudbhavam \|*  
*phalaṃ darśanajaṃ bhāvi narāṇāṃ dvijasattama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Similarly, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, can men attain the benefit of viewing all the deities, when a single deity has been viewed?

## \|\| 1.199.45 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā suciraṃ dhyātvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*abravīcchṛṇu rājeṃdra sarahasyaṃ vadāmi te \|\| 45 \|\|*

Sūta said:

45\. On hearing it and after meditiating for a long time, the great sage Viśvāmitra said: “Listen, O leading king, I shall tell you everything including the secret.

## \|\| 1.199.46 \|\|

*catvāryatra prakṛṣṭāni mukhyatīrthāni pārthiva \|*  
*yeṣu snāne kṛte rājañchrāddhe ca tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ snānajaṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There are four superior and most important Tīrthas here. The benefit arising from the holy ablution in all the Tīrthas is attained if the holy ablution is taken and Śrāddha is performed later in all the four of them.

## \|\| 1.199.47-49 \|\|

*saptaviṃśatiliṃgāni tathātraiva sthitāni ca \|*  
*siddheśvaraprapūrvāṇi sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*teṣu sarveṣu dṛṣṭeṣu bhaktyā pūtena cetasā \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ bhaveddarśanajaṃ phalam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ekasminnapi saṃdṛṣṭe pūjite vā surottame \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiliṃgānāṃ pūjā tena kṛtā bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Further, there are twenty-seven Liṅgas situated here itself beginning with Siddheśvara Liṅga. They are destructive of all sins. If all of them are viewed with devotion and sanctified mind, the benefit of viewing all the deities (of all the worlds) will be attained. If a devotee views and adores one excellent deity it is as efficacious as though all the twenty-seven Liṅgas have been adored by him.”

The king said;

## \|\| 1.199.50 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kāni catvāri tīrthāni tatra mukhyāni sanmune \|*  
*yeṣu snāto naraḥ samyaksarveṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O excellent sage, what are those four important Tīrthas by taking ablution in which a man obtains the benefit of all (Tīrthas)?

## \|\| 1.199.51 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*atrāsti kūpikā puṇyā yasyāṃ saṃśrayate gayā \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāmamāvāsyādine tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

51\. There is a meritorious Kūpikā (a small well) wherein Gayā takes resort on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half as well as on the New-Moon day.

## \|\| 1.199.52 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa mahābhāga kanyāsaṃsthe divākare \|*  
*nirviṇṇā bhūmilokānāṃ kṛtaiḥ śrāddhairanekadhā \|\| 52 \|\|*
