12\. Ponder over the various Itihāsas, Purāṇas and all the Vedānta works and prescribe the means of purity for me for the sake of my mother. I shall do so. Otherwise, I shall cease to live.

## \|\| 1.208.13 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā suciraṃ dhyātvā gautamaḥ prāha taṃ sutam \|*  
*pariṣvajya svabāhubhyāṃ mūrdhnyāghrāya tataḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

13\. On hearing it, Gautama pondered for a long time. He then embraced his son with both the arms and sniffed at his head. Thereafter, he said to his son:

## \|\| 1.208.14-18 \|\|

*yadyevaṃ vatsa mā kārṣīḥ sāhasaṃ pāpasaṃbhavam \|*  
*ātmadehavighātena śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

*medhyatve tava mātuśca śuddhirjñātā mayā purā \|*  
*yayā sā mama harmyārhā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*utpatsyate ravervaṃśe rāmarūpī janā rdanaḥ \|*  
*rāvaṇasya vadhārthāya mānuṣaṃ rūpamāsthitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasya pādasya saṃsparśādbhūyaḥ śuddhā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasmātpratīkṣya tāvattvamautsukyaṃ vraja putraka \|\| 17 \|\|*

*etatsamyaṅmayā jñātaṃ vatsa divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. “If it is so, dear son, do not commit any rash act in regard to (i.e. to get rid of) this sin, such as slaying yourself. Let my words be listened to: Even earlier I had known the means of purity of your mother whereby she will become worthy of my abode undoubtedly. Janārdana will be born in the solar race in the form of Rāma, in the guise of a human being, for the purpose of slaying Rāvaṇa. She will regain purity by the contact of his foot. Wait for it, dear son. Do not be over-eager.

Dear boy, this has been known perfectly by me through (my) divine vision.”

## \|\| 1.208.19 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tathetyuktvā śatānandaḥ praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*sthitaḥ pratīkṣamāṇastu taṃ kālaṃ mātṛvatsalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing this Śatānanda became highly delighted. After saying “So be it”, the boy, fond of his mother, waited patiently for that (auspicious) hour.

## \|\| 1.208.20 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā rāmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*rāvaṇasya vadhārthāya jāto daśarathālaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter, in due course, after a long time Janārdana in the form of Rāma was born in the abode of Daśaratha for the purpose of killing Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.208.21 \|\|

*sa mayā bhagavā viṣṇurbālabhāvena saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*nijayajñasyarakṣārthaṃ samānītaḥ svamāśramam \|*  
*rākṣasānāṃ vināśāya yajñakarmavināśinām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That Lord Viṣṇu, yet in his childhood, was brought by me to my hermitage for the protection of my own Yajñas by destroying the Rākṣasas who were bent upon destroying the sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 1.208.22-23 \|\|

*hataistai rākṣasai raudrairmama pūrṇo'bhavanmakhaḥ \|*  
*ayodhyāyāḥ samānītaḥ sa mayā raghunaṃdanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sītāyāśca vivāhārthaṃ lakṣmaṇena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā svayaṃvaraṃ tasyāḥ pārthivānāṃ samāgamam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. After the terrible Rākṣasas had been killed, my Makha was duly concluded. The scion of the family of Raghus was brought by me from Ayodhyā along with Lakṣmaṇa for the marriage of Sītā about whose Svayaṃvara and the assemblage of kings I had duly heard.

## \|\| 1.208.24 \|\|

*tato mārge mayā dṛṣṭā gautamasyāśrame śubhe \|*  
*ahilyā sā śilā rūpā pramāṇena mahattamā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then on the way, in the splendid hermitage of Gautama, Ahalyā was seen by me in the form of a huge stone image.

## \|\| 1.208.25 \|\|

*tataḥ prokto mayā rāmaḥ spṛśemāṃ vatsa pāṇinā \|*  
*mānuṣatvaṃ labhedyena gautamasya priyā muneḥ \|*  
*śāpadoṣeṇa saṃjātā śileyaṃ tasya sanmuneḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then Rāma was told by me: “Dear boy, touch her with your hand so that she may regain the human form. She is the beloved wife Sage Gautama. It was on account of the curse of the excellent sage that she was transformed into a stone image.”

## \|\| 1.208.26 \|\|

*avikalpaṃ tato rāmo mama vākyena tāṃ śilām \|*  
*pasparśa pārthivaśreṣṭha kautū halasamanvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O excellent king, at my behest and urged by curiosity, Rāma touched that rock unhesitatingly.

## \|\| 1.208.27 \|\|

*atha rāmeṇa saṃspṛṣṭā sahasaivāṃganā muneḥ \|*  
*śuśubhe mānuṣī jātā divyarūpavapurdharā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then, on being touched by Rāma, the wife of the sage became transformed into a human being. She shone with divine form and features.

## \|\| 1.208.28 \|\|

*tataḥ sā lajjayā'viṣṭā praṇipatya ca gautamam \|*  
*smaramāṇā'tmanaḥ kṛtyaṃ yacchakreṇa samanvitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Recollecting her affair with Śakra, she became ashamed. She then bowed down to Gautama (and said):

## \|\| 1.208.29-30 \|\|

*prāyaścittaṃ mama svāmindehi sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yannarasya samāyoge parasyāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ahaṃ duṣkaramapyetatkariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yena śuddhirbhavenmahyaṃ puraścaraṇasevanāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. “O my Lord, prescribe unto me an expiatory rite fully as laid down by Prajāpati in connection with the close intimacy of one with another (other than legally wedded spouse). Even if it is difficult, I shall undoubtedly carry it out, so that I can regain purity through the Puraścaraṇa rite.”

## \|\| 1.208.31-32 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃciṃtya suciraṃ provāca gautamastadā \|*  
*kuru cāndrāyaṇaśataṃ kṛcchrāṇāṃ ca sahasrakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prājāpatyāyutaṃ cāpi tīrthayātrāparāyaṇā \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu yāni tīrthāni bhūtale \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃdarśanātsamyaktataḥ śuddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. After thinking about it for a long time Gautama said: “Perform a hundred Cāndrāyaṇa expiations, a thousand Kṛcchra rites and ten thousand Prājāpatya rites. Observe the vow of pilgrimage to the sixty-eight holy places where all the Tīrthas on the earth are present. By visiting them all perfectly, you will regain purity.”

## \|\| 1.208.33-34 \|\|

*sā tathaiti pratijñāya nityaṃ vrataparāyaṇā \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭisu tīrtheṣu vārāṇasyādiṣu kramāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*babhrāma tāni liṃgāni pūjayantī prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*krameṇaiva tu saṃprāptā hāṭakeśvarasaṃbhavam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. She consented saying “So be it.” She observed the relevant vows and wandered over the sixty-eight excellent Tīrthas beginning with Vārāṇasī in due order. She devoutly worshipped all the Liṅgas. In due course she reached the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.208.35-36 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyati sā sādhvī tāvannāgabilo mahān \|*  
*pūrito nāgareṇaiva mārgaḥ pātālasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*gacchaṃti yena pūrvaṃ tu tīrthayātrāparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradevasya darśanārthaṃ munīśvarāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. As the chaste lady looked ahead, there was a great serpent hole. It was the path unto Pātāla whereby the great sages engrossed in pilgrimage used to go for the vision of Lord Hāṭakeśvara. It had been closed by Nāgaras themselves.

## \|\| 1.208.37-38 \|\|

*atha sā cintayāmāsa na dṛṣṭe tu sureśvare \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradeve ca na hi yātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tasmāttapaḥ kari ṣyāmi sthitvā caiva suduṣkaram \|*  
*yenāhaṃ tatprabhāvena taṃ paśyāmi sureśvaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then she began to think, ‘If the Lord of Suras, Hāṭakeśvara, is not visited one cannot attain the benefit of the pilgrimage. Hence I shall remain steady and perform a very difficult penance through the power whereof I can visualise the Lord of Suras.’

## \|\| 1.208.39 \|\|

*evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā tapastepe suduṣkaram \|*  
*darśanārthaṃ hi devasya pātālanilayasya ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After coining to such a decision, she performed a very severe penance for getting the vision of the Lord whose abode is in Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.208.40 \|\|

*paṃcāgnisādhakā grīṣme hemante salilāśrayā \|*  
*varṣāsvākāśaśayanā sā babhūva tapasvinī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In summer she performed the penance in the midst of five fires; in Hemanta (early winter) she resorted to the waters; in rainy season she lay under the open sky.

## \|\| 1.208.41 \|\|

*haraliṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya svanāmnā cāṃtike tadā \|*  
*trikālaṃ pūjayāmāsa gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After installing a Liṅga of Hara after her own name, she performed its worship by its side thrice a day with sweet scents, flowers, and unguents.

## \|\| 1.208.42 \|\|

*evaṃ tapasi saṃsthāyāstasyāḥ kālo mahāngataḥ \|*  
*na ca saṃdarśanaṃ jātaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃbhavam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A long period of time elapsed even as she continued her penance in this manner but she could not get even a glimpse of Lord Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.208.43 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya śatānandaśca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*sa tāmanveṣamāṇastu tasminkṣetre samāgataḥ \|*  
*mātṛsneha parītātmā tīrthānveṣaṇatatparaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Once her son Śatānanda who was extremely fond of his mother and was trying to find her came to this holy place.

## \|\| 1.208.44 \|\|

*atha tāṃ tatra saṃvīkṣya dāruṇe tapasi sthitām \|*  
*praṇipatya sthito dīnaḥ saduḥkho vākyamabravīt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He saw her engaged in the severe penance. Bowing down to her in great distress, he spoke these words to her in sorrow:

## \|\| 1.208.45-48 \|\|

*kimatra kliśyate kāyastapaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam \|*  
*saptaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu yāni liṃgāni teṣu ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*māheśvarāṇi liṃgāni tāni dṛṣṭāni ca tvayā \|*  
*etatpātālasaṃsthaṃ ca hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*na paśyati naraḥ kaściddṛṣṭaṃ kṣetre na kenacit \|*  
*tena śuddhiśca saṃjātā svabhartrā vihitā tu yā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmādāgaccha gacchāmastātāśrāmapade śubhe \|*  
*tvanmārgaṃ vīkṣate tātaḥ karṣuko varṣaṇaṃ yathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. “Why do you subject your body to great strain by performing this severe penance? All the Liṅgas pertaining to Maheśvara in sixty-seven Tīrthas have been visited by you. No man has ever seen this Liṅga situated in Pātāla and designated Hāṭakeśvara.

In view of what you have already done, the purity has been attained as indicated by your husband. Hence, do come. We shall go to our auspicious hermitage. Father is eagerly awaiting you like ā farmer awaiting the advent of rainy season.”

## \|\| 1.208.49-50 \|\|

*āhilyovāca \|*  
*yāvatpaśyāmi no devaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*tāvadgacchāmi no gehaṃ yadā paśyāmi taṃ haram \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tadā yāsye gṛhaṃ putra niścayo'yaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Ahalyā said:

49-50. I will not return home unless and until I have viewed the Lord designated as Hāṭakeśvara. Dear son, I will go home when I see Hara. This determination has been made by me.

## \|\| 1.208.51 \|\|

*tacchrutvā so'pi tāṃ prāha hyeṣa cenniścayastava \|*  
*mayā'pi tātapārśve tu pragaṃtavyaṃ tvayāpa \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing it he said, “If this is your resolve (nay determination) then I will go near father only along with you.”

## \|\| 1.208.52 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sopi sthāpayāmāsa śāṃbha vam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ ca pūjayāmāsa trikālaṃ tapasi sthitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After saying thus, he too installed the Liṅga of Śaṃbhu and worshipped it thrice a day and engaged himself in the penance.

## \|\| 1.208.53 \|\|

*śatānandastu rājarṣiḥ gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*naivedyairvividhaiḥ sūktairvedoktaiḥ paryatoṣayat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O saintly king, Śatānanda propitiated the Liṅga with various kinds of food offerings, sweet scents, flowers and unguents and Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 1.208.54 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhānnakālabhojyasya vratacaryāratasya ca \|*  
*evaṃ tasyā'pi saṃsthasya gataḥ kālo mahānmune \|*  
*na ca tuṣyati deveśa stābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kathañcana \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Even as the sage was engaged in the Vratas and rites, taking in food only once in six meal-times a long period of time elapsed. Yet the Lord of Devas did not become pleased with both of them.

## \|\| 1.208.55 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā gautamo'pi mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*ājagāma svayaṃ tatra putradarśanalālasaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In his eagerness to see his son, the great sage Gautama too came there himself then after a long time.

## \|\| 1.208.56 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā bhāryayā sārdhaṃ putraṃ tapasi saṃsthitam \|*  
*tutoṣa prathamaṃ tāvatpaścāduḥkhasamanvitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On seeing him along with his wife engaged in the penance, Gautama became pleased at the outset but later he became grieved.

## \|\| 1.208.57 \|\|

*aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ putro me kṛśatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tapasaḥ saṃprabhāvena nayāmi svagṛhaṃ katham \|*  
*bhāryeyaṃ ca tathā mahyaṃ vivarṇā tu kṛśā sthitā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. ‘Alas, it is a great pity! My son has become very lean as a result of the penance. How can I take him back to my abode? Similarly my wife too has become pallid and very lean!’

## \|\| 1.208.58 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃciṃtya manasā tāvubhau pratyabhāṣata \|*  
*gamyatāṃ svagṛhaṃ kṛtvā tapasaḥ saṃnivartanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After thinking thus in his mind he spoke to them both: “Desist from the performance of the penance and come home.”

## \|\| 1.208.59 \|\|

*śatānanda uvāca \|*  
*tātāṃbā bahudhā proktā tapasaḥ saṃnivartane \|*  
*no gacchati tathā harmyamadṛṣṭe hāṭakeśvare \|\| 59 \|\|*

Śatānanda said:

59\. Dear father, mother has already been told many times to stop the performance of penance. She will not go home if Lord Hāṭakeśvara is not seen.

## \|\| 1.208.60 \|\|

*ahaṃ tayā vihīnastu naiva yāsyāmi niścitam \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāga yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. It is also certain that I will not go without her. Know this, O highly esteemed one, and do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.208.61 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ niścayo vatsa tava mātuśca saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ te darśayiṣyāmi tapasā hāṭakeśvaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

Gautama said:

61\. O dear son, if (your) mother’s determination is such I shall show Hāṭakeśvara by means of my penance.

## \|\| 1.208.62 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ so'pi tapaścakre mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*ekāṃtaropavāsastu sthito varṣaśataṃ muniḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhānnakālabhojī ca tāvatkāle tato'bhavat \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After saying so the great sage too performed a penance. For a hundred years the sage undertook fast on alternate days. Then, for the same period he took food only once in six meal times.

## \|\| 1.208.63 \|\|

*trirātrabhojī paścācca sa babhūva munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tāvatkālaṃ phalairninye tāvatkālaṃ jalāśanaḥ \|*  
*vāyubhakṣastato bhūyastāvatkālamabhūnmuniḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Afterwards he took food only once in three days. Then the leading sage spent a similar period taking only fruits. A further similar period he spent taking in only water. Then the sage took in only air for a similar period.

## \|\| 1.208.64 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte parame saṃvyavasthite \|*  
*prabhidya medinīpṛṣṭhaṃ niṣkrāṃtaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then at the end of more than a thousand years, an excellent Liṅga came out piercing through the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.208.65 \|\|

*dvādaśārkapratīkāśaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitama \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare devaḥ śaṃbhuḥ pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. It resembled the splendour of twelve suns. It had all the characteristic features. In the meantime Lord Saṃbhu \[Śaṃbhu\] became visible.

## \|\| 1.208.66 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*tasya dṛṣṭipathaṃ gatvā vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. At the same time the Moon-crested Lord came within the range of his vision and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.208.67-71 \|\|

*gautamā'haṃ pratuṣṭaste tapasā'nena suvrata \|\| 67 \|\|*

*etacca māmakaṃ liṃgaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*pātālācca viniṣkrāṃtaṃ tava bhaktyā mahāmune \|\| 68 \|\|*

*etadarthaṃ tapastaptaṃ sabhāryeṇa tvayā hi tat \|*  
*saputreṇākhilaṃ jātaṃ phalaṃ tasya yathepsitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*etatpaśyatu te bhāryā ahilyā divyarūpiṇī \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭyudbhavaṃ yena yātrāphalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tvaṃ cāpi prārthaya varaṃ yena sarvaṃ dadāmi te \|\| 71 \|\|*

67-71. “O Gautama, O sage of excellent holy rites, I am pleased with this penance of yours.

This Liṅga of mine is designated as Hāṭakeśvara. O great sage; due to your devoutness this has come out from Pātāla.

Is it not for this purpose that the penance was performed by you along with your wife and son? The entire benefit thereof has taken effect as desired.

Let your wife Ahalyā of divine form and features view this, whereby she will attain the benefit of the pilgrimage to the sixty-eight holy places.

You too request for a boon which I shall grant entirely.”

## \|\| 1.208.72 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñe tu sakṛddṛṣṭe ca yatphalam \|*  
*pātālasthe ca yatpuṇyaṃ narāṇāṃ jāyate phalam \|*  
*dṛṣṭenānena tatpuṇyaṃ pūjitena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

Gautama said:

72\. Let the merit accrued to men by visiting once Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla be derived (by men) by viewing and especially by worshipping this Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.208.73 \|\|

*anye'pi ye janāstacca pūjayaṃti prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ te prayāṃtu triviṣṭapam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Other people too who worship it devoutly on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Cakra, will go to heaven.

## \|\| 1.208.74 \|\|

*etalliṃgaṃ na jānaṃti narāḥ siddhyabhikāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*viśaṃti vivaraṃ tena hāṭakeśvarakāṃkṣayā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Ordinary men do not know this Liṅga. Hence desirous of perfection and Siddhi, they enter a cavity of the earth with a desire for viewing Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.208.75-76 \|\|

*api pāpasamopetā liṃgasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*paradārodbhavā tpāpādahilyeśvaradarśanāt \|\| 75 \|\|*

*mucyaṃte mānavāstadvacchatānaṃdeśvarādapi \|*  
*tasmindine vihitayā tābhyāṃ caiva prapūjayā \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. By the power of this Liṅga, even sinners are freed from the sin arising from contact with other men’s wives. Men become free from sins by viewing, Ahalyeśvara as well as Śatānandeśvara. They will become sinless through the worship of both performed on that day.

## \|\| 1.208.77 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu vyāptaḥ svargo'khilo nṛpa \|*  
*mānuṣairapi pāpāḍhyaiḥ sarvadharmavivarjitaiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

77\. In the meantime, O king, the entire Svarga was filled with men full of sins and devoid of all virtues.

## \|\| 1.208.78 \|\|

*na kaścitkurute yajñaṃ tīrtha yātrāmathāparam \|*  
*na vrataṃ niyamaṃ caiva dānasyāpi kathāmapi \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. No one performs Yajña, pilgrimage, Vrata or other observances. They do not make any gift whatsoever.

## \|\| 1.208.79 \|\|

*tacca liṃgatrayaṃ dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Viewing those three Liṅgas, touching them and worshipping them devoutly (they used to go to heaven).

## \|\| 1.208.80 \|\|

*tato bhītāḥ surāḥ sarve saspardhairmānuṣairvṛtāḥ \|*  
*procuḥ puraṃdaraṃ gatvā vyathayā prayā yutāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Surrounded by men urged by great rivalry all the Suras became frightened. With great pain and anguish they went to Purandara and said:

## \|\| 1.208.81-87 \|\|

*martyaloke sahasrākṣa sarve dharmāḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*api pāpasamācārā abhyetya puruṣā iha \|\| 81 \|\|*

*asmābhiḥ saha garvāḍhyāḥ spardhāṃ kurvaṃti sarvadā \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre liṃgatrayamanuttamam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yatsthitaṃ sthāpitaṃ tatra gautamena mahātmanā \|*  
*saputreṇa sadāreṇa tasya pūjāprabhāvataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*api pāpasamācārā ihāgacchaṃti te'khilāḥ \|*  
*yamasya narakāḥ sarve sāṃprataṃ śūnyatāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*gautamena samānītaḥ pātālāddhāṭakeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tapasā toṣayitvā tu tatra sthāne sureśvaraḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tatprabhāvādayaṃ jāto vyavahāro dharātale \|\| 86 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā pravartaṃte yathā yajñāstathā kuru \|*  
*tairvinā naiva tṛptiḥ syādasmākaṃ ca kathaṃcana \|\| 87 \|\|*

81-87. “O Thousand-eyed One, all righteous acts have stopped in the mortal world. Even men of sinful conduct come here arrogantly and vie with us always. In the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara there are three excellent Liṅgas. They have been installed by the noble-souled Gautama in the company of his wife and son. By the power of their worship, all men of sinful conduct come here. All the Narakas of Yama have become vacant.

Hāṭakeśvara has been brought from Pātāla by Gautama after propitiating the Lord by means of his penance. It is by the power of the Lord that all these things have occurred on the earth. After knowing these, manage everything so that Yajñas will be performed. Without them, we can never become satisfied.”

## \|\| 1.208.88 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vāsavastatra samāhūya ca manmatham \|*  
*krodhaṃ lobhaṃ tathā daṃbhaṃ matsaraṃ dveṣasaṃyutam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. On hearing those words Vāsava summoned Manmatha, Krodha (Anger), Lobha (Greed), Dambha (Arrogance, Hypocrisy), Matsara (Jealousy) and Dveṣa (Hatred).

## \|\| 1.208.89-90 \|\|

*gatvā dharātalaṃ sarve mamādeśāddrutaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*svaśaktyā vārayadhvaṃ bho gautameśvarapūjakān \|\| 89 \|\|*

*ahilyeśvaradevasya śatānaṃdeśvarasya ca \|*  
*śakrādeśaṃ tu saṃprāpya te gatā dharaṇītale \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. “Go to the earth quickly at my behest. With your power restrain the worshippers of Gautameśvara, Ahalyeśvara and Śatānandeśvara.”

On getting the command of Śakra, They went to the earth.

## \|\| 1.208.91 \|\|

*kāmādikā narānbhejurgautameśvarapūjakān \|*  
*tathā'hilyeśvarasyāpi śatānaṃdeśvarasya ca \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Kāma and others overwhelmed the worshippers of Gautameśvara, Ahalyeśvara and Śatānandeśvara.

## \|\| 1.208.92 \|\|

*tato bhūyo makhā jātāḥ samagre dharaṇītale \|*  
*saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇāḥ sarve vatāni niyamāstathā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Thereupon, Yajñas began to be performed again all over the earth with the full complement of Dakṣiṇās (monetary gifts). So also Vratas and observances of holy rites.

## \|\| 1.208.93 \|\|

*tīrthayātrā japo homo yāścānyāḥ sukṛtakriyāḥ \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ mayā khyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dharādhipa \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Pilgrimages were undertaken. Japa, Homa and other holy rites also functioned properly. O king, I have thus narrated everything I was asked.

## \|\| 1.208.94-95 \|\|

*gayākūpyanuṣaṃgeṇa śakragautamaceṣṭitam \|*  
*bālamaṇḍanamāhātmyaṃ śakreśvarasamanvitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*indrasya sthāpanaṃ martye ahilyākhyānameva ca \|*  
*gautameśvaramāhātmyaṃ tathāhilyeśvarasya ca \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. In the context of extolling Gayākūpī I narrated the acts of Śakreśvara, the establishment of Indra in the mortal world, the story of Ahalyā and the greatness of Gautameśvara and Ahalyeśvara.

## \|\| 1.208.96 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*sa mucyetpātakātsadyaḥ paradārasamudbhavāt \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He who is endowed with great faith and listens to this shall instantly be rid of the sin arising from contact with other men’s wives.

## Chapter 209 - Origin of Śaṅkhāditya and Śaṅkhatīrtha

## \|\| 1.209.1-3 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ muniśārdūla śaṃkhatīrtha samudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vada me kṛtsnaṃ śraddhā me mahatī sthitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aho tīrthamaho tīrthaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*kṣetraṃ yacca dharāpṛṣṭhe sarvāścaryamayaṃ śubham \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāhaṃ tṛptiṃ dvijaśreṣṭha pragacchāmi kathaṃcana \|*  
*śṛṇvānastu sumāhātmyaṃ kṣetrasyāsya samudbhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

\[Full title: Origin of Śaṅkhāditya (Śaṅkha-āditya) and Śaṅkhatīrtha (Śaṅkha-tīrtha)\]

Ānarta said:

1-3. Now, O tiger among sages, tell me fully the greatness of Śaṅkhatīrtha. I have great faith therein.

Wonderful indeed is the Tīrtha! Wonderful indeed is the Tīrtha called Hāṭakeśvara! It is the only holy place which is the most splendid and full of miracles. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I am not fully satiated by listening to the excellent greatness of this holy place.

## \|\| 1.209.4 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*atra te kīrtayiṣyāmi pūrvavṛttaṃ kathāṃtaram \|*  
*śaṃkhatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ yathājātaṃ dharātale \|\| 4 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

4\. In this context, I shall narrate unto you the account of an earlier incident, of how the greatness of Śaṅkhatīrtha came to be established over the earth.

## \|\| 1.209.5 \|\|

*ānartādhipatiḥ pūrvamāsīdanyo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*yathā tvaṃ sāṃprataṃ bhūmau sarvalokaprapālakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Formerly, there was another king who ruled over Ānarta in the same manner as you who rule over all the peoples on the earth now.

## \|\| 1.209.6 \|\|

*so'kasmātkuṣṭhabhāgjāto vikalāṃgo babhūva ha \|*  
*aputraḥ śatrubhirvyāptastrastaśca nṛpasattamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All of a sudden, he became a leper and disabled in limbs. He had no sons. Overpowered by enemies the excellent king became frightened.

## \|\| 1.209.7 \|\|

*sa sarvairbhūmipālaiśca sarvataḥ paripīḍitaḥ \|*  
*rājyabhraṃśasamopetaḥ prāpto raivatakaṃ girim \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was harassed all round by all the kings. Ousted from his kingdom, he came to Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 1.209.8 \|\|

*tatrāpi pīḍyate nityaṃ sarvatastu malimlucaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There too he was disturbed by robbers all round.

## \|\| 1.209.9-10 \|\|

*hastyaśvarathahīnastu kośahīno yadā'bhavat \|*  
*sa tadā ciṃtayāmāsa kiṃ karomi ca sāṃpratam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kalatrāṇyapi sarvāṇi hriyaṃte taskarairbalāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. When he was deprived of his treasures and elephants,

horses and chariots, he began to think, ‘What shall I do now? All my wives are being carried off by robbers forcibly.’

## \|\| 1.209.11 \|\|

*sa evaṃ ciṃtayānastu gato vai nāradaṃ vibhum \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ pārthivaśārdūla vaiṣṇave divase sthite \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After thinking thus, O tiger among kings, he went to the holy Lord Nārada to meet him on the Vaiṣṇava day (eleventh lunar day, or the day with Śravaṇa constellation).

## \|\| 1.209.12 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyatsa saṃprāptaṃ nāradaṃ munisattamam \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena dāmodaradidṛkṣayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There he saw the excellent Sage Nārada. He had come there in the course of his pilgrimage with a desire to visit Dāmodara.

## \|\| 1.209.13 \|\|

*taṃ praṇamyātha śirasā kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*provāca vacanaṃ dīna upaviśya tadagrataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He lowered his head and bowed down with palms joined in reverence. In his dejected mood, he sat in front of him and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.209.14 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*śatrubhiḥ paribhūto'haṃ samatānmunisattama \|*  
*tato rājyaparibhraṃśātsaṃprāpto'tra mahāgirau \|\| 14 \|\|*

The king said:

14\. O excellent sage, I am assailed from all sides by my enemies. Then, having been ousted from the kingdom, I have come to this great mountain.

## \|\| 1.209.15-16 \|\|

*vipine taskaraiḥ pāpaiḥ prapīḍye'haṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*yatkiṃcidaśvanāgādyaṃ mayā saha samāgatam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ taskarairnītaṃ kośā dārāstathā vasu \|*  
*tasmādvada muniśreṣṭha vairāgyaṃ me mahatsthitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. In the forest I am harassed by sinful robbers all round. A few horses, elephants etc. that had accompanied me were entirely taken away by them. The treasury, the ladies and much of the cash on hand were also looted by them. Hence, O excellent sage, I am utterly disgusted. Do tell me now:

## \|\| 1.209.17 \|\|

*anyajanmodbhavaṃ kiṃcinmama pāpaṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*yenemāṃ ca daśāṃ prāptaḥ sahasā munisattama \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Is this the result of a terrible sin of mine committed in some previous birth, O excellent sage, which has put me in this miserable plight?

## \|\| 1.209.18 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*provācā'tha nṛpaṃ dīnaṃ jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing his words, the leading sage meditated for a long time. He understood everything through his divine vision and spoke thus to the distressed king:

## \|\| 1.209.19 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*na tvayā kutsitaṃ kiṃcitpūrva dehāṃtare kṛtam \|*  
*mayā jñātaṃ mahārāja sarvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 19 \|\|*

Nārada said:

19\. O great king, nothing despicable had been committed by you in the previous life. Everything has been understood by me through divine vision.

## \|\| 1.209.20 \|\|

*tvamāsīḥ pārthivaḥ pūrvaṃ siddhapannagasaṃjñite \|*  
*pattane somavaṃśīyaḥ sarva śatrunibarhaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Formerly, you were a king of the lunar race in the city named Siddhapannaga. You eliminated all enemies.

## \|\| 1.209.21 \|\|

*tvayā ceṣṭaṃ mahāyajñaiḥ sadā saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*mahādānāni dattāni pūjitā brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You performed great Yajñas always with full complement of monetary gifts. Other great gifts were also made and excellent Brāhmaṇas were honoured.

## \|\| 1.209.22 \|\|

*tena karma vipākena bhūyaḥ pārthivatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. As a result of those good acts, you have become a king once again.

## \|\| 1.209.23 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*iha janmani no kṛtyaṃ saṃsmarāmi vibho kṛtam \|*  
*tatkiṃ rājyapari bhraṃśaḥ sahasā me samutthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

23\. Even in this birth, O holy Lord, I do not remember having committed anything wrong. Then why was I ousted from the kingdom all of a sudden?

## \|\| 1.209.24 \|\|

*lakṣmyā hīnasya lokasya loke'sminvyarthatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*jīvitaṃ muniśārdūla vijñātaṃ hi mayā'dhunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In this world, O tiger among sages, the life of a person devoid of Lakṣmī (good fortune, affluence) shall become futile. This I have understood now.

## \|\| 1.209.25 \|\|

*mṛto naro gataśrīko mṛtaṃ rāṣṭramarājakam \|*  
*mṛtamaśrotriye dānaṃ mṛto yajñastvadakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A man bereft of fortune and glory is as good as dead. A kingdom without a ruler is as good as no kingdom. Religious gift offered to one who is not learned in the Vedas is as good as no gift. A Yajña without monetary gifts is as good as no Yajña.

## \|\| 1.209.26 \|\|

*lakṣmyā hīnasya martyasya bāṃdhavo'pi vijāyate \|*  
*prārthayiṣyati māṃ nūnaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ cānyato vrajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even kinsmen become estranged from a man devoid of fortune and wealth. On seeing him they think, ‘He will request us for something surely’ and they go elsewhere (to avoid him).

## \|\| 1.209.27 \|\|

*yathā māṃ sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭvā ye mayā'pi pratarpitāḥ \|*  
*te'pi dūrataraṃ yāṃti eṣa māṃ prārthayi ṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. This is just like my case now. Even those who were helped and propitiated by me, go far off on seeing me thinking, ‘Oh, this fellow, will request us for something!’.

## \|\| 1.209.28 \|\|

*dhanahīnaṃ naraṃ tyaktvā kulīnamapi cottamam \|*  
*gacchati svajano'nyatra śuṣkaṃ vṛkṣamivāṃḍajāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Like birds that leave a dry tree (on which they lived), kinsmen desert a man without money, though he may be excellent and of noble birth.

## \|\| 1.209.29 \|\|

*tatkāryakāraṇārthāya daridro' bhyeti cedgṛham \|*  
*dhanino bhartsayaṃtyenaṃ samāgacchaṃti nāṃtikam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If a poor man approaches the house of rich people even for doing their own task, they certainly rebuke him and do not go ṅeār him.

## \|\| 1.209.30 \|\|

*kṛpaṇo'pi dhanāḍhyaścedāgacchati hi yācitum \|*  
*eṣa dāsyati me kiṃci diti citte nṛṇāṃ bhavet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If a rich man, though miserly, actually comes to request for something, people rather think ‘He will give me something.’

## \|\| 1.209.31 \|\|

*mama tvaṃ pūrvavaṃśīyaḥ pitā te ca piturmama \|*  
*sadā snehaparaścāsīttvaṃ ca snehavivarjitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “You are one belonging to my ancestral family and your father to my fathers. He was always affectionate but you are devoid of affection.”

## \|\| 1.209.32-33 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvaṃti loke'tra dhanināṃ purataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*kulīnā api pāpānāṃ dṛśyaṃte dhanalipsayā \|*  
*daridrasya manuṣyasya kṣitau rājyaṃ prakurvataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*praśoṣaḥ kevalaṃ bhāvī hṛdayasya mahāmune \|*  
*dvāvimau kaṇṭakau tīkṣṇau śarīrapariśoṣiṇau \|*  
*yaścādhanaḥ kāmayate yaśca kupyatyanīśvaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In this world people of noble birth are seen standing before sinful yet rich people. They say this (as if) with a desire to get money. A person who rules over the earth is reduced to poverty. It results only in great distress of the heart. These two are sharp thorns causing distress to the body, viz. a poor man who aspires to love and a man though devoid of power becoming angry.

## \|\| 1.209.34 \|\|

*śmaśānamapi sevaṃte dhanalubdhā niśāgame \|*  
*janetāramapi tyaktvā nityaṃ yāṃti sudūrataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Men greedy of wealth resort to even the cremation ground at nightfall. They go to far-off lands forever forsaking their own progenitors.

## \|\| 1.209.35 \|\|

*sumūrkhopi bhavedvidvānakulīno'pi satkulaḥ \|*  
*yasya vittaṃ bhave ddharmye viparītamato'nyathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If one has wealth in one’s mansion one is sure to be considered as a learned man, although one is really utterly foolish and a man though of ignoble birth as of noble birth. In the contrary case everything becomes the very opposite.

## \|\| 1.209.36 \|\|

*nirviṇṇo'haṃ muniśreṣṭha jīvitasya ca sāṃpratam \|*  
*tasmādbrūhi kimarthaṃ me dāridryaṃ samupasthitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent sage, I am disgusted with my life now. So do tell me, why poverty has befallen me.

## \|\| 1.209.37 \|\|

*kuṣṭhaścāpi mamopetaḥ śatrubhiśca parābhavam \|*  
*anyajanmāṃtaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Leprosy also has come to me over and above the torment from the enemies. The other births are (can be) seen by you through your divine vision.

## \|\| 1.209.38 \|\|

*kukarmaṇā na saṃspṛṣṭaṃ svalpenāpi bravīṣi mām \|*  
*etajjanmātaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ smarāmi munisattama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. And you say that those births have not been defiled even by the least of misdeeds. O excellent sage, I remember the facts of this visible life of mine.

## \|\| 1.209.39 \|\|

*na mayā kukṛtaṃ kiṃcitkadācitsamanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*tatkiṃ rājyaparibhraṃśo jāto'yaṃ mama sanmune \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. (In this life) no evil act has ever been perpetrated by me. Then, O excellent sage, why has this ousting from the kingdom taken place in my case?

## \|\| 1.209.40 \|\|

*atra me kautukaṃ jātaṃ tasmāddehi vinirṇayam \|*  
*bhavenna vā bhavetkarma kṛtaṃ yacca śubhāśubham \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I am eager and inquisitive in this connection. Give me a decisive answer whether auspicious or inauspicious acts do find their results operative.

## \|\| 1.209.41 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā tu nāradaḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭastataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

41\. On hearing his words, Nārada meditated for a long time. He was overwhelmed with pity and he spoke respectfully:

## \|\| 1.209.42 \|\|

*śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi yathā śuddhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*tava rājyasya saṃprāptiryathā bhūyo'pi jāyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “Listen, O king, I shall tell you how purity can be regained and how you will get back the realm once again.

## \|\| 1.209.43 \|\|

*tava bhūmau mahāpuṇyamasti kṣetraṃ jagattraye \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthaṃ tatrāsti śobhanam \|*  
*śaṃkhatīrthamiti khyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In your land (Ānarta), there is a holy spot highly meritorious and well-known in all the three worlds by the name Hāṭakeśvara. There is a splendid Tīrtha there famous by the name Śaṅkhatīrtha. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.209.44-45 \|\|

*yastatra kurute snānaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ śuklapakṣasya saṃprāpte māsi mādhave \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sūryavāre tu samprāpte bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|*  
*sarvakuṣṭhavinirmukto jāyate sūryasaṃnibhaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. A person should be possessed of great faith. He should take his holy bath there at sunrise on the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Mādhava (Vaiśākha) coinciding with a Sunday. He becomes freed from all types of leprosy and (becomes) brilliant on a par with the Sun.

## \|\| 1.209.46 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyettaṃtaṃ sarveṣu durlabham \|*  
*sa tadā'pnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkheśvaraṃ śubham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Whatever desire he may cherish, he will undoubtedly get it by visiting the auspicious deity Śaṅkheśvara even if that desired thing is rare in ail the worlds.

## \|\| 1.209.47 \|\|

*kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ tatra svadeśe vasatā nṛpa \|*  
*tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ yattvamatra samāgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O king, You stayed in this land. Still, haven’t you heard the greatness of that Tīrtha? Wherefor have you come here (at all)?”

## \|\| 1.209.48 \|\|

*siddhasena uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ śaṃkheśvaro devaḥ saṃjāto vada sanmune \|\| 48 \|\|*

Siddhasena (The king) said:

48\. What is the origin of the deity Śaṅkheśvara? Do narrate, O excellent sage.

## \|\| 1.209.49 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*yathā śaṃkheśvaro jātaḥ śaṃkhatīrthaṃ tu pārthiva \|\| 49 \|\|*

Nārada said:

49\. O king, I shall tell you this age-old legend as to how the deity Śaṅkheśvara and Śaṅkha Tīrtha originated.

## \|\| 1.209.50 \|\|

*āsaturbrāhmaṇau pūrvaṃ likhitaḥ śaṃkha eva ca \|*  
*bhrātarau vedaviduṣau tapasyugre vyavasthitau \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Formerly, there were two Brāhmaṇas named Śaṅkha and Likhita. They were two brothers well-versed in the Vedas and engaged in severe penance.

## \|\| 1.209.51 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya likhitasyāśramaṃ prati \|*  
*bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya saṃprāpto namaskārakṛte nṛpa \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Once, O king, Śaṅkha went to the hermitage of his elder brother Likhita for paying respects.

## \|\| 1.209.52 \|\|

*so'paśyadāśramaṃ śūnyaṃ likhitena vivarjitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He found the hermitage vacant as Likhita was absent.

## \|\| 1.209.53 \|\|

*athāpaśyadvane tasmi nparipakvaphalāni saḥ \|*  
*praṇayātpratijagrāha matvā bhrāturnṛpā'śramam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He saw ripe fruits in that park. O king, he thought, ‘After all this is my brother’s hermitage’ and lovingly took (some) of the ripe fruits.

## \|\| 1.209.54 \|\|

*etasminnantare prāpto likhitastatra cāśrame \|*  
*yāvatpaśyati śaṃkhaṃ sa pragṛhī tabṛhatphalam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the meantime, Likhita came back to the hermitage and saw Śaṅkha with the big fruits plucked.

## \|\| 1.209.55-56 \|\|

*kimidaṃ vihitaṃ pāpa pāpaṃ sādhuvigarhitam \|*  
*cauryakarma tvayā niṃdyaṃ yaddhṛtāni phalāni ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*anena karmaṇā tubhyaṃ tapo yāsya ti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*cauryakarmapravṛttasya brāhmaṇairgarhitasya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. “O sinner, why is this evil deed despised by good people, committed by you? The despicable act of theft has been committed by you as the fruits have been plucked (by you). As a result of this deed, your power of penance will get dwindled; you have engaged yourself in the act of stealth; you are (thereby) despised by Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 1.209.57 \|\|

*śaṃkha uvāca \|*  
*ekodarasamutpanno jyeṣṭhabhrātā yathā pitā \|*  
*bhūyāditi śrutirloke prasiddhā sarvataḥ sthitā \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śaṅkha said:

57\. Elder brother born of the same womb is like one’s father, according to a very famous Vedic passage well-known everywhere.

## \|\| 1.209.58 \|\|

*tatkiṃ putrasya viprendra nādhikāraḥ piturdhane \|*  
*yathaivaṃ niṣṭhurairvākyairnirbhartsayasi māṃ vibho \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Therefore, O great Brāhmaṇa, has the son no right in his father’s wealth? O holy Sir, why do you rebuke me with very harsh words?

## \|\| 1.209.59-60 \|\|

*likhita uvāca \|*  
*na doṣo jāyate hartuḥ putrasyātra kathaṃcana \|*  
*ekatra saṃsthitasyātra piturvittamasaṃśayam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vibhaktastu yadā putro bhrātā vā'pahareddhanam \|*  
*tadā doṣamavāpnoti cauryotthaṃ matameva me \|\| 60 \|\|*

Likhita said:

59-60. It is my opinion that there is no harm if the son still remains in the family of his father and makes use of his father’s assets unhesitatingly. But, if the son or brother becomes separate after a division of the property and makes use of the father’s property, he incurs the sin of theft.

## \|\| 1.209.61 \|\|

*putrasya tu punarvittaṃ pitā harati sarvadā \|*  
*na tasya vidyate doṣo vibhakta syāpi karhicit \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A father can, of course, take the wealth or property from his son always. He incurs no sin or blame even if the son has become separate after the division of property.

## \|\| 1.209.62 \|\|

*atra ślokaḥ purā gīto manunā smṛtikāriṇā \|*  
*taṃ te'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi dharmaśāstrodbhavaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. In this context a verse has been composed by Manu, the author of the Smṛti. I shall quote those words of ethical code:

## \|\| 1.209.63 \|\|

*traya evādhaproktā bhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ \|*  
*yatte samadhigacchaṃti yasya te tasya taddhanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “One’s wife, servant and son—these three are said to be persons without assets. Whatever they get or inherit is the wealth of the person to whom they belong.”

## \|\| 1.209.64 \|\|

*śaṃkha uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ cauryadoṣo'sti mama tāta mahattaraḥ \|*  
*nigrahaṃ kuru me śīghraṃ yena na syāttapaḥkṣayaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

Śaṅkha said:

64\. If it is so, O dear one, I have incurred greater sin. Chastise me quickly, lest there should be loss of penance.

## \|\| 1.209.65 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā śastramādāya nirmalam \|*  
*cakartātha bhujau tasya bhrātā bhrātuśca nirghṛṇaḥ \|*  
*sopi cchinnakaro vipro vyathayāpi samanvitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

65\. On coming to know of his decision, the ruthless (elder) brother took up a clean weapon and cut off his (Śaṅkha’s) arms. The Brāhmaṇa whose hands had been cut, suffered much pain.

## \|\| 1.209.66 \|\|

*manyamānaḥ prasādaṃ taṃ bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya pārthiva \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O king, he considered this as a favour indeed of his elder brother.

## \|\| 1.209.67 \|\|

*tatastu kāmadaṃ kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*matvā prāpya tapastepe kaṃcitprāpya jalāśayam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He considered the holy place called Hāṭakeśvara as one that yields cherished desires. Having come there he resorted to a water tank and performed penance.

## \|\| 1.209.68 \|\|

*varṣāsvākāśaśāyī ca hemante salilāśrayaḥ \|*  
*pañcāgnisādhako grīṣme ṣaṣṭhakālakṛtāśanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. During rainy season he lay under the open sky; during winter he resorted to water reservoirs; in summer he performed the penance in the midst of five fires. He took food only once in the course of six meal times.

## \|\| 1.209.69 \|\|

*saṃsnāpya bhāskaraṃ sthāṇuṃ tatpuraḥ śatarudriyam \|*  
*japansāmoktarudrāṃśca bhava rudrāṃstathā japan \|*  
*prāṇarudrāṃstathā nīlānskandasūktasamanvitān \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He bathed (the images of) Bhāskara and Sthāṇu. Before them he recited Śatarudriya, the Rudra verses from Sāmaveda, Bhavarudra verses. Prāṇarudras and Nīlarudras along with Skanda Sūktas.

## \|\| 1.209.70 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte tuṣṭastasya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*provāca darśanaṃ gatvā saha sūrya vṛṣeśvaraiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then at the end of a thousand years, Maheśvara became pleased with him. He appeared before him in the company of the Sun-god and Indra.

## \|\| 1.209.71 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*śaṃkha tuṣṭo'smi te vatsa tapasānena suvrata \|*  
*tasmātkathaya me kṣipraṃ yaddadāmi tavā'dhunā \|\| 71 \|\|*

Maheśvara said:

71\. O my dear Śaṅkha of good holy rites, I am pleased with your penance. Tell me quickly what I shall offer you now.

## \|\| 1.209.72 \|\|

*śaṃkha uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*jāyetāṃ tādṛśau hastau yādṛśo me purā sthitau \|\| 72 \|\|*

Śaṅkha said:

72\. O Lord, if you are pleased, if a boon has to be granted to me, let both of my arms grow up again and be similar to the former ones.

## \|\| 1.209.73 \|\|

*tvayā'traiva sadā vāsaḥ kāryaḥ suravareśvara \|*  
*liṃge kṛtvā dayāṃ deva mamopari mahattarām \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O Lord of the excellent Suras, take great pity on me and reside in this Liṅga permanently.

## \|\| 1.209.74 \|\|

*etajjalāśayaṃ nātha mama nāmnā dharātale \|*  
*prasiddhiṃ yātu lokasya yāvaccandrārkatārakāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O Lord, let this water reservoir become famous all over the earth after my own name as long as the Moon, the Sun and the stars shine.

## \|\| 1.209.75 \|\|

*atra yaḥ kurute snānaṃ dhṛtvā manasi durlabham \|*  
*kiṃcidvastu samagraṃ tu tasya saṃpatsyate vibho \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A person may think of the rarest of things and take his bath here (in this tank). Let him attain that entirely, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.209.76-77 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adyāhaṃ darśanaṃ prāptastava caivāṣṭamīdine \|*  
*mādhavasya site pakṣe yasmādbrāhmaṇasattama \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tasmātsaṃkramaṇaṃ liṃge tāvake'smindvijottama \|*  
*kariṣyāmi na sandeho dinamekamasaṃśayam \|\| 77 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

76-77. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I appeared before you this day i.e. the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Mādhava. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I shall pass into your Liṅga on this day and remain there for a day undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.209.78-79 \|\|

*yaścātra divase prāpte tīrthe'traiva bhavodbhave \|*  
*snānaṃ kṛtvā ravervāra udayaṃ samupasthite \|\| 78 \|\|*

*pūjayiṣyati me mūrtiṃ tvayā saṃsthāpitāṃ dvija \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhivinirmukto mama lokaṃ sa yāsyati \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. He who takes his holy bath in this Tīrtha on a Sunday at sunrise and worships my image installed by you shall be rid of the disease of leprosy. He will go to my world.

## \|\| 1.209.80 \|\|

*śeṣakāle'pi viprendra ajñānavihitādaghāt \|*  
*muktiṃ prāpsyatyasaṃdigdhaṃ mama vākyāddvijottama \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Even on other occasions, O leading Brāhmaṇa, (if any one bathes therein) he gets rid of sins unwittingly committed. There is no doubt. This is my promise, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.209.81 \|\|

*tathā tavāpi yau hastau chinnāvetāvubhāvapi \|*  
*tasminyoge'bhiṣekāttauḥ syātāṃ bhūyo'pi tādṛśau \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. So also your hands that have been cut off shall crop up once again in the same manner as a result of the holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.209.82 \|\|

*eṣa me pratyayo vipra bhaviṣyati tavā'dhunā \|*  
*bhūyaḥ snānaṃ vidhāya tvaṃ tato mūrtiṃ mamārcaya \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. This is my conviction. O Brāhmaṇa, you will also become convinced now. Take the holy bath again and adore my image.

## \|\| 1.209.83 \|\|

*anye'pi vyaṃgatāṃ prāptāḥ saṃyoge'tra tava sthite \|*  
*snātvā māṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti muktiṃ yāsyaṃti te dvija \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Other persons too with crippled limbs should take their holy bath during this astral combination here. If after bath they adore me they will attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.209.84 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*śaṃkho'pi tatkṣaṇātsnātvā pūjayitvā divākaram \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. After saying thus, the Thousand-rayed Lord vanished. Śaṅkha immediately took bath and worshipped Divākara (Sun-god).

## \|\| 1.209.85 \|\|

*yāvatpaśyati cātmānaṃ tāvaddhastasamanvitam \|*  
*ātmānaṃ paśyamānastu vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. When he surveyed himself, he saw himself endowed with the hands. He was surprised.

## \|\| 1.209.86 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tatraiva kṛtvā'śramapadaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tapastepe dvija śreṣṭho gataśca paramāṃ gatim \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Ever since then, O king, he set up his penance grove. The excellent Brāhmaṇa performed penance and attained the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.209.87 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi rājeṃdra saṃyogaṃ prāpya tattvataḥ \|*  
*tenaiva vidhinā snātvā tvaṃ pūjaya divākaram \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Hence, O leading king, at such an astral combination, take your holy bath in accordance with the injunctions and worship Divākara.

## \|\| 1.209.88 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityaṃ paṭhedvā purato raveḥ \|*  
*tasyānvaye'pi no kuṣṭhī kadācitsamprajāyate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. If any one listens to this narration or reads it before (an image of) Ravi there shall be no leper at ail in his family.

## Chapter 210 - Importance of Tāmbūla

## \|\| 1.210.1-6 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya devarṣernāradasya ca \|*  
*siddhaseno mahīpālaḥ prāpya taṃ yogamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mādhave māsi saṃprāpte aṣṭamyāṃ sūryavāsare \|*  
*sūryodaye tu saṃprāpte yāvatsnātvā'rcayedravim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tāvatkuṣṭhavinirmuktaḥ sahasā samapadyata \|*  
*tato divyavapurbhūtvā santoṣaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ tataścakre tāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇam \|*  
*ajñānena kṛtaṃ yacca cūrṇapatrasamanvitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tataśca paramāṃ lakṣmīṃ saṃprāptaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ sa pracakre yathā purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ śaṃkhatīrthasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumi cchasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

1-6. On hearing the words of the celestial sage Nārada, king Siddhasena, awaited the excellent astral combination. On the eighth lunar day in the month of Mādhava (Vaiśākha) coinciding with a Sunday, he took his holy bath at sunrise and worshipped Ravi.

Immediately, he became rid of his leprosy. He attained a divine physical form and became highly pleased.

He then performed the expiatory rite for having chewed the broken betel leaves, unwittingly. Thereupon, the king regained the greatest splendour and glory. He then ruled over the ancestral kingdom as before.

Thus, O excellent king, the greatness of Śaṅkhatīrtha has been wholly narrated to you. What else do you wish to hear further?

## \|\| 1.210.7 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*atyāścaryamidaṃ brahmanyattvayā parikīrtitam \|*  
*yallakṣmīstasya sannaṣṭā cūrṇapatrasya bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

7\. O holy Sir, your statement that he (the king) lost his royal glory by chewing the broken betel leaves is extremely surprising.

## \|\| 1.210.8 \|\|

*kīdṛktena kṛtaṃ tasya prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhayre \|*  
*kīdṛktena kṛtaṃ tacca nijarājyaṃ yathā purā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Of what nature is the expiatory rite performed by him for gaining purity? How was his own kingdom ruled by him as before?

## \|\| 1.210.9 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*eṣā puṇyatamā medhyā nāgavallī narādhipa \|*  
*ayathāvatkṛtā vaktre bahūndoṣānprayacchati \|*  
*tasmādyatnena saṃbhakṣyā dattvā caiva svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

9\. O king, this Nāgavallī (betel leaf and its creeper) is sacred and pure. If it is placed within the mouth (i.e. chewed) in an improper manner it will result in many disasters and adverse effects. Hence, the leaf should be scrupulously eaten (chewed) after giving it (offering it) in accordance with one’s own capacity.

## \|\| 1.210.10 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*nāgavallī kathaṃ jātā kasmāddoṣo mahānsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*ayathāvadbhakṣaṇācca tanme vaktumihārhasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

10\. How did the Nāgavallī originate? How is it said that by chewing improperly there will be great defect? It behoves you to tell me.

## \|\| 1.210.11 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*praśnabhāro mahāneṣa tvayā me parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi ca vadiṣyāmi yadi te kautukaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*yasmātsañjāyate doṣaścūrṇapatrasya bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

11\. The importance of the questions asked by you is great. Still, O king, if you have any curiosity, I shall explain to you how evil results from chewing the broken leaves.

## \|\| 1.210.12 \|\|

*amṛtārthaṃ purā devairmathitaḥ kalaśodadhiḥ \|*  
*manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Formerly, the Milk Ocean was churned by Devas after making the Mandara mountain the churning rod and Vāsuki the cord.

## \|\| 1.210.13 \|\|

*mukhadeśe balirlagnaḥ pucchadeśe'khilāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*vāsudevamatenaiva sandadhārātha kacchapaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the suggestion of Vāsudeva, Bali engaged himself at the facial region (of thee serpent) and all the Suras in the region of the tail. The Kacchapa (Tortoise incarnation of Viṣṇu) held up (the mountain).

## \|\| 1.210.14 \|\|

*mandare bhramamāṇe tu prāgeva nṛpasattama \|*  
*ānarta sahasā jātaṃ ratnatritayameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O excellent king Ānarta, when Mandara was being whirled three Ratnas (jewels) came out at the outset.

## \|\| 1.210.15 \|\|

*nīlāṃbaradharaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ puruṣo vakranāsikaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇadantaḥ sthūlaśirā dīrghagrīvo mahodaraḥ \|*  
*śūrpākārāṃghrirevā'sau cipiṭākṣo bhayāvahaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The first one was a frightening person of crooked nose. He wore a dark-blue cloth. He was swarthy and blacktoothed. His head was big, neck long and belly bulging out. His feet resembled a winnowing basket. The eyes were flattened.

## \|\| 1.210.16 \|\|

*tathā tadrūpiṇī tasya kubhāryā rākṣasī yathā \|*  
*śiśunāṃgulilagnena garbhaśramaparāyaṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. His wife had the same hideous form like that of a Rākṣasī. An infant had caught hold of her fingers. She was experiencing great fatigue due to pregnancy.

## \|\| 1.210.17 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve dānavāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*manthānaṃ tatparityajya tāngrahītuṃ pradhāvitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereupon, all the groups of Devas and Dānavas in particular left the churning rod and ran after them to seize them.

## \|\| 1.210.18 \|\|

*atha tānvikṛtāndṛṣṭvā sarve śaṃkāsamanvitāḥ \|*  
*jagṛhurnaiva rājeṃdra jahasuśca parasparam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Seeing them hideous and horrible all of them hesitated, O leading king. They could not seize them. They looked at one another and laughed.

## \|\| 1.210.19-20 \|\|

*athovāca balirdaityaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*brahmā'di yallabhetsarvaṃ yatpurastātprajāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ratnatritayametaddhi tasmādgṛhṇātu padmajaḥ \|*  
*yena siddhirbhavedasminmanthane kasya cā'rpaṇāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then Daitya Bali stood with palms joined in reverence and spoke: “Brahmā is the first i.e. chief one, as usual. It is he who should get what comes out at the outset. Hence, let the Lotus-born take these three jewels. Thereby, we shall have Siddhi in this activity of churning because it (Trinity of Ratnas) is dedicated to Ka (Brahmā).”

## \|\| 1.210.21 \|\|

*tadvākyaṃ viṣṇunā tasya śaṃsitaṃ śaṃkareṇa tu \|*  
*iṃdrādyaiśca suraiḥ sarvairdānavaiśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That statement of his was approved by Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, Indra and other Suras and especially by all the Dānavas in particular.

## \|\| 1.210.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare brahmā jagrāha tritayaṃ ca tat \|*  
*dākṣiṇyātsarvadevānāmanicchannapi pārthiva \|*  
*mamanthuḥ sāgaraṃ rājanpunaste yatnamāśritāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime, Brahmā accepted the three things out of courtesy and consideration for the Devas, O king, though he did not relish it. They persevered more and churned the ocean again, O king.

## \|\| 1.210.23 \|\|

*tataśca vāruṇī jātā divyagandhasamanvitā \|*  
*balinā saṃgṛhītā sā pratyakṣaṃ balavidviṣaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then Vāruṇī (Liquor) came out effervescent with divine odour. Even as Indra watched, it was taken up by Bali.

## \|\| 1.210.24 \|\|

*āvarte cāpare jāte niṣkrāṃtaḥ kaustubho maṇiḥ \|*  
*sa gṛhīto mahārāja viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After one more round of churning the Kaustubha jewel came out. O great king it was taken by Viṣṇu, the powerful one.

## \|\| 1.210.25 \|\|

*athāpare sthite tatra mahāvarte niśāpatiḥ \|*  
*sañjātaḥ sa vṛṣāṃkena saṃgṛhītaśca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the next round, the Lord of the Night (the Moon) came out. It was instantly taken up by the Lord having the bull as his emblem (Śiva).

## \|\| 1.210.26 \|\|

*pārijātastato jāto divyagandhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa gṛhītvā suraiḥ sarvaiḥ sthāpito naṃdane vane \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Pārijāta with divine scent came up then. All the Suras took it up and planted it in the Nandana garden.

## \|\| 1.210.27 \|\|

*tasyānaṃtaramevātha surabhī vatsasaṃyutā \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtā vyomamārgeṇa golokaṃ samavasthitā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter, Surabhi (Divine cow) (Kāmadhenu) along with her calf came up and proceeded to Goloka by the heavenly path.

## \|\| 1.210.28-29 \|\|

*tato dhanvaṃtarirjāto bibhraddhaste kamaṃḍalum \|*  
*saṃpūrṇamamṛtenaiva sa devairdānavainṛpa \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gṛhīto yugapatkruddhaiḥ parasparajigīṣayā \|*  
*devānāṃ hastago vaidyo daityānāṃ ca kamaṇḍaluḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Then Dhanvantari came out holding the Kamaṇḍalu (Pot) filled with Amṛta (Nactar) in his hand. It was grasped simultaneously by both the Devas and the Dānavas who were furious and desired to conquer one another.

The Vaidya (physician Dhanvantari) came within the grasp of the Devas and the Kamaṇḍalu that of the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.210.30 \|\|

*tatastaṃ lobhasaṃyuktā mamaṃthuḥ sāgaraṃ nṛpa \|*  
*padmahastātra saṃjātā tato lakṣmīḥ sitāṃbarā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then, O king, those greedy ones churned the ocean. Thereupon, Lakṣmī clad in white garments, came out holding a lotus in her hand.

## \|\| 1.210.31-32 \|\|

*svayameva vṛto viṣṇustayā pārthivasattama \|*  
*mathyamāne tatotīva samudre devadānavaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kālakūṭaṃ samutpannaṃ yena sarve surāsurāḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ kaṣṭaṃ prabhagnāśca diśo daśa \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O excellent king, Viṣṇu was wooed by her herself. Then the ocean was churned further with more ardour by the Devas and the Dānavas. Then Kālakūṭa poison came up whereby both the Suras and the Asuras experienced great suffering. They scattered themselves in all the ten quarters.

## \|\| 1.210.33 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavāñchaṃbhustīvraṃ tīvaparākramaḥ \|*  
*bhakṣayāmāsa rājeṃdra nīlakaṇṭhastato'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing it, O leading king, Lord Śaṃbhu of great valour quickly swallowed and became Nīlakaṇṭha (one with a blue throat).

## \|\| 1.210.34 \|\|

*atha saṃtyajya maṃthānaṃ maṃdaraṃ vāsukiṃ tathā \|*  
*amṛtārthe'bhavadyuddhaṃ daityānāṃ vibudhaiḥ saha \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then the Daityas and the Suras left the churning activity, Mandara and Vāsuki. For the sake of Amṛta, the Devas fought a fierce battle with the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.210.35-39 \|\|

*atha strīrūpamādhāya viṣṇurdaityānuvāca tān \|*  
*tato hṛṣṭo balistasyai dattvā pīyūṣameva tat \|\| 35 \|\|*

*viśvāsaṃ paramaṃ gatvā yuddhaṃ cakre suraiḥ saha \|*  
*tato viṣṇuḥ parityajya strīrūpaṃ puruṣākṛtiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tadevāmṛtamādāya yayau yatra divaukasaḥ \|*  
*abravīttānsuhṛṣṭātmā pivadhvamamṛtaṃ surāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yenāmaratvamāsādya vyāpādayata dānavān \|*  
*te tatheti pratijñāya papuḥ pīyūṣamuttamam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*amarāśca tato jātā jaghnuḥ saṃkhye mahāsurān \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Then Viṣṇu assumed the guise of a woman and said to them such words as made Bali convinced and he handed over the Pīyūṣa (Nectar) to her. In great confidence, he fought with the Suras.

## \|\| 1.210.40 \|\|

*teṣāṃ pānavidhau tatra vartamāne mahīpate \|*  
*rāhurvibudharūpeṇa papau pīyūṣamutsukaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Viṣṇu left the female form and resumed the manly form. He then took the Amṛta to the place where the Heaven-dwellers were present. With great delight he said: “O Suras, drink the nectar. Thereby, you will gain immortality and slay the Dānavas. Affirming “It shall be so” they drank the excellent Pīyūṣa. Becoming immortal they slew the great Asuras in battle.

40\. Even as their drinking bout went on, O king, Rāhu drank Pīyūṣa in the guise of a Deva.

## \|\| 1.210.41 \|\|

*sa lakṣito mahādaityaścaṃdrārkābhyāṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*nivedito hare rājannāyaṃ devo mahāsuraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. At that very instant the great Daitya was noticed by Moon and Sun. O king they reported: “O Hari, this is a great Asura, not a Deva.”

## \|\| 1.210.42 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vāsudevena tasya cakraṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*vadhāya pārthivaśreṣṭha muktaṃ vajrasamaprabham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing it, O excellent king, the discus Sudarśana having adamantine lustre, was discharged in order to kill him.

## \|\| 1.210.43 \|\|

*yāvanmātraṃ śarīraṃ tattasya vyāptaṃ mahīpate \|*  
*amṛtena tataḥ kṛttamamoghenāpi tacchiraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Since, O king, only the body had been pervaded by the Amṛta, his head was cut off though the Amṛta was never futile.

## \|\| 1.210.44 \|\|

*tato'maratvamāpannaḥ sa yāvatsiṃhikāsutaḥ \|*  
*tāvatprokto'cyutenātha sāmnā paramavalgunā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereupon, the son of Siṃhikā (Rāhu) gained immortality and so Acyuta told him in excessively sweet conciliatory terms:

## \|\| 1.210.45 \|\|

*tyaja daityānmahābhāga devānāṃ saṃmato bhava \|*  
*saṃprāpsyasi parāṃ pūjāṃ sadā tvaṃ grahamaṃḍale \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O highly esteemed one, leave the Daityas and be honoured by the Devas. You will always be adored in the group of Planets.”

## \|\| 1.210.46 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya tyaktvā tāndaityasattamān \|*  
*pūjāṃ prāpnoti martyānāṃ saṃsthito grahamaṇḍale \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Saying “So be it”, he abandoned the excellent Daityas. Stationed in the midst of the Planets, he receives the adoration of human beings.

## \|\| 1.210.47 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare daityā nirjitāḥ surasattamaiḥ \|*  
*diśo jagmuḥ paritrastāḥ kecinmṛtyumupāgatāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In the meantime, the Daityas were defeated by the excellent Suras. Utterly frightened, they fled to different quarters. Some of them died too.

## \|\| 1.210.48 \|\|

*pītaśeṣaṃ ca pīyūṣaṃ sthāpitaṃ nandane vane \|*  
*nāgarājasya yatraiva sthitamālānameva ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Pīyūṣa that remained after they had drunk it, was placed in the Nandana garden where the king of elephants (i.e. Airāvata, the elephant of Indra) had been tethered to his post.

## \|\| 1.210.49 \|\|

*aharniśaṃ madasrāvī karīṃdraḥ so'pi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tatprabhāvaiḥ prabhinnaḥ sa pīyūṣasya kamaṃḍaluḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The leading elephant shed its ichor day and night. Due to its power, the pot of Pīyūṣa got split.

## \|\| 1.210.50 \|\|

*tato vallī samutpannā tasmāccaiva kamaṇḍaloḥ \|*  
*tatrālānasamārūḍhā vṛddhiṃ ca paramāṃ gatā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then a creeper grew up from the pot. It twined round the tethering post (of Airāvata) and had a luscious growth.

## \|\| 1.210.51 \|\|

*tadudbhavāni patrāṇi gṛhītvā surasattamāḥ \|*  
*apūrvāṇi sugaṃdhīni matvā te bhakṣayaṃti ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The excellent Suras found the leaves thereof extremely fragrant and hitherto unknown. Hence they plucked them and ate them.

## \|\| 1.210.52 \|\|

*vaktraśuddhikṛte rājanviśeṣeṇa praharṣitāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O king, they found them especially useful in purifying the mouth and they were delighted.

## \|\| 1.210.53 \|\|

*atha dhanvatarirvaidyaḥ svabuddhyā pṛthivīpate \|*  
*nāgālāne yato jātā nāgavallī bhaviṣyati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O king, Dhanvantari, the physician, came to know of it. Since the creeper grew out from the tethering post of an elephant (Nāga), it will be called Nāgavallī (a creeper from an elephant’s post) or ‘betel’.

## \|\| 1.210.54 \|\|

*sadā smarasya saṃsthānaṃ mama vākyādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*nāgavallīti vai nāma tasyāścakre tataḥ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. It will be the place or abode of Smara (god of Love). Then he named it Nāgavallī.

## \|\| 1.210.55 \|\|

*saṃyogaṃ ca cakārātha tāṃbūlaṃ jāyate yathā \|*  
*pūgīphalena cūrṇena khadireṇāpi pārthiva \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He stipulated its combination with areca-nut, lime powder and Khadira (catechu). The combination shall be Tāṃbūla.

## \|\| 1.210.56 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya vāṇīvatsarako nṛpaḥ \|*  
*pratoṣaṃ nītavāñchakraṃ tapasā nirmalena ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Once upon a time, King Vāṇīvatsaraka propitiated Śakra by means of his pure penance.

## \|\| 1.210.57 \|\|

*tatastattapasā tuṣṭa indro vacanamabravīt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then Indra who was pleased with his penance spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.210.58 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*bhobhoḥ pārthiva tuṣṭo'smi tapasā'nena sāṃpratam \|*  
*brūhi yatte varaṃ dadmi manasā vāṃchitaṃ sadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

Indra said:

58\. O king, I am pleased with this penance now. Tell me what boon I shall give, the boon you have been always cherishing.

## \|\| 1.210.59 \|\|

*so'bravīdyadi me tuṣṭo yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*vimānaṃ khecaraṃ dehi yenāgacchāmi te gṛhe \|*  
*nityameva dharāpṛṣṭhādvaṃdanārthaṃ tava prabho \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He replied: “If you are pleased with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, give me an aerial chariot that can go through the firmament. Thereby, I can come to your abode from the surface of the earth everyday, dear Lord, in order to offer obeisance to you.”

## \|\| 1.210.60 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya haṃsabarhiṇanāditam \|*  
*vimānaṃ pradadau tasmai manomārutavegadhṛk \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He consented saying “So be it” and gave him a Vimāna (aerial chariot). It produced the sounds of swan and peacock and had the velocity of mind and wind.

## \|\| 1.210.61 \|\|

*sa tatra nityamāruhya prayāti tridaśālayam \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ sahasrākṣaṃ pravaṃditum \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Imbued with great devotion, he rode in it everyday and went to the abode of Devas in order to pay respect to the Thousand-eyed One.

## \|\| 1.210.62 \|\|

*tasya śakraḥ svahastena tāṃbūlaṃ ca prayacchati \|*  
*sa ca tadbhakṣayāmāsa prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Śakra gave him the Tāṃbūla (betel leaves together with the other items for chewing) with his own hand and he chewed it with highly delighted mind.

## \|\| 1.210.63 \|\|

*vṛddhabhāve'pi saṃprāpte tasya kāmo'tyavarddhata \|*  
*tāṃbūlasya prabhāvena sumahānpṛthivīpate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thanks to the power of the Tāṃbūla, O king, his lust increased despite his old age.

## \|\| 1.210.64-65 \|\|

*atha śakramuvācedaṃ sa rājā vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*nāgavallīpradānena prasādo me vidhīyatām \|\| 64 \|\|*

*martyaloke samānetuṃ pracāraṃ yena gacchati \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya tasmai tāṃ pradadau tadā \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Then, endowed with excessive humility, the king said this to Śakra; “May I be favoured with the offer of Nāgavallī. I intend to take it to the mortal world, so that it can be propagated.”

He consented saying “So be it” and gave that (leaf) to him.

## \|\| 1.210.66 \|\|

*gatvā nijapuraṃ sopi svodyāne'sthāpayattadā \|*  
*tataḥ kālena mahatā pracāraṃ sā gatā kṣitau \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. He went to his home town and planted it in his own garden. Then, in the course of a long time it became popular all over the earth.

## \|\| 1.210.67 \|\|

*yasyāḥ svādanato lokaḥ kāmātmā samapadyata \|*  
*na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre yājanaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*anyā dharmakriyāḥ sarvāḥ praṇaṣṭā dharmasaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. By tasting it all the people became sex-minded. No one performed Yajña himself nor on behalf of another. All other religious rites and holy activities came to a standstill.

## \|\| 1.210.68 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve yajñabhāgavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*pīḍyamānāḥ krudhā viṣṭā gatvā procuḥ pitāmaham \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Thereupon, all the groups of Devas were deprived of their share in the Yajñas. They became afflicted and therefore furious. They went to Pitāmaha and reported:

## \|\| 1.210.69 \|\|

*martyaloke suraśreṣṭha naṣṭā dharmakriyā bhṛśam \|*  
*kāmāsakto yato lokastāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ no yenāsmākaṃ kriyā bhavet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “In the mortal world, O most excellent one among Suras, all sacred rites have ceased because by chewing Tāmbùla, the people have become indulgent in love play. Hence do this favour unto us so that our rites can be revived.”

## \|\| 1.210.70-72 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu puṣkarasthaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*yajanārthe samāyātaṃ daridro vīkṣya pārthiva \|\| 70 \|\|*

*praṇipatya tataḥ prāha vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*nirviṇṇo'haṃ suraśreṣṭha brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhe sthitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tasmātkīrtaya me sthānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vittavatāṃ hi yat \|*  
*tatra sañjāyate tṛptiḥ śāśvatī pracurā prabho \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. In the meantime, O king, a poor man saw Pitāmaha who was stationed in Puṣkara, arriving for performing of Yajña. He bowed down to him humbly and said: “O most excellent one among Suras, I have become disgusted with this continuous stay in the abodes of Brāhmaṇas. Hence suggest to me an excellent abode of wealthy people. O Lord, I can attain satisfaction there in plenty.”

## \|\| 1.210.73 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*abravīcca daridraṃ taṃ chidrārthaṃ dhaninā miha \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. On hearing his words, Pitāmaha pondered for a long time and spoke to the poor man about vulnerable points found in wealthy people:

## \|\| 1.210.74-76 \|\|

*cūrṇapatre tvayā vāsaḥ sadā kāryo daridra bhoḥ \|*  
*tāṃbūlasya tu parṇāgre bhāryayā mama vākyataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*parṇānāṃ caiva vṛṃteṣu sarveṣu tvatsutena ca \|*  
*rātrau khadirasāre ca tvaṃ tābhyāṃ sarvadā vasa \|\| 75 \|\|*

*dhanināṃ chidrakṛtproktametatsthānacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*pārthivānāṃ viśeṣeṇa mama vākyā dvraja drutam \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. “O poor man, you shall permanently stay in broken leaves at my instance. Your wife shall stay at the tip of the leaf. Your son shall stay around the stalks of the leaves. At night you always stay along with both of them in the Khadirasāra. These four spots are said to be the vulnerable points of the wealthy people and more so in the case of kings. At my instance do hurry up and go there.”

## \|\| 1.210.77 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi narādhipa \|\| 77 \|\|*

Nārada said:

77\. Thus, O king, everything that I have been asked has been narrated to you.

## \|\| 1.210.78 \|\|

*tāṃbūlotthāni chidrāṇi yathā syurdhanināmiha \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi cīrṇāni tvayā rājannajānatā \|*  
*tena vai vibhavocchittiḥ saṃjātā sahasā nṛpa \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O king, you have unwittingly employed all these vulnerable points in the case of betel leaves. It was on account of that, that all your riches became ruined all of a sudden.

## \|\| 1.210.79 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tadarthamapi me brūhi prāyaścittaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*kadācidbhakṣaṇaṃ me syāttāṃbūlasya tathāvidham \|\| 79 \|\|*

The king said:

79\. O leading sage, tell me the expiatory rite for that also. It is probable that sometimes I might have chewed betel leaves in that manner.

## \|\| 1.210.80 \|\|

*yena sañjāyate śuddhiḥ kutāṃbūlasamudbhavā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. By that expiatory rite purity can be regained (dispelling the adverse) effect of evil betel leaf.

## \|\| 1.210.81 \|\|

*viśvā mitra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi prāyaścittaṃ tu yaccaret \|*  
*āśvāsanena śuddhyarthaṃ kutāṃbūlasya bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

81\. O king, listen, I shall explain to you the expiatory rite to be performed confidently for purifying the evil arising from eating a bad betel leaf.

## \|\| 1.210.82 \|\|

*parvakālaṃ samuddiśya samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*ānayedbrāhmaṇaṃ rājanvedavedāṃgapāragam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. With festival occasion in view (i.e. at that time), a person equipped with perfect faith should bring a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, O king.

## \|\| 1.210.83-84 \|\|

*prakṣālya caraṇau tasya vāsasī paridhāpayet \|*  
*saṃpūjya gaṃdhapuṣpādyaistataḥ patraṃ hiraṇmayam \|*  
*svaśaktyā kārayitvā'tha cūrṇe muktāphalaṃ nyaset \|\| 83 \|\|*

*pūgīphalaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ khadiraṃ rūpyameva ca \|*  
*mantreṇānena viprāya tathaiva ca samarpayet \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. His feet should be washed and he should be made to wear two cloths. After honouring him with sweet scents, flowers etc. he should get a betel leaf made of gold in accordance with his capacity. In the place of lime paste, a pearl should be used. A heap of lazuli stones shall represent the arecanut and a piece of silver catechu. The devotee then offers the same repeating the following Mantra:

## \|\| 1.210.85-86 \|\|

*yanmayā bhakṣitaṃ pūrvaṃ vṛntaṃ patrasamudbhavam \|*  
*cūrṇapatraṃ tathaivānyadrātrau khadirameva ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tasya pāpasya śuddhyarthaṃ tāṃbūlaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*tatastu brāhmaṇo maṃtramevaṃ rājannudāharet \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. “Since the stalk of a betel leaf, a broken leaf and other things have been chewed by me earlier and catechu at night too, I have incurred sin. By way of dispelling it and regaining purity again, let this Tāṃbūla be accepted.” Thereafter, the Brāhmaṇa should repeat this Mantra, O king:

## \|\| 1.210.87-88 \|\|

*yajamānahitārthāya sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|*  
*ajñānājjñānato vāpi kutāṃbūlaṃ prabhakṣitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*bhakṣayiṣyasi yaccānyatkadācinme prasādanāt \|*  
*tasya doṣo na te bhāvī mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. “(I utter this Mantra) for the benefit of the

householder (devotee) and for the purification of all sins. If the despised betel leaf is chewed knowingly or unknowingly, if he is likely to swallow anything (similar), let the defect thereof be warded off undoubtedly at my instance and thanks for propitiating me.”

## \|\| 1.210.89 \|\|

*anena vidhinā dattvā tāṃbūlaṃ śuddhimāpnuyāt \|*  
*kutāṃbūlasya doṣeṇa gṛhyate na naro nṛpa \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. By offering the betel leaf (made of gold) etc. in this manner, one shall regain purity. O king, no man suffers from the defect of chewing an evil betel leaf.

## \|\| 1.210.90 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ hi mahārāja vratametatsamācara \|*  
*bahu puṇyatamaṃ hyetanmahābhogavivarddhanam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Hence, O great king, perform this rite. Indeed this is highly meritorious and it increases great enjoyment of pleasures.

## \|\| 1.210.91 \|\|

*yaḥ prayacchati rājendra vidhinānena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*janmajanmāntare vāpi na tāṃbūlena mucyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. If a person, O leading king, makes this gift devoutly in this manner, he will never be defiled in any of his birth thereafter by the evil betel leaf.

## \|\| 1.210.92 \|\|

*tāṃbūlaṃ bhakṣayitvā yo naitaddānaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*tāṃbūlavarjitaḥ so'tra bhavejjanmanijanmani \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A person who chews (such a) betel but does not make this gift, shall be deprived of Tāṃbūla in all subsequent births.

## \|\| 1.210.93 \|\|

*tāṃbūlavarjitaṃ yasya mukhaṃ syātpṛthivīpate \|*  
*kṛpaṇasya daridrasya tadbilaṃ na hi tanmukham \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. If anyone’s mouth is deprived of betel leaf, O king, it is the cavity of an impoverished miser and not a real mouth.

## \|\| 1.210.94 \|\|

*tāṃbūlaṃ brāhmaṇendrāya yo dattvā prākprabhakṣayet \|*  
*surūpo bhāgyavāndakṣo bhavejjanmanijanmani \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. He who offers (expiatory Tāṃbūla) at the outset i.e. a betel leaf to a leading Brāhmaṇas and then chews it himself, shall become handsome, fortunate and efficient in every birth.

## \|\| 1.210.95-96 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ kutāṃbūlasya bhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*yatphalaṃ jāyate puṃsāṃ yaddānena mahīpate \|\| 95 \|\|*

*śaṃkhādityānuṣaṃgeṇa tāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇe \|*  
*ye doṣā ye guṇā rājandānaṃ caiva prabhakṣaṇe \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. Thus the adverse effect of chewing an evil betel leaf has been described to you entirely. O king, by the gift thereof (purity is regained). In the context of the description of Śaṅkhāditya the good and evil effects of chewing a betel leaf etc. and the benefit of its gift have been stated.

## Chapter 211 - Greatness of Śaṅkha Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.211.1 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*rājño dāridryadoṣasya kuṣṭhavyādheśca kāraṇam \|*  
*kathayitvā punaḥ prāha nārado munisattamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

1\. After describing the cause of (king’s) poverty as well as of the defect of the fell disease of leprosy of the king, Nārada, the excellent sage, spoke again:

## \|\| 1.211.2-10 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ rājankuṣṭhasya kāraṇam \|*  
*dāridryasya ca yatsamyagjñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi yathā tava parābhavaḥ \|*  
*śatrubhyaḥ saṃprajāto'tra dvijānāmapamānataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ānartādhipatiryo'tra kaścidrājye'bhiṣicyate \|*  
*sa pūrvaṃ gacchati grāmaṃ nāgarāṇāṃ prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tvayā tatkalpitaṃ rājannaiva dattaṃ pramādataḥ \|*  
*parābhūtā dvijāste ca yācamānā muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tathā kopavaśādyāni śāsanāni dvijanmanām \|*  
*lopitāni tvayānyāni pitṛpaitāmahāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tena te'tra parābhūtiḥ saṃjātā śatrusaṃbhavā \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā dvijedrāṇāṃ śāsa nāni prayaccha bhoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*gṛhītāni ca yānyeva teṣāṃ mokṣaṃ samācara \|*  
*tacchrutvā pārthivaḥ so'tha śaṃkhatīrthe prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*snātvā viprānsamā hūya madhyagena samanvitān \|*  
*śaṃkhādityasya purataḥ prakṣālya caraṇau nṛpa \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dadau ca śāsanaśataṃ prakṣālya caraṇāṃstataḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikaṃ rājā nāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 10 \|\|*

2-10. “It is after knowing it through divine vision thus, that the entire cause of leprosy as well as of poverty has been described to you.

Now I shall tell you how your discomfiture resulted from (the attack of your) enemies as a sequel to the insult done unto the Brāhmaṇas.

Any Lord of Ānarta who is to be crowned here as king, first goes devoutly to the village of Nāgaras. This was contemplated by you, O king, but due to inadvertence, it was not done. The Brāhmaṇas who requested (for it) repeatedly were turned back. Due to anger, the charter of benefits offered to the Brāhmaṇas from the days of their fathers and grandfathers was ignored by you.

Therefore, you are faced with failure and defeat at the hands of enemies. Having realized this, O king, grant those charters to the Brāhmaṇas by way of restoration. What was forfeited should be restored.”

On hearing it, the king had his holy bath devoutly performed in Śaṅkha Tīrtha. He summoned those Brāhmaṇas through a Madhyaga. In front of the deity. Śaṅkhāditya, the king washed their feet and gave the noble-souled Nāgaras one hundred twenty-six Śāsanas (charters of benefit or grants).

## \|\| 1.211.11 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra śatravo ye ca saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*sarve mṛtyuṃ samāpannā brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In the meantime, with the favour of the Brāhmaṇas, all the enemies who were present there met with their death.

## \|\| 1.211.12 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ śaṃkhatīrthasamudbhavam \|*  
*prabhāvaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

12\. Thus, O excellent one among kings, everything concerned with the power of Śaṅkha Tīrtha has been narrated to you. What more do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 212 - Greatness of Ratnāditya

## \|\| 1.212.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ tīrthatrayaṃ puṇyaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñite \|*  
*kṣetre'tra yattvayā proktamasmākaṃ sūtanaṃdana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viśvāmitrīyamāhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāmahe vayam \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ tatsamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. O Sūtanandana, the meritorious trio of Tīrtha in the holy place designated as Hāṭakeśvara that has been described by you, has been listened to.

We now wish to hear about the greatness of (the Tīrtha of) Viśvāmitra which do explain to us. We have great eagerness.

## \|\| 1.212.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*samudrasyāpi pāro'tra lakṣyate ca kṣiterapi \|*  
*tārakāṇāṃ munestasya na guṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. The other shore of the sea can be seen, the limit of the earth can be observed but that cannot be so, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in the case of the good qualities of that sage that redeem (people).

## \|\| 1.212.4 \|\|

*lakṣyate kenacitpāro gādheḥ putrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyo'pi dvijatvaṃ yaḥ saṃprāpto dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Can the capacity of the intelligent son of Gādhi be estimated by anyone? O excellent Brāhmaṇas, though born a Kṣatriya, he attained the status of Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.212.5 \|\|

*aṃtyajatvaṃ gatasyāpi triśaṃkoḥ pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*yajñabhāgabhujo devāḥ pratyakṣeṇa vinirmitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By him were directly created Devas who took their shares from the Yajña of King Triśaṅku transformed into an Antyaja (low-born) formerly.

## \|\| 1.212.6 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ spardhayā yena purā sṛṣṭirdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*prārabdhā ca tato devaiḥ praṇipatya nivāritaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Competing with god Brahmā, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, even (a new) creation was attempted by him formerly but he was requested to desist from it by the Devas who bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.212.7 \|\|

*tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ sāprataṃ vadato mama \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśa nam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Now I shall expound the greatness of the Tīrtha pertaining to him. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, it is destructive of all sins. May it be listened to.

## \|\| 1.212.8 \|\|

*tena tatra kṛtaṃ kuṇḍaṃ svahastena mahātmanā \|*  
*śastraṃ vināpi bhūpṛṣṭhaṃ pravidārya samaṃtataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Without using any implement (of digging) the ground all round was dug up with his own hands by that noble-souled sage and a holy pit was created there.

## \|\| 1.212.9 \|\|

*tatra dhyātvā samānītā pātālājjāhnavī nadī \|*  
*martyaloke samāyātaṃ yasyāstoyaṃ sunirmalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There he meditated and brought the river Jāhnavī from Pātāla. The pure translucent water thereof came to the mortal world.

## \|\| 1.212.10 \|\|

*susvādu ca tathā snānātsarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*tenāpi sthāpitastatra bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*
