10\. The water is very tasty. It is destructive of all sins through holy ablution. Bhāskara, (Sun-god) the thief of waters (i.e. one who dries up water), was also installed by him there.

## \|\| 1.212.11 \|\|

*yaḥ saptamyāṃ sūryavāre snātvā tasya hṛde śubhe \|*  
*māghamāse site pakṣe namasyati divākaram \|*  
*sa kuṣṭhairmucyate sarvaistathā pāpairdvijo ttamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he who takes his holy bath there in that auspicious whirlpool on the seventh lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha coinciding with Sunday and bows down to Divākara (Sun-god) is rid of leprous ailments and sins.

## \|\| 1.212.12 \|\|

*paścimottaradigbhāge tasyāsti jalasaṃbhavā \|*  
*dhanvaṃtarikṛtā vāpī sarvarogavināśinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. To the north-western side thereof there is a water-tank created by Dhanvantari. It destroys all ailments.

## \|\| 1.212.13 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ tapastepe dhanvaṃ tarirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*vavande tapasā yukto dhyāyamānaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The liberal-minded Dhanvantari performed a penance there formerly. Equipped with good power of a penance and meditating with concentration, he bowed down (to Lord Sun).

## \|\| 1.212.14 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā saṃtuṣṭastasya bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasva mahāmate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After a long time, Bhāskara was pleased with him and said to him: “I shall grant a boon, O highly intelligent one. Request for the same.”

## \|\| 1.212.15 \|\|

*dhanvaṃtariruvāca \|*  
*atra kuṇḍe naro bhaktyā yaḥ snānaṃ kurute vibho \|*  
*tasya syātsarvarogāṇāṃ saṃkṣayaḥ surasattama \|\| 15 \|\|*

Dhanvantari said:

15\. O Lord, O most excellent one among Suras! If any man takes his holy bath here in the Kuṇḍa with great devotion, let every ailment in him be dispelled.

## \|\| 1.212.16-17 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adya śaste dine yo'tra saptamyāṃ ravivāsare \|*  
*sūryodaye naraḥ snānaṃ kariṣyati samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vyādhigrastaḥ sa nīrogastatkṣaṇātsaṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nīrogaścepsitānkāmānniṣkāmo mokṣameṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

16-17. He who takes his holy bath there on this praiseworthy day, the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday, early in the morning at sunrise, with great concentration, shall at that very instant be free from ailments even though (he be) afflicted will great diseases. One without ailment will obtain all desires and one without desires will attain salvation (Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.212.18 \|\|

*evamuktvā suraśre ṣṭhoṃ'tardhānaṃ sa gato raviḥ \|*  
*dhanvantariḥ prahṛṣṭātmā svasthānaṃ ca gatastataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After saying thus Ravi, the most excellent one among Suras, vanished. Dhanvantari too went back to his abode well pleased within himself.

## \|\| 1.212.19 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya ratnākṣo'tha mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*ayodhyādhi patiḥ khyātaḥ sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Once upon a time, there was a king named Ratnākṣa hailing from the Solar race. He was the well-known Lord of Ayodhyā.

## \|\| 1.212.20 \|\|

*kṛtajñaśca vadānyaśca svadāranirataḥ sadā \|*  
*śūraḥ paramatejasvī sarvaśatruniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He possessed the qualities of gratitude and munificence. He was always faithful to his wife. He was resplendent and heroic. He destroyed all enemies.

## \|\| 1.212.21 \|\|

*pūrvakarmavipākena tasya bhūmipaterdvijāḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhirabhūdraudro duścikitsyo jagattraye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Brāhmaṇas, as a result of his action in previous life that king became a victim of the terrible fell disease of leprosy very difficult to be cured the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.212.22 \|\|

*tadasti nauṣadhaṃ loke yattena na kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhagrastena vā dānaṃ yatra dattaṃ mahātmanā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There is no medicine in the world which he did not try, O Brāhmaṇas. There is no gift which the noble-souled king afflicted with leprosy, did not make.

## \|\| 1.212.23 \|\|

*yathāyathauṣadhānyeva sa karoti dadāti ca \|*  
*tathātathā tasya kāyo vyādhinā kṣāmito bhṛśam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The longer he continued to apply medicine and make over gifts, the more afflicted he became due to the disease and turned feeble.

## \|\| 1.212.24 \|\|

*tato vairāgyamāpannaḥ sa nṛpo dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*putraṃ rājye'tha saṃsthāpya vāṃchayāmāsa pāvakam \|*  
*niṣiddho'pi hi taiḥ sarvaiḥ kalatrairāptasevakaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the king became disgusted. He desired to immolate himself in fire, entrusting the kingdom to his son though his wife and loyal attendants prevented him.

## \|\| 1.212.25 \|\|

*dattvā dānāni viprebhyaḥ pūjayitvā surottamān \|*  
*saṃbhāṣya ca suhṛdvargaṃ śāsayitvā nijaṃ sutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He made ample religious gifts to Brāhmaṇas and worshipped gods. He held (final) conversations with his group of friends. He instructed his son (the prince). After this he became ready to enter fire.

## \|\| 1.212.26 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu bhramamāṇe yadṛcchayā \|*  
*kaścitkārpaṭikaḥ prāpto divyarūpavapurdharaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the meantime, a certain pilgrim endowed with divine form and features came there by chance during the course of his wandering.

## \|\| 1.212.27 \|\|

*athāsau vyākulaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatsarvaṃ nṛpateḥ puram \|*  
*apṛcchadvismayāviṣṭo dṛṣṭvā kañcinnaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He found the entire city distressed and morose. O Brāhmaṇas, he became surprised and enquired from a certain person seen by him.

## \|\| 1.212.28 \|\|

*kārpaṭika uvāca \|*  
*kimeṣā vyākulā bhadre sarvā jātā mahāpurī \|*  
*nirānandā'śrupūrṇākṣairbālavṛddhairniṣevitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

Kārpaṭika (the pilgrim) said:

28\. O fair Sir, how is it that the entire city has become upset and gloomy and cheerless? The children and the old people that live here have eyes filled with tears?

The man replied:

## \|\| 1.212.29 \|\|

*so'bravīnnṛpatiścāyaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sādhayiṣyati sandīptaṃ sunirviṇṇo hutāśanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The king hereof is affected by the fell disease of leprosy. He is disgusted with life and wants to immolate himself in fire.

## \|\| 1.212.30 \|\|

*teneyaṃ nagarī kṛtsnā paraṃ duḥkhamupāgatā \|*  
*guṇairasya samāviṣṭā nūnaṃ mṛtyuṃ prayāsyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Therefore, the entire city is extremely distressed. Certainly all will meet with their death because they are so overwhelmed by his good qualities.

## \|\| 1.212.31 \|\|

*tacchrutvā satvaraṃ gatvā nṛpaṃ kārpaṭiko'bravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On hearing these words the pilgrim hastened to the king and said:

## \|\| 1.212.32-35 \|\|

*sarvaṃ janaṃ narendrasya mṛtaṃ jīvāpayanniva \|*  
*mā nṛpānena duḥkhena vyādhijena hutāśanam \|*  
*praviśa tvaṃ sthite tīrthe sarvavyādhikṣayāvahe \|\| 32 \|\|*

*madīyo bhūpate deha īdṛgāsīdyathā tava \|*  
*tatra snātasya sadyo'tha jāta īdṛkpunaḥ prabho \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|*  
*yastatra kurute snānaṃ vyādhigrasto naro bhuvi \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sa vyādhinā vini rmuktastatkṣaṇātkalpatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*tathā pāpavinirmukto yathāhaṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. It appeared as though he would resuscitate all the people of the king. “O king, do not enter fire due to this grief arising from your disease when a Tīrtha capable of dispelling all ailments is available.

O king, my body too was like this as in your case. When I took the holy bath there immediately it became like this, as it is now, O Lord.

A man of the earth who is afflicted with an ailment and who takes his holy bath there at sunrise when Sunday coincides with the seventh lunar day shall instantly be relieved of it. He shall become hale and hearty, O excellent king, and also rid of sins like me.”

## \|\| 1.212.36 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kasmindeśe mahātīrthaṃ tādṛśaṃ vada me drutam \|\| 36 \|\|*

The king said:

36\. Tell me quickly in which country is such a great Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.212.37 \|\|

*kārpaṭikauvāca \|*  
*asti bhūmitale khyātaṃ nāgaraṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhisamākrāṃto gato'haṃ tatra bhūpate \|\| 37 \|\|*

Kārpaṭika said:

37\. There is the excellent holy place of Nāgaras well-known all over the earth, O king, When I was afflicted with the fell disease of leprosy I went there.

## \|\| 1.212.38 \|\|

*tasya sandarśanārthāya tīrthayātrāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra māṃ dīnamālokya vyādhigrastaṃ suduḥkhitam \|*  
*kaścittatrāśrayaḥ prāha tapasvī kṛpayānvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the course of the pilgrimage in which I was engaged, I went there to visit it. On seeing me grief-stricken and wretched, because I was afflicted with the disease a compassionate sage, an inhabitant of that place told me:

## \|\| 1.212.39-41 \|\|

*paścimottaradigbhāge devasya jalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*tīrthamasti mahāpuṇyaṃ viśvāmitrajalāvaham \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā kuru snānaṃ saptamyāṃ ravivāsare \|*  
*māghamāse tu saṃprāpte śuklapakṣe viśeṣataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yena niryāti te kuṣṭho bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|*  
*tacchrutvā'haṃ ca tatprāptaḥ saptamyāṃ sūryasaṃyuji \|*  
*tataśca kṛtavānsnānaṃ nirjhare tatra śāṃbhave \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41a. “To the north-western side of Lord Jalaśāyin (i.e. Lord Viṣṇu sleeping in the ocean) is the highly meritorious Tīrtha containing Viśvāmitra Jala (The sacred water brought from Pātāla by Viśvāmitra). Go there and take your holy bath on the day when the seventh lunar day coincides with a Sunday in the bright half of the month of Māgha. Thereby your leprosy will vanish at the time of sunrise.”

41bc. On hearing those words, I reached the place on the seventh lunar day in conjunction with the Sun (i.e. Sunday). Then I took the holy bath in the Śāṃbhava stream.

## \|\| 1.212.42 \|\|

*tatastasmādviniṣkrāṃto yāvatpaśyāmyahaṃ tanum \|*  
*tāvannṛpedṛśī jātā satyametattavoditam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then I came out from that (Tīrtha) and when I surveyed my body, O king, it had become like this. It is the truth that is said to you.

## \|\| 1.212.43 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi rājeṃdra tatra snānaṃ samācara \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hence, O leading king, you too take your holy bath on the Saptamī (seventh lunar) day, the day of the week being Sunday at the time of sunrise.

## \|\| 1.212.44 \|\|

*yena te naśyati vyādhirviśeṣamapi pātakam \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa nṛpastūrṇaṃ tenaiva sahito yayau \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereby, your illness and the sin as well will perish.

On hearing it, the king hastened in the company of that (Kārpaṭika).

## \|\| 1.212.45 \|\|

*cakāra sa tathā snānaṃ saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare \|*  
*māghamāse tu saṃprāpte viśvāmitrajale śubhe \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On the Saptamī day, in the month of Māgha coinciding with a Sunday, he took the holy bath in the auspicious water of Viśvāmitra Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.212.46 \|\|

*tataḥ kuṣṭhavinirmuktastatkṣaṇātsamapadyata \|*  
*divyarūpavapurddhārī kāmadeva ivāparaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereby, he instantly became rid of leprosy. Assuming a diving form, he appeared like another Kāmadeva.

## \|\| 1.212.47 \|\|

*atha tuṣṭo nareṃdrastu tasmai kārpaṭikāya ca \|*  
*dadau koṭitrayaṃ hemnaḥ provāca sa tato vacaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then the leading king who was satisfied gave thirty million gold pieces to the Kārpaṭika and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.212.48-49 \|\|

*tvatprasādādvimukto'smi rogādasmātsudāruṇāt \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha gehaṃ svaṃ sthāsye'haṃ cātra nirbharam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kariṣyāmi tapo nityaṃ svakalatrasama nvitaḥ \|*  
*rājye saṃsthāpitaḥ putraḥ samartho rājyakarmaṇi \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. “It is with your favour that I have been rid of this terrible ailment. Hence you do go home. I will stay here full in contentment.

I shall scrupulously perform the penance everyday in the company of my wife. My son has been enthroned in the kingdom. He is capable of administrating the realm.”

## \|\| 1.212.50 \|\|

*ityuktvā prerayāmāsa taṃ tathānyānsamāgatān \|*  
*sevakāsvagṛhāyaiva svayaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After saying this, he persuaded him (the pilgrim) and all others who had accompanied him and also his attendants to return home. He himself settled there.

## \|\| 1.212.51 \|\|

*kṛtvā'śramapadaṃ ramyaṃ svakalatrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaśca parāṃ siddhiṃ kālena dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He set up his own beautiful hermitage there and stayed there along with his wife. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in the course of time he attained Siddhi (spiritual perfection).

## \|\| 1.212.52 \|\|

*tasya nāmnā tataḥ khyātaṃ tīrtha metattriviṣṭape \|*  
*sarvavyādhiharaṃ ramyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Ever since then this Tīrtha has become well-known after his name in heaven. It dispels all sickness. It is charming and destructive of all sins,

## \|\| 1.212.53 \|\|

*tena saṃsthāpitastatra devadevo divākaraḥ \|*  
*ratnāditya iti khyāto nijanāmnā mahā tmanā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Divākara (Sun-god), the Lord of Devas, was installed by him there well-known after his noble name as Ratnāditya.

## \|\| 1.212.54 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa tatra snātvā prapaśyati \|*  
*yastu pāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He who takes his holy bath there and visits the deity on the Saptamī day in conjunction with a Sunday shall be relieved of sins and go to the world of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.212.55 \|\|

*yadanyattatra saṃvṛttaṃ kṣetrajātaṃ dvijo ttamāḥ \|*  
*tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, listen with concentration. I shall relate what other incident happened in that holy place.

## \|\| 1.212.56 \|\|

*āsīttatra pumānkaściddeśe grāmyo jarātmakaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhī tathāpi nityaṃ sa karoti paśu rakṣaṇam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There was an aged villager in that land. He was a leper. But he always looked after cows.

## \|\| 1.212.57 \|\|

*ekadā rakṣatastasya paśūṃstatra gireradhaḥ \|*  
*ekaḥ paśurviniṣkrāṃtaḥ satpathāttṛṇalobhataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Once, while he was looking after the beasts (cows) below the mountain, one of his cows strayed from the right track due to its greed for grass.

## \|\| 1.212.58 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ ravivāreṇa patitastasya nirjhare \|*  
*na ca saṃlakṣitastena gacchamānaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On a Sunday in conjunction with Saptamī the cow fell into the stream there. Going ahead thus somehow she was not noticed by him (the cowherd).

## \|\| 1.212.59 \|\|

*atha yāvadgṛhe so'tha bhojanāthaṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*tāvattasya paśoḥ svāmī bhartsayansamupāgataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At home he was getting ready to take his meal, when the owner of the cow came there and rebuked him:

## \|\| 1.212.60 \|\|

*nāyātaḥ sa paśuḥ kasmānmadīyo māmake gṛhe \|*  
*tasmādānaya taṃ śīghraṃ no cetprāṇānharāmi te \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. “How is it that my cow has not come back to ṃy house? So fetch it soon. If not, I will take away your life.”

## \|\| 1.212.61 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhaya saṃtrastaḥ sa kuṣṭhī satvaraṃ yayau \|*  
*tena mārgeṇa yenaiva divā bhrāṃto mahītale \|\| 61 \|\|*

Sūta said:

61\. On hearing it, the leper was terrified. He quickly went along the path whereby he had traversed the ground by day.

## \|\| 1.212.62 \|\|

*atha dūrātsa śuśrāva tasya rāvaṃ paśostadā \|*  
*patitasya mahāgarte niśāṃte tamasi sthite \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. During the night when darkness had enveloped everything he heard from a distance the cry of that cow that had fallen into the great pit.

## \|\| 1.212.63 \|\|

*tato gatvā'tha taṃ gartaṃ praviśya jalamadhyataḥ \|*  
*cakarṣa taṃ paśuṃ kṛcchrātpaṃkamadhyātsudāruṇāt \|*  
*samādāyātha taṃ harmyaṃ prajagāma śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He went there and got into the water within the pit. With great difficulty he drew up the cow from the horrible muddy expanse. He took her with him and went home slowly.

## \|\| 1.212.64 \|\|

*arpayitvātha taṃ tasya svakīyaṃ tvāśramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He gave the cow to the owner and went to his own abode.

## \|\| 1.212.65 \|\|

*tataḥ supto mahābhāgāḥ sa prabuddhaḥ punaryadā \|*  
*prabhāte vīkṣate gātraṃ yāvatkuṣṭhavivarjitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then he slept, O highly esteemed one. In the morning when he woke up, he found his body rid of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.212.66-67 \|\|

*śobhayā parayā yuktaṃ vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa kiṃ hyetadakasmādrogasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*nūnaṃ tasya prabhāvo'yaṃ tīrthasyādya niśāgame \|*  
*mayāvagāhitaṃ yacca paśorarthaṃ sukarddamam \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. It was highly refulgent. With his eyes beaming with wonder he began to think, ‘What is this? The sickness is dispelled! Certainly, this is the power of that Tīrtha full of mud where I fell during the night for redeeming the cow.’

## \|\| 1.212.68 \|\|

*tataśca vīkṣayāmāsa tena gatvā sukautukāt \|*  
*yāvatkaṃḍūvinirmuktastejasā parivāritaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He surveyed the body with curiosity. He found that he was rid of all itching sensations and found himself enveloped in refulgence.

## \|\| 1.212.69 \|\|

*tatra sthāne svayaṃ gatvā jñātvā ca tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tapastepe sa tatraiva dhyāyamāno divākaram \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He went to that holy spot again and realized that it was an excellent Tīrtha. He then meditated upon Divākara and performed a penance there.

## \|\| 1.212.70 \|\|

*araṇyavāsinaṃ samyagdivārātramataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*gataśca paramāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Alert and active throughout day and night he continued the penance of the deity stationed in the forest. He attained the greatest Siddhi very difficult even for Devas to attain.

## \|\| 1.212.71 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Hence, one should exert himself to perform the rite of ablution there.

## \|\| 1.212.72 \|\|

*pūjayeccāpi taṃ devaṃ bhāskaraṃ vāritaskaram \|*  
*adyāpi kalikāle'pi tatra snāto naraḥ śuciḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One should also adore Lord Bhāskara, the thief of water. Even today in Kali Age, a man who bathes there becomes pure and clean.

## \|\| 1.212.73 \|\|

*tatra puṇyajale kuṇḍe saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā so'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He should take his bath in the Kuṇḍa of meritorious waters on Sunday coinciding with the seventh lunar day. He who devoutly worships becomes rid of the sins.

## \|\| 1.212.74 \|\|

*gāyatryaṣṭasahasraṃ yo japettatpurataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*so'pi rogavinirmukto mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He who recites the Gāyatrī Mantra one thousand eight times before the deity, shall be rid of ailments and all the sins.

## \|\| 1.212.75 \|\|

*tasyoddeśena yo dadyāddhenuṃ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*na tasyānvayajāto'pi vyādhinā parigṛhyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. With the deity in view a devotee with perfect faith should make the gift of a cow. No one born of his family will be afflicted with the disease.

## \|\| 1.212.76 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ mayādityasya saṃbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ śravaṇādyasya naraḥ pāpādvimucyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus everything pertaining to Sun-god and his greatness has been narrated by me. By listening to this a man is rid of sins.

## Chapter 213 - Efficacy of Kuhara-vāsi-Sāṃbāditya

## \|\| 1.213.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ratnādityasya māhātmyametadvaḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*sarvakuṣṭhaharaṃ yacca sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*bhūyastathaiva māhātmyaṃ mahadvai śrūyatāṃ raveḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*purāsīdbrāhmaṇaḥ kaścitkuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ \|*  
*tena cārādhitaḥ sūryastatrasthena dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvadakṣiṇadigbhāge samāsādya tataḥ param \|*  
*rakta candanajāṃ kṛtvā pratimāṃ bhāvitātmanā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte tuṣṭastasya divākaraḥ \|*  
*varado'smīti taṃ prāha dṛṣṭigocaramāgataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. This greatness of Ratnāditya has been spoken to you all. It is destructive of all leprous ailments and all sins. Let a further instance of the greatness of Ravi be listened to.

Formerly there was a certain Brāhmaṇa afflicted with the disease of leprosy. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, staying there he propitiated the Sun-god.

He came to the south-eastern side and made an icon (idol) of the Sun of red sandalwood with the mind sanctified.

Then at the end of a thousand years Divākara was pleased with him. Appearing before him, he said, “I shall grant a boon to you.”

## \|\| 1.213.5 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva kuṣṭhavyādhiṃ hara prabho \|*  
*nānyena kāraṇaṃ me'sti rājyenāpi triviṣṭape \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

5\. O Lord, if you are pleased, cure the sickness due to leprosy. I have no other purpose, not even of the kingdom of heaven.

## \|\| 1.213.6 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa kuru vipra pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*śatamaṣṭottaraṃ yāvatsnātvā puṇyahrade śubhe \|*  
*phalahastaḥ pṛthaktvena tataḥ kuṣṭhena mucyase \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

6\. On the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday take your holy bath in the splendid and auspicious whirlpool, O Brāhmaṇa, and make one hundred eight circumambulations with fruits held in your hand. Then you will be rid of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.213.7 \|\|

*anyo'tra gāṃ gato yo'pi vratametatkariṣyati \|*  
*sarvarogavinirmukto mama lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Any other man of the earth who performs this Vrata shall be rid of all ailments and will attain my world.

## \|\| 1.213.8 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa tathā cakre brāhmaṇaḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*vimuktaśca tadā kuṣṭhāddivyadehamavāptavān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. \[Śrī Sūrya Uvāca.\] On hearing it the Brāhmaṇa did so with perfect faith. He became rid of leprosy and attained a divine physical form.

## \|\| 1.213.9 \|\|

*atha bhūyo'pi taṃ prāha nīrogaṃ bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*kiṃ te priyaṃ karomyanyadvada brāhmaṇasattama \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lord Ravi (Sun) said again to him when he was rid of the ailments: “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, what other thing pleasing to you shall I carry out?”

## \|\| 1.213.10 \|\|

*so'bravītsarvadaivātra sthātavyaṃ bhagavanvibho \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He said, “O Lord, you always stay here (permanently).”

## \|\| 1.213.11 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ mamāvāsaḥ sthāne'tra ca bhaviṣyati \|*  
*nāmnā kuharavāsākhyā saṃjñā mama bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

11\. Henceforth my stay will be in this holy place by the name Kuharavāsa. That will be my designation.

## \|\| 1.213.12 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya viṣṇuputro babhūva ha \|*  
*sāṃbonāma surūpāḍhyo jāṃbavatyāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Once upon a time, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there was a son of Viṣṇu (i.e. Śrī Kṛṣṇa) named Sāmba born of Jāṃbavatī. He was richly endowned with handsomeness,

## \|\| 1.213.13-14 \|\|

*kṣobhasaṃjananaḥ strīṇāṃ mātṝṇāmapi sa dvijāḥ \|*  
*atha taṃ rājamārgeṇa gacchaṃtaṃ yadusattamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*puranāryo'pi saṃtuṣṭā vīkṣāṃcakruḥ sukautukāt \|*  
*gṛhakāryāṇi saṃtyajya samārūḍhā gavākṣakān \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. He caused excitement among all women, even mothers, O Brāhmaṇas. When the excellent scion of the family of Yadus went along the highway the women of the city used to look at him with great delight and eagerness. They used to set aside all their domestic chores and come to the windows.

## \|\| 1.213.15-18 \|\|

*tasya kāmātmadehasya darśanārthaṃ samutsukāḥ \|*  
*kāścidardhānuliptāṃgyaḥ kāścidekāṃjitekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ardhasaṃyamitaiḥ keśaistathānyāstyaktabālakāḥ \|*  
*ekasmiṃścaraṇe kāścinniyojyopānahaṃ drutāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pādukāṃ ca dvitīye tu paryadhāvannitaṃbinīḥ \|*  
*vrajaṃtīṣu tathānyāsu vanitāsu gavākṣakān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vyākrośaṃti krudhāviṣṭāḥ śiśavo guravastathā \|*  
*nīvībandhanaviśleṣasamākulitacetasaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. They were extremely interested in looking at him whose body was similar to that of Kāma. Some of them might have smeared the unguents only partially over their bodies. Some had applied collyrium only to one of the eyes. Others had tied their tresses of hairs very loose (partially). Still others had abandoned their children. Some rushed (to the windows) having woven a shoe on one foot and a sandal on the second. The beautiful women thus ran about. In the case of some other women who rushed to the windows, children and elders getting furious began to shout at them. Their minds were agitated as the knots of their clothes became loose.

## \|\| 1.213.19-21 \|\|

*yayurevāparāḥ sveṣu gavākṣeṣu varāṃganāḥ \|*  
*sa cakarṣa tadā tāsāṃ patitairnetraraśmibhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hṛdayāni dharāpṛṣṭhe kāmadevasamo yuvā \|*  
*kāciddṛṣṭvaiva tadrūpaṃ tasya sāṃbasya kāminī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*niścalā kāmataptāṃgī likhiteva vibhābyate \|*  
*kācidagnisamānmuktvā niśvāsānkāmapīḍitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Still those excellent ladies rushed towards the windows. With the rays from his eyes falling on them he pulled their hearts to the ground as it were. He was such a young man on a par with Lord Kāma.

On seeing the beautifull form of Sāṃba, a certain beautiful woman felt her limbs scorched with (the fever of) love. She stood motionless (looking at him) as if she was painted in a picture.

## \|\| 1.213.22 \|\|

*ekāstaṃ ca samālokya rūpayauvanasaṃyutam \|*  
*gavākṣātprapataṃti sma niśceṣṭā dharaṇītale \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After seeing him richly endowed with handsome features and youthful form some fell down from the windows (of the upper storey) and lay unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 1.213.23 \|\|

*anyāḥ parasparālāpa prakurvaṃti varastriyaḥ \|*  
*ekā sā kāminī dhanyā yāsya cakrevagūhanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Other excellent women said to one another, “Only that woman is blessed who has embraced him.”

## \|\| 1.213.24-26 \|\|

*niḥśeṣāṃ rajanīṃ prāpya māghamāsasamudbhavām \|*  
*āstāṃ tāvatstriyo yāśca narā api nirargalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jalpaṃti cedṛśaṃ sarvaṃ tasya rūpeṇa vismitāḥ \|*  
*atraye vadanti sevāma enamarthena varjitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vīkṣyāmo vadanaṃ yena nityameveṃdusaṃnibham \|*  
*karṇābhyāṃ vāritā vṛddhirnetrayorapyasaṃśayam \|*  
*no cejjānīmahe naiva kiyatī saṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Throughout the nights in the month of Māgha not only women but even men sat down incessantly talking unrestrictedly such things. They were all surprised at his handsomeness. Others said: “We will (gladly) serve him without any remuneration. Thereby, we can always see his Moon-like face. The elongation of his eyes is undoubtedly restricted by his ears. Otherwise we cannot even imagine how large they would be.”

## \|\| 1.213.27 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvīkṣyamāṇastu kāminībhirnaraistathā \|*  
*niryayau rājamārgeṇa pitṛdarśanalālasaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Viewed at like this by women and men, he passed through the main street as he was very eager to meet his father.

## \|\| 1.213.28 \|\|

*bhaginyo mātaro yāśca bhrātṛpatnyaśca yāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*avasthāmīdṛśīṃ prāptā brāhmaṇānāmapi striyaḥ \|*  
*mātaro'pi ca yāstasya bhaginyaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His sisters, mothers, brother’s wives—all these and even the ladies of Brāhmaṇa household, came to (attained) such a plight, even his mother’s and sisters especially.

## \|\| 1.213.29 \|\|

*anyasminnahani prāpte prāvṛṭkāle niśāgame \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe tamobhūte alakṣye'pi gate puraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It was on another day in the rainy season (that this happened) at nightfall. The fortnight was the dark one fully enveloped in darkness. Even what was in front of one could not be seen distinctly.

## \|\| 1.213.30 \|\|

*tanmātā nandinīnāma kāmadevaśarārditā \|*  
*tatpatnyā veṣamādhāya tacchayyāyāmupasthitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. His (step) mother named Nandinī was extremely afflicted by the arrows of Kāmadeva. She assumed the guise of his wife and lay on his couch.

## \|\| 1.213.31 \|\|

*so'pi tāṃ dayitāṃ jñātvā sevayāmāsa kāminīm \|*  
*ratopacārairvividhairaśraddheyavinirmitaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sāṃba thought that it was his own beloved and enjoyed the lady thoroughly with diverse kinds of sexual dalliances effectively carried on with unbelievable eagerness.

## \|\| 1.213.32-33 \|\|

*tayā tatra yaduśreṣṭho vikalpamakarottadā \|*  
*aṃgarājasutā yā me prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 32 \|\|*

*naivaṃvidhaṃ rataṃ veda anayā yadvinirmitam \|*  
*veśyā api na jānaṃti ratamīdṛkkathañcana \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The excellent scion of the Yadu family (Sāṃba) began to ponder thus, ‘The daughter of the king of Aṅga is dearer to me than even my vital breath. She too is not capable of such coitus as has been displayed by this lady. Even courtesans do not know such methods at all.’

## \|\| 1.213.34 \|\|

*tato gāḍhaṃ kare dhṛtvā dīpamānīya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yāvatpaśyati sā mātā nandinīti ca yā smṛtā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then he held in hand firmly and brought a lamp instantly and beheld. Oh, it was his mother who was remembered (by the name) Nandini \[Nandinī?\].

## \|\| 1.213.35 \|\|

*tataśca garhayāmāsa rape kimidaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*garhitaṃ sarvalokānāṃ nara kārtipradaṃ tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he censured her: “Fie upon you, O sinful woman! What is this that has been committed by you? It is despised by all the people. It is conducive only to distress in hell.”

## \|\| 1.213.36 \|\|

*sāpi lajjāsamopetā mahābhayasamākulā \|*  
*praṇaṣṭā tatkṣaṇādeva bhayena mahatā'nvinā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She was overcome with shame and agitated through fear. She disappeared (in darkness) in a moment in the height of her fear.

## \|\| 1.213.37 \|\|

*sāṃbo'pi pralapannārto nidrāṃ lebhe na vai dvijāḥ \|*  
*rātriśeṣamabhūttasya tadā varṣaśatopamam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Sāṃba lamented in distress. He could not sleep at all. The rest of the night appeared like a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.213.38 \|\|

*atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prodgate ravimaṇḍale \|*  
*duḥkhena mahatā yuktaḥ protthitaḥ sa hareḥ sutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When the night passed off and the solar disc came up, the son of Hari got up with great grief still harassing him.

## \|\| 1.213.39 \|\|

*āvaśyakamapi tyaktvā kaṃcidbrāhmaṇasattamam \|*  
*dharmaśāstravidhānajñaṃ samānīyātha cābravīt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He eschewed all essential routine activities and summoned an excellent Brāhmaṇa conversant with the injunctions of the scriptural texts. He then said to him:

## \|\| 1.213.40-41 \|\|

*rahasye vinayopetaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sāṃba uvāca \|*  
*mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā svayaṃ syādyadi mohanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kathaṃ śuddhirbhavettasya paramārthena me vada \|*  
*dharmaśāstrāṇi saṃvīkṣya sarvāṇi ca yathākramam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. He spoke to him secretly with great humility with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.213.42 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*paranāryāḥ kṛte vatsa prāyaścittaṃ vinirmitam \|*  
*dharma droṇeṣu sarveṣu varṇānāṃ ca pṛthagvidham \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sāṃba said:

If one indulges in sexual intercourse with one’s mother, sister or daughter, how can one regain purity? Tell me the complete truth after poring over all the scriptural texts in due order.

The Brāhmaṇa said:

42\. O dear one, expiatory rite has been laid down in all the scriptural texts, the repositories of Dharma. They are of diverse kinds in the case of (contact) with another woman.

## \|\| 1.213.43 \|\|

*āsāṃ ca tisṛṇāṃ caiva trayāṇāṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*evamevaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśudaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Expiatory rites have been proclaimed in the case of these three women and the three men involved for the sake of purity.

## \|\| 1.213.44 \|\|

*mātrā mohanamāsādya bhaginyā vātha yādava \|*  
*duhitrā vā pramādācca kāryaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ budhaiḥ \|*  
*śuddhyarthaṃ tiṃginīmekāṃ nānyajjānāmyahaṃ yataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O scion of the family of Yadu, after indulging in sexual union with one’s mother, sister or daughter inadvertently, sensible persons should perform purificatory rites.

For the sake of purity one Tiṅginī rite (see vv 48-53) should be performed. I do not know anything else.

## \|\| 1.213.45 \|\|

*dharmadroṇeṣu sarveṣu nirṇayo'yamudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*yo mayā tava saṃdiṣṭo nānyosti yadupuṃgava \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In all the scriptural texts this decision has been cited, which I have proclaimed. O leading Yādava, nothing else.

## \|\| 1.213.46 \|\|

*anyathā yo vadetpṛṣṭaḥ prāyāścittaṃ svacchanda taḥ \|*  
*tasya pāpasya bhāgī syādyathā kartā tathaiva saḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On being asked, if anyone mentions any other expiatory rite as he pleases, he shall incur sin like that of the perpetrator himself.

## \|\| 1.213.47 \|\|

*sāṃba uvāca \|*  
*tiṃginyāḥ kiṃ svarūpaṃ ca kiṃ pramāṇaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi mamāstyatra prayojanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sāṃba said:

47\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, tell me the nature and details of this Tiṅginī rite in full. I have an interest therein.

## \|\| 1.213.48 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*govāṭacūrṇamādāya gartāṃ bhṛtvā svamānajām \|*  
*śayanaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ yāvadvaktreṇa yādava \|\| 48 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

48\. O Yādava (descendant of Yadu), one should fill a deep pit of one’s own size with cowḍung powder upto one:s own face and stand therein.

## \|\| 1.213.49 \|\|

*upariṣṭāttacca cūrṇaṃ dhāryaṃ govāṭasaṃbhavam \|*  
*yāvadvaktrapramāṇaṃ ca varjayitvā svamānanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The cowdung particles are to be strewn, above the head too avoiding the face.

## \|\| 1.213.50 \|\|

*tataḥ pādapradeśe tu jvālayeddhavyavāhanam \|*  
*yathā śanaiḥ śanairdāhaḥ śarīrasya prajāyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thereafter, it should be set on fire at the region of the foot (of the person undergoing expiation) and the fire should burn slowly.

## \|\| 1.213.51 \|\|

*na caiva cālayedaṃgaṃ kathaṃcittatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*naivākraṃdaṃ tathā kuryāddhyāyedekaṃ janārdanam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The person standing there should not move his limbs at all. Nor should be cry aloud. He must meditate on Janārdana.

## \|\| 1.213.52 \|\|

*tato jīvitanāśena gātraśuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When the life becomes extinct, the body is purified.

## \|\| 1.213.53 \|\|

*tiṃginyā yatsvarūpaṃ ca tanmayā parikīrtitam \|*  
*prāyaścittamidaṃ samyaṅmahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The nature of Tiṅginī has been explained by me. A due performance of this expiatory rite is destructive of great sins.

## \|\| 1.213.54 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya sāṃbo jāṃbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye niścayaṃ kṛtvā tiṃginīsādhakodbhavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On hearing his words, Sāṃba, the son of Jāmbavatī, resolved in his mind that he would perform the expiatory rite of Tiṅginī.

## \|\| 1.213.55-61 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca vijane vāsudevaṃ ghṛṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*tātāhaṃ vipralabdhastu naṃdinyā tava bhāryayā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhāryāyā rūpamādhāya pāpayā tamasi sthite \|*  
*sā mayā nijabhāryeyamiti matvā niṣevitā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tatastu ceṣṭitairjñātvā garhayitvā visarjitā \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛti gātre me kuṣṭhavyādhirayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*mayātha dharmaśāstrajñaḥ kaścitpṛṣṭo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ yathoktaṃ me vada mātṛniṣevaṇāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tenoktaṃ sādhanaṃ samyaktiṃginyā mama śuddhaye \|*  
*so'haṃ tāṃ sādhayiṣyāmi tasya pāpasya śuddhaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

*anujñāṃ dehi me śīghraṃ kāryaṃ yena karomyaham \|*  
*kṣaṃtavyaṃ ca mayā bālye yatkiṃcitkukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*mama mātā yathā duḥkhaṃ na kuryāttvaṃ tathā kuru \|\| 61 \|\|*

55-61. In an isolated place he spoke to Vāsudeva with contemptuous feelings of hatred (about himself): “O father, I have been deceived by Nandinī, your wife. The sinful woman adopted the guise of my wife. When there was darkness all round she was (carnally) approached by me thinking that it was my own wife.

I came to know the truth through her movements. I censured her and let her off. Ever since then there have appeared the spots of leprosy on my body.

A certain excellent Brāhmaṇa conversant with scriptural texts was asked by me, ‘Tell me the expiatory rite for the sin of (carnally) approaching one’s mother.’

He said that due performance of Tiṅginī is conducive to my purity. I shall perform it to get redemption from that sin.

Grant me the permission soon so that I can begin (expiatory) procedure. Whatever misdeed have been committed by me during childhood should be exonerated. Do something so that my mother (Jāṃbavatī) should not feel sorry.

## \|\| 1.213.62 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya vajrapātopamaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇo dīnastataḥ provāca gadgadam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On hearing his words like a blow of thunderbolt, Hari became grief-stricken. His eyes were filled with tears and he spoke in faltering words:

## \|\| 1.213.63 \|\|

*na tvayā kāmataḥ putra kṛtyametadanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*na jñānena kṛtaṃ yasmāttatsmātsvalpaṃ hi pātakam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “O son, this has not been committed by you deliberately. Since it has not been done knowingly the sin is but little.

## \|\| 1.213.64 \|\|

*jānatā yatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ taccaivākṣayatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*na karoti mahīpālo yadi tasya vinigraham \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Only that sin which has been committed knowingly will have everlasting effect, if the king does not restrain him or punish him.

## \|\| 1.213.65 \|\|

*tasmātte kīrtayiṣyāmi prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye \|*  
*dānaṃ caiva mahābhāga yena kuṣṭhaṃ praṇaśyati \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Hence, I shall tell you the requisite expiation for the sake of gaining purity, so that your leprosy will be dispelled, O highly esteemed one. I shall tell you what Dana you have to offer.

## \|\| 1.213.66 \|\|

*uktāni pratiṣiddhāni punaḥ saṃbhāvitāni ca \|*  
*sāpekṣanirapekṣāṇi munivākyānyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. All the statements of sages are either conditional or unconditional. Some are uttered, some are prohibited and some are re-iterated.

## \|\| 1.213.67 \|\|

*tadatra viṣaye putra mama vākyaṃ samācara \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahacchreya iha loke paratra ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Hence in this matter, O my son, carry out my instructions. Great welfare will befall you in this world as well as hereafter.

## \|\| 1.213.68 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre viśvāmitrapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*mārtaṇḍo'sti suvikhyātaḥ sarvakuṣṭhavināśakaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara there is the well-known deity Mārtaṇḍa (Sun) installed by Viśvāmitra. The deity is well-known and is destructive of all leprous ailments.

## \|\| 1.213.69-71 \|\|

*sūryavāreṇa saptamyāṃ saṃprāpte māsi mādhave \|*  
*nakṣatre pitṛdaivatye śuklapakṣe samāgate \|\| 69 \|\|*

*bhāskarasyodaye prāpte śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|*  
*śatamaṣṭottaraṃ yāvatkurute ca pradakṣiṇām \|\| 70 \|\|*

*phalaiḥ śreṣṭhatamaiścaiva tatpramāṇaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*tasya kuṣṭhaṃ viniryāti sadya eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. In the bright half of the ṃonth of Mādhava, on the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday and the constellation Pitṛdaivatya (‘having Pitṛs as the presiding deity’ i.e. Maghā) at sunrise a person must make one hundred eight circumambulations with the mind sanctified by faith. He should have with him excellent fruits severally according to the number of circumamblations. Undoubtedly his leprosy will vanish.

## \|\| 1.213.72 \|\|

*nīrogaḥ kurute yastu ravestasya pradakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*tāvadyugaṃ pumāneṣa sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He who has become free from ailments and made as many circumambulations will be honoured in the world of the Sun for as many Yugas as the number of circumambulations be makes.

## \|\| 1.213.73 \|\|

*sūryavāreṇa yo martyastasya kṛtvā ṇdakṣiṇām \|*  
*namaskaroti sadbhaktyā so'pi rogaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. A man who makes his circumambulations on a Sunday and bows down with great devotion shall also be rid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.213.74 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ hi mahārāja tamārādhaya bhāskaram \|*  
*devaṃ vai vidhinānena yo mayokto'khilastava \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Hence, O great king (?) do propitiate Lord Bhāskara in accordance with the procedure which I have mentioned in full to you.

## \|\| 1.213.75 \|\|

*avikalpena manasā samārādhaya satvaram \|*  
*muktaroge vipāpmātha dibyadehamavāpsyasi \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Propitiate him quickly with your mind free from confusion, and with the riddance of ailments and sins, you will attain a divine body.

## \|\| 1.213.76 \|\|

*mā kuruṣva viṣādaṃ tvaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhisamudravam \|*  
*tasminkṣetre sthite deve kuharāśrayasaṃjñite \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Do not feel distressed over the fell disease of leprosy as long as the Lord designated as Kuharāśraya is stationed in that holy spot.”

## \|\| 1.213.77 \|\|

*atha tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prasthito viṣṇunandanaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Then, on hearing his words, the son of Viṣṇu (Sāṃba) set off.

## \|\| 1.213.78 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vacastasya devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*cakāra gamane buddhiyogaṃ sāṃbo'rbudaṃ prati \|\| 78 \|\|*

Sūta said:

78\. On hearing these words of the Discus-bearing Lord of Devas, Sāṃba made up his mind to go to Arbuda (en route to Hāṭakeśvara).

## \|\| 1.213.79 \|\|

*tataḥ śubhe'hani prāpte hastyaśvarathasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pratasthe sa suto viṣṇoḥ senayā parivāritaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then, on an auspicious day, that son of Viṣṇu set off surrounded by an army and fully accompanied by elephants, horses and chariots.

## \|\| 1.213.80 \|\|

*anuyātaḥ sudūraṃ ca kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|*  
*bāṣpapūrṇe kṣaṇenaiva sarvamātṛjanena ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. He was followed for a long distance by Kṛṣṇa unwearied in his actions and all the mothers with eyes filled with tears.

## \|\| 1.213.81 \|\|

*balabhadreṇa vīreṇa cārudeṣṇena dhīmatā \|*  
*yuyudhānāniruddhābhyāṃ pradyumnena ca dhīmatā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. (He was followed by) the heroic Balabhadra, the intelligent Cārudeṣṇa, Yuyudhāna, Aniruddha and the wise Pradyumna.

## \|\| 1.213.82 \|\|

*tato jāṃbavatī putraṃ dṛṣṭvā tīrthonmukhaṃ tadā \|*  
*gacchamānaṃ pracakre'tha pralāpānkurarī yathā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thereupon, seeing her own son proceeding ahead towards the holy Tīrtha, Jāṃbavatī began her lamentations like a female osprey.

## \|\| 1.213.83 \|\|

*hā hatāsmi vinaṣṭāsmi maṃdabhāgyā hyabhāginī \|*  
*ekopi tanayo yasyā mamāpyenāṃ daśāṃ gataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. “Alas! I am doomed. I am ruined. I am unfortunate and deficient in luck. My only son has been reduced to this condition?”

## \|\| 1.213.84-85 \|\|

*atha tāṃ rudatīṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*kimamaṃgalametasya prasthitasya kariṣyasi \|\| 84 \|\|*

*bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā muktakeśī viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*eṣa vyādhivinirmuktastīrthayātrāphalānvitaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhavyādhiparityaktaḥ punareṣyati teṃ'tikam \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. On seeing her lamenting thus, Madhusūdana said: “Why do you indulge in inauspicious acts even as he is setting out? Your eyes are filled with tears. You are distressed and your tresses are dishevelled. He will come back to you once again, rid of all his ailments, free from leprosy and fully endowed with the benefit of his pilgrimage.”

## \|\| 1.213.86 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare yānādavatīrya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*sāṃbo'sau prasthitastatra yatra jāṃbavatī sthitā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. In the meantime Sāṃba hurriedly got down from his vehicle and went to the spot where Jāṃbavatī was standing.

## \|\| 1.213.87 \|\|

*sa tāṃ praṇamya hṛṣṭātmā kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya vihasyo ccairvākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Delighted in his heart, he bowed to her and stood with palms joined in reverence. After bowing down he laughed and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.213.88 \|\|

*mā tvaṃ mātarvṛthā duḥkhamasmadarthe kariṣyasi \|*  
*āgamiṣyāmyahaṃ śīghraṃ tīrthayātrāṃ vidhāya vai \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. “O mother, do not feel distressed in vain on my account. I will return soon concluding my pilgrimage.”

## \|\| 1.213.89 \|\|

*jāṃbavatyuvāca \|*  
*rakṣatu tvāṃ vane vatsa sarvāstā vanadevatāḥ \|*  
*śvāpadebhyaḥ piśācebhyo duṣṭebhyaḥ putra sarvataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

Jāṃbavatī said:

89\. O my dear son, may all the sylvan deities protect you in the forest from all beasts of prey, vampires, and wicked ones all round.

## \|\| 1.213.90 \|\|

*śiraste pātu goviṃdaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ ca madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*bāhudeśaṃ hṛṣīkeśo hṛdayaṃ daityanāśanaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. May Govinda protect your head. May Madhusūdana protect your neck (throat). May Hṛṣīkeśa protect your hands. May the Slayer of Daityas protect your heart (chest).

## \|\| 1.213.91 \|\|

*jaṭharaṃ puṃḍarīkākṣaḥ kaṭiṃ pātu gadādharaḥ \|*  
*jānunoryugalaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pādau ca dharaṇīdharaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. May Puṇḍarīkāṣa protect your stomach. May Gadādhara protect your hips. May Kṛṣṇa protect the pair of your knees; May Dharaṇīdhara protect your feet.

## \|\| 1.213.92 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃspṛśya hastena nijenāṃgāni tasya sā \|*  
*samāliṃgya samāghrāya mūrdhadeśe muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Thus (as per Nyāsa procedure) she touched the different limbs with her own hand, embraced him and repeatedly sniffed at his head.

## \|\| 1.213.93 \|\|

*preṣayāmāsa taṃ putraṃ kṛtarakṣaṃ yaśasvinī \|*  
*sā sarvāṃtaḥpurīyuktā nivṛtā tadanantaram \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The renowned lady then bade farewell to her son for whom she had prayed for adequate protection. Then she returned with all the members of Antaḥpura (Inner Apartment).

## \|\| 1.213.94 \|\|

*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā dīnā niḥśvasantī yathoragī \|*  
*tathā ca bhagavānviṣṇuryādavaiḥ sakalaiḥ saha \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. She was miserable, tears welling up in her eyes. She heaved sighs like a hissing serpentess. So also was Lord Viṣṇu along with all the Yādavas.

## \|\| 1.213.95 \|\|

*praviṣṭo dvārakāpuryā sāṃbaṃ proṣya tataḥ param \|*  
*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇo dīno balabhadrapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. After bidding farewell to Sāṃba, he reentered the city of Dvārakā keeping Balabhadra at the head. His eyes were filled with tears.

## \|\| 1.213.96 \|\|

*putraiḥ pautraistathā mitrairbāṃdhavairaparairapi \|*  
*dvārakāyā viniṣkramya sāṃbo'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He entered the city along with his sons, grandsons, friends and kinsmen. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Sāṃba set out from Dvārakā.

## \|\| 1.213.97 \|\|

*saṃprāptaśca krameṇātha siṃdhusāgarasaṃgame \|*  
*yatra yogīśvaraḥ sākṣādaṃbarīṣapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. In due course, he reached the confluence of the rivers and the ocean where the deity Yogīśvara had been installed by Aṃbarīṣa.

## \|\| 1.213.98 \|\|

*adyāpi tiṣṭhate viṣṇurjaṃtūnāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā samabhyarcya devaṃ yogīśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Lord Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the sins of all creatures still stands there (as Yogīśvara deity). The scion of the Yadu family took his holy bath and worshipped Yogīśvara.

## \|\| 1.213.99 \|\|

*dadau dānāni viprebhyo nānārūpāṇi śaktitaḥ \|*  
*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇebhyaśca tathaivānyebhya eva ca \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Then he offered various gifts to the Brāhmaṇas as well as others, the distressed, the blind and the miserable ones, according to his capacity.

## \|\| 1.213.100 \|\|

*yānāni vastraratnāni yadyacca yena vāṃchitam \|*  
*sa trirātraṃ hareḥ putraḥ sthitvā tatra samāhitaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The son of Harī gave away whatever is desired by any one such as vehicles, jewels and clothes. He stayed there for three nights with great concentration.

## \|\| 1.213.101 \|\|

*cyavanasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ jagāmātha tataḥ param \|*  
*yatra saṃtiṣṭhate viṣṇuścyavanena pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then he went to the hermitage of Cyavana, where Viṣṇu had been installed by Cyavana.

## \|\| 1.213.102 \|\|

*siṃdhostaṭe ca puṇye ca sarvapātakanāśanaḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi vipramukhyebhyo dadau dānāni yādavaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The deity that is destructive of all sins is on the sacred banks of Sinḍhu. There too the Yādava offered gifts to the most important Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.213.103 \|\|

*vāṃchitāni yathoktāni śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*tatrāpi saṃyataḥ sāṃba sa sthitvā śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. He gave them every thing that they desired and expressed so. The gift was made in accordance with the rules laid down in the scriptural texts. There too, Sāṃba stayed with perfect continence and faith.

## \|\| 1.213.104 \|\|

*trirātraṃ prajagāmātha snātvā siṃdhūdake śubhe \|*  
*tatastu puṣkarādīni samuddiśya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. He halted there for three nights and took regular baths in the auspicious waters of Sindhu. Then he started slowly towards the holy spots beginning with Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.213.105 \|\|

*puṣkarāvāsinaṃ devaṃ dhyāyamāno hyaharniśam \|*  
*tastu puṣkaraṃ prāpya krameṇa yadusattamaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. He continued the journey incessantly meditating on Lord Puṣkaravāsin. The most excellent one among the descendants of Yadu reached Puṣkara in due course.

## \|\| 1.213.106 \|\|

*puṇye kuṇḍajale snātaḥ saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa gṛhītvātha phalāni ca \|*  
*gataḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yatra devo vai viṣṇu sūcitaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. He took his holy bath in the meritorious waters of the Kuṇḍa and offered libations to the Pitṛs and Devas. On a Sunday coinciding with Saptamī, he took fruits with him and went to the place where the deity mentioned by Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) was present.

## \|\| 1.213.107 \|\|

*pūjayitvā tato bhaktyā devaṃ kuharavāsinam \|*  
*vastrānulepanairdhūpairnaivedyaistu pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. He devoutly worshipped Lord Kuharavāsin through garments, unguents, incenses and food offerings of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.213.108 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇāścakre phalahastaḥ śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*prapaṭhansūryagāyatrīṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then he made the circumambulations slowly with fruits in his hands. Equipped with the greatest faith, he repeated the Sūryagāyatrī Mantra.

## \|\| 1.213.109 \|\|

*yathāyathā karotyeṣa ravestasya pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*tathātathā ca saṃyāti tasya kuṣṭhaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, as he continued his circumambulations of Ravi, the disease of leprosy began to vanish.

## \|\| 1.213.110 \|\|

*tatra kṣaṇe'bhavattasya citte sāṃbasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*mukto'haṃ kuṣṭharogeṇa nirvikalpaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. There, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in an instant this thought arose in the mind of the intelligent Sāṃba: ‘I am rid of the disease of leprosy without the least trace of doubt.’

## \|\| 1.213.111-112 \|\|

*tataśca sahitaṃ tena yatkiṃcittatra cāgatam \|*  
*hastyaśvaratharatnāḍhyaṃ tatsarvaṃ bhaktipūrvakam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*nāgarāṇāṃ dadau sarvaṃ tathānyadgrāmapaṃcakam \|*  
*sāṃbā'dityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tataḥ saṃprasthito gṛham \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. Whatever had come there along with him in the form of elephants, horses, chariots and jewels he gave unto the Nāgaras entirely in addition to five villages granted by him. After installing Sāṃbāditya he started homewards.

## \|\| 1.213.113 \|\|

*kiṃcidurvaritaṃ yacca tatsarvaṃ bhaktisaṃyutam \|*  
*pradadau sūryaviprebhyaḥ pūjayitvā divākaram \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Whatever few things remained (after giving gifts to Nāgaras), he gifted away devoutly to the Sūryavipras (Brāhmaṇas devoutly worshipping Sun-god) after adoring Divākara.

## \|\| 1.213.114 \|\|

*aṣṭau vājisahasrāṇi nāgānāṃ ca śatatrayam \|*  
*rathānāṃ ṣaṭśatānyeva aśvairyuktāni vājibhiḥ \|*  
*anaṃtāni ca ratnāni dattvā sāṃbo gṛhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Sāṃba went home after giving away eight thousand horses, three hundred elephants and six hundred chariots yoked with fast horse as well as an indefinite number of precious stones.

## \|\| 1.213.115 \|\|

*ya etatpaṭhate bhaktyā sāṃbākhyānamanuttamam \|*  
*śṛṇoti vā'nvaye tasya na kuṣṭhaṃ saṃprajāyate \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. If anyone devoutly reads this excellent narrative of Sāṃba or listens to it, no one in his family will be afflicted with leprosy.

## \|\| 1.213.116 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ viśvāmitrīyamuttamam \|*  
*caturthaṃ ca puṇyatīrthaṃ strīṇāṃ caiva śubhāvaham \|\| 116 \|\|*

Sūta said:

116\. Thus has been fully described to you the excellent fourth Tīrtha of Viśvāmitra, the meritorious Tīrtha causing welfare unto women too.

## Chapter 214 - Procedure of Gaṇapati Worship

## \|\| 1.214.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyopi ca tatrāsti viśvāmitrapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*gaṇanātho dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvasiddhiprado nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*māghamāse caturthyāṃ ca śuklāyāṃ pūjayettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa ca saṃvatsaraṃ yāvatsarvai vighnairvimucyate o \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Further, there is another deity installed by Viśvāmitra there, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. It is Gaṇanātha, the bestower of all Siddhis unto men.

He who worships the deity on the fourth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha is rid of all the obstacles for the whole of year.

## \|\| 1.214.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*gaṇanāthasya cotpattiṃ sāṃprataṃ sūta no vada \|*  
*kathameṣa samutpannaḥ kiṃ māhātmyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. O Sūta, explain to us now the origin of Gaṇanātha. How did he originate? Of what greatness has he been proclaimed?

## \|\| 1.214.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*eṣa cotpādito gauryā nijāṃgamalataḥ svayam \|*  
*krīḍārthaṃ mānuṣairaṃgairmātaṃgānanaśobhitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. He was created by Gaurī from the dirt of her body herself just for sport. He has the limbs of human beings and he looks splendid with an elephantine head.

## \|\| 1.214.5 \|\|

*caturhastasamopeta ākhuvāhanagastathā \|*  
*kuṭhārahastaśca tathā modakāśanatoṣakṛt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He possesses four hands. He moves about on his vehicle, the mouse. He holds an axe in his hand. He feels satisfied by eating Modakas (sweetmeats).

## \|\| 1.214.6-7 \|\|

*sarvasiddhiprado loke bhaktānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*eṣa pūrvaṃ prabhoḥ kārye saṃgrāme tārakāmaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saṃgrāmamakarodraudraṃ na kṛtaṃ yacca kenacit \|*  
*nihatā dānavāḥ sarve saṃkhyayā parivarjitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He is the bestower of all Siddhis in the world especially unto the devotees. Formerly, he fought a formidable battle in the course of hostilities against Tāraka and carried out the task of the Lord, as has never been performed by any one. All the numberless Dānavas were killed.

## \|\| 1.214.8 \|\|

*tataḥ śakreṇa tuṣṭena proktaḥ saṃgrāmabhūmipaḥ \|*  
*kṣata vikṣatasarvāṃgo rudhireṇa pariplutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then this king of the battle-ground was told by the delighted Śakra as he came with all the limbs deeply wounded and covered with blood:

## \|\| 1.214.9-11 \|\|

*asmadarthe tvayā yuddhaṃ yatkṛtaṃ sugajānana \|*  
*nihatā dānavāḥ sarve saṃkhyayā parivarjitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ sarvadevānāmapi pūjyo bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*kiṃpunarmānuṣāṇāṃ ca ye nityaṃ vighnasaṃplutāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ye tvāṃ saṃpūjayiṣyaṃti kāryāraṃbheṣu sarvataḥ \|*  
*kāryasiddhirna saṃdehasteṣāṃ bhūyādgirā mama \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. “O Lord of excellent elephantine countenance, this battle has been fought by you for our sake. Innumerable Dānavas were killed. Hence you will be worthy of the adoration by all the Devas, still more by all the human beings who are always overwhelmed by obstacles?

If at the beginning of their tasks and activities people worship you there is no doubt about it that they will achieve Siddhi (success) in their undertaking. There is my word for it.”

## \|\| 1.214.12 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrākṣo visasarjātha taṃ tadā \|*  
*saṃmānya bahumānena gaurīśaṃkarapārśvataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After saying thus the Thousand-eyed One (Indra) honoured him duly and sent him off to Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.214.13 \|\|

*ayamarthaḥ purā pṛṣṭo rohitāśvena dhīmatā \|*  
*sarvavipravināśārthaṃ mārkaṃḍeyaṃ mahāmunim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. This very topic was proposed for discussion by the intelligent Rohitāśva to the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya for the purpose of dispelling all obstacles.

## \|\| 1.214.14 \|\|

*tamevārthaṃ mahābhāgāḥ kathayiṣye yathārthataḥ \|*  
*tacchṛṇudhvaṃ purāvṛttaṃ sarvaṃ sarve samāhitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O highly esteemed ones, I shall factually mention the same theme. So, listen to the incident of the days of yore, ye all with great concentration.

## \|\| 1.214.15 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*bhagavannatra ye martyāḥ sarve vighnasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*śubhakṛtyeṣu sarveṣu jāyaṃte śucayo'pi ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

15\. O holy Sir, all the men here (in this world) are entangled in obstacles in the course of all their auspicious activities, although they themselves are very pure.

## \|\| 1.214.16 \|\|

*prārabdheṣu ca kāryeṣu dharmajeṣu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tāni vighnāni jāyante yaistatkāryaṃ na sidhyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In all the tasks undertaken, especially in those connected with holy rites, these obstacles crop up whereby the task does not get concluded (successfully).

## \|\| 1.214.17 \|\|

*tasmādvighnavināśāya kiṃcinme vratamā diśa \|*  
*vrataṃ vā niyamo vā'tha tapo vā dānameva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence, enjoin to me some Vrata for the purpose of dispelling the obstacles. Let it be a Vrata, Niyama (restraint), penance or Dāna (holy gift).

## \|\| 1.214.18 \|\|

*sakṛccīrṇena yenātra yāvajjīvati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tāvanna jāyate vighnamājanmamaraṇāṃtikam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If those rites are performed only once, there should not be any obstacle from birth to death, for the entire period of the life of a man.

## \|\| 1.214.19 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*atra te kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvavighnavināśanam \|*  
*vrataṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*viśvāmitreṇa sañcīrṇaṃ yatpurā bhāvitātmanā \|\| 19 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

19\. In this context, I shall describe to you a Vrata endowed with all good features and also destructive of all obstacles. It quells all sins. It was formerly performed by Viśvāmitra of sanctified soul.

## \|\| 1.214.20 \|\|

*viśvāmitra iti khyāto gādhiputraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*vasiṣṭhena samaṃ tasya vairamāsīnmahātmanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The valorous son of Gādhi became well-known as Viśvāmitra. The noble-souled one contracted enmity with Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.214.21 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyārthe na samproktaḥ kathaṃcitsa mahātapāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇastvaṃ vasiṣṭhena tato vairamajāyata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It was for the sake of the Brāhmaṇical status. Somehow, that sage of great penance was not addressed by Vasiṣṭha with the words “You are a Brāhmaṇa”. So the enmity ensued.

## \|\| 1.214.22 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*kasmānna proktavānvipro vasiṣṭhastu kathaṃcana \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ sa paraṃ proktobrahmādibhirapi svayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

22\. Why did the Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha not say so by all means, when he was called a Brāhmaṇa by Brahmā and others themselves?

## \|\| 1.214.23 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*kṣatriyaśca sthitaḥ pūrvaṃ viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*mṛgayāsu paribhrāṃto vasiṣṭhasya tadā'śramam \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ kṣutpipāsārttaḥ sa tenātha prapūjitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

\[Note: This episode of confrontation between Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra for the cow Nandinī is given in Mahābhārata, Ādi 174.\]

23\. Viśvāmitra was formerly a Kṣatriya king. While hunting, he strayed into the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha. Distressed with hunger and thirst, he entered the hermitage and he was honoured by him (i.e. Vasiṣṭha).

## \|\| 1.214.24 \|\|

*tasyāsīnnandinīnāma dhenuḥ kāmadughā sadā \|*  
*sā sūte vāñchitaṃ sadyo yadvasiṣṭho'bhivāñchati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He had a cow named Nandinī which always yielded whatever was desired. The cow immediately yielded whatever was desired.

## \|\| 1.214.25-26 \|\|

*tatprabhāvātsa bhūpālaḥ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ \|*  
*tena tṛptiparā nīto miṣṭānnairvividhaistataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pārthivo'yamiti jñātvā hyarghyādyairbhojanaiḥ sa ca \|*  
*so'pi dṛṣṭvā prabhāvaṃ taṃ sarvaṃ dhenośca saṃbhavam \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa tāṃ mūlyairgajavājisamu dbhavaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26a. Thanks to the power of that cow, the king together with his servants, army and vehicles, was rendered extremely satisfied through different kinds of sweet cooked foodstuffs. Knowing that he was the king of the land, he was duly honoured with Arghya and other things as well as foodstuffs.

26b. On noticing that everything was the result of the power of the cow, he requested for her against the price of his elephants and horses.

## \|\| 1.214.27 \|\|

*na dadau sa tadā vipraḥ sāmnā dānena vā punaḥ \|*  
*bhedena ca tato daṇḍaṃ yojayāmāsa vai nṛpaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Brāhmaṇa did not give the cow and refused to yield to conciliatory overtures, promise of gifts and to threats. Therefore, the king employed Daṇḍa (the expediency of punishment).

## \|\| 1.214.28 \|\|

*kālayāmāsa tāṃ dhenuṃ tataḥ kopātsa pārthivaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The king angrily seized the cow and (was about to take her away).

## \|\| 1.214.29 \|\|

*sā'bravīnnīyamānā'tha vasiṣṭhaṃ kiṃ tvayā vibho \|*  
*dattāhamasya nṛpateryanmāṃ nayati yatnataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. While being taken away she (the cow) said to Vasiṣṭha: “O holy Sir, have I been handed over to the king, for he is taking me away with forceful efforts?”

## \|\| 1.214.30 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*na mayā tvaṃ mahābhāge dattā cāsya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*balānnayati yadyeṣa tasmādyuktaṃ samācara \|\| 30 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

30\. O highly esteemed one, you have not been given away to this king. If he takes you away forcibly, do what is proper.

## \|\| 1.214.31 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kopasaṃyuktā nandinī dhenuruttamā \|*  
*jṛṃbhāṃ cakāra tatsainyaṃ samuddiśya nṛpodbhavam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On hearing it the excellent cow Nandinī yawned (opened her mouth and made a lowing sound) with the army of the king in view.

## \|\| 1.214.32 \|\|

*dhūmāvartistato jātā tasyā vaktrāttataḥ param \|*  
*tato jvālā mahāraudrāstato yodhāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then a curling column of smoke arose from her mouth. From it terrible flames issued forth and then thousands of warriors.

## \|\| 1.214.33 \|\|

*nānāśastradharā raudrā yamadūtā yathā ca te \|*  
*pulindā barbarābhīrāḥ kirātā yavanāḥ śakāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. They held various kinds of weapons and appeared like the messengers of Yama. The Pulindas, Barbaras, Ābhiras, Kirātas, Yavanas and Śakas issued forth thus.

## \|\| 1.214.34 \|\|

*te procustāṃ vadāsmākaṃ kasmātsṛṣṭā vayaṃ śubhe \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They said to her, “Say, O auspicious one, why have we been created?”

## \|\| 1.214.35 \|\|

*nandinyuvāca \|*  
*ete māṃ ye balātpāpā nayaṃti nṛpasevakāḥ \|*  
*tānnighnantu samādeśānnānyadvāṃchāmi kiṃcana \|\| 35 \|\|*

Nandinī said:

35\. These sinful servants of the king are taking me away forcibly. At my behest all of you should assail them. I do not desire anything else.

## \|\| 1.214.36 \|\|

*tatastaistasya tatsainyaṃ viśvāmitrasya sūditam \|*  
*yudhyamānaṃ mahārāja daśarātreṇa saṃyuge \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O great king, that army of Viśvāmitra fought the battle for ten days and got annihilated.

## \|\| 1.214.37 \|\|

*viśvāmitro'pi taddṛṣṭvā brāhmyaṃ balamanuttamam \|*  
*pratijñāmakarottatra tāreṇa susvareṇa ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On thus noticing the excellent power of a Brāhmaṇa, Viśvāmitra took a vow in a high pitch:

## \|\| 1.214.38-39 \|\|

*athāhaṃ saṃbhaviṣyāmi brāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*mamāpi jāyate yena prabhāvaścedṛśo'dbhutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmāttapaḥ kariṣyāmi yadasādhyaṃ surairapi \|*  
*svaputraṃ sve pade dhṛtvā tataścakre tapo mahat \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39a. “I will undoubtedly become a Brāhmaṇa whereby I too can possess such a wonderful power as this. Hence I shall perform a penance that even Suras cannot perform.”

39b. Then he installed his son as king of the realm and performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.214.40 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyārthaṃ mahāraudraṃ sumahadduṣkaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ tena naivāptaṃ vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He performed a highly terrible and difficult penance for the sake of Brāhmaṇahood. But Brāhmaṇahood was not attained by him. So he became utterly despondent.

## \|\| 1.214.41 \|\|

*tataḥ kailāsamāsādya devadevaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*samyagārādhayāmāsa gaurīyuktaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then he went to Kailāsa and perfectly propitiated Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, Maheśvara accompanied by Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.214.42-43 \|\|

*ahaṃ tapaḥ kariṣyāmi brāhmaṇyasya kṛte prabho \|*  
*tvadīye parvataśreṣṭhe kailāse śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tasmādvighnasya me rakṣāṃ devadevaḥ prayacchatu \|*  
*yathā no nāśamāyāti tapaḥ sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ mahat \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. “O Lord, I shall perform a penance for the sake of Brāhmaṇahood. Therefore, I seek refuge in you in Kailāsa, your excellent mountain. Hence, may the Lord of Devas accord protection from obstacles, lest the great penance performed should be destroyed.”

## \|\| 1.214.44-45 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*śuddhyarthaṃ caiva yatkāryaṃ kāryesminnṛpasattama \|*  
*vināyakasamudbhūtāṃ tattvaṃ pūjāṃ samācara \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yena te jāyate siddhiḥ samyagbrāhmaṇyasaṃbhavā \|\| 45 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

44-45. O excellent king, in connection with your aim, carry out that task which should be performed for the sake of purity. Hence do the worship of Vināyaka. Thereby you will achieve the Siddhi and attain the status of Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.214.46 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*tadvadasva suraśreṣṭha tathā tasya karomyaham \|*  
*pūrvaṃ pūjāṃ gaṇeśasya sarvavighnapraśāntaye \|\| 46 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:

46\. Hence, O excellent one among Suras, explain at the very outset, the method of the adoration of Gaṇesa for the sake of the suppression of all obstacles, so that I can perform it duty.

## \|\| 1.214.47 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*eṣa gauryā purā kṛtvā nijāṃgodvartanaṃ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*nirmalena kṛtaḥ paścānnarākāraścaturbhujaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

47\. Formerly, Gaurī smeared her limbs with some perfumes and unguents. With the dirt thereof she made a being in the form of a man with four arms.

## \|\| 1.214.48 \|\|

*krīḍārthaṃ mama putro'yaṃ bālabhāvaḥ prakalpitaḥ \|*  
*gajavaktro mahākāyo laṃbodaralaghūrukaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In order to play with him saying “my son” the state of childhood was assigned. He had the face of an elephant, a huge body with protruding belly and short thighs.

## \|\| 1.214.49 \|\|

*tato'hamanayā proktaḥ sajīvaḥ kriyatāmayam \|*  
*putrako me yathā bhāvī loke pūjya tamo vibho \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then I was told by her, “O Lord, let my son be made alive so that he will become most worthy of adoration.”

## \|\| 1.214.50 \|\|

*tato mayāpi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ sṛṣṭisūktena pārthiva \|*  
*jīvasūktena samyaksa prāṇavānsamajāyata \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then, O king, uttering Sṛṣṭisūkta (‘Hymn of Creation’) I touched him. When Jīvasūkta was uttered, perfectly he became alive.

## \|\| 1.214.51 \|\|

*tato mayā prahṛṣṭena proktā devī himādrijā \|*  
*caturthīdivase prāpte mayā'dyāyaṃ vinirmitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then the goddess, the daughter of the Mountain, was told by me in great delight, “The day today is the fourth lunar day and this (boy) has been created by me today.

## \|\| 1.214.52 \|\|

*putrastava mahābhāge jīvasūktaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*eṣa sarvāgaṇānāṃ ca madīyānāṃ sureśvari \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sadā'dhyakṣa stasmācca gaṇanāyakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O highly esteemed lady, your son has been created through the power of Jīvasūkta. O goddess of Suras, he will become the permanent presiding deity of all the Gaṇas of mine. Hence, he will be (called) Gaṇanāyaka.

## \|\| 1.214.53-54 \|\|

*paṭhyamānena yaścainaṃ jīvasūktena sundari \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati sadbhaktyā caturthīdivase śubhe \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tasya sarveṣu kṛtyeṣu sarvavighrāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*prayāsyaṃti kṣayaṃ devi tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. O beautiful woman, a devotee should worship him on the auspicious Caturthī day along with,the utterance, (chanting) of the Jīvasūkta; with great devotion. O goddess, in all his activities all obstacles shall be destroyed like darkness at sunrise.

## \|\| 1.214.55-57 \|\|

*namo laṃbodarāyeti namo gaṇavibho tathā \|*  
*kuṭhāradhāriṇe nityaṃ tathā vāksaṃgatāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*namo modakabhakṣāya namo dantaikadhāriṇe \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ebhirmantraiḥ samabhyarcya paścānmoda kajaṃśubham \|*  
*naivedyaṃ ca pradātavyaṃ tataścārghyaṃ nivedayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. The devotee then utters the following Mantras: “Obeisance to Laṃbodara, obeisance to him, to the Lord of Gaṇas. Obeisance to the Lord holding Kuṭhāra (an axe) for ever. Obeisance to Vāksaṅgata (the eloquent one); obeisance to Modakabhakṣa (one who eats sweetmeat). Obeisance to one having a single tooth (i.e. tusk).” After adoring by means of these Mantras the food offering of Modaka is to be made. Then Arghya is offered.

## \|\| 1.214.58 \|\|

*ahaṃ karma kariṣyāmi yatkicicchaṃbhusaṃbhavam \|*  
*avighnaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ sarvadaiva tvayā vibho \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. (The Mantra) “Whatever rite I perform in regard to Śaṃbhu, O Lord, you will ward off the obstacles therein.”

## \|\| 1.214.59 \|\|

*tatastu brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanaṃ modakodbhavam \|*  
*yathāśaktyā pradātavyaṃ vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then Brāhmaṇas should be fed with the Modakas in accordance with one’s capacity. There should not be stinginess in regard to the money spent.

## \|\| 1.214.60 \|\|

*evamuktaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ svayameva nṛpottama \|*  
*gaṇanāthaṃ samuddiśya gauryāḥ purata eva ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O excellent king, I myself said thus to Gaurī with regard to Gaṇanātha.

## \|\| 1.214.61-64 \|\|

*tataḥ prahṛṣṭā sā devī vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti yaḥ putraṃ madīyaṃ gaṇanāya kam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā samyakcaturthyāṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*tasya vighnāni sarvāṇi nāśaṃ yāsyaṃtyasaṃśayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*smṛtvā vā pūjayitvā vā yaḥ kāryāṇi kariṣyati \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃdehastatosyāvicalāni ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

*na sandehastato'sya śrīracalaiva bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. Thereupon, the delighted goddess uttered these words: “From today onwards, if anyone perfectly worships my son Gaṇanāyaka in accordance with this procedure on the Caturthī day, all obstacles of his shall undoubtedly vanish.

If any one performs the rites after remembering or worshipping him, all those rites shall become firm. There is no doubt about this that his fortune and glory will be stable (permanent).”

## \|\| 1.214.65 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ hi mahābhāga caturthyāṃ samyagācara \|*  
*vināyakodbhavāṃ pūjāṃ yenābhīṣṭena yujyase \|\| 65 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

65\. Hence, O highly esteemed one, you also perform perfectly the adoration of Vināyaka so that you will achieve whatever you desire.

Mārkaṇḍeya said;

## \|\| 1.214.66-67 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*gaṇanāthasamudbhūtāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathocitām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tapaścacāra vipulaṃ sarvavighnavivarjitam \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ ca tataḥ prāptaṃ sarveṣāmapi durlabham o \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. On hearing his words, King Viśvāmitra duly performed the worship of Gaṇanātha and practised an elaborate penance bereft of obstacles. Then Brāhmaṇahood was also attained which is very rare to get.

## \|\| 1.214.68 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ hi mahābhāga vināyakasamudbhavām \|*  
*pūjāṃ kuru caturthyāṃ ca saṃprāptāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpnoṣi mahābhogānhṛdisthānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Hence you also, O highly esteemed one, perform the adoration of Vināyaka specially on the Caturthī day. There is no doubt about this that you will attain all pleasures cherished in the heart.

## \|\| 1.214.69 \|\|

*yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya gaṇanāthaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*sa taṃ sarvamavāpnoti maheśvaravaco yathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. As per words of Maheśvara, one obtains everything if one worships Gaṇanātha with some desire in view.

## \|\| 1.214.70 \|\|

*aputro labhate putraṃ dhanahīno mahaddhanam \|*  
*śatrūñjayati saṃgrāme smṛtvā taṃ gaṇanāyakam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. One without a son obtains a son; one without wealth gets great wealth. By remembering Gaṇanāyaka one conquers enemies.

## \|\| 1.214.71 \|\|

*yā nārī patinā tyaktā durbhagā ca virūpitā \|*  
*sā saubhāgyamavāpnoti gaṇanāthasya pūjayā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. If a woman is ugly, or unfortunate, or if she is deserted, by her husband, she regains conjugal felicity through the adoration of Gaṇanātha.

## \|\| 1.214.72 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*na vighnaṃ jāyate tasya sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. If anyone reads this always or listens to this with concentration, he will never meet with obstacles in any of his activities.

## Chapter 215 - Necessity of the Performance of Śrāddha

## \|\| 1.215.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ vada naḥ sūta śrāddhakalpasya yo vidhiḥ \|*  
*vistareṇa mahābhāga yathā taccākṣayaṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. Now tell us, O Sūta, O highly esteemed one, the injunctions regarding the procedure of Śrāddhakalpa in full detail, so that the benefit shall be everlasting.

## \|\| 1.215.2 \|\|

*kasminkāle prakartavyaṃ śrāddhaṃ pitṛparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśairbrāhmaṇaistacca tathā dravyairmahāmate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. At what time should Śrāddha be performed by those devoted to the Pitṛs? O highly intelligent one, of what nature should the Brāhmaṇas be? What shall be the nature of the articles and requisites?

## \|\| 1.215.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo mārkaṃḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*rohitāśvena vipreṃdrā hariścandra sutena saḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. It was for this purpose that Mārkaṇḍeya, the great sage, was formerly asked, O leading Brāhmaṇas, by Rohitāśva, the son of Hariścandra.

## \|\| 1.215.4-6 \|\|

*hariścandre gate svargaṃ rohitāśve nṛpe sthite \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena mārkaṇḍo munisattamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarayvāḥ saṃgame puṇye snānārthaṃ samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā pitṝndevānsaṃtarpya vidhipūrvakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*praviṣṭastāṃ purīṃ ramyāmayodhyāṃ satyanāmikām \|*  
*rohitāśvo'pi taṃ śrutvā samāyātaṃ munīśvaram \|*  
*padātiḥ prayayau tūrṇaṃ dūradeśaṃ tu sammukham \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-5a. When Hariścandra had gone to heaven and king Rohitāśva was established (as a king), the excellent sage Mārkaṇḍeya in the course of his pilgrimage came to take holy bath in the holy confluence of Śarayū.

5b-6. He took his holy bath there and offered libations to the Pitṛs and Devas in accordance with the injunctions. He entered the beautiful and charming city Ayodhyā of truthful name. On hearing that the leading sage was on his way there, Rohitāśva hastened on foot over a long distance to meet him face to face.

## \|\| 1.215.7 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ mūrdhnā kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ vinayena samanvi taḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then he bowed down his head and stood with palms joined in reverence. He then humbly spoke these sweet words:

## \|\| 1.215.8 \|\|

*svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha bhūyaḥ susvāgataṃ mune \|*  
*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ saṃprāptaḥ paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*yatte pādarajobhirme mūrddhajā vimalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “O excellent one among sages, welcome unto you. O sage, a very good welcome to you. I am blessed. I have performed meritorious deeds. I have attained the greatest goal since my hairs have been rendered pure by the dust particles of your feet.”

## \|\| 1.215.9 \|\|

*evamuktvā gṛhītvā taṃ svahastālaṃbanaṃ tadā \|*  
*yayau tatra sabhāsthānaṃ bṛhatsiṃhāsanāśrayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying thus and grasping him by the hand, he took him to the hall of his assembly where there was a large throne.

## \|\| 1.215.10 \|\|

*siṃhāsane niveśyātha taṃ muniṃ pārthivottamaḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭo dharāpṛṣṭhe kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After making the sage seated on the throne, the excellent king sat on the ground with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.215.11-12 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca madhuraṃ vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*niḥspṛhasyāpi vipreṃdra ki vā'gamanakāraṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tadbravīhi yathātathyaṃ karomi tava sāṃpratam \|*  
*adeyamapi dāsyāmi gṛhāyātasya te vibho \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. He spoke these sweet words in great humility: “O eminent Brāhmaṇa, you are no doubt one with no special desire (for worldly objects). What may be the reason For your visit?

Do tell me now in what way shall I be hospitable to you (How shall I extend the hospitality unto You)? You have come to my abode; I shall give you, O holy Sir, even the things that cannot ordinarily be given.”

## \|\| 1.215.13 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena vayamatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*sarayvāḥ saṃgame puṇye kalye yāsyāmyahe punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

13\. We have come here in the course of our pilgrimage to the auspicious confluence of Śarayū. We are proceeding ahead in the morning.

## \|\| 1.215.14 \|\|

*niḥspṛhairapi draṣṭavyā dharmavanto dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ proktaṃ purāṇa jñairbrāhmaṇaiḥ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Even people without any particular desire should meet righteous, excellent Brāhmaṇas. Brāhmaṇas with scriptures as their eyes and well-versed in the purāṇas say thus:

## \|\| 1.215.15 \|\|

*dharmavantaṃ nṛpaṃ dṛṣṭvā liṃgaṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ tathā \|*  
*nadīṃ sāgaragāṃ caiva mucyetpāpāddinodbhavāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “By meeting a righteous king, viewing a Liṅga that has sprung up by itself, and seeing a river falling into the ocean, one shall be rid of the sin occurring that day.”

## \|\| 1.215.16 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataścakre pṛcchāṃ sa munisattamaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpaśārdūlaṃ puraḥsthaṃ vinayānvitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After saying thus and meeting the tiger among kings standing humbly in front, the excellent Sage made these enquiries:

## \|\| 1.215.17 \|\|

*kaccitte saphalā vedāḥ kaccitte saphalaṃ śrutam \|*  
*kaccitte saphalā dārāḥ kaccitte saphalaṃ dhanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “I hope, the Vedas are fruitful in regard to you. I hope, you have acquired fruitful learning. I hope, your wife is fruitful. I hope, your riches are fruitful.”

## \|\| 1.215.18 \|\|

*rohitāśva uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ syuḥ saphalā vedāḥ kathaṃ syātsaphalaṃ śrutam \|*  
*kathaṃ syuḥ saphalā dārāḥ kathaṃ syātsaphalaṃ dhanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Rohitāśva said:

18\. How do the Vedas become fruitful? How do we know that learning is fruitful? On what basis do we say that the wife is fruitful? How do the riches become fruitful?

## \|\| 1.215.19 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*agnihotraphalā vedāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam \|*  
*ratiputraphalā dārā dattabhuktaphalaṃ dhanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

19\. When Agnihotra is performed the Vedas are fruitful. When good manners and habits are acquired learning is fruitful. Sexual pleasure and the progeny are the fruits of having a wife. If gifted and/or enjoyed riches are fruitful.

## \|\| 1.215.20 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā mahārāja nānyathā kartumarhasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After realizing this, O great king, it does not behove you to do otherwise.

## \|\| 1.215.21 \|\|

*catvāryetāni kṛtyāni mayoktāni ca tāni te \|*  
*yathā tāni prakṛtyāni lokadvayamabhīpsatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. These four duties stated by me should be carried out by one who aspires for (the benefit of) the two worlds.

## \|\| 1.215.22 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataścakre kathāścitrāśca tatpuraḥ \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After having said thus, the sage made diverse discourses on the saintly kings and ancient celestial sages in particular.

## \|\| 1.215.23 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāvasāne ca kasmiṃściddvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*papraccha taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ rohitāśvo mahīpatiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then at the conclusion of one of the discourses, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, King Rohitāśva asked the excellent sage:

## \|\| 1.215.24 \|\|

*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi śrāddhakalpamahaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*dṛśyaṃte bahavo bhedā dvijānāṃ śrāddhakarmaṇi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “O holy Sir, I wish to hear (exactly) about the Śrāddhakalpa, since many versions are met with in the Śrāddha rite of Brāhmaṇas.’

## \|\| 1.215.25 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāga yatpṛṣṭo'smi nṛpottama \|*  
*śrāddhasya bahavo bhedāḥ śākhābhedairvyavasthitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

25\. O highly esteemed one, O excellent one among kings, what I have been asked about is true. There are different versions of Śrāddha as established through the different Śākhās (branches or schools of Vedic learning).

## \|\| 1.215.26 \|\|

*tasmātte nirṇayaṃ vacmi bhartṛyajñena yatpurā \|*  
*ānarttādhipateḥ proktaṃ samyakchrāddhasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hence I shall decisively tell you the exact features of Śrāddha as mentioned formerly by Bhartṛyajña to the Lord of Ānarta.

## \|\| 1.215.27 \|\|

*bhartṛyajñaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ nijāśramapade nṛpaḥ \|*
