10\. The word Śarman is uttered in Arghya and other activities. The word Śarmā in the Tarpaṇa rite; the word Śarmaṇe when the Sasya (vegetable dish) is offered and Śarmaṇaḥ at the time of Akṣayyaka Vidhi.

## \|\| 1.225.11 \|\|

*mātarmātre tathā māturāsane kalpane'kṣaye \|*  
*gotre gotrāyai gotrāyāḥ prathamādyā vibhaktayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The words Mātaḥ, Mātre and Mātuḥ are uttered respectively when the seat is offered, when Saṅkalpa is made and when Akṣayya is offered. The words Gotre, Gotrāyai and Gotrāyāḥ are also uttered as well as the nominative and other case endings.

## \|\| 1.225.12 \|\|

*devi devyai tathā devyā evaṃ mātuśca kīrtayet \|*  
*prathamā ca caturthī ca ṣaṣṭhī syācchrāddhasiddhaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The words Devī, Devyai and Devyāḥ are pronounced unto the mother. Thus there Prathamā (actually vocative case), Caturthī and Ṣaṣṭhī should be used to make the Śrāddha fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.225.13 \|\|

*vibhaktirahitaṃ śrāddhaṃ kriyate vā viparyayāt \|*  
*akṛtaṃ tadvijānīyātpitṛṇāṃ nopatiṣṭhati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If the Śrāddha is performed without the used Vibhaktis (case endings) or contrarily, one should know that it is no better than not performed. It does not reach the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.225.14 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena brāhmaṇena vijānatā \|*  
*vibhaktibhiryathoktābhiḥ śrāddhe kāryo vidhiḥ sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence the rites should always be performed in the Śrāddha scrupulously along with the case-endings as mentioned now, by a wise Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.225.15 \|\|

*tataḥ sapiṃḍīkaraṇaṃ vatsarā dūrdhvataḥ sthitam \|*  
*vṛddhirvā'gāminī cetsyāttadārvāgapi kārayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then after a year, the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite is to be performed. If any auspicious ceremony ensues thereafter this rite can be performed even before this stipulated period (of one year).

## \|\| 1.225.16 \|\|

*pārvaṇoktavidhānena tridaivatyamadaivikam \|*  
*pretamuddiśya kartavyameko ddiṣṭaṃ ca pārthiva \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O king, Ekoddiṣṭa should be performed in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Pārvaṇa texts. It is performed with the departed one in view. It may have the three deities or no deities.

## \|\| 1.225.17-20 \|\|

*ekenaiva tu pākena mama caitanmataṃ smṛtam \|*  
*arghapātraṃ samādāya yatpretārthaṃ prakalpitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pitṛpātreṣu triṣveva tridhā tacca parikṣipet \|*  
*evaṃ piṃḍaṃ tridhā kṛtvā pitṛpiṃḍeṣu ca triṣu \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ye samāneti mantrābhyāṃ na syātpretastataḥ param \|*  
*avanejanaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pitṛpūrvaṃ yathākramam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*gandhadhūpādikaṃ sarvaṃ punareva pradāpayet \|*  
*pitṛpūrvaṃ samuccārya varjayecca caturthakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. The dish cooked is single. This is my opinion.

The devotee takes up the Arghya utensil intended for the departed one and pours the contents in the three Pitṛpātras in three equal quantities.

Similarly, the Piṇḍa is split into three and put along with the three Pitṛpiṇḍas uttering the two Mantras ye samānā etc. He will no longer remain a Preta thereafter.

The Avanejana rite (sprinkling of water on the Darbha grass) is performed then in due order beginning with the father.

The sweet scents, incense etc. shall be offered once again. The names are uttered beginning with the father and the fourth (ancestor) is dropped.

## \|\| 1.225.21 \|\|

*keciccaturthaṃ kurvaṃti pretaṃ ca svapitustataḥ \|*  
*pituḥ pūrvaṃ bhavecchrāddhaṃ paraṃ naitanmataṃ mama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Some people offer the rite unto the fourth (ancestor) and then to the departed soul of one’s own father. The Śrāddha of the father shall be at the outset. But this is not approved by me.

## \|\| 1.225.22 \|\|

*sapiṇḍīkaraṇādūrdhvamekoddiṣṭaṃ na kārayet \|*  
*kṣayāhaṃ ca parityajya śastrāhata caturdaśīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Except in the case of Kṣayāha (New-Moon day) and Caturdaśī of those who are killed with weapons, one should not perform Ekoddiṣṭa after the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite.

## \|\| 1.225.23 \|\|

*yaḥ sapiṇḍīkṛtaṃ pretaṃ pṛthakpiṇḍe niyojayet \|*  
*akṛtaṃ tadvijānīyātpitṛhā copajāyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If the son (or descendant) joins with a separate rice-ball, the Preta to whom Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa has already been performed, one should know that it is almost not performed. The son then becomes the slayer of the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.225.24 \|\|

*pitā yasya tu nirvṛtto jīvate ca pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*pituḥ sa nāma saṃkīrtya kīrtayetprapitāmaham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the case of one whose father has passed away but the grandfather is alive, he shall after uttering the name of his father utter the name of the great-grandfather.

## \|\| 1.225.25 \|\|

*pitāmahastu pratyakṣaṃ bhuktvā gṛhṇāti piṇḍakam \|*  
*pitāmahakṣayāhe ca pārvaṇaṃ śrāddhamiṣyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The grandfather shall take food directly and accept the Piṇḍaka. Pārvaṇa Śraddha is recommended on the Pitāmaha Kṣayāha (day on which the grandfather passed away).

## \|\| 1.225.26 \|\|

*janakaṃ svaṃ parityajya kathaṃcinnāsya dīyate \|*  
*tasyākṛtena śrāddhena na svalpaṃ pitṛto bhayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The Śrāddha is not offered to him at all discarding one’s own father. If his Śrāddha is not performed there is no bit of fear from the Pitṛs (or from one’s father).

## \|\| 1.225.27 \|\|

*amāvāsyāsu sarvāsu mṛte pitari pārvaṇam \|*  
*nabhasyāparapakṣasya madhye caitadudāhṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If the father is dead, Pārvaṇa is performed in all the Amāvāsyās. In the middle of the latter half of Nabhasya too this is mentioned.

## \|\| 1.225.28 \|\|

*yāvatsapiṃḍatā naiva na tāvacchrāddhamācaret \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One should not perform Śrāddha unless Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa is performed.

## \|\| 1.225.29 \|\|

*janake mṛtyumāpanne śrāddhapakṣe samāgate \|*  
*pitāmahādeḥ kartavyaṃ śrāddhaṃ yannaikapiṃḍatā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At the advent of Śrāddhapakṣa if the father passes away the Śrāddha of grandfather etc. is to be performed and there is no Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa.

## Chapter 226 - Tortures in Twenty-one Hells

## \|\| 1.226.1-2 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*yataḥ sapiṃḍatā proktā pitṛpiṇḍaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*yāvatsapiṇḍatā naiva tāvatpretaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 1 \|\|*

*api dharmasamopetastapasā'pi samanvitaḥ \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇātproktā munibhistu sapiṃḍatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

1-2. Since Sapiṇḍatā is cited as (performed) all round the Pitṛpiṇḍas, the departed soul remains behind unless and until the Sapiṇḍa rite is performed even if the departed one might have been equipped with all virtues and power of penance. It is for this reason that the sages have prescribed Sapiṇḍa rites.

## \|\| 1.226.3 \|\|

*yasyayasya ca yo'nyatra yoniṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*tatrasthastṛptimāpnoti yaddattaṃ tasya vaṃśajaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The man may attain next births anywhere. Yet he gets what is offered by the members of his family even as he stays therein and becomes satisfied.

## \|\| 1.226.4 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*ye dṛśyaṃte nijāḥ svapne cirātpitṛpitāmahāḥ \|*  
*prārthayaṃti nijānkāmāṃstataḥ kiṃ syānmahāmune \|\| 4 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

4\. After a long time, the ancestors—father, grandfathers, are seen in dream. They request for the fulfilment of their desires. O great sage, what shall happen then?

## \|\| 1.226.5 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*yeṣāṃ gatirna saṃjātā pretatve ca vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*darśayaṃti ca te sarve svayamātmānameva hi \|\| 5 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

5\. Those who have not attained emancipation, those who continue to remain in the state of Preta, reveal themselves (in dreams).

## \|\| 1.226.6 \|\|

*svavaṃśyānāṃ na cānye tu satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*yathā loke'tra saṃjātā ye ca kṛtyaiḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Only they reveal themselves to their descendants, not to others. It is the truth that has been spoken by me. (They mention) how they were born in this world and how they incurred the same by means of auspicious and inauspicious activities.

## \|\| 1.226.7 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*yasya no vidyate putraḥ sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ katham \|*  
*tasya kāryaṃ bhavedatra tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

7\. If one has no son, how can one get the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite performed? It behoves you to explain this to me.

## \|\| 1.226.8-9 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*yasya no vidyate putra aurasaśca mahīpate \|*  
*caturṇāṃ svapitṝṇāṃ tu kathaṃ sa syāccaturthakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prakarṣeṇa vrajedyasmāttasmātpretaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*putreṇa bhrātrā patnyā vā tasya kāryā sapiṃḍatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

8-9. O king, if one has no bosom-born son, how can one become the fourth person among the four Pitṛs. Preta (Pra+ita) is so called because it goes (eti) With intensity (Prakarṣa). Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa should be performed for him by the son of his brother or by his wife.

## \|\| 1.226.10-12 \|\|

*caturtho yadi rājeṃdra jāyate na kathaṃcana \|*  
*kṣetrajādīnsutānetānekādaśa yathoditān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*putrapratinidhīnāhuḥ kriyālopānmanīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kāle yadi na rājeṃdra jāyate'syottarakriyā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇabaliḥ kāryaḥ pretatvasya vināśakaḥ \|*  
*yathānyeṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāmapamṛtyumupeyuṣām \|*  
*kāryaścaivātmahaṃtṝṇāṃ brāhmaṇānmṛtyumīyuṣām \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. If the fourth one is not at all born, O eminent king, they must have the representatives of the son such as the eleven types of sons like Kṣetraja etc. as mentioned before.

Learned men say that in that case, there will not be loss of rite. O great king, if the subsequent rites are not performed at the proper times, Nārāyaṇabali should be offered and it dispels the state of being Preta.

The rites in the case of those who commit suicide or meet with their death from a Brāhmaṇa, are to be performed as in the case of men who meet with premature death.

## \|\| 1.226.13-14 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ mṛtyumavāpnoti puruṣo'tra mahāmate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*svargaṃ vā narakaṃ vāpi karmaṇā kena gacchati \|*  
*mokṣaṃ vā'tha mahābhāga sarvaṃ me vista rādvada \|\| 14 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

13-14. O highly intelligent one, how does a person meet with death here? How does he go to heaven or hell? By means of which type of activity? O highly esteemed one, how does a person attain salvation? Narrate everything in detail.

## \|\| 1.226.15 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*dharmī pāpī tathā jñānī tisro'tra gatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dharmātsaṃprāpyate svargaḥ pāpānnaraka eva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

15\. The goals are of three types: (1) that of the meritorious, (2) that of a sinner and (3) that of a possessor of spiritual knowledge. Svarga (Heaven) is attained through merit (Dharma) and Naraka (Hell) alone is obtained through sin.

## \|\| 1.226.16-17 \|\|

*jñānātsaṃprāpyate mokṣaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*enamarthaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ tu bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ nṛpa \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhiro mahārāja dharmaputro nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇena saha rājeṃdra pitāmahamapṛcchata \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Salvation is obtained through spiritual wisdom. It is the truth that has been averred by me. O king, Yudhiṣṭhira, the excellent king, the son to Dharma, asked Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, this very question about the future. O leading king, at that time Kṛṣṇa was with him.

## \|\| 1.226.18 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kiyaṃto narakāḥ khyātā yamaloke pitāmaha \|*  
*kena pāpena gacchaṃti teṣu sarveṣu jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

Yudhiṣṭhira said:

18\. O Pitāmaha, how many Narakas are well-known in the world of Yama? Through what sort of sin do all the creatures go to them?

## \|\| 1.226.19 \|\|

*śrībhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*ekaviṃśatpramāṇāḥ syurnarakā yamamaṃdire \|*  
*prāṇinasteṣu gacchaṃti nijakarmānusārataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrī Bhīṣma said:

19\. The Narakas in the abode of Yama are twenty-one in number. Creatures go there in accordance with their Karmas.

## \|\| 1.226.20 \|\|

*khyātau citravicitrau ca kāyasthau yamamaṃdire \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Two Kāyasthas (scribes) in the abode of Yama are well known as Citra and Vicitra.

## \|\| 1.226.21 \|\|

*citro'tha likhate dharmaṃ sarvaṃ prāṇisamudbhavam \|*  
*vicitraḥ pātakaṃ sarvaṃ paramaṃ yatnamāsthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Citra records in writing the entire virtuous acts of a living being. Vicitra exerts himself and writes in full all the sins with great care.

## \|\| 1.226.22 \|\|

*yamadūtāḥ sadaivāṣṭau dharmarājasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*ye nayaṃti narānmṛtyulokātsvavaśagānsadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The messengers of Yama born of Dharmarāja, are eight in number. They all take men under their control (to Yama’s place) from the mortal world.

## \|\| 1.226.23 \|\|

*karālo vikarālaśca vakranāso mahodaraḥ \|*  
*saumyaḥ śāṃtastathā naṃdaḥ suvākyaścāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They are Karāla, Vikarāla, Vakranāsa, Mahodara, Saumya, Śānta, Nanda and the eighth one Suvākya.

## \|\| 1.226.24 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ ye purā proktāścatvāro raudrarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*pāpaṃ janaṃ ca te sarve nayanti yamasādanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Among these the first four are terrible in form. All of them take sinning people to the abode of Yama.

## \|\| 1.226.25 \|\|

*catvāro ye pare proktāḥ saumyarūpavapurddharāḥ \|*  
*dharmiṇaṃ te janaṃ sarvaṃ nayaṃti yamasādanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The latter four are gentle in form and features. All of them take virtuous people to the abode of Yama.

## \|\| 1.226.26 \|\|

*vimānena samārūḍhamapsarogaṇasevitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Those virtuous people ride in aerial chariots. They are attended upon by groups of Apsarās (celestial damsels).

## \|\| 1.226.27 \|\|

*likhitasyānurūpeṇa pāpadharmodbhavasya ca \|*  
*eteṣāṃ kiṃkarā ye ca teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na jāyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The people are taken in accordance with the written report about their sinful and virtuous acts. There is no limit to the servants of these people.

## \|\| 1.226.28 \|\|

*aṣṭottaraśataṃ teṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ parikalpitam \|*  
*sahāyārthaṃ yamenātra jvarayakṣmāṃtarasthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Of those servants, one hundred eight are the ailments set up to assist himself by Yama. They are the ailments beginning with fever and ending with Yakṣman (tuberculosis).

## \|\| 1.226.29 \|\|

*te gatvā vyādhayaḥ pūrvaṃ vaśe kurvaṃti mānavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Those ailments go at the outset and bring a man under their control.

## \|\| 1.226.30-31 \|\|

*yamadūtāstato gatvā nābhimūlavyavasthitam \|*  
*vāyurūpaṃ samādāya janaiḥ sarvairalakṣitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gacchaṃti yamamārgeṇa dehaṃ saṃsthāpya bhūtale \|*  
*ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yamamārgaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Then the messengers of Yama go there unobserved by all the people and seize the aerial form lying embedded at the root of the navel. They leave off the physical body on the ground and go along the Yamamārga (the pathway to Yama) which is proclaimed to be eighty-six thousand Yojanas in length.

## \|\| 1.226.32 \|\|

*tatra vaitaraṇīnāma nadī pūrvaṃ pariśrutā \|*  
*srotobhyāṃ sā mahābhāga tatra saṃsthā sadaiva hi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There is a river named Vaitaraṇī there. We have heard about it before, O highly esteemed one, that it has two perpetual streams there,

## \|\| 1.226.33 \|\|

*tatra śoṇitamekasminsrotasyasyā vaha tyalam \|*  
*śastrāṇi ca sutīkṣṇāni tanmadhye bharatarṣabha \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In one of the streams it is blood that flows. O great scion of the family of Bharata, there are very sharp weapons in its centre

## \|\| 1.226.34 \|\|

*mṛtyukāle prayacchaṃti ye dhenuṃ brāhmaṇāya vai \|*  
*tasyāḥ pucchaṃ samāśritya te taraṃti ca tāṃ nṛpa \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those who make the gift of a cow to a Brāhmaṇa at. the time of death, O king, cross that river by holding on to its tail,

## \|\| 1.226.35 \|\|

*svabāhubhistathaivānye śatayojanavistṛtam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ caiva tatsroto vaitaraṇyā vyavasthitam \|*  
*tasyāstatsalilasrāvi gamyaṃ dharmavatāṃ sadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Others cross the hundred Yojanas of width by means of their own arms. The second stream of that Vaitaraṇī consists of water always available unto the righteous.

## \|\| 1.226.36 \|\|

*ye narā gopradātāro mṛtyukāle vyavasthite \|*  
*te gopucchaṃ samāśritya tāṃ taraṃti pṛthūdakām \|*  
*anye svabāhubhiḥ kṛtvā gopradānavivarjitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those men who give cows at the time of death hold on to the tail of the cow and cross the current of profuse quantity of water. Others who had not made gifts of cows cross it by means of their arms.

## \|\| 1.226.37 \|\|

*gopradānaṃ prakartavyaṃ tasmāccaiva viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*mṛtyukāle'tra saṃprāpte ya icchedgatimātmanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Hence the gift of cows should be made at the time of death by those people who wish good goal for themselves.

## \|\| 1.226.38 \|\|

*tasyā anantaraṃ yāṃti pāpamārgeṇa pāpinaḥ \|*  
*dharmiṣṭhā dharmamārgeṇa vimānavaramāśritāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After that (after crossing Vaitaraṇī) sinners go along the Pāpamārga (path of sin). The virtuous ride on excellent aerial chariots and go along the Dharmamārga (path of virtue).

## \|\| 1.226.39 \|\|

*vaitaraṇyāḥ paraṃ pāre paṃcayojanamāyatam \|*  
*asipatravanaṃnāma pāpalokasya duḥkhadam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On the other side of Vaitaraṇī, there is a great forest named Asipatravana, five Yojanas in extent. It accords misery unto sinful people.

## \|\| 1.226.40 \|\|

*tatra lohamayānyevāsipatrāṇāṃ śatāni ca \|*  
*yāni kṛntaṃti martyānāṃ śarīrāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There are hundreds of Asipatras (sword-like leaves) made of steel in it and these cut the bodies of the men around.

## \|\| 1.226.41 \|\|

*yairhṛtaṃ paravittaṃ ca kalatraṃ ca durātmabhiḥ \|*  
*nava śrāddhāni teṣāṃ cettasmānmuktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If wicked persons had taken away the wealth of others and kidnapped other men’s wives, their bodies will be split by those leaves. If the nine Śrāddhas are performed on their behalf they will be liberated from them.

## \|\| 1.226.42 \|\|

*tasmātparataro jñeyo vikhyātaḥ kūṭaśālmaliḥ \|*  
*adhomukhāḥ pralaṃbaṃte tasminkaṃṭakasaṃkule \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It should be, known that beyond it is the well-known Naraka named Kūṭaśālmali. It is full of thorns and (the sinners) are suspended (therein) with face down.

## \|\| 1.226.43 \|\|

*adhastādvahninā caiva dahyamānā divāniśam \|*  
*viśvāsaghātakā ye ca sarvadaiva sunirdayāḥ \|*  
*tasmānmuktiṃ prayāṃti sma śrāddhe hyekādaśe kṛte \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Those who are always ruthless and are guilty of breach of trust, get scorched day and night by the fire beneath them. If Śrāddha an the eleventh day is performed they get liberated therefrom.

## \|\| 1.226.44 \|\|

*yaṃtrātmakastataḥ prokto narako dāruṇākṛtiḥ \|*  
*brahmaghnāstatra pīḍyaṃte ye cā'nye pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Beyond it, it is said, is a Naraka of horrible nature named Yantra. Brāhmaṇa-slayers and other sinful persons are tortured there.

## \|\| 1.226.45 \|\|

*śrāddhena dvādaśotthena tebhyo dattena pārthiva \|*  
*tasmānmuktiṃ pragacchanti yantrākhyanarakātsphuṭam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O king, if the twelfth-day Śrāddha is offered they get liberated completely from the Naraka called Yantra.

## \|\| 1.226.46 \|\|

*tato lohasamāḥ staṃbhā jvalamānā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*āliṃgaṃti ca tānsarvānparadāraratāśca ye \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Beyond it are well-established the furiously burning pillars. Those who had been enamoured of other men’s wives (are made to) embrace them all.

## \|\| 1.226.47 \|\|

*māsikotthe kṛte śrāddhe tebhyo muktimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If the Māsika Śrāddha (monthly Śrāddha) is performed, they will attain liberation.

## \|\| 1.226.48 \|\|

*lohadaṃṣṭrāstato raudrāḥ sārameyā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣayaṃti ca te pāpānpṛṣṭhamāṃsā śino narān \|*  
*traipakṣike kṛte śrāddhe tebhyo muktimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Beyond it stand the hideous dogs with steel-like canine teeth. These dogs bite those sinners, the men who had been biting the fleshy portion of the back (i.e. slanderers and backbiters). If Traipakṣika (performed once in three fortnights) Śrāddha is performed, they will get relief from them.

## \|\| 1.226.49-50 \|\|

*lohacaṃcumayāḥ kākāḥ saṃsthitāstadanaṃtaram \|*  
*sarāgairlocenairyaiśca īkṣitāḥ para yoṣitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ netrāṇi te ghnaṃti bhūyo jātāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*dvimāsikaṃ ca yacchrāddhaṃ tena muktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Beyond it are to be found crows with beaks of steel. They peck at the eyes of those by whom other men’s wives had been viewed with passionate eyes. While here they do have fresh eyes in plenty. If the Śrāddha is performed once in two months, they will have relief from this.

## \|\| 1.226.51 \|\|

*tataḥ śālmalikūṭastu tathānye lohakaṇṭakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhyena nīyaṃte paiśunyaniratā narāḥ \|*  
*trimāsikaṃ tu yacchrāddhaṃ tena muktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Beyond that is Śālmalikūṭa (certain trees with thornlike protuberance and iron-like thorns). Men engaged in calumny are taken through them and tortured. If the Śrāddha is performed once in three months they will have relief.

## \|\| 1.226.52 \|\|

*rauravo'tha suvikhyāto dāruṇo narako mahān \|*  
*brahmaghnānāṃ samādiṣṭaḥ sa mahākleśakārakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then there is the very well-known great Naraka named Raurava. It has been specially intended for according acute torture to slayers of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.226.53 \|\|

*chidyaṃte vividhaiḥ śastraistatrasthā ye muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*caturmāsikaśrāddhena muktisteṣāṃ prajāyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Those who are cast into it are repeatedly cut and torn with various kinds of weapons. Their salvation can be effected through the Śrāddha performed once in four months.

## \|\| 1.226.54 \|\|

*aparastu samākhyātaḥ kṣārodastu sudāruṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaghnānāṃ samādiṣṭaḥ sadaiva bahuvedanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Another extremely horrible hell is named Kṣāroda. It is always pain-giving and is particularly intended for ungrateful persons.

## \|\| 1.226.55 \|\|

*adhomukhā ūrdhva pādāḥ pīḍyaṃte yatra laṃbitāḥ \|*  
*pañcamāsikadānena muktisteṣāṃ prajāyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. They are suspended with feet up and faces down when they are tortured. Their emancipation can take place by offering Śrāddha once in five months.

## \|\| 1.226.56 \|\|

*kumbhīpākastato jñeyo narako dāruṇākṛtiḥ \|*  
*tailena kṣipyamāṇāstu yatra daṇḍābhisaṃdhitāḥ \|*  
*dṛśyaṃte janahaṃtāro bālahaṃtāra eva ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It should be known that the Naraka named Kuṃbhīpāka of extremely hideous features, is beyond that. Persons who have killed children and were guilty of genocide are hurled into (hot) oil and struck with stout sticks there.

## \|\| 1.226.57 \|\|

*pataṃti narake raudre narā viśvāsaghātakāḥ \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsikapradānena mucyaṃte tatra saṃkaṭāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Persons who betray trust fall into this horrible Naraka. They are liberated from that ordeal by offering Śrāddha once in six months.

## \|\| 1.226.58 \|\|

*sarpavṛścikasaṃyuktastathā'nyo narakaḥ śrutaḥ \|*  
*tatra ye dāṃbhikā loke te gacchanti narādhamāḥ \|*  
*saptamāsikadānena teṣāṃ muktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Similarly there is another Naraka about which it is heard that it has serpents and scorpions. Those base men who are hypocrites in the world go there. Their salvation lies in offering Śrāddha once in seven months.

## \|\| 1.226.59-60 \|\|

*tathā saṃvartakonāma narako'nyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*vedaviplāvakāḥ sādhuniṃdakāśca durātmakāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*utpāṭyate tato jihvā sandaṃśairva hnisambhavaiḥ \|*  
*svakārye ye'nṛtaṃ brūyustadgātraṃ khādyate śvabhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. There is another Naraka named Saṃvartaka. Persons of wicked souls who censure good men and insult the Vedas (are cast into it). With fiery tongs and pincers their tongues are plucked. The body of those who utter lie to achieve their ends is bitten by dogs.

## \|\| 1.226.61 \|\|

*parārthe'pi ca ye brūyusteṣāṃ gātrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamāsikadānena teṣāṃ muktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The bodies of even those who speak lies for the sake of others (are also bitten by the dogs). Their salvation becomes effective by offering Śrāddha once in eight months.

## \|\| 1.226.62 \|\|

*agnikūṭo mahāplāvo dāruṇo narako mahān \|*  
*tatra te yāṃti vai mūḍhāḥ kūṭasākṣyipradā narāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There is a great hideous hell causing great ruin, named Agnikūṭa. Those foolish men who are guilty of perjury go there.

## \|\| 1.226.63 \|\|

*tatrasthā yātanāṃ raudrāṃ sahaṃ te'tīva duḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*navamāsikadānaṃ ca teṣāmāhlādanaṃ param \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who lie there are miserable. They have to endure terrible torture. The offer of Śrāddha once in nine months causes great delight to them.

## \|\| 1.226.64-65 \|\|

*tato lohamayaiḥ kīlaiḥ saṃcito'nyaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tatra cāgnipradātāraḥ strīṇāṃ hantāra eva ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tatra dhāvaṃti duḥkhārtāstāḍyamānāśca kiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*daśamāsikajaṃ dānaṃ tatra teṣāṃ pramuktaye \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. There is another hell around, full of steel and iron spikes. Persons guilty of arson and murder of women go there. On being hit and struck by the Servants (of Yam a) they run about in great sorrow. The offer of Śrāddha once in ten months is conducive to their liberation.

## \|\| 1.226.66 \|\|

*tatoṃ'gāramayaiḥ puṃjairāvṛtābhūḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*svāmidroharatāstatra bhrāmyaṃte sarvato diśaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Beyond that is the ground covered by heaps of burning charcoals. Those who had been traitors to their masters wander there in every direction.

## \|\| 1.226.67-68 \|\|

*ekādaśodbhavaṃ dānaṃ tatra muktyai prajāyate \|*  
*saṃtaptasikatāpūrṇo narako dāruṇākṛtiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*svāminaṃ cāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*ye bhavanti narāstatra pacyaṃte te'pi duḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dvādaśamāsīyaṃ śrāddhaṃ caivopatiṣṭhati \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Śrāddha offered once in eleven months (or in the eleventh month) is conducive to liberation from there.

There is a Naraka filled with hot sands. It has terrible features. Those men who are engaged in (secret) flight on seeing that the master has arrived are cooked there. They undergo misery. Śrāddha offered in the twelfth month reaches them.

## \|\| 1.226.69 \|\|

*yatkiṃciddīyate toyamannaṃ vā vatsarāṃtare \|*  
*prabhuṃjate ca tanmārge pradattaṃ nijabāndhavaiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Whatever is offered by their kinsmen, whether it be water or cooked rice, at the close of a year these (people in the hell) eat on their way.

## \|\| 1.226.70 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvatsarādūrdhvaṃ nijakarmasamudbhavam \|*  
*śubhāśubhaṃ prapadyaṃte dharmarājasamīpagāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thereafter, beyond the year, they get auspicious or inauspicious conditions in accordance with their Karmas and remain near Dharmarāja.

## \|\| 1.226.71 \|\|

*evaṃ paṃcadaśaitāni saṃsevya narakāṇi te \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti tato janma martyaloke punarnarāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Thus after enduring the torments of these fifteen Narakas, those men are reborn into the mortal world.

## \|\| 1.226.72 \|\|

*prāpnuvaṃti videśe ca janma ye hetuvādakāḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ tarpaṇadānena teṣāṃ tṛptiḥ prajāyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Those who indulge in disputation and controversy take their birth in alien countries. Their satisfaction can be effected by offering libation every day.

## \|\| 1.226.73 \|\|

*svāmidroharatā ye ca kurājye janma cāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*haṃtakārapradānena teṣāṃ tṛptiḥ prajāyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who had been indulging in treachery towards the master, will attain their rebirth in an inglorious realm. If ‘Hantakāra’ (‘Alas, it is a pity’) is offered they will become satisfied.

## \|\| 1.226.74 \|\|

*adattvā ye naro'śnaṃti pitṛdevadvijātiṣu \|*  
*durbhikṣe janma teṣāṃ tu tena pāpena jāyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. If people take food without first offering unto the Pitṛs, Devas and Brāhmaṇas, they incur sins, whereupon they are reborn in a famine-infested area.

## \|\| 1.226.75 \|\|

*kṣayāhe śrāddhasaṃprāptau tata stṛptiḥ prajāyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. If on New-Moon day, Śrāddha is preformed they will become satisfied.

## \|\| 1.226.76 \|\|

*ye prakurvaṃti dampatyorbhedaṃ vai sānurāgayoḥ \|*  
*parasparamasatyāni teṣāṃ bhāryā'satī bhavet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If people cause dissension between a husband and his wife who love each other, by uttering falsehoods about the one to the other, their wives will be unchaste.

## \|\| 1.226.77 \|\|

*ekasminvacane prokte daśa brūte krudhānvitā \|*  
*virūpā bhramamāṇā ca sarvalokavigarhitā \|*  
*kanyādānaphalaisteṣāṃ tatrāsāṃ ca sukhaṃ bhavet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. If a woman utters ten words angrily when one is spoken to her, she becomes despicable to all the people and very ugly. She wanders here and there. If her kinsmen make gifts of virgins (in marriage) those women shall have happiness there.

## \|\| 1.226.78 \|\|

*kanyakādānavighnaṃ hi vikrayaṃ vā karoti yaḥ \|*  
*sa kanyāḥ kevalāḥ sūte na putraṃ kevalaṃ kvacit \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. He who puts an obstacle to gifts of virgins or who sells (girls) begets only daughters and never a son.

## \|\| 1.226.79 \|\|

*jāyaṃte tāśca baṃdhakyo vidhavā durbhagāstathā \|*  
*kanyādānaphala prāptyā tāsāṃ saukhyaṃ prajāyate \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Those girls (daughters of such a person) become harlots, widows and unlucky. Their happiness can be brought about as a result of gifting virgins (in marriage).

## \|\| 1.226.80 \|\|

*yairhṛtāni ca ratnāni tathā śāstrāṃtarāṇi ca \|*  
*te daridrāḥ prajāyaṃte mūkāḥ khaṃjā vicakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ śāstra pradānena iha saukhyaṃ prajāyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If jewels are stolen or other scriptural texts (are taken up) those people become poor, dumb, blind or lame. By the gift of scriptural texts here, they will have happiness there (in the other world).

## \|\| 1.226.81 \|\|

*ete tu narakāḥ proktā martyalokasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*etairvijñāyate sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thus these Narakas arising from the world of mortals (i.e. created for the punishment of sinning mortals) have been mentioned. Through these it becomes known whether an act done is good or bad.

## \|\| 1.226.82 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāphalaistasya tataḥ śuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Purity is regained as a result of pilgrimages.

## \|\| 1.226.83-84 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi narādhipa \|*  
*ekaviṃśatpramāṇaṃ ca narakāṇāṃ yathā sthitam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*bhūyaśca pṛccha rājeṃdra saṃdeho yo hṛdi sthitaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

83-84. Thus, O king, everything that I was asked has been explained to you. The Narakas number twenty-one. O leading king, if you have any doubt in your heart ask me again.

## Chapter 227 - Means to Save One from Tortures in Hells

## \|\| 1.227.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*narakāṇāṃ svarūpaṃ ca śrutvā me bhayamāgatam \|*  
*kathaṃ muktirbhavetteṣāṃ pāpānāmapi pārthiva \|*  
*vratairvā niyamairvāpi homairvā tīrthasaṃśrayaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Yudhiṣṭhira said:

1\. Fear has gripped me after listening to the description of the Narakas. O king, how can even those persons be liberated who have committed sins? Is it through Vratas, observances of restraints, Homas or by resorting to holy centres and shrines?

## \|\| 1.227.2 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*gaṃgāyāmasthipāto'tra yeṣāṃ saṃjāyate nṛṇām \|*  
*na teṣāṃ nārako vahniḥ prabhavenmadhyavartinām \|\| 2 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

2\. If bones of the men are cast into Gaṅgā the Naraka (hellish) fire is incapable of adversely affecting those people remaining in between (dead but not having attained the final results of Karmas).

## \|\| 1.227.3 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāṃ kriyate śrāddhaṃ yeṣāṃ nāmnā svakaiḥ sutaiḥ \|*  
*te vimānaṃ samāśritya prayāṃti narakopari \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. If Śrāddha is performed in Gaṅgā by the sons (and descendants in their name,) those ancestors go beyond the Naraka, after being seated in an aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.227.4 \|\|

*pāpaṃ kṛtvā prakurvaṃti prāyaścittaṃ yathoditam \|*  
*hema yacchaṃti vā bhūpa na teṣāṃ narako bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After committing a sin, O king, if the people perform expiatory rites as laid down or make gifts of gold, they will not fall into Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.5 \|\|

*śeṣāḥ svakarmaṇaḥ prāptyā sevaṃte ca yathocitam \|*  
*svarga vā narakaṃ vāpi sevante te narādhipa \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The remaining ones attain Svarga or Naraka in accordance with their Karma, O king.

## \|\| 1.227.6 \|\|

*dhārātīrthe mriyaṃte ye svāminaḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*te gacchaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ narakāṇāṃ sudūrataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who die in front of their master in Dhārātīrtha (holy Tīrtha in the form of battle) (i.e. those who die in battle on behalf of their king) attain the greatest goal far beyond Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.7 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ kurukṣetre naimiṣe nāgare pure \|*  
*prayāge vā prabhāse vā yastyajettanumā tmanaḥ \|*  
*mahāpātakayukto'pi narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He who casts off his body in Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, Nāgarapura (i.e. Vadnagara), Prayāga or Prabhāsa will never see Naraka even if he has incurred Mahāpātakas (great sins).

## \|\| 1.227.8 \|\|

*nīlo vā vṛṣabho yasya vivāhe saṃniyujyate \|*  
*svaputreṇa na saṃpaśyennarakaṃ brahmahā'pi saḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If one’s own son performs the rite of Utsarga (dedicatory release) of a dark bull along with the celebration of its marriage with a heifer, he will never see Naraka even if he happens to be a Brāhmaṇa-slayer.

## \|\| 1.227.9 \|\|

*prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtvā hṛdayasthe janārdane \|*  
*yastyajetpuruṣaḥ prāṇānnarakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After adopting Prāyopaveśana (religious fast unto death) with due meditation on Janārdana, if a person casts off his life, he never sees Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.10 \|\|

*prāyopaveśanaṃ yo ca citreśvaraniveśane \|*  
*kurvanti narakaṃ naiva te gacchaṃti kadācana \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those who perform Prāyopaveśana in the holy shrine Citreśvara will never fall into Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.11 \|\|

*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇānāṃ ca pathiśramamupeyuṣām \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparāṇāṃ ca yo yacchati sadā'śanam \|*  
*kāle vā yadi vā'kāle narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He who serves food in time or out of time to the distressed, the blind and the miserable while they are going on a pilgrimage and are excessively fatigued on the way, never sees a hell.

## \|\| 1.227.12 \|\|

*jaladhenuṃ ca yo dadyāddhṛṣasaṃsthe divākare \|*  
*tiladhenuṃ mṛgasthe ca narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He who makes the gift of Jaladhenu (water in the shape of a cow’s mouth) when the Sun is in Taurus or Tiladhenu (gingelly seeds in the shape of a cow) when the Sun is in Capricorn never sees Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.13 \|\|

*some somagrahe caiva somanāthasya darśanāt \|*  
*samudre ca sarasvatyāṃ snātvā na narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By viewing Somanātha on a Monday or at the time of lunar eclipse and by taking the holy dip in the ocean or in Sarasvatī, one never goes to hell.

## \|\| 1.227.14 \|\|

*sannihityāṃ kurukṣetre rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*sūryavāreṇa yaḥ yāti narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He who takes his holy bath in river Sannihiti in Kurukṣetra on a Sunday when there is solar eclipse (when Rāhu swallows the Sun), never sees Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.15 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge yaḥ karoti pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*tripuṣkarasya maunena narakaṃ na sa paśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He who silently circumambulates Tripuṣkara on Full-Moon day in the month of Kārttika when the constellation is Kṛttikā, never sees Naraka.

## \|\| 1.227.16 \|\|

*mṛgasaṃkramaṇe ye tu sūryavāreṇa saṃsthite \|*  
*caṇḍīśaṃ vīkṣayaṃti sma na te narakagāminaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those who view Caṇḍīśa at the time of the transit of the Sun into Capricorn on a Sunday, never fall into hell.

## \|\| 1.227.17 \|\|

*gāṃ paṃkādbrāhmaṇīṃ dāsyātsādhūnstenāddvijaṃ vadhāt \|*  
*mocayanti ca ye rājanna te narakagāminaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O king, those who save a cow from quagmire, a Brāhmaṇa lady from slavery, good people from a thief, a Brāhmaṇa from murder, never fall into hell.

## \|\| 1.227.18 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi narādhipa \|*  
*yathā na narakaṃ yāti puruṣastu svakarmaṇā \|*  
*yathā ca narakaṃ yāti svalpapāpo'pi mānavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus, O king, everything I was asked has been narrated to you, viz. How a man falls into hell even if he commits a minor sin and how he avoids falling therein by means of his (good) activities.

## Chapter 228 - Disobedience by Andhakāsura

## \|\| 1.228.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyacca biladvāri śayanārthe vyavasthitam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā pramucyate pāpī devaṃ ca jalaśāyinam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*snātvā tasminbiladvāre pavitre lokasaṃśraye \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā śeṣaparyaṃkaśāyinam \|*  
*ājanmamaraṇātpāpātsa ca muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*caturo vārṣikānmāsānsuprasuptaṃ sureśvaram \|*  
*saṃpūjayati yo bhaktyā na sa bhūyo'tra jāyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. There is another deity at the entrance to the cave. By viewing the Lord engaged in sleeping and lying down in water (i.e. Viṣṇu) even a sinner becomes liberated.

After taking his bath at the entrance to the cave, that is a holy resort to all the worlds, the devotee should adore with great devotion the Lord lying on. his bedstead of Śeṣa. He shall attain liberation from the sins committed between birth and death.

He who devoutly worships the Lord of Suras who has sound sleep for the four months of the rainy season is not reborn here again.

## \|\| 1.228.4-5 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ mahābhāgā munayaḥ sevya taṃ prabhum \|*  
*mṛttikāgrahaṇaṃ kṛtvā tasya cāyatane śubhe \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ tadriṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*yatphalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ tasya pūjāyāṃ cāturmāsyāṃ prajāyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Formerly the highly esteemed sages adored (and served) that Lord. They took the clay from his splendid shrine. Thereby they attained the great place, the great region of Viṣṇu. From this Lord’s adoration during these four months, one gets that benefit which accrues from all the Tīrthas and all the Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.228.6 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ gograhe mṛtyuṃ saṃprāptā yāṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ caturo māsānpūjayā jalaśāyinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By the adoration of Jalaśāyin (Lord Viṣṇu) for four months, men attain that merit which men obtain after meeting with death while saving a cow.

## \|\| 1.228.7 \|\|

*api pāpasamācāraḥ paradārarato'pica \|*  
*brahmaghno'pi surāpo'pi strīhantā'pi vigarhitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayā caturo māsāṃstasya devasya mucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Even a man of sinful conduct, one who indulges in other men’s wives, a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, a person who regularly drinks liquor and a despised person that murders women, becomes liberated through the adoration of the Lord for these four months.

## \|\| 1.228.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tatrasthaṃ jalaśāyinam \|*  
*biladvāre kathaṃ sūta tatra naḥ saṃśayo mahān \|\| 8 \|\|*

The sages said:

8\. It has been said by Your Holiness that the Lord there lies down in water at the entrance to the cave. O Sūta, we have a great doubt there.

## \|\| 1.228.9 \|\|

*sa kila śrūyate devaḥ kṣīrābdhau madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*sadaiva bhagavāñchete yoganidrāṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It is heard that Lord Madhusūdana lies down in the Milk Ocean resorting to the yogic slumber for ever.

## \|\| 1.228.10 \|\|

*kathaṃ sa bhagavāñchete biladvāre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*etatkīrtaya kārtsnyena paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. How does that Lord settle down at the entrance to the cave and lie down there? Do narrate this entirely. We have great deal of interest therein.

## \|\| 1.228.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāgāḥ kṣīrābdhau madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*yoganidrāṃ gataḥ śete śeṣaparyaṃkaśā yakaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sūta said:

11\. O highly esteemed ones, it is true that Madhusūdana (Viṣṇu) lies down on his couch of Śeṣa in his yogic slumber in the Milk Ocean.

## \|\| 1.228.12 \|\|

*sa yathā tatra kṣetre tu saṃśrito bhagavānsvayam \|*  
*jalaśāyisvarūpeṇa tacchṛśudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Listen with attention as to how that Lord himself resorted to that holy place in the form of Jalaśāyin.

## \|\| 1.228.13 \|\|

*yathā ca caturo māsānpūjitastatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*muktiṃ dadāti puṃsāṃ sa tathā saṃkīrtayāmyaham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I shall describe how he grants salvation to men on being adored for four months as staying there well settled.

## \|\| 1.228.14 \|\|

*catvāro'pi yathā māsā garhaṇīyā dharātale \|*  
*sarvakarmasu mukhyeṣu yajñodvā hādiṣu dvijāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. During these four months are to be avoided all holy rites, and important ceremonies like Yajñas, marriages etc., O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.228.15 \|\|

*tadvo'haṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi namaskṛtya dvijotamāḥ \|*  
*tasmai devādhidevāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, after bowing down to that Lord of Devas, one endowed with all the Guṇas within, though without attributes, I shall explain it unto you.

## \|\| 1.228.16 \|\|

*avyaktāyā'prameyāya sarvadevamayāya ca \|*  
*sarvajñāya kavīśāya sarvabhūtātmane tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance unto that unmanifest one, identical with all the Devas, the omnicient one, the Lord of Kavis (Seers and Poets) and the soul of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.228.17 \|\|

*purāsīddānavo raudro hiraṇyakaśipurmahān \|*  
*nārasiṃhaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā viṣṇunā yo nipātitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Once upon a time (in days of yore) there was a terrible Dānava, the great Hiraṇyakaśipu, who was struck down by Viṣṇu after assuming the body of Man-lion.

## \|\| 1.228.18 \|\|

*tasya putradvayaṃ jajñe sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*prahlādaścāṃdhakaścaiva vīryeṇāpratimau yudhi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He had two sons Prahlāda and Andhaka who were endowed with all (auspicious) characteristics and were unrivalled in battlefield.

## \|\| 1.228.19 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipau prāpte paraṃ lokaṃ mahāsure \|*  
*amātyairabhiṣekāya prahlādaḥ sa niyojitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the great Asura, Hiraṇyakaśipu passed on to the other world, Prahlāda was persuaded by the ministers to get himself crowned.

## \|\| 1.228.20 \|\|

*sa naicchata tadā rājyaṃ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat \|*  
*samāgatamapi prājño yasmāttadvo vadāmyaham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He never desired that great kingdom belonging to his father and grandfather that came to him (by succession). He was such a wise demon. Why he did so I shall explain.

## \|\| 1.228.21 \|\|

*dānavānāṃ sadā dveṣo devena saha cakriṇā \|*  
*na karoti punardveṣaṃ taṃ samuddiśya sarvadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Dānavas have a permanent hatred for the Discus-bearing Lord. But he never had any hatred at all for him.

## \|\| 1.228.22 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇātsarve tena tyaktā diteḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*svarājyamapi saṃtyajya viṣṇustena samāśritaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For this reason all the sons of Diti were abandoned by him. Even abandoning his own kingdom, he resorted to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.228.23 \|\|

*tatastairdānavaiḥ kṣudrairviṣṇudveṣaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*andhakaḥ sthāpito rājye pitṛpaitāmahe tadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereupon, Andhaka was set up on the hereditary realm by the petty-minded Dānavas bent upon hating Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.228.24 \|\|

*andhako'pi samārādhya devadevaṃ caturmukham \|*  
*amaratvaṃ tato lebhe yāvaccandrārkatārakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By propitiating the Four-faced Lord of Devas, Andhaka obtained immortality as long as the Sun, the Moon and the stars shine.

## \|\| 1.228.25 \|\|

*varapuṣṭastataḥ so'pi cakre śakreṇa vigraham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Being well equipped thus, thanks to the boon, he started confrontation with Śakra.

## \|\| 1.228.26 \|\|

*jitvā śakraṃ mahāsaṃkhye yajñāṃśāñjagṛhe svayam \|*  
*gatvā'marāvatīṃ daityo niḥsārya ca śatakratum \|*  
*svavargeṇa samopetaḥ svargaṃ samaharattadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He defeated Śakra in the great battle. He forcibly seized the shares (of gods) in the Yajñas, He went to Amarāvatī and drove Śatakratu out. Accompanied by his own people he captured Svarga.

## \|\| 1.228.27 \|\|

*śakro'pi ca samārādhya śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*sarvadevasamopeto bhṛtyavatparivartate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śakra propitiated Śaṅkara, the benefactor of all the worlds. He served the Lord like a servant accompanied by all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.228.28 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tasya tuṣṭaḥ pinākadhṛk \|*  
*taṃ prāha varado'smīti vada śakra karomi kim \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After a great deal of time, the Pināka-bearing Lord became pleased with him. He said to him: “I shall grant you a boon, O Śakra, tell me, what I should do.”

## \|\| 1.228.29 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*aṃdhakena hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ mama vīryātsureśvara \|*  
*yajñabhāgaiḥ samopetaṃ hatvā'śu tatprayaccha me \|\| 29 \|\|*

Indra said:

29\. O Lord of Suras, Andhaka has taken away my kingdom forcibly, Retrieve it from him quickly along with the shares in the Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.228.30 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tasya dīnasya bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*provāca tava dāsyāmi rājyaṃ trailokyasaṃbhavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On hearing the words of the distressed one, the Moon-crested Lord said: “I shall give you the kingdom of the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.228.31-33 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa dūtaṃ tasya vicakṣaṇam \|*  
*gaṇeśaṃ vīrabhadrākhyaṃ gatvā taṃ brūhi cāṃdhakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mamādeśātparityajya svargaṃ gaccha dharātalam \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahaṃ sthānaṃ rājyaṃ tatra samācara \|\| 32 \|\|*

*parityajasva yajñāṃśānno ceddhaṃtāsmi satvaram \|*  
*sa gatvā cāṃdhakaṃ prāha yathoktaṃ śaṃbhunā sphuṭam \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. He sent his efficient leader of the Gaṇas named Vīrabhadra as a messenger to him: “Go and tell Andhaka: ‘It is my command that you leave off Svarga. Go to the earth, your traditional abode, and rule over that kingdom. Renounce the shares in the Yajñas. If not I will kill you quickly.’

He then went to Andhaka and conveyed to him clearly what was said by Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 1.228.34 \|\|

*saviśeṣamahābuddhiḥ svāmikāryaprasiddhaye \|*  
*atha taṃ cādhakaḥ prāha pravihasya mahābalaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The leader of the Gaṇas, of exceptionally great intellect, did everything towards the fulfilment of the task of his Lord. Thereupon, the excessively powerful Andhaka laughed and said:

## \|\| 1.228.35-39 \|\|

*avadhyo hi yathā dūtastena tvāṃ na nihanmyaham \|*  
*ka syādvai śaṃkaronāma yo māmevaṃ prabhāṣate \|\| 35 \|\|*

*na māṃ vetti sa kiṃ mūḍhaḥ kiṃ vā mṛtyu mabhīpsate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*athavā satyamevaitānnirviṇṇo jīvitācca saḥ \|*  
*daridropahato nityaṃ sarvabhogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*smaśāne krīḍanaṃ yasya bhasma gātravilepanam \|*  
*bhūṣaṇaṃ cāhayo vastraṃ diśo yasya jaṭālakā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kastasya jīvitenārthastenedaṃ māṃ bravīti saḥ \|*  
*tasmādgatvā drutaṃ brūhi madvākyaṃ dūta sasphuṭam \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. “As it is, a messenger should not be killed. Therefore, I am not killing you. By the way, who can this Śaṅkara be who dares to speak to me thus? Does’t \[Doesn’t\] that deluded one know me? Or does he wish for his own death?

Or this may be the truth. He is disgusted with life. He is oppressed with perpetual poverty. He is without the enjoyment of any pleasure. His playground is the cremation ground. Ashes constitute his physical unguent. The serpents are his ornaments. The quarters are his garments and matted hairs are his forelocks of hair.

How can such a man have any interest in life? This is why he speaks to the thus. So, O messenger, go immediately and convey to him these words of mine:

## \|\| 1.228.40-41 \|\|

*tyaktvā kailāsamenaṃ tvaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ tapaḥ kuru \|*  
*mayā sthānamidaṃ dattaṃ kailāsaṃ svasutasya ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vṛkasyāpi na sandeho vibhavena samanvitam \|*  
*no cetprāṇānhariṣyāmi seṃdrasya tava śaṃkara \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. ‘Leave off this Kailāsa. Go to Vārāṇasī and perform penance. This place Kailāsa has been granted to my son Vṛka by me along with all its riches. There is no doubt about it Otherwise, O Śaṅkara, I will take away your life along with that of Indra.’

## \|\| 1.228.42 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vīrabhadrastu nirbhartsya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*krodhena mahatāviṣṭaḥ kailāsaṃ samupāviśat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing it, Vīrabhadra rebuked him repeatedly, infuriated excessively, he went back to Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.228.43 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa tadvākyaṃ ca pinākinaḥ \|*  
*atikrūraṃ viśeṣeṇa tata kruddhaḥ pinākadhṛk \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then he told Pinākin about the harsh words of the Dānava. That infuriated the Wielder of Pināka Bow.

## Chapter 229 - Birth of Bhṛṅgīriṭi

## \|\| 1.229.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare śambhurgaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*indrādyaiśca suraiḥ sarveḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*jagāma vṛṣamāruhya purīṃ caivāmarāvatīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. In the meantime, Śaṃbhu, with eyes turned red due to anger, mounted his bull and proceeded towards Amarāvatī. He was accompanied by all his Gaṇas and all the Suras beginning with Indra.

## \|\| 1.229.2 \|\|

*aṃdhako'pi samālokya saṃprāptāṃ devavāhinīm \|*  
*sagaṇāṃ ca mahādevaṃ paritoṣaṃ paraṃ gataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On seeing that the army of Devas and Mahādeva along with his Gaṇas had arrived Andhaka attained great delight.

## \|\| 1.229.3 \|\|

*niścakrāmātha yuddhāya balena caturaṃgiṇā \|*  
*varaṃ syaṃdanamāruhya suśvetāśvavahaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then he came out for battle along with his army consisting of four divisions. He got into his excellent chariot fitted with horses of splendid white colour.

## \|\| 1.229.4 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*gaṇaiśca vikṛtākārairmṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then a battle ensued between the Dānavas and the Devas as well as the Gaṇas of hideous shapes making death to the point of no return (i.e. no return from battle till death).

## \|\| 1.229.5 \|\|

*ekavarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ yāvadyuddhamavartata \|*  
*dinedine kṣayaṃ yāṃti tatra devā na dānavāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. For a full thousand years the battle (war) lasted. The (strength of) Devas became dwindled day by day but not that of the Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.229.6 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte saṃkruddhaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ \|*  
*triśūlena samudyamya svahastena vyabhedayat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At the close of a thousand years, the infuriated Moon-crested Lord raised his trident and pierced him (Andhaka) with his own hand.

## \|\| 1.229.7 \|\|

*sa viddho'pi svayaṃ tena triśūlena mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇo varamāhātmyānnaiva prāṇaiviryujyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Though pierced with that trident, the great Asura did not meet with his death, thanks to the power of the boon of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.229.8 \|\|

*tato bhūyo'pi cotthāya cakre yuddhaṃ mahātmanā \|*  
*jaghāna ca sa saṃkruddho viśeṣeṇa bahūngaṇān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He rose up again and fought with the great Ātman (Śiva). In his fury he killed many Gaṇas.

## \|\| 1.229.9 \|\|

*śaṃkaraṃ tāḍayāmāsa gadāghātairmuhurmuhuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He repeatedly struck Śaṅkara with his mace.

## \|\| 1.229.10 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃtamabhūtsārddhaṃ pinākinā \|*  
*raudraṃ yuddhamandhakasya sarvalokabhayāvaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus the terrible fight of Andhaka with the Pināka-bearing Lord continued for a thousand years. It instilled terror into all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.229.11-13 \|\|

*triśūlabhinno daityaḥ sa yadā mṛtyuṃ na gacchati \|*  
*utthāyotthāya kurute prahārāngadayā balī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tathā taṃ śaṃkaro jñātvā mṛtyunā parivarjitam \|*  
*brahmaṇo varadānena sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tato nirbhidya śūlāgraiḥ protkṣipya gaganāṃgaṇe \|*  
*chatravaddhārayāmāsa laṃbamānamadhomukham \|*  
*akṣaradrudhiraṃ bhūmau gātrebhyo varṣmasaṃbhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. The Daitya did not meet with his death though pierced with the trident. The powerful demon rose up again and again and began to hit (the enemies) with his club. Śaṅkara realized that he was not to be killed (he could not be killed) by any of the Heaven-dwellers, by the power of the boon granted by Brahmā: He pierced the Daitya, with the tip of his trident and raised him up in the sky.

He lifted the trident like an umbrella even as he (Andhaka) hung with face down. Blood oozed out of his body and fell on the Ground.

## \|\| 1.229.14 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃte carmāsthi snāyureva ca \|*  
*dhātutrayaṃ sthitaṃ tasya naṣṭamanyaccatuṣṭayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At the close of a thousand years only three of the constituents of his body, viz. skin, bone and sinews, remained. The remaining four were lost.

## \|\| 1.229.15 \|\|

*sa jñātvā bala saṃhīnamātmānaṃ dhātusaṃkṣayāt \|*  
*sāmopāyaṃ tataścake stutvā sārdhaṃ pinākinā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Realizing that he had become feeble due to the wastage of the constituents of his body, he adopted conciliatory tactics with the Pināka-bearing Lord by eulogizing him.

## \|\| 1.229.16 \|\|

*andhaka uvāca \|*  
*na tvaṃ devo mayā jñāto vāgduṣṭena durātmanā \|*  
*īdṛgvīryasamopetastadyuktaṃ bhavatā kṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Andhaka said:

16\. I am an evil soul and defiled in speech. Hence I did not know that you have such vigour as this. Hence what is done by you is proper.

## \|\| 1.229.17 \|\|

*anurūpaṃ madāṃdhasyāvivekasya surottama \|*  
*svavīryamadayuktasya viveka rahitasya ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent one among Suras, this is proper for me who have become blind due to pride and am bereft of the power of discrimination. I am over-arrogant due to my prowess and am left without discretion.

## \|\| 1.229.18 \|\|

*durvinītaḥ śriyaṃ prāpya vidyāmaiśvaryamevaca \|*  
*na tiṣṭhati ciraṃ kālaṃ yathā'haṃ madagarvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. An impudent fellow without humility cannot stay long even after obtaining fortune, learning and prowess as in my own case. I am over-puffed up due to arrogance.

## \|\| 1.229.19 \|\|

*pāpo'haṃ pāpakarmā'haṃ pāpātmā pāpasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*trāhi māṃ deva īśāna sarvapāpaharo bhava \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I am a sinner. I have been indulging in sinful activities. Even my very soul is sinful. I am born of sin. O Lord Īśāna, save me. Be the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 1.229.20 \|\|

*duḥkhito'haṃ varāko'haṃ dīno'haṃ śaktivarjitaḥ \|*  
*trātumarhasi māṃ deva prapannaṃ śaraṇaṃ vibho \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I am grief-stricken. I am a piteous creature. I am a wretched one devoid of power. O Lord, it behoves you to save me. O Lord, I have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 1.229.21 \|\|

*duṣṭo'haṃ pāpayukto'haṃ sāṃprataṃ parameśvara \|*  
*tena buddhiriyaṃ jātā tavopari mamānagha \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I am a wicked one. O Parameśvara, I am a sinner. Hence this thought about you has risen in me, O sinless one.

## \|\| 1.229.22 \|\|

*sarvapāpakṣaye jāte śive bhavati bhāvanā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When all the sins are destroyed, one begins to contemplate on Śiva.

## \|\| 1.229.23 \|\|

*nāmamātramapi tryakṣa yaste kīrtayati prabho \|*  
*so'pi muktimavāpnoti kiṃ punaḥ pūjane rataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Three-eyed Lord, he who simply repeats your name, attains salvation. Why not then one who is engaged in your worship?

## \|\| 1.229.24 \|\|

*tava pūjā vihīnānāṃ dinānyāyāṃti yāṃti ca \|*  
*yāni deva mṛtānāṃ ca tāni yāṃti na jīvatām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Days come and go in the case of those devoid of your worship. Those of the dead cannot come back to the living.

## \|\| 1.229.25 \|\|

*kuṣṭhī vā rogayukto vā paṃgurvā badhiro'pi vā \|*  
*mā bhūttasya kule janma śaṃbhuryatra na devatā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. (Let me be) a leper, a sickly one, a lame or a deaf one. But let not (my) birth be in the family of that person to whom Śaṃbhu is not a deity.

## \|\| 1.229.26 \|\|

*tasmānmocaya māṃ deva svāgataṃ kuru sāṃpratam \|*  
*gato me dānavo bhāvastyaktaṃ rājyaṃ tathā vibho \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hence, O Lord, release me. Welcome me now. My demoniac nature has gone away. The kingdom has been left off by me, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.229.27 \|\|

*tyaktāḥ putrāśca pautrāśca patnyaśca vibhavaiḥ saha \|*  
*triḥ satyena suraśreṣṭha tava pādau spṛśāmyaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. My sons, my grandsons and wives, along with my riches have been abandoned by me. O most excellent one among the Suras, uttering the solemn oath thrice I touch your feet.

## \|\| 1.229.28-30 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā jñātvā taṃ gatakalmaṣam \|*  
*uttārya śanakaiḥ śūlādvinayāvanataṃ sthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tato nāma svayaṃ cakre bhṛṃgirīṭiriti prabhuḥ \|*  
*abravīcca sadā me tvaṃ vallabhaḥ saṃbhaviṣyasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nandino'pi gajāsyasya mahākālasya putraka \|*  
*tiṣṭha saumya mayā saukhyaṃ na smariṣyasi bāṃdhavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. On hearing his words, the Lord knew for certain that he had been rid of sins. He was slowly lowered down from the trident and he stood there humbly. The Lord then named him Bhṛṅgīriṭi, and said: “You will always be my favourite. O dear son, you will also be a favourite of Nandin, Mahākāla and the Elephant-faced One (Gaṇeśa). O gentle one, stay here happily. You will never remember your kinsmen.”

## \|\| 1.229.31 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya praṇamya śaśiśekharam \|*  
*tasthau sarvagaṇairyuktaḥ prabhusaṃśrayasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He promised, “So it shall be”. He bowed down to the Moon-crested One. He stayed there along with all the Gaṇas and took refuge in the Lord.

## Chapter 230 - Vṛka’s Conquest of Indra’s Kingdom

## \|\| 1.230.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ gaṇatvamāpanne hyandhake dānavottame \|*  
*tasya putro vṛkonāma nirutsāho dviṣajjaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhayena mahatā yukto hataśeṣaiśca dānavaiḥ \|*  
*praviveśa samudrāṃtaṃ sudurgaṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ śakraḥ prahṛṣṭātmā praṇamya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*tasyādeśaṃ samāsādya praviveśāmarāvatīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

*cakāra ca sukhī rājyaṃ trailokye'pi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yajñabhāgānpunarlebhe yathārthaṃ ca dharātale \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Thus, when the excellent Dānava Andhaka attained the status of Gaṇa, his son named Vṛka became disinterested in conquering the enemies.

He was terrified extremely, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Along with the Dānavas that survived he entered the inner region of the ocean that cannot be easily approached.

Thereupon, Śakra becaṃe delighted in mind. He bowed down to the Bull-emblemed One and with his permission entered Amarāvati.

O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he ruled over the kingdom of all the three worlds happily. He regained his usual shares in the Yajñas performed on the earth.

## \|\| 1.230.5 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu hyaṃdhakasya suto vṛkaḥ \|*  
*niṣkramya sāgarāttūrṇaṃ jaṃbudvīpaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the meantime, Vṛka, the son of Andhaka, quickly came out of the ocean and reached Jaṃbūdvīpa.

## \|\| 1.230.6-7 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ matvā puṇyaṃ susiddhidam \|*  
*pitrā yatra tapastaptamaṃdhakena durātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saguptastu tapastepe'yathā vetti na kaścana \|*  
*dhyāyamānaḥ suraśreṣṭhaṃ bhaktyā kamalasaṃbhavam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He believed that the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara was highly meritorious and it yielded excellent Siddhi. \[Here?\] his father Andhaka, when he was a wicked one, had performed penance.

He (Vṛka) remained there well concealed without the knowledge of anyone. He performed penance there. He meditated devoutly upon the Lotus-born Lord, the most excellent one among Suras.

## \|\| 1.230.8 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ jalāhāro dvitīyakam \|*  
*tapastepe sa daityendro dhyāyamānaḥ pitāmaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He thus performed a penance for a thousand years. For another thousand years the leading Daitya meditated on Pitāmaha and performed the penance subsisting on water.

## \|\| 1.230.9 \|\|

*vāyubhakṣastato jātastāvatkālaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhāgreṇa bhūpṛṣṭhaṃ sparśamāno jitendriyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, for the same period of time, he had the intake of air only. Conquering all the sense-organs, he remained touching the ground with the tip of his toe.

## \|\| 1.230.10 \|\|

*evaṃ ca pañcame prāpte sahasre dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*brahmā tasya gatastuṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya tapo mahat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, when the fifth millennium arrived, Brahmā became pleased op observing his great penance.

## \|\| 1.230.11-12 \|\|

*tato'bravīttamāgatya tāṃ gartāṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*bhobho vṛka nivartasva tapaso'smātsudāruṇāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yo nityaṃ mana si sthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he came to that Gartā (chasm where he stayed) and said to him: “O Vṛka, desist from this terrible penance, Welfare unto you. Choose as boon what has been always cherished by you in the mind.”

## \|\| 1.230.13 \|\|

*vṛka uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*jarāmaraṇahīnaṃ māṃ tatkuruṣva pitāmaha \|\| 13 \|\|*

Vṛka said:

13\. O Lord Pitāmaha, if you are pleased with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, then make me free from old age and death.

## \|\| 1.230.14 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*mama prasādato vatsa jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyasi na sandehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

14\. O dear one, you will become free from old age and death, with my favour. There is no doubt about it. It is the truth that has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.230.15 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato brahmā tatraivāṃtaradhī yata \|*  
*vṛko'pi kṛtakṛtyastvāgataśca svagṛhaṃ pituḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After saying thus, Brahmā vanished there itself. Well contented, Vṛka returned to his own father’s abode.

## \|\| 1.230.16 \|\|

*giriṃ raivatakaṃ nāma sarvartukusumojjvalam \|*  
*tatra gatvā nijāmātyaiḥ samaṃ mantrya ca satva ram \|*  
*indropari tataścakre yānaṃ yuddhaparīpsayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He went to the mountain named Raivataka that remains splendid with the flowers of all the seasons. There he took counsel with his ministers immediately. Then with a desire to fight with Indra he marched against him.

## \|\| 1.230.17-18 \|\|

*iṃdro'pi ca parijñāya dānavaṃ taṃ mahābalam \|*  
*jarāmṛtyuparityaktaṃ prabhāvātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*parityajya bhayāccaiva purīṃ caivāmarāvatīm \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gatastūrṇaṃ devaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Indra realized that the powerful Dānava was free from death and old age due to the power of Parameṣṭhin. He then forsook Amarāvatī, his city, due to fear and hurriedly went to the world of Brahmā accompanied by all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.230.19 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto vṛkaśca tridaśālaye \|*  
*sasainyaparivāreṇa prahṛṣṭena samanvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the meantime, Vṛka too reached heaven accompanied by his delighted attendants and soldiers.

## \|\| 1.230.20 \|\|

*tataścaiṃdrapade tasminsvayameva vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*śukrātprāpyābhiṣekaṃ ca puṣpasnānasamudbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then he underwent the coronation ceremony along with floral bath administered by Śukra and set himself in the position (place) of Indra.

## \|\| 1.230.21 \|\|

*so'bhiṣiktastu śukreṇa devarājyapade vṛkaḥ \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa daiteyāndevatānāṃ padeṣu ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Having been crowned in the realm of the Devas by Śukra, Vṛka established (appointed) Daityas in the posts of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.230.22 \|\|

*ādityānāṃ vasūnāṃ ca rudrāṇāṃ marutāmapi \|*  
*yajñabhāgakṛte viprāḥ śukraśāsanamāśritāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of the shares in the Yajñas, they subjected themselves to the control of Śukra and appropriated the shares of Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras and Maruts.

## Chapter 231 - Importance of Ekādaśī Vrata

## \|\| 1.231.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vṛko'pi tatsamāsādya rājyaṃ trailokyasaṃbhavam \|*  
*yadṛcchayā jagatsarvaṃ samājñāpayattadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*soṃ'dhakasya bale vīrye dhairye kope ca dānavaḥ \|*  
*sahasraguṇitaścāsīdraudraḥ paramadāruṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare kaścinna martyo yajati kṣitau \|*  
*na homaṃ naiva jāpyaṃ ca daityāñjñātvā surāspade \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. After gaining control over the kingdom of the three worlds by chance, he commanded the entire universe (with certain do’s and don’t’s).

He had a thousand times more of strength, vitality, courage and fury than that of Andhaka. He was highly hideous and horrible.

No man on the earth was to perform Yajña, Homa and Jāpa, (This order he promulgated) after being convinced that the Daityas were well-established in the position of the Suras.

## \|\| 1.231.4 \|\|

*atha yaḥ kurute dharmaṃ homaṃ vā japameva vā \|*  
*suguptasthānamāsādya karotyamaratuṣṭaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There were a few devout fellows. Whenever they wanted to perform holy rites, Homa or Japa in order to propitiate the Devas, they did so after resorting to a secret place.

## \|\| 1.231.5 \|\|

*atha svargasthitā daityā yajñabhāgavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*tathā martyodbhavairbhāgaiḥ saṃdehaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then, the Daityas staying in Svarga, became deprived of shares in the Yajñas. They became highly suspicious on account of the shares received from human beings.

## \|\| 1.231.6 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā preṣayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|*  
*martyaloke carānguptānnipuṇāṃścābravīttataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereupon, the Dānava became extremely furious. He sent efficient secret agents to the mortal world and ordered them:

## \|\| 1.231.7 \|\|

*yaḥ kaściddevatānāṃ ca pragṛhṇāti karoti ca \|*  
*tadarthaṃ yajanaṃ homaṃ dānaṃ vā pṛthivītale \|*  
*sa ca vadhyaśca yuṣmābhirmama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “Whoever performs Yajña, Homa or Dāna on the earth for Devas and whoever among Devas accepts it, should be killed by you all unhesitatingly. That is my order.”

## \|\| 1.231.8 \|\|

*atha te tadvacaḥ śrutvā dānavā balavattarāḥ \|*  
*gatvā ca medinīpṛṣṭhaṃ guptāḥ sarpaṃti sarvataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing his order, the extremely powerful Dānavas went to the earth and moved round secretly.

## \|\| 1.231.9 \|\|

*yaṃ kañcidvīkṣayaṃtisma japahomaparāyaṇama \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ vā prakurvāṇaṃ taṃ nighnaṃti śitāsibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If they found anyone engaged in Japa, Homa and Svādhyāya (self-study and chanting of the Vedas), they killed him with sharp swords,

## \|\| 1.231.10 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu sāṃkṛtirmunisattamaḥ \|*  
*guptaścakre tatastasyāṃ gartāyāṃ channavarṣmakaḥ \|*  
*yatra pūrvaṃ tapastaptaṃ vṛkeṇa ca dvijāḥ purā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the meantime, an excellent sage Sāṅkṛti hid himself in the Gartā (chasm) where, O Brāhmaṇas, penance had been formerly performed by Vṛka. He performed the penance secretly.

## \|\| 1.231.11 \|\|

*atha te taṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā tadguhāyāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*bhartsamānāstapastacca procuśca paruṣākṣaraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing him ensconced in the cave and performing penance, they rebuked him and spoke harsh words.

## \|\| 1.231.12-13 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tasyāgrataḥ saṃsthāṃ gandhapuṣpaiśca pūjitām \|*  
*vāsudevātmikāṃ mūrtiṃ caturhastāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tataste śastramudyamya nirjaghnustaṃ krudhānvitāḥ \|*  
*na śekuste yadā haṃtuṃ saṃvṛtaṃ viṣṇutejasā \|*  
*kuṇṭhatāṃ sarvaśastrāṇi gatāni vimalānyapi \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they saw a four-armed idol of Vāsudeva installed in front of him and adored with scents and flowers. Thereupon, they angrily raised the weapons and struck him. They were unable to kill him, because he was enveloped (and protected) by the refulgence of Viṣṇu. Even their bright weapons became entirely blunted.

## \|\| 1.231.14 \|\|

*atha vailakṣyamāpannā nirviṇṇāḥ sarva eva te \|*  
*tāṃ vārtāṃ dānavendrāya vṛkāyocuśca te tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They were disgusted and ashamed due to this discomfiture and conveyed the information to Vṛka, the leader of the Dānavas:

## \|\| 1.231.15-17 \|\|

*kaścidvipraḥ samādhāya vaiṣṇavīṃ pratimāṃ puraḥ \|*  
*tapastepe mahābhāga kṣetre vai hāṭakeśvare \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yatra tvayā tapastaptaṃ bhītyā sarvadivaukasām \|*  
*api cauryeṇa cāsmākaṃ tapastapati tādṛśam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yena sarvāṇi śastrāṇi kuṇṭhatāṃ pragatāni ca \|*  
*tasya gātre prahāraiśca tasmātkuru yathocitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. “O highly esteemed one, in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, a certain Brāhmaṇa had placed the image of Viṣṇu in front of him and was performing penance. It is the place where penance has been performed by you out of fear of all the Heaven-dwellers. Stealthily hiding himself from us, he performs a similar penance. On account of this, when we struck him, all the weapons became blunted. So, do what is proper here.”

## \|\| 1.231.18 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vṛkaḥ kopasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma satvaṃ tatra yatrāsau sāṃkṛtiḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing their words Vṛka became furious. He hurriedly went to the place where Sāṅkṛti was present.

## \|\| 1.231.19 \|\|

*sa gatvā vaiṣṇavīṃ mūrtiṃ tāmutkṣipya sudūrataḥ \|*  
*śvabhrādbahiḥ pracikṣepa bhartsamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After going there, he threw the image of Viṣṇu out of the pit very far off and rebuked him repeatedly.

## \|\| 1.231.20-21 \|\|

*jaghāna pādaghātena dakṣiṇenetareṇa tam \|*  
*abravīnmama vadhyastvaṃ yanmacchatruṃ janārdanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*saṃpūjayasi cauryeṇa tena prāṇānharāmyaham \|*  
*evamuktvātha khaḍgena taṃ jaghāna sa daityapaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He kicked him with his right foot and then with the left one. Then he said to him: “You should be killed by me because you secretly worship my enemy Janārdana. Therefore, I will kill you.” After saying thus the Lord of Daityas struck him with a sword.

## \|\| 1.231.22 \|\|

*tatastasya sa khaḍgastu tīkṣṇo'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tasya kāye prahīṇastu śatadhā samapadyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Though his sword was very sharp, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the moment it was employed (struck) on his body, it split into a hundred pieces.

## \|\| 1.231.23 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparītātmā taṃ śaśāpa sa sāṃkṛtiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereupon, Sāṅkṛti became furious and cursed him:

## \|\| 1.231.24 \|\|

*yasmātpāpa tvayāhaṃ ca pādaghātaiḥ pratāḍitaḥ \|*  
*tasmātte patatāṃ pādau sadya eva dharātale \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “O sinful one, since I have been kicked by you with the feet, therefore those two feet will fall off instantly on the ground.”

## \|\| 1.231.25 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*uktamātre tatastena pādau tasya dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*patitau medinīpṛṣṭhe paṃcaśīrṣāvivoragau \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sūta said:

25\. As soon as this was uttered by him, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the feet fell on the ground like five-hooded serpents.

## \|\| 1.231.26 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu ākrandaḥ sumahānabhūt \|*  
*vṛkasya sainikānāṃ ca nārīṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the same time, there was a great commotion among the soldiers and Vṛka as well as among the women in particular.

## \|\| 1.231.27 \|\|

*atha devāḥ parijñāya taṃ tadā paṃgutāṃ gatam \|*  
*āgatya merupṛṣṭhaṃ ca nijaghnustatparigraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On coming to know that he had become lame Devas came to the top of Meru and killed his attendants.

## \|\| 1.231.28-29 \|\|

*hataśeṣāśca daityāste pātālāṃtaḥsamā gatāḥ \|*  
*vṛko'pi paṃgutāṃ prāptastasthau tapasi susthiram \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvairaṃtaḥpuraiḥ sārdhaṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*indro'pi prāptavānrājyaṃ tadā nihata kaṃṭakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29a. The Daityas who survived the slaughter went into the nether worlds. Vṛka who had become, lame remained steadfastly engaged in his penance.

He was attended upon by all the women of his household. He was extremely grief-stricken and miserable.

29b. Indra regained his kingdom with all the thorns (enemies) exterminated.

## \|\| 1.231.30 \|\|

*dharmakriyāḥ pravṛttāśca tato bhūyo rasātale \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereupon, holy rites were revived on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.231.31 \|\|

*atha dīrgheṇa kālena tasya tuṣṭaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*uvāca tatra cāgatya garttāmadhye dvijottamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After the lapse of a long period of time, Pitāmaha became pleased with him. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he came into the Gartā and spoke:

## \|\| 1.231.32 \|\|

*vṛka tuṣṭo'smi te vatsa varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*ahaṃ dāsyāmi te nūnaṃ yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O Vṛka, O dear one, I am pleased with you. O devotee of excellent holy rites, choose your boon. I shall certainly grant it even if it be a rare one.”

## \|\| 1.231.33 \|\|

*vṛka uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*pādadānaṃ tadā deva mama brahmansamācara \|*  
*paṃgutā yāti śīghraṃ me yeneyaṃ te prasādataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Vṛka said:

33\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if a boon has to be granted to me, then, O Lord Brahmā, grant me the gift of feet so that, with your favour, my lameness may be cured.

## \|\| 1.231.34-35 \|\|

*tacchrutvā taṃ samānīya sāṃkṛtiṃ tatra padmajaḥ \|*  
*provāca sāṃtvapūrvaṃ ca vṛkasyāsya dvijottama \|\| 34 \|\|*

*madvākyātpaṃgutā yāti yenāsya tvaṃ tathā kuru \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On hearing it, the Lotus-born One, summoned Sāṅkṛti there and said to him in conciliatory terms: “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, do that unto this Vṛka whereby his lameness disappears. Do this at my behest.”

## \|\| 1.231.36 \|\|

*sāṃkṛtiruvāca \|*  
*anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me svaireṣvapi pitāmaha \|*  
*jñāyate devadeveśa tatkathaṃ tatkaromyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sāṅkṛti said:

36\. O Pitāmaha, falsehood has never been uttered by me before, even in a joke. It is known to you, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, How can I then do it?

## \|\| 1.231.37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*mama bhaktiparo nityaṃ vṛko'yaṃ daityasattamaḥ \|*  
*pautrastvaṃ dayito nityaṃ tena tvāṃ prārthayāmyaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

37\. This Vṛka, the most excellent one among Daityas, is always devoted to me. You are my grandson and a favourite of mine always. Therefore, I request you:

## \|\| 1.231.38 \|\|

*tava vākyaṃ ca no mithyā kartuṃ śaknomi sanmune \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Of course, O excellent sage, I am not able to nullify (make false) your statement.

## \|\| 1.231.39 \|\|

*sāṃkṛtiruvāca \|*  
*eṣa daityaḥ suduṣṭātmā devānāmahite sthitaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣādvāsudevasya purormama mahātmanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Sāṅkṛti said:

39\. This Daitya is an extremely wicked soul. He has established himself contrary to the interests of Devas. He is (more so) in the case of the noble-souled Vāsudeva, my preceptor.

## \|\| 1.231.40 \|\|

*paṃgutāmarhati prāyaḥ pāpātmā dvijadūṣakaḥ \|*  
*balena mahatā yukto jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. This sinner and defiler of Brāhmaṇas deserves the state of lameness in general because he has inordinate strength and is free from death and old age.

## \|\| 1.231.41 \|\|

*purā kṛtastvayā deva sa cetpādāvavāpsyati \|*  
*haniṣyati jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Lord, it was you who have made him so formerly. If he regains the feet, he will destroy (kill) the entire world including Devas Asuras and human beings.

## \|\| 1.231.42 \|\|

*tasmāttiṣṭhatu tadrūpo na kalpaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*tvayāpi cintā kartavyā trailokyasya yataḥ prabho \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence let him remain in the same form. It does not behove you to worry over it, since, O Lord, you have to think about the three worlds.

Brahmā said.:

## \|\| 1.231.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*prāvṛṭkāle tu sañjāte yānaṃ kartuṃ na yujyate \|*  
*vijigīṣorviśeṣeṇa muktvā śītātapāgamam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At the advent of rainy season, it is not proper to undertake a campaign of victory on the part of a victorious warrior in particular, except in the case of onset of winter and summer.

## \|\| 1.231.44 \|\|

*tasmācca caturo māsānvārṣikānpādasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*agamyaḥ sarvalokānāṃ kuryātkarmāṇi dhairyataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence, if he were to be endowed with feet during the four months of rainy season and also made unapproachable to all the worlds, he may very well carry on his activities patiently.

## \|\| 1.231.45 \|\|

*tadbhūyātpādasaṃyuktaḥ sa vṛko dāna vottamaḥ \|*  
*yena kṣemaṃ ca devānāṃ dvijānāṃ jāyate dvija \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. So, let Vṛka, the most excellent one among Dānavas, be endowed with feet whereby, O Brāhmaṇa, the welfare of Devas and Brāhmaṇas may take place (unfettered).

## \|\| 1.231.46 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛte na mithyā te vākyaṃ vipra bhaviṣyati \|*  
*phalaṃ ca tapasastasya na vṛthā saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If this arrangement is followed, O Brāhmaṇa, your word will not become falsified. Nor will his penance become futile.

## \|\| 1.231.47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva tenokte sāṃkṛtena mahātmanā \|*  
*utthitau sahasā pādau tasya gātrātpunarnavau \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sūta said:

47\. “So may it be”, said the noble-souled Sāṅkṛti. When he said so, the feet came out afresh from his body.

## \|\| 1.231.48 \|\|

*punaśca dānavo raudraḥ paśutvaṃ samapadyata \|*  
*tasyāmeva tu gartāyāṃ saṃtiṣṭhati dvijottamāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Again the hideous Dānava became lame, O excellent Brāhmaṇas and remained in the Gartā.

## \|\| 1.231.49 \|\|

*māsānaṣṭau sa duḥkhena sakalatraḥ sabāṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*smaramāṇo mahadvairaṃ daivaiḥ sārdhaṃ divāniśam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. For those eight months he remains there extremely miserable along with his wives and kinsmen. He could not do anything excepting the recollection of his great enmity with the Devas day and night.

## \|\| 1.231.50 \|\|

*anyāṃśca caturo māsānniṣkramya sa ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*sadā pīḍayate devānsaheṃdrānmānuṣānapi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. During the remaining four months he angrily came out and inflicted injuries on the Devas including Indra and human beings.

## \|\| 1.231.51-52 \|\|

*vidhvaṃsayati sarvāṇi dharmasthānāni yāni ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vidhvaṃsayati devānāṃ striyo māsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*udyānāni ca sarvāṇi sapurāṇi gṛhāṇi ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. He used to destroy all the sacred place. He used to molest the womenfolk of the Devas, all the parks, houses and cities during the four months.

## \|\| 1.231.53 \|\|

*tato devāḥ samabhyetya devadevaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*kṣīrābdhau saṃsthitaṃ nityaṃ śeṣaparyaṃkaśāyinam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thereupon, the Devas approached Janārdana, the Lord of Devas, who permanently lay down on his couch of Śeṣa in the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 1.231.54 \|\|

*caturo vārṣikānmāsāṃstatra sthitvā tadaṃtike \|*  
*māsānaṣṭau punarjagmustridivaṃ prati nirbhayāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. They stayed near him for the duration of the four rainy months. For the remaining eight months they went back to heaven without the least trace of fear.

## \|\| 1.231.55 \|\|

*tasminpaṃgutvamāpanne daitye paramadāruṇe \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya devarājo bṛhaspatim \|*  
*provāca duḥkhasaṃtapta āṣāḍhāṃte suro ttamaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. (Their only respite was) when the extremely terrible Daitya became lame.

Once the king of Devas, the most excellent one among Suras, said to Bṛhaspati towards the close of Āṣāḍha. He was then extremely distressed:

## \|\| 1.231.56 \|\|

*guro sa māsaḥ saṃprāptaḥ prāvṛṭkālo bhayāvahaḥ \|*  
*āgamiṣyati yatrāsau labdhapādo vṛkāsuraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “O venerable preceptor, that month in the rainy season has arrived instilling fear into us. It is now that the demon Vṛka will descend on us after regaining his pair of feet.

## \|\| 1.231.57 \|\|

*gantavyaṃ ca tato'smābhiḥ kṣīrode keśavālaye \|*  
*maivaṃ dīnaistathā bhāvyaṃ parāśrayanivāsibhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. So we have to go perforce to the Milk Ocean, the abode of Keśava. Let it not be that we continue to be distressed and stay as dependents of others.

## \|\| 1.231.58 \|\|

*svagṛhāṇi parityajya śayanānyāsanāni ca \|*  
*vāhanāni vicitrāṇi yaccānya ddayitaṃ gṛhe \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. We are compelled to leave our abodes, beds, seats, diverse kinds of vehicles and many other favoured objects in the house.

## \|\| 1.231.59 \|\|

*tasmātkathaya cāsmākamupāyaṃ kañcideva hi \|*  
*vrataṃ vā niyamaṃ vātha homaṃ vā munisattama \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Hence, O excellent one among the sages, tell us some Vrata, Niyama or Homa.

## \|\| 1.231.60 \|\|

*aśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ yena svakalatreṇa jāyate \|*  
*tathā na gṛhasaṃtyāgaḥ svakīyasya prajāyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thereby we will have our beds not bereft of our spouses. Thereby we will not be compelled to leave our abodes.

## \|\| 1.231.61 \|\|

*nirviṇṇo'haṃ nijasthānabhraṃśāddvijavarottama \|*  
*varṣevarṣe ca samprāpte sthānakasya cyutirbhavet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I am utterly disgusted, O excellent one among chiefs of Brāhmaṇas, with the repeated loss of my position whenever the rainy season sets in every year.

## \|\| 1.231.62 \|\|

*punarbhūmau śayiṣyāmi yāvanmāsacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*niṣkalatro bhayodvigno brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*
