*tāvadbhramaṃti saṃsāre pitaraḥ piṃḍatatparāḥ \|*  
*yāvatkule bhaktiyutaḥ sto naiva prajāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Pitṛs eagerly expecting the ritualistic balls of rice, roam about in their mundane existence only as long as a devout son is not born in the family.

## \|\| 1.263.10 \|\|

*tāvaddvijāni garjaṃti tāvadgarjati pātakam \|*  
*tāvattīrthānyanekāni yāvadbhaktiṃ na viṃdati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dvijas roar, sin exists in the world and many Tīrthas have their utility only as long as one does not acquire devotion (to Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 1.263.11 \|\|

*sa eva jñānavāṃlloke yogināṃ prathamo hi saḥ \|*  
*mahākratūnāmāhartā haribhaktiyuto hi saḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He alone who is endowed with devotion to Hari, is the man of wisdom in the world; indeed he is the first among Yogins; he is the performer of great Kratus (sacrifices).

## \|\| 1.263.12 \|\|

*nimiṣaṃ nirnayanmeṣaṃ yogaḥ samabhijāyate \|*  
*vāṇījaye yoginastu gomedhaśca prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Moments pass on without winking and Yoga takes place When speech is mastered by the Yogin, it is proclaimed as Gomedha (sacrifice of GO, cow, speech).

## \|\| 1.263.13 \|\|

*manaso vijaye nityamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*kalpanāvijayānnityaṃ yajñaṃ sautrāmaṇiṃ labhet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When he acquires control over mind, he attains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice. By a perpetual conquest (mastery) of Kalpanā (imagination, stray thoughts) he acquires the benefit of the sacrifice Sautrāmaṇi.

## \|\| 1.263.14-15 \|\|

*dehasyotsarjanānnityaṃ narayajñaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*paṃceṃdriyapaśūnhatvā'nagnau śīrṣe ca kuṇḍale \|\| 14 \|\|*

*gurūpadeśavidhinā brahmabhūtatvamaśnute \|*  
*sa yogī niyatāhārodaṇḍatritayadhārakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. It is glorified as Narayajña (human sacrifice) as it involves the renunciation of the body. The sacrificial animals are the five sense-organs but they are not consigned to the fire. The earrings remain on the head; In accordance with the instructions of the preceptor he attains the status of Brahman. With the diet restricted, that Yogin holds the three Daṇḍas (Staff).

## \|\| 1.263.16 \|\|

*tridaṃḍī sa tu vijñeyo jñāte deve niraṃjane \|*  
*manodaṇḍaḥ karmadaṇḍo vāgdaṃḍo yasya yoginaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When the unsullied Lord is realized he (the Yogin) should be known as Tridaṇḍin. He has (the control of) the three Daṇḍas viz. mano-daṇḍa (the staff in the form of mind), Karma-daṇḍa (the staff in the form of Karmas, actions done) and Vāg-daṇḍa (the staff in the form of speech).

## \|\| 1.263.17 \|\|

*sa yogī brahmarūpeṇa jīvanneva samāpyate \|*  
*ajñānī bādhyate nityaṃ karmabhirbaṃdhanātmakaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even as he continues to live that Yogin gets merged into the form of Brahman. It is the ignorant one who is harassed always through the Karmas that are of the nature of bondage.

## \|\| 1.263.18-22 \|\|

*kurvanneva hi karmāṇi jñānī muktiṃ prayāti hi \|*  
*yadā hi gurubhiḥ sthānaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pratipādyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadaiṣa muktimāpnoti dehastiṣṭhati kevalam \|*  
*yāvadbrahmaphalāvāptyai prayāti puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tāvatkarmamayī vṛttirbrahma vṛkṣāṃtarābhavet \|*  
*avāṃtarāṇi parvāṇi jñeyāni munibhiḥ sadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mokṣamārgo dvijaiścaiva śrutismṛtisamuccayāt \|*  
*mokṣo'yaṃ nagarākāraścaturdvāra samākulaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dvārapālāstatra nityaṃ catvārastu śamādayaḥ \|*  
*ta eva prathamaṃ sevyā manujairmākṣadāyakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. The wise one indeed attains liberation even as he continues to do Karma here.

When he is led unto the region of Brahman by his Gurus (Preceptors) he attains liberation. Only the body stays (behind).

By the time the excellent Puruṣa proceeds on for the attainment of the Brahmaphala (fruit in the form of attainment of Brahma) the Karmamayī Vṛtti (tendency to indulge in Karma) shall be near in the Brahma Vṛkṣa. (Tree in the form of the Brahma). Other Parvans should always be got known by sages (obscure).

It is by a synthesis of Śrutis and Smṛtis that the path to Mokṣa (should be known) by Dvijas.

This liberation is like a city having four gates (exits). The sentries there are the four attainments, Śama (self-control) etc. These alone should be resorted to by the men at the outset as they are the bestowers of salvation.

## \|\| 1.263.23 \|\|

*śamaśca sadvicāraśca saṃtoṣaḥ sādhusaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*ete vai hastagā yasya tasya siddhirna dūrataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Siddhi (perfection, achievement) cannot be far from him who has acquired Śama, (quietude), Sadvicāra (good thoughts), Santoṣa (contentment) and Sādhu Saṅgama (association with good people).

## \|\| 1.263.24 \|\|

*yogasiddhirviṣṇubhaktyā saddharmācaraṇena ca \|*  
*prāpyate manujairdevi hyetajjñānamalaṃ viduḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O goddess, the attainment of Yoga by men is effected through devotion to Viṣṇu and the practice of excellent Dharma. It is said that this is sufficient knowledge (for the purpose).

## \|\| 1.263.25 \|\|

*jñānārthaṃ ca bhramanmartyo vidyāsthāneṣu sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*sadyo jñānaṃ sadguruto dīpārciriva nirmalā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A man moves around everywhere in the places of learning for the sake of (spiritual) wisdom, (but) the sudden emergence of knowledge through a good preceptor is free from impurities like the flame of a lamp.

## \|\| 1.263.26 \|\|

*muhūrtamātramapi yo layaṃ ciṃta yati dhruvam \|*  
*tasya pāpasahasrāṇi vilayaṃ yāṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is certain that thousands of sins instantly get dissolved if one ponders over dissolution (absorption in Brahma?) even for a Muhūrta (short time).

## \|\| 1.263.27 \|\|

*rāgadveṣau parityajya krodhalobhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sarvatra samadarśī ca viṣṇubhaktasya darśanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Passion and hatred should be discarded. Anger and greed should be avoided. He should view everyone impartially and visit a devotee Of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.263.28 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi jīvānāṃ dayā yasya hṛdi sthirā \|*  
*śaucācārasamāyukto yogī duḥkhaṃ na viṃdati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A Yogin endowed with Śauca (purity) and Ācāra (excellent behaviour), in whose heart abides perpetual compassion for all living beings, never meets with misery.

## \|\| 1.263.29 \|\|

*māyādhipaṭalairhīno mithyā vastuvirāgavān \|*  
*kusaṃsargavihīnaśca yogasiddheśca lakṣaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. These are the characteristics of Yogasiddhi: He is free from the massive coatings of Māyā (deception) and Ādhi (anguish). He is detached from unreal things. He shuns association with evil ones.

## \|\| 1.263.30 \|\|

*mamatāvahnisaṃyogo narāṇāṃ tāpadāyakaḥ \|*  
*utpannaḥ śamanaṃ tasya yogināṃ śāṃticāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Contact with the fire of Mamatā (sense of possession—“This is mine” etc.) causes great distress to men when it arises. Subduing it when arisen, brings about peace of mind to Yogins.

## \|\| 1.263.31 \|\|

*indriyāṇāmathoddhṛtya manasaiva niṣedhayet \|*  
*yathā lohena lohaṃ ca gharṣitaṃ tīkṣṇatāṃ vrajet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The sense-organs should be sublimated by the mind itself and denied access (to the objects of pleasure). (They will then be keen) just like a piece of steel that when rubbed against another piece attains sharpness.

## \|\| 1.263.32 \|\|

*buddhirhi dvividhā dehe deyā grāhyā viśuddhidā \|*  
*saṃsāraviṣayā tyājyā parabrahmaṇi sā śubhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There are two types of intellectual proclivities in regard to the body. One pertains to the worldly objects. It should be discarded. That which is directed towards Parabrahman is auspicious. It is to be accepted and it causes purity.

## \|\| 1.263.33 \|\|

*ahaṃkāro yathā devi pāpapuṇyapradāyakaḥ \|*  
*jñāte tattve śubhaphale kṛtaḥ saṃdhāya nānyathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O goddess, egotism causes sin and merit. If it is rendered steady, and not otherwise, it leads to the realization of the Tattva (eternal truth) that yields auspicious benefit.

## \|\| 1.263.34 \|\|

*śyāmalaṃ ca upasthaṃ ca rūpātītānnarāḥ śivam \|*  
*hṛdisthaṃ siraśisthaṃ ca dvayaṃ baddhavimuktaye \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The organ of generation is dark and impure, but if it transcends the worldly form, it yields weal. In both the ways, when it is retained within the heart or restrained in the head it is conducive to the liberation of one who is in bondage.

## \|\| 1.263.35 \|\|

*etadakṣaramavyakamamṛtaṃ sakalaṃ tava \|*  
*rūparūpaviṣṇurūparūpamūrtiniveditam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus the imperishable, unmanifest, immortal form of Viṣṇu, that which is one with all attributes has been told to you.

## \|\| 1.263.36 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā vimucyeta yogī saṃsārabandhanāt \|*  
*gurūpadeśādgṛhastho labhate nānyathā kvacit \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After realizing thus, a Yogin shall become liberated from the worldly bondage. A householder obtains it through the advice and guidance of the preceptor and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.263.37 \|\|

*yadā guruḥ prasannātmā tasya viśvaṃ prasīdati \|*  
*guruśca toṣito yena saṃtuṣṭāḥ pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If the preceptor is pleased, the entire universe becomes pleased with him (the disciple). If the preceptor is rendered pleased by anyone, the Pitṛs and Devas too are rendered pleased by him.

## \|\| 1.263.38 \|\|

*gurūpadeśaḥ pratimā sadvicāraḥ same manaḥ \|*  
*kriyā ca jñānasahitā mokṣasiddherhi lakṣaṇam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. These are the characteristics of the acquisition of salvation: the instruction of the preceptor, the image, good thoughts, the mind in poise and physical activity in association with perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.263.39 \|\|

*kriyāpatirviṣṇureva svayameva hi niṣkri yaḥ \|*  
*sa ca prāṇavirūpāya dvādaśākṣaravījakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Viṣṇu alone is the Lord of Kriyās (physical activity, sacred rites) though he himself is Niṣkriya (devoid of activities). He too is in the form of Praṇava, the Bīja of the Mantra of twelve syllables.

## \|\| 1.263.40 \|\|

*dvādaśākṣarakaṃ cakraṃ sarvapāpanibarhaṇam \|*  
*duṣṭānāṃ damanaṃ caiva parabrahmapradāyakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The wheel of twelve-syllabled Mantra is destructive of all sins. It suppresses wicked ones and leads to Parabrahman.

## \|\| 1.263.41 \|\|

*etadeva paraṃ brahma dvādaśākṣararūpadhṛk \|*  
*mayā prakāśitaṃ devi skande hi vimalaṃ tava \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This selfsame supreme Brahman having the pure twelve-syllabled form has been revealed to you, O goddess, in the Skanda (Purāṇa).

## \|\| 1.263.42 \|\|

*etatsāraṃ yogināṃ dhyānarūpaṃ bhaktigrāhyaṃ śraddhayā cintayecca \|*  
*cāturmāsye janmakoṭyāṃ ca jātaṃ pāpaṃ dagdhvā muktidaḥ kaiṭabhāriḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This is the essence to Yogins and is of the form of meditation. It can be assimilated only through devotion. One should ponder over it with faith during Cāturmāsya. After burning the sins incurred in the course of ten million births, the Enemy of Kaiṭabha shall bestow liberation.

## \|\| 1.263.43-44 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnagare tatra kṣīrasāgaramadhyataḥ \|*  
*ujjahāra vimānāgre tejobhārābhipīḍitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*uro bāhukṛtiṃ kurvansānnidhyaṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*mahāmatsyo'jñātapūrvaḥ sannidhāne'nahaṃkṛtiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

43-44. In the meantime (Read etasminnantare for etasminnagare in the text) a great fish, hitherto unknown rose up from the centre of the Milk Ocean on the top of an aerial chariot. It had a mass of refulgence. Making movements with its chest and arms (fins?) it came near the presence (of Lord Śiva). He was without any egotism or pride.

## \|\| 1.263.45 \|\|

*huṃkāragarbhe matsyaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā taṃ sa maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tejasā staṃbhayāmāsa vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. While making a hissing sound, Lord Maheśvara saw that fish and benumbed it through his refulgence. He then spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.263.46 \|\|

*kastvaṃ matsyodarasthaśca devo yakṣo'tha mānuṣaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ jīvasi dehāṃtargato mama vada prabho \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “Who are you stationed will in the belly of a fish? A Deva, Yakṣa or man? How do you live within the body? O Lord, tell me”.

## \|\| 1.263.47 \|\|

*matsya uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ matsyodare kṣiptaḥ samudre kṣīrasaṃbhave \|*  
*mātrā tu pitṛvākyena nāyaṃ mama kulānvitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Matsya said:

47\. I have been hurled into the belly of a fish in the Milk Ocean by my mother at the instance of my father: “This boy is unworthy of my family.”

## \|\| 1.263.48 \|\|

*kulakṣayabhayāttena jātaṃ svakulanāśanam \|*  
*gaṃḍāṃtayogajanito bālo na gṛhakarmakṛt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He was afraid of the destruction of the whole family. I was a child born in the Yoga (astronomical combination) named Gaṇḍānta. “Such a child cannot perform domestic duties. It will be the destroyer of its own family.”

## \|\| 1.263.49 \|\|

*iti mātrā duḥkhitayā nirastaḥ śṛṇu vaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*jhaṣeṇāpi gṛhīto'smi kālo me'tra mahānabhūt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thus I was cast off by my sorrowing mother. Though I am of the same family, I was seized by a fish. A great deal of time since then elapsed.

## \|\| 1.263.50 \|\|

*tava vākyāmṛtairebhirjñānayogo mahānabhūt \|*  
*tena tvaṃ sakalo jñāto mayā mūrto'tha mūrttagaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thanks to your nectar-like words, the great Jñānayoga became known to me. Though you are Amūrta (incorporeal), I know you entirely as being corporeal as well.

## \|\| 1.263.51 \|\|

*anujñāṃ mama deveśa dehi niṣkramaṇāya ca \|*  
*yathā'haṃ pitṛpo brahmanbhavānyāścāpi lakṣyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Lord of Devas, grant me permission to come out. O Lord, let me be seen by Bhavānī as Pitṛpa (Protector of Pitṛs?).

## \|\| 1.263.52 \|\|

*hara uvāca \|\| vipro'si sutarūpo'si pūjyosyāsi babhāṣataḥ \|*  
*bahirniṣkrama vegena staṃbhito'si mahājhaṣaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Hara said:

52\. You are a Brāhmaṇa. You are in the form of my son. You are worthy of being worshipped by this one who speaks. You have been benumbed, O great fish. Come out quickly.

## \|\| 1.263.53 \|\|

*tato'sau śirasā jāta utkleśānmatsyayojitaḥ \|*  
*tato hi vikṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kṣaṇādbahirupāgataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thereupon, the fish that was undergoing suffering emerged headlong. He came out instantly with a distortion of his face.

## \|\| 1.263.54 \|\|

*rūpavānpratimāyukto matsyagaṃdhena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*somakāṃtisamastatra hyabhavaddivyagaṃdhabhāk \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He acquired beauty and intellect. His lustre now resembled that of the moon. Once stinking like, a fish, he now possessed divine fragrance.

## \|\| 1.263.55 \|\|

*umāpi praṇataṃ cāmuṃ sutaṃ svotsaṃgabhājanam \|*  
*cakāra tasya nāmāpi haraḥ paramaharṣitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. When the son bowed down, Umā took him on her lap. Hara who was extremely delighted gave him a name.

## \|\| 1.263.56-58 \|\|

*yasmānmatsyodarājjāto yogināṃ pravaro hyayam \|*  
*tasmāttu matsya nātheti loke khyāto bhaviṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

*acchedyaḥ syānnaratanurjñānayogasya pāragaḥ \|*  
*nirmatsaro'pi nirdvaṃdvo nirāśo brahmasevakaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*jīvanmuktaśca bhavitā bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|*  
*ityuktaśca maheśānaṃ praṇamaṃśca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*maheśvareṇa sahito maṃdarācalamāyayau \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. “This most excellent one among Yogins was born from the belly of a fish. Hence, he will become well-known in the world as Matsyanātha.

He shall be endowed with human body which will never be split or cut. He will master Jñānayoga. He shall be devoid of rivalry, Dvandvas (mutually opposed pairs) and ambitions and hopes (Nirāśa). He will be a server of Brāhmaṇas. He will be a living liberated soul in all the fourteen worlds.”

On being told thus, he repeatedly bowed to Maheśāna. Accompanying Maheśvara he went to the Mandara Mountain.

## \|\| 1.263.59-62 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ devīṃ skandamāliṃgya so'gamat \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tataḥ sā pārvatī hṛṣṭā prāpya jñānamanuttamam \|*  
*evaṃ sā paramāṃ siddhiṃ praṇavasyaprabhā janam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*sā prāpya jagatāṃ mātā dvādaśākṣarajāṃbunā \|*  
*imāṃ matsyendranāthasya cotpattiṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 62 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

59-62. He circumambulated the goddess, embraced Skanda and went away.

After acquiring the excellent Jñāna, Pārvatī became delighted. She acquired the great Siddhi due to the power of Praṇava. The mother of the worlds acquired this Praṇava through the watery medium of the twelve-syllabled Mantra.

He who listens to this origin of Matsyendranātha especially during Cāturmāsya shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## Chapter 264 - Tārakāsura Killed

## \|\| 1.264.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kārtikeyaśca pārvatyāḥ prāṇebhyaścātivallabhaḥ \|*  
*saṃkrīḍati samīpastho nānāceṣṭābhirudyataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. Kārttikeya, the most beloved of Pārvatī, greater than her own life, plays about nearby. He is engaged in different kinds of (playful) activities.

## \|\| 1.264.2 \|\|

*raktakāṃtirmahātejāḥ ṣaṇmukho'dbhuta vikramaḥ \|*  
*kvacidgāyati cātyarthaṃ kvacinnṛtyati svecchayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He is highly refulgent with a red lustre and wonderful in his exploits. The Six-faced One sings loudly at will at some place and dances as he pleases in some other place.

## \|\| 1.264.3 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vinayāvanataḥ kvacit \|*  
*kvacicca gaṃgāpuline sikatālepanākṛtiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He looks at his mother and father and stands bowing down humbly. Somewhere, on the sandy banks of Gaṅgā, he is found smearing his body with sand particles.

## \|\| 1.264.4 \|\|

*gaṇaiḥ saha vicinvāno vividhānvanabhūruhān \|*  
*evaṃ prakrīḍitastasya divasāḥ paṃca jajñire \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Accompanied by the Gaṇas, he is found searching about different kinds of trees in the forest. Thus five days passed off even as he played about.

## \|\| 1.264.5 \|\|

*tato devā mahendrādyāstārakatrāsavidrutāḥ \|*  
*stuvantaḥ śaṃkaraṃ sarve tārakasya jighṛkṣayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, Mahendra and other Devas who had fled due to the fear of Tāraka desired to catch hold of Tāraka. So they all eulogized Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.264.6 \|\|

*cakruḥ kumāraṃ senānyaṃ jāhnavyāṃ svagaṇaiḥ surāḥ \|*  
*sasvanurdevavādyāni puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Through their Gaṇas the Suras made Kumāra their commander-in-chief on the (bank of) river Gaṅgā. The musical instruments (war drums etc.) of the Devas were sounded and there was shower of flowers.

## \|\| 1.264.7-8 \|\|

*vahnistu svāṃ dadau śaktiṃ himavānvāhanaṃ dadau \|*  
*sarvadevasamudbhūtagaṇakoṭisamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*praṇamya munisaṃghebhyaḥ prayayau ripuvigrahe \|*  
*tāmravatyāṃ nagaryāṃ ca śaṃkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The Fire-god gave him his Śakti and Himavān offered a vehicle. He was surrounded by crores of the groups of all the Devas. Kārttikeya bowed down to the groups of sages and proceeded ahead for battle with the enemies. At the city of Tāmravatī, the valorous one blew his conchshell.

## \|\| 1.264.9 \|\|

*tatastārakasainyasya daityadānavakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*samājagmustasya purācchaṃkhanādabhayāturāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing the sound of the conch, crores of the soldiers of the Dānava came out from his city overwhelmed with distress and fear.

## \|\| 1.264.10 \|\|

*svavāhanasamārūḍhāḥ saṃyatā baladarpitāḥ \|*  
*devāḥ sarve'pi yuyudhuḥ skandatejopabṛṃhitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All the Devas were emboldened and encouraged by the brilliance of Skanda. They rode their respective vehicles. They were proud due to their prowess, but they fought with self-control.

## \|\| 1.264.11 \|\|

*tadā dānavasainyāni nijaghāna ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇucakreṇa te chinnāḥ petururvyāṃ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He (the Lord) moved down the armies of the Dānavas. Split by the discus of Viṣṇu, they fell on the ground in thousands.

## \|\| 1.264.12 \|\|

*tato bhagnāśca śataśo dānavā nihatāstadā \|*  
*nadyaḥ śoṇitasaṃbhūtā jātā bahuvidhāmune \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Split and killed in hundreds, the Dānavas fell down everywhere, O sage. Rivers of blood of diverse forms began to flow.

## \|\| 1.264.13-14 \|\|

*tadbhagnaṃ dānavabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa yuyudhe raṇe \|*  
*babhaṃja sadyo deveśo bāṇajālairanekadhā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śaktināyudhya gaṃginyāścikṣepa kṛṣṇapreritāḥ \|*  
*sarathaṃ ca sayaṃtāraṃ cakre taṃ bhasmasātkṣaṇāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

13a. On seeing the army of Dānavas broken (routed), he fought in the battle (more vigorously).

13b-14a. The leader of Devas (i.e. Kārttikeya) immediately crushed the Daitya army with shower of arrows of various kinds.

14b. Gāṅgeya (Kārttikeya) fought with Tāraka. Directed by Kṛṣṇa he hurled his Śakti at Tāraka and reduced him to ashes along with his chariot and charioteer in a moment.

## \|\| 1.264.15 \|\|

*śeṣāḥ pātālamagamanhataṃ dṛṣṭvā'tha tārakam \|*  
*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve śasaṃsustasya vikramam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing Tāraka killed, the remaining Dānavas went to Pātāla. Thereupon, all the groups of the Devas praised his valour.

## \|\| 1.264.16-17 \|\|

*devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭistathā'bhavat \|*  
*te labdhavijayāḥ sarve maheśvarapurogamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*siṣicuḥ sarvadevānāṃ senāpatye ṣaḍānanam \|*  
*tataḥ skaṃdaṃ samāliṃgya pārvatī harṣagadgadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The war-drums of the Devas were sounded. There was a shower of flowers. After attaining victory, all of them with Maheśvara at their head, crowned the Six-faced One as the Commander-in-chief of all the Devas. Choked with delight, Pārvatī embraced Skanda.

## \|\| 1.264.18 \|\|

*māṃgalyāni tadā cakre svasakhībhiḥ samāvṛtā \|*  
*evaṃ ca tārakaṃ hatvā saptame'hani bālakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sorrounded by her female companions, she performed all the benedictory and auspicious rites. In this manner the boy killed Tāraka on the seventh day.

## \|\| 1.264.19 \|\|

*maṃdarācalamāsādya pitarau saṃpraharṣayan \|*  
*uvāca sakalaṃ skandaḥ paramānaṃdanirbharaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He then went to mountain Mandara. Filled with excessive joy, he delighted his parents by telling them everything.

## \|\| 1.264.20 \|\|

*kāle dārakriyāṃ tasya cintayāmāsa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sa uvāca prasannātmā gāṃgeyamamitadyutim \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the proper time, Śaṅkara thought about getting a wife for him (Skanda). With a happy mind he spoke to Gāṅgeya of unlimited lustre:

## \|\| 1.264.21-22 \|\|

*prāptaḥ kālastava vibho pāṇigrahaṇasaṃmataḥ \|*  
*kuru dārānsamāsādya dharmaste puṃsasaṃmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*krīḍasva vividhairbhogairvimānaiḥ saha kāmikaiḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhagavānskandaḥ pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22a. “O powerful one, the time suitable for your marriage has arrived. Get a suitable wife. This is your commonly approved duty. Sport about with different kinds of pleasures with aerial chariots that can go as you please.”

22b. On hearing it, Lord Skanda spoke these words to his father:

## \|\| 1.264.23 \|\|

*ahameva hi sarvatra dṛśyaḥ sarvagaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*dṛśyādṛśyapadārtheṣu kiṃ gṛhṇāmi tyajāmi kim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “Everywhere, among all the Gaṇas, among the objects visible and invisible I am alone the person to be seen; what shall I accept? What shall I reject?

## \|\| 1.264.24 \|\|

*yāḥ striyaḥ sakalā viśve pārvatyā tāḥ samā hi me \|*  
*narāḥ sarve'pi deveśa bhavadvattānvilokaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All the women in the world are on a par with Pārvatī for me. O Lord of Devas, I view all the men like you.

## \|\| 1.264.25 \|\|

*tvaṃ gururmāṃ ca rakṣasva punarnarakamajjanāt \|*  
*yena jñātamidaṃ jñānaṃ tvatprasādādakhaṃḍitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You are my preceptor. Save me from getting submerged in Naraka. I am one by whom this entire knowledge has been attained completely unmutilated, thanks to your grace.

## \|\| 1.264.26-33 \|\|

*punareva mahāghorasaṃsārābdhau nimajjaye \|*  
*dīpahasto yathā vastu dṛṣṭvā tatkaraṇaṃ tyajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tathā jñānamadhiprāpya yogī tyajati saṃsṛtim \|*  
*jñātvā sarvagataṃ brahma sarvajña parameśvara \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nivarttaṃte kriyāḥ sarvā yasya taṃ yoginaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*viṣaye lubdhacittānāṃ vane'pi jāyate ratiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvatra samadṛṣṭīnāṃ gehe muktirhi śāśvatī \|*  
*jñānameva maheśāna manuṣyāṇāṃ sudurlabham \|\| 29 \|\|*

*labdhaṃ jñānaṃ kathamapi paṃḍito naiva pātayet \|*  
*nāhamasmi na mātā me na pitā na ca bāṃdhavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ prāpya pṛthakbhāvamāpanno bhuvaneṣvaham \|*  
*prāpyaṃ bhāgamidaṃ daivātprabhāvāttava nārhasi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vaktumevaṃvidhaṃ vākyaṃ mumukṣorme na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yadāgrahaparā devī punaḥpunarabhāṣata \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tadā tau pitarau natvā gato'sau krauñcaparvatam \|*  
*tatrāśrame mahāpuṇye cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

26a. Let it not be that I submerge myself into the extremely terrible ocean of worldly existence.

26b-27a. A man holding light in his hand leaves it after seeing the desired object. Similarly, after attaining knowledge a Yogin leaves off the mundane existence.

27b-28a. O omniscient, supreme Lord, he is known as a Yogin whose activities recede after knowing the omnipresence of Brahman.

28b-31a. In the case of persons whose minds are covetous of sensual objects, they have attraction even while living in the forest. In the case of persons of equanimous vision indeed liberation is eternal even while staying at home. O Maheśāna, knowledge is very rare indeed, in the case of human beings.

By no means should a learned man lose the knowledge attained. Neither I am nor do I have a mother, a father or any kinsman. Having attained the knowledge I have realized separateness from the worlds.

31b-33. This attitude should be attained as a divine gift not as a result of your power.

It does not behove you to make a statement like this. Undoubtedly, I am desirous of salvation.

When the goddess was persistent and said so (about his marriage) repeatedly, he bowed down to his parents and went to the Krauñca mountain. There in a highly meritorious hermitage he performed the greatest austerity.

## \|\| 1.264.34 \|\|

*jajāpa paramaṃ brahma dvādaśākṣarabījakam \|*  
*pūrvaṃ dhyānena sarvāṇi vaśīkṛtyendriyāṇi ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At the outset he brought all the sense-organs under his control by means of meditation. He performed the Japa of the greatest Brahman (i.e. Mantra) with the twelve syllables as the Bījas.

## \|\| 1.264.35-38 \|\|

*mamatāṃ saṃviyujyātha jñānayogamavāptavān \|*  
*siddhayastasya nirvighnā aṇimādyā yadā'gatāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tadā tāsāṃ gaṇā kruddho vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*mamāpi du्ṣṭabhāvena yadi yūyamupāgatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tadāsmatsamaśāṃtānāṃ nābhibhūtiṃ kariṣyatha \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā maheśo'pi yato jñānamahodayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*matto'pi jñānayogenaskando'pyadhikabhāvabhṛt \|*  
*vismayāviṣṭahṛdayaḥ pārvatīmanuśiṣṭavān \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. After echewing Mamatā (sense of possession) he attained Jñānayoga.

When the Siddhis beginning with Aṇimā (ability of becoming very minute) came to him unobstructedly he spoke these words angrily to the groups of those Siddhis:

“If you have approached me with wicked (evil) intention then (this is my assertion) that you will never afflict persons of quiescence on a par with us.”

## \|\| 1.264.39 \|\|

*putraśokaparāṃ comāṃ śubhairvākyāmṛtairharaḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsasya māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Even Maheśa, knowing the great rise (manifestation) of spiritual knowledge (in Skanda) said: “Skanda has attained through Jñānayoga more Bhāva (emotional steadiness).” On knowing this Maheśa was overwhelmed with wonder in his heart. He narrated to Pārvatī (everything)

39\. Pārvatī was overwhelmed with grief over her son. Hara told Umā in nectar-like auspicious words the greatness of Cāturmāsya as being destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.264.40 \|\|

*maheśvaro vā madhukaiṭabhārirhṛdyāśrito dhyānamayo'dvitīyaḥ \|*  
*abhedabuddhyā paramārtihaṃtā ripuḥ sa evātipriyo bhavettataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If Maheśvara or the Enemy of Kaiṭabha (Vìṣṇu) is retained in the heart by meditation, with the realization of non-difference and non-duality, he shall be the destroyer of the intense distress. Thereby, even an enemy shall become extremely affectionate.

## \|\| 1.264.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ kathitaṃ viprāścāturmāsyasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vistareṇaiva kimanyacchrotumicchatha \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:

41\. O Brāhmaṇas, thus the greatness resulting from (observances etc. in) Cāturmāsya has been narrated to you in detail. What other (topic) do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 265 - Aśūnyaśayana-Vrata

## \|\| 1.265.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*prabhūtāni tvayoktāni vratāni niyamāstathā \|*  
*prasupte puṃḍarīkākṣe yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aśaktyā hi śarīrasya niyamānāṃ kathaṃ caret \|*  
*vrataṃ hi sukumārāṃgo dānairvāpi vadasva naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. The Vratas and Niyamas mentioned by you are numerous. They are to be observed when the Lotus-eyed Lord is asleep There is no limit to their number.

How shall a man of delicate limbs observe these Niyamas in view of the weakness of his body? Or can charity be an alternative to that? Tell us.

## \|\| 1.265.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*aśakto niyamaṃ kartuṃ sukumāro bhavettu yaḥ \|*  
*tena tatra prakartavyaṃ vikhyātaṃ bhīṣmapaṃcakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3\. If anyone is of delicate limbs and if he is incompetent to observe the Niyamas, the reputed Bhīṣma-pañcaka is to be performed by him.

## \|\| 1.265.4 \|\|

*kārttikasya site pakṣa ekādaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*prātarutthāya vipreṃdra kartavyaṃ daṃtadhāvanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, he should get up early in the morning with mental concentration and purity, on the eleventh day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika. Then he should brush his teeth.

## \|\| 1.265.5 \|\|

*tatastu niyamaṃ kuryādvāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pūrvoktānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ niyamānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, with devotion to Vāsudeva, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he should perform the Niyama representative of all the Niyamas mentioned before.

## \|\| 1.265.6 \|\|

*upavāsaḥ prakartavyastasminnahani bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*aśaktyā vā śarīrasya hemaṃ dadyātsvaśaktitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Fast is to be observed on that day with devotion. Or if there be weakness in the body he should give (as religious gift) gold according to his capacity.

## \|\| 1.265.7 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya haviṣyānnaṃ dātavyaṃ vaiṣṇavairnaraiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ pañcadinaṃ yāvatkartavyaṃ vratamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Haviṣyānna (rice cooked in ghee) should be given to a Brāhmaṇa by those men who are devotees of Viṣṇu. This excellent Virata should be observed for five days.

## \|\| 1.265.8 \|\|

*pūjanīyo hṛṣīkeśo jalaśāyisvarūpadhṛk \|*  
*gaṃdhairdhūpaiśca naivedyai rātrijāgaraṇairapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Hṛṣīkeṣa in the form of Jalaśāyin (one who lies in water) should be adored through scents, incense, food offerings and keeping awake during the nights.

## \|\| 1.265.9 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhe'hani tato jāte pūjayedbrāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*tāṃśca vastrairhiraṇyena miṣṭānnena prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the arrival of the sixth day, the observer of the Niyama should adore with great devotion excellent Brāhmaṇas with garments, gold and delicious food.

## \|\| 1.265.10 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛtāṃjalirbhūtvā yācayedbrāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*sarve me niyamāḥ prāptā yuṣmākaṃ ca prasādataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should then remain with palms joined in reverence and request the excellent Brāhmaṇas thus: “Thanks to your favour, all the observances have become (successfully) complete in my case.”

## \|\| 1.265.11 \|\|

*tatastairapi vaktavyaṃ caturmāsīsamudbhavam \|*  
*vratānāṃ niyamānāṃ ca vrataṃ bhūyāttavākhilam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the Brāhmaṇas should say: May (the credit of duly observing) this representative of Vratas and Niyamas pertaining to Cāturmāsya be entirely yours.

## \|\| 1.265.12 \|\|

*tato visarjya tānviprānbhojanaṃ svayamācaret \|*  
*sarvāhāreṇa rājeṃdra paṃcagavyaprapūrvakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter, he sends those Brāhmaṇas away and takes food himself. O great king, anything can constitute his diet but Pañcagavya must be taken at the outset.

## \|\| 1.265.13 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti vrataṃ tasya phalaṃ syādbahupuṇyadam \|*  
*yaḥ punarvratametaddhi kurute dinapaṃcakam \|*  
*upavāsaparastasya phalaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If anyone observes Vrata thus, he will earn much merit as a result thereof. He who undertakes this Vrata observing fast for five days, the benefit he gets is hundredfold.

## \|\| 1.265.14-18 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ hareḥ pūjāṃ jātipuṣpaiḥ samācaret \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ bilvapatreṇa śatapatryā tataḥ param \|*  
*trayodaśyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ surabhyā bhaktipūrvakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhṛṃgarājena puṇyena paurṇamāsyāṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*pratipaddivase sarvaiḥ pūjanīyo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pratipaddivase sarvānprāśayetkāyaśuddhaye \|*  
*agaraṃ guggulaṃ caiva karpūraṃ tagaraṃ tvacā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ekaikaṃ nirvapeddhūpaṃ pratipaddivase'khilam \|*  
*jalaśāyī jagadyoniḥ śeṣaparyaṃkamāśritaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*arghaṃ gṛhṇātu me devo bhīṣmapaṃcakasiddhaye \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena dātavyo hyargho devasya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. The devotee performs Hari’s worship on the eleventh day by means of Jāti flowers, on the twelfth day by means of Bilva leaves, on the thirteenth day with Śatapatrī (lotus) and on the fourteenth day by means of fragrant Kalhara flower with great devotion.

He should worship with the meritorious Bhṛṅgarāja flower on the Full-Moon day. Janārdana should be worshipped with all these flowers on the Pratipad day.

For the sake of the purity of the body the devotee should take in all these on the Pratipad day: Cow’s urine, dung, milk, curds, ghee and water mixed with Kuśa grass.

For the purpose of incense these are used severally (on the eleventh, twelfth etc.)—Aguru, Guggulu, Karpūra, Tagara and Tvacā and all these on the Pratipad day.

The Mantra for the offering of Arghya is as follows: “May the Lord, the original cause of the universe, lying on the watery expanse, resorting to the bed of serpent Śeṣa, accept this Arghya in order to facilitate the fulfilment of Bhīṣmapañcaka.” With this Mantra, the Arghya is to be offered to the Lord devoutly.

## \|\| 1.265.19 \|\|

*śaṃkhatoyaṃ samādāya sapuṣpaphalacaṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ paramānnaṃ ca svaśaktyā nirvapeddvijāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Water in a conchshell along with flowers, sandal-paste and fruits should be offered as Arghya.

Paramānna (milk pudding) should be offered as Naivedya, O Brāhmaṇas. It should be offered in accordance with one’s capacity.

## \|\| 1.265.20 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ vrataṃ vai bhīṣmapaṃcakam \|*  
*saṃprāpyate phalaṃ caiva vratānāṃ niyamaiḥ saha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus the Vrata called Bhīṣmapañcaka has been entirely described to you. The fruit of the Vratas is obtained along with that of the Niyamas.

## \|\| 1.265.21 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\| yadetadbhavatā proktamaśūnyaśāyinīvratam \|*  
*indreṇa yatkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ tuṣṭyarthaṃ cakrapāṇinaḥ \|*  
*prasuptasya mahābhāga phalaṃ caiva prakīrtitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

The sages said:

21\. The Vrata named Aśūnyaśayanī Vrata has been described by you as was performed earlier by Indra, for the propitiation of the sleeping Discus-holding Lord, O highly esteemed one.

## \|\| 1.265.22 \|\|

*kasminkāle prakartavyaṃ kenaiva vidhinā tathā \|*  
*tasmātsūta mahābhāga vidhānaṃ vistarādvada \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At what time should it be performed? By what procedure? Hence, O Sūta, describe its procedure in detail.

## \|\| 1.265.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrāvaṇyāṃ samatītāyāṃ dvitīyādivase sthite \|*  
*prātarutthāya viprendrā nakṣatre viṣṇudaivate \|*  
*pāpiṣṭhaiḥ patitairmlecchaiḥ saṃbhāṣaṃ naiva kārayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:

23\. On the second day after the Full-Moon in the month of Śrāvaṇa, when there is the asterism Viṣṇu-Daivata (i.e. Śravaṇa) a devotee should get up in the morning, O leading Brāhmaṇas. He Should not talk to sinners, barbarians and fallen ones.

## \|\| 1.265.24 \|\|

*tato madhyāhnasamaye snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*jalaśāyinamāsādya maṃtreṇānena pūjayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At mid-day he should take his bath and remain clean, wearing washed cloth. Approaching Jalaśāyin (Lord Viṣṇu) he should worship the Lord reciting this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.265.25-28 \|\|

*śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkāṃta śrīdhāmañchrīpate'vyaya \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmadam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pitaro mā praṇaśyaṃtu mā praṇaśyaṃtu cāgnayaḥ \|*  
*devatā mā praṇaśyaṃtu matto dāṃpatyabhedataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*lakṣmyā viyujyase kṛṣṇa na kadācidyathā bhavān \|*  
*tathā kalatrasambandho deva mā me praṇaśyatu \|\| 27 \|\|*

*lakṣmyā hyaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ yathā te deva sarvadā \|*  
*śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathā janmani janmani \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. “O Lord having the mark Śrīvatsa, O Consort of Śrī, O Śrīdhāman (abode of glory), O immutable Lord of Śrī, let not my Gārhasthya (state of being a householder) be ruined. It yields virtue, wealth and love.

May the Pitṛs be not destroyed. May the sacred fires be not extinguished. May the deities be not destroyed through my default in the practice of Dāṃpatya (state of being a married householder),

O Kṛṣṇa, just as you are not separated from Lakṣmī at any time, so also, O Lord, may there not be the destruction of my association with my wife.

Just as your bed is never bereft of Lakṣmī, so also let not my bed be bereft (of my wife) in the course of every birth.”

## \|\| 1.265.29 \|\|

*evamarthaṃ nivedyātha tato vipraṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*yathāśaktyā dvijaśreṣṭhā vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Having prayed thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the devotee honours a Brāhmaṇa in accordance with his capacity. He shall avoid Vittaśāṭhya (villainy or dishonesty in regard to money in giving Dakṣiṇā).

## \|\| 1.265.30 \|\|

*evaṃ bhādrapade māsi āśvine kārtike tathā \|*  
*pūjayecca jagannāthaṃ jalaśāyinamacyutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In this same manner, the devotee should worship Acyuta, the Lord of universe, lying in the watery expanse in the months of Bhādrapada, Āśvina and Kārttika.

## \|\| 1.265.31 \|\|

*akṣārabhojanaṃ kāryaṃ viśeṣāttailavarjitam \|*  
*samāptau ca tato dadyādbrāhmaṇeṃdrāya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The diet should be without salt and oil should be excluded. At the conclusion, the devotee offers (these) to a leading Brāhmaṇa devoutly:

## \|\| 1.265.32 \|\|

*phalavrīhisamopetāṃ śayyāṃ vastrasamanvitām \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ ca tathaiva ca phalaṃ labhet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A bed is given along with garments, grains and food. Gold is to be offered as monetary gift. He attains the benefit in the same manner.

## \|\| 1.265.33 \|\|

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute samyagvratametatsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭipathaṃ yāti jalaśāyī jagadguruḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If the devotee perfectly observes this Vrata with concentration and mental purity, Jalaśāyin, the preceptor of the universe, shall be pleased with him.

## \|\| 1.265.34 \|\|

*yathā śakrasya saṃtuṣṭaḥ pūrvameva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*aśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ tasya bhavejjanmani janmani \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He will be pleased with him, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in the same way as he was pleased formerly with Śakra. His bed shall never be empty in the course of any birth.

## \|\| 1.265.35 \|\|

*aṣṭamāsakṛtaṃ pāpamajñānājjñānato'pi vā \|*  
*aśūnyaśayanātsarvaṃ vratānnāśaṃ nayetpumān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The devotee shall dispel all the sins committed in the course of eight months knowingly or unknowingly. Thanks to the Aśūnyaśayanavrata, all (evil) gets destroyed.

## \|\| 1.265.36 \|\|

*putrahīnā ca yā nārī kākavandhyā ca yā bhavet \|*  
*vidhavā yā karotyetadvratamevaṃ samāhitā \|*  
*tasyāstuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ kāyaśuddhiṃ prayacchati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If a woman without a son, or a woman who has only one child, or a widow observes this Vrata with concentration, the Lord of the universe becomes pleased with her and bestows bodily purity.

## \|\| 1.265.37 \|\|

*na tasyā jāyate buddhiḥ kadācitpāpasaṃbhavā \|*  
*na kāmopahatā buddhiḥ kathaṃcidapi jāyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Her intellect never turns to evil. Her intellect is not at all overwhelmed by lust.

## \|\| 1.265.38 \|\|

*kumārikāpi yā samyagvratametatsamācaret \|*  
*sā patiṃ labhate viprāḥ kulīnaṃ rūpasaṃyutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If a virgin perfectly observes this Vrata, O Brāhmaṇas, she obtains a noble-born handsome husband from a noble family.

## \|\| 1.265.39 \|\|

*niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu vratametatsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsyudbhavānāṃ ca niyamānāṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If a devotee without any specific desire observes this Vrata with concentration, he shall get the benefit of the Niyamas pertaining to Cāturmāsya.

## Chapter 266 - Greatness of Śivarātri

## \|\| 1.266.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrutāni mukhyatīrthāni tatkṣetraprodbhavāni ca \|*  
*yeṣu snāto naraḥ smyaksarva tīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgāni ca mahābhāga tatra mukhyāni yāni ca \|*  
*yairdṛṣṭairlabhyate śreyaḥ sarveṣāṃ tāni no vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. Important holy places have been heard (described) and so also the origins of those shrines. It was made clear that a man who takes his holy bath there scrupulously obtains the benefit of all the Tīrthas.

Now, O highly esteemed one, describe to us all those Liṅgas, the important ones which, when seen (visited), grant the benefit of seeing all the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.266.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatra ca maṃkaṇākhyaṃ tu liṃgamasti suśobhanam \|*  
*tathā siddheśvaraṃ nāma gautameśvarasaṃyutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kapāleśvamanyacca caturthaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*ekaikaṃ sarvaliṃgānāṃ phalaṃ yacchatyasaṃśayam \|*  
*yathoktavidhinā samyagyathoktaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

3-4. There is that highly auspicious Liṅga named Maṅkaṇa; so also, there is Siddheśvara along with Gautameśvara. A fourth Liṅga is glorified by the name Kapāleśvara. Each of these grants the benefit of all the Liṅgas. There is no doubt about it. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, (they should be visited and adored) in accordance with the injunctions laid down.

## \|\| 1.266.5 \|\|

*tatra tāvatpravakṣyāmi maṃkaṇeśvarajaṃ phalam \|*  
*makārākṣarayuktasya liṃgasyātra dvijottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There I shall describe the benefit accruing from Maṅkaṇeśvara, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that of the Liṅga containing the syllable MA.

## \|\| 1.266.6-7 \|\|

*śivarātriṃ samāsādya yastasya puruṣo dvijāḥ \|*  
*kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ rātrau nirāhāraḥ sthitaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sarvaliṃgodbhavaṃ caiva phalaṃ darśanasaṃbhavam \|*  
*jāyate nātra saṃdeha ityuvāca haraḥ svayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O Brāhmaṇas, at the advent of Śiyarātri a man should observe fast and remain pure. He should also keep awake during the night. Hara himself says that there is no doubt that he will have the benefit resulting from a visit to all the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.266.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śivarātrirmahābhāga kasminkāle tu sā bhavet \|*  
*vidhyānaṃ caiva māhātmyaṃ sarvaṃ no vistarādvada \|\| 8 \|\|*

The sages said:

8\. O highly esteemed, one, when does Śivarātri occur? Describe to us in detail everything regarding the mode of worship and the greatness.

## \|\| 1.266.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| māghasya kṛṣṇapakṣe yā tithiścaiva caturdaśī \|*  
*tasyā rātriḥ samākhyātā śivarātrisamudbhavā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:

9\. The fourteenth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Māgha (is auspicious). The night thereof is termed Śivarātri.

## \|\| 1.266.10 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sarveṣu liṃgeṣu sadā saṃkramate haraḥ \|*  
*viśeṣātsarvapuṇyeṣu khyāteyaṃ maṃkaṇeśvare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On that night Hara always extends his presence over all the Liṅgas. Especially, the night at Maṅkaṇeśvara is well-known amongst all the meritorious (shrines).

## \|\| 1.266.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śivarātriḥ kathaṃ jātā kenaiṣā ca vinirmitā \|*  
*kasmādbahuphalā jātā sarvaṃ no vistarādvada \|\| 11 \|\|*

The sages said:

11\. How did Śivarātri come into being? By whom was this laid down? Why has it become a giver of many benefits? Describe everything to us in detail.

## \|\| 1.266.12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi pūrvavṛttaṃ kathānakam \|*  
*bhartṛyajñasya saṃvādamaśvasenasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12\. In this context I shall narrate to you an event that occurred earlier, the dialogue between Bhartṛyajña and King Aśvasena.

## \|\| 1.266.13 \|\|

*ānartādhipatiḥ pūrvamaśvasena iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*āsīddharmaparo nityaṃ vedavedāgaṃpāragaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Formerly, there was a monarch of Ānarta remembered by the name Aśvasena. He was pious and righteous always. He had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 1.266.14 \|\|

*bhartṛyajñaḥ purā tena idaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ kutūhalāt \|*  
*kalikālaṃ samudvīkṣya vardhamānaṃ dinedine \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing the (evil) period of Kali on the increase day be day, Aśvasena asked Bhartṛyajña thus in all earnestness:

## \|\| 1.266.15 \|\|

*aśvasena uvāca \|*  
*kalikālakṛte kiṃcidvrataṃ me vada sanmune \|*  
*svalpāyāsaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

Aśvasena said:

15\. O excellent sage, suggest unto me some Vrata proper for the period of Kali. It should be highly meritorious and destructive of all sins, but should involve very little effort or strain.

## \|\| 1.266.16 \|\|

*svalpāyuṣaḥ sadā martyā brahmankṛtayuge purā \|*  
*tretāyāṃ dvāpare caiva kimu prāpte kalau yuge \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Brāhmaṇa, men have always been of short span of life formerly even in Kṛtayuga, Tretāyuga and Dvāpara and still more so at the advent of Kaliyuga.

## \|\| 1.266.17 \|\|

*tasmādvarṣavrataṃ tyaktvā kiṃcidekāhnikaṃ vada \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence, exclude all the Vratas extending over a year. Tell me something covering only a single day.

## \|\| 1.266.18 \|\|

*śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikam \|*  
*na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vāsya na vā kṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One should carry out tomorrow’s work today itself, the work of afternoon in forenoon. The god of Death does not wait to see whether his (victim’s) work is completed or not.

## \|\| 1.266.19 \|\|

*tasya tadvacaṃ śrutvā bhartṛyajña udāradhīḥ \|*  
*abravītsuciraṃ dhyātvā jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing his words Bhartṛyajña of exalted intellect and liberal mind, meditated for a long time and spoke after knowing it through his divine vision:

## \|\| 1.266.20 \|\|

*asti rājanvrataṃ puṇyaṃ śivarātrītisaṃjñitam \|*  
*ekāhnikaṃ mahārāja sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

20\. O great king, there is an auspicious Vrata called Śivarātri Vrata. It lasts for only one day; O king, it destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.266.21 \|\|

*tatra yaddīyate dānaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti rātri jāgaraṇe kṛte \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If anything is given as a gift on that day, if a Homa is performed, and if Japa is practised, all these shall have everlasting benefit. The devotee should keep awake during the night.

## \|\| 1.266.22 \|\|

*aputro labhate putrānadhano dhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*svalpāyurdīrghamāyu्ṣyaṃ śatrūṇāṃ caiva saṃkṣayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. (As a result thereof) one without a son shall obtain sons, one without wealth shall get wealth, one of a short span of life will obtain longevity and also the destruction of his enemies.

## \|\| 1.266.23 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyanvratametatsamācaret \|*  
*taṃtaṃ samāpnuyānmartyo niṣkāmo mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A man shall obtain all desired objects in view of which he observes the Vrata. If he be desire-less, he attains Mokṣa (liberation from Saṃśāra).

## \|\| 1.266.24 \|\|

*kārpaṇyenātha vittena yadi kuryātprajāgaram \|*  
*tathā varṣakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If one observes the night vigil giving some money (even) in a niggardly spirit, one is undoubtedly rid of the sins committed during that year.

## \|\| 1.266.25 \|\|

*yāni kānyatra liṃgāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|*  
*teṣu saṃkramate devastasyāṃ rātrau yato haraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On that night, Lord Hara extends his presence unto all the Liṅgas, both mobile and immobile ones.

## \|\| 1.266.26 \|\|

*śivarātristataḥ proktā tena sā haravallabhā \|*  
*prārthitaḥ sa suraiḥ sarvairlokānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Therefore, it is called Śivarārti. It is a favourite of Hara. With a desire to bless all the worlds he was requested by all the Suras:

## \|\| 1.266.27-29 \|\|

*bhagavankalikāle'sminsarvapāpasamanvite \|*  
*varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ dinamekaṃ kṣitau vraja \|*  
*yena tvatpūjayā pūtā martyāḥ śuddhimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tato dattaṃ hutaṃ teṣāmasmākamupatiṣṭhati \|*  
*yaducchiṣṭaṃ narairdattaṃ tadvṛthā jāyate'khilam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kalikāle na cāsmākaṃ kiṃcidevopatiṣṭhati \|*  
*aśuddhairmānavairdattaṃ prabhūtamapi śaṃkara \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. “O Lord, during this age of Kali full of all kinds of sins, do go for a day to the earth for the purification of the sins of the year, so that by. performing your worship mortals may attain purity.

Thereupon, what is given and what is offered as oblation to fire by them shall come unto us. If men offer Ucchiṣṭa (leavings of food), that entirely goes to waste.

O Saṅkara, nothing offered by impure men during the period of Kali comes to us even if it be ample and plentiful.”

## \|\| 1.266.30 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*māghamāsasya kṛṣṇāyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ sureśvara \|*  
*ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhūpṛṣṭhe rātrau naiva divā kalau \|\| 30 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

30\. O Lord of Suras, on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of Māgha, I will go to the earth in the Kali age during the night and not by the day.

## \|\| 1.266.31 \|\|

*liṃgeṣu ca samasteṣu caleṣu sthāvareṣu ca \|*  
*saṃkramiṣyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ varṣapāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Undoubtedly, I will move over to all the Liṅgas mobile and immobile for the purpose of purifying sins committed during the year.

## \|\| 1.266.32 \|\|

*tasyāṃ rātrau hi me pūjāṃ yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*maṃtrairetaiḥ suraśreṣṭha vipāpmā sa bhaviṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On that night, O excellent one among Suras, a man who performs my worship by means of these Mantras shall be free from sins:

## \|\| 1.266.33 \|\|

*oṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ ghorāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ īśānāya namaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vaktrāṇi saṃpūjya gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*vastrairdīpaiśca naivedyaistato'rghaṃ saṃpradāpayet \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena saṃpūjya māṃ dhyātvā manasi sthitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “Oṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta. Oṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva. Oṃ, obeisance to Ghora. Oṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa. Oṃ, obeisance to Īśāna.” The devotee should worship these faces thus by means of scents, flowers and fragrant pastes as well as garments, lamps and food offerings.

Then Meditating on me as stationed in the mind he should offer Arghya after worshipping me with this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.266.34 \|\|

*gaurīvallabha deveśa sarvādya śaśiśekhara \|*  
*varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthamargho me pratigṛhyatām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “O Lord of Devas, O lover of Gaurī, O moon-crested one, O primordial one among all, may the Arghya be accepted for the purpose of purifying all the sins committed during the year.”

## \|\| 1.266.35 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjayedvipraṃ bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ \|*  
*dattvātha dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he should honour a Brāhmaṇa with food, garments etc. Without resorting to miserliness, monetary gift has to be made liberally.

## \|\| 1.266.36 \|\|

*dharmākhyānakathābhiśca salāsyaistāṃḍavaistathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. There should be narration of religious stories along with dances of graceful as well as Tāṇḍava type.

## \|\| 1.266.37 \|\|

*evaṃ kariṣyate yo'tra vratametatsureśvara \|*  
*varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Sureśvara, if anyone observes the Vrata thus for the purification of sins committed during the year, it shall be the proper atonement.

## \|\| 1.266.38 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tridaśāḥ sarve praṇamya śaśiśekharam \|*  
*saṃprahṛṣṭā naraśreṣṭha svāni sthānāni bhejire \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing this all the Devas bowed down to the Moon-crested Lord, O most excellent one among men. With great delight they went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 1.266.39 \|\|

*preṣayāmāsururvyāṃ ca nāradaṃ munisattamam \|*  
*prabodhanāya lokānāṃ śivarātrikṛte sadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In order to enlighten people always in regard to Śivarātri, they sent Nārada, the greatest sage, to the earth.

## \|\| 1.266.40 \|\|

*so'pi gatvā dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ śrāvayāmāsa sarvataḥ \|*  
*śivarātrestu māhātmyaṃ yaduktaṃ śūlapāṇinā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He too went to the earth and proclaimed everywhere the greatness of Śivarātri as narrated by the Trident-bearing One.

## \|\| 1.266.41 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti saṃjātā śivarātrirdharātale \|*  
*sarvakāmapradā puṇyā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Ever since then there came into vogue on the earth, the meritorious Śivarātri that grants all the cherished desires and destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.266.42 \|\|

*atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi purāvṛttaṃ kathānakam \|*  
*yadvṛttaṃ naimiṣāraṇye lubdhakasyātra kasyacit \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In this connection I shall relate unto you all, the story of an incident that happened long ago to a fowler in the Naimiṣa forest.

## \|\| 1.266.43 \|\|

*tatrāsīllubdhakaḥ kaścijjātimātrānna karmataḥ \|*  
*vyasenānābhibhūtātmā paravittāpahārakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There was a fowler who was so only by birth and not through mere activities of his caste. His mind was overwhelmed by indulgences (in vice). He stole other’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.266.44 \|\|

*na kadācidvrataṃ tena na dattaṃ na japaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*kevalaṃ ca hṛtaṃ vittaṃ lokānāṃ chalasaṃśrayāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He was one who never observed a Vrata, practised charity or performed Japa. The only work he did was to take away other people’s money by fraudulent means.

## \|\| 1.266.45 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya śivarātriḥ samāgatā \|*  
*māghamāse'sitepakṣe sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Once it was the holy night of Śivarātri in the dark half of the month of Māgha-Śivarāri \[Śivarātri?\] that destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.266.46 \|\|

*tatrāstyāyatanaṃ puṇyaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*tatra jāgaraṇaṃ rātrau prārabdhaṃ bahubhirjjanaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There was a holy shrine of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas. Many people had just started the vigil at night.

## \|\| 1.266.47 \|\|

*nārībhirnaraśārdūla bhūṣitābhiḥ subhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*athāsau ciṃtayāmāsa coro dṛṣṭvātha jāgaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O tiger among men, the place was filled by women adorned by excellent ornaments. Seeing that people were keeping awake, the thief thought thus:

## \|\| 1.266.48-49 \|\|

*gacchāmi yadi kāṃcitstrīṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ paribhūṣitām \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtāṃ bāhyataścāsya prāsādasyāpnuyāmaham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tato hatvā samādāya bhūṣaṇāni vrajāmyaham \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. ‘I shall go there and see if I can get at some woman well-adorned with ornaments coming out of that mansion. Then I shall kill her, snatch the ornaments and get away.’

## \|\| 1.266.50 \|\|

*evaṃ niścitya manasā gatastasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*karṇikāraṃ samāruhya sthito guptastato hi saḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After resolving thus mentally, he approached the shrine. Climbing up a Karṇikāra tree, he hid himself there.

## \|\| 1.266.51 \|\|

*vīkṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvā nārīniṣkrāmaṇodbhavāḥ \|*  
*caurakarmapravṛttasya śītārtasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He was watching the different quarters from where there was the possibility of some woman coming out. The fellow who was thus ready to commit robbery was very severely distressed due to cold.

## \|\| 1.266.52 \|\|

*alpāpi nidrā nāyātā na ca nārī vinirgatā \|*  
*tasyādhastāttato liṃgamabhavattu dharodbhavam \|*  
*gatvā ca patrāṇyādāya pracikṣepāsya copari \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He could not sleep even for a wink. Nor was there any sign of any woman coming out. There was a Liṅga beneath the tree. It had sprung up from the ground. He went up, plucked a few leaves and threw them over the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.266.53 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu prodgatastīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*asatīnāṃ ca caurāṇāṃ kāmināmasukhāvahaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In the meantime, there rose up in the sky the sun of hot rays, who never causes happiness to unchaste women, thieves and lustful persons.

## \|\| 1.266.54 \|\|

*tato narāśca nāryaśca jagmuḥ svaṃsvaṃ niketanam \|*  
*upacāraparāḥ śāṃtāḥ praṇipatya maheśvaram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then the men and women bowed down to Maheśvara. After rendering the services to the Lord, they became quiescent and went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 1.266.55 \|\|

*so'pi cauro nirāśaśca kṣutkṣāmaḥ śītavihvalaḥ \|*  
*avatīrya drumāttasmādupāyaṃ kaṃcidāśritaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Having lost all hope and becoming distressed due to hunger and cold the thief got down from the tree by some means.

## \|\| 1.266.56 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā paṃcatvaṃ samapadyata \|*  
*jāto jātismaraḥ so'tha daśārṇādhipatergṛhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. After a long time he met with his death. He was reborn in the palace of the ruler of Daśārṇa. He could then remember the previous birth.

## \|\| 1.266.57 \|\|

*upavāsaprabhāvena balādapi prajāgarāt \|*  
*śivarātrestathā tasya liṅgasyāpi prapūjayā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All this was due to the power of his fast and vigil kept under duress on the Śivarātri day as well as to the adoration of that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.266.58 \|\|

*tato rājyaṃ samāsādya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat \|*  
*kārayāmāsa liṃgasya prāsādaṃ tasya śobhanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After inheriting the great kingdom of his father and grandfather, he got a great and splendid mansion erected over the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.266.59-60 \|\|

*varṣevarṣe samāśritya śivarātrau prajāgarāt \|*  
*upavāsaparobhūtvā gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dharmākhyānakathābhiśca gītadhvanibhireva ca \|*  
*pūrvoktamaṃtraiḥ saṃpūjya arghaṃ dattvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*saṃtarpya brāhmaṇānkāmairjagāma nilayaṃ nijam \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Every year on the Śivarātri day he used to come there, observe fast and keep awake during the night singing and playing on musical instruments, listening to religious discourses and narration of pious stories. He used to adore reciting the Mantras cited before and offer Arghya in accordance with the injunctions. He then propitiated Brāhmaṇas by giving them whatever they desired. Thereafter, he used to return to his abode.

## \|\| 1.266.61 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya śivarātrau samāgatāḥ \|*  
*prāsāde tatra munayaḥ prāptā śāṇḍilyapūrvakāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Once, on the Śivarātri day, Śāṇḍilya and other sages came to the mansion of that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.266.62 \|\|

*śāṃḍilyo'tha bharadvājo yavakrīto'tha gālavaḥ \|*  
*pulastyaḥ pulaho gārgyastathānye bahavo nṛpa \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They were Śāṇḍilya, Bharadvāja, Yavakrīta, Gālava, Pulastya, Pulaha, Gārgya and many others, O king.

## \|\| 1.266.63 \|\|

*so'pi rājā bṛhatseno daśārṇādhipateḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpto jāgaraṃ kartuṃ tasya liṃgasya cāgrataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. King Bṛhatsena, son of the ruler of Daśārṇa, also came there for the observance of vigil in front of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.266.64 \|\|

*pūjayitvā tato devaṃ praṇipatya munīśvarān \|*  
*upaviṣṭastasya cāgre hyanujñāto dvijottamaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. After adoring the Lord, and bowing down to the leading sages, he sat before the Liṅga with the permission of the excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.266.65 \|\|

*tatastasyāgrataścakruḥ kathāste bahudhā nṛpa \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāmatītānāṃ brahmarṣīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then, O king, they held various discourses and religious dialogues, and told and listened to especially the stories of ancient saintly kings and Brāhmaṇa-sages who had passed away.

## \|\| 1.266.66 \|\|

*atha kasminkathāṃte sa taiḥ pṛṣṭo brahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*kautukāviṣṭacittaiśca vismayotphullalocanaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then at the conclusion of a certain discourse, he was asked by the expounders of the, Vedas whose curiosity had been aroused and whose eyes shone remarkably due to Wonder:

## \|\| 1.266.67 \|\|

*rājanpṛcchāmahe sarve vayaṃ kautūhalānvitāḥ \|*  
*yadi bravīṣi naḥ satyaṃ devatāyatane sthitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “O king, urged by curiosity, we are inclined to ask you something if only you will speak out the truth, as you are in the holy shrine.”

## \|\| 1.266.68 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*yadi jñāsyāmi vipreṃdrāḥ kathayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|*  
*devasyāgre ca saṃpṛṣṭaḥ satyenātmānamālabhe \|\| 68 \|\|*

The king said:

68\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, if I know I will undoubtedly speak it out. Now asked in the presence of the Lord, I take a solemn pledge to tell the truth.

## \|\| 1.266.69 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*puṣkalāni parityajya kasmāddānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*jāgaraṃ kartukāmo'tra svadeśādupatiṣṭhasi \|\| 69 \|\|*

The sages said:

69\. Having refused to make a number of abundant religious gifts instead, merely for keeping a vigil, you have come over here from your native place.

## \|\| 1.266.70 \|\|

*varṣevarṣe sadā prāpte nūnaṃ tvaṃ vetsi kāraṇam \|*  
*rahasyaṃ yadi te na syāttadbravīhi narādhipa \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. This occurs every year. Indeed you know the purpose and reason thereof. O king, if it not be a closely guarded secret, do tell us about it.

## \|\| 1.266.71-72 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*savailakṣyaṃ smitaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ prāha sa durmanāḥ \|*  
*rahasyaṃ paramaṃ hyetadavācyaṃ hi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tathāpi ca vadiṣyāmi pṛṣṭo devāgrato yataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

Sūta said:

71-72. The king was rather moody. He vaguely smiled under chagrin and said: “O excellent Brāhmaṇas, indeed this is a great secret not to be divulged ordinarily. Still I shall tell it since I have been asked in the presence of the deity.”

## \|\| 1.266.73 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa pūrvadehasamudbhavam \|*  
*malimlucastato nūnaṃ śivarātrisamudbhavam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then he disclosed everything that happened in the previous birth of the thief on the night of Śivarātri.

## \|\| 1.266.74 \|\|

*cauryabhāvena devasya pūjanaṃ jāgarastathā \|*  
*upavāsaṃ vinā tena śivarātrau purā kṛtam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He mentioned to them how he had to keep awake though with an intention of committing theft and how he had to refrain from taking food without the direct adoration of the Lord on the Śivarātri day.

## \|\| 1.266.75 \|\|

*jātismaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ janmajātaṃ yathātatham \|*  
*tataste munayaḥ sarve sādhuvādānpṛthagvidhān \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. He told them how he was reborn with the power of recollecting the previous birth. Thereupon, all the sages expressed the warmest appreciation in diverse ways.

## \|\| 1.266.76 \|\|

*nṛpottamasya rājarṣerdattvāśīrbhiḥ samanvitān \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prajagmuste nijāśramān \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. After congratulating the saintly king, the most excellent king, they bestowed their benedictions on him. After keeping awake during the night, they went to their hermitages.

## \|\| 1.266.77 \|\|

*so'pi rājāsamabhyarcya taṃ devaṃ tāndvijottamān \|*  
*jagāma svapuraṃ paścātkṛtvā rātrau prajāgaram \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The king too duly worshipped the deity and honoured the excellent Brāhmaṇas. Afterwards he kept awake during the night and returned to his city.

## \|\| 1.266.78 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*śivarātriḥ samutpannā evaṃ bhūmitale nṛpa \|*  
*evaṃvidhaṃ ca māhātmyaṃ tasyāste parikīrtitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

78\. It was thus, O king, that Śivarātri came into vogue on the earth. The greatness of it has been already described to you.

## \|\| 1.266.79 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryā sa nṛpasattama \|*  
*kalikāle viśeṣeṇa ya icchedbhūtimātmanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Hence, O excellent king, that should be observed with all efforts, particularly in Kali Age, by one who wishes for his own prosperity.

## \|\| 1.266.80-81 \|\|

*eṣā kṛtā dilīpena nalena nahuṣeṇa ca \|*  
*māndhātrā dhuṃdhumāreṇa sagareṇa yuyutsunā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*tathānyaiśca viśeṣeṇa samyakchraddhāsamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*prāptāśca hṛdgatāḥ kāmā ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. This was observed by Dilīpa, Nala, Nahuṣa, Māndhātṛ, Dhundhumāra, Sagara, Yuyutsu and others who entertained perfect faith. Of course they attained their cherished desires both divine and human.

## \|\| 1.266.82-83 \|\|

*tathā caiva tu sāvitryā śriyā devyā tu sītayā \|*  
*aruṃdhatyā sarasvatyā menayā raṃbhayā tathā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*iṃdrāṇyātha dṛṣadvatyā svadhayā svāhayā tathā \|*  
*ratyā prītyā prabhāvatyā gāyatryā ca nṛpottama \|*  
*sarvāḥ prāptāḥ priyānkāmānatisaubhāgyasaṃyutān \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Similarly, it was observed by goddesses Śrī, Sāvitrī, Sītā, Arundhatī, Sarasvatī, Menā, Raṃbhā, Indrāṇī, Dṛṣadvatī, Svadhā, Svāhā, Rati, Prīti, Prabhāvatī and Gāyatrī, O excellent king. All of them attained their cherished objects along with greatest conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.266.84 \|\|

*yaścaitāṃ paṭhate vyuṣṭiṃ bhāvena śivasaṃnidhau \|*  
*dinajātpātakātso'pi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. If anyone reads about this benefit in the presence of Śiva with devotional fervour, he shall undoubtedly get rid of the sin committed that day.

## \|\| 1.266.85 \|\|

*nāsti gaṃgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti devo haropamaḥ \|*  
*śivarātreḥ paraṃ nāsti tapaḥ satyaṃ mayoditam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. There is no Tīrtha on a par with Gaṅgā; there is no other Lord comparable to Śiva; there is no penance greater than Śivarātri. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.266.86 \|\|

*sarvaratnamayo meruḥ sarvāścaryamayaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*sarvadharmamayī rājañchivarātriḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Meru is full of all Ratnas (jewels); penance is full of all miracles. O king, Śivarātri has been glorified as being full of all righteousness (Dharma).

## \|\| 1.266.87 \|\|

*garuḍaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ yadvannadīnāṃ sāgaro yathā \|*  
*pradhānaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ śivarātristathottamā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Just as Garuḍa is the most important one among birds, just as ocean is the chief of all rivers, so also the observance of Śivarātri is the most important one among all holy rites.

## Chapter 267 - Importance of Tulāpuruṣadāna (Tulāpuruṣa-dāna)

## \|\| 1.267.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasmādeṣā mahārāja śivarātrirvipaścitā \|\| \|*  
*kartavyā puruṣeṇātra lokadvayamabhīpsunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*maṃkaṇeśvaramāhātmyaṃ mayā vistarataḥ śrutam \|*  
*śivarātrisamopetaṃ yattvayā parikīrtitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sāṃprataṃ vada me kṛtsnaṃ siddheśvarasamudbhavam \|*  
*vistareṇa mahābhāga paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 3 \|\|*

Note: Tulāpuruṣadāna is a Mahādāna. In this the donor is to weigh himself against gold or silver in the other pan of the balance and distribute it to Brāhmaṇas. For details see Matsya P. ch. 274. See also Hemādri’s Dāna Khaṇḍa.

Sūta said:

1-3. Hence, O great king, this Śivarātri is to be observed by a wise man desirous of getting the benefit of both the worlds.

## \|\| 1.267.4 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*siddheśvara iti khyāto mahādevo mahīpate \|*  
*tasyotpattistvayā pūrvaṃ śrutātra vadato mama \|\| 4 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

The greatness of Maṅkaṇeśvara has been listened to by me in its detail along with the celebration of Śivarātri as has been glorified by you. Now do describe to me entirely the glory of Siddheśvara in detail. O highly esteemed one, my eagerness is great.

Bhartṛyajña said:

4\. O king, there is a Mahādeva shrine well-known as Siddheśvara. its origin has been listened to by you from my statement.

## \|\| 1.267.5 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ tatphalaṃ vacmi tasmindṛṣṭe tu dānajam \|*  
*yatphalaṃ jāyate nṝṇāṃ cakravartitva saṃbhavam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Now I shall tell you the fruit of a visit to that deity. It is the same as accrues to an emperor when he makes a gift of his entire kingdom.

## \|\| 1.267.6 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca tatra rājanpraśaśyate \|*  
*ya iccheccakravartitvaṃ samaste dharaṇītale \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The gift called Tulāpuruṣa (donating gold or silver equal to one’s own weight) there, is being praised, O king. One who desires imperial power over the entire earth should make such a gift.

## \|\| 1.267.7 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*tulāpuruṣadānasya yo vidhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ me sarvaṃ samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmune \|\| 7 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

7\. O great sage, tell me in detail the procedure for the Dāna called Tulāpuruṣa, that has been so glorified.

## \|\| 1.267.8-10 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*caṃdrasūryoparāge vā ayane viṣuve tathā \|*  
*tīrthe vā puruṣaśreṣṭha tulāpuruṣasaṃbhavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*praśaṃsaṃti vidhiṃ samyakprāpte vā ceṃdusaṃkṣaye \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ sudāṃtānāmanuṣṭhānavatāṃ satām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vedādhyayanayuktānāṃ nirdoṣāṇāṃ ca pārthiva \|*  
*vibhajya sa bhaveddeyo naikasya ca kathaṃcana \|\| 10 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

8-10. The proper time for Tulāpuruṣadāna is the event when a solar or lunar eclipse occurs, the two main transits of the Sun take place, the equinoxes and the waning of the Moon (i.e. the New Moon) occur. People praise the gift of Tulāpuruṣa in a holy spot.

The said gift is to be made to Brāhmaṇas of great self-control, good people who regularly practice the study of the Vedas, O king! They should be free from defects. The gift is not to be restricted to a single individual at all. It should be distributed among many.

## \|\| 1.267.11 \|\|

*śucau deśe same puṇye pūrvottaraplave śubhe \|*  
*maṃḍapaṃ kārayedvidvānramyaṃ ṣa़ोśahastakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A beautiful pavilion should be constructed by a wise person (the donor). It should be sixteen hands in extent. The place selected should be holy and pure and level with a declivity towards the north-east.

## \|\| 1.267.12 \|\|

*tanmadhye kārayedvediṃ caturhasta pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*yajamānasya hastena hastaikena samucchritām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Vedi (Altar) should be made in the centre. Its width should be four Hastas (hands), and the height, one Hasta of the donor.

## \|\| 1.267.13 \|\|

*caturhastāni kuṇḍāni caturdikṣu prakalpayeta \|*  
*ekahastapramāṇāni āyāmavyāsavistarāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Four Kuṇḍas (holy pits) should be dug in the four quarters. Each of them should be four Hastas in depth and one Hasta in girth.

## \|\| 1.267.14 \|\|

*aiśānyāmaparāṃ vediṃ hastamātrāṃ nyasecchubhām \|*  
*ratnimātrotthitāṃ caiva grahāṃstatra prakalpayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On the north-eastern corner a splendid Vedi should be made. It should have a width of a Hasta and the height should be one Ratni (half of a Hasta, a span).

## \|\| 1.267.15 \|\|

*yugmāṃśca ṛtvijaḥ kāryāścaturdikṣu yathākramam \|*  
*bahvṛco'dhvaryaścaiva cchaṃdogātharvaṇāvapi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Two Ṛtviks should be placed in each quarter. They shall be posted in due order viz. two Bahvṛcas (Ṛgveda), two Adhvaryus (Yajurveda), two Chāndogas (Sāmavedins) and two Atharvaṇas).

## \|\| 1.267.16 \|\|

*tūṣṇīṃ tu devatāhomastaiḥ kāryaḥ susamāhitaiḥ \|*  
*talliṃgairnṛpatemaṃtraiḥ svaśaktyā japa eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Homa to deities should be performed by them silently and with great concentration. O king, they should perform Japa in accordance with their capacity with Mantras signifying their purpose.

## \|\| 1.267.17 \|\|

*ekahastapraviṣṭaṃ tu caturhastocchritaṃ tathā \|*  
*staṃbhadvayaṃ tu kartavyaṃ vediyāmyottare sthitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Two pillars are to be erected to the south and the north of the Vedi. The pillars should be four Hastas above the ground and they go down to one Hasta in the ground.

## \|\| 1.267.18-19 \|\|

*tanmadhye suśubhaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ staṃbhajātyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ nyaset \|*  
*candanaḥ khadiro vātha bilvovā'śvattha eva vā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tiṃduko devadārurvā śrīparṇī vā vaṭo'thavā \|*  
*aṣṭau vṛkṣāḥ śubhāḥ śastāḥ staṃbhārthaṃ nṛpasattam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. In the middle thereof one should fit in a log very firmly. This log should be of the same timber as that of the pillar. Eight different types of timber are recommended much for the purpose of a pillar, O excellent king, viz. Candana, Khadira, Bilva, Aśvattha, Tinduka, Devadāru, Śrīparṇī or Vaṭa.

## \|\| 1.267.20 \|\|

*śikyadvaya samopetāṃ tanmadhye vinyasettulām \|*  
*snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The balance should have two pans and it should be placed therein. The devotee should have had his bath. He must be clad in white garments. He should wear garlands of white flowers and smear himself with white unguents.

## \|\| 1.267.21 \|\|

*pūrayitvā samaṃtācca lokapālānyathākramam \|*  
*staṃbhānsaṃpūjayatpaścādgandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At the outset he must adore the Guardians of the Quarters around in due order. Thereafter, he should worship the pillars with sweet scents, garlands and unguents.

## \|\| 1.267.22-23 \|\|

*tulāṃ ca pārthivaśreṣṭha puṇyāhaṃ ca prakīrtayet \|*  
*yajamāno nijaiḥ sarvairāyudhaiḥ kāyasaṃsthitaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*paścimāṃ diśamāsthāya prāṅmukhaḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā imaṃ maṃtramudīrayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. O excellent king, he should adore the balance too and then recite the Punyāhavācana Mantras. The householder then keeps all his weapons on his person, stands at the western extremity (pan); facing the East with great faith with the palms joined in reverence he should utter this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.267.24-25 \|\|

*brahmaṇo duhitā nityaṃ satyaṃ paramamāśritā \|*  
*kāśyapī gotrataścaiva nāmato viśrutā tulā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tvaṃ tule satyanāmāsi svabhīṣṭaṃ cātmanaḥ śubham \|*  
*kariṣyāmi prasādaṃ me sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru sāṃpratam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. “It is the daughter of Brahma resorting permanently to the greatest truth. It is Kāśyapī by lineage and is well-known by the name Tulā.

O Tulā, you are the very truth by your very name. I shall make my desire auspicious. Be pleased now and be present.”

## \|\| 1.267.26-27 \|\|

*tatastasyāṃ samāruhya svaśaktyā yatsamāhṛtam \|*  
*dānārthaṃ pūrvamāyojyaṃ śikyenyasminnarottama \|\| 26 \|\|*

*suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vā'tha vastraṃ cānyadabhīpsitam \|*  
*yāvatsāmyaṃ bhavedrājannātmano'bhyadhikaṃ ca vā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Thereafter, he gets on to one of the pans. O excellent king, he then places on the other pan what he has already thought of and collected together to the extent of his capacity for the purpose of the gift.

## \|\| 1.267.28-29 \|\|

*tato'bhīṣṭāṃ samāsādya devatāṃ śikyamāśritaḥ \|*  
*udakaṃ jalamadhye ca tadarthaṃ prakṣipeddrutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*satilaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ ca sākṣataṃ vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*avatīrya tataḥ sarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. He then mentally approaches (thinks of) the deity loved remaining on the pan itself. He then drops a little water along with gingelly seeds, raw rice grain and gold in accordance with injunctions for the deity. He then gets down and distributes everything to the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.267.30 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ prāpyate paścāttadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Listen with attention to the fruit that is going to be obtained.

## \|\| 1.267.31 \|\|

*ajānatā jānatā vā yatpāpaṃ tu bhavetkṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśayenmartyo dānasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By the power of the Dāna, this man gets rid of all the sins committed (by him) knowingly or unknowingly.

## \|\| 1.267.32 \|\|

*yāvanmātraṃ kṛtaṃ pāpamatītaṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*tāvanmātraṃ kṣayaṃ yāti tulāpuruṣadānataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O excellent king, as a result of the Puruṣadāna only that much of the sin already committed earlier is dissolved,

## \|\| 1.267.33 \|\|

*īśvarāṇāṃ samādiṣṭaṃ kāyakleśabhayātmanām \|*  
*puraścaraṇametaddhi dānaṃ taulyasamudbhavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Dāna pertaining to the weighing in the balance has been enjoined as Puraścaraṇa (preparatory rite) in the case of lordly ones afraid of physical strain.

## \|\| 1.267.34 \|\|

*etaddattaṃ dilīpena kārtavīryeṇa bhūpate \|*  
*pṛthunā purukutsena tathānyairapi pārthivaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. This was performed by Dilīpa, Kārtavīrya, Pṛthu, Purukutsa and other kings as well, O king.

## \|\| 1.267.35 \|\|

*etatpuṇyaṃ praśasyaṃ ca sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca sarvopadravanāśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This Tulāpuruṣadāna is destructive of all torments. This is praiseworthy and meritorious. It grants to men all their cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.267.36 \|\|

*ādhayo vyādhayo na syurna vaidhavyaṃ gadodbhavam \|*  
*saṃjāyate nṛpaśreṣṭha na viyogaḥ svabandhubhiḥ \|*  
*tulāpuruṣadānasya phalametadudāhṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. One will never have anxieties and ailments. Widowhood is averted. There will never be misery due to sickness. O excellent king, one will never be separated from one’s kinsmen. This has been cited as the fruit of offering Tulāpuruṣadāna.

## \|\| 1.267.37 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣadānasya pradattasya nṛpottama \|*  
*na śakyate kathayituṃ phalaṃ yatsyātkalau yuge \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O excellent king, it is impossible to express adequately the benefit that may accrue in Kali Age when Tulāpuruṣadāna is performed.

## \|\| 1.267.38 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāmūrtimāsādya siddheśvaravibhoḥ puraḥ \|*  
*yaḥ prayacchati bhūpāla sahasraguṇitaṃ phalam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If a devotee approaches Lord Dakṣiṇāmūrti, O king, and offers it before Lord Siddheśvara, the benefit is thousandfold.

## \|\| 1.267.39 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena prāpya siddheśvaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ suvivekinā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence, a man of discrimination should perform Tulāpuruṣadāna by all means after approaching Lord Siddheśvara.

## \|\| 1.267.40 \|\|

*ekatra sarvatīrthāni sarvāṇyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre kathitāni svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On one side are all the Tīrthas, all the shrines, mentioned by the Self-born Lord in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, and on the other is Siddheśvara, the most excellent of all Suras. O excellent King, if he is seen, touched and adored, the man obtains the benefit of all (in the manner) glorified.

## Chapter 268 - Description of Pṛthvīdāna (Pṛthvī-dāna)

## \|\| 1.268.1 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*karmaṇā kena martye ca narāṇāṃ jāyate vada \|*  
*cakravartitvamakhilaṃ sarvaśatruvimardanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Pṛthvīdāna or Dharādāna is another Mahādāna. It is described in the Matsya Purāṇa, Chapter 284. Another name of this Dāna is Himadharādāna which means gifting a symbolic gold replica of the Earth, which is to be prepared with recitation of certain prescribed verses. Half of that gold is to be given to the preceptor and half to other Brāhmaṇas.

Ānarta said:

1\. Do tell me how and by what rite and act in the mortal world do men attain emperorship that is destructive of all enemies.

## \|\| 1.268.2-3 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*durlabhaṃ bhūmipālatvaṃ sarvapāpairnarādhipa \|*  
*tapobhirniyamairdānaistathānyaiśca śubhairvrataiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yaḥ punarbhūpatirbhūtvā pṛthvīṃ dadyāddhiraṇmayīm \|*  
*gautameśvaradevasya purataḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*cakravartī bhavennūnamevamāha pitāmahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

2-3. It is difficult to attain the rulership of the earth on account of all sorts of sins. If at all one becomes the ruler of a kingdom by means of austerities, restraints, Dānas and other auspicious Vratas, one should then make a gift of the earth made of gold with perfect faith, before Lord Gautameśvara. One shall then become an emperor certainly. So says Pitāmaha.

## \|\| 1.268.4 \|\|

*māṃdhātā dhundhumāraśca hariścaṃdraḥ purūravāḥ \|*  
*bharataḥ kārtavīryaśca ṣaḍete cakravartinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Māndhātṛ, Dhundhumāra, Hariścandra, Purūravas, Bharata and Kārtavīrya—these six were the emperors of the world.

## \|\| 1.268.5 \|\|

*pṛthvīdānaṃ purā kṛtvā gautameśvarasaṃnidhau \|*  
*dattvā hiraṇmayīṃ pṛthvīṃ sārvabhaumāstataḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It was due to the gift of Pṛthvī formerly in the presence of Gautameśvara. They made a gift of the earth made of gold and then became imperial monarchs.

## \|\| 1.268.6 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*bhagavankena vidhinā dātavyā sā vasundharā \|*  
*ahaṃ dāsyāmi tāṃ nūnaṃ śraddhā me mahatī sthitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

6\. O holy Sir, what is the procedure whereby the earth is to be gifted over? I will certainly make Dāna of the earth. I entertain a great faith therein (that Dāna).

## \|\| 1.268.7 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*kāryā palaśatenorvī vṛttākārā nṛpottama \|*
