*tadardhenāthavā śaktyā paṃcaviṃśatpalātmikā \|\| 7 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

7\. O excellent king, a (globular symbol of the) Earth should be made with a hundred Palas of gold, or with a half thereof or if one’s capacity is less the replica is made with twenty-five Palas.

## \|\| 1.268.8 \|\|

*dharādāne mahārāja vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*naiva paṃcapalādarvākpradātavyā kathañcana \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In regard to the Dāna called Dharā-dāna, O great king, one should avoid Vittaśāṭhya, i.e. dishonesty in spending money for the rite.

## \|\| 1.268.9 \|\|

*lavaṇekṣusurāsarpirdadhidugdhajalodbhavāḥ \|*  
*samudrāḥ sapta caitāṃstu kakṣāyāṃ tatra darśayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Anyway no less than five Palas should be used. The devotee should mark there (on the replica) in separate areas (cavities) the seven great oceans namely those of salt, sugarcane juice, liquor, ghee, curd, milk and water.

## \|\| 1.268.10 \|\|

*jaṃbūplakṣakuśakrauṃcaśākaśālmalipuṣkarāḥ \|*  
*samudrānsaritaḥ sapta dvaiguṇyena prakalpayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the continents of Jaṃbū, Plakṣa, Kuśa, Krauñca, Śāka, Śālmali and Puṣkara and the seven rivers and oceans should be marked, each of the continents and oceans being double the previous one.

## \|\| 1.268.11 \|\|

*mahendro malayaḥ sahyo himavāngaṃdhamādanaḥ \|*  
*viṃdhyaḥ śṛṃgī ca saptaiva kalpayetkulaparvatān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then should be marked the seven Kulaparvatas viz. Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Himavān, Gandhamādana, Vindhya and Śṛṅgī.

## \|\| 1.268.12 \|\|

*madhye prakalpayenmeruṃ dikṣu viṣkambhaparvatān \|*  
*jaṃbūnyagrodhanīpāṃśca plakṣaścaiva tathā drumān \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the centre the devotee shows Meru and the Viṣkaṃbhas (the supporters i.e. adjacent mountains) in four directions (these were supposed to prop up Mount Meru). Similarly he shows the trees Jaṃbū, Nyagrodha, Nīpa and Plakṣa.

## \|\| 1.268.13 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāḥ saritastatra prādhānyena prakalpayet \|*  
*evaṃ nirmāpya vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ hemamayīṃ nṛpa \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Gaṅgā and other rivers should be shown there prominently. This concludes the building up of the replica of entire earth in gold, O king.

## \|\| 1.268.14 \|\|

*maṃḍapaṃ kārayetpaścādyathāpūrvaṃ prakalpitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, he sets up a pavilion as was done before (in Tulāpuruṣadāna).

## \|\| 1.268.15 \|\|

*kuṇḍāni toraṇānyeva brāhmaṇagrahapūjane \|*  
*pūrvavatsakalaṃ kṛtvā madhye vediṃ prakalpayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Arched gateways, etc. should be made, Kuṇḍas for the adoration of the Brāhmaṇas and the planets. After doing everything as before (in the Tulāpuruṣadāna) a Vedi (altar) is made in the centre.

## \|\| 1.268.16 \|\|

*tatra saṃsthāpayetpṛthvīṃ paṃcagavyena pārthiva \|*  
*yathoktamaṃtraistalliṃgaistataḥ śuddhodakena tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There the donor should place the (replica of the) earth after bathing it in Pañcagavya with the prescribed Mantras as well as their Liṅgas (signs or marks). Then, it is bathed in pure water.

## \|\| 1.268.17 \|\|

*imaṃ me gaṃge yamune paṃcanadyastripuṣkaram \|*  
*śrīsūktaṃ pāvamānaṃ ca haimīṃ ca tadanaṃtaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Mantras are those beginning with imam me gaṅge yamune (RVX. 155), pañcanadyaḥ (VS 34.11), tripuṣkaram, śrīsūkta, pāvamāna and haimi.

## \|\| 1.268.18 \|\|

*snānakarmaṇi yogyāṃśa svādiṣṭhāyanamuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. All these Mantras are very much relevant to the rite of ablution. “It shall be the excellent and tastiest base.” (obscure)

## \|\| 1.268.19 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃsnāpya vidhivadvāsāṃsi paridhāpayet \|*  
*yuvā suvāsā maṃtreṇa sūkṣmāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After bathing in this manner, the devotee recites yuvā suvāsā Mantra and covers (the replica) with different kinds of cloths of delicate fabric.

## \|\| 1.268.20 \|\|

*ye bhūtānāmadhītyevaṃ tataḥ procya prapūjayet \|*  
*dhūrasīti ca maṃtreṇa dhūpaṃ dadyātsamāhitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After reciting the Mantra beginning with ye bhūtānām, adhi (Vāi-saṃ 16.59) the devotee worships. With great concentration he offers incense reciting the Mantra dhūrasi.

## \|\| 1.268.21 \|\|

*agnirjyotīti maṃtreṇa kuryādārārtikaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*ahamasmīti maṃtreṇa saptadhānyaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Reciting the Mantra agniḥ jyotiḥ etc. he performs Ārārtika (waving of the lights). The seven kinds of grain are offered reciting the Mantra aham asmi etc.

## \|\| 1.268.22 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā'khilaṃ tasyā yajamānaḥ sitāṃbaraḥ \|*  
*puraḥ sthitoṃjaliṃ baddhvā maṃtrānetānudāharet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After performing all these things, the householder (donor) clad in white garments stands before it (the replica of the Earth) with palms joined in reverence. He should recite these Mantras:

## \|\| 1.268.23-25 \|\|

*tvayā saṃdhāryate viśvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*tava dānaṃ kariṣyāmi sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru medini \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śarīreṣvapi bhūtānāṃ tvaṃ devi prathamaṃ sthitā \|*  
*tataścānyāni bhūtāni jalādīni vasundhare \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ye tvāṃ yacchaṃti te bhūyastvāṃ labhaṃte na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva pārthivaṃ rūpamāśritā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. “O Earth, this whole universe including both mobile and immobile beings is being supported by you. I am making a gift of you. Be present (here).

O goddess in the physical bodies of all living beings, you are the fifth element. Then follow other elements like water etc.

Those who make a gift of you do get you back once again. There is no doubt about it. They do so by assuming a royal form here or hereafter.”

## \|\| 1.268.26 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā samādāya toyaṃ hemākṛtiṃ nṛpa \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ hṛdi sthāpya maṃtreṇānena kalpayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After eulogizing thus, O king, the devotee takes up the golden replica and water. Retaining Vāsudeva in the heart, he recites this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.268.27 \|\|

*pātālāduddhṛtā yena pṛthvī sā lokakāriṇā \|*  
*asyā dānena ca sadā prīyatāṃ me janārdanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “By the gift of this (replica) let Janārdana be always pleased. He is the creator of the world by whom the Earth was lifted up from Pātāla.”

## \|\| 1.268.28 \|\|

*evamuccārya tattoyaṃ toyamadhye parikṣipet \|*  
*na bhūmau naiva haste ca brāhmaṇasya nṛpottama \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After saying this, the devotee pours the water in water itself, not on the ground, nor into the hand of the Brāhmaṇa, O excellent king.

## \|\| 1.268.29-30 \|\|

*tato visarjayeddevīṃ mantreṇānena bhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*āgatā ca yathānyāyaṃ pūjitā ca yathāvidhi \|\| 29 \|\|*

*asmākaṃ tvaṃ hitārthāya yatreṣṭaṃ tatra gamyatām \|*  
*usrā vedeti maṃtreṇa samuccārya tataḥ param \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradātavyā saṃvibhajya narādhipa \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Thereafter, the devotee ritualistically sends away the goddess by means of the following Mantra partially:

“You duly came and you have been adored in accordance with the injunction. For the sake of our welfare you have done so. Now, may you be pleased to go wherever you wish.” Thereafter, the Mantra usrā veda etc. is recited and gift articles are distributed among the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.268.31 \|\|

*evaṃ te sarvamākhyātaṃ pṛthivīdānamuttamam \|*  
*śṛṇuyātpārthivo bhāvī dātā janmanijanmani \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus, everything regarding the excellent gift of Pṛthvī has been described to you. Let this be heard that the donor shall become a king in every birth.

## \|\| 1.268.32 \|\|

*yo rājā pṛthivīṃ dadyādvidhinānena pārthiva \|*  
*rājyabhraṃśo na vaṃśe'pi tasya saṃjāyate kvacit \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If a king, O king, makes the gift of the Earth as per this procedure, there shall never be any case of dethronement in his family.

## \|\| 1.268.33 \|\|

*rājyabhraṃśasamopetā ye dṛśyaṃte mahībhujaḥ \|*  
*na tairvasundharā dattā brāhmaṇānāṃ dhṛtātmanām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If kings are being seen dethroned, then it means that the Earth has never been gifted by them to Brāhmaṇas of controlled selves.

## \|\| 1.268.34 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pṛthvīdānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*na haretparadattāṃ ca kathaṃcidapi medinīm \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence, (a king) should make the gift of Pṛthvī by all means. None shall take away the Earth given over to others.

## \|\| 1.268.35 \|\|

*etatpuṇyaṃ praśasyaṃ ca pṛthivīdānamuttamam \|*  
*śṛṇvatāmapi rājeṃdra taddehādyaghanāśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This excellent gift of Pṛthivī is meritorious and praiseworthy. O great king, even to those who listen to this it shall be destructive of all the sins of those bodies.

## \|\| 1.268.36 \|\|

*āstāṃ tāvatpradānaṃ ca pṛthivyāḥ pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*dātuḥ saṃpreraṇaṃ yasyā ajñānaughavināśanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Let alone the actual gift of Pṛthivī, O king. Even prompting someone to make the gift is destructive of masses of ignorance.

## \|\| 1.268.37-39 \|\|

*rūpavānsubhagaścaiva tathā ca priyadarśanaḥ \|*  
*ādhivyādhivinirmuktaḥ putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*medhāvī jāyate martyo dānasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*itthaṃbhūtā mahārāja kṛtvā rājyamakaṇṭakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*prītā viṣṇoḥ padaṃ yāṃti śāśvataṃ yannirāmayam \|*  
*anyatrāpi dharādānātprakuryāccakravartitām \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. By the power of this gift, a man becomes handsome, graceful, pleasing to look at and one endowed with sons and grandsons. He shall be rid of mental anguish and physical ailments. He becomes intelligent and wise. O great king, those who become (kings) like this shall joyously rule over the kingdom without hindrance. They attain the eternal and blemish-free region of Viṣṇu. If the gift if made elsewhere too they shall become emperors also.

## \|\| 1.268.40-41 \|\|

*ekajanmāṃtaraṃ yāvatsamyagdattaṃ nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*gautameśvaradevasya yatpurā purataḥ kṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*saptajanmāṃtaraṃ yāvatprakaroti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra deyā mahī nṛpa \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. What is perfectly gifted before Lord Gautameśvara, O excellent king, shall be effective for the duration of seven rebirths. There is no doubt about it. Hence by all efforts gift of Earth should be made, O king.

## Chapter 269 - Greatness of Kapālamocaneśvara (Kapālamocana-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.269.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kapāleśasya māhātmyaṃ śrūyatāmadhunā dvijāḥ \|*  
*caturthasya mahābhāgāstatra kṣetre sthitasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. O Brāhmaṇas, let the greatness of Kapāleśa be listened to now. O highly esteemed ones, it is the fourth deity stationed in that holy spot. As soon as it is listened to, the man is rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.269.2-4 \|\|

*śrutamātreṇa yenātra naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*trayāṇāṃ caiva liṃgānāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ mahāmate \|*  
*śrutāsmābhiḥ samutpattiḥkapāleśvaravarjitā \|*  
*kenāyaṃ sthāpito devaḥ kapāleśvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasmindṛṣṭe phalaṃ kiṃ syātpūjite ca vadasva naḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

2-4. O highly esteemed one, of the four Liṅgas mentioned earlier, the origin of three has been heard by us excepting that known as Kapāleśvara. Tell us what fruit can be derived by visiting and adoring it.

## \|\| 1.269.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iṃdreṇa sthāpitaḥ pūrvameṣa devo dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kapāleśvasaṃjñastu brahmahatyā vimuktaye \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. Formerly, this deity named Kapāleśvara was installed by Indra for the purpose of riddance from the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.269.6 \|\|

*tatprabhāvatsuraśreṣṭha stayā mukte dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pāpaṃ pūruṣadānena ityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*anyo'pi yo narastaṃ ca pūjayitvā prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It was by its power, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Suraśreṣṭha (the most excellent one among Suras i.e. Indra) was rid of that sin. This Vedic passage is heard: “The sin (is eradicated) by the gift of Pūruṣa.’

## \|\| 1.269.7 \|\|

*prayacchedbrāhmaṇendrāya śuddhaye pāpapūruṣam \|*  
*sa mucyetpātakādghorādbrahmahatyāsamudbhavāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Any man who adores that (deity) with great devotion and gifts away the Pāpapuruṣa to a leading Brāhmaṇa for the purpose of purity, is liberated from the terrible sin arising from Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.269.8 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāmūrtimāsādya provācedaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre gatvā taṃ vīkṣya śaṃkaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Bṛhaspati went to Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra and approached Dakṣiṇāmūrti. Looking at that deity Śaṅkara, he spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.269.9 \|\|

*yo dadāti śarīraṃ ca kṛtvā hemamayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdehaḥ pātakaiḥ pūrvasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “A devotee who goes to the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara, visits the deity Śaṅkara and offers a form (Puruṣa) made of gold by him, is liberated from all earlier sins. There is no doubt about this.”

## \|\| 1.269.10 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyā kathaṃ jātā surendrasya hi sūtaja \|*  
*etannaḥ sarvamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

The sages said:

10\. O Sūtaja, how did the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter befall Surendra (Indra)? Do narrate this fully. We are very eager.

## \|\| 1.269.11 \|\|

*kapāleśvarasaṃjñastu kathaṃ devo'tra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyā kathaṃ naṣṭā tatprabhāvāddivaspateḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. How did the Lord named Kapāleśvara get installed here? How did the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter of Divaspati (Indra) get destroyed by its power?

## \|\| 1.269.12 \|\|

*sa pāpapūruṣo deyo vidhinā kena sūtaja \|*  
*kairmaṃtraiḥ sa hi deyaḥ kaiścaiva hyupaskaraiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Sūtaja, what is the procedure whereby the Pāpapūruṣa should be gifted? By means of what Mantras and by means of what supplementary articles should it be given?

## \|\| 1.269.13 \|\|

*darśanātpūjanāccāpi kiṃ phalaṃ jāyate nṛṇām \|*  
*adattvā svaśarīraṃ vā pūjayā kevalaṃ vada \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What benefit accrues to men by visiting and worshipping the deity even without offering the Pāpapūruṣa? Do mention what the benefit will be attained solely through the adoration.

## \|\| 1.269.14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvāpi mahābhāgā naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sūta said:

14\. I shall describe unto you all this ancient legend, on hearing which, O highly esteemed ones, a man is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.269.15 \|\|

*ajñānājjñānato vāpi vihitairanyajanmajaiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭamātreṇa yenātra pātakāttaddinodbhavāt \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sins may have been committed knowingly or unknowingly in the course of the previous births. Merely by visiting the deity, one is liberated from the sin committed on that day. There is no doubt about this. It is the truth that has been told by me.

## \|\| 1.269.16 \|\|

*purā tvaṣṭuḥ suto jajñe vṛtro hi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*pulomaduhituḥ pārśvādvibhāvaryāḥ suvīryavān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Formerly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Vṛtra, a very powerful son, was born to Tvaṣṭṛ of Vibhāvan, the daughter of Puloman.

## \|\| 1.269.17 \|\|

*sa bāla eva dharmātmā āsītsarvajanapriyaḥ \|*  
*dānavaṃ bhāvamutsṛjya dvijabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even as a boy, he was a pious soul, a favourite of, all the people. He had completely eschewed the characteristic trait of a Dānava. He was eagerly engaged in devotional activities towards Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.269.18 \|\|

*sa gatvā puṣkarāraṇyaṃ parameṇa samādhinā \|*  
*toṣayāmāsa deveśaṃ padmajaṃ tapasi sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He went to the holy forest of Puṣkarāraṇya and engaged himself in a great austerity. By means of deep meditation, he propitiated the Lotus-born Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.269.19 \|\|

*tasya tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ brahmā dṛṣṭigocaramāgataḥ \|*  
*provāca varado'smīti kiṃ te kṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Brahmā was pleased with him and came directly within his vision. He said: “I am the bestower of boons. What purpose of yours shall I carry out?”

## \|\| 1.269.20-21 \|\|

*vṛtra uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭosi me deva brāhmaṇatvaṃ prayaccha me \|*  
*brāhmaṇatvaṃ samāsādya sādhayāmi paraṃ padam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tena kiṃcidasādhyaṃ na brāhmaṇyena bhavenmama \|*  
*brāhmaṇena samaṃ cānyanna kiṃcitpratibhāti me \|\| 21 \|\|*

Vṛtra said:

20-21. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, grant Brāhmaṇa-hood to me. Having attained Brāhmaṇa-hood, I shall achieve the greatest region. Being endowed with Brāhmaṇical power, there shall be nothing unattainable to me. It appears to me that there is nothing unattainable to me. It appears to me that there shall be nothing on a par with a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.269.22 \|\|

*paramaṃ daivataṃ kiṃcinna viprādvidyate param \|*  
*tasmānme hṛtsthitaṃ nānyadapi rājyaṃ triviṣṭape \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There is no greater divinity than a Brāhmaṇa. Hence nothing else remains (cherished) within my heart, not even mastery over the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.269.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭastasya pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇatvaṃ svayaṃ dattvā tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:

23\. On hearing his words, Pitāmaha was pleased within him. Awarding to him the status of Brāhmaṇa, he spoke courteously:

## \|\| 1.269.24 \|\|

*mayā tvaṃ vihito vipra putra prakuru vāṃchitam \|*  
*prasādayasva satataṃ brāhmaṇānbrahmavittamān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Dear son, you have been converted to Brāhmaṇahood by me. Do whatever you wish to. Always propitiate Brāhmaṇas, the most excellent ones among the knowers of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.269.25 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaiḥ suprasannaiśca prīyaṃte sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjanīyā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With Brāhmaṇas rendered delighted, all the Devas become pleased. Hence excellent Brāhmaṇas should be adored with all efforts.”

## \|\| 1.269.26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktastadā tena vṛtro'bhūdbrāhmaṇastataḥ \|*  
*brāhmyā lakṣmyā samopeto brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sūta said:

26\. On being told thus by him, Vṛtra became a Brāhmaṇa. Endowed then with the Brāhmaṇical glory, he became very earnest in maintaining celibacy.

## \|\| 1.269.27 \|\|

*tasmiṃstapasi saṃsthe tu hatā iṃdreṇa dānavāḥ \|*  
*vaṃśocchede samāpanne dānavānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When he was engaged in austerities, Dānavas were killed by Indra. It came well nigh to the extermination of the noble-souled Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.269.28 \|\|

*tataste dānavāḥ sarve parābhūtāḥ suraistataḥ \|*  
*svaṃ sthānaṃ saṃparityajya duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On being defeated and harassed by Suras, all those Dānavas became miserable and grief-stricken and they abandoned their original abode.

## \|\| 1.269.29-30 \|\|

*tanmātaraṃ puraskṛtvā tatsakāśamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*sa ca tāṃ mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛtāṃ taiśca samanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dānavaiśca parābhūtaistathābhūtāṃ ca mātaram \|*  
*kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ ca duḥkhitānāṃ mamāṃtike \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. They approached him (Vṭtra) with his mother at their head. On seeing his mother in such a plight surrounded by the defeated Dānavas, he said: “What is the purpose of your coming to me in such a miserable state?”

## \|\| 1.269.31 \|\|

*dānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ devaiḥ parābhūtā bhavaṃtaṃ śaraṇāgatāḥ \|*  
*kva yāmo'nyatra cā'smākaṃ tvāṃ vinā nāsti saṃśrayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

The Dānavas said:

31\. We have been defeated and harassed by Devas. We are seeking refuge in you. Where else can we go? We have none to offer succour except you.

## \|\| 1.269.32-33 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vṛtraḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*devānahaṃ haniṣyāmi gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tavāgamanakṛtyaṃ ca mātaḥ kathaya sāṃpratam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. On hearing their words Vṛtra said respectfully, “I shall slay the Devas. Go there without delay.

Tell me now, O mother, the purpose of your arrival.”

## \|\| 1.269.34 \|\|

*mātovāca \|*  
*tathā kuru mahābhāga śīghraṃ dāraparigraham \|*  
*vaṃśavṛddhau pramāṇaṃ cedvākyaṃ tava mamodbhavam \|\| 34 \|\|*

The mother said:

34\. O highly esteemed one, hasten to get yourself tied to (married) a wife for the sake of the increase in the family, if you consider my words sufficiently authoritative.

## \|\| 1.269.35 \|\|

*eṣa eva paro dharma eṣa eva paro nayaḥ \|*  
*putrasya jananīvākyaṃ yatkaroti samāhitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This alone is the greatest Dharma. This alone is the greatest strategic step that the son carries out the suggestions of his mother with great concentration.

## \|\| 1.269.36 \|\|

*tathā strīṇāṃ patiṃ muktvā nānyāsti bhuvi devatā \|*  
*jananyāṃ jīvamānāyāṃ tathaiva ca sutasya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Just as in the case of women, there is no deity unto them on the earth other than their husbands, so also as long as the mother is alive, there is no other deity for a son.

## \|\| 1.269.37 \|\|

*atikramya ca yā nārī patiṃ dharmaparā bhavet \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ viphalaṃ tasyā jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If a woman transgresses her husband and apparently pretends to be righteous, all her actions become fruitless. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.269.38-39 \|\|

*putraḥ svajananīvākyaṃ yo'tikramya yathāruci \|*  
*karoti dharmakṛtyāni tāni sarvāṇi tasya ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhavaṃti ca tathā nūnaṃ vṛthā bhasmahutaṃ yathā \|*  
*araṇye ruditānīva ūṣare vāpitāni ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. If a son transgresses the instructions of his mother and engages himself in pious rites as he pleases, all those rites become futile as in the case of a Homa performed on ashes, or of cries in wilderness, or of sowing seeds in an arid land.

## \|\| 1.269.40 \|\|

*yathaiva badhirasyāgre gītaṃ nṛtyamacakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*tadvanmātṛmatādanyakṛtaṃ putrasya dharmajam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even an act of piety performed by a son in direct contravention of his mother’s instruction, is like a musical note played before the deaf and graceful dance in front of the blind.

## \|\| 1.269.41 \|\|

*sarvaṃ karma na saṃdehastenāhaṃ tvāmupāgatā \|*  
*baṃdhūnāṃ vacanātputra duḥkhārtā ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All the rites are so. There is no doubt. Therefore, I have come to you, O dear son, at the instance of the kinsmen. I am all the more distressed.

## \|\| 1.269.42 \|\|

*kiṃ vā te bahunoktena bhūyo bhūyaśca putraka \|*  
*ānṛṇyaṃ jāyate yadvatpitṝṇāṃ tattathā śṛṇu \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Of what avail are repeated importunities in your case, dear son? Listen and carry out my suggestion so that the freedom from, indebtedness to Pitṛs can be accomplished.

## \|\| 1.269.43 \|\|

*tava vatsa pramāṇaṃ cetkuruṣva ca vaco mama \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā vṛtraḥ saṃciṃtya cetasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Dear one, if my words are considered authoritative by you, do so.

On hearing her words Vṛtra thought this mentally:

## \|\| 1.269.44 \|\|

*śrutismṛtyuktamārgeṇa na māturvidyate param \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya ānināya parigraham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. ‘In accordance with the path laid down in the Śrutis and Smṛtis, there is nothing greater than one’s mother.’

He therefore assented promisingly and brought a bride.

## \|\| 1.269.45 \|\|

*tvaṣṭā tasmai dadau prītastato ratnānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*saṃkhyāhīnāni tasyaiva kupyākupyamanaṃtakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Tvaṣṭṛ was highly pleased. He gave innumerable gems as well as endless number of precious and base metals.

## \|\| 1.269.46 \|\|

*hastyaśvayānakośāḍhyaṃ so'bhiṣiktaḥ pade nije \|*  
*dānavānāṃ mahāvīryo brāhmaṇyena samanvitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He was coronated in his position (as the king) with ample wealth in the treasury and numerous elephants, horses and vehicles in the army. Endowed with great prowess and further strengthened by means of Brāhmaṇa-hood, (he became the king) of Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.269.47-48 \|\|

*abhiṣiktaṃ tadā vṛtraṃ svarājye te'surādayaḥ \|*  
*śrutvābhiṣekaṃ saṃhṛṣṭāstasya vṛtrasya bāṃdhavāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dānavāśca samājagmurye tatrāsanpurogatāḥ \|*  
*pātālādgiridurgācca sthaladurgebhya eva ca \|*  
*kṛtavairāḥ samaṃ devaiḥ kopena mahatā vṛtāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. On hearing that Vṛtra had been crowned in his own kingdom, the kinsmen of Vṛtra, the Dānavas who had earlier left the city returned from Pātāla, from the mountain fortresses as well as the level ground fortresses. They were extremely angry because of their enmity with the Devas.

## \|\| 1.269.49 \|\|

*tataḥ protsāhitaḥ sarvairdānavaiḥ sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*prasthitaḥ śatrunāśāya mahendrabhavanaṃ prati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Encouraged by all the Dānavas, that mighty one set off towards the abode of Mahendra in order to destroy their enemies.

## \|\| 1.269.50 \|\|

*śakro'pi vṛtramākarṇya samāyāṃtaṃ yuyutsayā \|*  
*sanmukhaḥ prayayau hṛṣṭaḥ sarvadevasamanvitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On hearing that Vṛtra was on his move towards him with a desire to fight, Śakra became delighted and accompanied by all the Devas he started from heaven to face him squarely.

## \|\| 1.269.51 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*merupṛṣṭhe suvistīrṇe nityameva divāniśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereupon, there was a fight between Devas and Dānavas on the extensive highlands of Meru day and night.

## \|\| 1.269.52-56 \|\|

*nityaṃ parājayo jajñe devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*tatrovāca guruḥ śakra mā yuddhaṃ kuru devapa \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vṛtro'yaṃ dāruṇo yuddhe baladvayasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*catvāraścāgrato vedāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ saśaraṃ dhanuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tena jeyatamo daityastavaiva ca mahāhave \|*  
*tasmātsaṃdhānametena tvaṃ kuruṣva śacīpate \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tato viśvāsamāyā taṃ jahi vajreṇa dānavam \|*  
*ṣaḍupāyai ripurvadhya iti śāstranidarśanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhuṃjānaśca śayānaśca dattvā kanyāmapi svakām \|*  
*vipradānena saṃyojya kṛtvāpi śapathaṃ gurum \|*  
*māyāprapaṃcamāsādya tasmādevaṃ samācara \|\| 56 \|\|*

52-56. Everyday Devas suffered defeat at the hands of Dānavas. Then Guru (Bṛhaspati) said: “O Śakra, O ruler of Devas, do not fight.

This Vṛtra is very terrible in battle possessing two types of powers, the four Vedas at the forefront and the bow fitted with arrows at the back.

With this, the Daitya is sure to defeat you in the great fight. Hence, O Consort of Śacī, enter into a deceitful alliance (peace) with him.

Thence as he becomes confident, kill the Dānava with your Vajra (thunderbolt). It is the injunction of the scriptures that the enemy could be killed by means of six expedients.

When he is taking food, when he is lying (relaxing), by giving one’s daughter (or a girl), employing a Brāhmaṇa bribed (for the purpose) and by taking a solemn vow—by resorting to deceitful tactics (one should kill one’s enemy), so you follow this.”

## \|\| 1.269.57 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ ca svayaṃ gatvā tvaṃ viśvāse niyojaya \|*  
*tava vākyena viśvāsaṃ nūnaṃ yāsyati dānavaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Indra said:

57\. If it is to be so, do go yourself and win his confidence. At your instance, the Dānava will certainly become trustful.

## \|\| 1.269.58 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śakrasya matamājñāya pratasthe ca bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*yatra vṛtraḥ sthito daityo yuddhārthaṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

Sūta said:

58\. Having understood the view of Śakra Bṛhaspati set off to the place where Vṛtra, the Daitya, was stationed with his resolve to fight.

## \|\| 1.269.59 \|\|

*vṛtro'pi taṃ samālokya svayaṃ prāptaṃ bṛhaspatim \|*  
*sadaiva dvijabhaktaḥ sa hṛṣṭātmā samapadyata \|*  
*viśeṣātpraṇipatyoccairvākyametadabhāṣata \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On seeing that Bṛhaspati himself had come, Vṛtra who had always been a devotee of Brāhmaṇas, became glad in his heart. Bowing down before him specifically, he spoke these words loudly:

## \|\| 1.269.60 \|\|

*vṛtra uvāca \|*  
*svāgataṃ te dvijaśreṣṭha kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām \|*  
*priyā me brāhmaṇā yasmāttasmātkīrtaya sāṃpratam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Vṛtra said:

60\. Welcome to you, O excellent Brāhmaṇa; what shall I do? Command me. Since Brāhmaṇas have always been dear to me speak out now (anything you may desire).

## \|\| 1.269.61 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|\| saṃdigdho vijayo yuddhe yasmāddaivena sattama \|*  
*tasmātkuru maheṃdreṇa vyavasthāṃ vacanānmama \|\| 61 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

61\. O excellent one, since victory in battle is doubtful, as it is controlled by fate, do enter into an agreement (of peace) with Mahendra at my instance.

## \|\| 1.269.62 \|\|

*tvaṃ bhuṃkṣva bhūtalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śakraścāpi triviṣṭapam \|*  
*vyavasthayā'nayā nityaṃ vartitavyaṃ parasparam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. You rule the entire earth. Let Śakra rule heaven. You should abide by this agreement always.

## \|\| 1.269.63 \|\|

*vṛtra uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tava vaco brahmankariṣyāmi sadaiva hi \|*  
*saṃgamaṃ kuru śakreṇa sāṃprataṃ mama saddvija \|\| 63 \|\|*

Vṛtra said:

63\. O Brāhmaṇa, I shall carry out your suggestion for ever. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, get me in touch with Śakra now.

## \|\| 1.269.64 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha śakraṃ samānīya bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*vṛtreṇa saha saṃdhānaṃ cakre caiva parasparam \|\| 64 \|\|*

Sūta said:

64\. The liberal-minded Bṛhaspati brought Śakra and brought about a mutual accord with Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.269.65 \|\|

*ekārimitratāṃ gatvā tāvubhau daityadevapau \|*  
*prahṛṣṭau gatavantau tau tataścaiva nijaṃ gṛham \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. After having been principal enemies, both of them, the rulers of Daityas and Devas, turned into fast friends and they joyously went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 1.269.66 \|\|

*atha śakracchalānveṣī sadā vṛtrasya vartate \|*  
*na cchidraṃ labhate kvāpi vīkṣamāṇopi yatnataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Of course, Śakra was always seeking an opportunity to employ deception but he did not find any loophole, though he was diligently looking for it.

## \|\| 1.269.67 \|\|

*kathaṃcidapi so'bhyeti tatsakāśaṃ puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃcicchidraṃ samāsādya tatpratāpena dahyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Sometimes with great difficulty, Purandara did get at a vulnerable point but he got scorched by his refulgent prowess.

## \|\| 1.269.68 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*na śaknomi ca taṃ daityaṃ vīkṣituṃ ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*tejasā sarvato vyāptaṃ tatkathaṃ sūdayāmyaham \|\| 68 \|\|*

Indra said:

68\. I am unable to look at that Daitya at all, since he is enveloped on all sides by a brilliant refulgence. How can I slay him?

## \|\| 1.269.69 \|\|

*tasmātkaṃcidupāyaṃ me tadvadhārthaṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*yathā śaknomi tatsoḍhuṃ tejastasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Hence suggest some means to me to facilitate slaying him by enabling me to bear the brilliance of that wicked-souled one.

## \|\| 1.269.70 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ provāca taṃ śakraṃ vinayāvanataṃ sthitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

Sūta said:

70\. On hearing his words, Bṛhaspati meditated for a long time. Then he said to Śakra who was standing humbly by:

## \|\| 1.269.71 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*tasya brāhmyaṃ sthitaṃ tejaḥ samyaggātre puraṃdara \|*  
*vīkṣituṃ naiva śaknoṣi tena tvaṃ tridaśādhipa \|\| 71 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

71\. O Purandara, a Brāhmaṇical splendour envelopes his body. Hence, O Lord of Devas, you cannot look at him.

## \|\| 1.269.72 \|\|

*tathā te kīrtayiṣyāmi tasyopāyaṃ vadhodbhavam \|*  
*vadhayiṣyasi yenātra taṃ tvaṃ dānavasattamam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Hence I shall tell a means whereby you will easily kill that excellent Dānava.

## \|\| 1.269.73 \|\|

*prācīsarasvatītīre puṣkarāraṇyamāśritaḥ \|*  
*dadhīcirnāma viprarṣiḥ śatayojanamucchritaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. On the banks of Prācīsarasvatī, there is a Brāhmaṇa sage named Dadhīci. He is a hundred Yojanas tall. He resides in the Puṣkara forest.

## \|\| 1.269.74 \|\|

*tatra nityaṃ tapaḥ kurvanstauti nityaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*sa nirviṇṇo muniśreṣṭhaḥ prāṇānāṃ dhāraṇe hare \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Performing penance there he continuously eulogizes Pitāmaha. O Hari (Indra), the excellent sage is fed up with (the fact of) clinging to life.

## \|\| 1.269.75 \|\|

*ciraṃtano muniḥ sa syājjarayātisamāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*taṃ prārthaya drutaṃ gatvā tasyāsthīni gurūṇi ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. This sage of pretty long existence has already become overwhelmed with marks of old age. Go to him quickly and request him for his weighty bones.

## \|\| 1.269.76 \|\|

*sa te dāsyastyasaṃdigdhaṃ tyaktvā prāṇānatipriyān \|*  
*tasyāsthibhiḥ praharaṇaṃ vajrākhyaṃ te bhaviṣyati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. He will give up his life though very dear to him, and undoubtedly place the bones at your service. With his bones the weapon named Vajra can be fashioned.

## \|\| 1.269.77 \|\|

*amoghaṃ te tato nūnaṃ tvaṃ vṛtraṃ sūdayiṣyasi \|*  
*tasya vajrasya tattejo brahmatejo'bhibṛṃhitam \|*  
*tena vṛtrodbhavaṃ tejaḥ praśamaṃ saṃprayāsyati \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. It shall be your never-failing weapon. You will certainly slay Vṛtra. The refulgence of that Vajra, being evolved out of Brāhmaṇical splendour, will counteract and subdue the refulgence of Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.269.78 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā satvaraṃ śakraḥ sarvairdaivagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*jagāma puṣkarāraṇye yatra prācī sarasvatī \|\| 78 \|\|*

Sūta said:

78\. On hearing it, Śakra hastened to the Puṣkara forest in the company of all the groups of Devas. It was there that Prācīsarasvatī flowed.

## \|\| 1.269.79 \|\|

*trayastriṃśatsamopetā tīrthānāṃ koṭibhiryutā \|*  
*dadhīcerāśramaṃ tatra so'viśaccitrasaṃyutam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The river had thirty-three crores of Tīrthas within it. The hermitage of Dadhīci was nearby. It was full of miracles. Śakra entered the hermitage.

## \|\| 1.269.80 \|\|

*krīḍaṃte nakulaiḥ sarpā yatra tuṣṭiṃ gatā mithaḥ \|*  
*mṛgāḥ paṃcānanaiḥ sārdhaṃ vṛṣadaṃśāstathā'khubhiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Serpents sported about there along with mongooses there and both were happy in company. So also deer were happy with lions and cats with mice.

## \|\| 1.269.81 \|\|

*ulūka sahitāḥ kākā mitho dveṣavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*prabhāvāttasya tapaso dadhīceḥ sumahātmanaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Crows resided side by side with owls without any mutual hatred due to the power of the penance of the noble-souled Dadhīci.

## \|\| 1.269.82 \|\|

*dadhīcirapi cālokya devāñchakrapurogamān \|*  
*samāyātānprahṛṣṭātmā satvaraṃ saṃmukhobhyagāt \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On seeing that Devas had come with Śakra at their head, Dadhīci became highly delighted and came directly before them immediately.

## \|\| 1.269.83-84 \|\|

*tataścārghyaṃ samādāya praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*śakramabhyāgataṃ prāha kiṃ te kṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 83 \|\|*

*gṛhāyātasya deveśa tacchīghraṃ me nivedaya \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Then he took the Arghya in his hands and bowed to him repeatedly. He then said to Śakra, the guest: “What task of yours can I carry out? You have come to my house, O Lord of Devas. Tell me quickly.”

## \|\| 1.269.85 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*ātithyaṃ kuru vipreṃdra gṛhāyātasya sanmune \|*  
*tvadasthīni nijānyāśu mama dehyavikalpitam \|\| 85 \|\|*

Indra said:

85\. O great Brāhmaṇa, render hospitality unto me. O excellent sage, I have come to your house. Give me unreservedly your own bones.

## \|\| 1.269.86 \|\|

*atadarthamahaṃ prāptastvatsakāśaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*asthibhiste paraṃ kāryaṃ devānāṃ siddhimeṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O great sage, it is for this alone that I have approached you. Something great has to be wrought out of your bones. It will facilitate achieving the purpose of Devas.

## \|\| 1.269.87 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iṃdrasya tadvacaḥ śrutvā dadhīcistoṣasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prāha sahasrākṣaṃ sarvairdevaiḥ samanvitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

Sūta said:

87\. On hearing those words of Indra, Dadhīci became happy and satisfied. Then he said to the Thousand-eyed One who was accompanied by all the Devas:

## \|\| 1.269.88-90 \|\|

*aho nāsti mayā tulyaḥ sāṃprataṃ bhuvi kaścana \|*  
*puṇyavānyasya deveśaḥ svayamarthī gṛhāgataḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*dhanyāni ca mamāsthīni yāni deveśa te hitam \|*  
*kariṣyaṃti sadā kāryaṃ rakṣārthaṃ tridivaukasām \|\| 89 \|\|*

*eṣo'haṃ saṃpradāsyāmi priyānprāṇānkṛte tava \|*  
*gṛhāṇa svecchayā'sthīni svakāryārthaṃ puraṃdara \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. “Indeed, there is no one on the earth as meritorious as me, because the Lord of Devas has himself come to my house seeking something.

Blessed indeed are my bones, O Lord of Devas, which will do some good unto you. Everything should always be done for the sake of the protection of the Heaven-dwelleres.

Here I am willing to surrender my very life for your sake. Accept my bones as you please, O Purandara, for the realization of your own purpose.”

## \|\| 1.269.91 \|\|

*evamuktvā maharṣiḥ sa dhyānamāśritya satvaram \|*  
*brahmaraṃdhreṇa niḥsārya prāṇamātmānamatyajat \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. After saying thus, the great sage resorted to meditation immediately. He let off his vital airs through the Brahmarandhra (cerebral aperture) and gave up his body.

## \|\| 1.269.92 \|\|

*tadātmanā parityaktaṃ tasya gātraṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*patitaṃ medanīpṛṣṭhe vyasu taddvijasattamāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Bereft of the soul, his body fell down on the ground instantly, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.269.93 \|\|

*tasminneva kāle tu tasyāsthīni śatakratuḥ \|*  
*pragṛhya viśvakarmāṇaṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. In the meantime, Śatakratu (Indra) collected together his bones and then respectfully addressed Viśvakarman:

## \|\| 1.269.94 \|\|

*etairasthibhiḥ śīghraṃ me kuru tvaṃ vajramāyudham \|*  
*yena vyāpādayāmyāśu vṛtraṃ dānavasattamam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. “With these bones you fashion out quickly the weapon Vajra wherewith I can immediately slay Vṛtra, the most excellent one among Dānavas.”

## \|\| 1.269.95 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā viśvakarmā tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*yathāyudhaṃ tathā cakre vajrākhyaṃ dāruṇākṛti \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. On hearing his words, Viśvakarman hurriedly made the weapon named Vajra, terrible in its very form.

## \|\| 1.269.96 \|\|

*ṣaḍasri śataparvākhyaṃ madhye kṣāmaṃ vibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*pradadau ca tatastasmai sahasrākṣāya dhīmate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. It had six Aśris (sharp edges) and hundred knots with the middle slender and depressed. It was terrible. He gave it to the intelligent Thousand-eyed One.

## \|\| 1.269.97 \|\|

*atha taṃ sa samādāya dvādaśārkasamaprabham \|*  
*samādhisthaṃ carairjñātvā vṛtraṃ saṃdhyārcane ratam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Seizing the weapon that had the lustre of twelve suns (Indra stood ready for his mission) on coming to know through spies that Vṛtra was performing the Sandhyā rites and was in deep meditation.

## \|\| 1.269.98 \|\|

*tataśca pṛṣṭhabhāgaṃ sa samāśritya trilokarāṭ \|*  
*cikṣepa vajramuddiśya tadvadhārthaṃ samutsukaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The king of the three worlds stood behind him and in his eagerness to kill him, he hurled the Vajra at him.

## \|\| 1.269.99 \|\|

*sa hatastena vajreṇa dānavo bhasmasādgataḥ \|*  
*śakropi hatamajñātvā bhayāttasyātha dudruve \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Struck down with the Vajra, the Dānava was reduced to ashes, but Śakra did not know that he had been killed. In his great fright, he fled away from the spot.

## \|\| 1.269.100 \|\|

*manuṣyarahite deśe viṣame gulmasaṃvṛte \|*  
*lilye śakrastadā sarvaṃ mene vṛtramayaṃ jagat \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. He fled to a far-off place devoid of human beings. He hid himself in a rugged cluster of bushes and hedges. Śakra imagined that the entire universe was filled with Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.269.101 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāḥ paśyaṃtaḥ sarvato diśam \|*  
*siddhacāraṇagandharvā ājagmuśca śatakratum \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. In the meantime Devas, Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Gandharvas who hid been searching for Śatakratu (Indra) all round, came there.

## \|\| 1.269.102 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛcchrācca tairdṛṣṭaḥ śakro'sau gahane vane \|*  
*nilīno bhayasaṃtrasto gulmamadhye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. With very great difficulty they espied Śakra lying amidst the hedges in a deep forest. He was found extremely terror-stricken.

## \|\| 1.269.103 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tvaṃ bhītaḥ sahasrākṣa vṛtro'yaṃ ghātitastvayā \|*  
*parivāreṇa sarveṇa vīkṣito'smābhireva ca \|\| 103 \|\|*

The Devas said:

103\. Why are you afraid, O Thousand-eyed One? This Vṛtra has been killed by you along with his entire family. We have ourselves seen him.

## \|\| 1.269.104 \|\|

*asmādāgaccha gacchāmo gṛhaṃ prati puraṃdara \|*  
*kuru trailokyarājyaṃ tvaṃ sāṃprataṃ hatakaṇṭakam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Come out from this place, O Purandara. We shall go homewards. Now that the thorn (Vṛtra) has been dislodged, you can rule the domain of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.269.105 \|\|

*tacchrutvā'tha viniṣkrāṃto gulmamadhyācchatakratuḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭaromā hataṃ śrutvā vṛtraṃ dānavasattamam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. On hearing their words, Śatakratu came out from the middle of the bushes. On coming to know that Vṛtra, the excellent Dānava, had been killed he experienced a thrill with hairs standing on end.

## \|\| 1.269.106 \|\|

*atha paśyaṃti yāvattaṃ devāḥ sarve śatakratum \|*  
*tāvattejovihīnaṃ tadgātraṃ durgaṃdhitāyutam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Even as all the Devas were looking at Śatakratu, his body lost all its lustre and began to stink with a bad odour.

## \|\| 1.269.107-110 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā lokagururbrahmā devānsarvānuvāca ha \|*  
*śakro'yaṃ sāṃprataṃ vyāptaḥ pāpayā brahmahatyayā \|\| 107 \|\|*

*yadanena hato vṛtro brahmabhūtaśchalena saḥ \|*  
*tasmāttyājyaḥ sudūreṇa no cetpāpamavāpsyatha \|\| 108 \|\|*

*brahmaghnena samaṃ sparśaḥ saṃbhāṣo'tha vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*pāpāya jāyate puṃsāṃ tasmāttaṃ dūratastyajet \|\| 109 \|\|*

*āstāṃ saṃsparśanaṃ tasya saṃbhāṣo vā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*darśanaṃ vāpi tasyāhuḥ sarvapāpapradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 110 \|\|*

107-110. On noticing this, Brahmā, the preceptor of the worlds, said to all those Devas: “This Śakra has now been infected (and defiled) by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, Since Vṛtra who was Brāhmaṇa has been killed by him through deception, he should be shunned from afar. Otherwise you will also incur the sin.

The contact with a Brāhmaṇa-slayer as well as a dialogue with him causes sin in men. Hence he should be abandoned and kept at a distance. Let alone the personal touch or dialogue in particular, they say that even his mere sight causes all sins in men.”

## \|\| 1.269.111-113 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ śakro dṛṣṭvā'tmanastanum \|*  
*tejasā saṃparityaktāṃ durgandhena samāvṛtām \|\| 111 \|\|*

*tataḥ provāca lokeśaṃ dīnaḥ praṇatakandharaḥ \|*  
*tavāhaṃ kiṃkaro deva tvayeṃdratve niyojitaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me brahmahatyāvināśanam \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ vibho brūhi yena śuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 113 \|\|*

Sūta said:

111-113. On hearing the words of Brahmā and seeing his own body bereft of all brilliance and vitiated by badly stinking odour, Śakra spoke to the Lord of the worlds with shoulders stooping down in wretched despair: “O Lord, I am a mere servant unto you. I have been assigned the office of Indra by you. Hence grant me the favour of destroying the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. O almighty one, do suggest a means of expiation whereby purity can be gained.”

## \|\| 1.269.114 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu tvaṃ snātvā balasūdana \|*  
*ātmānaṃ hemajaṃ dehi pāpapūruṣasaṃjñitam \|\| 114 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

114\. O Slayer of Bala, You have to take your bath in the sixty-eight Tīrthas. Give away a gold replica of yourself called Pāpapūruṣa.

## \|\| 1.269.115 \|\|

*maṃtravattaṃ yathoktaṃ ca brāhmaṇāya mahātmane \|*  
*snātvā puṇyajale tīrthe brahmaghno'hamiti bruvan \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Reciting the Mantras as mentioned before the gold replica is to be given to a noble-souled Brāhmaṇa after taking your bath in the sacred water, all the while saying, “I am a Brāhmaṇa-slayer.”

## \|\| 1.269.116 \|\|

*snātamātrasya te hastādyatra tatpatati kṣitau \|*  
*tejaḥ saṃjāyategātre durgaṃdhaśca praṇaśyati \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. As soon as you have had your bath (the Kapāla-skull of Vṛtra) shall fall down from your hand. A bright refulgence will cover your body and the bad odour shall vanish.

## \|\| 1.269.117 \|\|

*tasmiṃstīrthe tvayā tacca sthāpyaṃ śakra kapālakam \|*  
*maheśvarasya nāmnā ca pūjanīyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. O Śakra, that Kapāla is to be installed by you in that Tīrtha. Thereafter, it should be worshipped by you under the name Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.269.118 \|\|

*paṃcabhirvaktramaṃtraiśca tato deyā'tmatastanūḥ \|*  
*hemodbhavā dvijendrāya tataḥ śuddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. The adoration shall be done with the recitation of the Five Mantras of the five faces. Thereafter, the golden replica of your own body should be given to a leading Brāhmaṇa. Then you will regain your purity.

## \|\| 1.269.119 \|\|

*śakrastu tadvacaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*kapālaṃ vṛtrajaṃ gṛhya tīrthayātrāṃ tato gataḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. On hearing the words of Brahmā of unknown birth, Śakra took up the skull of Vṛtra and set off on his pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.269.120 \|\|

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu gacchansa ca sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre samāyātaḥ krameṇa ca \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. After visiting the sixty-eight Tīrthas, the Lord of Suras came to Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in due course.

## \|\| 1.269.121 \|\|

*viśvāmitrahrade snātvā yāvattasmādvinirgataḥ \|*  
*kapālaṃ patitaṃ tasmātsvayameva hatātmanaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. When he came out of Viśvāmitra Hrada after the holy ablution, the skull of the slain soul (Vṛtra) dropped down automatically by itself.

## \|\| 1.269.122 \|\|

*tatastaṃ pūjayāmāsa mantrairvaktrasamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaiḥ puṇyairyathoktairbrahmaṇā purā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Then he adored it with recitation of the holy Mantras pertaining to the faces (i.e. sadyojātam prapadyāmi etc.) that destroy all sins, and that are very meritorious as mentioned by Brahmā earlier.

## \|\| 1.269.123 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu durgandho nāśamāptavān \|*  
*taccharīrāddvijaśreṣṭhā mahattejo vyajāyata \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. In the meantime the stinking odour vanished from his body, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. A great refulgence appeared instead.

## \|\| 1.269.124 \|\|

*etasminnantare brahmā saha devaiḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyāvimuktaṃ taṃ jñātvā sarvasurādhipam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Then on coming to know that the Lord of all the Suras has been relieved of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, Brahmā came there along with the Devas.

## \|\| 1.269.125 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*brahmahatyākṛto doṣo gataste surasattama \|*  
*śeṣapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ svarṇadānaṃ prayaccha bhoḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

125\. O most excellent one among Suras, Your blemish caused by the Brāhmaṇa-slaughter has vanished. Make the gift of gold for the purpose of purifying the vestige of the sin.

## \|\| 1.269.126 \|\|

*kapālametaddeśe'tra yattvayā paripūjitam \|*  
*vṛtrasya paṃcabhirmaṃtrairharavaktrasamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Let the skull of Vṛtra adored by you along with the recitation of the five Mantras of Lord Śiva’s five faces be installed here itself.

## \|\| 1.269.127 \|\|

*pradāsyasi tato bhaktyā hemajāmātmanastanum \|*  
*vidhinā maṃtrayuktena tava pāpaṃ prayāsyati \|*  
*yadyatpūrvakṛtaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pradāya brāhmaṇāya bhoḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Then you shall devoutly make the gift of your own body made of gold in accordance with the injunctions along with the recitation of the relevant Mantras. Your sin, the entire sin that may have been committed by you, shall be dispelled on making the gift to a Brāhmaṇa:

## \|\| 1.269.128 \|\|

*evamuktastataḥ śakro brahmaṇā surasaṃnidhau \|*  
*tathetyuktvā tu tatkālaṃ pāpapiṃḍaṃ nijaṃ dadau \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. On being told thus in the presence of the Suras by Brahmā, Śakra said, “So it shall be” immediately and made the gift of the Pāpapiṇḍa (Pāpa-pūruṣa).

## \|\| 1.269.129 \|\|

*kṛtvā hemamayaṃ viprā brāhmaṇāya mahātmane \|*  
*gartātīrthasamutthāya vātākhyāyāhitāgnaye \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. It was made of gold and given to a noble Brāhmaṇa hailing from Gartātīrtha. He was a Brāhmaṇa who maintained the sacred fires and was called Vāta.

## \|\| 1.269.130-131 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vipro garhitaḥ so'tha nāgaraiḥ \|*  
*dhigdhikpāpa vṛthā vedā ye tvayā pāritāḥ purā \|\| 130 \|\|*

*nāsmābhiḥ saha saṃparkaṃ kadācittvaṃ kariṣyasi \|*  
*gṛhītaṃ yattvayā dānaṃ pāpapiṃḍasamudbhavam \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. In the meantime, that Brāhmaṇa was despised by Nāgaras saying, “Fie upon you! O sinner, the Vedas that were mastered by you earlier are worthless and futile. Since the Dāna of the Pāpapiṇḍa has been accepted by you, you will never have any association with us hereafter.”

## \|\| 1.269.132 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca vipraḥ sa upamanyukulodbhavaḥ \|*  
*vivarṇavadano bhūtvā nāmnā khyātaḥ sa vātakaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Thereupon, that Brāhmaṇa, hailing from the family of Upamanyu, well-known by the name Vātaka (Vāta) turned pale in his face and said:

## \|\| 1.269.133-136 \|\|

*tvayā śakra pradatto me pāpapiṃḍaḥ svako yataḥ \|*  
*mayā pratigrahastena dākṣiṇyena kṛtastava \|\| 133 \|\|*

*na lobhena suraśreṣṭha paśyataste vigarhitaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ ca brāhmaṇaiḥ sarvairetairnagaravāsibhiḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

*tasmānnāhaṃ grahīṣyāmi etaṃ tava pratigraham \|\| 135 \|\|*

*bhūyo'pi tava dāsyāmi na tvaṃ gṛhṇāsi cetpunaḥ \|\| bra \|*  
*hmaśāpaṃ pradāsyāmi dāruṇaṃ ca kṣayātmakam \|\| 136 \|\|*

133-136. “O Śakra, it was the Pāpapiṇḍa of yourself that has been gifted by you. Out of consideration for you I have accepted the Pratigraha. O most excellent one of the Suras, I did not take it on account of greed. But, even as you have been witnessing, I have been rebuked by all these Brāhmaṇas, the residents of Nagara. So I will not take this Pratigraha from you.

I will hand this back to you. If you do not accept it I shall invoke a terrible Brāhmaṇical curse on you to contact the terrible disease of Kṣaya (Wastage—Tuberculosis).”

## \|\| 1.269.137 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*vedāgaṃpārago vipro yadi kuryātpratigraham \|*  
*na sa pāpena lipyeta padmapatramivāṃbhasā \|\| 137 \|\|*

Indra said:

137\. If a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas and the Aṅgas (of Vedas) accepts a Pratigraha, he is never smeared with sin like a lotus-leaf that is never contaminated by water.

## \|\| 1.269.138 \|\|

*tasmātte pātakaṃ nāsti śṛṇuṣvātra vaco mama \|*  
*etaistvaṃ garhite yasmādbrāhmaṇairnagarodbhavaiḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Hence, listen to my words. You incur no sin. Since you have been censured by these Brāhmaṇas hailing from Nagara (I shall lay down these injunctions).

## \|\| 1.269.139-141 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu pradhānastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*eteṣāṃ putrapautrā ye bhaviṣyaṃti tathā tava \|\| 139 \|\|*

*te sarve cājñayā teṣāṃ vartayiṣyaṃtyasaṃśayam \|*  
*yuṣmadvākyavihīnaṃ yatkṛtyaṃ svalpamapi dvija \|\| 140 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ saṃpatsyate vandhyaṃ yathā bhasmahutaṃ tathā \|*  
*kapālamocanaṃ nāma khyātametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 141 \|\|*

139-141. You will be the chief in all the rites of these. The sons and grandsons of these (Nāgaras) shall undoubtedly be guided by the behests of these i.e. your sons and grandsons.

But, O Brāhmaṇa, even the least of a rite of theirs without your permission shall be futile like the Homa performed on ashes. This Tīrtha will become well-known by the name Kapālamocana.

## \|\| 1.269.142 \|\|

*ye tu saṃsmṛtya manujāḥ kapālaṃ mama saddvija \|*  
*tatra śrāddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti te narā muktisaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*śrāddhapakṣe viśeṣeṇa prayāsyaṃti parāṃgatim \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, those men who remember this skull installed by me and perform Śrāddha shall become liberated. If they remember this particularly in the Śrāddha Pakṣa, they will attain the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.269.143-144 \|\|

*sthānabāhyadvijātīnāṃ kule dāraparigraham \|*  
*kṛtvā tvadgotrasaṃbhūtā brāhmaṇā matprasādataḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

*vyavahāryā bhaviṣyaṃti nagare sarvakarmasu \|*  
*evamuktvā sahasrākṣastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

143-144. The Brāhmaṇas born of your family shall marry a girl from the family of the Brāhmaṇas other than those of this locality. Yet with my favour, they shall be entitled to preside over all the rites in Nagara.

After saying thus the Thousand-eyed One vanished.

## \|\| 1.269.145 \|\|

*vātopi tena vittena pratigrahakṛtena ca \|*  
*cakāra tatra prāsādaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. With the money received as Pratigraha, Vāta (the Nāgara Brāhmaṇa) erected a palace unto the Trident-bearing Lord of Devās \[Devas?\].

## \|\| 1.269.146-147 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca śakrastānbrāhmaṇānnagarodbhavān \|*  
*kapālamocane snātvā yo devaṃ hyarcayiṣyati \|\| 146 \|\|*

*brahmahatyodbhavaṃ pāpaṃ tasya naśyatyasaṃśayam \|*  
*mahāpātakayukto vā vipāpmā saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. Then Śakra told those Brāhmaṇas hailing from Nagara: “If anyone takes his holy bath in Kapālamocana and worships the Lord, his sin arising from Brāhmaṇa- slaughter definitely vanishes. One that incurred great sins (Mahāpātaka) shall become sinless.”

## \|\| 1.269.148 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya brāhmaṇānnagarodbhavān \|*  
*tatraiva svāśramaṃ kṛtvā pūjayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. He promised “So it shall be” to the Brāhmaṇas hailing from Nagara. He built his hermitage there itself and adored Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.269.149 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti yatkiṃcitteṣāṃ kṛtyaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*tadvākyena prakurvaṃti tatra ye nāgaraḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. Ever since then, the Nāgaras who lived there performed whatever rite they had to perform at his instance.

## \|\| 1.269.150 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇājjāto madhyago dvitīyastviha \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. It was for this reason that the second Madhyaga came to be established.

## \|\| 1.269.151-152 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātamākhyānaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kapāleśvaradevasya śṛṇvatāṃ paṭhatāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 151 \|\|*

*yathā deveśvarasyātra pāpaṃ naṣṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyā yathā naṣṭā tasmiṃstīrthe dvijottamāḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. Thus the narrative that is destructive of sins has been entirely recounted to you. It pertains to the deity Kapāleśvara and those men who listen to it or recite it become sinless. Their sin will be destroyed like the sin of the chief of Devas, the noble-souled Indra. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, their sin will be destroyed like the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter of Indra.

## Chapter 270 - Making Gift of Pāpapiṇḍa

## \|\| 1.270.1-2 \|\|

*ānarta uvāca \|*  
*mūrkhatvādvā pramādādvā kāmādbālasyato'pi vā \|*  
*yo naraḥ kurute pāpaṃ prāyaścittaṃ karoti na \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasya pāpakṣayakaraṃ puṇyaṃ brūhi dvijottama \|*  
*yena muktirbhavetsadyo yadi tuṣṭo'si me prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

Ānarta said:

1-2. If a man commits a sin out of foolishness, inadvertence, lustfulness or lethargy but does not expiate, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, then what could be a meritorious rite to destroy his sin and also help him attain salvation. Do tell me this, if you are pleased with me, O holy Sir.

## \|\| 1.270.3 \|\|

*lobhamohaparo yo'sau pāpapiṃḍaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*pradadāti vidhiṃ brūhi yena yacchāmyahaṃ drutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O great sage, tell me the procedure for offering Pāpapiṇḍa if one who offers it is greedy or deluded. I also intend to offer the same very soon.

## \|\| 1.270.4 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*dadyātsvapiṃḍaṃ sauvarṇaṃ paṃcaviṃśatpalātmakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

4\. One should offer a gold replica of one’s own body weighing twenty-five Palas.

## \|\| 1.270.5 \|\|

*vidhāyāparapakṣe tu snāpayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*maṃḍapādyaṃ ca prākkṛtvā snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The image (replica) should be made in the later half (i.e, dark half) of the month. It should be bathed duly. After erecting the Maṇḍapa etc., the devotee takes his bath and wears washed clothes. He remains clean.

## \|\| 1.270.6 \|\|

*tadā svarūpaṃ pṛthvyādi pūjayetpāpakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*tathā sa mucyate pāpāttatkṛtāddhi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The man who has committed the sins should adore elements constituting the body e.g. Pṛthivī etc. as his own form. He is liberated from the sin committed by those respective things (i.e. Pṛthivī etc.)

## \|\| 1.270.7 \|\|

*caturviṃśatitattvāni pṛthivyādīni yāni ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ nāmabhistatpiṃḍaṃ pūjayetannarādhipaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O king, the devotee should adore the Piṇḍa with the names of the twenty-four Tattvas (constituents) beginning with Pṛthivī (Earth).

## \|\| 1.270.8 \|\|

*oṃ pṛthivyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ adbhyo namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ tejase namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ vāyave namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ ākāśāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ ghrāṇāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ jihvāyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ cakṣuṣe namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ tvace namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ śrotrāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ gandhāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ rasāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ rūpāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ sparśāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ śabdāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ vāce namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ pāṇibhyāṃ namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ pādābhyāṃ namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ pāyave namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ upasthāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ manase namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ buddhyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ cittāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ ahaṃkārāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ kṣetrātmane namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ paramātmane namaḥ \|*  
*dhūpaṃ dhūrasi maṃtreṇa agnirjyotīti dīpakam \|*  
*yuvā suvāseti ca tato vāsāṃsi paridhāpayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Om, obeisance to Pṛthvī. Om, obeisance to Ap. Om, obeisance to Tejas. Om, obeisance to Vāyu. Om, obeisance to Ākāśa. Om, obeisance to Ghrāṇa (nose). Om, obeisance to Jīhvā (tongue). Om, obeisance to Cakṣus (eye). Om, obeisance to Tvak (skin). Om, obeisance to Śrotra (ear). Om, obeisance to Gandha (odour). Om, obeisance to Rasa (taste). Om, obeisance to Rūpa (colour). Om, obeisance to Sparśa (touch). Om, obeisance to Śabda (sound). Om, obeisance to Vāk (speech). Om, obeisance to Pāṇis (hands). Om, obeisance to Pādas (feet). Om, obeisance to Pāyu (anus). Om, obeisance to Upastha (the organ of generation). Om, obeisance to Manas (mind). Om obeisance to Buddhi (intellect). Om, obeisance to Citta (thinking faculty). Om, obeisance to Ahaṃkāra (ego). Om, obeisance to the Kṣetrātman (individual soul). Om, obeisance to Paramātman (the Supreme Soul).”

The incense is offered with the Mantra dhūrasi etc. The lamp is offered with the Mantra agnirjyoti etc. Thereafter one offers garments with the Mantras yuvā suvāsa etc.

## \|\| 1.270.9 \|\|

*tato brāhmaṇamānīya vedavedāṃgapāragam \|*  
*prakṣālya caraṇau tasya vāsāṃsi paridhāpayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then a Brāhmaṇa is invited. He should be one who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. His feet should be washed and he should be offered garments.

## \|\| 1.270.10-11 \|\|

*keyūraiḥ kaṃkaṇaiścaiva aṃgulīyakabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhūṣayitvā tanuṃ tasya tato mūrtiṃ samānayet \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena rājeṃdra brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. His body should be adorned with bracelets, arm-lets, rings and other ornaments. Then the image is to be brought. It should be offered to the Brāhmaṇa with this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.270.12 \|\|

*eṣa ātmā mayā dattastava hemamayo dvija \|*  
*yatkiṃcidvihitaṃ pāpaṃ pūrvaṃ bhūyāttavākhilam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O Brāhmaṇa, this, my own body in the form of gold (image), is given to you. Whatever sin was committed by me formerly may he yours now entirely.” This is the Mantra for the Dāna.

## \|\| 1.270.13 \|\|

*iti dānamaṃtraḥ \|*  
*tatastu brāhmaṇo rājanmaṃtrametaṃ samuccaret \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then, O king, the Brāhmaṇa accepting the Dāna should utter this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.270.14 \|\|

*yatkiṃcidvihitaṃ pāpaṃ tvayā pūrvaṃmayā hi tat \|*  
*gṛhītaṃ mūrtirūpaṃ tattatastvaṃ pāpavarjitaḥ \|*  
*iti pratigrahamaṃtraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “Whatever sin has been committed by you earlier has been taken over by me in the form of this image. So you are rid of sins.” This is the Mantra for Pratigraha.

## \|\| 1.270.15-16 \|\|

*evaṃ dattvā vidhānena tato vipraṃ visarjayet \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte tato rājaṃstasmai dattvātha dakṣiṇām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yathā tuṣṭiṃ samabhyeti tataḥ pāpaṃ nayatyasau \|*  
*tasminkṛte mahārāja pratyayastatkṣaṇādbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. After making the gift in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee bids farewell to the Brāhmaṇa. After doing thus, O king, and after offering the monetary gift, if the Brāhmaṇa is satisfied, he takes away the sin. If that is concluded, O great king, there shall appear evidence of riddance of the sin instantly.

Ì7-18. The body becomes light. There is increase in brilliance. At night he sees persons with contented minds in dream. He sees men and women clad in white garlands and unguents He sees white cows and ballocks and horses and various kinds of Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.270.19 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ pāpapiṃḍasya dāpanam \|*  
*śravaṇādapi rājeṃdra yasya pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus, everything regarding the Dāna of Pāpapiṇḍa has been narrated to you entirely. O great king, even if this is listened to one is rid of sins

## \|\| 1.270.20 \|\|

*anyatrāpi mahādānaṃ pāpapiṇḍo harennṛpa \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In other holy places also the great gift of Pāpapiṇḍa shall dispel sins, O king.

## \|\| 1.270.21 \|\|

*ekajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nijakāyena nirmitam \|*  
*kapāleśvaradevasya sahasraguṇitaṃ haret \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. But the sin dispelled shall be only what is committed in the course of a single birth by one’s own body. But the rite performed in Kapāleśvara Deva shall dispel the sins thousand times over.

## \|\| 1.270.22 \|\|

*pūrvavaccaiva kartavyo vedimaṃḍapayorvidhiḥ \|*  
*paraṃ homaḥ prakartavyo gāyatryā kevalaṃ nṛpa \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The vedi and Maṇḍapa are to be erected as before. But the Homa is to be performed only through (Japa of) Gāyatrī, O king.

## Chapter 271 - Creation of Seven Liṅgas

## \|\| 1.271.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athānyadapi tatrāsti supuṇyaṃ liṃgasaptakam \|*  
*yenārcitena dṛṣṭena pūjitena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dīrghāyurjāyate martyaḥ sarvarogavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeśvara ityuktastatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*indradyumneśvaro'nyastu sarvapāpaharo haraḥ \|*  
*pāleśvarastathā caiva sarvavyādhivināśanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tato ghaṃṭaśivaḥ khyāto yo ghaṃṭena pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*kalaśeśvarasaṃjñastu vānareśvarasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*īśāna śiva ityuktastatra kṣetreśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*pūjito mānavairbhaktyā kāmānyacchatyamānuṣān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vāṃchitānmanasā sarvānkalikāle'pi saṃsthite \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-6. There is another very meritorious set of seven Liṅgas there. By visiting, honouring and worshipping them particularly, a man becomes long-lived and free from ailments.

One of them is Lord Maheśvara called Mārkaṇḍeśvara. Another Lord Indradyumneśvara, Hara, who dispels all sins. Similarly, Pāleśvara is the destroyer of all diseases. Then there is the famous of Ghaṇṭaśiva installed by Ghaṇṭa. The Lord named Kalaśeśvara is conjoined with Vānareśvara. The deity called Īśānaśiva is Kṣetreśvara (Lord of the chiefs of the holy spot). On being worshipped devoutly, the Lord fulfils superhuman wishes. Even after the advent of Kali Age, he bestows everything desired mentally.

## \|\| 1.271.7 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko'yaṃ mārkaṃḍasaṃjñastu yena liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*indradyumno mahīpālaḥ katamo vada sūtaja \|\| 7 \|\|*

The sages said:

7\. Who is this person named Mārkaṇḍa by whom the Liṅga was installed? O Sūtaja, tell us who this king Indradyumna was.

## \|\| 1.271.8 \|\|

*tathā pālakanāmā ca yenāyaṃ sthāpito haraḥ \|*  
*tathā yo ghaṇṭasaṃjñastu kasmiñjātaḥ sa cānvaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. So also who is this person named Pālaka by whom Hara was installed? In which royal family was born the person named Ghaṇṭa?

## \|\| 1.271.9 \|\|

*kalaśākhyastu yaḥ khyāto vānareṇa samanvitaḥ \|*  
*īśānopyakhilaṃ brūhi paraṃ naḥkautukaṃ sthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Who was this well-known person named Kalaśa accompanied by Vānara? Who was this Īśāna? Describe everything. Our eagerness is great.

## \|\| 1.271.10 \|\|

*yato'tra jāyate śreyaḥ punaḥ puṃsāṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*yairetaiḥ sthāpitā devāḥ kṣetre'sminmānavottamaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Also describe that which will do good to men. Then tell the story of those excellent men by whom these deities were installed.

## \|\| 1.271.11 \|\|

*tathā teṣāṃ samācāraṃ prabhāvaṃ caiva sūtaja \|*  
*dānaṃ vāpi yathākālaṃ maṃtrāṃśca vistarādvada \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. So also, O Sūtaja, describe their activities, power etc. Recount the procedure of Dāna with their proper occasion and let the Mantras pertaining to them be known in detail.

## \|\| 1.271.12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*kathitāṃ bhartṛyajñena ānartādhipateḥ svayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sūta said:

12\. I shall tell you the ancient legend narrated to king Ānarta by Bhartṛyajña himself.

## \|\| 1.271.13 \|\|

*śrutayāpi yayā martyo dīrghāyurjāyatenaraḥ \|*  
*nāpamṛtyumavāpnoti kathaṃcittatprabhāvataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If this is listened to, a man shall become long-lived. By its power, one does not meet premature death.

## \|\| 1.271.14 \|\|

*yo mārkaṃḍa iti khyātaḥ prathamaṃ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*saṃbhūtistasya saṃproktā yuṣmākaṃ pāpanāśinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The sin-destroying (legend about the) origin of the deity mentioned at the outset, well-known as Mārkaṇḍa has already been narrated to you.

The Legend of Indradyumma:

\[Note: This legend is practically a repetition of the same legend in Mahābhārata, Vana, Ch. 199. Camatkārapura is not known to Mahābhārata. It is the pro-Nāgara turn given by this Purāṇa.\]

## \|\| 1.271.15 \|\|

*iṃdradyumnaṃ pravakṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*yadvaṃśo yatprabhāvaśca sarvabhūpālamānitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Now, O excellent Sages, I shall narrate the story of Indradyumna, what his family was, what his power was and how he was honoured by all the kings.

## \|\| 1.271.16 \|\|

*iṃdradyumno mahīpāla āsītpūrvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca sādhulokaprapālakaḥ \|*  
*yajvā dānapatirdakṣaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas! Formerly there was a king named Indradyumna. He was a patron of Brāhmaṇas. He offered succour to all. He was a protector of good people. He used to perform Yajñas. He was a great donor. He was efficient and engaged in everything beneficial to all living beings.

## \|\| 1.271.17 \|\|

*na durbhikṣaṃ na ca vyādhirna ca caurakṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*tasmiñchāsati dharmajñe āsīllokasya kasyacit \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There was no famine, no epidemic, no ailment and no fear caused by thieves to any of the people, when that righteous king was ruling.

## \|\| 1.271.18-19 \|\|

*yathaiva varṣato dhārā yathā vā divi tārakāḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ sikatā yadvatsaṃkhyayā parivarjitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadvattena kṛtā yajñāḥ sarve saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*agniṣṭomo'tirātraśca ukthaḥ ṣoḍaśikāstathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Just as the streams of downpour during rains are numerous, just as the stars in the sky are innumerable, just as sand-particles on Gaṅgā are numberless so (innumerable) were the Yajñas performed by him. All of them were completed with full monetary gifts. He performed Agniṣṭomas, Atirātras, Ukthas and Ṣoḍaśikas.

## \|\| 1.271.20-21 \|\|

*sautrāmaṇyā'tha paśavaścāturmāsyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vājapeyāśvamedhāśca rājasūyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pauṇḍarīkāstathaivānye śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, with his mind sanctified by faith, he performed many Paśuyajñas, Sautrāmaṇis, Cāturmāsyas, Vājapeyas, Aśvamedhas, Rājasūyas, Pauṇḍarikas and others.

## \|\| 1.271.22 \|\|

*tena dānāni dattāni tīrtheṣu ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*miṣṭānnāni dvijeṃdrāṇāṃ dakṣiṇāsahitāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Many gifts were made by hiṃ, particularly in holy spots. Delicious foodstuffs were served to leading Brāhmaṇas along with monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.271.23 \|\|

*na tadasti dharāpṛṣṭhe nagaraṃ pattanaṃ tathā \|*  
*tīrthaṃ vā yatra no tasya vidyate tridaśālayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the whole of the earth, there is not a single town or city or holy spot where a temple (erected by him) did not find a place.

## \|\| 1.271.24 \|\|

*tena kanyāsahasrāṇi acyutānyarbudāni ca \|*  
*brāhamaṇebhyaḥ pradattāni brāhmaṇānāṃ dhanārthinām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Many thousands, trillions and crores of virgins were given in marriage to Brāhmaṇas in need of wealth by him.

## \|\| 1.271.25-26 \|\|

*daśamīdivase tasya rātrau ca gajapṛṣṭhigaḥ \|*  
*dundubhistāḍyamānastu babhrāma sakalaṃ puram \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pratyūṣe vaiṣṇavaṃ bhāvi pāpahāri ca vāsaram \|*  
*upavāsaḥ prakarttavyo muktvā vṛddhaṃ ca bālakam \|*  
*anyathā nigrahiṣyāmi bhojanaṃ yaḥ kariṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. On the Daśamī day (the tenth lunar day) at night would be beaten his big wardrum installed on the back of an elephant and taken around the entire city, which proclaimed: “At daybreak it shall be the sin-destroying day of Viṣṇu. All, excepting the aged and children, should observe fast. If anyone takes food I will punish him.”

## \|\| 1.271.27 \|\|

*iṃdradyumnaḥ sa rājarṣistadā viṣṇoḥ prasādataḥ \|*  
*tenaiva svaśarīreṇa brahmalokaṃ tadā gataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That saintly king Indradyumna went to Brahmaloka with the same physical body due to the favour of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.271.28 \|\|

*tatra kalpasahasrāṃte sa prokto brahmaṇā svayam \|*  
*iṃdradyumna dharāṃ gaccha na sthātavyaṃ tvayā'dhunā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the end of a thousand Kalpas, he was told by Brahmā himself: “O Indradyumna, go to the earth. Now you cannot stay here.”

## \|\| 1.271.29 \|\|

*iṃdradyumna uvāca \|*  
*kasmāccyāvayase brahmannijalokāddrutaṃ hi mām \|*  
*apāpamapi deveśa tathā me vada kāraṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

29\. Why do you drop me down hurriedly from your world, O Brahmā, though I am devoid of any sin. O Lord of Devas, tell me the reason.

## \|\| 1.271.30-32 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*tava kīrtisamucchedaḥ saṃjāto'dya dharātale \|*  
*yāvatkīrtirdharāpṛṣṭhe tāvatsvarge vasennaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*etasmātkāraṇāllokāḥ svanāmāṃkāni cakrire \|*  
*vāpīkūpataḍāgāni devatāyatanāni ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmādgaccha dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ svāṃ kīrtiṃ nūtanāṃ kuru \|*  
*yadi vāṃchasi loke'sminmāmake vasatiṃ ciram \|\| 32 \|\|*

Śrī Brahmā said:

30-32. Your glory has come to an end today on the surface of the earth. A man can stay in heaven only so long as his renown remains on the earth. It is for this reason that people inscribe their names on holy temples, tanks, wells and lakes they construct or dig. Hence, go back to the earth. Renew your glory and renown if you desire a long stay in this world.

## \|\| 1.271.35 \|\|

*te tamūcuḥ paraṃ caitatkāṃpilyamiti viśrutam \|*  
*ānartanāmā deśo'yaṃ rājātra pṛthivījayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

3S. Even as the great king surveyed himself, he found that he had instantly reached the city of Kāmpilya on the earth.

## \|\| 1.271.34 \|\|

*atha papraccha lokānsa kimetannagaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ko'yaṃ deśaḥ ko'tra rājā kiṃ puraṃ nagaraṃ ca kim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then he asked the people: “What is this city? What is this land? Who is the king? What are the towns and cities?”

## \|\| 1.271.35-36 \|\|

*te tamūcuḥ paraṃ caitatkāṃpilyamiti viśrutam \|*  
*ānartanāmā deśo'yaṃ rājātra pṛthivījayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ko bhavānkimihāyātaḥ kiṃcitkāryaṃ vadasva naḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. But they simply replied: “This is the city well-known as Kāmpilya. The land is called Ānarta and the king here is Pṛthivījaya.

But who are you please? Why have you come here? Have you any specific purpose? Tell us.”

## \|\| 1.271.37 \|\|

*iṃdradyumna uvāca \|\| iṃdradyumno mahīpālaḥ purāsīdrocake pure \|*  
*deśe vaijaruke pūrvaṃ sa deśaḥ kva ca tatpuram \|\| 37 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

37\. Formerly, there was a king named Indradyumna in the city of Rocaka in the land Vaijaruka. Where is that land? Where is that city?

## \|\| 1.271.38 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*na vayaṃ tatpuraṃ vidmo na deśaṃ na ca bhūpatim \|*  
*indradyumnābhidhānaṃ ca yaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasi bhadraka \|\| 38 \|\|*

The people said:

38\. We do not know that city, nor the land nor that king named Indradyumna about whom you are asking, O gentle Sir.

## \|\| 1.271.39 \|\|

*iṃdradyumna uvāca \|*  
*cirāyurasti ko'pyatra yastaṃ vetti mahīpatim \|*  
*deśaṃ vā tatpuraṃ vāpi tanme vadatha mā ciram \|\| 39 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

39\. Is there any aged person here, of long life, who might have known that king, land or city? Tell me quickly.

## \|\| 1.271.40 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*saptakalpasmaro nāma mārkaṃḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*śrūyate naimiṣāraṇye taṃ gatvā pṛccha vetsyasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

The people said:

40\. It is heard that there is a great sage named Mārkaṇḍeya in the Naimiṣa forest, who remembers (events of) seven Kalpas. Go and ask him. You may come to know then.

## \|\| 1.271.41 \|\|

*athāsau satvaraṃ gatvā vyomamārgeṇa taṃ munim \|*  
*papraccha praṇipatyoccairnaimiṣāraṇyamāśritam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereafter, he immediately travelled by the aerial path, bowed down to that sage residing in Naimiṣāraṇya and asked him:

## \|\| 1.271.42 \|\|

*iṃdradyumneti vai bhūpastvayā dṛṣṭaḥ śruto'tha vā \|*  
*cirāyustvaṃ śruto'smābhiḥ pṛcchāmastena sanmune \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “O excellent sage, we hear that you are an ancient one of long life. Hence this question. Was a king named Indradyumna seen or heard by you?”

## \|\| 1.271.43 \|\|

*śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|\| saptakalpāṃtare bhūpo na dṛṣṭo na mayā śrutaḥ \|*  
*iṃdradyumnābhidhāno'tra tatra kiṃ nu vadāmi te \|\| 43 \|\|*

Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said:

43\. In the course of these seven Kalpas, a king named Indradyumna has neither been seen nor heard about by me. So what can I say to you?

## \|\| 1.271.44 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā nirāśaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gatvā maraṇe kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing those words of his, the king lost all hopes. He became extremely disgusted and so he resolved to die.

## \|\| 1.271.45 \|\|

*tena cānīya dārūṇi prajvālya ca hutāśanam \|*  
*praveṣṭukāmaḥ sa prokta indradyumno mahīpatiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then he gathered some wood and kindled a fire. As he was about to step into the fire, king Indradyumna was thus addressed by sage Mārkaṇḍa:

## \|\| 1.271.46-47 \|\|

*tvayā cātra na kartavyamahaṃ te mitratāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*nāśayiṣyāmi te mṛtyuṃ yadyapi syānmahattaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*nīrogo'si subhavyo'si kasmānmṛtyuṃ pravāṃchasi \|*  
*vada me kāraṇaṃ mṛtyoḥ pratīkāraṃ karomi te \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. “This you must not do. I have now become your friend. I shall dispel the (cause of your) death even if it be greatly difficult. You are not sick. You are hale and hearty. Why do you wish to die? Tell me the reason for taking away your life. I shall take a counter-measure.”

## \|\| 1.271.48 \|\|

*iṃdradyumna uvāca \|*  
*cirāyurme bhavānproktaḥ kāṃpilyapuravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*tenāhaṃ tava pārśve'tra samāyāto mahāmune \|\| 48 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

48\. I was told by the residents of the city of Kāmpilya that you are a long-lived one. Hence, O great sage, I have come to you.

## \|\| 1.271.49 \|\|

*iṃdradyumnodbhavāṃ vārtāṃ tvaṃ vadiṣyasi sanmune \|*  
*matkīrtirna parijñātā tato mṛtyuṃ vrajāmyaham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O excellent sage, (I expected) that you will tell me the tidings of Indradyumna. (I came to know) that my reputation was unknown to you. So I am causing my own death.

## \|\| 1.271.50 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā dayāvānsa munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*vṛthāśramaṃ ca taṃ jñātvā dākṣiṇyādidamabravīt \|\| 50 \|\|*

Sūta said:

50\. On coming to know of his decision, the great sage was moved with pity. He fully knew that his endeavour was fruitless. Hence out of courteous consideration for him he spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.271.51-53 \|\|

*yadyevaṃ mā viśāgniṃ tvamahaṃ jñāsyāmi taṃ nṛpam \|*  
*nāḍījaṃgho bako nāma mamāsti paramaḥ suhṛt \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ciraṃtanaśca so'smākaṃ nūnaṃ jñāsyati taṃ nṛpam \|*  
*tasmādāgaccha gacchāvastasya pārśve himācale \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sādhūnāṃ darśanaṃ jātu na vṛthā jāyate kvacit \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. “If that be so, do not enter the fire. I will learn more about that king. There is a great friend of mine, a crane named Nāḍījaṅgha. He is an aged ancient one. He would certainly know about our king. Hence, do come; we shall go to him to Himālaya. Meeting with good persons can never go in vain anywhere.”

## \|\| 1.271.54 \|\|

*evamuktvā tatastau tu prasthitau munipārthivau \|*  
*vyomamārgeṇa saṃtuṣṭau bakaṃ prati himācale \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After saying thus, the sage and the king joyously set off to Himālaya by the aerial path to meet the crane.

## \|\| 1.271.55 \|\|

*bako'pi taṃ samālokya mārkaṇḍeyaṃ samāgatam \|*  
*saṃmukhaḥ prayayau tuṣṭaḥ svāgatenābhyapūjayat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On seeing Mārkaṇḍeya approaching, the crane became highly pleased. He came facing them and honoured them with due welcome greetings:

## \|\| 1.271.56 \|\|

*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ yasya me tvatsamāgamaḥ \|*  
*bho bho brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭha ātithyaṃ te karomi kim \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “Blessed am I. I am indeed meritorious, since I have come in contact with you, O most excellent one among the knowers of Brahman. How best can I extend my hospitality to you?”

## \|\| 1.271.57 \|\|

*śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*mattopi tvaṃ cirāyuśca yato mitraṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*indradyumno mahīpālastvayā dṛṣṭaḥ śruto'thavā \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said:

57\. You are longer-lived than I and you have become my friend. Has king Indradyumna been seen or heard about by you?

## \|\| 1.271.58 \|\|

*etasya mama mitrasya tena dṛṣṭena kāraṇam \|*  
*anyathā jāyate mṛtyustato'haṃ tvāṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. This friend of mine has something to do with someone seen by him. Otherwise it will end in his death. So I have come to you.

## \|\| 1.271.59-60 \|\|

*baka uvāca \|\| saptadviguṇitānkalpānsmarāmyahamasaṃśayam \|*  
*na smarāmi kathāmeva iṃdradyumnasamudbhavām \|\| 59 \|\|*

*āstāṃ hi darśanaṃ tāvatsatyametanmayodim \|\| 60 \|\|*

The Crane said:

59-60. I certainly remember fourteen Kalpas, but I do not remember any legend connected with Indradyumna; let alone seeing him personally. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.271.61 \|\|

*iṃdradyumna uvāca \|*  
*tapasaḥ kiṃ prabhāvo'yaṃ dānasya niyamasya ca \|*  
*yadāyurīdṛśaṃ jātaṃ bakatve'pi vadasva naḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

61\. Is this the power of penance, or of the observance of restraints or of making gifts that your life span has become so long despite the fact that you are only a crane? Do tell us.

## \|\| 1.271.62 \|\|

*baka uvāca \|\| ghṛtakaṃbalamāhātmyāddevadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*mamāyurīdṛśaṃ jātaṃ bakatvaṃ muniśāpataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

Crane said:

62\. My life has become so long due to the efficacy of Ghṛtakaṃbala (covering the Liṅga with ghee) of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas. My being crane is the result of the curse of a sage.

## \|\| 1.271.63 \|\|

*ahamāsaṃ purā bālo brāhmaṇasya niveśane \|*  
*camatkārapure ramye pārāśaryasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Formerly, I was a boy in the household of a wise Brāhmaṇa named Pārāśarya (i.e. of Parāśara Gotra) in the beautiful city of Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.271.64 \|\|

*nāmnā ca viśvarūpākhyo nāmnā 'nyena baka smṛtaḥ \|*  
*atīva capalatvena saṃyuktaḥ pitṛvallabhaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. My name was Viśvarūpa and I was often remembered by the nick name “Baka” because I was very fickle-minded and a darling of my father.

## \|\| 1.271.65 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya saṃkrāṃtau makarasya bhoḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpyātīva cāpalyālliṃgaṃ jāgeśvaraṃ mayā \|*  
*ghṛtakumbhe parikṣiptaṃ pūjitaṃ janakena yat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Once, at the time of the transit of the Sun into Capricorn, I became excessively frivolous. I took the Liṅga which my father regularly adored, the Jāgeśvara Liṅga, and put it into the jar of ghee.

## \|\| 1.271.66 \|\|

*atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ pṛṣṭo'haṃ janakena ca \|*  
*tvayā putra parikṣiptaṃ nūnaṃ jāgeśvaraṃ kvacit \|*  
*tasmādvada prayacchāmi tena te bhakṣyamuttamam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. As the night passed away, I was questioned by my father. “Certainly, the Jāgeśvara Liṅga has been dropped down somewhere by you, dear boy. Do tell me. I shall give you something excellent to munch and crunch.”

## \|\| 1.271.67 \|\|

*tato mayājyakumbhācca tasmādādāya satvaram \|*  
*bhakṣyalaulyātpiturhaste vinyastaṃ ghṛtasaṃplutam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Urged by a desire to eat the (promised) luscious stuff, I immediately retrieved the Liṅga from the jar of ghee and placed it on the hand of my father even as it dripped with ghee.

## \|\| 1.271.68-69 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya paṃcatvaṃ ca samāgataḥ \|*  
*jātismarastato jātastatprabhāvānnṛpālaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ānartādhipaterharmye nāmnā khyātastvahaṃ bakaḥ \|*
