*tataśca yauvanaṃ prāptaḥ krameṇa nṛpasattama \|*  
*yadā tadā niśi tyaktvā tāvubhau cātra saṃgataḥ \|\| 349 \|\|*

349\. Gradually, I attained the prime of youth. On a certain night, I left off both of them and came to this place.

## \|\| 1.271.350 \|\|

*tato hṛṣṭamanā nityaṃ pūjayāmi samāhitaḥ \|*  
*īśānaṃ parayā bhaktyā saṃsnāpya salilena ca \|\| 350 \|\|*

350\. Ever since then I have been worshipping Īśāna with great concentration and ardent devotion with a delighted heart and bath the Liṅga with cool water.

## \|\| 1.271.351 \|\|

*brāhmaṇītīrthajātena trikālaṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*śiloṃchavṛttimāsādya prāṇayātrāṃ samācaran \|*  
*nīvārairbadaraiḥ śākaiścirbhaṭaiḥ phalapatrakaiḥ \|\| 351 \|\|*

351\. With the waters of the holy river Brāhmaṇī\[2\], O excellent king, I performed the ablution thrice a day. I adopted the practice of gleaning of ears of corn and sustained my life with Nīvāra rice, Badara seeds, green vegetables, cucumber pieces, fruits and leaves.

## \|\| 1.271.352 \|\|

*tato me bhagavānrudraḥ sarvadeveśvaro haraḥ \|*  
*abravīddarśanaṃ gatvā meghagambhīrayā girā \|\| 352 \|\|*

352\. Thereafter, Lord Rudra, Hara, the Lord of all Devas, appeared before me and spoke in words as majestic as rumbling of a cloud:

## \|\| 1.271.353 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa varaṃ varaya suvate \|*  
*adeyamapi dāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 353 \|\|*

353\. “O dear one, I am pleased with you. O Brāhmaṇa of excellent holy rites, choose a boon I shall grant you even those things that cannot be ordinarily granted, even if they are very rare.”

## \|\| 1.271.354 \|\|

*tatastaṃ praṇipatyoccaiḥ stutvā vākyaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*mayā proktaṃ kuru vibho jarāmaraṇa varjitam \|\| 354 \|\|*

354\. Then I bowed down to him and eulogized him with various kinds of eulogies. Then I said to him: “O Lord, make me free from old age and death.”

## \|\| 1.271.355 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|\| amaratvaṃ yato nāsti martyaloke'tra karhicit \|*  
*maryādāṃ kuru tasmāttvaṃ jīvitasya svakasya vai \|\| 355 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

355\. Since there is nothing like immortality here in the mortar world, set a limit to your span of life.

## \|\| 1.271.356-357 \|\|

*tato me bhagavānuktaḥ kalpāṃte samupasthite \|*  
*romṇa ekasya me nāśo jāyatāṃ tridaśeśvara \|\| 356 \|\|*

*yadā ca sarvaromṇāṃ me vināśaḥ saṃprajāyate \|*  
*tadā mama gaṇatvaṃ ca jāyatāṃ tāvakaṃ vibho \|\| 357 \|\|*

356-357. Then the Lord was told by me: “O Lord of Devas, let one hair of mine drop away at the end of a Kalpa. When all the hairs of mine drop away let me attain the state of your Gaṇa, O Lord.”

## \|\| 1.271.358-362 \|\|

*evaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktaṃ paraṃ liṃga sadā mama \|*  
*snāpyaṃ jalena caitena brāhmaṇīsaṃbhavena ca \|\| 358 \|\|*

*brahmādyaiḥ pūjanīya ca trikālaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*mamakaivāsaraṃ yāvattava cāyurbhaviṣyati \|\| 359 \|\|*

*anyo'pi yo naro bhaktyā pūjayiṣyati māmiha \|*  
*snāpayiṣyati sadbhaktyā vipāpmā sa bhaviṣyati \|\| 360 \|\|*

*nāpamṛtyurbhavettasya kadāciddvijasattama \|*  
*sakṛtsaṃpūjite 'pyevaṃ brahmādyairmatkalevare \|\| 361 \|\|*

*sakṛtpibati yastoyaṃ brahmatīrthasamudbhavam \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā tatkṣaṇājjāyate hi saḥ \|\| 362 \|\|*

358-362. (The Lord said:) “It shall be so but my Liṅga should be bathed always with the water of this Brāhmaṇī river.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, this Liṅga is worthy of being adored by Brahmā and others thrice a day. You will have the span of life equal to a single day of mine.

Any other man who adores me devoutly and bathes the Liṅga shall become free from sins.

He will never meet with accidental or unnatural death, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, even if my person adored by Brahmā and others is adored only once.

He who drinks even once the water of Brahma Tīrtha, shall instantly become a purified soul bereft of all sins.”

## \|\| 1.271.363 \|\|

*evamuktvātha deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 363 \|\|*

363\. After saying thus the Lord of Devas vanished.

## \|\| 1.271.364 \|\|

*ahaṃ tu saṃsthitaścātra tataḥ prabhṛti pārthiva \|*  
*pūjayānaśca sadbhaktyā liṃgametatsadaiva hi \|\| 364 \|\|*

364\. O king, ever since then I have been staying here worshipping this Liṅga always with excellent devotion.

## \|\| 1.271.365 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇājjātaṃ mamāyurativistṛtam \|*  
*śaṃkarasya prasādena nānyadastīha kāraṇam \|\| 365 \|\|*

365\. On account of this, by the grace of Śaṅkara, the span of my life has become very long. There is no other cause.

## \|\| 1.271.366 \|\|

*indradyumna uvāca \|*  
*ahamapyarcayiṣyāmi liṃgameta ttvayā saha \|*  
*nānyatra vā gamiṣyāmi mamaivaṃ hṛdi niścayaḥ \|\| 366 \|\|*

Indradyumna said:

366\. I too shall worship this Liṅga along with you. I will not go elsewhere. This is the resolve in my heart.

## \|\| 1.271.367 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ kuru mahābhāga tvamavāpsyasi vāṃchitam \|*  
*harabhaktasya lokasya vāṃchitaṃ nāsti dularbham \|\| 367 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

367\. O highly esteemed one, do this. You will achieve your desire. What is desired (by a devotee) is not difficult to get for the people devoted to Hara.

## \|\| 1.271.368 \|\|

*nāḍījaṃgho gṛhaṃ yātu mārkaṃḍagṛdhakauśikāḥ \|*  
*kacchapena samāyuktastvaṃ hi tiṣṭha mamā śrame \|\| 368 \|\|*

368\. Let Nāḍījaṅgha go home. So also Mārkaṇḍa, the vulture and the owl. Only you, accompanied by the tortoise stay in my hermitage.

## \|\| 1.271.369 \|\|

*tataḥ procuśca te sarve na vayaṃ tu nareśvara \|*  
*tvāṃ vinā saṃprayāsyāmo bhūya eva nijālayam \|*  
*liṃgamārādhayiṣyāmo yadetadbhavatā rcitam \|\| 369 \|\|*

369\. Then all of them said: “O king, we will not go back without you to our abodes again. We will worship and propitiate this Liṅga that is being adored by you.”

## \|\| 1.271.370 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu te sarve lomaśasya varāśrame \|*  
*tasthuḥ saṃpūjayāmāsustrikālaṃ liṃgameva tat \|\| 370 \|\|*

370\. After saying thus all of them stayed in the excellent hermitage of Lomaśa and worshipped that Liṅga thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.271.371 \|\|

*saṃsnāpya brāhmaṇītoyaiḥ padmā dyaiḥ pūjayaṃti ca \|\| 371 \|\|*

371\. They bathed the Liṅga with the waters of Brāhmaṇī river and worshipped with lotuses and other flowers.

## \|\| 1.271.372 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena saṃprāptastatra yatra te \|\| 372 \|\|*

372\. Once upon a time, in the course of his pilgrimage, Nārada, the excellent sage, came to the place where they were (staying).

## \|\| 1.271.373 \|\|

*atha  nāradaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtvā caivārhaṇakriyām \|*  
*viśrāṃtaṃ ca tato jñātvā papracchurvinayānvitāḥ \|\| 373 \|\|*

373\. On seeing Nārada, they performed duly all the rites of honouring him. Coming to know that he had had his rest, they asked him with all humility:

## \|\| 1.271.374-376 \|\|

*śāpabhraṣṭā vayaṃ sarve yataḥ saṃvartadarśanāt \|*  
*bakādyāścaiva catvāraḥ kūrmāṃtāśca mahāmune \|\| 374 \|\|*

*na sa vijñāyate kvāpi kasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃrūpaḥ kiṃpramāṇaśca kimācāraḥ kva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 375 \|\|*

*sa tvaṃ yadi vijānāsi yatra taṃ saṃsthitaṃ munim \|*  
*tadvadasva mahābhāga na kiṃcitte'styagocaram \|\| 376 \|\|*

374-376. (Corrupt text) “We four beginning with the Baka and ending with the Kūrma (tortoise) (can be free from our curses), O great sage, only on the sight of Saṃvarta.

It is not known at what place he resides, what his form is, what his status is, what he does and where his permanent resort is.

O highly esteemed one, if you know where he stays permanently, kindly let us know. Nothing is beyond the ken of your perception.

## \|\| 1.271.377 \|\|

*śrīnārada uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ jānāmi taṃ samyaksaṃvartaṃ munisattamam \|*  
*guptācāreṇa tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ nānyo vetti kathaṃcanam \|\| 377 \|\|*

Śrī Nārada said:

377\. I know that Saṃvarta perfectly. The excellent sage remains in seclusion. His conduct is well-concealed. No one else knows him at all.

## \|\| 1.271.378 \|\|

*vārāṇāsyāṃ sthito nityaṃ so'vadhūto mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*vivastro maladigdhāṃgaḥ sadāraṇyaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 378 \|\|*

378\. That Avadhūta (nude ascetic or ascetic without worldly attachment), the great sage, resides in Vārāṇasī permanently. He is naked. He smears himself with filth and rubbish. He always resorts to forest.

## \|\| 1.271.379 \|\|

*bhikṣārthaṃ kutape kāle samāgacchati tāṃ purīm \|*  
*pāṇipātrakṛtāhāro gṛhaiḥ kaiścitsadaiva hi \|\| 379 \|\|*

379\. At the Kutapa hour (eighth Muhūrta) he comes to that city. He receives alms from only a few houses. He receives everything on the palm of the hand (that works as a pot) once and eats it.

## \|\| 1.271.380-381 \|\|

*bhūyopi yāti sāyāhne kiṃcideva vanāṃtaram \|*  
*tasyāṃ puryāṃ tathārūpāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 380 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhaṃti tāpasaśreṣṭhāstasya vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ sa yathā jñeyo mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 381 \|\|*

380-381. In the evening he goes back to some forest region.

In that city there are hundreds and thousands of ascetics with the same (routine) features. Many of them are excellent ascetics. They stay in the city. But I shall describe to you the characteristics of (that Saṃvarta) so that you can recognize him without doubts.

## \|\| 1.271.382 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāḥ pratolyāṃ ca sthāpanīyaṃ suyatnataḥ ḥ \|*  
*kuṇapaṃ caiva guptaṃ ca yathā no vetti kaścana \|\| 382 \|\|*

382\. A corpse should be secretly and cautiously placed in the main street of Vārāṇasī so that no one shall know it.

## \|\| 1.271.383 \|\|

*yāsyaṃti tāpasāḥ sarve tamatikramya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*saṃvarto divyadṛṣṭistu śalyaṃ nātikramiṣyati \|\| 383 \|\|*

383\. All the ascetics shall mostly cross over it, but Saṃvarta endowed with divine vision will not transgress this obstacle.

## \|\| 1.271.384 \|\|

*nivartanaṃ tu yaścakre bhūbhāgātkuṇapāśrayāt \|*  
*sa saṃvartaḥ parijñeyaḥ praṣṭavyaśca tataḥ param \|\| 384 \|\|*

384\. He who retreats from the ground where the corpse is concealed, should be known as Saṃvarta. Thereafter, he should be asked.

## \|\| 1.271.385 \|\|

*yadi pṛcchati kenāhaṃ bhavatāṃ saṃniveditaḥ \|*  
*nāradena tato vācyaṃ sa tvāṃ jānāti vai sadā \|\| 385 \|\|*

385\. If he asks, “By whom have I been described to you,” you must say “By Nārada who has always known you.”

## \|\| 1.271.386-387 \|\|

*yadi pṛcchati bhūyaḥ sa nāradaḥ kva sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 386 \|\|*

*tato vācyo nivedya tvāṃ pratiṣṭo havyavāhanam \|\| 387 \|\|*

386-387. If he asks again, “Where is Nārada staying,” then he should be told, “After describing you, he has entered fire.”

## \|\| 1.271.388 \|\|

*tacchrutvā nāradavacaḥ sarve vai lomaśādayaḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ purīṃ prāptāstasya darśanalālasāḥ \|\| 388 \|\|*

388\. On hearing the words of Nārada, all those beginning with Lomaśa came to the city of Vārāṇasī with a desire to see him.

## \|\| 1.271.389 \|\|

*pratolyāṃ kuṇapaṃ sthāpya guptaṃ lokairalakṣitam \|*  
*svayaṃ caiva sthitā dūraṃ prekṣamāṇāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 389 \|\|*

389\. They hid a corpse in the main street without being seen by the people. They themselves stood far away watching carefully.

## \|\| 1.271.390 \|\|

*tatastu kutape kāle saṃvartastu samāgataḥ \|*  
*yādṛgrūpaḥ purā prokto nāradena mahātmanā \|\| 390 \|\|*

390\. Then at the Kutapa hour (eighth Muhūrta of the day) Saṃvarta came with the same form and features as described by the noble-souled Nārada.

## \|\| 1.271.391 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā kuṇapaṃ tatra divyadṛṣṭyā mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*nivṛttaḥ kṣutpipāsārto naiva śalyamalaṃghayat \|\| 391 \|\|*

391\. With his divine vision, the great sage saw the corpse. He retreated though he was distressed with hunger and thirst. He did not cross over the Śalya (obstacle, corpse).

## \|\| 1.271.392 \|\|

*atha te taṃ samuddiśya pṛṣṭhato'nuyayustadā \|*  
*tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti jalpaṃtaḥ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 392 \|\|*

392\. They closely followed him saying, “Stop! Stop! Be pleased to do us a favour.”

## \|\| 1.271.393 \|\|

*so'pi nirbhartsayannetānnivartadhvamiti bruvan \|*  
*mā gacchata matsamīpamiti procya palāyitam \|\| 393 \|\|*

393\. He rebuked these saying, “Go back. Do not come near me.” Then he fled.

## \|\| 1.271.394 \|\|

*atha dūrataraṃ gatvā sa provāca kṣudhānvitaḥ \|\| 394 \|\|*

394\. After going far away he said because he was hungry:

## \|\| 1.271.395 \|\|

*kenādiṣṭo'smi yuṣmākaṃ sa śīghraṃ me nivedyatām \|*  
*śāpāgnau yena taṃ pāpaṃ bhasmasātprakaromyaham \|\| 395 \|\|*

395\. “By whom have I been revealed to you? Let him be exposed so that I shall reduce him to ash in the fire of curse.”

## \|\| 1.271.396 \|\|

*ta ūcuḥ \|*  
*nāradena samākhyāto bhavānatra sthito hi naḥ \|*  
*kathayitvā tato vahnau saṃpraviṣṭaḥ sa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 396 \|\|*

They said:

396\. That you are stationed here has been divulged to us by Nārada. After doing this, he instantly entered fire.

## \|\| 1.271.397 \|\|

*saṃvarta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tadeva kartā ca tasya duṣṭasya sāṃpratam \|*  
*nirdiṣṭo yena yuṣmākaṃ guptācāraṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 397 \|\|*

Saṃvarta said:

397\. I will do the same to that wicked one now, by whom I have been revealed to you though I was remaining hidden in my activity.

## \|\| 1.271.398 \|\|

*ta ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavannāradenoktastvamasmākaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*cirādanveṣyamāṇānāṃ nānyastvāṃ vetti kaścana \|\| 398 \|\|*

They said:

398\. O holy Sir, O great sage, you have been revealed to us by Nārada. We have been searching for you for a long time, and no one else knows you.

## \|\| 1.271.399 \|\|

*tāvannivedya cāsmākaṃ praviṣṭo havyavāhanam \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādeva vipreṃdra na vidmastatra kāraṇam \|\| 399 \|\|*

399\. After revealing to us, he has entered the sacred fire instantly. O leading Brāhmaṇa, we do not know the reason thereof.

## \|\| 1.271.400-401 \|\|

*saṃvarta uvāca \|*  
*ahamapyatisaṃkruddhaḥ śāpātkartuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*etadevahi tasmācca svayameva kṛtaṃ ca yat \|\| 400 \|\|*

*tasmādvadatha me śīghraṃ kasmādyūyaṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 401 \|\|*

Saṃvarta said:

400-401. I am excessively angry. By means of curse I was about to do the same thing as he has himself done. So tell me quickly why you all have come.

## \|\| 1.271.402 \|\|

*ciraṃ sthāsyāmi nātrāhaṃ bhramiṣyāmi purīṃ prati \|*  
*prāṇayātrākṛte bhikṣāṃ kariṣyāmi svayaṃ yataḥ \|\| 402 \|\|*

402\. I will not stay here long. I will be roaming about in the direction of the city because I have to beg for alms for sustaining my life.

## \|\| 1.271.403 \|\|

*viśalyaḥ kriyatāṃ mārgaḥ kuṇapaṃ hriyatāṃ ca yat \|*  
*nocecchāpaṃ pradāsyāmi yadyevaṃ na kariṣyatha \|\| 403 \|\|*

403\. Let the road be rid of this obstacle. Let this corpse be taken away. If you do not do so I will curse you.

## \|\| 1.271.404 \|\|

*tathāhaṃ naiva vaktavyaḥ kasyaciccātra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*anveṣayati māṃ nityaṃ maruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 404 \|\|*

404\. Further, I should not be revealed to anyone as staying here. King Marutta has always been in search of me.

## \|\| 1.271.405 \|\|

*yajñārthaṃ naiva taṃ bhūpaṃ yājayiṣye kathaṃcana \|*  
*dhiṣaṇena parityakto guruṇā sa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 405 \|\|*

405\. It is for the sake of a Yajña. I will not at all perform the Yajña on his behalf. That king has been abandoned by Dhiṣaṇa (Jupiter), the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.271.406 \|\|

*guruputraṃ ca māṃ jñātvā tato'nveṣayate hi mām \|\| 406 \|\|*

406\. Knowing that I am the son of Guru he is in search of me.

## \|\| 1.271.407 \|\|

*ta ūcuḥ \|*  
*śāpabhraṣṭā vayaṃ sarve catvāro'pi bakādayaḥ \|*  
*pakṣitvaṃ caiva saṃprāptā brahmaśāpena sanmune \|\| 407 \|\|*

They said:

407\. We four beginning with the Baka have fallen down due to curses. O excellent sage, we attained the state of birds due to the curse of Brahmā (or Brāhmaṇas).

## \|\| 1.271.408 \|\|

*maheśvaragaṇāścaiva vayaṃ trailokyavaṃditāḥ \|*  
*tiryagyoniṃ samānītā vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 408 \|\|*

408\. We were Maheśvara Gaṇas held in respect in all the three worlds. We have been brought down to the level of lowly creatures. We are hence disgusted and dejected very much.

## \|\| 1.271.409 \|\|

*śāpāṃtastu samādiṣṭastairvipraiḥ strīsamu dbhavaḥ \|*  
*tavopadeśatastena bakādyāḥ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 409 \|\|*

409\. End to the curses originating from women had been indicated by those Brāhmaṇas namely through your instructions. So the Baka and others have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 1.271.410 \|\|

*tasmāttrāhi mahābhāga pakṣitvātsāṃprataṃ vibho \|\| 410 \|\|*

410\. O highly esteemed holy Sir, save us now from the state of birds.

## \|\| 1.271.411 \|\|

*nirviṇṇāścirakālaṃ ca pakṣitvasya niṣevaṇāt \|*  
*etacca kāraṇaṃ nānyattava saṃgasamudbhavam \|\| 411 \|\|*

411\. We have become despondent and disgusted after, enduring this state of being birds for a long time. This is the reason for coming into contact with you.

## \|\| 1.271.412 \|\|

*saṃvarta uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ camatkārapuraṃ prati \|*  
*bhartṛ yajñaḥ sthito'pyatra sarvasaṃdehahārakaḥ \|\| 412 \|\|*

Saṃvarta said:

412\. If it is so, do go to the city of Camatkārapura. Bhartṛyajña too is there. He is one who removes all doubts.

## \|\| 1.271.413 \|\|

*sa vai dāsyati sarveṣāmupadeśaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*tena prāpsyatha saṃdehaṃ pūrvīyaṃ ca yathāsthitam \|\| 413 \|\|*

413\. He will give everyone excellent instruction. Thereby all of you will get clarification of your earlier doubts.

## \|\| 1.271.414 \|\|

*sa pūrvaṃ yājñavalkyo'bhūtsarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|*  
*tato bhavāṃtare'nyasminkātyāyana iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 414 \|\|*

414\. Formerly, he was Yājñavalkya, the master of all the scriptural topics. In another birth, he was remembered as Kātyāyana.

## \|\| 1.271.415 \|\|

*tato dehāṃtaraṃ prāpya khyāto vararucirdvijaḥ \|*  
*tato dehāṃtare'nyasminveśyāputro babhūva ha \|\| 415 \|\|*

415\. In the next rebirth he became well-known as Brāhmaṇa Vararuci. Again in the next rebirth he became the son of a harlot.

## \|\| 1.271.416 \|\|

*ārādhitā brahmasutā devī vāgrūpiṇī sadā \|*  
*na ca tuṣṭā svayaṃ devī kāraṇaṃ vīkṣya kiṃcana \|\| 416 \|\|*

416\. The goddess, the daughter of Brahmā, was propitiated always in the form of Speech. But the goddess did not become satisfied because she had some reason therefor.

## \|\| 1.271.417 \|\|

*brāhmaṇena prajātastu dehāṃtaṃ prāpya kiṃcana \|*  
*tasya vaktraṃ samāpannā svayameva sarasvatī \|\| 417 \|\|*

417\. Born of a Brāhmaṇa he met with his death. Then Sarasvatī occupied the mouth (tongue) herself.

## \|\| 1.271.418 \|\|

*pūrvamārādhitā nityaṃ na sā tyajati karhicit \|*  
*tasyāścaryamabhūccānyadyajñe veśyāsutasya hi \|\| 418 \|\|*

418\. If she is propitiated earlier, she never abandons him at any cost. In the course of the Yajña of the son of the harlot, there happened a miracle.

## \|\| 1.271.419 \|\|

*brahmasūtraṃ samabhyeti skaṃdhe niryāti gacchati \|\| 419 \|\|*

419\. The Brahmasūtra comes to the shoulder, coming out and goes away.

## \|\| 1.271.420 \|\|

*pūrveṣāmeva lokānāṃ yajñakarmasu saṃsthitān \|*  
*sa saṃdehānharatyeva yathā nānyo'tra kaścana \|\| 420 \|\|*

420\. He dispelled the doubts regarding the Yajña rites, of even the earlier people. None else could do so.

## \|\| 1.271.421 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*gatāste kuṇapaṃ yatra saṃvartena praṇoditāḥ \|\| 421 \|\|*

Sūta said:

421\. On hearing his words, they bowed down to him repeatedly. On being directed by Saṃvarta, they went to the place where the corpse had been kept.

## \|\| 1.271.422-426 \|\|

*taccākṛṣya tataḥ sarve camatkārapuraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vāstusthānapade tīrthe taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra saṃsthitam \|\| 422 \|\|*

*praṇipatya tataḥ procuḥ sarve vinayasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*brahmaśāpena nirdagdhā vayaṃ catvāra eva hi \|\| 423 \|\|*

*pakṣitvaṃ samanuprāptāstrayaḥ kūrmatvamanyakaḥ \|*  
*ya ete ca trayo'smākaṃ sthitāḥ pārśve mahattarāḥ \|\| 424 \|\|*

*mārkaṃḍaḥ kathito hyeṣa iṃdradyumnastathā paraḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyo lomaśo nāma vikhyātaḥ sumahātapāḥ \|\| 425 \|\|*

*jīvitavyasya nirviṇṇāstraya eva ca sāṃpratam \|*  
*upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 426 \|\|*

422-426. They removed the corpse and all went to Camatkārapura. In the Tīrtha called Vāstusthānapada they saw him (Bhartṛyajña) stationed. They bowed down to him and said with humility: “We four have been completely scorched by the curse of Brāhmaṇas. Three of us attained the state of birds and the last one that of tortoise. Those who are standing nearby are even greater ones. This is Mārkaṇḍa and the other is known as Indradyumna. The third one is a sage of well-known great austerity named Lomaśa. Now all these are disgusted with their lives. It behoves you to bless them by giving them proper instruction.”

## \|\| 1.271.427 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhartṛyajño mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*abravītsuciraṃ dhyātvā jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 427 \|\|*

Sūta said:

427\. On hearing their words, Bhartṛyajña, the great sage, meditated for a long time. Having understood everything through the divine vision he said:

## \|\| 1.271.428-430 \|\|

*yūyaṃ saptaiva liṃgāni sthāpayadhvaṃ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre nāmnā caivāṃtike nibhoḥ \|\| 428 \|\|*

*tato dānāni saptaiva teṣāmagre prayacchata \|*  
*kulaparvatasaṃjñāni sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|\| 429 \|\|*

*tataḥ prāpsyatha cābhīṣṭaṃ vapurdivyaṃ manoramam \|*  
*gaṇatvaṃ devadevasya trine trasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 430 \|\|*

428-430. “O ye who have come here, install seven Liṅgas in the Hāṭakeśvara shrine very near to the deity, after your own names. Then, in front of them, make seven Dānas named after the Kula Parvatas. They shall be destructive of all the sins.

Then you will have the divine and charming body of Gaṇas of the noble-souled Three-eyed Lord of Devas.”

## \|\| 1.271.431 \|\|

*ta ūcuḥ \|*  
*prakīrtaya vibho dānaṃ teṣāṃ yacchāmahe yathā \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ ca vidhānaṃ ca vistareṇa mahāmune \|\| 431 \|\|*

They said:

431\. O Lord, O great sage, describe to us the relevant Dāna, so that we can start giving it away. Let us know the magnitude and procedure in detail.

## \|\| 1.271.432-433 \|\|

*bhartṛyajña uvāca \|*  
*deyo hemamayo meruḥ kailāso rajatodbhavaḥ \|*  
*kārppāsena himādristu guḍajo gaṃdhamādanaḥ \|\| 432 \|\|*

*suvelastu tilairdeyo viṃdhyaḥ śarkarayā tathā \|*  
*lavaṇena tathā śṛṃgī yathoktavidhinā tataḥ \|\| 433 \|\|*

Bhartṛyajña said:

432-433. (The Dāna named after) Meru should be made in gold, Kailāsa in silver, Himādri in cotton, Gandhmādana \[Gandhamādana?\] in jaggery. Suvela should be given in the form of gingelly seeds, Vindhya in that of sugar and Śṛṅgī in that of salt. All these gifts should be made in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.271.434 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃsthāpya vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*saptaliṃgāni taiḥ paścātpradattāḥ kulaparvatāḥ \|\| 434 \|\|*

Sūta said:

434\. On hearing his words, the seven Liṅgas were duly installed by them. (The. Dānas named after) Kulaparvatas were given thereafter.

## \|\| 1.271.435 \|\|

*iṃdradyumneśvarasyāgre iṃdradyumnaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*meruṃ hemamayaṃ kṛtvā bhartṛyajñamate sthitaḥ \|\| 435 \|\|*

435\. Before the deity Indradyumneśvara, the valorous Indradyumna who abided by the instruction of Bhartṛyajña, prepared (a replica of) Meru in gold (and gifted it).

## \|\| 1.271.436 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeśvaradevasya mārkaṃḍena ca dhīmatā \|*  
*kailāso rājato datto bhaktipūrvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 436 \|\|*

436\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, a silver replica of Kailāsa was given devoutly by the wise Mārkaṇḍa in front of Mārkaṇḍeśvara.

## \|\| 1.271.437-441 \|\|

*kārpāso himavāndattaḥ pālakena dvijātaye \|*  
*gaṃdhamādanasaṃjñastu pradatto guḍajaḥ puraḥ \|\| 437 \|\|*

*ghaṃṭakeśvaradevasya ghaṃṭakena dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kacchapena tu saṃdattaḥ suvelaḥ parvatottamaḥ \|\| 438 \|\|*

*kacchapeśvaradevasya purastilamayastathā \|*  
*śārkarastu tadā śailaḥ pradatto bhaktipūrvakam \|\| 439 \|\|*

*śaila īśānasaṃjñena nijadevasya cā'grataḥ \|*  
*vānareśvara devasya purato dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 440 \|\|*

*gṛdhreṇātha pradattastu lavaṇākhyo mahāgiriḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgī nāma mahābhāgaḥ śraddhāpūtena cetasā \|\| 441 \|\|*

437-441. Himavān made of cotton was gifted away to a Brāhmaṇa by Pālaka. Gandhamādana mountain made of jaggery was gifted by Ghaṇṭaka, O excellent Brāhmaṇas in front of Lord Ghaṇṭakeśvara. The excellent mountain Suvela made of gingelly seeds was given by the tortoise in front of Lord Kacchapeśvara. Mountain Vindhya was devoutly given by the person named Īśāna before his deity. It was made of sugar. The great mountain named Śṛṅgī made of salt was gifted by the Gṛdhra in front of the deity Vānareśvara Deva. All of them made the gifts with their minds purified by faith.

## \|\| 1.271.442 \|\|

*tatrāścaryamabhūdviprā dattamātrairnagottamaiḥ \|*  
*pakṣitvaṃ nirgataṃ teṣāṃ kūrmatvamitarasya ca \|\| 442 \|\|*

442\. There a miracle happened, O Brāhmaṇas, as soon as the excellent mountains were gifted away. The state of their being birds in the case of three vanished along with the state of being a tortoise in the case of the other.

## \|\| 1.271.443 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu sarve te tatprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*divyamālyāṃbaradharā divyagaṃdhānulepanāḥ \|*  
*saṃjātā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā ye ca tatsaṃmukhe sthitāḥ \|\| 443 \|\|*

443\. In the meantime, by the power thereof, all of them became persons wearing divine garlands and garments and smeared with divine scents and unguents. All those who stood in front of them also were so.

## \|\| 1.271.444 \|\|

*vimānāni ca sarveṣāṃ samāyātāni tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*bhartṛyajñamanuprāpya praṇipatya ca tāndvijān \|*  
*kailāsaṃ parvataṃ prāptā vimānavaramāśritāḥ \|\| 444 \|\|*

444\. In an instant, aerial chariots also came for the sake of all of them. They approached Bhartṛyajña and bowed to all the Brāhmaṇas. Then they rode on the excellent aerial chariots and reached the Kailāsa mountain.

## \|\| 1.271.445 \|\|

*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā talliṃgasaptakam \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃjātaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 445 \|\|*

445\. Thus, everything has been narrated to you, as to how that set of seven Liṅgas originated in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.271.446 \|\|

*anyo'pi yaḥ punasteṣāṃ liṃgānāṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kulaparvatadānaṃ ca kuryātso'pi śivaṃ vrajet \|\| 446 \|\|*

446\. Any other man endowed with devotion who makes the gift of the Kulaparvatas in front of those Liṅgas shall attain Śiva.

## \|\| 1.271.447 \|\|

*tāni liṃgāni yo martyaḥ prātarutthāya vīkṣate \|*  
*ajñānavihitātpāpātso'pi muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 447 \|\|*

447\. If a man gets up early in the morning and looks at those Liṅgas, he shall be rid of the sin committed unwittingly.

## \|\| 1.271.448 \|\|

*yaścaitānparvatānsapta krameṇātra prayacchati \|*  
*dvijātibhyaḥ svaliṃgānāṃ puratastridivaṃ vrajet \|\| 448 \|\|*

448\. He who makes the gift of these seven mountains in due order in front of their respective Liṅgas to Brāhmaṇas shall go to heaven.

## \|\| 1.271.449 \|\|

*sthitvā kalpāṃtaraṃ tatra saṃsevya ca varāpsarāḥ \|*  
*divyānbhogāṃśca saṃsevya yadā bhūmau prajāyate \|*  
*cakravartitvamāsādya sārvabhaumaḥ prajāyate \|\| 449 \|\|*

449\. For the period of a Kalpa, he enjoys the excellent Apsarās there and also divine pleasures. Then when he is born on the earth he becomes an emperor and monarch of all.

## \|\| 1.271.450 \|\|

*ekena tu pradattena jāyate pāpasaṃkṣayaḥ \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca vāṃchitāni phalāni ca \|\| 450 \|\|*

450\. If a single mountain is gifted, sins are dispelled. If two mountains are gifted, one gets sons, grandsons and desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.271.451 \|\|

*tribhiḥ saṃjāyate rājā caturbhirmaṃḍaleśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhāratasya ca khaṇḍasya svāmī bhavati paṃcabhiḥ \|\| 451 \|\|*

451\. Through three gifts one becomes a king and through four a Maṇḍaleśvara (Monarch of a Zone). Through five gifts, one becomes the master of Bharatakhaṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.271.452 \|\|

*jaṃbudvīpādhipaḥ ṣaṅbhiścakravartī ca saptabhiḥ \|*  
*vidhivatparvatairdattaireta dāha pitāmahaḥ \|\| 452 \|\|*

452\. Through six gifts one becomes the Lord of Jaṃbūdvīpa and through seven gifts an emperor. This is the outcome of gifting the mountains in accordance with injunctions. Pitāmaha said so.

## \|\| 1.271.453 \|\|

*naraḥ syādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sadājanmanijanmani \|*  
*na duḥkhito daridro vā vyādhito vā prajāyate \|\| 453 \|\|*

453\. A man shall always, in every birth, become an excellent Brāhmaṇa. Never is he miserable, poor or sick.

## \|\| 1.271.454 \|\|

*saubhāgyasukhasaṃyuktaḥ sudeho ratnavānbhavet \|*  
*sarvarājyavinirmuktaḥ pratāpī vijitendriyaḥ \|\| 454 \|\|*

454\. He will become endowed with conjugal felicity and happiness. His body shall be splendid. He will possess gems. He will be free from all enemies. He will subdue all the senses and become valorous.

## \|\| 1.271.455 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena bhūmipālairviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*etaṃ ca parvatā deyā uddiśya nijadevatāḥ \|\| 455 \|\|*

455\. Hence all, especially kings, shall assiduously make gifts of these mountains. They should keep their own deities in view.

## Chapter 272 - Characteristics of Different Yugas

## \|\| 1.272.1-7 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|\| \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktamīśānasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*īśvareṇa purā dattamāyuryāvatsvavāsaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kiṃpramāṇaṃ bhavettasya divasasya bravīhi naḥ \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ divasasya tu \|\| 2 \|\|*

*māheśvarasya viprendrāḥ śrūyatāṃ gadataḥ sphuṭam \|*  
*nimeṣasya caturbhāgastruṭiḥ syāttaddvayaṃ lavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*lavadvayaṃ yavaḥ proktaḥ kāṣṭhā te daśa paṃca ca \|*  
*triṃśatkāṣṭhāḥ kalāmāhuḥ kṣaṇastriṃśatkalo mataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kṣaṇaiḥ ṣaṣṭyā palaṃ proktaṃ ṣaṣṭyā teṣāṃ ca nāḍikā \|*  
*nāḍikādvitayenaiva muhūrtaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*triṃśanmuhūrttamuddiṣṭamahorātraṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*māsastriṃśadahorātraidvau dvau māsāvṛtuṃ viduḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ṛtutrayaṃ cāpyayanamayane dve tu vatsaram \|*  
*mānuṣāṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ sa eva parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Note: This topic is popular with Purāṇas. We find it dealt with in BhP XII.2, Kūrma 1.29, Nārada I. 41. 1-123, to mention a few. There is a remarkable similarity (even textual) in the descriptions given in various Purāṇas.

The sages said:

1-7. Your Holines \[Holiness\] earlier said that Lord Īśvara granted King Īśāna a span of life equal to a day of his own life. Do tell us what the magnitude of that day may be.

## \|\| 1.272.8 \|\|

*sa devānāmahorātraṃ purāṇajñāḥ pracakṣate \|*  
*ayanaṃ cottaraṃ śuklaṃ yaddevānāṃ dinaṃ ca tat \|*  
*yaddakṣiṇaṃ tu sā rātriḥ śubhakarmavigarhitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sūta said:

I shall recount to you all the extent of that day of Maheśvara, O leading Brāhmaṇas.

May it be heard even as I speak out clearly: A fourth of a Nimeṣa is, a Truṭi. Two Nimeṣas make one Lava. Two Lavas make one Yava, it is said. Fifteen Yavas make one Kāṣṭhā. They say, thirty Kāṣṭhās make one Kalā. A Kṣaṇa is considered to be constituted by thirty Kalās. A Pala is said to be made up to sixty Kṣaṇas and sixty Palas make one Nāḍikā. Two Nāḍikās make a Muhūrta, it is proclaimed. Learned men declare that a day and a night together contain thirty Muhūrtas. Thirty Ahorātras (day and night) make one Māsa (month). They know that a Ṛtu (season) contains two months. Three Ṛtus make one Ayana (Sun’s transit) and two Ayanas make one year (Vatsara). The same is reiterated in the case of all men.

8\. Those who are conversant with the Purāṇas say that a Vatsara (year) of men is an Ahorātra of the Devas. The Uttara (Northern) Ayana is Śukla (White) and it is the day of the Devas. The Dakṣiṇa (Southern) Ayana is the night, disapproved for performing auspicious rites.

## \|\| 1.272.9 \|\|

*yathā supto na gṛhṇāti kiṃcidbhogādikaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*tathā devāśca yajñāṃśānna gṛhṇanti kathaṃ cana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Just as a sleeping man does not indulge in enjoying pleasures, so also Devas do not accept shares in the Yajñas (in Dakṣiṇāyana).

## \|\| 1.272.10-11 \|\|

*anenaiva tu mānena mānavena dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*lakṣaiḥ saptadaśākhyaistu vatsarāṇāṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aṣṭāviṃśatsahasraistu vatsarāṇāṃ kṛtaṃ yugam \|*  
*tasmiñchveto'bhavadviṣṇurbhagavānyo jagadguruḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, calculating in this way, one million seven hundred twenty-eight thousand years according to human reckoning comprise Kṛtayuga. During that period Viṣṇu who is Jagadguru (the preceptor of the universe) appeared white.

## \|\| 1.272.12 \|\|

*lokāḥ pāpavinirmuktāḥ śāṃtā dāṃtā jitendriyāḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuṣastathā sarve sadaiva tapasi sthitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The people were bereft of sins. They were quiescent with full control over the limbs and the sense-organs fully conquered. All of them were long-lived and always engaged in austerities.

## \|\| 1.272.13 \|\|

*yo yathā janma cāpnoti tathā sa mriyate naraḥ \|*  
*na putrasaṃbhavo mṛtyurvīkṣyate janakaiḥ kvacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Just as a man takes birth so does he (normally) meet death. Seldom was the death of a son born seen by (their) fathers (i.e. son’s death was never seen by fathers).

## \|\| 1.272.14 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho daṃbho matsara eva ca \|*  
*na jāyate nṛṇāṃ tatra yuge tu dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lust, anger, covetousness, hypocrisy and rivalry were never seen in men in that Yuga, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.272.15 \|\|

*tatastretāyugaṃ bhāvi dvitīyaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*pādenaikena pāpaṃ tu raudraṃ dharme tadāviśat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then follows the second one, Tretāyuga, O excellent sages. Then the terrible sin entered Dharma with a single foot.

## \|\| 1.272.16 \|\|

*tato raktatvamabhyeti bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*pāpāṃśe'pi ca saṃprāpte sasparddho jāyate janaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Lord Madhusūdana turns red when a part of sin gets introduced, People become vitiated with jealousy and rivalry.

## \|\| 1.272.17 \|\|

*svargamārgakṛte sarve cakruryajñāṃstataḥ param \|*  
*agniṣṭomādikāṃstatra bahuhomādikāṃstathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. All people then performed Yajñas with the intention of proceeding to heaven. They performed Agniṣṭoma and many other Homas.

## \|\| 1.272.18 \|\|

*devalokāṃstato yāṃti mūlādyāvaccaturdaśa \|*  
*brahmalokasya paryaṃtaṃ svakīyairya jñakarmabhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By means of their holy rites such as yajña etc., they go to the fourteen worlds of Devas (and others) starting with the first and ending with Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.272.19 \|\|

*kiṃcitsvalpāyuṣastatra jāyante spardhayā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ tatrāpi no yāṃti mṛtyuṃ putrāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sons vitiated by rivalry, may be somewhat short-lived. But even so they never meet with death (before their fathers).

## \|\| 1.272.20 \|\|

*janake vidyamāne ca sva lpadoṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodhādayo ye ca bhavaṃti na bhavaṃti ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When father is alive (sons do not die). Lust, anger etc. may or may not occur but they are proclaimed to be of very slight defect.

## \|\| 1.272.21 \|\|

*ekayā velayā tatra vāpitaṃ sasyamuttamam \|*  
*saptavārānpragṛhṇaṃti vaiśyāḥ kṛṣiparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Seeds sown once yielded excellent crops. Vaiśyas engaged in agriculture reap the harvest seven times.

## \|\| 1.272.22 \|\|

*sarvā ghaṭasravā gāvo mahiṣyaśca caturguṇāḥ \|*  
*prayacchaṃti tathā kṣīramuṣṭryastāsāṃ caturguṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All cows yield potfuls of milk. She-buffaloes yield four times that. Female camels yield four times more than that of buffaloes.

## \|\| 1.272.23 \|\|

*ajāvikāstathā pādaṃ nāryaḥ sarvāstathaiva ca \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ pratigrahavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*śāpānugrahakṛtyeṣu samarthāḥ saṃbhavaṃti ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Goats and sheep yield one-fourth of the quantity (of cow’s yield). Women also are so. (People) were richly endowed with the study of Vedas. They avoid Pratigraha (money, gifts). They were capable of cursing and blessing.

## \|\| 1.272.24 \|\|

*kṣatriyāḥ kṣātradharmeṇa pālayaṃti vasuṃdharām \|*  
*na tatra dṛśyate cauro na ca jāraḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*svadharmaniratāḥ sarve varṇāścaiva vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kṣatriyas protected the earth with the Kṣātra Dharma (duties of a real Kṣatriya). No thief is seen and no adulterer can be seen. All the different castes were primarily engaged in their own duties.

## \|\| 1.272.25 \|\|

*tacca dvādaśabhirlakṣairvatsarāṇāṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*ṣaṇṇavatyā sahasraistu dvitīyaṃ yugamuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. This second excellent Yuga consisted of one million two hundred ninety-six thousand years.

## \|\| 1.272.26 \|\|

*tataśca dvāparaṃ bhāvi tṛtīyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*dvau pādau tatra pāpasya dvau ca dharmasya saṃsthitau \|*  
*bhagavānvāsudevaśca kapilastatra jāyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereafter, comes the third, Dvāpara Yuga, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. There the sin has two feet and Dharma (Piety) too, the same. Lord Vāsudeva is tawny-coloured then.

## \|\| 1.272.27 \|\|

*taccāṣṭalakṣamānena vatsarāṇāṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭibhiranyaistu sahasrāṇāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is proclaimed as comprising eight hundred sixty-four thousand years, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.272.28 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho daṃbho matsara eva ca \|*  
*ṣaḍete tatra jāyaṃte īrṣyā caiva tu saptamī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then lust, anger, delusion, covetousness, hypocrisy and rivalry—all these six bad qualities along with jealousy the seventh persist there.

## \|\| 1.272.29 \|\|

*atha saṃsevitāstaistu mānavāśca parasparam \|*  
*viruddhāṃśca prakurvaṃti nāpnuvaṃti yathā divam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Affected by these, human beings are antagonistic to one another and commit crimes. They do not attain heaven.

## \|\| 1.272.30 \|\|

*kecittatrāpi jāyaṃte śāṃtā dāṃtā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*na sarve'pi dvijaśreṣṭhā yato'rddhaṃ pātakasya tu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even there a few are, of course, born quiescent, having mastery over their limbs and conquest of their sense-organs. Not all of them (are so), O excellent Brāhmaṇas, because there is the prevalence of sin in half of the space.

## \|\| 1.272.31 \|\|

*tataḥ kaliyugaṃ proktaṃ caturthaṃ ca sudāruṇam \|*  
*ekapādo vṛṣo yatra pāpaṃ pādaistribhiḥ sthitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then Kaliyuga is mentioned (as commenced). It is the fourth one and excessively terrible. Piety stands on one foot there and sin is stationed with three feet.

## \|\| 1.272.32 \|\|

*kṛṣṇatvaṃ yāti devo'pi tatra caiva caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*eka pādo'pi dharmasya yāvattāvatpravartate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Four-armed Lord turns black then. Even the single-foot of piety functions only now and then.

## \|\| 1.272.33-40 \|\|

*paścānnāśaṃ samabhyeti yāvattāvacchanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ tasya nirdiṣṭaṃ lakṣāścatvāra eva hi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dvātriṃśacca sahasrāṇi yugasyaivāṃtimasya ca \|*  
*kalinā tatra saṃpṛṣṭā martyāḥ sarve parasparam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vibudhaiste pravartaṃte rāgadveṣaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*yasyayasya gṛhe vittaṃ tathā nāryo manoramāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tenatena samaṃ maitrīṃ kalau kurvaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*vidhavānāṃ yatīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ ca tapasvinām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*lokadvayavināśaḥ syādyataśceto na śudhyati \|*  
*prāvṛṭkāle'pi saṃprāpte durbhikṣeṇa prapīḍitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhramaṃti ca kalau lokā gaganāsaktadṛṣṭayaḥ \|*  
*jānāti cāpi tanayaḥ pitā cennidhanaṃ vrajet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tatohaṃ gṛhapo bhūyāṃ bāṃdhavo hyapi bāṃdhavam \|*  
*snuṣāpi vetti cittena yadi śvaśrūḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet \|\| 39 \|\|*

*mama syādgṛha aiśvaryaṃ tatsarvaṃ nānyathā vrajet \|*  
*kāvyairupahatā vedāḥ putrā jāmātṛkaistathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

33-34a. Afterwards it perishes itself slowly. The span of the final Yuga is stated to be four hundred thirty-two thousand years.

34b-35a. All human beings, influenced by Kali and overpowered by attachment and hatred behave so mutually and with learned people.

35b-37a. In Kaliyuga, people befriend any person who has got ample wealth in the house and beautiful wives.

In the case of widows and all the ascetics and sages both the worlds will be ruined if the mind is not pure.

37b-38a. In Kali Age, even in rainy season, people are afflicted by famine. They wander with their eyes fixed to the sky.

38b-39a. A son thinks thus: ‘If my father dies, I can become master of the house.’ A kinsman thinks about a kinsman thus.

39b-40a. A daughter-in-law thinks thus in her mind: ‘If mother-in-law dies, there shall be prosperity in the house; all the wealth shall remain with us; nothing will go elsewhere.’

40b. The Vedas are vitiated by the epics and secular poets. Sons are over-ruled by sons-in-law.

## \|\| 1.272.41 \|\|

*śālakairbāṃdhavāścaiva hyasatībhiḥ kulastriyaḥ \|*  
*śūdrāstapasvinaścaiva śūdrā dharmasya sūcakāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Kinsmen are over-ruled by brother-in-law. Ladies of noble birth are overwhelmed by unchaste ladies. Ascetics are afflicted by Śūdras. Śūdras become guides and directors of holy rites.

## \|\| 1.272.42 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ tataḥ śūdrā upadeśaṃ vadaṃti ca \|*  
*alpodakāstathā meghā alpasasyā ca medinī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Śūdras begin to give advices to Brāhmaṇas. Clouds shower only very little rain. The earth yields very little crop.

## \|\| 1.272.43 \|\|

*alpakṣīrāstathā gāvaḥ kṣīre sarpistathā'lpakam \|*  
*sarvabhakṣāstathā viprā nṛpā niṣkaruṇāstataḥ \|*  
*kṛṣyā lajjaṃti vaiśyāśca śūdrā brāhmaṇapreṣakāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Cows produce very little milk. Ghee (and fat-content) is but very little in milk. Brāhmaṇas eat everything indiscriminately. Kings are cruel. Vaiśyas are ashamed of agriculture. Śūdras become persons who make Brāhmaṇas run errands.

## \|\| 1.272.44 \|\|

*hetuvādaratā ye ca bhaṃḍaṃvidyāparāśca ye \|*  
*tete syurbhūmipālasya sadā'bhīṣṭāḥ kalau yuge \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In Kaliyuga, kings very much like people who are engaged in disputations and obscene conversations.

## \|\| 1.272.45 \|\|

*śvaḥśvaḥpāpīyadivasāḥ pṛthivī gatayauvanā \|*  
*atikrāṃta śubhāḥ kālāḥ paryupasthitadāruṇāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Every tomorrow finds more and more sins. The earth has lost its youthful state. Auspiciousness has receded and terrible things have arrived.

## \|\| 1.272.46 \|\|

*yathāyathā yugaṃ bhāvi vṛddhiṃ yāṃti striyo narāḥ \|*  
*tathātathā prayāṃti sma laghutāṃ jaṃtubhiḥ saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. As the Yuga advances and men and women grow in number they along with the ordinary creatures, become more and more despicable.

## \|\| 1.272.47 \|\|

*dvādaśame caiva kanyā syādbhartṛsaṃyutā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Girls begin to be united with husbands (i.e. married) in their twelfth year.

## \|\| 1.272.48 \|\|

*tataḥ ṣoḍaśame varṣe narāḥ palitayauvanāḥ \|*  
*śaucācāraparityaktā nijakāryaparāstathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In their sixteenth year, men become grey-haired with receding youthful period. They abandon personal cleanliness and purity of conduct. They are devoted to selfish ends.

## \|\| 1.272.49 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃti yugasyāṃte narāḥ aṃguṣṭhamātrakāḥ \|*  
*gṛhaṃ ca te'tha kurvaṃti bilairākhusamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. By the end of the Yuga, men will be reduced to the size of only the thumb. They will set up their abodes in rat-holes.

## \|\| 1.272.50 \|\|

*tathā prāvaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ kṛmivastraṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ekavarṇā bhaviṣyaṃti varṇāḥ sarve tataḥ paraḥ \|*  
*mlechībhūtā durācārā dharmakṛtyavidūṣakāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They will wear garments (of stuff) produced by worms. All the castes will be reduced into one caste. All will become barbarians, evil in conduct and defilers of pious rites.

## \|\| 1.272.51 \|\|

*evaṃ jāte tato loke brāhmaṇo haripiṃgalaḥ \|*  
*kalkigotrasamutpannastānsarvā nsūdayettataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When the situation turns out to be thus, a Brāhmaṇa Haripiṅgala of Kalki Gotra will kill all.

## \|\| 1.272.52 \|\|

*paścātkṛtayugaṃ bhāvi bhūyo'pi dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Afterwards, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Kṛtayuga will appear once again.

## \|\| 1.272.53 \|\|

*evaṃ yugasahasreṇa saṃprāptena tataḥ param \|*  
*brahmaṇo divasaṃ bhāvi rātriścaiva tataḥ param \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A day of Brahmā will comprise one thousand such Yugas. A night (of the same duration) follows then.

## \|\| 1.272.54 \|\|

*tataścānena mānena ṣaṣṭyā yuktaistribhiḥ śataiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇo vatsaraṃ bhāvi keśavasya ca taddinam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. According to this reckoning, three hundred sixty days of Brahmā make his year which is equal to one day of Keśava.

## \|\| 1.272.55 \|\|

*ātmīye jīvite brahma yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*keśavo'pi svamānena varṣāṇāṃ jīvite śatam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Brahmā lives a full life-span of one hundred years according to his own reckoning, Keśava also lives a hundred years according to his own reckoning.

## \|\| 1.272.56 \|\|

*varṣeṇa vāsudevasya dinaṃ māheśvaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*nijamānena sopyatra yāva dvarṣaśataṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A year of Vāsudeva constitutes a day of Maheśvara. He will also live a hundred years according to his own reckoning.

## \|\| 1.272.57 \|\|

*tataḥ śaktisvarūpaḥ syātso'kṣayī kīrtyate yataḥ \|*  
*sadāśivasya niḥśvāsaḥ śaivaṃ varṣaśataṃ bhavet \|*  
*ucchvāsastu punastasya śaktirūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then he will merge into Śakti form whereby he is glorified as Akṣayī (everlasting). A hundred years of Śiva constitute the Niḥśvāsa (inspiration) of Sadāśiva. His Ucchvāsa (respiration) remains in the form of Śakti.

## \|\| 1.272.58-59 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ śivaśaktisamudbhavam \|*  
*yāvadāyuḥ pramāṇaṃ ca mānuṣāḍhyaṃ ca yadbhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

*bhavadbhiḥ śāṃkaraṃ pṛṣṭo dvijā asmi dinaṃ purā \|*  
*mayā punastu sarveṣāṃ martyādīnāṃ tu kīrtitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

Sūta said:

58-59. Thus everything connected with Śiva and Śakti has been narrated to you and also the extent of human life. Earlier, O Brāhmaṇas, I was asked by you all about one day of Śaṅkara. But I have explained the same in regard to all including that of the mortals (human beings).

## Chapter 273 - Reckoning of Yugas

## \|\| 1.273.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*eteṣāṃ tu sahasreṇa bhavedgrāhyaṃ dinaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*caturdaśa sahasrākṣā jāyaṃte tatra vāsare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saptamastu sahasrākṣaḥ sāṃprataṃ vartate'tra yaḥ \|*  
*ekasaptatisaṃvartacaturdaśadine vidheḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yugānāṃ kurute rājyaṃ manavaśca tathā pare \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvaprabhṛtayo yathā śakrāstathā sthitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. O Brāhmāṇas, a thousand Caturyugas (group of four Yugas) constitute one day of Brahmā. In that single day fourteen Thousand-eyed Ones (Indras) are born. The present Indra is the seventh one. In one day of Vidhi (Brahmā), there are fourteen units of seventy-one Saṃvartas (Caturyugas). One Śakra reigns supreme for a period of seventy-one Caturyugas. So also in the case of Manus beginning with Svāyaṃbhuva. These Manus and Śakras rule in the same way.

## \|\| 1.273.4-5 \|\|

*jāyanto nāma śakro'yaṃ sāṃprataṃ vartate tu yaḥ \|*  
*vaivasvato manuścaiva aṣṭāviṃśatpramāṇakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caturyugasya saṃjāto gatesmiñcheṣamātrake \|*  
*bhaviṣyati baliḥ śakro vāsudevaprasādataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The Śakra who rules now is called Jayanta and the Manu is Vaivasvata Manu. In his reign, twenty-eighth unit of Caturyugas runs now (27 elapsed. 28th is current). When the present Śakra passes away, Bali will become Śakra with the favour of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.273.6 \|\|

*tena tasya pratijñātaṃ rājyaṃ caivāṣṭame manau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He had promised this kingdom to Bali in the reign of the eighth Manu.

## \|\| 1.273.7 \|\|

*evaṃ sarve surāścānye trayastriṃśatpramāṇataḥ \|\| \|*  
*koṭayaḥ prabhaviṣyaṃti yathā caiva tathā purā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The same is the case of all other Suras. They are thirty-three crores in number. They remain in the same way as was in the earlier periods.

## \|\| 1.273.8 \|\|

*yo'yaṃ brahmā sthito viprāḥ sāṃprataṃ sṛṣṭikārakaḥ \|*  
*tasyānena pramāṇena jātaṃ saṃvatsarāṣṭakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Eight years have gone by, O Brāhmaṇas, in the case of. the Brahmā who is the present creator and those too according to his own reckoning.

## \|\| 1.273.9 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsāśca dinārdhaṃ ca prathamaṃ śuklapūrvakam \|*  
*saurasāvanacaṃdrārkṣairmānairebhiścaturvidhaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. So also six months, one Pakṣa (i.e. Śukla, the bright fortnight) and half a day have also gone by.

The calculation of Saṃvatsara (year) is of four types based on Saura, Sāvana, Cāndra and Ārkṣa (Nakṣatra) reckoning.

## \|\| 1.273.10 \|\|

*kalau niryāti sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ kṣitimaṇḍale \|*  
*paṃcaṣaṣṭyā'dhikaiścaiva dinānāṃ ca śataistribhiḥ \|*  
*bhavetsaṃvatsaraṃ sauraṃ pañconaistaiśca sāvanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In Kaliyuga all the living beings in the region of the earth pass away. The Saura (Solar) Saṃvatsara consists of three hundred sixty-five days. If it is less by five it is the Sāvana year (i.e. 360 days).

## \|\| 1.273.11 \|\|

*cāṃdra ekādaśonastu triṃśaddhīna uḍūdbhavaḥ \|*  
*śītātapau tathā vṛṣṭiḥ sauramānena jāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Cāndra (lunar) Saṃvatsara is less by eleven days (354 days) and the Uḍūdbhava (Stellar) is less by thirty days (335 days).

The coolness of winter, the heat of summer, and the rainfall are based on Saura reckoning.

## \|\| 1.273.12-14 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṇāṃ phalaniṣpattiḥ sasyānāṃ ca tathā parā \|*  
*agniṣṭomādayo yajñā vartaṃte ye dharātale \|\| 12 \|\|*

*utsāhāśca vivāhāśca sāvanena bhavaṃti ca \|*  
*kusīdādyāśca ye kecidvyavahārāśca vṛttijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*adhimāsaprayuktena te syuścāṃdreṇa nirmitāḥ \|*  
*nākṣatreṇa tu mānena sidhyaṃte grahacārikāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The outcome of fruits on trees, the harvesting stage of the plants, Agniṣṭoma and other Yajñas that are being conducted on the earth, festivals and marriages are based on the Sāvana reckoning.

Calculation of interests and dealings of professional activities are based on Cāndra reckoning with the intercalary month taken into consideration.

The movements of the planets are calculated on the basis of the Nakṣatra (or Ārkṣa-stellar) reckoning.

## \|\| 1.273.15-17 \|\|

*nānyatkiṃciddharāpṛṣṭha etanmānacatuṣṭayāt \|*  
*etena tu pramāṇena devadaityāśca mānavāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*varttaṃte brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ śrutireṣā purātanī \|*  
*etadyugapramāṇaṃ tu yaḥ paṭhedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*eteṣāmeva liṃgānāṃ saptānāṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*nāpamṛtyu bhayaṃ tasya kathaṃcitsaṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Beyond these four types of reckoning there is no other type of calculation in the whole of the world. O excellent Brāhmaṇas. Devas, Daityas and human beings accept these reckonings. This is the eternal dictum of the Śruti.

If, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, anyone reads with devotion the extent of the Yugas before these seven Liṅgas, he will never have the fear of premature or accidental death.

## Chapter 274 - Origin of Duḥśīleśvara (Duḥśīla-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.274.1-3 \|\|

*\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānyadapi tatrāsti durvāsaḥsthāpitaṃ purā \|*  
*talliṃgaṃ devadevasya trinetrasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*caitramāsi naro yastu tamārādhayate dvijāḥ \|*  
*nṛtyagītapravādyaiśca trikālaṃ vihitakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sa nūnaṃ tatprasādena gandharvādhipatirbhavet 1 \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*durvāsā nāmakaścāyaṃ kenāyaṃ sthāpito haraḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle mahābhāga sarvaṃ no vistarādvada \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. There is another Liṅga installed earlier by Durvāṣas. It is the Liṅga of the three-eyed, noble-souled Lord of Devas.

O Brāhmaṇas, a person who in the month of Caitra undertakes to propitiate it (the Liṅga) with dancing, vocal and Instrumental music thrice a day, will be the king of Gandharvas with his favour.

## \|\| 1.274.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsītpurā niṃbaśuco vaidiśe ca purottame \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

Who is this sage named Durvāsas? By whom was Hara installed? O highly esteemed one, at what time was it installed? Mention everything in detail.

Sūta said:

4\. Formerly, there was one Niṃbaśuca in the excellent city Vaidiśa.

## \|\| 1.274.5-7 \|\|

*sa ca pūjayate liṃgaṃ kiṃcinmaṭhapatiḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sa yatkiṃcidavāpnoti vastrādyaṃ ca tathā param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*māheśvarasya lokasya vikrīṇīte tatastataḥ \|*  
*tato gṛhṇāti nityaṃ sa hema mūlyena tasya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na karoti vyayaṃ tasya kevalaṃ saṃcaye rataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kālena mahatā maṃjūṣā'sya nirargalā \|*  
*jātā hemamayī viprāḥ kārpaṇyaniratasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. He was the head of a Maṭha and he worshipped a certain Liṅga. Whatever he got like clothes etc., he used to sell to devotees of Maheśvara. As the cost of those things, he used to take gold from those people. He never spent anything. He was engaged only in hoarding. After a long time, his cash-box became profusely filled with gold. O Brāhmaṇas, you know, he won very miserly.

## \|\| 1.274.8 \|\|

*atha saṃsthāpya bhūmadhye maṃjūṣāṃ tāṃ prapūritām \|*  
*karoti vyavahāraṃ sa kakṣāṃ tāṃ naiva muṃcati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He placed the cash-box under the ground and went on with his trading activities. He never left the room.

## \|\| 1.274.9 \|\|

*kadāciddevapūjāyāṃ so'pi brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*viśvāsaṃ naiva niryāti kasyacicca kathaṃcana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, even for the worship of the Lord, he never trusted anyone. Nor did he leave his room.

## \|\| 1.274.10 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya paravittāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*alakṣadbrāhmaṇastacca duḥśīlākhyo vyaciṃtayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In course of time, a Brāhmaṇa called Duśśīla who robbed others of their wealth, noticed that treasure, He thought:

## \|\| 1.274.11-13 \|\|

*tataḥ śiṣyo bhaviṣyāmi viśvāsārthaṃ durātmanaḥ \|*  
*sudīnaiḥ kṛpaṇairvākyaiścāṭukāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ālasyaṃ ca divānaktaṃ sādhayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|*  
*anyasminnahani prāpte dṛṣṭvā taṃ maṭhamadhyagam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tataḥ samīpamagamaddaṃḍākāraṃ praṇamya ca \|*  
*abravītprāṃjalirbhūtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. ‘To gain the confidence of this wicked-minded one, I shall become his disciple. With piteous utterances and flattering remarks of various kinds continuously spoken day and night, I shall contrive to make him idle.’

## \|\| 1.274.14-19 \|\|

*bhagavaṃste prabhāvo'dya tapasā vai mayā śrutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yadanyastāpaso nāsti īdṛśo'tra dharātale \|*  
*tenāhaṃ dūrataḥ prāpto vairāgyeṇa samanvitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*saṃsārāsāratāṃ jñātvā janmamṛtyujarātmikām \|*  
*arthātsvapnapratīkāśaṃ yauvanaṃ ca nṛṇā miha \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yadvatparvatasaṃjātā nadī ca kṣaṇabhaṃgurā \|*  
*putrāḥ kalatrāṇi ca vā ye cānye bāṃdhavādayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*te sarve ca parijñeyā yathā pāpa samāgamāḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃsārasamudrasya tāraṇārthaṃ bravīhi me \|\| 18 \|\|*

*upāyaṃ kaṃcidadyaiva upadeśe vyavasthitam \|*  
*tarāmi yena saṃsāraṃ prasādāttava suvrata \|\| 19 \|\|*

One day, he saw him seated in the middle of his Maṭha. He approached him and prostrated before him. With palms joined in reverence, he stood humbly and said:

14-19. “O holy Sir, today your power of penance was heard by me. In the whole of the world, there is no other sage like you; hence I have come here from a far-off place, because I am prompted by Vairāgya (absence of attachment to worldly pleasures).

I have realized that the worldly existence is worthless. What is it but a series of births, deaths and old age! It means that youthful days of men are nothing but evanescent dreams just like a river which originates from a great mountain. It is not permanent. Its power is momentary.

Sons, wives and other kinsmen—all these should be known as associations of sinful ones. Hence tell me something for the purpose of crossing the ocean of worldly existence.

Mention today some means of crossing this vast ocean; which is well founded in instructions, so that, O Brāhmaṇa of excellent holy rites, I can cross the sea of worldly entanglement with your favour.”

## \|\| 1.274.20 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā romāṃcita tanūruhaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā māheśvaraḥ ko'yaṃ ciṃtāvānsamupasthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing his words, he (i.e. Niṃbaśuca) became glad and experienced horripilation all over his body. He thought: ‘Who may be this devotee of Maheśvara perpetually engaged in meditation who has come to me?’ (and then said:)

## \|\| 1.274.21 \|\|

*yathā bravīṣi dhanyo'si yasya te matirīdṛśī \|*  
*tāruṇye vartamānasya sukumārasya caiva hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “From what you say, it is evident that you are very blessed. Your intellect is such a fine one though you are still very young and so tender!

## \|\| 1.274.22 \|\|

*tāruṇye vartamāno yaḥ śāṃtaḥ so'tra nigadyate \|*  
*dhātuṣu kṣīyamāṇeṣu śamaḥ kasya na jāyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If a person, in the prime of youth is calm and quiescent, he is to be really called a tranquil man. Who does not attain tranquillity when the primary secretions of the body become feeble?

## \|\| 1.274.23 \|\|

*yadyevaṃ suviraktiḥ syātsaṃsāropari saṃsthitā \|*  
*samārādhaya deveśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaśiśekharam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If you have such a strong detachment with worldly pleasures, do propitiate Śaṅkara, the moon-crested Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.274.24 \|\|

*nānyathā ghorajāpyena tīryate bhavasāgaraḥ \|*  
*mayā samyakparijñātametacchāstrasamāgamāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The ocean of worldly existence cannot be crossed otherwise, even through Japa of severe sort is resorted to. This has been well understood by me through my contact with (meditation and study of) scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.274.25-26 \|\|

*śūdro vā yadi vā vipro mlecho vā pāpakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*śivadīkṣāsamopetaḥ puṣpamekaṃ tu yo nyasait \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ṣaḍakṣareṇa maṃtreṇa liṃgasyopari bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa tāṃ gatimavāpnoti yāṃyāṃ yāṃtīha yajvinaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. One may be a Śūdra or a Brāhmaṇa, a barbarian or a sinner. If he gets initiated in Śivadīkṣā (Śaiva cult) and places a flower devoutly on the top of the Liṅga while reciting the six-syllabled Mantra, he attains that goal which even the performers of Yajñas do not attain.

## \|\| 1.274.27 \|\|

*yo dadāti prabhaktyā ca śivadīkṣānvitāya ca \|*  
*vastropānahakaupīnaṃ sa yajñaiḥ kiṃ kariṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If a man makes the gift of a garment, shoe or underwear devoutly to one endowed with Śivadīkṣā initiation, what has he to do with Yajñas?”

## \|\| 1.274.28 \|\|

*tacchrutvā caraṇau tasya duḥśīlo'sau tadā'dade \|*  
*vinyasya svaśira stābhyāṃ tatovākyamuvāca ha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing these words, Duḥśīla placed his head on his feet which he grasped firmly and uttered these words:

## \|\| 1.274.29 \|\|

*śivadīkṣāpramāṇena prasādaṃ kuru me prabho \|*  
*śuśrūṣāṃ yena te nityaṃ prakaromi samāhitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O holy Lord, do me this favour of granting Śivadīkṣā, so that with great concentration, I can serve you everyday.”

## \|\| 1.274.30-32 \|\|

*tato'sau tāpaso viprāściṃtayāmāsa cetami \|*  
*dakṣo'yaṃ dṛśyate ko'pi pumāṃścaiva samāgataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mamāsti nāparaḥ śiṣyastasmādenaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*tato'bravītkare gṛhya yadyevaṃ vatsa me samam \|*  
*samayaṃ kuru yena tvāṃ dīkṣayāmyadya caiva hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tvayā kuṭīrakaṃ kāryaṃ maṭhasyāsya vidūrataḥ \|*  
*praveśo naiva kāryastu mamātrāstaṃ gate ravau \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-31a. Thereupon, O Brāhmaṇas, this ascetic thought in his mind: ‘Some extraordinary man has come here. He appears to be very brilliant. I have no other disciple. Hence, I shall make him my pupil.’

3lb-32. Then he caught hold of his hands and said: “If it is so, O dear one, enter into an agreement with me so that I can initiate you today itself. You should build your hut very far away from this Maṭha. Once the sun sets you should never enter this place.”

## \|\| 1.274.33 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*tavādeśaḥ pramāṇaṃ me kevalaṃ tāpasottama \|*  
*kiṃ maṭhena kariṣyāmi viśeṣādrā trisaṃgame \|\| 33 \|\|*

Duḥśīla said:

33\. O excellent one among ascetics, your command is authoritative to me. What shall I do with the Maṭha especially after nightfall?

## \|\| 1.274.34 \|\|

*yaḥ śiṣyo guruvākyaṃ tu na karoti yathoditam \|*  
*tasya vrataṃ ca tadvyarthaṃ narakaṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If a disciple does not carry out the behest of the preceptor precisely as it is uttered, his holy vow (Vrata) is futile. Thereafter, he has to fall into Naraka.

## \|\| 1.274.35 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tuṣṭimāpannaḥ śivadīkṣāṃ tato dadau \|*  
*tasmai vinayayuktāya tadā niṃbaśuco muniḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing those words, Niṃbaśuca, the sage, became pleased. He duly granted the initiation to that man who (appeared to be) endowed with humility.

## \|\| 1.274.36 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti so'tīva tasya śuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ \|\| \|*  
*raṃjayāmāsa taccittaṃ paricaryāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Ever since then, he engaged himself in serving him and charmed his mind with his eagerness for service.

## \|\| 1.274.37 \|\|

*manasā cintayānastu tanmātrārthaṃ dinedine \|*  
*na cchidraṃ vīkṣate kiṃcidvīkṣamāṇo'pi yatnataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. But he mentally pondered over his sole objective day by day. Though he watched very carefully, he could not see any loophole.

## \|\| 1.274.38 \|\|

*śaivo'pi ca sa kakṣyāṃ tāṃ tāṃ mātrāṃ hemasaṃbhavām \|*  
*kathaṃcinmokṣate bhūmau bhojye devārcane'pi na \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The devotee of Śiva (i.e. Niṃbaśuca) never left that room nor the cash-box filled with gold to the brim even at the time of taking food or worshipping the Lord.

## \|\| 1.274.39-42 \|\|

*tato'sau cintayāmāsa duḥśīlo nijacetasi \|*  
*maṭhe tāvatpraveśo'sti naiva rātrau kathaṃcana \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sūryāstamānavelāyāṃ yatprayacchati tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*parighaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ pāpastatkaromi ca kiṃ punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*maṭho'yaṃ suśilābaddho naiva khātaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*tuṃgatvānna praveśaḥ syādupāyairvividhaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tatkiṃ viṣaṃ prayacchāmi śastrairvyāpādayāmi kim \|*  
*divāpi paśumāreṇa paṃcatvaṃ vā nayāmi kim \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. Then Duḥśīla thought thus in his mind: ‘I have no access to the Maṭha at all during the night. At sunset the sinful fellow bolts it firmly in an instant. What can I do then?

This Maṭha is built with excellent stones. There is no question of digging it up. Since it is very tall, other means too will not facilitate entry.

Hence shall I administer poison to him or kill him with weapons? Shall I even during the day cause his death like that of an animal beaten to death?’

## \|\| 1.274.43-45 \|\|

*evaṃ cintayatastasya prāvṛṭkāla upasthitaḥ \|*  
*śrāvaṇasyāsite pakṣe karkaṭasthe divākare \|\| 43 \|\|*

*prāpto maheśvarastasya ko'pi tatra dhanī drutam \|*  
*tenoktaṃ praṇipatyoccaiḥ kariṣyāmi pavitrakam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*caturddaśyāmahaṃ svāminyadyādeśo bhavettava \|*  
*yadyāgacchasi me grāmaṃ prasādena sama nvitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Even as he continued to ponder thus, rainy season set in. It was the dark half of Śrāvaṇa. The sun was in Cancer. A devotee of Maheśvara, a rich man, came there in a hurry, bowed to him and loudly announced thus: “I will perform a holy rite on the fourteenth day, O Lord, if you grant me permission and come to my village gracing it with your benign presence.”

## \|\| 1.274.46 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā tuṣṭimāpannastato niṃbaśuco muniḥ \|*  
*tatheti caivamuktvā taṃ preṣayāmāsa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

Sūta said:

46\. On hearing it, sage Niṃbaśuca became glad. Saying “So it shall be”, he immediately sent him back.

## \|\| 1.274.47 \|\|

*āgamiṣyāmyahaṃ kāle svaśiṣyeṇa samanvitaḥ \|*  
*kariṣyāmi paraṃ śreyastava vatsa na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “I shall come at the proper time accompanied by my pupil. I shall do something very beneficial to you, O dear one, there is no doubt about it.”

## \|\| 1.274.48 \|\|

*atha kāle tu saṃprāpte cintayitvā prabhātikam \|*  
*prabhātasamaye prāpte sa śaivaḥ prasthitastadā \|*  
*duḥśīlena samāyuktaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When the stipulated time arrived, the devotee of Siva finished his morning routine and started in the morning itself accompanied by Duḥśīla. Throughout he experienced a great thrill with hair standing on their ends.

## \|\| 1.274.49 \|\|

*tato vai gacchamānasya tasya mārge vyavasthitā \|*  
*puṇyā nadī suvikhyātā muralā sāgaraṃgamā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. As he proceeded along his path, he came to the sacred river that falls into the sea. It was the well-known Muralā (Narmadā—De, p.134).

## \|\| 1.274.50 \|\|

*sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā'bravīdvākyaṃ vatsa śiṣya karomyaham \|*  
*bhavatā saha devārcāṃ muralāyāṃ sthiro bhava \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On seeing the river, he said these words: “Dear disciple, I shall in your company, perform the adoration of the Lord in Muralā itself. Be ready.”

## \|\| 1.274.51-53 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā saṃsthito'syāstaṭe śubhe \|*  
*so'pi niṃbaśucastasya raṃjitaḥ sarvadā guṇaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*suśiṣyaṃ taṃ parijñāya viśvāsaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sthagitāṃ tāṃ samādāya hemamātrāsamudbhavām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*jāgeśvarasamopetāṃ sa kanthāṃ vyākṣipatkṣitau \|*  
*purīṣotsargakāryeṇa tatastokāṃtaraṃ gataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. “Of course”, he said and stayed behind on the excellent banks of the river. As for Niṃbaśuca, he had already been favourably impressed by his good qualities. He thought him an excellent disciple and fully confided in him. He took the rags wherein the cash-box had been wrapped up and concealed along with Jāgeśvara Liṅga. He threw it down and went a short distance for the purpose of evacuating his bowels.

## \|\| 1.274.54 \|\|

*yāvaccādarśanaṃ prāpto vetasaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*tāvanmātrāṃ samādāya duḥśīlaḥ prasthito drutam \|*  
*uttarāṃ diśamāśritya prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When he went out of sight behind a thicket surrounded by canes, Duḥśīla took up the cash-box and set off quickly towards the northern side. He was extremely pleased with himself.

## \|\| 1.274.55 \|\|

*athāsau cāgato yāvadduḥśīlaṃ naiva paśyati \|*  
*kevalaṃ dṛśyate kanthā jāgeśvarasamanvitā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. When he (Niṃbaśuca) returned he could not see Duḥśīla. Only the rag was seen with the Jāgeśvara Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.274.56 \|\|

*tataḥ śīghrataraṃ śaucaṃ kiñcitkṛtvā sudurmanāḥ \|*  
*vinaivācamanaṃ prāptaḥ sā kanthā yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He washed himself quickly and slightly. Uneasy in mind he did not perform the rite of Ācamana (ritualistic rinsing of the mouth) and returned to the place where the rag had been left.

## \|\| 1.274.57 \|\|

*yāvanmātrāvihīnāṃ ca tato jñātvā ca tāṃ hṛtām \|*  
*tena śiṣyeṇa mūrcchāḍhyo nipapāta mahītale \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. When he found out that the cash-box with his collection had been taken away by the disciple, he fell on the ground in swoon,

## \|\| 1.274.58 \|\|

*tataśca cetanāṃ prāpya kṛcchrāccotthāya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*śilāyāṃ tāḍayāmāsa nijāṃgāni śirastathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After regaining consciousness, he rose up with great difficulty and beat his limbs and head against the rock.

## \|\| 1.274.59 \|\|

*hā hato'smi vinaṣṭo'smi muṣṭastena durātmanā \|*  
*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ taṃ vīkṣayāmyaham \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. (He lamented:) “Alas, I am ruined! I am duped! I have been robbed by that evil-minded rogue. What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I see him?”

## \|\| 1.274.60 \|\|

*tatastu padavīṃ vīkṣya tasya tāṃ calito dhruvam \|*  
*vṛddha bhāvātpariśrāṃto vāvṛtya sa maṭhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On seeing his footprints he followed briskly but due to his old age he became tired. Hence he returned to his Maṭha.

## \|\| 1.274.61 \|\|

*duḥśīlo'pi samādāya mātrāṃ sthānāṃtaraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tatastena suvarṇena vyavahārānkaroti saḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Taking the cash-box Duḥśīla went to another place and practised trading activities with the gold he took.

## \|\| 1.274.62 \|\|

*tato gṛhasthatāṃ prāptaḥ kṛtadāraparigrahaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhabhāvaṃ samāpannaḥ saṃtānena vivarjitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He took a wife and had a life of a householder. He grew into an old man without any child.

## \|\| 1.274.63 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya tīrthayātrāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā sahito vipraścamatkārapuraṃ gataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Once, accompanied by his wife, the Brāhmaṇa went to Camatkārapura with a great interest in pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.274.64 \|\|

*snātvā tīrtheṣu sarveṣu devatāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*bhramamāṇena saṃdṛṣṭo durvāsā nāma sanmuniḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He wandered visiting all the shrines and taking his holy bath in all the Tīrthas. The excellent sage named Durvāsas was seen by him.

## \|\| 1.274.65 \|\|

*nijadevasya sadbhaktyā nṛtyagītaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā namaskṛtya vākyametaduvāca saḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. With great devotion, he was engaged in dancing and singing in front of his deity. On seeing him the Brāhmaṇa bowed down and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.274.66 \|\|

*kenaitatsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ nirmalaṃ śaṃkarodbhavam \|*  
*kiṃ tvaṃ nṛtyasi gītaṃ ca puro'sya prakaroṣi ca \|*  
*munīnāṃ yujyate naiva yadetattava ceṣṭitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. “By whom was this pure Liṅga of Śaṅkara installed? Why do you dance before it and indulge in singing? What you are doing does not befit sages.”

## \|\| 1.274.67 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*mayaitatsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*nṛtyagītapriyo yasmāddevadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

67\. It was by me that this Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas was installed. (I dance and sing) because Maheśvara is fond of dancing and singing.

## \|\| 1.274.68 \|\|

*na me'sti vibhavaḥ kaścidyena bhogaṃ karomyaham \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I do not have sufficient assets to make a befitting food offering to the idol.

## \|\| 1.274.69 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptaścirbhaṭirnāma yogavit \|*  
*tena pṛṣṭaḥ sa durvāsā vedāṃtikamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. In the meantime, a saint practising Yoga came there. His name was Cirbhaṭi. Durvāsas was asked the following Vedāntic passage.

## \|\| 1.274.70 \|\|

*asūryā nāma te lokā aṃdhena tamasā vṛtāḥ \|*  
*tāṃste pretyā'bhigacchaṃti ye kecātmahano janāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “Those worlds are devoid of the Sun. They are enveloped in blinding darkness. Those people who murder their own souls go over to them after death.”

## \|\| 1.274.71 \|\|

*upaviśya tatastena tasya dattastu nirṇayaḥ \|*  
*duḥśīlenāpi tatsarva vijñātaṃ tasya saṃstutam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He then sat down and then clarified the passage. What he narrated was understood by Duḥśīla too.

## \|\| 1.274.72 \|\|

*tato viśeṣato jātā bhaktistasya haraṃ prati \|*  
*taṃ praṇamya tataścoccairvākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereupon, he got a deeper devotion for Hara generated in him. Bowing down to the Lord (i.e. Durvāsas) he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.274.73-74 \|\|

*bhagavan brāhmaṇo'smīti jātyā caiva na karmaṇā \|*  
*na kasyacinmayā dattaṃ kadācinnaiva bhojanam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*kevalaṃ devaviprāṇāṃ vaṃcayitvā dhanaṃ hṛtam \|*  
*vyasanenābhibhūtena dyūtaveśyodbhavena ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. “O holy Sir, I am a Brāhmaṇa only by birth and not by my activities. Never have I given anyone any food to eat. Only through deceptive means, I have amassed a great deal of wealth of the deities and Brāhmaṇas, I am overcome by indulgence in vices such as dice (gambling) and harlots.

## \|\| 1.274.75 \|\|

*tathā ca brāhmaṇenāpi mayā śaivo guruḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*vaṃcitaśca tathānekaiścāṭubhirvihṛtaṃ dhanam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Though I am a Brāhmaṇa, I made a devotee of Śiva my preceptor. With many flattering remarks, he was deceived by me and his hoarded cash was looted.

## \|\| 1.274.76 \|\|

*tasya saktaṃ dhanaṃ bhūyaḥ sādhumārgeṇa cāhṛtam \|*  
*sa cāpi ca gururmahyaṃ paralokamihāgataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The money thus looted was employed in legitimate means and made to increase. But that preceptor of mine has moved to the other world.

## \|\| 1.274.77 \|\|

*paścāttāpena tenaiva pradahyāmi divāniśam \|*  
*puraścaraṇadānena tatprasādaṃ kuruṣva me \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. With this repentance I get scorched day and night. I wish to perform the rite of Puraścaraṇa and give away the wealth in charity. Hence do me this favour.

## \|\| 1.274.78 \|\|

*asti me vipulaṃ vittaṃ na saṃtānaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*tanme vada mune śreyastadvittasya yathā bhavet \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva yena sarvaṃ karomyaham \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. I have ample wealth, O leading sage, but no child. Hence, O sage, tell me how to make use of that wealth as means of sacred welfare both here and hereafter. I shall do everything accordingly.”

## \|\| 1.274.79 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*kṛtvā pāpasahasrāṇi paścāddharmaparo bhavet \|*  
*yaḥ pumānso'tikṛcchreṇa taretsaṃsārasāgaram \|\| 79 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

79\. After committing thousands of sins, one who becomes devoted to piety thereafter can cross the ocean of worldly existence (though) with great difficulty.

## \|\| 1.274.80 \|\|

*dinenāpi gururyo'sau tvayā śaivo vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*adharmeṇāpi saṃjātaḥ sa gurustena saṃśayaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. You adopted a Śaiva as your preceptor in (early) days. Thereby the Guru (preceptor) has become so even unrighteously. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.274.81 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo brahmacārī syādgrahasthastadanaṃtaram \|*  
*vānaprastho yatiścaiva tata ścaiva kuṭīcaraḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. A Brāhmaṇa shall first become a celibate religious student, then a householder, thereafter a Vānaprastha (forest hermit) and a recluse, then a Kuṭīcara (one dwelling in a hut).

## \|\| 1.274.82 \|\|

*bahūdakastato haṃsaḥ paramaśca tato bhavet \|*  
*tataśca muktimāyāti mārgamenaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Then, he becomes a Bahūdaka (one who bathes in many rivers), Thereafter a Haṃsa and ultimately Paramahaṃsa. Then he attains salvation by resorting to this path.

## \|\| 1.274.83 \|\|

*tvayā punaḥ kumārgeṇa yadvrataṃ brāhmaṇena ca \|*  
*śaivamārgaṃ samāsthāya tanmahāpātakaṃ kṛtam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. But you have followed a wrong path because though a Brāhmaṇa you adopted the path of a Śaiva, Thus a great sin has been committed.

## \|\| 1.274.84 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*sarveṣveva hi vedeṣu rudraḥ saṃkīrtyate prabhuḥ \|*  
*tatkiṃ doṣastvayā proktastasya dīkṣāsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

Duḥśīla said:

84\. In all the Vedas, Rudra is glorified as the supreme Lord. Why then have you pointed out a defect in regard to his initiation (into Śaivism)?

## \|\| 1.274.85 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*satyametattvayā khyātaṃ vede rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*bahudhā vāsudevo'pi brahmā caiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

85\. It is the truth that has been mentioned by you that Rudra is glorified in the Veda. Vāsudeva too is glorified on many occasions and Brahmā also with special emphasis.

## \|\| 1.274.86-88 \|\|

*paraṃ viprasya yā dīkṣā vratavaṃdhasamudbhavā \|*  
*gāyatrī paramā jāpye gururvrataparo hi saḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavīṃ cātha śaivīṃ ca yo'nyāṃ dīkṣāṃ samācaret \|\| 86 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇo na bhavetso'tra yadyapi syātṣaḍaṃgavit \|*  
*aparaṃ liṃgabhedaste saṃjātaḥ kapaṭādiṣu \|\| 87 \|\|*

*vratatyāgānna saṃdehastatra te nāsti kiṃcana \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ mayā samyaksmṛtimārgeṇa ciṃtitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

86-88. The Dīkṣā pertaining to a Brāhmaṇa is based on institution of the sacred thread. The Gāyatrī Mantra should be used as the main Mantra for Japa and the Guru (preceptor) shall be one devoted to Vratas.

If any one adopts Śaiva or Vaiṣṇava Dīkṣā, he shall not be a true Brāhmaṇa though he may have studied all the six Aṅgas. Another thing, in your fraudulent activities you have broken Liṅgas because you have caused avoidance in Vratas. Hence you have no means of expiation. I have thought over it very well in accordance with the line of Smṛtis.

## \|\| 1.274.89 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*satāṃ saptapadīṃ maitrīṃ pravadaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*mitratāṃ tu puraskṛtya kiṃcidvakṣyāmi tacchṛṇu \|\| 89 \|\|*

Duḥśīla said:

89\. Learned men say that friendship of good people is based on seven Padas (steps, words) (i.e. If some one walks along with another seven steps or speaks to him seven words, the friendship has been initiated). On the strength of such friendship, I am now saying something to you. Listen to it.

## \|\| 1.274.90 \|\|

*asti me vipulaṃ vittaṃ yadi tena prasiddhyati \|*  
*tadvadasva mahābhāga yena sarvaṃ karomyaham \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. I have vast assets. If anything can be achieved thereby do tell me, O highly esteemed one; I shall do everything.

## \|\| 1.274.91 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*eka eva hyupāyo'sti tava pātakanāśane \|*  
*taṃ cetkaroṣi me vākyādviśuddhaḥ saṃbhaviṣyasi \|\| 91 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

91\. There is only one way whereby your sin can be eliminated. If you perform it at my instance you will become pure.

## \|\| 1.274.92 \|\|

*tapaḥ kṛte praśaṃsaṃti tretāyāṃ jñānameva ca \|*  
*dvāpare tīrthayātrāṃ ca dānameva kalau yuge \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. They praise penance in Kṛtayuga, knowledge in Tretā, pilgrimage in Dvāpra and only Dāna in Kaliyuga.

## \|\| 1.274.93 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ kalikālo'yaṃ vartate dāruṇākṛtiḥ \|*  
*tasmātkṛṣṇājinaṃ dehi sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Now, it is the time of Kali. It is current in its terrible form. Hence make a gift of Kṛṣṇājina (skin of black antelope) in order to wipe off all sins and gain purity.

## \|\| 1.274.94 \|\|

*tathā ca te ghṛṇā'pyasti guruvittasamudbhavā \|*  
*tadarthaṃ kuru tannāmnā śaṃkarasya niveśanam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Similarly, if you feel some compunctions about the preceptor’s cash, then build an abode (shrine) of Śaṅkara in the name of the Guru.

## \|\| 1.274.95-96 \|\|

*yena tasmādapi tvaṃ hi ānṛṇyaṃ yāsi tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*anyatrāpi ca tadvittaṃ yatkiṃcicca prapadyate \|\| 95 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇebhyo viśiṣṭebhyo nityaṃ dehi samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tilapātraṃ sadā dehi sahiraṇyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. In that case you will instantly become free from indebtedness to him also. If his wealth is put into use elsewhere, give that unto specially qualified Brāhmaṇas with great mental concentration. Always give a pot filled with gingelly seeds along with gold. Thereby all your sin will be expelled from your body.

## \|\| 1.274.97-98 \|\|

*yena te sakalaṃ pāpaṃ dehānnāśaṃ pragacchati \|*  
*aparaṃ caitramāse'haṃ sadā'gacchāmi bhaktitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*kalpagrāmātsudūrācca prāsāde'tra svayaṃ kṛte \|*  
*punaryāmi ca tatraiva vratametaddhi me sthitam \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. Another thing, during the month of Caitra, I always come here devoutly from the far-off Kalpa (?Kalāpa) village to the palace here built by myself. Thereafter, I go. This is my Vrata.

## \|\| 1.274.99 \|\|

*tasmācciṃtyastvayāhyeṣa prāsādo yo mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtanīyaṃ sadaiveha snānādibhiranekaśaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Hence, with care you must look after this palace which has been built by me. It should be remembered always in the matters of ablution etc. in various ways.

## \|\| 1.274.100 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*kariṣyāmi vacaste'haṃ yathā vadasi sanmune \|\| 100 \|\|*

Duḥśīla said:

100\. I shall carry out your instructions, O excellent sage, strictly as you say.

## \|\| 1.274.101 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ datte kṛṣṇājine dvijaḥ \|*  
*prayaccha tilapātrāṇi guptapāpasya śuddhaye \|\| 101 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

101\. O Brāhmaṇa, after the antelope skin has been gifted away, give the vessels of gingelly seeds for the purification of secret sins. Thereby, all the sins shall be purified (dispelled).

## \|\| 1.274.102 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dattaṃ tena mahātmanā \|*  
*tataḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ bhaktyā brāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye \|\| 102 \|\|*

Sūta said:

102\. On hearing his words the noble soul gave devoutly antelope skin to a Brāhmaṇa maintaining the sacred fires.

## \|\| 1.274.103-105 \|\|

*durvāsasaḥ samā deśādyathoktavidhinā dvijāḥ \|*  
*yacchatastilapātrāṇi tasya nityaṃ prabhaktitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*gatapāpasya dīkṣāṃ ca dadau nirvāṇasaṃbhavām \|*  
*tathāsau gatapāpasya dīkṣāṃ dattvā yathāvidhi \|\| 104 \|\|*

*tataḥ provāca madhuraṃ dehi me gurudakṣiṇām \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. O Brāhmaṇas, at the bidding of Durvāsas he did everything in accordance with the injunction. As he gifted the vessels filled with gingelly seeds everyday with great devotion, he became free from sins. So (the sage) granted him initiation into salvation and activities pertaining to it. After granting the initiation duly, he spoke to him sweetly: “Give me the monetary fees due to a preceptor.”

## \|\| 1.274.106 \|\|

*duḥśīla uvāca \|*  
*yācasva tvaṃ prabho śīghraṃ yāṃ te yacchāmi dakṣiṇām \|*
