*tāṃ pradāsyāmi cecchaktirvittaśāṭhyavivarjitām \|\| 106 \|\|*

Duḥśīla said:

106\. O holy Sir, ask for any monetary gift quickly. If I have the capacity, I shall give it without any dishonesty in regard to my wealth.

## \|\| 1.274.107 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*kalpagrāmaṃ gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ vartate kaliḥ \|*  
*nāhamatrāgamiṣyāmi yāvannaiva kṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 107 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

107\. I shall go to Kalpa village. Now it is Kali Age. I will never come here before the advent of Kṛta Age.

## \|\| 1.274.108 \|\|

*ardhaniṣpādito hyeṣa prāsādo yo mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*paripūrtiṃ tvayā neya eṣā me gurudakṣiṇā \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The palace that has been built by me is only half completed. You must see that it is completed. This is the monetary fee due to me as a preceptor.

## \|\| 1.274.109 \|\|

*nṛtyagītādikaṃ yacca tathā kāryaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*purato'sya balirdeyastathānyatkusumādikam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The programme of dance, music etc. should be followed in accordance with your capacity. Oblations should be offered before the deity, viz. flowers etc.

## \|\| 1.274.110 \|\|

*evamuktvā gataḥ so'tha kalpagrāmaṃ munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*duḥśīlo'pi tathā cakre yattena samudāhṛtam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. After saying this that leading sage went to Kalpa village. Duḥśīla did everything that he had suggested.

## \|\| 1.274.111 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya prabhaktasya tatkāryāṇi prakurvataḥ \|*  
*tannāmnā kīrtyate so'tha duḥśīla iti saṃjñitaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

Sūta said:

111\. Even as he did everything with great devotion that Brāhmaṇa named Duḥśīla is being glorified by that very name.

## \|\| 1.274.112 \|\|

*caitramāse ca yo nityaṃ taṃ ca devaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sa pāpena vārṣikeṇa pramucyate \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. He who visits that Lord in the month of Caitra, is rid of his annual sin in an instant.

## \|\| 1.274.113-114 \|\|

*yaḥ punaḥ snapanaṃ tasya sarvaṃ caiva karoti ca \|*  
*triṃśadvarṣodbhavaṃ pāpaṃ tasya gātrātpraṇaśyati \|\| 113 \|\|*

*yaḥ punarnṛtyagītādyaṃ kurute ca tadagrataḥ \|*  
*ājanmamaraṇātpāpātso'pi muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. If anyone carries out the bathing rite etc., his sins arising in the course of thirty years are expelled from his body.

He who conducts dance and music programme before the deity, is rid of all the sins committed ever since his birth and upto the death. He shall attain salvation.

## Chapter 275 - Nimbeśvara and Śākaṃbharī

## \|\| 1.275.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*duḥśīlo'pi ca tatkṛtvā gurornāmnā śivālayam \|*  
*nimbeśvara iti khyātaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*cakāra parayā bhaktyā tatpādābjamanusmaran \|*  
*tathā tasya tu bhāryā yā nāmnā śākaṃbharī smṛtā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*svanāmāṃkā tatra durgā tathā saṃsthāpitā tayā \|*  
*tatastu taddhanaṃ tābhyāṃ kiciccheṣaṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūjārthaṃ devatābhyāṃ ca brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samarpitam \|*  
*bhikṣābhujau tato jātau dampatī tau tataḥ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. Duḥśīla thus built the shrine of Śiva after the name of his preceptor i.e. it became well-known as Nimbeśvara. It was in the southern direction.

He did everything with great devotion and always remembered his lotus-like feet.

His wife had the name of Śākaṃbharī. Durgā was installed by her after her own name. After these activities, they had some cash left with them which they gave over to Brāhmaṇas for conducting the worship of the deities. Thereafter, the couple ate and sustained themselves with alms.

## \|\| 1.275.5-8 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya duḥśīlo nidhanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śākaṃbharyapi tatkāyaṃ gṛhītvā havyavāhanam \|*  
*praviṣṭā nṛpaśārdūla nirvikalpena cetasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tato vimānamāruhya varāpsaraḥsusevitam \|*  
*gatau tau dvāvapi svargaṃ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etaṃ duḥśīlajaṃ yastu paṭhedākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*sa sarvairmucyate pāpairajñānavihitairnṛpa \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. After some time Duḥśīla passed away. Śākaṃbharī took his body and entered the (sacred) fire, O tiger among kings, with unfaltering mind.

They got into an excellent aerial chariot attended upon by excellent celestial damsels, and went to heaven with hair standing on end due to great delight.

He who reads this excellent narrative pertaining to Duḥśīla becomes rid of all sins incurred by deeds unwittingly committed.

## Chapter 276 - Origin of Eleven Rudras

## \|\| 1.276.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathānye'pi vasantīha rudrā ekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*sañjātā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā munīnāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yairdṛṣṭaiḥ pūjitai rvāpi stutairvātha namaskṛtaiḥ \|*  
*vipāpmā jāyate martyaḥ sarvadoṣavivarjitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Similarly, there are others too installed here viz the eleven rudras. They originated here, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, with a desire for the welfare of the sages.

If they are duly visited, worshipped, eulogized or bowed to by a man he becomes free from sins and relieved of all defects.

## \|\| 1.276.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*eka eva śruto rudro na dvitīyaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*gaurī bhāryāpriyā yasya skandaḥ putraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. Only one Rudra is heard about (mentioned in the Veda) and no second one. His beloved wife is Gaurī and Skanda is glorified as his son?

## \|\| 1.276.4 \|\|

*tenaikaṃ vidmahe rudraṃ nānyamīśaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*tasmādbrūhi mahābhāga sarvānetānsuvistarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Therefore, we know only one Rudra and none at all as Īśa (Almighty). Hence, O highly esteemed oṇe, mention all these in detail.

## \|\| 1.276.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahābhāgā yadbhavadbhirudāhṛtam \|*  
*eka eva sthito rudro na dvitīyaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. O highly esteemed ones, it is indeed the truth that has been cited. Rudra is one only. There is no second one at all.

## \|\| 1.276.6 \|\|

*paraṃ yathā ca sañjātā rudrā ekādaśātra bhoḥ \|*  
*tathāhaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. But, I shall describe how these eleven Rudras originated. Listen with concentration.

## \|\| 1.276.7 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ purā saṃsthā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaradevasya darśanārthaṃ samutsukāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly, the sages of praiseworthy holy rites congregated together at Vārāṇasī. They were eager to visit Lord Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.276.8-9 \|\|

*prasthitāḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā spardhamānāḥ parasparam \|*  
*ahaṃpūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ vīkṣayiṣyāmi taṃ vibhum \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmagrato bhūtvā pātāle hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*yaścādau tatra gatvā ca nekṣayiṣyati taṃ haram \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ śramajaṃ pāpaṃ tasyaikasya bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. They made one agreement and started to reach there. They vied with one another saying, “I will view the Lord first. I will view the Lord first.” Everyone wanted to be the first to visit Lord Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla. “Whoever does not go at the outset and does not see the Lord shall alone bear the brunt of the sin of all arising out of the effort.”

## \|\| 1.276.10 \|\|

*evamuktvā tataḥ sarve vārāṇasyāṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*prasthitā dhāvamānāśca vegena mahatā tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After saying thus they set out from Vārāṇasī running with very great speed.

## \|\| 1.276.11-14 \|\|

*etasminnantare devo hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā teṣāmabhiprāyaṃ mithaḥ sparddhāsamudbhavam \|*  
*ātmano darśanārthāya bahubhaktipuraskṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*laghunā rakṣyamāṇena sarveṣāṃ ca mahātmanām \|*  
*nāgaraṃdhreṇa niṣkramya pātālāccaiva tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ekādaśaprakāraṃ sa kṛtvā rūpaṃ manoharam \|*  
*triśūlabhṛttrinetraṃ ca kapardena vibhūṣitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śaśikhaṃḍadharaṃ caiva ruṇḍamālāpradhārakam \|*  
*samaṃ caiva sthitasteṣāṃ darśane śaṃkaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. In the meantime, the Lord named Hāṭakeśvara understood their intention to view him with very great devotion and their mutual rivalry too. He went out through a very minute serpent-hole from Pātāla immediately. He assumed seven distinct forms having the same charming features, holding the trident, three-eyed and decorated with Kaparda (matted hairs). Each had the crescent moon as crest jewel and wore a garland of headless bodies. Lord Śaṅkara thus stood within their simultaneous view.

## \|\| 1.276.15 \|\|

*tataste vai samālokya purasthaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā stutiṃ cakrustatastataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, on seeing the Bull-emblemed One standing before, they knelt down on the ground and began to eulogize.

## \|\| 1.276.16 \|\|

*eko jānāti devo'yaṃ mama saṃdarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*devadevo mahādevaḥ prathamaṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One of them thought, ‘O, This Lord Mahādeva, the Lord of Devas, endearing to the devotees has appeared before me at the outset.’

## \|\| 1.276.17 \|\|

*anyo jānāti me pūrvaṃ jātaste tāpasottamaḥ \|*  
*stutiṃ cakruśca vipreṃdrā jānubhyāmavaniṃ gatāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Another thought, ‘The excellent one among the ascetics appeared before me at the outset.’ O excellent Brāhmaṇas, they knelt on the ground and eulogized:

## \|\| 1.276.18 \|\|

*tāpasā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namo devādhidevāya sarvadevamayāya ca \|*  
*namaḥ śāṃtāya sūkṣmāya namaścāṃdhakabhedine \|\| 18 \|\|*

The ascetics said:

18\. Obeisance to the presiding deity of Devas. Obeisance to the quiescent one, to the subtle one. Obeisance to the Lord who split (killed) Andhaka.

## \|\| 1.276.19 \|\|

*namo'stu sarvarudrebhyo ye divaṃ saṃśritāḥ sadā \|*  
*jīvāpayaṃti jagatīṃ vāyubhiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance to all the Rudras who have occupied heaven always. They enliven the earth with the winds of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.276.20 \|\|

*namo'stu sarvarudrebhyo ye sthitā vāruṇīṃ diśam \|*  
*rakṣaṃti sarvalokāṃśca piśācānāṃ durātmanām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Obeisance to all the Rudras who are stationed in the western quarters and protect all the worlds from the danger of the wicked-minded Piśācas.

## \|\| 1.276.21 \|\|

*namo'stu sarvarudrebhyo diśamūrdhvaṃ samāśritāḥ \|*  
*rakṣaṃti sakalāṃllokānbhūtārnāṃ jaṃbhakādbhayāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Obeisance to all the Rudras who have resorted to the northern quarters and who protect all the worlds from the danger of the devouring goblins.

## \|\| 1.276.22 \|\|

*namo'stu sarvarudrebhyo ye'dha ūrdhvaṃ samāśritāḥ \|*  
*rakṣaṃti sakalāṃllokānkūṣmāṃḍānāṃ bhayātsadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Obeisance to all the Rudras who have resorted to regions beneath and above and always protect all the worlds from the danger of the Kūṣmāṇḍas.

## \|\| 1.276.23 \|\|

*asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi ye rudrā bhūmimāśritāḥ \|*  
*namastebhyo'pi sarvebhyasteṣāṃ rakṣaṃti ye rujaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Obeisance to those numberless thousands of Rudras who have resorted to the earth. They protect us from ailments.

## \|\| 1.276.24 \|\|

*evaṃ stutāstu te rudrā ekādaśatapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*ekādaśāpi tānprocurbhaktinamrāṃstu tāpasān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On being eulogized by the eleven ascetics, those eleven Rudras spoke to the ascetics who stood humbly with devout feelings:

## \|\| 1.276.25 \|\|

*rudrā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ekādaśaprakāro'haṃ tuṣṭo vastāpasottamāḥ \|*  
*bahubhaktyatirekeṇa vriyatāṃ ca yathepsitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

The Rudras said:

25\. I who have assumed eleven forms am pleased with your excessive devotion, O excellent ascetics. Whatever is desired may be requested now:

## \|\| 1.276.26 \|\|

*tāpasā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭosi no deva yadi yacchasi vāṃchitam \|*  
*ekādaśaprakāraistu sadā stheyamihaiva tu \|\| 26 \|\|*

The ascetics said:

26\. If you are pleased with us, O Lord, if you are ready to grant what is desired, then you should stay here always in all those eleven forms.

## \|\| 1.276.27 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvatīrthamaye śubhe \|*  
*ārādhanaṃ prakurvāṇā vasāmo yena vai vayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then we shall stay here in the auspicious holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara containing all the Tīrthas. We shall continue to propitiate you.

## \|\| 1.276.28 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ekādaśaprakārā yā mūrtayo nirmitā mayā \|*  
*etābhireva sarvābhiḥ sthāsyāmyatra sadaiva hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

28\. I shall stay here always in all these forms of eleven kinds assumed by me.

## \|\| 1.276.29 \|\|

*ādyā tu mama yā mūrtiḥ sā kailāsaṃ samāśritā \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhati sadaivātra kailāse parvatottame \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. My original and primordial form shall resort to Kailāsa and stay always on the excellent mountain.

## \|\| 1.276.30 \|\|

*etāstu mūrtayo'smākaṃ sthāsyaṃtyatraiva sarvadā \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva lokānāṃ hitāya dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. But these forms of mine shall stay here always, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, for the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.276.31 \|\|

*nāmabhiśca krameṇaiva yuṣmadīyaiḥ svayaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitrahrade snātvā etā mūrtīrmamātra vai \|*  
*pūjayiṣyaṃti ye martyāste yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Men shall take their holy ablution in the Viśvāmitra Hrada (whirlpool) and worship these forms of mine uttering your names in order, O Brāhmaṇas. They will attain the greatest goal, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.276.32 \|\|

*kiṃ vācā bahunoktena bhūyobhūyo dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yā tāsāṃ kriyate pūjā ekādaśaguṇā bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, of what avail is the repeated utterance of many words? The adoration performed unto them shall have eleven times more benefit.

## \|\| 1.276.33 \|\|

*evamuktvā trinetrastu tatraivādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*te'pi tatrāśramaṃ kṛtvā śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*mūrtīśca tāḥ samārādhya saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After saying thus the Three-eyed Lord vanished there itself. They too built their hermitages there. They were endowed with great faith. By propitiating those forms they attained the greatest region.

## \|\| 1.276.34 \|\|

*anyo'pi yaḥ pumāṃstāśca ārādhayati śraddhayā \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Any other man who propitiates them with faith goes to that greatest region where Lord Maheśvara is present.

## \|\| 1.276.35 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te jātā rudrā ekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*saṃkhyayā devadevasya maheśvaravapurdharāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Ever since then they became the eleven Rudras having the physical forms of Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.276.36 \|\|

*tejottamāste saṃyuktāstrinetrāḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All of them united together are highly excellent in their refulgence. They are three-eyed and trident-armed.

Thus everything I have been asked, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, has been recounted to you.

## \|\| 1.276.37-38 \|\|

*ekādaśaprakārastu yathā jāto maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*caitre māsi site pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ dine sthite \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yastānpūjayate bhaktyā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*adhano dhanamāpnoti hyaputraḥ putravānbhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. I have explained how Maheśvara assumed the eleven forms.

He who devoutly adores them on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, attains the greatest goal. One who has no wealth attains wealth. One without a son shall beget sons.

## \|\| 1.276.39 \|\|

*sarogo rogamuktastu parābhūto ripukṣayam \|*  
*tatsamārādhanādeva kāmānaṃtyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A sick man shall be rid of ailments. A vanquished man shall meet with destruction of enemies. Through their propitiation alone one shall realize infinite desires.

## \|\| 1.276.40 \|\|

*yaḥ punaḥ śivadīkṣāḍhyo bhasmasnānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatsamārādhanaṃ kuryācchṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Listen to the benefit obtained by one who propitiates them after being blessed with Śivadīkṣā (initiation) and becoming engaged in Bhasma (holy ash) bath.

## \|\| 1.276.41 \|\|

*yadanyaḥ prāpnuyānmartyastatpūjāsaṃbhavaṃ phalam \|*  
*ṣaḍakṣareṇa maṃtreṇa puṣpeṇaikena tatphalam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He shall attain (in return to worship performed) with a single flower that benefit which another man attains as a result of adoration with the utterance of the six-syllabled Mantra.

## \|\| 1.276.42 \|\|

*śivadīkṣādharo yastu śataghnaṃ labhate phalam \|*  
*tasmācchataghnamāpnoti śaivātpāśupataśca yaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkālamukho yaśca mahāvratadharaśca yaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He who practises Śivadīkṣā obtains hundred times more the benefit. A devoted Pāśupata obtains hundred times more benefit than a Śaiva. Kālāmukha obtains hundred times more benefit than the previous one and a Mahāvaratadhara still hundred times more.

## \|\| 1.276.43 \|\|

*mūrtīryāstāśca ye bhaktyā vinatāḥ pūjayaṃti ca \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva teṣāṃ tu phalaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Those who are humble and worship those forms devoutly shall have hundred times more benefit.

## Chapter 277 - In Praise of Dāna Performed in front of Rudras

## \|\| 1.277.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ki nāmāno dvijāste ca vārāṇasyāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*ekādaśaprakāro'sau yeṣāṃ rudraḥ prabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃjñāśca samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. What are the names of those Brāhmaṇas who came from Vārāṇasī and due to whose great devotion, Rudra assumed the eleven forms? O great sage, narrate in detail their names.

## \|\| 1.277.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ekasteṣāṃ mṛgavyādho vikhyāto bhuvanatraye \|*  
*dvitīyaḥ sarvasaṃjñaśca niṃditaśca tṛtīyakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. One of them is well-known all over the three worlds as Mṛgavyādha. The second one is called Sarva (Śarva?) and the third Nindita.

## \|\| 1.277.3 \|\|

*mahāyaśāścaturthastu kathyate munisattamāḥ \|*  
*ajaikapāda ityuktaḥ paṃcamo muni sattamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O excellent sages, the fourth one is called Mahāyaśāh. The fifth one is called Ajaikapāda, O excellent sages.

## \|\| 1.277.4 \|\|

*ahirbudhnyastathā ṣaṣṭhaḥ pinākī saptamastathā \|*  
*paraṃ tapastathānyastu dahano navamastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Ahirbudhnya is the sixth. Pinākin is the seventh. Parantapa is the other one (i.e. eighth). Dahana is the ninth one.

## \|\| 1.277.5 \|\|

*īśvaro daśamaḥ proktaḥ kapālī cāṃti mastathā \|*  
*teṣāmetāni nāmāni sthitānyeva hi yāni ca \|*  
*rudrāṇāmapi tānyeva vihitāni hareṇa tu \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The tenth is mentioned as Īśvara and Kapālin is the last one. Hara gave the Rudras also the same names as they possessed.

## \|\| 1.277.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kāni dānāni śasyāni tadarthaṃ vada no drutam \|*  
*japaścaiva purā proktastvayā kāryo yathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:

6\. Tell us quickly what Dānas are, recommended in their case. The Japa has been earlier mentioned by you. What is the procedure for carrying it out?

## \|\| 1.277.7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*taduddiśya pradātavyamekaikasya pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*pratyakṣāśca mahābhāga dātavyā dhenavaḥ kramāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sūīa said:

7\. O highly esteemed ones, cows are to be offered to them directly and separately in each case.

## \|\| 1.277.8 \|\|

*mṛgavyādhāya pratyakṣā gaurdeyā ca guḍodbhavā \|*  
*kapāline pradātavyā navanītasamudbhavā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Cow made of jaggery should be directly given to Mṛgavyādha. That made of fresh butter should be given to Kapālin.

## \|\| 1.277.9 \|\|

*ajapādāya cājyotthā ahirbudhnyāya hemajā \|*  
*pinākine pradātavyā dhenurlavaṇasambhavā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A cow made of ghee should be offered to Ajaikapāda and that made of gold to Ahirbudhnya. A cow made of salt should be offered to Pinākin.

## \|\| 1.277.10 \|\|

*paraṃtapāya viprendrāstathaiva rasasa mbhavā \|*  
*annajā dahanāyoktā īśvarāya jalodbhavā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, a cow made of Rasa (Juice) is to be offered to Parantapa. That made of cooked rice is assigned to Dahana and that of water to Īśvara.

## \|\| 1.277.11 \|\|

*etā dadāti yo viprā eteṣāṃ ca mahātmanām \|*  
*cakravartī bhavennūnametadāha pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Brāhmaṇas, he who gives these to noble souls shall certainly become an emperor. Pitāmaha said thus.

## \|\| 1.277.12 \|\|

*anyatrāpi pradattāśca kiṃ punarbhavasaṃnidhau \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena etā deyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They are beneficial if given to others too and still more so if they are given in the presence of Bhava. Hence by all means these should be given.

## \|\| 1.277.13 \|\|

*dhenavo yo na śaktaḥ syādekā deyā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva rudrāṇāṃ bhartṛyajñavaco yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If one is unable to give many cows, one should give at least one cow to all the Rudras together in accordance with the words (opinion) of Bhartṛyajña.

## Chapter 278 - The Legend of Yājñavalkya

## \|\| 1.278.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ye cānye bhāskarā statra saṃti brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yastānpūjayate bhaktyā hṛdi kṛtvā'bhivāṃchitān \|*  
*saptamyāṃ caiva saptamyāṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the other shrines in the holy spot of Hāṭakeśvara are (those of) Bhāskaras (Sun-gods) installed by Yājñavalkya.

One who entertains something in his heart and devoutly worships them on Saptamī days (i.e. seventh lunar days) attains them. There is no doubt in it.

## \|\| 1.278.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ucuḥ \|*  
*eka eva sthitaḥ sūryo dṛśyate ca nabhastale \|*  
*tatkathaṃ dvādaśaite ca tatra kṣetre pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle tathā kṛtye kimarthaṃ sūtanandana \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

3\. There is only one Sun to be seen in the sky. Then how are twelve suns installed in that holy spot? At what time and for what purpose were they installed, O Sūtanandana?

## \|\| 1.278.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āsītpūrvaṃ kṛtirnāma śunaḥśepasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasya putraḥ śunaḥ putro babhūva munisattamaḥ \|*  
*cārāyaṇaḥ sutastasya vabhūva munisattamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4-5. Formerly there was a sage named Kṛti. He was the son of Śunaḥśepa. His son i.e. the grandson of Śunaḥśepa became a great sage. His son Cārāyaṇa also became an excellent sage.

## \|\| 1.278.6 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya brahmā loka pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*sāvitrīśāpanirdagdho hyavatīrṇo dharātale \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once upon a time, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, was completely burnt down (as it were) by a curse pronounced by Sāvitrī. He took incarnation on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.278.7 \|\|

*gāyatrī ca yadā viprāstenoḍhā yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*prāksthitāṃ ca parityajya sarvadevasamāgame \|*  
*kālātyayo bhavennaiva sāvitryāgamane sthire \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The curse was pronounced at the time when Gāyatrī was taken over as wife for the purpose of the Yajña rite, after rejecting (the wife) already he had. He did this in the assembly of all the Devas, thinking that there would be delay in the arrival of Sāvitrī.

## \|\| 1.278.8 \|\|

*tatastasya samādeśādgāyatrī gopakanyakā \|*  
*śakreṇa ca samānītā divyalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then, at his bidding, Gāyatrī, the daughter of a cowherd, endowed with all divine characteristics, was brought by Śakra.

## \|\| 1.278.9 \|\|

*gopakanyāṃ ca tāṃ jñātvā gośca vaktreṇa padmajaḥ \|*  
*praveśyākarṣayāmāsa guhyena ca tataḥ param \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Knowing that she was the daughter of a cowherd, the Lotus-born Lord pressed her through the mouth of a cow and dragged her out through the anus.

## \|\| 1.278.10 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ caiva kulamekaṃ dvidhā sthitam \|*  
*ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhaṃti havirekatra saṃsthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There is a single family in the case of Brāhmaṇas and cows, only separated into two. The Mantras are stationed in one (Brāhmaṇa) and the Havis (ghee for sacrificial oblation) in the other.

## \|\| 1.278.11 \|\|

*tena tāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ kṛtvā paścāttasyāḥ parigraham \|*  
*gṛhyoktavidhinā cakre puraḥstho'pi pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereby, she was made a Brāhmaṇa girl and Pitāmaha standing in front accepted her as his wife in accordance with the injunctions in the scriptures (Gṛhya Sūtra).

## \|\| 1.278.12 \|\|

*patnīśālopaviṣṭāyāṃ tatastasyāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sāvitrī samanuprāptā devapatnībhirāvṛtā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When she occupied the Patnī-Śālā (the chamber intended for the wife of the performer of sacrifice), O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Sāvitrī too came there surrounded by the wives of Devas.

## \|\| 1.278.13 \|\|

*tatastāṃ sā samālokya raśanāsamalaṃkṛtām \|*  
*daurbhāgyaduḥkhamāpannā śaśāpa ca vidhiṃ tataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing her (Gāyatrī) bedecked in sacrificial girdle, she became grief-stricken due to her loss of conjugal felicity. She then cursed Vidhi.

## \|\| 1.278.14 \|\|

*sāvitryuvāca \|*  
*yasmāttvayā parityaktā nirdoṣāhaṃ pitāmaha \|*  
*pitāmaho'si me nūnamadyaprabhṛti saṃgame \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sāvitrī said:

14\. O Pitāmaha, though I am blemishless, I have been adandoned by you. Hence for the purpose of physical contact, you are only my grandfather (not worthy of contact).

## \|\| 1.278.15 \|\|

*manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavetkṛtyamanyanārīparigrahaḥ \|*  
*etattvayā kṛtaṃ yasmānmā nuṣastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is the practice of human beings to take another woman as wife. Since you have done this, you will become a human being.

## \|\| 1.278.16 \|\|

*kāmārtaśca viśeṣeṇa mama vākyādasaṃśayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At my instance (curse), you shall undoubtedly be one afflicted by lust.

## \|\| 1.278.17 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu sāvitrī tyaktvā taṃ yajñamaṃḍapam \|*  
*gireḥ śikharamārūḍhā tapaścakre mahattataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After saying this, Sāvitrī left the pavilion of the Yajña. She climbed on to the peak of a mountain and performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.278.18 \|\|

*pitāmaho'pi tacchāpāccārāyaṇaniveśane \|*  
*avatīrṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe kālena mahatā tataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Due to that curse, after a long time, Pitāmaha was born into the household of Cārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 1.278.19 \|\|

*sa yadā yauvanaṃ bheje mānuṣaṃ ca purā sthitaḥ \|*  
*tathātathā ca tāpena kāmotthena prapīḍyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When he attained the prime of youth in his human life, he became afflicted by the distress born of lust.

## \|\| 1.278.20 \|\|

*tato'sau vīkṣate nārīṃ kanyāṃ vātha tapasvinīm \|*  
*avikalpamanā bheje rūpasaubhāgyagarvitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He became proud due to his handsome features and he began to enjoy indiscriminately any woman he saw, be she a virgin or a sage girl.

## \|\| 1.278.21 \|\|

*tatastaṃ byasanārtaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cārāyaṇo muniḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ niḥsārayāmāsa prakopena nijāśramāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing him indulging in vice, sage Cārāyaṇa angrily banished him from his hermitage.

## \|\| 1.278.22 \|\|

*sa ca pitrā parityakto bhramamāṇastatastataḥ \|*  
*camatkārapuraṃ prāptaḥ śākalyo yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Abandoned by his father, he began to roam about here and there and ultimately came to the city of Camatkārapura to the place where Śākalya stayed.

## \|\| 1.278.23 \|\|

*nāmnā brāhmaṇaśārdūlo nāgaro vedapāragaḥ \|*  
*vṛtaḥ śiṣya sahasreṇa vedavidyāṃ pracārayan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. That tiger among Brāhmaṇas was a Nāgara who had mastered the Vedas. He was surrounded by a thousand disciples and he propagated the Vedic lore.

## \|\| 1.278.24 \|\|

*atha taṃ sa praṇamyoccaiḥ śiṣyatvaṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpanno babhūvātha cirādapi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He (Cārāyaṇa’s son) devoutly bowed down to him and became his disciple. After a long time, he became a master of Vedic study.

## \|\| 1.278.25 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle nu ānartādhipatiḥ svayam \|*  
*āgatastiṣṭhate yatra jalaśāyī hariḥ svayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meantime, the king of Ānarta came to the place himself where Hari was Jalaśāyin (lying in the water).

## \|\| 1.278.26 \|\|

*cāturmāsyavrataṃ tena gṛhītaṃ tatpurastadā \|*  
*prārthitastu tato viprāḥ śākalyastaina bhūbhujā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Before that deity, the holy rite of Cāturmāsya was adopted by him. O Brāhmaṇas, then Śākalya was requested by that king:

## \|\| 1.278.27 \|\|

*śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ nityaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mamālaye \|*  
*yāvattiṣṭhāmyahaṃ cātra prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “As long as I stay here, kindly do me this favour. The rites of Śāntika and Pauṣtika \[Pauṣṭika?\] (one for peace, the other for prosperity) should be performed by you in our abode.”

## \|\| 1.278.28 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā dākṣiṇyena dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ekaikaṃ preṣayāmāsa svaśiṣyaṃ tasya maṃdire \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He (Śākalya) said “Of course” out of courtesy, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. He then sent his disciples one by one to his (King’s) abode.

## \|\| 1.278.29 \|\|

*sa śāṃtikaṃ vidhāyātha dattvāśīḥ pārthivasya ca \|*  
*saṃprāpya dakṣiṇāṃ tasmātpunareti ca taṃ dvijam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Every disciple performed the Śāntika rite and blessed the king. Accepting the monetary gift, he used to return to the Brāhmaṇa (Preceptor).

## \|\| 1.278.30 \|\|

*śākalyāya ca tāṃ dattvā dakṣiṇāṃ nijamaṃdire \|*  
*jagāma nityamevaṃ hi vyavahāro vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The monetary gift was handed over to the preceptor Śākalya and the disciple went to his own abode. This became the regular practice.

## \|\| 1.278.31 \|\|

*anyasminnahani prāpte śākalyena visarjitaḥ \|*  
*śāṃtyarthaṃ yājñavalkyastu pārthivasyaniveśanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On another day Yājñavalkya was despatched to the king’s abode by Śākalya for performing the Śānti rite.

## \|\| 1.278.32 \|\|

*tasya bhūpasya rūpāḍhayā maṃtharāsti vilāsinī \|*  
*rātrau ca kāmitā tena kāmāḍhayena sukāminī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. (On the previous night) the king’s beautiful wife Mantharā, a charming damsel, was enjoyed by this over-passionate youth.

## \|\| 1.278.33 \|\|

*bhāvairvātsyāyanaproktaiḥ samāliṃganapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*sa tayā vividhaiḥ kṛtto mayūrapadakādibhiḥ \|*  
*śarīre cādhare caiva tathā maṇipravālakaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She had indulged in various amorous acts with him as elaborately prescribed by Vātsyāyana beginning with close embraces, infliction of marks with finger nails (and precious stones?) etc. in the form of peacock’s foot on his lips and body.

## \|\| 1.278.34 \|\|

*saṃprāpto'dhyayanārthāya yāvacchākalyasannidhau \|*  
*tāvatsaṃpreṣitastena śāṃtyarthaṃ bhūpamaṃdire \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. (After the night-long escapade) the fellow came to Śākalya’s presence for the daily lesson but he was immediately sent to the abode of the king for performing the Sānti rite.

## \|\| 1.278.35 \|\|

*so'pi saṃpreṣitastena gatvā taṃ pārthivālayam \|*  
*śāṃtikaṃ ca tataścakre yathoktavidhinā dvijāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On being sent there by him, the disciple went to the abode of the king and performed the Śāntika rite in accordance with the injunctions in scriptures, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.278.36-37 \|\|

*śāṃtikasyāvasāne tu pragṛhya kalaśodakam \|*  
*paṃcāṃgaiḥ kalpitaṃ rudraiḥ svayamevābhimaṃtritaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sākṣataṃ sumanoyuktaṃ samādāya gatastataḥ \|*  
*saṃtiṣṭhate nṛpo yatra ānarto tratasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. At the conclusion of the Śāntika rite, the disciple (Yājñavalkya) took the water pot where the water charged with the Rudra Mantras with five ancillaries had been poured. He took also raw rice grains and flowers and went to the place where Ānarta was performing the Vrata.

## \|\| 1.278.38-39 \|\|

*dyāmālekhīti maṃtraṃ sa proccārya vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*chaṃdarṣisahitaṃ caiva yāvatkṣipati mastake \|*  
*tāvannirīkṣitastena nakhalekhāvikartitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*khaṃḍitenādhareṇaiva tato'bhūddurmanā nṛpaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The disciple duly uttered the Mantra dyāmālekhi etc. along with the names of the sage and the Chandas. He was about to sprinkle the holy water over the head of the king, when the king observed that the fellow had nail-marks over his body and that his lips had been cut. This made the king unhappy.

## \|\| 1.278.40-42 \|\|

*viṭaprāyaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā malināṃbaradhāriṇam \|*  
*taṃ provāca vihasyoccai dehi viprā'kṣatāñjalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*maṃdurāyāṃ sthitaṃ yacca kāṣṭhametatpradṛśyate \|*  
*yājñavalkyastato dṛṣṭvā sakopastamupādravat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṣiptvā tatra jalaṃ viprāḥ sākṣataṃ gṛhamāgamat \|*  
*agṛhya dakṣiṇāṃ tasya pārthivasya yathāsthitām \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. The king clearly observed that the fellow with the defiled garments was a debauchee. He laughed loudly and said, “O Brāhmaṇa, pour the water and the raw rice grains over the stump seen in the stable.” Yājñavalkya approached it angrily and poured there the water along with the raw rice grains. He went home without taking the monetary gift placed duly by the king.

## \|\| 1.278.43 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tasya dhavakāṣṭhasya sarvataḥ \|*  
*niṣkrāṃtā vividhāḥ śākhāḥ pallavaiḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the meantime the stump of the Dhava tree had put forth sprouts. There were small branches of sprouts all round beautifying it.

## \|\| 1.278.44-46 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā vismitaḥ so'tha ānartādhipatirnṛpaḥ \|*  
*paścāttāpaṃ paraṃ cakre dhiṅmayaivamanuṣṭhitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sa nūnaṃ vibudhaḥ ko'pi viprarūpeṇa saṃgataḥ \|*  
*yenedṛśaḥ prabhāvo'yaṃ tasya maṃtrasya saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yadyahaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi tasya mantroditaṃ jalam \|*  
*jarāmaraṇahīnastu tadbhavābhi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. On seeing it, the Ānarta king was wonder-struck. He regretted and said: “Fie upon me! I have committed this blunder. Indeed that was some divine being who had come here in the form of a Brāhmaṇa. The power of his Mantra is such as this!! If only I had accepted the Mantra charged holy water I would have become one free from death and old age.”

## \|\| 1.278.47 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya taddinaṃ vismitasya ca \|*  
*pārthivasya dvijaśreṣṭhā jātaṃ varṣaśatopamam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even as the king thought thus with wonder and dismay, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that single day became (i.e. was fell as long as) a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.278.48 \|\|

*divase tu samākrāṃte kathaṃcittasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*vibhāvarī kṣayaṃ yāti kathaṃcinnaiva śāradī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The day was somehow passed by the king but the autumnal night appeared to be never-ending.

## \|\| 1.278.49 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhātasamaye samutthāya mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*āhvayāmāsa śākalyaṃ puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After daybreak the king got up and summoned Śākalya through trustworthy servants.

## \|\| 1.278.50-51 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca vinayātsādaraṃ prāṃjaliḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*kalye śiṣyaḥ samāyāto yastvadīyo mamāṃtikam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śāṃtyarthaṃ preṣaṇīyastu so'dyāpi ca dvijottama \|*  
*tasyopari parā bhaktirmama jātā'dya kevalam \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. With humility and respect, the king stood with palms joined in reverence. He said: “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, yesterday one of your disciples had come to me for the Śānti rite. He should be sent today also. I feel drawn towards him with great devotion.”

## \|\| 1.278.52 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya gatvā'tha nijamandiram \|*  
*provāca yājñavalkyaṃ ca śāṃtyarthaṃ ślakṣṇayā girā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He promised “So it shall be” and returned to his abode. He spoke to Yājñavalkya in sweet words referring to the Śānti rite:

## \|\| 1.278.53 \|\|

*gaccha vatsa tvamadyaiva pārthivasya niveśanam \|*  
*śāṃtyarthaṃ tena bhūyo'pi tvamevāśunimaṃtritaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “O dear one, today also do go to the abode of the king. He has invited you specially again.”

## \|\| 1.278.54 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ yāsyāmi taddharmye śāṃtyarthaṃ dvijapuṃgava \|*  
*anādareṇa dṛṣṭo'haṃ nāśīrme ca samāhṛtā \|\| 54 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

54\. O leading Brāhmaṇa, I will not go to his palace for the Śānti rite. I have been looked at with disrespect. My benediction was not accepted.

## \|\| 1.278.55 \|\|

*kāṣṭhopari mayā dattā tasya vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*tasmātpreṣaya cānyaṃ tvaṃ guro śiṣyaṃ vicakṣaṇam \|*  
*ānartaṃ raṃjayedyastu vivekena samanvitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I poured the holy water etc. over the stump of a Dhava tree undoubtedly at his own instance. So, O preceptor, send some other clever disciple who may humour the king of Ānarta and bring some sense to him.

## \|\| 1.278.56 \|\|

*śākalya uvāca \|*  
*rājā'deśaḥ sadā kāryaḥ puruṣairdeśavāsibhiḥ \|*  
*yogakṣemavidhānāya tathā lābhāya kevalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

Śākalya said:

56\. The command of the king should always be obeyed by persons living in the country, if only for one’s own gain and for acquiring and preserving things (so) acquired.

## \|\| 1.278.57 \|\|

*pratikūlo bhavedyastu pāthivānāṃ sa mandadhīḥ \|*  
*na tasya jāyate saukhyaṃ kathaṃciddvijasattama \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He who is against kings is dull-witted. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, he will never have happiness.

## \|\| 1.278.58 \|\|

*ye jātyādi mahotsekānna nareṃdrānupāsate \|*  
*teṣāmāmaraṇaṃ bhikṣā prāyaścittaṃ vinirmitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Begging for alms has been laid down as atonement for those who do not serve kings due to haughtiness born of higher birth etc.

## \|\| 1.278.59 \|\|

*evaṃ tayorvivadatostadā vai guruśiṣyayoḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'pi tatra saṃprāptāḥ puruṣāḥ pārthiveritāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Even as the preceptor (Śākalya) and the disciple (Yājñavalkya) were arguing thus, the servants sent by the king once again came there.

## \|\| 1.278.60 \|\|

*procuśca tvarayā yuktāḥ śākalyaṃ prāṃjalisthitāḥ \|*  
*śiṣyaṃ taṃ preṣaya kṣipraṃ rājā mārgaṃ pratīkṣate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In their hurry they said to Śākalya with palms joined in reverence: “Do send that disciple quickly. The king is waiting for him.”

## \|\| 1.278.61 \|\|

*asakṛtprocyamāno'pi yadā gacchati naiva saḥ \|*  
*tadā saṃpreṣayāmāsa uddālakamathāruṇim \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In spite of being repeatedly urged he did not go. Then he sent Uddālaka, the son of Āruṇi.

## \|\| 1.278.62-63 \|\|

*śiṣyaṃ vinayasaṃpannaṃ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaṃ sthitam \|*  
*gaccha vatsa samādeśātsāṃprataṃ nṛpamaṃdiram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*śāṃtikarma vidhāyātha svādhyāyaṃ ca tataḥ kuru \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. He was one of his humble (obedient) disciples and was (standing) by his side with palms joined in reverence. “Do go, O dear one, to the abode of the king at his bidding. After performing the Śāntika rite proceed with your self-study of the Vedas.”

## \|\| 1.278.64 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya gatvā taṃ pārthivālayam \|*  
*cakāra śāṃtikaṃ karma vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He promised “So it shall be” and went to the abode of the king. He then performed the Śāntika rite in accordance with the injunctions for the rites.

## \|\| 1.278.65 \|\|

*tataḥ kalaśatoyaṃ sa sākṣataṃ sumanonvitam \|*  
*gṛhītvopādravattatra yatra rājā vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Taking the holy water in the pot along with raw rice grains and flowers, he came to the place where the king was seated.

## \|\| 1.278.66 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*svakīyamantraliṃgena abhiṣekaṃ tu yaccha bhoḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭhasyāsya yadagre te protthitaṃ tiṣṭhate dvija \|\| 66 \|\|*

The king said:

66\. O Brāhmaṇa, give the ablution uttering the requisite Mantras unto the stump of the tree which is seen high up in front of you.

## \|\| 1.278.67 \|\|

*tatastena śubhaṃ maṃtraṃ procyābhīṣṭaṃ jalaṃ svayam \|*  
*abhiṣicya ca tatkāṣṭhaṃ tataśca svagṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then he uttered the Mantras and sprinkled the water over the stump. Then he went home.

## \|\| 1.278.68 \|\|

*tāvadrūpaṃ ca tatkāṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvā'narto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*viṣādasahitaścaiva paścāttāpasamanvitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He saw the stump of the tree as it was originally. King Ānarta became sad and he regretted (for his previous conduct).

## \|\| 1.278.69 \|\|

*bhūyastu preṣayāmāsa yājñavalkyakṛte tadā \|*  
*anyaṃ dūtaṃ vidagdhaṃ ca śākalyasya dvijāśrayam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The king thereupon sent another efficient messenger to the abode of Śākalya for the sake of fetching Yājñavalkya:

## \|\| 1.278.70-73 \|\|

*vedanā kāyasaṃsthā me vartate dvijasattama \|*  
*śāṃtyarthaṃ preṣayā kṣipraṃ taṃ śiṣyaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*apamānaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya mayā kalye dvijottama \|*  
*tena me sahasā vyādhirāśīrvādamanicchataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tasmātpreṣaya me śīghraṃ yena me svasthatā bhavem \|*  
*asakṛtprocyamāno'pi yadā naiva sa gacchati \|\| 72 \|\|*

*yājñavalkyastataḥ śiṣyamanyaṃ provāca sādaram \|*  
*tatastaṃ madhukaṃ paigyaṃ preṣayāmāsa tadgṛhe \|\| 73 \|\|*

70-73. “O excellent Brāhmaṇa, there is pain all over my body. Send the disciple previously referred to quickly for the purpose of the Śānti rite.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, yesterday he was insulted by me. That accounts for my sudden ailment, as I did not express my wish for benediction directly.

Hence send him quickly to me so that I can feel relief.”

In spite of being urged repeatedly, Yājñavalkya did not go. So he said pleadingly to another disciple. Hence Madhuka Paiṅgya was sent to the royal abode.

## \|\| 1.278.74 \|\|

*tenāpi vihitaṃ tacca yathoddālakanirmitam \|*  
*āśīrvādo nṛpoddeśāddattaḥ kāṣṭhasya tasya ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. What was performed by Uddālaka was performed by him too. According to the king’s direction the benediction was offered to the stump of the tree.

## \|\| 1.278.75 \|\|

*tadrūpamapi tatkāṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo'pi pārthivaḥ \|*  
*anyaṃ saṃpreṣayāmāsa yājñavalkyakṛte naram \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On seeing the stump of the tree unchanged in form, the king once again sent another man for fetching Yājñvalkya.

## \|\| 1.278.76 \|\|

*asakṛtprocyamāno'pi yājñavalkyo vrajenna hi \|*  
*yadā tadā bahuguṇamanyaṃ śiṣyaṃ pradiṣṭavān \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In spite of being repeatedly asked to go Yājñavalkya would not go. Then he sent another disciple of many qualities.

## \|\| 1.278.77 \|\|

*pracūḍaṃ bhāgavittiṃ ca so'pi gatvā yathā purā \|*  
*cakāra śāṃtikaṃ karma yathā tābhyāṃ purā kṛtam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. It was Pracūḍa Bhāgavitti (Son of Bhagavitti). He too went there like the other two earlier ones and performed the Śāntika rite as done by them before.

## \|\| 1.278.78 \|\|

*tataḥ śāṃtyudakaṃ tasminprākṣipaccaiva dāruṇi \|*  
*maṃtravacca tathāpyeva tadrūpaṃ ca vyavasthitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thereafter, he poured the holy water of the Śāntika rite over the wood with due utterance of the Mantra. Yet it remained unaltered from its original form.

## \|\| 1.278.79 \|\|

*tataḥ svayaṃ yayau rājā śākalyasya niveśanam \|*  
*yājñavalkyasya mantrārthaṃ paścāttāpasamanvitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then the king himself with due regret for his earlier misdemeanour went to the abode of Sākalya for the purpose of inviting, Yājñavalkya.

## \|\| 1.278.80 \|\|

*praṇamya sa dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ śākalyaṃ ca dvijottamam \|*  
*śāṃtyarthaṃ mama harmye tvaṃ kalye śiṣyaṃ samādiśa \|*  
*yena me jāyate śāṃtiḥ śarīrasya dvijottama \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, he bowed down to the excellent Brāhmaṇa Śākalya (and said): “Instruct your disciple to come to my palace in the morning for performing the Śānti rite so that, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, there shall be (restored) calmness and relief in my body.”

## \|\| 1.278.81 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca śākalyo yājñavalkyaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'pi śṛṇvatastasya ānartasya mahīpateḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thereupon, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Śākalya said to Yājñavalkya once again even as the king Ānarta remained listening:

## \|\| 1.278.82 \|\|

*yājñavalkya drutaṃ gaccha mamādeśānnṛpālayam \|*  
*rājñosya roganāśāya śāṃtikaṃ kuru putraka \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. “O dear son Yājñavalkya, at my bidding do go quickly to the abode of the king and perform the Śāntika rite for the purpose of quelling the ailment of this king.”

## \|\| 1.278.83 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi guro maivaṃ bravīhi mām \|*  
*apamānaḥ kṛto'nena guro mama mahībhujā \|\| 83 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

83\. I will not go there, O revered Sir. Do not tell me to do so. O venerable one, I have been insulted by the king.

## \|\| 1.278.84 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa kopaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*abravīdbhartsamānastu yājñavalkyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On hearing his words (Śākalya) became extremely angry. Then he rebuked Yājñavalkya and said:

## \|\| 1.278.85-86 \|\|

*ekamapyakṣaraṃ yastu guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā cānṛṇī bhavet \|\| 85 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ śiṣyatāṃ gatvā mama vākyaṃ karoṣi na \|*  
*tasmāttvāṃ yojayiṣyāmi brahma śāpena sāṃpratam \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. “If a preceptor imparts but a single syllable to a disciple, there is no such article on the earth by giving which he (disciple) can get redemption from the indebtedness to him.

Since, after being my disciple (for a long period) you do not carry out my instructions, I am going to subject you to my Brahma-Śāpa (Brāhmaṇa’s curse).”

## \|\| 1.278.87 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*anyāyena hi cecchāpaṃ guro mama pradāsyasi \|*  
*ahamapyeva dāsyāmi pratiśāpaṃ tavādhunā \|\| 87 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

87\. O venerable Sir, if you are going to curse me unjustifiably, I will also curse you in return now.

## \|\| 1.278.88 \|\|

*gurorapyavaliptasya kāryākāryamajānataḥ \|*  
*utpathe vartamānasya parityāgo vidhīyate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. He may be a preceptor but if he is haughty, does not know distinctly what should or should not be done and proceeds along the wrong path, it is laid down (in scriptures) that he be abandoned.

## \|\| 1.278.89 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ hi mayā tyaktaḥ sāṃprataṃ hi na me guruḥ \|*  
*aviśaṣeṇa śiṣyārthaṃ yadādeśaṃ prayacchasi \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Hence you have been abandoned by me. You are no longer my preceptor since you pass orders to the disciple indiscriminately.

## \|\| 1.278.90 \|\|

*yāvaṃtaste sthitāḥ śiṣyāstāvadbhirdivasairaham \|*  
*tavādeśaṃ kariṣyāmi nocedyāsyāmi dūrataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Within as many days as you have disciples here, I will either carry out your directions or else go away far off.

## \|\| 1.278.91 \|\|

*śākalya uvāca \|*  
*yadi gacchasi cānyatra tattvaṃ vidyāṃ parityaja \|*  
*yāṃ mayā pāṭhitaḥ pāpa vraja paścātkuśiṣya bhoḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

Śākalya said:

91\. If you wish to go elsewhere then give up the knowledge that I have taught you, O sinful, evil disciple. You can go thereafter.

## \|\| 1.278.92 \|\|

*mayābhimaṃtritaṃ toyaṃ kṣurikāmuṇḍasaṃbhavam \|*  
*piba tasyāḥ prabhāveṇa śīghrameva tyajiṣyasi \|*  
*jaṭharānmāmakīṃ vidyāṃ tvayādhītā purā tu yā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Holy water has been charged with the Atharvaṇa Mantra, kṣurikā muṇḍa etc. by me. Drink it. By its power you will soon cast off from your belly the knowledge taught by me and acquired by you earlier.

## \|\| 1.278.93 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa cāmaṃtrya maṃtrairātharvaṇairjalam \|*  
*pānāya pradadau tasmai vāṃtyarthaṃ sadvijottamaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. After saying this he charged the holy water with the Atharvaṇa Mantra. The excellent Brāhmaṇa then gave it to the disciple so that he might vomit it out.

## \|\| 1.278.94 \|\|

*yājñavalkyo'pi tatpītvā jalaṃ tenābhimaṃtritam \|*  
*vāṃtiṃ kṛtvā sahānnena tadvidyāṃ tāṃ parityajat \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Yājñvalkya quaffed off the holy water charged by him with Mantras. He then vomited his lore along with the food taken in. He cast off the lore.

## \|\| 1.278.95 \|\|

*tato mūḍhatvamāpanno viśvāmitrahradaṃ śubham \|*  
*gatvā snāto vidhānena śuci rbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Thereupon, he became deluded and ignorant. He went to the holy Viśvāmitra Hrada and took his holy bath in accordance with the injunctions. He thus became clean and endowed with concentration.

## \|\| 1.278.96 \|\|

*cakāra mūrtīstā bhaktyā raverdvādaśasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya tataḥ sarvāḥ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He made twelve images of the twelve Ādityas, installed them and worshipped them devoutly.

## \|\| 1.278.97 \|\|

*dhātā mitro'ryamā śakro varuṇaḥ sāṃba eva ca \|*  
*bhago vivasvānpūṣā ca savitā daśamastathā \|*  
*ekādaśastathā tvaṣṭā viṣṇurdvādaśa ucyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The twelve Adityas \[Ādityas\] are: Dhātā, Mitra, Aryamā, Śakra, Varuṇa, Sāṃba, Bhaga, Vivasvān, Pūṣan, the tenth one Savitṛ, the eleventh one Tvaṣṭṛ and the twelfth Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.278.98 \|\|

*evaṃ dvādaśadhā sūryaḥ sthāpito'tra vipaścitā \|*  
*ārādhitastato nityaṃ gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The Sun-god was installed by the learned one in twelve forms. Then all the different Ādityas were propitiated by him everyday with sweet scents, flowers and unguents.

## \|\| 1.278.99 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā gatvā pratyakṣatāṃ raviḥ \|*  
*provāca sundaraṃ prītyā vākyametanmuniṃ prati \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. After a long time, Ravi appeared before him and said charming words to this sage:

## \|\| 1.278.100 \|\|

*yājñavalkya pratuṣṭo'haṃ tava brāhmaṇasattama \|*  
*iṣṭaṃ dadāmi te brūhi yadyatsaṃprati vāṃchitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. “O Yājñavalkya, I am much delighted with you, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. I shall grant you what is desired. Tell me now whatever has been desired by you.”

## \|\| 1.278.101 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ dadāsi cenmahyaṃ vedapāṭhe niyojaya \|*  
*māṃ vibho yena śiṣyatvaṃ tava gacchāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 101 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

101\. If you wish to grant me a boon, engage me in the study of the Vedas. O Lord, therefore, I shall become your disciple now.

## \|\| 1.278.102 \|\|

*āditya uvāca \|*  
*mayā paryaṭanaṃ kāryaṃ sadaiva dvijasattama \|*  
*meroḥ pradakṣiṇārthāya lokālokakṛte dvija \|\| 102 \|\|*

Āditya said:

102\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, I have to be always moving about. It is to circumambulate the Meru, O Brāhmaṇa, and for the illumination of the whole world.

## \|\| 1.278.103 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ yojayāmi tvāṃ vedapāṭhena sa dvija \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, how can I engage you in the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.278.104-106 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ laghutāṃ gatvā mama mukhyahayasya ca \|*  
*śravaṇe tiṣṭha madvākyāttejasā caiva yena me \|\| 104 \|\|*

*na dahyasi mahābhāga tatra stho'dhyayanaṃ kuru \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya praviśyādityavājinaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*karṇe'paṭhattato vedāṃścaturo'pi ca tanmukhāt \|*  
*aṃgopāṃgasamopetānpariśiṣṭasamanvitān \|\| 106 \|\|*

104-106. So become small in form and stay in the ear of my chief horse at my instance. Thereby, O highly esteemed one, you will not get singed by my refulgence. Settled there you can study.

He promised, “It shall be so” and entered the ear of the horse of the Sun. From there he learnt all the four Vedas from his mouth with their Aṅgas, Upāṅgas and the Pariśiṣṭas (appendices).

## \|\| 1.278.107 \|\|

*tataḥ samāpte sa prāha prārthayasva vibho hi mām \|*  
*pradāsyāmi na sandehastavādya gurudakṣiṇām \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. When it was concluded he said: “O Lord, say to me. I shall undoubtedly give you the fee due to the preceptor.”

## \|\| 1.278.108-109 \|\|

*āditya uvāca \|*  
*yāni sūktāni ṛgvede madīyāni dvijottama \|*  
*sāvanāni yajurvede sāmāni ca tṛtīyake \|\| 108 \|\|*

*kalpoktāni caturthe ca tāni sarvāṇi bhūtale \|*  
*tvayā pracāraṇīyāni kṛtvā vyākhyānamuttamam \|\| 109 \|\|*

Āditya said:

108-109. You must propagate Sūktas of the Ṛgveda, Sāvanas of the Yajurved \[Yajurveda?\], Sāmans of the third and the Kalpoktas of the fourth, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. They all must be propagated with excellent exposition by you on the earth.

## \|\| 1.278.110 \|\|

*ye dvijāstāni sarvāṇi kīrtayiṣyaṃti me puraḥ \|*  
*te sarve pāpa nirmuktāḥ prayāsyaṃti divālayam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Those Brāhmaṇas who recite all of them before me will be relieved of sins. They will go to heaven.

## \|\| 1.278.111 \|\|

*vyākhyāsyaṃti punarye ca mama bhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*te yāsyaṃti dvijā muktiṃ satyametanmayoditam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Those who are devout and write further comments thereon, O Brāhmaṇa, will attain salvation. It is the truth that has been uttered by me.

## \|\| 1.278.112 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vedānpaṭhitvā sa pradattvā gurudakṣiṇām \|*  
*sūryāyābhyāgato bhūyaścamatkārapuraṃ prati \|\| 112 \|\|*

Sūta said:

112\. He learnt the Vedas, gave the Gurudakṣiṇā (fee in return for the study) to the Sun-god and returned once again to Camatkārapura.

## \|\| 1.278.113 \|\|

*tataḥ śākalyamabhyetya gurustvaṃ prāṅ mama sthitaḥ \|*  
*prārthayasva mahābhāga dāsyāmi gurudakṣiṇām \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. He then approached Śākalya and said: “You have been my previous preceptor. O highly esteemed one, ask for Gurudakṣiṇā

## \|\| 1.278.114 \|\|

*jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā caiva mātā caiva gurustathā \|*  
*vairuddhyenāpi vartaṃte yadyete dvijasatama \|*  
*tathāpi pūjanīyāśca puruṣeṇa na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. The elder brother, father, mother and preceptor, even if these are opposed to oneself, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, should be revered. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.278.115-116 \|\|

*sāṃgopāṃgā mayādhītā vedāścatvāra eva ca \|*  
*adhītāścaiva sarveṣāṃ teṣāmartho'vadhāritaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ vada mahābhāga kāṃ te yacchāmi dakṣiṇām \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. All the four Vedas were learned by me along with their Aṅgas and Upāṅgas. Further the meanings of all of them were understood. Hence, O highly esteemed one, speak out what Dakṣiṇā should I offer to you?”

## \|\| 1.278.117-118 \|\|

*śākalya uvāca \|*  
*yāni vedarahasyāni sūryeṇa kathitāni te \|\| 117 \|\|*

*yaiḥ syātpāpapraṇāśaśca vyākhyātaiḥ paṭhitaistathā \|*  
*tāni me kīrtaya kṣiprameṣā me gurudakṣiṇā \|\| 118 \|\|*

Śākalya said:

117-118. Whatever secrets of the Vedas have been imparted to you by the Sun-god recount them to me quickly. If they are learned and commented upon, sins can be dispelled. This is my Gurudakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 1.278.119 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*tadāgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ yatra sūryāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*mayā dvādaśa teṣāṃ ca kīrtayiṣyāmi cātrataḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

119\. So do come along with me to the place where the twelve Ādityas have been installed by me. I shall expound everything in their presence.

## \|\| 1.278.120 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śiṣyasaṃyuktaḥ śākalyastaiśca saddvijaiḥ \|*  
*śiṣyaistiṣṭhanti ye tatra sthāpitāstena bhāskarāḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. On hearing it, Śākalya went there along with his disciples and excellent Brāhmaṇas. He stood there where the Bhāskaras had been installed by him (Yājñavalkya).

## \|\| 1.278.121 \|\|

*tatastu kīrtayāmāsa vyākhyānaṃ tatpuraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vedāntānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yathoktaṃ raviṇā purā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Then standing before them, he narrated the commentary. He expounded all the Vedāntas as told by Ravi earlier.

## \|\| 1.278.122 \|\|

*avasāne ca teṣāṃ tu catuścaraṇasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇairyājñavalkyastu vedāntajñaiḥ pratoṣitaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. At the conclusion Yājñavalkya was propitiated by those Brāhmaṇas born in families following the four Vedas and conversant with the Vedānta.

## \|\| 1.278.123 \|\|

*proktastava prasādena vedāṃtajñā vayaṃ sthitāḥ \|*  
*śrutādhyayanasaṃpannā yācasva gurudakṣiṇām \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. He was requested: “It is due to your favour that we have become conversant with Vedanta and well learned in Vedic study. Ask for the Gurudakṣiṇā.”

## \|\| 1.278.124 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*eteṣāṃ bhāskarāṇāṃ ca madīyānāṃ puro dvijāḥ \|*  
*kīrtayiṣyaṃti ye viprāsteṣāṃ yuṣmatprasādataḥ \|*  
*bhūyā svargagatirviprā eṣā me guru dakṣiṇā \|\| 124 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

124\. My Gurudakṣiṇā is: Those Brāhmaṇas who expound the Vedas in front of these my Bhāskaras (i.e. Bhāskaras installed by me) should have access to heaven with your favour.

## \|\| 1.278.125 \|\|

*ye punarbhaktisaṃyuktāḥ kariṣyaṃti vicāraṇam \|*  
*teṣāṃ turyapadaṃ yacca jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Those who are endowed with devotion and conduct discourses, shall attain the fourth region bereft of death and old age.

## \|\| 1.278.126 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kalau viprā dausthyabhāvasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*paṭhane naiva śaktāśca vyākhyānasya ca kā kathā \|\| 126 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

126\. In Kali Age, Brāhmaṇas will be ignorant. They will not be capable of even reciting, to say nothing of expounding, them.

## \|\| 1.278.127 \|\|

*tasmātsārasvataṃ brūhi vedānāṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*api dausthyasamāyuktā yena te kīrtayaṃti ca \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, mention the essence (gist) of the Vedas. Thereby even ignorant persons can recite them.

## \|\| 1.278.128-135 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*rathaṃ yuñjaṃti sūktaṃ yatprathamaṃ vittalakṣaṇam \|*  
*triṣṭubheti ca yatsūktaṃ tathādyaṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*citraṃ devānāmiti ca tathānyattasya vallabham \|*  
*haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityuktaṃ tataścāpi praharṣadam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*pāvamānaṃ tathā sūktaṃ ye paṭhiṣyaṃti bahvṛcaḥ \|*  
*ityeṣāmādyamevaṃ tu te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 130 \|\|*

*ekaviṃśatisāmāni ādityeṣṭāni yāni ca \|*  
*sāmagāḥ kīrtayiṣyaṃti ye'trasthāḥ śucayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

*niścayaṃ tu paraṃ dhṛtvā ye'pi stoṣyaṃti bhāskaram \|*  
*tataste'pi prayāsyaṃti nirbhidya ravimaṃḍalam \|\| 132 \|\|*

*kṣurikāsaṃpuṭaṃ caiva sūryakalpaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*śāṃtikalpasamāyuktaṃ kīrtayiṣyaṃti ye dvijāḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

*atharvapāṭhakāste'pi prayāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*mūrkhā api samāgatya saṃprāpte sūryavāsare \|\| 134 \|\|*

*praṇāmaṃ ye kariṣyaṃti śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|*  
*saptarātrakṛtātpāpānmuktiṃ prāpsaṃti te dvijāḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

Yājñavalkya said:

128-135. (His advice in brief:) The Brāhmaṇas of Ṛk Śākhā should recite at least these Sūktas, the Sūkta beginning with rathaṃ yuñjanti: the Sūkta beginning with Triṣṭubh, that beginning with citram devānām (RV. I. 115), haṃsaḥ śuciṣat, etc. and also the Pāvamāna Sūkta commonly recited by Bahvṛcs (persons conversant with many Ṛk Mantras).

Yajurvedins should recite these Ṛk Sūktas, Sāmavedins shall recite the twenty-one Sāmans loved by Āditya. These shall be sung by those Sāmagas who are pure and stay here. Those who retain in memory the decisive meaning and eulogize Bhāskara will be able to pierce the solar disc.

Atharvapāṭhaka Brāhmaṇas who recite Sūryakalpa and Śāntikalpa in Kṣurikāsaṃpuṭa, will attain the greatest goal.

Even foolish (ignorant) persons should assemble together on Sunday and bow down to the Sun-god with great faith. Those Brāhmaṇas shall be relieved of the sins committed in the seven previous days and nights.

## \|\| 1.278.136 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatheti taiḥ pratijñāte catuścaraṇasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇairyājñavalkyastu vijñāto yena kena tu \|\| 136 \|\|*

Sūta said:

136\. When the Brāhmaṇas of the four Vedas promised saying, “So it shall be”, Yājñavalkya became well-known to all of them.

## \|\| 1.278.137 \|\|

*videhena tataḥ prāptaḥ śravaṇārthaṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*vedāṃtānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ ratnākhyena mahībhujā \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The Videha king named Ratna (Janaka?) came there to listen to all the Vedāntas.

## \|\| 1.278.138 \|\|

*tenāpi ca parijñāya māhātmyaṃ sūryasaṃ bhavam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃsthāpitaḥ sūryastasminsthāne dvijottamāḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. He too realized the greatness of the Sun-god, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, and installed him at that spot.

## \|\| 1.278.139 \|\|

*taṃ cāpi sūryavāreṇa yaḥ prapaśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*saptarātrakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. A man who visits that idol on a Sunday, shall be relieved of the sins committed the previous week.

## \|\| 1.278.140 \|\|

*etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ māhātmyaṃ sūryasaṃbhavam \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Thus the greatness of the Sun-god has been narrated to you all. A man who listens to it with devotion shall get the merit of a horse sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.278.141 \|\|

*saṃkrāṃtau yatpradānena sūrye vā śravaṇena tu \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti śrutvā māhātmyamutamam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. By listening to the excellent greatness, one gets that merit which one gets by making a gift on the Saṅkrānti day of the Sun or by listening to the same.

## Chapter 279 - Merit of Listening to the Purāṇa

## \|\| 1.279.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etatpurāṇamakhilaṃ purā skandenabhāṣitam \|*  
*bhṛgave brahmaputrāya tasmāllebhe tathāṃgirāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataśca cyavanaḥ prāpa sa ṛcīkastato muniḥ \|*  
*evaṃ paraṃparāprāptaṃ sarveṣu bhuvaneṣvapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*skāṃdaṃ purāṇametacca kumāreṇa puroddhṛtam \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti satāṃ madhye naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-3. The whole of this Purāṇa was formerly narrated by Skanda to Bhṛgu. The son of Brahmā-Aṅgiras learnt it from him. Then Cyavana got it. Thereafter Sage Ṛcīka got it. Thus this text was traditionally handed over to all in all the worlds. A man who listens to this Skanda Purāṇa retold formerly by Kumāra becomes redeemed from sins.

## \|\| 1.279.4 \|\|

*idaṃ purāṇamāyuṣyaṃ varṇānāṃ ca sukhāvaham \|*  
*nirmitaṃ ṣaṇmukheneha niyataṃ sumahātmanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This Purāṇa is conducive to longevity. It is pleasing to people of all the Varṇas. This is definitely composed by the noble-souled Six-faced Lord (Skanda).

## \|\| 1.279.5 \|\|

*evametatpurā khyātamākhyānaṃ bhadramastu vaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It was thus that this narrative became famous formerly. Welfare unto you all.

## \|\| 1.279.6 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarakṣetrasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇute naraḥ \|*  
*na tasya puṇyasaṃkhyānaṃ kartuṃ śakyeta kenacit \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. No one can calculate adequately the merit of that man who listens to the greatness of the holy place of Hāṭakeśvara.

## \|\| 1.279.7 \|\|

*ya idaṃ dharmamāhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchati \|*  
*svargaloke vasettāvadyāvadakṣarasaṃkhyayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He who gifts this text describing the greatness of Dharma to a Brāhmaṇa, shall live in heaven for as many (Kalpas) as there are syllables therein.

## \|\| 1.279.8 \|\|

*yathā hi varṣato dhārā yathā vā divi tārakāḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ sikatā yadvattadvatsaṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Just as there is no limit to the number of drops of water in the streams of downpour, just as there is no limit of the number of sand particles in Gaṅgā, so also there is no limit to the merit thereof.

## \|\| 1.279.9 \|\|

*yo naraḥ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā dināni ca kiyaṃti vai \|*  
*sarvārthasiddho bhavati ya imāṃ paṭhate kathām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A man who devoutly listens to this or reads this story for some days, shall become one who has achieved everything.

## \|\| 1.279.10 \|\|

*putrārthī labhate putrāndhanārthī labhate dhanam \|*  
*labhate patikāmā yā patiṃ kanyā manoramam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person who seeks a son gets sons; one who seeks wealth gets wealth; a woman who desires a husband gets a husband; and a girl gets a charming bridegroom.

## \|\| 1.279.11 \|\|

*samāgamaṃ labhaṃte ca vāṃdhavāśca pravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*skāṃdaṃ purāṇaṃ śrutvā tu pumānā pnoti vāṃchitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By listening to the Skandapurāṇa kinsmen get united with those who have gone abroad; a man gets what is desired.

## \|\| 1.279.12 \|\|

*śṛṇvataḥ paṭhataścaiva sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*mahīṃ vijayate rājā śatrūṃścāpyadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This scripture bestows all desired things on men, on one who listens and who reads. A king conquers the earth and rules over the enemies.

## \|\| 1.279.13 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ śrutvā purāṇaṃ vai dīrghamā yuśca viṃdati \|*  
*vedavicca bhavedvipraḥ kṣatriyo rājyamāpnuyāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By listening to the meritorious Purāṇa, one gets long life. A Brāhmaṇa becomes conversant with the Vedas. A Kṣatriya obtains kingdom.

## \|\| 1.279.14 \|\|

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā vaiśyaḥ śūdraḥ sukhamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaḥ ślokapādaṃ śṛṇuyādviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A Vaiśya gets wealth and food-grains. A Śūdra attains happiness. He who listens to even a fourth of a verse goes to the region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.279.15 \|\|

*śrutvā purāṇametaddhi vācakaṃ yastu pūjayet \|*  
*tena brahmā ca viṣṇuśca rudraścaiva prapūjitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If after listening to this Purāṇa, anyone adores the expounder, it is as good as the adoration of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra.

## \|\| 1.279.16 \|\|

*ekamapyakṣaraṃ yastu guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet \|*  
*pṛthivyā nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā hyanṛṇī bhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If a preceptor teaches at least a syllable to a disciple, there is no object in the whole of the earth by giving which, he can become free from indebtedness.

## \|\| 1.279.17 \|\|

*ataḥ saṃpūjanīyastu vyāsaḥ śāstropadeśakaḥ \|*  
*gobhūhiraṇyavastrādyairbhojanaiḥ sārva kāmikaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence Vyāsa (expounder of the Purāṇa) is to be adequately adored with cows, plots of land, gold, garments etc. and foodstuffs which all like, because he is the scriptural instructor.

## \|\| 1.279.18 \|\|

*ya evaṃ bhaktiyuktastu śrutvā śāstramanutamam \|*  
*pūjayedupadeṣṭāraṃ sa śaivaṃ padamāpnuyāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who is endowed with devotion, listens to the excellent scripture and adores the expounder shall attain the region of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.279.19 \|\|

*purāṇaśravaṇādeva anekabhavasaṃcitam \|*  
*pāpaṃ praśamamāyāti sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Only by listening to the Purāṇa the sin accumulated in the course of many births becomes quelled. He derives the benefit of all the Tīrthas.

:: End of Nāgara Khaṇḍa ::
